eng: Pakistan gingerly marks the end of a long nine year dynasty.
swa: Ni katika hali ya tahadhari kubwa kwamba Pakistani inaadhimisha mwisho huu wa miaka tisa ya utawala wa familia hii.

eng: His concluding remarks were mostly a walk back into history as penned down by The Pakistani Spectator, which was just to highlight his services for the people and for the country.
swa: Hotuba yake ya mwisho ilijaa hasa kurejelea historia na hii ni kama ilivyonukuliwa na The Pakistani Spectator, yaani hasa kuelezea ni kwa namna gani alitumikia nchi na watu wake.

eng: Pakistani bloggers reacted with mixed feelings, on one hand some celebrated Musharraf by chiming in with the 'For he is a Jolly Good Fellow' tune, while some faithfuls were quick to lend him a standing ovation but most cautiously celebrated the end of a dictatorship.
swa: Wanablogu wa KiPakistani walipokea taarifa hizi kwa hisia tofauti, wapo waliomshabikia kwa miluzi yenye kuashiria kwamba alikuwa ‘a Jolly Good Fellow’ (mtu mwema na mchangamfu), wakati huohuo washabiki wake waaminifu hawakukawia kumpigia mbija za kumpongeza, hata hivyo wapo waliochukua hali hii kwa tahadhari huku wakisherehekea kumalizika kwa utawala wa kidikteta.

eng: Sarcastically Yeah That too had a few words to share, Ammar wrote about how the new 'Cat Fight' is now about to begin, Chowrangi talks about Pakistan's future after Musharraf, Psychotic Discourses sheds light on the new form of Demon-cracy, MB confuses us with the talk about circle of circuses.
swa: Katika namna ya kukejeli, Yeah That Too alishirikisha maneno machache, Ammar kwa upande wake aliandika kuhusu namna ‘Mpambano mpya wa manyau’ unavyokaribia kuanza, Chowrangi anazungumizia mustakabali wa nchi ya Pakistani baada ya Musharraf, Psychotic Discourses anatupatia mwanga juu ya muundo mpya wa ‘Utawala wa Kishetani’ (Demon-cracy), wakati ambapo MB anatuchanganya zaidi kwa kuzungumizia hali hii kama moja ya mizunguko ya kisarakasi.

eng: The immediate question that remains lurking is whether Musharraf is allowed to seek asylum outside of Pakistan or will he be put to trial for the charges alleged against him.
swa: Swali kubwa kwa sasa linabaki kuwa endapo Musharraf anaruhusiwa kutafuta ukimbizi nje ya Pakistani au endapo atafikishwa mbele ya sheria ili kujibu tuhuma mbalimbali zinazomkabili.

eng: Its definitely a tough juncture for Pakistan with a lot at stake.
swa: Ama kwa hakika ni changamoto kubwa kwa Taifa la Pakistani na ambayo inaweza kuwa na matokeo mengi.

eng: One does wonder what next, wherein lies a huge mixture of political wannabes eying for the top slot, though the onus of pulling the country out of the mess lies squarely on the shoulder of Asif Zardari and Nawaz Sharif, both unelected politicians entrusted with the faith of a nation to hopefully pull this country out of the mess it now finds itself in.
swa: Mtu anabaki kujiuliza, hivi nini kinafuata, hasa katika kipindi hiki ambapo kuna wanasiasa wenye matumaini ya kunyakua cheo hicho cha juu zaidi katika taifa hili, ambapo hata hivyo jukumu la kuiondoa nchi katika mkanganyiko huu mkubwa liko zaidi mabegani mwa Asif Zardari na Nawaz Sharif, ambapo wote wawili ni wanasiasa ambao hawakuchaguliwa lakini ambao wengi wanawawekea matumaini makubwa ya kuiondoa nchi hii kutoka katika lindi la vurugu ambamo imo kwa sasa.

eng: Ali Kordan, Iran's new Minister of the Interior, has recently been under fire for presenting a "fake" Ph.D. degree from the prestigious Oxford University in the United Kingdom.
swa: Ali Kordan,Waziri wa Mambo ya Ndani wa Irani, Katika siku za hivi karibuni, ameshutumiwa vikali kwa kuonyesha Shahada 'feki' ya Udaktari (PhD) aliyodai kupata kutoka katika chuo kikuu chenye sifa kubwa duniani cha Oxford cha nchini Uingereza.

eng: Several websites, including the conservative Alef have published a scan of Kordan's "Oxford Honorary Doctorate of Law Degree".
swa: Tovuti mbalimbali, pamoja na ile ya kihafidhina wa Alef, zimechapisha picha ya cheti hicho 'feki' cha Kordan kinachoonyesha kwamba ametunukiwa Shahada ya Udaktari wa Heshima na Chuo Kikuu cha Oxford.

eng: Alef points out that there are several grammatical errors in the so called Oxford certificate, such as: "to be benefitted from its scientific privileges".
swa: Alef inaonyesha makosa kadhaa ya kiuandishi yaliyojitokeza kwenye cheti hicho kinachodaiwa kuwa cha Oxford, kwa mfano, “to be benefitted from its scientific privileges”.

eng: Also, "entitled" was spelled "intitled".
swa: Pia neno“entitled” liliandikwa kimakosa “intitled”.

eng: Alef has also uploaded several faxes that this site exchanged with Oxford University on the issue.
swa: Vilevile tovuti ya Alef imepandisha kwenye ukurasa wake faksi kadhaa ambazo iliandikiana na Chuo Kikuu cha Oxford kuhusiana na jambo hili.

eng: The website was then filtered in Iran.
swa: Baada ya hapo tovuti hiyo ilizuiwa kuonekana nchini Iran.

eng: While Iranian authorities are investigating this case, Oxford University announced that they have no record of Mr. Kordan graduating from there.
swa: Wakati ambapo mamlaka nchini Irani inafanya upelelezi kuhusiana na jambo hili, Chuo Kikuu cha Oxford kimetangaza kwamba hakina kumbukumbu kwamba Bwana Kordan alipata kuhitimu katika chuo hicho.

eng: Iranian blogger, Mr. Behi, writes:
swa: Mwanablogu wa Irani, Bwana Behi, anaandika:

eng: President Ahmadinejad performed yet another miracle: He selected someone as interior minister who claimed to have a Ph.D. degree in law from The University of Oxford!
swa: Rais Ahmadinejad amefanya muujiza mwingine. Amemteua mtu anayedai kuwa na Shahada ya Udaktari katika Sheria kutoka Chuo Kikuu cha Oxford kama waziri wa mambo ya ndani!

eng: When questions rose on the authenticity of the degree, the guy outraged, threatened the media and produced this to shut them up.
swa: Yalipoibuliwa maswali kuhusu uhalisia wa shahada hiyo, huyo jamaa alijawa na jazba, alivitishia vyombo vya habari na kuonyesha cheti chake hiki.

eng: A degree so suspicious that is feared to be faked, with grammar mistakes and with names signing it who are not even members of the Faculty of Law!
swa: Cheti chenyewe kinatia mashaka makubwa na kinadhaniwa kuwa ni cha kughushi, tena kimejaa makosa ya kiuandishi na wakati huo huo majina yanayoonekana kwenye saini wala si ya yeyote miongoni mwa wanaofundisha katika Kitivo cha Sheria cha chuo hicho!

eng: If Ahmadinejad wants to fake the next election, he'd better employ someone who does it less obviously.
swa: Ikiwa Ahmadinejad anataka kughushi katika uchaguzi ujao, basi heri atafute mtu makini wa kumsaidia katika kugushi pasipo kugundulika kwa urahisi.

eng: Mohmmad Ali Abtahi, former reformist vice president and blogger, writes that when he was the deputy of the Ministry of Culture and Islamic Guidance, he met an Iranian official who had "bought" his Ph.D. According to Abtahi, it seems the price was around US$1000.
swa: Mohmmad Ali Abtahi, aliyekuwa Makamu wa Rais katika serikali ya kimageuzi na ambaye pia ni mwanablogu, anaandika kwamba enzi zake alipokuwa Naibu Waziri wa Utamaduni na Miongozo ya Kiislamu, aliwahi kukutana na afisa mmoja wa Irani ambaye aliwahi 'kununua' Shahada 'feki' ya Udaktari. Abtahi anasema kwamba bei ya kununua cheti kama hicho ilikuwa ni karibu dola za Marekani 1000.

eng: According to another blogger, Shirzad it seems that Ali Kordan does not even hold an undergraduate degree.
swa: Mwanablogu mwingine, Shirzad , anadai kwamba kuna uwezekano mkubwa kuwa Ali Kordan hana hata shahada ya kwanza.

eng: The blogger adds:
swa: Mwanablogu huyu anaongeza:

eng: It means he cheated all these years and got paid as a Ph.D. holder...
swa: Inamaanisha kwamba miaka yote hii waziri huyu ametumia udanganyifu kulipwa kama mtu mwenye Shahada ya Udaktari ...

eng: One of deputies in the Iranian Parliament asked Kordan: "How did you get your Ph.D. in Law, when you say you wrote your thesis in Islamic Education?"
swa: Mmoja wa wasaidizi katika Bunge la Irani aliwahi kumuuliza Kordan: “Ulipataje Shahada yako ya Udaktari katika Sheria wakati wewe unadai kwamba uliandika Utafiti (Thesis) wako kuhusu Elimu ya Kiislamu?"

eng: How did you defend it when you cannot speak English. 	Je, ulifanya vipi utetezi wako wakati ambapo wewe huwezi kuzungumza Kiingereza?"
Kordan replied, "I had a translator."
swa: Kordan alijibu, "Nilikuwa na mfasiri."

eng: Blogger Jomhour says Iranian president, Mahmoud Ahmadinejad defended his Minister and asked, "Who needs these torn papers!"
swa: Mwanablogu Jomhour anaandika kwamba Rais wa Irani, Mahmoud Ahmadinejad alimtetea Waziri wake kwa kuuliza, "Je, ni nani aliye na haja na makaratasi haya yanayoweza kuchanwa (yasiyo na maana)!”

eng: The blogger asks:
swa: Mwanablogu huyu anauliza:

eng: if the certificates are useless, torn, paper why did Ahmadinejad's Minister pretend to have one... It is not the first time that Ahmadinejad calls official documents torn papers.
swa: Endapo vyeti havina maana, ni makaratasi yanayoweza kuchanwa wakati wowote, hivi basi kwa nini Waziri wa Ahmadinejad alijihangaisha kutafuta walau cheti hicho feki ... na hii si mara ya kwanza ambapo Rais Ahmadinejad anaita (anakebehi) nyaraka muhimu kuwa ni makaratasi yanayoweza kuchanwa wakati wowote kumaanisha kwamba hayana maana.

eng: Previously he has also called United Nations resolutions against an Iranian nuclear program just useless torn papers.
swa: Hapo mwanzo aliwahi kusema kuwa nyaraka zilizoonyesha msimamo wa Umoja wa Mataifa dhidi ya Mpango wa Nyuklia wa Irani kama makaratasi yasiyo na maana.

eng: Ali Akbar Javanfekr, Ahmadinejad's media adviser, says the Ministry of Sciences should take a decision about Kordan's Ph.D. and suggests it would be better we not to involve personal political opinions on the issue.
swa: Ali Akbar Javanfekr, Mshauri wa Rais Ahmadijad katika masuala ya mawasiliano na vyombo vya habari, anasema kwamba Wizara ya Sayansi itoe uamuzi kuhusu Shahada ya Udaktari ya Kordan na anapendekeza kwamba tusiingize au kuhusisha katika siasa mtazamo na maoni binafsi kuhusu suala hili.

eng: The final results of the Parliamentary Elections disclosed late last night by Angola's National Electoral Commission confirmed the ruling party the Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola's victory with 81,64% (5,266,216 votes).
swa: Matokeo ya mwisho ya uchaguzi wa bunge yalitolewa jana usiku na Tume ya Uchaguzi ya Taifa yamethibitisha kuwa chama tawala kijulikanacho kama Chama Maarufu kwa Ajili ya Ukombozi wa Angola (MPLA) kimeshinda kwa asilimia 81.64 (yaani kura 5, 266,216).

eng: The runner up, the main opposition party National Union for the Total Independence of Angola, had 10.39% (670,363 votes).
swa: Mshindi wa pili, chama kikuu cha upinzani cha Umoja wa Kitaifa wa Mapinduzi Kamili ya Angola (UNITA) kilipata asilimia 10.39 (yaani kura 670,363).

eng: A total of 7,213,246 Angolans went to the polls, out of 8,256,584 people who had registered to vote - an 87% turnout.
swa: Jumla ya Waangola 7,213,246 walipiga kura kati ya watu 8,256,584 waliojiandikisha kupiga kura - asilimia 87 walijitokeza.

eng: This means that the MPLA makes 191 of the 220 elected Members of Parliament, while UNITA will have 16, PRS 8 and the ND and FNLA both will have 2 seats (click here for a full list of those elected, by region).
swa: Hii inamaanisha kwamba MPLA imepata wabunge 191 kati ya 220 waliochaguliwa, wakati UNITA watakuwa na 16, PRS 8 na ND pamoja na FNLA watakuwa na viti 2. (bofya hapa kwa ajili ya orodha nzima ya wale waliochaguliwa, kimikoa).

eng: Jorge Santos from Leste de Angola was among the first bloggers announcing the following results:
swa: Jorge Santos kutoka Leste de Angola alikuwa ni mmojawapo wa mabloga waliotangaza matokeo yafuatayo:

eng: This Friday September 05 was a special day in Angola.
swa: Ijumaa hii ya tarehe 5 Septemba ilikuwa ni siku maalum katika Angola.

eng: After lukewarm elections campaigning, the population was excited to vote for a new parliament in the first elections in 16 years.
swa: Baada ya kampeni vuguvugu za uchaguzi, umma ulijawa shauku ya kupiga kura kwa ajili ya bunge jipya baada ya miaka 16.

eng: For many people, this was the first opportunity to exercise their right to vote.
swa: Kwa watu wengi, hii ilikuwa ni fursa yao ya kwanza kutumia haki yao ya kupiga kura.

eng: Most of the population went peacefully to about 12,000 polling stations, however voting is to continue today at 320 stations in the capital Luanda, due to yesterday's logistical problems that caused delays in the delivery of ballots.
swa: Wengi wa watu hao walikwenda kwa amani kwenye vituo vipatavyo 12, 000 vya kupigia kura, ingawa upigaji kura huo utaendelea katika vituo 320 vilivyoko Luanda kutokana na matatizo ya kimipango yaliyosababisha uchelevu wa makasha ya kura jijini humo.

eng: As reactions start to appear on the blogosphere, a full report is on its way. For now here are some pictures showing the run up to the historic day, registered by José Manuel Lima da Silva, Flickr user Kool2bBop, along with his own remarks:
swa: Wakati ambapo maoni yanaanza kujitokeza katika mtandao wa wanablogu, ripoti kamili iko njiani.Kwa sasa zifuatazo ni picha zinazoonyesha siku hiyo ya kihistoria, kama zinavyoorodheshwa na Jose Manuel Lima da Silva, mtumiaji wa huduma ya Flickr Kool2bBop, pamoja na nukuu zake:

eng: Hook, Line, Sinker by ToastyKen On blogs, through videos and on facebook, Colombian Diego Alejandro is exposing the deceit and scams behind pyramid schemes that masquerade as investment options.
swa: Hook, Line, Sinker na ToastyKen kuhusu blogu, Kwa kupitia picha za video na mtandao wa marafiki wa Facebook, raia wa Colombia, Diego Alejandro, anaweka wazi udanganyifu na utapeli mkubwa uliojificha nyuma ya michezo ya upatu ambayo inatangazwa kama njia mbadala za uwekezaji.

eng: In a country where it doesn't make sense to have a savings account because the handling fees are higher than the interest gained from the savings, these get rich quick plans where citizens can pay to participate and then invite 7 other friends to enroll before they can enjoy sky high interest (between 40 and 70%) on their savings seem like a great deal.
swa: Katika nchi ambapo akaunti za benki zimepoteza maana kwa sababu ada za uendeshaji ziko juu kuliko riba anayopata mwenye akaunti, michezo hii ya upatu inayoshawishi kumjaza mtu mapesa, ambapo raia wanalipa kiasi fulani cha pesa ili kujiunga na kisha kuingiza marafiki zao 7 kabla wao hawajaanza kufurahia riba ya juu ajabu (kati ya asilimia 40 mpaka 70) basi imekuwa ni kivutio kikubwa mno.

eng: Currently the ranks of those cheated by the system keep growing, and the government tries to establish methods to punish those who take advantage of citizens who fall prey to their scam.
swa: Hivi sasa idadi ya wale wanaoingizwa mkenge na michezo hii inazidi kukua huku serikali ikijaribu kuweka mikakati ya kuwaadhibu wale wanaotumia umbumbu wa raia ili kuwakamua pesa kwa njia hizi za kidanganyifu.

eng: DiegoAlejandro1985 posts a video of people lining up outside one of these investment options known as DRFE, trying to claim their money after the General Attorneys searched the premises and took hold of money that could've been used to pay those with savings invested in the organization, but this search was deemed illegal and the pyramid scheme is still in operation.
swa: DiegoAlejandro1985 ametuma picha ya video inayoonyesha watu wakiwa katika mstari wa kuingia katika moja ya taasisi zinazoendesha michezo hiyo inayojulikana kama DRFE wakijaribu kudai pesa zao mara baada Ofisi ya Mwanasheria Mkuu kuivamia na kuipekua, ambapo kuna fedha zilizokutwa zilizodhaniwa kuwa ilikuwa zitumike kulipa wale waliowekeza pesa zao kwenye taasisi hiyo, hata hivyo, msako huu unasemekana kwamba ulikuwa batili na hivyo mchezo wa upatu katika jengo hilo bado unaendelea.

eng: Diego Alejandro explains in his blog Denuncias y Más where he's been following the ups and downs of several other pyramid scheme enterprises.
swa: Kupitia blogu yake, Denuncias y Más, Diego Alejandro anaeleza anayoyaona kwa kuwa amekuwa akifuatilia yale yanayoendelea katika michezo mbalimbali ya upatu inayoendeshwa nchini humo.

eng: Radio Zamaneh (Persian: رادیو زمانه) is an Amsterdam-based Persian language radio.
swa: Redio Zamaneh ni redio ya lugha ya kipersia yenye makao yake huko mjini Amsterdam.

eng: Zamaneh is the Persian literary term for "time".
swa: Zamaneh ni neno linalomaanisha "wakati" katika lugha hiyo.

eng: Radio Zamaneh (RZ) is an independent broadcasting organisation, registered as a non-profit organisation in the Netherlands, with headquarters and a studio in Amsterdam.
swa: Redio Zamaneh (RZ) ni chombo huru cha utangazaji kilichosajiliwa kama asasi isiyo ya kiserikali huko Uholanzi, kikiwa na studio na makao yake makuu mjini Amsterdam.

eng: The coordinator of the radio is the Dutch NGO Press Now.
swa: Mratibu wa redio hiyo ni Asasi isiyo ya kiserikali ya Kidachi ijulikanayo kama Press Now.

eng: It launched about two years ago and calls itself a 'radio for bloggers'.
swa: Redio hiyo ilizinduliwa yapata miaka miwili iliyopita na imejipachika lahaja kwa jina la "redio ya mabloga".

eng: RZ has called itself a radio for bloggers.
swa: RZ inajiita Redio ya mabloga.

eng: Why such a slogan?
swa: Kwa nini kauli mbiu hiyo?

eng: How much influence have bloggers had at RZ ?
swa: Ni kwa kuiwango gani mabloga wameweza kushawishi muelekeo wa wa RZ?

eng: In Iran many journalists have turned to blogging to communicate since many newspapers are continually harassed and shut down.
swa: Waandishi wengi wa habari nchini Irani wameanza kublogu kwa sababu magazeti mengi yanaendelea kughasiwa na kufungwa.

eng: Most of Radio Zamaneh's contributors were, and still are, bloggers.
swa: Wengi wa wachangiaji wa Redio Zamaneh walikuwa na bado ni mabloga.

eng: Our director, Mehdi Jami, started blogging several years before joining Radio Zamaneh.
swa: Mkurugenzi wetu, Mehdi jami, alianza kublogu kwa miaka kadhaa kabla ya kujiunga na Redio Zamaneh.

eng: As Radio Zamaneh has based its media policy on Citizen Journalism, reaching out to bloggers is natural.
swa: Kwa kuwa sera ya habari ya Redio Zamaneh imejikita kewenye uandishi wa kiraia, kuwafikia mabloga ilikuwa ni jambo la wazi.

eng: Since August 2006, when Radio Zamaneh started, we have actively promoted bloggers on our site and in our radio programs.
swa: Kuanzia mwezi wa Agosti 2006, wakati Redio Zamaneh ilipoanzishwa, tumewahusisha na kuwatangaza mabloga katika tovuti yetu na katika programu za redio yetu.

eng: Many were involved in the development of RZ.
swa: Wengi wao walihusika katika maendeleo ya RZ.

eng: Radio Zamaneh in many ways is connected to bloggers and blogging.
swa: Redio Zamaneh ina uhusiano na mabloga katika njia nyingi.

eng: Just take a look at our extensive blogroll.
swa: Jaribu kuangalia orodha ya blogu iliyoko kwenye tovuti.

eng: Radio Zamaneh aims for two-way communication.
swa: Redio Zamaneh inalenga kuwa na mawasiliano ya njia mbili.

eng: This is something that blogs are known for.
swa: Hilo ndilo jambo ambalo mabloga wanajulikana kwalo.

eng: This is why our site is working like a set of blogs.
swa: Hiyo ndiyo sababu ya tovuti yetu kufanya kazi kana kwamba ni seti ya blogu.

eng: Each regular contributor has their own page/blog and readers can comment on every page.
swa: Kila mchangiaji ana ukurasa wake/blogu na wasomaji wanaweza kuchangia maoni katika kila kurasa.

eng: There are several news sites, outside of Iran, such as Deutsche Welle (DW) Perisan site, covering Iranian blogs.
swa: Kuna tovuti mbalimbali za habari, nje ya Irani, kama vile Deustche Welle (DW) Idhaa ya Kipersia, ambayo huweka blogu za Ki-Irani.

eng: Is there a difference between RZ's approach toward blogging and theirs?
swa: Je kuna tofauti katika jinsi ya RZ inavyozichukulia blogu hizo na jinsi vyombo vingine vinavyochukulia?

eng: We don't just cover bloggers, we are bloggers and our style is bloggish: friendly, informal, different, personalized, and diverse.
swa: Hatutundiki habari za mabloga tu, bali sisi ni mabloga na mtindo wetu ni wa kiana-blogu: ukaribu, bila ukiritimba, tofauti, kila moja na mtindo binafsi na mchanganyiko.

eng: Blogging is a part of our daily life.
swa: Kublogu ni sehemu ya maisha yetu ya kila siku.

eng: We are talking on blogs and quoting blogs.
swa: Tunaongea ndani ya blogu na kunukuu kutoka kwenye blogu.

eng: We see them as a source of information about how people think about politics and social issues.
swa: Tunaziona kama vyanzo vya habari vya jinsi watu wanavyofikiri kuhusu masuala ya siasa na jamii.

eng: We see Iranian youth culture as a culture promoted by blogs and we are working to make the informality of blogging a trend in media making.
swa: Tunaona utamaduni wa vijana wa Ki-Irani kama utamaduni ambao unakuzwa kwenye blogu na tunafanya juhudi kuwezesha mtindo usio na ukiritimba wa kublogu uwe ni mtindo wa utengenezaji habari.

eng: Radio Zamaneh is derived from and inspired by blogging.
swa: Redio Zamaneh inatokana na, na kuhamasishwa na kublogu.

eng: That is very different from just covering blogs by other media outlets.
swa: Hivyo ni tofauti kabisa kutoka kwenye kunukuu blogu kama ilivyo katika vyombo vingine vya habari.

eng: How have Iranian bloggers reacted to RZ?
swa: Ni vipi mabloga wa Ki-Irani walivyoichukulia RZ?

eng: Collaborating or criticizing?
swa: Kwa kujishirikisha au kwa kuilaumu?

eng: A search at Technorati, will show you that there are more than 30,000 links to the items we publish on our site.
swa: Tafiti katika Technorati, itakuonyesha kwamba kuna zaidi ya viungo 30,000 vinavyounga habari zinazobandikwa kwenye tovuti yetu.

eng: In addition, Canada-based Iranian blogger, Arash Kamangir's Didish Report, which searches Iranian site feeds for links to other sites, consistently shows that we are at the top of the list for receiving links.
swa: Kadhalika, katika blogu Didish Report ya bloga wa Ki-Irani aishiye nchini Kanada Arashi Kamangir ambayo hutafiti tovuti zenye viungo kuelekea tovuti nyingine, inaonyesha kiudhabiti kuwa tupo juu kwenye orodha ya tovuti inayopata viungo kuwaelekea.

eng: These show that many bloggers are interested in RZ and referring to us.
swa: Hiyo inaonyesha kwambakwamba mabloga wengi wanavutiwa na RZ na wanatuunganisha kwa viungo hivyo.

eng: Many of them work with us in different ways and some are critical too.
swa: Wengi wao wanafanya kazi na sisi kwa namna tofauti-tofauti na wengine hutuchambua vikali.

eng: Bloggers are not ignoring what we publish.
swa: Mabloga hawadharau kazi tunayofanya.

eng: We welcome both collaboration and criticism.
swa: Tunakaribisha ushirikiano pamoja na kukosolewa.

eng: In fact, one of our contributors thinks we could use more people poking fun at us.
swa: Kwa hakika, mmoja wa wanahabari wetu anafikiri kuwa tunaweza kuwatumia vizuri wale watu wanaotukejeli.

eng: We invite criticism of Radio Zamaneh and even sponsored a competition with a review of the site as its focus.
swa: Tunakaribisha ukosoaji wa Redio Zamaneh hata tukafika hatua ya kudhamini shindano la kuchambua tovuti yetu.

eng: This competition helped us discover some of our current colleagues.
swa: Shindano hilo lilituwezesha kuwatambua wenzi wetu.

eng: Radio Zamaneh has a solid record of publishing differing opinions.
swa: Redio Zamaneh ina historia madhubuti ya kuchapa maoni yanayotofautiana.

eng: RZ has a list of bloggers in its first page.
swa: Tovuti ya RZ ina orodha ya mabloga kwenye ukurasa wake wa kwanza.

eng: Some have criticized RZ for only listing "politically correct" blogs, and not ones that are against the Islamic Republic.
swa: Kuna wengine wanaoilaumu RZ kwa kuorodhesha mabloga wenye "siasa laini" na siyo zile ambazo zinatofautiana ana Jamhuri ya Kiislamu.

eng: How do you answer them?
swa: Je uwajibu vipi hawa?

eng: The Berkman Center at Harvard University reports that more than 60,000 blogs in Iran are continually updated.
swa: Kituo cha Berkman kilichoko Chuo Kikuu cha Harvard kinaripoti kuwa, zaidi ya blogu 60,000 ndani ya Irani huwa zinaongezwa habari mara kwa mara.

eng: Obviously, we cannot link to all of them.
swa: Hivyo hatuwezi kuziunganisha zote kwenye tovuti yetu.

eng: Radio Zamaneh does not promote bloggers based on their political views.
swa: Redio Zamaneh haina nia ya kutangaza mabloga kulingana na mitazamo yao ya kisiasa.

eng: While we try to remain independent, we link to blogs with strong political points of view, including those that can be seen as *for* or *against* the regime.
swa: Wakati tunajitahidi kubaki huru, tunaunganisha blogu zenye miizamo mikali ya kisiasa, pamoja na zile ambazo huonekana kama zenye kushabikia au kupingana na utawala.

eng: We read many blogs and do not limit our list to a select group.
swa: Tunasoma blogu nyingi na hatujiwekei kikomo ili kuzijumuisha blogu chache teule.

eng: That said, Radio Zamaneh tries not to link to blogs with strong affiliations to political groups or extremists.
swa: Baada ya kusema hivyo, tovuti ya Redio Zamaneh inajaribu kuziunga blogu zenye mahusiano na makundi ya kisiasa au makundi ya wale wenye siasa kali.

eng: Some news sites are afraid to give more voices to citizen media because they consider them as unreliable sources of information.
swa: Baadhi ya tovuti za habari zinaogopa kuvipa sauti vyombo vya habari vya kiraia kwa sababu vinavichukulia kuwa ni vyanzo vya habari visivyoaminika.

eng: What do you think?
swa: Je wewe unafikiriaje?

eng: It's hard to give up control.
swa: Ni vigumu kuachia madaraka.

eng: Fortunately, most of us have been bloggers ourselves, so we see both sides.
swa: Kwa bahati, wengi wetu tumeshawahi kuwa mabloga, kwa hiyo tunaweza kuona pande zote mbili.

eng: What we normally get from blogs are views, not news.
swa: Kutoka kwenye blogu huwa tunapata maoni, na sio habari.

eng: Any news from blogs must be checked against other sources.
swa: Habari zozote katika blogu ni lazima zihakikishwe kwa kutumia vyanzo vingine vya habari.

eng: Blogs may be a starting point for a news story, but we do not rely on them as a source.
swa: Blogu zinaweza kuwa ni chanzo cha habari, lakini hatuzitegemei kuwa vyanzo vyetu pekee vya habari.

eng: At the same time, we try to do training and work with citizen journalists so that they can provide reliable information.
swa: Kadhalika tunajaribu kuendesha mafunzo pamoja na kufanya kazi na wanahabari wa kiraia ili kwamba waweze kutuletea habari zenye kuweza kutumainiwa kwamba ni za kweli.

eng: In fact, we are currently working on a special training site for citizen journalism which will be for our network and for registered users.
swa: Hivi sasa tunatayarisha tovuti ya mafunzo kwa ajili ya waandishi wa kiraia, tovuti ambayo itakuwa ni kwa ajili ya wanamtandao wetu na kwa ajili ya watumiaji maalum walioandikishwa.

eng: Outside of Iran many Persian sites covering politics, such as DW or Gozarr, have blog sections.
swa: Nje ya Irani blogu nyingi zinazoandika juu ya siassa kama vile DW au Gozzar zina safu ya blogu.

eng: Inside Iran very, very few mainstream news sites have such a section.
swa: Ndani ya Irani, ni vyombo vichache mno vya habari vyenye tovuti ambazo zina safu kama hiyo.

eng: Why the difference?
swa: Kwa nini kuwepo na tofauti kama hiyo?

eng: Inside Iran, they want to have more control over what people read.
swa: Ndani ya Irani wanataka kuwa na udhibiti zaidi kuhusiana na nini watu wanachoweza kukisoma.

eng: They just don't have the habit of presenting points of view that they cannot control.
swa: Hawana tu tabia ya kuwakilisha mitizamo ambayo hawawezi kuidhibiti.

eng: To be fair, major Western news sources have been slow to embrace bloggers as well.
swa: Tuktaka kuwa wakweli, hata vyombo vya habari vya magharibi vimechelewa kuwakumbatia mabloga vile vile.

eng: It's not normal for a news organization to link to competing sources of information.
swa: Siyo kawaida kwa shirika la habari kuunganisha vyanzo mbalimbali vya habari.

eng: What has been RZ's most important added value to Iranian media?
swa: Je ni faida gani ambayo RZ imeviongezea vyombo vya habari vya Irani?

eng: RZ has proven that it is possible to present an independent take on Iran and the news.
swa: RZ imeonyesha kwamba inawezekana kuwakilisha maoni huru kuhusu Irani na habari.

eng: It provides a voice for the unheard, and highlights marginalized groups in Iran: writers, Sunnis, women, bloggers, Armenians, Zoroastrians, and other ethnic and religious minorities.
swa: Inawapa sauti wale ambao ni vigumu kusikika, na inawapa mwangaza makundi yaliyotengwa katika Irani: waandishi, watu wa madhehebu ya Sunni, wanawake, mabloga, Wa-Armenia, Wa-Zoroastria, na makundi mengine ya kikabila au ya kidini.

eng: Radio Zamaneh republishes, highlights, and links to articles written on the web by domestic critics of Iranian politics, which are ignored by domestic media in Iran.
swa: Redio Zamaneh inachapa, inatoa mwangaza, inaunga makala zilizoandikwa kwenye mtandao na wakosoaji wa siasa za ndani ya Irani, ambazo huwekwa kando na vyombo vya habari vya ndani ya Irani.

eng: In addition we run programming that challenges the taboos of Iranian society such as relationships and sex.
swa: Pia, sisi huendesha programu ambazo huchachafya miiko ya jamii ya Irani kama ile inayohusiana na mahusiano na ngono.

eng: Sometimes, the challenge is with the official reading of politics and news; sometimes it is with the dogmatic views held by many inside and outside Iran.
swa: Wakati mwingine, changamoto huhusiana na msimamo wa kiserikali kisiasa, na wakati mwingine changamoto huhusiana na mitizamo mgando inayoshikiliwa na wengi, ndani na nje ya Irani.

eng: What are the most important challenges?
swa: Je ni changamoto zipi zenye umuhimu zaidi?

eng: If we want to stay on top of the game and hold on to our audience, we constantly need to stay in communication with them.
swa: Kama tunataka kuwa na umuhimu na kuweza kuwashikilia waasomaji na wasikilizaji wetu, inatupasa kudumisha mawasiliano baina yetu na wao.

eng: You have to have an open communication channel.
swa: Inakupasa uwe na mkondowazi wa mawasiliano.

eng: We need to encourage more reader and listener participation.
swa: Inabidi tuwape moyo wasomaji na wasikilizaji kujishirikisha zaidi.

eng: We need to keep our ears open.
swa: Inatupasa kufungua masikio yetu.

eng: We have to stay fresh and be our own harshest critic, and we have to work hard to remain fair and independent.
swa: Inatupasa tujipe uhai mpya kila siku na pia tuwe wakosoaji wa kazi zetu wenyewe, na inatupasa tufanye kazi kwa nguvu ili kuweza kuendelea kuwa wakweli na huru.

eng: A lot of people would like us to take sides, whether it's against the government in Iran or for them, but we work hard to remain independent despite whatever personal beliefs we have.
swa: Watu wangependa tufungamane na mirengo fulani fulani, ama iwe kuipinga serikali ya Irani au kuwaunga mkono wao, lakini sisi tumekuwa tukijitahidi kubakia huru bila kuhusisha imani zozote ambazo tunazo.

eng: The other major challenge for us is how to survive and make a sustainable media.
swa: Changamoto kuu kwetu ni namna ya kuendelea na kutengeneza chombo cha habari endelevu.

eng: We believe that for a sustainable civil society in Iran we need sustainable democratic media in and for Iran.
swa: Tunaamini kuwa ili kuwa na jamii za kiraia endelevu ndani ya Irani tunahitaji kuwa na vyombo vya habari vya kidemokrasia vilivyo ndani ya na kwa ajili ya Irani.

eng: How does RZ deal with filtering?
swa: RZ inakabili vipi uchujaji wa habari?

eng: It's a cat and mouse game.
swa: Ni mchezo wa paka na panya.

eng: We have to continually find new holes to hide in.
swa: Inatubidi tuendelee kutafuta mashimo ya kujificha.

eng: We have changed our domain name 5 times!
swa: Tumebadilisha jina la tovuti yetu mara 5!

eng: We send our newsletters every day to many people who want to read RZ and have no direct access.
swa: Tunatuma kijarida chetu kila siku kwa watu wengi ambao wanataka kuzoma RZ ambao hawana namna ya kusoma tovuti yetu moja kwa moja.

eng: But we cannot say that we can evade filtering.
swa: Lakini hatuwezi kusema kuwa tunaweza kuepuka uchujwaji wa habari.

eng: Many pages are blocked.
swa: Kurasa nyingi zimezuiliwa.

eng: Despite that, more than 60% of our readers are from Iran.
swa: Pamoja na hivyo, zaidi ya asilimia 60 ya wasomaji wetu wapo ndani ya Irani.

eng: Sometimes a piece gets published from provincial or local bloggers.
swa: Mara nyingine habari huchapwa na bloga aliyeko mikoani au na bloga aliyeko ndani ya jiji.

eng: Are there any sharp differences between what Tehran-based bloggers write and provincial ones?
swa: Je kuna tofauti kati ya bloga aliye mikoani na yule aliye Teherani?

eng: In many ways those who live outside the capital feel isolated and ignored.
swa: Kwa namna mbalimbali wale walioko nje ya mji mkuu hujisia wapweke na kutotiliwa maanani.

eng: For many, Iran means Tehran.
swa: Kwa wengi, Irani inamaanisha Teherani.

eng: Tehran is very important, but we do not ignore cities in Kurdistan, Khorasan, Azarbayjan, Khuzistan, Fars, and the rest of the country.
swa: Teherani ni muhimu sana, lakini hatuwachi kuipa umaanani miji iliyopo Kurdistan, Khorasan, Azarbayjan, Khuzistan, Fars, na nchi nzima kwa ujumla.

eng: We try to see them all and give them voice and confidence and support.
swa: Tunajaribu kuwajuisha wote na kuwapa sauti, uhakika na msaada.

eng: We have a program designed to find good provincial blogs and promote them by quoting from them and talking to them.
swa: Tunayo programu inayolenga kuwapata mabloga wazuri walioko mikoani na kuwakuza kwa kuwanukuu au kwa kuongea nao.

eng: We always welcome contributions from provincial areas even though we cannot spend as much time covering them as we do major cities.
swa: Tunakaribisha michango kutoka mikoani hata kama hatuwezi kutumia muda mwingi kuwanukuu kama ambavyo tunafanya kwa wale walioko mji mkuu.

eng: Queen Rania of Jordan has been named the most famous Arab video blogger on YouTube by Blogger Times, a blogging magazine run by Arab bloggers, following the success of a series of YouTube videos she launched to shake off stereotypes against Arabs.
swa: Chombo cha habari cha Blogger Times kinachoendeshwa na mabloga wa Kiarabu, kimemtaja Malkia Rania wa Jordan kuwa bloga maarufu zaidi wa video za kutoka Uarabuni katika chombo cha Video mtandaoni, YouTube, kufuatia mafanikio ya mlolongo wa video za YouTube aliouanzisha kuondoa dhana potofu dhidi ya Waarabu.

eng: لكن ما تتفرد به الملكة رانيا عن الباقي هو أنها الشخصية العربية الوحيدة التي تستخدم الإنترت للانخراط في حوار مع الغرب والترويج للخطاب الإسلامي المعتدل.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa makala hiyo:

eng: Queen Rania Al Abdullah sits inside large office in Amman, Jordon, with three cameras focused on her.
swa: Malkia Rania wa Jordan kaketi ndani ya ofisi yake kubwa huko Amman, jordan, na kamera tatu kubwa zikimuelekea.

eng: The first and second cameras were for BBC, while the third camera was for her office staff.
swa: Kamera ya kwanza na ya pili zilikuwa kwa ajili ya BBC, wakati kamera ya tatu ilikuwa kwa ajili ya wafanyakazi wa ofisi yake.

eng: The three cameras were recording the latest episode of her program that is broadcasted on a special channel on YouTube, better known as a Vlog.
swa: Kamera hizo tatu zilikuwa zikirekodi mapya katika mlolongo wa programu yake inayorushwa katika mkondo maalum kwenye YouTube, unaojulikana vyema kama Vlog.

eng: This is her 7th episode/video since she began broadcasting on Youtube, last March, where she speaks in English asking viewers to discuss the stereotypes they have heard about the Arab world, so she can “debunk them one after the other."
swa: Hii ni video yake ya 7 tangu alipoanza kutangaza katika YouTube, mwezi wa Machi uliopita, ambamo anazungumza kwa Kiingereza akiwaomba watazamaji kujadili dhana ambazo wamezisikia kuhusu dunia ya Kiarabu, ili kwamba aweze "kuzipopotoa moja baada ya nyingine."

eng: Perhaps the wife of Jordan's King Abdullah the Second, is not the only public figure who uses YouTube, that’s being watched by millions of people.
swa: Pengine mke wa Mfalme wa Jordan Abdullah wa Pili, si mtu maarufu pekee ambaye anatumia chombo cha YouTube, ambacho kinaangaliwa na mamilioni ya watu.

eng: There are other politicians and kings in different regions of the world who have created personal websites on the internet.
swa: Kuna wanasiasa na wafalme katika sehemu mbalimbali za dunia ambao wametengeneza tovuti binafsi katika mtandao wa intaneti.

eng: But what is unique about Queen Rania is that she is the only Arab figure who uses the internet to engage in a dialogue with the West to promote a moderate Islamic speech.
swa: Lakini jambo la kipekee kuhusu Malkia Rania ni kwamba yeye ni Muarabu pekee maarufu anayetumia mtandao wa intaneti kwa ajili ya mazungumzo na ulimwengu wa magharibi ili kutetea mtazamo wa wastani wa Kiislamu.

eng: Queen Rania says jokingly: “My adolescent son is a quiet person who doesn’t speak a lot by nature, but his impression towards the speeches I gave was ‘good’, and thus the viewers’ impression should be good as well.”
swa: Malkia Rania ansema kwa utani: "Mwanangu wangu wa kiume aliye kwenye umri wa balehe ni mkimya ambaye huwa si muongeaji sana kwa asili yake, lakini mtazamo wake juu ya risala niliyotoa ulikuwa "vyema", na kwa hivyo basi mtazamo wa wanaongalia pia unabidi uwe mzuri vilevile".

eng: It seems that YouTube visitors agreed with him on what he said, as around 2 million viewers watched the video episodes broadcasted on YouTube; which include along with her recording, contributions from different Jordanian musicians, comedians and citizens.
swa: Inaonekana kwamba wageni wengi katika YouTube walikubaliana na alivyosema (mwanawe Malkia), kwani takribani watazamaji milioni 2 waliangalia mlolongo huo wa video uliorushwa katika YouTube; ambao ulijumisha pamoja na kanda zake mwenyewe, michango kutoka kwa wanamuziki, wachekeshaji na raia mbalimbali wa Jordan.

eng: Queen’s Rania appearing on her channel on the internet, gave her the chance to receive criticism from millions of people.
swa: Kuonekana kwa Malkia Rania katika mkondo wake wa intaneti, kulimpa fursa ya kukosolewa kutoka kwa mamilioni ya watu.

eng: As she has said to me: “When the idea came to my head, some people looked at me as if I have totally lost my mind."
swa: Kama alivyoniambia: "wakati wazo hili liliponijia kichwani, watu wengine waliniangalia kama vile nimerukwa na akili."

eng: She continued: “I feel that our world is in a crisis at the present time, violence has replaced dialogue and anger replaced compassion.”
swa: Akaendelea: "nadhani kwamba dunia yetu imo katika machafuko hivi sasa, vurugu zimechukua nafasi ya maongezi na hasira zimechukua nafasi ya huruma."

eng: “I hope that this channel becomes a channel for communication and a bridge between the East and West, because I firmly believe our world is in dire need for this”.
swa: Natumaini kwamba mkondo huu utakuwa ni mkondo wa mawasiliano na daraja kati ya Mashariki na Magharibi, kwa sababu ninaamini kwamba dunia yetu inahitaji hili.

eng: This open letter comes after the Mozambican National Resistance (Renamo) leadership in the central Mozambican city of Beira announced on August 28 that Davis Simango, mayor of the city of Beira, would not run for his second term office for the local elections taking place on November 19, 2009.
swa: Barua hii ya wazi imekuja baada ya uongozi wa chama cha Mozambican Resistance Movement (Renamo) kutangaza tarehe 28 Agosti kwamba Davis Simango, Meya wa mji wa Beira, hatosimama kugombea kiti hicho kwa muhula wa pili wakati wa uchaguzi utakaofanyika tarehe 19 Novemba 2009.

eng: As an immediate response to the announcement, angry Renamo and Simango supporters took control of the party’s delegation in protest against president Afonso Dhlakama’s decision of substituting Simango by Manuel Pereira.
swa: Kama majibu ya haraka kwa tangazo hilo, wafuasi wa Renamo na Simango waliojawa na hasira waliushikilia ujumbe wa chama ili kupinga uamuzi ya Alphonso Dhlakama wa kumtoa Simango na kumuweka Manuel Pereira.

eng: The decision sparked off two days of demonstrations in Beira, as Simango's supporters came onto the streets and demanded that the decision be reversed.
swa: Uamuzi huo uliwasha cheche za maandamano ya siku mbili huko Beira, wakati watu wanaomuunga mkono Simango walipovamia mitaa na kudai uamuzi huo ubadilishwe.

eng: On the following Friday night, police used tear gas and rubber bullets against a crowd that had gathered in front of the Renamo offices in the neighbourhood of Munhava.
swa: Usiku wa ijumaa iliyofuatia, askari polisi walitumia mabomu ya kutoa machozi na risasi za mpira dhidi ya umati ambao ulikuwa umekusanyika mbele ya ofisi za Renamo katika maeneo ya Munhava.

eng: During the scuffles, a reporter from the Beira daily paper "Diario de Mocambique", Antonio Chimundo, was physically attacked by Renamo members who accused him of working for the ruling Frelimo Party.
swa: Wakati wa ghasia, ripota kutoka gazeti la kila siku la Beira, "Diario de Mocambique", Antonio Chimundo, alivamiwa na wanachama wa Renamo ambao walimshutumu kuwa alikuwa akifanya kazi kwa ajili ya chama tawala cha Frelimo.

eng: Many analysts including some Renamo parliamentarians condemn Dhlakama’s decision and praise Davis Simango for his decision to run as an independent candidate.
swa: Wachunguzi wengi wa mambo wakiwemo wabunge wa Renamo wanaulaumu uamuzi wa Dhlakama na kumsifu Davis Simango kwa uamuzi wake wa kusimama kama mgombea huru.

eng: The original version of the letter below is available on my blog in Portuguese.
swa: Nakala mama ya barua iliyo hapa chini inapatikana katika blogu yangu ya lugha ya Kireno.

eng: A former Roman Catholic bishop, Fernando Lugo, was recently sworn in as the new president of Paraguay on August 15.
swa: Askofu wa zamani wa kanisa Katoliki, Fernando Lugo, hivi karibuni aliapishwa kama rais mpya wa Paraguai, tarehe 15 Agosti.

eng: His ascent to power excited those Paraguayans at home, as well as those living abroad.
swa: Kuibuka kwake kukamata uongozi kumewasisimua WaParaguai walio nyumbani na walio ughaibuni.

eng: For those unable to be present in the capital city of Asunción to witness the festivities, photos can be found on his official Flickr account.
swa: Kwa wale ambao walishindwa kuwepo kwenye mji mkuu wa Asuncion kushuhudia sherehe, picha zinaweza kupatikana katika ukurasa rasmi wa picha za kiongozi huyo kwenye Flickr.

eng: The effort of documenting Lugo's appearances and activities started during his campaign in January 2008.
swa: Juhudi za kuorodhesha nyendo na shughuli za Lugo zilianza wakati wa kampeni yake mwezi Januari 2008.

eng: Now, with nearly 2,500 photographs all under a Creative Commons license, the use of this citizen's media tool will be carried over during his new administration.
swa: Hivi sasa karibia picha 2,500 zilizo katika haki miliki za huria kwa umma, inatarajiwa kuwa matumizi ya chombo hiki cha habari yataendelezwa hata wakati wa serikali yake mpya.

eng: In the past few days, photographs of Lugo during his inauguration demonstrated the excitement of the historical event.
swa: Katika siku chache zilizopita, picha za lugo wakati wa kuapishwa kwake zimeonyesha msisimko wa tukio hili la kihistoria.

eng: At Lugo's inauguration.
swa: Wakati wa Kuapishwa.

eng: Photo by Fernando Lugo APC and used under a Creative Commons license.
swa: Picha na Fernando Lugo zilizo chini ya haki miliki huria kwa umma.

eng: In addition, photographs with fellow South American heads of state can also be found.
swa: Na zaidi, picha pamoja na viongozi wenzie wa nchi za Marekani ya Kusini pia zinaweza kupatikana.

eng: Hugo Chávez of Venezuela and Lugo.
swa: Hugo Chavez wa Venezuela na Lugo.

eng: Photo by Fernando Lugo APC and used under a Creative Commons license.
swa: Picha na Fernando Lugo zilizo chini ya haki miliki huria kwa umma.

eng: Evo Morales of Bolivia and Lugo.
swa: Evo Morales wa Bolivia na Lugo.

eng: Photo by Fernando Lugo APC and used under a Creative Commons license.
swa: Picha na Fernando Lugo zilizo chini ya haki miliki huria kwa umma.

eng: Lula da Silva of Brazil and Lugo.
swa: Lula da Silva wa Brazil na Lugo.

eng: Photo by Fernando Lugo APC and used under a Creative Commons license.
swa: Picha na Fernando Lugo zilizo chini ya haki miliki huria kwa umma.

eng: Cristina Kirchner of Argentina and Lugo.
swa: Cristina Kirchner wa Argentina na Lugo.

eng: Photo by Fernando Lugo APC and used under a Creative Commons license.
swa: Picha na Fernando Lugo zilizo chini ya haki miliki huria kwa umma.

eng: Rafael Correa of Ecuador and Lugo.
swa: Rafael Correa wa Ecuador na Lugo.

eng: Photo by Fernando Lugo APC and used under a Creative Commons license.
swa: Picha na Fernando Lugo zilizo chini ya haki miliki huria kwa umma.

eng: Fernando Lugo's presidency started with an announcement that he would forgo his monthly salary.
swa: Utawala wa Rais Ferdinand Lugo umeanza na tangazo kuwa hatapokea mshahara wake wa mwezi.

eng: I don't need that salary, which belongs to the poor, said Lugo.
swa: Sihitaji mshahara huo, ambao unapaswa kumilikiwa na masikini, alisema Lugo.

eng: Different local bloggers see things differently, as one applauds the decision and another wonders how Lugo will pay for his own expenses.
swa: Mabloga nchini humo wanatofautiana mitazamo, wakati mmoja anausifu uamuzi huo, mwingine anajiuliza ni vipi Rais lugo atajilipia gharama binafsi za maisha.

eng: Carlos Rodríguez of Rescatar summarizes the reactions of some in the press who are downplaying the gesture by pointing out that the former priest does not have a wife or children to support, while others wonder whether he will spend the reserved funds at his disposition.
swa: Carlos Rodriguez wa Rescatar anatoa muhtasari wa jinsi baadhi ya wanahabari ambao wanarahisisha kitendo hicho kwa kusema kuwa padri huyo wa zamani hana mke wala watoto wa kuwalea, wakati wengine wanajiuliza iwapo atatumia fedha alizokwisha kuzihifadhi.

eng: However, Rodríguez sees things in a different light:
swa: Hata hivyo, Rodriguez anaangalia mambo tofauti:

eng: While there are no doubt restrictions for women living in Saudi Arabia, they do not necessarily match the oppressive image that many foreigners have of the country.
swa: WAKATI kukiwa hakuna shaka kwamba kuna vizuizi kwa wanawake waishio Saudi Arabia, havifanani na taswira iliyojengwa na wageni dhidi ya taifa hilo.

eng: In this post we have advice for women wanting to visit Jeddah alone, a review of a women-only hotel in Riyadh, and a plea to those foreigners who feel they want to speak on behalf of oppressed Saudi women.
swa: Katika makala hii tunao ushauri kwa wakina mama wanaotaka kutembelea jiji la Jeddah wakiwa peke yao, kuna muhtasari wa hoteli za kina mama pekee jijini Riyadh, na wito kwa wageni wote wanajihisi kuzungumza kwa niana ya kina mama wanaokandamizwa wa Saudia.

eng: We start with Hala, currently living in the US and blogging at HALA_IN_USA, who is giving advice to a single female friend visiting Jeddah for the first time:
swa: Tunaanza na Hala, ambaye anaishi Marekani hivi sasa na anablogu katika blogu yake HALA_IN_USA, anayetoa ushauri kwa marafiki zake akinamama wasio na waume watakaotaka kutembelea jiji la Jeddah kwa mara yao ya kwanza:

eng: Women in Jeddah are dressed in an outside gown called “Abaya”, it supposed to be worn over clothes so dress lightly beneath it especially in the summer.
swa: Wanawake katika jiji la Jeddah huvaa gauni lijulikanalo kama "Abaya", gauni hili hupaswa kuvaliwa juu ya mavazi mengine hivyo vaa nguo nyepesi za ndani haswa wakati wa majira ya kiangazi.

eng: The scarf however, is not a must for a female visitor in Jeddah but a preferred thing to wear (for safety and convenience) in traditional places.
swa: Ushungi si lazima kwa akina mama wageni lakini ni vazi linalopendekezwa kuvaliwa (kwa ajili ya usalama na kuepuka usumbufu usiokuwa wa lazima) katika maeneo ya kiutamaduni.

eng: There are a variety of places to see in Jeddah, I would suggest the Balad, the old city of Jeddah, with its historical architecture and old houses, Naseef house is a good example of one.
swa: Kuna maeneo mbalimbali ya kuyaona jijini Jeddah, ninapendekeza Balad, jiji la kale la Jeddah, likiwa na majengo yaliyosanifiwa kizamani, Jengo la Naseef ni mfano mmojawapo wa majengo ya kale.

eng: You can purchase traditional goodies from the old shops and enjoy the aroma of Arabic perfumes like Oud and Bukhour, there’s also the traditional handcrafts like the light bulbs or fanoos , the dates, the sweets and the textiles with various colors.
swa: Unaweza kununua bidhaa za kitamaduni za kale kutoka katika maduka ya kizamani na ukafurahia marashi ya Kiarabu kama vile Udi Bukhour, vilevile kuna bidhaa za kazi za mikono za kitamaduni kama balbu, , tende, pipi na vitambaa vya rangi mbalimbali.

eng: Then, there’s the famous Jeddah Corniche.
swa: Pia kuna barabara maarufu jijini Jeddah iliyokatiza ufukweni mwa bahari .

eng: I suggest visiting it early in the morning or at 6pm to see the open air sculptures along the sea side, there’s also Jeddah sea-fountain, one of the highest fountains in the world.
swa: Napendekeza upite katika barabara hiyo mapema alfajiri au jioni saa 12 ili uweze kujionea maumbile ya kupendeza baharini, pia kuna chemchem ya baharini, moja ya chemchem zilizoko juu zaidi kuliko nyingine yoyote duniani.

eng: There is a variety of food choices along the corniche from fancy eating in restaurants to fast food or even small booths for biscuits and chips.
swa: Kuna machaguo mbalimbali ya vyakula katika barabara ya kupendeza ufukweni mwa bahari, kuanzia migahawa ya ya anasa mpaka maduka ya vyakula vya haraka au hata vijiduka vidogo vya biskuti na chipsi.

eng: The local people would sit for hours by the sea side with their children playing around and watching the passersby.
swa: Wenyeji hukuketi katika ufukweni kwa masaa na watoto wao wakicheza karibu yao huku wakiwaangalia wapita njia.

eng: For more of Hala’s advice of what to see in Jeddah, see here.
swa: Kwa ushauri zaidi wa Hala kuhusiana na unachotaka kukiona jijini Jeddah, angalia hapa.

eng: Meanwhile American Bedu, an American living in Saudi Arabia, tells us what she thinks of a women-only hotel in Riyadh:
swa: Wakati huo huo bloga American Bedu, ambaye ni Mmarekani anayeishi Saudi Arabia, anatueleza kile anachokifikiri kuhusiana na hoteli za kina mama pekee jijini Riyadh.

eng: The Al Luthan hotel and spa is the first women only facility of its kind in Riyadh.
swa: Hoteli ya Al Luthan na bafu lake ni hoteli ya kwanza kabisa ya wanawake pekee ya aina yake jijini Riyadh.

eng: It is a luxurious hotel and spa for women only.
swa: Ni hoteli ya kifahari na ina bafu la chemchem maalumu kwa wanawake pekee.

eng: It is a full service hotel and spa offering deluxe, comfortable and safe accommodations.
swa: Ni hoteli ya huduma zote yenye kutoa huduma za uhakika na yenye kutoa malazi salama.

eng: Al Luthan welcomes both Saudi and non-Saudi females.
swa: Al Luthan inapokea wageni wa kike kutoka Saudia na wasio Wasudia.

eng: Now some women have spoken out to the media that the opening of Al Luthan is a step backwards.
swa: Hivi sasa baadhi ya wanawake wamezungumza na vyombo vya abari wakisema kuwa kuzinduliwa Al Luthan ni mojawapo ya upigani hatua nyuma.

eng: According to these women, they see it as a backwards movement for the Kingdom due to the fact that there is already so much enforced segregation and women not only have few rights but promoting and endorsing a women’s only hotel and spa further diminishes women from receiving rights.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa wanawake hawa, wanaona kama ni kupiga hatua kuelekea nyuma kwa ufalme wa taifa hilo kutokana na ukweli kwamba tayari kuna ubaguzi na siyo tu kwamba wanawake wana haki kidogo lakini kwa kushabikia na kuafiki uanzishwaji wa hoteli ya wanawake peke yao yenye eneo la kuogea inarudisha nyuma harakati za kina mama kudai haki.

eng: Maybe I am in the minority but I take the opposite view.
swa: Pengine nimo kwenye kundi dogo katika jamii, lakini nachukua mtazamo mbadala.

eng: Al Luthan is not unique when compared to the rest of the world.
swa: Al Luthan siyo hoteli ya kipekee ikilinganishwa na hoteli nyingine duniani.

eng: Women hotels or women-only floors are actually common in most major cities (and some not so major) all over the world.
swa: Hoteli za wanawake au hoteli zinazotenga safu nzima ya ghorofa kwaa jili ya wanawake zipo karibu katika kila jiji kubwa (na hata kwenye miji isiyo mikubwa) duniani.

eng: Back in earlier times when I was doing a lot of international travel, I enjoyed staying on a women-only floor, especially when in foreign cities which were not as accustomed to business women traveling alone.
swa: Siku za nyuma wakati nilipokuwa nikisafiri safari nyingi za kimataifa, nilikuwa nikifurahia kupanga katika hoteli zenye safu maalumu kwa ajili ya wanawake pekee. Haswa katika majiji ya kigeni ambayo hayakuzoea kuwa na wafanyabiashara wanawake wanaosafiri peke yao.

eng: So to me, I do not see a women’s only hotel as a step backward at all but another nice option to have for women in the Kingdom.
swa: Kwa hiyo mimi sioni kama kuanzishwa kwa hoteli hii maalumu kwa wanawake kuwa ni hatua ya kurudi nyuma asilani bali chaguo jema kwa wanawake kuwa nalo ndani ya falme.

eng: Riyadh blogger Sweet Anger is fed up of foreigners assuming that Saudi women are oppressed, while knowing nothing about their lives or society:
swa: Bloga kutoka Riyadh, Sweet Anger amechoshwa na wageni wanaodhani kuwa wanawake wa Kisaudia wanakandamizwa, wakati hawajui lolote kuhusu maisha yao au jamii:

eng: So I was googling one thing or another when I found a post about the abject horror of a reporter in Saudi who was female and was therefore not permitted to stay in the men's section of Starbucks, umm boo hoo hoo.
swa: Basi, nilikuwa nikitafiti mtandaoni kitu kimoja au kingine nikakutana na ujumbe kuhusu ripota aliyekuwa Saudia ambaye ni mwanamke na hivyo hakuruhusiwa kukaa kwenye sehemu ya wanaume ndani ya mgahawa wa Starbucks.umm boo hoo hoo.

eng: Now what grabbed my attention wasn’t the article itself, but the comments.
swa: Kitu kilichonishika zaidi siyo ile makala yenyewe, lakini maoni.

eng: Juuuuuust so we're clear, Saudi is not a bunch of tents stuck together with roaming camels, men in turbans singing "Allah o akbar" raping women cause it’s their right and having a harem of no less then 20.
swa: Nataka ieleweke kwamba Saudi siyo mahema machache yanayounganishwa na ngamia wanaorandaranda, na wanaume wenye vilemba waimbao "Allah o akbar" huku wakiwabaka wanawake kwa sababu ni haki yao na wanamiliki nyumba ya harimu yenye vigoli si chini ya 20.

eng: Oh and we don’t circumcise our women, man that’s just nasty and wrong on too many levels.
swa: Oh, na pia hatutahiri wanawake wetu, hilo ni jambo la hovyo na ni kosa katika ngazi nyingi.

eng: Women are not locked up at home and any who are is a matter of the family culture not the country, still with me?
swa: Wanawake hawafungiwi nyumbani na yeyote yule ambaye kwamba hilo ni jambo la utamaduni wa familia na siyo nchi, upo?

eng: Good.
swa: Vyema.

eng: We're not backwards you morons, we're conservative, i.e. if you want to go and mingle with the opposite sex you go to a specific place.
swa: Hatuko nyuma nyie mafidhuli, sisi ni wahafidhina, yaani, kama unapotaka kwenda kujichanganya na mtu wa jinsia tofauti kuna maeneo maalumu.

eng: Now my more important point is, since when do you get off judging people: "Close Starbucks!!
swa: Sasa hoja yangu ya msingi hapa ni kwamba hivi tangu lini mmeanza kuhukumu watu: "Fungeni Starbucks!!

eng: They shouldn’t support them by opening families sections" – umm, excuse me?
swa: Zisiwe na sehemu zinazokaribisha familia" – umm, hapana samahani?

eng: I ain’t complaining, and I need my coffee, so seriously man, GET LOST, I didn’t hire anyone to be my speaker.
swa: Silalamiki na ninahitaji kahawa yangu, tuache utani, POTEENI MBALI, sikukodi mtu yeyote awe msemaji wangu.

eng: For those of you who are still convinced we are an oppressed nation and us poor poor woman need to be taught how to fight back and if not well go ahead and fight for us, let me give you a little review of what a regular day in Riyadh is like.
swa: Kwa wale ambao bado mnashawishika kwamba sisi ni taifa kandamizi na kwamba sisi wanawake masikini tunahitaji kufunzwa namna ya kupambana na kama sivyo vyema vyema endeleeni kutupigania, ngojeni niwape maelezo mafupi namna siku ya kawaida inavyokuwa jijini Riyadh.

eng: Now yesterday I wake up, make my coffee … get dressed put my abaya on (if it’s too horrific to think about this, think of it as a jacket), pick up my little angel, get in my chauffeured car a.k.a. driver included, drop my girl off, and go to work.
swa: Jana niliamka nikatengeneza kahawa yangu… nikatinga vazi langu la abaya (kama unaona hili linatisha kufikirika, lifikirie kama jaketi), nikamchukua malaika wangu mdogo, nikaingia ndani ya gari yangu iendeshwayo na dereva ndani yake, nikamshusha binti yangu, halafu nikaenda kazini.

eng: By 1:30 I'm having lunch from Subway with the girls, then go back to work and leave at 4:30, go home, relax, take a shower, get dressed, wait for the driver to take me to the Chinese place since I invited the girls out.
swa: Mida ya saa 7:30 napata chakula cha mchana na marafiki zangu wa kike kutoka mgahawa wa Subway, halafu nikarejea kazini na kutoka saa 10:30 jioni, narejea nyumbani, napumzika, naoga natinga mavazi yangu, namsubiri dereva anipeleke mgahawa wa Wachina kwani nilikuwa nimewakaribisha marafiki zangu wa kike.

eng: Get there around 9:45 and leave around 12, get home, get online, check my facebook and hotmail, then hit the sack by 2am.
swa: Nafika pale mida ya saa 3:45 hivi halafu naondoka kama saa 6, nafika nyumbani, naingia mtandaoni, naangalia facebook na hotmail, halafu naingia kitandani saa 8.

eng: OH MY GOD, WHAT HORROR, HOW CAN I LIVE A LIFE SO OPPRESSED, AAAAHHHHHH!!!!
swa: MUNGU WANGU, JINAMIZI GANI HILI, NINAWEZAJE KUISHI MAISHA YA KIKANDAMIZWA NAMNA HII, AAAAHHHHHH!!!!

eng: My point is, some people have no knowledge about what goes on in our life yet they deem it their right to judge and be almighty.
swa: Hoja yangu ni kwamba baadhi ya watu hawana welewa kuhusu nini kinaendelea ndani ya maisha yetu na bado wanafikiri wana haki ya kuamua na kuwa wakuu.

eng: We're different, hell yeah, being different from what you think is right doesn’t make us bad or wrong it makes us us.
swa: Tuko tofauti, naam, na kwa kuwa tuko tofauti na vile ambavyo unafikiri ni sawa haitufanyi sisi kuwa wabaya au wenye makosa inatufanya sisi kuwa sisi.

eng: Deal with it and butt out.
swa: Kabiliana na ukweli huo au jitoe.

eng: An illegitimate girl of primary-school age in Zhuhai , South China, was turned away by the local schools, because her mother is not able to afford the hefty fine for illegitimacy, according to sohu blogger Han Tao’s report .
swa: Binti mdogo 'haramu' wa umri wa kuanza elimu ya msingi huko Zhuhai, Kusini mwa Uchina, alikataliwa kujiunga na shule za eneo hilo kwa sababu tu mama yake hakuweza kulipa faini inayotozwa dhidi ya watoto wanaochukuliwa kuwa haramu, tunapata taarifa hii kutoka kwa mwanablogu wa sohu Han Tao.

eng: Citizen media videos have been uploaded informing of the situation arising in Venezuela between the Yukpa Indians of the Perijá Mountains, landowners and President Chávez.
swa: Picha za video zinatumwa kwenye mtandao wa intaneti na vyombo vya habari vya kiraia zikionyesha yale yanayojiri kuhusu mgogoro unaoibuka nchini Venezuela kati ya Wahindi wa jamii ya Yukpa wanaoishi katika milima ya Perijá, wamiliki wa ardhi na Rais Chávez.

eng: This dispute over land limits is 30 years in the making, when military forces displaced the Indigenous communities of the Yukpa by force and established landowners who have cattle ranches and have been working the lands ever since.
swa: Mgogoro huu kuhusu mipaka ya ardhi umekuwapo kwa takribani miaka 30, yaani tangu pale vikosi vya jeshi vilipowandoa kwa nguvu wanajamii wenyeji ya Ki-Yukpa na kuwapa ardhi hiyo wamiliki wapya walioanzisha mashamba makubwa ya mifugo, hasa ng'ombe, ambao wameendelea kuitumia ardhi hiyo tangu wakati huo.

eng: The Yukpa Indians have attempted to reclaim the lands taken from them, and even the Venezuelan president Hugo Chávez declared 10 years ago that the problems with land ownership in the Perijá Mountains should be resolved, but nothing was done to advance solutions.
swa: Wahindi wa ki-Yukpa wamejaribu mara kadhaa bila mafanikio kuitwaa upya ardhi waliyoporwa, na hata Rais wa Venezuela, Hugo Chávez, alipata kutangaza miaka 10 iliyopita kwamba tatizo hilo la ardhi limalizwe, lakini mpaka sasa hakuna cha maana kilichofanywa ili kupata suluhisho la kubadili hali ya mambo.

eng: Currently the Yukpa Indians have taken over the ranches, and the landowners who live off meat and dairy production are unable to continue their work.
swa: Kwa sasa Wahindi wa ki-Yukpa wameyatwaa tena mashamba hayo makubwa, na wale wamiliki waliokuwa wakiyashikilia na ambao walitegemea nyama na uzalishaji wa mazao ya mifugo kuendesha maisha wanashindwa kuendelea na kazi zao.

eng: This situation has been made more difficult due to military presence in the area which has caused a siege state, where the Indigenous groups are not allowed to walk freely on their lands or out of them and journalists are blocked from going inside the area to report of Human Rights abuses such as the alleged hiring of Colombian hit-men who have been targeting entire communities and who beat to death a 109 year old indigenous elder.
swa: Hali imezidi kuwa tata kutokana na uwepo wa vikosi vya jeshi katika eneo hilo na kulitenga eneo hilo na maeneo mengine ya nchi, hali ni mbaya kiasi kwamba makundi ya Wenyeji hawawezi kutembea kwa uhuru katika ardhi yao na wakati huohuo waandishi wa habari wanazuiwa kuingia ili kuripoti kuhusu vitendo vya uvunjaji wa Haki za Binadamu, hasa vile vinavyosemekana kufanywa na wauaji wa kukodi wa Kikolumbia ambao wamekuwa wakilenga kila mtu; hivi karibuni tu walimshambulia mpaka kumuua kikongwe wa miaka 109 mwenyeji wa eneo hilo.

eng: Finally the Yukpa broke through the communication blocks, have gotten through to the media and have reached the community of Machique on August 26th 2008, and Hugo Chávez has declared that these lands should be given back and the indigenous community's rights should be respected.
swa: Pamoja na vikwazo vyote hatimaye WaYukpa walifaulu kujipenyeza katika vikwazo vyote vya kuwasiliana na kuifikia jumuiya ya Machique mnamo tarehe 26 Agosti 2008, na hapo Hugo Chávez ametangaza kwamba ardhi hiyo haina budi kurejeshwa na kwamba haki za wenyeji wa eneo hilo hazina budi kuheshimiwa.

swa: Mbeki aliwasilisha nyaraka hizo siku moja tu baada ya kulitangazia taifa kwamba amejiuzulu.

swa: Hatua hiyo inafuatia tamko la Jaji Nicholson hivi karibuni katika Mahakama Kuu ya Pietermaritzburg kwamba huenda Mbeki na Waziri wa Sheria waliingilia kati katika uamuzi wa kumfikisha mahakamani Jacob Zuma.
