swa: Dispatch Now anazungumzia mipango ya kuanzishwa kwa chama kipya cha siasa nchini Afrika Kusini...

eng: Outgoing President Thabo Mbeki’s mother, Epainette, is backing moves to split the African National Congress (ANC) and form a new breakaway political party.
swa: Mama wa Rais Thabo Mbeki anayeondoka madarakani, Epainette, anaunga mkono mipango ya kukigawa chama cha ANC na kuanzisha chama kipya cha siasa.

eng: News of the plans by Mbeki supporters to form a new breakaway party emerged this weekend after the ANC national executive committee (NEC) announced that it had resolved to recall Mbeki from his office. Defence Minister Mosiuoa Lekota, his deputy Mluleki George and Gauteng Premier Mbhazima Shilowa are believed to be spearheading the campaign to start the still-to-be-named political party.
swa: Taarifa za mipango ya wanaomwunga mkono Mbeki za kuunda chama kipya ziliibuka mwishoni mwa juma lililopita baada ya tamko la Kamati Kuu ya Taifa ya ANC kutangaza uamuzi wake wa kumuondoa madarakani Mbeki kutoka katika nafasi ya juu kabisa nchini humo.Waziri wa ulinzi, Mosiuoa Lekota, makamu wake Mluleki George na Gauteng Premier Mbhazima Shilowa wanasadikiwa kuongoza juhudi hizo za kupiga kampeni ili kuanzishwa kwa chama hicho kipya ambacho bado hakijapewa jina.

eng: On Sunday George would neither confirm nor deny the moves, saying only that an announcement would be made soon.
swa: Mpaka Jumapili iliyopita George hakuwa tayari kuthibitisha au kukanusha tetesi kuhusu juhudi hizo, alisema tu kwamba tangazo lingetoka katika siku za hivi karibuni.

eng: On Monday, Ma’Mbeki, as the 92-year-old struggle veteran is affectionately known, said she was aware of the the plans and backed the move to split the ANC as she saw no future in the organisation under current president Jacob Zuma.
swa: Mnamo siku ya Jumatatu, Ma'Mbeki, kama anavyojulikana nguli huyu katika medani za siasa za Afrika ya Kusini mwenye umri wa miaka 92 alisema kwamba alikuwa na taarifa kuhusu mipango hiyo na aliiunga mkono ili kukigawa chama cha ANC kwa sababu hana imani na hali ya baadaye ya chama hicho chini ya Rais Jacob Zuma.

eng: The East News Watch Blog also wrote of the ANC's favoured candidate for the position of president, before the ministers mentioned above had resigned...
swa: Blogu ya The East News Watch Blog pia ilikuwa na taarifa kuhusu mtu aliyekuwa akipendekezwa na ANC kushika nafasi ya urais kabla ya mawaziri waliotajwa hapo kujiuzulu...

eng: The ANC has confirmed that its Deputy President Kgalema Motlanthe has been chosen as the party’s preferred candidate to serve as the country’s interim president after Thabo Mbeki leaves office on Thursday.
swa: ANC ilikuwa imetangaza kwamba Makamu wa Rais wa chama hicho Kgalema Motlanthe alikuwa ameteuliwa na chama kushika nafasi ya Rais katika kipindi cha mpito mara baada ya kuondoka Rais Thabo Mbeki mnamo siku ya Alhamis.

eng: The ANC’s Jessie Duarte says while parliament still has to vote on the matter today - that will just be a formality.
swa: Kiongozi mwandamizi wa ANC Jessie Duarte alisema kwamba ingawa Bunge lilikuwa bado kupiga kura lakini kwa hakika hiyo ilikuwa ni utaratibu tu.

eng: “Mr Kgalema Motlanthe is the ANC’s preferred candidate to become the next president of the Republic of South Africa.
swa: “Bw Kgalema Motlanthe ndiye chaguo la ANC kuwa Rais wa mpito wa Jamhuri ya Afrika ya Kusini.

eng: He will probably be sworn in immediately after the resignation of President Mbeki takes effect on the 25th of September.”
swa: Bila shaka ataapishwa mara moja baada ya kujiuzulu kwa Rais Thabo Mbeki na kuanza majukumu yake rasmi tarehe 25 Septemba.”

eng: Many South Africans right now are in absolute shock as to the events which are unfolding before their eyes, what the future holds, no-one knows, all we know is that right now, people are fearful as to the outcome of this situation.
swa: Raia wengi wa Afrika ya Kusini wamegubikwa na mshtuko kutokana na matukio yanayotokea hivi sasa mbele ya macho yao, hakuna ajuaye nini kitaendelea baadaye, wengi wana mashaka na hatma ya mambo yote haya.

eng: Photo above of the South African Houses of Parliament in Cape Town is by Nick Boalch and shared under a Creative Commons "Attribution-Non-Commercial-No Derivative" license.
swa: Picha iliyoko juu ya majumba ya Bunge la Afrika ya kusini huko Cape Town imepigwa na Nick Boalch na inatumika kupitia hati miliki za umma.

eng: In late September Barbara Hogan was appointed as South Africa's new health minister by interim President Kgalema Motlanthe, ousting her controversial predecessor Manto Tshabalala-Msimang.
swa: Mwishoni mwa mwezi Septemba, Barbara Hogan, aliteuliwa na Rais wa mpito Kgalema Motlanthe kuwa waziri mpya wa afya wa Afrika ya Kusini, akichukua nafasi ya mtangulizi wake mwenye utata mwingi, Manto Tshabalala-Msimang.

eng: AIDS activists and many South Africans are hopeful that this move will signal a shift in the government's HIV/AIDS policies.
swa: Wanaharakati wa masuala ya UKIMWI na raia wengi wa Afrika ya Kusini wana matumaini makubwa kwamba hatua hii huenda ikaashiria mabadiliko ya sera za serikali kuhusu suala la VVU na UKIMWI.

eng: Hogan, a veteran anti-apartheid activist and a long-term ANC (African National Congress) member, was previously the chair of the finance portfolio committee.
swa: Hogan, mwanamama mwanaharakati mkongwe dhidi ya ubaguzi wa rangi na mwanachama wa muda mrefu wa ANC, yaani African National Congress, hapo awali alikuwa mwenyekiti wa kamati ya kusimamia masuala ya fedha.

eng: Since becoming health minister, she has broken from the former government's stance on HIV/AIDS and has
swa: Tangu kuteuliwa kwake kuwa waziri wa afya, amebadili mwelekeo wa serikali iliyopita kuhusu VVU na UKIMWI na kuapa

eng: In the past Hogan publicly criticized former President Thabo Mbeki's stance and policies on HIV/AIDS.
swa: Siku za nyuma Hogan alipata kumkosoa waziwazi Rais wa zamani Thabo Mbeki na msimamo wake juu ya sera ya VVU na UKIMWI.

eng: Roughly 5.7 million people in South Africa are living with HIV and 350,000 people died of the disease last year (almost 1,000 deaths a day).
swa: Wastani wa watu milioni 5.7 nchini Afrika ya Kusini wanasemekana kuishi na VVU na kiasi cha watu 350,000 walifariki kutokana na UKIMWI mwaka jana nchini humo (wastani wa watu 1,000 kila siku).

eng: Tshabalala-Msimang has also been blamed for inadequately responding to South Africa's HIV/AIDS problem.
swa: Kwa upande mwingine Tshabalala-Msimang amelaumiwa vikali kwa kutofanya juhudi za kutosha kukabili tatizo la VVU na UKIMWI nchini humo.

eng: The former health minister promoted beetroot, garlic, and other foods as treatment for HIV/AIDS, resulting in the nickname "Dr. Beetroot," and has been accused of creating confusion about anti-retroviral drugs.
swa: Waziri huyo wa zamani wa afya alihamasisha matumizi ya vyakula kama vile beetroot, vitunguu saumu na vinginevyo kama tiba ya VVU na UKIMWI, jambo lililosababisha watu kumbatiza jina la "Dkt Beetroot", na zaidi ameshutumiwa kwa kusababisha mkanganyo kuhusu matumizi ya dawa za kurefusha maisha (ARV).

eng: Stephen, posting on irreverence, calls Tshabalala-Msimang a national embarrassment and Hogan a glimmer of hope.
swa: Stephen, akiandika kwenye tovuti ya irreverence, alimuita Tshabalala-Msimang kama aibu ya taifa na papo hapo akimwita Hogan kama tumaini lililorejea.

eng: Ciaran Parker, blogging on Ciaran’s Peculier Blog, elaborates on Tshabalala-Msimang's unorthodox views:
swa: Ciaran Parker, akitumia blogu yake ya Ciaran’s Peculier Blog, anafafanua kuhusu msimamo wa Tshabalala-Msimang usiokubaliwa na wengi:

eng:
Kgalema Motlanthe, while stating a desire to pursue continuity, has got rid of some of Mbeki’s more controversial ministers. 	“Ingawa Kgalema Motlanthe ameahidi kutoleta mabadiliko makubwa, bado ameatosa baadhi wa mawaziri wenye utata mkubwa waliokuwa kwenye serikali ya Mbeki.
Chief among these is Health Minister Dr Manto Tshabalala-Msimang, the chief theoretician behind Mbeki’s AIDS denialist policies. 	Mmoja wao akiwa ni Waziri wa Afya, Dkt Manto Tshabalala-Msimang, aliyekuwa mwananadharia mkubwa katika hoja ya Mbeki ya sera za kukana uwepo wa UKIMWI.
Mbeki’s government refused to accept the role the HIV virus has in the spread of AIDS, and his health minister stated that anti-retroviral drugs, which have been shown to have some effect in fighting the disease, were too expensive…Medical professionals working in the South African health service who publicly disagreed with the minister’s bizarre theories have been victimised.
swa: Serikali ya Mbeki ilikataa katakata kuona uhusiano uliopo kati ya VVU na UKIMWI, na waziri wake wa afya alijenga hoja kwamba hata dawa za kurefusha maisha, ambazo kwa kweli zimeonyesha kusaidia katika juhudi za kukabili gonjwa hili, zilikuwa ghali mno ... Wataalamu wa afya wanaofanya kazi nchini Afrika ya Kusini na ambao walipingana waziwazi na nadharia za kushangaza za waziri huyu walijikuta wakifanywa kuwa wahanga."

eng: Earlier this week, at the opening of the International AIDS Vaccine 2008 conference in Cape Town, Hogan publicly declared that HIV does cause AIDS and should be treated with conventional medicine.
swa: Mapema juma lililopita, wakati wa uzinduzi wa mkutano juu ya Chanjo ya UKIMWI ya Kimataifa ya 2008 (International AIDS Vaccine 2008) huko Cape Town, Hogan, alitangaza hadharani kwamba VVU husababisha UKIMWI na kwamba ni lazima kukabiliana nao kwa kutumia dawa za hospitalini.

eng: She also said the government was committed to scale-up mother-to-child prevention programs, therapies that prevent HIV-positive pregnant moms from passing on the disease, and that an effective HIV vaccine was desperately needed.
swa: kuongeza nguvu katika programu za kuzuia uambukizaji wa kutoka kwa mama kwenda kwa mtoto, dawa zinazozuia akina mama wajawazito wenye VVU kuwapatia watoto wao ambao hawajazaliwa maambukizo na kueleza kwamba chango madhubuti ya VVU ilikuwa ikihitajika mno.

eng: Scientists, activists, and many bloggers have expressed relief and excitement following Hogan's address.
swa: Wanasayansi, wanaharakati na wanablogu wengi wameeleza furaha yao kufuatia hotuba iliyotolewa na Hogan.

eng: Haley, blogging on adventures as an ambassadorial scholar, says:
swa: Haley, akiblogu katika tovuti inayoitwa ujasura kama mwanafunzi balozi, ana hili la kusema:

eng:
So most people I talk to find it - surprising - that democratically elected government officials, in today's world, would deny such ideas as ... say... that HIV causes AIDS. 	“Kusema kweli, watu wengi ninaozungumza nao wanashangazwa na jambo hili - kwamba maafisa wa serikali waliochaguliwa kwa njia za kidemokrasi wanakana fikra ... kwamba ... VVU husababisha UKIMWI.
However, sadly in South Africa, that has been the case.... but no longer my friends, no longer.
swa: Hata hivyo, kwa bahati mbaya, hapa Afrika ya Kusini hivyo ndivyo hali ilivyokuwa ... lakini sasa mambo yamebadilika, msimamo si huo tena.”

eng: Ray Hartley, posting on The Times, South Africa, blog adds:
swa: Ray Hartley, anayeandika katika The Times, Afrika ya Kusini, anablogu akiongeza:

eng:
'We know that HIV causes AIDS.' 	“‘Tunajua kwamba VVU husababisha UKIMWI.'
With these words, the Health Minister, Barbara Hogan, ended an ignominious decade of Aids denial that has cost South Africa countless lives and has forced those with the virus to live in the shadows.
swa: Kwa kauli hii, Waziri wa Afya, Barbara Hogan, amehitimisha muongo mzima wa aibu ya kukana uwepo wa UKIMWI jambo ambalo limeigharimu Afrika ya Kusini idadi isiyohesabika ya maisha ya binadamu, wakati huohuo wale waliokuwa wakiishi na VVU wakiishia kuishi kana kwamba kwenye kivuli chao wenyewe.”

eng: It's difficult to determine how many lives were impacted by previous HIV/AIDS policies, but the Treatment Action Campaign (TAC) says that over two million South Africans died of AIDS during Mbeki's presidency and at least 300,000 deaths could have been avoided if he had met basic constitutional requirements.
swa: Ni vigumu kueleza idadi kamili ya watu walioathiriwa na sera zilizopita juu ya VVU na UKIMWI, lakini Shirika la Treatment Action Campaign (TAC) (Kampeni ya Kutetea Tiba) linakadiria kwamba kiasi cha raia milioni mbili wa Afrika ya Kusini walikufa kutokana na kuugua UKIMWI katika kipindi ambapo Mbeki alikuwa madarakani, na kwamba walau jumla ya vifo 300,000 vingeweza kuepukwa endapo tu angetimiza baadhi ya mambo ya msingi ya kikatiba.

eng: Some bloggers say that both Mbeki and Tshabalala-Msimang have blood on their hands.
swa: Baadhi ya wanablogu wanasema kwamba wote wawili, Mbeki na Tshabalala-Msimang wametapakaa damu mikononi mwao.

eng: Soneka Kamuhuza, blogging on Things That Make You Go Mmmh!, blames mostly Mbeki.
swa: Soneka Kamuhuza, anayeandika kupitia blogu ya Things That Make You Go Mmmh! anamshutumu vikali Mbeki.

eng:
Their intellectual apathy, targeted myopia and general dis-ingenuousness played dangerously to help continue the pandemic. 	“Umawazo mgando wao , umbumbumbu wa kukusudia na kujitia kwao kuwa wanyofu kulichochea tu uendelevu wa janga hili.
Pushing holistic approaches, which when used singularly, cannot be an effective treatment for the virus, they battered their nation with their fortified and unified ignorance. 	Kutumia njia ya kutazama tatizo zima kwa upana badala ya chanzo chake, pasipo kuingiza na njia nyingine, hakuwezi kuwa njia madhubuti ya kutibu VVU, waliingiza nchi katika wakati mgumu kwa kutumia umbumbumbu wao ambao waliulinda kwa njia zote.
It is now estimated that South Africa has the world's highest numbers of people infected with HIV.	Hivi sasa inakadiriwa kwamba Afrika ya Kusini inaongoza duniani kwa kuwa na idadi kubwa ya watu wanaoishi na VVU.
Somehow, I see Mbeki's hand all over this…In a country rich with natural resources, he has cheated its most important resource, the people of an opportunity to make a critical head start in the fight against AIDS.
swa: Kwa namna fulani, naona ushawishi wa Mbeki katika jambo hili ... Katika nchi ambayo ina utajiri mkubwa wa maliasili, amehadaa rasilimali watu iliyo muhimu sana, kwa kuwanyima fursa ya watu kuamua na kuanza kupambana na tatizo hili la UKIMWI kikamilifu.”

eng: Many hope that Hogan will reverse some of this damage.
swa: Wengi wanaamini kwamba Hogan atarekebisha mambo yaliyoharibika kwa sehemu fulani.

eng: A post on peripheries points out that many people expect that the period of politically-supported AIDS denialism in South Africa is over.
swa: Makala katika Peripheries inaonyesha kwamba watu wanatarajia kwamba wakati wa kuwa na ukanaji wa UKIMWI huku ukipewa nguvu na msukumo wa kisiasa nchini Afrika ya Kusini tayari umefikia kikomo.

eng: However, others remain cautious.
swa: Hata hivyo, wapo ambao hawako kupaparikia mambo haraka hivyo.

eng: BillyC, commenting on a blog post on The Times, South Africa, says:
swa: BillyC, akitoa maoni yake juu ya makala iliyoandikwa katika The Times, la Afrika ya Kusini anasema:

eng:
Barbara Hogan has a mountain to climb to reverse the almost terminal damage to health care on Manto’s watch. 	“Barbara Hogan ana kazi kubwa mbele yake ili kurekebisha mambo ambayo kwa kiasi fulani tayari amekwishasababisha madhara kwa mfumo wa afya katika uangalizi wa Manto.
Staff competency, morale and levels as well as a slew of health policies and legislation all have to be addressed. 	Uwezo wa wafanyakazi, ari ya kazi, na viwango vya utendaji ukiachia mbali sera za afya na sheria, yote ni mambo ambayo hayana budi kushughulikiwa.
In addition the promotion of voodoo medicine and demonisation of western science is now deeply embedded in the national psyche.	Zaidi ya hilo, kuna uhamasishaji wa matumizi ya dawa na upungaji pepo wa kivuduu, vilevile uhusianishaji wa kishetani na sayansi ya magharibi vyote vikiwa vimejikita sawasawa katika mfumo wa kufikiri wa taifa.
It will take years of hard, courageous and diligent work to get us back to a health system that’s respected and effective. 	Itachukua miaka mingi ya kazi ngumu, yenye kujaa ujasiri na unyoofu ili kuturejesha katika mfumo wa afya ulio wa heshima na wenye ufanisi.
We can only wish Barbara Hogan god speed.	Tumwombee Barbara Hogan apate kasi.
She’s gonna need it.
swa: Kusema kweli anaihitaji.”

eng: Photo of South African AIDS Ribbons by mvcorks on Flickr.
swa: Picha ya Utepe wa Ukimwi wa Afrika ya Kusini imetoka kwa mvcorks katika mtandao wa picha wa Flickr.

eng: Although Bahrain has a number of universities, both government and private, many Bahrainis have the opportunity to go abroad to pursue undergraduate and postgraduate studies, often by means of scholarships.
swa: Ingawa Bahrain ina idadi kadhaa ya vyuo vikuu, vya umma na binafsi, raia wengi wa nchi hiyo hupata fursa ya kwenda ng'ambo kwa masomo ya shahada ya kwanza na hata zile za juu, mara nyingi kwa kutegemea ufadhili.

eng: One of the first problems they face is that few people know where Bahrain is.
swa: Moja ya matatizo ya kwanza wanayokumbana nayo huko ughaibuni ni kwamba watu wachache tu hufahamu ni wapi Bahrain ilipo.

eng: In this post we hear about the experiences of three bloggers who have just gone abroad for higher studies, to Japan, Britain and the United States, and a fourth blogger who has been studying in India for some time.
swa: Katika makala hii tunafuatilia uzoefu wa wanablogu watatu ambao ndiyo kwanza wamekwenda ng'ambo kwa masomo: kule Japan, Uingereza na Marekani na mwanablogu wa nne ambaye anasoma India kwa kipindi fulani hivi sasa.

eng: Cradle of Humanity has just gone to study in Cleveland, Ohio, and she is feeling a little frustrated:
swa: Cradle of Humanity amekwenda masomoni huko Cleveland, Ohio (Moja ya jimbo la Marekani, na anajihisi kukanganyikiwa na hali ya mambo huko:

eng: I sometimes dread it when people ask where I come from.
swa: Mara nyingine huogopa pale watu wanaponiuliza juu ya kule ninakotoka.

eng: Not more than 10% of people who hear “Bahrain” as answer have some sort of idea where that country might be, but that’s not my cause of annoyance.
swa: Si zaidi ya asilimia 10 ya wale wanaosikia nikitamka "Bahrain" kama jibu la kule nitokako wanaelewa au kuwa na picha kichwani juu ya mahali nchi hii ilipo, lakini hicho siyo hasa kinachonisababishia simanzi.

eng: For those who know that Bahrain is indeed in the Persian Gulf, there is one thing that comes to mind – wealth.
swa: Kwa wale wanaofahamu kwamba Bahrain ipo katika Ghuba ya Ajemi, kuna kitu ambacho huwaingia vichwani - utajiri.

eng: Some people might ask, but it’s those who assume who annoy me the most.
swa: Mara nyingine baadhi yao huuliza, lakini hawa ni wale ambao nadhani hunitia simanzi zaidi.

eng: For the past two months I made a lot of friends, mainly Indians given the demographics of the student body in my program.
swa: Ndani ya miezi miwili iliyopita nimepata marafiki wengi sana, hasa Wahindi kwa kuzingatia idadi ya wanafunzi walio katika Kozi ninayochukua.

eng: Despite the fact that most of these are actually Indian elites, owners of chains of businesses and are wealthy themselves – they love to point out that I must be wealthy.
swa: Licha ya ukweli kwamba wengi wao katika hawa ni Wahindi wa hali ya juu, wanaomiliki biashara nyingi na wao wenyewe ni matajiri - wanapenda sana kunieleza kwamba kwa vyovyote mimi pia lazima niwe mtu tajiri.

eng: When at some occasions I said just that, it appeared that some have the notion that we’re unnecessarily wealthy, that is, it’s undeserved wealth; while theirs is hard worked for.
swa: Mara nyingine nilipoeleza kuhusu ninakotoka wapo wanaoamini kwamba sisi ni matajiri kupita kiasi, lakini utajiri ambao hatukuustahili; wakati ambapo wao waliufanyia kazi utajiri wao.

eng: Oh, and they use Bahrain and Dubai interchangeably.
swa: Zaidi sana ni kwamba mara nyingi wanachanganya kati ya Bahrain na Dubai.

eng: - Public transport here is not very good, but getting a car is very expensive. I would’ve got one
swa: - Usafiri wa umma hapa si mzuri sana, lakini kumiliki gari pia ni ghali mno, vinginevyo ningekuwa nimeshajipatia moja

eng: - Used or new?
swa: - La mtumba au jipya?

eng: - Used, I’m only here for a short period of time.
swa: - La mtumba, mie nipo hapa kwa kipindi kifupi tu.

eng: - Get a new one it’s better
swa: - Si afadhali ununue jipya, hilo ni bora zaidi.

eng: - It’ll be much more expensive
swa: - Lakini hilo litakuwa ghali sana.

eng: - But you come from Bahrain, you can buy a car!
swa: - Wewe si unatoka Bahrain, unaweza kununua gari!

eng: - You mean you’re not rich?
swa: - Unamaanisha wewe si tajiri?

eng: - Actually, no.
swa: - Kwa kusema ukweli mimi si tajiri.

eng: - Everyone in Dubai was rich.
swa: - Haiwezekani, kule Dubai kila mmoja ni tajiri.

eng: - I don’t know about that, but not everyone in Bahrain is rich.
swa: - Kuhusu Dubai, sijui, lakini kule Bahrain si kila mtu ni tajiri.

eng: Yagoob, who has just arrived in Nagoya, has to deal with something even more basic - language:
swa: Yagoob, ambaye amewasili huko Nagoya, yeye anakabiliana na tatizo la msingi zaidi - lugha:

eng: To be honest, the culture shock has hit me very hard!
swa: Kwa kusema ukweli, tofauti ya tamaduni imenistusha mno!

eng: Hardly anyone I’ve met so far had the slightest knowledge of the English language.
swa: Yaani nimekutana na watu wachache mno wanaozungumza Kiingereza.

eng: I feel like a 21st century caveman, trying to communicate with the most primitive of ways, hand waving and speaking English in a very slow and loud way.
swa: Najihisi kama mtu wa zama za mawe aliye katika karne ya 21, maana natumia njia za kijima kabisa ili kuwasiliana, huku nikitumia ishara za mikono na kuzungumza taratibu kwa sauti ya juu katika Kiingereza.

eng: My dorm room is quite Japanese, extremely tiny and everything is earthquake proof so it’s like living in an aluminium sardine can.
swa: Chumba changu cha kulala bwenini ama kwa hakika ni cha Kijapani, ni kidogo na kila kitu kimewekwa tayari kukabili matetemeko ya ardhi, yaani ni kama kuishi katika kopo la dagaa wa kusindika.

eng: Many of the things I have around the room seem to have instructions on it, but all in Japanese so I have no idea how they work so far!
swa: Karibu kila kitu kilicho chumbani mwangu kimewekewa maelekezo, lakini yote kwa Kijapani kwa hiyo sijui yanatumikaje mpaka sasa!

eng: The subway is quite reminiscent to the London Tube except that it’s much cleaner and a person like me sticks out like a sore thumb (as if a tall fat sweaty hairy Arab wouldn’t stick out anywhere).
swa: Njia ya treni za chini kwa chini inanikumbusha ile ya kule Landani tofauti tu ni kwamba hii ni safi zaidi na mtu kama mimi nakuwa nimejitokeza mno kama dole gumba lililovimba (bila shaka mahali popote mwarabu mrefu, mnene mwenye vinyweleo na jasho jingi angeonekana zaidi).

eng: The people of Nagoya seem to have never met a Bahraini before, at least that’s what the people at my dorm office say, although I am surprised that they know where it is (maybe because of the many hard fought battles on the football pitch over the last few years) and when I chatted with one of my Chinese neighbours, ‘Andy’, he said, “Aah, you are from West Asia!”
swa: Yaelekea watu wa hapa Nagoya hawajawahi kukutana na yeyote kutoka Bahrain, walau hicho ndicho wanachonieleza watu wanaofanya kazi katika bweni langu, hata hivyo nashangazwa na ukweli kwamba wanajua kule ilipo nchi hiyo (pengine ni kwa sababu ya mapambano makali katika viwanja vya kandanda miaka ya hivi karibuni) na nilipozungumza na mmoja wa majirani zangu wa Kichina, 'Andy', alisema, "Ooh, kumbe wewe unatoka Asia Magharibi!" na nafikiri yuko sahihi ... hasa ukizingatia kwamba sasa nipo huku Mashariki ya Mbali.

eng: I guess I am…especially when I’m in the Far East.
swa: MuJtAbA AlMoAmEn anasoma kule India, na anatuambia ni nini kinachomfanya apende kuwa huko:

eng: Perhaps being away from home has its negative aspects, but there is no doubt that there are positive aspects to it too.
swa: Inawezekana kwamba kuwa mbali na nyumbani kuna ubaya wake, lakini hakuna shaka kwamba kuna upande mzuri pia.

eng: I have previously discussed the pros and cons of being away from home; I have no intention of repeating myself, and will write about something different today.
swa: Nimewahi hapo kabla kujadili faida na hasara za kuwa mbali na nyumbani; sina lengo la kujirudia, na kwa hiyo leo nitaandika kuhusu kitu tofauti.

eng: I want to write about contemplation, calm, the ability to read, and the free time which I can spend usefully.
swa: Nataka kuandika kuhusu tafakari, utulivu, uwezo wa kusoma na muda wangu huru ninaoweza kuutumia kwa malengo mazuri.

eng: In Bahrain, among family and friends, I don't have much time to read newspapers, whether local, Arab or international.
swa: Niwapo Bahrain, kati ya ndugu na marafiki, huwa sipati muda wa kusoma magazeti, yawe ya palepale nchini, ya Kiarabu au hata ya kimataifa.

eng: I also don't have time to read books such as biographies, novels, or those on intellectual topics.
swa: Pia sipati muda wa kusoma vitabu kama vile kuhusu maisha ya watu binafsi, hadithi, au hata kuhusu mada za kujiendeleza kiakili.

eng: Here in India, there is a lot of time for reflection.
swa: Hapa India, kuna muda tele wa kujitafakari.

eng: I feel mentally calm and I can think a lot - I find solutions for any problems or obstacles I face and what is even sweeter is that I find more than one solution.
swa: Najisikia kuwa na utulivu wa kiakili na kwa hiyo naweza kufikiri sana - najikuta naweza kupata suluhu kwa karibu kila tatizo au kikwazo kinachonikabili, na kitamu zaidi ni kwamba napata suluhisho zaidi ya moja kwa tatizo fulani.

eng: I don't depend on one only, and weigh my options, and if this proves anything, it is a testimony to the mental and spiritual calmness I live in.
swa: Nakuwa sitegemei suluhisho moja tu, kwa hiyon naweza kupima masuluhisho mbalimbali niliyo nayo, na kama hii ina maana yoyote, basi walau ni ushahidi wa utulivu wa kiakili na kiroho nilio nao kwa sasa.

eng: I cannot deny how difficult it is to be away from home.
swa: Nashindwa kukana jinsi gani ilivyo vigumu kuwa mbali na nyumbani.

eng: The Earth is the Earth, the third planet in the solar system.
swa: Dunia ni Dunia, sayari ya tatu kutoka kwenye jua katika mfumo huu wa jua.

eng: We all studied that and know it scientifically.
swa: Sote tulijifunza jambo hilo na tunalichukulia kuwa ni ukweli wa kisayansi.

eng: But the truth is that our Earth isn't the same when you move from one place to the other.
swa: Lakini ukweli ni kwamba Dunia yetu siyo ileile endapo utaondoka na kwenda mahali pengine.

eng: That land where I lived all my life, with its share of good and bad, and which holds my family and friends is more dear to me than all the world's lands.
swa: Nchi ile nilikokulia na kuishi maisha yangu yote, pamoja na uzuri na ubaya wake, na ambayo imewabeba ndugu na marafiki zangu kwa kweli ni kipenzi changu kuliko nchi na ardhi nyingine zote Duniani.

eng: Despite the beauty of the land I live on now - it isn't worth a speck of sand from my beloved country.
swa: Licha ya uzuri wa nchi ninayoishi hivi sasa - haina thamani hata ya chembe ya mchanga ikilinganishwa na nchi yangu ninayoipenda sana.

eng: Here, in the UK, the weather is lovely.
swa: Hapa Uingereza, hali ya hewa ni ya kupendeza mno.

eng: I have seen an autumn like nothing I have seen in my life before.
swa: Nimeyaona majira ya mapukutiko ambayo sikuwahi kamwe kuyaona maishani mwangu.

eng: At school we used to study that there was an autumn in which leaves fall from the trees but I have never seen that with my very own eyes except here.
swa: Tulipokuwa shule tulijifunza kwamba kuna majira fulani ya mapukutiko ambapo miti ilipukutisha majani, nilikuwa sijawahi kuliona jambo hilo isipokuwa hapa.

eng: And while we suffer from the lack of rain in my country, it regularly rains here and makes me eager for life, a life that is rejuvenated by the rains, which make it the oasis it is now.
swa: Na wakati ambapo sisi kule nyumbani tuna uhaba wa mvua, hapa inanyesha sana na kunifanya kutamani maisha zaidi, maisha yanayohuishwa na mvua, na kufanya chemchem ambayo bado inaendelea kuwepo.

eng: Am I hallucinating?
swa: Hivi ninapata maruweruwe?

eng: I don't see any connection in what I have written on these pages except that they are words that have congested my mind and which I have translated in this small space and this window I look into the world from.
swa: Sioni uhusiano wowote uliopo kati ya maneno niliyoandika kwenye kurasa hizi zaidi ya maneno ambayo yamekuwa yakiisongasonga akili yangu na ambayo nimeyefasiri katika kidirisha hiki kidogo ninachotumia kuitazama dunia.

eng: Please forgive me my dear ones.
swa: Tafadhali nisameheni rafiki zangu.

eng: There is nothing I want to talk about today except for my love and longing for my land and nation.
swa: Sitaki kuzungumzia kingine chochote kile isipokuwa upendo na hamu ya kuwa katika ardhi na taifa langu.

eng: In 1985, a U.S. Congressman named John McCain traveled to Chile and met with dictator Augusto Pinochet, among other government officials.
swa: Mwaka 1985, Mbunge wa bunge la Marekani aitwaye John Mccain alizuru nchini Chile na kukutana na mtawala wa kiimla Augusto Pinochet, akiwa na viongozi wengine wa serikali.

eng: The previously unreported meeting was revealed by journalist John Dinges, who published the findings in his blog CIPER , as well as in the Huffington Post, where he writes about John McCain "who has harshly criticized the idea of sitting down with dictators without pre-conditions, appears to have done just that." with "Pinochet, one of the world's most notorious violators of human rights credited with killing more than 3,000 civilians and jailing tens of thousands of others."
swa: Mkutano huo ambao haujawahi kuripotiwa hapo awali umewekwa wazi na mwandishi wa habari John Dinges, ambaye amechapisha habari hiyo kwenye blogu yake CIPHER , kadhalika katika blogu ya Huffington Post, ambako huwa anaandika masuala yanayomhusu John McCain "ambaye amekuwa akishutumu vikali dhana ya kuketi na watawala wa kiimla bila ya masharti yoyote, inaonekana kuwa alifanya hivyo na "Pinochet, mmoja wa watawala wakiukaji wa haki za binaadamu ambaye anashutumiwa kuua zaidi ya raia 3,000 na kuwasweka gerezani makumi ya maelfu wengine"

eng: Chilean blogger Juan Guillermo Tejeda writes about some of the details of the meeting :
swa: Bloga wa KiChile juan Guillermo Tedeja anaandika kuhusu baadhi ya yaliyojiri kwenye mkutano huo :

eng: As the US Elections loom closer, international attention to US foreign policy and the candidates has increased.
swa: Kadiri uchaguzi wa Marekani unavyokaribia, ndivyo kadiri macho ya kimataifa yanavyozidi kuelekezwa katika sera za nje za taifa hilo na wagombea wakuu.

eng: Projects like Current TV's Collective Journalism and Global Voices' Voices Without Votes have taken the task to gather this information and bring a global perspective on a local issue.
swa: Kazimiradi kama vile ile ya Collective Journalism inayofanywa na Current TV (Uandishi wa Habari wa Umma wa Current TV) na Global Voices' Voices Without Votes (Mradi wa Global Voices - Sauti Zisizo na Kura) zimechukua jukumu la kukusanya taarifa na kuzipa mtazamo wa kimataifa katika masuala ya ndani ya sehemu fulani tu ulimwenguni.

eng: Current TV's Collective Journalism program has started a series of video reports on how the rest of the world views the US.
swa: Programu ya Collective Journalism inayorushwa na Current TV imeanzisha mfululizo wa ripoti za video zinaoonyesha maoni ya watu wengine ulimwenguni kuhusu Marekani.

eng: In The View from Over There, people from many different countries state their views on foreign policy, the war in Iraq, the situation with Iran and mention who they would want as the future president of the USA.
swa: Katika programu ya The View from Over There (Mtazamo Kutoka Kwingineko) watu kutoka mataifa mbalimbali wanatoa maoni yao kuhusu sera ya nje, vita vya Iraki, hali tete juu ya Irani na kumtaja ni nani wangependa awe rais anayefuata wa Marekani.

eng: The video interviews are sometimes in different languages, but all of it is subtitled in English.
swa: Mahojiano hayo ya video mara nyingine huwa katika lugha mbalimbali, lakini hewekewa tafsiri zake katika Kiingereza.

eng: This video also uses footage from other shows on the US Elections 2008, but this time concentrating on the foreign perspective.
swa: Video hii pia inatumia vipande vya video vinavyoonyesha Uchaguzi wa Marekani 2008, lakini hasa vile vinavyokazia mtazamo wa kigeni.

eng: This is something Global Voices and Reuters have been doing for a while now at Voices Without Votes: gathering opinions from all over the planet on the US elections.
swa: Hili ni jambo moja ambalo Global Voices na Shirika la Reuters wamekuwa wakifanya kwa kitambo fulani kupitia programu ya Voices Without Votes: kwa kukusanya maoni kutoka pande zote za ulimwengu juu ya uchaguzi wa Marekani.

eng: If you have any posts you would like to submit to the site, you can do it here.
swa: Kama kuna taarifa ungependa kutuma kwenye programu hii, unaweza kufanya hivyo hapa.

eng: Current TV's next Collective Journalism assignment will be a worldwide view on the US immigration policies.
swa: Programu ifuatayo ya Collective Journalism inayotolewa na Current TV katika kazi zake itakuwa ni mtazamo wa dunia nzima juu ya sera za Marekani za uhamiaji.

eng: In an article published in March, economists William Easterly and Yaw Nyarko noted that in Sub-Saharan Africa, remittances (money sent by immigrants abroad back to their home countries) on average amounted to 81 percent of the foreign aid received by an individual country.
swa: Katika makala iliyochapishwa mwezi Machi, wachumi William Easterly na Yaw Nyarko wanaeleza kwamba katika nchi zilizo chini ya Jangwa la Sahara, kiasi cha fedha kinachotumwa na wahamiaji wanaotoka bara hilo ni wastani wa asilimia 81 ya misaada ya fedha kutoka nchi za kigeni kwa kila nchi.

eng: The role of the diaspora in the development of Madagascar has been discussed previously in the Malagasy blogosphere.
swa: Dhima ya waMadagascar walio nchi za mbali kwa maendeleo ya nchi yao imewahi kujadiliwa hapo kabla katika ulimwengu wa wanablogu wa Madagascar.

eng: Bloggers recently discussed the impact of living abroad on the behavior of Malagasies and how it alters their relationships with their friends and relatives back home.
swa: Hivi karibuni wanablogu walijadili athari ya kuishi ughaibuni kwa mienendo ya WaMadagascar na jinsi mabadiliko hayo yanavyoathiri uhusiano na marafiki na ndugu zao walio nyumbani.

eng: News2dago narrates how a close friendship with an old friend from school slowly vanished because that friend left for France:
swa: News2dago anasimulia ni kwa namna gani alipoteza urafiki wa karibu aliokuwa na rafiki yake mmoja wa tangu enzi za shule. Anaeleza kwamba uhusiano wao ulififia polepole mara tu baada ya rafiki yake kuondoka kwenda zake Ufaransa:

eng: The success of Twitter has had an enormous influence on many new sites, that want to copy the formula: short messages, from all kinds of devices, for a restricted audience. One of the sites that follows this example is Reporting On, a kind of Twitter for journalists, that has been in working in beta phase since last year.
swa: Mafanikio ya huduma ya twitter (twita)yameweza kuleta mvuto mkubwa katika tovuti nyingi za habari,zinazotaka kuiga kanuni hii:taarifa fupi fupi, kutoka katika kila aina ya zana, kwa ajili ya kadamnasi fulani teule.Tovuti moja ambayo inafuata mfano huu ni Reporting on, aina ya Twita kwa wanahabari,ambayo umekuwa ikifanya kazi katika majaribio tangu mwaka jana.

eng: And if you register, you'll find the site is getting quite successful particularly among Latin American journalists.
swa: Kama ukijisajili utaona ni jinsi gani tovuti inavyofanikiwa miongoni mwa waandishi wa habari wa Kilatino.

eng: The structure is very similar to Twitter's; we can write up to 140 characters, which most users take advantage of to write news in the form of headlines.
swa: Muundo au utaratibu wake ni sawa na ule wa Twita; tunaweza kuandika herufi zisizozidi 140, na watumiaji wengi wanautumia utaratibu huo ipasavyo kwa kuandika habari katika mtindo wa vichwa vya habari.

eng: Each piece of news can be tagged with many words. In the left column, we can find the most popular tags.
swa: Kila kipande cha habari kinaweza kuunganishwa katika maneno mengi.

eng: We can comment in each others posts as well as reply to them, but we can't follow certain users or filter contents, except for the tags.
swa: Katika upande kushoto tunaweza kupata viunganisho maarufu.Tunaweza kutoa maoni katika kila bandiko pia kujibu maoni hayo,lakini hatuwezi kumfuatilia mtumiaji au kuchuja habari isipokuwa katika viunganisho.

eng: Pablo Mancini interviewed Ryan Sholin, who's behind the project, and he points out that Reporting On "is a non profit project financed by Knight News Challenge in order to improve local news, connecting people who don't talk with each other enough".
swa: Pablo Mancini alifanya mahojiano na Ryan Sholin ambaye yupo nyuma ya mradi huu, anabainisha kuwa Reporting On "ni mradi usiolenga katika faida unaofadhiliwa na Knight News Challenge ili kuimarisha habari za ndani, kuunganisha watu ambao huwa hawasemezani vya kutosha na wengine".

eng: And he adds: "once the site is working with a healthy amount of applications, I will make the code open source and invite developers and journalists to improve it so they can launch their own versions of the site".
swa: Anaongeza zaidi kuwa: “pindi tovuti ikianza kufanya kazi na kwa kutumia idadi nzuri ya zana au miundo, nitaufanya msimbo kuwa wa wazi kwa kila mtu na kuwakaribisha waendelezaji na waandishi wa habari kuuimarisha ili waweze kutengeneza matoleo yao ya tovuti hii.

eng: Also talk about Reporting On: Bloc de Periodista (en español); The Exploding Newsroom; Random Mumblings; and Linchpen. At DigiDave you can find another interview to Sholin.
swa: Pia kuongelea kuhusu Reporting on:Block de periodista(kihispania);The Exploding News room;Random Mumblings; na Linchepen At Digidaye unaweza kupata mahojiano mengine kwa Sholin

eng: We are all Laila, echo Egyptian female bloggers in one voice.
swa: Sisi sote ni Laila, ndivyo wanavyosikika kusema kwa sauti moja wanablogu wa kike wa Misri.

eng: Who is Laila and why do Egyptian girls and women associate themselves with her?
swa: Hivi, huyu Laila ni nani na kwa nini wasichana na wanawake wa kiMisri wanapenda kufananishwa naye?

eng: Read on to learn how Egyptian bloggers are working to break the gender barrier and make their voices heard.
swa: Hebu endelea kusoma ili uone ni kwa namna gani wanablogu wa Misri wanavyojihangaisha ili kuvunjilia mbali vikwazo vya jinsia na kufanya sauti zao zisikike.

eng: The story starts in September, 2006, when a group of bloggers decided the time has come for them to speak up and share their own stories and experiences, as well of those of other women, with injustice.
swa: Vuguvugu hili lilianza mnamo mwezi Septemba, 2006, wakati ambapo kikundi cha wanablogu kiliamua kwamba ilikuwa imefika wakati kwa wao kuzungumza na kushirikisha hisia na uzoefu wao, na yale yanayogusa wanawake wengine, hasa chini ya mfumo usio na haki.

eng: The initiative was launched as follows:
swa: Mwaka huu tutajaribisha kusahihisha makosa hayo.

eng: In China, an estimated 13,000 children have fallen ill since the tainted milk scandal broke.
swa: Nchini China inakadiriwa kuwa watoto 13,000 wameugua tangu sakata la maziwa yasiyofaa kuibuka.

eng: Chinese influence has grown in Africa, as have imports of all kinds products, from running shoes to instant noodles.
swa: Ushawishi na nguvu za China vimeongezeka Afrika, kama ulivyoongezeka uagizwaji wa bidhaa za kila namna, kuanzia viatu vya mazoezi mpaka chakula aina ya tambi.

eng: Bloggers as far afield as Congo and Senegal, concerned about the safety of Chinese products in their countries, are closely following the story.
swa: Mabloga hata wale walio mbali kama Kongo au Senegal, wanaguswa na usalama wa bidhaa za kutoka China katika nchi zao, na wanafuatilias habari hiyo (ya maziwa yasiyofaa).

eng: Blogging from Dakar, Naomed of Le Blog Politique du Senegal penned this short satire, a play on "melamine," the name of the chemical which was added to the fake milk.
swa: Kutoka Dakar, Bloga Naomed wa Le Blog Politique du Senegal ameandika mchezo huu mdogo wa kuigiza kuhusu dawa ijulikanayo kama "melamine," jina la hiyo dawa ambayo iliongezwa kwenye maziwa ili kudanganya ubora wa maziwa hayo.

eng: ("Melamine" sounds very close to "mélanine," the French word for melanin):
swa: ("Melamine" inakaribiana sana kimatamshi na neno "melanine," ambalo kwa Kifaransa ni neno linalomaanisha melanin):

eng: South Africa has found a new weapon in its fight against HIV/AIDS – cell phones.
swa: Afrika ya Kusini imegundua silaha mpya katika vita dhidi ya VVU/UKIMWI - simu za viganjani.

eng: A new initiative will be sending free text messages daily to encourage South Africans to get tested and treated for the disease.
swa: Kwenye mchakato mpya, jumbe za maandishi zitakuwa zikitumwa kila siku kuwahamasisha Wa-Afrika ya Kusini kwenda kupimwa na kutibiwa ugonjwa huo.

eng: The project, called Project Masiluleke or Project M, was announced last week at the Pop!Tech 2008 conference in Maine, U.S.A. It takes advantage of the popularity of cell phones in South Africa, using them to fight the country's high rates of HIV and tuberculosis (TB).
swa: Mradi huo, unaoitwa Mradi wa Masiluleke au Project M, ulitangazwa rasmi wiki iliyopita wakati wa kongamano la Pop!Tech 2008 huko Maine, Marekani. Mradi huo umerahisishwa na mteremko unaotokana na umaarufu wa simu za viganjani nchini Afrika ya Kusini, na unatumia simu hizo za viganjani kupambana na idadi kubwa ya VVU na kifua kikuu (TB).

eng: The first part of the project will send the general public approximately one million free text messages daily for a year, urging them to call HIV and TB call centers.
swa: Sehemu ya kwanza ya mradi huo itatuma takriban jumbe za bure zipatazo milioni moja kwa umma wa kawaida kila siku kwa mwaka mmoja, wakiuasa umma kwenda kwenye vituo vya VVU na kifua kikuu.

eng: These messages will be sent as part of “Please Call Me” messages, a type of text messaging widely used across Africa.
swa: Jumbe hizo zitatumwa kama sehemu ya jumbe zinazoitwa "Tafadhali Nipigie Simu", ambayo ni aina ya ujumbe unaotumiwa sana katika Afrika.

eng: White African elaborates on the project and this technology:
swa: White African anafafanua mradi huo pamoja na teknolojia yake:

eng: Gustav Praekelt - one of the most knowledgeable mobile phone specialists in Africa - is helping to run the program. 	Gustav Praekelt - mmoja wa wataalamu wa simu za viganjani wenye ufahamu mkubwa - anasaidia kuendesha programu hiyo.

It’s done using the 120 character free space in 'Please Call Me' SMS system that’s used in South Africa. They tack on messages to get people to come to get HIV treatment in private, so that they don’t have to worry about what stigma is attached to that treatment."
swa: Mradi huo unafanywa kwa kutumia nafasi ya bure ya herufi au alama 120 katika mfumo wa jumbe za "Tafadhali Nipigie Simu" unaotumika huko Afrika ya Kusini, wanaweka jumbe zitakazowafanya watu waende kutibiwa VVU kwa faragha, hivyo kutohofu doa au aibu inayoambatana na matibabu hayo.

eng: Stigma, along with misinformation, are believed to be the main reasons why so few South Africans get tested and treated for HIV.
swa: Doa au aibu, pamoja na taarifa potofu, vinaaminika kuwa ndiyo sababu kuu zinazosababisha Wa-Afrika ya Kusini wachache mno kujitokeza kutibiwa VVU.

eng: Even though roughly 5.7 million people in South Africa are living with HIV, according to the project's organizers just 5 percent of the population has been tested for the virus.
swa: Japokuwa takriban watu wapatao milioni 5.7 nchini Afrika ya Kusini wanaishi na VVU, kwa mujibu wa waandalizi wa mradi huo ni asilimia 5 tu ya watu wamepimwa virusi hivyo.

eng: South Africa also has one of the highest numbers of TB cases, a common killer of people with HIV.
swa: Afrika ya Kusini pia ina idadi kubwa ya kesi za Kifua Kikuu, ugonjwa ambao unaua wengi wenye VVU.

eng: Project M was created to help combat both of these diseases.
swa: Mradi M umeundwa ili kusaidia kupambana na magonjwa hayo mawili.

eng: It grew out of the Pop!Tech Accelerator program and brings together an international coalition of partners, including iTeach, the Praekelt Foundation, frog design, Nokia Siemens Networks and the National Geographic Society.
swa: Ulichipuka kutoka kwenye programu ya Pop!Tech Accelerator na umewakusanya pamoja wadau wa kimataifa, wakiwemo iTech, the Praekelt Foundation, frog design, Nokia Siemens Networks na the National Geographic Society.

eng: 3 Sheep points out that this project's use of cell phones shows how embedded they are in South African culture, adding:
swa: 3 Sheep anaeleza kwamba utumiaji wa simu za viganjani unaofanywa na mradi huu unaonyesha ni jinsi gani simu hizo zimejikita katika utamaduni wa Afrika ya Kusini, na anaongeza:

eng: Many countries do not have an established hardwired infrastructure and are looking to the mobile network as means of mass communication…Previously other media, such as radio, would have been used for such work but the South African project demonstrates the importance of considering all channels for outreach.
swa: Nchi nyingi hazina miundombinu inayotumia mtandao wa waya na zinaangalia mitandao ya simu za viganjani kama njia ya mawasiliano… huko nyuma njia nyingine za mawasiliano kama vile redio, zingetumika kufanya kazi kama hii lakini mradi huu wa Afrika ya Kusini unaonyesha umuhimu wa kuziangalia njia zote ili kuufikia umma.

eng: Though this is not the first of such projects in South Africa, organizers say it's the largest use ever of mobile phones for sending health information.
swa: Japo huu sio mradi wa kwanza wa aina hii huko Afrika ya Kusini, waandaaji wanasema haya ni matumizi makubwa zaidi ya simu za viganjani yaliyowahi kujaribiwa ili kutuma taarifa za afya.

eng: And so far the project holds much promise.
swa: Na mpaka sasa mradi huo una matumaini makubwa.

eng: Early testing of this text messaging campaign helped triple the average daily call volume to the National AIDS Helpline in Johannesburg.
swa: Majaribio ya kwanza ya kampeni hii inayotumia ujumbe wa simu za viganjani ulisaidia kuongeza wastani mara tatu zaidi ya watu wanaopiga simu kwenye huduma ya simu ya UKIMWI mjini Johannersburg.

eng: If the project is successful post-launch, it's hoped that this model can be expanded across Africa.
swa: Kama mradi utafaulu baada ya kuzinduliwa, kunamatumaini kwamba mradi huu utaweza kusambazwa sehemu nyingine Afrika.

eng: ahellgeth, commenting on a post on African Globalization, believes that this project has a lot of potential.
swa: Akitoa maoni katika ujumbe uliotumwa kwenye African Globalization, ahellgeth, anaamini kwamba mradi huu una matumaini makubwa.

eng: Using technology is a great way to get a strong message across to a mass amount of people. 	Utumiaji wa teknolojia ni njia nzuri ya kufikisha ujumbe wenye nguvu kwa umma.
The use of text messages offer people to view the message over and over, compared to seeing the message on a commercial or a flyer one time.
swa: Utrumiaji wa ujumbe wa simu za viganjani unatoa fursa kwa watu kuusoma ujumbe mara kwa mara, ikilinganishwa kuangalia ujumbe kwenye matangazo ya biashara au mara moja tu kwenye vipeperushi.

eng: A text message usually sits in a phones mailbox for a couple of days, allowing that person to go back and view it.
swa: Ujumbe kwenye simu za viganjani hukaa kwenye simu kwa siku kadhaa, hii inamruhusu mtumiaji kurejea na kuangalia ujumbe huo.

eng: I think the message would truly stick with people allowing them to act on it…These texts are PSA’s for cell phones."
swa: Nadhani ujumbe utawafikia watu na kunasa na utawahamasisha kuchukua hatua… jumbe hizi ni sawa na matangazo kwa ya wazi kwa umma kwa kutumia simu za viganjani."

eng: Dave, blogging on Design in Africa agrees that this project will likely be a success:
swa: Akiblogu katika Design in Africa, Dave anaafiki kwamba mradi huu una uwezekano wa kufanikiwa:

eng:
An important issue is being addressed, a simple, easy to understand solution has been designed by combining the resources of stakeholders, there are measurable benefits for people and communities and the cost of the incoming message is free. 	Ni suala muhimu linalotatuliwa, ufumbuzi rahisi na unaoeleweka umebuniwa kwa kujumuisha hazina au nguvu za wadau, na kuna manufaa yanayopimika kwa watu na jamii na gharama za kupokea ujumbe bure.
Brilliant.
swa: Safi sana!

eng: But lablady, blogging on Wise Advice, finds it unsettling that technology has taken center-stage in the fight against HIV/AIDS.
swa: Akiblogu katika Wise Advice, lablady, anaona ni jambo linalosumbua kidogo kwamba teknolojia imwekwa kwenye ulingo mkuu katika vita dhidi ya VVU/UKIMWI.

eng: She says:
swa: Anasema:

eng: At what point in time did society make it an easier, more obvious and appealing choice for an impoverished population in the grips of an HIV epidemic, to buy a cell phone rather than a condom? 	Katika nukta au wakati gani ambapo jamii imefanya chaguo hili kuwa rahisi, na lenye uwazi na mvuto kwa watu masikini waliobanwa na janga la VVU, kwenda kununua simu za viganjani badala ya kondomu?
I find it paradoxical that technology has now become the default vehicle to initiate what would have been at one time, a grass roots blood testing and education campaign.
swa: Naliona hili ni jambo lililo kinyume, kwamba teknolojia sasa imekuwa ni chombo kinachoanzisha kampeni ambayo katika wakati mwingine, ingekuwa ni kampeni ya umma kwenye ngazi za chini kwenda kupima damu na kuelimishwa zaidi.

eng: Is it arrogant of me to wonder why an entire population acquired cell phones before they had access to a successful public health strategy for a preventable disease?"
swa: Je dharau kwa upande wangu kuhoji kwa nini umma mzima umiliki simu za mkononi kabla ya kunufaika na mkakati wa kinga ya afya kupingana na ugonjwa unaoweza kuzuilika?"

eng: Catherine Forsythe, blogging on DogReader, adds that these messages may eventually be seen as "health spam."
swa: Naye Catherine Forsythe, akiblogu kwenye DogReader, anaongeza kwamba jumbe hizi hatimaye zitaweza kuchukuliwa kama "jumbe za kero" za afya.

eng: The question may be ‘how long will this methodology be effective?’ 	Swali linaweza kuwa 'ni kwa muda gani mbinu hii inaeweza kufanya kazi?'
After an initial viewing, these public health messages may be deleted as quickly as the usual text spam."
swa: Baada ya kusoma kwa mara ya kwanza, jumbe hizi za afya kwa umma zinaweza kufutwa mara moja kama vile zinavyofutwa jumbe nyingine za kero."

eng: Project M certainly hopes not.
swa: Ni matumaini ya Project M kwamba haitakuwa hivyo.

eng: Future phases of the project involve distributing at-home HIV testing kits, developing “virtual call centers,” and using text messages to provide personalized healthcare information for those being treated for AIDS.
swa: Awamu zijazo za mradi huu zitajumuisha usambazwaji wa vifaa vya kupimia VVU majumbani, pia uendelezwaji wa "huduma za vituo vya simu mtandaoni," na utumiaji wa ujumbe wa maandishi wa simu za mkononi ili kutoa huduma binafsi za taarifa za afya kwa wale wanaotibiwa UKIMWI.

eng: Two months ago fighting resumed in the DR Congo's Eastern province of North Kivu between the rebel group led by Laurent Nkunda and government forces, in violation of a peace accord signed in January.
swa: Miezi miwili iliyopita mapigano yamezuka tena katika jimbo la mashariki la Kivu katika Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasia ya Kongo kati ya kundi la upinzani linaloongozwa na Jenerali laurtent Nkunda na majeshi ya serikali, kinyume na makubaliano ya amani yaliyotiwa saini mwezi januari.

eng: As many as 250,000 people have been displaced since the violent conflict re-ignited in August, bringing the region's total displacement figure to over 2 million.
swa: Watu wapatao 250 000 wameteguliwa kutoka kwenye makazi yao tangu machafuko yalipolipuka tena mnamo mwezi wa Agosti, na kupelekea idadi ya watu waliopoteza makazi yao kufikia zaidi ya milioni 2 katika ukanda huo.

eng: Mobs of angry civilians have been attacking UN offices in Goma, North Kivu's provincial capital, infuriated that the UN hasn't been able to protect them.
swa: Vikundi vya raia wenye hasira vimekuwa vikishambulia ofisi za Umoja wa Mataifa huko Goma, mji mkuu wa jimbo la Kivu ya Kaskazini, vikundi hivyo vimekasirikia Umoja wa Mataifa kwa kushindwa kuwalinda.

eng: Fred R. at Extra-Extra gives some background to understand the population's frustration:
swa: Fred R. akiandika katika Extra-Extra anaelezea mazingira ya nyuma ili kuweza kufahamu kwa nini umma umeghafirika:

eng: … the task fell to cautious, over-stretched UN forces and a corrupt, inept national army barely that was composed of former warring factions.
swa: … jukumu liliwaangukia majeshi yaliyojaa tahadhari, na yaliyoelemewa kikazi kupindukia ya Umoja wa mataifa pamoja na jeshi la Taifa lililojaa rushwa na uzembe ambalo liliundwa na mjeshi pinzani yaliyokuwa yakipigana huko nyuma.

eng: With the huge country split into myriad, inaccessible local enclaves, it was never going to be easy to resolve all the problems of corruption, mismanagement, inter-ethnic rivalries and power struggles.
swa: Ndani ya nchi hii kubwa iliyogawanyika katika vitongoji visivyo rahisi kuvifikia, haingekuwa jambo rahisi kutatua matatizo yote ya rushwa, uzembe, ushindani wa kikabila pamoja na ushindani wa kutaka ukubwa.

eng: But the immediate post-election period offered a real window of opportunity for the new government to unite the country behind a clear vision and (with UN support) determined backing for the rule of law.
swa: Lakini kipindi kilichofuata baada ya uchaguzi mkuu kilitoa mwanya wa fursa kwa serikali mpya kuunganisha nchi kwa visheni au malengo makuu yaliyo wazi (kwa msaada wa Umoja wa Mataifa) vikiungwa mkono na mkondo wa sheria.

eng: They blew it.
swa: Walipoteza mwanya huo.

eng: Mark Leon Goldberg at the UN Dispatch comments on the population's frustration towards the UN:
swa: Mark Leon kwenye Toleo la Umoja wa Mataifa anatoa maoni kuhusu masononeko ya umma yanayoelekezwa kwa umoja wa Mataifa:

eng: Local's are understandably upset that the peacekeeping force had not done enough to stall the rebel advance.
swa: Wenyeji wanaweza kueleweka jinsi walivyokerwa kwani majeshi ya kulinda amani hawajafanya ipasavyo ili kusitisha mavamizi ya waasi.

eng: Protests outside the UN compound turned violent earlier this week as residents of Goma hurled rocks at the compound in frustration.
swa: Maandamano nje ya boma la Umoja wa Mataifa yaligeuka kuwa ghasia mwanzoni mwa juma wakati wenyeji wa mji wa Goma waliporusha mawe kwenye boma hilo kutokana na kukata tamaa.

eng: Unfortunately, the peacekeeping mission cannot repel this attack without reinforcement.
swa: Kwa bahati mbaya, majeshi ya kulinda amani hayawezi kuzuia mashabulizi hayo bila ya kuongezewa vikosi.

eng: It needs help.
swa: Wanahitaji msaada.

eng: Fast.
swa: Haraka.

eng: Fred's post offers a detailed recent background on the situation in North Kivu.
swa: Ujumbe wa Fred unatoa maelezo ya nyuma ya kina kuhusu hali ilivyo huko Kivu ya kaskazini.

eng: Michelle F. at the Stop Genocide blog offers a breakdown of the “alphabet soup of armed elements” in the DRC for those confused about the actors in this conflict:
swa: Michelle F. kwenye blogu ya Stop The Genocide anakokotoa picha ya majeshi yenye silaha aliyoiita "supu ya majeshi yenye silaha kwa herufi" katika Jamhuri ya Demokrasia ya Watu wa Kongo kwa wale ambao hawajui ni nani wahusika wakuu kwenye mzozo huu:

eng: -General Laurent Nkunda and his Congres National pour la Defense du Peuple (CNDP) claim to fight for the protection of the Congolese Tutsi population from the DRC's most uninvited and unwelcome guests,
swa: - Jenerali Laurent Nkunda na chama chake cha Taifa kwa Ajili ya Kulinda Watu au Congres National pour la Defense du Peuple (CNDP) anadai kupigana kwa ajili ya kuwalinda Wananchi wa Kongo wa kabila la Watusi dhidi ya wageni wasioalikwa na wala kutakiwa nchini humo,

eng: -The Forces Democratiques de Liberation du Rwanda (FDLR), or Interahamwe, the perpetrators of the 1994 Rwandan genocide, who set up shop in the eastern DRC following their reign of terror in their own country.
swa: - Jeshi la Wanademokrasia kwa Ajili ya Ukombozi wa Rwanda, Forces Democratiques de Liberation du Rwanda (FDLR), au Interahamwe, waliondesha mauaji ya kimbari nchini Rwanda mwaka 1994, amabo wameweka kambi huko mashariki ta Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasia ya Kongo baada utawala wao wa vitisho nchini mwao.

eng: The FDLR's ranks now include a substantial number of Congolese recruits, including chidlren.
swa: Majeshi ya FDLR hivi sasa yanajumuisha makuruta wengi kutoka Kongo, pamoja na watoto.

eng: -The Forces Armées de la République Démocratique du Congo (FARDC), the Armed Forces of the DRC, past masters of doing everything a national army is not supposed to do, and -MONUC, the United Nations Mission to the DRC, which, as Michael described, is currently under attack by civilians angered over the force's inability to offer protection.
swa: - Jeshi la Wananchi wa Kongo Forces Armées de la République Démocratique du Congo (FARDC), ambao huko nyuma walijulikana kama mamahiri wa kila jambo ambalo jeshi la wananchi halitakiwi kufanya, na - Ujumbe wa Umoja wa Mataifa nchini Kongo, MONUC, jeshi ambalo kama Michael alivyoliezea, hivi sasa linashambuliwa na wananchi waliokasirishwa na kutokuwa na uwezo kwa jeshi hilo kuwalinda raia.

eng: Refugees International describes MONUC's rock-and-a-hard-place here.
swa: Ofisi ya Kimataifa ya Wakimbizi, Refugees international inaeleza kuwa MONUC wamo kati-ya-jiwe-na-pahala-pagumu nchini humo.

eng: Four days ago the CNDP rebels seized a major military camp at Rumangabo as well as the headquarters of the 3,000 square mile (7,800 square kilometer) Virunga National Park that is home to 200 of the 700 endangered mountain gorillas in the world.
swa: Siku nne zilizopita waasi wa CNDP waliteka kambi kubwa ya jeshi huko Rumangabo kadhalika makao makuu ya Mbuga za Taifa za Virunga zenye ukubwa wa Maili Mraba 3000 (Kilometa za mraba 7,800) ambazo ni makazi ya sokwe wa milimani wapatao 200 kati ya jumla ya sokwe 700 wa aina hiyo duniani.

eng: The rebels have used the park as a base but had never seized its headquarters before.
swa: Waasi hao wamewahi kuitumia mbuga hiyo huko nyuma lakini walikuwa hawajawahi kuitumia kama makao yao makuu.

eng: The director of the park, Emmanuel de Merode, wrote about the events on Sunday at the official Virunga Park blog:
swa: Mkurugenzi wa mbuga hiyo, Emmanuel de Merode, anaandika kuhusu matukio ya Jumapili katika blogu rasmi ya ya Mbuga za Virunga:

eng: Fighting has now totally engulfed the park station and our Rangers have been forced to flee into the forests for their lives.
swa: Mapambano yamezingira kabisa kituo cha mbuga na walinzi wa doria mbugani wamelazimika kukimbilia misituni ili kuokoa maisha yao.

eng: The rebels now are the only occupants of the park station at Rumangabo.
swa: Waasi ndio wakazi pekee wa kituo cha mbuga cha Ramangabo hivi sasa.

eng: This has never happened before.
swa: Hili halijawahi kutokea wakati wowote kabla.

eng: This is a serious time.
swa: Huu ni wakati mgumu.

eng: We need to get our 50+ Rangers back to safety in Goma, 45km south of Rumangabo.
swa: Tunahitajika kuwafikisha walinzi wetu wa doria mbugani wapatao 50 na zaidi mjinin Goma kwenye usalama, Kilometa zipatazo 45 kusini mwa Rumangabo.

eng: The main road is blocked because of the fighting so they are walking through the forests of the park south, to Kibumba, about 20km away, where we aim to pick them up in trucks.
swa: Barabara kuu imefungwa kutokana na mapambano hivyo wanatembea kwa miguu kukatiza misitu kusini mwa mbuga, kuelekea Kibumba, takriban kilometa 20 hivi zaidi,ambako tunatarajia kwenda kuwachukua kwa kutumia malori.

eng: We are trying to maintain phone contact but they don’t have much battery life in their phones.
swa: Tunajaribu kuendelea kuwasiliana nao kwa simu lakini hawana nguvu za betri (mawe) ya kutosha kwenye simu zao.

eng: Two days later, 12 of the 53 rangers that had to flee into the forest were rescued and brought to Goma.
swa: Siku mbili baadaye, 12 katika wale askari wa doria waliokuwa wakikimbia katika misitu waliokolewa na kupelekwa Goma. .

eng: Innocent Mburanumwe described how tired, thirsty and hungry they were when the Goma team found them:
swa: Innocent Mburanumwe alielezea jinsi alivyokuwa mchovu, mwenye kiu na njaa wakati timu iliyotokea Goma ilipowakuta na kuwaokoa:

eng: The Rangers started off on Sunday at 9am as a group of 14 - and also with 4 members of the military who were also fleeing the rebels.
swa: Askari doria wa mbuga walianza safari Jumapili mnamo saa 3 asubuhi wakiwa kundi la watu 14 - kadhalika walikuwa na wanajeshi 4 ambao pia walikuwa wanwakimbia waasi.

eng: They walked through the park, often trying to emerge onto the road, but heard many bombs and mortars and so had to go back into the forest.
swa: Walikatiza mbugani, wakitarajia kutokeshezea barabarani, lakini walisikia milio ya mabomu na na mizinga na hivyo iliwabidi kurudi tena msituni.

eng: With no water they tried licking rocks to quench their thirst, and also tried sucking up the moisture from the mud, by putting a piece of clothing between their mouth and the moist mud.
swa: Bila ya maji walianza kufyonza mawe ili kutuliza kiu, pia walijaribu kunyonya umande kutoka kwenye matope kwa kuweka kitambaa kati ya midomo yao na tope lenye nyevunyevu.

eng: On Wednesday, a spokesperson of the CNDP announced a unilateral ceasefire, although the situation on the ground in Goma remains chaotic.
swa: Jumatano, msemaji wa CNDP alitangaza kusitishwa kwa mapigano, japokuwa hali huko Goma iliendelea kuwa kutoeleweka.

eng: As Kate Cronin-Furman from the blog Wronging Rights points out, “everyone seems to be preparing for war anyway, probably on account of Nkunda's previously-demonstrated questionable grasp of the word cease-fire.”
swa: Kama ambavyo Kate Cronin-Furman kutoka blogu ya Wronging Rights anavyodokeza, "kila mmoja inaonekana kuwa anajiandaa na vita, pengine kwa vile Nkunda huko nyuma amewahi kuonyesha kutoelewa maana ya neno usitishwaji wa mapigano."

eng: Samantha Newport writes about the confusion on the Virunga Park blog:
swa: Samantha Newport anaandika kuhusu utata uliopo kwenye blogu ya Mbuga za Taifa za Virunga:

eng: It’s total chaos in Goma.
swa: Goma ni vurugu tupu.

eng: I am being told, through various phone calls and text messages, that the army have now laid down their weapons at Kibumba, 12 miles north of Goma, and are fleeing the rebels.
swa: Nimeelezwa, kupitia simu mbalimbali na jumbe fupi za simu za viganjani, kwamba jeshi limeweka silaha chini huko Kibumba, malili 12 kaskazini ya Goma, na wanawakimbia waasi.

eng: In other words they have totally given up.
swa: Kwa maneno mengine wamekata tamaa kabisa.

eng: The governor of North Kivu has apparently also left town.
swa: Gavana wa Kivu ya Kaskazini pia ameukimbia mji.

eng: Now there is only the UN peacekeeping forces stopping Nkunda’s rebels from taking Goma.
swa: Hivi sasa ni majeshi ya kulinda amani ya Umoja wa Mataifa pekee yaliyopo kuzuia majeshi ya Nkunda kuuteka mji wa Goma.

eng: There is lots and lots of speculation right now - and panic.
swa: Kuna makisio mengi na ubashiri hivi sasa - na hofu.

eng: On another post at the Virunga Park blog, Emmanuel de Merode also writes about the confusion reigning in Goma:
swa: Katika ujumbe mwingine kwenye blogu ya Mbuga za Taifa za Virunga, Emmanuel de Merode pia anaandika kuhusu utata unaotawala Goma:

eng: Confusion is probably the only way to describe the situation.
swa: Pengine utata ndiyo njia pekee ya kuielezea hali ilivyo.

eng: There is a lot of shooting in town, with some heavy weapons further away.
swa: Kuna kutupiana risasi kwingi mjini, kukiwa na silaha kubwa mbali zaidi.

eng: Everyone is staying at home.
swa: Kila mtu anajificha nyumbani.

eng: There has been some looting, mainly armed men stealing cars and motorbikes.
swa: Pia kumekuwepo na uporaji, haswa na baadhi ya watu wenye silaha wanaopora magari na pikipiki.

eng: Laurent Nkunda made a statement on television and radio announcing a unilateral cease-fire, which is encouraging, but unfortunately does not translate into a peaceful evening.
swa: Laurent nkunda ametoa tamko kwenye televisheni na redio akitangaza kusitishwa kwa mapigano, jambo la kutia moyo, kwa bahati mbaya hilo halijasababisha jioni yenye utulivu.

eng: We’ve suffered a barrage of rumours including the invasion of the Rwandan army, Angolan mercenaries coming in from the west, just about everything, none of which is terribly helpful.
swa: Tumefikwa na wimbi la uzushi pamoja na ule wa uvamizi wa jeshi la Rwanda, mamluki wa Kiangola wakija kutokea magharibi, karibu kila kitu, na hakuna moja lenye msaada.

eng: This morning Samantha is giving another update on the situation, including a few photos from the compound where she's staying:
swa: Asubuhi hii Samantha anatoa habari mpya kuhusu hali ilivyo, pamoja na picha chache kwenye boma anamoishi:

eng: The CNDP rebels - Nkunda’s rebels - are in total control of Kiwanja and Rutshuru and have put in their own administration for the area.
swa: Waasi wa CNDP - waasi wa Nkunda - wanaushikilia Kiwanja na Rutshuru na wamesimika utawala wao kwenye eneo hilo.

eng: The national army, police and administators have all left - so a vast swathe of the province is now in CNDP control.
swa: Jeshi la taifa, polisi na wafanyakazi wa serikali wote wameondoka - kwa hiyo sehemu kubwa ya jimbo imo chini ya utawala wa CNDP hivi sasa.

eng: Innocent had an uncomfortable night.
swa: Innocent alikuwa na usiku uliokosa heri.

eng: His neighbor’s house was looted by fleeing military.
swa: Nyumba ya jirani yake iliporwa na askari waliokuwa wakiukimbia mji.

eng: Fortunately Innocent, his wife and 5 kids are okay and they were not robbed.
swa: Kwa bahati nzuri Innocent, mkewe na watoto 5 wako salama na hawakuporwa.

eng: Dawn Hurley, an American expat living in Goma, writes in her blog From Congo about the uncertainty and fear when night falls:
swa: Dawn Hurley, mfanyakazi wa kimataifa aishiye Goma anaandika katika blogu yake From Congo kuhusu ukosefu wa uhakika na hofu usiku unapoingia:

eng: The night here can be a scary thing.
swa: Usiku hapa unaweza kuwa ni jambo la kutisha.

eng: During the day, life seems tenable in Goma.
swa: Mchana, maisha yanaonekana kuwezekana mjini Goma.

eng: But night falls around 6:30 here and from then until morning everyone is on their own.
swa: Lakini usiku huingia majira ya 12.30 hapa na kuanzia hapo mpaka asubuhi kila mmoja na lwake.

eng: Most people don't have cars, so they can't go anywhere after dark.
swa: Watu wengi hawana magari, kwa hiyo hawawezi kwenda popote baada ya kuingia giza.

eng: And these days, even driving around in a car at night isn't recommended.
swa: Na siku hizi, haipendekezwi hata kuendesha gari wakati wa usiku.

eng: Most people don't have power, so they are often sitting in small shacks with their families, praying for the best, listening to shots echo through town, and waiting for daylight.
swa: Watu wengi hawana umeme, kwa hiyo mara nyingi huketi na familia kwenye vibanda vyao, wakijiombea salama, wakisikiliza miwangwi ya risasi ikirindima mjini, huku wakisubiri nuru ya asubuhi.

eng: There is no 911 to call if you have a problem.
swa: Hakuna simu ya dharura ya 911 ya kupiga kama una tatizo.

eng: At best people call their friends, who have little to offer, other than a voice on the other end of the line.
swa: Watu huwaita marafiki ambao wana kidogo cha kutoa, ghairi ya sauti iliyo upande wa pili wa simu.

eng: Colette Braeckman, a Belgian journalist and author of several books on Central Africa, reproduces in her blog the account of Dunia Ruyenzi, a human rights activist in Goma:
swa: Colette Braeckman, mwandishi wa habari wa Kibelgiji na mwandishi wa vitabu kadhaa vinavyohusu Afrika ya Kati, anaweka katika blogu yake maelezo ya Dunia Ruyenzi, mwanaharakati wa haki za binaadamu huko Goma:

eng: There is a bit of sporadic firing in the streets but it is much less intense than yesterday.
swa: Kuna kutupiana risasi kusikotabirika katika mitaa lakini kiasi pungufu ikilinganishwa na jana.

eng: The tension is beginning to diminish.
swa: Hali ile ya kutisha imeanza kupungua.

eng: Tomorrow, the US Assistant Secretary of State for Africa is supposed to be coming to Goma to help with the negotiations.
swa: Kesho, naibu katibu wa Masuala ya Afrika katika serikali ya Marekani anatarajiwa kuwasili Goma kusaidia majadiliano.

eng: Louis Michel, the European Commissioner for International Development is in Kinshasa and the Belgian Foreign Minister Carol de Gujt, is supposed to arrive in Kigali.
swa: Luis Michel, Kamishna wa Maendeleo ya Kimataifa wa Jumuiya ya Ulaya yupo jijini Kinshasa na waziri wa Mambo ya Nje wa Ubelgiji Carol de Gujt, anatarajiwa kuwasili mjini Kigali.

eng: Let’s hope…
swa: Na tuendelee kutumaini…

eng: Two weeks ago the journalist Jina Moore, formerly based in Rwanda and who covered the DR Congo as well, wrote on her blog News from Central Africa:
swa: Wiki mbili zilizopita mwandishi wa habari Jina Moore, ambaye alikuwa Rwanda huko nyuma ambaye pia aliandika juu ya Kongo, ameandika katika blogu yake News From Central Africa:

eng: I finally understand that thing I’ve read about in books, where hardened correspondents talk about the desperation they feel to return to the completely screwed places they’ve covered when things take a turn for the worse.
swa: Hatimaye nimefahamu lile jambo ambalo nimelisoma kwenye vitabu, ambapo waandishi wakongwe huliongelea kuhusu hisia ya kukata tamaa inayowapata wanapotaka kurejea kwenye maeneo yaliyoharibiwa kabisa ambayo waliwahi kuyaandika wakati mambo yalipochukua mkondo mbaya zaidi.

eng: It means something different when you know how that place looks in real life, and something gnaws at your gut, beckoning you back.
swa: Inamaanisha jambo jingine wakati unafahamu fika sehemu hiyo ikoje, na kuna jambo linalotafuna ndani yako, likikuita kurejea tena huko.

eng: Due to a new outbreak of the ebola virus in the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Angolan government has decided to shut down the border the two countries share, in an attempt to prevent the deadly virus entering the nation's territory. Thus, the constant migratory movement between Lunda Norte (a province in the northeast of the country) and DR Congo has been summarily suspended.
swa: Kutokana na kuzuka tena kwa virusi vya Ebola katika Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasi ya Kongo, serikali ya Angola imeamua kufunga mpaka kati ya nchi hizo mbili, katika jaribio la kuzuia kuingia kwa virusi hivyo hatari katika himaya ya taifa hilo., Hivyo kusitisha mara moja uhamiaji wa kawaida unaoendelea kati ya Lunda Norte (jimbo lililoko kaskazini mashariki ya nchi) na Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasi ya Kongo.

eng: It should be noted that the province of Lunda Norte is a gold mining area, a magnet for migrant workers.
swa: Lazima izingatiwe kwamba jimbo la Lunda Norte ni sehemu ya migodi ya dhahabu, anyowavuta wafanyakazi wengi wahamiaji.

eng: Nelo de Carvalho writes at Blog do Nelo Ativado about the border restrictions and the challenges the government faces:
swa: Nelo de Carvalho anaandika katika blog do Nelo Ativado kuhusu vizingiti vilivyoko kwenye mpaka huo na changamoto ambazo serikali inazikabili:

eng: Nominations for the Ninth Annual Weblog Awards: The 2009 Bloggies started January 1 and closed January 19.
swa: Blogu zilizopendekezwa kwa ajili ya Mashindano ya Tisa ya Zawadi za Weblog: Mapendekezo ya blogu katika mashindano ya Bloggies ya 2009 yalifunguliwa tarehe 1 Januari na kufungwa tarehe 19 Januari.

eng: According to the awards website, the Bloggies are the Web's longest-running blog awards, and the nominations, finalist selection, are up to the blog reader.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa tovuti ya waandalizi, mashindano hayo ya Bloggies ni mashindano ambayo yamedumu kwa muda mrefu zaidi mtandaoni, na mapendekezo, pamoja na uchaguaji wa washindani katika fainali, ni juu ya msomaji wa blogu.

eng: The winner of the awards gets 2,009 US cents!
swa: Mshindi hupata senti 2,009 za Marekani!

eng: Five blogs have been nominated in the Best African Weblog category:
swa: Blogu tano zimependekezwa katika kinyang'anyiro cha blogu Bora Zaidi:

eng: Being Brazen: This is a blog from South Africa.
swa: Blogu ya Being Brazen: Hii ni blogu iliyoko Afrika ya Kusini.

eng: The profile of the blogger reads:
swa: Wasifu wa mwanablogu huyo unaelezwa:

eng: Im a quirky, day dreaming, 20-something who believes in love, God, the power of words, having an open mind and that laughter is probably the best medicine.
swa: Sitabiriki, huota ndoto za mchana, umri wangu ni katika miaka ya 20, ninaamini katika mapenzi, Mungu na nguvu ya maneno, nina mawazo huru na pengine kucheka ndio dawa bora kuliko zote.

eng: I dont like flying, over crowded places, standing in lines and most bugs.I stumble in stilettos.
swa: Sipendi kuruka angani , sehemu zenye watu wengi, kupanga foleni, kadhalika sipendi wadudu.

eng: I write to stay sane.
swa: Ninaandika ili kuepuka wehu.

eng: Appfrica: A web portal for the latest news related to African innovation, education and entrepreneurship in technology.
swa: Blogu ya AppAfrica: Hii ni tovuti ya habari mpya mpya zinazohusu ubunifu wa Kiafrika, elimu na ujasiriamali kwenye teknolojia:

eng: Glad To Be a Girl: A South African blogger based in Johannesburg.
swa: Blogu ya Glad To Be A Girl: Ni mwanablogu wa Kiafrika ya Kusini anayekaa mjini Johannesburg.

eng: Her profile:
swa: Wasifu wake:

eng: Sift through my insanity and revel in my genius!
swa: Huchambua wehu wangu na hujisifu kwa akili zangu!

eng: Modesty drips off me in buckets ;) Sarcasm is my weapon of choice.
swa: Unyonge unanichirizika ndoo kwa ndoo :) kejeli ndiyo silaha yangu ninayoipenda.

eng: West Africa Wins Always: This is a blog by Pauline, a jounalist who has been living in Ivory Coast since 2003.
swa: Blogu ya West Africa Wins Always: Hii ni blogu ya mwanablogu Pauline, mwanahabari ambaye amekuwa akiishi nchini Ivory Coast tangu mwaka 2003.

eng: Last but not least is Scarlett Lion: She is a jounalist based in Liberia.
swa: Na blogu ya mwisho ni ile ya Scarlett Lion: Yeye ni mwanahabari aliyeko nchini Liberia.

eng: In her own words:
swa: Kwa mujibu wa maneno yake mwenyewe:

eng: Photographer, writer, reporter.
swa: Mpiga picha, mwandishi, ripota.

eng: Going through life with an eye towards creating records and histories.
swa: Napita maishani nikiwa na jicho linalolenga kutengeneza historia na kuiorodhesha.

eng: Previously in Uganda, now in Liberia.
swa: Awali katika nchi ya Uganda na sasa katika Liberia.

eng: This blog provides curiosities, cynicism, and commentary.
swa: Blogu hii inakuletea udadisi na maoni.

eng: And some photos.
swa: Pamoja na picha.

eng: Voting closes February 2 and the winners will be announced in March in Austin, Texas, USA at South by Southwest Interactive Festival.
swa: Upigaji kura utafungwa tarehe 2 Februari na washindi watatangazwa mwezi Machi mjini Austin, Texas, huko Marekani katika Tamasha la South by South West Interactive.

eng: A few days after passing Madagascar, the official toll from the damages caused by Cyclone Fanele have finally come in.
swa: Baada ya siku chache kupita nchini Madagaska, idadi rasmi ya madhara yaliyosababishwa na kimbunga kilichopewa jina la Fanele zimewasilishwa.

eng: President Ravalomanana president flew to one of the affected areas to assess the extent of the devastation.
swa: Rais Ravalomanana alikwenda kwenye moja ya maeneo yaliathirika na kimbunga ili kutathmini madhara yaliyotokea.

eng: Cyclone citizen media initiative
swa: Uandishi wa kiraia wakati wa kimbunga

eng: While the BGNRC (department of risk and disaster management) is still without an official website, reports pertaining to the damages are being aggregated on an open-source Google map by two bloggers, Marie Sophie Digne and Tomavana (fr).
swa: Wakati idara inayoangalia athari na majanga, BGNRC bado haina tovuti, taarifa zinahusu madhara yaliyotokea zinakusanywa na wanablogu wawili, Marie Sophie Digne pamoja na Tomavana katika zana-huria ya Google Map.

eng: Here is a summary of the damages, according to IRIN, via ReliefWeb:
swa: Ufuatao ni muhtasari wa uharibifu uliotokea, kwa mujibu wa shirika la IRIN kupitia Relief Web:

eng: New figures from Madagascar's National Office for Natural Disasters Preparedness (BNGRC) indicate that cyclone Fanele claimed eight lives and affected some 40,400 people The BNGRC said a further 63,000 people were at risk in Menabe if heavy rain continued to fall.
swa: Takwimu zilizotolewa na Idara Inayoangalia Athari na Majanga ya Madagaska (BGNRC) zinaashiria kwamba Kimbunga Fanele kimeua watu wanane na kuathiri watu wengine wapatao 40,400 . Pia, BGNRC ilieleza kuwa watu wengine 63,000 wako hatarini huko Menabe ikiwa mvua kubwa itaendelea kunyesha.

eng: Relief teams are still assessing the damage caused by the two storms, and figures are expected to rise as more information on the full extent of the damage is gathered.
swa: Timu za misaada bado zinaendelea kutathmini uharibifu uliosababishwa na vimbunga viwili, na takwimu zinategemewa kuongezeka wakati ripoti ya uharibifu uliotokea ikikusanywa.

eng: Political turmoil
swa: Machafuko ya Kisiasa

eng: The Malagasy blogosphere was also buzzing with political news and commentary about a new massive political gathering today (Jan 24th) and a call for a national strike to demand the resignation of the entire administration.
swa: Ulimwengu wa Blogu wa Kimalagasi kadhalika ulikuwa umeenea habari za kisiasa na maoni kuhusu maandamano makubwa leo (Januari 24) yanayotaka kufanyike kwa mgomo wa kitaifa ili kuishurutisha serikali ijiuzulu.

eng: Many bloggers have provided live blogging and images of the event (additional images on facebook).
swa: Wanablogu wengi wamekuwa wakiblogu moja kwa moja na kutuma picha za tukio hilo (picha nyingine zimetoka kwenye Facebook).

eng: Blogger Ariniaina provides a brief factsheet on the background of the turmoil:
swa: Bloga Ariniaina ametoa muhtasari wa mazingira yaliyopelekea kuzuka kwa machafuko hayo:

eng: Andry Rajoelina (or Andry TGV) had a TV Station named VIVA and still have a radio station with the same name.
swa: Andry Rajoelina (au Andry TVG) alikuwa na stesheni ya televisheni inayoitwa VIVA na bado anayo stesheni ya redioyenye jina hilohilo.

eng: The minister of the communication has decided to close the TV station VIVA due to a documentary movie that this station had broadcasted.
swa: Waziri wa Mawasiliano ameamua kuifunga stesheni ya Televisheni ya VIVA kwa sababu ya filamu iliyopeperushwa na stesheni hiyo.

eng: It was a message from the former President of Madagascar, Didier Ratsiraka Since then, the Mayor ( of Antanarivo, Andry Rajoelina) gave an ultimatum to the government to re-open VIVA TV station before January 13 As Andry didn’t get what he wanted, he invited the people of Tana to go on a strike AGAIN today, January 24.
swa: Ilikuwa niujumbe kutoka kwa rais wa zamani wa Madagaska, Didier Ratsiraka Kutokea hapo, Meya (wa jiji la Antananarivo, Andry Rajoelina) alitoa amri ya kufunguliwa tena kwa stesheni ya VIVA kabla ya tarehe 13 Januari Kwa sababu Andry hakupata kile alichokitaka, aliwaalika watu wa Tana kufanya mgomo TENA leo, tarehe 24 Januari.

eng: ( demonstration photo via ariniana )
