swa: (Picha ya maandamano na ariniana)

eng: Blogger Jentilisa provides in-depth analysis of the discourse on both sides of the political spectrum and cautions against the spreading of unverified rumors (mg):
swa: Maendeleo yenye mvuto wakati wa matukio haya ya kisiasa ni kuzuka kwa watumiaji hai wa Twita kwa Kimalagasi ambao walituma maendeleo ya kisiasa katika muda uliopo.

eng: Last week, flooding hit several areas in the Sarawak State of Malaysia.
swa: Wiki iliyopita mafuriko yaliyakumba maeneo kadhaa katika jimbo la Sarawak nchini Malaysia.

eng: More than 8,000 people in the Bau District were evacuated in 24 temporary shelters.
swa: Zaidi ya watu 8000 waliokolewa wilayani Bau na kupelekwa kwenye makazi 24 ya muda mfupi.

eng: The flooding was the worst in three years.
swa: Mafuriko hayo yalikuwa mabaya zaidi katika kipindi cha miaka mitatu.

eng: Water level rose up to the waist level.
swa: Maji yalifurika na kufikia wastani wa kima cha kiuno.

eng: Flooding in Bau, Sarawak. Pictures from the blog of Denis
swa: Mafuriko wilayani Bau, Sarawak.Picha kutoka kwenye blogu ya Denis.

eng: a better future advises the government to sum up the lessons of the flooding disaster:
swa: Mwanablogu a better future anaishauri serikali iorodheshe mafunzo yaliyotokana na mafuriko hayo:

eng: “Immediate relief was going on quite well but the Government could have done better if they had marked all the flood sections of the roads with bamboo poles or other alternatives with clear signs to show how deep the flood level is.
swa:
Msaada wa haraka uliendelea vizuri lakini serikali ingeweza kufanya vizuri zaidi kama wangeweka alama za maeneo yaliyofurika kwa kutumia minara ya mianzi au njia nyingine zenye vibao vinavyoeleza wazi vina vya maji.
It would have made it easier for monitoring as well as for traffic to decide whether to “swim” through or not.	Hilo lingefanya kazi ya ufuatiliaji iwe rahisi kadhalika ingewasaidia watumiaji wa barabara kufanya maamuzi ama ya kuogelea au la.
These markers can be used for future planning especially in the upgrading of the main trunk roads.	Alama hizo zingeweza kutumika wakati wa kupanga mustabali utakaoboresha barabara kuu.
“Thus unless we have proper records of flood levels in flood prone areas to guide future planning and implementation of projects, we will have more unnecessary problems due to poor implementations by the respective agencies involved in future. 	Bila ya kuwa na vielelezo sahihi ya vina vya mafuriko katika sehemu zinazoathirika mara kwa mara vitakavyosaidia mipango ya baadaye na pia utekelezaji wa miradi, tutaendelea kuwa na matatatizo yasiyo ya lazima yanayotokana na utekelezaji dhaifu wa vyombo husika.

eng: “Hopefully the Government has learned all the lessons so that future floods will be less disruptive, not only in Bau but throughout Sarawak and if possible Malaysia.
swa:
Ninatuamini kuwa serikali imeweza kujifunza na kwamba mafuriko yatakayotokea hapo baadaye hatakuwa na madhara, siyo tu katika wilaya ya Bau bali pia katika Sarawak yote na ikiwezekana Malaysia yote.
The main trunk roads should be built to be weather-proof, meaning the level to which they must be constructed must be above the highest known flood level. 	Barabara kuu ni lazima zijengwe ili kuhimili hali yoyote ya hewa, kwa maana kwamba kiwango ambacho barabara hizo zitajengwa ni lazima kiwe ni kiwango cha kitachakowa juu ya kima chochote cha mafuriko.
Police stations and critical government buildings must be sited in non flood prone areas, where possible. 	Vituo vya polisi na majengo muhimu ya serikali, ikiwezekana, ni lazima yawe kwenye sehemu ambazo haziathiriki na mafuriko.
If not, then the site of any buildings should be dumped to raise it above the known flood level at the very least. 	Kama haiwezekani, basi viwanja vitakapojengwa majengo ya serikali lazima yajazwe kifusi ili kiviinua juu ya kima cha mafuriko.
Access to these buildings must be also flood proofed where possible.”	Na njia za kufikia majengo hayo lazima zitengenezwe kuhimili mafuriko, ikiwezekana.

eng: The Lost Aborigine urges leaders to prioritize the flooding issue over other foreign matters:
swa: Mwanablogu, The Lost Aborigine anawahimiza viongozi walipe kipaumbele swala la mafuriko zaidi ya maswala mengine ya mambo ya nje:

eng: “How about the flood relief to those affected area especially those poor villages like Serian, Padawan, Bau and some in Sibu and Miri?
swa:
Vipi kuhusu misaada kwa sehemu zilizoathirika hasa vijiji masikini kama vile Serian, Padawan, Bau na sehemu kama vile Sibu pamoja na Miri?
Why we so busy with Gaza but our own people are helpless and dying?	Kwa nini tunashupalia mambo ya Gaza wakati watu wetu wenyewe wanakufa bila msaada?
The Malaysian attitude is that we ignore our household affair and get busy with other issue that it less related to us.”	Tabia ya Wamalaysia ni ya kudharau mambo ya ndani na kushupalia mambo mengine ambayo hayahusiki moja kwa moja nasi.

eng: Nana Natu notes that the flooding was the worst in 20 years:
swa: Nana Tatu naye anandika kwamba mafuriko yalikuwa mabaya zaidi katika miaka 20:

eng: Sarawak River showed yesterday its might when it burst it banks and water spilled into Kuching Waterfront.And the floods descrides by Kuchingites as the worst flood in 20 years, caused massive trafic jam, halted business and caused panic among some who anticipated that worst was yet to come. 	Mto Sarawak jana ulionyesha nguvu zake wakati ulipopasua kingo zake na kumiminikia kwenye ufukwe wa Kuching. Na wakazi wa Kuching wanaeleza kwamba mafuriko haya ni mabaya zaidi katika miaka 20, yalizua foleni kubwa za magari, yalisitisha biashara na kuwajaza hofu wale waliotegemea kwamba maafa zaidi yangelitokea.
There were no warnings.
swa: Hapakuwa na maonyo ya tahadhari.

eng: The flood this year is worse then the one in 2004.And the floods caused 119 schools closed."
swa: Mafuriko ya mwaka huu ni zaidi ya yale yaliyotokea mwaka 2004. Pia mafuriko haya yalisababisha shule 119 zifungwe."

eng: Sounding Intelligent writes the possible causes of the flooding:
swa: Mwanablogu, Sounding Intelligent anaandika sababu zilizosababisha mafuriko:

eng: I am in no position to say what the actual cause of the recent flood is but I firmly believe that it is man-made. 	Sipo katika nafasi ya kueleza ni nini hasa iliyokuwa sababu ya mafuriko ya hivi karibuni lakini ninaamini kwamba mafuriko haya yalisababishwa na watu.
After all, who constructed levees that forced rivers into narrow channels?
swa: Je ni nani aliyejenga kingo ambazo zilisababisha mito ipite kwenye mikondo myembamba?

eng: Who destructed the wetlands that once absorbed excess rainfall?
swa: Nani aliyeharibu makonde ambayo huko nyuma yaliweza kufyonza maji ya mvua?

eng: Who contributed to global warming?
swa: Ni nani aliyechangia ongezeko la joto duniani?

eng: Global warming is a real threat. 	Ongezeko la joto ni tishio la kweli.
It is affecting weather patterns, creating a modest increase in violent downpours and melting ice all over the world, causing an avalanche of effects.
swa: Linaathiri mizunguko ya hali ya hewa, linaongeza kiwango cha mvua na kuyeyusha barafu kila sehemu duniani, na kusababisha maporomoko ya athari.

eng: “Despite these warnings, some people still continue to be selfish, refuse to switch to cleaner fuels or reduce their carbon footprints somehow.”
swa: Pamoja na maonyo haya, watu wengine bado wanaendelea na ubinafsi, wanakataa kuupokea mfumo wa nishati safi au kupunguza nyayo zao za gesi ya ukaa.

eng: The flooding disaster was not limited to Malaysia.
swa: Janga la mafuriko halikutokea tu Malaysia.

eng: Flooding also hit several parts of the Philippines, Indonesia and Fiji.
swa: Mafuriko pia yalizikumba sehemu mbalimbali za Phillipines, Indonesia na Fiji.

eng: Mexico is facing a crime wave, in which both national and foreign citizens are being targeted for kidnappings.
swa: Meksiko inakabiliwa na wimbi la uhalifu wa jinai, ambamo wote raia wa ndani na wageni wanaviziwa kutekwa nyara.

eng: A recent case took place in Saltillo, Coahuila, when U.S. anti-kidnapping expert Félix Batista was abducted by masked gunmen.
swa: Tukio la karibuni lilitokea katika Saltillo, Coahuila, wakati mtaalamu wa kuzuia utekaji nyara wa Marekani, Felix Batista alitekwa na watu waliovaa vinyafo usoni.

eng: Batista was in the country providing seminars as a consultant for the Texas-based security firm ASI Global LLC.
swa: Batista alikuwapo nchini humo kuendesha semina kama mfanyakazi wa kukodiwa wa kampuni ya usalama yenye makao huko Texas ASI Global LLC.

eng: His experience throughout Latin America dealing with this crime is sought after for groups wanting to learn how to avoid this crime.
swa: Uzoefu wake katika nchi za Marekani ya Latini katika kupambana na uhalifu wa aina hii uantafutwa na vikundi ambavyo vina nia ya kuukwepa uhalifu huu wa jinai.

eng: However, his kidnapping proves that anyone is risk.
swa: Hata hivyo, kutekwa kwake kunadhihirisha kuwa kila mmoja yu hatarini.

eng: The Mex Files has a few questions about the kidnapping case:
swa: Bloga, The Mex Files ana maswali machache ya kuuliza kuhusiana na tukio hilo:

eng: If Batista was an expert, how did he get himself kidnapped?
swa: Kama Batista ni mtaalamu imekuwaje akaruhusu atekwe yeye mwenyewe?

eng: Batista was an employee of a Houston Texas “security consulting” firm called ASI Global.
swa: Batista alikuwa mfanyakazi wa "kampuni ya usalama" yenye makao huko Texas ASI Global.

eng: He reportedly was in Saltillo on personal business, but who was he working for?
swa: Imeelezwa kwamba alikuwa huko Saltillo kwa shughuli za kibinafsi, je alikuwa akimfanyia nani kazi huko?

eng: Is ASI Global one of the U.S. companies receiving funding for “Plan Merida”… and what does this say about the competence of the trainers?
swa: Je kampuni ya ASI Global si moja ya kampuni za Kimarekani zinazopokea fedha kwa ajili ya "Mpango wa Merida"… Na hili linatuambia nini juu ya utendaji kazi wa wataalamu wake wa ukufunzi?

eng: Some statistics place kidnappings as occurring approximately 2 per day and especially prevalant in the northern border states.
swa: Takwimu kadhaa zinaonyesha kuwa utekaji unatokea kwa takriban mara 2 kwa siku na hasa katika majimbo ya mpakani kaskazini mwa nchi.

eng: Mexico has the highest number of kidnappings per capita of any country in the world.
swa: Meksiko ina wastani wa juu zaidi wa utekaji ikilinganishwa na nchi yoyote ile duniani.

eng: These cases affect friends and family of the abducted, such as blogger Tony Scotti, who is a friend of Batista:
swa: Matukio haya huathiri marafiki na familia za waliotekwa, kama alivyoathirika bloga Tony Scotti, ambaye ni rafiki wa Batista:

eng: I know Felix, and he is a highly competent individual.
swa: Ninamfahamu Felix, na ni mtu anayeweza sana.

eng: Felix is a high profile guy, often quoted in the newspapers and in fact quoted in this month’s issue of Security Management Magazine.
swa: Felix ni mtu anayejulikana, ambaye mara nyingi hunukuliwa kwenye magazeti na hata katika jarida la mwezi huu la Usalama.

eng: His high profile might have been the catalyst for the abduction.
swa: Kujulikana kwake kunaweza kuwa ndio kulikopelekea kutekwa kwake.

eng: After reading the newspaper accounts it would be my guess that Felix was set up, and set up by someone he trusted.
swa: Baada ya kusoma magazeti ninaweza kuhisi kwamba Felix aliwekewa mtego, na aliwekewa mtego huo na mtu anayemuamini.

eng: El Nahual of México Para Los Mexicanos is worried about what this act may mean for the rest of the country:
swa: Bloga El Nahual wa blogu ya Mexico Para los Mexicanos anahofu kuhusu matokeo ya kitendo hiki katika nchi:

eng: Today marked an historic moment in United States history as Barack Obama was sworn in as the 44th President.
swa: Tukio la kihistoria limetokea Marekani leo wakati Barack Obama alipoapishwa kuwa rais wa 44.

eng: While Arab support of Obama has been waning over the past few months following the selection of his cabinet and his silence over Israel's attacks on Gaza, across the Middle East and North Africa bloggers still have plenty to say.
swa: Wakati kuungwa mkono kwa Obama kati ya Waarabu kumekuwa kukipungua katika miezi michache iliyopita kufuatia uteuzi wake wa baraza la mawaziri na ukimya wake kuhusu mashambulio ya Israeli huko Gaza, wanablogu wa Mashariki ya Kati na Afrika ya Kaskazini wanayo mengi ya kusema.

eng: A Syrian in London shares a timeline of the past few weeks of Israel's attacks, then remarks:
swa: Bloga A Syrian in London anaorodhesha matukio ya wiki chache zilizopita wakati wa mashambulizi ya Israeli, halafu anaeleza:

eng: Not since Kennedy, and some say not never, has an American President has had such attention with such high hopes, from around the world resting on his shoulders.
swa: Hapajatokea mwingine tangu Kennedy, na wengine wanasema hakuna rais mwingine wa Marekani aliyewahi kuwa na mvuto pamoja na matumaini makubwa, kutoka duniani kote, kwenye mabega yake.

eng: In his inauguration speech, President Obama said:
swa: Katika hotuba yake ya kuapishwa, Rais obama alisema:

eng: “we have chosen hope over fear, unity of purpose over conflict and discord”
swa: tumechagua matumaini dhidi ya hofu, umoja wa nia dhidi ya migogoro na kutoelewana

eng: “we come to proclaim an end to the petty grievances and false promises, the recriminations and worn out dogmas, that for far too long have strangled our politics.”
swa: tumetoa tamko la kumaliza manung'uniko yasiyo na maana na ahadi za uongo, visingizio na imani zilizopitwa na wakati, ambazo kwa muda mrefu zimekuwa zikinyonga siasa yetu.

eng: “In reaffirming the greatness of our nation, we understand that greatness is never a given.
swa:
Katika kutilia mkazo ukuu wa taifa letu, tunaelewa kwamba ukuu si haki yetu ya kupewa hivi hivi tu.
It must be earned.”	Ni lazima tuupiganie.

eng: “we reject as false the choice between our safety and our ideals”
swa: chaguo ama la usalama wetu au maadili yetu, ni la uongo na tunalikataa

eng: Dare we grieve the dead?
swa:
Je tunathubutu kuomboleza wafu?
Dare we hope for the living?	Je tunaweza kuwa na matumaini kwa wale wanaoishi?

eng: Jar of Juice, a blogger based in Dubai, felt that Obama's speech was a bit lacking:
swa: Bloga Jar of Justice aliyeko Dubai, anadhani kwamba hotuba ya Obama ilikuwa na mapungufu:

eng: While I think Obama’s speech was brilliant - he did not flinch when he said “Muslims” but was trying hard to sound genuine when he “thanked” the imbecile of whom we do not speak of after today - I think there was a crucial element missing in this event... ...but I guess Obama won’t lower himself to acknowledge that fool more than the diplomatic gesture in his speech.
swa: Pamoja na kufikiri kwamba hotuba ya Obama ilikuwa nzuri - hakusita pale aliposema 'Waislamu" lakini alijitahidi sana kuonekana mkweli pale "alipomshukuru" yule mpumbavu ambaye hatutamzungumzia tena baada ya leo - nafikiri kulikuwa na jambo muhimu lililokosekana kwenye htukio hili… … lakini ninahisi kuwa Obama hatajishusha na kumhusisha yule mjinga zaidi ya ishara tu ya kidplomasia kwenye hotuba yake.

eng: Moroccan blogger Laila Lalami, who is a US resident and admits to voting for Obama, is slightly more hopeful, and glad Obama's day has come:
swa: Bloga wa Kimoroko Laila Lalami, ambaye ni mkazi wa marekani ambye anakiri kumpigia kura Obama, kidogo ana matumaini zaidi na kuridhika kuwa siku ya Obama imewadia:

eng: I’m glad that day has come.
swa: Nimeridhika kwamba siku ya Obama imewadia.

eng: Eight years ago, I voted for Ralph Nader because I thought there really wasn’t much of a difference between Democrats and Republicans on the major issues.
swa: Miaka minane iliyopita, nilimpigia kura Ralph Nader kwa sababu nilifikiri kuwa hapakuwa na tofauti kubwa kati ya vyama vya Democrat an Republicanm kwenye masuala muhimu.

eng: But after the debacle in Florida, the Supreme Court decision, and the abysmal presidency that followed, I learned a simple lesson: Not all politicians are equal.
swa: Lakini baada ya upuuzi uliotokea Florida, maamuzi ya Mahakama ya Rufaa, na urais dhaifu uliofuatia, nilijifunza somo moja: Si kweli kuwa wanasiasa wote wako sawa.

eng: There are some who are so talentless, so impervious to common sense, so lacking in simple compassion that they make a mockery of the office.
swa: Kuna wengine ambao hawana vipaji, hawaguswi na busara zilizo wazi, ambao hawana huruma kiasi kwamba wanaifanya ofisi ya rais kuwa ni kitu cha mzaha.

eng: I suppose I’m too cynical now to expect vast differences in government policy but I am still fired up about this particular change, about Barack Obama, and about the departure of George W. Bush.
swa: Nadhani hivi sasa situmaini kama kutakuwa na tofauti kubwa katika sera za serikali, hata hivyo bado ninajawa na shauku kwenye haya mabadiliko, kwa Barack obama, na kwa kuondoka kwa George W. Bush.

eng: Moroccan Obama fans are still actively campaigning for President Obama to give his first foreign speech in Rabat.
swa: Washabiki wa Kimoroko wa Obama bado wanaendelea kupiga kampeni ya kumtaka rais Obama atoe hotuba yake ya kwanza nje ya nchi nchini Moroko.

eng: Using generators for power when necessary, a number of Palestinians and foreign activists are still managing to send out reports on what is happening in the Gaza Strip.
swa: Wapalestina wachache na wanaharakati wakigeni bado wanaweza kutuma ripoti za kile kinachoendelea kwenye ukanda wa Gaza kwa kutumia umeme wa jenereta inapobidi.

eng: Here are some of the blog posts of the last 24 hours.
swa: Zifuatazo ni jumbe za blogu katika masaa 24 yaliyopita.

eng: Prof. Said Abdelwahed, who teaches English at Al-Azhar University, writes at Moments of Gaza:
swa: Profesa Abdelwahed, ambaye anafundisha Kiingereza Chuo Kikuu cha Al-Azhar anaandika katika Moments of Gaza:

eng: Today was a ground offensive.
swa: Leo yalikuwa mashambulizi ya nchi kavu.

eng: Many civilians died in the bombing of areas at the edges of Gaza city.
swa: Raia wengi walifariki kwenye mashambulizi ya mabomu katika maeneo ya ukingoni mwa mji wa Gaza.

eng: Electricity and water are still major problems for all Gazans.
swa: Umeme na maji bado ni matatizo makubwa kwa wakazi wote wa Gaza.

eng: I am still operating a generator to be able to write those messages in minutes!
swa: Bado ninatumia jenereta kuweza kuandika jumbe hizi!

eng: Mobile phones are paralyzed and land telephones are static or distorted and other times, it is clear!
swa: Simu za mikononi zimezimika na zile za majumbani zimeganda au hazisikiki vyema na wakati mwingine, husikika!

eng: An air raid nearby minutes back; we do not know where it was but it was so frightening.
swa: Shambulio la anga karibu na hapa dakika chache zilizopita; hatujui lilitokea wapi lakini lilitisha.

eng: They hit a nearby building!
swa: Walipiga jengo lililo karibu!

eng: Its three building away from me; there are casualties!
swa: Ni majengo matatu kutoka hapa nilipo; kuna majeruhi!

eng: Israeli aircrafts are throwing down lighting bombs or perhaps it they are lights for military purposes.
swa: Ndege za Israeli zinatupa mabomu ya radi au pengine ni miangaza inayotumiwa kwa madhumuni ya kijeshi.

eng: Israel intercepted Al-Aqsa satellite channel several times.
swa: Israeli iliingilia idhaa ya setilaiti ya Al-Aqsa kwa mara kadhaa.

eng: They broadcasted anti-Hamas material.
swa: Walitangaza habari zinazoipinga Hamas.

eng: I will be back if could!
swa: Nitarejea tena kama nitaweza!

eng: Natalie Abou Shakra, a Lebanese activist, also blogs at Moments of Gaza:
swa: Natalie Abu Shakra, mwanaharakati wa Kilebanoni, ambaye pia anablogu katika Moments of Gaza:

eng: they're using new weaponry ... very frightening... as it goes through the air... you hear it very close to you... it's going to come, it's going to kill me, now now now... that's what you think of... it's terrifying... i admit not to care... i have gotten used to the old weaponry... now i have to get used to this one too... i cannot describe in words to you the extent of its terror... like a rocket being projected onto you... and the sound... the sound of a plane in the air coming towards you... magnifying its sound the closer it gets... then it passes above our heads... we are all on the floor
swa: Wanatumia silaha mpya… zinatisha sana… wakati zikipita angani… utazisikia ziko karibu sana na wewe… zinakuja, zinakuja kuniua, sasa hivi… hivi ndivyo unavyofikiri… inatisha mno… nakubali kwamba sijali tena… nimeshazoea zile silaha za zamani… na sasa inanibidi nizizowee na hizi pia… siwezi kukuelezea kwa maneno ukali wa vitisho hivi… ni kama kombora linaloelekezwa kwako… na mlio wake… mlio wa ndege angani ikikuelekea… ikiongeza sauti kadri inavyokukaribia zaidi… ikesha inapita juu ya vichwa vyetu… sote tumelala chini…

eng: Laila El-Haddad, whose parents are in Gaza, blogs at Raising Yousuf and Noor:
swa: Laila El-Haddad, ambaye wazazi wake wako mjini Gaza, anablogu katika Raising Yousuf and Noor:

eng: We've heard about the flyers the Israeli army is littering Gaza with - telling people Hamas is to blame for their woes, not their f-16s and cluster bombs.
swa: Tumesikia kuhusi vipeperushi ambavyo majeshi ya Israeli yanauchafua mji wa Gaza navyo - wakiwaambia watu kuwa Hamas ndio wa kulaumiwa kwa matatizo yao, na sio ndege za kijeshi za F-16 na mabomu mengine.

eng: Now, they have taken to robo-calling the citizens of Gaza a la Hilary Clinton, at all times of the night and day.
swa: Na hivi sasa wameanza kuwapigia watu simu kwa kutumia mashine za sauti kana kwamba ni Hilary Clinton, kwa muda wa masaa yote usiku na mchana.

eng: My father has received a number of calls – including one as we finished another CNN interview, and we were on skype.
swa: Baba yangu kapokea simu kadhaa - pamoja na ile wakati tulipokwa tunamaliza mahojiano na CNN, tulikuwa tukitumia Skype.

eng: He tried to put the phone on speaker for me.
swa: Alijaribu kuiweka simu kwenye kipaza sauti ili nami niisikie.

eng: The rough translations: "urgent message: warning to the citizens of Gaza.
swa: Tafasiri ya haraka haraka ni kuwa: "Ujumbe wa dharura: Onyo kwa raia wote wa Gaza.

eng: Hamas is using you as human shields.
swa: Hamas inawatumieni kama ngao.

eng: Do not listen to them.
swa: Msiwasikilize.

eng: Hamas has abandoned you and are hiding in their shelters.
swa: Hamas wamewakimbia na wamejificha kwenye maficho yao.

eng: Give up now..." He hung up in disgust, not wanting to hear the rest.
swa: Achaneni nao…" Aliweka simu chini kwa hasira, hakutaka kusikiliza ujumbe wote.

eng: The army has also been calling people to let them know their houses will be targeted.
swa: Jeshi pia limekuwa likiwapigia simu watu kuwafahamisha kuwa nyumba zao zitashambuliwa.

eng: People have stopped answering their phones now, and do not take calls from unknown numbers from fear.
swa: Watu wameacha kupokea simu zao, na hawapokei simu zenye namba wasizozifahamu kutokana na kuogopa.

eng: Sharon is an activist who blogs at Tales to Tell, and like many of the international activists in Gaza, is doing what she can to assist ambulance workers:
swa: Sharon ni mwanaharakati anayeblogu katika blogu ya Tales to Tell, na kama wanaharakati wengine wa kimataifa mjini Gaza, anafanya awezalo ili kuwasaidia wafanyakazi wa afya wa dharura:

eng: 7.30: Ambulances called out.
swa: 1.30: Magari ya wagonjwa yameitwa.

eng: We are unable to pass a huge crater in the road into which a car has already nosedived.
swa: Tunashindwa kulipita shimo kubwa barabarani ambamo kuna gari lilikwishanasa ndani yake.

eng: Taking the long way round, we collect a man in traditional dress, in his 60s, from what seems to be his family farm.
swa: Tulichukua njia ndefu ya mzunguko, tukamuokota mtu aliyevalia mavazi ya kitamaduni, wa makamo ndani ya miaka ya 60 hivi, kutoka katika linaloonekana ni shamba lake la ukoo.

eng: He is bleeding from the face and very frightened.
swa: Anatokwa damu usoni na mwenye hofu kubwa.

eng: On the way to Karmel Adwan hospital a particularly close explosion rocks the van.
swa: Njiani kuelekea hospitali ya Karmel Adwan mlipuko mmoja karibu kabisa na gari la wagonjwa ukalitetemesha gari.

eng: I mustn’t have jumped enough, because the driver mimes “did you hear that?” to me.
swa: Lazima nilishtuka kiasi, kwa sababu dereva aliniuliza "je umesikia?".

eng: I am beginning to realise Palestinians are fond of rhetorical questions, such as “how do you find Gaza at the moment?”
swa: Ninaanza kufahamu kuwa Wapalestina hupendelea sana kuuliza maswali yenye majibu yaliyo wazi, kama vile "unauonaje mji Gaza hivi sasa?"

eng: 10.55: We leave Al Shifa to head back to the Jabalia Centre.
swa: 4.55: Tunaondoka Al Shifa kurejea kwenye kituo cha Jabalia.

eng: There is coffee.
swa: Kuna kahawa.

eng: Mo makes a coffee sandwich, which is just weird.
swa: Mo anatengeza kahawa na mkate ambavyo si kawaida.

eng: There is a pause in the calls.
swa: Kuna ahueni kwenye idadi ya simu.

eng: Hassan asks me about my book, “Nature Cure”; I explain it is about an ecologist’s route out of depression.
swa: Hassan ananiuliza kuhusu kitabu changu, "Tiba Asilia"; Ninamueleza kuwa ni kitabu kinachohusu safari ya mtaalamu wa mahusiano ya viumbe na mazingira kutoka kwenye ugonjwa wa mawazo. "watu huugua ugonjwa wa mawazo kwenye nchi za magharibi?"

eng: “People get depressed in the West?” he asks in surprise.
swa: Aliuliza kwa mshangao.

eng: Understanding how implausible that must sound right now, I say that many people get caught up in a life that mainly holds work and buying stuff, and without some sort of meaning - religion, or the dream of your land being free, or something like that, people can get very lost.
swa: Ninaelewa isivyoweza kuyumkinika kusikika hivi sasa, nasema watu wengi hujikuta wamejitega katika maisha ya kazi na ununuaji wa vitu tu, bila ya kuwa na maana katika maisha yao - dini, au ndoto ya ukombozi wa nchi yako, au jambo kama hilo, watu wengi hupotea.

eng: “Actually Israel is trying to force us into a meaningless life like this,” he says. “Like, sometimes I feel that all that really matters to me right now is a kilo of gas. I built a stove for my family and I feel like I did something amazing.”
swa: Kwa kweli Israeli inataka kutufanya tuwe hivyo hivi sasa, alisema. "kwa mfano, saa nyingine jambo kubwa ambalo hulifikiria ni jinsi ya kupata kilo ya gesi, nilijenga jiko kwa ajili ya familia yangu na nilijisikia kana kwamba nilifanya jambo la kustaajabisha."

eng: In another post she tells us:
swa: Katika ujumbe mwingine anatuambia:

eng: We asked the Jabalia Red Crescent admin person how much of the emergency calls Israel is not letting them go to.
swa: Tulimuuliza mtumishi wa mapokezi wa shirika la Hilali Nyekundu la Jabalia ni simu ngapi za dharura wanazozipokea kutoka sehemu ambazo Waisraeli hawawaruhusu kwenda.

eng: These are in areas where co-ordination must be made with the invading forces via the Red Cross to enter.
swa: Maeneo hayo ni yale ambayo uratibu wake lazima ufanywe na majeshi ya uvamizi kupitia shirika la Msalaba Mwekundu.

eng: He said they are not being allowed to attend to about 80% of the calls from the north, covering the Beit Lahia, Beit Hanoun, and Jabalia area.
swa: Alisema kuwa hawaruhusiwi kuhudumia asilimia takriban 80 ya simu zote zinazotokea kaskazini, amabpo ni sehemu za Beit Lahia, Beit Hanoun, na Jabalia.

eng: Shall I repeat that? 80%.
swa: Naweza kurudia tena? Asilia 80.

eng: Eight of ten people calling for help are being prevented from receiving it.
swa: Wanane kati ya watu kumi wanaoomba msaada huzuiliwa kupokea msaada huo.

eng: Canadian activist, Eva Bartlett, blogs at In Gaza:
swa: Mwanaharakati kutoka Kanada, Eva Bartlet, anblogu katika In Gaza:

eng: The numbers slaughtered and injured are so high now – 521 and 3,000 as of this morning, Gaza time — that sitting next to a dead or dying person is becoming normal.
swa: Idadi ya walioteketezwa na kujeruhiwa ni kubwa mno hivi sasa – 521 na 3,000 kufikia asbuhi hii, kwa saa za Gaza – kuketi pembeni ya maiti au mtu anayefariki inakuwa ni jambo la kawaida.

eng: The stain of blood on the ambulance stretcher pools next to my coat, the medic warning me my coat may be dirtied.
swa: Doa la damu kwenye machela ya gari la wagonjwa linasogeea karibu ya koti langu, na mganga ananionya kwamba koti langu linaweza kuchafuka.

eng: What does it matter? The stain doesn’t revolt me as it would have, did, one week ago.
swa: Kwani ninajali?Doa lile haliwezi kunikera kama ambavyo ningekereka, au ambavyo nilikereka wiki moja iliyopita.

eng: Death fills the air, the streets in Gaza, and I cannot stress that this is no exaggeration.
swa: Mauti yamejaa hewani, kwenye mitaa ya Gaza, na siwezi kusisitiza zaidi kwamba siongei kwa kutia chumvi.

eng: Back in Gaza city briefly, after a day and night again with the medics, I’ll try to summarize, though there is too much to tell, too much incoming news, and it’s too hard to reach people, even those just a kilometer away.
swa: Nimerudi mjini Gaza kwa muda mchache, baada ya mchana na usiku wa kazi na wauguzi, nitajaribu kutoa muhtasari, ingawa kuna mengi ya kueleza, habari nyingi zinazojitokeza, na ni vigumu kuwafikia wananchi, hata wale walioko kilometa moja tu kutoka hapa.

eng: Before dropping me off, the medics had gone to different gas stations, searching for gas for the ambulances.
swa: Kabla ya kunishusha wauguzi walikwenda kwenye vituo mbalimbali vya mafuta, wakitafuta mafuta kwa ajili ya gari la wagonjwa.

eng: Two stations, no luck.
swa: Walipita vituo viwili bila kubahatika.

eng: Some at a final source fills their tanks.
swa: Na wengine walipofika kwenye kituo cha mwisho walibahatika kujaza mafuta.

eng: The absence of gas is critical.
swa: Uhaba wa mafuta umefikia hali mbaya.

eng: So is the absence of bread, which goes on, the lines longer than ever yet.
swa: Kadhalika uhaba wa mikate, ambao unaendelea, na foleni ni ndefu kuliko.

eng: A text tells me (at this point I have to rely on news from phone and text messages, when reception is available) that the UN says 13,000 have been displaced since these attacks, that 20% of the dead are women and children, 70 % are without drinking water.
swa: Ujumbe wa maandishi kwenye simu ya mkononi unaniambia ( katika kipindi hiki inanibidi nitegemee habari kutoka kwenye simu ya mkononi kama inawezekana kupokea) kwamba Umoja wa Mataifa unasema kuwa watu 13,000wamepoteza makazi yao, na kwamba asilimia 20 ya waliokufa ni wanawake na watoto, asilimia 70 hawana maji salama ya kunywa.

eng: There are many more facts to sober one drunk on apathy, but I can’t source or share them now.
swa: Kuna taarifa nyingi zinazoweza kumlevya mtu na ugonjwa wa kutojali, lakini siwezi kuwaambia yote hivi sasa.

eng: Safa Joudeh writes at Lamentations-Gaza:
swa: Safa Joudeh anaandika kwenye blogu ya Lamentations – Gaza:

eng: Israel has come into our homes, is fighting us in our streets and is expressing its brutality against us in full force.
swa: Israeli imetuingilia majumbani, inapigana katika mitaa yetu na unaonyesha unyama wake dhidi kwa nguvu zote.

eng: How do we react?
swa: Je tujibu vipi?

eng: All Palestinian factions have united and are out facing the enemy, using all the military capabilities that they collectively have.
swa: Makundi yote ya Wapalestinayameungana na yanampinga adui, kwa kutumia nguvu zao zote za kijeshi kwa pamoja.

eng: Although these capabilities are incomparable to the military strength exerted by Israel, yet it has made us more certain than ever that Palestinians will fight to the very end to protect their own.
swa: Japokuwa nguvu hizohaziwezi kulingana na nguvu zilizoshinikizwa na Israeli, zimetufanya tuwe na hakika zaidi kwamba Wapalestina watapigana mpaka mwisho kulinda kile kilicho chao.

eng: It has shown us that resistance, courage and love are an integral part of the Palestinian identity that will never change despite all the hardships we endure.
swa: Imetuonyesha kwamba mapambano ya upinzani, kujitoa muhanga na mapenzi ni sehemu ya Wapalestina ambayo haitaweza kubadilika pamoja na dhiki zote zinazotusibu.

eng: It has given us a moral boost, which comes at a time when we need it most.
swa: Imetutia mwamko adili katika hisia zetu, mwamko ambao umetufikia katika wakati tunaouhitaji zaidi.

eng: It's hard even to remember a time when basic necessities such as food, water, warmth and daylight weren't a luxury.
swa: Ni vigumu kukumbukawakati ambapo mahitaji ya msingi kama vile chakula, maji, vuguvugu la mapendo na mwanga wa juahavikuwa anasa.

eng: At this point, bare human instinct is at work, the need to protect your loved ones, the need to ensure shelter and the instinct of fight or flight.
swa: Katika kipindi hiki ni haja za kibinaadamu opekee ambazo zinafanya kazi, haja ya kuwalinda wale uwapendao, haja ya kuhakikisha unayo malazi na maamuzi ya haraka ya aidha kukimbia au kupigana.

eng: We have fled for too long, Gaza is our last refuge and our home after we were displaced from what is now called Israel.
swa: Tumekuwa tukikimbia kwa muda mrefu sana, Gaza ndiyo kwetu na ndiyo ngome yetu ya mwisho baada ya kupoteza makazi yetu kule panapoitwa Israeli hivi sasa.

eng: All this happened but 60 years ago.
swa: Haya yote yalitokea miaka 60 tu iliyopita.

eng: What more could they want?
swa: Jingine lipi wanalolitaka?

eng: We have nowhere left to go.
swa: Hatuna pengine pa kwenda.

eng: Now is a time when all forms of resistance are legitimate.
swa: Huu ndio wakati ambao kila mbinu ya upinzani ni ruksa kutumika.

eng: They have disregarded every single international law there is.
swa: Wamepuuza kila kila sheria ya kimataifa iliyopo.

eng: So now is the time to fight.
swa: Kwa hiyo huu ndio wakati wa kupigana.

eng: RafahKid makes a plea:
swa: Rafah Kid anatoa rai:

eng: Please...before everyone in Gaza is dead...perhaps try to understand that Hamas is a symptom....not a cause....the Occupation is the cause....the lack of a settlement for the forcible removal of people from their land....this is the cause...Hamas is a symptom....and the US doesn't like governments it doesn't choose.
swa: Tafadhali… kabla ya kila mmoja kufa mjini Gaza… labda jaribuni kuelewa kuwa Hamas ni dalili… na sio chanzo… chanzo ni kukaliwa kimabavu… uhaba wa makazi uliotokana na watu kuhamishwa kwa nguvu kutoka kwenye ardhi yao… hicho ndio chanzo… Hamas ni dalili… na Marekani haizipendi serikali ambazo haikuziteua.

eng: No electricity...no outgoing calls.
swa: Hakuna umeme… hakuna mawasiliano ya simu kwenda nje.

eng: Darkness and it's raining fire.
swa: Giza na mvua ya moto inanyesha.

eng: The children are screaming.
swa: Watoto wanapiga mayowe.

eng: Mutasharrid (‘homeless person’ or ‘vagrant’) is in Khan Younis, and is angry:
swa: Mutasharrid (mtu asiye na makazi) yupo huko Khan Younis, na ana hasira:

eng: I was asked yesterday whether the aid to Gaza was really getting in or if it was "newspaper talk".
swa: Niliulizwa jana kama misaada inafika Gaza au ni "habari tu ya kwenye magazeti".

eng: I refused to respond because the answer is clear, as clear as the sound of F16 strike right now: never mind, the aid got into Gaza, maybe in great quantities in the first days, but stopped two days ago on the pretext of the ground operation, however, that did not count for much!
swa: Nilikataa kujibu kwani jawabu liko wazi, liko wazi kama ngurumo ya ndege za kijeshi za F-16 zinavyonguruma hivi sasa;usijali, misaada inayoingia Gaza, labda kwa kiwango kikubwa wakati wa siku zile za mwanzo, lakini ilisitishwa siku mbili zilizopita kwa madai ya operesheni ya kijeshi ya nchi kavu, hata hivyo, hilo halikubadili chochote!

eng: I mean, how have the media succeeded in presenting the case of Gaza as one of a hungry person under siege, searching for food and "humanitarian" aid not worthy of dogs?!
swa: Yaani, ni vipi vyombo vya habari vimefanikiwa kuwasilisha shauri hili kama shauri moja la mtu mwenye njaa aliyezingirwa, anayetafuta misaada ya kibinaadamu na chakula kisichomfaa hata mbwa?!

eng: When I asked my friend he said, "The Arabs are like a person firing on a dog and throwing it a piece of meat!"
swa: Nilipomuuliza raki yangu alinijibu "Waarabu ni mfano wa watu wanaompiga mbwa huku wakimrushia mnofu wa nyama!"

eng: Gaza is not searching for an aspirin for its bloody wound, my friends, Gaza is not searching for a bandage for its continuous bleeding.
swa: Gaza haitafuti aspirini kutibu jeraha lake, rafiki zangu, Gaza haitafuti bandeji kwa ajili kuziba mtiririko wa damu.

eng: What hurts Gaza, indeed kills it more than rockets, are their voices: the voice of every person wearing a suit and tie speaking about Gaza.
swa: Kitu kinachoiumiza Gaza, na hasa kitu kinachoiua Gaza zaidi ya makombora ni sauti yake: sauti ya kila mtu anayevalia suti na tai anayeizungumzia Gaza.

eng: You wish you could scream in their faces, before the aircraft, "Stop!
swa: Utatatamani uwapayukie kwenye nyuso zao, kabla ya ndege, "Nyamaza!

eng: Your voice is wounding and is damned sharper than your silence, so stay silent… Have mercy on us, stay silent a little while..."
swa: Sauti yako inajeruhi na ina makali zaidi ya ukimya wako, kwa hivyo kaa kimya… Tuonee huruma, kaa kimya kwa kitambo kidogo…"

eng: Exiled (المنفي) says simply:
swa: Mwanablogu Exiled anasema kwa ufupi:

eng: I am off till the end of this Massacre
swa: Nakwenda mapumzikoni mpaka mwisho wa mauaji haya ya kinyama

eng: Pray 4 us
swa: Tuombeeni

eng: A blog called Harm to civilians during the fighting in Gaza and Southern Israel has been set up by Israeli human rights groups to document events that are not being covered by the media.
swa: Blogu yenye jina la Madhara kwa raia wakati wa mapambano mjini Gaza na Kusini mwa Israeli imetengenezwa na asaasi za haki za kibinaadamu za Kiisraeli ili kuorodhesha matukio ambayo hayaandikwi na vyombo vikubwa vya habari.

eng: Under normal circumstances and despite a high rate of literacy, Palestine's Internet penetration rate stands between 13 and 15 per cent (including both the West Bank and Gaza).
swa: Katika mazingira ya kawaida bila kiwango kikubwa cha wanaojua kusoma, usambaaji wa intaneti husimama kati ya asilimia 13 mpka asilimia 15 (Gaza na Ukingo wa Magharibi kwa pamoja).

eng: Given the ongoing attacks on Gaza, however, Internet access has been significantly diminished.
swa: Kutokana na mashambulizi yanayoendelea huko huko Gaza, uwezo wa kutumia intaneti umepungua sana.

eng: Although there is a small number of bloggers writing directly from Gaza, many Gaza residents are instead sending text messages and making phone calls abroad in the hopes that their stories will be told.
swa: Japokuwa kuna idadi ndogo ya wanablogu wanaoandika moja kwa moja kutokea Gaza, wakazi wengine wengi wanatumia ujumbe wa maandishi wa simu za mkononi pamoja na simu nje ya nchi katika matumaini kwamba ushahidi wao utapata sehemu ya kuelezwa.

eng: Mohammad of KABOBfest, who is based in the West Bank, has been reporting on Gaza for several days now.
swa: Mohammad wa KABOBfest, maybe anaishi Ukingo wa Magharibi, amekuwa akiripoti kuhusu Gaza kwa siku kadhaa sasa.

eng: In his first post on December 29, he tells us:
swa: Katika ujumbe wake wa kwanza wa tarehe 29 Desemba, anatuambia:

eng: I wanted to call my uncles and check up on them and their families, but for most of the day I couldn't.
swa: Nilitaka kuwapigia simu wajomba zangu ili kuwajulia hali wao na familia zao, sikuweza kwa siku nzima.

eng: I was too afraid to know the state they might be in.
swa: Nilikuwa nahofu sana kujua hali waliyokuwamo.

eng: But when I did call, I was pleasantly surprised.
swa: Lakini nilipopiga simu,nilipata mshangao mzuri.

eng: My uncle Jasim told me things were much better today, there was still a fear but people had begun to recover.
swa: Mjomba wangu Jasim aliniambia mambo yalikuwa mazuri zaidi leo, japo kulikuwa na hofu lakini watu wameanza kupata ahueni.

eng: We've managed to absorb the shock of that initial attack, he said, and that is helping us get by today.
swa: Tumeweza kuhimili mshtuko wa shambulio la kwanza, alisema, na hiyo imetusaidia kustahimili hii leo.

eng: He said the sky had been quiet for about half an hour over Khan Younis, but the warships were attacking the shore. His voice was strong, just like it was when I'd talk to him at any time before the massacre began, and told me to not worry so much.
swa: Alisema anga imekuwa kimya kwa muda wa saa moja na nusu hivi huko Khan Younis, lakini meli za kivita zilikuwa zinaendelea kushambulia sehemu za mwambao.Sauti yake likuwa imara, kama vile ilivyokuwa wakati wowote kabla ya mauaji kuanza, na aliniambia nisihofu sana.

eng: They had no power, as usual, so I told him about the ongoing demonstrations and clashes in the West Bank and the outpouring of support across the world.
swa: Hawakuwa na umeme kama kawaida, nikamueleza juu ya maandamano na ghasia zinazotokea Ukingo wa Magharibi na mvua za kuungwa mkono zinazomwagika duniani kote.

eng: I told him that nobody has forgotten them, and he told me to just keep praying for them.
swa: Nilimwambia kuwa hakuna aliyewasahau, na aliniasa niendelee kuwaswalia.

eng: His youngest kids were asleep, but his daughters, Haneen and Yaqeen, were still up.
swa: Wanawe wadogo walikuwa bado wamelala, lakini binti zake, Haneen na Yaqeen walikuwa bado wapo macho.

eng: I told him to tell them we're all thinking about them.
swa: Nilimuomba awaambie kwamba bado wako mioyoni mwetu.

eng: Next I called my uncle Mahmoud.
swa: Halafu nikampigia simu mjomba wangu Mahmood.

eng: Yesterday, he told me he was waiting for death.
swa: Jana aliniambia kuwa anasubiri kifo.

eng: The Israeli army had called him and told him they would bomb his home within a few minutes.
swa: Waisraeli walimpigia simu na kumwambia kuwa wangeipiga mabomu nyumba yake katika dakika chache.

eng: It had left us all terrified, but today he told me it had become apparent that the Israeli army had sent that message to tens of thousands of homes.
swa: Alituacha sote tukiogopa, lakini leo alituambia kuwa kumbe Waisraeli waliwapigia simu za namna hiyo kwenye makumi ya maelfu ya nyumba.

eng: It is a sadistic and cruel tactic, designed to terrorize hundreds of thousands inside their own homes.
swa: Ni mbinu ya utesi na ukatili, iliyoundwa ili kuwagaidi makumi ya mjaelfu ya raia wakiwa majumbani mwao.

eng: But his hopefulness soon disappeared.
swa: Lakini matumaini haya mara yalitoweka.

eng: On January 3, Mohammed reported again:
swa: Mnamo tarehe 3, Januari, Mohammed aliripoti tena:

eng: I managed to get through to my uncle Mohammad again in Gaza City.
swa: Nimeweza kumfikia mjomba wangu Mahmood kwa mara nyingine tena mjini Gaza.

eng: For the duration of the phone call, an explosion would be heard every 20 seconds or so.
swa: Wakati wote tuliokuwa tukiongea kwenye simu, mlipukjo ulisikika kila baada sekunde kama 20 hivi.

eng: In the bitter cold of the night, terror is blanketing the people of Gaza, and Gaza City in particular.
swa: Katika baridi kali ya usiku, vitisho vinawafunika watu wa Gaza, na hasa ndani ya jiji la Gaza.

eng: The gunfire and explosions are framed against a background of a blackened sky buzzing with invisible war planes and attack helicopters.
swa: Milio ya bunduki na milipuko inaiwamba mandhari ya anga jeusi yenye miungurumo ya ndege za kijeshi zisizoonekana na pia helikopta za kijeshi.

eng: Nobody knows what is being hit.
swa: Hakuna anayejua ni nini kinachopigwa.

eng: My uncle tells me there have been explosions all around them, near and far, from all sides, but even the local radio, which so far has been excellent at reporting what happens on the ground, cannot determine what the targets are that are being hit.
swa: Mjomba wangu nananiambia kumekuwa na milipuko katika sehemu zote zinazowazunguka, Karibu na mbali, kutoka kila upande, hata idhaa ya redio yao, ambayo imekuwa ikifanya kazi nzuri ya kuwaeleza ni nini kinachoendelea, haiwezi tena kueleza kwa hakika ni nini kinacholengwa na kupigwa.

eng: Nobody is sure if the airstrikes are targeting homes, buildings, mosques or previously bombed sites, therefore nobody knows if any change in tactics has occurred.
swa: Hakuna anyejua kama mashumbulizi hayo ya anga yazilenga nyumba za watu, majengo, miskiti au sehemu ambazo zilishashambuliwa awali, kwa hiyo hakuna nayejua kama mbinu zimebadilika au la.

eng: In war, for civilians as much as for soldiers, there isn't much that is more terrifying than not knowing.
swa: Katika vita, kwa raia kama vile ilivyo kwa wanajeshi, hakuna linalotisha zaidi kama kutokujua.

eng: In a third post, he details calls with several family members across Gaza, comparing the situation on the ground from Gaza City to Khan Younis.
swa: Katika ujumbe wake wa tatu, anasimulia kwa undani mazungumzo ya simu na wanafamlia wake walioko Gaza, akilinganisha hali ilivyo kutokea jijini Gaza mpaka Khan Younis.

eng: He describes one phone call with his uncle's wife:
swa: Anaielezea simu moja mojawapo akiongea na mke wa mjomba wake:

eng: I talked to Areej again.
swa: Niliongea tena na Areej.

eng: She had calmed down somewhat, but still sounded very scared.
swa: Amepoa kwa kiasi Fulani, lakini alikuwa bado na hofu.

eng: I asked her about the kids.
swa: Nilimuuliza kuhusu watoto.

eng: She said the baby, Yazeed, was asleep next to her.
swa: Akasema, mtoto, Yazeed, alikuwa amelala pembeni yake.

eng: Dina had also fallen asleep, and their mother had told Nada and Haya to go to their room, where it would be safer.
swa: Dina pia alikuwa amelala, na mama yao amewaambia Nada na Haya kwenda chumbani kwao ambako panaweza kuwa salama zaidi.

eng: I asked her if they were keeping warm with the windows always open to the wind, and she said when they sleep they wear as many layers as they can and are covered in as many blankets as possible, but during the day and evening it does get very cold.
swa: Nilimuuliza ikiwa wapata joto ikiwa madirisha yao yako wazi wakati wote yakipitisha upepo, akaniambia wakati wakilala wanajifunika na na tabaka nyingi za mablanketi kadiri inavyowezekana, lakini wakati wa mchana na jioni baridi si kali sana.

eng: I asked about Adham, her 11 year old son.
swa: Nilmuuliza kuhusu Adham, mwanawe mwenye umri wa miaka 11.

eng: She told me he had lit two candles and laid out his toys and was trying, despite the cold and fear and shelling and death and trauma, to play.
swa: Aliniambia kuwa mwanawe amewasha mishumaa miwili na amesambaza wanasesere wake anajaribu kucheza, pamoja na baridi na hofu na makombora na vifo na athari.

eng: He had lego blocks and toy cars, and some toy soldiers.
swa: Alikuwa na vifaa vya kuchezea vya Lego, na magari pamoja na sanamu za wanajeshi.

eng: I didn't bother asking her what he was doing with the soldiers.
swa: Sikutaka kumuuliza alikuwa anacheza mchezo gani na hao sanamu wanajeshi.

eng: I didn't want to know.
swa: Sikutaka kujua.

eng: Global Voices' own Ayesha Saldanha of Bint Battuta in Bahrain has also been posting updates from friends in Gaza.
swa: Mwandishi wa Global Voices Ayesha Saldanha wa blogu ya Bint Battuta wa Bahrain pia amekuwa akipandisha makala kutoka kwa marafiki zake walioko Gaza.

eng: Today's SMS update from her friend Hasan includes a telling last line:
swa: Ujumbe wa leo wa SMS kutoka kwa rafiki yake Hasan una mstari wa mwisho unaoleza wazi:

eng: 6.30 am: "Neither the telephone nor the electricity is working.
swa: 12.30 asubuhi: Si simu ya ndani wala ya umeme vinavyofanya kazi.

eng: I have just got up and saw your sms.
swa: Ndio kwanza nimeamka na kuuona ujumbe wako wa simu ya mkononi.

eng: I heard very loud tanks shelling outside.
swa: Nilisikia kelele kubwa za vifaru vikishambulia huko nje.

eng: Apache and the drone .
swa: Pamoja na helikoptas za kijeshi za Apache na drone.

eng: They might be nearer we don't know"
swa: Wanaweza wakawa karibu hatujui.

eng: 8.20 am: "Still not near. i hope so.
swa: 2.20 asubuhi: "Bado havijafika karibu.

eng: If electricity keeps off like in gaza we won't be able.
swa: Kama umeme ukiendelea hivi kama gaza hatutaweza.

eng: I am trying to call my sister or text her but in vain"
swa: Najaribu kumpigia simu au kumuandikia ujumbe wa simu ya mkononi dada yangu bila mafanikio"

eng: 1.30 pm: "my wife asked why are you frowning.
swa: 7.30 mchana: "mke wangu kaniuliza kwa nini nakunja sura.

eng: Give me anything that might give me a hope and I will smile I replyed.
swa: Nipe chochote kitakachoweza kunitia matumaini na nitatabasamu nilimjibu.

eng: Today after the lists of our needs became too much.
swa: Leo orodha ya mahitaji imezidi sana.

eng: Medicine, food, cleaning material.
swa: Dawa, chakula na vifaa vya usafi.

eng: I decided to go downtown although they struck a market in Gaza.
swa: Niliamua kwenda mjini japokuwa walikwisha shambulia soko moja mjini Gaza.

eng: They killed 5 and injured a group of people.
swa: Waliua watu 5 na kujeruhi kundi la watu.

eng: As I entered the market F16 struck 2 houses very near to the market.
swa: Nilipoingia tu sokoni ndege ya F-16 ikazipiga nyumba 2 karibu kabisa na soko.

eng: All the people thought like me.
swa: Kila mtu alifikiri kama nilivyofikiri mimi.

eng: Either the market or the mosque.
swa: Kama sio soko basi itakuwa Msikiti.

eng: I felt panic.
swa: Nikapatwa na kihoro.

eng: I bought half our needs and hurried home.
swa: Nikanunua nusu tu ya mahitaji yetu na kuharakia nyumbani.

eng: In my way they struck another house near my home.
swa: Wakati niko njiani wakapiga nyumba nyingine karibu na nyumba yangu.

eng: The tanks shelled a lot last night we were very worried" 6.30 pm: "If things got worse I'd put my in my wife's mobile.
swa: Vifaru vilipiga sana jana usiku mapaka tukawa tunaogopa. 12.30 jioni: " kama mambo yataendelea kuwa mabaya nitaitia kadi yangu ya simu kwenye simu ya mke wangu.

eng: F16 is shelling right now. and the sound of the ambulance is loud.
swa: Ndege za F-16 zinapiga hivi sasa. Na mlio wa gari ya wagonjwa ni mkubwa.

eng: Everyday is worse than the previous"
swa: Kila siku ni mbaya zaidi kuliko siku iliyopita"

eng: At approximately 6:00 p.m. (GMT+2), Al Jazeera English reported that a UN school was hit when two tank shells exploded outside of the school.
swa: Takriban majira ya saa 12 za jioni (GMT +2), Idhaa ya Kiingereza ya Al Jazeera iliripoti kuwa shule moja ya Umoja wa Mataifa ilipigwa wakati makombora mawili ya vifaru yalipolipuka nje ya shule hiyo.

eng: The school, located in Jabaliya, had been set up days ago as a shelter for Gaza residents who had lost or evacuated their homes.
swa: Shule hiyo, iliyopo Jabaliya, ilianza kutumiwa kama makazi ya raia wa Gaza waliozikimbia nyumba zao au waliopoteza makazi yao.

eng: According to Al Jazeera English, more than 40 people were killed.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa idhaa ya Kiingereza ya Al Jazeera, zaidi ya watu 40 wameuawa.

eng: On Al Jazeera English's television station (accessible globally via Livestation.com), it was reported that the IDF had been given GPS coordinates to all UN schools.
swa: Katika idhaa ya televisheni ya Kiingereza ya Al Jazeera (inayopatikana duniani kote kupitia Livestation.com) ilitangazwa kuwa jeshi la Israeli, IDF limepewa ramani za setilaiti, GPS, za mashule ya Umoja wa Mataifa.

eng: The Philistine reported quickly on the incident:
swa: Blogu ya Philistine iliripoti kwa haraka juu ya tukio hilo:

eng: Medical officials say the death toll from an Israeli airstrike outside a United Nations school in the Gaza Strip has risen to 30.
swa: Waganga na maafisa wa afya wanasema idadi ya waliofariki kutokana na shambulio hilo la anga la Israeli nje ya shule ya Umoja wa Mataifa kwenye ukanda wa Gaza imefikia 30.

eng: The attack occurred about 10 yards (meters) outside the school in northern Gaza.
swa: Shambulio hilo lilitokea kama yadi 10 hivi (mita) nje ya shule huko kaskazini mwa Gaza.

eng: It was the second deadly Israeli attack to strike a UN school in the past few hours.
swa: Ni shambulio la pili la Israeli lililopiga shule ya Umoja wa mataifa katika masaa machache yaliyopita.

eng: Hospital director Bassam Abu Warda confirmed the 30 deaths from the second airstrike.
swa: Mkurugenzi wa hospitali Bassa Abu Warda alithibitisha vifo 30 kutokana na shambulio la pili.

eng: In both cases, the schools had been used as shelters for people displaced by Israel’s offensive
swa: Katika mashambulio yote mawili, shule hizo zilitumiwa kama hifadhi ya watu waliopoteza makazi yao kutokana na mashambulizi ya Israeli.

eng: A top U.N. humanitarian official has condemned the violence and demanded an investigation.
swa: Afisa mmoja wa ngazi za juu wa Umoja wa Mataifa amelaani unyama huo na kutaka uchunguzi ufanywe.

eng: Israel isn’t commenting.
swa: Israeli haijatoa maoni yoyote.

eng: Syria News Wire also reported quickly, stating:
swa: Blogu ya Syria News Wire kadhalika iliripoti kwa haraka ikieleza:

eng: 40 people have now died after Israel’s bombing of a UN school in Gaza.
swa: Watu 40 wamefariki baada ya Israeli kutupa makombora kwenye shule ya Umoja wa Mataifa huko Gaza.

eng: 400 Palestinians were being given shelter there by the UN.
swa: Wapalestina 400 walipewa hifadhi shuleni hapo na Umoja wa Mataifa.

eng: Twitter user dominiccampbell, from London, reacted strongly to the news as well:
swa: Mtumiaji wa huduma ya Twita domoniccampbell, aliyeko mjini London, alitoa maoni makali kuhusiana na taarifa hiyo:

eng: Finnish Twitter user haloefekti expresses shock at the lack of outcry:
swa: Mtumiaji wa Twita wa Kifini haloefekti anaelezea kustushwa kwake na uhaba wa shutma kuhusu shambulio hilo:

eng: While several Iranian bloggers (including Islamist ones) multiplied their posts and digital initiatives, such as a "Google bomb" to condemn Israel's invasion of the Gaza Strip, some other bloggers are saying the Iranian government is using the "Gaza conflict moment” to repress media and civil society inside the country.
swa: Wakati wanablogu kadhaa wa Kiirani (pamoja na wale wa-Kiislamu) waliongeza makala zao na jitihada nyingine za kidijitali, kama vile "Google bomb" kulaani uvamizi wa Israeli katika ukanda wa Gaza, wanablogu wengine wanasema kwamba serikali ya Irani inatumia 'mwanya wa mgogoro wa Gaza' kukandamiza vyombo vya habari na asasi za kiraia ndani ya nchi hiyo.

eng: Last week, Iranian authorities shut down, Kargozaran, a leading reformist journal, because it published a statement of a student movement (Tahkim Vahdat) that condemned Israel but also referred to Palestinian militant groups who take refuge in hospitals and schools as terrorists.
swa: Wiki iliyopita, utawala wa Irani uliifungia Kargozaran, moja ya jarida mashuhuri la mabaliko, kwa sababu ilichapisha tamko la chama cha wanafunzi (Tahkim Vahadat) ambalo liliilaani Israeli lakini pia liligusia kundi moja la Wapalestina wenye siasa kali ambalo hujificha kwenye mahospitali na mashule, kama ni kundi la magaidi.

eng: Nik Ahnag, a leading cartoonist and blogger, has published a couple of cartoons about the Gaza invasion and the inequal power balance between Israel and Palestinians on one side, and Iranian government repression on the other side.
swa: Nik Ahnag, bloga mashuri na mchoraji wa vikaragosi, alichora picha za vichekesho zinazohusu uvamizi wa Gaza na mizani ya nguvu zisizolingana kati ya Israeli na Palestina kwenye upande mmoja na ukandamizaji wa serikali ya Irani kwenye upande mwingine.

eng: One of these cartoons shows a huge hammer labeled Gaza hitting the Kargozaran journal.
swa: Moja ya michoro hiyo inaonyesha nyundo kubwa yenye chapa ya Gaza ikilipiga jarida la Kargorazan.

eng: In the cartoon, it seems that teachers, women and students are the next targets in line.
swa: Ghasia zilikuwa kali kiasi kwamba ziliwafanya baadhi ya waunga mkono wa Fatah wakimbilie Israeli kwa ajili ya hifadhi.

eng: Blogger Jomhour writes about the statement that led to the closure of reformist journal.
swa: St Behesht anaandika kuhusu "Kushindwa kwa televisheni ya Irani pamoja na kuchujwa kwa habari".

eng: He says :
swa: Bloga huyo anasema :

eng: With the war raging in Gaza, news reports earlier this month about the routing of an extraordinarily large shipment of arms from the United States to Israel through the private Greek port of Astakos caused an uproar among Greek bloggers.
swa: Wakati vita vikiendelea huko Gaza, taarifa zilizotolewa mwanzoni mwa mwezi kuhusu usafirishwaji wa shehena kubwa ya silaha kutoka Marekani kuelekea Israeli kupitia bandari ya Astakos huko Ugiriki zimezua kelele kutoka kwa wanablogu wa Kigiriki.

eng: They used Twitter to investigate the matter and put pressure on the government to halt the transfer.
swa: Wanablogu hao walitumia huduma ya Twita kuchunguza swala hilo na kuitia shinikizo serikali ya Ugiriki kusimamisha usafirishwaji wa silaha hizo.

eng: Delivery of the munitions was suspended, just as the Greek government was coming under fire from opposition parties, and Amnesty International was calling for an arms embargo.
swa: Usafirishaji wa shehena hiyo ulisitishwa, wakati serikali ya Ugiriki ilipobanwa na vyama vya upinzani pamoja na Shirika la Msamaha Duniani lilipokuwa likitaka vikwazo vya uingizwaji wa silaha nchini Israeli vipitishwe.

eng: At first, official sources contested the story from the international news agency Reuters on January 9.
swa: Awali, vyanzo kutoka serikalini vilipingana na habari iliyotolewa tarehe 9 Januari na shirika la habari la Reuters.

eng: But it was picked up by Twitter users and investigated after Indy.gr - an offshoot of the Indymedia Athens group - provided a translation of the article in Greek.
swa: Lakini watumiaji wa huduma ya Twita waliipata habari hiyo na kuipeleleza baada ya Indy.gr - tawi mojawapo la Indymedia Athens - kutoa tafsiri ya makala hiyo katika lugha ya Kigiriki.

eng: The idea to organize an embargo of the port was proposed and widely "re-tweeted":
swa: Wazo la kuandaa vikwazo bandarini lilipendekezwa na likaenezwa kwa "kutuma tena na tena jumbe za Twita":

eng: itsomp: http://is.gd/f8Wa Can we organise an embargo of the port of Astakos?
swa: itsomp: http://is.gd/f8Wa Je tunaweza kuandaa vikwazo kwenye bandari ya Astakos?

eng: Only the US and Israeli ships...
swa: Vikwazo kwa meli za Marekani na Israeli pekee…

eng: Some tweeted direct queries to the Greek foreign minister, whose web team is operating a Twitter account:
swa: Hapana shaka kwamba shehena hiyo itasafirishwa, isipokuwa siyo hivi sasa na si kwa kutokea hapa.

eng: Bloggers in Bahrain are fuming at a decision by the country's Minister of Information to block access to scores of websites, as well as prevent access to proxy sites which enable surfers to get to sites in a roundabout manner.
swa: Wanablogu wa Bahrain wanaujia juu uamuzi wa Waziri wa habari wa nchi hiyo wa kuzuia upatikanaji wa tovuti mbalimbali, kadhalika kuzuia matumizi ya tovuti vivuli zinazoruhusu watumiaji kuperuzi tovuti nyingine zilizozuiwa na zana za kuchuja habari.

eng: Ammaro is defiant:
swa: Ayesha Saldanha anaangalia maoni kutoka Bahrain.

eng: MINISTRY; HERE'S A SPECIAL MESSAGE FOR YOU.
swa: WAZIRI; HUU NI UJUMBE MAALUM KWAKO.

eng: YOU CAN BLOCK A DOOR, YOU CAN BLOCK TWO, BUT YOU'LL NEVER BE ABLE TO CENSOR THE INTERNET, WHETHER YOU LIKE IT OR NOT.
swa: UNAWEZA KUFUNGA MLANGO, UNAWEZA KUFUNGA MILANGO MIWILI, LAKINI HAUTAWEZA KUUCHUJA MTANDAO WA INTANETI, UPENDE USIPENDE.

eng: THERE ARE A MILLION AND ONE WAYS TO GET AROUND YOUR BLOCKADES, AND YOU'LL NEVER KEEP UP WITH THEM.
swa: KUNA NJIA MILIONI MOJA NA MOJA ZA KUVIZUNGUKA VIZINGITI VYAKO, NA HAUTAWEZA KUKABILIANA NAVYO VYOTE.

eng: Rayyash says: I was surprised when I read the order issued by the Minister of Information to block websites on the Internet.
swa: Bloga Rayyash anasema: Nilistuka wakati nilipoisoma amri iliyotolewa na Waziri wa Habari wa kuzuia tovuti kwenye matandao wa intaneti.

eng: The reason I was surprised was not because of the part related to banning pornographic sites which I agree with and call for censoring, but the part which says that any other site could also be blocked.
swa: Sababu iliyonifanya nishangae haikuwa ile inayohusiana na uamuzi wa kuzuia tovuti za ngono, ambao nakubaliana nao na kuwataka wazifunge, lakini ni kwa ile sehemu inayosema kuwa tovuti yoyote ile inaweza kuzuiliwa.

eng: The reason for this is that I don't believe that Arab governments have good intentions
swa: Sababu ni kwamba siamini kuwa serikali za Kiarabu zina nia njema.

eng: Hussain Marhoon has a slightly different position: In principle, I am against the banning of websites altogether and that includes porn even though I don't know the value of being "against".
swa: Hussein Marhoon ana mtazamo tofauti kidogo: Kimsimamo, ninapinga kufungwa kwa tovuti zikijumuishwa zile za ngono hata kama sifahamu thamani ya "kupinga".

eng: I know that there is a religious wave that is starting to have an impact on all areas of our life.
swa: Ninajua kwamba kuna wimbi la kidini linaloanza kuathiri kila sehemu ya maisha yetu.

eng: Jenan asks: Why don't we enjoy freedom of speech and where are we as regards liberalising expression?
swa: Jenan anauliza: Kwa nini hatufaidi uhuru wa kujieleza na tuko wapi kwenye suala la kuruhusu uhuru wa kujieleza?

eng: Mohammed Marhoon also has a question: Aren't we in the era of reform and transparency?
swa: Mohammed Marhoon pia anauliza: Je hatumo kwenye zama za mageuzi na uwazi?

eng: There is no excuse for imposing a guardian on the sender and recipient at the same time!
swa: Hakuna kisingizio cha kumuweka mlinzi kwa mtumaji na mpokeaji!

eng: The Redbelt says:
swa: Bloga The Redbelt anasema:

eng: Let me try to paint you a picture:
swa: Ngoja nijaribu kukuchorea picha:

eng: It is the 1980’s.
swa: Ni katika miaka ya 1980.

eng: No internet and no Satellite TV channels and nothing.
swa: Hakuna intaneti wala setilaiti za idhaa za televisheni.

eng: The only communications we have with the outside world are videotapes, cassettes, books and magazines.
swa: Mawasiliani pekee tuliyonayo na dunia ni kwa kupitia mikanda ya video, kanda, vitabu na majarida.

eng: In these simpler times, banning something would actually work.
swa: Katika wakati huu, kufungiwa kwa kitu kuliweza kufanya kazi.

eng: If the government says for a reason or another that a film for example is unacceptable and not wanted, the majority of the population, if not all, will not get to see it.
swa: Kama serikali ikisema kutokana na sababu moja au nyingine kwamba filamu kwa mfano, haikubaliki na haitakiwi, wengi wa watu, kama sio wote, wasingeweza kuiona.

eng: Tapes will be easily found and confiscated.
swa: Kanda zingeweza kufikiwa na kupokonywa kwa urahisi.

eng: And then what?
swa: Halafu nini?

eng: Banning media at that age was quite effective.
swa: Kufungia vyombo vya habari katika zama zile kuliweza kufanya kazi.

eng: But that was a long, long, LONG time ago.
swa: Lakini hiyo ilikuwa zamani sana, ZAMANI sana.

eng: Just look at my brother, he was a mere idea in ’86 and was born in ’87.
swa: Hebu muangalie kaka yangu, alikuwa ni ndoto tu mwaka '86 na akazaliwa mwaka '87.

eng: Today he is a 186 cm tall man, with a goatee, driving license and a college degree.
swa: Hivi sasa ni mrefu wa sentimita 186, ana ndevu za beberu, ana leseni ya gari na shahada ya chuo.

eng: Media has grown that much too.
swa: Vyombo vya habari vimekua vivyo hivyo.

eng: Eyad wonders about the business logic:
swa: Eyad anajiuliza kuhusu mantiki ya biashara:

eng: Let’s not look at the internet as the super highway of information but look at it as a product, the people in their homes are paying a good amount of money and on a monthly bases just to access the internet and have a good time doing so, based on that fact are heavily investing in networks and technology to get that connection to every home and business in the country; what if people based on giving these circumstances stop subscribing to internet services or resorting to other options like subscription sharing, how can these ISP’s justify their investment and effort to improve services when the Government is not helping at all.
swa: Tusiangalie intaneti kama tu njia kuu ya mawasiliano bali pia kama bidhaa, watu majumbani wanalipia kiwango kizuri cha pesa kila mwezi ili kuweza kutumia intaneti, na wanaridhia kufanya hivyo, kwa kuzingatia ukweli kwamba yanawekeza vikubwa kwenye mitandao na teknolojia ili kuweza kufikisha huduma zao majumbani na kwenye biashara mbalimbali nchini, je itakuwaje, katika mazingira haya, kama watu wataacha kulipia huduma za intaneti au wakichukua hatua nyingine kama vile kuchangia malipo, watoa huduma za kuunganisha intaneti watawezaje kutetea uwekezaji na juhudi zao za kuboresha huduma wakati serikali haisaidii lolote.

eng: Funaki says:
swa: Funaki anasema:

eng: We have been blessed with a mind of our own that we can use to make decisions and distinguish between right and wrong.
swa: Tumebarikiwa na akili za kuweza kufanya maamuzi na kutofautisha kati ya mema na mabaya.

eng: I don’t need anyone from outside coming and telling me what is right and what is wrong.
swa: Sihitaji mtu wa nje aje kuniambia ni lipi jema na lipi baya.

eng: Yagoob makes a similar point - and has a request for the Minister:
swa: Yagoob anasisitiza jambo hilo hilo - na ana ombi kwa Waziri:

eng: People should be free to do whatever they want online, whether it’s safe or sinful is really none of the government’s business... We are not cattle that need to herded and shown the ‘righteous’ or better put ‘the government’s’ way.
swa: Watu lazima wawe huru kufanya watakalo mtandaoni, ikiwa ni jambo salama au ikiwa ni dhambi hiyo si biashara ya serikali… Sisi siyo ng'ombe ambao wanahitaji kuswagwa na kuonyeshwa njia ya 'za haki' au njia 'za serikali'.

eng: Your Excellency, blocking these websites will in the short and long term continue to undermine the freedoms given to the Bahraini people through the constitution and depriving useful websites from the residents of Bahrain for no reason whatsoever.
swa: Mheshimiwa, kuzuia tovuti hizi kutaendelea kudhalilisha uhuru waliopewa watu wa Bahrain kupitia katiba, kadhalika kuwanyima watu wa Bahrain tovuti za maana bila sababu yoyote.

eng: Please reconsider and lift the ban off these websites and let us as a people grow more knowledgeable, educated and inspired…
swa: Tafadhali fikiri tena na uondoe vizuizi vilivyowekwa kwenye tovuti hizo na uturuhusu sisi kama wananchi kuongeza maarifa, elimu na kuhamasishwa…

eng: Hussain Yousif says:
swa: Hussain Yousif anasema:

eng: I would like to thank the government for reminding us that Bahrain is still a new version of a third word country where freedom is something to talk about but not to experience.
swa: Ninapenda kuishukuru serikali kwa kutukumbusha kwamba Bahrain ni toleo jipya la nchi za dunia ya tatu ambako uhuru ni jambo linaloongelewa tu lakini halipo.

eng: Silly Bahraini Girl is scathing:
swa: Bloga Silly Bahraini Girl anachachafya:

eng: This isn't yet another move to curtail my freedom of expression as I am free to say and write what I want, not that anyone will listen to me.
swa: Hii siyo hatua nyingine ya kukinza uhuru wangu wa kujieleza kwani niko huru kusema na kuandika ninachotaka, hata yeyote hatanisikiliza.

eng: What I am not free to do is surf the Internet as I please, because I am a child in the eyes of the authorities - a child who should be told what I am allowed and not allowed to read.
swa: Kitu ambacho niko huru kufanya ni kuperuzi mtandao wa intaneti kama ninavyotaka, kwa kuwa mimi ni mtoto kwenye macho ya mamlaka - mtoto ambaye lazima aambiwe anachoruhusiwa na asichoruhusiwa kusoma.

eng: And since no one is listening, I would like to thank the authorities for blocking access to all those websites and would like to request it to block access to the entire Internet as frankly, we have no use with it.
swa: Na kwa kuwa hakuna anayenisikiliza, ningependa kuwashukuru watawala kwa kuzizuia tovuti zote hizo na ningependa kuwaomba waufunge mtandao mzima wa intaneti, kwani hatuna manufaa nao.

eng: Sous, a Swedish woman living in Bahrain, is furious:
swa: Sous, mwanamke wa Kiswidi anayeishi Bahrain, ana hasira:

eng: THIS IS INSANE!
swa: HUU NI WEHU!

eng: IMMENSLY INSANE!!
swa: WEHU MKUBWA!!

eng: I CAN’T BLOODY BREATHE!
swa: SIWEZI KUPUMUA!

eng: THIS IS INSANE!
swa: HUU NI WEHU!

eng: Suad wonders: ماذا استفاد المواطن أو الدولة من قرارات الحجب غير تراجع سمعة البحرين ومسيرتها الاصلاحية وانعدام الشفافية وانتهاك حرية التعبير وإرجاعنا الي عصور التخلف والظلام؟ Don't officials think of the negative side effects of their decisions and on the importance they give to sites which have no value or standing in society.
swa: Suad anajiuliza: Je maofisa hawafikirii madhara hasi yatakayotokana na uamuzi wao na umuhimu wanaozipa tovuti ambazo hazina thamani wala nafasi katika jamii.

eng: Don't they think that more people would want to access those sites now that everything which is illegal becomes more desirable?
swa: Je hawafikirii kwamba watu wengi zaidi watataka kuzifikia tovuti hizo hivi sasa kwani vyote ambavyo ni haramu hutamaniwa zaidi?

eng: What did the citizen and the nation benefit from those bans except for the tarnishing of Bahrain's reputation and its reform progress, its lack of transparency, its aggression against freedom of expression and our return to the dark ages of backwardness?
swa: Wananchi na taifa wamefaidika vipi na kufungwa kwa tovuti hizo isipokuwa kutia doa sifa ya Bahrain kwenye maendeleo ya mageuzi, kutokuwa kwake na uwazi, mabavu yake dhidi ya uhuru wa kujieleza na kurejea kwenye enzi za giza?

eng: Mohammed Zainal is in disbelief:
swa: Mohammed Zainal yuko katika hali ya kutoamini:

eng: It is sad, seriously its not funny, my previous post was about how technology is evolving and how people are using it to develop new applications everyday, changing the media landscape, inspiring people with the web2.0 ++ tools and elements …
swa: Inasikitisha, na haichekeshi, makala yangu iliyopita ilihusu jinsi gani teknolojia inavyoendelea na jinsi watu wanavyoitumia ili kuendeleza matumizi mapya kila siku, wanavyobadilisha namna za kupashana habari, wakiwahamasisha watu kwa kutumia zana za mtandao

eng: Is this what our “Age of Engage” ought to be?
swa: Je hii ndio "zama yetu ya kukutana" inavyopaswa kuwa?

eng: Again, I see no technical benefit from the ban and while I don't agree with the explosive sectarian situation, I accept that what is happening is a result of real people in crisis and immersed in sectarianism.
swa: Ni kweli kuwa kuna majukwaa ya kikabila mtandaoni ambayo yanapaswa kufungwa lakini ni lazima nikubali kwamba majukwaa ya kwenye mtandao yaliyo kwenye upande mwingine wa kisiasa/kidini hayakufungwa na yanaendelea kufanya kazi usiku na mchana yakirusha matusi na kutishia machafuko.

eng: What is happening on the forums reflects, to a large extent, the opinions of a large sector of our society.
swa: Kinachoendelea katika majukwaa ya kwenye mtandao kinaonyesha, kwa kiwango kikubwa, maoni ya walio wengi katika jamii yetu.

eng: And the political solution remains not in the hand of the Minister of Information or anyone else
swa: Na suluhisho la kisiasa halipo katika mikono ya Waziri wa habari au mwingine yeyote

eng: Hayat questions how the decision has been made: I believe that blocking those websites is primitive and backward and breaks the rights of freedom of expression and access to information.
swa: Hayat anahoji jinsi ya uamuzi ulivyofanywa: Ninaamini kuwa kuzuiwa kwa tovuti ni uamuzi duni na unavunja haki ya uhuru wa kujieleza na kupata habari.

eng: There is no democracy without freedom of expression...and no constitutional democracy which blocks websites...and it is not right to ban those sites through administrative orders which are arbitrary and which are taken by members of the executive authority, the judiciary and National Security Apparatus...It is not correct for these authorities to intertwine and work together and if they do...where is the separation between the different branches?
swa: Hakuna demokrasi bila ya uhuru wa kujieleza… na hakuna demokrasi ya kikatiba inayozuia tovuti… na si haki kufunga tovuti kupitia amri za kiholela za serikali ambazo hupitishwa na mamlaka ya serikali, mamlaka ya sheria na usalama wa taifa… si sahihi kwa mamlaka haya kuingiliana na kufanya kazi pamoja kama wanavyofanya… kuna utofautishaji upi kati ya matawi ya mamlaka haya?

eng: Khalid says: I believe the that judiciary is the only legal authority which can make decisions on whether or not to ban any website
swa: Khalid anasema: Ninaamini kwamba mamlaka ya sheria ndiyo mamlaka pekee yanayoweza kufanya uamuzi ama wa kufunga au kutofunga tovuti

eng: Qassim Ahmed has an idea: ...the Bahraini authorities want to block the Internet to make people cry over what was blocked, so that when they once again open up the sites for porn, violence and downloading movies and proxies as well as others...then people will say: "Freedom is now back again!"
swa: Qassim Ahmed ana fikira: … mamlaka ya bahrain yanataka kuzuia mtandao wa intaneti ili watu walilie kile walichozuiwa, ili kwamba wakiruhusu tena tovuti za ngono, unyama na za kuangalia filamu na tovuti vivuli pamoja na nyinginezo… watu watasema: "Uhuru umerejea tena!"

eng: In another post, Ammaro has decided he's figured out what's really going on:
swa: Katika ujumbe mwingine, Ammaro ameng'amua ni nini hasa kinachoendelea:

eng: Remember the Matrix?
swa: Je unakumbuka matrix?

eng: Remember how the whole world you lived in, which you believed was real, was in fact completely made up?
swa: Unakumbuka jinsi katika dunia yote unamoishi, ambayo uliamini ni ya kweli, ilikuwa katika ukweli halisi, ni ya kutengenezwa?

eng: Just a mirage?
swa: Ni mauzauza tu?

eng: That's probably what the internet is in Bahrain.
swa: Hivyo ndivyo pengine mtandao wa intaneti ulivyo nchini Bahrain.

eng: The internet was all a mirage created by the Bahrain government, to let you think that you're connecting to the outside world, when in reality we are kept very isolated from everything and everyone else.
swa: Intaneti ilikuwa ni mauzauza yaliyotengenezwa na serikali ya Bahrain, ili kukufanya ufikirie kuwa ulikuwa unawasiliana na dunia iliyoko nje, wakati katika ukweli halisi ulikuwa umetengwa na kila kitu, na watu wengine wote.

eng: All the sites you've ever visited were set up by creative individuals in the Ministry of Information; every single one.
swa: Kila tovuti uliyoitembelea ilitengenezwa na watu wa Wizara ya Habari; kila moja.

eng: There's a guy who writes the CNN website, and makes up the world news, another guy who writes the BBC website.
swa: Kuna jamaa anayeandika kwenye tovuti ya CNN, anayetunga habari za ulimwengu, na kuna jamaa mwingine anayeandika tovuti ya BBC.

eng: It's sort of obvious that they're sitting next to each other when doing this; the news is almost exactly the same on both sites... We've been living a lie.
swa: Ni dhahiri kuwa wanakaa pamoja wakati wanafanya hivyo; habari zinafanana sana katika tovuti hizi mbili… Tumekuwa tukiishi katika uongo.

eng: The new website bans aren't really websites being 'blocked'.
swa: Tovuti za habari zinazofungwa si tovuti za kweli na 'hazifungwi".

eng: It's actually a side effect from the Global Credit Crunch, where the Ministry has had to fire a large number of employees because of a shortage of funds, and couldn't sustain as many websites as it used to.
swa: Ukweli ni kwamba haya ni madhara ya hali mbaya ya kiuchumi ulimwenguni, na wizara imelazimika kuwafukuza kazi idadi kubwa ya wafanyakazi kwa sababu ya upungufu wa fedha, haikuweza kuhudumia tovuti nyingi kama ilivyokuwa awali.

eng: Therefore the ban.
swa: Kwa hiyo, zimefungwa.

eng: United States Secretary of State Hillary Clinton arrived in Indonesia last Wednesday.
swa: Katibu wa Mambo ya Nje wa Marekani Hillary Clinton aliwasili nchini Indonesia Jumatano iliyopita.

eng: She affirmed “Indonesia’s role in handling global problems, including terrorism, protectionism, climate change and the economic crisis.”
swa: Alitilia mkazo "jukumu la Indonesia katika kudhibiti matatizo ya dunia, yanayojumuisha ugaidi, uchumi wa kujihami, mabadiliko ya hali ya hewa(kuongezeka kwa joto) na matatizo ya kiuchumi."

eng: Indonesia is the largest Muslim nation in the world and the third largest democracy.
swa: Indonesia ndio taifa kubwa la Kiislamu duniani na nchi ya tatu kwa ukubwa kati ya zile zinazoongozwa kidemokrasia.

eng: Aside from meeting the leaders of Indonesia, Clinton found the time to visit a slum community in Jakarta.
swa: Pamoja na kukutana na viongozi wa Indonesia, Clinton alipata muda wa kutembelea makazi ya watu masikini mjini Jakarta.

eng: She also appeared in a teen-oriented TV show.
swa: Kadhalika alitokea kwenye kipindi cha televisheni cha vijana.

eng: Everything Indonesia believes Clinton's visit to Indonesia starts a new era in American foreign policy:
swa: Bloga Everything Indonesia anaamini kuwa ziara ya Clinton nchini Indonesia inafungua zama mpya ya sera ya nje ya Marekani:

eng: Secretary of State Hillary Clinton's visit to Indonesia starts a new era in American foreign policy.
swa: Ziara ya katibu wa Mambo ya Nje wa Marekani Clinton nchini Indonesia inafungua zama mpya za sera ya nje ya Marekani.

eng: A lot less unilateral arrogance, a lot more inclusiveness and so-called smart power.
swa: Sera iliyopungua dharau, inayojumuisha zaidi kama inavyoitwa nguvu-zenye-akili.

eng: Mbak Rita observes that Clinton looks younger today:
swa: Bloga Mbak Rita amegundua kwamba Clinton anaonekana kijana sana leo:

eng: I really think that she looks younger and more goodlooking, maybe it was because of her constant smile she gave during her visit here...Some people on some boring TV talkshow mentioned previously that Jakarta is a little overreacted with her visit. 	kwa kweli nafikiri anaonekana kijana na mrembo, pengine inatokana na tabasamu lake alilotoa wakati wa ziara yake hapa… Watu wengine katika kipindi cha maongezi cha televisheni nilichokitaja kabla walisema kwamba watu wa Jakarta walijawa jazba za bure kuhusu ziara yake.
I am glad that I was wrong about that."
swa: Nafarijika kuwa nilikosea."

eng: Devi Girsang was surprised about Jakarta’s traffic on the day Clinton arrived:
swa: Devi Girsang alishangazwa na hali ya barabarani siku aliyowasili Clinton:

eng: As a Jakartan who used to stuck in traffic, I tend to be panicky if the streets are quiet and deserted look-alike.
swa: Kama mkazi wa Jakarta niliyozoea kukwama kwenye foleni za magari, huwa nafadhaika kama barabara zikiwa tulivu na zenye watu pungufu.

eng: There are only two things popped in my mind in that case; there's a bomb terror or rampages.
swa: Ni mambo mawili yaliyoingia akilini mwangu; kuna vitisho vya mabomu au ghasia.

eng: Remember 1998 Jakarta riots or 2003 Marriott Hotel bombing?
swa: Unakumbuka machafuko ya Jakarta ya mwaka 1998 au shambulio la Hoteli ya Marriot la mwaka 2003?

eng: Then you must know what I mean Around 2 PM today, it turned out to be US Secretary of States Hillary Clinton's arrival in Jakarta that stopped the traffic!
swa: Umeshahamu namaanisha nini Majira ya saa 8 za mchana leo, iliondokea kuwa ni kuwasili kwa Katibu wa Mambo ya Nje wa Marekani mjini Jakarta ndio kulikosimamisha magari.

eng: Lucky for me, there's still battery power remained on my digital camera to take a few snapshots.
swa: Bahati yangu nilikuwa bado nina mawe kwenye kamera yangu ya kidijitali nikaweza kupiga picha kadhaa.

eng: Therry, in a comment, wonders if the US sent a fake Clinton:
swa: Katika safu ya maoni, Therry, anajiuliza kama Marekani ilimtuma Clinton wa uongo:

eng: I saw the speech Hillary made on television and I don't know whether it's just me but that woman doesn't look exactly like Hillary.
swa: Niliangalia hotuba aliyoitoa Clinton kwenye televisheni na sina hakika kama ni mimi tu, lakini yule mwanamke hafanani na Hillary.
