eng: The world stood silent as cries for help went unheeded.
swa: Ulimwengu ulikaa kimya wakati ambapo vilio vilipaazwa pasipo kuitikiwa.

eng: Please join us in lighting a candle in memory of those whose lives were taken and in hope for a future of peace, justice, and true reconciliation.
swa: Tafadhali unganeni nasi katika tukio la kuwasha mishumaa kwa kumbukumbu ya wale walioporwa maisha yao na kwa matumaini ya mustakabali uliojaa amani, haki na maelewano ya kweli.

eng: In succesive posts, Negrita posted a video for the campaign Candles for Rwanda, and the song 'Never Again' written and recorded in commemoration of the Genocide.
swa: Katika makala mfululizo, Negrita, alituma mtandaoni picha ya video ya kampeni ya Mishumaa kwa Rwanda, ambayo iliambatana na wimbo 'Hali hii isijirudie tena kamwe' uliotungwa na kuimbwa kwa ajili ya kumbukumbu ya Mauaji ya Kimbari.

eng: The song was composed by Rwanda's gospel singer Jean Paul Samputu in Kinyanrwanda, but its choruses are sung in different languages (English, French, Swahili, Kirundi and Kiganda) by various popular regional musicians.
swa: Wimbo huo ulitungwa na mwimbaji wa nyimbo za Injili wa Rwanda, Jean Paul Samputu. Ulitungwa kwa lugha ya Kinyarwanda, lakini viitikio vilikuwa katika lugha tofauti (Kiingereza, Kifaransa, Kiswahili, Kirundi na Kiganda) na uliimbwa na wanamuziki wengi maarufu kutoka eneo la Afrika ya Mashariki.

eng: Pictures of children victims of genocide at the Kigali Memorial Center (Photo by Elia Varela Serra)
swa: Picha za watoto wahanga wa mauaji ya Kimbari katika Kituo cha Kumbukumbu cha Kigali (Picha na Elia Varela Serra).

eng: Martin Leach, the head of the DFID (British Department for International Development) in Rwanda attended the ceremonies in Nyanza, which he describes in his blog:
swa: Martin Leach, ambaye ni mkuu wa Idara ya Uingereza ya Maendeleo ya Kimataifa (DFID) nchini Rwanda alishiriki katika kumbukumbu zilizofanyika Nyanza, na anaelezea kwenye blogu yake:

eng: Hundreds of people trudged up the long hill to Nyanza, many of them wearing something purple, a neckscarf, a wrap, even a purple wristband.
swa: Mamia ya watu walitembea polepole kwa huzuni kubwa kupitia njia ndefu iliyoelekea kwenye kilima kwenda Nyanza, wengi wao walivaa chochote chenye rangi ya zambarau, kitambaa cha begani, kanga, au utepe wa mkononi.

eng: The colour purple is the colour of mourning in Rwanda and yesterday, 7th April, was the 15th Anniversary of the Genocide.
swa: Rangi ya zambarau ni alama ya maombolezo nchini Rwanda na jana tarehe 7 Aprili, ilikuwa siku ya kuadhimisha Kumbukumbu ya miaka 15 tangu Mauaji ya Kimbari.

eng: At the top of the hill I joined the large crowd at the Commemoration Ceremony.
swa: Pale juu ya kilima niliungana na umati mkubwa katika Maadhimisho ya Kumbukumbu.

eng: Wedged between two ambassadors, I heard heart breaking accounts from survivors of the massacre which took place on the site where we were seated, with no one to protect them against the brutal attacks of the militia.
swa: Nikiwa nimebanwa katikati ya mabalozi wawili, nilisikiliza maelezo binafsi ya watu walionusurika katika mauaji yaliyotendeka mahali hapo tulipoketi, na hakukuwa na hata mtu mmoja wa kuwatetea dhidi ya mashambulizi ya kinyama ya wanamgambo.

eng: But it was the young people who moved me most: girls dressed in purple and white reciting poems in Kinyarwandan about the need to take courage for the future in spite of the sorrow and grief, and a youth choir with 'Never Again' emblazoned on their T-shirts and headbands, singing with emotion about the importance of never forgetting the genocide.
swa: Lakini ilikuwa ni vijana ndiyo walionigusa zaidi: wasichana waliovalia mavazi ya rangi ya zambarau na nyeupe walighani mashairi kwa lugha ya Kinyarwanda, hasa wakihimiza umuhimu wa kuvaa ushujaa kwa ajili ya siku za baadaye licha ya huzuni kubw, na pia kwaya ya vijana waliovalia Tii-sheti zenye maneno 'Hali hii isijirudie tena kamwe', maneno hayo pia yalikuwa kwenye vitambaa walivyojifunga kichwani, huku wakiimba kwa hisia kubwa juu ya umuhimu wa kutosahau kamwe mauaji ya kimbari.

eng: And it was emotional. Even the Government Ministers were shedding tears, remembering their experiences and lost loved ones.
swa: Na kwa kweli lilikuwa tukio la kuamsha hisia kali kwani hata mawaziri wa serikali waliokuwepo walitiririkwa na machozi, wakikumbuka yaliyotokea kipindi hicho na hasa kwa kuwapoteza watu waliowapenda.

eng: I can't imagine it - one million people killed in 100 days: as the Lady Mayor of Kigali said 'an unspeakable evil' had gripped the country.
swa: Nashindwa kuiaminisha akili yangu - yaani watu milioni moja kuuwawa katika muda wa siku 100: kama alivyosema mwanamama Meya wa Kigali, akiongeza 'mwovu asiyesemekana' aliinyakuwa nchi.

eng: Michael Abramowitz of the US Holocaust Memorial Museum was in Kigali for the ceremonies.
swa: Michael Abramowitz anayetoka katika Makumbusho ya Kumbukumbu ya Mauaji ya huko Marekani naye alikuwepo Kigali kwa ajili ya tukio hili.

eng: In the blog World is Witness, Abramovitz recounts the testimony of a genocide survivor called Venuste that moved the audience with his story during the ceremony:
swa: Katika blogu inayoitwa World is Witness, Abramovitz anasimulia ushuhuda wa aliyenusurika kwenye mauaji ya kimbari aliyeitwa Venuste, ambapo ushuhuda wake uliigusa mno hadhira iliyokuwepo wakati wa maadhimisho hayo:

eng: Venuste, who looked to be in his 50s or 60s, with a dignified bearing, proceeded to tell the hushed crowd how his family and neighbors decided to take refuge at the nearby L’Ecole Technique Officielle, thinking that might be a safe refuge because of the small contingent of Belgian United Nations soldiers stationed there.
swa: Venuste, aliyeonekana kuwa na umri wa kati ya miaka 50 hadi 60, huku akitembea kwa mwendo wa madaha, aliusimulia umati uliojazana jinsi gani familia yake na majirani zao walivyoamua kukimbilia katika kituo kilichokuwa karibu cha L’Ecole Technique Officielle, wakitumaini kwamba hapo pangekuwa na usalama kwao kwa kuwa kulikuwa na kikosi kidogo cha Wabelgiji chini ya Umaja wa Mataifa.

eng: But four days later, to their great shock, the small U.N. force departed, telling those gathered on the school grounds that “gendarmes” would rescue them.
swa: Lakini siku nne baadaye, kwa mshangao mkubwa wa kutisha, kikosi hicho kidogo cha Umoja wa Mataifa, kiliondolewa, huku wakiawaambia watu waliokimbilia pale kwamba "maaskari polisi" (gendarmes) wangekuja kuwaokoa.

eng: The U.N. soldiers ignored their desperate pleas not to leave them at the mercy of a menacing crowd of government soldiers and armed militia that surrounded them outside the gates of the school.
swa: Askari wa Umoja wa Mataifa walipuuzia kubembeleza kwao ili wasiondoke na kuwaacha mikononi mwa makundi ya askari wa serikali na wanamgambo wenye silaha waliokuwa wamewazingira nje ya milango ya shule walipokimbilia.

eng: After the departure of the last U.N. soldier, Venuste and some 5,000 others who were gathered on the school grounds were forced to walk a jeering gauntlet of Hutu militiamen, soldiers and civilians wielding machetes, guns and other weapons.
swa: Mara tu baada ya askari wa Umoja wa Mataifa kuondoka, Venuste na watu wengine wapatao 5000 waliokuwa kwenye viwanja vya shule hiyo walilazimishwa kutembea chini ya ulinzi wa wanamgambo wa Kihutu waliokuwa wakiwadhihaki, pia walikuwepo askari na raia waliobeba mapanga, bunduki na silaha nyingine.

eng: Some of those who survived described it as a “death walk.”
swa: Baadhi ya wale waliookoka kufa walieleza matembezi hayo kama "Matembezi ya kifo".

eng: Venuste lost his right arm, hacked off by one of the tormentors.
swa: Venuste alipoteza mkono wake wa kulia ambao ulikatwa na mmoja wa watesaji.

eng: The walkers came to this unremarkable hill, where they were encircled by a gang of killers and set upon with grenades, machetes and clubs.
swa: Mateka hao walitembea mpaka kwenye kilele cha kilima hiki ambapo walizingirwa na genge la wauaji na kisha kushambuliwa kwa mabomu, mapanga na marungu.

eng: Within a few hours, Venuste said, “We were lying in pools of blood.”
swa: Katika muda mfupi tu, anasimulia Venuste, "Tulikuwa tumelala kwenye madimbwi ya damu".

eng: Of the 5,000 or so who sought refuge from the U.N. near here, roughly 100 survived, according to Venuste.
swa: Kati ya watu wapatao 5000 walioomba ulinzi kutoka kikosi cha Umoja wa Mataifa, ni takribani 100 tu ndiyo walionusurika kufa, ndivyo alivyosimulia Venuste.

eng: He lived only because he laid still under dead bodies, overlooked by the killers searching the carnage for signs of life.
swa: Yeye anasema alipona kwa sababu alijilaza kimya chini ya maiti kadhaa, wakati huo huo wauaji waliendelea kuzagaa pale ili kuona kama kuna aliyekuwa hai bado.

eng: Impressed by the economic development of Rwanda, Abramowitz sees no traces of the atrocities experienced 15 years ago:
swa: Akiguswa na maendeleo ya uchumi yaliyofanywa na nchi ya Rwanda, Abramowitz haoni kama kuna dalili yoyote inayoonyesha kuwa kuliwahi kutokea mauaji ya kimbari miaka 15 iliyopita:

eng: As I first-time visitor to Rwanda, it’s hard not to be mystified by the mismatch between the ferocious events of just 15 years ago and apparent calm and prosperity in Rwanda, which aspires to be the hub of an economically vibrant East Africa.
swa: Kama mtu ambaye ndiyo mara yake ya kwanza kwenda Rwanda, ni vigumu mtu kutoshangazwa na kutoshabihiana kati ya matukio ya kutisha sana yaliyotokea miaka 15 iliyopita na hali inayoonekana kuwa ya utulivu mkubwa na ustawi wa aina yake inayotawala sasa nchini humo, ambapo nchi hiyo inaonekana kuwa kiini cha uchumi unashamiri kwa kasi wa Afrika ya Mashariki.

eng: As we drove out of town to one of the churches where you can still see the skulls and belongings of murdered Tutsi, we passed by workers digging up ditches on the side of the road to lay down new fiber optic lines.
swa: Tulipokuwa tukisafiri kwa gari kutoka katikati ya mji kwenda katika moja ya makanisa ambapo mtu unaweza kuona mafuvu na mali za Watutsi waliouwawa, tuliwapita wafanyakazi fulani waliokuwa wakichimba mitaro kandokando ya barabara maalumu kwa ajili ya kutandaza nyaya za mawasiliano ya Intaneti.

eng: A newcomer thinks: How can this beautiful country, routinely described by Africa hands as one of the better functioning countries on the continent, have experienced such savagery?
swa: Kwa mtu mgeni ni rahisi kujiuliza: Inawezekanaje kwamba nchi hii ya kupendeza, ambayo mara nyingi watu wengi barani Afrika huichukulia kama ya kupigiwa mfano kwa namna yake bora ya uendeshaji, inakuwaje kwamba iliingia katika unyama huo mkubwa usiosimulika?

eng: Ugandan fishermen pulling bodies out of Lake Victoria that had traveled hundreds of miles by river from Rwanda (Photo by Dave Blumenkrantz, used under a Creative Commons license)
swa: Wavuvi wa Uganda wakiopoa miili kutoka Ziwa Victoria baada ya kusafirishwa mamia ya maili kutoka Rwanda (Picha na Dave Blumenkrantz, una ruhusa ya kutumia chini ya utaratibu wa leseni za Ubunifu wa Pamoja)

eng: Colette Braeckman , a Belgian journalist and author of several books about Central Africa, was also present at the anniversary ceremony in Kigali of which she writes:
swa: Colette Braeckman , ambaye ni mwandishi wa habari wa Ubelgiji na mwandishi wa vitabu kadhaa kuhusu Afrika ya Kati, naye pia alikuwepo kwenye maadhimisho hayo kule Kigali, naye anaandika:

eng: This post is part of the Global Voices Special Coverage on Indian Elections 2009
swa: Makala hii ni moja ya Makala Maalum za Global Voices Kuhusu Uchaguzi Mkuu wa India wa 2009.

eng: World’s largest democracy, India, will hold general elections starting in a few weeks from now.
swa: Demokrasi kubwa zaidi duniani, India, itafanya uchaguzi mkuu utakaoanza katika wiki chache zijazo kutoka sasa.

eng: In a country of more than a billion people, general election is nothing sort of a “make or break” time for many interest groups, political parties and the common folk.
swa: Katika nchi yenye watu zaidi ya bilioni, uchaguzi mkuu ni wakati wa “kujenga au kuvunja” kwa makundi yenye maslahi, kwa vyama vya siasa na kwa watu wa kawaida.

eng: For how their life will be for next five years is decided on that day.
swa: Kutokana na ukweli kwamba maisha yao kwa miaka mitano ijayo yataamuliwa siku ya uchaguzi.

eng: A rainbow of colours of rural Indian women gathered as volunteers for social mobilisation and development in their villages.
swa: Upinde wa rangi za akina mama wa vijijini waliokusanyika kama wahamasishaji wa kujitolea kwenye vijiji vyao.

eng: Image by Flickr user mckaysavage and used under a creative commons license.
swa: Picha na Mtumiaji wa Flickr Mckaysavage na imetumika chini ya hatimiliki huru za jamii.

eng: Indian women, who have long been denied their rightful position at home, at work and at the helm of power also have a huge stake in upcoming elections.
swa: Wanawake wa India, ambao kwa muda mrefu wamekuwa wakinyimwa nafasi yao ya haki majumbani, kazini na katika hatamu za uongozi wana dau kubwa katika uchaguzi ujao.

eng: Female literacy in the country (based on 2001 census) is at 53.63% compared to 75.26% for male, but Indian women are not completely shut off from the political process.
swa: Wanawake wanaojua kusoma na kuandika nchini (kwa mujibu wa sensa ya mwaka 2001) ni asilimia 53 tu ikilinganishwa na asilimia 75 kwa wanaume, hata hivyo wanawake wa India hawajatengwa kabisa kutoka katika mchakato wa kisiasa.

eng: Level of their participation is increasing and a some prominent parties have women as leaders.
swa: Kiwango cha ushiriki wao kinaongezeka na vyama vingine mashuhuri vina viongozi wanawake.

eng: Although more and more women are becoming aware of their voting rights and participating at local level politics, a report suggests that this year less women are likely to be elected to the country’s parliament.
swa: Japokuwa wanawake wengi wanaanza kuwa na ufahamu wa haki zao za kupiga kura na wanashiriki katika siasa kwenye ngazi za chini, ripoti hii inaeleza kwamba inavyoelekea mwaka huu ni wanawake wachache zaidi watakaochaguliwa katika bunge la nchi.

eng: “The introduction of the Women’s Reservations Bill in 14th Lok Sabha has prompted more women asking for tickets from major parties this time, but the selection of candidates by the latter reveals that electoral politics in India still remains a male preserve.
swa: “Kuwasilishwa kwa Muswada wa Viti Maalum vya Wanawake katika kikao cha 14 cha Baraza la Wawakilishi (Lok Sabha) kumewafanya wanawake waanze kuwania tiketi kwenye vyama vikubwa, lakini uteuzi wa wagombea kwenye vyama hivyo unaonyesha kwamba siasa za uchaguzi nchini India bado ni hifadhi ya wanaume.

eng: Including party Chief Sonia Gandhi, only nine women figure in the list of 90-and odd Lok Sabha candidates announced by the Congress so far and the BJP list of 232 candidates, contains only 21 women.
swa: Pamoja na mkuu wa chama Sonia Gandhi, ni wanawake tisa tu katika orodha ya wagombea 90-na-ushee wa Baraza la Wawakilishi waliotangazwa na chama cha Congress mpaka hivi sasa na katika orodha ya wagombea 232 wa chama cha BJP kuna wanawake 21 tu.

eng: The Left Front, which has accused both the BJP and the Congress of lacking political will on the women’s reservation bill, has fielded only two women out of 42 candidates in its bastion West Bengal, down from five it had fielded in 2004 elections.”
swa: Chama cha Mrengo wa Kushoto, ambacho kimevishutumu vyama vya BJP na Congress kwa kutokuwa na nia ya kisiasa kuhusiana na sheria ya viti maalum vya wanawake, imewateua wagombea wawili tu wanawake kati ya wagombea 42 kwenye ngome yao ya jimbo la Bengali ya Mashariki, idadi hii ni ya chini zaidi ya wale watano ambao kiliwasimasha katika uchaguzi wa mwaka 2004."

eng: Samiya Anwar, a female voter, writes about upcoming elections focusing on her hometown of Hyderabad:
swa: Samiya Anwar, mpiga kura wa kike, anaandika kuhusu uchaguzi ujao, na anauangalia kwa makini mji anaotoka wa Hyderabad:

eng: “There are more women issues than men to be addressed.
swa:
Kuna masuala mengi yanayowahusu wanawake zaidi ya yale yanayowahusu wanaume ambayo yanapaswa kuangaliwa.
Isn’t it?	Au siyo?
First, it is the safety of women in society she dwells in. 	Kwanza, ni usalama wa wanawake katika jamii wanamoishi.
Many women in the Old City (of Hyderabad) do not trust police.	Wanawake wengi katika mji mkongwe (wa Hyderabad) hawawaamini polisi.
They go through domestic and physical violence and don’t complain.	Wanapitia mateso ya ndani ya nyumba pamoja na kupigwa bila ya kulalamika.
We need a system where women can approach cops fearlessly.	Tunahitaji mfumo ambao utawafanya wanawake waweze kuongea na mapolisi bila ya woga.
The issues like water shortage, frequent power cuts, road accidents and physical abuse of women at workplace should be given first thought.” 	Masuala kama vile ukosefu wa maji, kukatika kwa umeme kila mara, ajali za barabarani na unyanyasaji dhidi ya wanawake makazini ni lazima yapewe kipaumbele.

eng: Question of caste is a big one during election time in India.
swa: Utamaduni wa matabaka ni suala kubwa wakati wa uchaguzi nchini India.

eng: As someone said “Indians don’t caste their vote but vote their caste”, the politics of dividing people based on their caste and exploiting them as “vote banks” is a common practice.
swa: Kama alivyowahi kusema mtu mmoja “Wahindi hawapigi kura bali wanapigia kura matabaka”, siasa za kuwatenganisha watu kwa kadri ya matabaka yao na kuwatumia kama “benki za kura” ni utaratibu wa kawaida.

eng: Joshua Meah blogging about caste system and of women in Indian politics at Washington Note says:
swa: Joshua Meah akiblogu kuhusu utamaduni huo wa matabaka na wanawake katika siasa kwenye blogu ya Washington Note anasema:

eng: “India n. (perhaps it has potential as an adjective as well?): the land where the opposite of everything is always at least a little bit true.
swa:
Nchini India ambako kinyume cha kila kitu huwa ndio ukweli.
This is the same country that has produced a great number of enormously powerful female politicians long before America even honestly broached the subject - Indira Gandhi being the case in point.	Hii ni nchi ambayo imetengeneza wanawake kadhaa wanasiasa wenye nguvu kubwa, kitambo kirefu kabla hata Marekani haijaanza kulitaja somo hilo – Indira Gandhi ni mfano mmojawapo.
Even now, the head of Uttar Pradesh, India's most populous state and the home to 130 million people, is headed by a woman of dalit origin (India's lowest caste). 	Hata hivi sasa, Mkuu wa Uttar Pradesh, Jimbo lenye watu wengi zaidi nchini India na makazi ya watu milioni 130 linaongozwa na mwanamke anayetokea kwenye tabaka la Dalit (tabaka la chini kabisa).
The progress of India's democracy in terms of its movement toward social equality has in some ways been as breathtaking as it is heartbreaking.”	Maendeleo ya demokrasi nchini India katika maana ya kuelekea usawa wa jamii kwa namna fulani yamekuwa ni ya kuvutisha pumzi na kadhalika kukatisha tamaa.

eng: Vinod Sharmaalso discusses “vote bank” through an imaginary exchange of words between three powerful women- Mayawati (Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh) who is a “dalit” (lower caste), Maneka Gandhi (Indira Gandhi’s daughter-in-law) and prominent social and animal rights activist, and Sonia Gandhi (Maneka’s estranged sister-in-law) and Congress party supreme.
swa: Vinod Sharma pia analijadili suala la “benki ya kura” kwa kutumia majadiliano ya kubuni kati ya wanawake watatu wenye nguvu – Mayawati (Waziri Mkuu wa jimbo la Uttar Pradesh) ambaye ni wa tabaka la “Dalit” (tabaka la chini), Maneka Gandhi (mkwe wa Indira Gandhi) ambaye ni mwanaharakati za haki jamii, haki za binaadamu na za wanyama na Sonia Gandhi (wifi aliyetengwa wa Maneka) ambaye pia ni mkuu wa chama cha Congress.

eng: Here is an excerpt:
swa: Ifuatayo ni nukuu:

eng: “Sonia: The Congress party is a national party with a glorious history.
swa: “Sonia: Chama cha Congress ni chama cha kitaifa chenye historia tukufu.

eng: Mayawati: And no future.
swa: Mayawati: Na kisicho na mustakabali.

eng: Sonia: Don't say that.
swa: Sonia: Usiseme hivyo.

eng: Please.
swa: Tafadhali.

eng: It hurts.
swa: Inaumiza.

eng: We are confident of coming back to power on our own.
swa: Tunao uwezo wa kuchukua madaraka tena peke yetu (bila kuingia kwenye mseto na vyama vingine).

eng: Mayawati: Really?
swa: Mayawati: Kweli?

eng: Look, I don't care whether anyone is from the Gandhi family or a raja or maharaja.
swa: Angalia, Sijali ikiwa kuna mtu katokea kwenye familia ya Gandhi au raja au maharaja.

eng: If you or your son threaten my vote bank in any manner, I will put you both behind bars.”
swa: Kama wewe au mwanao akitishia benki yangu ya kura kwa njia yoyote ile, nitawatupa nyote jela.”

eng: Every year millions of Muslims converge to Mecca to perform Hajj (pilgrimage), one of the five pillars of Islam.
swa: Kila mwaka mamilioni ya Waislamu husafiri kwenda Maka kuhiji, moja ya nguzo tano za Uislamu.

eng: Is this year's Hajj season being threatened by the A/H1N1 or Swine Flu virus?
swa: Je, msimu wa hija ya mwaka huu utatishiwa na homa ya mafua ya nguruwe?

eng: Bloggers commenting on the region weigh in.
swa: Wanablogu wanayo maoni ya kusema.

eng: At CrossRoads Arabia, John Burgess explains:
swa: Kwenye blogu ya CrossRoads Arabia, John Burgess anaeleza:

eng: A Saudi researcher in Shariah law find that there is precedent to ban Umrah pilgrims (those who undertake the non-obligatory, ‘lesser’ pilgrimage) who come from areas beset with the A/H1N1 or swine flu virus.
swa: Mtafiti wa Kisaudi katika sheria za Kiislamu (Sharia) amegundua kuwa kuna uwezekano wa kuwazuia baadhi ya mahujaji (wale ambao walishahiji kabla yaani, mahujaji wa ‘kurudia’) hasa wanaotoka maeneo ambayo kwa sasa yanatishiwa na mlipuko wa mafua ya nguruwe.

eng: I suspect that this opinion is being floated now in anticipation of the Haj, which will take place in late November.
swa: Nina hisi kwamba wazo hili linakuja sasa kwa sababu ya Haji ambayo itafanyika mwishoni mwa mwezi Novemba.

eng: The Haj is obligatory, in that every Muslim is required to perform the pilgrimage at least once in his/her life, if feasible.
swa: Hija ni wajibu wa msingi, ambao kila Mwislamu hutakiwa kuutimiza angalau mara moja katika maisha yake, inapowezekana.

eng: Similar concerns were raised a few years ago, when bird flu (H5N1) was threatening.
swa: Hali kama hii ilijitokeza miaka michache iliyopita, ambapo homa ya mafua ya ndege (H5N1) ilikuwa tishio.

eng: One Saudi scholar called for Haj to be canceled if there were a severe outbreak, but that proposal was shot down by others.
swa: Msomi mmoja wa Kisaudi alitoa wito wa kuifuta Hija ikiwa mlipuko ungekuwa mkubwa zaidi, lakini pendekezo hilo lilizimwa na wenzake.

eng: The argument was that Haj had never been canceled on public health grounds and that to do so would be counter to Islam.
swa: Hoja ilikuwa kwamba Hija haijawahi kufutwa kwa minajili tu ya kiafya na kwamba kufanya hivyo kungekuwa kuukiuka Uislamu.

eng: Rather, those who are ill are morally obliged to not perform Haj.
swa: Badala yake, wale walio wagonjwa, kimaadili hutakiwa kutokuitimiza hija yao.

eng: Communicable diseases and Haj are historical companions.
swa: Magonjwa yaambukizwayo yana historia ndefu na Hija.

eng: There are many records of outbreaks of disease, from plague to cholera, killing thousands in Mecca, Madinah, and Jeddah over the years.
swa: Zipo kumbukumbu nyingi za milipuko ya magonjwa kama kipindupindu na maafa ya maelfu huko Maka, Madina na Jedah kwa miaka mingi sasa.

eng: Only toward the end of the 19th C. did strictly enforced quarantines work to stop the spread of diseases out of the region, back to the homes of the pilgrims.
swa: Ni kuelekea karne ya 19 ndipo ambapo sheria za kutenga wagonjwa zilianza kutumika ili kukomesha ueneaji wa magonjwa katika eneo hilo takatifu, hadi manyumbani mwa mahujaji.

eng: Quarantines and strict enforcement of medical screening can protect pilgrims and that might be enough.
swa: Sheria hizo pamoja na kutiliwa mkazo kwa mchujo wa kiafya kwa mahujaji unaelezwa kuweza kusaidia kuwalinda mahujaji.

eng: Only time will tell.
swa: Muda utahitajika kuona ikiwa hili linawezekana.

eng: Swine flu, as bird flu before it, may turn out to be a non-issue.
swa: Mafua ya nguruwe, kama ilivyokuwa kwa mafua ya ndege hapo awali, yanaweza kuja kuwa jambo lisilo na uzito unaoonekana hivi sasa.

eng: If it does not, however, it good that people are starting to think about it now.
swa: Isipokuwa hivyo, hata hivyo, ni vyema watu wakaanza kulitafakari kuanzia sasa.

eng: The Middle East Institute's Editor's Blog adds:
swa: Blogu ya Middle East Institute's Editor's Blog inaongeza:

eng: This is getting stranger and stranger.
swa: Jambo hili linazidi kuwa jipya kila uchao.

eng: The Grand Mufti of Egypt is suggesting Muslim scholars issue a collective fatwa to postpone the hajj due to swine flu.
swa: Mufti mkuu wa Misri anapendeza wanazuoni wa Kiislamu kutangaza fatwa kuahirisha Hija kwa sababu ya mafua ya nguruwe.

eng: Arabic version is here.
swa: Fatwa yenyewe inapatikana hapa kwa Kiarabu.

eng: Keep in mind — I know I keep repeating it — there have been no cases in Egypt.
swa: Tilia maanani –ninajua na naendelea kurudia hili –hapajawahi kuwapo suala kama hili katika Misri.

eng: In fact, according to WHO's rundown as of yesterday, the only cases confirmed in the entire Middle East are in Israel (seven cases).
swa: Kusema kweli, kwa mujibu wa Shirika la Afya Duniani (WHO), maambukizo yaliyothibitishwa katika Mashariki ya Kati yote ni Israel (wagonjwa saba).

eng: And WHO says, "WHO is not recommending travel restrictions related to the outbreak of the influenza A(H1N1) virus."
swa: Na Shirika hilo la Afya Duniani (WHO) linasema “ Shirika halijashauri kusitishwa kwa safari kwa sababu ya mlipuko wa virusi vya mafua ya nguruwe.”

eng: Oh, yes, and another thing: the hajj isn't until November.
swa: Ndio, na suala jingine: Hija haijafika, ni mpaka mwezi wa Novemba.

eng: Am I missing something here?
swa: Hivi kuna kitu nitakuwa nakosea hapa?

eng: Has the hajj ever been postponed for health reasons, in all of Islamic history?
swa: Je, katika historia ya Uislamu, hivi imewahi kutokea Hija ikaahirishwa kwa sababu tu za kiafya?

eng: I don't know, but I expect you'd need at least one infected person to justify it.
swa: Sijui, lakini ninatarajia kuwa tungehitaji walau mgonjwa mmoja ili kuhalalisha uamuzi huu.

eng: (Not only are there no cases in the Middle East, except Israel, but none in Indonesia, Malaysia, Pakistan — well, anywhere Muslim.)
swa: (Si tu kwamba hakuna taarifa za ugonjwa Mashariki ya Kati, isipokuwa Israel, lakini pia hakuna mgonjwa yoyote Indonesia, Malayasia, Pakistani – ndio hata kokote waliko Waislamu)

eng: The government of Sril Lanka announced via state media and SMS today (Monday, May 18, 2009) afternoon that the leader of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), Vellupillai Prabhakaran, is dead.
swa: Serikali ya Sri Lanka imetangaza kwa kupitia vyombo vya habari vya taifa pamoja na ujumbe wa simu za mkononi mchana leo (Jumatatu, 18 Mei, 2009) kwamba kiongozi wa Kundi linalotaka kujitenga la Wa-Tamil, the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), Vellupillai Prabhakaran, amefariki.

eng: News media are reporting that Prabhakaran, who was at the helm of one of the world's most violent rebellions, was killed by rocket grenade while in a van with the head of the LTTE's navy, Soosai, and the LTTE intelligence chief, Pottu Amman.
swa: Vyombo vya habari vinaripoti kwamba Prabhakaran, ambaye alikuwa kwenye uongozi wa moja ya maasi ya kikatili zaidi duniani, aliuwawa kwa kombora wakati alipokuwa kwenye basi dogo na mkuu wa jeshi la majini la LTTE, Soosai, pamoja na mkuu wa upelelezi, Pottu Amman.

eng: The body of the rebel leader will undergo DNA tests to confirm identity.
swa: Mwili wa kiongozi huyo wa waasi utafanyiwa uchunguzi zaidi wa DNA ili kuthibitisha utambuzi wake.

eng: About 250 members of the Tamil Tigers were reportedly killed in the final surge of fighting in the country's 26-year-old war.
swa: Kadri ya wanachama 250 wa waasi wa Chui wa Kitamil waliuwawa kwenye mapambano ya mwisho ya vita vilivyodumu kwa miaka 26.

eng: Obituaries of Prabhakaran note that he was a hero to some and a ruthless killer to others.
swa: Salamu za rambirambi zinaashiria kwamba alikuwa shujaa kwa baadhi ya watu kadhalika alichukuliwa kama muuaji katili kwa wengine.

eng: The BBC writes, "To his followers, Vellupillai Prabhakaran was a freedom fighter struggling for Tamil emancipation.
swa: Chombo cha habari cha BBC kimeandika, “kwa wafuasi wake, Vellupillai Prabhakaran alikuwa ni mpigania uhuru kwa ajili ya ukombozi wa Watamil.

eng: To his adversaries he was a secretive megalomaniac with a complete disregard for human life."
swa: Kwa maadui zake alikuwa ni mtu msiri anayependa kutawala na asiyejali kabisa maisha ya wanaadamu wengine.”

eng: The Hindu in India says, "A 'freedom fighter' for his supporters and a dreaded terrorist for others, Prabhakaran was wanted by Interpol and many other organisations since 1990 for terrorism, murder and organised crime." Long before the world was aware of Osama Bin Laden or Al-Qaeda, Prabhakaran started to use a new method of guerrilla warfare, suicide bombing.
swa: Gazeti la The Hindu nchini India linasema, Mpigania uhuru kwa wafuasi wake na gaidi wa kuogopwa kwa wengine, Prabhakaran alikuwa anatafutwa na Chombo cha Polisi cha Kimataifa, Interpol, pamoja na mashirika mengine mengi tangu mwaka 1990 kwa makosa ya ugaidi, mauaji na jinai. “kabla dunia haijamsikia Osama Bin Laden au Al-Qaeda, Prabhakaran alianza kutumia mbinu mpya ya vita, mabomu ya kujilipua kwa kujitoa muhanga.

eng: This cover story on Tehelka magazine reveals a lot about this war lord.
swa: Makala hii kwenye gazeti la Tehelka inatoa mwanga kuhusu kiongozi huyu wa vita.

eng: The Blogger of Beyond Skin explains it this way:
swa: Mwanablogu wa Beyond the Skin anafafanua hivi:

eng: First reaction: WHAAA!
swa: Hisia za mwanzo: WHAAA!

eng: Second reaction: Now what?
swa: Hisia zilizofuata: Sasa nini?

eng: After 26 years of fighting, after displacing and killing hundreds of thousands, after silencing those who dissent against both the government and the LTTE through assassinations, torture and disappearance, what now of the Tamil people?
swa: Baada ya miaka 26 ya mapambano, baada ya kuua mamia ya maelfu, baada ya kuwanyamazisha wale walioipinga serikali na waasi wa LTTE kwa kuwaua, mateso na watu kupotea, sasa itakuwaje kwa watu wa Tamil?

eng: United National Party organizer Ajith P. Perera wrote in his own obituary for Prabhakaran in his blog, Dare to be different: "He was a terrorist, no doubt, but Prabhakaran deserves an obituary, even in a language he barely understood," Perera wrote.
swa: Kada wa chama cha United National Party Ajith P. Perera ameandika salamu za rambirambi kwa Prabhakaran katika blogu yake, akitaka kuwa tofauti na wengine: “alikuwa muuaji, bila ya shaka, lakini Prabhakaran anastahili salamu za rambirambi, hata kama ni katika lugha ambayo alikuwa haielewi,”

eng: Did he achieve anything worthwhile for his community?
swa: Je alifanikisha lolote la maana kwa ajili ya jamii yake?

eng: The answer is a big NO.
swa: Jibu ni HAPANA.

eng: Ethnic (Jaffna) Tamils are worse off than they were in 1970s.
swa: Watamil wazawa (Jaffna) wako pabaya zaidi ya pale walipokuwa katika miaka ya 1970.

eng: More than half of the Tamil population has already left for good. Thousands of Tamil families had to live with eternal grief of losing one or more family members.
swa: Zaidi ya nusu ya Watamil wamehama moja kwa moja.

eng: Ethnic Tamils, the largest minority in Sri Lanka then, has now reduced to the pathetic third place after Muslims and Indian Tamils.
swa: Watamil Wazawa, kundi kubwa la walio wachache nchini Sri Lanka wakati ule, hivi sasa wapungua na kuchukua nafasi ya tatu baada ya Waislamu na Watamil wanaotokea India.

eng: Jaffna, the second most advanced city in Sri Lanka, with its famous education system, is now far behind.
swa: Jaffna, jiji la pili kimaendeleo nchini Sri Lanka, na mfumo wake maarufu wa elimu, hivi sasa iko nyuma sana.

eng: As a community Tamils, at least the unfortunate ones to still remain, have moved ten or twenty years backward.
swa: Kama jamii, Watamil, wale walio na bahati mbaya ya kubaki, wamerudi nyuma miaka kumi au ishirini.

eng: They were termed as terrorists across the world.
swa: Walitambuliwa kama magaidi duniani kote.

eng: North and East have become more and more economically dependent on Colombo.
swa: Kaskazini na mashariki pamekuwa tegemezi kwa Colombo kiuchumi.

eng: At least for the next few years, till a UNP government implements a political solution, they will be remotely controlled from Colombo.
swa: Kwa miaka michache ijayo, mpaka hapo serikali ya UNP itakapotekeleza sera zake kisiasa, watakuwa wanaendeshwa kutokea Colombo.

eng: All thanks to Prabhakaran.
swa: Yote haya ni shukrani kwa Prabhakaran.

eng: Sri Lankan Tamil activist and former LTTE member Nirmala Rajasingam explains in an opinion piece in The Independent that her sister was murdered by the LTTE 20 years ago.
swa: Mwanaharakati wa Kitamil na mwanachama wa zamani wa waasi wa LTTE Nirmala Rajasingam anafafanua katika makala kwenye gazeti la Independent kwamba dada yake aliuwawa na waasi wa LTTE miaka 20 iliyopita.

eng: For that reason, the news of the demise of the LTTE's top leadership – which ordered her killing and the killings of many other Tamil dissenters – brings overwhelming relief.
swa: Kwa sababu hiyo, habari za maangamizi ya uongozi wa juu wa LTTE – ambao uliamuru kuuwawa kwake pamoja na Watamil wengine wengi waliowapinga – kumeleta ahueni kubwa sana.

eng: The war and carnage has at last stopped and the insistent bloodletting of Tamil dissent is now over.
swa: Vita na ukatili hatimaye vimesitishwa na kumwagika kwa damu za Watamil kumefikia mwisho.

eng: But she cautions:
swa: Hata hivyo anaonya:

eng: The continued refusal of full access to humanitarian agencies does not allay suspicions about the government's intentions toward the refugees and the LTTE cadres who have surrendered.
swa: Pingamizi linaloendela la kutoruhusu mashirika ya misaada ya kibinaadamu kuingia halisaidii kupunguza mashaka juu ya nia ya serikali kwa wakimbizi na makada wa LTTE ambao wamesalimu amri.

eng: The last three years have seen a large number of abductions, extrajudicial killings and disappearances, almost exclusively targeting the Tamil community as the government of Sri Lanka relentlessly pursued its military campaign.
swa: Katika miaka mitatu iliyopita kumekuwa na matukio mengi ya utekaji, mauaji na kutoweka kwa watu, kulikolenga jamii ya Watamil wakati ambapo serikali ya Sri Lanka ilipokuwa ikitekeleza kampeni yake ya kijeshi.

eng: The militarisation of state and society has been able to suppress dissent in the south, even mounting attacks on journalists.
swa: Kushamiri kwa uongozi wa kijeshi kitaifa na kwenye jamii kumefanikisha ukandamizwaji wa maoni mbadala kusini mwa nchi, na kumewezesha mashambulizi dhidi ya wanahabari.

eng: We wait to see whether the government will reverse this downward spiral in democratic governance.
swa: Tunasuburi ili tuone kama serikali itageuza mwelekeo huu mbaya wa utawala wa kidemokrasi.

eng: Blogger and columnist Indi Samarajiva used Twitter to discuss the death of Prabhakaran while he was traveling.
swa: Akiwa safarini, mwanablogu na mwandishi wa makala Indi Sumarajiya ametumia zana ya Twita kujadili kifo cha Prabhakaran.

eng: He posted messages to his Twitter page on Monday afternoon:
swa: Alituma jumbe kadhaa kwenye ukurasa wake wa Twita jumatatu mchana:

eng: is in Hambantota.
swa: Nipo Hambantota.

eng: Fire crackers.
swa: Fataki.

eng: Seems Prabhakaran is dead.
swa: Pengine Prabhakan amefariki.

eng: No glory in death, but, well, good.
swa: Hakuna utukufu kwenye kifo, lakini, ni vyema.

eng: May Sri Lanka rebuild #fb
swa: Tunaomba Sri Lanka ijijenge upya#fb

eng: they're lighting firecrackers literally meters from the gas cylinder depot.
swa: Wanawasha baruti karibu kabisa na ghala ya mitungi ya gesi.

eng: The fishmongers are yelling to get back to work.
swa: Wauza samaki wanahimizwa kurejea kazini.

eng: Hambantota town is mostly Muslim, back to business.
swa: Mji wa Hambantota una Waislamu wengi, kazi inaendelea.

eng: Flag convoys thru Ambalantota.
swa: Misafara ya bendera katika Ambalantota.

eng: War's over, Prabha's dead.
swa: Vita vimekwisha, Prabha amekufa.

eng: Long live Sri Lanka #fb
swa: Idumu Sri Lanka #fb

eng: Prahalathan KK, a blogger in Chennai, India, says that rejoicing in Prabhakaran's death is a diservice to the civilians killed in order to make the LTTE's defeat possible.
swa: Mwanablogu aliyeko mjini Chennai, India, Prahalathan KK, anasema kuwa kushangilia kifo cha Prabhakaran ni utovu wa heshima kwa raia waliouwawa katika harakati za kuwezesha maangamizi ya LTTE.

eng:
So Prabhakaran the Terrorist has been killed. 	“Kwa hiyo Prabhakaran gaidi ameuwawa.
Happy?	Mmefurahi?
Rejoicing?	Mnashangilia?
Ever thought of the thousands of innocent Tamils who were slaughtered by the indiscriminate use of artillery and chemical weapons by the Sri Lankan army during the Genocidal war?
swa: Je mmeweza kuwafikiria maelfu ya Watamil wasio na hatia ambao waliuwawa kutokana na matumizi ya jumla ya makombora na silaha za sumu yaliyofanywa na jeshi la Sri Lanka wakati wa vita hivi vya kimbari?

eng: According to the Ministry of Defence website, the almost 150,000 civilians who have fled the war zone in less than a month are being cared for by the army.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa tovuti ya Wizara ya ulinzi, karibu ya raia 150,000 ambao walikimbia uwanja wa vita wanatunzwa na na jeshi.

eng: But The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the only independent organization that has had access to civilians in the conflict zone, called the situation "nothing short of catastrophic."
swa: Lakini Kamati ya Kimataifa ya Hilali Nyekundu (ICRC), shirika huru pekee ambalo liliweza kuwafikia raia katika eneo la mgogoro, liliita hali iliyokuwepo kama “si jingine zaidi ya balaa.”

eng: Today, they in a news release that the they have not had access to civilians in the north-east for nine days.
swa: Leo hii, wamesema katika taarifa yao kwa vyombo vya habari kwamba hawajaweza kuwafikia raia walioko kaskazini-mashariki kwa siku tisa.

eng: “This is all the more urgent since no humanitarian aid has reached those who need it for over a week,” said director of operations, Pierre Krähenbühl.
swa: “Hii ni dharura kwani hakuna msaada wowote wa kibinaadamu ambo umeweza kuwafikia wale wanaouhitaji kwa zaidi ya wiki moja’” alisema mkurugenzi wa mipango, Pierre Krähenbühl.

eng: Selvarasa Pathmanathan, head of the LTTE’s International Diplomatic Relations, released a statement on Sunday announcing that the Tigers will "silence our guns to save our people."
swa: Selvarasa Pathmanathan, mkuu wa kitengo cha Diplomasia cha LTTE, alitoa tamko Jumapili kuwa Chui “tutanyamazisha bunduki zetu ili kuwanusuru watu wetu.”

eng: He said that 3,000 civilians have died and 25,000 are injured.
swa: Alisema kuwa raia 3,000 walifariki na wengine 25,000 walijeruhiwa.

eng: Prominent South Asian diaspora blog Sepia Mutiny reports on continuing protests in Canada.
swa: Blogu maarufu ya Waasia wa Kusini Ughaibuni Sepia Mutiny inaripoti maandamano yanayoendelea nchini Kanada.

eng: In a post about a gathering in Winnipeg. Melvin writes:
swa: Katika makala inayohusu maandamano huko Winnipeg, Melvin anaandika:

eng: They held candles, signs, black flags and pictures of children whom they see as victims of the Sri Lankan government’s assault on civilians.
swa: Walibeba mishumaa, mabango, bendera nyeusi na picha za watotot ambao wanawachukulia kama waathirika wa mashambulizi ya serikali ya Sri Lanka dhidi ya raia.

eng: While people in Colombo and elsewhere celebrated the apparent end of the 25-year civil war, those at the vigil mourned the deaths of innocent people and wondered what, if anything, had been solved. “It doesn’t solve anything,” Singarajah said.
swa: Wakati ambapo watu jijini Colombo walikuwa wakisherehekea mwisho wa miaka 25 ya vita vya wenyewe kwa wenyewe, wale waliokuwa kwenye maandamano walikuwa wanaomboleza vifo vya raia wasio na hatia huku wakijiuliza, ni nini, kuma kuna chochote, kilichopatiwa ufumbuzi. “haijasuluhisha lolote,” alisema Singaraja.

eng: “People’s grievances aren’t going to be over.
swa: “Kero za wananchi hazitaisha.

eng: This government is so ruthless.
swa: Serikali ni katili mno.

eng: They don’t want to give us our rights.
swa: Hawataki kutupatia haki zetu.

eng: As long as that is the case, the problems will go on.”
swa: Na kama ni hivyo, matatizo yataendelea.”

eng: Protests have been ongoing in London, many parts of Canada and more recently in Australia.
swa: Maandamano yamekuwa yakiendelea jijini London, katika sehemu nyingi za Canada na hivi karibuni nchini Australia.

eng: But activist Rajasingam cautioned in Foreign Policy magazine that the Tamil diaspora has taken a misguided approach to its message:
swa: Mwanaharakati Rajasingham anaonya kwenye jarida la Foreign Policy kwamba Watamil walio ughaibuni wamechukulia vibaya ujumbe wake:

eng: As Sri Lanka's humanitarian crisis unfolds, the international community must make its message clear and forthright.
swa: Wakati mgogoro wa kibinaadamu unavyojitokeza nchini Sri Lanka, jumuia ya kimataifa inabidi itoe tamko wazi na la moja kwa moja.

eng: The Tigers and the diaspora that supports them have no claim as the "sole representation" of the Tamil people.
swa: Kwamba waasi na Watamil wanawaunga mkono ambao wanaishi ughaibuni hawana hati miliki ya kuwa “wawakili pekee” wa Watamil wote.

eng: Nor is secession a reasonable option.
swa: Na kujitenga siyo suluhisho pekee.

eng: Only this firm message will serve the cause of peace and democracy.
swa: Ni ujumbe huu imara pekee ambao utapelekea amani na demokrasia. Kwenye tovuti ya Moving Images, Moving People!

eng: At Moving Images, Moving People! blogger Nalaka Gunawardene says that he wants to believe that the war is truly over:
swa: Mwanablogu Nalaka Gunawardene anasema kuwa angependa kuamini, kwa hakika, kuwa vita vimekwisha:

eng: Sure, there is no independent verification – it has been a war without witnesses for the last few years.
swa: Hakuna vidhibitisho huru – vimekuwa ni vita visivyokuwa na shahidi kwa miaka michache iliyopita.

eng: But I am willing to take an unusual leap of faith if that’s what it takes to usher in the long-elusive peace.
swa: Lakini nipo tayari kuwa na imani isiyo ya kawaida, ikiwa kama ni hilo tu linalohitajika ili kukaribisha amani iliyotuchenga kwa muda mrefu.

eng: I will go to the ends of the earth, and suspend disbelief if I have to, in return for lasting and meaningful peace.
swa: Nitakwenda mpaka mwisho wa dunia, ili kusimamisha kutoamini kwangu, ili kupokea kurejea kwa amani na amani yenye maana.

eng: President Mahinda Rajapaksa is scheduled to address Parliament and the nation on Tuesday morning.
swa: Rais Mahinda Rajapaksa anategemewa kulihutubia Bunge na taifa jumanne asubuhi.

eng: Egyptians witnessed the most unexpected verdict in the history of their judiciary system: Billionaire Hesham Talaat Moustafa, along with his hired hitman Mohsen El Sokary, have both been sentenced to death for their roles in the murder of Lebanese singer Suzanne Tameem.
swa: Wamisri walishuhudia hukumu isiyotarajiwa katika historia ya vyombo vya sheria nchini humo: Bilionea Hesham Talaat Moustafa, pamoja na mamluki wake (mpiga risasi wa kukodi) Mohsen El Sokari wamehukumiwa adhabu ya kifo kutokana na kuhusika kwao katika mauaji ya mwimbaji wa Kilebanoni Suzanne Tameem.

eng: The gruesome murder took place in Dubai, UAE, and Thursday's sentence was met with shock and bewilderment as the blogosphere comes to terms with the verdict.
swa: Mauaji hayo ya kinyama yalitokea huko Dubai, UAE, na hukumu iliyotolewa Alhamisi imesababisha mshtuko na mshangao wakati wanablogu walipojaribu kukubaliana na yaliyotukia.

eng: Egyptian prolific blogger Zeinobia broke the news:
swa: Mwanablogu anayeandika sana wa Kimisri, Zeinobia alitangaza habari:

eng: On May 21, Judge Muhammadi Qunsuwa announced the case will be referred to Grand Mufti Ali Gomaa, the nation's highest religious official, who will rule on Moustafa's death sentence on June 25.
swa: Mnamo tarehe 21 Mei, Hakimu Muhammadi Qunsuwa alitangaza kuwa kesi hiyo itapelekwa kwa Mufti Mkuu Ali Gomaa, Kiongozi wa juu zaidi wa Kidini nchini humo, ambaye angetoa hukumu ya kifo kwa Moustafa siku ya tarehe 25 Juni.

eng: Shocking as it is to everyone, the verdict left the convicted in awe.
swa: Kama ilivyomstaajabisha kila mmoja, hukumu hiyo pia ilimuacha mshtakiwa akiwa na mshangao.

eng: Reactions varied outside the court house, but the majority of people saw that the punishment was fair for a man who abused his authority, influence and money, thinking that he was above the law.
swa: Maoni yalitofautiana nje ya jumba la mahakama, ambapo watu wengi waliiona ile adhabu ni stahiki kwa mtu ambaye aliyatumia mamlaka, ushawishi na pesa zake vibaya, akifikiri kwamba alikuwa yuko juu ya sheria.

eng: Reactions fluctuated, between approval and support to the verdict to sympathy and sadness.
swa: Maoni yalikuwa yakipishana, kati ya kukubali na kuiunga mkono ile hukumu na huruma pamoja na huzuni.

eng: Once the verdict was read, chaos erupted in court, with the families of Mohsen and Hesham screaming as well as the employees of the Talaat Moustafa Group, who couldn't believe what they heard.
swa: Baada ya kusomwa kwa hukumu, mushkeli ulizuka mahakamani, huku wanafamilia wa Mohsen na Hesham wakipiga mayowe kadhalika wafanyakazi wa kundi la Talaat Moustafa, ambao hawakuamini kile walichokisikia.

eng: Meanwhile, Hesham and Mohsen were completely silent.
swa: Wakati huo huo Hesham na Mohsen walikuwa kimya kabisa.

eng: Personally, I couldn't believe it because Hesham's crime was instigating murder while Mohsen was the one who killed.
swa: Binafsi, sikuamini kwa sababu kosa la Hisham lilikuwa ni kuchochea mauaji wakati Mohsen ndiye aliyeua.

eng: How can their punishment be the same?
swa: Iweje adhabu zao ziwe sawasawa?

eng: In some laws, the punishment is even more severe than that met to the criminal.
swa: Katika baadhi ya sheria, adhabu huwa kali zaidi kwa mchochezi kuliko kwa mtekelezaji.

eng: The Egyptian real-estate tycoon’s supporters on Facebook, reacted to the verdict on “Free Hesham Talaat Moustafa’ group as well.
swa: Wanaomuunga mkono mfanyabiashara huyu tajiri wa majengo nchini Misri kwenye huduma ya Facebook, waliijibu hukumu ile kwa kuanzisha kundi la “Muachieni Heshaam Talaat Moustafa.”

eng: Ashraf Elmanwaty said:
swa: Ashraf Elmanwaty alisema:

eng: I still have hope HTM will be free... This is an over reaction judgment
swa: Bado nina matumaini kuwa HTM ataachiwa huru… Hii ni hukumu iliyovuka mipaka

eng: While Miral El Ramlawy wrote:
swa: Wakati Miral El Ramlawy aliandika:

eng: 90% of Egyptians do NOT believe he did it and the court owes it to the Egyptians to announce what they based the verdict upon!!
swa: Asilimia 90 ya Wamisri hawaamini kuwa alifanya na mahakama inapaswa kuwaeleza Wamisri msingi wa hukumu hii!!!

eng: Phone calls that don't have any explicit message is NO PROOF...we are waiting for justification!
swa: Simu ambazo hazionyeshi ujumbe ulio wazi siyo USHAHIDI… tunasubiri ufafanuzi!

eng: After the shock, analysis took place.
swa: Baada ya mshtuko, uchambuzi ulianza kuchukua nafasi.

eng: Zeinobia explains:
swa: Zeinobia alifafanua:

eng: • when the judge says that that the papers of the convicted will be sent to the grand Mufti for consulting means in most situations that that convicted will face the death penalty.
swa: Ikiwa Hakimu anasema kuwa mafaili ya mkosefu yatapelekwa kwa Mufti Mkuu kwa ajili ya ushauri inamaanisha katika mazingira mengi kwamba mkosefu atakutana na adhabu ya kifo.

eng: The death penalty needs the opinion of the grand Mufti to support it from the religious point of view ,the Sharia point of view to fulfill justice.It is not everyday that you order the death of someone.
swa: Adhabu ya kifo inahitaji maoni ya Mufti Mkuu ili kuiunga mkono kutokana na mtazamo wa kidini, mtazamo wa Sharia ili kuitimiza hukumu. Siyo kila siku watu hutoa adhabu ya kifo kwa yeyote.

eng: • In most cases if not all of them the grand Mufti approves and supports the judge’s verdict.
swa: Katika kesi nyingi, kama siyo zote Mufti Mkuu hukubali na kuunga mkono hukumu ya hakimu.

eng: She then continues:
swa: Na anaendelea:

eng: • Second in case of Hisham and Sokary,the judge will announce the final verdict on the next 25th of June 2009 ,which is nearly about month and 5 days ,I believe it is a long period to stand in the death row.
swa: Pili katika kesi ya Hisham na Sokary, hakimu atatangaza hukumu ya mwisho tarehe 25 Juni 2009, karibu mwezi mmoja na siku 5, naamini ni muda mrefu kusubiri adhabu ya kifo.

eng: • Third when the judge announces the final verdict , the lawyers of the convicted will have the right to .
swa: Tatu, wakati ambapo hakimu atatangaza hukumu ya mwisho, mawakili wa mtuhumiwa watakuwa na haki ya kukata rufaa.

eng: So there might be a second round which is what we will figure out on June 25th.
swa: Kwa hiyo panaweza kuwa na duru la pili, jambo ambalo tutalifahamu siku ya tarehe 25 Juni.

eng: Meanwhile, there are questions and doubts about Hisham’s high profile real estate business.
swa: Wakati huo huo, kuna maswali na mashaka juu ya biashara ya majengo ya Hisham.

eng: The Mideast Institute Editor's blog reports:
swa: Blogu ya Middle East Intitute inaripoti:

eng: The Talaat Mustafa Group (TMG), a huge real estate conglomerate through which Mustafa made his billions, doesn't want any stockholders to worry just because the company's founder and namesake is under a death sentence.
swa: Kundi la Talaat Mustafa (TMG), ubia mkubwa wa biashara ya majengo ambao Mustafa alitengeneza mabilioni, hautaki wadau wahofu kwa sababu tu mwenye kampuni amehukumiwa adhabu ya kifo.

eng: A TMG official reassures investors:
swa: Kundi la TMG limewahakikishia wawekezaji:

eng: Sawaftah said that TMG’s corporate structure prevents “the absence of one individual” from affecting its activity
swa: Sawaftah alisema kwamba muundo wa kiufanisi wa TMG utakinga athari zitakazotokana na ‘kutokuwepo kwa mtu mmoja’.

eng: With the elections over and the incumbent president Bingu wa Mutharika sworn in for his second and last term, Malawian bloggers (Mabloga) are awed by two developments that went against the predictions of many, especially the punditry.
swa: Wakati uchaguzi umekwisha na rais aliye madarakani Bingu wa Mutharika ameshaapishwa kwa muhula wake wa pili na wa mwisho, wanablogu wa Malawi (mabloga) bado wanashangaa kuona maendeleo kinyume na utabiri wa wengi, haswa ule watalaamu wa mambo.

eng: First was the suggestion that the presidential contest would be very close.
swa: Utabiri wa kwanza ulikuwa kwamba ushindani ungelikuwa wa karibu sana.

eng: It wasn't.
swa: Haukuwa.

eng: Second was the perception that Malawians would once again vote on regional and ethnic lines.
swa: Pili kulikuwa na mtazamo kwamba Wamalawi wangepiga kura kwa kufuata mistari ya ukabila.

eng: They did not.
swa: Hawakufanya hivyo.

eng: Other fascinating aspects of the elections being discussed by the "Mabloga" include the role that Internet radio played in informing Diaspora Malawians on events as they unfolded, and what the new parliament might look like, what with a good number of the newly-elected members of parliament boasting university professorial and international civil service careers, long term PhDs, and other post-graduate qualifications.
swa: Masuala mengine ya uchaguzi ambayo yalikuwa yakijadiliwa na wanablogu au “Mabloga” yalijumuisha namna ambavyo redio za kwenye mtandao wa intaneti zingeweza kuwapasha Wamalawi waishio ughaibuni habari kama zinavyotokea, kadhalika jinsi bunge jipya litakavyokuwa, je nini watakachofanya wabunge wengi wapya ambao wana shahada za za uprofesa wa chuo kikuu pamoja na kazi za kimataifa, wenye shada za falsafa, kadhalika shahada nyingine za juu.

eng: The blog Chingwe's Hole reacts to both disproved predictions, then goes through a list of six aspects that make the May 2009 elections historic.
swa: Blogu ya Chingwe’s Hole inatoa maoni juu ya utabiri ambao haukutokea, kisha anachambua orodha ya mambo sita ambayo yameufanya uchaguzi wa mwezi Mei 2009 kuwa wa kihistoria.

eng: According to Chingwe's Hole, key structures of Malawi's institutions performed well.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Chingwe’s Hole, miundo mikuu ya taasisi za Malawi ilifanya kazi nzuri.

eng: And in marking the probable end of the political career of the 77 year-old leader of the Malawi Congress Party (MCP), John Tembo, these elections also ended the era of the nationalist generation that has ruled Malawi since 1964, a point also made by Paul Tiyambe Zeleza.
swa: Na pia kuhusu uwezekano wa mwisho wa shughuli za kisiasa kwa kiongozi wa chama cha Malawi Congress Party (MCP) mwenye umri wa miaka 77, Bwana John Tembo, uchaguzi huu pia ulihitimisha zama za viongozi wa kiuzalendo ambao wametawala Malawi kuanzia mwaka 1964, jambo ambalo Paul Tiyambe Zeleza pia ameling’amua.

eng: Tembo is reported to have already been put forward as the MCP's candidate in the next elections in 2014, according to Chris Banda on the Internet forum Malawitalk.
swa: Imedaiwa kwamba Bwana Tembo amependekezwa kuwa mgombea wa MCP katika uchaguzi ujao wa 2014, kwa mujibu wa Chris Banda kwenye mtandao wa Malawitalk.

eng: Chingwe's Hole's third aspect is that the voting pattern was driven by substantive matters of development, over personalities, and more poignantly for many bloggers as well, over ethnicity, Chingwe's Hole's fourth and fifth historical aspects of these elections.
swa: Suala la tatu analozungumzia Chingwe’s Hole ni kuwa namna ya upigaji kura ilisukumwa na masuala ya maendeleo dhidi ya wajihi wa wagombea, kadhalika dhidi ya ukabila. Suala la nne na la tano la kihistoria kuhusu uchaguzi huu kwa mujibu wa Chingwe’s Hole.

eng: The last aspect deals with how the punditry overestimated the strength of the main challenger, John Tembo, in his party's alliance with the United Democratic Front (UDF).
swa: Suala la mwisho linazungumzia jinsi wataalamu wa mambo walivyokisia vibaya uwezo wa mpinzani mkuu, John Tembo, haswa matokeo ya mseto alioingia na chama cha United Democratic Front (UDF).

eng: On this point Chingwe's Hole unleashes pointed criticism:
swa: Kuhusiana na suala hili Chingwe’s Hole anakosoa:

eng: And finally the elections have exposed the vacuity of some of the political punditry in Malawi.
swa: Na hatimaye uchaguzi umeonyesha utupu wa wataalamu wa mambo ya kisiasa nchini Malawi.

eng: Our most cited political pundits simply do not know what they are talking about... They kept analsising politics along the same old lines and seemed to base their views based only on whim srather than research and reflection.
swa: Wataalamu wetu wa kisiasa wanaonukuliwa sana hawajui ni nini wanachokizungumzia… wanashupalia kuchambua siasa kwa mitazamo ilei le ya kizamani na walionekana kusimamisha maono yao kwa hulka badala ya utafiti na tabaruku.

eng: Listening to our oft cited “political analysts” the coalition was supposed to be a formidable force; the elections would be a a”close call”; Bingu had made a fatal mistake chosing a Southern as running mate; the economy growth had not benefitted the majority etc . . .
swa: Ungewasikiliza ‘wataalamu wetu wa mambo ya siasa’ mseto wa vyamba vya upinzani ulipaswa kushinda kwa kishindo kikuu; uchaguzi ungekuwa wa ushundani wa karibu”. Bingu alifanya makosa makubwa kwa kumchagua mtu kutoka kusini kuwa mgombea mwenza; kukua kwa uchumi hakujawanufaisha Wamalawi n.k….

eng: As one of the pundits who predicted a strong showing for the MCP/UDF alliance and its candidate John Tembo, Boniface Dulani makes a confession mid-way through the vote counting when it is becoming apparent that Bingu wa Mutharika is defying expectations:
swa: Kama mmoja wa wachambuzi wa mambo amabye alitabiri ushindi wa MCP/UDF na mgombea wake John Tembo, Boniface Dulani anakiri wakati kura zilipokuwa bado zinahesabiwa wakati ilipodhihirika kwamba Bingu wa Mutharika anageuza yale yaliyokuwa yakitarajiwa:

eng: I must confess I did not expect the margin of victory that appears to be emerging from the election results as currently being announced.
swa: Lazima nikiri kuwa sikutegemea ushindi unaoanza kudhihirika kutokana na matokeo ya upigaji kura ambayo yanatangazwa hivi sasa.

eng: For all intents and purposes, Mutharika appears to be headed for a strong landslide performance.
swa: Kwa kila hali, inaonekana kuwa Mutharika anaelekea kuibuka na ushindi mithili maporomoko ya ardhi.

eng: While Bingu is performing strongly in the northern region as predicted, he has also performed just as strongly in the central region and the southern region.
swa: Wakati Bingu anafanya vizuri kwenye majimbo ya kaskazini kama ilivyotabiriwa, kadhalika nafanya vizuri katika majimbo ya kati na kusini.

eng: For Greenwell Matchaya, the incumbent's victory across the entire nation might be the beginning of the end of politics of ethnicity:
swa: Kwa mwanablogu Greenwell Matchaya, ushindi wa rais aliye madarakani nchini kote unaweza ukawa unaashiria mwisho wa siasa za kikabila:

eng: In the first place, the size of Bingu’s victory in the presence of a seemingly powerful opposition alliance is the first I have ever heard of in Africa.
swa: Kwanza, ushindi mkubwa wa Bingu mbele ya mseto wa nguvu wa upinzani ni ushindi wa kwanza kuusikia katika Afrika.

eng: Furthermore, the fact that there were no any reported cases of rigging, makes his win even more credible and even more and more wonderful.
swa: Zaidi ya hapo, ukweli kwamba hapakuwepo na tuhuma zozote za wizi wa kura, kunaufanya ushindi wake uwe wa haki na wa kuvutia.

eng: Bingu’s party, the DPP, won the presidential election with roughly 2,730,630 votes while the MCP/UDF alliance scooped circa 1,270,057, almost 200,000 votes below half of Bingu’s votes The strong message arising from these figures is that Bingu was voted into power by the entire nation, raising postulates about whether good leadership styles could obliterate the tribal cancer that many of us thought was out to consume our political and everyday lives.
swa: Chama cha Bingu, DDP, kimeshinda uchaguzi wa rais kwa kura takriban 2,730,630 wakati mseto wa MCP/UDF uliambulia kura 1,270,057, kura takriban 200, 000 pungufu ya zile za Bingu . Ujumbe mkuu unaotolewa na takwimu hizi ni kuwa Bingu alichaguliwa na taifa zima, na unazua wazo kuwa pengine uongozi bora unaweza kutokomeza sarakani ya ukabila ambayo wengi wetu tulidhani ilikuwa bado inazengea kutafuna siasa na maisha yetu.

eng: Clement Nyirenda also remarks on how the punditry got it wrong, and finds the voting pattern for the incumbent president's win epochal:
swa: Clement Nyirenda pia anatoa maoni kuhusu jinsi ambavyo wachambuzi wa mambo walivyokosea kutabiri, na anadhani kuwa upigaji kura uliompa ushindi rais aliye madarakani ulikuwa ni wa kihistoria:

eng: [. . . the pundits thought that John Tembo would garner more votes from the Southern region while beating Mutharika comprehensively in the Central Region, MCP’s stronghold.
swa: Wataalamu wa mambo walidhani kuwa john Tembo angepata kura nyingi kwenye majimbo ya kusini wakati angemshinda kabisa Mutharika kwenye majimbo ya kati, ambayo ni ngome ya MCP.

eng: Mutharika was expected to carry the day in the less populous Northern Region.
swa: Mutharika alitarajiwa kupata ushindi katika majimbo yenye watu wachache ya kaskazini.

eng: At the end of everything, the pundits have been proved wrong because Dr. Mutharika was proclaimed the winner with more than 6o% of the vote.
swa: Mwisho wa yote, wataalamu wa mambo wamedhihirika kuwa wamekosea kwa sababu Dr. Mutharika alitangazwa mshindi kwa zaidi ya asilimia 60 ya kura.

eng: Since the advent of multiparty democracy, I have never seen a presidential candidate getting votes from all the corners of the country like this.
swa: Tangu kuanza kwa mfumo wa demokrasi ya vyama vingi, sijawahi kuona kuona mgombea urais akipata kura kutokea kona zote za nchi kama hivi.

eng: And words of awe continue with Cryton Chikoko, who writes in the third person with the alias "Rambler":
swa: Na maneno ya kuhimidi yanaendelea na Cryton Chikoko ambaye anaandika katika nafsi ya tatu kwa kutumia jina la bandia la “Rambler”:

eng: Rambler has to confess he was not expecting Malawians to vote on merit.
swa: Rambler anakiri kuwa alikuwa hatarajii Wamalawi kupiga kura kwa kufuata sifa za mgombea.

eng: Admittedly Rambler wrongly thought that just like in the previous elections regionalism will rule the day.
swa: Rambler alifikiria kwa makosa kwamba kama livyokuwa katika chaguzi zilizopita siasa za majimbo zingetawala.

eng: The 2009 elections have come to him as a pleasant surprise.
swa: Uchaguzi wa 2009 umekuwa ni staajabu ya kuvutia.

eng: A fresh breath in our politics.
swa: Upepo mpya katika siasa yetu.

eng: Victor Kaonga pays tribute to the role that radio stations played in informing listeners of the results during the long breaks waiting for the Malawi Electoral Commission.
swa: Victor Kaonga anaienzi kazi ambayo idhaa za redio ziliifanya katika kuwapasha watu habari za matokeo wakati wa kusubiri Tume ya Uchaguzi ya Malawi (kutangaza matokeo).

eng: On Malawian Internet listserv forums, appreciation for the role of radio stations has especially focused on Zodiak Broadcasting Station, which broadcasts across Malawi, and recently started streaming live on the Internet.
swa: Katika mtandao wa Malawian Internet listserv, inashukuriwa kazi ambayo redio ilifanya hasa stesheni ya Zodiak Broadcasting, ambayo inatangaza katika Malawi yote, na hivi karibuni ilianza kutangaza moja moja kwenye mtandao wa intaneti.

eng: Listserv discussions have also widely debated what parliament might look like, given the large number of highly educated Malawians who have been elected to parliament, a topic also discussed by Chingwe's Hole.
swa: Listserv pia imejadili namna ambavyo bunge jipya litakavyokuwa, hasa ikizingatiwa kwamba kuna idadi kubwa ya wasomi wa kimalawi ambao wamechaguliwa kuingia bungeni, jambo ambalo pia lilijadiliwa na Chingwe’ Hole.

eng: On the Internet forum Nyasanet, the question of who will be chosen to fill cabinet posts is being debated on the basis of the intelligentsia voted into the legislature, which is being likened to an academic symposium.
swa: KAtika mtandao wa Nyasanet, swali la ni nani atakayechaguliwa kwenye baraza la mawaziri linajadiliwa katika msingi wa wasomi waliochaguliwa kuingia kwenye baraza la wawakilishi, ambalo linafananishwa na kongamano la wasomi.

eng: Blogger Kondwani Munthali has already provided his dream cabinet list.
swa: Mwanablogu Kondwani Munthali ameshatoa baraza lake la kufikirika la Mawaziri.

eng: This post is part of the Global Voices special coverage on the Indian Elections 2009
swa: Makala hii ni sehemu ya makala maalum za Global Voices za uchaguzi wa India 2009

eng: Election results are pouring in from all across the country and it is now clear that India has voted decisively for a stable government at the center, under the leadership of the Congress-led UPA.
swa: Matokeo ya Uchaguzi yanamiminika kutoka kila upande wa nchi na ni dhahiri kwamba India imepiga kura kwa kishindo ili kuchagua serikali imara ya mseto ya UPA, chini ya uongozi wa chama cha Congress.

eng: Dr. Manmohan Singh is going to be the Prime Minister for a second consecutive term.
swa: Dr Manmohan Singh atakuwa Waziri Mkuu kwa mara ya pili mfululizo.

eng: Even before all the results are in, just going by the trends, the BJP-led NDA alliance has publicly conceded defeat.
swa: Hata kabla matokeo hayajafika, kwa kuangalia tu mwelekeo, kundi la vyama vya mseto la NDA linaloongozwa na chama cha BJP limetangaza rasmi kushindwa kwake katika uchaguzi.

eng: The UPA Chairperson, Mrs. Sonia Gandhi congratulated the electorate on this mandate.
swa: Mwenyekiti wa UPA, Mama Sonia Gandhi aliwapongeza wapiga kura kwa kuwapa dhamana hii.

eng: At a press conference at her residence at 4.00pm IST, she said, "The people of India know what is good for them and they have made the right choice."
swa: Katika mkutano na waandishi wa habari uliofanyika nyumbani kwake saa 10 jioni Gandhi alisema, “Watu wa India wanafahamu ni nini kizuri kwao na wamefanya uteuzi sahihi.”

swa: Uchaguzi wa India (#indiavotes09) ndiyo mada inayoongoza kwenye huduma ya Twita leo hii.

eng: A few reactions from tweeters:
swa: Haya ni maoni ya baadhi ya watumiaji wa huduma hiyo:

swa: @jraghu – Wananchi wa India wametoa hukumu.

eng: Congress led UPA wins safe, free elections in largest free democracy.
swa: Ushindi wa mseto wa UPA unaoongozwa na chama cha Congress ni salama, uchaguzi huru katika demokrasia kubwa zaidi.

eng: Thank you, all #India #Indiavotes09
swa: Ahsanteni nyote Iindia # Indiavotes09

eng: @calamur - #indiavotes09 - Singh is King - Advani v/s PM. whining v/s strength. bitterness v/s vision.powerlust v/s duty.
swa: Utawala na si uana siasa. #indiavotes09 @calamur - #indiavotes09 – Singh ni mfalme – Advani dhidi ya PM.

eng: India chose well
swa: India imechagua vizuri.

eng: While there is jubilation in many quarters, there is gloom among the supporters of the BJP.
swa: Wakati kuna chereko chereko sehemu mbalimbali, pia kuna masikitiko kati ya wanaokiunga mkono chama cha BJP.

eng: Blogger Chakresh Mishra writes on his blog:
swa: Mwanablogu Chakresh Mishra anaandika katika blogu yake:

eng: my biggest sympathy is with BJP, which is the party I voted for.
swa: moyo wangu mkubwa wa huruma upo na BJP, chama ambacho nilikipigia kura.

eng: A nationalist party.
swa: Chama cha Kizalendo.

eng: It is a loss of face for BJP.
swa: Ni aibu kwa BJP.

eng: But friends, There are times in history of a nation when all seem lost and looks like wrong forces have won the final battle.
swa: Rafiki zangu, kuna wakati katika historia ya taifa ambapo kila kitu huonekana kimepotezwa na nguvu za kiza zimeshinda vita kuu ya mwisho.

eng: But dear friends, it is just a process, which goes on and on.
swa: Lakini rafiki zangu wapendwa, huu ni mchakato, ambao unaendelea.

eng: 5 years may be significant time period in life of a man, but in life of a nation (that too a nation like India) is just a flickr of eye.
swa: Miaka 5 inaweza ikawa ni muda wa muhimu sana katika maisha ya binaadamu, lakini katika maisha ya taifa (na taifa kama India) ni sawa tu na kupepeseka kwa jicho.

eng: The time after defeat is not for grief and blame-game.
swa: Kipindi cha baada ya kushindwa siyo wakati wa maasikitiko na kutupiana lawama.

eng: It is the time to introspect and start preparing to come out as winner in next battle.
swa: Ni wakati wa kujichunguza na kuanza kujipanga ili kuibuka kama mshindi katika vita ijayo.

eng: Though hopes are shattered and nightmares are prevailing, the dawn will surely come.
swa: Japokuwa matumaini yamevunjwavunjwa na majinamizi bado yanatawala, mapambazuko yatawadia tu.

eng: It is not the first black day of Indian history, we survived and fought back.
swa: Hii si siku ya kwanza ya giza katika historia ya India, tulijikusuru na kupigana.

eng: Let us do that again.
swa: Na tufanye hivyo tena.

eng: The day started across Honduras with news that President Mel Zelaya was arrested in his home by armed soldiers.
swa: Nchini Honduras siku ilianza na habari zinazosema kwamba Rais Mel Zelaya amekamatwa akiwa nyumbani kwake na wanajeshi wenye silaha.

eng: A referendum vote was scheduled for the same day, which was one that was opposed by the Supreme Court, the Armed Forces and the Honduran legislature.
swa: Kura ya maoni ilikuwa imepangwa kupigwa siku hiyo, kura hiyo ilikuwa inapingwa na mahakama ya juu, na majeshi ya nchi pamoja na baraza la wawakilishi.

eng: Days earlier, Zelaya had removed the head of the Armed Forces, General Romeo Vásquez Velásquez, which was followed by the resignation by other top military officials because they would not support the vote.
swa: Siku chache kabla, Zelaya alimuondoa madarakani mkuu wa majeshi, Jenerali Romeo Vasquez Velasquez, jambo ambalo lilifuatiwa na kujiuzulu kwa wanajeshi wengine wa vyeo vya juu kwa sababu hawakukubaliana na kura hiyo ya maoni.

eng: It was soon learned that Zelaya had been taken to Costa Rica, where he continued to call himself as the legal head of state.
swa: Mara baada ya hapo ilifahamika kuwa Zelaya amepelekwa nchini Costa Rica, ambako aliendelea kujiita kuwa yeye ndiye mkuu halali wa nchi.

eng: There was also a rumor that Zelaya had resigned.
swa: Kadhalika palikuwa na uvumi kuwa Zelaya amejiuzulu.

eng: However, the alleged letter turned out to be false notes Juan Carlos Rivera of Miradas de Halcón .
swa: Hata hivyo, barua inayodaiwa kueleza hivyo iligundulika kuwa ni ya uongo kama anavyobaini Juan Carlos Rivera wa Miradas de Halcón .

eng: The reaction from the blogosphere and twittosphere ranged from calling the situation a coup d'état to those who saw the move as the only way to stop Zelaya's controversial move.
swa: Maoni ya mwanzo katika ulimwengu wa blogu na ule wa Twita yalitofautiana kutokea yale yanayosema kwamba hali iliyopo ni sawa na mapinduzi ya kijeshi mpaka yale yanayosema kuwa ile ilikuwa ndio njia pekee ya kukomesha jitihada za Zelaya za kutaka kugombea urais kwa awamu nyingine tena.

eng: Photo by Roberto Brevé and used under a Creative Commons license. http://www.flickr.com/photos/breve/3668996322/
swa: Picha na Roberto Brevé na inatumika hapa chini ya hati miliki huria http://www.flickr.com/photos/breve/3668996322/

eng: There have been power outages in the capital city, as reported by Honduras Daily News, which speculates that it is an "attempt to limit the passing of information."
swa: Umeme umekuwa ukikatika-katika katika mji mkuu wa nchi, kama inavyoripotiwa na gazeti la Honduras Daily News ambalo linahisi kuwa kukatika huko kwa umeme ni moja ya “jitihada za kuzuia upashanaji habari.”

eng: However, information is currently being passed through social networking sites like Twitter and Blipea, which were very active throughout the day.
swa: Hata hivyo habari zimekuwa zikitoka kwa kutumia mitandao ya kijamii kama vile Twita na Blipea ambayo ilikuwa hai kutwa nzima.

swa: Hibueras, mmoja wa wanaomuunga mkono Zelaya aliandika :

eng: More than 100,000 people marched in Tehran on Monday in support of reformist presidential candidate, Mir Hussein Mousavi and his demands for an annulment of the election results that declared incumbent President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad the winner of the election on June 12.
swa: Zaidi ya watu 100,000 waliandamana mjini Tehran Jumatatu iliyopita ili kumuunga mkono mgombea urais mwanamageuzi, Mir Hussein Mousavi pamoja na madai yake ya kuataka kubatilishwa kwa matokeo ya uchaguzi ambayo yalimtangaza rais aliye madarakani Mahmoud Ahmadinejad kama mshindi katika uchaguzi wa tarehe 12 Juni.

eng: The march ended in bloodshed.
swa: Damu ilimwagika mwishoni mwa maandamano hayo.

eng: At least 7 people lost their lives.
swa: Watu wapatao 7 walipoteza maisha yao.

eng: According to a report on Britain's Channel 4 television, (aired in spite of a foreign reporting ban) a crowd threw rocks and set fire to a building that belonged to the pro-government Basij militia.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa ripoti kutoka idhaa ya televisheni ya Uingereza Channel 4 (iliyotangazwa bila kujali amri ya kuyazuia mashirika ya nje kutangaza habari) umati wa watu ulitupa mawe na kuchoma moto jingo linalomilikiwa na wanamgambo wanaoiunga mkono serikali, wajulikanao kama Basij.

eng: A helmeted militiaman on the roof fired his AK-47 rifle into the air before retreating from a shower of stones.
swa: Mwanamgambo aliyevalia kofia ya chuma aliyekuwa kwenye paa ya nyumba alipiga risasi hewani kabla ya kujificha ili kuepuka mvua ya mawe.

eng: On YouTube there is more citizen video of how this attack happened:
swa: Katika YouTube kuna video nyingi zinazoonyesha jinsi shambulio hilo lilivyotokea:

eng: The morning after this shooting, the staff of Rasool Akram Hospital in Tehran demonstrated against the killings.
swa: Asubuhi baada ya tukio hilo la kutupiana risasi, wafanyakazi wa hospitali ya Rasool Akram mjini Tehran waliandamana kupinga mauaji yaliyotokea.

eng: One demonstrator holds a placard that says: "8 martyrs"
swa: Muandamanaji mmoja alibeba bango linalosema “mashahidi 8”

eng: Shootings or repression have not stopped the protest movement, and thousands marched again in Tehran on Tuesday.
swa: Kupigwa risasi au kukandamizwa hakujazuia mwamko wa upinzani, na maelfu waliandamana tena mjini Tehran siku ya Jumanne.

eng: Demonstrations are growing in other cities too.
swa: Maandamano ya upinzani yanaongezeka katika miji mingine pia.

eng: In Shiraz, protesters shown in this video burned President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's photo.
swa: Katika mji wa Shiraz, wapinzani wanaoonyeshwa katika video hii waliichoma moto picha ya Ahmadinejad.

eng: Thousands of people demonstrated in Tehran, Mashhad and several other major cities in Iran to protest against President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's proclaimed victory in the Iranian presidential election on Friday.
swa: Maelfu ya watu waliandamana mjini Tehran, Mashdad na kwenye miji mingine mikubwa ya Irani ili kupinga ushindi wa Rais Mahmoud Ahmadinejad katika uchaguzi mkuu uliofanyika Ijumaa.

eng: Two different reformist rivals and their supporters insist there was election fraud at play.
swa: Washindani wawili wanamageuzi pamoja na mashabiki wao wanasisitiza kwamba palitokea udanganyifu.

eng: Mir Hussein Moussavi, the main challenger of Ahmadinejad said the results from "untrustworthy monitors" reflect "the weakening of the pillars that constitute the sacred system" of Iran and "the rule of authoritarianism and tyranny."
swa: Mir Hussein Mousavi, mpinzani mkuu wa Ahmedinejad alisema kuwa matokeo yaliyotolewa na “waangalizi wasioaminika” yanaakisi “udhaifu wa nguzo zinazosimamisha mfumo mtakatifu” wa Irani na “utawala wa mabavu.”

eng: Several scenes of street fights and demonstrations are uploaded on YouTube.
swa: Matukio kadhaa ya kupigana mitaani na maandamano yamewekwa kwenye YouTube.

eng: A demonstration in Valiasr street in Tehran where thousands of protesters demonstrated and chanted slogans against the Ahmadinejad government.
swa: Maandamano katika mtaa wa Valiasr mjini Tehran ambako maelfu ya waandamanaji walipinga kwa kuimba kauli mbiu dhidi ya serikali ya Ahmadinejad.

eng: And here people chanted: 'Moussavi, take back my vote!'.
swa: Na hapa watu waliimba: ‘Mousavi, rejesha kura yangu!’.

eng: Security forces repressed protesters:
swa: Vyombo vya usalama vilidhibiti waandamanaji:

eng: Another demonstration was held in Mashhad where protesters asked security forces to support them .
swa: Maandamano mengine yalifanyika mjini Mashad ambako waandamanaji waliwaomba wanausalama wawaunge mkono .

eng: Ghomar Ashegahne has published several photos showing security forces beating protesters (see photo above).
swa: Ghomar Ashegahne amechapisha picha kadhaa zinazoonyesha wanausalama wakiwapiga waandamanaji (tazama picha hapo juu).

eng: The blogger writes that the repression would be a good reason not to go to streets to protest, but 'what can we do with all this sorrow?'.
swa: Mwanablogu huyo anaandika kwamba udhibiti ungekuwa ni sababu nzuri ya kutokwenda kwenye maandamano, lakini ‘tufanye nini na uchungu huu?’

eng: He says Karoubi and Moussavi who wanted to change situation in country, should start now.
swa: Anasema kuwa Karoubi na Mousavi walitaka kubadili hali nchini, na inawabidi waanze sasa.

eng: Belgiran writes that Iranian Leader, Ali Khamenei, overthrew Moussavi by a coup before he even bacame president and replaced him with Ahmadinejad... He writes, "This regime just lost the little legitimacy that it had."
swa: Belgiran anaandika kwamba Kiongozi wa Irani, Ali Khamenei, alimpindua Mousavi hata kabla hajakuwa rais na akamweka Ahmadinejad… Anaandika, “Utawala huu umepoteza uaminifu mdogo uliokuwepo.”

eng: Mehrdadd writes on Twitter, that the Iranian Leader shows he is against the Iranian people.
swa: Mehrdadd anaandika kwenye Twita, kwamba kiongozi wa Irani anaonyesha kuwa yuko dhidi ya watu wa Irani.

eng: Now any political personality should take a position for or against people.
swa: Na sasa kila mwanasiasa anapaswa achukue msimamo ulio kwa ajili ya wananchi au dhidi ya wananchi.

eng: Mehri912 says on Twitter, "If Iran sleeps tonight, it will sleep forever".
swa: Mehri912 anasema kwenye Twita, “Kama Irani italala usiku wa leo, basi ndiyo italala daima”.

eng: Tehran protests, via jomhour.info
swa: Tehran protests, via jomhour.info

eng: Hundreds of thousands of Iranians in Tehran and several other cities have rallied to support presidential candidate Mir Hussein Mousavi, defying a government ban on demonstrations.
swa: Mamia ya maelfu ya Wairani mjini Tehran na katika miji mingine kadhaa wameandamana kumuunga mkono mgombea urais Mir Hussein Mousavi huku wakiikupuuza amri ya serikali inayokataza maandamano.

eng: Protesters are calling for the annulment of the presidential election results, saying President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's victory in the 12th of June election is a fraud.
swa: Waandamanaji wanadai kubatilishwa matokeo ya uchaguzi wa rais, wakisema kuwa ushindi wa Rais Mahmoud Ahmedinejad katika uchaguzi wa tarehe 12 Juni ulipatikana katika njia sizizo halali.

eng: Security forces have struck down hard on demonstrators, and at least one person was killed in Tehran today.
swa: Majeshi ya usalama yamewashukia wanaandamanaji, na mtu mmoja aliuwawa mjini Tehran leo.

eng: Although Twitter, Facebook and YouTube are currently blocked in Iran, many Iranians have been using proxies to bypass filters and report up-to-the-minute news.
swa: Japokuwa huduma za Twita, FaceBook pamoja na YouTube zimezuiliwa kwa kuzimwa nchini Iran, Wairani wengi wamekuwa wakitumia tovuti-vivuli ili kuvizunguka vichujio vilivyowekwa na wanaripoti habari kadiri zinavyotokea.

eng: Iranian authorities have also blocked SMS text messages, and are also filtering several news websites reflecting reformist opinions.
swa: Utawala wa Irani pia umezuia huduma za jumbe za maandishi kwa kutumia simu za mkononi (SMS), kadhalika utawala huo unachuja tovuti kadhaa zinazoakisi maoni ya wanamageuzi.

eng: Iran09 tweeted earlier today:
swa: Iran09 aliandika katika ujumbe wa Twita mapema leo:

eng: I confirm that there's a Basij station around the square and they shot ppl from the roof. #iranelection
swa: “Nimethibitisha kwamba kuna Basij waliopo kwenye viwanja na wanawapiga watu kutokea kwenye mapaa ya nyuma. #iranelection”

eng: Jadi tweeted:
swa: Jadi aliandika ujumbe wa Twita:

eng:
People are still joining to the demonstration. 	“Watu bado wanajiunga na maandamano.
Chanting 'Mousavi!	Wanaimba ‘Mousavi!
Mousavi!	Mousavi!
Take back my vote' #IranElection
swa: Ichukue kura yangu’ #iranelection”

eng: Mousavi spoke and called for the election results to be reviewed.
swa: Mousavi aliongea na kuomba matokeo ya uchaguzi yaangaliwe tena.

eng: He said he is ready to take part in a new election.
swa: Alisema yuko tayari kushiriki katika uchaguzi mpya.

eng: There are some video news clips about the election here.
swa: Kuna filamu za video zinazohuzu uchaguzi hapa.

eng: As protest grows so does repression
swa: Kadri upinzani unavyozidi ndivyo ukandamizaji unavyoongezeka
