eng: Students who protested against the presidential election at diffrent universities were attacked by security forces.
swa: Wanafunzi waliopinga uchaguzi wa rais katika vyuo vikuu mbalimbali walishambuliwa na vikosi vya usalama.

eng: Here is a video film showing a dormitory of the University of Tehran on Sunday night.
swa: Ifuatayo ni video inayoonyesha bweni la Chuo Kikuu cha Tehran jumapili usiku.

eng: Update: Here is a Flickr slideshow of photos showing more of the destruction left behind by security forces in University of Tehran dormitories on Sunday night.
swa: Habari mpya: Huu ni mlolongo wa picha kwenye huduma ya Flickr unaoonyesha uharibifu uliofanywa na vikosi vya usalama katika mabweni ya Chuo Kikuu cha Tehran jumapili usiku.

eng: According to the Flickr user, Agha Hadi, many students were jailed.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa mtumiaji wa Flickr, Agha Hadi, wanafunzi wengi walitiwa mbaroni.

eng: Below, is a film showing an Iranian woman taking on security forces by a bus stop.
swa: Ifuatayo ni filamu inayoonyesha mwanamke wa Ki-Irani anavyopambana na vikosi vya usalama kwenye kituo cha basi.

eng: Azarmehr comments on this film:
swa: Azarmehr anatoa maoni juu ya filamu hii:

eng: Look at this brave Iranian lioness, first she swing kicks and then she side kicks the neanderthal truncheon wielding riot guard!
swa: Muangalie huyu simba-jike jasiri wa Ki-Irani, kwanza anapiga teke halafu anampiga teke la pembeni askari mtuliza ghasia anayefanana na mtu wa kale aliyebeba rungu!

eng: She gets a few baton strikes but this is the price for freedom and she cares not.Blessed is our motherland Iran, for having such daughters.
swa: Anapigwa marungu machache lakini hiyo ndiyo thamani ya uhuru an hajali. Na ibarikiwe nchi yetu ya Irani, kwa kuwa na mabinti kama hawa.

eng: The fear is gone and the momentum continues.
swa: Woga umetoweka na kasi inapamba moto.

eng: Thanks to Tehranlive we have several photos of Iranian people's protest and resistance movement:
swa: Shukrani kwa Tehranlive kwani tumepata picha kadhaa za Wairani wanaopinga na za mwamko wa upinzani:

eng: Green Vote tweeted that one of people's slogan is, 'Don't be afraid, we are all together'.
swa: Green Vote alituma ujumbe wa Twita kwamba moja ya kauli mbiu ni, ‘Usiogope, tupo pamoja’.

eng: Green Vote also tweeted that Mohammad Ali Tarekh, a student activist, was arrested in Shiraz.
swa: Green Vote pia alituma ujumbe mwingine wa Twita unaosema kwamba Mohammad Ali Tarekh, mwanafunzi mwanaharakati, alitiwa mbaroni kwenye jimbo la Shiraz.

eng: Several bloggers such as Zeitoon report that people chant Allah-0-Akbar (God is Greater) from their houses during the night.
swa: Wanablogu kadhaa kama vile Zeitoon, waliripoti kwamba watu waliimba Allah-O-Akbar (Mungu Mkubwa) kutokea majumbani mwao nyakati za usiku.

eng: Mousavi asked people to chant Allah-o-Akbar from the rooftops of their homes.
swa: Mousavi aliwataka watu waimbe Allah-O-Akbar kutokea kwenye mapaa ya nyumba zao.

eng: During 1978-79 Islamic Revolution people use to do the same as a protest move against Shah.
swa: Wkati wa mapinduzi ya Kiislamu mwaka 1978-79 watu walikuwa wakifanya hivyo kama ishara ya upinzani dhidi ya Shah.

eng: Where is Obama?
swa: Obama yuko wapi?

eng: View from Iran, an American blogger, writes:
swa: Mwanablogu wa Kimarekani, View from Iran anaandika:

eng: Ultimately, I know that rhetoric is just rhetoric.
swa: Ninafahamu kwamba maneno matamu ni maneno matamu tu.

eng: That the words of a president do not actually change history even though they become part of it.
swa: Kwamba maneno ya rais huwa hayabadili historia japokuwa huwa ni sehemu .

eng: If ever there was a time for Obama to turn on his rhetorical charm, it is now.
swa: Kama kungelikuwa na wakati muwafaka kwa Obama kuwasha uwezo wa maneno yake matamu ni sasa.

eng: Today at 4 pm there will be demonstrations in 20 cities in Iran.
swa: Leo saa 10 jioni kulikuwa na maandamano katika miji 20 ya Irani.

eng: My friends *want to be on the streets.* They are parents, civil servants, accountants, receptionists, and yes students.
swa: Rafiki zangu *wanataka kuwepo mabarabarani.* Ni wazazi, wafanyakazi wa serikali, wahasibu, wapokezi, naam na wanafunzi pia.

eng: In the end, with all of the violence, I am not sure that they will show up.
swa: Mwisho wake, ukizingatia ghasia zote hizi, sina hakika kwamba wataendelea kujitokeza.

eng: So Obama, turn on your charm.
swa: Kwa hiyo Obama, washa uwezo wako wa kuhamasisha.

eng: Use your powers of rhetoric to tell Iranians that, while we won't be sending in the marines, our hearts are with you.
swa: Tumia uwezo wako wa maneno matamu kuwaambia Wairani kuwa, japokuwa hatutatuma majeshi, nyoyo zetu zi pamoja nanyi.

eng: I know you can do a better job than I can.
swa: Najua kuwa unaweza kufanya kazi vizuri zaidi yangu.

eng: Isfahan's suffering
swa: Mateso ya Isfahan

eng: Tehran is not the only city where people protesting have been repressed.
swa: Tehran siyo mji pekee ambako watu wanaopinga wanakandamizwa.

eng: Protesters in Isfahan, have also been the targets of security forces.
swa: Waandamanaji mjini Isfahan, pia wanalengwa na vikosi vya usalama.

eng: Iranevents has published several photos of Iranian protests.
swa: Iranevents imechapicha picha kadhaa za maandamano huko Irani.

eng: People are being chased by security forces here:
swa: Watu wanafukuzwa na vikosi vya usalama.

eng: and here:
swa: na hii pia:

eng: Malawians are currently voting in the presidential and parliamentary elections.
swa: Wamalawi wanapiga kura katika uchaguzi wa Raisi na Bunge.

eng: A group of Malawian bloggers were trained by PenPlusBytes, an International Institute of ICT Journalism in collaboration with New Media Institute to monitor and comment on the elections using blogs, twitter and mobile phones.
swa: Kikundi cha wanablogu kilipewa mafunzo na PenPlus Bytes, Taasisi ya kimataifa ya Uandishi wa TEKNOHAMA kwa ushirikiano na New Media Insitute kwa lengo la kuangalia na kutoa maoni yao kuhusu uchaguzi huo kwa kutumia blogu, teknolojia ya twita na simu za viganjani.

eng: Let's take a look at their blogs, which are hosted on The African Elections Portal.
swa: Hebu na tuziangalie blogu zao, ambazo zimehifadhiwa katika Potal ya chaguzi za Afrika.

eng: The African Elections Portal provides comprehensive election related information on the various countries in Africa.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa mwanablogu Eric Chilenje, uchaguzi wa 2009 nchini Malawi utakuwa na ushindani mzito:

eng: According to blogger Eric Chilenje, the 2009 elections in Malawi will be heavily contested:
swa: Uchaguzi Mkuu wa 2009 utakuwa kati ya chaguzi zile zinazoonekana kuwa na ushindani mzito.

eng: The 2009 General Elections will be one of those elections that appear to be heavily contensted.In the first place, we have seen the former head of state Dr Bakili Muluzi, being stopped by Malawi Electoral Commission from contesting for the third time as president.This was done in accordiance with the Malawi Constitution whiuch stipulates that a presiednt shall only serve two consecutive terms.
swa: Kwa kuanzia tu, tumemwona Kiongozi wa nchi mstaafu Dr. Bakili Muluzi, akizuiliwa na Tume ya Uchaguzi ya Malawi kugombea kwa mara ya tatu kama Rais. Hili lilifanywa na kwa mujibu wa katiba ya Malawi inayoelekeza kwamba Rais atakuwa madarakani kwa vipindi viwili mfululizo peke yake.

eng: One other interesting aspects during the 2009 General Elections is that we have seen United Democtracti Front , a party being being led by Dr Bakili Muluzi forming a 'coalition' with Malawi Congress Party of John Tembo.
swa: Suala jingine linalovutia katika Uchaguzi Mkuu wa 2009 ni kwamba tumeona chama cha UDF kinachoongozwa na Dr. Bakili Muluzi kikiunda ‘muungano’ na kile cha MCP cha John Tembo.

eng: Norman Fulatira makes a similar observation:
swa: Norman Fulatira ana maoni yanayofanana na hayo:

eng: The 2009 Elections in Malawi seem to be the first since the country attained multiparty democracy.
swa: Uchaguzi wa 2009 katika Malawi unaonekana kuwa wa kwanza tangu nchi iingie katika demokrasia ya vyama vingi.

eng: The hype that is there perhaps suggests that this time around the contest is high.
swa: Matangazo yanayowanadi wagombea yanaweza kutubashiria ushindani ni mkubwa wakati huu.

eng: I percieve that the 2009 elections in Malawi hangs around the issue of greed among the leaders.
swa: Natambua kuwa uchaguzi wa 2009 katika Malawi unabainisha suala la ulafi wa watawala.

eng: None of the leaders is mentioning about an ideology to follow once elected into power save for pressidential independent candidate Mr. James Nyondo.
swa: Hakuna mtawala anayetaja mfumo rasmi wa kiutawala atakaoufuata akiisha kuchaguliwa kushika madaraka ukimwacha labda Bw. James Nyondo mgombea binafsi wa Urais.

eng: McDonald Bamusi argues that what the decision of two political parties, UDF and MCP, to support a single candidate has made the race very tight:
swa: McDonald Bamusi anatoa hoja kwamba uamuzi wa vyama viwili vya siasa vya UDF na MCP, kumwuunga mkono mgombea mmoja umefanya mbio hizo za uchaguzi ziwe kali kweli kweli:

eng: This year's general elections in malawi have been one of the most closely contested.
swa: Uchaguzi Mkuu wa mwaka huu katika Malawi umekuwa mmoja ya chaguzi zenye ushindani wa karibu sana.

eng: This has been the case especially because of the agreement of UDF and MCP to support one candidate in the name of John Zenus Ungapake Tembo.
swa: Imekuwa hivi hasa kwa sababu ya makubaliano ya UDF na MCP kumwunga mgombea anafahamika kwa jina la John Zenus Ungapake Tembo.

eng: Michael notes that rural voters will not be taken for granted in this year's elections:
swa: Michael anaonesha kwamba wapiga kura wa vijijini hawawezi kutegemewa katika uchaguzi wa mwaka huu:

eng: This year's race for Malawi General Elections will be tight.
swa: Mbio za Uchaguzi Mkuu wa mwaka huu zitakuwa zito.

eng: All major political parties are concentrating their campaign in the rural areas.
swa: Vyama vikuu vya siasa vinaweka mkazo wa kampeni zao katika maeneo ya vijijini.

eng: These are the people that are in majority.
swa: Hawa ndio watu walio wengi.

eng: The rural masses may not be taken for granted this year as they now know and appreciate who the good leader is.
swa: Watu hawa wa vijijini hawatatumika vibaya mwaka huu kwa sababu wanatambua vyema kiongozi mzuri ni nani.

eng: The Civil Society, Media and Religious Institutions are playing a vital role in making sure that the Electorate have the right information concerning the elections.
swa: Vyama vya kiraia, Vyombo vya habari na Taasisi za kidini vinafanya wajibu wake muhimu katika kuhakikisha kuwa Wapiga kura wanazo taarifa sahihi kuhusiana na uchaguzi.

eng: This will help the public to make an informed decision on who to vote for on May 19.
swa: Hii itasaidia umma kufanya maamuzi yanayotokana na ufahamu wa kutosha kuhusu nani wa kumchagua ifikapo Mei 19.

eng: Wesysylas reports that the a Democratic Progressive Party bus was stoned in Machinga Distrtict:
swa: Wesysylas anaarifu kwamba basi la chama cha DPP kilitwangwa mawe katika Wilaya ya Machinga:

eng: Barely a day after some some nasty scenes occured at a rally organised by united democratict front national chairman Dr Bakili Muluzi at Goliati in Thyolo district, the scenerior wore a new face when a Democratic progressive Party Bus was on Wednsday stoned in machinga District.
swa: Kama siku moja baada ya matukio yasiyo ya kiungwana kutokea katika mkutano ulioandaliwa na Mwenyekiti wa Taifa wa UDF Dk. Bakili Muluzi huko Goliati wilayani Thyolo, tukio hilo lilichukua sura mpya pale basi la chama cha DPP kutwangwa mawe wilayani Machinga siku ya Jumatano.

eng: The good news is that, according to the Human Rights Consultative Committee, the levels of violence during the 2009 campaign period have decreased compared to the 2004 elections:
swa: Habari njema ni kwamba, kwa mujibu wa Kamati ya Ushauri wa Haki za Binadamu, kiwango cha matumizi ya nguvu katika kipindi cha kampeni yamepungua ukilinganisha na yale ya uchaguzi wa mwaka 2004:

eng: Human Rights Consultative Committee (HRCC) has said levels of violence during the 2009 campaign period in preparation for the 19 May general elections have decreased compared to what was experienced in 2004.
swa: Kamati ya Ushauri wa Haki za Binadamu (HRCC) imesema viwango vya matumizi ya nguvu katika kampeni cha kampeni za kuelekea maandalizi ya Uchaguzi Mkuu wa tarehe 19 Mei yamepungua ukilinganisha yale yaliyoshuhudiwa mwaka 2004.

eng: The campaign period has ended today at 6 o’clock in the morning.
swa: Kipindi cha kampeni kimehitimishwa leo saa 12 asubuhi.

eng: HRCC vice National Coordinator Cecilia Mussa said the development is a clear demonstration that Malawians have realized that power is not a tool to bring personal agenda.
swa: Naibu Mratibu wa Taifa wa HRCC Cecilia Mussa amesema mafanikio haya ni uthibitisho tosha kwamba wa –Malawi wameelewa kuwa nguvu si silaha ya kuingiza ajenda binafsi.

eng: The 2009 elections according to Nicolas Mbonela is one of its kind:
swa: Uchaguzi wa 2009 kwa mujibu wa Nicolas Mbonela ni wa aina yake:

eng: Malawi's fourth coming general election on 19 May 2009 will be of their own kind looking at the political developments that are transpiring in the country.
swa: Uchaguzi ujao wa tarehe 19 Mei 2009 utakuwa ni wa aina yake tukizingatia maendeleo ya kisiasa ambayo yanatukia nchini.

eng: The political rivals are busy castigating each other just to make sure that they woo support from most illiterate Malawians that form the majority of the country's population and electorate.
swa: Washindani katika siasa wanachabangana ili tu kuhakikisha kwamba wanawavutia wapiga kura wa Kimalawi ambao hawana elimu ambao ndiyo sehemu kubwa ya watu na wapiga kura.

eng: Malawi Elections Breaking News reports that property owners in Malawi are demanding money for campaign posters places on their property:
swa: Taarifa za hivi Punde za uchaguzi wa Malawi zinaripoti kwamba wamiliki mali wa Malawi wanadai fedha kwa ajili ya mabango yaliyobandikwa katika maeneo yao.

eng: Some small scale property owners in Blantyre are demanding, at least, K500 for political posters placed in their area of business or enterprise, it has been learnt.
swa: Baadhi ya wamiliki wadogo wa mali hizo huko Blantyre wanadai kama Kwacha 500 kwa mabango waliyowekwa katika maeneo yao ya biashara ama kazi, imegundulika.

eng: The development has prompted some property owners to openly advertise for their places, as one poster at Blantyre Old Town indicated Sunday morning.
swa: Maendeleo hayo yamewashawishi baadhi ya wamiliki kuzitangaza wazi sehemu zao, kama vile bango moja kubwa lililoko kwenye mji mkongwe wa Blatyre lilivyoashiria jumapili asubuhi.

eng: One of the places where politicians are said to have paid for a place is at the Curios centre, near Malawi Savings Bank in Blantyre .
swa: Mojawapo ya maeneo ambayo wanasiasa wanasemekana kuyalipia ni Kituo cha Curios, karibu na jengo la Benki ya Akiba ya Malawi huko Blantyre.

eng: One of the curios’ sellers disclosed in an interview the posters now selling themselves at the place were paid for, and that each did cost K500 for the depicted political parties.
swa: Mmoja wa wauzaji wa kituo hicho alibainisha katika mahojiano kwamba mabango yanayojiuza yenyewe kwenye eneo hilo yalilipiwa, na kwamba kila moja liling’arimu Kwacha 500 kwa vyama vya siasa vilivyoonyeshwa.

eng: The posters there include the faces of Bingu wa Mutharika and one for John Tembo, Malawi Congress Party’s torch bearer in the May19 polls.
swa: Mabango hayo yanajumuisha sura za Bingu wa Mutharika na nyingine ya John tembo, anayebeba mwenge wa chama wa MCP katika uchaguzi wa Mei 19.

eng: Jessie Puwapuwa observes that in 1994 Malawians voted in order to get rid of Kamuzu Banda who had ruled Malawi for 30 years:
swa: Jessie Puwapuwa anasema kwamba mwaka 1994 wa –Malawi walipiga kura ili kumuondoa Kamuzu Banda aliyekuwa ametawala Malawi kwa miaka 30:

eng: Election time as it is people cast their votes inorder to put into or remove people from positions.
swa: Kwa jinsi ilivyo, uchaguzi ni wakati ambapo watu hupiga kura zao ili kuwaweka ama kuwatimua watu katika nafasi zao.

eng: This is the third time Malawians will be going to polls to choose a leader after their hearts.
swa: Hii ni mara ya tatu wa –Malawi watakuwa wanaenda kupiga kura kumchagua anayegusa mioyo yao.

eng: In 1994 Malawians were eager to go to vote just to get rid of Malawi Cogress Party which had ruled the country for 30 years under what they called 'Dictatorship of late His Excellency Ngazi Dr. Hastings Kamuzu Banda.' this was the beginning of democratic dispensation and the United Democratic Party President Dr. Bakili Muluzi was the first leader to be elected and re-elected in 1999.
swa: Mwaka 1994 wa –Malawi walikuwa na ari ya kwenda kupiga kura ili tu kukitosa chama tawala cha MCP ambacho kilikuwa kimetawala kwa miaka 30 chini ya kile kilichoitwa “Udikteta wa Marehemu Mheshimiwa Ngazi Dk. Hastings kamuzu banda”.

eng: In 2004 Dr. Bingu Wa Mutharika was elected to this honourable office on a UDF.
swa: Mwaka 2004 Dk. Bingu Wa Mutharika alichaguliwa kuingia katika ofisi hii inayoheshimika kupitia UDF.

eng: In his post titled "Malawi: The Economy, Stupid?," Mujo writes, "Despite facing a strong alliance of the main opposition leader and a former president, the incumbent is expected to win on the back of an economic boom":
swa: Katika makala yake yenye kichwa cha habari “Malawi: Ni Uchumi tu, mjinga we?”, Mujo anaandika, “ Pamoja na kukumbana na upinzani mkali wa pamoja wa kiongozi mkuu wa upinzani na rais mstaafu, mtawala huyu anatarajiwa kushinda kwa mgongo wa kuuinua uchumi”.

eng: On May 19, voters in Malawi will go to the polls to elect their next president.
swa: Tarehe 19 Mei, wa –Malawi watakuwa wanaenda kupiga kura kumchagua rais mpya.

eng: The Democratic Progressive Party has been in power for the last four years and is fielding President Bingu wa Mutharika as its candidate once again.
swa: DPP kimekuwa madarakani kwa miaka minne iliyopita na kimemtengenezea njia Rais Bingu waMutharika kuwa mgombea wake kwa mara nyingine.

eng: Despite facing a strong alliance of the main opposition leader and a former president, the incumbent is expected to win on the back of an economic boom. Though critics accuse Mutharika of rigging his way into office, he is credited with helping to improve Malawi’s economy.
swa: Ingawa wapinzani wake wanamlaumu Mutharika kwa kujitengenezea njia ya kuingia Ikulu, anasifiwa kwa kuuboresha uchumi wa Malawi.

eng: Since he took over, the country has experienced an average economic growth of 7 percent.
swa: Tangu atwae madaraka, nchi imeshuhudia uchumi ukikua kwa wastani wa asilimia 7.

eng: “He inherited a very politically and economically mismanaged legacy … and it was a very tall order to get the country running, to try to get the confidence of very important external players in Malawi,” said Dimpho Motsamai, a political analyst at the Institute for Global Dialogue in South Africa who specializes on Malawi.
swa: “ Alirithi hali mbaya sana kisiasa na uchumi uliodorora…na ilikuwa kazi ngumu kuiendesha nchi, kurudisha imani ya watu muhimu wa nje,” alisema Dimpho Motsamai, Mchambuzi wa masuala ya kisiasa wa Taasisi ya majadiliano ya Kidunia ya Afrika Kusini anayejikita nchini Malawi.

eng: “So his vision was one of economic rejuvenation, stricter physical management of economic resources — very prudent management of economic resources — and one that would deal with socio-economic inequalities in Malawi,” she told Reuters Africa Journal.
swa: “Kwa hiyo maono yake yalikuwa kuufufua uchumi, kulinda vyanzo vya kiuchumi –uthibiti wa dhati vya vyanzo vya uchumi –na utakaoshughulika na matabaka ya kijamii na kiuchumi nchini Malawi,” alikiambia kipindi cha Reuters African Journal.

eng: George Kanyange expects the 2009 elections to be one of the most exciting elections in the history of Malawi:
swa: George Kanyange anategemea kuwa uchaguzi wa 2009 utakuwa uchaguzi unaosisimua zaidi katika historia ya Malawi:

eng: This year's elections are promising to be the most exciting ever in Malawi.
swa: Uchaguzi wa mwaka huu unaonyesha bayana kwamba utakuwa wenye msisimuko kuliko kawaida nchini Malawi.

eng: There certain factors that make our elections unique.
swa: Kuna sababu zinazoufanya uchaguzi wetu kuwa wa pekee.

eng: First is the fact that one of the key political parties contesting in the elections is the ruling party, the Democrartyic Progerssive Party (DPP), that was never ever eleected by the electorate for it to be in power.
swa: Kwanza ni ukweli kwamba mmoja wapo ya vyama muhimu kabisa vya siasa vinavyogombea katika uchaguzi huu ni chama tawala, DPP, ambacho hakikuwahi kamwe kuchaguliwa na wananchi kutwaa madaraka.

eng: Another interesting aspect is that the former ruling party, the United Democratic Party (UDF), is not fielding a presidential candiate after its leader, Bakili Muluzi, was rejected by the Electoral Commission, which has forced the party to go into an alliance with another leading positiion, the Malawi Congress Party (MCP) which is also the oldest party in the country.
swa: Na jambo lingine linalovutia ni kwamba chama tawala cha zamani, UDF hakina mgombea wa Urais baada ya kiongozi wake, Bakili Muluzi kukataliwa na Tume ya Uchaguzi, ikikilazimisha kuungana na chama kingine kikubwa cha upinzani, MCP ambacho nacho ni kikongwe kuliko vyote nchini.

eng: Media not considered in Party Manifestos, writes Big Up:
swa: Vyombo vya habari havijapewa umuhimu kwenye Ilani za vyama, anaandika Big Up:

eng: All seven presidential candidates, in next week’s general elections, have come under fire, for not incorporating anything tangible, to do with media in their manifestoes.These include, MCP/UDF’s John Tembo, DPP’s Bingu wa Mutharika, Aford’s Dindi Gowa Nyasulu, NARC’s Loveness Gondwe, RP’s Stanley Masauli, PETRA’s Kamuzu Chibambo and Independent James Nyondo.This has since prompted some journalists, to question the country’s political officials, on whether they indeed regard the media, as the fourth estate or not, in line with the constitution.
swa: Wagombea wote saba, katika uchaguzi mkuu wa Juma lijalo, wameonja joto la jiwe, kwa kutokuingiza jambo lolote linaloonekana, kuhusu vyombo vya habari katika ilani zao.

eng: And those fears are not without a basis and are too far from the truth. The voters roll remains a mess days before the elections are held; the opposition is yet to get over its grudge that the government shortchanged it in apoointing commissioners to the Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC); the state broadcasters, Malawi Broadcasting Corporation and Malawi Television, remain largely closed to the opposition and they are heavily manipulated in government's favour; the ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) is using (read abusing) government resources to campaign...
swa: Hawa ni pamoja na John Tembo wa MCP/UDF, Bingu wa Mutharika wa DPP, Dindi Gowa Nyasulu wa afford, Loveness Gondwe wa NARC, Stanley Masauli wa RP, Kamuzu Chibambo wa PETRA na mgombea binafsi James Nyondo.

eng: With such a situation, can anything ever be right with these elections?
swa: Hii imewafanya baadhi ya waandishi wa habari kuwauliza maofisa wa kisiasa nchini ikiwa wanathamini vyombo vya habari kama Mhimili wa nne ama la, kwa mujibu wa katiba.

eng: Mozambican bloggers Carlos Serra and Paulo Granjo respond to the attack yesterday against politician Daviz Simango, in the northern Mozambican port city of Nacala.
swa: Wanablogu wa Msumbiji Carlos Serra na Paulo Granjo waliandika kuhusu shambulio dhidi ya mwanasiasa Daviz Simango lililofanywa kwenye mji wa kaskazini wa bandari ya Nacala.

eng: In addition to the reactions from the blogosphere, Simango's party (@mdmwiki), tweeted the attack.
swa: Pamoja na maoni kutoka kwenye ulimwengu wa blogu, chama cha Simango (@mdmwiki), pia kilitumia huduma ya Twita kuandika kuhusu shambulio hilo.

eng: Simango is the mayor of Beira, and founded his new party MDM earlier this year, after falling out with traditional opposition party RENAMO.
swa: Simango ni Meya wa Beira, na alizindua chama chake kipya cha MDM mapema mwaka huu, baada ya kutofautiana na chama cha upinzani cha RENAMO.

eng: Just days ago, he and his party confirmed a planned bid for the Presidency and a campaign for the October election.
swa: Siku chache zilizopita, yeye pamoja na chama chake walithibitisha mipango yao ya kugombea urais na kampeni kwa ajili ya uchaguzi wa mwezi Oktoba.

eng: Simango was heading for a meeting of his party when his car was shot at by individuals in the assembled crowd who grabbed police weapons.
swa: Simango alikuwa anaelekea kwenye mkutano wa chama wakati gari lake lilipotupiwa risasi watu waliokuwa ndani ya umati uliokusanyika ambao walipora silaha za askari polisi.

eng: He escaped unharmed but media reports indicate three people were injured, including a policeman.
swa: Alinusurika bila ya kudhurika lakini taarifa za vyombo vya habari zinasema kwamba watu watatu walijeruhiwa, akiwemo polisi.

eng: Initial reports from Mozambican independent media suggest the shooters were members of RENAMO.
swa: Taarifa za mwanzo kutoka vyombo huru vya habari nchini nMsumbiji zinaashiria kwamba watu waliopiga risasi walikuwa ni wanachama wa RENAMO.

eng: Togo's National Assembly voted on Tuesday to end the death penalty for all crimes, making it the 15th member of the African Union to abolish capital punishment.
swa: Bunge la Taifa la Togo limepiga kura ya kukomesha adhabu ya kifo na kuifanya nchi hiyo kuwa mwanachama wa 15 wa Umoja wa Nchi za Afrika kuipiga marufuku adhabu hiyo.

eng: Although death sentences have been given for crimes as recently as 2003, Togo has not carried out an execution since 1978.
swa: Japokuwa adhabu ya kifo imekuwa ikitolewa kwa ajili ya makosa hadi kufikia mwaka 2003, Togo haijawahi kuitekeleza adhabu hiyo tangu mwaka 1978.

eng: Ephrem L on togosite.com writes:
swa: Ephrem L anaandika katika tovuti ya togosite.com:

eng: The Iranian presidential election will be held on June 12.
swa: Uchaguzi wa rais nchini Irani utafanyika tarehe 12 Juni.

eng: Only four men, out of more than 400 self-registered men and women, were given official approval by the Guardian Council for the candidacy.
swa: Ni watu wanne, kati ya watu zaidi ya 400 waliojiandikisha ambao walipewa idhini rasmi na Baraza la Walezi kuwa wagombea.

eng: The sharp eyes of blogger-photographers have captured moments and scenes in the streets of Iran where people promote their favorite candidates and political demands.
swa: Macho makali ya wanablogu-wapiga picha yamenasa nyakati na taswira katika mitaa ya Irani ambako watu waliwapigia debe wagombea wanaowapenda pamoja na madai yao ya kisiasa.

eng: Maryam Majd has published several photos on Feminist School about "women’s independent presence in the electoral space."
swa: Maryam Majd alichapisha picha kadhaa kwenye ukurasa wa Feminist School (Shule ya haki za wanawake) kuhusu “uwepo huru wa wanawake katika anga ya uchaguzi.”

eng: In Feminist School we read that "Tajrish sq.
swa: Kwenye Feminist School tunasoma kwamba “Tajrish sq.

eng: Emamzadeh Saleh (a holy shrine in the north of Tehran) and the memorable Tajrish Bazaar were hosts to the volunteer members of the "Coalition of Women’s Movement".
swa: Emamzadeh Saleh (eneo takatifu kaskazini ya Tehran) pamoja na soko maarufu la Tajrish Baazar vilikuwa wapokezi wa wanachama wa kujitolea wa “mseto wa vyama vya wanawake.”

eng: They enthusiastically demanded an independent presence for women in the city’s electoral space.
swa: Walidai uwepo huru wa wanawake kwenye anga ya uchaguzi.

eng: Their slogan was: "We Vote for Women’s Rights."
swa: Kauli mbiu yao ilikuwa: “Tunapigia kura haki za wanawake.”

eng: Their wish is for Iranian authorities to put an end to all discriminatory laws against women.
swa: Matumaini yao ni kuwa utawala wa Irani utakomesha sheria zote za kibaguzi dhidi ya wanawake.

eng: Saba Vasefi also captured this movement in action on Feminist School.
swa: Saaba Vasefi pia alilinasa kundi hili likiwa kwenye harakati kwenye Feminist School.

eng: In Zoherpix Photo blog we see how Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's and Mir Hussein Mousavi's supporters are waving the photos of their favorite candidates:
swa: Kwenye blogu ya picha ya Zoherpix tunaona jinsi waunga mkono wa Mahmoud Ahmadinejad na wale wa Mir Hussein Mousavi wanavyopepea picha za wagombea wanaowapenda:

eng: Janet Museveni
swa: Janet Museveni

eng: February's cabinet reshuffle has Ugandan bloggers making 2011 election predictions.
swa: Mabadiliko ya Baraza la Mawaziri yaliyofanyika mwezi Februari yanawapa wanablogu wa Uganda fursa ya kubashiri matokeo ya Uchaguzi Mkuu utakaofanyika mwaka 2011.

eng: Among the new appointments President Yoweri Museveni made was the posting of his wife Janet as state minister for Karamoja, a region in northeastern Uganda that has been plagued by conflict and extreme poverty for decades.
swa: Moja ya uteuzi aliofanya Rais Yoweri Museveni ni ule wa kumteua mke wake, Janet, kuwa Waziri wa Nchi wa Karamoja. Eneo hili liko kaskazini-mashariki mwa Uganda na kwa miongo mingi limegubikwa na migogoro na umaskini uliokithiri.

eng: While some bloggers think the high-profile appointment could bring much-needed attention to the region, others are more skeptical.
swa: Wakati ambapo baadhi ya wanablogu wanajenga hoja kwamba uteuzi huo wa ngazi ya juu utasaidia sana kufanya eneo linalohusika kutazamwa kwa karibu, wengine wanaonyesha wasiwasi.

eng: Ariaka notes:
swa: Ariaka anaeleza:

eng: Takinfg the cue, H.E President Yoweri finally made the cabinet reshuffle that had lingered in the grapvine for over six months.
swa: Kwa mtazamo wa haraka, Mheshimiwa Rais Yoweri hatimaye amefanya mabadiliko katika Baraza lake la Mawaziri, jambo ambalo limekuwa kwenye minong'ono kwa zaidi ya miezi sita sasa.

eng: And what a reshuffle.
swa: Ni ama kwa hakika ni mabadiliko ya aina yake.

eng: We saw the appointment of a first lady, also MP for Ruhama county of Ntungamo district to the Karamoja portfolio.
swa: Tumeshuhudia Mke wa Rais, ambaye pia ni Mbunge wa eneo la Ruhama katika Jimbo la Ntungamo, akiteuliwa kuwa waziri wa Karamoja.

eng: We saw Syda Bumba, transfered from Labour to the all important Finance docket.
swa: Tumeshuhudia Syda Bumba akihamishwa kutoka Wizara ya Kazi kwenda kwenye Wizara nyeti ya Fedha.

eng: It is the first time in Uganda that a first lady is a Minister, forget that hers is a junior portfolio.
swa: Hii ni mara ya kwanza katika historia ya Uganda kwamba Mke wa Rais anakuwa waziri, hata kama yeye ni waziri wa wizara ndogo tu.

eng: It is also the first time that a women has been appointed a finance Minister.
swa: Pia ni mara ya kwanza kwamba mwanamke anateuliwa kuwa Waziri wa Fedha.

eng: These are not simple appointments.
swa: Uteuzi wa aina hii si jambo rahisi.

eng: It is a political chess game where the master has his eye set on victory.
swa: Bila shaka ni sehemu ya mbinu za mchezo wa chesi katika siasa, ambapo mcheza kete anatupia jicho lake katika namna ya kupata ushindi.

eng: Daniel Kalinaki, a journalist who often blogs on political issues and who published an editorial on the appointment in Uganda's Daily Monitor, agrees:
swa: Daniel Kalinaki, ambaye mara nyingi huandika makala kwenye blogu kuhusu siasa na ambaye aliandika tahariri juu ya uteuzi huo kwenye gazeti linalochapishwa nchini Uganda la Daily Monitor, anakubaliana kwa kusema:

eng: There is, of course, nothing wrong with Janet’s ambitions.
swa: Kwa kusema ukweli, hakuna tatizo kuhusu harakati za Janeti.

eng: She is a Ugandan and has a right to seek or be appointed to any office for which she is qualified.
swa: Yeye ni raia wa Uganda na ana kila haki ya kuteuliwa kushika wadhifa wowote ambao anastahili kwa sifa.

eng: However, when a President has been in power for 23 years and begins to surround himself with relatives, friends and in-laws, he begins to look more like a village chief bent on carrying on his bloodline than a reforming democrat.
swa: Hata hivyo, pale ambapo Rais aliyekaa madarakani kwa miaka 23 anaanza kujirundikia ndugu, marafiki, mashemeji karibu yake, basi si aghalabu kuwa anaweza kufananishwa na chifu wa ukoo fulani mwenye makusudi ya kuhakikisha utawala unabaki katika ukoo wake kuliko kuleta mageuzi ya kweli ya kidemokrasi.

eng: Antipop at Let There Be Me takes a more humorous approach, speculating on how Museveni arrived at his decision.
swa: Kwa upande wake, Antipop at Let There Be Me, yeye anaeleza katika namna yenye tashwishi akidurusu kuhusu ni kwa jinsi gani Museveni alifikia uamuzi huo.

eng: She offers several theories, including that the announcement was a belated Valentine's Day gift:
swa: Anaeleza nadharia kadhaa, ambapo kwenye mojawapo anaeleza kwamba uteuzi huo ulikuwa ni zawadi iliyochelewa ya Siku ya Wapendanao, yaani Valentine:

eng: The one about Valentine's day
swa: kuhusu Siku ya Velentine:

eng: ...The next day at breakfast, realizing that he was in trouble, and not willing to get into any confrontation, he told her that last night was a deliberate move to get her all worked up but he had a surprise for her that would sure make up for everything.
swa: …Siku iliyofuata wakati wa kustafstahi, na alipogundua kwamba tayari yupo kwenye msukosuko, huku akiwa hapendi kuwa katika hali ya kukabiliana na yeyote, alimweleza kwamba kutompa kwake zawaidi usiku uliotangulia ulikuwa na madhumuni ya kumpa zawadi nyingine ya kumshtukiza, na ambayo kwa hakika itafunika yote yaliyopita.

eng: And on Tuesday Feb 17th, she learned of it in her favorite tabloid.
swa: Naye bibie alijipatia taarifa rasmi za zawadi hiyo kupitia gazeti alipendalo sana mnamo tarehe 17 mwezi Februari.

eng: She found out just how long she would have to travel to unveil her belated Valentine ’s Day gift and was not amused.
swa: Lakini pia aligundua kwamba ingempasa kusafiri umbali mrefu ili kujifungulia zawadi yake hiyo ya Siku ya Wapendanao, na kwa hiyo haikumshangaza.

eng: Lingerie would have done just fine.
swa: Kwake yeye zawadi ya nguo ya ndani ingemtosha kabisa.

eng: Not all bloggers are as critical, though.
swa: Hata hivyo, si wanablogu wote wamepokea uteuzi huo kwa ukosoaji mkali.

eng: Phantom of Even Steven ends a post on the Oscars by asking:
swa: Phantom wa Even Steven anamalizia makala yake kwenye blogu ya Oscars kwa kuuliza:

eng: In other news, what’s so bad about posting Janet Museveni to Karamoja?
swa: Kwa habari nyingine, je, nini kibaya katika kumtuma Janet Museveni huko Karamoja?

eng: Commenting on the post, chanelno5 defends Janet Museveni:
swa: Akiandika maoni kuhusu makala hayo, chanelno5 anamtetea Janet Museveni:

eng: There is nothing wrong with that.
swa: Hakuna ubaya na uteuzi huo.

eng: If she wants what everyone shuns go ahead.
swa: Ikiwa anataka kile ambacho wengine wanakikwepa, mwache achukue.

eng: In fact those people might benefit from her appointment.
swa: Kusema ukweli huenda watu wa kule watanufaika na uteuzi wake huo.

eng: Tumwijuke at Ugandan Insomiac considers this point of view, but she still questions the appointment:
swa: Tumwijuke katika blogu ya Ugandan Insomiac anatafakari juu ya uteuzi huo, hata hivyo bado anautilia mashaka uteuzi:

eng: Perhaps this appointment is Yoweri Museveni’s way of sending a message of solidarity to the people of Karamoja.
swa: Huenda kwa uteuzi huo, Rais Museveni anawatumia watu wa Karamoja salamu za mshikamano nao.

eng: Perhaps he hopes that the bevy of brown nose humanitarian types who support his wife’s every cause will transfer their ‘goodwill’ to developmental programs in Karamoja.
swa: Labda ana matumaini kwamba wale watu wanaounga mkono kila juhudi za Mke wa Rais basi watahamishia 'usamaria' wao katika miradi ya maendeleo ya Karamoja.

eng: Perhaps a picture of Mama Janet cuddling a snotty nosed Karamojong baby will be good PR for the Museveni government.
swa: Au labda picha inayomwonyesha Mama Janet akiwa amekumbatia mtoto mdogo wa jamii ya Karamojong itakuwa ni sehemu ya kujijengea sifa kwa upande wa Serikali ya Museveni.

eng: Still, I can’t shake this ominous feeling...
swa: Hata hivyo, bado siwezi kuondoa hisia zangu hizi mbaya...

eng: Dennis Matanda, who recently posted the second part of a four-part series titled "Uganda's Next President," offers his predictions on who will succeed Museveni:
swa: Dennis Matanda, ambaye siku za karibuni alituma sehemu ya pili ya mfululizo wake wenye jina la "Rais afuatiaye wa Uganda", anabashiri yafuatayo kuhusu yule atakayemrithi Museveni:

eng: Although the current President has not made an effort to groom a successor from the ruling National Resistance Movement, his wife Hon. Janet Museveni, MP who recently became appointed Minister and his son, Lt. Col. Muhoozi Kainerugaba are front runners.
swa: Ingawa Rais wa sasa hakufanya juhudi zozote za kumuandaa mrithi wa kiti chake kutoka katika chama chake cha National Resistance Movement, Vuguvugu, mkewe ambaye pia ni Mbunge, Janet Museveni, ambaye pia hivi karibuni ameteuliwa kuwa Waziri na mtoto wake, Luteni Kanali Muhoozi Kainerugaba, hawa wako mstari wa mbele.

eng: Joe in Uganda summarizes the shake-up in a post titled "Dynasty?", noting that Janet's appointment "was widely seen as a sign of things to come."
swa: Joe aliyeko Uganda anahitimisha mjadala huo kwa makala anayoiita "Utawala wa Kiukoo?" akieleza kwamba uteuzi wa Janet unaweza kuchukuliwa kama "ishara ya mambo yajayo."

eng: On a personal note, having worked on Karamoja for the past two months, I was delighted to see a high profile Minister taking over the portfolio.
swa: Kwa uzoefu wangu, baada ya kufanya kazi huko Karamoja kwa miezi miwili iliyopita, nimefurahi kusikia kuwa Waziri mwenye mizizi huko ngazi za juu atachukua nafasi kuongoza eneo hilo.

eng: The region is in urgent need of attention.
swa: Kwa kweli eneo hilo liko katika hitaji kubwa la kutazamwa kwa karibu.

eng: Uganda's Internet penetration rate is a little over six percent, a number that prevents large swaths of the population from joining Uganda's blogren or accessing the global blogosphere.
swa: Inakadiriwa kuwa matumizi na kuenea kwa intaneti nchini Uganda ni kwa kiwango cha asilimia sita tu, idadi ambayo inazuia sehemu kubwa ya watu kujiunga na ulimwengu wa blogu nchini Uganda au kuweza kuwasiliana na ulimwengu wa blogu duniani.

eng: For one village, the Guardian and Observer's Katine Project is working to change that.
swa: Mradi wa Katine unaoendeshwa na Guardian and Observer unafanya kazi kubadilisha hali hiyo katika kijiji kimoja.

eng: Since October 2007, the Katine Project has tracked the impact of a dedicated £2.5 million ($4 million) AMREF development project in Katine, a rural sub-county in northeastern Uganda (virtual tour).
swa: Tangu mwezi wa Kumi 2007, mradi wa Katine umefuatilia matokeo ya mradi wa maendeleo wa AMREF wa kiwango cha pauni milioni 2.5 (dola milioni 4), katika Katine, kitongoji kimoja cha kaskazini mashariki ya Uganda (talii kwenye mtandao).

eng: In addition to providing general news about Uganda and tracking developments in five key project areas, the project has been training local residents to use video cameras to document their lives:
swa: Zaidi ya kutoa habari za kawaida zinaihusu Uganda na kufuatilia maendeleo ya sehemu nne muhimu za mradi, mradi huo umekuwa ukiwafundisha wakazi wa sehemu hiyo jinsi ya kutumia kamera za video ili kusimulia maisha yao:

eng: , almost 20 people from Katine attended three video workshops held in the media and resource centre, now opened to villagers at the Amref office in the sub-county.
swa: , karibu ya watu 20 kutoka Katine walihudhuria warsha tatu za video zilizofanyika katika kituo cha habari, ambayo sasa imefunguliwa kwa ajili ya wanakijiji katika ofisi za AMREF kwenye kitongoji hicho.

eng: Four Flip video cameras and tripods have been left in the centre for villagers to borrow and tell their stories.... The aim of the centre is to give members of the Katine community a global platform to talk about their lives – the challenges and opportunities, their thoughts on the work being carried out by Amref - and to offer them access to information and expertise.
swa: Kamera nne za video na meza zake vimeachwa katika kituo hicho kwa ajili ya kuwaazima wanakijiji ili warekodi hadithi zao… Madhumuni ya kituo hicho ni kuwapatia wanachama wa jumuiya ya Katine jukwaa la kuongelea maisha yao – changamoto na fursa, mawazo yao kuhusu kazi inayofanywa na Amref – na kuwapa njia ya kupata habari pamoja na utaalamu.

eng: The resulting videos are presented in the project's Village Voices section.
swa: Video zinazotengenezwa huonyeshwa katika sehemu ya Sauti za Vijijini za mradi huo.

eng: In one, Katine resident John Ogalo shows viewers his homestead and attends a church service.
swa: Katika moja ya video hizo, mkazi wa Katine John Ogalo anawaonyesha watazamaji kaya yake na anahudhuria misa kanisani.

eng: Another video shadows bicycle taxi driver Dennis Ewalu as he repairs his bicycle, negotiates with customers and cycles nearly 80 km (50 miles) in one day.
swa: Video nyingine inamfuatilia mwendesha teksi Denis Ewalu wakati akifanya ukarabati wa baiskeli yake, akijadili bei na wateja wake na kuendesha karibu kilometa 80 (maili 50) katika siku moja.

eng: The Village Voices section also connects readers to local residents through text.
swa: Sehemu ya Sauti za Vijijini pia inawaunganisha wasomaji na wakazi wa sehemu hiyo kwa kutumia ujumbe wa maandishi.

eng: One post shares the stories of three schoolgirls who discuss their hopes for their future:
swa: Ujumbe mmojawapo unaelezea habari ya wanafunzi watatu wa kike ambao wanajadili matumaini yao ya maisha ya baadaye.

eng: Teresa Acupo
swa: Teresa Acupo

eng: In future, I want to study politics and become a member of parliament for my area.
swa: Huko mbeleni, ninataka kusoma siasa na kuwa mbunge wa eneo letu.

eng: Members of parliament earn a lot of money and they are respected.
swa: Wabunge wanapata pesa nyingi sana na wanaheshimiwa.

eng: Susan Amweso
swa: Susan Amweso

eng: My dream is to be a financially independent woman.
swa: Ndoto yang uni kuwa mwanamke huru kifedha.

eng: I need to control my own finances, not to depend on a husband for everything.
swa: Ninataka kudhibiti pesa zangu mimi mwenyewe, na sio kumtegemea mume wangu kwa kila kitu.

eng: Magdalene Atai
swa: Magdalene Atai

eng: My grandparents have been responsible for my entire upbringing and when I finish my education, I will buy them each a present.
swa: Babu na bibi yangu wamewajibika kunitunza wakati ninakua na nitakapomaliza masomo, niwanunulia zawadi kila mmoja.

eng: Because they may not be able to educate me up to university, I would like to train as a nurse after my secondary education.
swa: Na kwa sababu wanaweza wakashindwa kunisomesha mpaka chuo kikuu, ningependa kujifunza uuguzi baada ya kumaliza elimu ya sekondari.

eng: That is what most girls who cannot afford further education go for.
swa: Hivyo ndivyo wanavyofanya wasichana wengi ambao hawana uwezo wa kujilipia elimu ya juu.

eng: It is also easy to get employed as a nurse.
swa: Kadhalika ni rahisi kupata kazi kama muuguzi.

eng: One can easily start a private clinic in the village for survival.
swa: Mtu yeyote anaweza kuanzisha zahanati binafsi kijijini ili kujikimu.

eng: Katine's 25,000 residents live entirely off of Uganda's electricity grid.
swa: Wakazi 25, 000 wa Katine wanaishi nje ya maeneo yenye umeme.

eng: Without the Katine Project, it is unlikely that these people would ever get the chance to share their stories with the world.
swa: Bila ya mradi wa Katine, pengine watu hawa wasingeweza kuisimulia dunia hadithi zao.

eng: Discussions about the popular instrument called the vuvuzela blown by South African football fans have dominated the blogosphere since the beginning of Confederations Cup 2009 in South Africa, which ended last week.
swa: Mjadala kuhusu kifaa maarufu kinachoitwa vuvuzela kinachopigwa na mashabiki wa mpira wa miguu Afrika Kusini umetawala katika blogu mbalimbali duniani tangu kuanza kwa Kombe la Mabara la mwaka huu nchini Afrika Kusini, lililohitimika wiki iliyopita.

eng: Journalists, TV viewers, coaches and some foreign players called for a ban of the instrument during the 2010 World Cup in South Africa.
swa: Waandishi wa habari, watazamaji wa televisheni, makocha na baadhi ya wachezaji wa kigeni walitoa wito wa kusitisha matumizi ya kifaa hiki katika Kombe la Dunia la 2010 nchini Afrika Kusini.

eng: The debate is as loud as the instrument itself.
swa: Mabishano haya yana sauti kubwa kama chombo chenyewe.

eng: There is even an online petition to ban the instrument.
swa: Kuna hata kura ya mtandao ya kusitisha chombo hiki.

eng: FIFA has allowed vuvuzelas during the World Cup 2010 arguing that it is part of an authentic South African football culture.
swa: FIFA imeruhusu vuvuzela litumike wakati wa kombe la dunia mwaka 2010 ikitoa hoja kwamba hiyo ni sehemu ya utamaduni wa mpira wa Afrika Kusini.

eng: This is Wikipedia description of the vuvuzela:
swa: Haya ni maelezo ya Wikipedia kuhusu vuvuzela:

eng: a blowing horn, approximately one metre in length, commonly blown by fans at football matches in South Africa.
swa: pembe ya kupuliza, yenye urefu wa kadiri ya mita moja , kwa kawaida hupulizwa na mashabiki katika mechi za mpira wa miguu huko Afrika Kusini.

eng: The origin of the name is disputed. It may originate from the Zulu for "making noise," from the "vuvu" sound it makes, or from township slang related to the word for "shower."
swa: Asili ya jina hili ina utata. asili ya jina inaweza kuwa ni ya Kizulu yenye maana ya “kupiga kelele,” inayotokana na sauti kupulizwa kwake ya “vuvu” , au kutokana na lugha ya mtaani inayohusiana na neno “kuoga”

eng: Opinions in the blogosphere are deeply divided.
swa: Mitazamo katika ulimwengu wa blogu imepishana sana.

eng: Some bloggers are completely outraged by the sound produced by vuvuzelas while others call for tolerance and understanding.
swa: Wanablogu wengine wanakerwa na sauti inayotoka kwenye vuvuzela wakati wengine wanatoa wito wa watu kuwa na uvumilivu pamoja na uelewa wa mambo.

eng: One blogger goes as far as claiming that the instrument spreads HIV!
swa: Mwanablogu mmoja amefika mbali ha hata kudai kwamba kifaa hiki kinaeneza virusi vya UKIMWI!

eng: Dave Taylor describes vuvuzelas as "the traditional instruments of football mayhem."
swa: Dave Taylor anaelezea vuvuzela kama “kifaa cha asili cha ghasia za mpira wa miguu”

eng: To Chris of World Cup blog, the vuvuzela is "that giant swarm of insects...":
swa: Kwa Chris wa blogu ya Kombe la Dunia, vuvuzela ni “ile sauti kubwa ya jeshi la wadudu (kama vile nzige)”:

eng: That giant swarm of insects you’ve been hearing at every Confederations Cup game is not, in fact, one of the Biblical Plagues migrating south.
swa: Ile sauti kubwa kama ya kundi kubwa la nzige ambayo umekuwa ukiisikia katika kila mchezo Kombe la Mabara si, kwa hakika, mojawapo ya yale ‘mapigo’ yanayoelezwa katika biblia.

eng: It’s actually called a vuvuzela...
swa: Hiyo ndiyo inaitwa vuvuzela…

eng: Capitals Kremlin considers the vuvuzela the most annoying noisemaker:
swa: Capitals Kremlin anaichukulia vuvuzela kama kipiga kelele kinachokera kuliko vyote:

eng: Ladies and gentlemen, Caps Kremlin is pleased to present to you: the world's most annoying noisemaker, the vuvuzela.
swa: Mabibi na Mabwana, Caps Kremlin anayofuraha kuwaletea: kipiga kelele kinachokera zaidi duniani, vuvuzela.

eng: There is one long description of the vuvuzela from 24.com:
swa: Kuna maelezo marefu ya vuvuzela kutoka 24.com:

eng: ...take a sport from England called football, take a snort of glitter-eyed powder-nosed marketing gnomes, a large liquor conglomerate wanting to increase market share, add a white guy called Van Schalkwyk with a take-the-gap mentality and a plastics factory and what do you get?
swa: …chukua mchezo kutoka Uingereza unaoitwa kandanda, chukua kamasi ya kinyago chenye macho yanayong'ara na pua yenye unga ya mfanyabiashara wa kutangaza bidhaa, pamoja na wabia wa makampuni ya pombe ambao wanataka kuongeza hisa kwenye soko la biashara, muongeze jamaa aitwaye Van Schalkwyk mwenye ile akili-ya-kuhepa uchanganye na kiwanda cha plastiki, unajua unapata nini?

eng: The vuvuzela.
swa: Vuvuzela.

eng: Pitch Invasion calls the vuvuzela "Satan's instrument."
swa: Pitch Invasion anaiita vuvuzela “Chombo cha Shetani.”

eng: Welcome to plastic Africa:
swa: Karibu kwa plastic Africa:

eng: You then follow it up with a barrage of press releases about the kudu horn being used in ancient times to summon villagers to meetings, Christian cults claiming it as part of their sacred rituals and we get stuck with football games that can only be watched on TV with the mute button firmly on.
swa: halafu fuaatilia na mapigo makali ya taarifa rasmi za kutangaza habari juu ya jinsi pembe-ya-kudu ulivyokuwa ikitumika zama za kale kupiga mbiu za kuitawanakijiji mkutanoni, Vikundi vya wakristo vikidai kuwa hiyo ni sehemu ya ibada zao takatifu na tunaishia na mechi za soka ambazo zinaweza kuangaliwa kwenye televisheni pale tu sauti ikiwa imeminywa.

eng: And if you don’t like it, you must be at best a racist or at worst one of those guys who when he hears the word “culture” reaches for his gun.
swa: Na kama huipendi (vuvuzela), ni lazima uwe mbaguzi au mbaya zaidi kati ya wale jamaa ambao wakisikia neno “utamaduni” tayari huanza kuzifikia bunduki.

eng: Welcome to plastic Africa.
swa: Karibia kwenye blogu ya Afrika plastiki.

eng: And rue an opportunity missed.
swa: Na usikitikie fursa iliyopotea.

eng: From the Foreign Policy blog, "The World Cup's biggest concern is a trumpet,"
swa: Kutoka blogu ya Foreign Policy, “Jambo kubwa zaidi katika kombe la Dunia ni tarumbeta,”

eng: Five years ago, when South Africa won the right to host the 2010 World Cup, many were concerned whether the country had the infrastructure to host the huge tournament.
swa: Miaka mitano nyuma, wakati Afrika kusini iliposhinda haki ya kuandaa Kombe la Dunia la mwaka 2010, wengi walitaka zaidi kujua ikiwa nchi hiyo ilikuwa na miundo mbinu inayohitajika kuwa mwenyeji wa mashindano haya makubwa.

eng: With one year to go, though, most observers agree that the country will be pass that test. Instead, the biggest complaints have centered on an instrument called the vuvuzela.
swa: Mwaka moja tu ukiwa umebakia, ingawa, waangalizi wengi wanakubaliana kwamba nchi imeshinda mtihani huo; badala yake, walalamikaji wakubwa wanatumia muda mwingi kulalamikia chombo kinachoitwa vuvuzela.

eng: ReasonCheck wonders, "...if these heathen brutes could be introduced to the joys of producing actual musical notes from their hellish plastic pipes":
swa: ReasonCheck anawaza, “…laiti haya mapagani zuzu yangejua furaha ya kutengeneza nota za muziki kwa kutumia mabomba haya ya jehanamu”:

eng: If you’ve caught any of the games on TV, you would have heard a continuous droning sound, like a perpetually embittered swarm of hornets.
swa: Kama ulifanikiwa kuipata mechi yoyote kupitia luninga, bila shaka ulisikia sauti mbaya, kama ya kundi la wadudu wanaoleta kero.

eng: But you really have to be there to appreciate the full horror of the cacophony.
swa: Lakini pengine inabidi kuwa pale kuielewa kero hasa ya kelele ile mbaya.

eng: I took my son to a game a few nights ago and have been suffering from headaches ever since, and am sleeping fitfully.
swa: Nilimchukua mwanangu kwenda kwenye mchezo usiku wa siku chache zilizopita na tumekuwa tukitaabika na kuumwa kwa vichwa tangu wakati huo, na ninashitukashituka wakati nikilala.

eng: I then got to thinking that if these heathen brutes could be introduced to the joys of producing actual musical notes from their hellish plastic pipes there might just be a shift in Zeitgeist amongst them and they might seek to actually make music.
swa: Ndipo nikawaza kwamba ikiwa haya mapagani zuzu yangeonyeshwa furaha ya kutengeneza nota za muziki kwa kutumia mabomba haya ya plastiki basi pangeweza kutokea mabadiliko ya kifikra kati yao na wangejaribu kuanza kupiga muziki.

eng: Pitch Invasion looks at the history of noisemaking in world football starting with the first popular noisemaker in Britain, the wooden rattle:
swa: Pitch Invasion anaangalia historia ya upigaji kelele kwenye mpira wa miguu duniani akianzia na kipiga kelele maarufu Uingereza, yale manyanga au machekeche ya mbao:

eng: The first popular noisemaker in football — and one that made a sound to make even a vuvuzela wince — was the wooden rattle in Britain.
swa: Kipiga kelele maarufu cha kwanza mpirani – na kilichokuwa kinapiga kelele hata kuifanya vuvuzela kunyong'onyea - kilikuwa ni lile chekeche la mbao huko Uingereza.

eng: Writing in the Guardian, Simon Burnton hoped that “perhaps South Africa can learn from the loud wooden rattles that soundtracked British football in the post-war era – and fell out of favour when everyone realised just how annoying they were. I can only hope that one day soon a similar fate will befall the vuvuzelas.”
swa: Akiandika katika jarida la Guardian, Simon Burnton alitegemea kwamba “huenda Afrika Kusini ingejifunza kutoka kwenye yale manyanga ya mbao yaliyotumbuiza kandanda la Uingereza katika kipindi cha baada ya vita –na yaliyopoteza umaarufu wakati kila mmoja alivyogundua jinsi yanavyokera. natumaini kuwa siku hivi karibuni hatima mthili ya hiyo itayafikia haya mavuvuzela.”

eng: Yet it was a shift in the entire base of fan culture, rather than a simple realisation that rattles were annoying, that removed the rattle from the terraces.
swa: Hata hivyo, ni mageuzi ya kimsingi katika utamaduni mzima wa mashabiki na siyo utambuzi kwamba manyanga yale yalikuwa yanakera,ndiyo yaliyoyaondoa manyanga yale kwenye viambaza."

eng: Though a fairly recent instrument at South African football games, some trace the roots to African tradition.
swa: Ingawa ni chombo kilichojitokeza hivi karibuni tu katika mapambano ya kandanda, kuna baadhi ya watu wanaohusianisha asili yake na utamaduni wa Kiafrika.

eng: “The ancestor of the vuvuzela is said to be the kudu horn - ixilongo in isiXhosa, mhalamhala in Tshivenda - blown to summon African villagers to meetings.”
swa: “Asili ya vuvuzela inasemekana kuwa ni pembe la mnyama kudu liitwalo ixilongo kwa kiXhosa, mhalamhala kwa kiTshivenda –linapulizwa ili kuwaita wanakijiji kwenye mikutano.

eng: It seems to have been in 1992 that the vuvuzela was first used at South African football matches, by supporters of AmaZulu F.C..
swa: Inaonekana vuvuzela lilianza kutumika mwaka 1992 katika mapambano ya mpira wa miguu huko Afrika Kusini, na wapenzi wa Timu ya AmaZulu.

eng: Supporters made the horns out of discarded tin cans, and the use spread wildly, to the joy of many and the irritation of some: South African writer Jon Qwelane wrote in 2007 that “Nowadays, there is an instrument from hell, called the vuvuzela, which has largely formed my decision to abandon all live games and rather watch on TV, with the sound totally muted.”
swa: Mashabiki walitengeneza pembe kutokana na makopo yaliyotupwa, kwa furaha ya wengi na kero kwa wengine: Mwandishi wa Afrika Kusini Jon Qwelane aliandika mwaka 2007 kwamba “Siku hizi, kuna kifaa kilichotokea kuzimu, kinachoitwa vuvuzela, ambacho kimepelekea uamuzi wangu wa kuacha kuhudhuria mechi na badala yake kuzianngalia kwenye televisheni, huku sauti ikiwa imeminywa kabisa.”

eng: In the 2000s, with South Africa’s World Cup bid on the horizon, the vuvuzela became a mass produced commercialised phenomenon as the result of a grant given by SAB Miller (the giant South African brewer) to Neil van Schalkwyk’s company Masincedane Sport in 2001, who began to mass produce a cheap plastic version.
swa: Katika miaka ya 2000, huku Afrika ya kusini ikiwa imewasilisha maombi ya kuandaa Kombe la Dunia, vuvuzela ilizalishwa kwa wingi kibiashara kutokana na msaada uliotolewa na SAB Miller (Kiwanda cha kutengeneza Pombe Afrika Kusini) kwa kampuni ya Neil van Schalkwyk ya Masincedane Sport mwaka 2001, iliyoanza kuzalisha kwa wingi toleo nafuu la plastiki.

eng: SA Sucks disputes the "history" of the vuvuzela as "the ridiculous lie being spread via Wikipedia":
swa: SA Sucks anaipinga “historia” ya vuvuzela kama “uongo wa kijinga unaosambazwa kupitia Wikipedia”:

eng: Incredibly, the ridiculous lie is now being spread via Wikipedia (thanks Karooboy for pointing out) that the origin of the Vuvuzela is actually based on a “Kudu horn” that the blacks used to blow.
swa: Kuna uongo wa ajabu unasambazwa kupitia Wikipedia (asante Karooboy kwa kuuonyesha) kwamba asili ya vuvuzela imetokana na “pembe ya Kudu” ambalo lilikuwa likipulizwa na weusi.

eng: I almost died laughing at this pathetic fiction but suppose its to be expected - the truth that these destructive beasts ripped them from trains in orgies of vandalism is obviously too politically incorrect to swallow.
swa: Ilikuwa karibu nife kwa kucheka kutokana na hadithi hizi za kutunga, pengine ni jambo ambalo tungelitarajia - ukweli kuwa haya madudu maharibifu yaling'oa (tarumbeta za honi) kutoka kwenye magari moshi wakati yakifanya uharibifu wao kwa pamoja ni wazi kuwa kisiasa hautaweza kumezwa kirahisi rahisi (au kukubalika).

eng: A bit further down this article is an image of a yellow horn-shaped vuvuzela - I got this image from one of the hundreds of spam emails which landed up in my mailbox, urging me to order 10 000 of these pieces of shit, with my corporate logo stuck on them.
swa: Chini kidogo katika makala hii kuna picha ya vuvuzela la manjano lenye umbo la pembe - niliipata picha hii kwenye mamia ya barua pepe zinazoingia kutoka kwa watu nisiowajua, zikiniomba eti nikiweke “oda” 10 000 ya majitu haya, yakiwa yamebandikwa nembo yangu ya kibiashara.

eng: The horn shape is extremely unusual but as with the Wikipedia article, to be expected as PR companies do their best to bury the real history behind it.
swa: Umbo la pembe yenyewe liko kiajabu lakini kama ile makala ya Wikipedia, ni dhahiri kuwa makampuni ya PR wanafanya kila linalowezekana kuzika historia ya kweli nyuma ya madude haya.

eng: According to SA Sucks there is nothing authentic African about the vuvuzela:
swa: Kwa mujibu wa SA Sucks hakuna jambo lolote la dhati la Uafrika kwenye vuvuzela:

eng: One of the things I love most about the politicians that run this fair dominion is how, at their discretion, they can make up their own history as they go along. The vuvuzela is one such example.
swa: Moja ya mambo ninayopenda juu ya wanasiasa wanaoendesha himaya hii ni jinsi, kwa namna watakavyoamua, wanaweza kutunga historia wakati wowote.Vuvuzela ni mfano moja wapo.

eng: Those arguing for the vuvuzela maintain that it is part of the great South African soccer culture and that not allowing it would truly be an injustice. Bullshit.
swa: Wale wanaotetea vuvuzela wanasema kwamba vuvuzela ni sehemu ya utamaduni wa mpira wa miguu Afrika Kusini na kwamba kutokuliruhusu kuatakuwa ni uvunjaji wa haki. takataka.

eng: They’ve been around less than ten years.
swa: Yamekuwepo kwa miaka chini ya kumi.

eng: It was only when some bastard called “Neil van Schalkwyk, the co-owner of Masincedane Sport, which manufactures the plastic vuvuzela, won the SAB KickStart Award in 2001, which is an SAB-run project that assists entrepreneurs by providing grants and mentorship during the start-up phase of business.” that the vuvuzela really started making an impact.
swa: Ilikuwa mpaka mwanaharamu anayeitwa “Neil van Schalkwyk, mmiliki mwenza wa Masincedane Sport, inayozalisha mavuvuzela ya plastiki, aliposhinda Tuzo ya SAB KickSrart ya mwaka 2001, ambayo ni mradi wa kuwasaidia wajasiriamali kwa kutoa misaada na mwongozo katika kuanzisha biashara.” Ndipo vuvuzela lilipoanza kujulikana.

eng: Dave Taylor found the noise from the vuvuzela annoying and distracting:
swa: Dave Taylor anadhani kuwa sauti ya vuvuzela inakera na kusumbua:

eng: A half-dozen fans having one of these, or even a lot of fans who blow on them to celebrate a goal or terrific defensively play is one thing, but as those of us that watched the FIFA Confederations Cup learned, the practice in South Africa seems to be to keep a continuous drone of vuvuzela going throughout the match.
swa: Mashabiki nusu-dazeni wakiwa na moja ya madude haya, au hata mashabiki wengi wanapoyapuliza kushangilia goli ama mchezo mzuri wa kulinda goli hilo ni jambo moja, lakini wale tulioangalia Kombe la Mabara la FIFA tumejifunza kuwa, namna ya ushangiliaji nchini Afrika Kusini inaonekana kuwa ni kuendeleza kelele hii moja kwa moja wakati wote wa pambano.

eng: And we’re not talking about twenty or thirty people in the stadium, we’re talking about hundreds, if not thousands, of locals keeping a deafening racket during the entire match.
swa: Na hatuzungumzii watu ishirini ama thelathini kwenye uwanja, tunazungumzia mamia, kama sio maelfu ya wenyeji wanaoendeleza hii kelele inapasua masikio wakati wote wa mchezo.

eng: I found the constant clamor to be most distracting and annoying, and it even got in the way of being able to hear the crowd reaction to terrific plays or bad calls by referees both.
swa: Makelele haya ya moja kwa moja niliyaona kuwa yanakera na kusumbua, na yaliingilia kati uwezo wa kuwasikia watu wakishangilia kabumbu safi ama kuzomea maamuzi mabaya ya refa.

eng: Language Log notes that vuvuzela "is woth 23 scrabble points even before bonuses — or would be, if it were added to the official word list."
swa: Language Log anasema kwamba "thamani ya vuvuzela ni sawa na pointi 23 za mchezo wa bao la maandishi hata kabla ya kupewa faida - au pengine ni sawa na hivyo, kama lingeongezwa kwenye orodha rasmi ya maneno."

eng: Mark Gleeson at Reuters blog thinks that in the end money will talk louder than any vuvuzela.
swa: Mark Gleeson wa blogu ya Reuters blog anafikiri kwamba mwishowe pesa itazungumza zaidi ya vuvuzela lolote.

eng: He says that the debate around the vuvuzela has become "almost a neo-colonial conflict":
swa: Anasema mabishano kuhusu vuvuzela yamegeuka “sawa tu na mgogoro wa ukoloni mambo-leo”:

eng: The debate around the vuvuzela was always going to generate big noise but for some South African commentators it has become almost a neo-colonial conflict.
swa: Kwa vyovyote mjadala kuhusu vuvuzela ingeanzisha kelele kubwa lakini kwa baadhi ya wachambuzi wa mambo wa Afrika Kusini mabishano hayo yamegeuka kuwa sawa na mgogoro wa ukoloni mambo-leo.

eng: The noisy trumpet, which dominates the sound waves around the stadiums during the Confederations Cup, has got a lot of people covering their ears.
swa: Matarumbeta yenye kelele, yanayotawala viwanja vyote wakati wa Kombe la Mabara, yaliwasababishia watu wengi kufunga masikio yao.

eng: Complaints from TV viewers across Europe have been vociferous enough for the future of the plastic pest to become the major item on the agenda at the series of press conferences FIFA president Sepp Blatter has held during the tournament in South Africa.
swa: Malalamiko kutoka kwa watazamaji wa televisheni Ulaya nzima yamekuwa makali sana kiasi cha kumfanya mdudu huyu wa plastiki kuwa moja ya ajenda kuu katika mikutano ya waandishi wa habari na rais wa FIFA Sepp Blatter ambayo aliifanya wakati wa michuano huko Afrika Kusini.

eng: At the end the day, it is the big TV money that talks.
swa: Mwishoni mwa siku, ni fedha za televisheni ndizo zitakazoongea.

eng: If the world’s broadcasters feel the cacophony of vuvuzelas detracts from the viewing pleasure of their public, FIFA will be forced to back down and ban the trumpets from the 2010 World Cup stadiums.
swa: Kama watangazaji wakubwa wa matangazo hayo wataihisi kero inayosababishwa na mavuvuzela kiasi cha kuwaondolea raha ya kutazama kwa watazamaji wao, FIFA italazimika kujirudi na kuyasitisha mavuvuzela kwenye viwanja vitakavyotumika kwenye mechi za Kombe la Dunia mwaka 2010.

eng: It won’t have anything to do with any ‘ism, just cold hard cash.
swa: Uamuzi huo hautajali itikadi yoyote bali pesa.

eng: Bob of the unofficial blog of DC United does not understand the vuvuzela haters:
swa: Bob wa blogu isiyo rasmi ya DC United hawaelewi wale wanaoichukia vuvuzela:

eng: I personally don't understand the vuvuzela haters.
swa: Binafsi siwaelewi wanaoichukia vuvuzela.

eng: I guess some people have no ability to filter out these quiet buzzing sounds from the ubiquitous noisemakers in the stands during the Confederations Cup matches.
swa: Ninahisi watu wengine hawana uwezo wa kuchuja hizi kelele zinazotoka kwa wapiga kelele walio kwenye majukwaa ya uwanjani wakati wa mechi za Kombe la Mabara.

eng: Apparently, they are called vuvuzelas.
swa: Yanaitwa mavuvuzela.

eng: I want one.
swa: Ninahitaji moja.

eng: From the very first seconds of the very first Confederations Cup match that I watched this year, New Zealand v Spain, I thought, "what is that interesting sound?" and then promptly filtered it out.
swa: Kuanzia sekunde za mwanzo za pambano la kwanza kabisa la Kombe la Mabara ambalo nililiangalia mwaka huu, New Zealand dhidi ya Hispania, Nilifikiri, “ni kelele gani ile?” na haraka nikaichuja.

eng: In a similar way, when I lived in Rosslyn, under the flight path of the planes approaching National Airport, the noisy planes bothered me for about a week.
swa: Na kwa njia sawa na hiyo, wakati nilipoishi Rosslyn, chini ya njia za ndege zilizokuwa zikiwasili kwenye Uwanja wa Ndege wa Taifa, kelele za ndege nilinibugushi kwa kiasi cha wiki tu.

eng: Then I didn't hear it anymore.
swa: Baada ya hapo sikuzisikia tena.

eng: Anyone who has been to a live soccer match knows that it is an event of experiences.
swa: Yeyote ambaye amewahi kuhudhuria mechi anajua kwamba hilo huwa tukio la kujua mambo mengi tofauti.

eng: There is the game itself, but there are songs, Roman Candles, smoke bombs, drums, horns.
swa: Kuna mchezo wenyewe, lakini kuna nyimbo, Mishumaa ya Kirumi, mabomu ya moshi, ngoma, honi.

eng: Oh yeah, and drunk supporters too.
swa: Enhhee, na hata mashabiki walevi vile vile.

eng: Some of his readers disagree.
swa: Baadhi ya wasomaji wake wanapinga.

eng: One of them hates "the damn thing" because it destroys the game atmosphere:
swa: Mmoja wao anachukia “dubwana lile” kwa sababu linaharibu mandhari ya mchezo:

eng: I'm one of the haters, and I can't comprehend someone who actually enjoys watching soccer on TV liking them.
swa: Mimi ni mmoja wa wanaolichukia, siwezi kumuelewa yeyote ambaye anafurahia kuangalia soka kwenye televisheni ambaye anayapenda (mavuvuzela).

eng: I hate the damn things.
swa: Nayachukia madubwana haya.

eng: But it's not because they're loud and annoying.
swa: Lakini si kwa sababu yana kelele na yanakera.

eng: It's not because they're loud and annoying.
swa: Si kwa sababu wana kele na wanaudhi.

eng: It's because they absolutely, completely, utterly destroy the game-related atmosphere at the matches.
swa: Ni kwa sababu wanaharibu kabisa mandhari inayoendeana na pambano.

eng: Destroy it.
swa: Wanaiharibu.

eng: Another reader says, "it's insane":
swa: Msomaji mwingine anasema, “huu ni wehu”:

eng: *You* may have some wonderful ability to push it into your mental background, but for most of us, it's insane.
swa: *U*naweza kuwa na uwezo wa kuisukuma nyuma ya akili yako, lakini kwa wengi wetu, huu ni wehu.

eng: The sound is *not* "atmospheric", it is *not* a minor part of the viewing experience, and it is *not* acceptable.
swa: Sauti yake *si* ya “kimandhari”, *siyo* sehemu ndogo ya utazamaji, na haezi kukubalika.

eng: Setumo writes about the vuvuzela and intolerance:
swa: Setumo anaandika kuhusu vuvuzela na kutokuvumiliana:

eng: For the record, we do not blow the vuvuzela because we are Africans.
swa: Kuweka kumbukumbu sawa, hatupulizi vuvuzela kwa sababu sisi ni Waafrika .

eng: We blow the vuvuzela because we get an adrenalin rush from the creative noise it makes.
swa: Tunapuliza mavuvuzela kwa sababu tunapata mtawanyiko sawia wa homoni za adrenalini kutokana kelele zenye ubunifu zinazotoa.

eng: Also, we get an adrenalin rush because we are human.
swa: Vilevile, tunapata msisimuko wa adrenalini kwa sababu sisi ni binadamu.

eng: Not because we are Africans!
swa: Siyo kwa sababu sisi ni Waafrika!

eng: Now that we have moved away from the racial stereotype, it becomes easier to clear the noise.
swa: Na kwa vile hivi sasa tumeachana na imani potofu zinazotokana na ubaguzi wa rangi, inaweza kuwa rahisi kuisafisha kelele hii.

eng: Subsequently, we could agree in unison that this is a matter of like, dislike and intolerance.
swa: Hatimaye, tunaweza kukubaliana kwamba hili ni suala la kupenda, kutokupenda na kutokuvumiliana.

eng: One of Setumo's readers argues that World Cup is not and "African" thing:
swa: Mmoja wa wasomaji wa Setumo anatoa hoja kwamba hili (vuvuzela) si jambo la Kiafrika:

eng: So the Vuvu is an African thing??
swa: Kwa hiyo Vuvu ni jambo la Kiafrika??

eng: The FIFA 2010 fiasco is not an “African” thing .. it is an international thing.
swa: Kushindwa kwa FIFA 2010 si jambo la Kiafrika…ni suala la kimataifa.

eng: The fact is that SA is only hosting the tourno, and trying hard to get as many international visitors to SA next year.
swa: Ukweli ni kwamba Afrika Kusini inaandaa tu mashindano haya, na inajitahidi sana kupata wageni wa kimataifa kuja Afrika Kusini mwaka ujao.

eng: So, have a bit of understanding that most non-Africans find the V-noise irritating in the extreme.
swa: Kwa hiyo, kuweni na uelewa mdogo kwamba wale wasio Waafrika wanaioona kelele ya vuvuzela kuwa inakera kupita kiasi.

eng: Another reader likes the sound so much and would even buy vuvuzela ringtone!:
swa: Msomaji mwingine anaipenda sauti ya vuvuzela kiasi kwamba angeweza kununua sauti-mwito wa simu yake!:

eng: @mcOlly - As a Texan, I would totally buy that ringtone.
swa: @mcOlly – Kama mwenyeji wa Texas, ningependa kununua sauti-mwito hiyo ya simu.

eng: All this uproar over the vuvuzela is silly.
swa: Makelele haya dhidi ya vuvuzela ni ya kipuuzi.

eng: If it doesn’t sound nice on TV, then the broadcasters should turn the stadium mics down.
swa: Kama haivutii kwenye televisheni, basi warusha matangazo washushe sauti za vipaza sauti vilivyoko uwanjani.

eng: I just learned of the vuvuzela by watching the Confederations Cup, and it makes me want to go to the WC even more.
swa: Nimeijua vuvuzela kwa kuangalia Kombe la Mabara, na hiyo inanifanya nitamani kwenda kutazama Kombe la Dunia zaidi kuliko ilivyokuwa.

eng: Shine2010 thinks that vuvuzelas will teach the world tolerance and respect:
swa: Shine2010 anadhani mavuvuzela yataifundisha dunia heshima na uvumulivu:

eng: ...maybe an encounter with a few thousand vuvuzelas will force the world, and soccer, to actually adopt some of the ideals – tolerance, respect, etc. – that it constantly preaches.
swa: …Labda kukutana na maelfu machache ya mavuvuzela yatailazimisha dunia, na soka, kutekeleza kwa hakika baadhi ya fikra za kimaadili –uvumilivu, heshima n.k –ambazo inazihubiri kila wakati.

eng: Robyn has become a vuvuzela addict:
swa: Robyn amekuwa ‘mlevi’ wa vuvuzela:

eng: I first tried to blow a vuvuzela two weeks ago, at the start of the Confederations Cup which has been held in South Africa ahead of next year’s World Cup.
swa: Kwa mara ya kwanza nilijaribu kulipuliza vuvuzela wiki mbili zilozopita, mwanzoni mwa Kombe la Mabara ambalo lilifanyika Afrika Kusini kabla ya Kombe la Dunia la mwaka ujao.

eng: I failed miserably.
swa: Nilishindwa vibaya.

eng: I blew and I blew and nothing happened, just a few insipid little parps.
swa: Nilipuliza na kupuliza, hakuna kilichotokea, vijisauti fulani vidogo tu vilivyotoka.

eng: But at the Brazil vs. Italy game, I got the hang of the vuvuzela and quickly joined the crowd in a jaunty one-note tune.
swa: Lakini kwenye mechi kati ya Brazili na Italia, Niliupata ujanja wa vuvuzela na nikaungana haraka na umati katika mlio wa nota moja.

eng: Baaaah!
swa: Baaaah!

eng: Baaah!
swa: Baaaah!

eng: Baaah!
swa: Baaaah!

eng: It is a sound so irritating and so obnoxious that it’s best to stick with the maxim “if you can’t beat ‘em, join em.”
swa: Ni sauti inayoudhi na kukera kiasi kwamba inabidi kutumia ule usemi “kama huwezi kuwashinda, ungana nao.”

eng: Not blowing a vuvuzela at a South African football game not only makes you feel a bit left out but it also makes you resent the noise everyone else it making.
swa: Kutokulipuliza vuvuzela katika mechi za za soka Afrika Kusini si tu kwamba inakufanya ujisikie kutengwa bali pia inakufanya uichukie kelele ambayo kila mmoja anaipiga.

eng: I Luv SA has a piece of advice for vuvuzela haters, "Suck it up":
swa: Mwanablogu I Luv SA anacho kipande cha ushauri kwa wale wanaoichukia vuvuzela, “vumilieni”:

eng: Me, I'd say to Fifa, you bought the spiel to host the cup in South Africa, you get to eat up the whole enchilada which includes the main ingredient, the vuvuzela.
swa: Mie, ninawaambia FIFA, mlinunua maneno matamu ya kuandaa mashindano nchini Afrika kusini, inawabidi mle chakula chote ambacho kinajumuisha kiungo kikuu, vuvuzela.

eng: It's like telling English fans to shut the irritating background drone they call singing.
swa: Ni sawa na kuwaambia mashabiki wa uingereza kuizima kelele wanayoiita uimbaji.

eng: Suck it up.
swa: Vumilieni.

eng:
Critics are saying they are too noisy. 	“Wakosoaji wanasema yana kelele sana.
I say so what?, writes Ash on South Africa Football Fans blog:
swa: Sasa iweje,?” anaandika Ash kwenye blogu ya Wapenzi wa soka Afrika Kusini:

eng: That is the purpose of the Vuvuzela after all.
swa: Hilo ndilo lengo la mavuvuzela.

eng: It is there to get the atmosphere buzzzzing.
swa: Lipo pale ili kutengeneza mandhari yenye kelele.

eng: This is Africa and we are renowned for dancing and singing and generally creating a great vibe at our football matches.
swa: Hii ni Afrika na tunajulikana kwa kucheza na kuimba na kwa kawaida kwa kutengeneza mandhari nzuri katika mechi zetu za mpira wa miguu.

eng: It’s all part of the uniquely South African experience and I’m certain that if our foreign visitors attend the games and experience the electrifying atmosphere they will fall in love with the Vuvuzela.
swa: Ni sehemu ya mazoea ya aina yake Afrika Kusini na nina hakika kama wageni wetu watahudhuria michezo hii na kushuhudia hali hii ya hewa (iliyojaa kelele ya mavuvuzela) basi watayapenda.

eng: To me asking the local supporters to leave their Vuvuzela’s at home would be like asking the Liverpool fans not to sing You'll Never Walk Alone, or asking the Brazilian fans not to create the Samba atmosphere at their matches.
swa: Kwangu, kuwaambia mashabiki wa nyumbani kuyaacha mavuvuzela yao nyumbani itakuwa kama kuwaomba wapenzi wa Liverpool kuacha kuimba “Katu Hutotembea Peke yako”, au kuwaambia mashabiki wa Brazili kuacha kusakata Samba kwenye mechi zao.

eng: What happened to dancing and singing and costumes?, one reader asks and adds, "Don't let your only contribution to the world be an almost universally annoying one! ":
swa: “Nini kilichovikumba kucheza na kuimba na mavazi ya sare?.” Msomaji mmoja anauliza na kuongeza, “usiruhusu mchango wako kwa dunia uwe ni ule ambao unaudhi!”:

eng: If that is the only culture South Africa has to share, that is pretty bad.
swa: Kama huo ndio utamaduni pekee ambao Afrika Kusini inao, basi hali n mbaya sana.

eng: Whatever happened to dancing and singing and costumes?
swa: Ni nini kilichovifika kucheza na kuimba na uvaaji wa sare?

eng: Seems to work for other countries just fine. Don't let your only contribution to the world be an almost universally annoying one!
swa: Mambo hayo yanafanya kazi vyema kwenye nchi nyingine Usiruhusu mchango wako kwa dunia uwe ni ule ambao unaudhi!

eng: It's a question of hospitality too.
swa: Ni suala la ukarimu pia.

eng: Blasting noise in our ears is just plain rude.
swa: Kutupigia kelele masikioni ni ushenzi.

eng: I for one am turning the sound off.
swa: Mimi ninazima sauti.

eng: I feel sorry for anyone travelling to SA to watch the games.
swa: Namsikitikia yeyote anayekwenda Afrika Kusini kuangalia michezo.

eng: They have no choice in the matter.
swa: Hawatakuwa na chaguo lolote kuhusu suala hili.

eng: Another reader compares the vuvuzela sound to "an annoying swarm of bees buzzing around your head...":
swa: Msomaji mwingine analinganisha vuvuzela na kelele inayoudhi ya jeshi la nyuki linalozinghuka juu ya kichwa chako…”:

eng: The argument the blogger is making about comparing Liverpool songs and Brazil's samba atmosphere borders on retarded.
swa: Mtazamo anaotoa mwanablogu wa kufananisha nyimbo za Liverpool na mandhari ya samba huko Brazil uko karibu na utaahira.

eng: I would certainly ask a Liverpool fan to stop if they just screamed one note of YWNWA in my ear for an hour and a half.
swa: Bila ya shaka ningewataka mashabiki wa Liverpool waache ikiwa wangekuwa wanapiga kelele kwa nota moja tu ya YWNWA kwenye masikio yangu kwa muda wa saa moja na nusu.

eng: There is a big difference between an annoying swarm of bees buzzing around your head a samba dance.
swa: Kuna tofauti kubwa kati ya kelele inayoudhi ya nyuki wanaozunguka juu ya kichwa chako na ile ya dansi ya samba.

eng: You won't be watching your local teams or players, another reader responds:
swa: “Hautakuwa unatazama timu za nyumbani au wachezaji,” msomaji mwingine anajibu:

eng: How is South Africa telling the world that they are football visitors?
swa: Ni kwa jinsi gani Afrika Kusini inaweza kuimbia dunia kuwa yupi ni mgeni wa mpira wa miguu?

eng: Visitors to the country yes.
swa: Mgeni wa nchi, ndiyo.

eng: Visitors to football?
swa: Mgeni wa mpira wa miguu?

eng: Don't make me laugh.
swa: Usinifanye nicheke.

eng: This is not South African football next year.
swa: Hautakuwa mpira wa Afrika kusini mwaka ujao.

eng: It's world football in South Africa.
swa: Utakuwa mpira wa miguu wa dunia nchini Afrika kusini.

eng: You won't be watching your local teams or players.
swa: Hutakuwa unaangalia timu za nyumbani au wachezaji.

eng: Anders tells us that vuvuzela haters are the people who were watching the games on TV:
swa: Anders anatuambia kuwa wanaochukia vuvuzela ni wale watu ambao wanaangalia michezo kwenye televisheni:

eng: The vuvuzela outcry is mainly coming from those, like my friend, who are watching the tournament abroad.
swa: Malalamiko juu ya vuvuzela yatoka kwa wale, kama huyu rafiki yangu, wanaoangalia mashindano kutokea ng’ambo.

eng: In the stadium, the fans love them.
swa: Kwenye viwanja, mashabiki wanayapenda.

eng: It's one of those things you bemoan until you actually are able to try it: think laser pointer.
swa: Ni moja ya yale mambo ambayo unayachukia mpaka pale utakapokuwa na uwezo wa kuyajaribu; fikiria tochi ya miale.

eng: On TV the horns conflict with the commentary, among other things, but in the ground the ambient noise is part of the atmosphere.
swa: Kwenye televisheni matarumbeta yanaingiliana na utangazaji, pamoja na mambo mengine, lakini uwanjani hali ya kelele ni sehemu ya mandhari.

eng: It is undoubtedly less abrasive in person than it is via satellite.
swa: Bila ya shaka hayakwaruzi ukiwa nayo ana kwa ana kama vile ukiyasikia kwa kupitia setilaiti.

eng: The real vuvuzela war, we are told, is not on the Internet but in the Netherlands:
swa: Vita halisi ya vuvuzela, tunaambiwa haiko kwenye Mtandao bali nchini Uholanzi:

eng: There is a real Vuvuzela war threat in the Netherlands.
swa: Kuna tishio la vita ya mavuvuzela huko Uholanzi.

eng: The company SoccerID reported Monday to import the controversial South African horn to Europe.
swa: Kampuni ya SoccerID iliarifu siku ya Jumatatu kuwa itaingiza Ulaya mapembe haya yaliyosababishwa utata huko Afrika Kusini.

eng: Within three to four weeks the first Vuvuzela's should be for sale in the Netherlands.
