swa: Ndani ya majuma matatu ama manne mavuvuzela ya awali yatauzwa Uswisi.

eng: NoLimitation however, claims to have exclusive distribution rights for the Vuvuzela.
swa: Kampuni ya NoLimitation, inadai kuwa ina haki pekee ya kusambaza mavuvuzela hayo.

eng: NoLimitation BV acquired the exclusive rights to the Vuvuzela and use of the name through Urbas Kehrberg GmbH, the German company which claims to have the rights to all EU countries.
swa: Kampuni ya NoLimitation BV ilipata haki pekee ya mavuvuzela na ya kutumia jina hilo kupitia kampuni ya Kijerumani ya Kehrberg GmbH, inayodai kuwa na haki katika nchi zote za Umoja wa Ulaya.

eng: This means that, according NoLimitation, they are the only company in the Netherlands with the right to sell the three-piece horn under the name Vuvuzela.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa NoLimitation, hii ina maana kwamba wao ndio kampuni pekee nchini Uholanzi yenye haki ya kuuza tarumbeta hizi zenye vijipembe vitatu kwa jina la vuvuzela.

eng: Chris of World Cup blog agrees that the vuvuzela is "quintessentially South African" but...
swa: Chris wa blogu ya World Cup anaafiki kwamba vuvuzela “ina asili ya Afrika kusini” bali…

eng: Problem is, it’s also quintessentially obnoxious.
swa: Tatizo ni kuwa, ina asili ya maudhi.

eng: If you’ve watched even 30 seconds of a Confederations Cup, you’ve surely noticed the all-enveloping buzzing sound - and chances are those horns are the reason you only watched 30 seconds.
swa: Kama uliangalia japo sekunde 30 za Kombe la Mabara, uliweza kusikia ile kelele iwayo yote – na inawezekana kuwa matarumbeta yale yalikuwa ndiyo sababu iliyokufanya utazame kwa sekunde 30 tu.

eng: it’s just one long 90 minute droning sound. To the point you begin to wonder when the B-list horror movie is going to break out before your eyes.
swa: Ni kelele moja endelevu kwa dakika 90. mpaka inafikia unaanza kujiuliza ni muda gani ambapo filamu hii ya kutisha ya dalaja la B itakapovunjika mbele ya macho yako.

eng: I’ve personally begun watching the games on mute - what with the combination of ESPN’s commentary team and the vuvuzela capable of being substituted for lethal injection and all.
swa: Binafsi nimeanza kuangalia mapambano hayo huku nimezima sauti –mchanganyiko wa timu ya utangazaji wa ESPN na vuvuzela vina uwezo wa kutumika kama sindano m’badala ya sumu au kitu kama hicho.

eng: Phobian suggests that the vuvuzela be allowed when South Africa plays:
swa: Phobian anashauri kwamba mavuvuzela yaruhusiwe tu Afrika Kusini inapocheza:

eng: The World Cup is for everyone, not just the Vuvuzela blowers.
swa: Kombe la Dunia ni la kila mmoja, si kwa wapuliza mavuvuzela peke yao.

eng: Maybe they should only be allowed at games where SA plays.
swa: Labda yaruhusiwe tu pale Afrika Kusini inapocheza.

eng: The other soccer teams playing should also have some say in whether there should be Vuvuzelas or not at their games.
swa: Timu nyingine zinapocheza ziwe na sauti ya kuamua ikiwa wako tayari mavuvuzela yatumiwe ama yasitumiwe kwenye mechi zao.

eng: SA Sucks takes the vuvuzela debate to a totally new ground by arguing that apart from the possibility of damaging one's hearing, the instrument might spread HIV/AIDS!
swa: SA Sucks anayapeleka mbali zaidi mabishano ya vuvuzela kwenye uwanja mwingine kabisa akitoa hoja kwamba mbali na uwezekano wa kuharibu masikio ya mtu, chombo hiki kinaweza kusambaza VVU/UKIMWI!

eng: Medical experts are issuing warnings that the noise from a vuvuzela can permanently damage a person’s hearing, but that’s never mind the HIV/ AIDS dangers of this thing.
swa: Madaktari wataalamu wanaonya kwamba kelele za vuvuzela zinaweza kuharibu kabisa uwezo wa mtu kusikia, lakini hiyo haijazingatia hatari ya kuambukiza UKIMWI ya hili dude.

eng: From last week’s Confederations Cup matches, spectators were blasted from all directions by the earth-shattering noise of the vuvuzela. In addition to the health hazards of ringing ears and thundering headaches, a by-product of mindlessly blowing on this instrument is the accumulation of a huge amount of saliva.
swa: Tangu mechi za Kombe la Mabara, watazamaji walilipuliwa kutokea pande zote za uwanja na kelele zenye-kutikisa dunia za vuvuzela.Zaidi ya madhara ya kiafya ya masikio na maumivu ya kichwa, bidhaa nyingine itokanayo na upulizaji wa kifaa hiki ni mkusanyiko mkubwa wa mate.

eng: The vuvuzela is a symbol of everything that is wrong with the "Sub-Saharan Africoon":
swa: Vuvuzela ni alama ya kila jambo lililoharibika katika “Afrika chini ya jangwa la Sahara the “Sahara Sub Saharan Africoon”:

eng: Personally, I love it!
swa: Binafsi, ninalipenda (vuvuzela)!

eng: If anything is going to bring the World Cup 2010 down, and become a symbol of everything that is wrong with the sub-Saharan Africoon, it will be the damned vuvuzela.
swa: Kama kuna chochote kinaweza kuliangusha Kombe la Dunia la 2010, na kuwa ushahidi wa kila kisichofaa katika Afrika Nyeusi (Kusini mwa Jangwa la Sahara), yatakuwa haya mavuvuzela.

eng: Just think how the filth, squalor, violent ape-like behaviour and deafening racket this thing produces will be beamed into 500 million White Western homes, for all the world to see.
swa: Hebu fikiri namna uchafu unaokinaisha, ufukara uliokithiri, tabia za fujo za kinyani nyani na kele zilizokithiri zinazoletwa na hili dude; yote yatasafirishwa mpaka kwenye nyumba milioni 500 za Wazungu wa magharibi, huku dunia nzima ikishuhudia.

eng: SA Sucks warns World Cup visitors to prepare for an anthropological “baptism of fire."
swa: SA Sucks anawaonya wahudhuriaji wa Kombe la Dunia kujiandaa kwa “ubatizo wa moto” wa historia ya mwanadamu.”

eng: The blogger experienced himself "three hours of hell on earth":
swa: Mwanablogu huyu alishuhudia mwenyewe “masaa matatu ya kuzimu hapa hapa duniani”:

eng: But on Sunday I was subjected to more than three hours of this hell on earth.I vowed, then and there, that after that first (and only) evening of the authentic South African soccer experience, I would never ever allow myself to be subjected to it again.
swa: Jumapili nilijikuta kwenye masaa matatu ya kuzimu hapa hapa duniani. Nikaapa, pale pale, baada ya jioni ile ya kwanza (na ya pekee) ya kujionea mwenyewe soka la Afrika Kusini linavyokuwa kwamba, sitajiruhusu kujikuta mahala pale tena.

eng: There were many things amiss that left me disappointed and angry that evening, but none so offensive to my senses as the Vuvuzela.
swa: Yapo mengi yaliyonikwaza na kuniudhi jioni ile, lakini hakuna kililonikera kama Vuvuzela.

eng: If FIFA were to ban the vuvuzela then they may as well scrap the rotation policy of the World Cup and just stage it every year in Europe at times that suit the Europeans and with a European atmosphere at the stadia, writes Visual Guidance:
swa: “Kama FIFA wangeyapiga marufuku mavuvuzela basi na waifute sera ya mzunguko wa Kombe la Dunia kuyaandaa mshindano hayo Ulaya kila mwaka katika muda ambao unawafaa watu wa Ulaya na hali ya hewa ya Kiulaya katika viwanja,” anaandika Visual Guidance:

eng: Of course, there has to be something to moan about though.
swa: Ni lazima kiwepo kitu cha kulalamikia.

eng: No complaints from the people at the stadium.
swa: Hakuna malalamiko kutoka kwa watu waliopo kwenye viwanja.

eng: They love it.
swa: Wanaipenda vuvuzela.

eng: No, it is the sofa slobs thousands of miles away, slouched in front of their TV and whining that the noise is giving them a headache.
swa: Tatizo ni wazembe wanaoketi kwenye sofa maelfu ya maili mbali na viwanja, wanaojilaza kivivu vivu mbele ya televisheni zao na kulalamika kuwa kelele (za mavuvuzela) zinawapa maumivu ya kichwa.

eng: Boo hoo.
swa: Boo hoo.

eng: Answer me this – are the horns any more annoying than the Ultras with mega-phones at partisan stadia across the peninsula or the England Band droning out ‘The Great Escape’ constantly at Wembley?
swa: Nijibuni –hivi matarumbeta yanakera zaidi ya Wana-Ultra na vipaza-sauti vyao katika viwanja vyao vya nyumbani kwenye ghuba yote Ultra au bendi ya Uingereza ikipiga wimbo wa ‘Great Escape’ pale Wembley?

eng: This tournament is being played in Africa.
swa: Mashindano haya yanafanyikia Afrika.

eng: This is what they do at football games in their country, it’s their football culture.
swa: Hivi ndivyo wanavyofanya kwenye mechi za mpira nchini kwao, ndio utamaduni wao wa mpira.

eng: If FIFA were to ban the vuvuzela then they may as well scrap the rotation policy of the World Cup and just stage it every year in Europe at times that suit the Europeans and with a European atmosphere at the stadia.
swa: Kama FIFA watayapiga marufuku mavuvuzela basi na waifute sera ya mzunguko wa Kombe la Dunia kuyaandaa mshindano hayo Ulaya kila mwaka katika muda ambao unawafaa watu wa Ulaya na hali ya hewa ya Kiulaya katika viwanja.

eng: Garreth finds the vuvuzela's noise awful and horrifying but feels that the global football community needs to explore new footballing cultures:
swa: Garreth anaziona kelele za vuvuzela zinakera na mbaya lakini anafikiri kwamba jamii ya mpira duniani inahitaji kufahamu tamaduni mpya za mpira:

eng: Even though the noise is awful (horrifying really) I’m inclined to agree with the SAFA on this one.
swa: Hata kama sauti ni mbaya napelekea kukubaliana na SAFA (Shirikisho la Mpira wa Miguu Afrika Kusini) katika hili.

eng: As much as the World Cup is about football it is also about the global football community and exploring new footballing cultures.
swa: Pamoja na kwamba Kombe la Dunia linahusu mpira, vile vile kombe hilo linahusu jamii ya mpira wa dunia na kuzijua tamaduni mpya za mpira.

eng: If I’m starting to sound a bit like a hippy here I’m sorry, but it generally is the way I feel.
swa: Kama ninaanza kuonekana kama mtu wa siasa-za-ruksa, samahani sana, lakini hivyo ndivyo ninavyooona.

eng: The vuvuzela sound is annoying and that is why walls of Jericho fell!:
swa: Sauti ya vuvuzela inaudhi na ndiyo maana kuta za Yeriko zilianguka!:

eng: The sound is annoying!
swa: Sauti hii inaudhi!

eng: That’s why the walls of Jericho fell!
swa: Ndio maana kuta za Yericho zilianguka!

eng: The people of Jericho broke the walls down on themselves to escape the blaring!
swa: Watu wa Yeriko walijiangushia kuta wenyewe ili kuzikimbia zile kelele!

eng: Death was the sweeter option.
swa: Kifo kikawa chaguo lao sawia.

eng: Now, as for those South African fans, they are ALL LUNGS!
swa: Sasa, vivyo hivyo kwa mashabiki wa Afrika Kusini, WOTE NI MAPAFU!

eng: Don’t they realize the commotion they’re creating?
swa: Je. hawajagundua kelele wanazosababisha?

eng: I’m fully aware that it is the country’s soccer culture, but it has to be done away with! Nobody will buy a ticket to have some guy blow the crap out of a vuvuzela throughout the match!
swa: Hakuna atakayenunua tiketi ili eti jamaa ampigie kelele za vuvuzela mechi nzima!

eng: Cape Town Daily Photo does not think the noise was all that bad:
swa: Mwanablogu wa Cape Town Daily Photo hafikiri kama sauti hiyo ilikuwa ni mbaya kiasi hicho:

eng: I’ve never been a fan of the vuvuzela (that long plastic trumpet that South African supporters blow at soccer matches), but to be honest, it really wasn’t so bad.
swa: Sijawahi kuwa shabiki wa mavuvuzela (Tarumbeta la plastiki ambalo mashabiki wa Afrika Kusini hupuliza wakati wa mechi za mpira wa miguu) , lakini nikiwa mkweli, haikuwa mbaya sana.

eng: They weren’t too loud and I have to say that they did add to the atmosphere significantly.
swa: Haikuwa na sauti kubwa sana na ni lazima niseme mavuvuzela yaliongeza utamu wa mechi kwa kiasi kikubwa.

eng: They are an integral part of South African soccer culture and it just wouldn’t be the same without them.
swa: Ni sehemu ya utamaduni wa soka la Afrika Kusini na haitakuwa kawaida yasipokuwepo.

eng: Getting ready for World Cup 2010?:
swa: Unajiandaa kwa Kombe la Dunia 2010?:

eng: Buy ear plugs from a music store - you’ll still be able to enjoy the atmosphere, even if you find a vuvuzela positioned right next to your ear.
swa: Nunua viziba masikio kutoka kwenye duka la muziki –utaweza kufurahia mandhari, hata kama patakuwa na vuvuzela linalopigwa pembeni ya sikio lako.

eng: If you are a fan of vuvuzela, you can visit Blow Me website to blow the virtual vuvuzela.
swa: Kama wewe ni shabiki wa mavuvuzela, unaweza kutembelea tovuti ya Blow Me na uipulize vuvuzela.

eng:
Ever wanted to ask our Son from Nyangoma any questions? 	“Umeshawahi kutaka kumuuliza kijana wetu wa Nyangoma maswali yoyote?
In other words, would you like the American president, Barack Obama to answer your questions?, begins a post at Hot Secrets blog about Obama's use of new media to engage in a conversation with ordinary Africans.
swa: Kwa maneno mengine, je ungependa Rais wa Marekani, Barack Obama ajibu maswali yako?,” ndivyo inavyoanza makala kwenye blogu ya Hot Secrets inayohusu matumizi ya Obama ya zana mpya za habari ili kukutana na kuongea na Waafrika wa kawaida.

eng: Barack Obama is visiting Ghana on 10-11 July.
swa: Barack Obama anazuru Ghana tarehe 10 mpaka 11 Julai.

eng: This will be his first historic visit to Sub-Saharan Africa and will use tools such as Twitter, Facebook and SMS to speak directly to Africans.
swa: Hii itakuwa ni ziara yake ya kwanza ya kihistoria kwenye nchi za Kusini mwa Jangwa la Sahara na atatumia nyenzo kama Twita, Facebook na Ujumbe mfupi wa Simu za kiganjani (SMS) kuzungumza moja kwa moja kwa moja na Waafrika.

eng: Erik Hersman who blogs at White African, discusses media platforms Obama intends to use to reach out to Africans beyond Ghana.
swa: Erik Hersman anayeblogu kwenye blogu ya White African, anajadili majukwaa-nyenzo ya habari ambayo Obama anakusudia kuyatumia ili kuwafikia Waafrika zaidi ya wale wa Ghana.

eng: Erik worked with the White House in developing their new media strategy for Ghana and Africa.
swa: Erik alifanya kazi na ikulu ya Marekani katika kuandaa mikakati ya nyenzo mpya za habari kwa ajili ya Ghana na Afrika.

eng: He writes:
swa: Anaandika:

eng: Radio is still the number one communications medium across Africa, and Ghana has a particularly vibrant and active one with a lot of local and national community interaction.
swa: Redio bado ni nia ya kwanza ya mawasiliano barani Afrika, na Ghana ina sekta ya redio iliyo hai na yenye kushirikisha jamii zilizo vitongojini na jamii ya kitaifa.

eng: As everyone knows, mobile phone penetration has grown at an explosive rate in Africa, this means that SMS is a fairly democratic means for getting feedback from people of every demographic across the nation. (Funnily enough, not available to US-based residents – more below on that)
swa: Kama kila mmoja anavyojua, usambaaji wa simu za kiganjani umekua kwa kasi ya mlipuko barani Afrika, hii inamaanisha kwamba Ujumbe mfupi wa Simu (SMS) ni njia ya kidemokrasia ya kupata mrejesho kutoka kwa watu wa kila hali nchini. (jambo la kuchekesha ni kuwa huduma hii haipatikani kwa wakazi waaoishi Marekani – mengine juu ya suala hili yapo chini)

eng: Lastly, there are no major homegrown web-based social networks in Ghana, and like many other countries across Africa Facebook has a decent amount of penetration.
swa: Mwisho, hakuna mtandao wa kijamii ulioazaliwa nchini Ghana, na kama ilivyo kwa nchi nyingine kote Afrika, Facebook imeweza kusambaa kwa kiwango kizuri.

eng: In Ghana, it’s at 100,000+, so it makes the most sense for the new media team to engage and interact without splitting their energy over too many services.
swa: Nchini Ghana, watumiaji ni zaidi 100,000, kwa hiyo inaleta maana sana kwa timu inayoshughulikia nyenzo za habari kuwafikia watu bila kuzisambaza nguvu zao kwenye huduma nyingi nyingine.

eng: Having Twitter on as a backup is natural, as there will be a great deal of chatter there as well.
swa: Kuwa na huduma ya Twita kama nyenzo ya akiba ni jambo linalotarajiwa, kwa sababu kutakuwa na matumizi huko vile vile.

eng: He posts details from the White House:
swa: Na anatundika habari za kina kutoka Ikulu ya Marekani:

eng: SMS.
swa: SMS.

eng: We’re launching an SMS platform to allow citizens to submit questions, comments and words of welcome (in English and in French) .
swa: Tunazindua jukwaa la SMS ili kuwaruhusu wananchi kutuma maswali, maoni na maneno ya ukaribisho (Kwa Kiingereza ama Kifaransa).

eng: Using a local SMS short code in Ghana (1731) , Nigeria (32969) , South Africa (31958) and Kenya (5683), as well as a long code across the rest of the world*, Africans and citizens worldwide will be encouraged to text their messages to the President.
swa: Kwa kutumia vifupisho vya tarakimu vya mahali husika kwa huduma ya SMS nchini Ghana (1731) , Nigeria (32969) , Afrika Kusini (31958) na Kenya (5683), vile vile kutumia tarakimu ndefu kwa ajili ya wengine wote duniani *, Waafrika na raia ulimwenguni kote watahamasika kumwandikia Rais ujumbe mfupi wa maneno.

eng: SMS participants will also be able to subscribe to speech highlights in English and French.
swa: Washiriki wa SMS wataweza pia kuomba kupatiwa dondoo za hotuba kwa Kiingereza na Kifaransa.

eng: Long numbers for mobile registration pan-Africa: 61418601934 and 45609910343.
swa: Nambari zitakazotumika kwa ajili ya kuandikisha simu za mkononi kwa Afrika ni: 61418601934 na 45609910343.

eng: Radio.
swa: Redio.

eng: A live audio stream of the President’s speech will be pushed to national and local radio stations during the speech.
swa: Hotuba ya Rais itarushwa moja kwa moja kupitia vituo vya redio vya kitaifa na vile vya kanda wakati wa hotuba.

eng: After the speech, a taped audio recording of the President’s answers to the SMS messages received will be made available to radio stations and websites.
swa: Baada ya hotuba, jumbe zote zilizorekodiwa majibu ya Rais kwa jumbe zote fupi (SMS) zilizopokelewa zitapatikana katika vituo vya redio na wavuti.

eng: The President hopes to answer a variety of questions and comments by topic and region.
swa: Rais anatarajia kujibu maswali anuai na maoni kwa mpangilio wa mada na eneo.

eng: The audio recording will also be made available for download on White House website and iTunes.
swa: Sauti zilizorekodiwa pia zitapatikana kwa ajili ya matumizi ya kila mtu atakayezihitaji kupitia wavuti ya Ikulu ya Marekani na teknolojia ya iTunes.

eng: Video.
swa: Video.

eng: The speech will be livestreamed at www.whitehouse.gov/live.
swa: Hotuba itarushwa moja kwa moja kwenye www.whitehouse.gov/live.

eng: The embed code for this video is available so you may also host the livestream on any Website.
swa: Alama-funguo za video hiyo inapatikana ili uweze kuitumia katika wavuti yoyote.

eng: Online chat.
swa: Mazungumzo ya moja kwa moja kwenye mtandao.

eng: We will host a live web chat around the speech on Facebook (it will be at http://apps.facebook.com/whitehouselive).
swa: Tutawezesha gumzo la mtandaoni linalihusu hotuba kwenye Facebook (itakuwa hapa http://apps.facebook.com/whitehouselive).

eng: The White House will also create a Facebook “event” around the speech wherein participants from around the world can engage with one another.
swa: Ikulu ya Marekani itatengeneza “tukio” la Facebook kutokana na hotuba ambapo washiriki kutoka ulimwengu mzima wanaweza kujibishana.

eng: A Twitter hashtag (i.e. #obamaghana) will also be created and promoted to consolidate input and reaction around the event.
swa: Anuani ya Twita ( #obamaghana) pia itatengenezwa na kutangazwa ili kuboresha maoni juu ya tukio hilo.

eng: Internet users can also submit questions to AllAfrica website:
swa: Watumiaji wa mtandao wanaweza kutuma maswali yao kwenye wavuti ya AllAfrica:

eng: Your chance to query President Obama about Africa:
swa: Nafasi yako ya kumuuliza Rais Obama kuhusu Afrika:

eng: What do you want to ask President Obama as he prepares to visit sub-Saharan Africa for the first time as leader of the United States - a stop in Ghana on 10-11 July?
swa: Unataka kumuuliza nini Rais Obama anapojiandaa kuitembelea Afrika ya Kusini mwa Jangwa la Sahara kwa mara ya kwanza akiwa kiongozi wa Marekani –akitua Ghana tarehe 10-11 Julai?

eng: Write your question here, and we will compile your submissions.
swa: Andika swali lako hapa, na tutakusanya maombi yenu.

eng: Please, if you would, include your age and your occupation.
swa: Tafadhali, kama ungependa, usiasahau kutaja umri na kazi unayofanya.

eng: According to Michael Wilkerson who writes at Foreign Policy blog, Obama's use of new media might boost his global approval ratings:
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Michael Wilkerson anayeandika katika blogu ya Foreign Policy, matumizi ya Obama ya nyenzo mpya za mawasiliano kunaweza kuongeza umaarufu wake duniani:

eng: With no glitches, this demonstration of interest in the views of Africans will probably boost Obama's global approval ratings, which already are almost double those of the United States.
swa: Kama hapatakuwa na matatizo, udhihirishaji huu wa kupenda kupata mitazamo ya Waafrika huenda utapandisha umaarufu wa Obama duniani, ambao tayari ni kama mara mbili ya ule wa Marekani yenyewe.

eng: At Accra's tourist market, Obama t-shirts and paintings are flying off the shelves and Ghanaians are hoping for a boost in tourism after the visit.
swa: Katika soko la kitaalii la mjini Accra, fulana za Obama na michoro zinauzwa haraka kutoka kwenye safu na Waghana wanategema kupanda kwa biashara ya utalii baada ya ziara.

eng: Ghana Pundit reports that thousands of text messages have been sent to Obama:
swa: Mwanablogu Ghana Pundit anaripoti kuwa maelfu ya jumbe za simu za viganjani yametumwa kwa Obama:

eng: US President Barack Obama has received thousands of text messages about Africa after he asked people to send questions before his trip to Ghana on Friday.
swa: Rais wa marekani amepokea maelfu ya jumbe za simu za viganjani zinazoihusu Afrika baada ya kuwataka watu kumtumia maswali kabla ya ziara yake nchini Ghana siku ya Ijumaa.

eng: A Nigerian performer impersonates Michael Jackson at a concert in Abuja.
swa: Msanii wa Kinaijeria akimuiga Michael Jackson katika tamasha mjini Abuja.

eng: Photo courtesy of N.R. on Flickr.
swa: Picha kwa hisani ya N.R kwenye huduma ya Flickr

eng: The death of American pop star Michael Jackson has sparked an outpouring of emotion from nearly every corner of the world.
swa: Kifo cha mwanamuziki maarufu wa miondoko ya Pop, Michael Jackson kimeamsha hisia kutoka karibu kila ncha ya dunia.

eng: Fans are sharing their memories of Jackson on his official site in nearly a dozen languages, and the news made the front page of papers across the globe.
swa: Mashabiki wamekuwa wakishirikishana kumbukumbu za Jackson katika wavuti yake rasmi katika lugha zaidi ya kumi, na habari hiyo ya kifo imetawala kurasa za kwanza za magazeti dunia kote.

eng: In Africa, bloggers are paying tribute to the King of Pop by posting pictures and music videos.
swa: Barani Afrika, wanablogu wanatoa heshima za mwisho kwa Mfalme wa Pop kwa kutundika picha na video za muziki.

eng: Writing from Nigeria, Oluniyi David Ajao offers a list of his 26 favorite Michael Jackson songs, while Ugandan blogger Serakelz honors Jackson's memory with instructions on how to do the moonwalk, a dance move created by Jackson.
swa: Akiandika kutokea Nigeria, Oluniyi David Ajao anatoa orodha ya nyimbo 26 anazozipenda za Michael Jackson , wakati mwanablogu wa Uganda Serekelz anaienzi kumbukumbu ya Jackson kwa maagizo ya jinsi ya kucheza dansi ya mtindo wa kutembea mwezini, ambao ni muondoko wa dansi uliobuniwa na Jackson.

eng: In Ghana, Kent Mensah of Africa News collects reactions to Jackson's passing on Twitter and Facebook:
swa: Nchini Ghana, Kent Mensah wa Africa News anakusanya miitikio wa watu kuhusu kifo cha Jackson kwenye Twitter na Facebook:

eng: “Africa loves Michael Jackson... from birth you learn how to survive and that Michael Jackson is music... the most famous musician ever,” Rasco Patterson said on twitter @chickenwang4.
swa: “Afrika inampenda Michael Jackson… tangu kuzaliwa unajifunza namna ya kujikusuru na kwamba Michael Jackson ni muziki…mwanamuziki maarufu kuliko wote,” Rasco Patterson alisema kwenye twitter @chickenwang4.

eng: “Make this world a better place for me and you these are the words from a true legend like Michael Jackson.
swa: “Ufanye ulimwengu huu uwe sehemu nzuri zaidi kwako na kwangu haya ni maneno ya kutoka kwa gwiji wa kweli kama Michael Jackson.

eng: I will always remember you Waco Jaco,” Elton Afari, Accra, Ghana said on Facebook.
swa: Nitakukumbuka daima Waco Jaco, ,” alisema Elton Afari, Accra, Ghana kwenye Facebook.

eng: Echoing the sentiments of many African fans, Sudanese Thinker remembers the pop star fondly:
swa: Akiyapa mwangwi mawazo ya mashabiki wengi wa Kiafrika Sudanese Thinker anamkumbuka mwanamuzki huyu maarufu:

eng: In a lot of ways Michael Jackson was my childhood.
swa: Kwa namna nyingi Michael Jackson alikuwa ndiyo utoto wangu.

eng: His music filled it with lots of joy and beautiful memories.
swa: Muziki wake uliujaza utoto wangu na furaha na kumbukumbu nzuri.

eng: It uplifted me when I was down.
swa: Uliniamsha nilipokuwa chini.

eng: It made me happy when I was sad.
swa: Ulinifanya niwe na furaha nilipokuwa mwenye huzuni.

eng: And as awkward and flawed as he was, I will dearly miss him and his talents.
swa: Na hata kama alikuwa mtu wa ajabu na mwenye mapungufu, nitamkosa sana yeye pamoja na vipaji vyake.

eng: And Ugandan blogger Dickson Wasake honors Jackson with a poem:
swa: Na mwanablogu wa Uganda Dickson Wasake anamkumbuka Jackson kwa shairi:

eng: On the death of Michael Jackson;
swa: Kwenye kifo cha Michael Jackson:

eng: The tears fill the earth,
swa: Machozi yameijaza dunia,

eng: Black or white;
swa: Weusi kwa Weupe;

eng: The Liberian girl cries,
swa: Msichana wa Kiliberia analia,

eng: And so does dirty Diana,
swa: Na vivyo ndivyo afanyavyo Diana mchafu,

eng: even the stranger in Moscow,
swa: hata watu baki huko Moscow,

eng: We all scream;
swa: Wote tunapayuka;

eng: “Oh it’s too bad; oh it’s too sad;
swa: “Ah ni mbaya sana; ah yatia huzuni sana;

eng: The king is gone too soon,
swa: Mfalme ametutoka mapema sana,

eng: And I just can’t stop loving him!”
swa: Na siwezi kuacha kumpenda!”

eng: Though many bloggers are grieving over Jackson's death, others are questioning his eccentricities, including his changing skin color.
swa: Ingawa wanablogu wengi wanaombolezea kifo cha Michael Jackson, wengine wanahoji vituko vyake, pamoja na kubadilisha kwake rangi ya ngozi.

eng: In Ghana, blogger Emmanuel Bensa laments:
swa: Nchini Ghana, mwanablogu Emmanuel Bensa anaomboleza kwa malalamiko:

eng: ....the African culture tells us that we don't speak ill of the dead-and I am not about to do so anytime soon, but what I will do is to categorically state how much of a bad decision it was to become a white man.
swa: ….utamaduni wa Kiafrika unatuambia kwamba hatupaswi kuwasema vibaya marehemu– na sitarajii kufanya hivyo wakati wowote hivi karibuni, lakini nitakachokifanya ni kusema katika maana halisi jinsi uamuzi ulivyokuwa mbaya wa kujigeuza kuwa mweupe.

eng: Black is beautiful-and it will forever be so.
swa: Weusi ni mzuri–na utakuwa hivyo daima.

eng: As a Black Man, Michael Jackson had the looks, the voice; the talent.
swa: Kama mtu mweusi, Michael Jackson alikuwa na wajihi, sauti; kipaji.

eng: Oh what a shame.
swa: Ah aibu gani.

eng: For Ugandan blogger Rosebell, Jackson's death prompted reflections on why the news pays so much more attention to the death of a pop star than to other tragedies:
swa: Kwa Mwanablogu wa Uganda Rosebell, kifo cha kimeamsha tafakari ya kwa nini habari zinatoa uzito mkubwa kwa kifo cha mwanamziki huyu badala ya majanga mengine:

eng: As I watched the reaction around the world to Jackson’s death I wondered if really all humans can ever be equal.
swa: Nilipokuwa nikitazama maoni ya watu duniani kote baada ya kifo cha Michael Jackson, nilijiuliza kama ni kweli binadamu wote wanaweza kuwa sawa.

eng: Not that I don’t recognise MJ’s contribution to music and his great talent, I would be naïve to do so, but I wonder why we no longer get the shock when we see death around the world.
swa: Si kwamba sitambui mchango wa MJ katika muziki na kipaji chake kikubwa, nitakuwa mwenye welewa mdogo kwa kufanya hivyo, lakini ninashangazwa iweje hatuumizwi tunapoona vifo dunia nzima.

eng: Everyone seemed to say oh he died young at 50, and then I thought that actually in Uganda life expectancy is at 50. Do you know in many African countries dying of old age is almost history?
swa: Kila mmoja anaonekana kusema ah alikufa akiwa bado kijana wa miaka 50, na nilifikiri pia kwamba katika Uganda wastani wa umri wa kuishi ni miaka 50. je unajua kuwa katika Afrika kufa kwa uzee ni historia?

eng: Do you know that this shock we feel at the loss MJ’s death, many Iraqis face it everyday?
swa: Hivi unajua kwamba taharuki hii tuliyonayo kwa kumpoteza na MJ, Wairaki wengi wanakutana nayo kila siku?

eng: The fear for the loss of their own lives and the puzzles of how their children will grow, grips people in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
swa: Hofu ya kuyapoteza maisha yao na vitendawili vya namna watoto wao watakavyokua, vinawabana watu huko Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasia ya Kongo.

eng: Omar Basawad of Safari Notes dismisses these criticisms, focusing on Jackson's legendary talent:
swa: Omar Basawad wa Safari Notes anapingana na ukosoaji huu, akitilia mkazo kipaji cha ajabu cha Jackson:

eng: Whatever might be said about Michael Jackson, whatever one might think of him - one thing is certain: he defined an era.
swa: Chochote kinaweza kusemwa kuhusu Michael Jackson, vyovyote vile mtu anavyomfikiria – jambo moja liko wazi: aliandika kielelezo cha wakati.

eng: RIP MJ, writes Kenyan blogger WildeYearnings.
swa: “Pumzika Kwa Amani” anaandika Mwanablogu wa Kenya WildeYearnings.

eng: You now have the whole sky to moonwalk on...
swa: “Sasa unalo anga zima kucheza kwa madaha kwa staili ya kutembea mwezini…”

eng: U.S. President Barack Obama gave a speech in Ghana which could be considered as his Africa policy speech.
swa: Rais wa Marekani Barack Obama alitoa hotuba yake Ghana ambayo inaweza kuchukuliwa kuwa kama hotuba ya sera yake ya Afrika.

eng: Cameroonians at home and in the diaspora have been reacting to the words pronounced by the American leader with African roots via the blogosphere.
swa: Wakameruni wa nyumbani na wale wa ughaibuni wamekuwa wakijadili maneno yaliyotamkwa na Kiongozi wa Marekani mwenye asili ya Afrika kwa kupitia ulimwengu wa blogu.

eng: The speech was published in its entirety on Up Station Mount Club which is fledgling one-stop-shop of Anglophone Cameroonian blogging.
swa: Hotuba yote ilichapishwa kwenye blogu ya Up Station Mount Club ambayo ni maarufu sana kwa wanablogu wa Kikameruni wanoblogu kwa Kiingereza.

eng: The comments give the impressions of a people appreciative of the bright speech but wary of rhetoric.
swa: Maoni yanatoa picha ya kuwa watu wameikubali hotuba hiyo angavu lakini wana wasiwasi na kauli tamu.

eng: Augustine S, a Cameroonian based in Canada seems pleased with the speech's direct attack on corruption and bad governance but wants more:
swa: Augustine S, Mkameruni anayeishi Kanada anaonekana kuridhishwa na hotuba hiyo iliyokemea ufisadi moja kwa moja pamoja na utawala mbovu lakini anataka zaidi:

eng: Speech well delivered.
swa: Hotuba ilitolewa vizuri.

eng: It was above expectations.
swa: Ilizidi matarajio.

eng: He struck on corruption and good governance, what i wanted to hear.
swa: Alizungumzia ufisadi na Utawala mzuri, ndicho ambacho nilipenda kukisikia.

eng: African leaders are stifling the progress of their own nations.
swa: Viongozi wa Afrika wanakuwa kikwazo cha maendeleo ya nchi zao.

eng: I wish his administration goes a long way to exposing corrupt African leaders, punish them by freezing their assets and issuing traveling bans on them and their families.
swa: Ninatamani Uongozi wake uende mbele zaidi kuwaumbua viongozi mafisadi wa Kiafika, uwaadhibu kwa kushikilia mali zao na kuwazuia wao na familia zao kusafiri.

eng: Obama is the kind of leader we need in this world.
swa: Obama ni aina ya kiongozi tunayemuhitaji katika dunia ya leo.

eng: Still on the issue of tackling corruption and embezzlement by African leaders Oyez has some advice to western leaders like Obama:
swa: Bado akiwa kwenye suala la kupambana na rushwa na ufujaji wa viongozi wa Afrika, Oyez ana ushauri kwa viongozi wa Magharibi kama Obama:

eng: Just two more things are required, and it will go a long way:
swa: Ni mambo mawili tu yanahitajika, na tutafika mbali:

eng: 1) Deny African rulers, their families and their lieutenants the right to foreign bank accounts and foreign property of any kind.
swa: 1) Wanyimeni Viongozi wa Kiafrika, na familia zao na maswahiba wao haki ya kuwa na akaunti za benki na mali ya aina yoyote nje ya nchi.

eng: 2) Deny African rulers any kind of medical care outside of Africa.
swa: 2) Wazuieni watawala wa Afrika kupata matibabu aina yoyote nje ya Afrika.

eng: Those are the only two things we ask the West to do, and we will take care of the rest.
swa: Hayo ni masuala mawili pekee tunayoomba Wamagharibi wayafanye, na sisi tutayashughulikia yaliyobaki.

eng: A comment left by Nnokko Johnson brings the Obama speech to Cameroon's door-steps by reminding the country's President, Paul Biya, who has been in power since 1982 and in 2008 oversaw the amendment of the constitution to cancel limitation of presidential terms:
swa: Maoni yaliyoachwa hapo na Nnokko Johnson yanaisogeza hotuba ya Obama mlangoni mwa Kameruni kwa kumkumbusha Rais wa nchi hiyo, Paul Biya, ambaye amekuwa madarakani tangu mwaka 1982 na mwaka 2008 alibadili katiba ili kuondoa ukomo wa vipindi vya Rais kukaa madarakani:

eng: Africa doesn't need strongmen, it needs strong institutions.
swa: Afrika haiwahitaji viongozi wababe, inahitaji taasisi shupavu.

eng: MR Biya please take note of this phrase and learn,we dont want u out,but we need strong institutions,please please...
swa: Bw. Biya tafadhali iangalie sana sentensi hii na ujifunze, hatusemi uondoke, lakini tunahitaji taasisi zenye nguvu, tafadhali, tafadhali…

eng: However, reading from many of the comments posted one may come out with the view that Cameroonians see Obama's speech as "good talking" that cannot solve their problems.
swa: Hatahivyo, kwa kusoma maoni mengi yaliyowekwa pale, mtu anaweza kuondoka na wazo kuwa Wakameruni wanaiona hotuba ya Obama kama “mazungumzo mazuri” ambayo hayawezi kuwatatulia matatizo yao.

eng: Emmanuel says:
swa: Emmanuel anasema:

eng: Home run.
swa: Mbio za nyumbani (goli la kisigino).

eng: Talk, talk, talk, all of it old crap, and ghoulish, to boot.
swa: Sema, sema, sema, mambo ya kizamani, yasiyosaidia.

eng: It does take two to tango. And, Africans are silly to listen to lectures on corruption from the leader of the hegemon of financial, moral and political corruption; it took two to tango with the slave trade, colonialism, and now the era of "partnership."
swa: Ni lazima muwe wawili ili kucheza tango, na Waafrika ni wazembe kusikiliza mihadhara inayohusu ufisadi kutoka kwa kiongozi wa Ufisadi wa kiuchumi, kimaadili, na kisiasa; ilihitaji watu wawili kuendesha biashara ya utumwa, ukoloni, na sasa kwenye kipindi hiki kipya cha “Ushirikiano.”

eng: Look, this talk of "partnership" is a lie.
swa: Angalia, haya mazungumzo ya “ushirikiano” ni uwongo.

eng: Only subststantive, not notional equals, can enter into partnerships.
swa: Ni walio sawa kiukweli, na sio waliosawa kinadharia ndio wanaoweza kuingia katika ubia.

eng: Reex adds:
swa: Reex anaongeza:

eng: The same rhetoric... I wonder when people stop believing and start acting... We don't need speeches on hope and pledges -they serve to anesthetize the population, that their problems shall be solved -they should hope for the solutions.
swa: Hayo hayo…Ninajiuliza ni lini watu wataapocha kuamini na kuanza kutenda… Hatuhitaji hotuba za matumaini na ahadi –zinazopumbaza watu, kwamba matatizo yao yatatatuliwa –wategemee utatuzi.

eng: When the financial crisis hit the US, the President said something similar about the responsibility of Americans to take the charge...Well contri pipo, most Americans are not even in control of their financial lives, lest responsible for the financial collapse, which were created by a greedy clique of bankers....
swa: Mgogoro wa kifedha ulipoikumba Marekani, rais alisema hayo hayo kuhusu wajibu wa Wamarekani kuchukua majukumu… Lakini jamani, Wamarekani wengi hawana mamlaka na utawala wa maisha yao ya kifedha, hawawajibiki kabisa na na anguko la kiuchumi, lililotengenezwa na genge la waroho wa benki…

eng: Well, Obama's speeches are well-written by an impressive staff to do a formidable job.
swa: Naam, Hotuba za Obama huandikwa vizuri na wafanyakazi wanaojua vyema kufanya kazi ya kuleta matumaini.

eng: What else do we expect from him?
swa: Nini kingine tukitazamie kutoka kwake?

eng: Speeches from his heart about the realities of our current world?
swa: Hotuba zinazotoka moyoni kuhusu mambo ya halisi yanayoikabili dunia yetu ya sasa?

eng: The trend of thought seems to be that, it is for Africans to solve their own problems.
swa: Mtiririko wa mawazo unaonekana kuwa huo, ni suala la Waafrika kutatua matatizo yao wenyewe.

eng: As Reex says,
swa: Kama Reex anavyosema,

eng: ...let us Africans work out our solutions.
swa: …hebu Waafrika na tutafute masuluhisho yetu.

eng: We may afterward invite Obama to share roasted corn and groundnuts at the fire side and discuss the politics on the ground - neither Ivy League stuff nor the usual double-talk demonstrated by the Western World, those speeches could be reserved to later occasions, when every hungry stomach in Africa has been filled!
swa: Tunaweza baadae kumwalika Obama kula nasi mahindi ya kuchoma na karanga karibu na moto na kujadili siasa zenyewe –siyo mambo kitaaluma ya Ivy League wala mazungumzo ya kinafiki yanayoonyeshwa na Wamagharibi, zile hotuba zingeweza kuhifadhiwa kwa ajili ya nyakati nyingine, ambapo kila tumbo lenye njaa Afrika litakuwa limeshibishwa!

eng: A comment from a visitor called Isat is less diplomatic:
swa: Maoni ya mtembeleaji anayeitwa Isat hayana diplomasia:

eng: What we should really keep as a reminder are these words:"Africa's future is up to Africans."
swa: Tunachotakiwa kukitunza kama kikumbushi ni maneno haya: “Mustakabali wa Afrika uko kwa Waafrika wenyewe.

eng: And take note: Obama is not African.
swa: Halafu angalia: Obama si Mwafrika.

eng: His grand-father who cooked for the Brits and his father were Africans.
swa: Babu yake aliyewapikia Waingereza na baba yake walikuwa Waafrika.

eng: He is American and his country's interests rule supreme - no matter how many songs we sing in his praise.
swa: Yeye ni Mmarekani na anatetea maslahi ya nchi yake –haijalishi nyimbo ngapi tunaimba kumsifia.

eng: Man wey yi get ear make yi hear.
swa: Man wey yi get ear make yi hear.

eng: The Up Station Mountain Club, collective blog also carries a post - Barack Obama in Africa: "Beyond Yes We Can", yes we must, from Cameroonian blogger Aloysius Agendia in which he exhorts Africans to make a change:
swa: Blogu ya pamoja ya Up Station Mountain Club, pia ina makala nyingine - Barack Obama akiwa Afrika: “Zaidi Ya Ndio Tunaweza”, ndio tunalazimika, kutoka kwa mwanablogu wa Kikameruni Aloysius Agendia anayewasihi Waafrika wafanye mabadiliko:

eng: Yes, Africa can revolt against current misleading leadership and their shady deals that have impoverished the continent.
swa: Ndio, Afrika inaweza kufanya mapinduzi dhidi ya uongozi potofu wa sasa na mipango yao isiyoeleweka ambayo imelisababishia bara zima umasikini.

eng: Beyond the yes, we can, yes, we must implement the said changes to move forward
swa: Zaidi ya ndio, tunaweza, ndio, ni lazima tufanyie kazi mabadiliko yanayosemwa ili kwenda mbele.

eng: This blog also gives a rythmic flavour to this visit as the video of a Cameroonian musician hailing Barack Obama on his election is posted there.
swa: Blogu hii ina vionjo vya mirindimo vya ziara hii kama video inayomwonyesha mwanamuziki wa Kikameruni akimshabikia Barack Obama kwenye uchaguzi imewekwa pale.

eng: The song was released by Tata Kingue just before Obama's inauguration in January 2009 and Gef's Outlook had done a small translation at the time.
swa: Wimbo ulitolewa na Tata Kingue kabla tu ya kuapishwa kwa Obama mwezi Januari 2009 na Gef’s Outlook imetoa tafsiri kidogo pale.

eng: On Sunday July 12th, people in the Republic of the Congo voted in an election which opposition leaders boycotted over allegations it would be neither free nor fair.
swa: Siku ya Jumapili, Julai 12, watu wa Jamhuri ya Kongo walipiga kura katika uchaguzi ambao ulisusiwa na viongozi wa Upinzani kwa madai kwamba usingekuwa huru wala wa haki.

eng: Denis Sassou N’Guesso, who has ruled the Congo for about 25 years as head of state, is seeking another seven year term in power.
swa: Denis Sassou N’Guesso, ambaye ameitawala Kongo kwa takribani miaka 25 kama mkuu wa nchi, anatafuta kipindi kingine cha miaka saba madarakani.

eng: Despite protests from the opposition, election observers said the voting was peaceful, and that voter turnout was low.
swa: Pamoja na malalamiko kutoka upinzani, waangaliaji wa uchaguzi walisema kuwa upigaji kura ufanyika kwa amani, na kwamba idadi ya watu waliojitokeza kupiga kura ilikuwa ndogo.

eng: According to the main opposition, "90 per cent" of the country’s electorate did not go to the polls.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa chama kikuu cha upinzani, “asilimia 90” ya wapiga kura hawakujitokeza kupiga kura.

eng: Outgoing President Denis Sassou N’Guesso and his Rassemblement de la majorité présidentielle (RMP) is widely tipped to win the elections as the country’s electoral commission prepares to announce the results anytime from Monday evening.
swa: Rais anayemaliza muda wake Denis Sassou N’Guesso na chama chake cha Rassemblement de la majorité présidentielle (RMP) anatabiriwa kushinda uchaguzi huo wakati ambapo tume ya uchaguzi inajiandaa kutangaza matokeo wakati wowote kuanzia Jumatatu jioni.

eng: A BBC correspondent reportedly witnessed "money being handed out at a polling station in the south of the capital, to people who later said they had been asked to vote for Mr Sassou-Nguesso."
swa: Mwandishi wa BBC anadai kuwa alishuhudia fedha zikitembezwa katika vituo vya upigaji kura kusini mwa mji mkuu, kwa watu ambao baadae walisema kuwa waliombwa kumpigia kura Bw. Sassou-Nguesso.”

eng: One election observer, speaking on condition of anonymity, told Agence France Presse, "There are more observers than voters."
swa: Mwangalizi mmoja wa uchaguzi, akizungumza kwa masharti ya kutokutajwa jina, aliliambia shirikala habari la Ufaransa (AFP), “Kuna waangalizi wengi kuliko wapiga kura.”

eng: At the French news site France 24, a few commenters from Congo have expressed their opinions on the election.
swa: Katika kituocha habari cha Ufaransa cha France 24, watoa maoni wachache kutoka Kongo wametoa maoni yao kuhusu uchaguzi.

eng: Below is a selection of a few of them:
swa: Hapa chini ni sehemu ndogo ya maoni hayo:

eng: Maloumbi on voter intimidation:
swa: Maloumbi kuhusu kutishiwa kwa wapiga kura:

eng: Swine flu or H1N1 is still making headlines across the Arab world as new cases continue to be discovered by health authorities and announced in the Press on a daily basis.
swa: Homa ya mafua ya nguruwe au H1N1 bado inatawala vichwa vya habari vya magazeti katika nchi za Kiarabu kwani wagonjwa wapya wanaendelea kugunduliwa na mamlaka za afya na kutangazwa katika vyombo vya habari kila siku.

eng: In Bahrain, Silly Bahraini Girl (which is me) is back home and surprised at what she saw at her country's airport:
swa: Huko Bahraini, Silly Bahraini Girl (ambaye ni mimi) amerudi nyumbani na kushangazwa na kile alichokiona katika kiwanja cha ndege cha nchini mwake:

eng: Reality of how mad this place has become smacks you in the face the second you land at the Bahrain International Airport and see all the ground staff wearing surgical masks, from the ground handling staff to the immigration and customs officers.
swa: Ukweli wa jinsi sehemu hii ilivyogeuka na kuwa ya kiwendawazimu unakupiga usoni sekunde ile unapotua kwenye kiwanja cha ndege cha kimataifa na kuona wafanyakazi wa ardhini wamevaa vitambaa vya kitabibu kufunika pua, kuanzia wahudumu mpaka maofisa wa uhamiaji.

eng: What's wrong with you?
swa: “Mna tatizo gani?”

eng: I ask them.
swa: Ninawauliza.

eng: Is there a plague in Bahrain?
swa: “Kuna maambukizi Bahraini?”

eng: I continue questioning the situation seemed tense and and the level of swine madness was certainly the highest I have come across everywhere I have travelled through since pig mania gripped Planet Earth.
swa: Niliendelea kuuliza hali ilionekana kuwa ngumu na kiwango cha wendawazimu wa mafua haya ya nguruwe kilikuwa juu kuliko niliyokutana nao kokote nilikosafiri tangu matatizo haya ya nguruwe yalipoikamata dunia.

eng: Why wasn't there a single person wearing a mask at the airports of San Francisco, Chicago, Toronto and Heathrow which I have travelled
swa: Kwanini hapakuwepo hata mtu mmoja aliyevaa matambara haya kwenye viwanja vya San Fransisco, Chicago, Toronto na Heathrow ambako nilisafiri

eng: through over the past few weeks?
swa: katika majuma machache yaliyopita?

eng: Still in Bahrain, Sohail Al Gosaibi smells a conspiracy in the air, noting that exaggerating the effect of swine flu benefits the media, advertising and pharmaceutical industries.
swa: Bado tukiwa Bahraini, Sohail Al Gosaibi ananusa njama kwenye hewa, anaona kwamba kukuza sana madhara ya mafua ya nguruwe kunayanufaisha mashirika ya habari, watangaza biashara na viwanda vya madawa.

eng: The Saudi blogger writes:
swa: Mwanablogu wa Kisaudia anaandika:

eng: The media almost always exaggerate the situation, remember that fears sells.
swa: Vyombo vya habari siku zote hukuza hali ya mambo, kumbuka kwamba hofu huuza.

eng: And newspapers and news channels have to sell advertising space and airtime to make money, and the more shocking and scary their stories, the more viewers and readers they have, which leads to more advertisers, and more profits.
swa: Na magazeti na idhaa za habari ni lazima viuze nafasi za matangazo na muda wa kurusha matangazo hewani ili kutengeneza fedha, na kwa kadiri habari inavyokuwa inatishia na kuogopesha ndivyo wanavyopata watazamaji na wasomaji wengi zaidi, ambavyo huongeza watangaza biashara, na faida zaidi.

eng: Al Gosaibi also quotes an article he has read and concludes:
swa: Al Gosaibi ananukuu makala aliyoisoma na kuhitimisha:

eng: According to the article, the US and UK governments have billions of dollars worth of Tamifluiflu stock that they must use within the next few months, or they’ll expire.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa makala, Serikali za Marekani na Uingereza zina hifadhi ya madawa ya Tamifluiflu yenye thamani ya mabilioni ya dola ambazo lazima wazitumie ndani ya miezi michache ijayo, vinginevyo yatapita muda wake.

eng: Interesting, huh?
swa: Inafurahisha, eeh?

eng: And speaking of theories, Jordan Reform Watch also has something up his sleeve and writes:
swa: Na akizungumzia nadharia, mwanablogu wa Jordan Reform Watch pia anacho cha kusema na kuandika:

eng: Ahhh..The swine-flu with all the accompanying conspiracy theories..A Jordanian “Scientist” specializing in diseases claims that Mecca And Medina are somehow isolated from disease, thus there is no need for the talk about the possible outbreaks that might result from the millions of pilgrims being in extreme proximity while performing Hajj.. Kill them Pigs..Go To hajj..You will be disease free..
swa: Ahhh..mafua ya nguruwe pamoja na nadharia zote za njama zinazoambatana nayo… “mwanasayansi” wa Kijordani bingwa wa magonjwa anadai kuwa Maka na Madina ziko mbali na ugonjwa huo, kwa hiyo hakuna haja ya kuzungumzia uwezekano wa mlipuko ambao unaweza kutokea kutokana na mamilioni ya mahujaji kuwa karibu karibu wakati wa hija… Uweni nguruwe…Nendeni kwenye Hija…na mtakuwa mbali na ugonjwa…

eng: Egyptian blogger Zeinobia, who blogs at Egyptian Chronicles, is also concerned about how the disease will spread during the Hajj , where millions of pilgrims from around the world converge to Mecca to perform the ritual.
swa: Mwanablogu wa Kimisri Zeinobia, anayeblogu kupitia blogu ya Egyptian Chronicles, kadhalika anaguswa na jinsi ugonjwa utakavyosambaa wakati wa Haji , ambapo mamilioni ya mahujaji kutoka sehemu mbalimbali duniani hukusanyika Maka ili kutimiza nguzo hiyo.

eng: She notes:
swa: Anaandika:

eng: the discussion about the future of Pilgrimage "Hij" and Omra this year is still debatable.
swa: majadiliano kuhusu mustakabali wa Hija na Omra mwaka huu bado ni suala linaloendelea.

eng: The minister of health wants to cancel Omra where as the minister of tourism is against the cancellation , I do not need to speak about Pilgrimage.
swa: Waziri wa Afya anataka kuifuta Omra wakati Waziri wa Utalii anapinga kufutwa huko, sihitaji kuzungumzia kuhiji.

eng: Of course the debate is much hotter among the clerics themselves.
swa: Ni kweli majadiliano ni makali miongoni mwa mashehe wa dini wenyewe.

eng: Saudi Arabia understands the challenge it is facing already and decided to deal with the situation as much as it can in the Omra and pilgrimage , it recommends that pregenant women , elderly and kids to avoid pilgrimage this year , I really respect this move.
swa: Saudia Arabia inaelewa changamoto iliyonayo tayari na imeamua kushughulikia hali hiyo kwa kadiri inavyoweza katika Omra na hija, inashauri kuwa mahujaji wajawazito, wazee na watoto waepuke kuhiji mwaka huu, Ninauheshimu uamuzi huu.

eng: I also have a better suggestion.
swa: Pia ninalo pendekezo zuri zaidi.

eng: In such circumstances why not to limit Omra and pilgrimage for the first time pilgrims only from men and women
swa: kwa nini tusiwaruhusu tu wale mahujaji wa kwanza wake kwa waume kuhudhuria Omra na Hija.

eng: Our final stop is in Syria, where blogger Yaser Arwani links to a news story which says that Syria's first swine flu case was recently reported in a Syrian doctor, who works in Australia and was on a visit to her country.
swa: Kituo chetu cha mwisho ni Syria, ambapo mwanablogu Yaser Arwani anatuunganisha na habari inayosema kwamba mgonjwa wa kwanza wa mafua wa nguruwe kuripotiwa Syria ilitaarifiwa na daktari wa Ki-Syria, anayefanya kazi Australia na alikuwa akiitembelea nchi yake.

eng: The female doctor travelled to Syria through Dubai International Airport and the disease was not detected until a few days after her arrival.
swa: Daktari huyu wa kike alisafiri kwenda Syria kupitia Uwanja wa Kimataifa wa Dubai na ugonjwa haukuwa umegunduliwa mpaka siku chache baada ya kuwasili kwake.

eng: Tshering Tobgay, the Leader of the opposition party in the National Assembly of Bhutan, comments that: "the transition to our democracy has, indeed, been uniquely smooth.
swa: Tshering Tobgay, kiongozi wa chama cha upinzani katika Bunge la Taifa la Bhutan, anatoa maoni kuwa: “mpito wetu kuelekea demokrasi, kwa hakika, umetukia bila mikwaruzo.

eng: So smooth that most of us weren’t even paying attention."
swa: Umetukia bila mikwaruzo kiasi kwamba wengi wetu walikuwa hata hawaufuatilii.”

eng: Sina Vann was 13 when she came to Cambodia from Vietnam on what was supposed to be a vacation.
swa: Sina Vann alikuwa na umri wa miaka 13 wakati alikupoja Cambodia kutoka Vietnam kwa kile kilichopaswa kuwa likizo.

eng: Instead, she was sold as a sex slave and spent the next two years in a brothel.
swa: Badala yake, aliuzwa kama mtumwa kwa ajili ya ngono na alitumia miaka miwili iliyofuata ndani ya danguro.

eng: She was freed when Somaly Mam, an anti-slavery activist and the face of the Somaly Mam Foundation, organized a raid on Vann's brothel.
swa: Alikombolewa wakati Somaly Mam, mwanaharakati wa kupinga utumwa na sura ya Taasisi ya Somaly Mam, alipopanga uvamizi kwenye danguro alilokuwa akiishi Vann.

eng: Today, Vann is an activist with the Somaly Mam Foundation, helping fellow survivors of slavery as well as those still working in brothels.
swa: Leo, Vann ni mwanaharakati wa Taasisi ya Somaly Mam, akiwasaidia wanusurika wengine wa utumwa huo pamoja na wale wanaoendelea kutaabika kwenye madanguro.

eng: For Vann's work, she was honored with the Frederick Douglass Award.
swa: Kwa kazi aliyofanya Vann, alituzwa tuzo ya Frederick Douglass.

eng: The Frederick Douglass Award "honors the tremendous resilience of the human spirit and emphasizes that many of the survivors of modern-day slavery go on to help others to freedom."
swa: Tuzo ya Frederick Douglass “huenzi uwezo wa kumudu wa roho ya binadamu na husisitiza kwamba wengi wa wanaonusurika utumwa wa ki-leo huendelea kuwasaidia na wengine kuwa huru”

eng: More of Vann's story is revealed in this video:
swa: Habari zaidi kuhusu Vann zimeonyeshwa kwenye video hii:

eng: 2009 Frederick Douglass Award Winner - Sina Vann from Free the Slaves on Vimeo.
swa: 2009 Frederick Douglass Award Winner - Sina Vann from Free the Slaves on Vimeo.

eng: Recently, the United Nations granted a one-year extension on its mandate addressing the humans rights situation in Cambodia.
swa: Mshindi wa tuzo ya mwaka 2009 ya Frederick Douglass - Sina Vann kutoka Free the Slaves katika Vimeo. Hivi karibuni, Umoja wa Mataifa uliongeza mwaka mmoja zaidi wa mamlaka yake kushughulikia hali ya haki za binadamu nchini Cambodia.

eng: According to The Mirror, the U.N. Special Rapporteur, reporting to the Human Rights Council:
swa: Kwa mujibu wa gazeti la The Mirror, mwakilishi maalumu wa Umoja wa Mataifa, akitoa taarifa kwenye Baraza la Haki za Binadamu:

eng: expressed concerns about the human rights situation in Cambodia.
swa: Alionyesha kuguswa na hali ya haki za binadamu nchini Cambodia.

eng: According to his report, the rule of law in Cambodia is weak...Also, he mentioned the case of a Sam Rainsy Party parliamentarian – from the biggest opposition party in Cambodia – Ms. Mu Sochua, who had been sentenced by a court, controlled by the government of the Cambodian People’s Party, to lose her case unjustly, because she had dared to protest against the powerful in Cambodia.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa taarifa yake, utawala wa sheria nchini Cambodia ni dhaifu...Pia, alitaja suala la Mbunge wa Chama cha Sam Rainsy –kutoka kwenye chama kikuu cha upinzani nchini Cambodia – Bi. Mu Sochua, aliyehukumiwa na mahakama, kwa shinikizo la serikali ya Chama tawala cha CPP, kupoteza kesi hiyo katika mazingira yasiyo ya haki, kwa sababu alithubutu kupinga dhidi ya wenye nguvu nchini Cambodia.

eng: Others urged the Special Rapporteur not to forget about the women and children who remain victims of sexual slavery in Cambodia, noting that it must remain a human rights priority even as other human rights violations, such as freedom of expression, surface.
swa: Wengine walimsihi Mwakilishi huyo Maalum asiwasahau wanawake na watoto ambao bado ni wahanga wa utumwa wa ngono nchini Cambodia, kwa kuzingatia kwamba hilo ni lazima libaki kuwa kipaumbele cha haki za binadamu kwa sababu uvunjifu wa haki nyingine za binadamu, mfano uhuru wa kujieleza, unaendelea kushika kasi.

eng: A selection of books from and about the Caribbean.
swa: Baadhi ya vitabu kutoka na kuhusu Karibea.

eng: Photo by Nicholas Laughlin, originally posted at Flickr under a Creative Commons license.
swa: Picha ilipigwa na Nicholas Laughlin, na ilitumwa kwanza chini ya leseni ya Flick ya Creative Commons.

eng: The anglophone Caribbean's small but energetic literary blogosphere has taken notice of a new arrival to its conversation.
swa: Kundi dogo lenye nguvu na linaloendesha blogu za kiuandishi la wanaozungumza Kiingereza huko Karibea limeng'amua uwepo wa mgeni mpya katika mijadala yake.

eng: Caribbean Book Blog, created by the St. Lucian journalist Tony Williams, aims to "inform writers and readers about the latest developments in the international book trade and how they are likely affect the literary communities in the Caribbean and other small-island states."
swa: Blogu ya Vitabu ya Karibea iliyoanzishwa na mwandishi wa habari kutoka St. Lucian, Tony Williams, ina lengo la "kuwahabarisha waandishi wa vitabu na wasomaji kuhusu maendeleo ya hivi karibuni katika biashara ya kimataifa ya vitabu na jinsi gani maendeleo hayo yanaweza kuathiri jumuiya za usomaji katika ukanda wa Karibea na visiwa dola vingine vidogovidogo."

eng: Since launching on 11 October, 2009, Caribbean Book Blog has posted a series of thoughtful, statistics-laden essays on the issues facing Caribbean publishers, writers, and readers, at a time when literary publishing around the world is grappling with financial hardship and technological change.
swa: Tangu ilipoanzishwa rasmi tarehe 11 Oktoba 2009, Caribbean Book Blog (Blogu ya Karibea ya Vitabu) imeshapandisha mfululizo wa insha zinazotafakarisha na zilizosheheni takwimu kuhusu masuala yanayowakabili wachapishaji, waandishi na wasomaji waishio Karibea, hasa katika kipindi hiki ambapo uchapishaji wa fasihi mahali pengi duniani unahangaika kutokana na matatizo ya kifedha na mabadiliko ya kiteknolojia.

eng: Williams's posts have provoked thought and discussion both in the blog's comments fields and elsewhere.
swa: Makala za William zimeamsha fikra na mijadala katika sehemu ya kutolea maoni ya blogu hiyo na kwingineko.

eng: Caribbean Book Blog began with an essay titled "Breaking the Shackles", analysing the state of Caribbean publishing and the market for Caribbean books.
swa: Blogu hiyo ya Vitabu ya Karibea ilianza na insha iliyoitwa "Kuvunja pingu”, ambapo ilichambua hali ya uchapishaji katika Karibea na masoko ya vitabu vya Karibea.

eng: Otherwise we may well be faced with a situation where our literary griots end up being relegated to a state of obscurity and irrelevance.
swa: Vinginevyo, tutajikuta tukikabiliana na hali ambayo malenga wetu wataishia kupoteza hadhi na kuingia katika hali ya uduni na kukosa maana.

eng: To avoid this they must find new mediums to draw attention to themselves and their work.
swa: Ili kukwepa hali hii hawana budi kutafuta njia mpya za kujifufua pamoja na kazi zao.

eng: In his second essay, "Now Is the Time", Williams proposes that "a group of intellectual, editorial and IT visionaries with ... pioneering spirit and the entrepreneurial drive" ought to "take up the challenge of creating an online home for our struggling writers and poets to help them stand on their feet so they in turn can help usher in a new dawn of knowledge and enlightenment."
swa: Katika insha yake ya pili, "Wakati ni huu", Williams anapendekeza kwamba "kundi la wasomi, wahariri na wasanifu wenye visheni ... wanaosukumwa na roho chipukizi na ya kijasiriamali" hawana budi "kuchukua changamoto ya kuunda mahali katika mtandao patapotumiwa na waandishi na washairi wetu wanaohangaika ili kuwasaidia waweze kusimama kwa miguu yao ili kwa upande wao nao pia walete maarifa na msisimko mpya."

eng: Several writers based in the Caribbean have joined the discussion by leaving comments.
swa: Waandishi kadhaa waishio Karibea wamejiunga kwenye mjadala huo kwa kuacha maoni yao.

eng: Antiguan novelist Joanne C. Hillhouse writes:
swa: Mtunzi wa hadithi wa Ki-Antigua, Joanne C. Hillhouse anaandika:

eng: It does take away from the time and energy I have to give to my writing, and I’m still working on finding that balance, but I’ve come to terms with the fact that self-promotion (ugly word) is part of the process and the Internet is in many ways leveling the playing field.
swa: Hiyo inapunguza muda na nguvu ambazo ningewekeza katika kazi yangu ya kuandika, bado najaribu kutafuta mizani, lakini imefika wakati nimekubaliana na ukweli kwamba kujiuza (japo ni neno baya) ni sehemu ya mchakato na kwamba Intaneti inafanya kazi kubwa ya kusawazisha uwanja wa mapambano.

eng: Jamaican poet Tanya Shirley echoes these sentiments:
swa: Mshairi wa Kijamaika Tanya Shirley anatoa maelezo yanayounga mkono hoja hiyo hapo juu:

eng: I think as Caribbean writers we are now living in an age where we have to be more proactive in the process of marketing our work and using all the resources at our disposal to do so.
swa: Nafikiri kama Waandishi wa Kikaribea sasa tunaishi katika zama ambapo hatuna budi tuwe mstari wa mbele katika mchakato wa kutafuta masoko kwa kazi zetu na kutumia chochote kile tulichonacho kinachoweza kutusaidia.

eng: What is needed is a web site that is devoted full-time to Caribbean writing.
swa: Kinachotakiwa ni tovuti itakayotumia muda wake wote kushughulikia uandishi wa Kikaribea.

eng: The site as I envision it would be a clearing house for books published by Caribbean writers.
swa: Jinsi ninavyoitazama tovuti hiyo ni kwamba, itakuwa ni kama nyumba ya kupitisha vitabu vilivyochapishwa na waandishi wa Kikaribea.

eng: Publishers would submit their catalogues, writers could upload their photos and reading dates, and readers could subscribe via RSS, newsletters, or email.
swa: Wachapishaji wataleta huko katalogi zao, waandishi watapandisha picha zao na tarehe zao za usomaji, wakati ambapo wasomaji wataweza kujiandikisha kupitia RSS, majarida, au barua pepe.

eng: Philp also lists well over a dozen Caribbean literary and scholarly journals online, some of them traditional printed journals that also maintain a web presence, and some entirely web-based.
swa: Philp pia anaorodhesha zaidi ya dazeni nzima ya majarida ya mtandaoni kuhusu Usomaji wa Kikaribea, baadhi yake yakiwa ni majarida yaliyopigwa chapa na ambayo yanaendesha kurasa zao za mitandaoni, baadhi yakiwa ni ya mtandaoni pekee.

eng: Together with a few dedicated litbloggers and writers-who-blog, these sites, Philp suggests, could evolve into the nucleus of a future web-based Caribbean publishing community.
swa: Pamoja na baadhi ya wanablogu wachache waliojitolea na waandishi-wanaoblogu, tovuti hizi, ndivyo anavyopendekeza Philp, huenda zitagetuka na kuwa kiini cha baadaye cha jumuiya ya uchapishaji ya Kikaribea iliyo ya mtandaoni.

eng: In the three and a half years since Global Voices last comprehensively surveyed the Caribbean literary blogosphere, a handful of new journals has emerged, based online and in many cases using blogging software to publish quickly and inexpensively. tongues of the ocean, based in the Bahamas and running on WordPress, was launched in early 2009 as a poetry journal, but by its third issue it also included short fiction.
swa: Katika miaka mitatu na nusu tangu Global Voices ilipofanya taftishi ya kina na kamilifu kuhusu Usomaji wa Kikaribea katika ulimwengu wa blogu, majarida kadhaa yameibuka, yakiwa ni ya mtandaoni na mara nyingi yakitumia zana za kublogu ili kuchapisha kwa haraka na pasipo gharama. Moja wapo ni tongues of the ocean, ambalo hushughulika na mashairi na huchapishwa kutokea Bahamas kwa kutumia WordPress, lilizunduliwa mapema mwaka 2009, lilipofikia toleo la tatu lilichapisha pia hadithi fupifupi.

eng: Editor Nicolette Bethel (who also writes at her personal blog) in an interview with Antilles, the blog of the Caribbean Review of Books, described being inspired by online journals based in other parts of the world:
swa: Mhariri Nicolette Bethel (ambaye pia anaandika katika blogu yake binafsi) alielezea katika mahojiano aliyofanya na Antilles, blogu ya Kikaribea inayopitia vitabu, kwamba alihamasishwa na majarida ya mtandaoni yanayochapishwa kutoka katika pande mbalimbali za dunia:

eng: I was impressed by these journals’ integration of media into their offerings, which made them a substantially different, more alive, animal from the printed page.
swa: Nilivutiwa na mfungamano wa vyombo vya habari na majarida haya katika kile yalichotoa, jambo ambalo liliyafanya yawe tofauti sana, yawe na mshawasha zaidi, yaani tofauti na yale yaliyopigwa chapa kwenye karatasi.

eng: What was missing among them?
swa: Je, nini kilikosekana miongoni mwao?

eng: An online Caribbean journal for Caribbean writers with the kind of turn-around and quick publishing record that these other online journals had.
swa: Ni jarida la mtandaoni la Kikaribea kwa ajili ya waandishi wa Kikaribea ambalo litakuwa na rekodi ya kutengeneza na kuchapisha kwa haraka, kitu ambacho kilikuwepo kwenye majarida haya mengine.

eng: In mid-2009 another blog-based magazine project went live: Zafra Lit, which translates short fiction by contemporary Cuban writers into English.
swa: Katikati ya mwaka 2009, mradi wa gazeti lingine la mtandaoni ulizinduliwa: Zafra Lit, hili hutafsiri hadithi fupifupi zilizoandikwa na waandishi WaCuba kwenda katika Kiingereza.

eng: Edited by David Iaconangelo, a student at Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore, and running on Blogger, Zafra Lit draws on the efforts of student translators who volunteer their time and skills.
swa: Gazeti linahaririwa na David Iaconangelo, ambaye ni mwanafunzi katika Chuo Kikuu cha Johns Hopkins huko Baltimore, huku likiendeshwa katika zana ya Blogger,Zafra Lit linategemea juhudi za wafasiri wanafunzi ambao wanajitolea muda na ustadi wao.

eng: An even more recent arrival is Town, launched in October 2009.
swa: Kingine kipya kuingia na kilichozinduliwa mwezi Oktoba 2009 ni Town.

eng: At Tallawah, Jamaican journalist Tyrone S. Reid posts reviews and articles covering books, music, art, and film, in an effort to "help facilitate constructive discussion."
swa: Kwenye Tallawah, makala za mwandishi wa habari wa Kijamaika Tyrone S. Reid huwa juu ya mapitio na makala za vitabu, muziki, sanaa na filamu, huku akiwa na lengo la "kushajiisha uwepo wa mijadala inayojenga."

eng: And PLEASURE, a new blog by Trinidadian writer Andre Bagoo (who also has a personal blog, Tattoo), covers "art in all its forms", including a recently launched interview series which began with UK-based Trinidadian poet Vahni Capildeo.
swa: Wakati huohuo, PLEASURE, blogu mpya ya mwandishi wa KiTrinidadi, Andre Bagoo (ambaye pia ana blogu yake binafsi, Tattoo), inashughulikia "sanaa katika miundo yake yote", ambapo hivi karibuni ilijumuisha mfululizo wa mahojiano yaliyoanza na M-Trinidad mshairi anayeishi Uingereza, Vahni Capildeo.

eng: The most energetic recent arrival in the Caribbean online literary scene may be Repeating Islands, an arts and culture blog run by two literary scholars with roots in Puerto Rico, Ivette Romero-Cesareo and Lisa Paravisini-Gebert.
swa: Pengine ingizo jingine jipya na lenye nguvu katika uwanda wa usomaji wa Kikaribea mtandaoni ni Repeating Islands, blogu ya sanaa na utamaduni inayoendeshwa na wasomi wawili wa fasihi wenye mizizi huko Puerto Rico, Ivette Romero-Cesareo na Lisa Paravisini-Gebert.

eng: Covering literature, visual arts, music, performance, cultural studies, and more, Repeating Islands posts up to six or seven new items daily: links to articles and interviews, information about new books and exhibitions, and fascinating oddments.
swa: Jarida hilo linashughulikia fasihi, sanaa ya maonyesho, muziki, sanaa za kuchora, stadi za kitamaduni, na mengine mengi. Repeating Islands hupandisha kati ya makala sita hadi saba kila siku: viungo vya makala na mahojiano, taarifa kuhusu vitabu na maonyesho, and mambo mengine mengi ya kuvutia.

eng: An online writing and publishing network like the one Caribbean Book Blog and Geoffrey Philp imagine will need this kind of breadth and enthusiasm.
swa: Aina ya mtandao wa uandishi na uchapishaji wa mtandaoni ambao Blogu ya Kikaribea ya Vitabu na Geoffrey Philp wanawazia utahitaji aina hii ya umotomoto na umahiri.

eng: A foreign man who spent the last seven months in the Beijing No. 1 Detention Center sent DANWEI a detailed account of his daily life in Jail.
swa: Raia wa kigeni ambaye alitumia muda wa miezi saba iliyopita katika jela ya Beijing No. 1 Detention Center aliitumia idhaa ya DANWEI maelezo ya kina ya maisha yake ya kila siku katika jela hiyo.

eng: This month, the Chinese press and online forums are saturated with coverage of Charles Kao’s winning of the Nobel Prize in Physics.
swa: Mwezi huu, vyombo vya habari na majukwaa ya habari za mtandaoni nchini China yalijazwa na habari za ushindi wa tuzo ya Nobel katika Fizikia ya Charles Kao.

eng: Yet another overseas Chinese scientist has snatched the prestigious prize, this temporary moment of shared glory is quickly turned into a more profound question: when would China produce its first indigenous Nobel Prize winner?
swa: Hiyo ni mara nyingine tena kwamba mwanasayansi wa Kichina anayeishi ng'ambo amejishindia tuzo hiyo yenye kuheshimiwa sana duniani, hata hivyo, furaha hiyo ya muda inaamsha swali la msingi kwamba: Ni lini hasa Uchina itajipatia mshindi wake wa kwanza anayeishi nchini humo wa Tuzo hiyo ya Nobel?

eng: A commentary on Xinhua describes this psychology:
swa: Maoni yaliyotolewa kupitia Xinhua yanaeleza hali hiyo ya kisaikolojia:

eng: Blog Action Day, codenamed #bad09 by tech gurus and geeks, is an annual event that unites the world's bloggers in posting about the same issue on the same day.
swa: Siku ya Kublogu, iliyoitwa kwa jina maalum la #bad09 na wanateknolojia pamoja na waliobobea kwenye fani, ni tukio la kila mwaka linalowaunganisha wanablogu wote ulimwenguni kwa kutundika habari zinazozungumzia suala moja katika siku hiyo.

eng: The aim of the event is to raise awareness and trigger a global discussion on that particular day.
swa: Kusudi la tukio hilo ni kuongeza ufahamu na kuanzisha mijadala ya kidunia katika siku hiyo.

eng: This year Blog Action Day took place on October 15, with bloggers all over the world writing on the topic of climate change.
swa: Siku ya Kublogu mwaka huu ilifanyika Oktoba 15, ambapo wanablogu kote duniani waliandika kuhusu mada ya mabadiliko ya hali ya hewa.

eng: Below is a round-up of the various posts by members of the Ghana Blogging Group on Blog Action Day.
swa: Hapa chini ni mkusanyiko wa makala kadhaa zilizotundikwa na wanachama wa Kikundi cha Wanablogu wa Ghana siku hiyo ya Kublogu.

eng: Gameli Adzaho, author of The Gamelian World Blog, presented a post on "5 Voices on climate Change".
swa: Gameli Adzaho, mwandishi wa Blogu ya The Gamelian World, alitoa makala inayohusu Sauti 5 kuhusu Mabadiliko ya Hali ya Hewa.

eng: In it he sampled views from five global leaders.
swa: Katika makala hiyo alitomasa maoni ya viongozi watano duniani.

eng: In his opening remarks, he talked about the significance of Blog Action Day and how “the phenomenon of climate has engaged the world's attention over the past decade, provoking debates in science, politics, business and technology.”
swa: Katika maoni yake ya kufungua, alizungumzia umuhimu wa Siku ya Kublogu Duniani na jinsi “matukio ya hali ya hewa yalivyoweza kukamata hisia na kupewa uzito ulimwenguni kote katika muongo huu uliopita, kuanzisha mijadala ya sayansi, siasa, biashara na teknolojia.”

eng: The five global leaders he discussed were former US Vice-President Al Gore, Nobel Laureate Wangari Maathai, US President Barack Obama, former UN Secretary General Kofi Annan, former Cuban President Fidel Castro.
swa: Viongozi watano wa kidunia aliowajadili walikuwa Makamu wa Rais wa zamani wa Marekani Al Gore, Mshindi wa Tuzo ya Nobeli Wangari Maathai, Rais wa Marekani Barack Obama, Katibu Mkuu wa zamani wa Umoja wa Mataifa Kofi Annan, Rais wa zamani wa Cuba Fidel Castro.

eng: Gameli ended his post with a series of questions—"What are your views on climate change?
swa: Gameli alihitimisha makala yake na mlolongo wa maswali –“Una maoni gani kuhusu mabadiliko ya Hali ya hewa?

eng: Is it for real?
swa: Je, mabadiliko haya ni ya kweli?

eng: Is it a myth?
swa: Je, ni ya kusadikika tu?

eng: In what ways do you think that the world can use its resources more sustainably?
swa: Kwa njia gani unadhani dunia inaweza kutumia raslimali zake kwa uendelevu zaidi?

eng: Can developing countries contribute to reversing climate change?"—to which he hopes to get to answers to soon.
swa: Je, nchi zinazoendelea zinaweza kuchangia katika kubadili mwelekeo wa mabadiliko haya?” – akitegemea kupata majibu mapema.

eng: Next to post on Blog Action Day was The African Women’s Development Fund (AWDF) whose contributors are AWDF, Bisi and Roselyn.
swa: Makala iliyofuata wakati wa Siku ya Kublogu Kwa Vitendo Duniani ilikuwa ni Mfuko wa Maendeleo ya Wanawake wa Afrika (AWDF) ambao wachangiaji ni Bisi na Roselyn wa AWDF.

eng: Their post related to "Climate Change and Women".
swa: Makala yao ilihusiana na “Mabadiliko ya Hali ya hewa na wanawake”.

eng: AWDF is an Africa-wide grant-making foundation for African Women.
swa: AWDF ni mfuko wa Afrika nzima wa kutoa misaada kwa wanawake wa ki-Afrika.

eng: The vision of the AWDF is for African women to live in a world in which there is social justice, equality and respect for women’s human rights.
swa: Maono ya AWDF ni kwa wanawake wa Afrika kuishi katika dunia yenye haki za kijamii, usawa na heshima kwa haki za binadamu za wanawake.

eng: They started their post by taking issue with statements made by Arun Agrawal in his paper on Social Dimensions of Climate Change, which was prepared for the Social Development Department, The World Bank, Washington DC, March 5-6, 2008.
swa: Walianza makala yao kwa kuyapembua maneno yaliyosemwa na Arun Agrawal katika mada yake kuhusu Mitizamo ya kijamii ya Mabadiliko ya dunia, iliyoandaliwa kwa ajili ya Idara ya Maendeleo ya Jamii ya Benki ya Dunia, Washington, tarehe 5 mpaka 6, mwezi Machi 2008.

eng: In his paper, Agrawal stated that “climate change will be pivotal in redefining development in the twenty-first century.
swa: Katika mada yake hiyo, Agrawal alisema kwamba “mabadiliko ya hali ya hewa yatakuwa nguzo muhimu katika kufafanua upya dhana ya maendeleo katika karne ya ishirini na moja.

eng: How nations, societies, communities, and households respond to the impacts of climate changes and variability to which the world has already been committed will in many instances determine their prospects for growth, equity, and sustainability”.
swa: Jinsi gani mataifa, jamii, jumuiya na familia zitakavyochukua hatua dhidi ya athari za mabadiliko ya hali ya hewa na namna mbalimbali ambazo dunia tayari imeshajihusisha nazo kwa namna nyingi zitatapelekea matarajio yao katika mafanikio ukuaji, usawa na uendelevu”.

eng: AWDF views climate change as an environmental change, which is also driven by humans—fundamentally a human problem.
swa: AWDF inayatazama mabadiliko ya hali ya hewa kama mabadiliko ya mazingira, ambayo yanaharakishwa pia na binadamu –kimsingi likiwa tatizo la mwanadamu.

eng: The impacts of climate change are expected to seriously (and disproportionately) affect the livelihoods, health, and educational opportunities of people living in poverty.
swa: Athari za mabadiliko ya hali ya hewa zinatarajiwa kuathiri vibaya zaidi (na pasipo uwiano) mwenendo wa maisha, afya, na fursa za kielimu kwa watu wanaoishi kwenye ufukara.

eng: AWDF also made a few recommendations for dealing with the situation.
swa: AWDF ilitoa maoni yake machache ya namna ya kukabiliana na tatizo.

eng: Kajsa Hallberg Adu, co-founder of Ghana Blogging Group and author of the Rain In Africa blog, had a lot to say on Blog Action Day, but was shocked at "how not current the topic is in Ghana".
swa: Kajsa Hallberg Adu, mwanzilishi mshiriki wa Ghana Blogging Group na mwandishi wa blogu ya Rain In Africa, alikuwa na mengi ya kusema katika Siku ya Kublogu Duniani, lakini alistushwa na “namna ambavyo mada hii isivyokuwa na umuhimu katika wakati uliopo nchini Ghana”.

eng: Kajsa laments the absence of Ghana from a web site counting down to the UN Climate Change Summit and asks: "Really, when was the last time you heard someone discuss climate change around here?"
swa: Kajsa analalamikia kutokuwepo kwa Ghana kwenye wavuti ya Mkutano wa Umoja wa Mataifa unaohusu Mabadiliko ya Hali ya hewa na kuuliza: “Kweli, lini mara ya mwisho umesikia mtu akijadili mabadiliko ya hali ya hewa hapa?”

eng: Yet Ghana came in for some special praise from Kasja:
swa: Hata hivyo Ghana ilipewa sifa maalumu na Kasja:

eng: A way to globally reduce the carbon dioxide emissions is to make sure we travel with public transport rather than individually in our own cars.
swa: Njia ya kupunguza utoaji wa hewa ya ukaa ni kuhakikisha tunasafiri kwa usafiri wa umma badala ya kutumia usafiri binafsi kwenye magari yetu.

eng: Today, many Ghanaians travel in packed trotros, shared taxis or "Kufuor busses" and hence do not emit too much CO2.
swa: Leo, Waghana wengi wanasafiri kwa usafiri wa umma, taxi za kuchangia au “mabasi vya Kufour ” na hivyo hawatoi sana hewa ya ukaa.

eng: Can we say the same about the North/West?
swa: Je, tunaweza kusema hivi hivi pia kwa nchi za Kaskazini na Magharibi?

eng: But as Ghanaians grow richer - our goal is to become a middle income country as soon as possible - more Ghanaians can also afford their own cars.
swa: Lakini kwa kadri Waghana wanavyokuwa matajiri –lengo letu likiwa kuwa nchi ya kipato cha kati mapema iwezekanavyo –Waghana wengi wanaweza pia kumudu kuwa na magari yao wenyewe.

eng: In my opinion the problem in the discussion about climate change is that while developed countries are struggling to be sustainable, developing countries are already klimatsmarta, but not by choice.
swa: Kwa maoni yangu tatizo linalojitokeza katika mjadala kuhusu mabadiliko ya hali ya hewa ni kwamba wakati nchi zilizoendelea zinafanya bidii kuwa endelevu, nchi zinazoendelea tayari zipo klimatsmarta, sio kwa kuchagua.

eng: Rather the "environmental consciousness" or sustainable living is caused by last year's topic; poverty.
swa: Ila “uelewa wa kimazingira” ama maisha endelevu unasababishwa na mada ya mwaka jana; umasikini.

eng: Finally, Edward Tagoe, author of Tagoe Blogger blog and also a software developer-cum-poet, decided to share with his readers an interesting website called YOURENEW.COM. According to Edward, the site "is the perfect place for you to recycle or sell used cell phones, mp3 players, digital cameras and graphing calculators.
swa: Mwisho, Edward Tagoe, mwandishi wa Blogu ya Tagoe ambaye pia ni mshairi na mtengeneza nyenzo pepe, aliamua kuwashirikisha wasomaji wake wavuti yake nzuri iitwayo YOURENEW.COM. Kwa mujibu wa Edward, wavuti hiyo “ni sehemu muafaka ya kubadilisha ama kuuza simu, kicheza mziki cha mp3, kamera za dijitali na tarakilishi.

eng: You can also recycle and sell laptops, video game console, external hard drive, video game or DVD.
swa: Unaweza pia kuharibu na kuuza kompyuta za mapajani, michezo ya kompyuta, nyenzo ngumu za kompyuta na DVD.

eng: If you can’t find your device in our catalogue or we can’t pay for it, you can always ship it for free and we’ll recycle it safely.
swa: Kama huwezi kupata kifaa chako kwenye orodha ama hatuwezi kukilipia, unaweza kukituma bure na sisi tutakiharibu kw ausalama.

eng: So look up your device today, go green and get green!
swa: Kwa hivyo angalia kifaa chako leo, kuwa kijani na uwe kijani!

eng: So look up your device today and go green!"
swa: Kwa hiyo angalia kifaa unachotumia na kuwa kijani!”

eng: Also take note, October 24th, 2009 has been designated the International Day of Climate Action by 350.org.
swa: Pia zingatia, Oktoba 24, 2009 ni siku iliyopewa jina la Siku ya Dunia ya Kuchukua hatua za Hali ya Hewa na wavuti ya 350.org.

eng: Repeating Islands reports on the murder of four Haitians in the Dominican Republic.
swa: Repeating Islands anaripoti kuhusu mauaji ya Wahaiti wanne katika Jamhuri ya Dominica

eng: One Japanese in six is living in poverty says the latest Welfare Ministry report .
swa: Mjapani mmoja kati ya sita anaishi katika umasikini inasema ripoti mpya ya Wizara ya Ustawi wa Jamii .

eng: According to OECD figures , Japan has one of the highest poverty rates in the developed world and is 4th after only Mexico, Turkey and the U.S.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa takwimu za OECD, Japan ina kiwango kikubwa zaidi cha umasikini katika dunia iliyoendelea na ni ya 4 baada tu ya Mexico, Uturuki na Marekani.
