eng: By Flickr id: Ushio Shugo
swa: Na Flickr: Ushio Shugo

eng: In September, Makoto Yuasa, Secretary-general of Anti Poverty Network (反貧困 Han Hinkon) , had already pointed to the problem explaining Japan's poverty issue in this way :
swa: Mnamo mwezi wa Septemba, Makoto Yuasa, Katibu mkuu wa Mtandao wa Kupinga Umaskini (反貧困 Han Hinkon) , alilionyesha tatizo kwa kufafanua tatizo la umaskini nchini Japan kwa njia hii :

eng: Ever since the high economic growth of the 1960s, Japan has inhabited the myth that all Japanese people belong to the middle class.
swa: Tangu ukuaji mkubwa wa uchumi katika miaka ya 1960, Japan imerithi hadithi za ngano kuwa watu wote wa Japan wamo katika tabaka la kati (kiuchumi).

eng: However, Japanese-style employment, which is at the heart of this myth, has been transformed by the increase in nonregular employment and other factors, and a growing number of Japanese live in poverty.
swa: Hata hivyo, mtindo wa ajira wa Kijapani, ambao upo katikati ya ngano hii, umebadilishwa kutokana na ongezeko la ajira holela na sababu nyingine, na idadi inayoongezeka ya Wajapani wanaishi katika umaskini.

eng: As many debate on their blogs, nowadays the income gap in Japan is far from being new.
swa: Kama wengi wanavyojadili katika blogu zao, tofauti za mapato nchini Japan siku hizi si jambo jipya.

eng: When the economic Bubble burst in the early 90s it revealed the weaknesses in the Japanese system and since then many experts say the country has never completely recovered from recession.
swa: Wakati futuzo la uchumi lilipopasuka mwanzoni mwa miaka ya 90 udhaifu uliopo kwenye mfumo wa Kijapani ulionekana na tangu hapo wataalamu wengi wanasema kuwa nchi haijapona kutoka kwenye hali mbaya ya uchumi.

eng: Ysaki suggests how this problem has always existed but have been regarded by most Japanese as a somebody else's problem.
swa: Ysaki anaeleza jinsi tatizo hili lilivyoendelea kuwepo na jinsi lilivyochukuliwa na Wajapani wengi kana kwamba ni tatizo la watu wengine.

eng: Malaysia’s Prime Minister Najib Tun Razak introduced the One Malaysia concept, popularly referred as 1Malaysia, when he took office.
swa: Waziri Mkuu wa Malaysia Najib Tun Razak ameanzisha wazo la Malaysia Moja, maarufu kama Malaysia1, alipoingia madarakani.

eng: Being a multi-racial country, the main aim of 1Malaysia is to promote national unity and to strengthen the ties between various ethnic groups.
swa: Ikiwa ni nchi ya watu wa rangi tofauti, lengo kubwa la Malaysia1 ni kuukuza umoja wa kitaifa na kuimarisha ushirikiano baina ya makundi mbali mbali yenye rangi tofauti.

eng: 1Toilet policy is based on the 1Malaysia concept
swa: Sera ya Msala1 imeiga dhana ya Malaysia1

eng: Borrowing the branding of 1Malaysia, the state government of Terengganu recently introduces the '1Toilet' policy as a move for both teachers and students (of the same gender) to share toilets to promote a sense of oneness.
swa: Kwa kuiga chapa ya Malaysia1, serikali ya Jimbo la Terengganu hivi majuzi ilikuja na sera ya ‘msala 1’ kama hatua kwa walimu na wanafunzi (wa jinsia moja) kuchangia misala (vyoo) ili kukuza hisia za umoja.

eng: “When students share the toilets with the teacher, they (students) will believe that they are on par with academicians and this automatically invokes a sense of being important to an organisation, which, in this case, is the school,” says State Education, Higher Learning, Human Resource, Science and Technology Committee chairman Ahmad Razif Abd Rahman in local daily The Star.
swa: “Pale wanafunzi wanapochangia msala na mwalimu, wataamini (wanafunzi) kwamba wako sawa na wanataaluma na hii moja kwa moja huamsha hisia za kujichukulia kuwa na umuhimu katika taasisi, ambako, kwa mukhtadha huu, ni shule,” anasema mwenyekiti wa Kamati ya Elimu, Elimu ya Juu, Rasilimali watu, Sayansi na Teknolojia wa Jimbo hilo, Ahmad Razif Abd Rahman katika gazeti la mahali hapo la The Star.

eng: The policy will also extend beyond the loo as teachers are also encouraged to eat at the school’s cafeteria with the students.
swa: Sera pia itapanuliwa zaidi ya suala la choo ambapo walimu pia wanashauriwa kula katika mikahawa ya shule pamoja na wanafunzi.

eng: It is a way for both parties to mingle during recess.
swa: Ni njia ya makundi hayo mawili (walimu na wanafunzi) kujichanganya wakati wa mapumziko.

eng: There were mixed reactions from the blogosphere regarding this topic.
swa: Kumekuwa na maoni tofauti kutoka kwenye ulimwengu wa blogu kuhusiana na mada hii.

eng: Some took it as a joke, while others thought it was a positive initiative.
swa: Wengine waliichukulia kama utani, wakati wengine walifikiri ilikuwa ni ubunifu chanya.

eng: Jeff Ooi, who is a prominent blogger and now a Member of Parliament says:
swa: Jeff Ooi, ambaye ni mwanablogu mkubwa na sasa ni Mbunge anasema:

eng: This time, 1Malaysia's product extension is where you pee.
swa: Wakati huu, matunda ya kupanuka kwa Malaysia1 yako mahali pa kujisaidia.

eng: Life And Ti(m)es Of Liang Seng could not believe that the state government is actually introducing the 1Toilet concept:
swa: Mwanablogu wa Life And Ti(m)es Of Liang Seng hakuweza kuamini kwamba Serikali ya Jimbo hilo inakuja na wazo la ‘Msala mmoja’:

eng: I would understand the sharing of canteen part.
swa: Ningeelewa sehemu ya kuchangia mkahawa.

eng: But to share toilet to instill a sense of belonging and create excellence?
swa: Lakini hivi kweli kuchangia msala ni kukuza hisia za ushirikiano na kujenga mafanikio ya kitaaluma?

eng: Come on.
swa: Tuwe wakweli.

eng: We can do better.
swa: Tunaweza kufanya vyema zaidi.

eng: Journalist, blogger and Global Voices author Niki Cheong writes in his personal blog:
swa: Mwandishi wa habari, mwanablogu na mwandishi wa Global Voices Niki Cheong anaandika kwenye blogu yake binafsi:

eng: Which nutcase came up with this brilliant idea I think sharing a toilet with the teacher won’t help a student excel in his or her studies, proper teaching will!
swa: Kichaa yupi alikuja na wazo hili zuri Nadhani kuchangia msala na mwalimu hakutamsadia mwanafunzi kufanikiwa katika masomo yake, ufundishaji mzuri unaweza!

eng: What’s the heck is going on?
swa: Ni nini kinachoendelea?

eng: Are we going to have to start eating 1ton mee after this?
swa: Je, tunaenda kuanza kula ‘chakula kimoja’ baada ya hapa?

eng: Or only listen to 1Buck Short?
swa: Au kuanza kusikiliza ‘1 Buck Short’?

eng: Or are we going to get people registering names like 1Sharina for birth certificates?
swa: Au tutaanza kuwataka watu kuandikisha majina kama ‘Sharina1’ kwenye vyeti vya kuzaliwa?

eng: Thots Here And There believes that leaders should walk the talk before implementing any policies:
swa: Mwanablogu wa Thots Here And There anaamini kwamba viongozi ni lazima watende wayasemayo kabla ya kutekeleza sera zozote:

eng: Why don't we start with the elite groups first before going to the majority?
swa: Kwa nini tusianze na makundi ya tabaka la juu kwanza kabla kwenda kwa walio wengi?

eng: In my school, the upper crust get a special key to their own special toilet I know in certain companies in the private sectors there is such a privilege too.
swa: Shuleni kwangu, Kundi la tabaka juu hupata ufunguo maalumu kwa choo chao maalumu Najua kwenye makampuni fulani ya sekta binafsi kuna upendeleo wa namna hiyo pia.

eng: I remember a friend being all excited because he had reached that privileged level of having his own key to that special place!
swa: Nakumbuka rafiki yangu alipofurahi sana kwa sababu alikuwa amefikia kiwango cha upendeleo wa kuwa na ufunguo wake mwenyewe wa sehemu hiyo malum!

eng: Now, if we want to implement such a thing as 1toilet in school - imagine queueing up with the students to use the toilet - let us start with the upper level of administrators first.
swa: Sasa, kama tunataka kutekeleza kitu kama hiki cha msala mmoja shuleni –fikiria wanafunzi watakavyopanga foleni kutumia msala –hebu na tuanze na kundi la juu la watumishi kwanza.

eng: Leaders talk about 1Malaysia...come on, walk the talk.
swa: Viongozi wanazungumza kuhusu Malaysia1 ...tuwe wakweli, fanya usemacho.

eng: Show us, leaders of Malaysia that we are one in all ways inclusive in the use of toilet!!!!
swa: Tuonyesheni, enyi viongozi wa Malaysia kwamba sisi tu kitu kimoja kwa namna zote zinazoshirikisha matumizi ya msala!!!!

eng: Voices Inside My Head explains the positive aspect of the 1Toilet policy:
swa: Mwanablogu wa Voices Inside My Head anaeleza upande chanya wa sera ya msala1:

eng: When I was in school I did wonder the same thing, how come teachers get to pee in seperate toilets.
swa: Wakati nilipokuwa shuleni nilijiuliza jambo hili hili, inakuwaje walimu wajisaidie kwenye vyoo tofauti.

eng: Do they pee differently?
swa: Hivi wanajisaidia kwa namna tofauti?

eng: Do they have something else we don’t have?
swa: Hivi wana kitu kinginecho tusichokuwanacho sisi?

eng: I think it should be done across the board, even at work places top management sharing the same toilets!
swa: Nadhani inatakiwa kufanyika pote, hata kwenye maeneo ya kazi ya utawala wa juu watumie vyoo hivyo hivyo!

eng: Perhaps even ministers should share the same toilets as other government staff and that’s when I would really say our politicians are walking the talk!
swa: Labda hata mawaziri washirikiane vyoo na wafanyakazi wengine wa serikali na hapo ndipo nitakaposema wanasiasa wetu wanatenda wasemacho!

eng: This author, via his personal blog, says:
swa: Mwandishi huyu, kupitia kwenye blogu yake binafsi, anasema:

eng: Teachers should also lead by example and getting the best from their students.
swa: Walimu pia wanapaswa kuongoza kwa mifano na kupata matokeo mazuri kwa wanafunzi wao.

eng: If a student is already having an inferiority complex feeling in the classroom, how can he/she invoke a sense of importance with the 1Toilet policy?
swa: Kama mwanafunzi tayari ana tatizo la kujisikia duni awapo darasani, atawezaje kuibuka na hisia za kujiona wa maana kwa sera ya Msala1?

eng: Do we have to share the toilet to have a feeling of oneness between students and teachers?
swa: Hivi tunatakiwa kuchangia msala ili kuwa na hisia za umoja baina ya wanafunzi na walimu?

eng: Should this solidarity start in the classroom itself?
swa: Je, ushirikiano huu wapaswa kuanzia darasani kwenyewe?

eng: Last week, in Hammond, Louisiana, Beth Humphrey (who is white) and Terence McKay (who is black) applied for a marriage license and were refused on the basis of their races.
swa: Juma lililopita, huko Hammond, Louisiana, Beth Humphrey (ambaye ni mzungu) na Terence McKay (ambaye ni mweusi) walituma maombi ya kupata cheti cha ndoa na walinyimwa kwa misingi ya rangi zao.

eng: The justice of the peace, Keith Bardwell, claimed that in his experience, "interracial marriages do not last long" and stated that he was "doing it for the children."
swa: Afisa wa kutathmini na uandikishaji (Muamuzi wa Amani), Keith Bardwell, alidai kwamba katika uzoefu wake, “ndoa za rangi tofauti hazidumu kwa muda mrefu” na akasema alikuwa “akiamua hivyo kwa ajili ya watoto wa wanandoa hao”.

eng: Jim Crow laws which required separate facilities for black and white Americans ended in 1965, and anti-miscegenation laws that forbade interracial marriage or sex ended in all states by 1967.
swa: “Sheria za Jim Crow” ambazo ziliwataka Wamerekani weusi na weupe kuwa na huduma tofauti zilikomeshwa mwaka 1965, na sheria zilizozuia ndoa na mahusiano ya kimapenzi kati ya watu wenye rangi tofauti zilikomeshwa katika majimbo yote ya Marekani mwaka 1967.

eng: But racism still exists.
swa: Lakini ubaguzi wa rangi bado upo.

eng: Although much of the time it lies beneath the surface, occasionally racism rears its ugly head in a way that is impossible to miss; this story made headlines across the United States, prompting blog posts from the local community and beyond.
swa: Ingawa muda mwingi huwa upo chini ya ardh, mara nyingine ubaguzi huo hunyanyua kichwa chake kibaya kwa namna ambayo si haiwezekani kutoonekana; habari hii ilitawala vichwa vya habari katika vyombo vya habari nchini kote Marekani, na kusababisha makala za wanablogu kutokea kwenye jamii za sehemu hizo na zaidi.

eng: In response to Bardwell's "defense" that he marries black couples all the time, the anti-racist blog Stuff White People Do expressed outrage, saying:
swa: Katika majibu yaliyotokana na “utetezi” wa Bardwell kwamba huwafungisha ndoa watu weusi mara zote, blogu ya kupinga ubaguzi wa rangi iitwayo Stuff White People Do ilionyesha kuchukizwa kwake, kwa kusema:

eng: Well, how thoroughly magnanimous of you, Justice Bardwell.
swa: Sawa, u mtenda haki na mema wa namna gani, Jaji Bardwell.

eng: Not to mention, intrusively paternalistic.
swa: Bila kutaja, uingiliaji wako (katika maisha ya watu) na ubaba wa kulazimisha.

eng: Speaking of Bardwell's house, which I'm sure is just overrun with joyous hordes of black and white children carousing together, he also had this to say:
swa: Nikizungumzia nyumba ya Bardwell, ambayo nina hakika imezidiwa na kundi kubwa lenye furaha la watoto weusi kwa weupe wakicheza pamoja, alikuwa na haya pia ya kusema:

eng: I have piles and piles of black friends.
swa: Nina mabiwi na mabiwi ya marafiki weusi.

eng: They come to my home, I marry them, they use my bathroom.
swa: Huja nyumbani kwangu, ninawaoza, wanatumia msala wangu.

eng: I treat them just like everyone else.
swa: Ninawafanyia kama ninavyomfanyia yeyote.

eng: Ah yes, black friends too, piles of them.
swa: Mh ndio, marafiki weusi pia, wengi mno.

eng: Right there, in his bathroom!
swa: Pale kwake, hadi bafuni kwake!

eng: A commenter on the blog, Siditty (who also wrote her own post here), touched on the irony of Bardwell's anger:
swa: Mtoa maoni kwenye blogu hiyo, Siditty (ambaye pia aliandika makala yake hapa), aligusia hali ya kinyume cha hasira ya Bardwell:

eng: I always wonder about a man who comes from Louisiana, who has a strong history of race mixing, through the system of placage as well as creole culture, is now all the sudden concerned about the children.
swa: Huwa ninajiuliza kuhusu mtu ambaye katokea Louisiana, mwenye historia ndefu ya kujichanganya na watu wa rangi tofauti, kwa kupitia mfumo wa utamaduni wa ukazi kati ya watu weupe na wanawake weusi (placage) kadhalika na utamaduni mchanganyiko wa jamii ya Kispania na Kifaransa nma Weusi (Creole), sasa hivi ghafla tu anaonekana kujali sana watoto.

eng: They weren't concerned in the 1700s, he shouldn't be now.
swa: Jamii yake haikuwa inajali hivi kwenye miaka ya 1700, hapaswi kuwa hivyo anavyodai leo.

eng: The blog Racism Review countered Bardwell's "concern for the children" with evidence on children of interracial relationships:
swa: Blogu ya Racism Review ililichachafya suala la Bardwell “ kujali watoto” kwa ushahidi wa watoto waliotakana na uhusiano wa rangi tofauti:

eng: And, to further review the evidence, children of interracial marriages do not suffer in when compared to other children provided that they grow up in an environment that’s accepting of diversity and children of interracial marriages.
swa: Na, ili kuutazama zaidi ushahidi, watoto wa ndoa za wenzi wenye tofauti ya rangi huwa hawateseki ukilinganisha na watoto wengine kwa kigezo kwamba wanakulia katika mazingira yanayokubali tofauti za watu na watoto wa ndoa za rangi tofauti.

eng: If children of interracial marriages encounter racism (and other structural disadvantages), then they’re more likely to experience stress, and health-related risks due to that increased stress, such as smoking and drinking.
swa: Kama watoto wa namna hii watakutana na ubaguzi wa rangi (na matatizo mengine ya kimfumo), basi wana uwezekano mkubwa wa kukumbana na msongo, matatizo ya kiafya yanayohusiana na msongo wa mawazo, kama vile uvutaji sigara na matumizi ya madawa ya kulevya.

eng: That’s a result of racism, and yet another reason to work to end racism.
swa: Hayo ndiyo matokeo ya ubaguzi wa rangi, na hiyo ni sababu nyingine ya kufanya kazi ili kuukomesha ubaguzi wa rangi.

eng: It should not be used – turning logic on its head – as a reason to perpetuate racism.
swa: Isitumike – kwa kupindua mantiki juu chini –kama sababu ya kuendeleza ubaguzi.

eng: And Black Girl in Maine touched on the "what about the kids?" question as well, noting the experiences of her own biracial son:
swa: Na Black Girl in Maine aligusia pia kuhusu swali la “vipi kuhusu watoto?”, kwa kuelezea uzoefu wa mwanae ambaye ni chotara:

eng: As for the kids, what about the kids?
swa: Na kwa watoto, vipi kuhusu watoto?

eng: Yes, biracial kids sometimes catch flack from others but not always and I think among the youth today its almost considered cool to be biracial.
swa: Ndio, watoto chotara mara nyingine hupata usumbufu kutoka kwa wengine lakini sio mara zote na nadhani kati ya vijana wa leo inaonekana poa sana kuwa chotara.

eng: As a buddy mentioned to me my son most certainly doesn’t suffer from a lack of friends male or female.
swa: Kama rafiki yangu alivyoniambia mwanangu hapati matatizo na kupata marafiki wa kiume na wa kike.

eng: I think the only time biracial kids have real issues is when they have no one to talk to them about their roots.
swa: Nadhani wakati pekee ambapo watoto machotara huweza kupata shida ni pale wanapokosa mtu wa kuongea nao kuhusu asili yao.

eng: I think when kids are connected to their historical roots as well as community, it creates a safe space for them.
swa: Nadhani wakati ambapo watoto wameunganishwa na historia ya asili yao na ya jamii yao, hiyo huwatengenezea nafasi salama kwao.

eng: In the United States, anti-miscegenation laws in many states banned the marriage of white Americans to black Americans (and Americans of some other ethnicities) in a number of states.
swa: Nchini Marekani, sheria ya kuwazuia watu wa rangi tofauti kuoana ama kuwa na uhusiano wa kimapenzi katika majimbo mengi ilipiga marufuku ndoa za Wamarekani weupe na Wamerekani weusi (na wale wa asili nyinginezo) katika majimbo kadhaa.

eng: While in some states, these laws were repealed as early as 1780, in sixteen states the laws were not repealed until a 1967 case, Loving vs. Virginia, in which an interracial couple who had married in Washington, D.C. were arrested in their own bedroom.
swa: Wakati katika majimbo mengine, sheria hizi zilibatilishwa mwanzoni mwa miaka ya 1780, katika majimbo 16 sheria hizi hazikuondoshwa mpaka wakati wa kesi ya mwaka 1967 , kati ya Loving na Virginia, ambapo wenzi hawa wa rangi tofauti waliokuwa wameoana mjini Washington, D.C walitiwa chini ya ulinzi kwenye chumba chao cha kulala.

eng: Their legal battle made it all the way to the U.S. Supreme Court, at which point the laws were overturned.
swa: Vita yao ya kisheria ilifika mpaka Mahakama Kuu ya Marekani, ambapo sheria hizi zilifika mahali zikatupiliwa mbali.

eng: A number of bloggers touched on the legal aspects of the case.
swa: Wanablogu kadhaa waligusia mtazamo wa kisheria kwa suala hili.

eng: One blogger, Jay Says, writes:
swa: Mwanablogu mmoja, Jay Says, anaandika:

eng: As a Justice of the Peace, he should be aware that interracial marriage is not illegal anymore – having been deemed unconstitutional 40 years ago.
swa: Kama Jaji wa masuala ya Amani, anatakiwa kuelewa kwamba ndoa za rangi tofauti si kinyume cha sheria tena – baada ya kuonekana ni kinyume cha katiba miaka 40 iliyopita.

eng: This particular instance hits home after this weekends National Equality March wherein I briefly interviewed an straight, interracial couple, the Newmans (pictured) about why they are marching.
swa: Tukio hili limegusa hisia baada ya Maandamano ya Usawa Kitaifa mwishoni mwa wiki ambapo nilifanya mahojiano mafupi na wanandoa wa rangi tofauti, Bwana na Bibi Newman (pichani) kuhusu kwa nini wanaandamana.

eng: Racism, classism, sexism, homophobia, religious intolerance and other biases can and do exist in our society, but they must not exist under the law.
swa: Ubaguzi wa rangi, Uwepo wa matabaka, Ubaguzi wa watu wa jinsia tofauti, Hofu ya Ushoga, Kutovumiliana kidini pamoja na upendeleo wa aina nyingine vinaweza kuwapo na vipo katika jamii yetu, lakini havipaswi kuwepo kisheria.

eng: To allow an employee of the government who is paid by the taxes of the “free” people of the United States (or in this case, a state in the United States) to use his/her own personal beliefs to decide matters governed by civil law is abhorrent.
swa: Kumruhusu mwajiriwa wa Serikali anayelipwa kwa kodi za watu “huru” wa Marekani (au katika mukhtadha huu jimbo lililo nchini Marekani) kutumia imani zake binafsi kuamua masuala yanayotawaliwa kwa sheria za kiraia ni kichefuchefu.

eng: If he doesn’t agree with interracial marriage, he needs to find a new job – perhaps Grand Master of the Ku Klux Klan?
swa: Kama hakubaliani na ndoa za rangi tofauti, basi anahitaji kutafuta kazi nyingine –labda Mkuu wa Ku Klux Klan?

eng: Finally, one blogger has taken the opportunity to turn this incident into a moment of learning.
swa: Mwisho, mwanablogu mmoja amechukua fursa ya kuligeuza suala hili kuwa wakati muafaka wa kujifunza.

eng: The blogger, whose blog is called What Do I Know?, begs readers to think about their own feelings on the subject:
swa: Yeye, ambaye blogu yake inatwa Ni Nini Ninachojua?, anawasihi wasomaji kufikiri kuhusu hisia zao wenyewe kuhusu mada husika:

eng: If you doubt that racism still lives inside us all, consider your reaction to the idea of marrying outside your race, particularly if you are white and the other race is black.
swa: Kama una wasi wasi kwamba ubaguzi wa rangi bado unaishi ndani yetu wote, fikiria unavyojisikia unapopata wazo la kuoa au kuolewa nje ya watu wa rangi yako, hasa wewe ukiwa ni mzungu na mwingine ni mweusi.

eng: Yeah, it's ok for other people, but wouldn't you find some good, rational reasons why your daughter would be making her life far more difficult when she brings home her black fiance?
swa: Ndio, ni sawa kwa watu wengine, lakini hivi usingetafuta sababu nzuri zenye hoja zinzoshawishi za kuelezea kwa nini binti yako atayafanya maisha yake yawe magumu sana atakapomleta nyumbani mchumba wake mweusi?

eng: Be honest.
swa: Kuwa mkweli.

eng: Even if you said, "No problem" didn't you hesitate just a little?
swa: Hata kama ulisema, “Hakuna shida” hivi kweli haukusita hata kidogo kupata jibu?

eng: If you didn't you're unusual.
swa: Kama haikuwa hivyo, basi wewe si wa kawaida.

eng: With Bardwell now saying that he won't resign over the matter, one thing is certain: there is surely more news to come.
swa: Wakati Bardwell anasema sasa kuwa hatajiuzulu kwa sababu ya suala hili, jambo moja ni la hakika: bila ya shaka kuna habari zaidi zaja.

eng: After seeing pictures of Cameroon's first lady, Egyptian Zeinobia remarks: "I do not how much money she spent on her hair and her looks but I know the people of Cameroon need this money more."
swa: Baada ya kuziangalia picha za mke wa Rais wa Cameroon, Mmisri Zeinobia anasema: “Sijui ni ni kiasi gani cha pesa alichotumia kwa ajili ya nywele zake na muonekano wake lakini ninafahamu kuwa watu wa Camerron wanazihitaji zaidi hizo pesa.”

eng: A campaign has been launched to end forced sterilisation in Namibia: "A coalition of civil society organisations has called on Namibians to join a campaign condemning the sterilisation of women living with HIV without their informed consent."
swa: Kampeni ya kukomesha Chanjo kwa kulazimishwa nchini Namibia imezinduliwa: “ umoja wa Asasi za kijamii umetoa wito kwa Wanamibia wote kujiunga na kampeni ya kulaani chanjo kwa wanawake waishio na VVU bila ya ridhaa yao.

eng: At Do Unto Others, Samuel Nichols writes that Israeli military patrols have started setting fire to cars which are caught trying to cross the border from the West Bank into Israel.
swa: Kwenye Do Unto Others, Samuel Nichols anaandika kuwa doria ya jeshi la Israel imeanza kuchoma moto magari ambayo yanakamatwa yakijaribu kuvuka mpaka kutoka Ukanda wa Magharibikuingia Israel.

eng: He posts a video here.
swa: Ametundika video hapa.

eng: This is the first roundup of Somali blogs in 2009.
swa: Huu ni muhtasari wa kwanza wa blogu za Kisomali mwaka 2009.

eng: Yes, it's been more than a year since I took leave a long leave from blogging but now I'm back, for good.
swa: Naam, ni zaidi ya mwaka mmoja tangu nilipochukua likizo ya muda mrefu kutoka kwenye shughuli za kublogu lakini sasa nimerudi, moja kwa moja.

eng: This is the first post and expect more posts about Somali blogosphere.
swa: Hii ni makala ya kwanza na tarajieni makala zaidi zinazohusu ulimwengu wa blogu za Kisomali.

eng: Blogger Royale Somalia profiles a young female Somali doctor in Mogadishu who'd graduated last year, he writes:
swa: Mwanablogu Royale Somalia anatoa wasifu wa daktari mdogo wa kike jijini Mogadishu ambaye alimaliza masomo mwaka jana, anaandika:

eng: In December 2008, 20 Somali students overcame huge odds and graduated from medical school in Mogadishu—the first batch to do so for almost two decades in the failed Horn of Africa state.
swa: Mwezi Desemba mwaka 2008, wanafunzi 20 walishinda vigezo vikubwa na kufuzu kutoka chuo cha uganga huko Mogadishu – kundi la kwanza kufanya hivyo katika takriban miongo miwili ndani ya nchi iliyoshindwa katika pembe ya Afrika.

eng: Dr. Hafsa Abdurrahman Mohamed, 26, was one of those receiving a diploma from the capital’s Benadir University.
swa: Dr. Hafsa Abdurrahman Mohamed, 26, alikuwa ni mmoja wa waliopokea stashada kutoka katika Chuo Kikuu cha Benadir jijini humo.

eng: Upon completing her studies, she decided to work for the Doctors Without Borders/Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), using her skills to help provide free medical care in Somalia.
swa: Wakati anamaliza masomo yake aliamua kufanya kazi kwa Waganga Wasio na Mipaka/ Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), kwa kutumia ujuzi wake ili kutoa huduma za bure za afya nchini Somalia.

eng: The East African Philosopher comments on Somali President Sharif Ahmed's visit to US and the US government's policy shift in dealing with Sharif:
swa: Mwanafalsafa wa Afrika ya Mashariki anatoa maoni juu ya ziara ya Rais Sharif Ahmed nchini Marekani na mabadiliko ya sera ya serikali ya Marekani katika mahusiano yake na Sharif:

eng: In December of 2006 Sheikh Sharif Sheikh Ahmed, currently only-in-name president of the Transitional Federal Government of Somalia, was on the run from the Ethiopian army, the CIA, and the U.S. Rangers.
swa: Mwezi Desemba 2006, Sheikh Sharif Sheikh Ahmed, ambaye hivi sasa ni rais-kwa-jina-tu wa Serikali ya Mpito ya Shirikisho la Somalia, alikuwa analikimbia jeshi la Ethiopia, CIA, pamoja na wanamgambo wa Marekani.

eng: East African Philisophers continues:
swa: Mwanafalsafa wa Afrika ya Mashariki anaendelea:

eng: This week Sheikh Sharif is in Minneapolis, MN (and the home of this crazy congresswoman) meeting with Congressmen, Governor, and city councilmen/mayor.
swa: Wiki hii Sheikh Sharif yuko Minneapolis, MN (na nyumbani kwa mbunge mwendawazimu wa kike wa bunge la chini la Marekani) anakutana na wabunge, Gavana na madiwani/Meya.

eng: Couple of months ago he had a meeting with Secretary Clinton in Nairobi during her Africa trip.
swa: Miezi miwili iliyopita alikuwa na mkutano na Katibu Clinton jijini Naorobi wakati wa ziara yake ya Afrika.

eng: From terrorist to president for Sheikh Sharif in just two years.
swa: Kutokea gaidi mpaka kuwa rais kwa Sheikh Sharif katika miaka miwili.

eng: That, friends, must be a first.
swa: Jambo hilo, marafiki, ni lazima limetokea kwa mara ya kwanza.

eng: To me this says a lot about the U.S.’s awful foreign policy than anything else.
swa: Kwangu mimi hili linaongea vikubwa kuhusu sera mbaya ya nchi za nje ya Marekani zaidi ya jingine lolote.

eng: The Kenya Somali Blog says Somali government is recruiting Somali youth from Kenya:
swa: The Kenya Somali Blog anasema kuwa Serikali ya Somalia inawaandikisha vijana wa Kisomali kutoka Kenya:

eng: Somalia's U.N.-backed government has recruited more than 170 young Kenyans and former servicemen to help it fight rebels in the failed Horn of Africa state, local leaders in eastern Kenya said.
swa: Serikali ya Somalia inayoungwa mkono na Umoja wa Mataifa imewaandikisha zadi ya vijana 170 wa Kikenya na wanamgambo wa zamani ili wakasaidie kupigana na waasi katika nchi iliyoshindwa ya pembe ya Afrika, viongozi walio katika maeneo ya mashariki ya Kenya wamesema.

eng: Mohamed Gabow, the mayor of Garissa, told Reuters the enrolment of ethnic Somali Kenyans was being conducted at a home in Bulla Iftin village, on the outskirts of his town.
swa: Mohamed Gabow, Meya wa Garissa, aliiambia Reuters kuwa uandikishaji huo wa vijana wa Kikenya wenye asili ya Kisomali ulikuwa unafanywa katika nyumba moja kwenye kijiji cha Bulla Iftin, kilichopo pembezoni mwa mji wake.

eng: The recruitment is not a secret.
swa: Uandikishaji huo sio siri.

eng: Those involved are not worried.
swa: Wanaohusika hawaogopi.

eng: They are going around all the villages to announce the exercise," Gabow said in an interview late on Thursday.
swa: Wanakwenda vijijini kote kutangaza zoezi hilo,” Gabow alisema katika mahojiano siku ya Alhamis.

eng: Omar Mushawah reported the arrest of Haytham al-Maleh, a Syrian lawyer and human rights advocate who also spent 6 years in prison in the period between 1980 and 1986 for demanding constitutional reforms.
swa: Omar Mushawah ameripoti kukamatwa kwa Haytham al-Maleh, mwanasheria wa Ki-Syria na mtetezi wa haki za binaadamu ambaye pia alitumia muda wa miaka 6 jela kati ya 1980 na 1986 kwa kudai mabadiliko ya kikatiba.

eng: Al-Maleh is also a co-founder of the Syrian Human Rights Society.
swa: Al-Maleh pia ni mwanzilishi mwenza wa Jumuiya ya Haki za Binaadamu ya Syria.

eng:
Trinidad and Tobago is a wealthy small island developing nation rich in oil and natural gas. 	“Trinidad na Tobago ni kisiwa tajiri na nchi inayoendelea tajiri kwa mafuta na gesi asilia.

eng: Every day that I go through the news I become more convinced that I want to quit the 'I am a Trini' club and head off to somewhere else: Coffeewallah has had it with everything from crime to taxes.
swa: “Kila siku ambayo ninapitia habari ninazidi kushawishika kuwa ninataka kuachana na klabu ya ‘Mimi ni Mtrini’ na kwenda sehemu nyingine”: Coffeewallah ameshachoka na kila kitu kuanzia uhalifu mpaka kodi.

eng: What does a woman sacrifice for the cause she fights for?
swa: Je, mwanamke anatoa sadaka zipi ili kupigania jambo analiamini?

eng: How are her children affected by persecution taken against her?
swa: Je, watoto wake wanaathiriwa vipi na mateso yanayoelekezwa kwake?

eng: This post explores briefly the lives of women activists in Asia who are also mothers.
swa: Makala hii inachambua kwa kifupi maisha ya wanawake wanaharakati katika Asia ambao pia ni ma-mama (wazazi).

eng: Irene Fernandez is a women and migrant rights activist in Malaysia.
swa: Irene Fernandez ni mwanamke na mwanaharakati anayepigania haki za wahamiaji nchini Malaysia.

eng: For more than ten years, Irene has been faced with a ‘criminal defamation’ charge (which has now been dropped) for having published a memorandum, asking the Malaysian government to look into alleged atrocities taking place in migrant camps in the country.
swa: Kwa zaidi ya miaka kumi, Irene amekuwa akikabiliwa na mashtaka ya 'uhalifu wa kuvunjia heshima" (ambayo kwa sasa yamefutwa) baada ya kuchapisha memoranda akiihimiza serikali ya Maylasia kuchunguza tuhuma za mateso yanayofanywa katika kambi za wakimbizi nchini humo.

eng: Aside from being an activist, which had led to her receiving the Right Livelihood Award in 2005, Irene is also a mother to three children, Camverra Jose Maliamauv, Tania Jo and Katrina Jorene, and several foster children.
swa: Licha ya kuwa mwanaharakati, jambo ambalo limempatia tuzo ya Right Livelihood mwaka 2005, Irene pia ni mama wa watoto watatu, Camverra Jose Maliamauv, Tania Jo na Katrina Jorene, mlezi wa watoto wengine kadhaa.

eng: It is hard to imagine what goes on the mind of an activist like Irene, when she thinks of her children.
swa: Ni vigumu kufikiri kuhusu yale yanayopita kwenye vichwa vya wanaharakati kama Irene, hasa pale anapowawaza watoto wake.

eng: During her sentencing at the initial trial in 2003, Irene was reported to have said:
swa: Wakati alipokuwa akisomewa hukumu mwanzoni mwa mashtaka mwaka 2003, Irene aliripotiwa kusema:

eng: I want my children and the children of all the people I work with as head of Tenaganita to enjoy and live in a society that is peaceful, where we do not fear state violence.
swa: Nataka watoto wangu na watoto wa watu wote ninaofanya kazi nao kama kiongozi wa Tenaganita kufurahia na kuishi katika jamii iliyo na amani, ambapo hatuogopi misukosuko inayosababishwa na dola.

eng: Irene’s role as a mother perhaps can best be reflected in the eyes of her daughter, Katrina Jorene, who wrote on the Micah Mandate (a Christian-based blog seeking to raise public interest advocacy):
swa: Pengine dhima ya Irene kama mama inaelezwa vizuri zaidi katika macho ya binti yake, Katrina Jorene, ambaye aliandika katika blogu inayoitwa Micah Mandate (blogu ya Kikristu inayolenga kuamsha utetezi wa umma):

eng: I celebrate my mother who brought me up to be constantly vigilant in life and to be clear and maddeningly persistent for the truth and for what is just, true and right.
swa: Ninampongeza mama yangu ambaye alinilea niwe mstahimilivu katika maisha na kuwa wazi na king'ang'anizi wa kutafuta ukweli na katika haki, kweli na haki.

eng: I celebrate the countless heroes who have been present in my life especially my family members and the family at Tenaganita .
swa: Ninawapongeza mashujaa wasio na idadi ambao nimekuwa nao maishani mwangu, hasa wanafamilia yangu na familia ya Tenaganita .

eng: I celebrate all who have worked silently, tirelessly and with so much care all these years for the greater good of others.
swa: Ninawapongeza wote waliofanya kazi kimya kimya, pasipo kuchoka na kwa umakini mkubwa kwa miaka yote hii ili kupigania manufaa ya umma mpana zaidi.

eng: It appears Irene’s teachings have caused at least one of her children to take on the same activist mantle as herself.
swa: Yaelekea mafunzo ya Irene yamemvuta walau mmoja wa watoto wake kuchukua mrengo wa uanaharakati kama alivyo yeye mwenyewe.

eng: Now Katrina writes advocacy pieces dealing with minority rights and protection.
swa: Hivi sasa Katrina huandika makala mbalimbali zinazohusiana na haki na utetezi wa walio wachache katika jamii.

eng: Unlike Katrina Jorene, unfortunately, Alexander and Kim Aris, sons of Nobel Peace Prize laureate, Aung San Suu Kyi, have not had the opportunity to learn from their mother for more than a decade.
swa: Tofauti na ilivyo kwa Katrina Jorene, kwa bahati mbaya, Alexander na Kim Aris, watoto wa mshindi wa Tuzo ya Amani ya Nobel, Aung San Suu Kyi, hawakupata bahati ya kujifunza kutoka kwa mama yao kwa zaid ya muongo mmoja sasa.

eng: So strong was Ms Suu Kyi’s passion for Myanmar, she has spent close to fourteen years under detention in a lakeside villa in Yangon, choosing to stay for fear that the military junta would not allow her in again if she left.
swa: Mapenzi ya Bibi Suu Kyi kwa nchi yake ya Myanmar yamekuwa makubwa kiasi kwamba ametumikia kifungo cha nyumbani kwa takribani miaka kumi na nne katika nyumba iliyo kandokando ya ziwa huko Yangon, ambapo amechagua kuishi kwa kuhofia kwamba huenda utawala wa mabavu wa kijeshi hautamruhusu tena kurudi ikiwa atatoka.

eng: Womensphere, a blog by and about women, writes:
swa: Blogu inayohusu wanawake ya Womensphere inaandika:

eng: British husband, the Oxford scholar, Michael Aris, died of cancer in 1999 at the age of 53.
swa: Mume wa Bibi Suu Kyi, aliyekuwa raia wa Uingereza na mkufunzi katika Chuo Kikuu cha Oxford, Michael Aris, alifariki kwa kansa mwaka 1999 akiwa na umri wa miaka 53.

eng: She was unable to see him as he was dying – the junta refused to give him an entry visa, and she feared that, if she left Burma, she would not be allowed back in.
swa: Mama huyu hakuweza kumwona mumewe wakati alipokuwa anafariki - serikali ya kijeshi ilimkatalia mume huyo viza ya kuingia nchini, wakati kwa upande wake mama huyo naye alihofia kutoka Burma, kwamba pengine asingeruhusiwa kurudi tena nchini humo.

eng: She has not seen either of her two sons, now men in their thirties, for a decade.
swa: Kwa hiyo hajakutana na watoto wake wawili, ambao hivi sasa wana umri wa zaidi ya miaka thelathini, kwa zaidi ya muongo mmoja sasa.

eng: Little has been written about (or by) Alexander or Kim.
swa: Kuna machache sana yaliyoandikwa juu ya (au kuandikwa na) Alexanderson au Kim.

eng: However, in 1991, Ms Suu Kyi’s older son, Alexander, accepted the Nobel Peace Prize in Oslo on her behalf.
swa: Hata hivyo, mnamo mwaka 1991, mtoto mkubwa wa Bibi Suu Kyi, Alexander, alipokea tuzo ya Amani ya Nobel huko Oslo kwa niaba ya mama yake.

eng: Again, looking through the lens of her child, we might be able to better understand Ms Suu Kyi as a mother:
swa: Hapa tena, tunaweza kutumia lensi za mtoto huyu ili kupata kumwelewa vema zaidi Bibi Suu Kyi kama mama:

eng: Speaking as her son, however, I would add that I personally believe that by her own dedication and personal sacrifice she has come to be a worthy symbol through whom the plight of all the people of Burma may be recognised.
swa: Nikizungumza kama mtoto wake, ningependa kuongeza kwamba mimi binafsi naamini kwamba kwa kujitolea kwake na kutoa sadaka yake binafsi, ametokea kuwa alama yenye thamani ambapo kupitia kwake, mateso ya watu wote wa Burma yametambulika.

eng: And no one must underestimate that plight.
swa: Na, hakuna aliye na haki ya kuyapuuza mateso hayo.

eng: We must also remember that lonely struggle taking place in a heavily guarded compound in Rangoon is part of the much larger struggle, worldwide, for the emancipation of the human spirit from political tyranny and psychological subjection.
swa: Pia tukumbuke kwamba, mapambano yake akiwa katika upweke wake huku akiwa chini ya ulinzi mkali katika makazi yake ya huko Rangoon ni sehemu ya mapambano mapana zaidi, ulimwengu kote, katika kutafuta kuikomboa roho ya kibinadamu kutoka katika tawala za kimabavu za kisiasa na manyanyaso ya kisaikolojia.

eng: Although my mother is often described as a political dissident who strives by peaceful means for democratic change, we should remember that her quest is basically spiritual.
swa: Ingawa mama yangu anaelezwa mara nyingi kama mpigania haki za kisiasa na ambaye anajaribu kwa njia za amani kuleta mabadiliko ya kidemokrasia, hatuna budi kukumbuka kwamba mapambano yake, kimsingi, ni ya kiroho.

eng: It is my hope that soon my mother will be able to share this feeling and to speak directly for herself instead of through me.
swa: Ni matumaini yangu kwamba hivi karibuni mama yangu ataweza kuwashirikisha hisia zake na kuzungumza moja kwa moja yeye mwenyewe badala ya kuzungumza kupitia kwangu.

eng: Meanwhile, many activist mothers in Asia still face persecution.
swa: Wakati huo huo, wanawake wengi wanaharakati barani Asia wanaendelea kukabili mateso.

eng: For example, Fan Guijuan, whose house was said to have been demolished as a result of the Shanghai World Expo project, was arrested in Beijing and sent back to Shanghai, placed immediately in detention.
swa: Kwa mfano, Fan Guijuan, ambaye nyumba yake iliamriwa kubomolewa sababu ya Mradi wa Shangai World Expo, alikamatwa huko Beijing na kurejeshwa Shanghai, na kisha kuwekwa kizuizini.

eng: Her son has no place to live, due to the demolition.
swa: Mtoto wake wa kiume hana mahali pa kuishi, kwa sababu ya bomoabomoa hiyo.

eng: Meanwhile, in the Philippines, Dr Edita Burgos, mother of Jonas Burgos, fights for justice for her activist son, who is said to have desaparecido (“disappeared”).
swa: Wakati huohuo, huko Ufilipino, Dkt Edita Burgos, ambaye ni mama wa Jonas Burgos, anapigania haki ya mtoto wake huyo mwanaharakati, ambaye inasemekana "ametoweka".

eng: Dr Burgos is the chair of Desaparecidos (Families of Desaparecidos for Justice), an organization seeking justice for the many unaccounted for, said to be a hallmark of the Arroyo regime.
swa: Dkt Burgos ni mwenyekiti wa chama cha haki za Familia za watu Waliotoweka, yaani asasi inayotafuta haki za watu waliopoteza maisha yao pasipo kujulikana, jambo ambalo linasemekana ni kielelezo cha utawala wa Arroyo.

eng: Now, in Iran, humanitarian activist mothers are fast becoming global icons for human rights causes worldwide.
swa: Hivi sasa, huko Irani, akina mama wanaharakati wa haki za binadamu, wanazidi kuwa alama za ulimwengu katika kupigiania haki za binadamu ulimwenguni kote.

eng: In silent public protest, the ‘Mourning Mothers of Iran,’ known in Tehran as the ‘Mothers of Laleh,’ peaceably seek justice for their dead or incarcerated children.
swa: Katika mgomo baridi wa kimyakimya ulioshirikisha umma, 'Akina Mama Wanaoomboleza wa Irani', ambao wanajulikana huko Tehran kama "Akina Mama wa Laleh", kwa njia za amani wanatafuta haki kwa ajili ya watoto wao waliokufa au waliofungwa.

eng: “A mother is a mother as long as she lives.”
swa: “Mama ni mama ili mradi tu aishi.”

eng: As predicted, president Zine Al Abidine Ben Ali won the Tunisian elections for a fifth term.
swa: Kama ilivyotabiriwa, rais Zine Al Abidine Ben Ali ameshinda uchaguzi kwa mara ya tano.

eng: What wasn't expected was that he would win with 89.62 per cent of the over all votes.
swa: Ambalo halikutarajiwa ni kuwa angeshinda kwa asilimia 89.62 ya kura zote.

eng: The prediction was that he would garner more votes.
swa: Utabiri ulikuwa kwamba angepata kura zaidi.

eng: Ben Ali's ruling party, the Democratic Constitutional Rally, also fared as well.
swa: Chama kinachotawala cha Ben Ali, Democratic Constitutional Rally nacho pia kilifanya vizuri.

eng: It won 161 of the 214 parliament seats.
swa: Kilishinda viti vya bunge 161 katika viti 214.

eng: The remaining 53 seats were won by six different parties: Movement for Democratic Socialists, 16 seats; Party of People's Unity, led by Mohamed Bouchiha, 12 seats; Ahmed Inoubli's Union of Democratic Unionists, 9 seats; Social Liberal Party, 8 seats; Party of Greens for Progress, 6 seats and Ahmed Brahim’s Ettajdid Party, 2 seats.
swa: Viti 53 vilivyobaki vilinyakuliwa na vyama sita tofauti: Movement for Democratic Socialists, viti 16; Party of People's Unity, kinachoongozwa na Mohamed Bouchiha, viti 12; chama cha Union of Democratic Unionists cha Ahmed Inoubli, viti 9; Social Liberal Party, viti 8; Party of Greens for Progress, viti 6 na chama cha Ettajdid cha and Ahmed Brahim, viti 2.

eng: The ruling party announced the fairness and the impartiality of the 2009 elections.
swa: Chama tawala kilitangaza haki na usawa katika uchaguzi wa 2009.

eng: But opposition leaders and bloggers have another opinion: they think that repressive acts and stifling controls on the election process have characterized the 2009 presidential and legislative elections in Tunisia on October 25, 2009.
swa: Lakini viongozi wa upinzani na wanablogu wana maoni mengine: wanafikiri kuwa vitendo vya ukandamizaji na udhibiti mkali kwenye taratibu za uchaguzi vilitawala uchaguzi wa rais na wabunge nchini Tunisia mnamo tarehe 25, Oktoba 2009.

eng: لإنتصر الرئيس بسبعة و سبعين في المية
swa: Arabasta anasema kwa kejeli:

eng: The Ugandan anti gay bill has been tabled in parliament and now it awaits the president Yoweri Museveni to sign and make homosexuality officially illegal.
swa: Muswada wa kupinga ushoga nchini Uganda umepelekwa bungeni na sasa unamsubiri Rais Yoweri Museveni kutia saini ili kuufanya ushoga kuwa ni kinyume na sheria.

eng: The previous code was not clear but now the bill called "The anti homosexuality Bill 2009" tabled by a member of parliament David Bahati which states that any homosexuality act or tendencies might face the death penalty or face life imprisonment.
swa: Sheria ya awali haikuwa wazi sana lakini sasa muswada unaoitwa ‘Muswada wa kupinga ushoga wa mwaka 2009’ ulioletwa na mbunge David Bahati unaosema kwamba tendo lolote la ushoga ama tabia za kishoga zinaweza kuhukumiwa adhabu ya kifo ama kifungo cha jela.

eng: The Ugandan writes:
swa: The Ugandan anaandika:

eng: The multiple laws that I will be breaking as soon as the president signs this law.
swa: Nitakuwa nikiwaleteeni sheria kadhaa mara tu rais atakapoitia saini sheria hii.

eng: Well, our detractors had already said that we would be stiffed with a tougher law, but this goes way beyond that.
swa: Naam, wabaya wetu wameshasema tunatakiwa kudhibitiwa kwa sheria ngumu zaidi, lakini hili linaenda mbali zaidi ya hapo.

eng: If I attempt to commit the offense… (god, the number of times that I have made passes and they have been rejected!)
swa: Nikijaribu kufanya kosa...(mungu, mara ambazo nimetongoza na kukataliwa!)

eng: Each of those times was worth 7 years in jail.
swa: Kila moja ya mara hizo inastahili miaka 7 jela.

eng: Good heavens!!!!
swa: Mbingu nzuri!!!!

eng: Before, we could be liable to life imprisonment. gug hereby declares that, when the President of the Republic signs this law, gug will be liable to the death penalty… because I and my lover are serial offenders, breaking this law.
swa: Kabla, tungeweza kustahili kufungwa kifungo cha maisha. gug anatangaza kwamba, Rais wa Jamhuri atakapoisaini sheria hii, gug atakuwa anastahili adhabu ya kifo...kwa sababu mimi na mpenzi wangu ni wakosaji, tunaivunja sheria hii.

eng: The bill further prohibits adoption by gay couples; any person who aids, promotes counsels any acts of homosexuality in any way will face up to seven years imprisonment, or risk a fine of sh100m.
swa: Mswada pia unawazuia mashoga waliooana kuasili watoto; mtu yeyote anayesaidia, anayetetea ktuoa ushauri wa kisheria kwa tendo lolote la kishoga kwa namna yoyote atakabiliwa na adhabu ya kifungo kisichozidi miaka saba, au kutozwa faini ya shilingi milioni 100 za Uganda.

eng: It states the ill effects of homosexuality as:
swa: Muswada unasema kwamba madhara ya ushoga ni pamoja na:

eng: Research indicates that the homosexuality has a variety of negative consequences including higher incidences of violence, sexually transmitted diseases, and use of drugs.
swa: Utafiti unaonyesha kwamba ushoga una madhara mabaya yafuatayo pamoja na uwezekano wa matumizi zaidi ya nguvu, magonjwa ya zinaa, na matumizi ya madawa ya kulevya.

eng: The higher incidence of separation and break-up in homosexual relationships also creates a highly unstable environment for children raised by homosexuals through adoption or otherwise, and can have profound psychological consequences on those children.
swa: Uwezekano wa kutengana na kuachana katika mahusiano ya kishoga pia yanasababisha mazingira yasiyoaminika kwa watoto wanaolelewa na mashoga kwa kuasili ama vinginevyo, na yanaweza kuwa na matokeo mabaya kisaikolojia kwa watoto hao.

eng: In addition, the promotion of homosexual behavior undermines our traditional family values.
swa: Na zaidi ya hayo, kutetea tabia za kishoga kunaharibu maadili yetu ya asili ya kifamilia.

eng: Given Uganda’s historical, legal, cultural and religious values which maintain that the family, based on marriage between a man and a woman is the basic unit of society.
swa: Kwa kuzingatia historia, sheria, utamaduni na maadili ya kidini ambayo yanasema kwamba familia, yenye misingi ya ndoa baina ya mwanaume na mwanamke ni kiini cha jamii.

eng: This Bill aims at strengthening the nation’s capacity to deal with emerging internal and external threats to the traditional heterosexual family.
swa: Muswada huu unakusudia kuimarisha uwezo wa nchi wa kupambana na matishio yanayoanza kujitokeza ya ndani na nje dhidi ya familia za kitamaduni baina ya watu wa jinsia tofauti.

eng: These threats include: redefining human rights to elevate homosexual and transgender behavior as legally protected categories of people.
swa: Matishio haya yanajumuisha: dhana mpya wa haki za binadamu inayozipa nafasi tabia za mahusiano ya jinsia moja na tabia za kujibadilisha jinsia kuwa makundi ya watu yanayolindwa kisheria.

eng: There is also need to protect our children and youths who are made vulnerable to sexual abuse and deviation as a result of cultural changes, uncensored information technologies, parentless child developmental settings and increasing attempts by homosexuals to raise children in homosexual relationships through adoption, foster care, or otherwise.
swa: Aidha kuna hitaji la kuwalinda watoto wetu na vijana wanaofanywa kuwa wepesi kudhurika na ukatili wa kingono na kuharibiwa maadili yao kama matokeo ya mabadiliko ya kiutamaduni, teknolojia holela ya habari, ukuaji wa watoto bila wazazi na kuongezeka kwa majaribio ya mashoga kulea watoto katika mahusiano ya jinsia moja kwa njia ya kuasili, malezi ya kambo, ama vinginevyo.

eng: Producers, publishers and distributors of material containing homosexuality especially if a business, an NGO will have its certificate or registration canceled and the director will face seven years in prison.
swa: Waandaaji, wachapaji na wasambazaji wa kazi zenye mambo ya kishoga hasa kama ni biashara, asasi hiyo isiyo ya kiserikali (AZISE) itafutiwa leseni ama usajili wake na mkurugenzi wake atakabiliwa na kifungo cha miaka saba jela.

eng: That includes gay blogs in Uganda:
swa: Hii inajumuisha blogu za mashoga nchini Uganda:

eng: Poor sympathizers.
swa: Masikini wale wanaowaunga mkono.

eng: You are not left to love us.
swa: Hamjakosea kutupenda.

eng: No, all lovers of gays, and gays in Uganda will suffer, and be punished by this law.
swa: Hapana, wapenzi wote wa mashoga, na mashoga wote Uganda watataabika, na kuadhibiwa na sheria hii.

eng: Any press conferences?
swa: Mkutano wowote na waandishi wa habari?

eng: Not by gay Ugandans.
swa: Hautaitishwa na mashoga wa Kiganda.

eng: You see, we are a pariah people that will never be like all other Ugandans.
swa: Unaona, sisi ni watu waliotengwa ambao hatuwezi kufanana kamwe na Waganda wengine.

eng: Ha ha ha ha ha!
swa: Ha ha ha ha ha!

eng: Oh, the gayuganda blog is one of the things which are illegal, as per that bill.
swa: Oh, blogu ya gayuganda ni mojawapo ya vitu ambavyo ni haramu, kwa mujibu wa muswada huu.

eng: I am furiously promoting homosexuality on this blog, complaining about a law like this.
swa: Mimi ninautangaza ushoga kwa hasira katika blogu hii, nikilalamikia sheria kama hii.

eng: So, 5 years in prison, and my (non existent) bank balance will be set back by 100M Uganda shillings…!
swa: Kwa hiyo, miaka mitano gerezani, na akaunti yangu ya benki (isiyokuwepo) itakwapuliwa shilingi za kiganda milioni 100...!

eng: And the people who dare to give us condoms and lubricant for sex… Or, if you dare to have an HIV prevention program for homosexuals in Uganda... or even try to teach safer sex.
swa: Na watu wanaothubutu kutupatia kondomu na vilainishaji kwa ajili ya ngono...au, kama utathubutu kuwa na mpango wa kuzuia maambukizi ya virusi vya UKIMWI kwa mashoga nchini Uganda...au hata kujaribu kufundisha ngono salama.

eng: Well, the penalties are stiff.
swa: Kweli, adhabu ni ngumu.

eng: Very stiff.
swa: Ngumu mno.

eng: Jail, and jail and other things.
swa: Jela, na jela na mambo mengine.

eng: Here are the objective of the bill.
swa: Haya ni melengo ya huo muswada.

eng: The objectives of the Bill The objectives of the Bill are:
swa: Malengo ya Mswada ni:

eng: (a) To protect marriage as that only between a man and a woman in Uganda;
swa: (a) Kuilinda ndoa kuwa ni ile kati ya mwanaume na mwanamke nchini Uganda;

eng: (b) To prohibit homosexual behavior and related practices in Uganda as they constitute a threat to the traditional family;
swa: (b) Kuzuia tabia za kishoga na vitendo vinavyohusiana nchini Uganda kwa sababu vinatishia familia za kitamaduni;

eng: (c) To safeguard the health of Ugandan citizens from the negative effects of homosexuality and related practices;
swa: (c) Kulinda afya za wananchi wa Uganda dhidi ya madhara mabaya ya ushoga na vitendo vinavyohusiana;

eng: (d) To establish progressive legislation protective of the traditional family that can serve as a model for other countries;
swa: (d) Kuanzisha sheria endelevu zinazolinda familia za kitamaduni ambazo zinaweza kuwa mfano kwa nchi nyingine;

eng: (e) To prohibit ratification of any international treaties, conventions, protocols and declarations which are contrary or inconsistent with the provisions of this Act;
swa: (e) Kuzuia makubaliano ya mkataba wowote wa kimataifa, mikutano na matamko ambayo yanapingana au hayakubaliani na vipengele vya sheria hii;

eng: (f) To ensure that no international instruments to which Uganda is already a party can be interpreted or applied in Uganda in a way that was never intended at the time the document was created;
swa: (f) Kuhakikisha kuwa hakuna vyombo vya kimataifa ambavyo Uganda ni sehemu yao vinaweza kutafsirika ama kutumika nchini Uganda kwa njia ambayo haikukusudiwa wakati ambapo viliundwa;

eng: (e) To withdraw from any international agreements to which Uganda already is a party, or file reservations to them, which are re-interpreted to include protection for homosexual behavior, or that promote same-sex marriage, or that call for the promotion or teaching about homosexuality as being healthy, normal, or an acceptable lifestyle choice, or that seek to establish sexual behavior, sexual orientation, or gender identity, or sexual minorities as legally protected categories of people; and (f) To prohibit Uganda from becoming a party to any new international instruments that expressly include protection for homosexual behavior; promote same-sex marriage; call for the promotion or teaching about homosexuality or homosexual relations as being healthy, normal, or an acceptable lifestyle choice; and/or seek to establish sexual behavior, sexual orientation, gender identity or sexual minorities as legally protected categories of people
swa: (e) Kujitoa kwenye makubaliano yoyote ya kimataifa ambayo Uganda tayari ni mwanachama, au kuweka masharti ya kujihadhari, ambayo yanatafsiriwa upya ili kujumuisha kulindwa kwa tabia za kishoga, au kutetea ndoa za jinsia moja, au kutoa wito wa kutangaza au kufundisha kuhusu ushoga kama tabia yenye afya, ya kawaida au uchaguzi unaokubalika wa utaratibu wa maisha, au kutafuta kuanzishwa kwa tabia za kingono, mtazamo wa kingono, au utambilsho wa kijinsia au makundi madogo ya kijinsia kama makundi ya watu yanayolindwa kisheria; na (f) Kuizuia Uganda kuwa mwanachama wa chombo chochote cha Kimataifa ambacho kinatamka wazi ujumuishaji na kulindwa kwa tabia za kishoga; kushabikia ndoa za jinsia moja; kutoa wito wa kushabikia na kufundisha kuhusu ushoga na mahusiano ya jinsia moja kama yenye kumaanisha afya njema, kawaida, ama uchaguzi wa namna ya maisha unaokubalika; na/au kutafuata kuanzisha tabia za kingono, mtazamo wa kingono, utambulisho wa kijinsia au makundi madogo ya kijinsia kama makundi ya watu yanayolindwa kwa nguvu ya sheria.

swa: Kusanyiko la watu wako linaweza kujulishwa mazuri yote ambayo baadhi ya Wakristo wa Uganda wanawatakia wenye dhambi waitwao mashoga wa Kiganda.

swa: Ndio, tunathubutu kuwaomba msaada kaka na dada zetu mashoga, hasa wakati ambapo wananchi wenzetu wanaamini tunapaswa kuwa wazalendo kiasi cha ‘kufa’ kwa jina la uongofu wa kimaadili, kwa mungu na kwa nchi.

eng: Afrogay another Ugandan blogger compares the Ugandan to the government to the Nazis, he says the time to flag down the bill is now:
swa: Afrogay mwanabogu mwingine wa Uganda anaifananisha serikali ya Uganda na kikundi za Nazi, ansema wakati wa kuufutilia mbali muswada huu ni sasa:

eng: Again, as I have argued here and elsewhere, we are best advised to keep our powder dry for the real battle if the bill is ever passed and signed into law.
swa: Tena, kama nilivyotoa hoja hapa na kwingineko, tunashauriwa vyema kutunza marisawa kwa ya vita halisi kama muswada huu utapitishwa na kutiwa saini kuwa sheria.

eng: So, I for one don't plan on saying too much about the nuts and bolts of what is wrong with it.
swa: Kwa hiyo, Mimi sitarajii kusema mengi kuhusu nati na boriti za nini kina makosa katika (muswada) huo.

eng: And the reason is simple: if we point out what is wrong with it now, our detractors will use what we say to clean up the bill.
swa: Na sababu ni rahisi: kama tukionyesha nini ni kibaya hivi sasa, wabaya wetu watatumia hayo tunayoyasema ili kuuosha muswada huo.

eng: Best then to shout foul as loud as we can on the discriminatory elements of the bill without guiding them around the glaring technical, legal, constitutional and human rights minefield they are sleep-walking towards with this bill.
swa: Cha Ni bora kupigia kelele kwa kosa hili la makusudi kwa sauti sana tuwezavyo dhidi ya chembechembe za kibaguzi za muswada huu bila kuwaongoza kuhusu udhaifu wa kiufundi unaojionyesha, kisheria, kikatiba na katika mitego (uwanja wa mabomu) ya haki za binadamu ambayo wanajiingiza wenyewe na muswada huu huku wakiwa wanatembea wakati wamelala usingizi.

eng: A Nigerian blogger Anengiyefa thinks the bill is flawed and the panel who made the bill are ignorant about homosexuality, He says homosexuality cannot be an offense, you cannot punish someone for having sexual feelings for another person:
swa: Mwanablogu wa Naijeria Anengiyefa anafikiri kwamba muswada huu una makosa na jopo lililoutengeneza halina ufahamu wa kutosha kuhusu ushoga. Anasmea ushoga hauwezi kuwa kosa, huwezi kumwadhibu mtu kwa kuwa na hisia za kimapenzi na mtu mwingine:

eng: Mr Bahati goes on to demand the death penalty for what he calls "aggravated homosexuality".
swa: Ndugu Bahati anaendelea na kutaka adhabu ya kifo kwa kile anachokiita “ushoga uliovuka mipaka”.

eng: I read this and I wondered if the said Mr Bahati has ever had the opportunity to sit inside a classroom in his life, given that unless he is starkly illiterate, he ought to know that there are no law books in any Common Law jurisdiction, (including Uganda), that refer to an offense known as 'homosexuality'.
swa: Nimesoma na nikajiuliza kama Ndugu Bahati amewahi kuwa na fursa ya kukaa darasani maishani mwake, kwa kuzingatia kwamba isipokuwa awe mjinga aliyekubuhu, anatakiwa ajue kuwa hakuna vitabu vya sheria kwenye hukumu za kawaida za kisheria, (pamoja na Uganda), ambavyo vinarejea kosa linaloitwa ‘ushoga’.

eng: Homosexuality cannot be an offense!
swa: Ushoga hauwezi kuwa kosa!

eng: You cannot make it an offense and punish a person for having feelings of sexual and emotional attraction towards others of the same gender.
swa: Huwezi kulifanya kuwa kosa na kumwadhibu mtu kwa kuwa na tamaa ya kimapenzi na hisia za kuvutiwa na mtu mwingine wa jinsia yake.

eng: You cannot prove 'homosexuality' in a court of law to the standard of proof that is required in a criminal court.
swa: Huwezi kuuthibitisha ‘ushoga’ kwenye mahakama ya kisheria kwa viwango vya ushahidi vinavyotakiwa kwenye mahakama ya jinai.

eng: Anengiyefa sees that Uganda has just seen hypocrisy of MPs who have unified and are ready to pass a law victimizing homosexuality in the name of morality: this beats the purpose why the system is so anxious to criminalize consensual sex amongst two adults of the same gender and omitting important issues like ethnic violence, tribalism, AIDS, child rape etc:
swa: Anengiyefa anaona kwamba Uganda imeona unafiki wa wabunge waliungana na wako tayari kupitisha sheria ya kuufanya ushoga kuwa kosa kwa jina la maadili; hii inalishinda kusudi la kwa nini mfumo uko makini kuyafanya mahusiano ya hiari baina ya watu wawili wazima wa jinsia moja yawe jinai na kuacha masuala muhimu kama mapigano ya kikabila, ukabila, UKIMWI, ukabaji wa watotot nk:

eng: This outbreak of frenzied homophobia is the epitome of the hypocrisy that pervades political life in Africa.
swa: Kulipuka kwa ushabiki huu wa hofu ya ushoga ni ushahidi wa unafiki unaotawala maisha ya siasa ya Afrika.

eng: At a time when expensive legislative time should be judiciously expended on the issues that really matter to the people of the country; when Ugandan lawmakers and the Ugandan government should be concerned about the welfare of vulnerable Ugandans, (including those same-gender loving men and women in their society, who are susceptible to wanton physical abuse and discrimination); when the Ugandan authorities should be looking to protect those of the country's citizens whose welfare is their responsibility; when the challenges that face our continent in this 21st Century are enormous; what we hear of instead is an Anti-Homosexuality Bill being introduced to Parliament.
swa: Wakati ambapo muda wa gharama za bunge ulitakiwa kutumika kisheria katika mambo ambayo yana tija kwa maisha ya watu wa nchi hii; wakati watunga sheria wa Uganda na serikali ya Uganda ilitakiwa kuguswa na ustawi wa Waganda wanaoteseka, (ikijumisha watu wale wanaowapenda watu wa jinsia yao katika jamii yao, ambao wanahatarishwa kwa matumizi ya nguzu na unyanyapaa); wakati ambapo mamlaka za Uganda zilitakiwa kuangalia namna ya kulinda wale wananchi wa vijijini ambao ustawi wao ni jukumu lao; wakati ambapo changamoto zinazolikabili bara letu katika karne hii ya 21 zinatisha; tunachokisikia badala yake ni Muswada wa kupinga ushoga ukiletwa Bungeni.

eng: This bill is deemed necessary according to the MP David Bahati who introduced it.
swa: Muswada huu unaonekana kuwa muhimu kwa mujibu wa Mbunge Davidi Bahati aliyeuleta.

eng: He claims that the purpose of the bill is to protect children and the "traditional family".
swa: Anadai kwamba lengo la muswada huu ni kuwalinda watoto na ‘familia zilizozoeleka kitamaduni’.

swa: Tayari nimo ndani ninayeyuka na ninatumaini kukuona pale na wewe pia kwani mazungumzo kuhusu Afrika na Waafrika yanachukua kasi na kupamba moto.

eng: Who knows, it may generate enough heat to force some of the changes we so badly need."
swa: Ni nani ajuaye, inaweza kutengeneza joto la kutosha na kulazimisha mabadiliko tuayoyahitaji sana.”

eng: Sokari writes about Pambazuka News special Women’s issues focusing on the last 15 years since Beijing Platform for Action and the future for women’s rights on the continent.
swa: Sokari anaandika kuhusu Toleo Maalum la Masuala ya Wanawake la Pambazuka linaloangalia miaka 15 iliyopita tangu mkutano au Jukwaa la Vitendo mjini Beijing pamoja na mustakabali wa haki za wanawake barani.

eng: As the children's show Sesame Street celebrates its 40th anniversary this month, premiering its new season today, one cute and cuddly Muppet on its South African edition continues to help combat and raise awareness about HIV/AIDS.
swa: Wakati kipindi cha watoto cha Mtaa wa Sesame (Sesame Street) kikisherehekea maadhimisho ya miaka 40 mwezi huu, kwa kizindua msimu wake mpya leo, kikaragosi kizuri kinachovutia cha Muppet katika toleo la Afrika Kusini kinaendelea kusaidia kupambana na kuelimisha kuhusu VVU/UKIMWI.

eng: While Sesame Street is seen in over 140 countries, each version addresses local issues and has different Muppets.
swa: Wakati kipindi cha Sesame Street kinatazamwa katika zaidi ya nchi 140, kila toleo huzungumzia masuala yanayotokea kwenye jamii husika na kwa kumtumia vikaragosi tofauti.

eng: Golden-yellow Kami made her debut on the South African Sesame Street co-production, called Takalani Sesame, in 2002 in response to the country's HIV/AIDS problem.
swa: Kami mwenye rangi ya Njano-dhahabu alionekana kwa mara ya kwanza kwenye kipindi mwenza cha Sisame Street cha Afrika Kusini kinachoitwa Takalani Sesame, mwaka 2002 kujibu matatizo ya nchi yanayohusiana na UKIMWI.

eng: The world's first HIV-positive Muppet, she helps educate kids about the disease and confronts issues related to being HIV-positive.
swa: Kama kikaragosi cha kwanza duniani chenye VVU, kinasaidia kuwaelimisha watoto kuhusu ugonjwa na kushughulikia masuala yanayohusiana na kuwa mwathirika wa UKIMWI.

eng: The name Kami is derived from the Setswana word “Kamogelo,” meaning “acceptance.”
swa: Jina la Kami linatoka kwenye neno la kiSetswana “Kamogelo”, lenye maana ya “kukubalika.”

eng: Sunshinestar110, blogging on U Don't Like My Opinion...That's Fine! talks more about Kami:
swa: Sunshinestar110, anayeblogu kwenye U dont Like My Opinion...That’s Fine! anazungumzia zaidi kuhusu Kami:

eng:
Kami is a healthy HIV Positive, affectionate 5 year old orphan who is a little shy but quickly joins when approached in a friendly way, She also knows a lot about HIV, she lost her mother to the disease. 	“Kami ni mwathirika wa VVU mwenye afya, yatima wa miaka mitano mwenye bashasha ambaye ana aibu kidogo lakini huchangamka akijongelewa kwa njia ya kirafiki, pia anajua mengi kuhusu Virusi vya UKIMWI, alimpoteza mama yake kwa ugonjwa huo.
When Kami was unveiled, with her mop of brown hair and she also wore a vest, wandering onto Sesame Street and wondering nervously if the residents will want to play with her. 	Kami alipozinduliwa, akiwa na nywele zake za kahawia na pia alivaa fulana, na kutembea kwenye mtaa wa Susame na kujiuliza huku akihofu kama wenyeji watataka kucheza nae.
She didn't have to worry because the other Muppets enthusiastically welcomed her.
swa: Hakuwa na haja ya kuogopa kwa sababu vikaragosi vingine vilimpokea kwa bashasha”

eng: Kami was introduced to help the many children in South Africa who are dealing with the HIV/AIDS crisis.
swa: Kami aliletwa kuwasaidia watoto wengi wa Afrika Kusini wanaotaabika na janga la VVU/UKIMWI.

eng: In addition to the physical complications of having HIV, there's also the stigma and taboo that comes with having the disease, which makes it harder for people to receive adequate treatment and support.
swa: Zaidi ya madhara ya kimwili ya kuwa na VVU, vilevile kuna unyanyapaa na miiko inayotokana na kuwa na ugonjwa, ambayo husababisha ugumu kwa watu kupata matibabu stahiki na msaada.

eng: Takalani Sesame, which incorporates all 11 of South Africa's official languages, tries to help children address some of these issues head on through Kami.
swa: Takalani Sesame, ambayo inajumuisha lugha zote rasmi 11 za Afrika Kusini, inajaribu kuwasaidia watoto kuyatazama masuala haya kwa ujasiri kupitia Kami.

eng: However, there was much controversy when Kami was introduced, particularly in the U.S., as many were outraged that a children's show would feature an HIV-positive character.
swa: Hata hivyo, kulikuwa na mkanganyiko wakati Kami alipoanza kuonyeshwa, hasa hasa nchini Marekani, ambapo wengi walikasirishwa na kuwa kipindi cha watoto kinanamchezesha mhusika mwenye VVU.

eng: Haven on Earth elaborates on the debate:
swa: Haven on Earth anafafanua mjadala huo:

eng:
Although it was reported that Kami's arrival on Sesame Street in South Africa was welcomed (I have a hard time accepting this as fact because of the still high level of denial still there), there was definite controversy here in United States. 	“Ingawa ilitaarifiwa kuwa ujio wa Kami kwenye kipindi cha Sesame Street nchini Afrika Kusini ulikuwa unakaribishwa.(Nina wakati mgumu kukubaliana na ukweli huu kwa sababu kiwango kikubwa cha kukataa bado kipo), kulikuwa na mkanganyiko ulio wazi hapa Marekani.
I remember reading about this (which is why I was so pleased to actually encounter a show airing while in South Africa - it would have never occurred to me to look for it).	Ninakumbuka kusoma kuhusu suala hili (hii ni sababu ya mimi kufurahia kukutana na kipindi kikirushwa kutokea Afrika Kusini – nisingelifikiria kukitafuta).
Apparently a group of Republican congressmen sent a letter to the President of PBS (Public Broadcasting Service) that airs Sesame Street.	Iliondokea kuwa kundi la wabunge wa Congress wa chama cha Republican walituma barua kwa Rais wa Shirika la Utangazaji la Umma (PBS) linalorusha kipindi cha Sesame Street.
The letter protested that plans to introduce a similar HIV-positive character in the United States in due course were inappropriate, given the age of the audience. 	Barua ilidai kwamba mipango ya kuleta mhusika kama huyo ambaye ni mwathirika wa UKIMWI nchini Marekani haikuwa sahihi, kwa kuzingatia umri wa watazamaji.
They suggested that such a move might threaten public funding of PBS .
swa: Walipendekeza kwamba hatua hiyo ingeathiri ufadhili wa umma kwa Shirika hilo (PBS).”

eng:
Since most South African children know someone who has AIDS, the character has become a national hero, beloved by the country's people. 	“Kwa sababu watoto wengi wa Afrika Kusini wanamfahamu mtu fulani mwenye UKIMWI, mhusika huyo amekuwa shujaa wa taifa, anayependwa na watu wa nchi hiyo.
Kami has appeared at the United Nations and the World Bank and was interviewed by Katie Couric.	Kami ameonekana kwenye Umoja wa Mataifa na Benki ya Dunia na alihojiwa na Katie Couric.
She has also been named a UNICEF ambassador for children and has appeared in Takalani segments alongside Desmond Tutu and Nelson Mandela.
swa: Ameteuliwa kuwa balozi wa UNICEF wa watoto na ameonekana kwenye vipande vya onyesho la Takalami pembeni mwa Desmond Tutu na Nelson Mandela.”

eng: Despite Kami's success, some bloggers still believe that she's not an appropriate character for the American version of Sesame Street.
swa: Pamoja na mafanikio ya Kami, wanablogu wengine bado wanaamini kuwa si mhusika sahihi kwa toleo la Kimarekani la Sesame Street.

eng: Emily Meyer, blogging for her honors class, says:
swa: Emily Meyer, anayeblogu kwa ajili ya darasa lake la heshima, anasema:

eng:
Although it is important for Americans to know about HIV/AIDS and the seriousness of the diseases, I think teaching kids at the ages of two and three is a little extreme. 	“Ingawa ni muhimu kwa Wamerekani kufahamu kuhusu VVU/UKIMWI na hatari ya ugonjwa wenyewe, nadhani kuwafundisha watoto katika umri wa miaka miwili na mitatu ni kwenda mbali sana.
Children this young would most likely not understand about HIV and would not understand its consequences.	Watoto wadogo kiasi hiki hawataweza kuelewa kuhusu VVU na hawataelewa madhara yake.
If Kami was to be introduced in the United States as a way to spread knowledge and combat AIDS, I do not think the intended results would occur...Kids in America are not forced to deal with the issue of HIV/AIDS at that young of an age. 	Kama Kami alitakiwa aletwe Marekani kama njia kueneza elimu na kudhibiti UKIMWI, sidhani kama matokeo yaliyokusudiwa yangetokea...Watoto nchini Marekani hawalazimishwi kuhusika na masuala ya UKIMWI katika umri huo mdogo.
I think the appropriate time for kids in America to learn about the seriousness of HIV is when they are older, about ten or eleven years old or when the student becomes sexually active
swa: Nadhani wakati sahihi kwa watoto nchini Marekani kujifunza kuhusu hatari ya virusi vya UKIMWI ni wanapokuwa wakubwa, kadri ya miaka kumi ama kumi na moja au wakati mwanafunzi anapoanza kujihusisha na vitendo vya mapenzi kimwili”

eng: Still, many bloggers, such as this one writing on Muppets and History, see Kami has another example of how Sesame Street has pushed the boundaries.
swa: Bado, wanablogu wengi, kama huyu hapa anayeandika kwenye Muppets and History, anamwona Kami kama mfano mwingine wa namna Sesame Street inavyosukuma mipaka.

eng: Others profess their love for the Muppet and the message she brings to children.
swa: Wengine wanaonyesha upendo wao kwa kikaragosi huyo na ujumbe anaowaletea watoto.

eng: And still others think she should be introduced on other versions of Sesame Street.
swa: Na wengine wanadhani anatakiwa atumike kwenye matoleo mengine ya Sesame Street.

eng: On her personal blog, Steisha Pintado says:
swa: Katika blogu yake binafsi, Steisha Pintado anasema:

eng:
She shows children that it is okay to hug someone who is HIV positive, and she explains what to do when she has a cut on her finger or if you have a cut yours. 	“Anawaonyesha watoto kwamba ni sawa kumkumbatia mtu mwenye virusi vya UKIMWI, na anaeleza nini cha kufanya anapokuwa na kidonda kwenye kidole chake au kama umejikata mwenyewe.
She teachers her young audience about coping with illness and loss...Even though sex is never mentioned when talking about Kami’s condition, some people have said that having an HIV positive character would be inappropriate for a young viewing audience. 	Anaifundisha hadhira ya watoto wadogo kuhusu kukabiliana na kuumwa na kupotelewa....Ingawa ngono huwa haitajwi kamwe katika kuzungumzia hali ya Kami, watu wengine wamesema kuwa kuwepo kwa mhusika mwenye virusi vya UKIMWI lisingekuwa jambo sahihi kwa hadhira ya watazamaji wadogo.
One legislature even claimed that the Sesame Workshop would lose its government funding if it aired a program with such a character in our country.	Mbunge mmoja hata alidai kuwa Warsha ya Sesame ingepoteza msaada wa kifedha kutoka serikalini kama ingerusha kipindi chenye mhusika huyo kwenye nchi yetu.
It is so shocking to hear these words.	Inashangaza kusikia maneno haya.
Parents spend less and less time with their children, and allow the television to educate them more and more. 	Wazazi wanatumia muda mfupi (na unaopungua kila siku) na watoto wao, na wanaruhusu runinga kuwaelimisha zaidi na zaidi.
So obviously many parents aren’t teaching their children how to handle delicate subjects of awareness and acceptance.	Ni wazi wazazi wengi hawawafundishi watoto wao namna ya kuyakabili masuala nyeti ya uelewa na kukubalika.
Parents have already allowed the Sesame Workshop to introduce acceptance with those who have disabilities and illnesses, and also with those who are a different race or religion. 	Wazazi tayari wamewaruhusu Warsha ya Sesame kuingiza suala la kukubalika kwa wale wenye ulemavu na kuugua, na pia kwa wale wenye rangi na dini tofauti.
How is this any different?
swa: Je, hii ina tofauti gani?

eng: The contamination of drinking water and food sources, which leads to a slew of health risks.
swa: Uchafuzi wa maji ya kunywa na vyanzo vya chakula, jambo ambalo linapelekea hatari nyingi za kiafya.

eng: Lack of sanitation is the world’s biggest cause of infection and kills 1.8 million people, mostly children, a year.
swa: Ukosefu wa mfumo wa usafi ndiyo sababu kubwa ya maambukizi na huua watu milioni 1.8, hasa watoto, kila mwaka.

eng: Even countries with abundant toilets have to deal with problems ranging from unhygienic public toilets to waterway-destroying sewage disposal.
swa: Hata nchi zenye vyoo vya kutosha huwa zinakabiliana na matatizo yanayotokana na vyoo vichafu vya umma mpaka utupaji majitaka unaoharibu njia za maji.

eng: Vanilla, blogging on Let's Look At It This Way from Singapore, says that people should care about toilets:
swa: Vanilla, anayeblogu kwenye Let's Look At It This Way kutokea Singapore, anasema kuwa watu wanapaswa kutilia maanani vyoo:

eng:
I know this is a crappy topic to most people. 	“ Ninajua kwamba hii ni mada chafu kwa watu wengi.
It is unfortunate that it is a 'taboo' topic to talk about openly and many people remain ignorant about the scale of the problem.	Ni bahati mbaya kwamba hii mada bado ni ‘mwiko’ kuiongelea wazi na watu wengi hawana uelewa kuhusu ukubwa wa tatizo.
I fail to understand how this can be an unimportant topic when, on an average, we visit the toilet 2500 times a year, or 6-8 times a day. 	Ninashindwa kuelewa ni kwa jinsi gain hii inaweza kuwa mada isiyo na maana wakati, kwa wastani, huwa tunakwenda chooni mara 2500 kwa mwaka, au mara 6-8 kwa siku.
In our life time, we would have spent 3 years in the toilet.
swa: Wakati wa maisha yetu, hutumia muda wa miaka 3 vyooni."

eng: Organized by the nonprofit The World Toilet Organization, World Toilet Day is being celebrated globally with various events.
swa: Chini ya maandalizi ya asasi isiyo ya kibiashara The World Toilet Organisation, Siku ya Vyoo Duniani inasherehekewa dunia nzima kwa matukio mbalimbali.

eng: To further increase awareness, WaterAid announced the launch of its new ToiletFinder UK App for iPhone users this week.
swa: Ili kuuelimisha umma zaidi, wiki hii WaterAid ilitangaza uzinduzi wa zana mpya ya Kutafutia Vyoo nchini Uingereza ya simu za mkononi za iPhone.

eng: The free app helps Brits find the nearest public toilet while reminding them how lucky they are to have clean and safe toilets.
swa: Zana hiyo ya bure inawasaidia Waingereza kutafuta choo cha umma kilicho karibu zaidi wakati pia inawakumbusha jinsi walivyo na bahati ya kuwa na vyoo safi na salama.

eng: The largest event today, called The Big Squat, asks people to stop and squat for one minute in a public place to raise awareness.
swa: Tukio kubwa zaidi leo, linaloitwa Mchuchumao Mkubwa, linawataka watu wasimame na wachuchumae kwa dakika moja katika sehemu za umma ili kuongeza utambuzi.

eng: These photos show people squatting globally, including this one of preschoolers in Singapore:
swa: Picha hizi zinaonyesha watu waliochuchumaa dunia nzima, pamoja na hii ya watoto wa chekechea huko Singapore:

eng: A blog from Brunei, the world according to panyaluru ..., also shows appreciation for the toilet by putting it into perspective:
swa: Blogu inayotokea Brunei, the world according to panyaluru …, pia inaonyesha kuridhika na vyoo kwa kuliweka suala hili kwenye muktadha sawia:

eng:
Imagine if we are walking along in the row of shops in Kiulap or Gadong. 	“Fikiria ikiwa tunatembea mbele ya mlolongo wa maduka kule Kiulap au Gadong.
Suddenly the tummy grumbles, just like the worst ribut you can think off. 	Mara tu tumbo linaunguruma kama vile ambavyo haujawahi kusikia.
No rest bite.	Halisimami kukupa mapumziko.
Grumble and grumble.	Linaunguruma na kuunguruma.
Rumblings.	Ngurumo.
The light is on amber and ready to turn green.	Taa ni ya manjano tayari kubadilika kuwa ya kijani.
But no toilets in sight.	Lakini hakuna vyoo unavyoviona.
Not a single public toilet in the rows of shops...Add to that no water, no tissue, nothing! 	Hakuna hata choo kimoja cha umma kwenye mlolongo wa maduka… ongezea pia kuwa hakuna maji, karatasi ya chooni, hakuna chochote!
That could be the worst day of your life, your worst nightmare, ever worse than the nightmares those kids have in the Nightmare on Elm Street Movies. 	Hiyo inaweza kuwa siku mbaya zaidi katika maisha yako, jinamizi baya, au jinamizi baya zaidi ya yale yaliyowakuta watoto kwenye filamu za Elm Street.
On this day, let’s show our appreciation to our toilets.
swa: Katika siku hii, hebu na tuvienzi vyoo.”

eng: Some bloggers point out that toilets alone may not be the answer.
swa: Baadhi ya wanablogu wanasema kuwa vyoo pekee vinaweza visiwe jibu.

eng: Sandhya, blogging on Maradhi Manni in India, says many men don't use available toilets:
swa: Sandhya, anayeblogu kwenye Maradhi Manni nchini India, anasema wanaume wengi hawatumii vyoo vilivyopo:

eng:
In a city like Chennai, where the climate is hot nearly 10 months of the year, I see men urinating on the roadside all the time. 	Kwenye mji kama Chennai, ambako hali ya hewa ni ya joto kwa karibu miezi 10 ya mwaka, huwaona wanaume wanakojoakando ya barabara kila wakati.
When women can control and go home and relieve themselves, why can't men do so, I don't know. 	Wkati wanawake wanaweza kujidhibiti na kwenda nyumbani kujisaidia, kwa nini wanaume hawawezi kufanya hivyo, sijui kwa nini.
So, first of all people should be fined heavily for doing this crime (yes, it is crime) on the spot. 	Kwa hiyo, kwanza watu wote wanabidi wapigwe faini kali kwa kufanya kosa hili (naam, ni kosa) pale pale wanapokamatwa.
I have seen them doing this on the wall of the public toilets!	Nimewahi kuwaona wakifanya hivyo kwenye ukuta wa vyoo vya umma!
In Srirangam, I saw them urinating on the compound wall of the temple even though every street surrounding the temple had toilets, which were clean, but pay toilets!
swa: Kule Srinagam, nimewahi kuwaona wakikojoa kwenye ukutra wa boma la hekalu pamoja na kuwa kila mtaa unaolizunguka hekalu una vyoo, ambavyo vilikuwa visafi, lakini vya kulipia!”

eng: While lack of sanitation impacts everyone, the taboo around toilets can disproportionately affect women.
