eng: it had been opened by various puzzled customs and postal employees who, at a loss, defined the product in writing as "containing an unknown red liquid" – and awaited my description.
swa: Nilikuta kimeshafunguliwa na maafisa mbalimbali wa forodha na posta ambao, baada ya kukosa majibu, waliandika utambulisho wa bidhaa hiyo kama “yenye majimaji mekundu yasiyofahamika” – na walisubiri maelezo yangu.

eng: He told them it was "cinematographic make-up" and took the item home:
swa: Aliwaeleza kuwa ni “vipodozi vya wacheza sinema” na kuichukua bidhaa ile nyumbani:

swa: Kikiwekwa ukeni kabla ya kujamiiana, plastiki hiyo huganda kidogo, na hupasuka wakati wa tendo.

swa: Matone machache ya “damu” huchafua shuka, na kutunza “heshima” ya mwanamke, familia yake au jamii yake.

eng: Whether it does actually work or not I cannot answer.
swa: Kama fanya kazi au la siwezi kujibu.

eng: The complete absence of medical information on the product, as well as online accusations that this product can cause infections, made me unwilling to give it to a volunteer to test.
swa: Kutokuwepo kabisa kwa maelezo ya kitaalamu kwenye bidhaa hiyo, pamoja na shutuma mtandaoni kuwa bidhaa hii inaweza kusababisha magonjwa, vilinifanya nisite kumpoatia mtu atakayejitolea kufanya jaribio.

eng: Mona El Tahawy did not like how Egyptians were hot and bothered over fake hymensWith all the troubles Egypt faces these days — spiralling cost of living, a president in power for 28 years whose son looks likely to succeed him, etc. — why all the fuss over hymens, real or fake?
swa: Mona El Tahawy hakupendezwea na jinsi Wamisri walivyopamba moto na kuguswa juu ya bikira bandia pamoja na matatizo yote Wamisri wanayoyakabili siku hizi – gharama za maisha zinazopanda, rais aliye madarakani kwa miaka 28 ambaye mwanawe anaelekea kumrithi, nk. – kelele zote za nini juu ya bikira, iwe ya kweli au ya bandia?

eng: Welcome to the hypocrisy and denial that together drum at the heart of conservative religious views on women and chastity.
swa: Karibuni kwenye unafiki na kujidanganya ambavyo kwa pamoja vinadunda katikati ya roho mitazamo ya kihafidhina ya kidini juu ya wanawake na uadilifu katika kufanya mapenzi.

eng: And in the case of Egypt, that conservatism applies equally to Muslims and Christians.
swa: Na katika shauri la Misri, uhafidhina huo upokatika mizani sawa kote, kwa Waislamu na Wakristu.

eng: As a Muslim, I know the Qur’an preaches chastity for men and women, but the conservative obsession with women means only females are expected to abide by the prohibition on extramarital sex.
swa: Kama Muislamu, ninajua kuwa Qur’an inahubiri uadilifu katika kufanya mapenzi kwa wanaume na wanawake, lakini kushupaliwa huku kwa wanawake na wahafidhina kunamaanisha kuwa ni wanawake tu ambao wanatarajiwa kuzingatia makatazo juu ngono nje ya ndoa.

eng: This obsession with virginity is shallow at best and deadly at worst.
swa: Huku kushupaliwa kwa bikira kumekosa kina zaidi ya yote na kuna hali ya umauti zaidi.

eng: Mohamed El Rahhal strongly condemns:
swa: Mohamed El Rahhal anashutumu vikali:

swa: Unafiki ambao unaturuhusu kubagua dhidi ya asilimia 50 ya jamii wakati tunatoa kibali cha bure kwa nusu nyingine.

eng: I am against forcing women to go such lengths, sometimes endangering their health, to allow us to delay a long-awaited national moratorium on gender relations.
swa: Ninapinga kuwalazimisha wanawake kwenda umbali huo, mara nyingine kuhatarisha afya zao, ili kuruhusu kucheleweshwa kwa sheria ya kitaifa juu ya mahusiano ya kijinsia.

eng: Morality is worst interpreted by anatomy.
swa: Uadilifu unatafsiriwa vibaya zaidi na maumbile.

eng: And if we're waiting upon a small piece of plastic to define morality, then we've already failed – and ought to find a better definition.
swa: Na kama tunasubiri kipande kidogo cha plastiki kifafanue uadilifu, basi tumeshashindwa – na ni budi tutafute ufafanuzi mzuri zaidi.

eng: In much of the world, nothing is more unifying - or in some instances, more polarizing - than a football match.
swa: Katika sehemu nyingi duniani, hakuna linalounganisha zaidi – au wakati mwingine kutenganisha – zaidi ya pambano la mpira wa miguu.

swa: Washabiki wa Misri na Aljeria, katika ulimwengu wote wa Waarabu na zaidi, walilidhihirisha hilo Jumamosi hii wakati timu zao zilipokwenda sambamba wakati wa kuwania kuingia fainali za Kombe la Dunia huko Afrika Kusini.

swa: Wakati vihoro vilipanda juu huko mjini Cairo, pia vilikuwa hai na katika hali nzuri kwenye uwanja yakini mtandaoni, pamoja na kwenye Twita, ambako watumiaji walitaarifu kuwa skrini zao zilijaa hisia za mpira.

swa: Chidi Opara anamkumbuka Ken Saro-Wiwa, Mwandishi wa Kinaijeria, mwanaharakati wa mazingira na haki za walio wachache ambaye aliuwawa na watawala wa kijeshi wa Naijeria tarehe 10 Novemba, 1995.

eng: It's well known that Nigeria has an image problem – 419 Internet scams, corruption, oil piracy in the Delta region – for many people, these are the associations that come to mind when Africa's most populous country is mentioned.
swa: Inajulikana vyema kuwa Naijeria ina tatizo la muonekano – utapeli wa 419 kwenye intaneti, rushwa, uharamia wa mafuta katika jimbo la Delta – kwa watu wengi, huu ndio uhusiano unaokuja akilini wakati nchi yenye watu wengi zaidi Afrika inapotajwa.

eng: However, the last year has been especially hard on Nigeria's reputation abroad: over the past few months, a series of events depicting Nigeria in a questionable light have triggered discussions throughout the blogosphere.
swa: Hata hivyo, mwaka uliopita umekuwa mgumu kwa watu wa Najeria walio ughaibuni: katika miezi michache iliyopita, mfululizo wa matukio yanayoionyesha Naijeria katika mwanga wa utata ulizua majadiliano kwenye ulimwengu wa blogu.

eng: In September, Sony released an ad for Playstation 3 which included the line, “You can't believe everything you read on the Internet – otherwise, I'd be a Nigerian millionaire by now.”
swa: Mwezi Septemba, Sony ilitoa tangazo la mchezo wa Playstation 3 ambalo lilikuwa na mstari unaosema, “Usiamini kila kitu unachosoma kwenye intaneti – vinginevyo, ningekuwa milionea wa Kinaijeria hivi sasa.”

eng: The ad was met with consternation from many Nigerians, and the Federal Government requested that Sony make a formal apology (Sony did apologize and later withdrew the ad).
swa: Tangazo hilo lilikumbana na mawazo ya kuchanganyikiwa kutoka kwa Wanaijeria wengi, na Serikali ya Shirikisho iliitaka Sony kuomba radhi (Sony iliomba msamaha na baadaye ikaliondoa tangazo).

eng: Around the same time came the release of District 9 – a sci-fi blockbuster which was critically well-received but irksome to many Nigerians.
swa: Katika wakati huo huolilikuja toleo la filamu ya District 9 – filamu ya kisayansi ambayo ilipokewa kwa mapitio mazuri lakini yaliyowakasirisha Wanaijeria.

eng: The Nigerian government took offense at the film's depiction of Nigerians as criminals and cannibals, banning the film within Nigeria and asking the Censor's Board to confiscate it from theaters.
swa: Serikali ya Naijeria ilichukizwa na jinsi filamu hiyo ilivyowaonyesha Wanaijeria kama wahalifu na wala watu, na iliipiga marufuku ndani ya Naijeria na kulitaka Baraza la Udhibiti kuikamata kutoka kwenye majumba ya sinema.

eng: Online, the movie provoked varied reactions, with some taking the view that the film presents a racist view of Nigerians, while others defended it as a fictional representation with little bearing on reality.
swa: Kwenye mtandao, filamu hiyo ilisababisha maoni yaliyopishana, huku baadhi ya watu wakichukua mtizamo kuwa filamu ina mtizamo wa kibaguzi dhidi ya Wanaijeria, wakati wengine waliitetea kama wakilisho la kubuni lenye chembe ndogo ya ukweli.

eng: Adamu Waziri at EVCL points out that often Nigerian depictions of Nigerians are equally unflattering:
swa: Adamu Waziri katika EVCL anasema kuwa mara nyingi jinsi Wanaijeria wanavyoonyeshwa na Wanaijeria pia huwa hakufurahishi:

eng: Nollywood, our indigenous movie industry, has portrayed us in a much harsher light to both national and international audiences.
swa: Nollywood, kiwanda cha filamu cha wazawa, kimetuonyesha katika mwanga mbaya zaidi kwa wote, watazamaji wa kitaifa na wale wa kimataifa.

eng: There was a time where you couldn’t get Nollywood movie that didn’t include one of the following or a combination of them; fraud, juju/witchcraft, armed robbery, incest, adultery, cannibalism and of course our favourite, corruption.
swa: Kuna wakati usingeweza kupata filamu ya Nollywood ambayo haikuwa na haya yafuatayo au mchanganyiko wake: utapeli, uchawi, ujambazi wa kutumia silaha, ngono kati wanandugu, mapenzi nje ya ndoa, kula watu na pia suala tunalolipenda, rushwa.

eng: Nollywood has been pumping out thousands of movies with these themes for years with no real opposition from the general public or any Ministry.
swa: Nollywood imekuwa ikitoa maelfu ya filamu zenye maudhui haya kwa miaka bila pingamizi la kweli kutoka kwa umma wa kawaida au wizara.

eng: ... Banning films sets the wrong precedent; in fact it can be dangerous.
swa: … kupiga marufuku filamu kunaanzisha mfano mbaya; na kunaweza kuwa hatari.

eng: Let us the public debate the issue.
swa: Tuachieni sisi umma tujadili hili suala.

eng: We are mature enough to do so.
swa: Tumekomaa vya kutosha kufanya hivyo.

eng: In fact our Minister has succeeded in giving the movie more publicity which I’m sure she didn’t intend to do.
swa: Kwa kweli, waziri wetu amefanikiwa kuipatia filamu hiyo matangazo zaidi jambo ambalo nina hakika hakulikusudia.

eng: Nicole Stamp comments on race in District 9:
swa: Nicole Stamp anatoa maoni kuhusu masuala ya rangi katika District 9:

eng: The thing that really upsets me is that most people who see this movie won’t question, or even notice, this incredibly racist portrayal....
swa: Jambo ambalo linanikera ni kuwa watu wengi wanaoiangalia filamu hii hawaulizi, au hata hawaoni, muonekano huu usioaminika wa kibaguzi….

eng: Why can’t the Nigerians just be people with logical motives like money and weapons?
swa: Kwa nini Wanaijeria wasiweze kuwa watu wenye kutaka vitu vyenye mantiki kama vile pesa na silaha?

eng: Why do they have to go out of their way to be ooga-booga savages? ….it is impossible to disregard the charged portrayal of Nigerians which when viewed in a larger context, is beyond damaging or defamatory but is dangerous.
swa: Kwa nini wanaenda nje ya njia zao na kuwa washenzi wa ki-ooga-booga?... haiwezekani kutojali jinsi Wanaijeria wanavyoonyeshwa ambavyo kukiangaliwa katika muktadha mpana, kumepita hali ya kuumiza au kudhalilisha lakini ni hali ya hatari.

eng: Read more on the debate at Nigerianstalk.org or google "district 9 race".
swa: Unaweza kusoma zaidi mjadala huu kwenye tovuti ya Nigerianstalk.org au tafuta kwenye google kwa kutumia maneno haya “district 9 race”.

eng: More recently, Time magazine published a slide show by the South African photographer Pieter Hugo which featured scenes from Nigeria's “Nollywood” movie industry.
swa: Katika siku za karibuni zaidi, gazeti la Time lilichapisha onyesho la picha na mpiga picha wa Afrika Kusini Pieter Hugo ambazo zilionyesha picha kutoka kwenye kiwanda cha sinema cha "Nollywood" huko Naijeria.

eng: Though not so controversial as District 9 or the Playstation commercial, the photographs nonetheless prompted debate in the blogosphere, with discussions over whether such depictions of Nigeria fall under the category of artistic freedom or cultural bias.
swa: Japokuwa halikuwa onyesho tata kama ilivyokuwa District 9 au tangazo la Playstation, mpiga picha huyo hata hivyo alichochea mdahalo katika ulimwengu wa blogu, na mjadala kuhusu kama uonyeshwaji huo wa Wanaijeria uko chini ya fungu la uhuru wa kisanii au upendeleo wa kitamaduni.

eng: Solomon Sydelle at Nigerian Curiosity writes:
swa: Solomon Sydelle kwenye blogu ya Nigerian Curiosity anaandika:

eng: I definitely understand the need to push the envelope, after all that desire has led to some of the most creative masterpieces and accomplishments of all time.
swa: Ninaelewa fika haja ya kusogeza mipaka, kwani shauku hiyo imepelekea kupatikana kwa ubunifu wa kazi za hali juu sana na mafanikio ya wakati wote.

eng: However, with these pictures, I struggle to develop an appreciation of them and/or what they represent and believe that they unnecessarily relied on biases that will only confirm certain stereotypes for Hugo's mainly Western audience.
swa: Hata hivyo, kwa picha hizi, ninahangaika kuzithamini pamoja na kile kinachoonyeshwa na ninaamini kuwa bila ulazima wowote zilitegemea upendeleo ambao unathibitisha imani fulani potofu za kadamnasi ya Hugo ambayo kwa kiasi kikubwa ni ya Magharibi.

eng: These events are especially ill-timed as they correspond to a new initiative launched earlier this year to “Re-brand Nigeria.”
swa: Matukio haya yametukia katika wakati mbaya kwani yanawiana na mpango mpya uliozinduliwa mwanzoni mwa mwaka huu wa “kutengeneza chapa mpya ya Naijeria” (Re-brand Nigeria).

eng: The initiative is sponsored by Dr. Dora Akunyili, Nigerian Minister of Information and Communication, and has been met with both praise and criticism (see here for the discussion at Global Voices).
swa: Mpango huo unadhaminiwa na Dk. Dora Akunyili, Waziri wa Habari na Mawasiliano wa Naijeria, na ambao umekumbana na yote mawili, sifa na kukosolewa (angalia hapa ili kusoma mjadala huo kwenye Global Voices)

eng: Bunmi Oloruntoba at A Bombastic Element discusses the re-branding campaign in the context of a recent BBC discussion on the subject:
swa: Bunmi Oloruntoba katika blogu ya A Bombastic Element anajadili kampeni ya kutengeneza chapa mpya katika muktadha wa mjadala wa hivi karibuni kwenye BBC juu ya suala hilo:

eng: The minister has a good case when she argues that Nigeria is overlooking a lot of positives, has not been telling her stories and is making the mistake of letting the world define her image based on its notoriety alone.
swa: Waziri alikuwa na shauri zuri aliposema kuwa Naijeria haiyatazami mengi yaliyo chanya, haielezi simulizi zake na inafanya makosa ya kuiachia dunia kufafanua taswira yake inayoelemea kwenye sifa zake mbaya pekee.

eng: And she has some good examples of the positives.
swa: Na anayo mifano mizuri ya mambo chanya.

eng: But the BBC sought out a few PR and branding experts who counter by saying, if the country wants to rebrand itself, it needs to give any PR team a lot more to build on.
swa: Lakini BBC ilitafuta maafisa uhusiano na wataalamu wa chapa wachache ambao wanapinga kwa kusema, kama nchi inataka kujitengenezea chapa mpya, inapaswa kuipatia timu yoyote ya mahusiano nyenzo zaidi.

eng: Those interviewed said, consistent power supply and an end to a diesel generator economy will make rebranding Nigeria "effortless."
swa: Wale waliohojiwa walisema, ugavi wa umeme wa uhakika na mwisho wa uchumi unaotegemea mashjine za jenereta kutaizifanya jitihada za kutengeneza chapa mpya ya Naijeria kuwa “rahisi.”

eng: And to prove their point, 13:40 mins into the program... well, you don't need to be a Nigerian to figure out what happened.
swa: Na kuthibitisha maneno yao, dakika 13:40 baada ya kipindi kuanza… naam, haupaswi kuwa Mnaijeria kujua ni nini kilichotokea.

eng: A bright spot in the discussion of Nigeria's image was a widely circulated video of Nigerian author Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie speaking on “The danger of a single story.”
swa: Sehemu angavu ya mjadala wa taswira ya Naijeria ilikuwa ni video iliyosambazwa sana ya mwandishi wa Kinaijeria Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie akiongelea juu ya “Hatari ya simulizi moja.”

eng: Adichie comments on the pitfalls of a monolithic image of Africa as a site of catastrophe; she cautions that limiting ourselves to a “single story” flattens experience and creates stereotypes.
swa: Adichie anatoa maoni juu ya mitegoya taswira kubwa ya Afrika kama sehemu ya majanga; anatahadharisha kuwa kujekea upeo wa “simuli moja” kunasiliba uzoefu na kutengeneza imani potofu.

eng: For many bloggers, Adichie's remarks resonated with their frustration at the depictions of Nigeria prevalent outside the country.
swa: Kwa wanablogu wengi, maneno ya Adichie yalitoa mwangwi wa kughafirika kwao na taswira ya Naijeria iliyozoeleka nje ya nchi.

eng: Shade NonConformist writes of the connection between Adichie's speech and Nigeria's image:
swa: Mwanablogu Shade NonConformist anaandika kuhusu uhusiano wa rissala ya Adichie na taswira ya Naijeria:

eng: I believe this is what Chimamada Adichie meant about The Danger of a Single Story lecture she gave at TED.
swa: Ninaamini kuwa hivi ndivyo Adichie alivyomaanisha katika hotuba ya Hatari ya Simulizi Moja aliyoitoa kwenye TED.

eng: It becomes a problem when the only portrayal of Africa that we see is one involving dead animals, poverty, disaster, death, corruption, celebrity adoptions...you know the whole nine yards.
swa: Inageuka kuwa tatizo pale sura pekee ya Afrika tunayoiona ni ile inayohusisha wanyama waliokufa, umaskini, majanga, vifo, ufisadi, watu mashuhuri wanaasili watoto… unafahamu yadi zote tisa.

eng: Now I'm not saying Africa does not have these issues.
swa: Sasa sisemim kuwa Afrika haina mambo hayo.

eng: We can all agree that we do.
swa: Wote tunaweza tukaafikiana kuwa tunayo.

eng: I'm arguing that these issues are not specific to African countries.
swa: Ninachosema ni kuwa mambo hayo si ya nchi za Kiafrika peke yake.

eng: ... I/We will never stop criticizing depictions of Africa that are unbalanced and prejudiced.
swa: …Mimi/sisi hatutasikoma kukosoa taswira za Afrika ambazo hazina mizani na zenye ubaguzi.

eng: Presenting a balance depiction of Africa is crucial.
swa: Kuonyesha taswira zenye mizani iliyolingana ni jambo muhimu.

eng: As Africans we also need to act as vessels who are willing to be instrumental in the change we want to see (and will see) in our beloved continent.
swa: Kama Waafrika pia tunapaswa kiujifanya kuwa kama vyombo ambavyo viko radhi kutumika katika mabadiliko tunayotakja kuyaona (ambayo tutayaona) katika bala letu tunalolienzi.

eng: A Biogas plant.
swa: Kituo cha gesi inayotokana na samadi.

eng: Image by Flickr user Marufish.
swa: Picha na mtumiaji wa Flickr Marufish.

eng: Used under a creative commons licenseBiogas technology is starting a green revolution in Nepal.
swa: Na imetumika chini ya leseni ya hati miliki huru. Teknolojia ya gesi inayotokana na samadi inaanzisha mapinduzi ya kijani nchini Nepal.

eng: According to WWF firewood is the preferred energy source in the country as almost 87% of households depend on it.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa WWF kuni ni chanzo cha nishati kinachopendwa zaidi nchini kwani takriban ya 87% ya kaya zinategemea chanzo hiki.

eng: However, biogas is emerging as a viable alternative.
swa: Hata hivyo, gesi inayotokana na samadi imejitokeza kama mbadala wenye uhakika.

eng: A recent report by AFP divulges that Nepal is making money (almost 600,000 US$ in 2007) trading carbon emissions with the help of numerous biogas plants across the country.
swa: Taarifa ya hivi karibuni ya AFP inadokeza kwamba Nepal inatengeneza pesa (karibu dola 600,000 za Kimarekani mwaka 2007) kwa kuuza kaboni kwa msaada wa vituo kadhaa vya gesi inayotokana na samadi nchini kote.

eng: For a nation struggling find cheap and sustainable source of energy, biogas certainly brings good news for Nepal.
swa: Kwa nchi inayohangaika kutafuta chanzo nafuu na endelevu cha nishati, gesi inayotokana na samadi ni habari njema kwa nepal.

eng: Globalwarming Arclein, a blog on how agriculture can help reduce carbon emission, says that the low tech approach of biogas makes it accessible to the majority of Nepalese people who live in villages:
swa: Globalwarming Arclein, blogu inayoandika kuhusu jinsi kilimo kinavyoweza kusaidia kupunguza gesi ya ukaa, inasema kwamba teknolojia ya hali ya chini ya gesi inayotokana na samadi inasababisha gesi hiyo kuwafikia Wanepali walio wengi ambao wanaishi vijijini:

eng: Biogas production is not high technology. 	Uzalishaji wa gesi inayotokana na samadi hauna teknolojia ya hali ya juu.
It takes a cistern that can be made with a shovel and perhaps setting liner stones as is often done in a modern septic field.
swa: Inahitaji mtungi au tanki ambalo linaweza kutengenezwa kwa beleshi nap engine kuweka matofali ya uzio kama inavyofanya kwenye sehemu za kisasa za maji-taka.

eng: Capping this and drawing of the produced gas into a holding tank is simple and usage after that needs again fairly minimalist hardware that can be jury-rigged together.
swa: Kufunika na kunyonya gesi iliyotengenezwa kwenda kwenye mtungi wa kuhifadhia ni rahisi na matumizi baada ya hapo yanahitaji vifaa vichache vya kuokoteza.

eng: The major requirement is to simply know that it can be done and that it will work.
swa: Hitaji kubwa ni kufahamu kuwa inawezekana na kwamba itafanya kazi.

eng: Recovery of the produced slurry later is unpleasant but no different than similar tasks attended to.It is not a convenient way to produce enough gas for household heating, but certainly sufficient to support incidental heating for cooking and producing hot water in a healthy way."
swa: Upakuzi wa mboji iliyotengenezwa hapo baadaye hakuvutii na hauna tofauti na kazi nyingine za namna hiyo. Siyo njia inayofaa ya kutengeneza gesi ya kutosha ili kupasha moto nyumba, lakini inatosha kabisa kuongezea moto wa kupikia na kuchemsha maji ya moto kwa njia bora.”

eng: Nepal's success in biogas could inspire its neighbors too.
swa: Mafinikio ya Nepal katika gesi inayotokana na samadi imewahamasisha majirani zake pia.

eng: Nepal's closest ally India is also looking forward to develop alternative energy sources to deal with the growing demand in its rapidly industrialized states.
swa: Mshirika wa karibu wa Nepal, India nayo pia inatarajia kuendeleza vyanzo vya nishati mbadala ili kukabiliana na mahitaji yanayoongezeka katika majimbo yake yanayokua kwa haraka katika nyanja ya viwanda.

eng: Razib Ahmed at South Asia Blog, which focuses on the region's business and social issues, says:
swa: Razib Ahmed kwenye South Asia Blog, blogu yenye kutilia makini biashara na masuala ya jamii katika kanda hiyo, anasema:

eng: I am interested about biogas a lot because I believe that it has immense potential not only for Nepal but also for neighboring countries like India and Bangladesh. 	Ninavutiwa sana na gesi inayotokana na samadi kwa sababu ninaamini kuwa ina uwezo mkubwa siyo tu kwa Napal bali hata kwa nchi jirani kama vile India na Bangladeshi.
Biogas Sector Partnership Nepal (BSP-Nepal) is an NGO that is actively working for the promotion of biogas in the country.
swa: Sekta ya ubia wa gesi inayotokana na Samadi Nchini Nepal (BSP-Nepal) ni Asasi Isyo ya Kiserikali ambayo inafanya kazi kwa ajili ya kuitangaza gesi hiyo nchini.

eng: Until June 2008, 172,858 biogas plants have been made with their support.
swa: Hadi mwezi Juni 2008, vituo 172,858 vya gesi inayotokana na samadi vimetengenezwa kutokana na msaada wao.

eng: As a result, more than 1 million people are getting the benefits.
swa: Na matokeo yake, zaidi ya watu milioni 1 wanazipata faida zake.

eng: 1 million people may not sound to be that much to you but you have to remember that it is mainly the poor people living in rural areas who got benefited through this technology.
swa: Watu milioni 1 wanaweza kusikika kama vile si wengi sana kwako lakini inakupasa ukumbuke kuwa kwa kiasi kikubwa ni watu masikini wanaoishi sehemu za vijijini ambao wamenufaika na teknolojia hii.

eng: Not only that, I would also like to catch your attention about the fact that Nepal imports almost 100% of its oil.
swa: Si hivyo tu, lakini pia ningependa kukamata mawazo yako juu ya ukweli kuwa Nepal inaagiza Karibu asilimia 100 ya mafuta yake.

eng: So, every biogas plant made means saving some foreign currency for the country."
swa: Kwa hiyo, kila kituo cha gesi inayotokana na samadi kinachotengenezwa kunamaanisha uokoaji wa fedha za kigeni kwa nchi.”

eng: And the interest in biogas is not a passing fad for Nepal.
swa: Na kuvutiwa na gesi inayotokana na samadi si jambo linalopita kwa Nepal.

eng: After many years of hard work and careful planning, it has been able to generate significant attention.
swa: Baada ya miaka mingi ya kazi ngumu na mipango, imeweza kuongeza hali ya kujulikana.

eng: Back in 2005, Mallika Aryal at RenewableEnergyAccess reported on Nepal's quest to generate sustainability and revenue through biogas.
swa: Tukirudi nyuma mwaka 2005, Mallika Aryal katika RenewableEnergyAccess alitoa taarifa iliyohusu jitihada za Nepal kuataka kuzalisha uendelevu na faida kupitia gesi inayotokana na samadi.

eng: Nepal's Biogas Support Program has extended its work to 66 of the nation's 75 districts and plans to have 200,000 biogas plants installed by 2009. 	Mpango wa kuunga mkono gesi inayotokana na samadi nchini Nepal umeeneza kazi yake kuzifikia wilaya 66 kati ya 75 katika tsaifa hilo na una mpango wa kusimika vituo 200,000 mwaka 2009.
A plant suitable for a rural household costs US $300.
swa: Kituo kinachofaa kwa kayta iliyoko vijijini inagharimu dola za Kimarekani 300.

eng: Government subsidies have made the plants affordable.
swa: Ruzuku za serikali zimefanya vituo hivyo kuwa na gharama nafuu.

eng: An individual invests only $200 and his investment is recouped in three years.
swa: Mtu binafsi anawekeza dola za Kimarekani 200 tu na kitega uchumi chake hurejea baada ya miaka mitatu.

eng: A very good deal indeed!
swa: Mpango mzuri sana!

eng: Now the Nepali biogas plants are on their way to becoming a "good deal" for the global environment.
swa: Hivi sasa vituo vya kutengeneza gesi inayotokana na samadi vimo njiani kuwa “mpango mzuri” kwa ajili ya mazingira ulimwenguni.

eng: When Kyoto Protocol, the global climate treaty, will enter into force for Nepal in December 2005, it would be eligible to start trading the carbon dioxide not emitted by using biogas and earn up to $5 million per year."
swa: Wakati Itikadi ya Kyoto, mkataba wa hali ya hewa duniani, utaanza kutekelezwa Nepal Disemba mwaka 2005, itakuwa na haki ya kuanza kuuza hewa ya ukaa ambayo haikuzalishwa kwa kutumia gesi inayotokana na samadi na kuweza kupata hadi dola milioni 5 kwa mwaka.”

eng: To learn more about how biogas is helping Nepal, here is a video produced by the Nepal Project at Tokyo City University, Japan.
swa: Ili kujua zaidi kuhusu jinsi gesi inayotokana na samadi inavyoisaidia Nepal, ifuatayo ni video iliyotengenezwa na Mradi wa Nepal katika Chuo Kikuu cha Mji wa Tokyo, Japan.

eng: On November 6, a police officer at the Department of Internal Affairs in Novorossiysk used his personal Web site to address Russian Prime Minister Vladimir Putin and talk about numerous problems police officers face in Russia.
swa: Mnamo tarehe 6 Novemba, afisa wa polisi katika Idara ya Mambo ya Ndani huko Novorossiysk alitumia tovuti yake binafsi kuwasiliana na Waziri Mkuu Vladimir Putin na kuzungumzia matatizo lukuki yanayowakabili maafisa wa polisi nchini Urusi.

eng: I think many people will understand me.
swa: Nafikiri watu wengi watanielewa.

eng: I want to work but I am fed up with fictional plans when we are forced to investigate crimes that don’t exist.
swa: Nataka kuchapa kazi, lakini nimechoshwa na mipango ya kingano ambapo tunalazimishwa kupeleleza jinai ambazo hazipo.

eng: I am fed up with fictional plans when we are told that we need to imprison certain people.
swa: Nimechoshwa na mipango ya kutunga ambapo tunaambiwa tuwafunge watu fulani.

eng: I am fed up with staged crimes designed to put some people in jail.
swa: Nimechoshwa na jinai za kutunga zinazoandaliwa ili kuwatupa watu fulani gerezani.

eng: Continuing with his revelations, Dymovskiy admits putting an innocent person in jail under the pressure from his supervisor:
swa: Akiendelea kuweka wazi mambo mbalimbali, Dymovskiy anakiri kumtupa mtu asiye na hatia gerezani kwa sababu ya kulazimishwa na mkubwa wake kazini:

eng: The director of the Department of Internal Affairs awarded me rank of a major, which I received in May, because I promised him to put an innocent person in jail.
swa: Mkurugenzi wa Idara ya mambo ya Ndani alinitunukia cheo cha Meja, ambacho nilikipata mwezi Mei, kwa sababu tu nilimwahidi kutumpa mtu asiye na hatia gerezani.

eng: I’m not afraid to say that.
swa: Siogopi kueleza jambo hili.

eng: I understand that it can be punishable.
swa: Naelewa kuwa naweza kuadhibiwa kwa sababu hii.

eng: But it is the truth and I admit that.
swa: Lakini ni ukweli nami ninaukiri.

eng: Dymovsky also appeals to Russian Prime Minister Vladimir Putin urging him to investigate those problems and put an end to the widespread corruption in the police.
swa: Dymovsky pia anamwomba Waziri Mkuu Vladimir Putin kupeleleza matatizo hayo na kumalizia mbali tatizo la ufisadi katika jeshi la polisi.

eng: The video hit a “viral” stage within hours after its publication with several hundreds of thousands of clicks on YouTube.
swa: Video yake hiyo ilipata watembeleaji wengi sana muda mfupi tu tangu ichapishwe na vilevile maelfu waliibofya kwenye YouTube.

eng: It was widely covered by the Russian mainstream media and discussed on the countless blogs.
swa: Ilichukuliwa pia sana na kuchapishwa na vyombo vikuu vya habari za Urusi na kujadiliwa sana katika blogu nyingi.

eng: It is one of the first examples when Russian citizens successfully deploy new media platform to draw attention of the government toward hot issues in the country.
swa: Ni mfano mmoja kati ya kadhaa ya kwanza ambapo raia wa Urusi wanafaulu vema kabisa kutumia miundo mipya ya majukwa ya habari ili kuwasiliana na serikali hasa kuhusu masuala nyeti yanayoikabili nchi.

eng: The novelty of “citizen video addresses” in Russia is best indicated by a cautious comment from one of the most popular bloggers in the country dolboeb:
swa: Upekee wa "hotuba za kiraia kwa njia ya video" nchini Urusi inaelezwa vema zaidi kwa maoni yenye tahadhari kutoka katika moja ya blogu maarufu zaidi nchini inayoitwa dolboeb:

eng: A monologue with enormous force.
swa: Risala yenye nguvu ya pekee.

eng: I won’t be surprised if it turns out to be a viral marketing.
swa: Sitashangaa kama itageuka kuwa mbinu ambukizi ya utafutaji masoko.

eng: The character is too out-of-this-word.
swa: Mhusika mkuu anaonekana kama mtu wa kutoka sayari nyingine.

eng: Another blogger marchenk writes:
swa: Mwanablogu mwingine marchenk anaandika:

eng: None of us is an angel... I wouldn't admire him as an honest policeman and the lover of the truth (he admits himself that he received the rank of major for putting an innocent person in jail).
swa: Hakuna hata mmoja wetu aliye malaika... simhusudu kama askari mwaminifu na mpenda ukweli (mwenyewe amekiri kwamba alitunukiwa cheo cha Meja kwa kumfunga mtu asiye na hatia gerezani).

eng: However, sincere respect for bravery.
swa: Hata hivyo, nampa heshima kwa ajili ya ujasiri wake wa kuwa mkweli.

eng: There are honest police officers after all.
swa: Kwa hiyo, kumbe kuna maafisa wengine wa polisi walio waaminifu.

eng: Because of them, it makes sense to push forward police reforms.
swa: Kwa sababu yao, ni muhimu kuhakikisha kunakuwepo na mabadiliko katika jeshi la polisi.

eng: I hope to God his publicity gives him protection and honest consideration of his situation.
swa: Ninamwombea Mungu ili kwamba uwekaji wake wazi huu wa mambo umpe kinga na atendewe haki katika hali yake.

eng: On Sunday, November 8, Rashid Nurgaliev, the Russian minister of internal affairs, announced the audit of police forces in Novorossiysk.
swa: Siku ya Jumapili, tarehe 8 Novemba, Rashid Nurgaliev, Waziri wa Urusi wa Mambo ya Ndani, alitangaza ukaguzi wa jeshi la polisi huko Novorossiysk.

eng: Meanwhile, Dymovskiy has been fired “for libel and actions that damage the honor" of the police.
swa: Wakati huohuo, Dymovskiy amefukuzwa kazi kwa sababu ya “uzushi na vitendo ambavyo vinaharibu sifa” ya polisi.

eng: In his interview to Russian radio station "Ekho Moskvy," Dymovskiy said he had been followed and was considering sending his family to Moscow for security reasons.
swa: Katika mahojiano yake na kituo cha redio cha Urusi, “Ekho Moskvy,” Dymovskiy alisema kwamba amekuwa akifuatiliwa na kwa hiyo alikuwa akifikiria kuhamishia familia yake jijini Moscow kwa sababu za kiusalama.

eng: Mohammad Malick comments on the recent terror attack in Peshawar's market area for lower and middle class people: "(it) showed that it is a war with terrorists standing on one side of the blood line, and we the people on the other."
swa: Mohammad Malick anatoa maoni juu ya shambulizi la kigaidi la hivi karibuni kwenye soko la watu wa tabaka chini na la kati huko Peshawar: “limeonyesha kuwa hii ni vita ambyo magaidi wanasimama upande mmoja wa mstari wa damu, na sisi wananchi upande mwingine.”

eng: Eman at AquaCool comments on the first Twitter-inspired street name, in a West Bank Palestinian refugee camp.
swa: Eman katika AquaCool anatoa maoni kuhusu mtaa wa kwanza kupata jina linalotokana na huduma ya Twita, katika kambi ya wakambizi huko ukingo wa Magharibi.

eng: In eastern Paraguay, 217 members of the Ava Guaraní indigenous community recently came down with health symptoms that include nausea and headaches.
swa: Huko Mashariki mwa Paraguay, jumla ya watu 217 wa jumuiya ya wenyeji ya Ava Guaraní walianza kusumbuliwa wakionyesha dalili mbalimbali za kiafya zinazoaminika zilisababishwa na unyunyiziaji wa makusudi wa dawa za kuua wadudu hasa baada ya wao kuwa wamegoma kuhama kutoka katika ardhi waliyoirithi kutoka kwa mababu zao.

eng: It is believed that these individuals became sick as a result of intentional aerial spraying with pesticide, after they refused to vacate their ancestral lands. Governmental officials confirm that parts of the indigenous group's land located in the Itakyry district in the Department of Alto Paraná had been sprayed where no crops are present .
swa: Watendaji wa serikali wamethibitisha kwamba baadhi ya sehemu za ardhi ya wenyeji iliyo katika Wilaya ya Itakyry katika Idara ya Alto Paraná ilinyunyiziwa wakati ambapo hakukuwa na mazao yoyote .

eng: Many of the signs point to Brazilian soy growers as those responsible for the spraying, in part because the indigenous community's land is valuable for the crop and that they had been in a dispute with the Ava Guaraní over the ownership of approximately 3,000 hectares , according to the blog Interparaguay .
swa: Ishara nyingi zinaelekezwa kwa walima maharage ya soya wa KiBrazili kwamba ndiyo wanaohusika na unyunyiziaji huo, kwani kwa kiasi kikubwa ardhi iliyo mikononi mwa jamii za wenyeji ingefaa sana kwa zao hilo na kwamba hawa wamekuwa katika mgogoro na Ava Guaraní kuhusu umiliki wa takribani hekta 3,000, kwa mujibu wa blogu ijulikanayo Interparaguay .

eng: José Ángel López Barrios of Bienvenidos! describes the isolated community where the incident took place:
swa: Sehemu ya ardhi hii iko kwenye ardhi ya kurithi ya mababu wa jamii za wenyeji, kama vile Guaraní.

eng: A 40-fee Dita Tree became a refuge for 36 members of 7 families in Barangay Bagong Silangan (New East Village), Quezon City, Metro Manila as flood waters rose last September 26.
swa: Mti wa aina ya m-dita wenye futi 40 ulikuwa kimbilio la hifadhi kwa watu 36 wa familia saba huko Barangay Bagong Silangan (kijiji cha New East), kwenye mji wa Quezon, Metro Manila wakati maji yalipofurika tarehe 26 Septemba.

eng: The flashflood was caused by a record rainfall unleashed by Typhoon Ketsana which hit the Philippines last September.
swa: Mafuriko hayo yalisababishwa na mvua kubwa iliyovunja rekodi iliyotokana na kimbunga cha Ketsana kilichoikumba nchi ya Ufilipino mwezi Septemba.

eng: It was the worst flooding in the country in the past 40 years.
swa: Ilikuwa ni gharika mbaya zaidi kutokea nchini katika miaka 40 iliyopita.

eng: There are only few Dita Trees left in urban Metro Manila.
swa: Kuna miti michache ya mi-dita iliyobaki kwenye maeneo ya Manila mjini.

eng: Barangay Bagong Silangan is an urban poor community located in the northeastern part of the country’s capital.
swa: Barangay Bagong Silangan ni jamii masikini ya mjini iliyo sehemu ya kaskazini mashariki mwa mji mkuu wa nchi.

eng: More than 30 individuals died in this community during the flooding disaster.
swa: Zaidi ya watu 30 walipoteza maisha yao katika jamii hii wakati wa janga la mafuriko haya.

eng: Arkibong Bayan provides more details:
swa: Arkibong Bayan anatoa undani zaidi wa tukio hili:

eng: 36 members of 7 families climbed up this dita tree as the flood waters was rising and were saved.
swa: Watu 36 wa familia 7 walipanda mti huu wa m-dita wakati maji yanayofurika yalipokuwa yanaongezeka na waliokoka.

eng: They stayed on the branches of this tree from 10 AM of Sept. 26 up to 3 AM of the following day when they climbed down with the waters still waist deep because they were cold and hungry for 17 hours.
swa: Walibaki kwenye matawi ya mti huu kuanzia saa 4 asubuhi ya terehe 26 mpaka saa 9 alfajiri ya siku iliyofuata walipoteremka, na maji yakiwa usawa wa kiuno kwa sababu walipatwa na baridi kali na njaa kwa masaa 17.

eng: The oldest was 60 years old and the youngest 2 weeks old Moral lesson: Don't cut trees, they may save your life one day.
swa: Kati yao mkubwa kuliko wote alikuwa na miaka 60 na mdogo zaidi alikuwa na umri wa majuma mawili tu. Somo la kimaadili: Usikate miti, inaweza kuyaokoa maisha yako siku moja.

eng: (In this case, literally.)
swa: (Katika suala hili, kwa maana ya moja kwa moja.)

eng: Survivors recounted that there were many big snakes which also sought refuge in the Dita Tree.
swa: Walionusurika wanasema kwamba kulikuwa pia na majoka makubwa yaliyokuwa yakitafuta hifadhi kwenye mti huo.

eng: Aside from the Dita Tree, there was another tree which residents claimed also saved the lives of other villagers
swa: Ukiacha mti huo wa m-dita, kulikuwa na mti mwingine ambao wakazi wengine walidai kuwa nao pia uliokoa maisha ya wanakijiji wengine.

eng: We were also shown what we now call the “Tree of Life”, the Dita tree where 7 families (34 individuals) sought refuge during the flood and were saved from the raging flood waters.
swa: Tulionyeshwa pia tunaouita sasa ‘Mti wa Uzima’, m-Dita ambako familia 7 (watu 36) walitafuta hifadhi wakati wa mafuriko na wakaokoka na mafuriko ya maji.

eng: The surviving residents, who were surveying their homes for repairs, talked of how they climbed from roof to roof seeking higher grounds.
swa: Wakazi walionusurika, waliokuwa wanakagua nyumba zao kwa ajili ya ukarabati, walizungumzia namna walivyopanda kutoka paa hadi paa kutafuta eneo lililoinuka zaidi.

eng: They recounted how they rescued a 2 month old baby on floating aluminum roofing.
swa: Walielezea namna waliovyoweza kumwokoa mtoto wa umri wa miezi miwili kwenye paa la bati lililokuwa linaelea.

eng: Arkibong Bayan received a comment from a reader who shared a similar story about how a mango tree saved lives during a natural disaster three years ago
swa: Arkibong Bayan alipokea maoni kutoka kwa msomaji aliyesimulia kuhusu jinsi mti wa mwembe ulivyookoa maisha wakati wa janga mitatu iliyopita.

eng: During the onslaught of Supertyphoon Reming on November 30, 2006, a mango tree saved 5 lives in Padang, Legazpi City (Bicol Region in Luzon Island).
swa: Wakati wa Kimbunga kabambe kilichoitwa Reming Novemba 30, 2006, mwembe uliokoa maisha ya watu watano huko Padang, mjini Lagazpi (mkoa wa Bicol katika kisiwa cha Luzon).

eng: One survivor had two choices: the mango tree or the slab roof of a house.
swa: Mtu mmoja aliyenusurika alikuwa na machaguo mawili: Mwembe ama paa la nyumba.

eng: She chose the tree; those on the slab roof were entirely swept away to the sea.
swa: Akachagua mti; wale waliokuwa kwenye paa walisombwa na mafuriko kuelekea baharini.

eng: Lesson: Plant a tree.
swa: Somo: Panda mti.

eng: It may save your life
swa: Unaweza kuyaokoa maisha yako

eng: After surviving the deadly flood last September, residents of Barangay Bagong Silangan are facing a bigger challenge: rebuilding their homes and their lives.
swa: Baada ya kunusurika na mafuriko mabaya ya mwezi Septemba, wakazi wa Barangay Bagong Silangan wanakabiliwa na changamoto kubwa zaidi: kujenga upya nyumba zao na maisha yao.

eng: The community is a changed community.
swa: Jamii imekuwa jamii iliyobadilika.

eng: Houses were swept away and many basic infrastructure were damaged.
swa: Nyumba zilisombwa na maji na miundo mbinu iliharibiwa vibaya.

eng: We were told that before Ondoy (Typhoon Ketsana) the area was congested like any other urban poor area.
swa: Tuliambiwa kwamba kabla ya Ondoy (Kimbunga cha Ketsana) eneo hilo lilikuwa lina msongamano mkubwa wa watu kama maeneo mengine ya kimasikini mijini.

eng: Now, only the relatively sturdy homes survived.
swa: Sasa, nyumba bora tu ndizo zilipona.

eng: All photos courtesy of Arkibong Bayan
swa: Picha zote kwa hisani ya Arkibong Bayan

eng: Saudi bloggers are rallying to the support of a fellow blogger who claims that a newspaper had lifted photographs and copy from his blog without permission.
swa: Wanablogu wa Kisaudia wanaungana ili kumuunga mkono mwanablogu mwenzao anayelituhumu gazeti moja kuwa limetumia picha na kuzinakili kutoka mwenye blogu yake bila ruhusa.

eng: Saudi Jeans' Ahmed Al Omran has little praise for the paper being accused of plagiarism:
swa: Saudi Jeans‘ Ahmed Al Omran anazo sifa kiduchu mno kwa gazeti hilo linalotuhumiwa kwa kitendo cha kutumia kazi za wengine kinyume cha haki miliki:

eng: Although al-Yaum newspaper has enjoyed a monopoly in the Eastern Province (EP) for a very long time, it remains one of the weakest publications in the country.
swa: Ingawa gazeti la al – Yaum, kwa muda mrefu limefurahia nafasi kubwa katika Jimbo la Mashariki, (EP) linabaki kuwa kati ya machapicho duni zaidi nchini.

eng: I was born and raised in the EP, and I used to read Ashraq al-Awsat, al-Hayat and al-Watan but not al-Yaum.
swa: Nilizaliwa na kukuzwa katika Jimbo la Mashariki, na nilizoea kusoma magazeti ya Ashraq al-Awsat, al-Hayat na al-Watan lakini sio al-Yaum.

eng: Al Omran's distaste was further fueled after Saudi Aggie, a student named Nathan at the newly opened King Abdulla University of Science and Technology (KAUST) raised the alarm that the paper had used his photographs and coverage of the recent students elections.
swa: Kutofurahishwa kwa Al Omran kulichochewa zaidi baada ya Saudi Aggie, mwanafunzi mwenye jina la Nathan wa Chuo Kikuu cha Sayansi na Teknolojia cha Mfalme Abdulla (KAUST) kilichofunguliwa hivi karibuni alipoleta malalamiko kwamba gazeti hilo limetumia picha zake pamoja na uchambuzi wake kuhusu uchaguzi wa wanafunzi hivi majuzi.

eng: He posts a copy of the clipping from the paper and asks his readers:
swa: Ameweka nakala ya habari hizo kutoka gazetini na kuwauliza wasomaji wake:

eng: I can't believe this!
swa: Siwezi kuamini hili!

eng: Look at this article that was published recently in the major Saudi Arabian newspaper, Al Yaum.
swa: Angalia makala hii iliyochapishwa hivi majuzi kwenye gazeti maarufu la Saudi Arabia, Al Yaum.

eng: Do those pictures look familiar?
swa: Je, picha hizi zinaonekana kana kwamba zinafahamika?

eng: How about the words?
swa: Vipi kuhusu maneno?

eng: If you can't read Arabic, this was taken almost verbatim from my blog post "Elections" published October 7th, 2009.
swa: Kama huwezi kusoma Kiarabu, hii ilichukuliwa karibu neno kwa neno kutoka kwenye makala ya blogu yangu niliyoipa jina la ‘uchaguzi’ na kuichapa Oktoba 5, 2009.

eng: This can't be legal, not even in Saudi Arabia!
swa: Hii haiwezi kuwa sahihi kisheria, hata hapa Saudi Arabia!

eng: The American student further adds:
swa: Mwanafuzi huyo wa Kimarekani anaongeza:

eng: If I was in the USA I would file an intellectual property rights case against Al Yaum.
swa: Kama ningekuwa Marekani ningefungua kesi ya haki miliki ya utaaluma dhidi ya Al Yaum.

eng: If it was the New York Times that plagiarized my blog I would be rich right now.
swa: Kama lingekuwa ni Gazeti la New York Times limetumia kazi yangu bila ruhusa, ningekuwa tajiri sasa hivi.

eng: Do intellectual rights to published thoughts and photos have any value here?
swa: Hivi haki miliki za utaaluma kwa mawazo na picha zilizochapishwa zina thamani yoyote hapa?

eng: Al Omran notes:
swa: Al Omran anazingatia:

eng: Nathan is thinking about suing them, which would be awesome, but probably they have already embarrassed themselves enough.
swa: Nathan anafikiria kuwashitaki, jambo ambalo nadhani litakuwa zuri sana, lakini labda wameshajitia aibu vilivyo wao wenyewe.

eng: Commentators on Nathan's blog are sympathetic to the blogger's plight.
swa: Watoa maoni kwenye blogu ya Nathan wanaguswa na yaliyompata mwanablogu:

eng: Mazoo writes:
swa: Mazoo anaandika:

eng: I'm sorry to see that happening to you ..
swa: Ninasikitika kuona hili linatokea kwako...

eng: however , it's a common thing here in KSA :D ..
swa: Lakini, hili ni jambo lililozoeleka hapa Saudi Arabia...

eng: I heard about many many cases in which my friends content ( blog entries , pictures and ideas ) have been stolen by some lazy journalists.
swa: Nimesikia kesi nyingi ambazo kazi za marafiki zangu (maandiko ya blogu, picha na mawazo) yameibwa na waandishi habari wavivu.

eng: They complained about it and some wrote to the chief editor - some of them post an apology and some of them fired the person who stole the content
swa: Walilalamikia hali hii na wengine waliaandikia wahariri wakuu –wengine wao huandika taarifa za kuomba msamaha na wengine wao humfukuza kazi mtu aliyeiba maudhui

eng: Al Hanouf, who describes herself as a law student, is seeking justice:
swa: Al Hanouf, anayejielezea mwenyewe kuwa ni mwanafunzi wa sheria, anataka haki itendeke:

eng: If this action considered under a computer-related crimes , then he - the journalist - should be in jail for more than 6 months and he should pay to you not less than 250,000 SR .
swa: Kama kitendo hiki kikiangaliwa chini ya makosa ya jinai yanayohusiana na kompyuta, basi huyu – mwana habari – inatakiwa awe jela kwa zaidi ya miezi sita na kukulipa si chini ya fedha ya Riyali za Saudia 250,000.

eng: You should go to a lawyer , and please don't end this by emailing the newspaper!
swa: Unapaswa uende kwa mwanasheria, na tafadhali usilimalize hili kwa kuliandikia gazeti barua pepe!

eng: there is a law , and it wouldn't be able to correct the mistakes if we end the issues in our lazy way !
swa: Kuna sheria, na (gazeti) halitaweza kurekebisha makosa yake kama tutalimaliza suala hili kwa njia zatu za kizembe!

eng: And Chiara advises:
swa: Na Chiara anashauri:

eng: I share in the revulsion for plagiarism, and the common tactic of translating and plariagizing is no better.
swa: Nami ninashiriki katika kuchefuka na uvunjifu huu wa sheria ya haki miliki, na njia iliyozoeleka ya kutafsiri na ‘kuiba’ kazi za wengine si nafuu.

eng: You can copyright your whole blog as other bloggers have done, and have your name embedded on the photos.
swa: Unaweza kuweka blogu yako nzima chini ya haki miliki kama ambavyo wanablogu wengine wamefanya, na kufanya namna ambayo jina lako litaonekana kwenye picha.

eng: In a follow up post, Nathan writes:
swa: Kwenye makala fuatilizi, Nathan anaandika:

eng: In Saudi Arabia, gossip spreads like the plague.
swa: Nchini Saudi Arabia, umbea huenea kama vile ugonjwa wa mlipuko.

eng: This blog has received tens of thousands of new visitors in one week alone.
swa: Blogu hii imepokea makumi elfu ya watembeleaji wapya katika juma moja tu

eng: I came to Saudi Arabia to build bridges, not to make enemies.
swa: Nilikuja Saudia kujenga madaraja (ushirikiano), sio kutengeneza maadui.

eng: I came to study and research at a university which is striving with all of its might to be one of the best research universities in the world, not to get money from people or organizations.
swa: Nilikuja kusoma na kutafiti katika Chuo kikuu ambacho kinajitahidi kwa nguvu zote kuwa moja wapo ya vyuo vikuu bora vya utafiti duniani, na sio kupata fedha kutoka kwa watu ama mashirika.

eng: I do want accountability.
swa: Ninataka uwajibikaji.

eng: What Al Yaum did was wrong, but the tone of the discussion is also wrong.
swa: Ilichokifanya Al Yaum kilikuwa ni makosa, lakini mwenendo wa mjadala pia una makosa.

eng: And his final words to his readers are:
swa: Na maneno yake ya mwisho kwa wasomaji wake ni:

eng: If you want to borrow something from my blog, please ask first.
swa: Kama unataka kuazima kitu kutoka kwenye blogu yangu, tafadhali omba kwanza.

eng: Nobody, myself included, enjoys misunderstandings.
swa: Hakuna mtu, nikijijumuisha na mimi, anayependa kutokuelewana.

eng: Using a translation tool, the journalist concerned writes to Nathan stating his case.
swa: Kwa kutumia kifaa cha kutafsiri, mwandishi husika anamwandikia Nathan akilielezea vyema suala lake.

eng: The Somali Media Centre is a forum of Somali journalists and bloggers living in Somalia and outside.
swa: Kituo cha habari cha Somalia ni jukwaa la waandishi na wanablogu wa Kisomali wanaoishi ndani na nje ya Somalia.

eng: The Centre distributes news content and publishes blogs written by journalists.
swa: Kituo kinasambaza machapicho ya habari na kuchapisha blogu zilizoandikwa na waandishi wa habari.

eng: The Somali Media Centre is an independent forum for the Somali journalists in and outside the country.
swa: Kituo cha Habari cha Somalia ni jukwaa linalojitegemea kwa ajili ya waandishi wa Kisomali ndani na nje ya nchi hiyo.

eng: It is established to promote the profile of the brave, hardworking journalists who devoted their lives to serve their people worldwide.
swa: (Kituo hicho) kimeanzishwa kukuza wasifu wa waandishi werevu, na wachapa kazi waliyoyatoa maisha yao kuwatumiakia watu dunia nzima.

eng: Somalia has been dubbed as a failed state, a country associated with death, long running civil strife, warlords, terrorism and modern piracy.
swa: Somalia imekuwa ikichukuliwa kama nchi iliyoshindwa, nchi inayohusishwa na vifo, mapigano ya wenyewe kwa wenyewe yasiyoisha, vita, ugaidi na uharamia wa kisasa.

eng: But one of the most successful stories over the years has been the rise of the independent media and freedom of thought.
swa: Lakini moja wapo ya habari za mafanikio kwa miaka mingi imekuwa ni kukua kwa uhuru wa habari na maoni.

eng: However, the dedication and reporting of the truth come at a price.
swa: Hata hivyo, kuupa kipaumbele na kuutangaza ukweli huja kwa gharama kubwa.

eng: The Centre publishes running blogs by these journalists.
swa: Kituo hicho huchapisha blogu za waandishi hawa.

eng: Also, the Centre distributes news content and reports by the journalists.
swa: Pia, kituo kinatawanya habari na taarifa za waandishi wa habari.

eng: The Centre coordinates between the Somali and non-Somali journalists.
swa: Kituo pia kinaratibu waandishi wa Kisomali na wale wasio Wasomali.

eng: It gives non-Somali journalists who may be traveling to Somalia with first hand advice and contacts.
swa: Kinawapa waandishi wasio Wasomali wanaoweza kuwa wanasafiri kwenda Somalia ushauri na mawasiliano ya awali.

eng: The Centre also works with high profile international media organizations in commissioning, producing and filing stories and reports about Somalia and the Horn of Africa region.
swa: Kituo pia kinafanya kazi na mashirika makubwa ya kimataifa ya habari kwa ushirikiano, kuzalisha na kujazia habari na taarifa kuhusu Somalia na eneo lote la Pembe ya Afrika.

eng: Solana Larsen writes about the origin of Somali Media Centre project:
swa: Solana Larsen anaandika kuhusu asili ya Mradi wa Kituo cha Habari cha Somalia:

eng: In case you hadn't guessed, I'm not Somali.
swa: Kama haujahisi bado, mimi si Msomali.

eng: In journalism school in London in 2002 I had a classmate named Harun Hassan who I used to ask a lot of questions about life in Mogadishu and Somali politics.
swa: Katika shule ya Uandishi wa Habari jijini London mwaka 2002 nilikuwa na mwanafunzi mwenzangu aitwaye Harun Hassan ambaye nilizoea kumuuliza maswali mengi kuhusu maisha yake ya Mogadishu na Siasa za Somalia.

eng: After we graduated, we remained friends and I introduced him to writing for openDemocracy.net where I was a commissioning editor for a few years.
swa: Baada ya kuhitimu, tulibaki kuwa marafiki na nilimfahamisha kuhusu uwezekano wa yeye kuandikia mtandao wa openDemocracy.net ambapo nilikuwa mhariri kwa miaka michache.

eng: Later on, I became a managing editor at Global Voices Online, where we occasionally also have stories about Somali bloggers.
swa: Baadaye, nikawa mhariri mtendaji wa Global Voices Online, ambapo mara chache tulikuwa na habari kuhusiana na wanablogu wa kiSomali.

eng: Harun used to tell me about ideas he had for media projects involving the Somali community in London.
swa: Harun alizoea kuniambia kuhusu mawazo aliyokuwanayo kwa ajili ya Mradi wa Habari uliojumuisha jamii ya Kisomali mjini London.

eng: He created a newsletter on paper in Somali, and at one point he approached me about making a website for something he called the Somali Media Centre.
swa: Alianzisha gazeti la Kisomali, na wakati fulani alinifuata nimsaidie kutengeneza tovuti kwa ajili ya kitu alichokiita Kituo cha Habari cha Somalia.

eng: Media coverage of the Somali community in the UK was so negative and inaccurate, Harun felt the only way to correct it, was to make it easier for UK journalists to find Somali journalists and researchers to talk to.
swa: Habari za jamii ya KiSomali kwenye vyombo vya habari nchini Uingereza zilikuwa hasi na zisizo sahihi, Harun alifikiria kuwa namna pekee ya kusahihisha hilo,ilikuwa ni kuwarahisishia waandishi wa Uingereza kuwapata waandishi wa Kisomali na watafiti wa kuongea nao.

eng: We made a website and blog, but we were soon distracted by other work and the project lay dormant.
swa: Tulitengeneza tovuti na blogu, lakini baadae kidogo tukakabiliwa na kazi nyingine na mradi ukadumaa.

eng: The website you are looking at now, is our second attempt at creating a networking tool for Somali journalists and others to use to help improve global understanding of Somalis and Somalia.
swa: Wavuti unayoipitia sasa, ni jaribio letu lapili la kutengeneza nyenzo ya mtandao kwa ajili ya waandishi wa Kisomali na wengine kuitumia ili kusaidia kuboresha uwelewa wa kidunia wa Wasomali na Somalia yenyewe.

eng: Below are some of latest blog posts from The Somali Media Centre:
swa: Hapa chini ni baadhi ya makala za blogu za hivi karibuni kabisa kutoka kwenye Kituo cha Habari cha Somalia:

eng: In a post titled, Affair to Remember, Fathia Absie writes about the conviction of Joshua Asisa, a peace-keeper in Somalia, for engaging in an affair with a young Somali woman:
swa: Katika makala yenye kichwa cha habari, Uzinifu wa Kukumbuka, Fathia Absie anaandika kuhusu kushitakiwa kwa Joshua Asisam mlinzi wa amani katika Somalia, kwa kujihusisha na uhusiano wa kimapenzi na mwanamke wa Kisomali:

eng: Military court in Kampala convicted Joshua Asisa to a one-and-half years in prison.
swa: Mahakama ya Kijeshi ya Kampala ilimhukumu Joshua Asisa kifungo cha mwaka mmoja na nusu jela.

eng: Mr. Asisa who is a member of the AMASOM peace-keepers in Somalia have been found guilty for engaging in an affair with a young Somali woman by the name of Nimco Omar and impregnating her after marrying her under a false pretence by telling her that he was a Muslim.
swa: Asisa ambaye ni mwanachama wa walinzi wa amani wa AMASOM nchini Somalia alipatiaka na hatia ya kujuhusisha na uhusiano wa kimapenzi na mwanamke wa Kisomali aitwaye Nimco Omar na kumpa ujauzito baada ya kumuoa kwa kumdanganya kuwa alikuwa Mwislamu.

eng: This story took place last year in Mogadisho but no one heard of it till this young woman went to Kampala and took Mr. Asisa to court for lying to her.
swa: Habari hii ilitokea mwaka uliopita huko Mogadisho lakini hakuna aliyesikia mpaka mwanamke huyu mdogo alipokwenda Kampala na kumshitaki Bw. Asisa mahakamani kwa kumdanganya.

eng: Mohamed Abukar Ahmed who is the Journalist that broke the story has told me that he has learned the story after it was reported by a news paper in Uganda.
swa: Mohamed Abubakar Ahmed ambaye ni mwandishi aliyeiibua habari hiyo aliniambia kuwa aliipata habari hiyo baada ya kuwa imeripotiwa na magazeti ya Uganda.

eng: After that Mr. Ahmed tried to get in touch with the leaders of the Somali community in Kambala and was able to get in touch with the girl.
swa: Baada ya hapo, Bw. Ahmed alijaribu kuonana na viongozi wa jamii ya Kisomali waishio Kampala na akaweza kukutana na msichana huyo.

eng: He told me that Ms. Omar told him about her story and how she met Mr. Asisa who is doctor.
swa: Aliniambia kuwa Bi. Omar alimwambia kuhusu habari hiyo na jinsi alivyokutana na Bw. Asisa ambaye ni daktari.

eng: He was working at a private hospital for the Uganda military in Mogadisho.
swa: Alikuwa akifanya kazi kwenye hospitali binafsi kwa ajili ya jeshi la Uganda mjini Mogadisho.

eng: in the spirit of spreading the word.., writes Idil Osman:
swa: “kwa nia ya kutawanya neno..,” anaandika Idil Osman:

eng: The recruitment taking place in the Somali refugee camps in Dadaab, Northeastern Kenya has stirred some controversial outbursts by many in and outside the region.
swa: Mafunzo ya kijeshi yanayofanyika katika makambi ya wakimbizi wa Kisomali huko Dadaab, Kaskazini mashariki ya Kenya yamechochea kelele zinazochanganya wengi ndani na nje ya eneo.

eng: However what I am particularly bewildered with is the stand-point of the Kenyan government.
swa: Hata hivyo ninashangazwa sana na msimamo wa serikali ya Kenya.

eng: I did an investigative report on this issue earlier on at work where the defense minister of Kenya firmly claimed Kenya had not given permission for this recruitment to take place.
swa: Nilifanya ripoti ya uchunguzi katika suala hili mapema kazini ambapo waziri wa ulinzi wa Kenya alidai kwa msimamo kwamba Kenya haikutoa ruhusa kwa mafunzo haya kufanyika.

eng: Meanwhile witnesses and human rights activists are recording and documenting evidence of these youngsters being put in Kenyan military trucks and driven to Kenyan military training bases.
swa: Wakati huo huo mashahidi na wanaharakati wa haki za binadamu wanarekodi na kuweka kumbukumbu za ushahidi wa vijana hawa wanaowekwa katika magari ya kijeshi ya Kenya na kusafirishwa kwa magari kwenda kwenye vyuo vya mafunzo ya Kijeshi vya Kenya.

eng: Many of these youngsters are taken under false pretence and the promise of regular salary and a stable job with a UN/EU/AU backed military project.
swa: Wengi wa vijana hawa wanachukuliwa kwa kudanganywa na kuahidiwa mshahara mzuri pamoja na kazi inayoaminika kwenye miradi ya kijeshi ya Umoja wa Mataifa/Umoja wa Ulaya/Umoja wa Afrika..

eng: In reality they are being recruited to go and fight in the very war they fled from and had turned them into refugees.
swa: Kiukweli wanafunzwa kwenda na kupigana kwenye vita ile ile waliyoikimbia na kuwafanya wawe wakimbizi.

eng: Many of these young refugees are reported to be underage and taken without their parents' consent.
swa: Wengi wa wakimbizi hawa vijana wanaarifiwa kuwa chini ya umri unaotakikana na wamechukuliwa bila ridhaa ya wazazi wao.

eng: It also violated their international human right as refugees according to the recently released Human Rights Watch press release, because refugees are meant to be kept in civilian conditions.
swa: Imevunja haki zao za kimataifa za binadamu kama wakimbizi kwa mujibu wa tangazo la kwenye vyombo vya habari lilitolewa hivi karibuni na Shirika la Human Rights Watch, kwa sababu wakimbizi wanatakiwa kuwekwa kwenye mazingira ya kiraia.

eng: Solana discusses the issue of "unnamed sources" in Western media reports in her post titled "When Local Sources go Unnamed":
swa: Solana anajadili suala la ‘chanzo kisichotaka kufahamika’ katika taarifa za vyombo vya habari vya Kimagharibi kwenye makala yake aliyoipa jina la “Wakati vyanzo vya mahali vinapochagua kutokuwa na jina”

eng: just picked up the latest edition of National Geographic Magazine for their story on "Shattered Somalia".
swa: nimechukua toleo la hivi karibuni la jarida la National Geographic Magazine kwa habari yao inayohusu ‘Somalia iliyovunjika’.

eng: The photos of Mogadishu by Pascal Maitre are beautiful, though they show a lot of destruction.
swa: Picha za Mogadishu zilizopigw ana Pascal Maitre ni nzuri, ingawa zinaonyesha uharibifu mkubwa.

eng: And the writer, Robert Draper gives a fair and sympathetic summary of a complicated history.
swa: Na mwandishi, Robert Draper anatoa muhtasari wa haki na wenye mguso kuhusu historia tata.

eng: He also definitely makes the challenges of foreign reporting in Somalia clear.
swa: Pia anaziweka wazi changamoto za upashaji habari wa kigeni.

eng: Curiously, Somali journalist Harun Hassan is mentioned by name in a photo caption of a traffic guard in Mogadishu, but as far as I can see nowhere in the text itself.
swa: Katika hali inayoacha maswali, mwandishi wa Kisomali Harun Hassan anatajwa kwa jina kwenye maelezo ya picha inayomwonyesha mlinzi wa barabarani mjini Mogadishu, lakini kwa kiwango ninachoona haionekani kwenye habari yenyewe.

eng: Why the reluctance to reveal sources?
swa: Kwa nini kuna ugumu wa kuweka wazi chanzo?

eng: If Draper has taken the trouble of contacting and interviewing Somali media sources, why not share this information with the readers?
swa: Kama Draper alihangaika kuwasiliana na kuvihoji vyanzo vya Habari vya Somalia, kwa nini asiwaeleze wasomaji wake habari hiyo?

eng: Is this a typical experience of Somali journalists who assist Western journalists with their reporting?
swa: Je, huu ndio uzoefu wa wandishi wa Kisomali wanaowasaidia waandishi wa Kimagharibi kuhabarisha?

eng: I hope members of the Somali Media Centre will help shed light on what it's like to be on that end of the reporting team.
swa: Ninatumainii wanachama wa Kituo cha Habri cha Somalia watasaida kutupa mwanga wa jinsi inavyokuwa kwenye sehemu hiyo ya timu inayotengeneza ripoti.

eng: You can see the list of current members of the Centre here.
swa: Unaweza kuona orodha ya wanachama waliopo wa Kituo hicho hapa.

eng: An English literature professor from the little Mediterranean city of Tartous and a Syrian-Canadian writer on a trip to her mother country exchange glances at a cafe called Sea Breeze.
swa: Profesa wa Fasihi ya Kiingereza kutoka mji wa mdogo wa Tartous huko Mediterranean na mwandishi mwenye asili mchanganyiko ya Siria na Canada wakiwa safarini kuelekea kwenye nchi yake ya asili wanatizamana wakiwa kwenye mgahawa unaoitwa Sea breeze.

eng: That's how Mariyah and Abu Fares chose to start their adventure, and their readers' new addiction.
swa: Hivyo ndivyo Mariya na Abu Fares walivyoamua kuanza shani yao na kunaswa kwa wasomaji wao.

eng: A low rumble in my stomach broke into my daydream as a waft of spices and seafood drifted enticingly by me.
swa: Mngurumo mdogo tumboni mwangu uliingilia ndoto yangu ya mchana wakati harufu ya viungo na samaki iliponipita.

eng: I felt as though I hadn’t eaten in days.
swa: Nilijisikia kana kwamba sijakula kwa siku kadhaa.

eng: I looked back through the window and spotted the waitress, resting casually near what appeared to be the kitchen door.
swa: Niliangalia nyuma kupitia dirishani nikamuona muhudumu wa kike, akipumzika karibu na mlango ulioonekana kana kwamba ni wa jikoni.

eng: She had been immersed in a book but as though she had a sixth sense, she caught my gaze within seconds of it falling on her.
swa: Alikuwa amezama kwenye kitabu lakini kana kwamba alikuwa na hisia ya sita, alibaini macho yangu ndani ya sekunde chache baada ya kuanza kumuangalia.

eng: She smiled knowingly and approached my table.
swa: Alitabasamu kwa ufahamu na kuijongelea meza yangu.

eng: “Hungry?”
swa: “Una njaa?”

eng: “Oh, yes!
swa: “Oh, ndio!

eng: Do you have a menu?”
swa: Je una orodha ya vyakula?”

eng: “Not here.
swa: “Sinayo hapa.

eng: But I’ll tell you what’s being made fresh today.”
swa: Lakini nitakueleza ni chakula kipi kinachopikwa leo.”

eng: “Oh heaven.”
swa: “Ah mbingu.”

eng: I thought to myself and smiled back at her, enthusiastically awaiting her description of dinner.
swa: Nilijiwazia na kumrejeshea kutabasamu, kwa hamu nikisubiri ufafanuzi wa chakula cha jioni.

eng: The story starts out as simple as that.
swa: Hadithi inaanza kwa urahisi kama hivyo.

eng: The two writers, who are switching places every week, went from there.
swa: Waandishi hao wawili, ambao wanabadilishana sehemu kila juma, waliendelea kutokea hapo.

eng: We learn about Yasmina, Prof. Youssef's former student and the waitress at Sea Breeze, and Yazan, the nonchalant chef, all to the backdrop of Tartous' marvelous sea side, and Abu Fares' and Mariyah's exquisite writing.
swa: Tunajifunza juu ya Yasmina, mwanafunzi wa zamani wa Profesa Youseff na mhudumu kwenye mgahawa wa Sea Breeze, na Yazan, mpishi asiyejali, yote yakiwa katika mandhari ya ufukweni mwa mji Tartous, pamoja na uandishi maridhawa wa Abu Fares na Mariyah.

eng: When Yasmina was introducing herself my eyes were distracted by the other woman.
swa: Pale Yasmina alipojitambulisha kwangu macho yangu yalivutwa na mwanamke mwingine.

eng: With delicate fingers, she picked a small hot fish by the tail, dipped it slightly in a bowl of sauce, brought it close to her lips, blew on it to cool it down then swallowed it all, head, bones and tail like a true gourmet.
swa: Na vidole vyake laini, alichukua samaki wa moto mdogo kwa kumkamata mkiani, akamtosa kwenye bakuli la mchuzi, akamsogeza Karibu na midomo yake, akapuliza ili ampoze halafu akammeza wote, kichwa, mifupa pamoja na mkia kama vile mtaalamu wa chakula wa kweli.

eng: She closed her eyes and swam in her own pool of ecstasy.
swa: Alifumba macho yake na akjitosa katika bwawa la kilele cha hisia.

eng: Then… then with her other hand, she pulled at a lock of hair which went astray in front of her face and shepherded it to join the others behind her ear.
swa: Kisha… kwa kutumia mkono wake mwingine, alivuta kiasi cha nywele zake zilizokuwa zimezagaa usoni kwake na kuzirejesha kuungana na nyingine zilikuwa nyuma ya sikio lake.

eng: It was precisely the way she pulled at her hair that made me utterly defenseless.
swa: Namna alivyovyozirekebisha nywele zake kwa usahihi mkubwa ndiko kulikonifanya niwe mdhaifu bila kinga yoyote.

eng: We are at Part 16 at the moment, but be sure to catch it from the beginning.
swa: Tuko katika sehemu ya 16 hivi sasa, lakini hakikisha unaipata hadithi yote kuanzia mwanzo.

eng: Indonesia has a vibrant blogging scene with a strong emphasis on community.
swa: Indonesia ina uwanja wa blogu uliosisimka na wenye msisitizo mkubwa kwa jamii.

eng: The annual Blogger Festival (Pestablogger) Indonesia attracted bloggers and tech lovers from all over the vast island nation.
swa: Tamasha la mwaka la wanablogu (Pestablogger) la Indonesia liliwavutia wanablogu na wapenzi wa teknolojia kutoka sehemu zote za taifa.

eng: Packed venue for Indonesia Blogger Festival Scenes from the bloggers festival.
swa: Ukumbi uliojaa wa tamasha la blogu la Indonesia Taswira kutoka kwenye tamasha la blogu.

eng: This was the third time the annual event was being held and it is nice to see the number of participants increase every year. Indonesian bloggers tend to be a varied bunch, not just in geography but also in terms of age and profession.
swa: Hii ilikuwa ni mara ya tatu kwa tukio hili la mwaka kufanyika na ni vizuri kuona idadi ya washiriki inaongezeka kila mwaka.

eng: A breakout session on blogging ethics
swa: Kipindi cha majadiliano juu ya maadili ya kublogu

eng: A breakout session on citizen journalism
swa: Kipindi cha majadiliano juu ya uanahabari wa kiraia

eng: A citizen journalist shares his experience with bloggers
swa: Mwanahabari wa kiraia akielezea uzoefu wake kwa wanablogu

eng: A breakout session on bridging the divide within Indonesia via blogging.
swa: Kipindi cha majadiliano juu ya kuunganisha kwenye utengano ndani ya Indonesia kwa kutumia blogu.

eng: The participants also discussed the ways in which blogs can be used to connect Indonesia with the outside world.
swa: Washiriki pia walijadili njia ambazo Indonesia inaweza kutumia kuiunganisha na dunia ya nje.

eng: Tristam(representing a sponsoring organisation), Chip (tech enthusist from Vietnam) and Retty (Indonesian blogger) in a discussion.
swa: Tristam (aliyewakilisha shirika la wadhamini), Chip, (mkereketwa wa teknolojia kutoka Vietnam) na Retty (Mwanablogu wa Indonesia) wakiwa katika majadiliano.

eng: Indonesian event do not see the level of outside participation that Cambodian or Thai events do.
swa: Tukio hili la Indonesia halikushuhudia viwango vya ushiriki kutoka nje ambavyo Kampuchea au Thailand huvishuhudia.

eng: Still, curious people are trickling in and we hope to have more people from the wider South East Asian region the next time.
swa: Hata hivyo, watu waliojaa udadisi wanatiririka na tunatumaini kupata watu zaidi kutoka maeneo ya Kusini Mashariki ya Asia wakati ujao.

eng: A batik artist making the blogger fest t-shirt.
swa: Msanii wa Batik akitengeneza shati la tamasha la blogu

eng: Blogger take a break from their discussions to enjoy some music.
swa: Wanablogu wanachukua mapumziko kutoka kwenye majadiliano na kuburudika na muziki.

eng: Tunisian blogger Fatma Riahi, who blogs as Fatma Arabicca, has been charged with defamation on her own blog and is now being detained. A group has been formed on Facebook in support of the 34-year-old blogger, who is also being accused of blogging on Debat Tunise (Tunisia Debate).
swa: Mwanablogu wa Kitunisia Fatma Riahi ambaye hublogu kama Fatma Arabicca, ameshtakiwa kwa udhalilishaji katika blogu yake na hivi sasa amewekwa kizuizini.Kundi limeundwa kwenye Facebook kumuunga mkono mwanablogu huyu mwenye umri wa miaka 34, ambaye pia anatuhumiwa kublogu kwenye Debat Tunise (Mdahalo wa Tunisia).

eng: The start of this year's French literary season saw French-Senegalese novelist and playwright Marie N'Diaye awarded a much-awaited Prix Goncourt.
swa: Mwanzo wa msimu wa Fasihi ya Kifaransa mwaka huu ulishuhudia mwandishi wa riwaya na michezo ya kuigiza mwenye asili ya Kisenegali na Kifaransa Marie N’Diaye akipewa tuzo iliyosuburiwa sana ya Prix Goncourt.

eng: However, N'Diaye and her family move to Berlin to years ago, in large part because of French president Nicolas Sarkozy's politics.
swa: Lakini, N’Diaye na familia yake walikwishahamia mjini Berlin miaka miwili iliyopita, hasa kutokana na siasa za rais wa Ufaransa Nicolas Sarkozy.

eng: Last year, the panel of this prestigious award created a sensation when it chose Afghan writer Atiq Rahimi, for his French language novel, Syngué Sabour.
swa: Mwaka jana, jopo la tuzo hii yenye hadhi walizusha hisia kali pale walipomchagua mwandishi wa Kiafghani Atim Rahimi, kwa kitabu chake cha Kifaransa, Syngué Sabour.

eng: Will this be another opportunity to celebrate diversity in a changing French society?
swa: Je hii itakuwa ni fursa nyingine ya kusherehekea mchanganyiko wa aina mbalimbali katika jamii inayobadilika ya Kifaransa?

eng: Or will the moment be spoiled by controversy?
swa: Au itakuwa ni wasaa utakaoharibiwa na utete wa tukio?

eng: Explains DW-World :
swa: DW-World anaeleza:

eng: In an interview with "Inrockuptibles" magazine last summer, N'Diaye said she had decided to leave France and move to Berlin in 2007 "in great part because of Sarkozy."
swa: Katika mahojiano na gazeti la “Inrockuptibles” kiangazi kilichopita, N’Diaye alisema kuwa aliamua kuondoka Ufaransa na kuhamia Berlin mwaka 2007 ‘kwa kiwango kikubwa kutokana na Sarkozy”

eng: The controversy began after Eric Raoult, a lawmaker and member of Sarkozy's ruling UMP party, wrote to the culture minister last week recommending that NDiaye be reminded of the "duty of restraint" that comes with the Goncourt.
swa: Sakata hilo lilianza baada ya Eric Raoult, mtungasheria na mwanachama wa chama tawala cha Sarkozy, UMP, aliandika barua kwa waziri wa utamaduni wiki iliyopita akishauri kuwa N’Diaye akumbushwe “wajibu wa kujiheshimu” ambao unaambatana na tuzo ya Goncourt.

eng: In response, France's cultural establishment has thrown accusations of censorship into the debate.
swa: Katika kutoa majibu, wenye nguvu katika sekta ya utamaduni walishutumu kuwa kuna uchujaji katika malumbano haya.

eng: Bernard Pivot, a Goncourt jury member, accused Raoult of knowing nothing about the literary scene.
swa: Bernard Pivot, mwanachama katika jopo la Goncourt, alimshutumu Raoult kuwa hafahamu chochote katika uwanja wa fasihi.

eng: N'Diaye, born in 1967 to a French mother and a Senegalese father, won the Goncourt prize for her novel, "Trois femmes puissantes" ("Three Powerful Women"), a story about three women caught between France and Senegal and the hellish ordeal of illegal migration from Africa.
swa: N’Diaye, aliyezaliwa mwaka 1967 na mama Mfaransa na baba Msenegali, alishinda tuzo ya Goncourt kutokana na riwaya yake “Trois femmes puissantes” (”Wanawake watatu wenye nguvu”), hadithi inayohusu wanawake waliojikuta katikati ya Ufaransa na Senegal na katika mkasa wa dhiki mbaya ya uhamiaji usio halali kutokea Afrika.

eng: The story of these migrants has been told many times before, but if this can help people understand their fate a bit better, I will be happy, said NDiaye.
swa: “Hadithi ya hawa wahamiaji imesimuliwa mara nyingi kabla, lakini kama hii itawasaidia watu kufahamu hatima yao vyema zaidi, basi nitafurahi,” alisema N’Diaye.

eng: What was it that stirred Eric Raoult's ire?
swa: Ni kitu gain kilichochochea hasira ya Eric Raoult?

eng: No less than an interview of the woman novelist, when she answered magazine Les Inrocks's question : "Do you feel well in Sarkozy's France?" saying :
swa: Si pungufu ya mahojiano ya mwanamke huyu mwandishi, wakati alipojibu swali la gazeti la Les Inrocks: “Je unajisikia vizuri katika Ufaransa ya Sarkozy?” alisema :

eng: Ugandan politicians are behaving like grasshoppers: "Following the pattern of most dictator regimes coming to an end, Museveni and his collaborators in the armed occupation of Buganda are starting to behave like grasshoppers."
swa: Wanasiasa wa Uganda wanakuwa kama panzi: "kufuatia hali ya kufikia kikomo kwa tawala nyingi za kiimla, Museveni na washirika wake katika ukaliaji wa mabavu wa Buganda kwa kutumia silaha wanaanza kuwa kama panzi."

eng: Do all pregnant women deserve equal human rights, or do pregnant women in prison forfeit those rights?
swa: Je, wanawake wote wajawazito wanastahili haki sawa za binadamu, au wanawake wajawazito walio jela huziacha haki hizo?

eng: There are a few questions that come to mind regarding a pregnant woman's right to live and to raise her child when she has been convicted for some sort of crime: What is it like for them to be pregnant and have their child behind bars?
swa: Kuna maswali machache yanayokuja akilini kuhusu haki ya mwanamke mjamzito kuishi na kumlea mwanae anapokuwa kapatikana na hatia kwa kosa la jinai la namna fulani: • Inakuwaje kwao wanapokuwa wajawazito na kupata mtoto wakiwa gerezani?

eng: Should they be a priority when there are other women outside of correctional facilities without medical assistance?
swa: • Je, wanapaswa kuwa kipaumbele wakati kuna wanawake wengine nje ya vyuo vya mafunzo bila msaada wa kitabibu?

eng: Should maternity overrule any other legal conditions to ensure a pregnant woman's human rights?
swa: • Je, ujauzito unapaswa kuwa juu ya hali nyinginezo za kisheria kumhakikishia mwanamke mjamzito haki zake za kibinadamu?

eng: USA: women in labor no longer to be shackled.
swa: Marekani: wanawake walio kwenye uchungu wa kuzaa hawatafungwa tena minyororo.

eng: What happens to an inmate's baby after childbirth?
swa: Kitu gani hutokea kwa mtoto mchanga wa wa mfungwa baada ya kuzaliwa?

eng: Different countries have different regulations regarding children in prisons.
swa: Nchi mbalimbali zina kanuni tofauti kuhusiana na watoto magerezani.

eng: For example, in Argentina, according to Ajintem, an information portal for migration information, a law was passed last year specifying that pregnant women, women with children younger than 5 and those with handicapped children would benefit from spending their prison term at home under house arrest.
swa: Kwa mfano, nchini Argentina, kwa mujibu wa Ajintem, chombo cha mawasiliano cha taarifa za uhamamiaji, sheria ilipitishwa mwaka uliopita ikifafanua kwamba wanawake wajawazito, wanawake wenye watoto wadogo chini ya miaka mitano na wale wenye watoto walemavu wangenufaika na mpango wa kutumikia kifungo chao makwao chini ya ulinzi wa nyumbani.

eng: This law would benefit not only the mother, who in prison wouldn't receive suitable health care during her pregnancy, but also the child, who would either be raised in an unsafe environment deprived of freedom with deficient health controls and food, or be raised away from the mother, causing another series of problems.
swa: Sheria hii ingewanufaisha si tu akina mama, ambao kwa kuwa gerezani wasingepata huduma za afya wakati wa ujauzito, lakini pia (ingemnufaisha) mtoto, ambaye angelelewa ama katika mazingira yasiyo salama yanayokosa uhuru na upungufu wa udhibiti wa afya na chakula, au wangelelewa mbali na mama, na hivyo kusababisha mlolongo wa matatizo mengine.

eng: However, the message is for magistrates to follow the spirit of the law and grant this permission to those women not involved in violent crimes, to ensure that the rest of the civilian population doesn't see pregnancy as a get out of jail free card.
swa: Hata hivyo, ujumbe ni kwa ajili ya mahakimu kufuatilia kiini cha sheria na kutoa ruhusa hii kwa wanawake wale ambao hawahusishwi na mashitaka ya jinai ya matumizi ya nguvu, kuhakikisha kwamba idadi kubwa ya raia iliyobaki haiuchukulii ujauzito kama kadi ya kumtoa mtu jela bure.

eng: In the Canary Islands, according to the Prisiones y Penas blog, which writes about the issues surrounding jails and prisons, women are allowed to keep their children of up to 3 years of age with them in their cells, but in the company of other inmates, which isn't the best environment.
swa: Katika visiwa vya Canary, kwa mujibu wa blogu ya Prisiones y penas, ambayo huandika kuhusu habari zinazohusu jela na magereza, wanawake wanaruhusiwa kuishi na watoto wao hadi umri wa miaka mitatu ndani ya selo zao, lakini wakiwa pamoja na wafungwa wenzao, kitu ambacho sio mazingira mazuri sana kwako.

eng: Thus, pregnant women or women with children under 3 are told upon entry to the prison that it isn't good for the child to grow up behind bars, and options are given for them to send the child off to family members.
swa: Kwa hiyo, wanawake wajawazito au wanawake wenye watoto wenye umri wa chini ya miaka 3 huambiwa kuhusiana na kuingia kwenye magereza kuwa si vizuri kwa mtoto kukualia gerezani, na hupewa uchaguzi wa kumpeleka mtoto kwa wanafamilia wengine.

eng: This is also the case in Peru and Russia.
swa: Hali ni hii hii huko Peru na Urusi.

eng: In the US, there are only two correctional facilities which allow for this, in New York and in Nebraska, as told by renowned photographer Jane Evelyn Atwood in her 3 part photo documentary for Amnesty International, called Too Much Time, where she visited dozens of prisons all over the world to record and document the lives of inmates.
swa: Nchini Marekani, kuna magereza mawili tu yenye kuruhusu jambo hili, huko New York na Nebraska, kama ilivyoonyeshwa na mpiga picha maarufu Jane Evelyn Atwood kwenye insha ya picha zake tatu kwa ajili ya Shirika la kimataifa la Amnesty International, inayoitwa Too Much Time, ambapo alitembelea dazani nyingi za magereza kote duniani kurekodi na kuweka kumbukumbu za maisha ya wafungwa.
