swa: Samer, anayetwiti kama @meetsameer, pia alieleza kuchukizwa kwake na vyombo vya habari na kusema:

eng: Lebanese media has no decency or any sense of ethics, they're already referring to the missing ppl as "dead" #ET409 #Lebanon
swa: Vyombo vya habari vya Lebanoni havina ustaarabu au aina yoyote ya maadili, tayari vinawaita watu ambao hawajapatikana kama “waliokufa” #ET409 #Lebanon

eng: Amer Tabsh (@arzleb) shares similar sentiments and writes:
swa: Amer Tabsh (@arzleb) anaelezea hisia kama hizo na anaandika:

eng: LBC (Lebanese Broadcasting Corporation) analysis of the #ET409 is very stupid and wrongful #fail
swa: Uchambuzi wa LBC (Shirika la Habari la Lebanoni) wa #ET409 ni wa kipumbavu na potofu #fail

eng: He also shares the hotline number for information and inquires on the crash:
swa: Pia anatoa namba ya simu ya maelezo na maswali juu ya ajali:

eng: Meanwhile, Tala is shaken by the news and tweets:
swa: Wakati huo huo, Tala amestushwa na habari hii na kutwiti:

eng: 25 bodies have been taken out of the water, 2 of them were children.
swa: Miili 25 imechukuliwa kutoka majini, 2 kati yake ilikuwa ni ya watoto.

eng: And they hardly identify any of them.
swa: Na bado hawajaweza kuitambua.

eng: R.I.P #ET409
swa: Pumzikeni kwa Amani #ET409

eng: CNN's Cal Perry was also tweeting and in one message says:
swa: Cal Perry wa CNN pia alikuwa anandika jumbe za twita na katika ujumbe mmoja anasema:

eng: Such a sad day #et409 - tomorrow we'll try to get down to the beach.
swa: Siku ya masikitiko #et409 – kesho tutajaribu kwenda pwani.

eng: Tonight's piece from the airport.
swa: Hii ndio habari ya usiku wa leo kutokea uwanja wa ndege.

eng: PM Hariri trying his best to console
swa: Waziri Mkuu Hariri anajaribu kwa nguvu zote kufariji

eng: Nathan Redd is in agony and writes:
swa: Nathan Redd yumo katika uchungu na anaandika:

eng: I seriously cannot concentrate on anything today. #ET409 is the only thing on my mind today.
swa: Siwezi kabisa kuwa makini katika kitu chochote leo. #ET409 ndio jambo pekee kwenye akili yangu leo.

eng: My heart is broken.
swa: Moyo wangu umevunjika.

eng: And @nightS sums up the day saying:
swa: Na @nightS anatoa muhtasari wa siku kwa kusema:

eng: It's a very sad and horrible day :( #ET409
swa: Ni siku mbaya na ya masikitiko :( #ET409

eng: Martin Luther King, Jr. was born on January 15, 1929 and became arguably the American Civil Rights Movement's most prominent advocate and speaker.
swa: Martin Luther King Jr. alizaliwa tarehe 15 Januari, 1929 na akawa mmoja wa wasemaji na watetezi wakuu wa Harakati za Haki za Kiraia huko Marekani.

eng: In the United States, he is honored by a national holiday, observed the third Monday in January of each year.
swa: Nchini Marekani, anaenziwa kwa sikukuu ya taifa, inayoadhimishwa kila mwaka siku ya Jumatatu ya tatu ya mwezi Januari.

eng: Today, many bloggers in the United States are honoring his memory with dedicated posts, linking his legacy of social justice with issues of today, demonstrating that 42 years after King's assassination, his words are just as relevant.
swa: Leo, wanablogu wengi nchini Marekani wanaadhimisha kumbukumbu yake kwa kuandika makala za kumuenzi, huku wakiungalisha urithi wake wa masuala ya haki za jamii na masuala ya leo, wakionyesha wazi kuwa miaka 42 baada ya kuuwawa kwa King, maneno yake bado yana maana.

eng: Many Americans thought that Barack Obama’s election was the culmination of Dr. King’s dream and concrete proof that we have evolved into a “post-racial,” colorblind society.
swa: Wamarekani wengi walifikiri kuwa kuchaguliwa kwa Barack Obama kulikuwa ndio kilele cha kutimia kwa ndoto ya Dkt. King na uthibitisho madhubuti wa kuwa tumeendelea na kufikia kwenye jamii “baada-ya-ubaguzi,” jamii isiyoona rangi.

eng: Unfortunately, as I and many other sociologists and commentators have argued, even in this past year, we have seen numerous incidents that illustrate just how prevalent racial distinctions and racism still are in American society.
swa: Kwa bahati mbaya, kama mimi na wataalamu wa sayansi ya jamii pamoja na watoa maoni tulivyosema, hata katika mwaka huu uliopita, tumeona matukio kadhaa ambayo yanaonyesha kwa kiasi gani utofauti wa rangi na ubaguzi wa rangi bado uemeenea katika jamii ya Marekani.

eng: Following the discussion of numerous examples of racial issues in the United States, the blogger concludes:
swa: Kufuatia mijadala na mifano mingi ya masuala ya rangi katika Marekani, mwanablogu huyo anahitimisha:

eng: Ultimately, the best way for us to work toward achieving the ultimate colorblind ideal is to recognize, accept, and understand that racial distinctions still matter and that they are still the basis for continuing discrimination and inequality in American society today.
swa: Hatimaye, njia yetu bora zaidi katika kufikia njozi ya kutoona rangi za wengine ni kwa kutambua, kukubali, na kuelewa kuwa utofauti wa rangi bado upo na kwamba ubaguzi huo bado ni msingi unaoendeleza ubaguzi na ukosefu wa usawa katika jamii ya Kimarekani leo.

eng: Only by doing so will we move forward on achieving Dr. King’s final ideal — true racial equality.
swa: Ni kwa kufanya hivyo tutaweza kusonga mbele kufikia njozi ya mwisho ya Dkt. King – usawa wa kweli wa watu wa rangi zote.

eng: Global Voices' own Lova Rakotomalala, who is from Madagascar but resides in the United States, wrote a post entitled "Lesson from Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. to Madagascar," in which he said (in reference to the events in Madagascar last year):
swa: Lova Rakotomalala wa Global Voices, Mmadagaska ambaye anaishi Marekani, aliandika makala yenye kichwa “Somo kutoka kwa Dkt. Martin Luther King, Jr kwa Madagaska,” ambayo kwayo alisema (akilinganisha na matukio ya mwaka jana nchini Madagaska):

eng: Leadership matters.
swa: Uongozi ni jambo muhimu.

eng: Real leaders give speeches and then walk the talk, in front of the line.
swa: Viongozi wa kweli hutoa hotuba na hufuata kwa vitendo maneno yao, wakiwa mstari wa mbele.

eng: Leaders do not vanish in a sheltered place when they know things are about to get dangerous and let protesters walk in harm's way to serve their agenda.
swa: Viongozi huwa hawatokomei kivulini wakati wanapofahamu kuwa mambo yanakaribia kuwa ya hatari na kuwaacha waandamanaji waingie matatani ili kutimiza ajenda (za kiongozi).

eng: The only thing we know for sure about what really happened in Madagascar a year ago is that we could have used a Dr. King back then.
swa: Jambo pekee tunalojua kwa hakika kuhusu kile kilichotokea nchini Madagaska mwaka mmoja uliopita ni kuwa tungeliweza kumtumia mtu kama Dkt. King wakati ule.

eng: US-based blog Immigration Impact drew parallels between the civil rights movement of the 1960s and immigration today, writing:
swa: Blogu iliyoko Marekani Immigration Impact iliweka sambamba mambo yanafanana kati ya harakati za haki za kiraia za miaka ya 1960 na uhamiaji wa leo, inaandika:

eng: Now, more than ever, it’s important to remember Dr. King’s message that all men are created equal—not just for Hispanics and African Americans, but for all people who come to this country in search of the American Dream.
swa: Hivi sasa, zaidi ya wakati mwingine wowote, ni muhimu kukumbuka ujumbe wa Dkt. King unaosema watu wote wanaumbwa sawa – sio tu kwa wale wenye asili ya Kihispania na Waafrika-Wamarekani, bali kwa watu wote wanaohamia katika nchi wakitafuta ile Ndoto ya Marekani.

eng: The blogger behind Preventing Homelessness reminds us that honoring Martin Luther King, Jr. means service:
swa: Mwanablogu wa Preventing Homelessness anatukumbusha kuwa kumuenzi Martin Luther King, Jr. maana yake ni utumishi:

eng: Today is Martin Luther King Jr. Day.
swa: Leo ni siku ya Martin Luther King, Jr.

eng: A day for all of us to work to improve lives, bridge social barriers, and move our nation closer to the “Beloved Community” that Dr. King envisioned.
swa: Siku yetu ya kufanya kazi ili kuboresha maisha, kujenga madaraja kwenye vikwazo vya kijamii, na kuipeleka nchi yetu Karibu zaidi na “Jamii Pendwa” ambayo Dkt.

eng: Today is a day of service, but we don't have to stop there.
swa: Leo ni siku ya kutumikia, lakini hatupaswi kuishia hapo tu.

eng: We can resolve to make this a year of service and make a real difference in our community!
swa: Tunaweza kuazimia kuufanya mwaka huu kuwa mwaka wa kutumikia na hivyo kubadilisha hali kikweli katika jamii yetu!

eng: And last but not least, the anti-racist blog Racism Review leaves us with a thought about heeding King's lessons:
swa: Na mwisho lakini si kwa uchache, blogu inayopinga ubaguzi wa rangi, Racism Review inatuacha na wazo juu ya kusikiliza somo la King:

eng: This Martin Luther King, Jr.
swa: Katika siku hii ya Dkt.

eng: Day, I hope and pray we will learn the lessons Dr. King taught us.
swa: Martin Luther King, Jr., natumaini na kuomba kwamba tutajifunza masomo ambayo Dkt.

eng: Regardless of what the majority of people say, progressive American rhetoric remains miles ahead of its deeds (see King’s brilliant sermon “Paul’s Letter to American Christians”) and gradualism is not the answer.
swa: Bila ya kujali watu wengi wanasema nini, kauli za Marekani ya uanaharakati wa maendeleo ziko maili nyingi mbele ya matendo (angalia mahubiri ya King “Waraka wa Paulo kwa Wakristu wa Marekani”) na utaona kuwa harakati za kufikia malengo pole pole siyo jibu.

eng: Only collective action, creative and sustained civil disobedience, and mobilization of people of color and poor–for whom cooptation and/or cessation are not viable options—are the only potential means for achieving and sustaining real and systemic change.
swa: Harakati za pamoja, upinzani wa kijamii wa kibunifu na wa muda mrefu, uhamasishaji wa watu wa rangi na maskini – ambao kwao kuzama kwa njia ya maingiliano ndani ya jamii kubwa au kusitisha uhusiano kabisa na jamii kubwa si machaguo yanayowezekana – ndiyo njia pekee za kuweza kufikia na kudumisha mabadiliko ya kweli nay a kimfumo.

eng: Temporary Protected Status (TPS) is a special status given by the United States to foreign nationals from specific countries where there has been some sort of recent turmoil or trauma, such as war or an earthquake.
swa: Hadhi ya Hifadhi ya Muda (inayojulikana kama TPS) ni hadhi maalumu inayotolewa na Marekani kwa raia wa kigeni wanaotoka katika nchi fulanifulani ambamo kunakuwa kumetokea aina fulani ya janga au pigo la karibuni, kama vile vita au tetemeko la ardhi.

eng: The status requires that the individual already be in the United States, and the individual must apply for consideration under TPS.
swa: Hadhi hiyo inamtaka mtu anayenufaika nayo awe tayari kwenye ardhi ya Marekani, na mtu hana budi kutuma maombi ya kuomba kupata hifadhi hiyo na maombi yatafikiriwa.

eng: Currently, TPS is given to citizens of El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua, Somalia, and Sudan.
swa: Mpaka sasa hifadhi ya aina hii imekwishatolewa kwa raia wa nchi za El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua, Somali na Sudani.

eng: As the name implies, the status is temporary and does not automatically qualify an individual for permanent residency (green card) or citizenship.
swa: Kama inavyooneshwa na muda wa hifadhi hiyo, utaratibu huo ni jambo la muda tu na haiwezi kubadilika kumfanya mtu awe na sifa za kupata ukaazi wa kudumu (kupitia mpango wa Kadi ya Kijani) au hata kuwa raia wa Marekani.

eng: This week, following the horrific 7.0 earthquake that hit Haiti, a number of politicians and journalists began calling on the United States to give TPS to the one to two million (by most estimates) Haitian nationals that live in the country.
swa: Juma hili, kufuatia tetemeko baya lililofikia kipimo cha 7.0 ambalo liliikumba nchi ya Haiti, wanasiasa na waandishi wa habari kadhaa waliitaka Marekani kuwapa hifadhi ya aina hiyo raia wa Haiti wapatao milioni moja au mbili (kwa makisio ya juu) ili waweze kuishi katika nchi hiyo bila bugudha.

eng: Several petitions, including one by breakthrough, were circulated, and 83 Congresspersons signed a letter to President Obama requesting TPS for Haitians.
swa: Majaribio kadhaa ya kushawishi uwezekano huo, likiwemo lililofanywa na breakthrough, yalitumwa huku na huko, na wajumbe 83 wa Baraza la Kongresi walitia saini barua iliyotumwa kwa Rais Obama kuomba raia wa Haiti wapewe hadhi hiyo ya hifadhi ya muda.

eng: On Friday, January 15, Homeland Security Secretary Janet Napolitano granted TPS to all Haitians currently living in the US for eighteen months.
swa: Ilipotika Ijumaa tarehe 15 January, Waziri wa Usalama wa Ndani wa Marekani, Janet Napolitano, alitoa ruhusa ya raia wa Haiti wanaoishi Marekani hivi sasa kupewa TPS kwa kipindi cha miezi 18.

eng: Prior to the announcement, blogger The Latin Americanist noted:
swa: Kabla ya tangazo hilo, mwanablogu The Latin Americanist alitoa maoni haya:

eng: Haitian expats and immigration advocates have long clamored for TPS for Haitians, especially in light of numerous hurricanes and major storms over the past decade.
swa: Wataalamu kuhusu nchi ya Haiti na watetezi wa masuala ya uhamiaji kwa muda mrefu sasa wamekuwa wakihimiza kwamba ruhusu itolewe ili raia wa Haiti wapate hadhi ya TPS hasa kwa kuzingatia majanga ya vimbunga na dhoruba nyingine ambazo zimekuwa zikiipiga nchi hiyo katika muongo uliopita.

eng: Though their pleas had fallen on deaf ears by both the Bush and Obama administrations, support for Haitian TPS has gained backing from key lawmakers
swa: Ingawa maombi yao hayo yameangukia katika masikio kiziwi ya watawala wa awamu zote mbili za Bush na Obama, utetezi wa upewaji TPS kwa raia wa Haiti umepata uungaji mkono wa watunga sheria muhimu.

eng: Also prior to the decision, American blogger and immigration scholar Koulflo Memo called TPS a "no-brainer":
swa: Vilevile, kabla ya uamuzi huo, mwanablogu wa Kimarekani na mtaalamu wa masuala ya uhamiaji, Koulflo Memo, alibainisha kwamba TPS "si kihitaji akili""

eng: The right wing Federation for American Immigration Reform (FAIR) has announced opposition to granting TPS for Haiti.
swa: Mrengo wa kulia wa Shirikisho la Mageuzi ya Mfumo wa Uhamiaji Marekani (Federation for American Immigration Reform (FAIR)) umetangaza kupinga utolewaji wa TPS kwa raia wa nchi ya Haiti.

eng: The reason they give is that they assume Haitians won’t leave after TPS is lifted.
swa: Sababu wanayoitoa ni kwamba wanaamini kuwa mara baada ya kupita muda wa hadhi hiyo, raia wa Haiti hawatataka kurejea kwao.

eng: They also say the Haiti situation does not meet TPS criteria.
swa: Wanasema pia kwamba hali iliyotokea nchini Haiti haikidhi vigezo vya mtu kupewa TPS.

eng: FAIR’s opposition is dishonest and wrongheaded.
swa: Ama kwa hakika upinzani huu unaotolewa na FAIR hautazami mambo kwa haki bali unatokana na kiburi tu.

eng: It is also racist.
swa: Vilevile una mwelekeo wa kibaguzi.

eng: I hope President Obama is not over-calculating his chances for comprehensive immigration reform later this year by appeasing the FAIR constituency on this crucial humanitarian issue.
swa: Natumaini Rais Obama hatumii jambo hili kupima fursa zake za kuleta mageuzi makubwa katika mfumo wa uhamiaji baadaye mwaka huu kwa kuwafurahisha FAIR kuhusu jambo hili lenye umuhimu wa pekee katika masuala ya kiutu.

eng: Such a non-response would indeed forsake Haiti in its time of need.
swa: Kama hataitikia miito anayopewa ya kutoa ruhusa hiyo, basi atakuwa amewatupa mkono raia wa Haiti walio katika hali ya kuhitaji sana msaada.

eng: American blogger Deep Thought commended the Obama administration's decision, writing:
swa: Mwanablogu wa Kimarekani anayejulikana kama Deep Thought alitoa maoni kuhusu uamuzi wa utawala wa Rais Obama, aliandika akisema:

eng: President Obama showed real leadership in moving quickly to help the people of Haiti.
swa: Rais Obama ameonyesha kuwa ni kiongozi makini baada ya kufanya uamuzi huo mzito kwa haraka ili kuwasaidia watu wa Haiti.

eng: He and Secretary Napolitano also showed compassion in suspending deportations to Haiti for eighteen months by granting TPS (temporary protected status) to Haitians currently in the United States; dumping a bunch more people into the current scene of devastation would be unhelpful at best and disastrous at worst.
swa: Yeye na Waziri Napolitano pia walionyesha huruma kwa kusogeza mbele uondoshwaji kwa nguvu wa raia wa Haiti kutoka nchini Marekani kwa miezi kumi na nane baada ya kuwapa TPS raia wanaoishi nchini humo hivi sasa; kuwatupilia mbali baadhi ya watu katika kipindi hiki halitakuwa jambo lenye msaada, sana sana litakuwa na mwisho mbaya.

eng: Yes, they are getting some heat from Nativist groups but the real test of leadership is the ability to make tough decisions because they are right.
swa: Ndiyo, viongozi hawa wanapata upinzani mkali kutoka kwa vikundi vya kutetea wenyeji lakini kipimo cha kweli cha uongozi ni uwezo wa uongozi huo kufanya maamuzi magumu kwa sababu maamuzi hayo yako sahihi.

eng: Blogger and adoptive parent all buttoned up discusses thanking her representative for pushing for TPS and also requests help for Haiti's many orphans, writing:
swa: Mwanablogu na mzazi anayeasili all buttoned up waliungana na kumshukuru mwakilishi kwa kusaidi upatikanaji wa TPS na pia wanaomba kwamba msaada zaidi utolewe kwa mayatima wengi walio nchin Haiti, anaandika:

eng: This issue is getting a lot of press at the moment.
swa: Jambo hili limekazaniwa sana kwenye vyombo vya habari hivi sasa.

eng: I hope that it makes a difference, but you and I both know that people grow tired of seeing the same sadness over and over again.
swa: Natumaini kwamba juhudi hizo zitaleta matunda, lakini wewe na mimi tunajua kwamba watu wanachoka kuona huzuni ileile tena na tena.

eng: There were more than 200,000 orphans living in Port-au-Prince before all of this began, and however you feel about these issues- and they are complicated- none of this intervention is meant to undermine the integrity of the Haitian people or their desire to look after their own children.
swa: Kulikuwa na zaidi ya mayatima 200,000 walikokuwa wakiishi jijini Port-au-Prince kabla ya tukio hili la majuzi, na kwa vyovyote vile unavyoyachukulia mambo haya - na ni magumu - na hakuna hata uingiliaji kati mmoja unaopuuzia mshikamano wa watu wa Haiti au hamu yao ya kuwatunza watoto wao wenyewe.

eng: It is just not possible for them to do so.
swa: Imetokea tu kwamba kwa sasa hawawezi kufanya hivyo.

eng: This is a humanitarian issue.
swa: Hili ni suala la kiutu.

eng: Although Haitians in the United States are now protected for the next 18 months at minimum and able to work, the people of Haiti still need help.
swa: Ingawa raia wa Haiti hivi sasa wana kinga kwa muda wa miezi 18 ijayo kwa uchache huku wa wakifanya kazi, bado Haidi inahitaji msaada.

eng: Here are a few organizations providing relief in Haiti, and here are a few ways you can donate hotel or frequent flier miles.
swa: Hapa kuna baadhi ya asasi zinazotoa misaada nchini Haiti, na hapa kuna njia chache zinazokupa fursa ya kuchangia.

eng: Please visit the Global Voices Haiti Earthquake page for more coverage of the event.
swa: Tafadhali pitia Ukurasa wa Global Voices wa Tetemeko la Ardhi la Haiti kwa taarifa zaidi.

eng: Respect Religions by Sarah Carr
swa: Heshimu Dini, na Sarah Carr

eng: Coptic Christians celebrate Christmas on January 7.
swa: Wakristu wa madhehebu ya Koptiki husherehekea Krismasi tarehe 7 Januari.

eng: On the eve of their celebrations in Egypt, Copts go to churches and celebrate the holy event.
swa: Wakati wa mkesha wa sherehe hizo nchini Misri, waumini hueelekea makanisani na kusherehekea tukio hilo takatifu.

eng: But this year an unexpected incident happened in Naga Hammady, in Upper Egypt, where an unknown criminal opened his fire randomly on people there after they finished their prayers and were on their way back to their homes.
swa: Lakini mwaka huu tukio lisilotarajiwa lilitokea huko Naga Hammady, Misri ya Juu, ambapo mhalifu asiyejulikana alianza kupiga risasi hovyo hovyo kwenye umati watu baada ya watu hao kumaliza maombi wakiwa wanaelekea majumbani kwao.

eng: Zeinobia wrote a new post about the massacre in her blog saying:
swa: Zeinobia aliandika makala mpya kuhusu mauaji hayo ya kinyama katika blogu yake akisema:

eng: I am really very sorry and angry for what happened in Naj Hammadi yesterday.
swa: Nimesikitishwa sana na pia nimekasirika kwa kile kilichotokea Naj Hammadi jana.

eng: It hurts me more than the Egyptian Christians because what happened is against all Egyptians.
swa: Inaniuma zaidi ya Wamisri Wakristu kwani kilichotokea ni dhidi ya Wamisri wote.

eng: My condolences to the families of those who were killed and injured in this disgusting attack.
swa: Rambirambi zangu ziwafikie familia za wale wote waliouwawa na kujeruhiwa katika shambulio hili linalochefua.

eng: Another blog, Coptic File, wrote about the incident: A shooting gun was used from inside a car (green Fiat), to randomly kill eight people and many others were wounded.
swa: Mwanablogu mwingine, Coptic File, aliandika kuhusu tukio hilo:

eng: She also blames the ministry of interior for the whole thing: And with my all respect this is ridiculous , fighting a crime by a group of crimes.
swa: Na kwa heshima yangu yote huu ni ujinga wa ajabu, kupigana na uhalifu kwa makundi ya uhalifu.

eng: I blame the ministry of interior in all of this , if there is a real respect and fear of the law nothing of this could happen.
swa: Nailaumu Wizara ya Mambo ya Ndani katika hili, kama kuna heshima ya kweli na hofu ya sheria pasingetokea kitu kama hiki.

eng: Also, Nawara shares echoes similar sentiments.
swa: Nawara, kadhalika, anashiriki hisia kama hizo.

eng: On the Ministry of Interior's press release regarding the shooting, she says: The strangest release I've ever read in my entire life, I've never seen a press release blaming the victims and encouraging mass punishment.
swa: Kuhusu Taarifa ya Wizara ya mambo ya Ndani kwa vyombo vya babari juu mauaji, anasema:

eng: More than 20 Egyptian bloggers were arrested when their train arrived in the village of Naga Hammady in Upper Egypt.
swa: Zaidi ya wanablogu 20 wa Misri wametiwa mbaroni mara baada ya gari moshi walilokuwa wakisafiria kuwasili katika kijiji cha Naga Hammady huko Misri ya Juu.

eng: Led by Dr Mostafa Al Naggar, the bloggers left Cairo, Alexandria, and other cities in Egypt to pay their respects to the families of the victims of the Naga Hammady massacre.
swa: Walikuwa wakiongozwa na Dkt. Mostafa Al Naggar. Wanablogu hao waliotoka Cairo, Alexandria na miji mingine ili kwenda kutoa heshima zao kwa familia za watu waliouwawa katika mauaji ya Naga Hammady.

eng: Seven Christian Copts were shot dead on the eve of their Christmas, on January 7.
swa: Wakristo 7 wa madhehebu ya Kikopti walipigwa risasi katika mkesha wa sikukuu ya Krismas ya Kikopti mnamo Januari 7 mwaka huu.

eng: Many others were injured as they left a church after the Christmas mass.
swa: Wengine wengi walijeruhiwa.

eng: The bloggers unpoliticized visit to Naga Hammady was halted when the bloggers got off the train.
swa: Shambulio hilo lilifanyika wakati Wakristo hao walipokuwa wakitoka kanisani mara baada ya misa ya Krismas.

eng: 3- Bassem Samir 4- Bassem Fathy 5- Ahmed Badawy
swa: Dkt.

eng: Most if not all these bloggers are among the famous citizen journalists.
swa: Wengi kama sio wote miongoni mwa wanablogu hawa ni kati ya waandishi wa habari wa kiraia walio maarfu zaidi.

eng: I do not understand why these bloggers have been detained.
swa: Sielewi kwa nini wanablogu hawa wametiwa mbaroni.

eng: In late December, the Council of Ministers of Mozambique made a significant announcement.
swa: Mwishoni mwa Mwezi Disemba, Baraza la Mawaziri la Msumbiji lilitoa tamko muhimu.

eng: A 30,000ha land concession to biofuels firm Procana in the District of Massingir had been revoked.
swa: Kibali cha kutumia Hekta 30,000 za ardhi kwa kampuni ya mazao nishati (biofuels) Procana, kimebatilishwa.

eng: The Mozambican Land Law, passed in 1997, is quite unique.
swa: Sheria ya Ardhi ya Msumbiji iliyopitishwa katika 1997, ni ya kipekee.

eng: Land was nationalized at independence, and the Land Law did not change this.
swa: Ardhi ilitaifishwa wakati wa uhuru, na Sheria ya Ardhi haikubadilisha jambo hilo.

eng: It gives the state clear tools for managing land use.
swa: Inaipa serikali zana wazi kwa ajili ya kudhibiti matumizi ya ardhi.

eng: Private sector investors must seek 50 year land-use rights agreements, known as DUAT, or "Land Use and Benefit Rights".
swa: Wawekezaji wa sekta binafsi wanalazimika kuomba mkataba wa kutumia ardhi kwa miaka 50, ambao unajulikana kama DUAT, au “Haki ya Kutumia Ardhi na Manufaa Yake”.

eng: These DUATs are not binding for the full 50 years until after an interim two year period, when investors have to prove that they use the land productively.
swa: Mikataba hiyo ya DUAT haina nguvu kwa muda wote wa miaka 50 mpaka pale kipindi cha kwanza cha miaka miwili kitakapopita, wakati wawekezaji wanapopaswa kuthibitisha kuwa wanaitumia ardhi hiyo kuzalisha.

eng: The case of the Procana DUAT, a massive area bordering on the cross-border Limpopo National Park, was polemic from the beginning in 2007.
swa: Shauri la Mradi wa Procana, ulipo kwenye eneo kubwa linalopakana na Mbuga ya Taifa ya Limpopo ambayo imetanda mpaka nje mpaka wa nchi, lilikuwa na utata pamoja na mvutano mkubwa tangu (shauri hilo) lilipoanza mwanzoni mwa mwaka 2007.

eng: Communities were to be resettled from the Park area to the lands then subsequently conceded to Procana for sugarcane production.
swa: Jamii zilikuwa zihamishwe kutoka kwenye eneo la mbuga kwenda kwenye eneo ambalo kabla ya hapo lilikuwa limetolewa kwa Procana kwa ajili ya kuzalisha miwa.

eng: These communities needed the lands for grazing, as they survive from cattle rearing.
swa: Jamii hizi ziliitaji ardhi kwa ajili ya kulisha mifugo, kwani jamii hizo hujikimu kutokana na ufugaji wa ng’ombe.

eng: There appeared to be no real plan to deal with the brewing conflict.
swa: Inaonekana kuwa hapakuwa na mipango yoyote ya kukabiliana na mgogoro ambao ulikuwa unatokota.

eng: Moreover, there were worries that Procana's need for water would disturb local food production.
swa: Na zaidi ya hilo, kulikuwa na hofu kuwa mahitaji ya maji ya Procana yangetibua uzalishaji wa chakula wa sehemu hiyo.

eng: Civil society groups supported the communities in their negotiations with Park officials through a project called Lhuvuka, but there appeared to be no progress with Procana.
swa: Vikundi vya Jamii za Kiraia viliziunga mkono jamii katika majadiliano yao na maofisa wa Mbuga kwa kupitia mradi unaoitwa Lhuvuka, lakini inaonekana kuwa hapakutokea maendeleo yoyote kati yao na Procana.

eng: Massingir school photo by Ralph Pina, published under a Creative Commons license
swa: Picha ya shule ya Massingir iliyopigwa na Ralph Pina, na kuchapishwa kwa idhini ya Creative Commons

eng: Lhuvuka's website has an article that claims the conflicts were summed up
swa: Tovuti ya Lhuvuka ina makala ambayo imekusanya madai kati katika mgogoro huo

eng: Nigerian curiosity writes about the case of Uzoma Okere in Nigeria: "Uzoma Okere is the young Nigerian lady whose assault by military officers became a viral video that raised the ire of many."
swa: Nigerian curiosity anaandika kuhusu kesi ya Uzoma Okere huko Naijeria: "Uzoma Okere ni msichana wa Kinaijeria ambaye kipigo alichopata kutoka kwa maafisa wa jeshi kiliondokea kuwa video iliyosambazwa sana na kuamsha hasira za wengi."

eng: A partylist group in the Philippines wants to introduce a law that would put a ten-year expiration date on marriage contracts.
swa: Kikundi kimoja cha masuala maalum ya jamii nchini Philippines kinataka kuwasilisha sheria ambayo itaufanya mkataba wa ndoa kuwa na nguvu kwa miaka kumi tu.

eng: The unique proposal is the group’s answer to lengthy and expensive annulment proceedings in the country.
swa: Pendekezo hili la kipekee ni jibu la kutatua tatizo la utaratibu mrefu na wa gharama wa kubatilisha ndoa.

eng: The Catholic-dominated Philippines does not have a divorce law.
swa: Nchi hii yenye Wakatoliki wengi haina sheria ya talaka.

eng: According to the group, the “Renewable Marriage Bill” would “spare incompatible couples the expense of lengthy legal proceedings before their marriages are annulled.”
swa: Kwa mujibu wa kikundi hicho, “Muswada wa Ndoa Jadidifu” utawakinga wanandoa wasioelewana dhidi ya gharama zinazoambatana na utaratibu mrefu wa kisheria kabla ndoa zao hazijabatilishwa.”

eng: The group added that a marriage contract “should be just like a passport or driver’s license.
swa: Kikundi hicho kiliongeza kuwa mkataba wa ndoa “unatakiwa uwe kama pasi ya kusafiria au leseni ya kuendesha gari.

eng: If we are not interested to renew it, then it expires.”
swa: Ikiwa hatuna haja ya kuongeza muda wake, basi (mkataba huo) unapoteza nguvu yake.”

eng: More than 500,000 marriages are administered by the Catholic Church every year with less than 10 percent getting annulled and reported.
swa: Zaidi ya ndoa 500,000 husimamiwa na Kanisa Katoliki kila mwaka wakati ndoa zinazobatilishwa na kuripotiwa ni pungufu ya asilimia 10.

eng: As expected, the proposed marriage license with expiration date generated an intense reaction in the blogosphere.
swa: Kama ilivyotarajiwa, muswada huo wa ndoa uliopendekezwa ambao una muda wa kuwa na nguvu kisheria umezua mijadala katika ulimwengu wa blogu.

eng: Writing for Lex Fori Philippines, Oscar underscores the impact of this proposal on property relations.
swa: Akiandika kwa ajili ya Lex Fori Philippines, Oscar anasisitiza athari za pendekezo hili kwenye uhusiano wa mali.

eng: If we are going to equate marriage with a driver’s license, can we then take the future spouse for a test drive?
swa: Ikiwa tutalinganisha ndoa na leseni ya gari, je tunaweza kumchukua mwanandoa mtarajiwa ili kumjaribu kwanza?

eng: That way, both persons will be spared from having to go through renewing or not renewing the expirable marriage license and save them money from holding the costly marriage ceremony.
swa: Kwa njia hiyo, watu hao wawili wataepuka kupitia adha ya kujadidisha au kutojadidisha leseni yao ya ndoa inayokwisha muda wake na kuokoa fedha ambazo huandaa shughuli aghali ya harusi.

eng: Supposing that marriage will expire in ten years, what will happen to the property relations after 10 years? the validity of contracts entered into by the spouses jointly?
swa: Tuchukulie kuwa ndoa itakwisha muda wake baada ya miaka kumi, ni nini kitachotokea kwenye uhusiano wa mali baada ya miaka 10? Uhalali wa mikataba ambayo wanandoa waliingia pamoja?

eng: Do we liquidate the properties, terminate valid contracts, and tell the children to expect lesser legitimes in the event one or both their parents remarry and have additional children?
swa: Je mali hizo zitataifishwa, mikataba itasitishwa, na kuwaambia watoto wategemee muda mchache na wazazi wao ikiwa wazazi wote watafunga ndoa tena na kupata watoto wengine?

eng: John Odonnell R. Petalcorin prefers a bill that would decrease the cost of annulment case proceedings
swa: John Odonnell R. Petalcorin anapendelea muswada ambao utapunguza gharama za kesi za kubatilisha ndoa.

eng: ...if the proposal was conceptualized because of the expensive annulment case proceedings, I would rather propose a counter-bill to put a price cap on the cost of annulment.
swa: … kama pendekezo hili lilianza kufikiriwa kwa sababu ya gharama kubwa za kesi za kubatilisha ndoa, basi ningependekeza muswada wa kupinga ili kuweka kikomo cha gharama za kubatilisha.

eng: To make the process speedy, we can also incorporate a provision that the annulment can be approved immediately if both the husband and wife will exchange a verbally denounciation of their love for each other for three times
swa: Ili kuufanya mchakato uwe wa haraka, tunaweza pia kujumuisha kipengele kinachosema kuwa kubatilisha kunaweza kupitishwa mara moja ikiwa wote, mume na mke, watabadilishana kwa mdomo ahadi za kukana mapenzi kwa mwingine mara tatu

eng: Ice9web Blog wonders whether a new marriage vow will be uttered in ceremonies
swa: Ice9web Blog anajiuliza kama watu watatoa ahadi mpya ya ndoa kwenye sherehe za harusi.

eng: If this will happen, gone are the days when the marriage vows are to be taken seriously "Til death do us part"?
swa: Ikiwa itatokea, basi siku za ahadi za ndoa kupewa umuhimu unaostahili “Mpaka kifo kitakapotutenganisha” zimepita?

eng: Now what will the vow be?
swa: Sasa ahadi hiyo itakuwaje?

eng: Till renewal to us part?
swa: Mpaka mwisho wa mkataba utakapotutenganisha?

eng: Some said that this will be the answer here in Philippines, since we don't have divorce and annulment takes time and lots of money... is renewal really the answer?
swa: Wengine wanasema kuwa hilo ndilo jibu hapa Philippines ambako hatuna talaka na kubatilisha ndoa kunachukua muda na pesa nyingi… je ujadidishaji ndiyo jibu la kweli?

eng: Pinoy Politico doesn’t understand why incompatible couples have to wait for ten years before they can terminate their marriage
swa: Pinoy Politico haelewi kwa nini wanandoa wasioelewana wasubiri mpaka miaka kumi ipite kabla ya kufuta ndoa yao

eng: I don't understand why a person has to wait for a decade just to ditch his cheating wife.
swa: Sielewi kwa nini mtu asubiri kwa muongo ili amtose mke wake anayetembea nje.

eng: This is also the same for the women.
swa: Hii ni kwa wanawake pia.

eng: If my husband beats me up everyday after 1 year of marriage, why should I wait for 9 years more?
swa: Ikiwa mume wangu ananipiga kila siku baada ya mwaka 1 wa ndoa, kwa nini nisubiri miaka mingine 9?

eng: Maybe you should propose daily renewal so that you can check their marriage status.
swa: Pengine mngependekeza kujadidisha ndoa kila siku ili kwamba mfuatilie hali ya ndoa yao.

eng: Capt. Nemo is supportive of the proposal
swa: Capt. Nemo anaunga mkono pendekezo hilo

eng: well this proposition just want to address the PRESENT situation that most of the Filipino couples are facing nowadays.
swa: Naam pendekezo hili linataka kutatua hali YA SASA ambayo wanandoa wengi wa Kifilipino wanakabiliwa nayo siku hizi.

eng: Based on my perception, this is for the better and a solution that treat both sexes equality regarding marriage.
swa: Kutokana na mtazamo wangu, jambo hili ni bora na ni suluhisho ambalo linawatendea sawa watu wa jinsia zote mbili kuhusiana na ndoa.

eng: For annulment can be acquired by those who are capable to “pay” the process.
swa: Kwani ubatilishwaji wa ndoa unaweza kufanywa na wale wenye uwezo wa “kulipia” utaratibu mzima.

eng: How about the poor who want to put an end in their not working relationship, can they go with the same process? this proposition will motivate couples to value their existing relationship.
swa: Vipi kuhusu maskini ambao wanataka kusitisha uhusiano wao usiofanya kazi, wanaweza kufuata utaratibu huo huo? Pendekezo hili litawahamasisha wanandoa kuthamini uhusiano wao uliopo.

eng: In fact, they have the FREE WILL to either renew their marriage contracts or just junk the paper after 10 years.
swa: Kwa kweli, wana UTASHI HURU wa ama kujadidisha mkataba wao wa ndoa au kuitupa hiyo karatasi baada ya miaka 10.

eng: Jappysworld is concerned about the welfare of children if a couple decides not to renew their marriage
swa: Jappysworld ana hofu juu ya ustawi wa watoto ikiwa wanandoa wataamua kutojadidisha ndoa yao

eng: This is not the solution.
swa: Hili sio suluhisho.

eng: I do understand that there are many people who couldn’t stand being married a minute longer, but what would happen to the children if this proposal takes effect.
swa: Sielewi ni vipi kuna watu wengi ambao hawawezi kuwa kwenye ndoa hata kwa dakika moja zaidi, je nini kitakachotokea kwa watoto wao ikiwa pendekezo hili litafanya kazi.

eng: This may be beneficial to estranged couples but their children would be the one to suffer the most.
swa: Linaweza kuwa na manufaa kwa wapenzi waliotengana lakini watoto wao ndio watakaoteseka zaidi.

eng: It’s like saying on the 1st day after the 10th year of Marriage; a married person could do anything they want without regarding their responsibility and loyalty to their family.
swa: Ni sawa na kusema katika siku ya kwanza ya kuadhimisha miaka 10 ya ndoa; mtu aliye kwenye ndoa anaweza kufanya chochote atakacho bila ya kujali wajibu wao na na uaminifu kwa familia zao.

eng: Maureen Flores believes the proposed bill bypasses the sanctity of marriage
swa: Maureen Flores anaamini kuwa muswada uliopendekezwa unauzunguka utakatifu wa ndoa

eng: This has been a laughing matter between my husband and I over the week.
swa: Hili limekuwa suala la kuchekesha kati ya mume wangu na mimi kwa wiki nzima.

eng: We're celebrating our 10th wedding anniversary today, you see.
swa: Tunasherehekea maadhimisho ya miaka 10 ya ndoa yetu leo, unaona.

eng: But really, the proposed 10-year expiry on marriage contracts is not funny.
swa: Lakini kweli, pendekezo la mkataba wa ndoa unaoisha nguvu baada ya miaka 10 halichekeshi.

eng: I am also expressing my sincere disapproval on this proposal.
swa: Na pia ninaeleza kutokukubaliana kwangu kwa dhati juu ya pendekezo hili.

eng: I am concerned about how it will affect families and our society itself should this be passed.
swa: Nina hofu na vile litakavyoathiri familia na jamii yetu ikiwa litapitishwa.

eng: The sanctity of marriage is bypassed.
swa: Utakatifu wa ndoa unaepukwa.

eng: On January 18 Global Voices will launch the Technology for Transparency Network, a collaborative research mapping of internet projects that promote greater transparency, government accountability, and civic engagement.
swa: Siku ya Januari 18 Global Voices itazindua Mtandao wa Teknolojia na Uwazi, ambao ni utafiti wa pamoja wa kuorodhesha na kuiweka kwenye ramani miradi ya kwenye mtandao wa intaneti ambayo inatangaza na kutetea uwazi, uwajibikaji wa serikali, na makutano ya kijamii.

eng: This is the first in a series of posts that will explore related issues through the eyes of bloggers worldwide.
swa: Hii ni ya kwanza kabisa katika mfululizo wa makala ambazo zitavinjari mada zinazohusiana kwa kupitia macho ya wanablogu duniani kote.

eng: To kick things off we look at how bloggers responded to International Anti-Corruption Day, which was signed into law in 2003 at the United Nations Convention against Corruption and takes place every year on December 9th.
swa: Kwa kuanza tunaangalia jinsi wanablogu walivyoitikia Siku ya Kimataifa Dhidi ya Rushwa, ambayo ilitiwa saini kuwa sheria mwaka 2003 kwenye Mkutano wa Umoja wa Mataifa Dhidi ya Rushwa na huadhimishwa kila mwaka tarehe 9 Disemba.

eng: On Space for Transparency, the official blog of Transparency International, Georg Neumann looks back at the state of anti-corruption activism for 2009:
swa: Katika Sehemu ya Uwazi, blogu rasmi ya Transparency International, Georg Neumann anaangalia hali ya uanaharakati dhidi ya rushwa kwa mwaka 2009:

eng: Increasingly, anti-corruption activists have been in the line of attack.
swa: Wanaharakati dhidi ya rushwa wamekuwa katika mstari wa mashambulizi.

eng: Activists from Bosnia and Herzegovina, Burundi, Guatemala or Zimbabwe have faced threats or were being silenced.
swa: Wanaharakati kutoka Bosnia na Herzegovina, Burundi, Guatemala au Zimbabwe wamekabiliana na vitisho au wamenyamazishwa.

eng: Anti-Corruption Day stands for a day to remember, recognise and honour these brave and fearless people, who went to prison or lost their lives believing that through fighting corruption they will make the world a better place.
swa: Siku ya Kupinga Rushwa inasimama kama siku ya kuwambuka, kuwatambua na kuwaenzi watu hawa majasiri na wasio na woga, ambao walikwenda jela au walipoteza maisha yao wakiamini kuwa kwa kupigana dhidi ya rushwa wataifanya dunia kuwa bora.

eng: Neumann also notes that 2009 saw the passing of a flawed review mechanism which doesn't require member states to seek input from independent NGO's based in their countries.
swa: Neumann pia anabaini kuwa mwaka 2009 pia ulishuhudia kupitishwa kwa vigezo vya kupima vyenye kasoro ambavyo havizitaki nchi wanachama kupata mapendekezo kutoka kwa Asasi huru Zisizo za Kiserikali zenye makao ndani ya nchi wanachama.

eng: In a five-minute YouTube video Peter Eigen, the founder of Transparency International, describes the important role of civil society in fighting corruption and improving governance:
swa: Katika video ya dakika tano ya YouTube Peter Eigen, mwanzilishi wa Transparency International, anaeleza jukumu muhimu la jamii za kiraia katika kupigana na rushwa na kuboresha utawala:

eng: But it wasn't all bad news in 2009, writes Neumann.
swa: Lakini mwaka 2009 haukuwa na habari mbaya pekee, anaandika Neumann.

eng: There are now 40 Advocacy and Legal Advice Centers worldwide providing legal advice to victims of corruption.
swa: Hivi sasa kuna Vituo 40 vya Utetezi na Ushauri wa Kisheria duniani vinavyotoa ushauri wa sheria kwa waathirika na rushwa.

eng: Also, online social media has proven itself a powerful tool in promoting transparency and fighting against corruption.
swa: Pia, uanahabari wa kijamii mtandaoni umejidhihirisha kuwa chombo chenye nguvu katika kutangaza uwazi na kupigana dhidi ya rushwa.

eng: In India, for example, J. N. Jayashree started a wiki to protect her husband whose safety was threatened as a result of his whistle-blowing activities.
swa: Nchini India, kwa mfano, J.N. Jayashree alianzisha ukurasa shirikishi ili kumlinda mume wake ambaye usalama wake ulikuwa hatarini kutokana na vitendo vyake vya kufichua siri.

eng: In Morocco an anonymous anti-corruption activist has begun posting videos to YouTube of police officers accepting bribes.
swa: Nchini Morocco mwanaharakati asiye na jina ameanza kutuma video za maaskari wanaopokea rushwa kwenye YouTube.

eng: Arruda Out'.
swa: ‘Arruda Atoke.’

eng: Twitpic by Cleudson Fernandes, Twitter user @cleudsonf, published with permission
swa: Picha ya Twitpic na Cleudson Fernandes, mtumiaji wa Twita @cleudsonf, iliyochapwa kwa idhini yake

eng: In Brazil violence broke out on Anti-Corruption Day between police and protesters:
swa: Huko Brazil ghasia zilizuka katika siku ya Kupinga Rushwa kati ya polisi na waandamanaji:

eng: Protesters have been demanding the impeachment of the Governor of the Federal District, Jose Roberto Arruda, and his deputy, Paulo Octavio, in addition to a thorough investigation into all parties cited in the bribery scandal that led to a police operation codenamed Pandora Box.
swa: Waandamanaji wamekuwa wakidai kuondolewa madarakani kwa Gavana wa Wilaya ya Kitaifa, Jose Roberto Arruda, na makamu wake, Paulo Octavio, pamoja na uchunguzi wa kina wa pande zote zilizotajwa katika kesi ya hongo ambayo ilipelekea operesheni ya polisi iliyopewa jina la Kasha la Pandora.

eng: According to the investigation, Governor Arruda is the possible head of a R$ 600,000 (approximately $340,000) per month bribery scheme that has benefited allies among district members of parliament, businessmen and government officials.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa uchunguzi, Gavana Arruda anawezekana akawa ndiye kiongozi wa mpango wa rushwa wa R$ 600,000 (Takriban dola za Kimarekani 340,000 ) kwa mwezi ambao umewanufaisha wabunge, wafanyabiashara na maofisa wa serikali.

eng: Global Voices editors also point readers to a number of posts around the blogosphere related to transparency, corruption, and government accountability.
swa: Wahariri wa Global Voices pia wanawaelekeza wasomaji wao zilipo makala zinazohusiana na uwazi, rushwa na uwajibikaji serikalini katika ulimwengu wa blogu.

eng: Peter Marton looks at the harmful role of corruption in rebuilding Afghanistan.
swa: Peter Marton anaangalia athari mbaya ya rushwa katika kuijenga tena Afghanistan.

eng: In Ukraine, meanwhile, Petro congratulates the residents of Kabul for sentencing their mayor to four years of prison for corruption and imagines how quickly Kyiv's prisons would fill up if the same laws were enforced in his country.
swa: Wakati huo huo huko Ukraine, Petro anawapongeza wakazi wa Kabul kwa kumhukumu meya wao mika minne jela kwa kosa la rushwa na wanafikiria ni kwa haraka kiasi gani magereza ya Kyiv yatajaa ikiwa sheria hizo hizo zingefuatiliwa katika nchi yake.

eng: Writing in Registan.net, Alexander Visotzky looks at the corruption charges against Mukhtar Dzhakishev for the illegal sale of Uranium and concludes, "The fight against corruption in Kazakhstan is apparently much more of a political game than an attempt to root out corruption."
swa: Akiandika katika tovuti ya Registan.net, Alexander Visotsky anaangalia mashtaka ya rushwa dhidi ya Mukhtar Dzhakishev yaliyotokana na uuzaji wa madini ya Uranium kinyume cha sheria na kuhitimisha, “Vita dhini ya rushwa nchini Kazakhstan ni mchezo wa kisiasa zaidi ya jitihada za kuing’oa rushwa.”

eng: Writing from Japan, Scilla Alecci points to Transparency International's Ten Worst Corruption Cases of 2009 in Japan.
swa: Akiandika kutoka Japan Scilla Alecci anaonyesha kesi kumi mbaya zaidi za Transparency International nchini Japan.

eng: Finally, writing from the Caribbean island of Puerto Rico, "Gil the Jenius" asks for tougher punishments against public officials convicted of corruption.
swa: Na mwisho, akiandika kutokea Kisiwa cha Karibea cha Puerto Rco, “Gil the jenius” anaomba adhabu kali zaidi dhidi ya maofisa wa serikali wanaoshtakiwa dhidi ya rushwa.

eng: Looking back on anti-corruption activism in 2009 we see that an entrenched culture of corruption is still pervasive worldwide.
swa: Tukiangalia nyuma katika uanaharakati dhidi ya rushwa katika mwaka 2009 tunaona kuwa utamaduni wa rushwa bado umeenea duniani kote.

eng: But we also see a growing online discussion about what can be done to curb corruption, promote transparency, and increase civic engagement.
swa: Lakini pia tunauona mjadala wa mtandaoni unaokua juu ya nini kinachoweza kufanywa kuzuia rushwa, kutangaza uwazi na kuongeza makabiliano ya kijamii.

eng: In future posts we'll look more specifically at online discussions and internet-based projects to promote transparency and fight against corruption in Nigeria and China.
swa: Katika makala zitakazofuata baadaye tutaangalia zaidi na hasa majadiliano ya mtandaoni pamoja na miradi ya kwenye intaneti inayotangaza uwazi na kupigana dhidi ya rushwa nchini Naijeria na China.

eng: Malawians are digesting news that the country's president Dr Bingu wa Mutharika is on May 1 to marry his former tourism minister Callister Chimombo.
swa: Wamalawi wanatafakari taarifa kuwa mnamo tarehe 1 Mei, rais wa nchi Dkt. Bingu wa Mutharika anatarajiwa kumuoa waziri wa zamani wa utalii Callister Moyo.

eng: This will be preceeded by a tradional custom engament on Valenetine's Day 14 February.
swa: Harusi hiyo itatanguliwa na sherehe za kitamaduni za uchumba wakati wa siku ya wapendanao ya Valentino tarehe 14 Februari.

eng: A couple of bloggers have wished the president well in his new found love following the death of his wife Ethel three years ago.
swa: Wanabloga wachache wamemtakia heri rais katika mapenzi mapya aliyoyapata baada ya kifo cha mkewe Ethel miaka mitatu iliyopita.

eng: Emmanuel Sobilika of Malawi Digest writes:
swa: Emmanuel Sobilika wa Malawi Digest anaandika:

eng: In a press statement issued on Wednesday made available to Malawi Digest, the State House says that President Mutharika is expected to marry Chimombo on 1st May, 2010.
swa: Katika taarifa kwa vyombo vya habari iliyotolewa Jumatano ambayo Malawi Digest iliruhusiwa kuisoma, Ikulu inasema kuwa Rais Mutharika anatarajiwa kumuoa Chimbombo katika Mei mosi, 2010.

eng: However, before the official marriage itself, the two will have their traditional custom engagement on 14th February, 2010.
swa: Hata hivyo, kabla ya kufunga ndoa rasmi, wawili hao watakuwa na sherehe zxa kitamaduni za uchumba tarehe 14, Februari 2010.

eng: 14th February is the world’s Valentines Day where people commemorate love with their loved ones.
swa: Tarehe 14 Februari ni siku kimataifa ya Valentino ambapo watu husherehekea mapenzi na wale wanaowapenda.

eng: The official statement discloses that both Dr Mutharika and Miss Callista Chapola Chimombo are a widower and widow respectively.
swa: Taarifa hiyo rasmi inaweka wazi kuwa wote, Dkt Mutharika na Bi Callista Chapola Chimombo ni wajane.

eng: State House says that both Dr Bingu wa Mutharika and Chimombo are devout Roman Catholics.
swa: Ikulu inaeleza kuwa wote Dkt Bingu wa Mutharika na Chimombo ni waumini wa kanisa Katoliki la Roma.

eng: Journalist Kondwani Munthali congratulates the president for what he calls:
swa: Mwanahabari Kondwani Munthali anampongeza rais kwa kile alichokiita:

eng: leading the way by announcing their intentions for Holy Matrimony, adding hopefully we will find a card for the event and share with many of my freinds here the pictures.
swa: Kuongoza njia kwa kutangaza nia ya Ndoa Takatifu, na kuongeza tunatumaini kuwa nitapata kadi na kuwaonyesha marafiki zangu wengi picha za tukio hilo

eng: Callista was spoted at several state functions sitting next to the president.
swa: Callista alionekana katika dhifa nyingi za kitaifa akiwa ameketi pembeni ya rais.

eng: She earlier on denied the love story.
swa: Awali alikanusha habari za mapenzi.

eng: State house officials also refused to explain the protocol and justify the former minister's closeness to the president at the state functions.
swa: Maofisa wa Ikulu pia walikataa kufanunua itifaki na uhalali wa waziri huyo wa zamani kuwa Karibu sana na rais katika dhifa za kitaifa.

eng: Richard Chirombo in Malawi's commercial capital Blantyre wrote:
swa: Richard Chirombo aliye katika jiji la kibiashara la Malawi, Blantyre aliandika:

eng: Chimombo has since mid-December 2009 been seen sitting next to Mutharika, a position reserved for high government officials and trusted pals.
swa: Kuanzia katikati ya mwezi Disemba 2009 Chimombo amekuwa akiketi pembeni ya Mutharika, nafasi inayotengwa kwa maofisa wa juu serikalini na maswahiba wanaoaminiwa.

eng: Instead, Chimombo says it is the president who chooses who to sit next to him, and as such it was "just a previlege" that Mutharika has allowed her to sit next to him.
swa: Badala yake, Chimombo anasema kuwa ni rais ambaye huamua ni nani anayeketi pembeni yake, na kwa hiyo ilikuwa ni “ustahiki” kwamba Mutharika alimruhusu kuketi Karibu naye.

eng: This will be the second state wedding in Malawi after Bakili Muluzi's in 1999.
swa: Hii itakuwa ni harusi ya pili ya taifa nchini Malawi baada ya ile ya Bakili Muluzi mwaka 1999.

eng: President Wade, pictured here at the 2002 World Economic Forum, wants to grant Haitian earthquake survivors free land in Senegal (image source: Wikipedia)
swa: Rais Wade, akiwa katika Mkutano wa Dunia wa uchumi 2002, anataka kuwapatia ardhi ya bure walionusurika na tetemeko la ardhi (picha na: Wikipedia)

eng: In the aftermath of the devastating earthquake, politicians and citizens around the world have scrambled to join the global outpouring of solidarity for Haiti, and poor countries, including many in Africa, are no exception.
swa: Baada ya tetemeko la ardhi, wanasiasa na raia duniani kote wanagombania kujiunga na harakati za mshikamano zinazomiminika kwa ajili ya Haiti, na nchi maskini, zikijumuishwa nyingi zilizoko barani Afrika, hazijapitwa.

eng: Rwanda, Liberia, South Africa, Gabon, Nigeria and many others have already pleged financial aid.
swa: Rwanda, Liberia, Afrika Kusini, Gabon, Naijeria na nyingine nyingi zimekwishatoa ahadi za misaada ya fedha.

eng: However, it is the 84 year-old Senegalese president, Abdoulaye Wade, who has been making headlines.
swa: Hata hivyo, ni rais wa Senegal mwenye umri wa miaka 84, Abdoulaye Wade, ambaye anatawala vichwa vya habari.

eng: Wade is offering free land to any Haitian earthquake survivors who wish to "return to their origins," according to a spokesperson.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa msemaji, Wade ametoa ardhi ya bure kwa Mu-Haiti yeyote aliyenusurika na tetemeko na ambaye “atapenda kurejea kwenye asili yake.”

eng: Online, the proposal has been received with almost universal ridicule.
swa: Kwenye wavuti, tangazo hilo limepokelewa na watu wengi kwa kejeli.

eng: Although Blog Politique au Senegal has yet to comment on either Wade's offer or the earthquake, it did post this commentary by Dr. EL Hadji Malick Ndiaye on the importance of "South-South" solidarity, published before Wade's announcement:
swa: Japokuwa blogu ya Blog Politique au Senegal haijatoa maoni yake kuhusu pendekezo la rais Wade wala kuhusu tetemeko la ardhi, blogu hiyo ilituma maoni ya Dkt. El hadji Malick Ndiaye juu ya umuhimu wa mshikamano baina ya nchi za kusini, ambayo yalichapishwa kabla ya Wade kutoa tangazo lake:

eng: ...Dakar, which has trouble taking off and solving its many problems related to sanitation and urbanization, whose suburbs are wading in flood waters from years past, by what means can she accommodate a population or a whole country at the other end of the world?...
swa: … Dakar, ambayo inashindwa kushika kasi na kutatua matatizo yake mengi yanayohusiana na majitaka na mipango miji, ambayo vitongoji vyake vinaelea katika maji ya mafuriko yaliyotokea miaka mingi iliyopita, kwa uwezo gani itaweza kuwachukua watu au nchi nzima kutoka ng’ambo nyingine ya dunia?...

eng: Abdoulaye Wade, in a of solidarity and pan-Africanism, proposes to depopulate Haiti, thereby forgetting that charity begins at home... ... Abdoulaye Wade, very nostalgic the 19th century, believes that Marcus Garvey is still alive, and that the "Back to Africa" movement is still valid.
swa: Abdoulaye Wade, katika kuonyesha mshikamano na Uafrika (PanAfricanism), anatoa pendekezo la kupunguza watu Haiti, na kusahau kuwa wema huanzia nyumbani… … Abdoulaye Wade, mwenye kupenda sana kumbukumbu za karne ya 19, anaamini kuwa Marcus Garvey bado yu hai, na kwamba harakati za “Kurudi Afrika” bado zina maana.

eng: One day, he will eventually tell us is that the Ku Klux Klan who made the earth tremble in Haiti...each country has its own calamities.
swa: Siku moja hatimaye atatuambia kuwa walikuwa ni Wabaguzoi wa Ku Klux Klan ambao waliitetemesha dunia kule Haiti. .. kila nchi ina majanga yake.

eng: Haiti has its own, which generate a lot of compassion, and we have ours, which do as much damage as an earthquake, such as statements by a president who has trouble staying above the fray, and whose is a source of controversy.
swa: Haiti ina majanga yake, ambayo yanasababisha moyo wa huruma, na sisi tuna majanga yetu, ambayo hufanya uharibifu sawa tu na ule wa tetemeko, matamko kama haya ya rais ambaye anashindwa kuwa mbali na mitafaruku, na ambaye rekodi yake ni chanzo zha utata.

eng: The Haitian people, as was said and reiterated by the President ¨"Are entitled to the African soil".
swa: Watu wa Haiti, kama ilivyoelezwa na rais ‘ Wana haki katika ardhi ya Afrika”.

eng: The question remains, if they want it.
swa: Swali linabaki, ikiwa wataitaka (ardhi hiyo).

eng: PascaleBoulerie, a reader at tak2.00221.info writes:
swa: PascaleBoulerie, msomaji katika tak2.00221.info anaandika:

eng: We are Global Voices.
swa: Sisi ni Sauti za Dunia.

eng: If you wish to support our work, please visit our Donate page.
swa: Kama unapenda kuunga mkono kazi yetu, tafadhali tembelea ukurasa wetu wa Michango.

eng: Rising Voices Director David Sasaki has written a lovely retrospective for Global Voices' fifth birthday.
swa: Mkurugenzi wa Sauti Zinazokua, David Sasaki ameandika kumbukumbu ya kuvutia kwa ajili ya siku ya kuadhimisha miaka mitano ya Global Voices.

eng: Five years ago this month, David traveled across the United States from California to Harvard for a day-long workshop on global blogging.
swa: Miaka mitano iliyopita mwezi huu, David alisafiri katika Marekani kuanzia California mpaka Havard kwa ajili ya warsha ya siku nzima kuhusu kublogu ulimwenguni.

eng: The workshop - little more than a structured brainstorming session - was called "Global Voices Online."
swa: Warsha hiyo – zaidi kidogo ya wasaa wa kushirikiana mawazo – iliitwa “Sauti za Dunia Kwenye Wavuti.”

eng: The website you are reading today started out as a blog that Ethan Zuckerman and I set up to organize that workshop.
swa: Tovuti unayoisoma leo ilianza kama blogu ambayo Ethan Zuckerman na mimi tuliitengeneza ili kuandaa warsha hiyo.

eng: Our aim, put very simply, was to discuss how "to use blogging and blog tools to help people in different countries hold more meaningful and direct conversations with each other."
swa: Lengo letu, tukiliweka kirahisi, lilikuwa kujadili jinsi ya “kutumia kublogu na zana za kublogu ili kuwasaidia watu katika nchi tofauti kufanya mazungumzo yenye maana na ya moja kwa moja baina yao.”

eng: The day's discussion was part of a larger Internet and Society conference put on by Harvard's Berkman Center for Internet and Society.
swa: Majadiliano ya siku hiyo yalikuwa ni sehemu ya kongamano kubwa la Wavuti na Jamii lililoandaliwa na Kituo cha Berkman cha Wavuti na Jamii chuoni Harvard.

eng: The Open Society Institute generously granted us some funds to fly in bloggers from various parts of the world.
swa: Taasisi ya Jamii Wazi kwa ukarimu ilitufadhili fedha kiasi ili kuwasafirisha wanablogu kutoka sehemu mbalimbali duniani.

eng: We publicized the event on the web, and many others - like David - just showed up.
swa: Tulilitangaza tukio hilo kwenye wavuti, na wengine wengi – kama David – walijitokeza.

eng: Thank goodness.
swa: Tunashukuru.

eng: Here is an article I wrote soon after the meeting.
swa: Hii ni makala niliyoiandika mara baada ya mkutano.

eng: Here is Ethan's "day after" blog post.
swa: Hii ni posti ya blogu ya Ethan “siku iliyofuata.”

eng: We did not emerge with a concrete plan for world domination - or even for a coherent project.
swa: Hatukutoka na mpango mahsusi wa kuitawala dunia – au hata mradi thabiti.

eng: Participants agreed to set up a wiki to share information, an Internet Relay Chat (IRC) for further on-line meetings, and an aggregator of blogs by conference participants and others like them who we began to call "bridge bloggers."
swa: Washiriki walikubaliana kuanzisha ukurasa wa ushirika katika wavuti ili kushirikiana habari, pamoja na Mazungumzo ya Maandishi Kwenye Wavuti (Internet Relay Chat (IRC) kwa ajili ya mikutano mingine kwenye wavuti, pamoja na kikusanya blogu kitakachoendeshwa na washiriki wa kongamano pamoja na wengine kama wao ambao tulianza kuwaita “wanablogu kiungo.”

eng: We weren't sure where we would go from there.
swa: Hatukuwa na hakika tungeelekea wapi baada ya pale.

eng: One thing, however, was clear: a critical mass of bloggers with similar values was emerging around the globe.
swa: Jambo moja, hata hivyo, lilikuwa wazi: umma amuzi wa wanablogu wenye maadili yanayofanana na yetu ulikuwa unaanza kujitokeza duniani kote.

eng: It seemed like a good idea to "connect the dots" (as Jeff Ooi put it) amongst these people and create a platform for this emergent community.
swa: Ilionekana kama ni wazo zuri “kuunganisha nukta zote” (kama Jeff Ooi anavyosema) baina ya watu hawa na kuunda jukwaa linalotokana na jamii hii inayokua.

eng: In the weeks following the conference, a number of participants used a wiki to articulate this community's shared values.
swa: Katika majuma yaliyofuata baada ya kongamano, baadhi ya washiriki walitumia ukurasa wa ushirika kwenye wavuti ili kuyaweka maadili ya jamii hii.

eng: The Global Voices Manifesto was the result.
swa: Matokeo yake yalikuwa ni Ilani ya Global Voices.

eng: It's worth reproducing in full here because everything Global Voices does today continues to be driven by these fundamental values:
swa: Ni muhimu kuiweka (Ilani hiyo) tena hapa katika ujumla wake kwani kila kitu ambacho Global Voices inakifanya leo hii kinaendelea kuendeshwa na maadili hayo ya msingi:

eng: We believe in free speech: in protecting the right to speak — and the right to listen.
swa: Tunaamini katika uhuru wa kujieleza: katika kulinda haki ya kutoa kauli – na haki ya kusikiliza.

eng: We believe in universal access to the tools of speech.
swa: Tunaamini katika upati huru wa nyenzo za kujieleza.

eng: To that end, we seek to enable everyone who wants to speak to have the means to speak — and everyone who wants to hear that speech, the means to listen to it.
swa: Ili kufanikisha hilo, tanataka kumwezesha kila mmoja ambaye anataka kujieleza kuwa na njia za kujieleza – na kila mmoja anayetaka kusikiliza, awe na njia za kusikiliza.

eng: Thanks to new tools, speech need no longer be controlled by those who own the means of publishing and distribution, or by governments that would restrict thought and communication.
swa: Shukrani kwa nyezo mpya, kauli hazihitaji kudhibitiwa na wale wanaomiliki njia za uchapishaji na usambazaji, au na serikali ambazo zinaweza kudhibiti fikra na mawasiliano.

eng: Now, anyone can wield the power of the press.
swa: Hivi sasa, mtu yeyote anaweza kuwa na nguvu za vyombo vya habari.

eng: Everyone can tell their stories to the world.
swa: Kila mtu anaweza kusimulia simulizi yake kwa dunia.

eng: We seek to build bridges across the gulfs that divide people, so as to understand each other more fully.
swa: Tunataka kujenga madaraja katika mabonde yanayotenganisha watu, ili kwamba tuweze kuelewana zaidi.

eng: We seek to work together more effectively, and act more powerfully.
swa: Tanataka kufanya kazi kwa ufanisi zaidi, na kutenda kwa nguvu zaidi.

eng: We believe in the power of direct connection.
swa: Tunaamini katika nguvu ya kukutana moja kwa moja.

eng: The bond between individuals from different worlds is personal, political and powerful.
swa: Mshikamano kati ya watu kutoka dunia tofauti niwa kibinafsi, kisiasa na wenye nguvu.

eng: We believe conversation across boundaries is essential to a future that is free, fair, prosperous and sustainable - for all citizens of this planet.
swa: Tunaamini kuwa maongezi yanashinda mipaka ni muhimu kwa mustakabali ambo ni huru, wa haki, wenye kuneemesha na endelevu – kwa raia wote wa dunia hii.

eng: While we continue to work and speak as individuals, we also seek to identify and promote our shared interests and goals.
swa: Huku tukiendelea kufanya kazi na kuongea kama watu binafsi, pia tunataka kutambua na kukuza malengo na maslahi tunayoshirikiana pamoja.

eng: We pledge to respect, assist, teach, learn from, and listen to one other.
swa: Tunaahidi kuheshimu, kusaidia, kufundisha, kujifunza na kusikiliza kutoka kwa kila mmoja wetu.

eng: We are Global Voices.
swa: Sisi ni Sauti za Dunia.

eng: We now have an amazing multinational team who act as stewards for various parts of Global Voices.
swa: Hivi sasa tuna timu ya watu wa mataifa mbalimbali ambao wanashika nafasi kama wasimamizi wa sehemu mbalimbali za Global Voices.

eng: But the soul of GV are the hundreds of volunteers who take time out from their jobs, studies, and and family obligations to help build a more open and participatory global public discourse.
swa: Lakini roho ya ya GV ni mamia ya watu wanaojitolea ambao wanatenga muda kutoka kwenye kazi zao, masomo, na majukumu ya kifamilia ili kusaidia kujenga majadiliano ya umma wa dunia yaliyo huru zaidi na shirikishi.

eng: Members of the Global Voices community at the 2006 Summit in Delhi, India.
swa: Wanachama wa jamii ya Global Voices katika Mkutano wa Delhi India, mwaka 2006.

eng: Photo by Jace.
swa: Picha na Jace.

eng: The detailed story of how Global Voices evolved and how its various branches operate - including Rising Voices, Global Voices Advocacy, and Global Voices Lingua - can be found in many places, including this website's About section and FAQ.
swa: Habari ya kina ya jinsi Global Voices ilivyokua na jinsi matawi yake tofauti yanavyofanya kazi – kujumuisha Sauti Zinazokua, Idara ya Utetezi ya Global Voices pamoja na Idara ya Lugha ya Global Voices – inaweza kupatikana kwenye sehemu nyingi, pamoja na sehemu Kuhusu ya tovuti hii na ile ya Maswali Yanayolizwa Kila Mara (FAQ).

eng: News stories about the project are here.
swa: Habari kuhusu mradi huu zipo hapa.

eng: Since 2004 we've had physical gatherings in London (2005), Delhi (2006), and Budapest (2008).
swa: Tangu mwaka 2004 tumekuwa na mikutano inayokutanisha watu mjini London (2005), Delhi (2006) na Budapest (2008).

eng: We are looking forward to another gathering in 2010 (location and date to be announced soon).
swa: Tunatazamia kuwa na mkutano mwingine mwaka 2010 (mahali na tarehe vitatangazwa hivi karibuni).

eng: In 2006 Ethan and I wrote an article for the Nieman Reports magazine in which we sought to explain the relationship between Global Voices and journalism.
swa: Mwaka 2006 mimi na Ethan tuliandika makala kwa ajili ya jarida la Nieman Reports ambamo tulitaka kuelezea uhusiano kati ya Global Voices na uanahabari.

eng: David has another excellent post about why outreach, advocacy and translation are necessary to help people overcome the obstacles to speaking, being heard, and listening to others.
swa: David anayo makala nyingine nzuri sana inayohusu kwa nini shughuli za kivuko, utetezi na ufasiri ni muhimukatika kuwasaidia watu kuvishinda vikwazo vya kuongea, kisikilizwa, na kuwasikiliza wengine.

eng: Many people around the world are frustrated that the global English-language mainstream media ignores their country much of the time, or only covers the bad things about their country, or tends to stereotype them.
swa: Watu wengi duniani wanakerwa kwa kuwa vyombo vya habari vikuu vya kiingereza duniani havitilii maanani nchi zao kwa muda mrefu, na kuandika tu habari mbaya kuhusu nchi zao, au vyombo hivyo huendeleza tu imani potofu kuwahusu.

eng: They see GV as a valuable platform through which to get their stories and viewpoints amplified to a broader global audience.
swa: Wanaiona GV kama jukwaa la thamani ambalo wanaweza kukuza simulizi na mitazamo yao kwa hadhira pana zaidi duniani.

eng: Others are frustrated that their own domestic news media fail to report on much of the world, do it badly, or do it in a slanted manner that supports their government's worldview, and thus believe that by translating GV content into their local language they can improve their community's understanding of the world.
swa: Wengine wanakereka na kwamba vyombo vya habari vya ndani ya nchi zao vinashindwa kuripoti juu ya sehemu nyingi za dunia, wanafanya vibaya, au wanaripoti katika namna iliyopinda ambayo inaunga mkono mtazamo wa dunia wa serikali zao, na hivyo wanaamini kuwa kwa kutafsiri maudhui ya GV katika lugha zao za nyumbani wanaweza kuboresha ufahamu wa dunia wa jamii zao.

eng: Others focus on helping communities who are not yet taking advantage of new technologies to get their story out.
swa: Wengine wanatilia makini kuzisaidia jamii ambazo hazijachukua hatua za kunufaika na teknolojia mpya ili kuzitoa simulizi zao nje.

eng: Others have joined in common cause against censorship and repression of those who are merely exercising their universal right to free expression according to Article 19 of the United Nations Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
swa: Wengine wamejiunga kwa dhumuni la pamoja dhidi ya kuchuja habari na ukandamizwaji wa wale ambao wanatumia haki yao ya kujieleza kwa uhuru kwa mujibu wa kipengele cha 19 cha Azimio la Umoja wa Mataifa la Haki za Binadamu.

eng: The GV community has not let itself get bogged down in endless debates about whether bloggers are or aren't journalists, or what the Internet means for the news business.
swa: Jamii ya GV haijaruhusu kujikwamisha katika mijadala isiyoisha kama wanablogu ni wanahabari au la, au wavuti unamaanisha nini katika biashara ya habari.

eng: Nor does GV get tangled up in arguments about whether the Internet is or is not going to be a force for global democratization.
swa: Kadhalika GV haijifungi katika mizozo kuhusu je Wavuti utakuwa ni nguvu ya demokrasi duniani au la.

eng: As a community we're more interested in rolling up our sleeves and getting to work addressing a more tangible problem: filling a few of the gaping holes in the global public discourse, and doing what we can about the huge imbalances, inequities, and injustices in global media.
swa: Kama jamii tunatilia mkazo kukunja mikono ya mashati yet una kuingia kazini ili kukabiliana na tatizo hai zaidi: kuziba mapengo yaliyo kwenye mjadala wa umma duniani, na kufanya tunaloweza kuhusu mizani isiyo sawa, uonevu na ukiukwaji wa haki katika vyombo vya habari duniani.

eng: However you define this work, we believe that what we're doing has value and makes a difference.
swa: Haijalishi namna utakavyobainisha kazi hii, tunaamini kuwa kile tunachokifanya kina thamani na kinabadilisha mambo.

eng: We are grateful that a range of organizations have deemed our work to be worthy of their financial support.
swa: Tunashukuru kwamba mashirika kadhaa yameiona kazi yetu kuwa ina thamani kwa ufadhili wao kifedha.

eng: We have developed relationships with news organizations who follow our work and seek us out because - however you define what we do - our community is a valuable source of global information and fresh perspectives.
swa: Tumeendeleza uhusiano na vyombo vya habari ambavyo vinafuatilia kazi zetu na kututaka kwa sababu – kwa namna yoyote utakavyoeleza tunachofanya – jamii yet uni chanzo chenye thamani cha habari za dunia na mitazamo mipya.

eng: This is why Reuters provided critical core support in our first three years, and why a many news organizations continue to work with our editors and to contact our volunteers for interviews.
swa: Hii ni sababu ambayo Reuters ilitoa usaidizi wa kiini katika miaka yetu mitatu ya kwanza, na sababu ambayo mashirika mengi ya habari yanaendelea kufanya kazi na wahariri wet una kuwasiliana na watu wanaojitolea kwa ajili ya mahojiano.

eng: While we can't say we've completely transformed global media, we do believe that we've brought global media attention to a range of stories that might otherwise not have been reported, and provided fresh perspectives on numerous other major international news stories.
swa: Wakati hatuwezi kusema kuwa tumebadilisha kabisa uanahabari wa ulimwengu, tunaamini kuwa tumeweza kuyaelekeza macho ya vyombo vya habari kwenye habari nyingi ambazo vinginevyo zisingeweza kuripotiwa, na kutoa mitazamo mipya juu ya hamari nyingi za kimataifa.

eng: That in itself has made the entire enterprise worthwhile.
swa: Jambo hilo pekee limeifanya jitihada hii kuwa ya thamani.

eng: What's even more exciting is the way in which Global Voices has impacted the lives of our editors, volunteers, and broader community members.
swa: Jambo la kusisimua zaidi ni jinsi Global voices ilivyobadilisha maisha ya wahariri wetu, watu wanaojitolea na jamii pana ya wanachama.

eng: We have become a hub through which an amazing group of talented, articulate, and caring people can find fulfillment, global recognition, and community support.
swa: Tumekuwa kituo ambacho kundi la kuvutia la watu wenye vipaji, werevu na wanaojali wengine hupata kuridhika, kutambuliwa duniani, na usaidizi wa kijamii.

eng: Click here to read about how Rising Voices has brought more diverse voices into national and global conversations, and what that has meant for the individuals and communities involved.
swa: Bonyeza hapa ili kusoma juu ya jinsi ambavyo Sauti Zinazokua ilivyozileta sauti zenye utofauti katika mazungumzo ya kitaifa na ya kidunia, na maana ya jambo hilo kwa watu binafsi na kwa jamii husika.

eng: To get a sense of how amazing our volunteers are, read and listen to some of the blogger profiles posted here.
swa: Ili kuapata kionjo cha namna ambavyo waandishi wetu wa kujitolea walivyo, soma na kusikiliza baadhi ya wasifu wa wanablogu hao hapa.

eng: GV has also had an impact on various blogging communities around the world with whom we have no formal relationship - other than linking to and translating some of their blog posts from time to time.
swa: GV pia imekuwa na msukumo kwa jamii mbalimbali za wanablogu duniani ambazo tuna uhusiano rasmi nazo – zaidi ya kuweka viunganishi na kutafsiri baadhi ya makala zao za kwenye blogu katika wakati tofauti tofauti.

eng: Just one example: Ethan recently described an eye-opening conversation with a young Kyrgyz blogger, Bektour Iskender about the impact some of our work has had in Central Asia.
swa: Mfano mmoja tu: Ethan hivi karibuni alielezea mazungumzo yanayofungua macho na mwanablogu kijana wa jamii ya Kyrgiz, Bektour Iskander kuhusu athari za baadhi ya kazi zetu huko Asia ya Kati.

eng: What might result from a slightly more democratic, open, and participatory global media environment is not clear.
swa: Kile kitakachotokea kutoka katika mazingira ya uanahabari duniani yaliyo na demokrasia zaidi kidogo, yaliyo wazi na shirikishi bado hakijajulikana wazi.

eng: At the 2004 meeting, Iranian blogger Hossein Derakhshan expressed the hope that the spread of online citizen media would make societies more democratic and war more difficult for governments to justify.
swa: Katika mkutano wa 2004, mwanablogu wa Kiirani Hossein Derakhshan alielezea matumaini kwamba kuenea kwa uanahabari wa kiraia kwenye wavuti kutazifanya jamii kuwa za kidemokrasi zaidi na kwa serikali kuapta ugumu zaidi katika kuhalalisha vita.

eng: Hoder, as he's known on the Internet, has been imprisoned by Ahmedinejad's regime for over a year now, and it's not clear whether expanded contacts between Iranians and Westerners would be a deciding factor in a U.S. decision about whether or not to attack Iran.
swa: “Hoder” kama anavyojulikana kwenye wavuti, amefungwa na utawala wa Amhedinejad kwa zaidi ya mwaka mmoja sasa, haieleweki kama uhusiano mpana kati ya Wairani na Wamagharibi utakuwa ndiyo sababu kuu katika uamuzi wa Marekani wa ama kuivamia au kutoivamia Irani.

eng: Writers like Evgeny Morozov argue that contrary to early optimism about the Internet as a democratizing force, dictatorships are figuring out how to use the Internet to solidify their power and suppress dissent - and that the Internet in many countries is dominated by manipulated spin, disinformation and hate.
swa: Waandishi kama Evgeny Morozov wanadai kuwa kinyume na matumaini ya awali kuhusu wavuti kuwa nguvu ya demokrasi, tawala za kiimla zinang’amua jinsi ya kutumia wavuti ili kuimarisha nguvu zao na kukandamiza upinzani – na kwamba wavuti katika nchi nyingi inatawaliwa na upindishaji wa habari, utoaji wa habari potofu na chuki.

eng: Others like Clay Shirky and Patrick Meier argue that there is still reason for optimism.
swa: Wengine kama Clay Shirky na Patrick Meier wanadai kwamba bado kuna sababu ya kutumaini.

eng: Still others point out that most of the world's people have more pressing problems - like physical survival - and all of the above including Global Voices' work is irrelevant to them anyway.
swa: Na bado wengine wanaonyesha kuwa wengi wa watu duniani wana matatizo makubwa zaidi – kama vile kuishi tu – na yote hapo juu pamoja na kazi za Global Voices hazina maana kwao.

eng: Five years ago Ory Okolloh - who went on to found the wildly successful citizen reporting platform Ushahidi - made some comments that are worth revisiting in the context of those debates.
swa: Miaka mitano iliyopita Ory Okolloh – ambaye aliendelea na kuanzisha jukwaa lililofanikiwa sana la kuripoti la jamii Ushahidi – alitoa maoni fulani yanayopaswa kurejewa katika muktadha wa midahalo hii.

eng: Here's how I reported her words at the time:
swa: Hivi ndivyo nilivyoripoti maneno yake wakati huo:

eng: Kenyan blogger Ory Okolloh doesn't expect Africa to be transformed by blogging any time soon.
swa: Mwanablogu wa Kenya Ory Okolloh hategemei kuwa Afrika itabadilishwa na kublogu katika wakati wowote hivi karibuni.

eng: Bridging the digital divide is perhaps the least of Africa's many problems.
swa: Kuunganisha utengano wa kidijitali pengine ni jambo la chini sana katika matatizo mengi ya Afrika.

eng: Nonetheless, she thinks blogging is important – if not transformative – for the small number of Africans who do blog.
swa: Haidhuru, ory anafikiri kuwa kublogu ni jambo muhimu – kama si jambi linalobadilisha – kwa idadi ndiogo ya Waafrika wanaoblogu.

eng: For young people, we have not been heard, we don't have a space in Africa within politics or in other arenas to express ourselves, Okolloh says.
swa: “Kwa vijana, hatujasikilizwa, hatuna sehemu katika Afrika ndani ya siasa au katika majukwaa mengine kuweza kujieleza,” anasema Okolloh.

eng:
I think it could provide a forum for young people to create their own space. 	“Nafikiriinaweza kutoa jukwaa kwa vijana kuunda sehemu yao wenyewe.
I don't think it will change politics per se or determine an election but I think it can breed community in ways that have not been able to take place before.
swa: Sidhani kama itabadilisha siasa kabisa au itaelekeza uchaguzi bali ninafikiri itaweza kuzaa jamii katika nia ambazo hazijawahi kuweza kutokea kabla.”

eng: Online citizen media is breeding new forms of community at the local, national, and global level.
swa: Uanahabari wa kijamii kwenye wavuti unazaa namna mpya za jamii katika ngazi za sehemu husika, kitaifa na kidunia.

eng: GV has become a loose connective tissue between Ory's Kenyan blogging community and other bloggers around the world who share similar values.
swa: GV imekuwa chembe hai tepe inayonganisha jamii ya wanablogu wa Kikenya ya Ory na wanablogu wengine duniani ambao wanashiriki maadili yanayofanana.

eng: While Global Voices seeks to influence the stories reported by traditional news media - most of which serve specific nations or regions - we are also building a platform for global discourse, and a community of global citizens around that discourse.
swa: Wakati Global Voices ina nia ya kuelekeza habari zinazoripotiwa na vyombo vya habari vya kitamaduni - ambavyo vingi vyake vinahudumia mataifa au maeneo malum – kadhalika tunajenga jukwaa kwa ajili ya mazungumzo ya kidunia, na jamii ya raia wa dunia katika mazungumzo hayo.

eng: We use the Internet not to escape from our humanity, but to assert it.
swa: Tunatumia wavuti si kwa ajili ya kutoroka kutoka katika ubinadamu wetu, bali kwa ajili ya kuusisitiza.

eng: We believe individual choices and actions make a difference.
swa: Tunaamini kuwa maamuzi binafsi na vitendo vianasababisha mabadiliko.

eng: Whether the Internet will ultimately empower more than it enslaves depends on whether we take responsibility for our future and act.
swa: Ikiwa wavuti hatimaye utawezesha zaidi kuliko unavyotia watu utumwani kutategemea kama tutachukua wajibu kwa ajili ya mustakabali wetu na kutenda.

eng: Building a multi-cultural, multi-lingual community focused on specific projects underpinned by a core set of humanistic values is just one small effort in that direction.
swa: Kujenga jamii ya tamaduni mbalimbali na lugha mbalimbali inayomakinikia miradi mahsusi inayounganishwa na seti ya maadili ya kiutu ni jitihada ndogo katika mwelekeo huo.

eng: The relations between the two neighboring countries, Slovakia and Hungary, went bad last year, especially because of the so-called "language law" introduced in Slovakia.
swa: Uhusiano kati ya nchi mbili jirani za Slovakia na Hungaria ulianza kutetereka katika mwaka uliopita, hasa kwa sababu ya kile kinachoitwa "sheria ya lugha" iliyoanzishwa huko Slovakia.

eng: Hungarian and Slovak people could even see their politicians involving an EU institution, the Organisation for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) into their discussion.
swa: Raia wa Hungaria na Slovakia walijikuta wakishuhudia wanasiasa wao wakianza hata kuhusisha taasisi ya Jumuiya ya Ulaya, yaani, Shirika la Usalama na Ushirikaiano la Ulaya, kwa kifupi OSCE, katika mivutano hiyo.

eng: At the end of 2009, Hungarian and Slovak citizens started an online campaign which will turn into more visible formats in January 2010.
