eng: “I want all other children born in Liberia- and the world- to lead full lives free of pain and filled with the blossoms of love, like mine,” writes Mahmud Johnson at the blog for the youth-oriented HIV/AIDS group Global 40 Forum.
swa: “Ninataka watoto wengine wote waliozaliwa Liberia –na duniani kote–kuishi maisha makamilifu yasiyo na maumivu na yaliyojawa na maua ya upendo, kama yangu,” anaandika Mahmud Johnson kwenye blogu ya vijana kuhusu VVU/UKIMWI kwenye jukwaa la Global 40.

eng: He is an 18-year old former co-host of the Liberian youth radio show, "Let’s Talk About Sex", which deals with issues relating to the spread of HIV/AIDS and pregnancy prevention.
swa: Ana umri wa miaka 18 mtangazaji mwenza wa zamani wa kipindi cha redio kwa vijana nchini Liberia, “Na Tuzungumzie Ngono”, ambacho kinachoshughulika na masuala yanayohusiana na maambukizi ya VVU/UKIMWI na kuzuia mimba zisizotarajiwa.

eng: Liberia is gradually transitioning from the nearly 15 years of intermittent civil war that ended in 2003 and moving towards mainstream development.
swa: Taratibu Liberia inapitia hatua kwa hatua kutoka kwenye karibu miaka 15 ya vita vya wenyewe kwa wenyewe ambavyo vilimalizika mwaka 2003 na kusonga mbele kuelekea kwenye maendeleo.

eng: The barriers that remain are great.
swa: Vizingiti vilivyobaki ni vikubwa.

eng: Nearly 250,000 people were killed during the war, and several hundred thousand were exiled in neighboring countries or in Europe or the United States.
swa: Karibu watu 250,000 waliuawa wakati wa vita, na malaki kadhaa walikimbilia nchi jirani au Ulaya na Marekani kama wakimbizi.

eng: The effects of war on youth
swa: Madhara ya vita kwa vijana

eng: The effects of the war on children are well documented.
swa: Madhara ya vita kwa vijana yamewekwa vizuri kwenye kumbukumbu.

eng: When the fighting began, different military groups searched for soldiers in the ranks of children.
swa: Mapigano yalipoanza, vikundi mbalimbali vya kijeshi vilitafuta wanajeshi kutoka kwenye rika la watoto.

eng: Perhaps as many as 20,000 children, some as young as 6-years-old, were recruited, often forcibly.
swa: Pengine watoto wengi kiasi cha 250,000, wengine wadogo wa miaka 6, waliandikishwa, mara nyingi kwa nguvu.

eng: “They were forced to kill friends and family members including their parents, rape and be raped, serve as sexual slaves and prostitutes, labor, take drugs, engage in cannibalism, torture and pillage communities,” says the report from the Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Liberia.
swa: “Walilazimishwa kuwaua rafiki zao na wanafamilia wao ikiwa ni pamoja na wazazi, walibaka na kubakwa, walitumika kama watumwa wa ngono na Malaya, walifanya kazi nguvu, walitumia madawa ya kulevwa, walijihusisha na ulaji wa nyama za binadamu, utesaji na kuiibia jamii”, inasema taarifa ya tume ya Ukweli na Maridhiano ya Liberia.

eng: Women and girls also suffered greatly.
swa: Wanawake na wasichana waliteseka sana.

eng: Liberia’s TRC received nearly 7,000 reported cases of sexual violence.
swa: Tume hiyo ilipokea karibu visa 7,000 vya ngono ya nguvu.

eng: Girls and women aged 15–19 make a majority of those reported cases.
swa: Wasichana na wanawake wa umri wa miaka 15 mpaka 19 walikuwa kundi kubwa zaidi lililoathirika na visa hivyo vilivyotaarifiwa.

eng: Despite seven years of peace, bad news can still cascade out of Liberia like a waterfall.
swa: Pamoja na miaka saba ya amani, habari mbaya bado zinaweza kutmiminika kutoka Liberia kama maporomoko ya maji.

eng: Three out of four Liberians live on less than one dollar a day; only half the country's children attend school; Fifty percent of households in the capital Monrovia are classified as food secure.
swa: Waliberia watatu kati ya kumi wanaishi chini ya dola moja kwa siku, nusu tu ya watoto wa nchi hii wanahudhuria shule; asilimia hamsini ya kaya katika mji mkuu wa Monrovia wanaangukia kwenye kundi lenye uhakika wa chakula.

eng: The economic prognosis remains bleak and repatriating young people – some of them former child soldiers – into the economy continues to cause the government problems.
swa: Mwelekeo wa uchumi hauleti matumaini na vijana wanaorejea nchini mwao–baadhi yao wakiwa ni wanajeshi watoto wa zamani – katika uchumi unaoendelea kusababisha matatizo kwa serikali.

eng: This can be especially troubling because half of Liberia’s population is under 20.
swa: Hili linaweza kusumbua sana hasa kwa sababu nusu ya idadi ya watu Liberia ni wenye umri chini ya miaka 20.

eng: On the Ceasefire Liberia blog, a Rising Voices project, Stephen R. Johnson writes:
swa: Katika blogu ya Ceasefire Liberia, mradi wa Rising Voices, Stephen R. Johnson anaandika:

eng: Liberia’s youth face many challenges in gaining an education that delivers them the right set of skills and knowledge to become productive in today’s labor market.
swa: Vijana wa Liberia wanakabiliwa na changamoto nyingi katika kupata elimu ambayo itawapatia amana ya ujuzi na ufahamu kuwa wazalishaji katika soko la leo la ajira.

eng: As a result, the transition from school to work is more often than not unsuccessful and youth end up either unemployed or underemployed in the rural, suburban and urban informal sectors.
swa: Matokeo yake, mpito kutoka shule kwenda kazini mara nyingi zaidi huwa bila mafanikio na vijana wanaishia kuwa ama wasio na kazi au wenye kazi duni zisizo rasmi katika maeneo ya vijijini, mijini midogo na mijini.

eng: Yet, the country and its people are determined to put the past behind them.
swa: Bado, nchi hiyo na watu wake wameazimia kuiacha nyuma historia yao.

eng: The country’s economy has been growing and the government is modernizing its infrastructure.
swa: Uchumi wa nchi hiyo umekuwa ukikua na serikali inaimarisha miundombinu.

eng: Groups like the YMCA have been training ex-combatants for employment or to start their own businesses.
swa: Makundi kama YMCA yamekuwa yakiwafunza wapiganaji wa zamani kwa ajili ya ajira au kuanza biashara zao wenyewe.

eng: Poverty and tough decisions
swa: Umasikini na maamuzi magumu

eng: However, the continuing economic problems have created a ripple effect in other areas.
swa: Hata hivyo, matatizo yanayoendelea ya uchumi yamesababisha madhara mengi katika maeneo mengine.

eng: Poverty has forced many women into making difficult and dangerous decisions regarding their sex life, says Jerry B. Tarbolo Jr, from the Federation of Liberian Youth.
swa: Umasikini umewalazimisha wanawake kufanya maamuzi magumu na ya hatari kuhusiana na maisha yao ya kimapenzi, anasema Jerry B. Tarbolo Jr, kutoka Umoja wa Vijana wa Liberia.

eng: He said this combination has helped intensify the HIV/AIDS transmission rate in Liberia’s urban areas.
swa: Anasema mchanganyiko huu umesaidia kukuza kiwango cha maambukizi ya VVU/UKIMWI katika maeneo ya mijini nchini Liberia.

eng: If this continues, the disease will mainly affect the younger generation, he says, which is one of Liberia’s great resources.
swa: Kama hali hii itaendelea, ugonjwa huu utaathiri vibaya kizazi kipya, anasema, ambacho ni moja ya vyanzo vikuu vya Liberia.

eng: The connection between economic survival and sexual violence has a legacy in Liberia.
swa: Uhusiano kati ya kujikimu kiuchumi na ngono za nguvu vina kumbukumbu ndefu nchini Liberia.

eng: A 2008 UNFPA study of women in Liberia’s Lofa County found that during the war, nine out of ten women had lost their livelihoods, 96 percent had lost shelter and nearly 75 percent had lost a relative.
swa: Utafiti wa UNFPA wa mwaka 2008 kwa wanawake wa jimbo la Lofa nchini Liberia uligundua kwamba wakati wa vita, wanawake tisa kati ya kumi walipoteza njia zao zinazowawezesha kuishi, asilimia 96 walipoteza malazi na karibu asilimia 75 waliwapoteza ndugu zao.

eng: More than half of the women were victims of sexual violence, and of those women, half of them reported providing sex for some form of favors.
swa: Zaidi ya nusu ya wanawake walikuwa waathirika wa ngono za nguvu, na kati ya hao, nusu waliripotiwa kutoa ngono kama namna ya kupata upendeleo wa namna fulani.

eng: Misconceptions of HIV/AIDS
swa: Imani potofu za VVU/UKIMWI

eng: Pauline Wleh, a nurse counselor at a Monrovia-based YMCA Youth Centre, says one thing young Liberians today need is education regarding sexual health.
swa: Paulie Wleh, muuguzi mnasihi wa Kituo cha vijana cha YMCA mijini Monrovia, anasema kitu kimoja ambacho Waliberia vijana leo wanakihitaji ni elimu kuhusu afya ya ngono.

eng: She spoke to a writer for Merlin, an international NGO that builds health services in fragile states.
swa: Alizungumza na mwandishi wa Merlin, AZISE ya kimataifa inayojenga huduma za afya katika mazingira magumu.

eng: “Years of conflict here disrupted our formal schooling system and broke up health services so that youths today know very little about HIV and AIDS.
swa: “Miaka ya migogoro hapa iliharibu mfumo wetu wa zamani wa elimu na kubomoa huduma za afya ndio maana vijana leo wanajua kidogo sana kuhusu VVU/UKIMWI.

eng: Because of the lack of knowledge, there is a lot of stigma and misconceptions surrounding AIDS now.
swa: Kwa sababu ya kutokuwa na uelewa, kuna unyanyapaa wa hali ya juu na mikanganyiko kuhusiana na UKIMWI sasa.

eng: Youths are too scared to talk to their parents and there is a lack of accessible information.
swa: Vijana wanaogopa kuzungumza na wazazi wao na hakuna upatikanaji wa taarifa.

eng: But they can discretely drop in on me between basketball games or after a trip to the computer lab to ask questions, access services and get advice.”
swa: Lakini wanaweza kunijia wenyewe wakati wa michezo ya mpira wa kikapu au baada ya ziara ya kutembelea maabara ya tarakilishi kuniuliza maswali, kupata huduma na ushauri. ”

eng: She says some changes in attitudes have become apparent.
swa: Anasema mabadiliko mengine katika dhana yamekuwa dhahiri.

eng: “In the two years since the centre opened, I have seen thousands of young people but only given 291 HIV tests.
swa: “Katika kipindi cha miaka miwili tangu kituo kifunguliwe, nimeona maelfu ya vijana lakini kati yao 291 walipata vipimo vya VVU.

eng: Although people are keen to talk to me, they are rarely convinced to take an HIV test because they are scared.”
swa: Ingawa watu wanahitaji sana kuongea nami, ni nadra sana kushawishika kuchukua vipimo vya VVU kwa sababu wanaogopa.”

eng: The majority who opt out of the testing, claim they will ‘come back later,’ or more honestly ‘don’t want to know my status, because I don’t want to worry.’
swa: Wengi wao wanaochagua kutokupima afya zao, wanadai ‘watakuja siku nyingine,’ au kwa ukweli zaidi ‘sipendi kujua hali yangu, kwa sababu sitaki kuhofu.’

eng: The fight for awareness
swa: Vita vya uelewa

eng: This social avoidance is what programs like "Let’s Talk About Sex" are designed to educate against.
swa: Ukwepaji huu wa jamii ni kile kilichofanya vipindi kama “Na tunzungumze kuhusu ngono” vibuniwe kuwaelimisha kinyume chake.

eng: The weekly 30-minute show, funded in part by UNFPA, provides listeners with 30 minutes of information and conversation about sex and reproductive health issues, all tailored toward young people.
swa: Kipindi hicho cha kila wiki cha urefu wa dakika 30, kwa ufadhili wa UNFPA, kinawapa wasikilizaji wake dakika 30 za taarifa na mazungumzo kuhusu ngono na masuala ya afya ya uzazi, vyote vikiwa vimelengwa kwa vijana.

eng: Each program is researched and written by the four young hosts, who control all the programming, including research, writing and performing each episode.
swa: Kila kipindi kinatafitiwa na kuandikwa na watangazaji wanne, wanaodhibiti utaratibu mzima, ikijumuisha utafiti, kuandika na kuigiza kila kipande.

eng: “My work as co-host of the LTAS show gave me a working knowledge on the actual realities faced by my fellow Liberian youth in the fight against HIV," Mahmud Johnson writes.
swa: “Kazi yangu kama mtangazaji mwenza wa kipindi cha ‘Na tuzungumze kuhusu ngono’ imenipa ufahamu wa namna ya kufanya kazi kwenye uhalisia unaokabiliwa na vijana wenzangu wa Kiliberia katika vita dhidi ya VVU,” Mahmud Johnson anaandika.

eng: He says you can’t separate Liberia’s economic problems from issues regarding sexual health.
swa: Anasema huwezi kutenganisha matatizo ya kiuchumi ya Liberia na masuala yanayohusu afya ya ngono.

eng: As the show’s outreach team usually traveled to leeward communities and villages to teach the youth there about HIV, I became aware, first hand, of the economic and traditional issues many people are faced with, and how those issues contribute to the spread of HIV in Liberia.
swa: Kama timu ya kivuko ya kipindi hicho kwa kawida hutembelea kwenye maeneo ya makondeni na vijiji kwa ajili ya kipindi kuwafundisha vijana kuhusu VVU, nimeelewa sasa, kwa uzoefu wangu wenyewe, kuhusu masuala ya kiuchumi na kiutamaduni wanayokabiliana nayo watu wengi, na namna masuala hayo yanayochangia kusambaza virusi vya UKIMWI nchini Liberia.

eng: I also became aware of some bizarre myths young people harbor on HIV spread and treatment.
swa: Nimeelewa pia imani potofu ambazo vijana wanazikumbatia kuhusu usambazaji virusi vya UKIMWI na matibabu yake.

eng: A very huge percentage of the youth population in Liberia has practically no knowledge about the transmission and prevention of HIV, and this phenomenon is due in no small part to the country’s spiralling illiteracy rate.
swa: Asilimia kubwa kabisa ya vijana nchini Liberia haina ufahamu kuhusu uambukizaji na kukabiliana na VVU, na dhana hii imetokana si kwa sehemu ndogo, na kiwango kinachotisha cha ujinga (wa kutokujua kusoma na kuandika.)

eng: Even the youth who go to school have minimal information about HIV, as such reproductive health issues are not taught in Liberian schools.
swa: Hata vijana wanaokwenda shule wana taarifa kidogo sana kuhusu VVU, kama mfano masuala ya afya ya uzazi hayafundishwi kabisa katika shule za Liberia.

eng: Hence, many myths abound amongst Liberian youth about HIV and other sexually transmitted infections, prominent amongst which is the myth that smoking pot prevents HIV infection.
swa: Matokeo yake, imani potofu zinawafunika vijana kuhusu VVU na magonjwa mengine yanayoenezwa kwa ngono, zaidi ni imani kwamba kuvuta bangi kunazuia maambuzi ya VVU.

eng: Because of these potentially dangerous myths, the radio show’s team developed a ‘Myths vs. Reality’ segment, in which (in colloquial Liberian language) we addressed several of those myths on a weekly basis.
swa: Kwa sababu ya imani hizi zenye hatari, kipindi cha redio kilianzisha sehemu ya “Imani zikipambanishwa na Ukweli wa mambo”, ambapo (katika lugha ya mtaani ya Kiliberia) tunazizungumzia imani hizo kwa mtindo wa kila wiki.

eng: The show offers a useful medium for young people to learn about the virus.
swa: Kipindi kinatoa nafasi muhimu kwa vijana kujifunza kuhusu virusi.

eng: And, of course, talk about sex.
swa: Na, bila ya shaka, kuzungumzia ngono.

eng: Today, the LTAS radio show is aired all over Liberia, and uses other reinforcement channels such as brochures, dramas, road shows, focus groups discussions, and peer training to spread the message about HIV transmission and pregnancy prevention.
swa: Leo, kipindi cha redio cha “Na tuzungumze kuhusu ngono” kinarushwa kote nchini Liberia, na kinatumia namna nyinginezo za kusisitiza kama vile vipeperushi, maigizo, maonyesho ya barabarani, majadilioano ya makundi lengwa, na elimu rika kusambaza ujumbe kuhusu maambukizi ya VVU na namna ya kuepuka mimba zisizotarajiwa.

eng: The show is so popular that the Liberian populace have even used the show to coin a joke in response to the recent shortage of chicken eggs on the Liberian market: chickens in Liberia now listen to ‘Let’s Talk About Sex!’ and practice safe sex!
swa: Kipindi hiki ni maarufu kiasi kwamba Walaiberia wengi hata wamekitumia kipindi kutania juu ya upungufu wa hivi karibuni wa wayai ya kuku katika masoko ya Liberia: Kuku wa Liberia sasa wanasikiliza kipindi cha “Na tuzungumze kuhusu Ngono!” na wanafanya ngono salama!

eng: I am aware of the reality that not every single youth in Liberia will heed the health messages disseminated on the show.
swa: Ninajua uhalisia kwamba si kila kijana nchini Liberia atafanyia kazi jumbe zinazotolewa kwenye kipindi.

eng: But even if one person’s life is changed in the process, that would a phenomenal success for me as a pioneer host on the LTAS show.
swa: Lakini hata kama maisha ya mtu mmoja tu yatabadilika katika mchakato huo, hilo litakuwa ni fanikio kwangu kama mtangazaji mhanga wa kipindi cha “Na tuzungumze kuhusu Ngono.”

swa: …moja ya wavuti mbaya zaidi nilizowahi kuziona.

swa: Iko taratibu sana, ina mambo mengi yasiyopangiliwa, na ina sura mbaya.

eng: ...as easy to navigate as a 1920’s Russian steam boat.
swa: …ni rahisi sana kuipitia kama ile boti ya moshi ya Kirusi ya miaka ya 1920.

eng: The Daily Star, Lebanon's only English paper, has been providing online news from Beirut for over a decade.
swa: The Daily Star, Jarida pekee la Kiingereza la Lebanon, limekuwa likitoa habari za mtandaoni kutoka Beirut kwa zaidi ya mwongo mmoja.

eng: Since its launch online, the paper has refused to upgrade its website, frustrating many of its readers.
swa: Tangu kuzinduliwa mtandaoni, gazeti limegoma kufanya wavuti hiyo iendane na wakati, ikiwachanganya wasomaji wake.

eng: The "ugly" Daily Star has prompted Lebanese bloggers to act, with an online campaign launched by creator of the Beirut Spring blog, Mustapha.
swa: Jarida ‘baya’ la Daily Star limewafanya wanablogu wa Kilebanoni kuchukua hatua, kwa kampeni ya mtadaoni iliyozinduliwa na mbunifu wa blogu ya Beirut Spring, Mustapha.

eng: Mustapha has cleverly created a mock Daily Star website - the Better Daily Star Project or #BDSP on Twitter - using WordPress functionality to highlight the incompetence of The Daily Star's IT and web design team.
swa: Mustapha ametengeneza kwa werevu wavuti ya kuigiza ya Daily Star- Mradi wa daily Star ulio bora zaidi au #BDSP kwenye twita –akitumia nyenzo ya WordPress kuonyesha uwezo duni wa timu ya Teknolojia ya Habari (TH) na wabunifu wa wavuti wa The daily Star.

eng: Although his actions might raise eyebrows at The Daily Star, Mustapha insists his intentions are positive:
swa: Ingawa alichokifanya kinaweza kuwafanya watu kufungua macho yao dhidi ya The daily Star, Mustapha anasisitiza kwamba nia yake ni chanya:

eng: -The aim of #BDSP is not to steal away viewers from The Daily Star's website.
swa: -Nia ya #BDSP si kuwaiba wasomaji wa wavuti ya The Daily Star.

eng: It's to regain back readers who have left them in frustration.
swa: Ni kuwarudisha wasomaji walioacha kuisoma kwa kukata tamaa.

eng: In fact, the DS should pay us to do this :)
swa: Kwa hakika, jarida hili lingepaswa kutulipa kwa kufanya hivi:)

eng: -This project is not meant in any way to hurt the reputation of the Daily Star.
swa: -Mradi huu haukukusudiwa kwa namna yoyote kuharibu sifa ya Daily Star.

eng: The point of this project is to try to steer the Daily Star's website away from what we believe is the wrong course
swa: Hoja ya mradi huu ni kujaribu kuielekeza tovuti ya daily Star kutoka kwenye kile tunachoamini ni mrengo usiosahihi.

eng: -When the Daily Star finally puts a better website in place, this project will no longer have to exist.
swa: -Wakati daily Star watakapoweka tovuti bora zaidi badala ya hii iliyopo, mradi huu hautakuwa na haja tena ya kuwepo.

eng: Our mission will be done.
swa: Lengo letu litakuwa limetimia.

eng: In fact, we will turn into their biggest cheerleaders
swa: Kwa hakika tutageuka kuwa mashabiki wakubwa wa mstari wa mbele.

eng: - We completely respect intellectual property rights.
swa: -Tunaheshimu kabisa haki miliki za kitaaluma.

eng: We never pretend that we own this stuff or that we wrote the articles, this is why this project strives to make the correct attributions to each and every article
swa: Hatujajidai kumiliki kitu hiki au kudai eti tuliandika makala. Hii ndio maana mradi huu unajitahidi kuweka majina ya sahihi ya wachangiaji kwa kila makala.

eng: Why am I doing it.
swa: Kwa nini nafanya hivi.

eng: What's the point?
swa: Suala ni nini?

eng: Well, I am trying to say this: If one guy (yours humbly) can use freely available opensource software (wordpress if you must know) to create this alternative, arguably better website in two weeks, why can't a newspaper with an actual IT department do it?
swa: Naam, ninajaribu kusema hivi: kama jamaa mmoja (wako mnyenyekevu) anaweza kutumia kwa uhuru programu zinazopatikana wazi (wordpress kama utataka kujua) ili kutengeneza mbadala huu, tena tovuti bora zaidi kuliko yao ndani ya majuma mawili, kwa nini gazeti hilo na Idara yao ya Teknolojia ya Habari wasifanye hivyo?

eng: In other words, I'm shooting down the argument that it would be too expensive to do.
swa: Kwa maneno mengine, ninamaliza majadiliano kwamba eti itakuwa ghali sana kufanya hivyo.

eng: Listen to me well: They're just being lazy.
swa: Nisikilizeni: Wamekuwa wavivu tu.

eng: But isn't this Illegal?
swa: Lakini je, hii si kinyume cha sheria?

eng: Probably.
swa: Inawezekana.

eng: But I'm not making any money out of it (in fact, I'm paying some in effort and hosting fees), and I promise that as soon as they do something about their site, I'll gladly bow out.
swa: Lakini sitengenezi fedha yoyote kwa njia hii (kwa hakika, ninalipa kiasi fulani katika jitihada na ada ya kutunziwa wavuti hii), na naahidi kwamba mara tu watakapofanya kitu kwa tovuti yao, nitajiondoa kwa furaha.

eng: Besides, it will cost them more to sue me than to actually fix their site and let me off their back.
swa: Hata hivyo, itawagharimu kunifungulia mashitaka mimi zaidi ya (gharama za) kurekebisha wavuti yao na kunifanya niondoke migongoni mwao.

eng: On Thursday, February 18th a coup took place in Niger in which President Mamadou Tandja was captured after a gun battle in the capital, Niamey, led by led by Col. Abdoulaye Adamou Harouna (who was was the former aide-de-camp of Niger's previous coup leader Maj. Daouda Mallam Wanke).
swa: Alhamisi Februari 18 mapinduzi ya kijeshi yalifanyika nchini Niger ambayo kwayo Rais Mamadou Tandja alikamatwa baada ya mapambano ya bunduki katika mji mkuu, Niamey, yaliyoongozwa na Kanali Abdoulaye Adamou Harouna (Amabaye alikuwa mpambe wa aliyekuwa kiongozi wa mapinduzi ya kijeshi yaliyopita Meja Daouda Mallam Wanke).

eng: In a quite unpoplar move, a few months ago Tandja illegally changed the constitution to allow him a third term in what was generally considered a mass fraud referendum (see Jen Brea's roundup on the reactions caused by that decision).
swa: Katika hatua ambayo haikupendwa, miezi michache iliyopita Tandja alibadilisha katiba kinyume cha sheria ili ajiruhusu kuongoza kwa muhula wa tatu katika kile ambacho kilionekana kama dhuluma ya halaiki kwenye kura maoni (angalia muhtasari wa Jen Brea kuhusu maoni yaliyosababishwa na uamuzi huo).

eng: For a few hours, confusion reigned about what was going on.

eng: Raffaella Toticchi in Niamey wrote on Thursday afternoon :
swa: Raffaella Toticchi aliyekuwa mjini Niamey aliandika siku ya Alhamisi mchana :

eng: First, about 7.8 million (3/5) of Niger's citizens experience severe or moderate food insecurity.

eng: Mass starvation is never a stabilizing force. Second, and more importantly, President Tandja had angered many Nigeriens in 2009 when he dissolved parliament and enacted constitutional reforms that gave him broad powers with few checks or balances.

eng: Tandja was constitutionally required to step down from office in December, as that was the end of his second five-year term in office, but the changes he made to the constitution allowed him to stay in office for three more years.
swa: Tandja alitakiwa na katiba kuondoka madarakani mwezi Disemba, kwani huo ndio ulikuwa mwisho wa muhula wake wa pili wa kipindi cha miaka mitano mitano madarakani, lakini mabadiliko aliyoyafanya kwenye katiba yalimruhusu akae kwenye madaraka kwa miaka mimgine mitatu.

eng: These moves were extremely unpopular; 10,000 protesters came out on Sunday to dispute Tandja's actions.
swa: Hatua hizo hazikupendwa kabisa; waandamanaji 10,000 walijitokeza Jumapili ili kupinga vitendo vya Tandja.

eng: Clearly, this coup is the result of the ongoing political crisis.
swa: Wazi, mapinduzi haya ya kijeshi ni matokeo ya mgogoro wa kisiasa unaoendelea.

swa: Kama ilivyowekwa na mtoa maoni wa Ki-Niger Ali Dan-Bouzoua katika mjadala kuhusu intaneti katika Niger, kwa bahati mbaya hakuna kiwango cha kutosha cha uanahabari wa kiraia unaoandika juu ya tukio hili:

swa: Hiki ndicho kinachotokea pale ambapo raia na taasisi za kiraia zinapokwa dhaifu mno, zinazoogopa sana, na zenye “maneno matupu,” katika kulinda uhuru wao kutoka kwa wanyakuaji wa madaraka wanaoitwa viongozi.

eng: This describes Nigeria perfectly: so, Nigeria is next in the coup movement: it is only logical and ripe.
swa: Hili linaielezea naijeria fika: kwa hiyo, Naijeria inafuata katika msululu huu wa mapinduzi; ni mantiki tu na mambo yameshaiva.

swa: Toyin Ade:

swa: Kama kutakuwa na mapinduzi yoyote ya kijeshi nchini naijeria, yanapaswa yalengwe kwa vikaragosi wasio na maana wanaojiita jiko/choo cha baraza la mawaziri la Yar’Ardua amabo wamejipatia yale ambayo hawana.

eng: While bleeding on the wedding night is still the proof of the bride's honor in Egypt and Middle Eastern countries, Radio Netherlands broadcast an Arabic translation of the Chinese advertisement of the Artificial Virginity Hymen kit.
swa: Wakati kuvuja damu kwenye usiku wa harusi bado ni ushahidi wa heshima ya bibi harusi nchini Misri na nchi za Mashariki ya Mbali, Radio Uholanzi imetangaza tafsiri ya Kiarabu ya tangazo la Kichina la Kifaa cha Ngozi nyembamba ya kutengenezwa yenye kurudisha ubikra wa mwanamke.

eng: Youm7 newspaper announced that the product will be available on the Egyptian market for LE 83.
swa: Gazeti la Youm7 lilitangaza kwamba bidhaa hiyo itapatikana kwenye soko la Misri kwa ajili ya LE 83.

eng: And as if Egyptian women were all waiting for the miracle hymen to embark on pre-marital sex, conservative parliament members want the product banned and any importer exiled or beheaded.
swa: Na kama vile wanawake wote wa Misri walikuwa wakiungoja muujiza huo wa bikra ya kutengeneza, wabunge wahafidhina wanataka bidhaa hiyo ipigwe marufuku na mwagizaji yoyete afukuzwe ama kukatwa kichwa.

eng: Egyptians began wondering if Egypt will start importing Chinese Hymens and Amira Al Tahawi, who used to work with Radio Netherlands at the time, got fired for blowing the whistle over the fabricated Chinese hymen story.
swa: Wamisri wameanza kujiuliza ikiwa Misri itaanza kuingiza ‘vijingozi hivyo vya bikra’ na Amira Al Tahawi, ambaye alikuwa akifanya kazi na Radio Uholanzi kwa wakati huu, alifukuzwa kazi kwa kupuliza kipenga dhidi ya habari hiyo ya ‘bikra ya Kichina.’

eng: On her blog Amira Al Tahawi wrote: Yes!
swa: Katika blogu yake Amira Al Tahawi aliandika: Ndio!

eng: I was fired over a blog post I published last December!
swa: Nilifukuzwa kazi kwa ajili ya posti ya blogu yangu niliyoiweka mwezi Desemba!

eng: On 26 January, 2010, I received a termination letter putting an end to my job as a Cairo correspondent for Radio Netherlands.
swa: Tarehe 26 Januari, 2010, nilipokea barua ya kusitiza ajira yangu kuhitimisha kazi yangu kama mwandishi wa Kairo wa Radio Uholanzi.

eng: In my post I proved that that station published false unverified information on 22 August, 2009, regarding the penetration of the Chinese "Artificial Hymen" in the Arab world.
swa: Katika posti yangu nilionyesha kwamba kituo hicho kilikuwa kimetangaza habari za uongo zisizodhibitishwa tarehe 22 Agosti, 2009 kuhusu kuingizwa kwa ‘Bikra za kichina’ katika nchi za kiarabu.

eng: The information broadcast on the Radio said that the fake hymen is manufactured specially for Arab and Muslim women ignoring the fact that the product has been available in Japan since 1993 and it was not specially produced by the Chinese who realized the schizophrenic condition of Arab women who need to fake their virginity.
swa: Kutangazwa kwa taarifa hiyo kwenye redio ilidai kwamba bikra hiyo bandia ilikuwa imetengenezwa maalumu kwa ajili ya wanawake wa Kiarabu na Waislamu ikipuuza ukweli kwamba bidhaa hiyo imekuwapo Japan tangu mwaka 1993 na haikuwa imetengenezwa maalumu na Wachina waliogundua ugonjwa wa akili wa wanawake wa Kiarabu wanaohitaji kudanganya kuhusu ubikra wao.

eng: I asked the station to correct the factual errors with that piece of fabricated news in an email dated 14 September.
swa: Nilikiomba kituo hicho cha redio kurekebisha makosa hayo ya kiuhalisia kwa habari hiyo ya kutengeneza kwa njia ya barua pepe ya tarehe 14 Septemba.

eng: My request fell on deaf ears and many Egyptian news portals further spread the lie without bothering to investigate the facts or the sources quoted.
swa: Maombi yangu yaliangukia kwenye masikio yasiyosikia na watunza habari wa mtandaoni wa Kimisri walisambaza zaidi uongo huo bila kujali kuchunguza ukweli au kunukuu chanzo cha habari.

eng: Many bloggers found the decision to fire her ridiculous and unjustified; Nawara Negm wondered: عايزين نصيح لها بقى يا شباب Why are they firing her?
swa: Wanablogu wengi wameuona uamuzi huo wa kumfukuza kazi kama wa kijinga na usiweza kuhalalishwa; Nawara Negm alijiuliza: Kwa nini wanamfukuza kazi?

eng: She did not write anything offensive about Radio Netherlands.
swa: Hakuandika chochote kwa madhumuni ya kuishambulia Redio Uholanzi.

eng: Anyway, She is suing them ... let's give her a hand guys!
swa: Anawashtaki...hebu na tumwonge mkono jamani!

eng: Eman Hashim is lamenting the integrity of journalism; she wrote: و كل ده عشان قالت لأة
swa: Eman Hashim analalamikia uadilifu wa uandishi wa habari; anaandika:

eng: Amira got fired and is being denied her financial and moral rights because she said NO!
swa: Amira amefukuzwa kazi na amenyimwa haki zake za fedha na maadili kwa sababu alisema HAPANA!

eng: Amira wrote the details on her blog so let's give her a louder voice and let everyone know the truth.
swa: Amira aliandika kwa kina kwenye blogu yake kwa hiyo hebu na tumpe sauti kubwa zaidi ili kila mtu aujue ukweli.

eng: We blame the silent for their silence but we owe those who have a voice a microphone.
swa: Tunawalaumu wakimya kwa ukimya wao lakini tunawadai wale wenye sauti kwenye kipaza sauti.

eng: Is that how Radio Netherlands deal with false news?
swa: Je, hivyo ndivyo Radio Uholanzni wanashughulikia habari za uongo?

eng: Where is their integrity?
swa: Uko wapi uadilifu wao?

eng: Where is their respect to their readers and listeners?
swa: Iko wapi heshima yao kwa wasomaji na wasikilizaji wao?

eng: They could have easily published a correction or anything ... anything at all.
swa: Wangeweza kirahisi tu kutangaza marekebisho au jambo fulani...chochote kile.

eng: The fact that they did not publish a clarification or a verification of any sort is sad but firing an honest journalist for exposing fallacies is a practical joke.
swa: Ukweli kwamba hawakutangaza ufafanuzi au uthibitisho wa lolote katika hili unasikitisha lakini kumfukuza kazi mwandishi mwaminifu kwa kuibua mkanganyiko wa hoja ni kitendo cha mzaha.

eng: Dr. Mostafa El Nagaar wrote in Amira's defense saying: Amira is now suffering the dire consequences of her professionalism and nobility.
swa: Dkt. Mostafa El Nagaar aliandika katika utetezi wa Amira akisema: Amira sasa anaathirika na matokeo ya utaaluma na uthamani wake.

eng: She is paying the high price for ethical journalism.
swa: Analipia gharama kubwa sana kwa uandishi wenye maadili.

eng: She needs someone to defend her the way she defended Egyptian girls when imposters claimed that they are waiting for the fake hymen to cover up for their immorality.
swa: Anahitaji mtu kumtetea kwa namna alivyowatetea wasichana wa Kimisri wakati waongo walipodai kwamba wanasubiri kudanganya kuhusu ubikra wao ili kufunika ukosefu wao wa kimaadili.

eng: I urge every Egyptian woman to return the favor and defend Amira who lost her job.
swa: Ninatoa wito kwa kila mwanamke Mmisri kurudishia fadhila kwa kumtetea Amira aliyepoteza kazi.

eng: I am asking all Women's Rights organizations to show their solidarity with Amira.
swa: Ninayaomba mashirika yote ya Haki za Wanawake kuonyesha mshikamano wao na Amira.

eng: We officially ask for a clear apology from those who tarnished our reputation and I am asking all those who speak in the name of honor to show their support.
swa: Tunaomba rasmi tamko lililo wazi la kuomba msamaha kutoka kwa wale waliotupaka matope na ninawaomba wote wanaozungumza kwa jina la heshima kuonyesha ushirikiano wao.

eng: Mostafa Fathi also posted a note on Facebook and Karim El Beheiry published a post on his blog in solidarity with Amira.
swa: Mostafa Fathi pia aliweka makala yake kwenye Facebook na Karim El Beheiry akaiweka posti hiyo kwenye blogu yake kushikamana na Amira.

eng: In October 2009, Mohamed Al Rahal ordered a hymen kit and posted photos in his blog, as noted in a previous Global Voices story.
swa: Mwezi Oktoba 2009, Mohamed Al Rfahal aliagiza kikabrasha chenye bikra hiyo na kuweka picha kwenye blogu, kama ilivyoonekana kwenye habari zilizopita za Global Voices.

eng: The Egyptian football team beat Ghana in the African Cup of Nations' final match, and achieved its third consecutive championship.
swa: Timu ya kandanda ya Misri iliifunga Ghana katika fainali ya Kombe la Mataifa ya Afrika, na ikapata ushindi wake kwa mara ya tatu mfululizo.

eng: This is also Egypt's seventh championship since the launch of the tournament in the 50's.
swa: Huu pia ni ushindi wa saba tangu kuanzishwa kwa mashindano hayo kwenye miaka ya hamsini.

eng: Bloggers join the rest of the country in celebrating the achievement.
swa: Wanablogu wanaungana na wananchi wa nchi hiyo kusherehekea mafanikio hayo.

eng: Zeinobia wrote here about the Egyptian victory saying: We played a good game against Ghana, and at the end fate made Gedo the reason of making nearly 80 million Egyptian happy around the globe, uniting them in a very rare occasion regardless of its psychological meaning or political meaning or whatever.
swa: Zeinobia aliandika hapa kuhusu ushindi huo kwa Misri akisema: Tulicheza mchezo mzuri dhidi ya Ghana, na mwishowe Gedo akawa sababu ya kuwafanya karibu ya Wamisri milioni 80 kufurahi duniani kote, akawaunganisha pamoja katika wakati huo adimu bila kujali maana yake ya kisaikolojia au maana ya kisiasa au vyovyote.

eng: Coach Hassan Shehata is insisting to become one of the best coaches not only in Egypt's football history but also in Africa's football history.
swa: Kocha Hassan Shehata anasisitiza kuwa mmoja wa Makocha wazuri zaidi sio tu kwenye historia ya kandanda la Misri, lakini pia katika historia ya Afrika.

eng: This man managed to make something great from our national team for real.
swa: Mtu huyu ameweza kufanya jambo kubwa kutokana na timu yetu kwa hakika.

eng: His discovery Mohamed Nagi aka Gedo. Ahmed Hassan was fantastic.
swa: Kumgundua yeye Mohamedi Nagi ama kwa jina jingine Gedo Ahmed Hassan ilikuwa ni ajabu sana.

eng: All of the players were great.
swa: Wachezaji wote walikuwa vizuri sana.

eng: The victory wasn't only celebrated here in Egypt.
swa: Ushindi haukusherehekewa tu hapa Misri.

eng: In Qatar, Qatar Living wrote here about the victory, and the expected sleepless night in Doha: Egypt beats Ghana 1-0 to earn African Cup title..
swa: Huko Qatar, Qatar Living aliandika hapa kuhusu ushindi huo, na akategemea watu kukesha usiku kucha huko Doha: Misri imeichapa Ghana 1-0 kujivika taji la Kombe la Afrika...

eng: Mod Note : It's going to be a noisy night in Doha!
swa: Mod anaandika: Itakuwa ni usiku wa kelele nyingi mjini Doha!

eng: Congratulations to all the Egyptians in Qatar!
swa: Hongera kwa Wamisri wote waishio Qatar!

eng: An Egyptian blogger living in USA, Egyptian Wish, wrote a new post here saying: Dear Egyptians,
swa: Mwanablogu wa Misri aishiye Marekani, Egyptian Wish, aliandika kwenye posti yake mpya hapa akisema:

eng: Congratulations for CAN2010!
swa: Hongereni sana kwa Kombe la Mataifa ya Afrika 2010!

eng: Egyptian-in-USA
swa: Mmisri aliye Marekani

eng: Also in Palestine, Hamas didn't miss the opportunity, and congratulated the Egyptians on their seventh Championship.
swa: Pia nchini Palestina, Hamas hawakuiacha fursa hiyo ipite, na kuwapongeza Wamisri kwa Ushindi wao huo wa saba.

eng: Kelmety wrote about it here: Hamas has congratulated the Egyptian president, government, and people on their winning their seventh African Cup of Nations, and their third consecutive championship.
swa: Kelmety aliandika kuhusu hilo hapa:

eng: Zeinobia wrote another post here, about the Egyptian president's sons, who went to Angola to support the Egyptian football team: I believe that the photos of the Mubarak brothers should have its own post.
swa: Ninaamini kwamba picha za vijana wa Mubarak inabidi ziwe na posti yake ya kujitegemea.

eng: As I hinted before the brothers went to Angola to watch the final match between Egypt and Ghana.
swa: Kama nilivyogusia hapo awali, hawa vijana walienda Angola kutazama mechi ya Fainali kati ya Misri na Ghana.

eng: Some people will see it as political publicity stunt , others knowing how crazy the brothers about football.
swa: Watu wengine wanaweza kulichukulia hili kama suala la kisiasa la kutafuta umaarufu, wengine wakijua jinsi vijana hawa walivyo na ‘ulevi’ wa mpira.

eng: Another blogger, My Oblivia, had a different point of view here: Therefore, will someone please bother explaining how can one lousy tournament make us cheer for the same country where this happens…
swa: Mwanablogu mwingine, My Oblivia, alikuwa na mtazamo tofauti hapa: Kwa hiyo, je kuna mtu atakayeweza kujisumbua tafadhali kueleza ni namna gani shindano moja la kizembe linatufanya kuishangilia nchi hiyo hiyo ambako haya yaafanyika...

eng: In this country people die of hunger, they die of torture, they simply die because they don’t have half the basic humane standards of living and medical attention, let alone awareness…
swa: Katika nchi hii watu wanakufa kwa njaa, wanakufa kwa kuteswa, wanakufa tu kwa sababu hawana hata nusu ya mahitaji ya misingi kwa ajili ya kuishi na hawana huduma za matibabu, acha ile tu kujua kama wanahitaji...

eng: So God did not want us to win our daily battles of mere survival, instead, He destined us for winning a soccer game, and entire tournament, hallelujah, we’re saved!
swa: Kwa Mungu hakutaka sisi tushinde vita vyetu vya kila siku vya kule tu kubaki hai, badala yake, Ametupangia kushinda mpambano wa kandanda, ana mashindano yote, haleluya, tumeokolewa!

eng: So, this is our destined victory, in soccer…
swa: Kwa hivyo, huu ni ushindi wetu tuliopangiwa, kwenye kandanda...

eng: And now, all out other problems are solved and we are eternally blessed!
swa: Na sasa, matatizo tyote mengine yametatuliwa na tumebarikiwa milele!

eng: And finally, the Egyptian national team usually adds a new star on their jersey every time they win the African Cup of Nations.
swa: Na hatimaye, timu ya kandanda ya Wamisri mara nyingi humwongeza nyota mwingine kwenye jezi zao kila mara wanaposhinda Kombe la Mataifa Ya Afrika.

eng: But there is one problem here: where will we put all those stars on our national team's jerseys now that we have won our seventh championship.
swa: Lakini Adel Ghaly alikuwa akijiuliza hapa kama tuna nafasi imebaki kwa ajili ya nyota mwingine:

eng: Yar'Adua's absence created a leadership vacuum which frustrated many Nigerians, particularly in the wake of crises such as Umar Abdulmutallab's attempted terror attract and the religious conflict in the central Nigerian city of Jos.
swa: Kutokuwepo kwa Yar’Adua kulisababisha ombwe la kiuongozi ambalo liliwasumbua Wanaijeria wengi, hasa wakati ambao matatizo yalijitokeza kama pale Umar Abdulmutallab alipofanya jaribio la ugaidi na mgogoro wa kidini katika mji wa katikati ya Naijeria wa Jos.

eng: Many Nigerians called for Vice-President Goodluck Jonathan to step into Yar'Adua's shoes, but the situation was complex: As a southerner, Jonathan's assumption of the Presidency would threaten to destabilize the delicate power-sharing arrangement between Northern and Southern Nigeria.
swa: Wanaijeria wengi walitoa wito kwa Makamu wa rais Goodluck Jonathan kuvaa viatu vya Yar’Adua, lakini hali ilikuwa tata: Kama mtu anayetoka Kusini, kukaimu madaraka ya Urais kwa Jonathan kungehatarisha kudhoofishwa kwa mpango wa kuachiana madaraka kati ya maeneo ya Kaskazini na Kusini mwa Naijera.

eng: Further, without written instructions from the President himself, the legal extent of Jonathan's position were unclear.
swa: Zaidi, bila maelekezo ya kiamandishi kutoka kwa Rais yeye mwenyewe, uhalali wa nafasi ya Jonathani kisheria ungekuwa haueleweki vyema.

eng: For more than two months Nigerian bloggers lamented the leadership void.
swa: Kwa zaidi ya miezi miwili wanablogu wa Najieria walilalamikia pengo hili la kiungozi.

eng: Chinedu Vincent Akuta at Briefs from Akuta wrote:
swa: Chinedu Vincent Akuta kwenye Briefs from Akuta aliandika:

eng: Enough of power vacuum, near constitutional crisis, and over heating of the polity all due to the fact that the ruling party (PDP) does not trust the Vice President (Jonathan Goodluck) to formally act as President until President Yar’Adua recovers from his illness.
swa: Ombwe la kimadaraka limetosha sasa, karibu na mgogoro wa kikatiba, na kuchemka kwa machakato wa kiserikali yote yalikuwa ni kwa sababu chama tawala (PDP) hakimwamini Makamu wa Rais (Janathan Goodluck) kukaimu rasmi Urais mpaka Rais Yar’Adua atakapopona ugonjwa wake.

eng: There is no choice other than to respect the wishes of the Nigerian people, power belongs to the people.
swa: Hakuna uamuzi mwingine zaidi ya kuheshimu matakwa ya watu wa Naijeria, nguvu ni ya watu wenyewe.

eng: And indeed, many Nigerians shared his sentiments.
swa: Na kwa hakika, Wanaijeria wengi walikuwa na maoni kama yake.

eng: During the month of January frustrated Nigerians marched in Lagos, Abuja, and London.
swa: Wakati wote wa mwezi wa Januari Wanaijeria waliochanganyikiwa (na hali hiyo) waliandamana kwenye miji ya Lagos, Abuja na London.

eng: Adeolu Akinyemi wrote on why he marched:
swa: Adeolu Akinyemi aliandika juu ya kwa nini waliandamana:

eng: We are not happy with a Plane load of 300 people dying in the streets of Jos in Religious wars because of inaction from a missing leader.
swa: Hatuna furaha na watu 300 kufa kwenye mitaa ya Jos kwenye vita vya kidini kwa sababu ya kutokuwepo hatua zinazochukuliwa kwa sababu tu hakuna kiongozi.

eng: Enough is Enough!
swa: Imetosha sasa basi!

eng: We will not accept the label of terrorism bestowed on us by the 58 days inactivity of our president’s mobile phone.
swa: Hatutakubali kubandikwa alama ya ugaidi kwa sababu ya siku 58 za kutokufanya kazi kwa simu ya kiganjani ya Rais.

eng: Enough is Enough!
swa: Imetosha sasa basi!

eng: Leadership Vacuum is dangerous and is responsible for killings in the north, kidnapping in the east, Militants gang raping in the South South and intellectual indifference in the west.
swa: Ombwe la uongozi ni hatari na linawajibika kwa mauaji ya eneo la kaskazini, utekaji nyara mashariki ya nchi, magenge ya wanajeshi kubaka watu kusini mwa nchi na tofauti za kiufahamu zilizoko magharibi.

eng: Enough is Enough!
swa: Imetosha sasa basi!

eng: Yusef, a commenter on Akinyemi's blog, was more skeptical (edited from the original English version):
swa: Yusef, mtoa maoni kwenye blogu ya Akinyemi, alikuwa si mtu rahisi kuamini (imehaririwa kutoka kwenye toleo halisi la kiiingereza):

eng: How many times will I read this celebrated line "Enough is Enough"?????
swa: Mara ngapi nitasoma mstari huu maarufu “Imetosha sasa basi”?????

eng: It's very strange how we display so much hypocrisy when faced with some adversity and yet are able to make very sharp u-turns once the weather is stormed.
swa: Ni ajabu namna tunayoonyesha unafiki wa hali ya juu tunapokabiliwa na hali ngumu na bado tukawa na uwezo wa kugeuka mara moja hali ya hewa inapoharibika.

eng: If I call on anyone to do what will be absolutely necessary to get our system working, how will I be 100% sure that being a northerner, he will not change his mind once he gets some sense spoken to him by his kinsman... Or being a Muslim and he being of another faith, wont see me in the deep recesses of his heart, as being an enemy.
swa: Kama nitamwomba yeyote kufanya kile kitakachokuwa muhimu sana kuufanya mfumo wetu ufanye kazi, nitakuwaje na uhakika wa asilimia mia kwamba ninayenatokea kaskazini, hatabadili akili yake mara moja anaposikia suala lenye mantiki limesemwa kwake na mtu wa kabila lake…Au kwamba kwa kuwa Mwislamu na yeye kuwa wa imani nyingine, hataniona kutokea kwenye kilindi cha moyo wake, kwa kule kuwa adui.

eng: There is no such thing as "Enough is Enough" Deolu.
swa: Hakuna kitu kama “Imetosha sasa basi!”

eng: We do not know what a nation is yet, not to even talk of kinsmanship.
swa: Hatujui maana ya taifa bado, bila hata kuzungumzia undugu.

eng: It's not enough to brandish posters of Ernesto Che on our walls to pretend to imagine or understand what it takes to lay down ABSOLUTELY everything for a better day.
swa: Haitoshi kubandika mabango ya Ernesto Che kwenye kuta zake ukadhania kutafakari ama kuelewa kile kinachostahili kufanywa ili kuachana na yote ili kuwa na siku njema.

eng: We do not know this adversity . . . or we are too selfish hoping that "one day e go better for our side"! ! ! !
swa: Hatuijui hali hii ngumu…au tu wabinafsi sana kiasi cha kudhania kwamba “siku moja kila kitu kitakwenda vyema kwa upande wetu”!!!!

eng: Our so-called leaders did not drop from Hell, but are actually just a reflection of our society.
swa: Hawa wanaoitwa viongozi wetu hawakushuka kutoka kuzimu, lakini wanaakisi jamii yetu.

eng: Replace with even yourself and you will be surprised at what you will do or become.
swa: Chukua nafasi yao hata wewe mwenyewe na utashangazwa na kile ambacho ungefanya au ungekuwa.

eng: Popular broadcast journalist Funmi Ayanda also wrote about her frustration with the prevalence passive hand-wringing:
swa: Mwandishi Maarufu wa utangazaji Funni Ayanda pia aliandika kuhusu mkanganyiko wa hali iliyopo ya kuvutana mikono kimya kimya:

eng: I have sat in the company of bank MDs who stole billions of money, ruling party leaders who manipulate the electoral process and steal billions on naira, pastors of un taxed mega churches where all the above pay staggering sums in tithes and contribution and listened in disbelief as they all moan about bad leadership and the Nigerian situation.
swa: Nimekaa kati ya Wakurugenzi Waendeshaji wa benki waliokwapua mabilioni ya fedha, viongozi wa chama tawala wanaoharibu michakacho ya uchaguzi na kuiba maibilioni ya naira, wachungaji wa makanisa mkubwa yasiyotozwa kodi ambako wote hapo juu wanalipa kiasi kikubwa sana cha mafungu ya sadaka na michango na kusikiliza bila kuamini namna wote hao wanavyolalamika kuhusu uongozi mbaya na hali ya Naijeria.

eng: I have often mentally checked my teeth for visible spinach; perhaps the joke is on me?
swa: Nimeangalia mara nyingi kwa tafakuri kwenye meno yangu kama kuna mabaki ya mboga za majani; labda nafanyiwa utani mimi mwenyewe?

eng: So make l for no crase finish l ask simple questions like, “so what do you think we should do” what is within our own control immediately and how do we build on that?
swa: Kwa hiyo sitaki kuhitimisha kwa kukakakaka ninauliza maswali rahisi kama vile, “kwa hiyo unafikiri tufanyeje” kile kilichopo kwenye uwezo wetu na kwa namna gani tutaweza kuendeleza kutokea hapo?

eng: “What will my role be in that”?
swa: “Nafasi yangu itakuwa nini kwenye hilo?”

eng: Usually, the conversation goes no further because l sometimes think both Nigerians and foreigners have a morbid fascination with Nigeria’s undeniable failures.
swa: Mara nyingi, mazungumzo huwa hayafiki mbali kwa sababu mara nyingine mimi hufikiri Wanaijeria na watu wa mataifa ya nje wana mvuto wa huzuni katika na kushindwa kwa Naijeria ambako hakuwezi kukanwa.

eng: On February 9th, after weeks of political wrangling, the Senate confirmed Jonathan as acting President.
swa: Tarehe 9 Februari, baada ya majuma kadhaa ya mivutano ya siasa, Baraza la Seneti lilimthibitisha Jonathan kama kaimu Rais.

eng: Many in the blogosphere saw the event as cause for celebration.
swa: Wanablogu wengi wameliona tukio hilo kama sababu ya kusherehekea.

eng: Solomonsydelle of Nigerian Curiosity provided an excellent analysis of the situation as it unfolded (See here for her coverage).
swa: Solomonsydelle wa Nigeria Curiosity alitoa uchambuzi mzuri sana wa hali ya mambo kama ilivyojionyesha (angalia hapa kwa alichokiandika).

eng: She wrote:
swa: Aliandika:

eng: February 9th could possibly go down in history as a day when democratic political measures where used to take Nigeria one step further down the path to becoming a true democratic nation.
swa: Februari 9 ingeweza kwenda kwenye historia kama siku ambapo hatua za kidemorasia za kisiasa zilichukuliwa kuifanya Naijeria kupiga hatua moja bele kuelekea kwenye njia ya kufanyika taifa la kidemokrasia ya kweli.

eng: Akin, too, was guardedly hopeful:
swa: Akin, pia, alikuwa na matumaini yenye masharti:

eng: Maybe and just maybe, we might just have a good President and the good luck in his name brings good fortune to Nigeria, maybe, we can hope, maybe, we can dream, maybe, we can expect, maybe, we can realise – A New Nigeria.
swa: Labda na labda tu, tunaweza kuwa na Rais mwema na bahati njema kwenye jina lake litaleta bahati njema kwa Naijeria, labda, tunaweza kutumaini, labda, tunaweza kuota, labda, tunaweza kutegemea, labda, tunaweza kuipata –Naijeria mpya.

eng: But others saw reason for concern, pointing out that although Jonathan's assumption of power might be a political necessity, it was not explicitly permitted by the Nigerian Constitution.
swa: Lakini wengine wanaona sababu ya kuangalia, wakionyesha kwamba ingawa kukaimu madaraka kulikofanywa na Jonathan kunaweza kuwa na umuhimu wa siasa, haikuwa imeruhusiwa moja kwa moja na Katiba ya Naijeria.

eng: Max Siollun summed up the predicament as follows:
swa: Max Siollum alijumuisha hali hiyo mbaya kama ifuatavyo:

eng: Jonathan’s confirmation as VP will hopefully put an end to the controversy (at least temporarily), and will give the leadership some semblance of order and due process.
swa: Kuthibitishwa kwa Jonathani kama Makamu wa Rais kunaweza kumaliza utata (angalau kwa muda), na kutaupa uongozi namna fulani ya uwepo kwa taratibu na michakacho inayokubalika.

eng: While we have arrived at a PRACTICAL solution, I am not sure that the manner and circumstances in which Jonathan was appointed acting VP was LEGAL.
swa: Wakati tumefikia kwenye suluhisho la KIHALISIA, sina uhakika kama suala hili na hali ya mambo iliyomteua Jonathan kuwa Makamu wa Rais ilikuwa kwa MUJIBU WA SHERIA.

eng: Jide Salu acknowledged the constitutional ambiguity, but was primarily thankful that the country finally has a leader.
swa: Jide Salu anakiri kuwepo kwa utata wa kikatiba, lakini kimsingi alikuwa na shukrani kwamba nchi hatimaye ina mtawala.

eng: I just want some peace and direction.
swa: Ninahitaji amani na mwelekeo.

eng: If you were residing in the country, you would understand better.
swa: Kama ulikuwa unakaa nchini, ungeweza kuelewa zaidi.

eng: Nigeria was not only headless, it was directionless with all the looting that has gone on and still going.
swa: Naijeria si tu kuwa haikuwa na kiongozi, ilikuwa bila uelekeo pamoja na mitikisiko yote iliyopitia na inayoipitia.

eng: Which for now is under wraps.
swa: Ambayo kwa sasa iko chini ya mfuniko.

eng: Ana Nimmos was optimistic, but also saw cause for concern:
swa: Ana Nimmos alikuwa na matumaini, lakini aliona sababu ya kuangalia:

eng: may not be the actual end of this logjam as it presents its own challenges.
swa: hauwezi kuwa mwisho wa kukingana kwa magogo kama kunavyoonyesha changamoto zake.

eng: For instance, by this resolution - if we accept it for arguments sake - Nigeria now has two Presidents -though one is acting.
swa: Kwa mfano, kwa utatuzi huu –kama tutaukubali kwa sababu ya majadiliano –Naijeria kwa sasa inayo marais wawili –japokuwa mmoja ndiye anayefanya kazi.

eng: Yar'adua never left power and Goodluck should be very careful what actions he takes.
swa: Yar’adua hajawahi kuacha madaraka na Goodluck itabidi awe makini na hatua anazozichukua.

eng: Loomnie also highlighted unanswered questions for the future:
swa: Loomnie pia aliyaonyesha maswali yasiyo na majibu kwa mustakabali (wa nchi hiyo):

eng: One also has to think about the machine that was ruling the country all the while Yar’Adua was not available.
swa: Mtu lazima afikiri kuhusu mashine ambayo ilikuwa inatawala nchi mara tu baada ya Yar’dua kutokuwepo.

eng: Is the new President Goodluck Jonathan going to be able to take charge of the machine?
swa: Je, Rais mpya Goodluck Jonathan ataweza kuwa na uwezo kuishughulikia mashine hiyo?

eng: Is he going to be deferring to it/them?
swa: Je, ataweza kuiweka pembeni/nazo?

eng: Those are going to be crucial questions in the next few months.
swa: Hayo ni maswali ya msingi katika kipindi cha miezi kadhaa ijayo.

eng: This week we will take a random walk around different blogs, and different topics in a maze that is little different than the random markets of Aleppo.
swa: Juma hili, bila utaratibu maalum, tutafanya ziara ya kutembea kwenye blogu mbalimbali, na mada anuai katika mchanganyiko wa tofauti kidogo na masoko holela ya Aleppo.

eng: We leave Hanzala to ponder the derelict state of Syria's public sector and his decision to quit, and we move to a little more joyful topic. As with every Friday, the blogosphere was blessed with the new installment of Abufares and Mariyah's Sea Side collaborative story. In Part 29, you'll read:
swa: Kituo chetu cha kwanza kitakuwa kwenye Mwondoko wa Hanzala kwenda kwa Mungu, ambako anaandika kuhusu uamuzi wake wa kuacha kazi:

eng: Yasmina sat down on the couch behind me.
swa: Yasmina aliakaa kwenye kochi nyuma yangu.

eng: Obviously she had seen way beyond the sexy smile.”Oh, Houssam.
swa: Dhahiri alikuwa na mvuto zaidi ya tabasamu ya kimapenzi. “Ah, Houssam.

eng: Oh god, Houssam.”
swa: Uh mungu wangu, Houssam.”

eng: She couldn’t hold back her tears and as she cried her heart out again, I knew that I couldn’t let her down.
swa: Hakuweza kuzuia machozi yake na kadri aliavyouliza moyo wake, nilijua nisingeweza kumwangusha.

eng: I would just have to hope that Youssef would forgive me…someday.
swa: Ningepaswa tu kutumaini kuwa Youssef angenisamehe...siku moja.

eng: “We’ll go in the morning, Yasmina.
swa: “Tutaenda asubuhi, Yasmina.

eng: I’ll be here early.
swa: Nitakuwa hapa mapema.

eng: Ok?”
swa: Sawa eh?”

eng: I said as soothingly as I could.
swa: Nilisema kwa upole kama nilivyoweza.

eng: And on the topic of love and Valentines, Untold Damascene Stories, the blog of FW Magazine, publishes a report about the commercialization of Valentine's Day on the streets of Damascus:
swa: Na kwenye mada ya mapenzi na Valentini, Untold Damascene Stories, blogu ya jarida la FW, linachapisha taarifa kuhusu kukua kwa u-biashara wa siku ya wapendanao kwenye mitaa ya Dameski:

eng: For Syrians, who also aren’t safe from the hands of commercialism, the rituals of valentine start a month before Feb the 14th.
swa: Kwa Wasyria, ambao hawako salama dhidi ya mikono ya mfumo wa biashara, desturi za siku ya Valentino huanza mwezi mmoja kabla ya tarehe 14 Februari.

eng: Guys start calling their friends to ask for money; No “man” wants to be caught penniless in front of their girl friends on Valentine’s.
swa: Jamaa wanaanza kuwapigia rafiki zao kuwaomba fedha; Hakuna mtu anataka kuonekana hana fedha mbele ya rafiki wa kike kwenye siku ya wapendanao.

eng: Restaurants start preparations with decorations and special offers “For Families Only,” “No single men allowed.” 50 liras red roses magically gain an extra zero, turning to 500 liras.
swa: Migahawa huanza matayarisho kwa kuweka mapambo na ofa maalumu “Kwa Familia Pekee,” “Hakuna kapera anaruhusiwa.” Maua ya waridi yauzwayo lira 50 ghafla kimiujiza yanaongezwa sifuri mwishoni na kuwa kueguka kuwa lira 500.

eng: And finally, cell phone companies start spamming their customers with bulk messages, such as: “Send a message to #### with your partner’s name to join the ‘Lover’s Day competition’ or to ‘test your compatibility.’”
swa: Na mwishowe, makampuni ya simu huanza kuwatumia wateja wake meseji nyingi, kama vile: “Tuma ujumbe kwenda #### ikiwa na jina la mwenzi wako ili kushiriki ‘Mashindano ya Siku ya Wapendanao’ au ‘kuangalia kama mnafanana kihaiba.”

eng: Politics is also a featured staple in any conversation, and Syria Comment brings us the latest updates and analysis from around Syria and the world, with the provocative headline of "Has Washington Decided to Focus on Syrian-Israeli Peace?":
swa: Siasa pia ni chakula kikuu katika mazungumzo yoyote, na blogu ya Syria Comment inatuletea taarifa za hivi karibuni na uchambuzi wake kutoka Syria na duniani kote, zikiwa na kichwa kinachofikirisha cha ‘Je, Washington imeamua kutilia mkazo suala la amani ya Syria na Waisraili?’:

eng: In short, the return of an ambassador is good, but playing along with a peace process that is long on process and short on peace will be difficult for Syria, which has none of the media savvy that Israel has.
swa: Kwa kifupi, kurudi kwa balozi ni habari njema, lakini kuchezea mpango wa kutafuta amani ambao ni mrefu kimchakato na mfupi kiamani utakuwa mgumu kwa Syria, ambayo haina vyombo vya habari vyerevu kama ilivyonavyo Israili.

eng: Damascus undoubtedly fears that Mitchell will ask Syrians to meet with Netanyahu without conditions.
swa: Dameski bila shaka inahofia kwamba Mitchell atawataka Wasyria kukutana na Netanyahu bila masharti.

eng: Syria believes this is tantamount to normalizing relations without any Israeli concession.
swa: Syria inaamini hii ni sawa na kurejesha mahusiano bila ya Waisraeli kulipia chochote.

eng: And finally, we'll sit down with Syrian Foodie in London, and finish our tour with a delicious Damascene treat, Ful Nabit:
swa: Na mwishowe, tutakaa kitako na Syrian Foodie in London, na kumaliza ziara yetu kwa chakula kitamu cha Damascene, Ful Nabit:

eng: Ful Nabit is boiled fava beans served with salt and cumin.
swa: Ful Nabit ni maharage yaliyochemshwa na chumvi na mdalasini.

eng: The seller cart will have huge pot with the beans slowly simmering.
swa: Muuzaji huwa na surufia kubwa lenye maharage lenye kupashwa moto taratibu.

eng: The beans are served in a proper glass or china bowls rather than paper wrap or a plastic plate, which I find adds a nice touch. to the experience.
swa: Maharage hupakuliwa katika bilauri au bakuli za kauri badala ya sahani za karatasi au za plasiti, ambazo mie huona zinaongeza mwonjo katika zoezi zima.

eng: You usually get a glass of the cooking stock and half a lemon to accompany your ful.
swa: Kwa kawaida unapata bilauri ya mchuzi na nusu ndimu kusindikiza mlo wako.

eng: The cooking stock flavoured with salt, cumin and a squeeze of lemon makes a delicious (but not at all pretty) side drink.
swa: Mchuzi huo huwa na chumvi, mdalasini na kamuo dogo la ndimu huufanya uwe mtamu (lakini si mzuri sana) kama kinywaji kinachoambatana na mlo.

eng: We're delighted to announce the Global Voices Citizen Media Summit 2010!
swa: Tunayo furaha kutangaza Mkutano Mkuu wa Uanahabari wa Kiraia wa Global Voices 2010!

eng: Our gathering takes place this year in Santiago, Chile on May 6-7, 2010.
swa: Mwaka huu mkutano wetu utafanyika mjini Santiago, Chile tarehe 6-7, 2010.

eng: Visit the Summit web site for background information on the goals of the meeting, the program of events, registration details and information about the vibrant city of Santiago.
swa: Tembelea tovuti ya Mkutano kwa habari zaidi juu ya malengo ya mkutano, programu ya matukio, maelekezo ya kujiandikisha na maelezo juu ya mji mchangamfu wa Santiago.

eng: Among the highlights of the proceedings will be the announcement of the winners of the Breaking Borders award, a new prize created by Google and Global Voices to honor outstanding web projects initiated by individuals or groups demonstrating courage, energy and resourcefulness in using the Internet to promote freedom of expression.
swa: Kati ya vivutio vya mkutano huo kitakuwa ni kutangazwa kwa washindi wa Tuzo Ya Kuvunja Mipaka, tuzo mpya iliyoundwa na Google pamoja na Global Voices ili kuenzi miradi ya kipekee katika wavuti iliyoanzishwa na watu au vikundi vinavyoonyesha ujasiri, ari na uwezo wa kutumia Intaneti ili kukuza uhuru wa kujieleza.

eng: Over the next few days and weeks we'll be fleshing out the program, adding speaker bios, a list of attendees and more — and do keep checking in at the site for blog posts and commentary from Summit participants and others, as well as to join in the conversation.
swa: Katika siku na majuma machache yajayo tutakuwa tunaiamba programu, kwa kuongeza wajihi wa watoa mada, orodha ya wahudhuriaji na mengine mengi – na endelea kupitia pitia tovuti ili kusoma makala za blogu na maoni kutoka kwa washiriki wa mkutano na wengine, na ili kushiriki katika mazungumzo vile vile.

eng: You can also help spread the word about the Global Voices Summit by flying one of our Summit badges or banners on your blog or web site.
swa: Pia unaweza kusambaza habari kuhusu Mkutano wa Global Voices kwa kubandika moja ya vibeji au tangazo kwenye blogu au tovuti yako.

eng: The Global Voices Citizen Media Summit 2010 has been made possible thanks to the generous support of the MacArthur Foundation, Google, Open Society Institute, Knight Foundation and Yahoo!. Current major sponsors include MacArthur Foundation, Google, Open Society Institute, Knight Foundation and Yahoo!
swa: Mkutano Mkuu wa Uanahabari wa Kiraia wa Global Voices 2010 umewezekana kutokana na msaada wa MacArthur Foundation, Google, Open Society Institute, Knight Foundation na Yahoo!.

eng: Broken elephant tusk found in Hwange National Park in Zimbabwe, by Terry FeuerbornOpposition is mounting against Zambia's and Tanzania's proposals to be allowed by CITES, the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora, to sell their government held ivory stockpiles.
swa: Pembe ya ndovu iliyovunjika iliyopatikana kwenye Hifadhi ya Taifa ya Hwange nchini Zimbabwe, Na Terry Feuerborn Upinzani unaongezeka dhidi ya mapendekezo ya Zambia na Tanzania ya kuruhusiwa na Makubaliano ya Biashara ya Kimataifa ya Makundi ya Mimea na Wanyama Walio Katika Hatari ya Kutoweka (CITES), kuuza hifadhi ya pembe za ndovu walizonazo.

eng: The Baraza blog published the content of the proposals that Zambia and Tanzania have put forward and Kenya's opposing proposal.
swa: Blogu ya Baraza ilichapicha maudhui ya makubaliano hayo ambayo Zambia na Tanzania imeyaleta pamoja na pendekezo la Kenya la kuupinga.

eng: Maina explains on Baraza
swa: Maina anaelezea kwenye Baraza

eng: On the one hand is the anti-trade range states consisting of Congo, Ghana, Kenya, Liberia, Mali and Sierra Leone.
swa: Kwa upande mmoja ni ukanda wa nchi zinazopinga biashara ukijumuisha Kongo, Ghana, Kenya, Liberia, Mali na Sierra Leone.

eng: On the other hand, each with it’s own proposal is Zambia and Tanzania, who want to be allowed to sell their ivory stockpiles come the March 13-25 Doha meeting – the 15th CITES Conference of Parties (CoP15).
swa: Kwa upande mwingine, kila mmoja ikiwa na pendekezo lake ni Zambia na Tanzania, ambazo zinataka kuruhusiwa kuuza hifadhi ya pembe za ndovu zilizonazo kwa mkutano ujao wa Doha Machi 13-25 –mkutano wa 15 wa CITES.

eng: Both sides have sent their proposals to the CITES secretariat and the secretariat has generously posted the proposals on their website.
swa: Pande zote zimetuma mapendekezo kwa sekretarieti ya CITES ba sekretarieti imekuwa na uungwana kwa kuweka mapendekezo hayo kwenye wavuti yao.

eng: In a different blog post on Baraza, Paula writes about the UK's resolve to vote against the two proposals:
swa: Katika posti nyingine kwenye blogu hiyo ya Baraza, Paula anaandika kuhusu kusudio la Uingereza la kupiga kura ya kupinga mapendekezo yote mawili:

eng: The UK has said no to ivory sales.
swa: Uingereza imesema hapana kwa uuzaji wa pembe za ndovu.

eng: Environment Secretary Hilary Benn said last night: “At the CITES meeting in March, the UK will vote against the proposals from Tanzania and Zambia to sell ivory stocks, and we would urge other countries to vote against such a sale.
swa: Waziri wa Mazingira Hillary Benn alisema usiku wa jana: “Katika mkutano wa CITES mwezi Machi, Uingereza itapiga kura kupinga mapendekezo hayo kutokaTanzania na Zambia ya kuuza pembe za ndovu, na tutazitaka nchi nyingine kupiga kura ya kupinga uuzaji huo.

eng: Paula writes on Ban Ivory - a new blog at WildlifeDirect dedicated to the campaign against ivory - asking "Are elephants worth more than their teeth".
swa: Paula anaandika kwenye blogu mpya ya WildlifeDirect iitwayo Ban Ivory -inayojitoa mahususi kupiga kampeni kupinga pembe za ndovu- akiuliza “Je, tembo wanathamani kuliko meno yao?”.

eng: She asks: "Are elephants just a source of a valuable commodity, ivory?
swa: Anauliza: “Je, tembo ni chanzo tu cha bidhaa ya thamani, pembe zake?

eng: Or do elephants deserve special treatment?"
swa: Au, je, tembo wanastahili kutendewa kwa upekee?”

eng: Paula points out that inspite of all the support that Africans can expect from outside, the battle for the elephant will have to start with Africans.
swa: Paula anasema kwamba pamoja na kuungwa mkono ambako Waafrika wanakutegemea kutoka nje, vita kwa ajili ya tembo itabidi ianze na Waafrika wenyewe.

eng: She says:
swa: Anasema:

eng: At the end of the day the protest against the trade in ivory will have to be led by Africans if the rest of the world is to take any notice which makes Kenya’s campaign so powerful.
swa: Mwisho wa siku maandamano upinzani dhidi ya biashara ya pembe za ndovu itabidi uongozwe na Waafrika ikiwa ulimwengu uliobaki utatakiwa kuona kile kinachoifanya kampeni ya Kenya kuwa na nguvu.

eng: But as long as the Chinese and other Asians markets continue to provide markets for ivory trinkets and refuse to implement domestic enforcement, a renewed ban on trade in ivory will fail and we will continue to lose elephants.
swa: Lakini ikiwa Wachina na Waasia wengine wataendelea kuwa masoko ya pembe za ndovu na kukataa kufanyia kazi makubaliano ya ndani, katazo hili jipya kwa biashara ya pembe litashindwa na tutaendelea kupoteza tembo.

eng: A group known as the Kenya Elephant Forum is leading the Kenyan civil society in the protest against ivory trade resumption and have produced fact sheets on the issue.
swa: Kikundi kinachojulikana kama Jukwaa la Ndovu Kenya kinaongoza jamii ya kiraia ya Kenya katika upinzani dhidi ya biashraa ya pembe za ndovu na yameandaa maelezo muhimu kuhusu suala hilo.

eng: Harvey Croze, blogging on the Amboseli Trust for Elephants pages says
swa: Harvey Coroze, anayeblogu kwenye blogu ya Mfuko wa Amboseli kwa Tembo anasema:

eng: ATE is against the trade.
swa: Asasi ya ATE inapinga biashara hiyo.

eng: We have been working with like-minded NGOs and individuals under the aegis of the Kenya Elephant Forum (KEF) to provide strategic information to a body of sympathetic African elephant range states called the African Elephant Coalition (AEC).
swa: Tumekuwa tukifanya kazi na AZISE pamoja na watu wenye msimamo uanaoshabihiana chini ya mwamvuli wa Jukwaa la Tembo Kenya (KEF) kutoa taarifa za kimkakati kwa vyombo vya nchi za Afrika zenye tembo vinavyoitwa Umoja wa Tembo Afrika (AEC).

eng: In this blog post, Harvey has included links to the KEF Fact Sheets that you may want to read in order to understand the ivory problem and the likely implication of the Tanzania/Zambia proposals.
swa: Katika makala hii ya blogu yake, Harvey ameweka viungo vya maelezo muhimu kuhusu suala hilo ya KEF ambayo unaweza kutaka kuyasoma ili kuona tatizo la pembe za ndovu na maana ya mapendekezo ya Tanzania/Zambia.

eng: At least 7,000 protesters gathered on the streets of Kaliningrad , the country's westernmost city, on January 30 to demand, among other things, the resignation of the regional governor Georgy Boos and Russian Prime Minister Vladimir Putin.
swa: Wanaandamanaji wasiopungua 7,000 walikusanyika kwenye mitaa ya Kaliningrad, mji ulio magharibi zaidi mwa nchi hiyo, Januari 30 ili kudaii, pamoja na mambo mengine, kujiuzulu kwa gavana wa mkoa Georgy Boos na Waziri Mkuu wa Urusi Vladimir Putin.

eng: But don't count on the leading Russian media outlets to tell you about it.
swa: Lakini usivitegemee vyombo vya habari vya Urusi kukwambia hayo.

eng: The biggest and most popular TV channels keep their silence.
swa: Idhaa kubwa na maarufu za televisheni zimekuwa kimya.

eng: Mainstream newspapers and radio stations ignore the rally and go about their business like nothing happened.
swa: Magazeti makubwa na vituo vya redio vimeyapuuza maandamano hayo na vinaendelea na shughuli zao kama vile hakuna kilichotokea.

eng: But it only takes a quick glance at the most popular blog posts on RuNet (Russian Internet) to realize that the protest in Kaliningrad is the hottest topic of the day.
swa: Lakini inakuchukua mtipitio mmoja tu katika posti maarufu kwenye RuNet (Mtandao wa Urusi) kutambua kuwa maandamano ya mjini Kaliningrad ni mada moto moto ya siku.

eng: Famous political leaders, journalists and regular netizens flooded the blogosphere with their takes on the protest.
swa: Viongozi maarufu wa siasa, waandishi wa habari na watumiaji wa kawaida wa mtandao wa tarakilishi walifurika kwenye uwanja wa blogu wakiwa na mitazamo yao kuhusu maandamano hayo.

eng: LJ user b-nemtsov), a former Russian Deputy Prime Minister, wrote an inspiring post "Kaliningrad is the hope of free Russia" where he stressed the uniqueness of the protest in Kaliningrad :
swa: Boris Nemtsov (anayejulikana pia kama mtumiaji wa LJ b-nemtsov), Naibu Waziri wa zamani wa Urusi, aliandika posti yenye mguso wa pekee “Kaliningrad ni tumaini la Urusi iliyo huru” ambapo alisisitiza upekee wa maandamano hayo ya Kaliningrad :

eng: Since the proposed bans on the wearing of the burqa in France, the issue has been simmering in the Australian blogosphere.
swa: Tangu mapendekezo ya kupiga marufuku uvaaji wa burqa au hijab huko Ufaransa, suala hilo limekuwa likitokota katika ulimwengu wa bloghu wa Australia.

eng: An Australian radio shock-jock, and ex-police officer, drew criticism recently over his opposition to the wearing of the burqa in public.
swa: Mtangazaji wa redio katika mtindo wa kushtua umma, ambaye pia ni askari polisi wa zamani, alishutumiwa hivi karibuni juu ya kupinga kuvaliwa kwa hilo vazi la burqa.

eng: Michael Smith argued that bank staff and shop assistants are concerned with possible criminal misuse.
swa: Michael Smith alidai kuwa wafanyakazi wa benki na wahudumu madukani wanahofia matumizi mabaya yanayoweza kutokea ya vazi hilo.

eng: He also suggested that young children are frightened by encounters with women wearing the “full-on burqa”, comparing it to “kids crying, getting the fright of their lives when seeing Santa Claus”.
swa: Pia alisema kuwa watoto wadogo huogopa wanapokuna na wanawake waliovaa “vazi zima la burqa”, alilinganisha kuogopa huko na “watoto wanapolia, wanapoogopa sana wanapomuona Santa Claus”.

eng: A radio interview with Smith can be heard at Michael Smith Meets the Press.
swa: Mahojiano ya redio na Smith yanaweza kusikika kwenye blogu ya Michael Smith Meets the Press.

eng: When the French bans were proposed during the middle of 2009, Canberra journalist Virginia Haussegger argued on her blog for its prohibition on the grounds of gender equality:
