eng: Although the community of Congolese (DRC) nationals based abroad was not granted the right to vote during the November 28, 2011, presidential and parliamentary elections, it has shown its commitment to being involved in the political debate.
swa: Ingawa jumuiya ya raia wa Kongo (DRC) waishio ng’ambo hawakupewa haki yao ya msingi ya kupiga kura wakati wa uchaguzi wa Rais na wabunge uliofanyika Novemba 28, 2011, raia hao wameonyesha kujitolea kwao kwa kujihusisha na majadiliano ya kisiasa.

eng: Using various online channels, the Congolese diaspora have organised several initiatives to raise awareness amongst fellow citizens and members of the international community.
swa: Kwa kutumia chaneli kadhaa za mtandoni, raia hao wa Kongo waiishio nje ya nchi yao wameunda majukwaa mbalimbali ya kukuza uelewa miongoni mwa raia wenzao pamoja na wanachama wa jumuiya yao kimataifa.

eng: Indeed, the diaspora have succeeded in making themselves heard.
swa: Kwa hakika, raia hao wamefanikiwa kufanya sauti yao isikike.

eng: On December 7, the ambassadors of France, the United Kingdom and Belgium in Kinshasa pressed the long-time opposition leader and candidate in the presidential election Etienne Tshisekedi to ask his partisans to stop violence in foreign capitals.
swa: Mnamo Desemba 7, Mabalozi wa Ufaransa, Uingereza na Ubeligiji walio jijini Kinshasa walimshinikiza kiongozi wa muda mrefu wa upinzani na aliyekuwa mgombea wa kiti cha urais Etienne Tshisekedi kuwasihi wafuasi wake kuacha ghasia katika miji mbalimbali nje ya nchi hiyo.

eng: Tshisekedi came in second in the polls according to the temporary results announced by the National Independent Electoral Commission (CENI).
swa: Tshisekedi alishika nafasi ya pili katika uchaguzi huo kwa mujibu wa matokeo ya awali yaliyotangazwa na Tume Huru ya Taifa ya Uchaguzi (CENI).

eng: According to Nicolas-Patience Basabose, Director of Publication of Le Congo Hebdo (Congo Weekly), who is based in South Africa, the diaspora is still strongly connected to their homeland :
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Nicolas-Patience Basabose, Mkurugenzi wa Chapisho la Le Congo Hebdo (Congo Weeklu), anayeishi Afrika Kusini, raia hao waishio nje ya nchi bado wana uhusiano imara na wenzao waishio nyumbani :

eng: We denounce, accuse and complain against these officials for their support and involvement in the Joseph Kabila government that the Congolese have rejected during the November 28, 2011 elections.
swa: Tunawapinga, tunawalaumu na kuwalalamikia hawa maafisa kwa kumwunga mkono na kujihusisha na serikali ya Joseph Kabila ambayo wa-Kongo wameikataa kwenye uchaguzi wa Novemba 28.

eng: They are criminals in Congo and they are also criminals in Canada and criminals according to international laws. (...) We have information from reliable sources about all the names of all the Canadian public figures whose companies are involved in the illicit exploitation of mines in Congo. Johannesburg also witnessed the march of hundreds of Congolese nationals.
swa: Hawa watu ni wahalifu wanaoishi Kongo na ni wahalifu wanaoishi Kanada na ni wahalifu wa sheria za kimataifa. (…) Tunazo taarifa kutoka kwenye vyanzo vya uhakika kuhusiana na majina ya watu maarufu wa ki-Kanada ambao makampuni yao yanajihusisha na unyonyaji haramu wanaoufanya kwenye madini yetu nchini Kongo.

eng: Other protests occured in Africa, particularly in Morocco.
swa: Maandamano mengine yalitokea Afrika, hususani nchini Morocco.

eng: Kim Jong Il, the North Korean dictator who ruled the hermit kingdom for the past three decades, has died at the age of 69.
swa: Kim Jong Il, dikteta aliyetawala ufalme wa Korea Kaskazini kwa miongo mitatu, amefariki akiwa na umri wa miaka 69.

eng: According to North Korean state television's official report on Monday, Kim passed away from "mental and physical strain" during a train ride on December 17, 2011.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa taarifa rasmi iliyotolewa Jumatatu , kupitia runinga ya taifa, Kim alifariki kwa sababu ya “uchovu wa kiakili na kimwili” wakati akisafiri kwa gari moshi mnamo tarehe 17 Desemba, 2011.

eng: The South Korean Twittersphere erupted with various responses.
swa: Watumiaji wa twita wa Korea Kusini walilipuka wakionyesha hisia mchanganyiko.

eng: Although the death of one of the world's most notorious dictators is something people might welcome, most South Koreans have expressed concern about the instability his sudden death might bring to Korean peninsula.
swa: Ingawa kifo cha dikteta huyo katili zaidi duniani ni tukio ambalo raia wengi wa Korea Kusini wangelifurahia, wengi wameonyesha mashaka kwa kuwa tukio hilo lilimaanisha kuanza kwa hali tete ya usalama inayoweza kusababishwa na kifo hicho katika pembe ya bahari (peninsula) ya Korea.

eng: The South Korean public's initial response to the news was pure shock.
swa: Mwitikio wa awali kabisa wa wananchi wa Korea Kusini kwa habari hizi ulikuwa ni taharuki.

eng: While Madagascar attempts to find a way out of a prolonged political crisis, Malagasy bloggers are discussing the value of foreign direct investment (FDI).
swa: Wakati Madagaska ikijaribu kutafuta suluhisho la matatizo ya muda mrefu ya kiasa, Wanablogu wa ki-Malagasi wanajadili thamani ya Uwekezaji unaofanywa Moja kwa Moja na raia wa Kigeni.

eng: The worth of foreign investment came into sharp contrast when a land deal with Korean investor Daewoo came under criticism and partly triggered the current crisis.
swa: Uhalali wa uwekezaji huu wa kigeni uliingia kwenye sura mpya wakati mkataba wa kuuza ardhi uliokuwa ufanywe na mwekezaji wa Kikorea aitwaye Daewoo ulipopata upinzani mkubwa na kwa sehemu kubwa kuchochea mgogoro uliopo.

eng: Many Malagasy believe that Madagascar, like many other African countries is rich in natural resources but that the land has been plagued by poor governance and unfair trade deals.
swa: Wa-Malagarasi wanaamini kwamba Madagaska, kama nchi nyingine za Kiafrika inao utajiri mkubwa wa rasili mali lakini tatizo likiwa ardhi yenyewe kupokonywa kwa sababu ya utawala mbovu na biashara zisizoangalia maslahi ya wananchi.

eng: Ten years ago, The Economist labeled Africa "The Hopeless Continent".
swa: Miaka kumi iliyopita, Jarida la kimataifa la The Economist liliita Afrika “bara lisilo na matumaini”.

eng: Their most recent publication highlights the rapid growth of many African countries' GDP.
swa: Katika toleo la hivi karibuni jarida hilo lilionyesha ukuaji wa kasi wa pato la taifa la nchi nyingi za Kiafrika (GDP).

eng: Still, the growth is not equally felt throughout the continent.
swa: Bado hata hivyo, ukuaji huo hauonekani kuwa na uwiano sawa katika nchi za bara hili.

eng: In fact, Madagascar is projected to have one of the lowest level of growth in all of Africa.
swa: Kwa kweli, Madagaska inabashiriwa kuwa nchi yenye kiwango cha kidogo zaidi cha ukuaji barani Afrika.

eng: Additionally, the capital city Antananarivo and other cities are currently experiencing frequent running water and power outages that have provoked frustration and outrage among Malagasy citizens.
swa: Kwa kuongeza, mji mkuu wa Antananrivo na majiji mengine yamekuwa yakikabiliwa na ukosefu wa maji na nishati ya umeme mambo yaliyochochea vurugu na ghadhabu miongoni mwa raia wa Malagasi.

eng: The current situation is one of the reasons Antananarivo has been ranked as one of the cities with the lowest quality of life in the world by the Mercer’s 2011 quality of living survey.
swa: Hali ilivyo sasa ni moja wapo ya sababu ya jiji la Antananarivo kuwa katika orodha ya moja wapo ya majiji yenye kiwango duni kabisa cha maisha duniani katika Utafiti wa 2011 wa Mercer kuhusu hali ya maisha ya watu.

eng: Having been marred in a lengthy political quagmire, the Malagasy blogosphere is trying to steer the debate away from a political solution to an overall debate on how to re-ignite an economy that has faltered over the past three years.
swa: Kwa kule kukabiliwa na historia mbaya ya migogoro isiyoisha ya kisiasa, ulimwengu wa wanablogu wa Kimalagasi unajaribu kuchochea mijadala itakayotoa suluhisho la kisiasa kwa mjadala wa jumla wa namna ya kuukuza upya uchumi ambao umedororora katika miaka mitatu iliyopita.

swa: Kuufanya Uwekezaji wa Kigeni wa moja kwa moja kuwasaidia watu wa Malagasi

eng: Land deals have been discussed at length in Madagascar as a way to get out of poverty; the aborted Daewoo deal was the most publicized case but similar deals have been implemented without much hesitation or reaction.
swa: Makubaliano ya matumizi ya ardhi yamejadiliwa kwa kirefu nchini Madagaska kama njia ya kuondokana na umasikini; mkataba uliovunjwa wa Daewoo uliokuwa umetangazwa sana pengine kuliko yote lakini mikataba inayofanana na huo imekuwa ikitekelezwa bila kuchelewa wala miitikio kutoka kwa raia.

eng: The soundness of deals related to the mineral wealth of Madagascar has been recently debated by Malagasy experts.
swa: Mantiki ya mikataba hiyo inayohusiana na utajiri wa madini wa Madagaska ulijadiliwa hivi karibuni na wataalamu wa Kimalagasi.

eng: Blaise Stephen is working at the International Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Madagascar.
swa: Blaise Stephen anafanya kazi katika Chemba ya Kimataifa ya Biashara na Viwanda ya Madagaska.

eng: He voiced his frustration with the current status-quo in the Madagascar political system that according to him is the main roadblock preventing more bilateral cooperation with foreign investors :
swa: Alionyesha kushangazwa kwake na hali inavyoendelea kuwa ilivyo katika mfumo wa kisiasa wa Madagaska kiasi kwamba kwa mujibu wake hicho ni kikwazo kikuu cha kuzuia ubia wa pamoja na wawekezaji wa kigeni (fr):

eng: Two students, Jorge Alexis Herrera Pino and Gabriel Echeverría de Jesús, were killed on December 12, 2011, during a protest held by students of the rural school Raúl Isidro Burgos in Ayotzinapa, Chilpancingo, the capital of the state of Guerrero, Mexico.
swa: Wanafunzi wawili, Jorge Alexis Herrera Pino na Gabriel Echeverría de Jesús, waliuwawatarehe 12 Desemba 2011, wakati wa maandamano ya wanafunzi wa shule ya vijijini ya Raúl Isidro huko Ayotzinapa, mji mkuu wa Guerrero, Chilpancingo, nchini Mexico.

eng: The protest blocked the highway “Autopista del Sol” which leads to the tourist area of Acapulco.
swa: Maandamano yaliifunga barabara kuu ya “Autopista del Sol” inayoelekea kwenye eneo la kitalii Acapulco.

eng: Contradicting versions of events have been published online, including the version given by the authorities of Guerrero who said this protest was “unusual”, and that “strange agents” not related to the students participated in the mobilization.
swa: Mitazamo yenye utata kuhusu yalioyotokea imechapishwa mtandaoni, ukiwemo ule uliotolewa na mamlaka za Guerrero iliyosema kuwa maandamano haya “si ya kwaida” na kuwa kuna “watu wengine” wasiohusiana na wanafunzi ambo walishiriki katika maandalizi ya maandamano.

eng: La Jornada de Guerrero published a chronicle of the events:
swa: La Jornada de Guerrero ilichapisha mtiririko wa matukio:

eng: Everything started with a smoke curtain, provoked by the tear gas bombs that came out of the hands of the federal police.
swa: Mambo yote yalianza na pazia la moshi, lilisababishwa na mabomu ya machozi ambayo yalitokea mikononi mwa polisi (wa serikali kuu).

eng: After that came the first gust of bullets form the federal police, who were authorized to proceed via radio.
swa: Baada ya hapo ukafuata mfumuko wa kwanza wa risasi kutoka kwa polisi ambao walipewa kibali kupitia redio.

eng: The second gust, which was longer, came from different hands: ministerial police opened fire against the students from the right lane (of the highway from north to south) It didn't take long for the federal police to aim at the same target.
swa: Mfumuko wa pili ambao ulikuwa mrefu zaidi, ulitokea kwenye mikono tofauti: polisi wa wizara waliwafytulia risasi wanafunzi kutokea upande wa kulia (wa barabara kuu kutokea kaskazini kwenda kusini) haikuwachukua muda mrefu polisi wa serikali kuu kulenga shabaha ile ile.

eng: On the other side, Ayotzinapa's side, the rural students with a daily budget for food of 3.50 dollars, responded with sticks and stones.
swa: Upande mwingine, upande wa Ayotzinapa, wanafunzi wa vijijini wenye bajeti ya chakula ya dola 3.5 kwa siku, walijibu kwa mawe na magongo.

eng: The domestic bombs that they had weren't used because they didn't have time to load them with gas from the 2 gas stations on of each side of the highway.
swa: Mabomu ya kujitengenezea hayakutumiwa kwa kuwa hawakupata muda wa kununua mafuta kutoka kwenye vituo vya mfuta viwili vilivyo kandokando ya barabara hiyo.

eng: Some, trying to defend themselves, had time to light up the bottles they got from the service station.
swa: Baadhi, katika harakati za kujitetea, waliwasha mitungi waliyopata kwenye vituo vya mafuta.

eng: The police then threw some fragmentation grenades at the students, that by then were seeking refuge in the space between the buses and concrete walls that divide the highway.
swa: Ndipo polisi wakawatupia wanafunzi mabomu ya kusambaratisha ya mkono, ambao kwa wakati huo walikuwa wakijitahidi kujiokoa kwa kujificha kwenye nafasi katikati ya misururu ya magari na ukuta uanotenganisha barabara hiyo kuu.

eng: There were five grenades in total and none detonated, but they provoked panic .
swa: Kwa ujumla kulikuwa na mabomu ya kutupa kwa mkono matano ambayo hayakulipuka lakini yalileta mtafaruku kwa wanafunzi hao. .

eng: The only ones not moving were two students, both 22 years old
swa: Ni wanafunzi wawili tu ambao hawakukimbia, wote walikuwa na umri wa miaka 22.

eng: The normalista school involved in the protest has been historically in resistance and belongs to an old tradition of 'escuelas normalistas rurales', which are schools that form teachers from very poor and disadvantage communities.
swa: Shule ya normalista iliyoshiriki katika maandamano ina historia ya kuwa na upinzani katika utamaduni wa kizamani wa 'escuelas normalistas rurales', ni shule ambazo zinatengeneza walimu wa kutoka kwenye jamii maskini na zenye duni.

eng: The school in question belongs to the Federación de Estudiantes Campesinos Socialistas de México (Federation of Rural Socialist Students of México).
swa: Shule hii inamilikiwa na Federación de Estudiantes Campesinos Socialistas de México (Shirikisho la Jamii ya Wanafunzi wa Kisoshalsti wa vijijini nchini Mexico).

eng: Journalist Diego Osorno, who specializes in social conflicts, wrote a story for the blog Nuesta Aparente Rendición about the normalistas conflict in Guerrero , specifically the school of Ayotzinapa.
swa: Mwanahabari Diego Osorno, ambaye amejikita zaidi katika kuandikia migogoro ya jamii, aliandika habari kwenye blogu ya Nuesta Aparente Rendición kuhusu mgogoro wa normalistas huko normalistas huko Guerrero , hasa wa shule ya Ayotzinapa.

eng: The school issued a communique in which they denied having any weapons and demand justice for the killings, which they labeled as “extrajudicial execution”.
swa: Shule hiyo ilitoa tangazo ambalo lilikanusha kuwa na silaha zozote na kudai haki katika mauaji hayo, ambayo waliyaita kuwa ni “mauaji nje ya utaratibu wa mahakama”.

eng: The text also explains the repeated cancellations of scheduled meetings with the Minister of Education of Guerrero and demand the governor's resignation
swa: Maandishi (ya tangazo hilo maalum) pia yanaelezea kusitishwa mara kwa mara kwa mikutano iliyopangwa ya kukutana na Waziri wa Elimu wa Guerrero na kumtaka gavana kujiuzulu.

eng: Wall of the Normalistas School “Isidro Burgos” in Ayotzinapa.
swa: Ukuta wa shule ya Normalistas ya “Isidro Burgos” huko Ayotzinapa.

eng: Foto via @kradprro
swa: Picha na @kradprro

eng: On December 13, Justice Authority Alberto López Rosas, during a radio interview with Carmen Aristegui , declared that one of the detainees -who is 19-years-old- had an AK-47, but they didn't know if the bullets matched the caliber that killed the two students.
swa: Mnamo Desemba 13, Mkuu wa Sheria Alberto López Rosas, wakati wa mahojiano ya redio Carmen Aristegui , alitangaza kuwa mmoja wa waliowekwa kizuizini - ambaye ana umri wa miaka 19 alikuwa na bunduki aina ya AK-47, lakini bado hawajajua kama risasi zinawiana na zile zilizowauwa wanafunzi wawili.

eng: However he said the weapon is not the kind used by police, and made it clear that the police's actions did not constitute repression, that they only wanted to bring order.
swa: Hata hivyo alisema kuwa bunduki hiyo haifanani na zile zinazotumiwa na polisi, na aliweka wazi kuwa matendo ya polisi hayakuwa ya kikandamizaji na kuwa walitaka kuleta utulivu tu.

eng: In relation to this,La Jornada published a report about the use of torture to "fabricate" a confession related to the AK-47.

swa: Kiongozi huyu wa Rwanda anasifiwa kwa kumaliza mauaji ya kimbari ya mwaka 1994 yaliyoangamiza zaidi ya watu 800,000.

eng: In recent years, human rights organizations have raised concerns over the country's deteriorating human rights record.
swa: Katika miaka ya hivi karibuni, mashirika ya haki za binadamu yameonyesha kusikitishwa na rekodi inayoendelea kushuka ya haki za binadamu nchini humo.

swa: Wanaharakati wa Rwanda wanaofanya kampeni kwa ajili ya demokrasia "walisikitishwa sana " na tangazo hili.

eng: The activists believe that President Kagame is pursuing a third term as a strategy to shield himself from future prosecution.
swa: Wanaharakati wanaamini kwamba Rais Kagame anatafuta awamu ya tatu kama mbinu ya kujikinga dhidi mashtaka yanayoweza kumkabili siku za usoni.

eng: In particular, they identify the recently released United Nations Mapping report that accuses him of war crimes against members of the Hutu ethnic group.
swa: Kwa mfano, wanaonyesha ripoti iliyotolewa hivi karibuni ya Umoja wa Mataifa (United Nations Mapping report) inayomtuhumu kwa makosa ya uhalifu wa kivita dhidi ya jamii ya kabila la wa-Hutu.

eng: The same report emphasized that the crimes could amount to genocide if proven in a court of law.
swa: Taarifa hiyo hiyo inasisitiza kwamba uhalifu huo unaweza kufikia kiwango cha mauaji ya kimbari kama yatathibitishwa na mahakama ya sheria.

eng: Analysts are also alarmed that this decision to seek another term could destabilize the Great Lakes region by leaving no option open to the Rwandan opposition other than to take up arms.
swa: Wachambuzi pia wana wasiwasi kuwa uamuzi huu wa kutafuta awamu nyingine unaweza kuhatarisha usalama katika ukanda wa Maziwa Makuu kwa kuwalazimu wapinzani wa Rwanda kutokuwa na namna nyingine zaidi ya kubeba silaha.

eng: The presidential term limits debate in Rwanda is championed by internal security minister, Sheikh Musa Fazil Harerimana.
swa: Mjadala wa ukomo wa kipindi cha urais nchini Rwanda unaongozwa na waziri wa mambo ya ndani, Sheikh Musa Fazil Harerimana.

eng: Sheikh Fazil is also campaigning for the legal recognition of polygamous marriages, which are currently outlawed.
swa: Sheikh Fazil pia anafanya kampeni ya kutambuliwa kisheria kwa ndoa za mitala, ambazo kwa sasa haziruhusiwi.

eng: President Kagame seems to agree with the Sheikh Fazil:
swa: Rais Kagame anaonekana kukubaliana na Sheikh Fazil::

eng: This Sheikh has a right to express himself and it's as if people expect me to go to this person and say 'you shut up.
swa: Huyu Sheikh ana haki ya kujieleza na inakuwa kama watu wananitarajia niende kwa huyu bwana na kumwambia “Nyamaza.

eng: Don't talk about this anymore.' No.
swa: Usizungumzie hili tena” Hapana.

eng: This is not my business.
swa: Hiyo siyo kazi yangu.

eng: @TimKalyegira: Thousands of tearful Rwandans will soon start narrating to world media how betrayed they will feel if Kagame does not seek a third term.
swa: @TimKalyegira: Maelfu ya wa-Nyarwanda wenye kutiririkwa na machozi hivi karibuni wataanza kuviambia vyombo vya habari vya kimataifa namna gani watajisikia kusalitiwa kama Kagame hatagombea kwa awamu ya tatu.

eng: British journalist Ian Birell was equally unimpressed:
swa: Mwandishi wa Uingereza Ian Birell vivyo hivyo alionyesha kutokufurahishwa:

eng: @ianbirell: People are free to say they want me to be president again, says Kagame.
swa: @ianbirell: Watu wako huru kusema wananihitaji kuwa rais kwa mara nyingine, asema Kagame.

eng: They're not free, of course, to say he should go...
swa: Hawako huru, na kwa kweli ndivyo ilivyo, kusema aondoke…

swa: Lakini maoni ya Ian Birell ndani ya muda mfupi yalivuta ghadhabu ya balozi wa Rwanda nchini Uingereza, Erneste Rwamucyo, aliyemtuhumu kwa kuwa na mtazamo wa tawala za kimagharibi:

eng: A pple out to be respected.
swa: Watu wana haki ya kuheshimiwa.

eng: To which Mr. Birell responded:
swa: Maneno ambayo Bw.

swa: @ianbirell: Hakuna kitu kinachofanana na uelekezaji wa kimagharibi kuhusu kuunga mkono haki za binadamu na kupinga tawala kandamizi na za kimabavu

swa: Kwa kadiri mjadala ulivyoendelea kupamba moto, majibizano makali yakiwahusisha waandishi kadhaa wa habari wa ki-Ganda yalijitokeza.

swa: Mambo yalianza pale Bob Muheebwa alipouliza ikiwa kulikuwa na waandishi wengine wa ki-Ganda nje ya Andrew Mwenda na Alan Kasuja waliopenda kumhoji Rais Kagame.

eng: The journalists wondered why Mwenda and Kasuja are never critical of President Kagame in their writings.
swa: Waandishi walishangaa kwa nini Mwenda na Kasuja kamwe hawamkosoi Rais Kagame kwenye makala zao.

eng: George Bankole's answer was more blunt.
swa: Jibu la George Bankole halikuwa la moja kwa moja.

eng: In an apparent reference to both journalists, Mwenda and Kasujja, he said: @Snottyganda: @tijo5 Cos both hve been compromised with Cash incentives @mugumya@TimKalyegira@Gilespies@AndrewMwenda@kasujja

eng: @TimKalyegira: @Snottyganda@tijo5@mugumya@AndrewMwenda@kasujja Others compromised by the sheer flattery of being on casual terms with a head of state.
swa: @TimKalyegira: @Snottyganda@tijo5@mugumya@AndrewMwenda@kasujja Wengine wamenunuliwa kwa sifa tu za kuwa na mahusiano ya kirafiki na wakuu wa nchi.

swa: Andrew Mwenda aliendelea kuwa kimya kwa suala hili, lakini Allan Kasujja baadae akakanusha madai hayo:

eng: @kasujja: @TimKalyegira @tijo5 @mugumya @AndrewMwenda I am amazed at how simplistic your arguments have become.
swa: @kasujja: @TimKalyegira @tijo5 @mugumya @AndrewMwenda Ninashangazwa na namna hoja zenu zilivyokuwa rahisi.

swa: Hivi haiwezekani nikasukumwa na haki

swa: @TimKalyegira: @kasujja Inaweza kuwa ni haki.

swa: Inafikirisha kwa wengine wetu, mbio hizi za waandishi wa ki-Ganda kuimba sifa za Kagame.

swa: Rwanda hivi sasa inao ukomo wa vipindi viwili vya kikatiba kwa urais.

swa: Kila kipindi kina jumla ya miaka saba, ambacho ni kipindi kirefu kuliko vyote barani Afrika.

eng: The buzz is growing louder online that Syrian blogger Razan Ghazzawi, arrested on the Syrian-Jordanian border while on her way to a workshop on press freedom in the Arab world in Amman on December 4, 2011, will be released.
swa: Mazungumzo yanaendelea kuongezeka mtandaoni kwamba Mwanablogu wa ki-Syria Razan Ghazzawi, aliyekamatwa kwenye mpaka wa Syria na Jordan wakati akiwa njiani kuhudhuria warsha iliyohusu uhuru wa vyombo vya habari katika nchi za ki-Arabu mjini Amman Desemba 4, ataachiwa huru.

eng: Eight days after her arrest, Ghazzawi was charged with a list of crimes - refuted by the blogging community and described as a farce.
swa: Siku nane baada ya kukamatwa, Ghazzawi alishtakiwaorodha ndefu ya mashtaka - yaliyopingwa na jumuiya ya wanablogu na kuyaelezea kama mchezo wa kuigiza.

eng: Among her accusations were "establishing an organization that aims to change the social and economical entity of the state” and “weakening the national sentiment, and trying to ignite sectarian strife,” reported the Lebanese Daily Star at the time.
swa: Miongoni mwa mashitaka yake ni, “kuanzisha taasisi ambayo inayokusudia kubadilisha hali ya nchi kijamii na kiuchumi” na “kudhoofisha hisia za utaifa, na kujaribu kuchochea migogoro ya kidini,” liliandika jarida la Lebanese daily Star wakati huo.

eng: On her Free Razan page on Facebook, supporters made the announcement that Ghazzawi would be freed, citing Syrian lawyer and human rights activist Razan Zaitouneh.

eng: The post does not say when Ghazzawi is expected to be freed.
swa: Makala haisemi hata hivyo, ni lini hasa Ghazzawi anatarajiwa kuachiwa huru.

eng: The Free Razan poster many supporters replaced their Facebook and Twitter avatars with, calling for the release of Razan Ghazzawi

swa: Desemba 9, 2011, ni siku maalumu kwa Watanzania wakati Tanganyika, ambayo ni sehemu ya Muungano wa Tanzania ikitimiza miaka 50 ya uhuru.

eng: Official logo for Tanzania at 50.

eng: Do they really love being shouted at to get off the road because the President, a minister or a regional commissioner is taking an afternoon drive? (…) Do they really feel a surge of pride and patriotism every time they are expected to stop what they are doing and stand at attention just become some newly-appointed official whom they many not even have seen before is being serenaded with the national anthem? swa: Je, wanapenda (wananchi wa kawaida) kweli kupigiwa kelele za kuondoka barabarani kwa sababu rais, waziri au mkuu wa mkoa anaendeshwa mchana? (…) Utu hauhitaji ubinafsi kuuondoa: na ubinafsi wa namna zake zote ni mbaya.

eng: Even if it were proved that the people really enjoyed it – which I very much doubt- it would still be a wrong; and it would still be our duty to put a stop to it and to tell the people that what they had learned to enjoy was wrong. (…)
swa: Hata kama ilikuwa imehakikishwa kwamba watu wanaufurahia –kitu ambacho sikiamini sana –bado ubinafsi ungeendelea kuwa mbaya; na ingeendelea kuwa wajibu wetu kuumaliza na kuwaambia watu kwamba kile walichojifunza kukifurahia ni kibaya (…)

eng: After pointing out a few things that Tanzania could do better, David Mugo who lived in Tanzania for 18 months, finishes his post by saying:

eng: In conclusion, I still think Tanzania is still one of the greatest countries I have been to in Africa.
swa: Kwa kuhitimisha, bado ninadhani Tanzania ingali moja ya nchi nzuri za Kiafrika nilizowahi kuzizuru.

eng: The people are definitely the best.
swa: Watu wake ni wema sana.

eng: Happy independence day, reflect on what independence you have, what it means to you, to this generation and future generations.
swa: Heri ya siku ya Uhuru, tafakarini uhuru gani mlionao, unamaanisha nini kwenu, kwa kizazi hiki na vizazi vijavyo.

eng: I challenge young people to view things beyond the eyes of our aging leaders.
swa: Ninawapa changamoto vijana kuyatazama mambo zaidi ya macho ya watawala wetu wanaozeeka.

eng: Congratulations again.
swa: Hongera sana.

eng: Long live Tanzania and its people.
swa: Idumu Tanzania na watu wake.

eng: Tanzanian activist and blogger, Ashura, wonders, "Where are we at 50?":

eng: In the Arusha Declaration of 1967 by Mwalimu Nyerere he stated ‘Independence means self-reliance.
swa: Katika Azimio la Arusha la mwaka 1967 la Mwalimu Nyerere alisema “Uhuru maana yake ni Kujitegemea.

eng: Independence cannot be real if a nation depends on gifts and loans from another for its development…’ lets ask ourselves today does Tanganyika not depend on gifts and loans for her development?

eng: The answer is yes that is why most of the land is sold to foreign company while leaving Tanzanians with neither land nor compensation.
swa: Jibu ni ndiyo ndio maana sehemu kubwa ya ardhi inauzwa kwa makampuni ya kigeni ikiwaacha watanzania bila ardhi wala fidia.

eng: Our government thinks our development will be brought by foreigners in exclusion of Tanzanians, according to Mwalimu Nyerere we cannot depend on foreign company and act as we please!
swa: Serikali yetu inafikiri maendeleo yataletwa na wageni kwa kuwaacha wa-Tanzania, kwa mujibu wa Mwalimu Nyerere hatuwezi kutegemea makampuni ya kigeni na kufanya tunavyojisikia!

eng: Its fifty years since Tanganyika got its independence on the 09th of December 1961 the country is almost regress and not progressing at all.
swa: Ni miaka 50 tangu Tanganyika ilipopata uhuru wake Desemba 9, 1961 na nchi ni kama inarudi kinyume nyume na imedumaa kabisa.

swa: Mwaka 1967, paundi moja ya Uingereza ilibadilishwa kwa Tsh.

swa: 16.6 leo paundi hiyo hiyo ina thamani ya Tsh.

swa: Hili lina maana mbaya kiuchumi.

eng: In celebrating 50 years of independence, The Wayward Press writes:

eng: Right now, our country finds itself at a moment of transition and great uncertainty.
swa: Hivi sasa, nchi yetu imejikuta kwenye wakati wa mpito na usiotabirika kabisa.

eng: Our politics lacks a sense of direction or grand ideological vision anchoring us forward.
swa: Siasa zetu zinakosa mwelekeo na muono mpana wa kiitikadi kututegemeza kuelekea mbele.

eng: Our leaders seem to be making it up as they go along.
swa: Watawala wetu wanaonekana kukata tama kadri siku zinavyoendelea.

eng: Our knowledge of our history is fragmented and rooted in skewed nostalgic visions of the past.
swa: Ufahamu wetu wa kihistoria uko katika vipande vipande na umejikita kwenye maono tenge yanayotilia mkazo yaliyopita.

eng: Our cultural identity is confused, informed more by foreign forms than any sense of a local aesthetic.
swa: Utambulisho wetu wa kiutamaduni umeparaganyika, ukiiga zaidi ule wa kigeni kuliko namna yoyote ya utamaduni wa ndani.

eng: To be a contemporary Tanzanian at the moment is to be a person of great potential unclear about what the future holds for him.
swa: Kuwa Mtanzania wa kisasa siku hizi ni kuwa mtu wa usiye na uhakika na vile mustakabali wako ulivyo.

eng: The Creatively Maladjusted looks at blogging and social media in Tanzania at 50:
swa: Blogu ya The Creatively Maladjusted inatazama kublogu na vyombo vya habari vya kijamii nchini Tanzania katika miaka 50:

eng: In a country such as Tanzania where media coverage is likely censored or at the very least is inconsistent / unreliable, blogging (and social media generally) open up a whole new world of opportunities.
swa: Katika nchi kama Tanzania ambapo habari zinazotawala vyombo vikuu vya habari zinauwezekano wa kufuatiliwa na kudhibitiwa na serikali ama kwa uchache sana haziaminiki (kwa kuwa mwelekeo wake unabadilika badilika), kublogu (na vyombo vya habari vya kijamii kwa ujumla) kunafungua nafasi pana zaidi kwa fursa.

eng: “Social media can give Tanzanians their own public voices.
swa: “Vyombo vya habari vya kijamii ninaweza kusema vinawapa watanzania sauti yao wenyewe.

eng: That’s the most powerful opportunity I can think of to be frank”- Elsie from The Mikocheni Report blog.
swa: Hiyo ni fursa yenye nguvu ninayoweza kuifikiria nikiwa wazi” –Elsie wa The Mikocheni Report Blog.

eng: A common (often intended at ending any further conversation) response that I hear in discussions about social media in Tanzania is that most people don’t have access to the internet.
swa: Jibu la kawaida (mara nyingi likikusudia kuhitimisha majadiliano zaidi) ninalolisikia katika mijadala kuhusu vyombo vya habari vya kijamii ni kwamba watu wengi hawajaunganishwa na mtandao wa intaneti.

eng: In rural areas where 75% of the population lives, access is without doubt the major challenge (related to poor electricity coverage as well as few and expensive internet cafes), but this situation is rapidly changing from both supply and demand vantage points, with increasingly cheaper internet access on mobile phones and younger generations attracted to the connectivity that social media offers.
swa: Katika maeneo ya vijijini ambapo asilimia 75 ya watu wanaishi, basi kutokuunganishwa bila shaka ni changamoto kubwa (kwa kuhusianisha na mtandao duni wa umeme na huduma ndogo na ghali za mikahawa ya mtandao wa intaneti), lakini hali hii inabadilika kwa kutazama upatikanaji na uhitaji, kwa kujumlisha ongezeko kubwa upatikanaji wa huduma rahisi za intaneti kwenye simu za viganjani na vijana wa kizazi kipya wanavutiwa na uunganishwaji unaopatikana kwenye vyombo vya habari vya kijamii.

eng: In towns I would argue that a large proportion of the population are at least on Facebook, and via links on Facebook probably have much more direct access to blogs / citizen journalism than people living in the West...
swa: Mijini ninaweza kusema kwamba idadi kubwa ya watu angalau wamejiunga na Facebook, na kwa kupitia viunga vya Facebook labda wana uwezekano wa kuunganishwa moja kwa moja na blogu/uandishi wa kuraia kuliko watu wanaoishi Magharibi…

eng: Ahmed at VijanaFM asks, "Tanzania at 50 what do we have to show for it?":
swa: Ahmed wa VijanaFM anauliza, “Tanzania kwenye miaka 50 tuna nini cha kuonyesha?”:

eng: I think there is a challenge right now of galvanizing the people to reflect on the past fifty years.
swa: Ninadhani kuna changamoto hivi sasa ya kuwalazimisha watu watafakari yaliyofanyika kwa miaka 50.

eng: We do remember the good times but are constantly reminded about the bad.
swa: Tunakumbuka nyakati nzuri lakini wakati huo huo tunabaki kukumbushwa zile mbaya.

eng: We have immense challenges and, as the saying goes, do Tanzanians feel they are better off today than they were ten years ago, let alone 50 years ago?
swa: Tuna changamoto nyingi na, kama usemi ulivyo, je watanzania wanajisikia afadhali leo kuliko walivyokuwa miaka kumi iliyopita, achilia mbali miaka 50 iliyopita?

eng: The answer is probably no.
swa: Jibu labda ni hapana.

eng: I think instead of being nostalgic about the good old days we should really look inside ourselves, both the mwananchi and the leadership and interrogate how we can build a better tomorrow.
swa: Ninafikiri badala ya kukumbuka siku nzuri za kale twapaswa kukujitazama ndani yetu, sote wananchi na watawala na kujihoji namna gani tutaijenga kesho yenye nafuu.

eng: This is because I think the majority of us are concerned about what the next 50 years will look like.
swa: Hii ni kwa sababu ninadhani wengi wetu tunawiwa kuhusu namna gani miaka mingine 50 itakavyokuwa.

eng: Karim Hirji, a professor of biostatics at the Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences, discusses the education system in Tanzania after 50 years of independence:
swa: Karim Hirji, Professor wa takwimu-viumbe wa Chuo Kikuu cha Afya na Sayansi za Tiba, anaujadili mfumo wa elimu nchini Tanzania baada ya miaka 50 ya uhuru:

eng: At the time of Uhuru, not a single doctor was being trained in Tanzania.
swa: Wakati wa uhuru, hakuna hata daktari mmoja alifunzwa hapa Tanzania.

eng: Now, my research methods class at the Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences has 150 students.
swa: Sasa, darasa langu la mbinu za utafiti kwenye Chuo Kikuu cha Muhimbili cha Afya na Sayansi za Tiba lina wanafunzi 150.

eng: My dilemma reflects the situation in most of the subjects taught at my university and, in fact, at all universities across the nation.
swa: Utata wangu unaakisi hali ilivyo katika kila somo linalofundishwa katika chuo changu na, kwa hakika, katika vyuo vyote vikuu nchini.

eng: Student numbers have expanded sharply, but the number of lecturers and teaching resources have not.
swa: Idadi ya wanafunzi imeongezeka kwa kasi, lakini idadi ya wahadhiri na vifaa vya kufundishia havijaongezeka.

eng: Some universities have a department with 20 or so academic staff, yet none has a doctoral degree We have just gone through a multimillion-dollar curriculum review exercise.
swa: Baadhi ya vyuo vikuu bina idara zenye wahadhiri kadri ya 20 hivi, na bado hakuna mwenye Shahada ya Uzamivu…Tumetoka kuhitimisha zoezi la kupitia upya mitaala lililogahrimu Mamilioni ya dola za mikamrekani.

eng: Yet, hardly any department has changed the substance of what it teaches.
swa: Bado, hakuna idara iliyobadili kile inachokifundisha.

swa: Tanganyika ilijipatia uhuru wake kutoka Uingereza Desemba 9, 1961, na baade Tanganyika iliungana na Zanzibar kuunda Jamhuri ya Muungano wa Tanzania.

eng: Human rights activist Moncef Marzouki, 66, has been elected as Tunisia's new interim president today.
swa: Mwanaharakati wa haki za binadamu Moncef Marzouki, (66), amechaguliwa hii leo kuwa raisi wa mpito wa Tunisia.

eng: The opposition figure, who has been imprisoned and exiled under the regime of former President Zeine El Abidine Ben Ali, will stay in power until the new constitution of the country is drafted, and legislative and presidential elections are held.
swa: Mpinzani aliyewahi kufungwa jela na hata kukimbilia uhamishoni wakati wa utawala wa Rais Zeine El Abidine Ben Ali, atakuwa rais hadi hapo katiba mpya ya nchi itakapo kuwa tayari na uchaguzi wa wabunge na rais utakapofanyika.

eng: His appointment drew reactions from Tunisian netizens, who were divided between critics and supporters.
swa: Kuteuliwa kwake kulizua maoni mbalimbali kutoka kwa wanamtandao wa Tunisia waligawanyikakatika makundi mawili ya wanokosoa na wanaounga mkono.

eng: Elsewhere in the Arab world, Marzouki's appointment, which was followed by a moving acceptance speech, was noted by netizens, who cheered on Tunisia's progress towards democracy, wishing the same for their countries.
swa: Na kwingineko Uarabuni, uteuzi wa Marzouki, uliofuatiwa na hotuba yake yenye mvuto ya kuukubali, ulipokelewa na raia mtandaoni kwa kuwasifu waTunisia kwa hatua nzuri waliyopiga kuelekea demokrasia, na kuombea iwe hivyo hata kwa nchi zao.

eng: Inaugural address of Mr. Marzouki, the new president of the Republic of Tunisia.
swa: Hotuba siku yakusimikwa kwa Bw. Marzouki, rais mpya wa Jamhuri ya Tunisia.

eng: Image by hamideddine Bouali, copyright Demotix (13/12/11).
swa: Picha na Hamideddine Bouali, hakinakili Demotix (13/12/11).

eng: Tunisia was the launching pad of an Arab revolution which started in the town of Sidi Bouzid when unemployed Mohammed Bouazizi set himself ablaze on December 17.
swa: Tunisia ndio ilikuwa sehemu iliyoanzisha kasi ya mapinduzi Uarabuni yalioanza katika mji wa Sidi Bouzid ambapo Mohammed Bouazizi aliyekuwa hana ajira wakati huo alipojichoma moto mnamo Desemba 17.

eng: Since that day, millions of Arabs across the region took to the streets of their cities, towns and villages, calling for democracy, equality, human rights and political, economic and legislative reforms.
swa: Tangu siku hiyo, Mamilioni ya waarabu kote katika ukanda huo waliingia katika mitaa ya majiji, miji na vijiji vyao kuandamana wakidai demokrasia, usawa, haki za kibinadamu, kisiasa, kiuchumi na pia mageuzi ya mfumo wa uwakilishi.

eng: Here is a snap shot of reactions from Arab netizens from Twitter.
swa: Haya ni maoni ya wanamtandao wa kiarabu katika Twitter.

swa: Noon Arabia wa Yemen anaota:

swa: @NoonArabia: Ninatamani siku moja na sisi hapa Yemen tujisikie fahari na mtu ambaye “sisi” tumekumchagua mtu kuwa kiongozi wetu, kama ilivyo leo Tunisia. #Yemen #Tunisia

eng: @abubakrabdullah: Amazing - Marzouki's speech at the Tunisian parliament today - I hope to see something similar in Yemen one day..
swa: @abubakrabdullah: Inafurarahisha – hotuba ya Marzouki bungeni Tunisia leo – Natumai kuona siku moja kitu kama hicho kikitokea yemen..

eng: During his swearing in ceremony, Marzouki cried when he mentioned the martyrs during Tunisia's revolution.
swa: Katika hafla ya kuapishwa kwake, Marzouki alilia wakati alipowataja mashahidi waliouwawa wakati wa mapinduzi ya Tunisia.

eng: Journalist Andrew Hammond reports:
swa: Mwanahabari Andrew Hammond anataarifu:

swa: @Hammonda1: #Tunisia rais wa #Tunisia Marzouki alipata kwikwi ya uchungu alipozungumzia wahanga wa mapinduzi; akitoa mfano wa yanayotokea sasa Palestina, Syria na Yemeni.

eng: On this, Egyptian Menna Alaa comments :
swa: Katika hili, Mmisri Menna Alaa anasema :

eng: @TheMiinz: Egypt is not Tunisia because you will never see any one of our officials shedding tears over the martyrs.
swa: @TheMiinz: Misri sio Tunisia kwasababu kamwe hutomuona afisa yeyote akitokwa chozi kwa uchungu wa mashahidi wanaokufa.

eng: And you will never see the Parliament rise up and chant: "If the people wanted to live, destiny would have to respond."
swa: Na kamwe hautaona Bunge likinyanyuka na kuimba: “kama watu wanataka kuishi, takidiri itabidi ikubali.”

swa: Wimbo huo ni sehemu ya wimbo wa taifa wa Tunisia.

eng: Facebook seems to have started playing an important role in Uzbek politics.
swa: Facebook inaonekana kuanza kuchukua jukumu muhimu katika siasa za Uzbek.

eng: However, so far it is more a tool for playing games with fake accounts, rather than an instrument of civil protests.
swa: Hata hivyo , facebook ni imekuwa ni zaidi kwa ajili ya michezo na akaunti za kugushi kuliko chombo kuwa chombo cha harakati za kiraia.

eng: Planted suicide story?
swa: Je habari hii ya kujiua ni ya kupandikizwa?

eng: On 6 December, 2011, Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty reported on a suicide committed by a young woman in the western Uzbek city of Andijan.
swa: Mnamo tarehe 6 Disemba, 2011, Redio Free Europe/Redio Liberty ilitoa taarifa ya kujiua kwa msichana huko kwenye mji wa magharibi ya Uzbek uitwao Andijan.

eng: After coming home on vacation, Gulsumoi Abdujalilova, a 32-year-old university student in Germany, was allegedly interrogated by police for four days.
swa: Baada ya kurudi nyumbani kutoka mapumzikoni, Gulsumoi Abdujalilova, mwenye umri wa miaka 32 mwanafunzi wa chuo kikuu nchini Ujerumani, inasemekana alihojiwa na polisi kwa muda wa siku nne.

eng: According to the Uzbek NGO Human Rights Alliance, Abdujalilova was beaten at the police station and forced to write statements against Muhammad Salih, the self-exiled leader of the opposition People's Movement of Uzbekistan (PMU).
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Shirika Lisilo la Kiserikali la Haki za Binadamu (Uzbek NGO Human Rights Alliance), Abdujalilova alipigwa akiwa kituo cha polisi na kushinikizwa kuandika maelezo dhidi ya Muhammad Salih, kiongozi wa upinzani wa People's Movement of Uzbekistan (PMU) aliye ukimbizini.

eng: The movement was formed in May 2011 from a number of foreign-based Uzbek opposition movements and rights organizations and stated its goal as being the downfall of President Islam Karimov's regime.
swa: Harakati hizi zilianzishwa mnamo Mei 2011 na vikundi mbalimbali vilivyo nje ya Uzbek vyenye msimamo wa kuipinga serikali kwa lengo la kuhakikisha kuwa utawala wa Rais Islam Karimov unaangushwa.

eng: Facebook profile picture of Gulsumoy Abdujalilova, which is actually a photo of turkish model Armine Eşarpları
swa: Picha ya utambulisho wa Gulsumoy Abdujalilova katika ukuta wake wa Facebook, ambayo kiuhalisia ni picha ya mwanamitindo wa Uturuki Armine Eşarpları

eng: According to her Facebook account, Abdujalilova was a supporter of this movement, and a person with the name Muhammad Salih was among her Facebook friends. That was the reason, some netizens believe, that the young woman came to attention of the Uzbek authorities.
swa: Kwa Mujibu wa akaunti yake ya Facebook, AAbdujalilova alikuwa ni mfuasi wa harakati hizo, na mtu aliyejitambulisha kwa jina Muhammad Salih alikuwa mmoja kati ya rafiki zake wa kwenye Facebook.Wanahabari wa mtandaoni na watumiaji wengine wa wavuti wanaamini kuwa hiyo ndio sababu iliyofanya binti huyu kuanza kutupiwa macho na mamlaka za Uzbek.

eng: However, the PMU website has stated that Abdujalilova was never a member of the opposition movement.
swa: Hata hivyo, tovuti ya PMU imeeleza kwamba Abdujalilova hakuwahi kamwe kuwa mwanchama wa harakati hizo.

eng: It’s worth mentioning that Interior Ministry officials in Andijan gave no comment.
swa: Ni vyema pia kueleza kuwa maafisa wa Wizara ya Mambo ya Ndani mjini Andijan hawajatoa maoni yoyote.

eng: Abdujalilova’s relatives (according to her Facebook profile she is married, and Human Rights Alliance mentioned Abdujalilova’s sister who allegedly found her suicide note) have also kept silent.
swa: Ndugu zake Abdujalilova (kwa mujibu wa maelezo yake ya utambulisho kwenye Facebook ameolewa, na Asasi ya Haki za Binadamu imemtaja dada yake Abdujalilova ambaye ndiye aliyeuona ujumbe wa kujiua ulioachwa na mdogo wake) nae pia amekaa kimya.

eng: The story became more perplexing when two days later, on 8 December, the opposition site Uzmetronom.com published an article with the results of a journalistic investigation, carried out by the website.
swa: Habari hii ilizidi kuwa na utata siku mbili baadaye, mnamo tarehe 8 desemba, pale tovuti ya upinzani Uzmetronom.com ilipochapisha makala yenye matokeo ya uanahabari wa kipelelezi uliofanywa na tovuti hiyo.

eng: The author of the article, who remained anonymous, concluded that the entire story is provocation prepared by Muhammad Salih to destabilize Uzbek society and gain international attention.
swa: Mwandishi wa makala hiyo ambaye hakujifahamisha, alihitimisha kuwa habari hii yote ni uchochezi ulioandaliwa na Muhammad Salih ili kutikisa jamii ya Uzbek na kutafuta kujulikana kimataifa.

eng: The story has attracted the attention of netizens.
swa: Habari hii imewavuta watumiaji wa wavuti.

eng: One of them comments on the idea that it may have been planted by members of the Uzbek opposition in order to smear the Uzbek government.
swa: Mmoja wao ametoa maoni juu ya dhana kuwa inawezekana kuwa jambo hili limepandikizwa na upinzani wa kuichafua serikali ya Uzbek.

eng: Other suggest that it was made up by the national security services to show people the dangers of supporting the opposition movement.
swa: Mwingine akasema kwamba hii imefanywa na kitengo cha usalama wa taifa ili kuwaonesha raia hatari za kushirikiana na wapinzani wa serikali.

eng: It still remains unclear who could benefit from the made-up story and probably this will not be known.
swa: Bado haijawa wazi nani atafaidika katokana na habari hii ya kutungwa na p ngine hilo halitajulikana kamwe.

eng: Sarah Kendzior from Registan.net sums up:
swa: Sarah Kendzior wa Registan.net anakamilisha:

eng: it reveals a great deal of how rumor operates on the Uzbek political internet.
swa: inaweka wazi ni kwa kiasi gani uvumi unavyofanya kazi katika mtandaoni wa siasa wa Uzbek.

eng: The assumption that all information is unreliable, and all sources biased, has had the perverse effect of ensuring that all rumor is taken seriously.
swa: Dhana ya kwamba taarifa zote si za kuaminika, na kuwa vyanzo vyote hupendelea upande fulani, imeweza kuwa na madhara ya makusudi ili kuhakikisha kwamba kila uvumi unachukuliwa maanani.

eng: Prime Minister’s fake Facebook account
swa: Akaunti ya uongo ya Waziri Mkuu katika Facebook

eng: Another topic that has sparked controversy among Uzbek bloggers was the Facebook account of Uzbekistan’s Prime-Minister Shavkat Mirziyoyev.
swa: Mada nyingine ambayo imeleta utata mkubwa kati ya wanablogu wa Uzbek ni akaunti ya Facebook ya Waziri Mkuu wa Uzbekistan Shavkat Mirziyoyev.

eng: His Facebook page, created early in May this year, has about 2,000 friends and identifies him as a 100% Muslim with conservative political views, interested in women and married.
swa: Akaunti hii ilianzishwa mapema mwezi Mei mwaka huu, ina takribani marafiki 2,000 na inamtambulisha yeye kama Muislamu kwa asilimia 100 mwenye mtazamo wa siasa za kihafidhina, aneyependelea wanawake na ameoa.

eng: Catherine A. Fitzpatrick from Eurasianet.org comments:
swa: Catherine A. Fitzpatrick wa Eurasianet.org anasema:

eng: you can see that Mirziyoyev is inspired by Nicolas Sarkozy, Lee Myung-bak, Barack Obama, Vladimir Putin and Islam Karimov.
swa: unaweza kuona kuwa Mirziyoyev ametiwa moyo na Nicolas Sarkozy, Lee Myung-bak, Barack Obama, Vladimir Putin and Islam Karimov.

eng: His gmail address is provided, so write and ask any questions!
swa: Anuani yake ya barua pepe ya gmail imewekwa, kwa hiyo mwandikie na uulize swali lolote!

eng: Don't expect any cat or dog photos, however.
swa: Hata hivyo usitarajie picha za paka au mbwa.

eng: Others wonder why the Prime Minister doesn’t have a personal page on Uzbekistan’s local social network Muloqot.uz and speculate that the main goal of his Facebook page is to attract a Western audience.
swa: Wengine wanajiuliza kwa nini Waziri Mkuu hana ukurasa katika mtandao ya kijamii nchini humo Muloqot.uz wanakisia kuwa lengo la ukurasa wake wa facebook ni kuvutia watu wa Magharibi

eng: However, after a semi-official statement from the Prime Minister's “offline office” about contacting the Facebook administration with a request to delete the page, it became clear that the account is not authentic.
swa: Hata hivyo, baada ya tamko lisilo rasmi kutoka kwenye ofisi ya Waziri Mkuu kuhusu kuwasiliana na uongozi Facebook wakiwa na ombi la kuufuta ukurasa huo, ndipo ilipojulikana wazi kuwa akaunti hiyo haikuwa halisi

eng: Dangers of being too public
swa: Hatari ya kuwa hadharani sana

eng: This is not the first time that high-ranking Uzbek public figures’ names have been used for suspicious accounts in social networks.

eng: This post is part of our special coverage on Refugees. In recent weeks Global Voices has presented to its readers more examples of how citizen media is used to amplify the voices of refugees and displaced people.
swa: Katika wiki za hivi karibuni Global Voices imeendelea kuwakilisha kwa wasomaji wake mifano zaidi ya jinsi uanahabari wa kiraia unavyotumika kuwawezesha wakimbizi na watu wasio na makazi.

eng: However, while blogs and social networking sites clearly have a role to play in empowering marginalized groups, so too do ICTs in general.
swa: Hata hivyo, wakati ambapo blogu na mitandao ya kijamii ikiwa bado inaendelea kukuza sauti, hivyo pia ndivyo tasnia ya TEKNOHAMA inavyofanya kwa ujumla.

eng: MobileActive, for example, is encouraged by the potential for mobile phones to allow refugees to not only remain in contact with loved ones, but to also more easily locate them.
swa: Kwa mfano, MobileActive, inahamasishwa na uwezo wa simu za mkononi zinavyowawezesha wakimbizi siyo tu kuwasiliana na wapendwa wao, bali pia kuweza kujua mahali walipo.

eng: Attention is especially drawn to a special issue of Forced Migration Review which takes an in-depth look at the use of ICTs in this context.
swa: Tovuti hiyo inawaonyesha wasomaji wake makala maalum ya Jarida la Uhamiaji wa Kulazimishwa ambalo linaangalia kwa kina suala la Teknohama katika muktadha huu.

eng: Refugees in Uganda are using SMS and cellphones to reconnect with family members and close friends.
swa: Wakimbizi nchini Uganda wakitumia simu za mkononi kuwasiliana na jamaa pamoja na marafiki wa karibu.

eng: Photo via MobileActive
swa: Picha kupitia Mobile Active.

eng: Refugees often experience a compound trauma: The situation that caused them to flee in the first place, as well as the fact that many families become separated during migration.
swa: Wakimbizi mara nyingi hufikwa na athari lukuki: Hali ambayo kwanza ilisababisha wakimbie, vile vile ukweli kwamba familia nyingi husambaratika wakati wa kuhama.

eng: For refugee's health and well-being and ability to resettle, it is vital to know the whereabouts of relatives, their safety, and their ability to remain in contact.
swa: Ili kuwa na afya njema na ustawi na uwezo wa kutulia tena, ni muhimu kufahamu walipo ndugu na jamaa, usalama wao, na uwezo wao wa kuendelea kuwasiliana.

eng: Today, mobile phones are the most important technology for refugees to find relatives and remain in contact.
swa: Leo hii, simu za mkononi ni teknolojia ya muhimu zaidi kwa wakimbizi ili kuweza kuwapata ndugu na kuendelea kuwasiliana nao.

eng: The Forced Migration Review Issue 38, The Technology Issue covers technologies for refugees in particular.
swa: Jarida la Uhamiaji wa Kulazimishwa Toleo la 38, Nakala ya Teknolojia inapitia teknolojia hususan kwa ajili ya wakimbizi.

eng: Two chapters shine a light on the use of mobile phones among refugees, as well as some of the problems with this tech to find and contact family member such as issues of security, and accessibility.
swa: Sura mbili (za jarida hilo) zinaangaza nuru juu ya matumizi ya simu za mkononi baina ya wakimbizi, aidha juu ya baadhi ya matatizo ya teknolojia hii katika kutafuta na kuwasiliana na ndugu kama vile suala la usalama na upatikanaji.

eng: Deputy UN High Commissioner for Refugees T Alexander Aleinikoff provides an introduction to the special issue:
swa: Naibu Kamishna wa Umoja wa Mataifa kwa Ajili ya Wakimbizi T Alexander Aleinikoff ametoa utangulizi katika toleo hilo maalum:

eng: Superficially at least, today’s refugee camps do not appear significantly different from those that existed 30 or 40 years ago.
swa: Japokuwa kwa juu juu, kambi za wakimbizi za leo hazionekani tofauti sana na vile zilivyokuwa miaka 30 au 40 iliyopita.

eng: Modernisation seems to have passed them by.
swa: Inaonekana kana kwamba maendeleo yamewapitia mbali.

eng: But upon a closer look, it becomes apparent that things are changing.
swa: Lakini ukiangalia kwa karibu, ni wazi kuwa mambo yanabadilika.

eng: Today, refugees and IDPs in the poorest of countries often have access to a mobile phone and are able to watch satellite TV.
swa: Hivi sasa, wakimbizi na watu walipoteza makazi katika nchi maskini zaidi mara nyingi huwa na uwezo wa kupata simu za mkononi na wana uwezo wa kuangalia televisheni za setilaiti.

eng: Internet cafés have sprung up in some settlements, the hardware purchased by refugee entrepreneurs or donated by humanitarian organisations such as UNHCR.
swa: Migahawa ya intaneti imechipuka katika sehemu walizofikia, na vifaa vimenunuliwa na wajasiriamali wakimbizi au vilivyotolewa na mashirika ya misaada ya kibinadamu kama vile UNHCR.

eng: And aid agencies themselves are increasingly making use of advanced technology: geographic information systems, Skype, biometric databases and Google Earth, to give just a few examples.
swa: Na mashirika ya misaada yanaongeza matumizi ya teknolojia za kileo zaidi: kama vile mifumo ya taarifa za jiografia, Skype, takwimu za biometrika pamoja na Google earth, vikiwa kama ni mifano michache.

eng: In one article, the example of a tracing project implemented by the Refugee Consortium of Kenya (RCK) in cooperation with Refugees United (RU) is highlighted:
swa: Katika makala moja, mfano wa mradi wa kutafuta watu ulitekelezwa na ushirika wa Wakimbizi nchini Kenya (RCK) kwa kushirikiana na Umoja wa Wakimbizi (RU) umeonyeshwa:

eng: In 1991 Ahmed Hassan Osman* fled the conflict in Somalia, leaving his family in Kismayu, and made his way to Kenya in search of asylum.
swa: Mwaka 1991 Ahmed Hasan Osman* alikimbia mtafaruku huku Somalia, na kuiacha familia yake mjini Kismayu, na kufanya safari ya kuelekea Kenya ili kutafuta hifadhi.

eng: Ahmed lived for a while in Ifo refugee camp before being resettled to Colorado in the US where he was granted full US citizenship.
swa: Ahmed aliishi kwa muda kwenye kambi ya wakimbizi ya Ifo kabla ya kupewa makazi huko Colorado nchini Marekani ambako alipewa uraia kamili wa Marekani.

eng: In 1992, his cousin Abdulahi Sheikh arrived in Kenya in search of support. Granted refugee status, Abdulahi ended up in Dagahaley camp in Dadaab.
swa: Mwaka 1992, binamu yake Abdulahi Sheikh aliwasili nchini Kenya akitafuta msaada, alipopewa hadhi ya ukimbizi, Abdulahi aliishia kwenye kambi ya Dagahaley huko Dadaab.

eng: He believed Ahmed was either in Dadaab or had been there but his efforts to find him were unsuccessful and he soon gave up hope of ever finding him.
swa: Aliamini kuwa Ahmed alikuwa ama mjini Dadaab au aliwahi kuwepo pale lakini jitihada zake za kumtafuta hazikuzaa matunda na pindi alikata tama ya kumpata.

eng: In fact, Abdulahi believed Ahmed had gone back to Somalia.
swa: Bila ya shaka, Abdulahi aliamini kuwa Ahmed alikuwa kesharejea Somalia.

eng: In early 2011 RCK employed Abdulahi to assist the RU project in Dagahaley refugee camp.
swa: Mapema mwaka 2011 RCK ilimuajiri Abdulahi ili kusaidiamradi wa RU kwenye kambi ya wakimbizi ya Dagahaley.

eng: Abdulahi registered with the tracing project and began a search for missing loved ones.
swa: Abdilahi alijiunga na mradi wa kutafuta watu na kuanza kuwatafutwa wapendwa waliopotea.

eng: Coming across a name that was familiar, he contacted the person through the RU message system.
swa: Alipoliona jina analolifahamu, aliwasiliana na mtu huyo kwa kupitia mfumo wa ujumbe mfupi wa simu wa RU.

eng: When he received a reply he realised that, after 20 years of separation and search, he had found his beloved cousin. They exchanged phone numbers and Ahmed called, breaking 20 years of silence.
swa: Pale alipopata majibu aligundua kwamba, baada ya miaka 20 ya kutengana na kutafutana, alimpata binamu yake mpendwa.

eng: Today, the two keep in touch regularly and both Abdulahi and Ahmed continue to search for more friends and family members.
swa: Leo hii, watu hawa wawili wanawasiliana kila mara na wote Abdulahi na Ahmed wanaendelea kusaka marafiki na wanafamilia zaidi.

eng: Of course, as MobileActive also stresses, some problems with local infrastructure remain an obstacle to the widespread adoption of such systems:
swa: Bila ya shaka, kama vile MobileActive inavyosisitiza, matatizo kadhaa ya miundombinu yanaendelea kuwa kizuizi kwa matumizi makubwa ya mfumo huo:

eng: In some areas of Africa, there is no telecommunications coverage.
swa: Kwenye baadhi ya maeneo ya Afrika, hakuna mtandao wa mawasiliano.

eng: Workshop participants commented that where it does exist, phone connections are regularly cut off, and some of them had also experienced intrusion in communication such as crossed lines.
swa: Washiriki wa warsha walitoa maoni kuwa pale ambapo (mtandao) upo, simu hukatwa mara kwa mara, na baadhi hukutwa na maingiliano ya mawasiliano kama vile kuingiliana kwa simu.

eng: The strength of the network signal overseas is weak, and the lack of a reliable or steady source of electricity in a recipient’s country can be a major problem, although this varies by region.
swa: Nguvu ya mtandao wa mawasiliano kwenda nje ya nchi ni dhaifu, na ukosefu wa chanzo cha uhakika na madhubuti cha umeme kwenye nchi za wapokeaji unaweza kuwa tatizo, japokuwa hili linatofautiana kanda kwa kanda.

eng: Growth of populations in some areas weakens network strength, due to the drain on power.
swa: Ongezeko la idadi ya watu katika baadhi ya maeneo hudhoofisha nguvu ya mtandao, kutokana na matumizi makubwa ya umeme.

eng: Individuals may also have difficulty accessing electricity to charge their mobile phones.
swa: Watu wanaweza pia kuwa na ugumu wa kupata umeme wa kuchaji simu zao za mkononi.

eng: Finding the best technology to use for different family members can be difficult, particularly if they themselves are displaced, because of factors such as the variety of available services, whether the family member could afford them and whether they have the skills to use them.
swa: Kupata teknolojia bora zaidi ya kutumia kwa wanafamilia tofauti kunaweza kuwa vigumu, hasa iwapo wao wenyewe wamepoteza makazi, kutokana na sababu kama wingi wa huduma zilizopo, kama wanafamilia wanaweza kuzimudu na kama wana ujuzi wa kuzitumia.

eng: One participant observed that the majority of their family members overseas needed to access communication technology through others.
swa: Mshiriki mmoja alibainisha kuwa wengi wa wanafamilia walio ng’ambo inawabidi kupata teknolojia za mawasiliano kwa kupitia watu wengine.

eng: One participant described the difficulties she had in contacting her husband in a camp.
swa: Mshiriki mmoja alielezea matatizo aliyoyapata kuwasiliana na mumewe aliyekuwa kambini.

eng: She sent money to him to buy a phone but other people in the camp would also use it leaving her often waiting for hours to get in touch.
swa: Alimtumia pesa za kununulia simu lakini watu wengine kambini pia hutumia simu hiyo hiyo na aghalabu kumfanya asubiri kwa masaa ili apate kuwasiliana na mumewe.

eng: Cheap options such as email, voice-over-internet or instant messaging may not be accessible or affordable, and access to the internet in Africa is very expensive.
swa: Njia mbadala za bei nafuu kama vile barua pepe, au simu za kwenye intaneti au ujumbe mfupi wa maneno zinaweza kuwa hazipatikani au aghali, na upatikanaji wa intaneti barani Afrika ni ghali mno.

eng: Furthermore, displaced family members overseas may not know how to use these facilities.
swa: Zaidi ya hivyo, wanafamilia waliopoteza makazi walioko ng’ambo wanaweza kuwa hawajui kutumia vifaa hivi.

eng: From providing refugees with access to information on health and educational opportunities to using Facebook, Gmail Chat and Skype to maintain connections with family members and friends across geographical divides, the issue provides a comprehensive overview of how ICTs are being used.
swa: Kutoka kuwapa wakimbizi upatikanaji wa habari juu ya afya na fursa za elimu mpaka utumiaji wa Facebook, maongezi kwa ktumia Gmail na Skype ili kudumisha mawasiliano na wanafamilia na marafiki kuvuka mipaka ya kijiografia, toleo hili limetoa picha kamili ya jinsi gani Tknohama inavyotumika.

eng: Ushahidi also gets a mention in relation to the 2010 earthquake in Haiti as well as in general as it pertains to conflict, disaster and refugees.
swa: Ushahidi pia imetajwa ikihusishwa na tetemeko la ardhi nchini Haiti mwaka 2010 na vile vile kwa ujumla wakekama inavyohusiana na migogoro, majanga na wakimbizi.

eng: Indeed, PBS' Idea Lab takes a look at an Al Jazeera and Ushahidi collaboration to connect and empower Somalis separated by conflict and famine:
swa: Kadhalika, Maabara ya Fikra ya PBS inaangalia ushirikiano wa Al Jazeera na Ushahidi katika kuwaunganisha na kuwawezesha waSomali waliotenganishwa na vita pamoja na ukame:

eng: Somalia Speaks is a collaboration between Souktel, a Palestinian-based organization providing SMS messaging services, Ushahidi, Al Jazeera, Crowdflower, and the African Diaspora Institute.
swa: Somalia Speaks (Somalia Inaongea) ni ushirika kati ya Souktel, shirika lililoko Palestina linalotoa huduma za ujumbe wa simu za mkononi, Ushahidi, Al Jazeera, Crowdflower, pamoja na Taasisi ya Waafrika Walio Ughaibuni.

eng: We wanted to find out the perspective of normal Somali citizens to tell us how the crisis has affected them and the Somali diaspora, Al Jazeera's Soud Hyder said in an interview.
swa: “Tulitaka tupate mitizamo ya raia wa kawaida wa Somalia ili kwamba ituambie jinsi ambavyo mgogoro ulivyowaathiri wao pamoja na waSomali walio ighaibuni,” Soud Hyder wa Al Jazeera alisema katika mahojiano.

eng: The goal of Somalia Speaks is to aggregate unheard voices from inside the region as well as from the Somalia diaspora by asking via text message: How has the Somalia Conflict affected your life?
swa: Lengo la Somalia Speaks ni kukusanya sauti ambazo hazisikiki kutokea ndani ya eneo vile vile kutokea kwa waSomali walio ughaibuni kwa kuuliza kupitia ujumbe mfupi wa simu za mkononi: Kwa jinsi gani mgogoro wa Somalia umekuathiri?

eng: Responses are translated into English and plotted on a map.
swa: Majibu hutafsiriwa kwa Kiingereza na kupachikwa kwenye ramani.

eng: Since the launch, approximately 3,000 SMS messages have been received.
swa: Tangu kuzinduliwa, takriban jumbe 3,000 za simu za mkononi zimepokelewa.

eng: For Al Jazeera, Somalia Speaks is also a chance to test innovative mobile approaches to citizen media and news gathering.
swa: Kwa Al Jazeera, Somalia Speaks pia ni fursa ya kujaribu mbinu bunifu za simu za mkononi katika uanahabari wa kiraia na ukusanyaji habari.

eng: In October 2010, MobileActive also profiled a mobile-based project implemented by Refugees United in Uganda with the support of Ericsson, UNHCR and the Omidyar Network, noting that one blog called it "the social network that is more important than Facebook.”
swa: Mnamo mwezi Oktoba 2010, MobileActive ilionyesha pia mradi wa simu za mkononi uliotekelezwa na Asasi ya Refugees United nchini Uganda kwa msaada wa Ericsson, UNHCR na Mtandao wa Omidyar, na kueleza kuwa kuna blogu moja ilyouita (mradi huo) “mtandao wa kijamii ambao ni muhimu zaidi ya Facebook.”

eng: The Technology Issue by Forced Migration Review can be read online here. This post is part of our special coverage on Refugees.
swa: Nakala ya teknolojia ya Jarida la Uhamiaji wa Kulazimishwa inaweza kusomwa kwenye mtandao hapa.

eng: Christmas 2011 in Côte d'Ivoire was different from those of previous years.
swa: Sikukuu ya Noeli ya mwaka 2011 nchini Ivory Coast ilikuwa tofauti na zile za miaka iliyopita.

eng: Eight months after the change of regime, the authorities wanted to mark it with completely new decorations in the country and by organizing huge fireworks displays on December 30-31, 2011.
swa: Miezi nane tangu kubadilika kwa utawala, serikali ilitaka kuiadhimisha sikukuu hii kwa mapambo mapya kabisa ya Noeli nchini humo na kwa kuandaa maonyesho makubwa ya milipuko ya fataki mnamo Desemba 30-31, 2011.

eng: A great many Ivorians went out to take advantage of these various spectacles and the supporting technology, and everyone left with souvenir photos.
swa: Wananchi wengi wa Ivory Coast walitoka kwenda kushuhudia burudani hizi pamoja na teknolojia inayotumika, na kila mtu aliondoka na picha za ukumbusho.

eng: If it was a good experience for these amateur photographers, that was not the case for Audrey Carlalie .
swa: Kama huo ulikuwa ni uzoefu mzuri kwa wapiga picha hawa wasio na utaalamu mkubwa, basi haikuwa hivyo kwa Audrey Carlalie .

eng: This young Ivorian student, a professional part-time photographer, saw her photos of the fireworks display published by certain Ivorian newspapers and even the largest online Ivorian information portal - without her permission.
swa: Mwanafunzi huyu mdogo wa ki-Ivory Coast, mpiga picha mwenye taaluma hiyo ambaye hukodiwa kwa muda maalumu, aliziona picha zake za milipuko ya fataki zikiwa zimechapishwa na magazeti fulani ya nchi hiyo na hata kwenye mtandao maarufu zaidi wa kukusanya habari nchini humo –pasipo ruhusa yake.

eng: She did not hesitate to complain on her Facebook page, and soon the blogs and other social networks had picked up the buzz.
swa: Hakuchelewa kulalamika kwenye ukurasa wake wa Facebook, na muda mfupi baadae zogo zikatapakaa kwenye blogu na mitandao mingine ya kijamii.

swa: Mwanablogu huyo wa Ivory Coast Edith Brou anaanzisha habari hiyo kwenye blogu yake na anaeleza:

swa: Makala hii ni sehemu ya habari zetu maalumu za Global Voices mwaka 2011.

eng: Our top 20 list of most read posts on Global Voices for 2011 includes four from Japan, three from Egypt, and two from the Philippines.
swa: Orodha yetu ya makala 20 bora zilizosomwa zaidi kwenye tovuti ya Global Voices kwa mwaka 2011 ni pamoja na nne kutoka Japan, tatu kutoka Misri, na mbili kutoka Ufilipino.

eng: But only one story is about a giant crocodile!
swa: Lakini habari moja tu inahusu yule mamba mkubwa!

eng: It's been an incredible year for the reach and recognition of citizen media around the world, and that means Global Voices is no longer as lonely a media voice when it comes to reporting tweets and blog posts.
swa: Umekuwa mwaka wa ajabu kwa vyombo vya kiraia duniani kote ambavyo viliweza kufika mbali zaidi na kutambuliwa, na hiyo ina maana Global Voices haijabaki kuwa sauti pweke ya vyombo vya habari vya kiraia linapokuja suala la twita zinazotuma taarifa na posti za kwenye blogu.

eng: Still, where mainstream media interest wanes, we're the ones who strive to continue documenting what local bloggers everywhere need the world to know.
swa: Bado, hata hivyo pale ambapo shauku kwa vyombo vikuu vya habari ikindelea kupungua, sisi ndio tunaojibidiisha kuendelea kuweka kumbukumbu ya kile ambacho wanablogu wadogo popote pale walipo wanataka dunia ikifahamu.

eng: Self Defence Forces arrive at the scene of the tsunami in Japan.
swa: Kikosi cha Ulinzi kikiwasili kwenye eneo lililokubwa na Tsunami nchini Japan.

eng: Image by cosmobot, copyright Demotix (13/03/11).
swa: Picha ya cosmobot, haki miliki Demotix (13/03/11).

eng: Some of our proudest moments of 2011 will never be reflected on a top 20 list like the one below.
swa: Baadhi ya nyakati tulizojivunia zaidi mwaka 2011 hazitaweza kuakisiwa katika orodha ya makala bora 20 kama hii iliyopo hapa chini.

eng: This year we exceeded 500 active volunteer authors and translators of countless languages and countries, and we've published more than 2,600 long posts and 6,300 short ones in English alone.
swa: Mwaka huu idadi ya waandishi na wafasiri hai ilizidi 500 wa lugha na nchi zisizo na idadi, na tulichapisha zaidi ya makala ndefu 2,600 na zile fupi fupi zipatazo 6,300 kwa Kiingereza peke yake.

eng: Inevitably, many of the stories that don't get as wide a readership as they deserve are from countries that tend to be overlooked in international media.
swa: Haikwepeki kwamba, habari nyingi ambazo huwa hazipati usomaji mkubwa kuliko zinavyostahili zinatoka kwenye nchi ambazo hupuuzwa na vyombo vikuu vya habari.

eng: Unique coverage from across Africa, the Caucasus, Macedonia, the Russian language Internet, Latin America and indigenous rights are among some of the highlights.
swa: Uhabarishwaji wa aina yake kuanzia Africa, Caucasus, Macedonia, the Mtandao wa lugha ya Kirusi, , Marekani ya Kusini na haki za wenyeji ni baadhi tu ya dondoo za habari hizi.

eng: See the 2011 regional reviews by our editors and authors for a glance of what you may have missed.
swa: Angalia mapitio ya kimaeneo kwa mwaka 2011 yaliyofanywa na wahariri na waandishi ili kupata taswira ya haraka ya kile ambacho huenda ulikikosa.

eng: Our Middle East and North Africa team deserves special mention this year.
swa: Timu yetu ya Mashariki ya Kati na Afrika Kaskazini inastahili kutambuliwa kwa uzito wa pekee mwaka huu.

eng: Throughout protests, blackouts, threats, they have managed to pull though and keep writing.
swa: Wakati wote wa maandamano, kukatwa kwa mawasiliano, vitisho nk waliweza kujipiga moyo konde na kuendelea kuandika.

eng: The bloody images still proliferate, but our authors seek out constructive voices and angles for dialogue.
swa: Picha za mauaji bado zinashika kasi, lakini waandishi wetu wanatafuta sauti zinazojenga na mitazamo inayofaa kwa majadiliano.

eng: So often, they've shared local humor and context that is difficult to appreciate from abroad without a guide.
swa: Mara nyingi wametushirikisha habari za ucheshi kutoka maeneo yao na mikhtadha ambayo huwa ni vigumu kuielewa ukiwa nchi nyingine bila miongozo yao.

eng: Perhaps for the first time ever, China doesn't figure on our top 20 list of the year.
swa: Huenda ni kwa mara ya kwanza kabisa, China haionekani kwenye orodha yetu ya makala 20 bora zaidi kwa mwaka huu.

eng: These are particularly chilling times to blog about controversial subjects - something Global Voices authors in many other countries unfortunately also experience.
swa: Hizi pengine ni nyakati ngumu kublogu kuhusu mada tete –jambo ambalo kwa bahati mbaya sana waandishi wengi wa Global Voices katika nchi nyingine nyingi wanakabiliana nalo.

eng: This makes the stories that do come from anywhere free speech is frowned on even more precious.
swa: Hali hii ndiyo inayozifanya habari zinazokuja kutoka mahali popote ambapo haki ya kujieleza imebanwa kuwa na uthamani wa pekee.

swa: Mwaka 2011 dunia imejifunza zaidi juu ya nguvu ya mabadiliko iliyo kwenye vyombo vya habari za kiraia vya mtandaoni.

eng: We believe the best way to support these emerging voices on a global scale is to listen.
swa: Tunaamini njia bora zaidi ya kuunga mkono sauti hizi zinazochipukia kwa kiwango cha dunia ni kusikiza.

swa: Asante kwa kusoma tovuti ya Global Voices!

swa: Na tafadhali fikiria kuunga mkono kazi yetu kwamchango wako
