swa: Makala hii ni sehemu ya habari zetu maalumu za Global Voices mwaka 2011.

eng: With the following statement, Senior Minister of State for Ministry of Environment and Water Resources Grace Fu sparked off an online controversy amongst Singaporeans:
swa: Kufuatia tamko lifuatalo, Waziri wa Nchi mwenye dhamana ya Mazingira na Maji, Grace Fu, aliibua mkanganyiko miongoni mwa raia wa Singapore:

eng: When I made the decision to join politics in 2006, pay was not a key factor.
swa: Nilipofanya uamuzi wa kuingia kwenye siasa mwaka 2006, suala la malipo halikuwa kichocheo.

eng: Loss of privacy, public scrutiny on myself and my family and loss of personal time were.
swa: Nilitambua wazi kuwa ningepoteza faragha, mimi na familia yangu tungechunguzwa sana, na hata kupoteza muda wangu mwingi.

eng: The disruption to my career was also an important consideration.
swa: Nilizingatia pia kwamba kazi yangu ya kitaaluma ingeingiliwa.

eng: I had some ground to believe that my family would not suffer a drastic change in the standard of living even though I experienced a drop in my income.
swa: Hata hivyo, nilikuwa na sababu za kuamini kwamba familia isingeathiriwa sana, japokuwa uamuzi huo ulifanya kipato kupungua.

eng: So it is with this recent pay cut.
swa: Na ndivyo ilivyokuwa kwenye punguzo la kipato la hivi karibuni.

eng: If the balance is tilted further in the future, it will make it harder for any one considering political office.
swa: Kama kilichobaki kitaendelea kupunguzwa siku za baadaye, basi wale wanaotaka kuwania nafasi ya kisiasa itawapasa kujiuliza mara mbilimbili.

eng: Minister Grace Fu.
swa: Waziri Grace Fu.

eng: Image from Wikipedia.
swa: Picha imechukuliwa kwenye mtandao wa Wikipedia.

eng: Following the recent announcement of paycuts for ministers – which many Singaporeans feel are still not enough – Ms Fu's comments angered many who felt that those who go into public service should not do so in the expectation of huge public rewards.
swa: Kufuatia tangazo la hivi karibuni la kupunguza mishahara kwa mawaziri –hatua ambayo wa-Singapore wengi bado wanaamini bado si ya kiwango cha kuridhisha –Maoni ya Mhe. Fu yaliwakasirisha wengi waliofikiri kwamba wale wanaowania utumishi wa umma hawapaswi kufanya hivyo kwa matarajio ya kupata malipo makubwa kupitia fedha za wananchi.

eng: Ms Fu has since come out to say that her statement had been misunderstood, something which I have observed to happen to the ruling People's Action Party members very often:
swa: Fu kujitokeza na kueleza kwamba tamko lake lilieleweka visivyo, jambo ambalo nimekuwa nikiliona likijitokeza kwa wananachama wa chama tawala cha PAP (People’s Action Party) mara nyingi:

eng: Teenagers, goths and emos should just step aside.
swa: Hebu vijana wadogo, watu wasiostaarabika na watu wasiodhibiti hasira zao wakae pembeni.

eng: People’s Action Party (PAP) members are by far the most misunderstood group of people in the world.
swa: Wanachama wa chama cha People’s Action Party (PAP) ndilo kundi la watu wanaoongoza kwa kutokueleweka duniani.

eng: It appears as if they can’t say or do a thing without being misunderstood.
swa: Inaonekana kama vile hawawezi kusema ama kufanya kitu bila kutokueleweka.

eng: If they went to a MacDonald’s to buy a Big Mac with extra lettuce and no pickles they’d probably get Fillet o’ Fish.
swa: Kama wakienda kwenye duka la MacDonald kununua chakula cha Big Mac chenye mbogamboga zaidi ila bila rojo ya pilipili bila shaka wangenunua mnofu wa samaki (Fillet o’Fish).

eng: Ms Fu's clarification of her statement hasn't been successful in placating irked Singaporeans, as many have observed that she is still extremely well-paid compared to the average Singaporean.
swa: Ufafanuzi wa Mhe. Fu kuhusu tamko lake haujafanikiwa kupooza hasira za wa-Singapore waliokerwa na maneno yake, kwa sababu wengi wanaona kwamba bado analipwa vizuri kupindukia ikilinganishwa na wa-Singapore wa kawaida.

eng: Mollymeek writes sarcastically about how Ms Fu could have been misunderstood:
swa: Mollymeek anaandika kwa kejeli kuhusiana na namna Mhe. Fu alivyoeleweka vibaya:

eng: Because of our inability to imagine the standard of living that would be compromised by a million-dollar salary, it is easy for us to think that she is materialistic.
swa: Kwa sababu ya kukosa kwetu uwezo wa kufikiri mtindo wa maisha unaoweza kuhalalishwa kwa mshahara wa dola za marekani milioni moja, ni rahisi kwetu kufikiri kwamba anajali mali zaidi.

eng: It is our fault.
swa: Ni kosa letu.

eng: She is not materialistic.
swa: Huyu mama haangalii mali.

eng: She is not demanding a higher pay.
swa: Wala hadai mshahara mnono zaidi.

eng: It is just that her standard of living is so inconceivably high that she may face difficulties making ends meet if she were to be paid the average salary of a minister in the developed world.
swa: Ni ile tu kwamba mtindo wake wa maisha uko juu kupita kiasi kwamba anaweza kukumbana na ugumu wa kulipia anavyovitumia kama angekuwa alipwe mshahara wa kawaida wa Waziri katika nchi zilizoendelea.

eng: Ms Fu's comment soon turned into an Internet meme, with people posting their own versions.
swa: Fu ndani ya muda mfupi yaligeuka kuwa zogo la mtandaoni, ambapo watu waliiga na kuweka maneno yao wenyewe.

eng: Lee Kin Mun writes about his choice to become Singapore's "blogfather" mrbrown:
swa: Lee Kin Mun anaandika kuhusu uchaguzi wake wa kuwa “baba wa blogu” ya Singapore yaani Mrbrown:

eng: When I made the decision to be mrbrown in 1997, pay was not a key factor.
swa: Nilipofanya uamuzi wa kuwa mrbrown mwaka 1997, malipo hayakuwa sababu ya msingi.

eng: Kena lim kopi by ISD, kena sue until tng kor by ministers and having my newspaper column suspended were.
swa: Kena limy kopi ya ISD, “kena sue” mpaka “tng kor” ya mawaziri na kusimamishwa kwa safu yangu ya gazeti ndivyo vilikuwa sababu.

eng: The disruption to my computer gaming time was also an important consideration.
swa: Kupoteza muda niliokuwa nautumia kwenye kucheza michezo ya kompyuta nayo ilikuwa sababu muhimu kuiangalia.

eng: I had some ground to believe that my family would not suffer a drastic change in the standard of living but we did have to sell the car and now I ride a bicycle.
swa: Nilikuwa na sababu ya kufikiri kwamba familia yangu isingekumbana na mabadiliko makubwa ya mtindo wa maisha lakini tuliuza gari na sasa naendesha baiskeli.

eng: I fear if the balance is tilted further in the future, I will fall off my bicycle.
swa: Ninaogopa kwamba kama hata kilichobaki kitapunguzwa kwa mara nyingine huko mbeleni, nitakula mweleka na baiskeli yangu pia.

eng: Joshua Chiang on his decision to join socio-political website The Online Citizen:
swa: Joshua Chiang katika uamuzi wa kujiunga na wavuti ya masuala ya kijamii na kisiasa The Online Citizen:

eng: When I made the decision to join TOC in 2009, pay was not a key factor (since it was non-existent).
swa: Joshua Chiang Nilipofanya uamuzi wa kujiunga na wavuti wa The Online Citizen mwaka 2009, mshahara haukuwa sababu ya msingi (kwanza haukuwepo).

eng: Loss of freedom vis-a-vis ISA , character assassination by the mainstream press on myself and my family and loss of my entire fortunes via defamation suits was.
swa: Kupoteza uhuru hasa hasa ISA, kuchafuliwa mimi binafsi pamoja na familia yangu kulikofanywa na vyombo vikuu vya habari na kupoteza fursa zangu zote kupitia mashitaka ya kuchafuana ndizo hasa zilikuwa sababu.

eng: The disruption to my sanity was also an important consideration.
swa: Kupoteza kwa utulivu wa akili yangu lilikuwa suala la kutazama sana.

eng: I had some ground to believe that my family would have more room space at home if I were ever jailed.
swa: Nilikuwa na sababu ya kuamini kwamba familia yangu ingekuwa na nafasi zaidi ya chumba kimoja pale nyumbani kama ningewekwa ndani.

eng: Especially when TOC was gazetted.
swa: Hasa wakati ule tovuti yetu ilipotangazwa kwenye gazeti la serikali.

eng: If the balance is tilted further in the future, it will make it harder for any one considering citizen journalism/activism.
swa: Kama malipo yaliyobaki yataendelea kuminywa zaidi huko mbeleni, itakuwa vigumu kwa yeyote anayefikiri kujiunga na uandishi/uanaharakati wa kiraia.

eng: Even Danny the Democracy Bear, mascot of alternative political party the Singapore Democratic Party, weighed in:
swa: Hata Danny the Democracy Bear, alama ya chama mbadala cha siasa, SDP (Singapore Democratic Party) alikuwa na tarafakari ifuatayo:

eng: When I made the decision to join the SDP, pay was not a key factor.
swa: Nilipofanya uamuzi wa kujiunga na chama cha SDP (Singapore Democratic Party) malipo halikuwa suala la msingi sana.

eng: Loss of privacy, public scrutiny on myself and my loss of personal time were.
swa: Kukosa usiri, kuchambuliwa na umma mimi binafsi na kupoteza muda kwa mambo binafsi ndiyo hasa yalikuwa masuala ya msingi.

eng: That fact that I might be the party's mascot because I'm the only bear there was an important consideration.
swa: Ukweli huo kwamba ningekuwa alama ya majaliwa ya chama kwa sababu nilikuwa mwenyewe tu pale lilikuwa suala la kutazama.

eng: I had solid ground to believe that my family would not suffer a drastic change in the standard of living even though the PAP always likes to sue SDP members.
swa: Nilikuwa na sababu nzito kuamini kwamba familia yangu isingeathirika sana na kubadilika kwa mtindo wa maisha hata kama chama cha PAP kinapenda siku zote kuwashitaki wanachama wa SDP.

eng: If the balance is tilted further and animals are prohibited to join political parties in the future, it will be harder for my fellow bears to support, let alone join the SDP.
swa: Kama malipo yataendelea kuminywa zaidi na wanyama wakazuiwa kujiunga na vyama vya siasa huko mbeleni, itakuwa vigumu kwa jamaa zangu wengine kuunga mkono, wala si tu kuungana na chama cha SDP.

eng: The Tumblr blog 'When I made the decision...' has now been set up to share these variations on Ms Fu's comment.
swa: Blogu ya Tumblr iitwayo'Nilifanya uamuzi...' imetengenezwa kwa ajili ya kuweka mitazamo mbalimbali kuhusu maoni ya Mhe. Fu.

eng: 18 December was the occasion to celebrate The International Migrants Day .
swa: Tarehe 18 Disemba ilikuwa ni siku ya kusherehekea Siku ya Kimataifa ya Wahamiaji .

eng: During the current global financial crisis, immigration from developing countries has been blamed by several political parties as the source of unemployment in their countries.
swa: Wakati wa mgogoro uliopo wa hali mbaya ya fedha duniani, uhamiaji kutoka nchi zinazoendelea umelaumiwa na vyama kadhaa vya kisiasa kuwa ndiyo chanzo cha ukosefu wa ajira katika nchi hizo.

eng: Even though there hasn't been a single study, so far, that has proved that immigration has had in fact a meaningful role in the employment crisis, this belief remains strongly anchored in the minds of many.
swa: Japokuwa hapajakuwa na utafiti wowote, mpaka sasa, ambao umethibitisha kuwa uhamiaji umekuwa na mchango wowote muhimu katika tatizo la ukosefu wa ajira, imani hii imeendelea kujikita katika fikra za watu wengi.

eng: Another phenomenon is also strongly anchored in the fabric of many developed societies: the increase in frequency of humanitarian campaigns around the holiday season.
swa: Jambo jingine ambalo limelojikita sana katika jamii zilizoendelea: ni ongezeko la kampeni za misaada ya kibinadamu wakati wa kipindi cha sikukuu (za mwisho wa mwaka).

eng: Indeed, at every year's end in the more developed countries, one can observe campaigns that encourage their citizens to make donations to fight poverty in distant, less fortunate countries.
swa: Naam, kila mwisho wa mwaka katika nchi zilizoendelea zaidi, uanweza kuona kampeni ambazo zinahimiza raia wake kutoa michango ya kupigana na umaskini katika nchi za mbali ambazo hazina bahati.

eng: In addition to the recurring images of extreme poverty around the holidays (also referred to as "poverty porn" in the development sector whenever pictures of poor people are excessively exploited by charities), there are some worrying statistics: 1.4 billion people live with less than $1.25 a day.
swa: Na zaidi ya taswira za umaskini uliokithiri zinazoonekana mara kwa kwa mara wakati wakipindi cha sikukuu (ambazo pia zinaitwa"picha za ngono ya umaskini" katika sekta ya maendeleo pale ambapo taswira za watu maskini zinapotumiwa sana na mahirika ya misaada), pia kuna takwimu za kuogopesha:watu bilioni 1.4 wanaishi kwa chini ya dola 1.25 kwa siku.

eng: Despite some undeniable economic progress in many African nations, social inequality is still even more striking on the African continent.
swa: Bila kujali maendeleo yasiyopingika katika nyingi ya nchi za kiAfrika, ukosefu wa usawa wa kijamii bado unaendelea kustua barani Afrika.

eng: Economists also project that 1/3 of the poor in the world will reside on the African continent by 2015.
swa: Wanauchumi wanakadiria kuwa 1/3 ya watu maskini duniani watakuwa wanaishi katika bara la Afrika ifikapo mwaka 2015.

eng: In fact, economic hardship is one of the key factors mentioned by the 700 million people worldwide who are eager to leave their countries of origin.
swa: Ni ukweli, kuwa hali ngumu ya uchumi ni moja ya sababu zilizotajwa na milioni 700 duniani ambao wako tayari kuhama kutoka nchi zao za asili.

eng: Nomads in Morocco on Flickr by Antonioperezrio (CC-NC-2.0)
swa: watu wanaohamahama nchini Morocco kwenye Flickr na Antonioperezrio (CC-NC-2.0)

eng: It often seems that the least developed countries just cannot escape the scourge of poverty, apparently powerless against the magnitude of the task at hand.
swa: Mara nyingi inaonekana kana kwamba nchi ambazo hazijaendelea kabisa haziwe tu kuepuka laana ya umaskini, bil ya shaka hazina uwezo wa kukabili ukubwa wa majukumu waliyonayo.

eng: Moreover, these countries are often reminded of their inability to meet the needs of the population without international support.
swa: Na zaidi ya hivyo, nchi hizo mara nyingi hukumbushwa jinsi zisivyokuwa na uwezo wa kukidhi mahitaji ya watu wao bila ya misaada ya kimataifa.

eng: Although international aid is a consequence of urgent crises, this situation is often felt as a recurring affront to national pride.
swa: Japokuwa misaada ya kimataifa ni matokeo ya matatizo ya dharura, hali hii mara nyingi huchukuliwa kama tusi kwa fahari ya utaifa.

eng: Various experts postulate, however, that extreme poverty isn't inevitable.
swa: Wataalamu kadhaa wanadai hata hivyo, kuwa umaskini uliokithiri hauepukiki.

eng: The most radical solution to drastically reducing global poverty would be, for many economic experts, opening the borders between countries and allowing workers to migrate where labor is most needed.
swa: Kwa wataalamu wengi wa kiuchumi, suluhisho la kiradikali zaidi la kupunguza umaskini kwa haraka duniani ni, kufungua mipaka kati ya nchi na kuruhusu wafanyakazi kuhamia sehemu ambazo nguvukazi inahitajika zaidi.

eng: Professors Marko Bagaric and Lant Pritchett are two of the first scholars to introduce the concept of "open borders" as a solution to reducing global poverty.
swa: Maprofesa Marko Bargaric na Lant Pritchett ni wanazuoni wawili wa kwanza kuwasilisha dhana ya “mipaka iliyo wazi” kama suluhisho la kupunguza umaskini duniani.

eng: To this effect, Bagaric writes::
swa: Ili kuhitimisha hivyo, Bagaric anaandika::

eng: Sending resources to impoverished places has merit.
swa: Kutuma rasilimali kwenda sehemu maskini kuna tija.

eng: But it is a slow and fickle way of enhancing well-being.
swa: Lakini ni njia ya taratibu na isiyotabirika ya kuboresha ustawi wa watu.

eng: Instead, we directly pursue this aim by freeing up the flow of people so they can travel to where the goods are.
swa: Badala yake, tunafuatilia lengo hili kwa kuwezesha uhamiaji wa watu ili kwamba waweze kusafiri kwenda kule ambapo rasilimali zipo.

eng: The starvation crisis is simply one of food distribution, not shortage.
swa: Tatizo la njaa kwa kifupi ni tatizo la usambazaji, na si la upungufu.

eng: The best way to ameliorate Third World poverty is by massively increasing migration to the West.
swa: Njia bora zaidi ya kuongeza kasi ya kupunguza umaskini katika Dunia ya Tatu ni kuongeza uhamiaji kelekea (nchi za) Magharibi kwa kiwango kikubwa.

eng: Left to their own devices many people would gravitate to life-sustaining resources, leading to a rough equilibrium between the world's resources and its population.
swa: Wakiachwa watumie mbinu zao wenyewe watu wengi wataishia kwenye njia endelevu za kujikimu, amabzo zitapelekea kwenye mizani butu kati ya rasilimali zilizoko duniani na watu wake.

eng: Lant Pritchett explains this notion in details in his book: Let Their People Come: Breaking the Policy Deadlock on International Labor Mobility.
swa: Lant Pritchett anafafanua dhana hii kwa kina katika kitabu chake: Waache Watu Wake Waje; Kuvunjwa kwa Ukomo wa Sera ya Uhamiaji wa Kimataifa wa Nguvukazi.

eng: He quotes the results of a study claiming that:
swa: Ananukuu matokeo ya tafiti inayodai kuwa:

eng: Eliminating the planet’s remaining trade barriers would increase global GDP by around $US100 billion.
swa: Kuondoa vikwazo vya uchumi vilivyobakia duniani kutaongeza Kipato (GDP) Cha dunia kwa takriban Dola za Kimarekani bilioni 100.

eng: Eliminating immigration barriers, by comparison, would as much as double world income: that is, increase global GDP by $US60 trillion.
swa: Kuondoa vikwazo vya uhamiaji, tukilinganisha, kutaweza kuongeza maradufu kipato cha dunia: yaani, ongezeko la kipato cha dunia kwa dola za Kimarekani trilioni 60.

eng: This added wealth would be shared, but the overwhelming beneficiaries would be people who now live in poor countries.
swa: Ongezeko hili la utajiri litagawanywa, lakini watakaonufaika kwa wingi watakuwa ni watu ambao sasa wanaishi katika nchi maskini.

eng: Demonstrations held in favor of the immigrants’ right to work in Paris by austinevan on Flickr (CC-NC-SA-2.0)
swa: Maandamano ya kuunga mkono haki ya wahamiaji kufanya kazi jijini Paris na austinevan kwenye Flickr (CC-NC-SA-2.0)

eng: The World Bank published a study about immigrants' contribution to the economy of their native countries through remittances from abroad.
swa: Benki ya Dunia ilichapisha tafiti kuhusu mchango wa wahamiaji katika uchumi wa nchi zao za asili kwa njia ya utumaji pesa kutoka nje.

eng: The study also shows that remittances are expected to reach as high as 351 billion dollars to the developing countries, and 481 billion dollars globally including the high-income countries.
swa: Tafiti hiyo pia inaonyesha kuwa pesa zinazotumwa kutoka nje kuelekea nchi zinazoendelea zinatarajiwa kuongezeka na kufikia mpaka dola bilioni 351, na kufikia dola bilioni 481 duniani zikijumuishwa nchi zilizoendelea.

eng: The study also mentions that:
swa: Tafiti hiyo pia inaeleza kuwa:

eng: Needless to say, these non-orthodox theories are questioned by various experts and politicians.
swa: Haihitaji kueleza kuwa, nadharia hizi zilizo tofauti na nadharia za kihafidhina zinahojiwa na wataalamu kadhaa pamoja na wanasiasa.

eng: Frank Salter explains that the main concerns come from the inherent dysfunctions of every multicultural society:
swa: Frank salter anafafanua kuwa hofu kubwa iko kwenye matatizo yaliyopo kwenye kila jamii yenye tamaduni mbalimbali:

eng: Unrestricted migration would harm (Australia’s) national interests in ways documented by scholars in economics, sociology and related disciplines.
swa: Uhamiaji usio na kikomo utaharibu maslahi ya taifa (la Australia) kwa namna ambazo zimeandikwa na wanazuoni wa uchumi, soshiolojia na fani zinazohusiana nazo.

eng: Much of the harm is predictable from what is known about the dysfunctions of diversity.
swa: Madhara makubwa yanatabiriwa kutokea kwenye kile kinachojulikana kuhusu matatizo yaliyopo kwenye (jamii zenye) utofauti.

eng: They include growing inequality in the especially invidious form of ethnic stratification Diversity has also been associated with reduced democracy, slowed economic growth, falling social cohesion and foreign aid, as well as rising corruption and risk of civil conflict
swa: Yanayojumuisha ongezeko la ukosefu wa usawa hasa kwenye namna ya ubaguzi wa matabaka yanayotokana na asili za watu Utofauti pia umehusishwa na kupungua kwa demokrasia, kuzorota kwa uchumi, kuporomoka kwa mshikamano wa kijamii na misaada kutoka nje, vile vile ongezeko la ufisadi pamoja hatari ya migogoro ya kiraia

eng: From a political point of view, Europe is far from opening the borders, rather the contrary.
swa: Kutokea kwenye mtazamo wa kisiasa, bara la Ulaya lipo mbali na kufungua mipaka, na pengine ni tofauti ya hivyo.

eng: In France, the Guéant Act restricts foreign graduates' possibility of recruitment, giving birth to various reactions.
swa: Nchini Ufaransa Sheria ya Guéant inazuia uwezekano wa wahitimu wa masomo kutoka nje kuajiriwa, jambo ambalo limezua miitiko mablimbali.

eng: Julie Owono, Global Voices member, describes the implications of this law and the reactions of various African bloggers that see this law as an additional reason to contribute to the development of their countries.
swa: Julie Owono, mshirika wa Global Voices, anaelezea maana ya sheria hii na miitiko ya wanablogu mbalimbali wa kiAfrika ambao wanaiona sharia hii kama sababu ya ziada ya kuchangia maendeleo kwenye nchi zao.

eng: On the Rue89's blog, Owono adds that the Guéant Act also ostracizes financially limited foreign students .
swa: Katika blogu ya Rue69, Owono anaongezakwamba Sheria ya Gueant pia inawabagua wanafunzi kutoka nje ambao wana uwezo mdogo wa kifedha. .

eng: In Africa, only a few experts have studied the concept of open borders, an idea that is, without doubt, too distant from the continent realities to persist.
swa: Barani Afrika, ni wataalamu wachache tu ambao wameisoma dhana ya mipaka iliyo wazi, dhana ambayo, bila ya shaka, iko mbali sana na ukweli uliopo barani ili kuendelezwa.

eng: McGill University philosophy professor, Arash Abizadeh, doesn't encourage the opening of borders, yet states that the current border system can't be justified by a liberal egalitarian logic.
swa: Profesa wa falsafa wa Chuo Kikuu cha McGill, Arash abizadeh, hataki kuhimiza kufunguliwa kwa mipaka, hata hivyo nasema kuwa mfumo uliopo wa mipaka hauwezi kuhalalishwa kwa mantiki ya uwazi ya kiliberali.

eng: Abidazeh states that if we want to stick to the belief that "All men are born free and equal", the constitution of borders is by itself a violation of such a principle.
swa: Abidazeh anasema kuwa ikiwa tunataka kushikilia imani kuwa “binadamu wote wanazaliwa wakiwa huru na sawa”, mfumo wa mipaka, wenyewe, ni uvunjifu wa kanuni hiyo.

eng: Malagasy blogger Sly writes about the risks of opening the borders:
swa: Mwanablogu wa kiMalagasi Sly anaandika kuhusu hatari za kufungua mipaka:

eng: I'm African and while it seems that this would be a good idea there are some drawbacks
swa: Mimi ni muAfrika na wakati inaonekana kana kwamba wazo hili litakuwa zuri kuna madhara kadhaa:

eng: -child trafficiking
swa: -biashara ya watoto

eng: -drug trafficking
swa: -biashara ya mihadarati

eng: -spread of HIV and other diseases.
swa: -Kusambaa kwa VVU na magonjwa mengine

eng: -refugees will form camps in more prosperous nations causing some problems.
swa: -wakimbizi wataunda kambi kwenye nchi tajiri zaidi na kusababisha matatizo

eng: Having said this some countries in Africa do have open borders with some neighbourig countries.
swa: Pamoja na kusema hivyo baadhi ya nchi barani Afrika zina mipaka iliyo wazi na baadhi ya majirani zao.

eng: Sly refers to the fact that opening the borders between Kenya, Uganda and Ethiopia, in an attempt to increase regional economic integration, raised some major challenges in the region during the recent food crisis.
swa: Sly anagusia ukweli kuwa kufungua mipaka kati ya Kenya, Uganda na Ethiopia, katika jaribio la kuongeza mshikamano wa kiuchumi, ulizua changamoto kubwa katika kanda hiyo wakati wa balaa la njaa la hivi karibuni.

eng: This concept of using open borders to reduce global social inequalities implies that reducing global poverty would be the highest priority in the world.
swa: Dhana hii ya kutumia kufungua mipaka ili kupunguza ukosefu wa usawa kijamii duniani inamaanisha kwamba kupunguza umaskini duniani kungekuwa ndiyo kipaumbele cha juu zaidi duniani.

eng: It would come before other important considerations such as national security and the national interests of each country.
swa: Kingekuja kabla ya masuala mengine muhimu kama vile usalama wa taifa na maslahi ya taifa ya nchi yoyote.

eng: This theory of Pritchett and Magric certainly has a contentious side that aims to provoke a debate.
swa: Nadharia hii ya Pritchett na Magric bila ya shaka ina upande tata ambao una nia ya kuchokoza mdahalo.

eng: However, despite the claims of the international community that wants to reduce poverty worldwide, the open borders solution is only to be considered in specific contexts and won't take precedence over other items on the international agenda.
swa: Hata hivyo, mbali ya madai ya jumuiya ya kimataifa inayotaka kupunguza umaskini duniani, suluhisho la mipaka iliyo wazi linaweza tu kufikiriwa katika muktadha wa namna zake na hauwezi kupewa kipaumbele juu ya vipengele vingine kwenye ajenda ya kimataifa.

eng: This post is part of our special coverage Tunisia Revolution 2011.
swa: Makala haya ni sehemu ya habari zetu maalumu za Mapinduzi ya Tunisia 2011.

eng: The year 2011 has been an extraordinary year for Tunisia - a historic year that will be engraved into the memory of every Tunisian.
swa: Mwaka 2011 haukuwa wa kawaida kwa nchi ya Tunisia – mwaka wa kihistoria ambao utaingia katika kumbukumbu za kila m-Tunisia.

eng: What started as a spontaneous act of despair in the forgotten and marginalised region of Sidi Bouzid, turned into a popular uprising that would sweep the country, topple the 23-year rule of Zeine el Abidine Ben Ali, and change the face of the entire region as one Arab country after the other picked up the revolution fervour.
swa: Kile kilichoanza kama kitendo cha mlipuko wa ubeuzi (kukata tama) kilichoanzia katika eneo lililosahauliwa na lililotengwa la Sidi Bouzid, kiligeuka kuwa maasi makubwa ambayo yangeikumba nchi hiyo, kuuangusha utawala wa miaka 23 wa Zeine el Abidine Ben Ali, na kubadili kabisa sura ya eneo hilo baada ya nchi za Kiarabu moja baada ya nyingine zikiambukizwa joto hilo la mapinduzi.

eng: A bloody beginning of the year
swa: Mwaka ulianza kwa mauaji

eng: Dead young Tunisian man in Tala (central-west of Tunisia), January 10, 2011.
swa: Kijana wa ki-Tunisia aliyepoteza maisha yake mjini Tala (Magharibi ya Kati ya Tunisia), Januari 10, 2011.

eng: Photo from Nawaat.
swa: Picha kutoka Nawaat.

eng: The year had a bloody and violent beginning.
swa: Mwaka ulianza kwa mauaji na vurugu.

eng: Authorities responded to the protesters' demands of "employment, freedom, and national dignity" with live bullets, and tear gas, killing more than 300 protesters and injuring many more.
swa: Tawala husika zilijibu madai ya waandamanaji ya “ajira, uhuru, na heshima ya taifa” kwa kutumia risasi za moto, mabomu ya machozi, mauaji ya zaidi ya waandamanaji 300 na kujeruhi wengine wengi zaidi.

eng: The day the former president fled to Saudi Arabia
swa: Siku ambayo rais wa zamani alikimbilia Saudi Arabia

eng: Photo by Talel Nacer, copyright Demotix (14/01/2011).
swa: Picha kwa hisani ya Talel Nacer, haki miliki Demotix (14/01/2011)

eng: On January 14, 2011, thousands of protesters gathered outside the building of the Interior Ministry in the capital Tunis.
swa: Mnamo Januari 14, 2011, maelfu ya waandamanaji walikusanyika nje ya jengo la Wizara ya Mambo ya Ndani lililoko katika mji mkuu wa Tunis.

eng: The protesters were chanting "Interior Ministry is a Terrorist Ministry", and "Ben Ali Dégage" (Ben Ali Get Out).
swa: Waandamanaji waliimba “Wizara ya Mambo ya Ndani ni Wizara ya Ugaidi”, na “Ben Ali Dégage” (Ben Ali Toka).

eng: The demonstration which started peaceful, ended up with police violently dispersing protesters.
swa: Maandamano ambayo yalianza kwa amani, yaliisha kwa polisi kuwatawanya waandamanaji kwa nguvu.

eng: Later on the same day, Ben Ali fled to Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.
swa: Baadae siku hiyo hiyo, Ben Ali alikimbilia Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

eng: Police use tear gas to disperse protesters outside the Interior Ministry on January 14.
swa: Polisi wakitumia gesi kuwatawanya waandamanaji nje ya Wizara ya Mambo ya Ndani tarehe 14 Januari.

eng: Photo by Wassim Ben Rhouma via Flickr (CC BY-NC-ND 2.0).
swa: Picha ya Wassim Ben Rhouma kupitia mtandao wa Flickr (CC BY-NC-ND 2.0).

eng: The dictator is gone, but what about dictatorship?
swa: Dikteta ameondoka, lakini vipi kuhusu udikteta?

eng: Protest against interim government presided by Mohamed Ghannouchi, a close ally of Ben Ali, on February 25.
swa: Maandamano dhidi ya serikali ya mpito inayoongozwa na Mohamed Ghannouchi, mshirika wa karibu wa Ben Ali, tarehe 25.

eng: One day later, Ghannouchi resigned.
swa: Siku moja baadae, Ghannouchi alijiuzulu.

eng: Photo by Kahled Nciri.
swa: Picha kwa hisani ya Kahled Nciri.

eng: Tunisians were keen to cut all ties with the past, and the battle for democracy in Tunisia, did not stop with Ben Ali fleeing the country.
swa: Wa-Tunisia walikuwa makini kukata mifungamano yoyote na utawala ulioangushwa, vita kwa ajili ya demokrasia nchini Tunisia, haikumzuia Ben Ali kuikimbia nchi. .

eng: Kasbah square, where the Cabinet building is located, became an epicenter of sit-ins and protests, which sought to overthrow the so hated former ruling party (now dissolved), the RCD (from its French acronym Le Rassemblement Constitutionnel Démocratique, Constitutional Democratic Rally in English), which was associated with corruption and oppression.
swa: Kasbah square,lilipo jengo la Baraza la Mawaziri, likawa shabaha ya waandamanaji na wale wengine waliokuwa wamekaa, ambayo ilitafuta namna ya kukiangusha chama tawala cha kilichokuwa kimechukiwa sana (sasa kimesambaratishwa), RDC (yaani kwa vifupisho vya Kifaransa Le Rassemblement Constitutionnel Démocratique, kwa Kiswahili Mkutano wa Kikatiba na Kidemokrasia), ambacho kilihusishwa na ufisadi na unyanyasaji.

eng: First democratic election
swa: Uchaguzi wa kwanza wa Kidemokrasia

eng: Voters lining up to vote.
swa: Wapiga kura wakiwa wamejipanga kwa ajili ya kupiga kura.

eng: Photo by Erik (@kefteji).
swa: Picha kwa hisani ya Erik (@kefteji).

eng: October 23, 2011, was a turning point for Tunisia.
swa: Mnamo Oktoba 23, 2011, ndipo ilipowadia siku ya mageuzi kwa ajili ya Tunisia.

eng: Voters waited for hours to elect their representatives, in the first free and fair election of the so called Arab Spring.
swa: Wapiga kura walisubiri kwa saa kadhaa ili kuwachagua wabunge, , katika uchaguzi wa kwanza ulio huru na haki kwa kile kinachoitwa Maasi ya Uarabuni.

eng: Rise of Islamists
swa: Kuibuka kwa Waislamu wenye msimamo mkali

eng: November 21, 2011, in a protest outside the assembly.
swa: Mnamo Novemba 21, 2011, katika maandamano nje ya jengo la bunge.

eng: Photo by Soukaina W Ajbetni Rouhi via Facebook.
swa: Picha kwa hisani ya Soukaina W Ajbetni Rouhi kupitia Facebook.

eng: The Islamist party Ennahdha won 41 per cent of the votes, and gained 89 out of 217 seats at the constituent assembly.
swa: Chama chenye mrengo wa Kiislam Ennahdha kilishinda kwa asilimia 41 ya kura zilizopigwa, na kujinyakulia viti 89 kati ya viti 217 vya bunge la uwakilishi.

eng: For liberals, the rise of Islamists in Tunisia, is a threat to the secular values of the state, and Tunisian women's rights, considered as the most advanced in the Arab region.
swa: Kwa waliberali, kuibuka kwa makundi ya Waislamu wenye msimamo mkali nchini Tunisia, ni tishio kwa tunu zisizo za kidini za nchi hiyo, na haki za wanawake wa ki-Tunisia, unaoaminika kuimarika zaidi katika eneo la Uarabuni.

eng: Moncef Marzouki - New President of the Republic
swa: Moncef Marzouki - Rais Mpya wa Jamhuri

eng: Moncef Marzouki, new president of Tunisia.
swa: rais mpya wa Tunisia.

eng: Image by Hamideddine Bouali, copyright Demotix (13/12/11)
swa: Picha kwa hisani ya Hamideddine Bouali, haki miliki Demotix (13/12/11)

eng: On December 12, the national constituent assembly elected human rights activist Moncef Marzouki, who was imprisoned, and exiled under Ben Ali' regime, as the new President of the Republic of Tunisia.
swa: Moncef Marzouki, Mnamo Desemba 12, bunge la taifa la kikatiba lilimchagua mwanaharakati wa haki za kibinadamu Moncef Marzouki, ambaye aliwahi kuwekwa jela, na kulazimishwa kuishi uhamishoni wakati wa utawala wa Ben Ali, kuwa Rais mpya wa Jamhuri ya Tunisia..

eng: As the year comes to an end, protests and sit-ins for democracy, employment, and dignity continue in Tunisia, as heated debates sweep the national constituent assembly, and an interim government presided by Hamadi Jebali (from Ennahdha) takes up duties.
swa: Wakati mwaka ukielekea kumalizika, waandamanaji na wale waliokuwa wakikaa mahali pamoja kushinikiza demokrasia, ajira, na heshima yanaendelea nchini Tunisia, kwa namna mijadala mikali ikifanyika kwenye bunge la nchi hii, na serikali ya mpito inayoongozwa na Hamadi Jebali (kutoka chama cha Kiislam cha Ennahdha) wakichukua majukumu yao.

eng: Stay tuned for more Tunisia coverage in 2012.
swa: Jiandae kwa habari zaidi kuhusu Tunisia kwa mwaka 2012.

eng: This post is part of our special coverage Tunisia Revolution 2011.
swa: Makala haya ni sehemu ya habari zetu maalumu za Mapinduzi ya Tunisia 2011.

eng: Iran's President, Mahmud Ahmadinejad, arrived in Venezuela on Sunday January 8, 2012, in his first stop in a tour that will continue to Nicaragua, Cuba and Ecuador.
swa: Rais wa Iran, Mahmud Ahmadinejad, aliwasili nchini Venezuela siku ya Jumapili, tarehe 8 Januari, katika siku yake ya kwanza ya ziara itakayoendelea kwenye nchi za Nicaragua, Cuba na Ecuador.

eng: His visit has sparked strong reactions on social networks, where users are questioning whether his presence might be of some benefit for the nation.
swa: Ziara yake imechochea miitikio mikali kwenye mitandao ya kijamii, ambapo watumiaji wanahoji ikiwa uwepo wake huko unaweza kuwa na faida yoyote kwa taifa hilo.

eng: On Twitter, some criticize Ahmadinejad's presence and the welcoming he received by the Venezuelan government.
swa: Kwenye Twita, baadhi wanakosoa kuwepo kwa Ahmadinejad na mapokezi aliyopewa na serikali ya Venezuela.

eng: Luis Carlos Díaz (@LuisCarlos) writes:
swa: Luis Carlos Díaz (@LuisCarlos) anaandika:

eng: Undoubtedly, two events in Zambia will go down as having shaken the country in seismic ways.
swa: Bila ya shaka, matukio mawili nchini Zambia yatatambuliwa kama matukio yaliyoitikisa nchi kama vile tetemeko la ardhi linavyotikisa.

eng: The first was the death of Second Republican President Frederick Chiluba, a maverick trade unionist turned-politician who defeated Zambia’s founding president Dr Kenneth Kaunda who had been in power for 27 years but was swept out of office in the first multi-party elections after 17 years of one party “democracy”.
swa: Tukio la kwanza lilikuwa ni kifo cha Rais wa pili wa Jamhuri , Frederick Chiluba, mmpigania haki za wafanyakazi ngangari, aliyegeuka kuwa mwanasiasa na ambaye alimshinda rais wa kwanza wa Zambia Dk Kenneth Kaunda ambaye alikuwa madarakani kwa miaka 27 na kuondolewa katika wadhifa huo kwenye uchaguzi wea kwanza wa vyama vingi baada ya miaka 17 ya ‘demokrasia’ ya chama kimoja.

eng: This is how one Zambian blogger, Munshya, remembered Chiluba:
swa: Hivi ndivyo mwanablogu mmoja wa Zambia, Munshya, alivyomkumbuka Chiluba:

eng: Here a man without High School education worked hard as a bus conductor to read a few A Level courses which he later admitted to have flanked.
swa: Huyu ni mtu asiyekuwa na elimu ya juu ya sekondari aliyefanya kazi kwa bidii ili kuweza kusoma kozi chache za cha daraja A ambazo baadaye alikubali kuwa aliziacha kando.

eng: Additionally, not to be outdone by his many challenges, Chiluba went as far as Tanzania looking for opportunities.
swa: Na zaidi, ili kwamba asishindwe na changamoto zilizomkabili, Chiluba alikwenda hata Tanzania kutafuta fursa.

eng: When he came back to Zambia in his twenties, he translated the knowledge he acquired while working in the Tanzanian Sisal industry into good use.
swa: Na aliporudi nchini Zambia akiwa na umri kwenye miaka ya ishirini, alitafsiri ujuzi ujuzi alioupata alipokuwa akifanya kazi kwenye nyanja mkonge nchini Tanzania kwa manufaa.

eng: He used his courageousness and his fearlessness to become a defender of his fellow workers.
swa: Alitumia ujasiri na kutokuwa na hofu kwake kuwa mlinzi wa wa wafanyakazi wenzake.

eng: Through the trade union, a diminutive Chiluba had found an opportunity to talk and walk the tallest.
swa: Kwa kupitia chama cha wafanyakazi, Chiluba ambaye alikuwa na umbile dogo alipata nafasi ya kuongea na kutembea kama mtu mrefu kupita wote.

eng: @ictjournalist tweeted:
swa: @ictjournalist aliandika ujumbe wa twita:

eng: @ictjournalist: @GNdhlovu i remember him as a person who who started a revolution in Africa which has spread all over
swa: @ictjournalist: @GNdhlovu namkumbuka kama mtu ambaye alianzisha mapinduzi barani Afrika ambayo yameenea kila sehemu

eng: Afriwoman was a little sad:
swa: Afriwoman alikuwa na huzuni kidogo:

eng: @afriwoman: Listening to Zambian radio stations, going through pics of #Chiluba's funeral courtesy of @QfmZambia .
swa: @afriwoman: Nasikiliza stesheni za redio za Zambia, napitia picha za mazishi ya #Chiluba kwa hisani ya @QfmZambia .

eng: Didn't like the guy but a little sad
swa: Sikumpenda lakini nina masikitiko kiasi

eng: The second was the defeat of the ruling MMD after clocking 20 years in power and only three years in office of the incumbent president Rupiah Banda who lost to PF’s Michael Sata at his fourth attempt at the presidency.
swa: Tukio la pili lilikuwa ni kushindwa kwa chama tawala cha MMD baada ya kutimiza miaka 20 madarakani na miaka mitatu tu katika ofisi rais aliyekuwepo Rupiah Banda ambaye alishindwa na Michael Sata wa PF ambaye alikuwa katika jaribio lake la nne kugombea urais.

eng: After his election president Sata, in another political masterstroke, surprised the world when he appointed his long time ally and his party’s vice president, Dr Guy Scott, a white Zambian who has been on the country’s political scene for over 20 years.
swa: Baada ya kuchaguliwa, rais Sata, katika taktiki yake yake nyingine kabambe kisiasa, aliistua dunia pale alipomteua swahiba wake wa siku nyingi na makamu wa rais wa chama chake, Dk Guy Scott, mZambia mweupe ambaye amekuwa kwenye ulingo wa siasa nchini humo kwa zaidi ya miaka 20.

eng: Reacting to Guy Scott's appointment, Zambian tweep and blogger @missbwalya noted:
swa: Akitoa maoni juu ya uteuzi wa Guy Scott, mtumiaji wa twita na mwanablogu wa Zambia @missbwalya alibaini:

eng: @missbwalya: Zambia is the only African country with a white VP. Wonder how that will be received by “anti-white African” militants.
swa: @missbwalya: Zambia ndiyo nchi pekee ya kiAfrika yenye makamu wa rais Mzungu, Najiuliza hili litapokewa vipi na wale waAfrika wenye siasa kali “dhidi ya watu weupe”.

eng: Image from the ruling Patriotic Front website.
swa: Picha kutoka tovuti ya chama tawala cha Patriotic Front.

eng: Chiluba’s death, which citizens first learnt of through Twitter, shocked the nation which only three years before, had buried a sitting president, Levy Mwanawasa who died in France after collapsing in Egypt while on international duty.
swa: Kifo cha Chiluba ambacho wananchi walikisikia kwanza kwa kupitia Twita, kililishtua taifa ambalo miaka mitatu tu kabla, lilimzika rais aliyekuwa madarakani, Levy Mwanawasa ambaye alifariki nchini Ufaransa baada ya kuzimia akiwa katika ziara ya kimataifa ya kikazi nchini Misri.

eng: Chiluba’s death became a hot campaign issue for the MMD whose cadres threatened to beat Sata if he attended the funeral of his once boss under whom he saved not only as cabinet minister but as the MMD’s national secretary.
swa: Kifo cha Chiluba kiliondokea kuwa suala moto katika kampeni kwa chama cha MMD ambacho wanachama wake walitishia kumpiga Sata ikiwa angehudhuria mazishi ya aliyewahi kuwa kiongozi wake ambaye chini yake alitumikia siyo tu kama waziri bali pia kama katibu mkuu wa MMD.

eng: Sata never set foot at the funeral venue following threats to beat him up by MMD cadres but he unexpectedly turned up at the Mulungushi International Conference Centre where Chiluba’s body lay in state and paid his last respects, viewing it along ordinary citizens, vexing even security officials who did not know what to do with the then opposition leader who was clearly in bad books with President Banda.
swa: Sata hakukanyaga katika eneo la mazishi kufuatia vitisho vya kumpiga vilivyotolewa na makada wa MMD lakini bila kutarajiwa alitokea katika Kituo cha Mikutano cha Kimataifa cha Mulungushi ambapo mwili wa Chiluba ulilazwa na kutoa heshima zake za mwisho, huku akiutazama pamoja na raia wa kawaida, na kuwachukiza maafisa wa usalama ambao hawakujua cha kufanya na mtu huyu ambaye wakati huo alikuwa ni kiongozi wa upinzani ambaye ni wazi alikuwa katika uhusiano mbaya na Rais Banda.

eng: By the time the belligerent MMD cadres turned up to sort Sata out, he had already left Mulungushi.
swa: Hadi wakati ambapo makada wanazi wa MMD walipofika ili kumshughulikia Sata, alikuwa amekwishaondoka Mulungushi.

eng: This was probably one move that increased Sata’s stature in potential voters’ minds.
swa: Taktiki hii pengine ni moja ambayo ilimuongezea ukubwa Sata katika fikra za wapiga kura watarajiwa.

eng: The irony, however, is that Chiluba, before his demise, touted himself as President Banda’s political consultant who vowed to deliver Sata’s perceived regional strongholds to the MMD.
swa: Jambo la kejeli, hata hivyo, ni kuwa Chiluba, kabla ya kifo chake, alijitangaza kuwa mshauri wa kisiasa wa Rais Banda na aliyeapa kuwa atazileta ngome za Sata vijijini kwenye kambi ya MMD.

eng: Supporters in a truck celebrate the victory of opposition leader Michael Sata as he was sworn in as the fifth Zambian president.
swa: Mashabiki katika lori wakisherehekea ushindi wa kiongozi wa upinzani Michael Sata wakati alipoapishwa kama rais wa tano wa Zambia.

eng: Image by Owen Miyanza, copyright Demotix (23/12/2011).
swa: Picha na Owen Mayiza, haki miliki ya Demotix (23/12/2011).

eng: Related to Chiluba’s death was the presidential election for which the MMD was sure to win with its well-financed campaign vis-à-vis a Spartan and low key campaign strategy of the PF which adopted the slogan “Donchi Kubeba” with donchi being a corruption of the English word, don’t and kubeba being tell.
swa: Linalohusiana na kifo cha Chiluba lilikuwa ni uchaguzi wa rais ambao MMD ilikuwa na uhakika wa kushinda kutokana na kampeni yake iliyokuwa na fedha za kutosha dhidi ya mkakati wa kampeni yenye hali mbaya kifedha na ya chini chini ya PF ambayo ilitumia kauli mbiu ya “Donchi kubeba”, donchi ni neno lililopotoshwa la Kiingereza, don’t na kubeba ni kusema.

eng: The MMD government tried to suppress the release of poll results when it became apparent that things were not going their way but netizens where clearly a step ahead releasing the results on Twitter, Facebook and social networks.
swa: Serikali ya MMD ilijaribu kuzuia tmatokeo ya kura pale ilipokwa wazi kuwa mambo yalikuwa hayaendi njia yao lakini watumiaji wa mtandao waliokuwa hatua moja mbele walitoa matokeo kwa njia ya twita, Facebook na mitandao ya kijamii.

eng: President Sata has embarked on a massive investigation of corrupt activities under the previous administration and within a few weeks of commencement of the investigations, security wings dug out billions of Zambian Kwacha from a former minister’s farm.
swa: Rais Sata ameanzisha uchunguzi mkubwa wa matukio ya kifisadi yaliyofanywa katika utawala uliopita na ndani ya wiki chache baada ya uchunguzi kuanza, vitengo cya usama vilichimbua mabilioni ya Kwacha za Zambia kutoka katika shamba la waziri wa zamani.

eng: Several other former cabinet ministers have since been arrested or have had their properties suspected to have been corruptly obtained, seized.
swa: Mawaziri wengine kadhaa wamekamatwa ama mali zao ambazo zinashukiwa kupatikana isivyo halali zimechukuliwa.

eng: When the scale of impropriety became apparent, citizens started calling for the removal of President Banda's immunity from prosecution.
swa: Pale upeo wa ufisadi ulipojulikana wazi, wananchi walianza kudai iondolewe kinga inayomlinda rais Banda asishitakiwe. .

eng: Netizens also wondered whether the former president implicated himself in his farewell speech.
swa: Wanamtandao pia walijiuliza ikiwa rais aliyepita alijishtaki mwenyewe katika hotuba yake ya kuaga.

eng: On Facebook, Gongs Jhala asked:
swa: Kwenye Facebook, Ghong Jhala aliuliza:

eng: Do you think RB and his sons will face criminal prosecution?
swa: Unafikiri RB na wanawe watashitakiwa kwa jinai?

eng: I found it interesting when he said they did not “knowingly abuse public resources” that mean they abused public resources but did not know they were doing so?
swa: Niliona ni jambo la ajabu pale aliposema kuwa “hawakutumia vibaya rasilimali za taifa huku wakiwa na ufahamu huo” je, ina maana kuwa walitumia vibaya rasilimali za taifa lakini hawakujua kuwa walikuwa wanafanya hivyo?

eng: Many netizens weighed in on the fight against corruption:
swa: Wanamtandao wengi walichangia juu ya vita dhidi ya ufisadi:

eng: @lwangamwilu: Some people miraculously acquired wealth in 3 years in office, let them be investigated - Milupi #Zambia
swa: @lwangamwilu: Baadhi ya watu kwa miujiza walipata utajiri katika miaka miaka 3 waliyokuwa madarakani, hebu waache wachunguzwe – Milupi #Zambia

eng: @stevenputter: #Zambia, 1000 bicycles “for personal use” thought it was only God that could be in more than one place at a time, no wonder investigated
swa: @stevenputter: #Zambia, baiskeli 1000 “kwa matumizi binafsi” nilidhani ni Mungu peke yake ambaye anaweza kuwa sehemu zaidi ya moja kwa wakati mmoja, si ajabu wanachunguzwa

eng: Perhaps we should mention the Barotseland Agreement debate, which picked up in 2011.
swa: Pengine tugusie mdahalo wa Makubaliano ya Barotseland, ambao ulipamba moto mwaka 2011.

eng: Long considered a non-issue during decades of one party rule, Barotseland became an issue of political contention in 2011.
swa: Kwa muda mrefu ulichukuliwa kama suala lisilo na maana wakati wa miongo ya utawala wa chama kimoja, Barotseland iligeuka suala tata kisiasa mwaka 2011.

eng: Two people were killed in January 2011 after riots broke out in Mongu, the capital of Western Province over reinstatement of the Barotseland Agreement of 1964.
swa: Watu wawili waliuwawa mwezi Januari 2011 baada kuzuka machafuko hukoMongu, mji mkuu wa jimbo la Magharibi baada ya kusimikwa tena kwa Mkataba wa Barotseland wa mwaka 1964.

eng: Some activists in the region argue that the Barotseland Agreement provides for separation from the rest of Zambia.
swa: Baadhi ya wanaharakati wanadai kwamba Mkataba wa Barotseland unaruhusu kujitenga kutoka Zambia.

eng: Zambia’s opposition National Restoration Party (NAREP) president Elias Chipimo Jr. has become the country’s first politician to “address” the make believe 1,318 member Facebook Zambian parliament after he was allowed by the “Speaker” to post his end of year message.
swa: Rais waChama cha upinzani cha NAREP (National Restoration Party) Elias Chipimo Jr. amekuwa mwanasiasa wa kwanza katika nchi hiyo “kulihutubia” bunge la Facebook nchini Zambia linaloaminika kuwa na wanachama 1,318 baada ya kuruhusiwa na “Spika” kutuma ujumbe wake wa mwisho wa mwaka.

eng: The Hon Speaker first posted the following message before he posted Chipimo’s speech:
swa: Mhe Spika aliweka ujumbe ufuatao kabla hajaweka hotuba nzima ya Chipimo:

eng: IMPORTANT ANNOUNCEMENT
swa: TANGAZO MUHIMU

eng: Hon Members.
swa: Naomba tumkaribishe Mhe.

eng: May we welcome Hon Elias Chipimo, NAREP President to officially address this House by delivering end of year message from NAREP.
swa: Elias Chipimo, Rais wa (chama cha) NAREP ili aweze kulihutubia bunge hili rasmi kwa kutoa salaam za mwisho wa mwaka kutoka chama cha NAREP.

eng: As usual, the House ll proceed to debate his address.
swa: Kama kawaida, bunge litaendelea kwa kuijadili hotuba yake.

eng: Once we get hold of UPND President, Hon HaKainde Hichilema, and also Republican President, H. E. Michael C. Sata, we shall let them address the House.
swa: Mara tu tutakapowapata Rais wa UPND, Mhe. HaKainde Hichilema, na Rais wa chama cha Republican, Mhe Michael C. Sata, tutawaruhusu na wao walihutubie bunge.

eng: President Chipimo, its an honour to have you in the House.
swa: Rais Chipimo, ni heshima kubwa kuwa nawe Bungeni.

eng: You may address this august House.
swa: Sasa unaweza kulihutubia Bunge hili tukufu.

eng: Part of Chipimo's post reads:
swa: Sehemu ya posti ya Chipimo inasomeka hivi:

eng: President for the National Restoration Party (NAREP) Elias Chipimo.
swa: Rais wa chama cha NAREP (National Restoration Party Elias Chipimo.

eng: Photo courtesy of Elias Chipimo Facebook page.
swa: Haki miliki ya Picha ni ukurasa wa Facebook wa Elias Chipimo.

eng: Year-end message from the National Restoration Party (NAREP)
swa: Salaam za mwisho wa mwaka kutoka chama cha NAREP.

eng: Looking beyond 2011: What the PF administration can start to do in its next 90 days in office
swa: Tukitafakari zaidi ya mwaka 2011: Kile ambacho serikali ya PF inaweza kuanza kufanya katika siku 90 zijazo wakiwa madarakani.

eng: Zambia faces many challenges ranging from poor healthcare, dilapidated and inadequate infrastructure, limited access to quality education and an economy that is still not meeting the development needs of the majority of the people in spite of its strong performance over the last few years.
swa: Zambia inakabiliwa na changamoto nyingi kuanzia huduma mbovu za afya, miundo mbinu iliyotelekezwa siku nyingi na kwa kweli isiyofaaa, kutokupatikana kwa elimu yenye ubora na uchumi ambao bado hauwezi kuwapatia wananchi walio wengi mahitaji ya kimaendeleo pamoja na kuimarika kwake katika miaka michache iliyopita.

eng: Tackling these problems will no doubt require long-term focus, energy and vision.
swa: Kupambana na matatizo haya hapana shaka tunatakiwa kuwa na malengo ya muda mrefu, nguvu na dira.

eng: There are, however, 3 pressing issues that require a clear, committed and immediate response: (1) unemployment; (2) corruption; and (3) excessive presidential and executive power.
swa: Kwa hivyo kuna, masuala matatu makubwa yanayohitaji hatua zilizo bayana, zinazohitaji kujitoa na za haraka. 1) ukosefu wa ajira; 2) ufisadi; na 3) madaraka makubwa ya rais na wakubwa wa serikalini.

eng: Although the fight against corruption has been boosted by the PF administration, there has been a lamentable failure to find a formula for addressing each of these issues in a sustainable manner As far as globally defining moments go, the year 2011 belonged almost exclusively to the Arab Spring – that sense of democratic consciousness that seemed to emanate spontaneously from the streets of Tunis and spread like a virus through North Africa and the Middle East.
swa: Ingawa vita dhidi ya ufisadi imepewa nguvu na serikali ya PF, yamekuwepo malalamiko ya kushindwa kupata kanuni ya kukabili kila kimoja katika masuala haya kwa namna iliyo endelevu Kwa jinsi nyakati hizi katika ulimwengu wote zinavyoonyesha, mwaka 2011 umekuwa wa Majira ya Kuchipua ya Urabuni –hali hiyo ya uelewa wa kidemokrasia ambao umeonekana kuanzia ghafla katika mitaa ya mji wa Tunis na kuweza kusambaa kama virusi kwenda Afrika Kaskazini na Mashariki ya Kati.

eng: Sub-Saharan Africa, and indeed Zambia, was not unaffected by these events.
swa: Afrika ya Kusini mwa Jangwa la Sahara, na kwa hakika Zambia, haikuachwa bila madhara kufuatia matukio haya.

eng: Remote though the idea may seem, the sentiments that prompted the democratic revolutions in Tunisia, Egypt, Yemen and Libya were similar to those that resulted in the conclusive Patriotic Front (PF) victory on 23 September.
swa: Hata kama wazo hili linaweza kuonekana kuwa mbali sana, madai yaliyochochea mapinduzi ya kidemokrasia nchini Tunisia, Misri, Yemen na Libya yalikuwa yanafanana sana na yale yaliyosababisha ushindi wa mkubwa wa chama cha Patriotic Front (PF) tarehe 23 Septemba.

eng: Clearly, after 20 in power, something must went seriously wrong within the Movement for Multiparty Democracy (MMD) – the party that brought an end to UNIP’s 27 year rule.
swa: Ni wazi, baada ya miaka 20 madarakani, lazima kuna jambo lilikwenda vibaya ndani ya chama cha MMD (Movement for Multiparty Democracy –chama ambacho kiliung’oa utawala wa UNIP uliodumu kwa miaka 27.

eng: A number of “Members of Parliament” in debating the “speech”, hailed the move to engage politicians in the virtual parliament.
swa: Baadhi ya “Wabunge” katika kuijadili “hotuba” hiyo, waliipongeza hatua ya kuwashirikisha wanasiasa katika bunge hilo la kufikirika.

eng: One member, Rodger Chali praised the opposition politician for being new media savvy:
swa: Mbunge mmoja, Rodger Chalialimsifu mwanasiasa wa upinzani kwa kuwa na uelewa mkubwa wa vyombo vipya vya habari:

eng: Mr Speaker Sir, let me thank Hon. Chipimo for his submission and for being one the the leaders who understands the power of new media.
swa: Ndugu Mhe Spika, naomba nimshukuru Mhe Chipimo kwa kuwasilisha hotuba yake na kwa kuwa mmoja wa viongozi wanaoelewa nguvu ya vyombo hivi vipya vya habari.

eng: Let me submit however that, Zambia is not lacking intelligent presidents , but a system which allows provinces and districts to flourish without looking to Lusaka.
swa: Naomba kuwasilisha hata hivyo kwamba, Zambia haina tatizo la ukosefu wa Marais wenye akili, bali mfumo unaoyawezesha majimbo na wilaya kujiendeleza bila kulazimika kuitegemea Lusaka.

eng: I would therefore wish to challenge Hon. Chipimo to champion the cause of a free Zambia from Lusaka control.
swa: Ningependa kwa hiyo kumpa changamoto Mhe Chipimo kuongoza madai ya kuikomboa Zambia kutoka katika udhibiti wa Lusaka.

eng: This is the only agenda which will bring prosperity.
swa: Hii ni ajenda pekee ambayo italeta fanaka.

eng: If he can deliver this one issue before 2016, i can trust him to be president.
swa: Kama anaweza kutekeleza suala hili moja kabla ya mwaka 2016, ninaweza kumwamini awe rais.

eng: Mr Speaker , I would not what to hear that the hon. can only do this if elected president.
swa: Ndugu Spika, nisingependa kusikia kwamba mheshimiwa huyu atalitekeleza hili pale tu atakapochaguliwa kuwa rais.

eng: Kasololo Chisenga said:
swa: Kasololo Chisenga alisema:

eng: Hon Zapp Speaker Sir indeed presidential candidate Hon.Elias Chipimo raises some important points that are worth debati ng in the house.
swa: Mhe Spika kwa kweli mgombea wa urais Mhe Elias Chipimo ameibua hoja muhimu ambazo zinastahili kabisa kujadiliwa bungeni.

eng: I am particularly taken by his suggestion of growing biofules and coming up with a 'new economy ' in Z...ambia.
swa: Nimevutiwa hasa na pendekezo lake kuhusu kukua kwa bayoanuai na kuja na wazo la “uchumi mpya” nchini Zambia.

eng: This is indeed innovaribve and is what is expected from a youthful leader such as him.
swa: Hili kwa kweli limejaa ubunifu na ndicho hasa kinachotegemewa kutoka kwa viongozi vijana kama yeye.

eng: It is my hope that such ideas can be ytaken seriously to reduce the leve of unemployment in the land.
swa: Ni matumaini yangu kwamba mawazo kama haya yanaweza kuchukuliwa kwa uzito unaostahili kupunguza kiwango cha ukosefu wa ajira nchini.

eng: On the same issue of bio-fuel, Nicholas Mutalama added:
swa: Katika suala hilo hilo la bayoanuai, Nicholas Mutalama aliongeza:

eng: Hon. Speaker Sir, the exploration of bio-fuel is now extensive in the West and farmers busy utilising this initiative through government and privately funded programmes.
swa: Mhe Spika, utafiti wa nishati ya bayoanuai hivi sasa umeshika kasi huko kwenye nchi za Magharibi na wakulima (wa huko) wako kwenye harakati za kutumia mbinu hii kupitia mipango inayofadhiliwa na serikali na watu binafsi.

eng: Why does it take us so long to jump on sustainable opportunities such... as these to move forward.
swa: Kwa nini inatuchukuwa muda mrefu kurukia kwenye fursa endelevu kama… hizi ili tusonge mbele.

eng: Sir, the previous regimes together with the current administration have focused on programmes that hardly produce anything worthy.....!
swa: Mheshimiwa, tawala zilizopita pamoja na utawala huu uliopo madarakani zimeelekeza mipango yake ambayo kimsingi haiwezi kuzalisha kitu chochote cha maana…!

eng: This we can do or maybe just maybe, we are waiting for another investor or donor to come to our rescue when clearly through serious fiscal responsibility and accountability would give us the much needed funds for the initial investment.
swa: Hili tunaweza kulifanya au labda ni labda tu, tunasubiri mwekezaji mwingine au mfadhili aje kutuokoa wakati suala lilikuwa ni uwajibikaji ulio makini wa kifedha na kubeba wajibu wetu ambao ungeweza kutupatia fedha nyingi zinazohitajika kwa ajili ya hatua za mwanzo za uwekezaji.

eng: Zambian People's Parliament (ZAPP) was formed shortly after the September 20 elections which saw an opposition party, the Patriotic Front (PF), unseat the ruling MMD that had been in power for 20 years.
swa: Zambian People's Parliament (ZAPP) ni bunge la mtandaoni lilianzishwa mara tu baada ya uchaguzi wa Septemba 20 uliokifanya chama cha upinzani, PF (Patriotic Front) kuking’oa chama tawala cha MMD ambacho kimekuwa madarakani kwa miaka 20.

eng: The group was formed on the back of another Facebook group, the Zambian Peoples Pact which campaigned against the former ruling party.
swa: Kikundi hiki cha Facebook kilianzishwa kwa nguvu ya kikundi kingine cha cha Facebook kiitwachoZambian Peoples Pact ambacho kilifanya kampeni kukipinga chama tawala kilichoangushwa.

eng: The following is the group’s description:
swa: Yafuatayo ni maelezo yanayokitambulisha kikundi hicho:

eng: The Zambian People’s Parliament (ZAPP) is a replication of the Zambian Parliament comprising a cross-section of citizens who constructively discuss, analyze, debate, persuade and agree on issues which border on democratic governance.
swa: Bunge la Watu wa Zambia (ZAPP) ni maigizo ya Bunge la Zambia linaloundwa na makundi mbalimbali ya raia ambao kwa minajili ya kujenga hujadili, huchambua, kubishana, kufuatilia na kukubaliana katika masuala ambayo yanahusu utawala wa kidemokrasia.

eng: Specifically, ZAPP is a place where citizens contribute their voice on Zambia’s democratic governance, political and socioeconomic development.
swa: Kimahususi, ZAPP ni mahali ambapo raia huchangia sauti zao kwa ajili ya utawala wa kidemokrasia wa Zambia na maendeleo ya kisiasa, kijamii na kiuchumi.

eng: The essence of these online debates shall be to enable citizens make input into parliamentary and government’s policy and decision-making and provide a fora for issue-based discussion by politically-minded citizens, leaders in our communities and experts thus enabling the group to mold an opinion and influence decision-making.
swa: Umuhimu wa mijadala hii ya mtandaoni itakuwa kuwawezesha raia kuchangia mawazo katika sera na maamuzi ya bunge na serikali kwa ujumla na kutengeneza jukwaa kwa mijadala ya masuala ya msingi inayoendeshwa na raia wenye uelewa wa masuala ya kisiasa, watawala katika jamii na wataalam na hivyo kuliwezesha kundi kufinyanga wazo linaloweza kutumika katika ufikiwaji wa maamuzi ya serikali.

eng: Mission Statement
swa: Tamko la Lengo

eng: The Mission of ZAPP is to engage citizens, leaders in parliament and government, public and private sectors in jointly setting policy direction and ensuring decisions made at all levels reflect the will of the Zambian people to be governed according to democratic tenets.
swa: Lengo la ZAPP ni kuwahusisha raia, watawala walio bungeni na serikalini, kwenye sekta za umma na zile binafsi katika kutengeneza muelekeo wa sera kwa pamoja na kuhakikisha maamuzi yanayofanywa katika ngazi zote yanaakisi matakwa ya watu wa Zambia kuongozwa kwa mujibu wa kanuni za kidemokrasia.

eng: Vision Statement ZAPP’s Vision is a leading platform for both ordinary and empowered Zambians who freely express themselves and are heard in Zambia’s democratic governance and promotion of socioeconomic activities of the nation.
swa: Tamko la Dira Maono ya ZAPP ni kuongoza jukwaa la wa-Zambia wa kawaida na wale wenye nafasi katika uongozi ambao hujieleza kwa uhuru na kusikiwa katika serikali ya kidemokrasia ya Zambia na kukuza shughuli za kijamii na kiuchumi katika taifa.

eng: Citizen journalist Bladimir Sánchez has already received threats for making a video showing the forced evictions of farmers and fishermen protesting the construction of a hydroelectric dam in the department of Huila, Colombia on February 14 and 15.
swa: Mwanahabari Bladimir Sanchez ameshapata vitisho kwa maisha yake kwa kutengeneza video inayoonyesha kufukuzwa kwa lazima kwa wakulima na wavuvi wanaopinga kutengenezwa kwa bwawa la kuzalisha umeme katika eneo la Huila, nchini Colombia mnamo tarehe 14 na 15 Februari.

eng: In less than three days, more than 600,000 people have watched it.
swa: Takriban baada ya siku tatu, video hiyo imetazamwa na watu zaidi ya laki sita.

eng: On Publimetro , Camilo Andrés García Cortés states that the video may be making history as the most watched Colombian citizen video, due to its half a million views during only two days.
swa: Katika Publimetro , Camilo Andrés García Cortés anasema kuwa video hii yaweza kuwa inafanya historia kwa kuwa video iliyotazamwa mara mengi zaidi nchini Colombia, kwa sababu ishapata kutazamwa mara laki tano baada ya masiku mawili tu.

eng: The Video the Colombian Government Doesn't Want Us to See shows the violent eviction faced by two river bank communities standing up peacefully against the building of the dam, and pulls together the testimonies of those who faced the violence and were injured.
swa: Video ambayo Serikali ya Colombia Haitaki Tuone yaonyesha fujo inayotumiwa dhidi ya jamii mbili zilizoko ukingoni wa mto, ambazo zimetumia njia za amani kupinga kujengwa kwa bwawa hilo. Video hiyo pia inakusanya maoni na ushuhuda ya waliokumbana na vurugu hizo, pamoja na waliojeruhiwa.

eng: The communities are against the dam construction because it will leave them without livelihoods if the river is diverted for the project.
swa: Jamii zitakazoathiriwa zimepinga kujengwa kwa bwawa hili, kwani litawaacha bila jinsi ya kupata riziki yao kama mto utaelekezwa kwingine.

eng: When describing the clash that injured protesters, both the community members and journalists present describe that there was no violence towards the authorities in spite of the attacks, and that the police restricted the access of journalists, peace observers and human right organizations to the area of the protest.
swa: Wakieleza jinsi waandamanaji walivyojeruhiwa, wanajamii na wanahabari waliopo katika eneo hilo wanaeleza kwamba hapakuwa na fujo dhidi ya wenye mamlaka, ilhali ya uwepo na vurugu, na polisi waliwazuia wanahabari, waangalizi wa amani na shirika za kupigania haki za kibinadamu kufika sehemu ambako maandamano yalikuwa yakiendelea.

eng: Since early February 2012, a series of global vigils have taken place in all over the world to express solidarity with Tibetans, following a call from Kalong Tripa Dr. Lobsang Sangay.
swa: Tangu mwanzoni mwa Februari 2012, kumekuwa na mikesha kadhaa duniani kuonyesha ushikamano na Wanatibeti kufuatia mwito wa Kalong Tripa Dkt.

eng: As February 22 is the Tibetan New Year, activists are calling for another round of solidarity action.
swa: Lobsang Sangay.Kwa vile tarehe 22 Februari ni sikukuu ya kukaribisha mwaka mpya Tibet, wanaharakati wamekuwa wakitoa wito wa duru mpya ya harakati za mshikamano.

eng: A map on global vigils in solidarity with Tibetans on February 8, 2012.
swa: Ramani inayoonyesha kesha za kuonyesha ushikanamo na Wanatibeti tarehe 8 Februari, 2012.

eng: In addition, more than 240 have signed up for a Butter Lamp Pray event* to express their solidarity with Tibetans: In Tibet, from 27 Feb 2009 to 19 Feb 2012, 23 Tibetans have self-immolated to protest for a free Tibet and the return of The Dalai Lama.
swa: Nchini Tibet, kuanzia tarehe 27 Februari 2009 hadi 19 Februari 2012, Wanatibeti 23 wamejichoma ili kushinikiza uhuru Tibet, pamoja na kurudi kwa Dalai Lama.

eng: 15 of them had lost their lives.
swa: Kati ya hao, watu 15 walifariki.

eng: Under the repressive circumstance in Tibet, self-immolation is an ultimate act of nonviolence demonstration.
swa: Chini ya mazingira kandamizi huko Tibet, kujichoma ndiyo tendo la mwisho la upinzani usiotumia fujo.

eng: Tibet question seems so far away from us, but as a human being, it doesn’t mean that we can do nothing.
swa: Swala la Tibet linaonekana kuwa mbali nasi, lakini kama binadamu, haimaanishi kuwa hatuwezi kufanya kitu.

eng: At least, we should pray for the death.

eng: Anyone following online citizen media closely this month, would inevitably have come across the heated global debate over the Invisible Children viral campaign to stop Ugandan war criminal and rebel army leader Joseph Kony.
swa: Yeyote anayefuata habari kutoka kwa raia wa kawaida katika mtandao mwezi huu hakika ameona mjadala ulioenea duniani kuhusu kampeni lijulikanalo kama 'Invisible Children', ambalo limeenea duniani, na lina nia ya kumkomesha mhalifu na kiongozi wa jeshi la waasi, Joseph Kony.

eng: While the Kony 2012 campaign certainly received the attention it sought, many Ugandans and Africans felt its message lacked the nuance required by context, and was more focused on raising funds for the organisation's own survival rather than empowering the people affected by the conflict.
swa: Ilhali kampeni la Kony 2012 hakika limepata usikivu lililotaka, Waganda na Waafrika wengi wanaona kwamba ujumbe wake umekosa muktadha na maelezo sahihi kuhusu Joseph Kony. Zaidi ya hiyo, kampeni lenyewe lilijishughulisha na kuchanga pesa kwa shirikisho lililoanzisha kampeni lenyewe badala ya kuwawezesha watu walioathiriwa na vita hivyo kujiendeleza.

eng: Furthermore, many African citizens felt that once again, the narrative of a highly publicized story about Africa centered on a negative story and neglected the upwards trends the continent has been witnessing.
swa: Zaidi ya hayo, raia wengi wa Afrika wanaona kuwa habari kuhusu Bara la Afrika ambazo zinaonyesha mabaya zaendelea kuenezwa, badala ya wanahabari kuripoti kuhusu maendeleo mazuri ambayo yameenea barani Afrika hivi karibuni.

eng: As a counter measure, many people started posting stories on Twitter about "what they love about Africa" with the hash tag #WhatILoveAboutAfrica.
swa: Ili kukabiliana na hali hii, watu wengi wameanza kuandika hadithi na kadalika katika Twitter kusema ni nini haswa wanapenda kuhusu Afrika, wakitumia maneno #WhatILoveAboutAfrica.

eng: what I love About Africa trending worlwide by Semhar Araia - @Semhar

eng: The initiative, spearheaded by Semhar Araia, a blogger at the Diaspora African Women Network (DAWNS), started to trend worldwide on Twitter on March 13, 2012.
swa: Hatua hii, iliyoongozwa na Semhar Araia , mwanablogu katika Diaspora African Women Network (Shirika la Wanawake Walio Ugenini), ilianza kuenea duniani katika Twitter tarehe 13 Machi 2012.

eng: While no one argues with the merit of exposing the despicable crimes perpetuated by Kony's Lord's Resistance Army, the following citizen media commentaries explain why this debate is more than just a "meme war" but a struggle to reclaim the international perception and narrative about an entire continent.
swa: Ilhali hakuna anayepinga umuhimu wa kuonyesha uhalifu uliotendwa na Jeshi la Kony, lijulikanalo kama LRA, ripoti zifuatazo kutoka kwa raia wa kawaida zaeleza jinsi mjadala huu ni zaidi ya mawazo matupu yanayoenezwa kutumia mtandao, au meme kwa Kiingereza, lakini ni vita vya kukomboa mawazo na mtazamo wa walimwengu kuhusu bara zima.

eng: When a group of North Ugandans, the main victims of Kony's crimes, were showed the Invisible Children's video in a public screening, they were not particularly pleased with the content of the video as is seen in an Al Jazeera English video below.
swa: Wakati kundi la wenyeji wa Kaskazini mwa Uganda, ambao waliathiriwa zaidi na uhalifu wake Kony, walionyeshwa video ya Invisible Children katika onyesho la hadhara, hawakupendezwa na waliyoona katika video hilo, kama inavyoonekana katika video ya Al Jazeera English ifuatayo.

eng: If people in those countries care about us, they will not wear t-shirts with pictures of Joseph Kony for any reason, says one man interviewed.
swa: Kama watu walio katika nchi hizo wanatujali, hawatavaa shati zilizo na picha za Joseph Kony kwa nia yoyote, alisema mwanaume mmoja aliyehojiwa.

eng: That would celebrate our suffering.
swa: Huko ni kusherehekea kuteseka kwetu.

eng: A Ugandan man at another screening says, "There is some kind of people, some NGO, who are trying to mobilize funds using the atrocities committed in Northern Uganda."
swa: Kuna watu fulani, shirika fulani linalotaka kutafuta pesa kwa kutumia ghasia iliyofanyika Kaskazini mwa Uganda, Mganda mwingine katika onyesho lingine alisema.

eng: Thanks to activists the international courts following the genocide proceedings against Guatemala will be taking into account the violence indigenous women faced for more than 36 years where they were victims because they were women and because they were indigenous.
swa: Shukrani kwa wanaharakati na mahakama za kimataifa kufuatia taratibu za mashtaka dhidi ya Guatemala. Tunaamini zitazingatia matumizi ya nguvu waliyokumbana nayo wanawake wenyeji kwa zaidi ya miaka 36, ambapo walikuwa waathirika kwa sababu tu ya kuwa wanawake na kwa sababu ya kuwa wenyeji.

eng: A documentary and several video testimonials tell their harrowing stories, stories that due to the discrimination the victims faced in their communities and the fear of retribution many kept silent for decades.
swa: Simulizi hilo la kina pamoja na shuhuda kadhaa za video vinasimulia masaibu ya kutisha waliyoyapitia, masimulizi ambayo kwa sababu ya unyanyasaji waliokumbana nao waathirika hao kwenye jamii zao na hofu ya adhabu wengi wao walinyamaza kwa miongo kadhaa.

eng: In Valencia, school children decided to protest budget cuts that affected their schools, forcing them to carry blankets with them due to lack of heating, in what has been a particularly cold winter in Europe.
swa: Mjini Valencia, wanafunzi wameamua kuandamana kupinga kupungua kwa bajeti kwa kuwa kunaathiri shule zao. Imefika mahali wanalazimika kwenda na mablanketi kwa sababu ya kukosekana kwa vipasha joto, katika msimu huu wa baridi kali barani Ulaya.

eng: Police reacted to the protests violently with students injured and detained; many videos have been made showing the abuses against minors, females and the elderly.
swa: Polisi wamewashambulia waandamanaji wakitumia nguvu kupita kiasi na kuwajeruhi baadhi yao huku wakiwatupa mahabusu wengine; video vyingi zinaonyesha kudhalilishwa kwa makundi ya watu wanaonyanyasika, wanawake na wazee.

eng: Just a few days after the brutal police crackdown at the Luis Vives Institute of Secondary Education in Valencia , students have again been the target of beatings, pushing and violence from the police at a pacific protest in which they were, precisely, demonstrating against police violence.
swa: Siku chache baada ya mapambano makali ya polisi katika taasisi ya Elimu ya Sekondari ya Luis Vives mjini Valencia , wanafunzi wamekuwa ndio shabaha ya vipigo, kusukumwa na ghasia kutoka kwa polisi wakati wakiwa katika maandamano ya amani, kwa kweli, wakiandamana kupinga ghasia za polisi.

eng: This time,the crackdown started on the afternoon with unexpected force.
swa: Wakati huu mapigano yalianza mchana kwa nguvu isiyotarajiwa.

eng: One of the oldest slave descendent communities in Brazil, Quilombo Rio dos Macacos, where around 50 families live, has a date for eviction: March 4, 2012.
swa: Moja wapo ya jamii zilizotokana na uzao wa kale wa kitumwa nchini Brazil, Quilombo Rio dos Macacos, ambapo kadri ya familia 50 zinaishi, wapatiwa tarehe kamili ya kuondolewa: Machi 4, 2012.

eng: The claim for the land comes from the Navy of Brazil, that intends to broaden a condo for its officers in that territory, in the border area between Salvador and Simões Filho, state of Bahia... Descendants of original peoples from Africa who, during colonialism, were taken from their land to become slaves in Brazil, the Quilombolas now see themselves under threat of losing their homes again, despite their right to the land they inhabit enshrined in the constitution.
swa: Dai la kuwanyang’anya ardhi linakuja kutoka kwa jeshi la Brazil, ambalo linakusudia kuongeza makazi kwa maafisa wake katika eneo hilo, mpakani mwa eneo la Salvado na Simoes Filho, katika jimbo la Bahia… Uzao wa watu wa asili ya Afrika ambao wakati wa ukoloni, walichukuliwa kutoka kwenye nchi yao kuwa watumwa nchini Brazil, wa-Quilmbola sasa wanajiona kwenye tishio jingine la kupoteza nyumba zao, pamoja na haki waliyonayo ya kumiliki ardhi wanayoishi inayolindwa na katiba ya nchi.

eng: This short documentary shows the situation the Quilombolas are facing: afraid to leave their houses, unable to move freely and fearing for their well-being, their families and their homes.
swa: Simulizi hili fupi la video linaonyesha hali wanayokabiliana nayo wa-Quilombola: wanaoogopa kupoteza nyumba zao, wakishindwa kuhama kwa uhuru wakihofia usalama wao, familia na nyumba zao.

swa: Video hiyo iliyotengenezwa kwa ghasia zilizosababishwa na serikali dhidi ya waandamanaji waliosimama kidete kupinga kuchepushwa kwa mto kwenye jamii yao ili kupisha ujenzi wa bwawa umesabaisha mwandishi wa kiraia kupokea tishio la kuuawa.

eng: Recent events in Latin American prisons that cost the life of hundreds of inmates have people looking into the living situation and overcrowding faced in many penitentiary centers, and analyzing if they are tragedies waiting to happen.
swa: Matukio ya hivi karibuni katika magereza ya Amerika ya Kusini yanayogharimu maisha ya mamia ya wafungwa yamesababisha watu kuyaangalia mazingira ya kuishi na kujazana mno kunakoyakabili magereza hayo, na kuainisha iwapo kuna majanga yanayongoja kutokea.

eng: People who are being deprived of their liberty as punishment for their crimes should be guaranteed minimum living conditions, and sometimes these aren't met, as shown in the documentary of life in Brazilian prisons, which also provides possible solutions for this difficult situation.
swa: Watu ambao wamenyimwa uhuru kama adhabu ya makosa yao wanapaswa kuhakikishiwa angalau hali za maisha ya kawaida, na wakati mwingine haya hayapatikani kama inavyooneshwa katika masimulizi ya kina maisha ya magereza ya Brazili, , yanayotoa suluhisho kwa kwa hali hii ngumu.

swa: HIYO NDIYO HALI YA SASA, TUNACHOTAKA NI MABADILIKO.

swa: HATUTAKI TENA “SIASA ZA KICHINA ZA KWENYE KASRI”.

swa: NDIYO SABABU TUMEKUJA KUPIGA KURA.

eng: WE DO THIS BECAUSE WE DO NOT WANT OUR NEXT GENERATION COME THROUGHT ALL THIS AGAIN.
swa: TUNAFANYA HIVI KWA SABABU HATUTAKI VIZAZI VYETU VIJAVYO KUPITIA HALI HII TENA.

eng: I HOPE LOSO WILL UNDERSTAND.
swa: NATUMAINI LOSO ITAELEWA.

eng: Eventually, 222,990 people voted in the mock election, in which 54.6% cast blank votes.
swa: Hatimaye jumla ya watu 222,990 walishiriki kwenye uchaguzi huo wa majaribio, ambapo asilimia 54.6 walipiga kura bila kuandika chochote kwenye karatasi za kura.

eng: Leung Chun-ying only got 17.8% of the votes, a huge contrast with the result of small circle election, which was held in the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Center.
swa: Leung Chun-ying alipata tu asilimia 17.8 ya kura zote, ambapo matokeo yalikuwa kinyume kabisa na uchaguzi wa kundi lile dogo la wateule, ambao uliendeshwa katika Kituo cha Mikutano na Maonyesho cha Hong Kong.

eng: Protest outside the city hall on March 25
swa: Maandamano nje ya ukumbi wa jiji tarehe 25 Machi

eng: On March 25, more than 2,000 people protested outside the temporary election venue.
swa: Mnamo tarehe 25 Machi, zaidi ya watu 2,000 waliandamana nje ya ukumbi wa muda wa uchaguzi.

eng: Outraged by Leung's victory, they pushed the police barricades.
swa: Huku wakiwa wamekasirishwa sana na ushindi wa Leung, walipambana na kusukumana na ukuta wa polisi.

swa: Hapa chini kuna baadhi ya picha zilizopigwa na waandishi wa habari za kiraia kama zilivyotumwa inmediahk.net kuhusiana na mwonekano wa maandamano hayo:

swa: Picha na mtumiaji wa Flickr inmediahk (CC BY-NC).
