eng: I Paid a Bribe is an initiative of Kenyan anti-corruption activists fighting corruption in Kenya using the new technologies to crowdsource corruption experiences.
swa: I Paid a Bribe ni njia mojawapo inayotumiwa na wanaharakati dhidi ya ufisadi nchini, kwa kutumia teknolojia mpya ili kuwawezesha kupata ripoti za utoaji wa hongo.'

eng: I Paid a Bribe, modeled after India's anti-corruption portal (IPAB), is a partnership between IPAB and Wamani Trust of Kenya to bring IPAB to East and Central Africa.
swa: I paid a Bribe' imefuatia muundo wa 'India Anti-Corruption Portal (IPAB)' na ni ushirkiano kati ya IPAB na Wamani Trust ya Kenya ili kuleta IPAB katika Afrika Mashariki na Kati.

eng: I Paid a Bribe is:

eng: On June 24, a new president has been officially declared in Egypt and his name is Mohammed Morsi.
swa: Tarehe 24 Juni, raisi mpya wa Misri alitangazwa rasmi na jina lake ni Mohammed Morsi.

eng: The Muslim Brotherhood's Morsi has become Egypt's first freely elected president, and like all other candidates, he has his own presidential program and promises that voters - supposedly - elected him based on.
swa: Morsi wa chama cha Muslim Brotherhood, amekuwa raisi wa kwanza wa Misri kuchaguliwa kwa uchaguzi huru, na kama ilivyo kwa wagombea wengine wote, alikuwa na mikakati yake na ahadi ambazo wapiga kura walizikubali na kuamua kumchagua.

eng: But how can Egyptians hold Morsi accountable for his promises and watch the progress in achieving them?
swa: Lakini, watu wa Misri watawezaje kumbana Morsi awajibike katika kutimiza ahadi zake na kufuatilia mienendo ya namna ahadi zitakavyotimizwa?

eng: Wael Ghonim tweeted about a new application for that.
swa: Wael Ghonim alitwiti kuhusu kitumizi kipya kwa ajili ya kuhakikisha Morsi anawajibika kutimiza ahadi zake na kufuatilia kila hatua ya namna ya utimizaji wa ahadi hizo:

eng: @Ghonim: Tracking the performance of #Morsi (Egypt's newly elected president): http://www.morsimeter.com (via @ezzatkamel)
swa: @Ghonim: Kinafuatilia utendaji wa Morsi (Raisi mpya mteule wa Misri): http://www.morsimeter.com (via @ezzatkamel)

eng: MorsiMeter, Tracking the performance of Morsi, the newly elected president of Egypt
swa: Kipimio cha Morsi, kinafuatilia utendaji wa Morsi, raisi mpya mteule wa Misri.

eng: The application is created by Zabatak, (@Zabatak), a non-profit initiative which aims at making Egypt become bribery free, corruption-free and safe.
swa: Kitumizi hiki kimebuniwa na Zabatak, (@Zabatak),ni mkakati usio wa kimaslahi wenye lengo la kuifanya Misri isiwe na hongo, wala isiwe na rushwa na iwe salama.

eng: And on MorsiMeter's Facebook page, they describe the application as follows : The is an initiative to document and monitor the performance of the new Egyptian president, Mohammed Morsi, and we will monitor what has been achieved from what he had promised in his program during his first 100 days in power.
swa: Na katika ukurasa wa Facebook, wa kipimio cha Morsi,wanaelezea kitumizi hiki kama ifuatavyo: Huu ni mkakati wa kurekodi na kufuatilia utendaji wa raisi mpya wa Misri, Mohammed Morsi, na tutafuatilia kila litakalotimizwa kwa yale yote aliyoyaahidi katika mpango wake kwa muda wa siku 100 za kwanza akiwa madarakani.

eng: Egyptian netizens shared their thoughts and opinions about the meter on Twitter as follows:
swa: Watumiaji wa mtandao Misri walitoa mitizamo na mawazo yao kuhusiana na kipimio hiki katika Twita kama ifuatavyo:

eng: @omarkamel: MorsiMeter NOT a bad idea.
swa: @omarkamel: Kipimio cha Morsi si wazo baya.

eng: But must also measure how good we think those ideas are to start with.
swa: Lakini lazima pia kipime tunawazaje vizuri kwa namna ambavyo mawazo haya yaanze.

eng: Security plan SUCKS.
swa: Mpango wa ulinzi unakera.

eng: @AbdoRepublic: Brilliant idea to assess #morsi 's performance.
swa: @AbdoRepublic: Ni wazo zuri sana la kupima utendaji wa Morsi.

eng: Goodbye Dictatorship
swa: Kwa heri udikteta.

eng: This post is part of our special coverage of Egypt Elections 2011/2012.
swa: Makala hii ni miongoni mwa makala zetu maalumu kuhusiana na chaguzi za Misri 2011/2012.

eng: The cheerful global blog, PocketCultures has published an e-book about 15 children's games from different countries that can easily be played by readers.
swa: Blogu changamfu la Kimataifa, PocketCultures limechapisha limechapisha kitabu kuhusu michezo kumi na tano ya watoto kutoka nchi mbalimbali na amabayo inaweza kuchezwa kwa urahisi na msomaji.

eng: The book is called Games for Kids of the World and can be downloaded for free on iPad, Mac or PC.
swa: Kitabu kinaitwa 'Games for Kids of the World' na kinaweza kupatikana kwa bure kwenye iPad, Mac au kwenye kompyuta.

eng: Mehdi Hassan Khan also famously known as the ‘King of Ghazal’ passed away on Wednesday, 13, June, 2012 after a protracted illness, in a local hospital in Karachi city of Pakistan.
swa: Mehdi Hassan Khan ambaye alijulikana kama ‘Mfalme Ghazal’ alifariki jumatano ya tarehe 13, Juni, 2012 baada ya kuugua kwa muda mrefu katika hospitali ya jiji la Karachi nchini Pakistan.

eng: The 84 years old Ghazal Singer was suffering from illness for the past 12 years.
swa: Mwimbaji huyo wa Ghazal, aliyekuwa na umri wa miaka 84, alikuwa akiugua kwa takribani miaka 12.

eng: After his death ‘#MehdiHassan’ had been trending on Twitter across Pakistan and India.
swa: Baada ya kifo chake, 'MehdiHassan', amekuwa akitawala sana katika mtandao wa Twita katika nchi za Pakistan na India.

eng: Hundreds of his fan including popular singers, famous celebrities and politicians shared their condolences and tribute to the legendary singer.
swa: Mamia ya mashabiki wake, wakiwemo waimbaji, watu maarufu, na wanasiasa waliotoa salamu za rambirambi na heshima zao kwa mwimbaji huyo maarufu.

eng: His fans are also sharing his hit Ghazals in social networks.
swa: Mashabiki wake pia wamekuwa wakiweka katika mitandao mbalimbali ya kijamii nyimbo zake za Ghazal zilizowahi kuwa maarufu.

eng: Indian Prime Minister Manmohan Singh (@PMOIndia) writes in Twitter sharing his deep grief:
swa: Waziri mkuu wa India Manmohan Singh ameandika katika ukurasa wake wa Twita akionesha huzuni yake::

eng: @PMOIndia: The influence of his passion for Urdu poetry and early grooming in Dhrupad tradition earned for him a special place in the world of music.
swa: @PMOIndia: “ushawishi wa mapenzi yake kwa ushairi wa Urdu na kutayarishwa kwake mapema katika utamaduni wa Dhrupad umemzawadia nafasi muhimu sana katika ulimwengu wa muziki”

eng: Popular Indain actor Shahrukh Khan (@imsrk) tweets about his memories from the famous Gahzal singer:
swa: Muigizaji maarufu wa Kihindi Shahrukh Khan katika ukurasa wake wa Twita anaeleza ni kwa namna gani anavyomkumbuka mwimbaji mashuhuri Ghazal:

eng: @imsrk: memories of my mom cooking in a grimy kitchen as it rained outside, while mehdi hassan floated out of a Beltek 2 in 1 (cassette player).
swa: @imsrk: “Ninakumbuka kipindi ambacho mama yangu alikuwa akipika katika jiko lililojaa masizi huku mvua ikinyesha, sauti ya Mehdi Hassan ilikuwa ikitumbuiza kupitia redio kaseti”.

eng: Singer Lata Mangeshkar offered her condolence to Mehdi Hassan's family talking to the media and said that his demise is a great loss to music industry.
swa: Mwimbaji Lata Mangeshkar alitoa salamu za rambirambi kwa familia ya Mehdi Hassan alipoongea na vyombo vya habari na alisema kuwa kifo chake ni pigo kubwa katika tasnia ya muziki.

eng: Asif Noorani in Dawn blog says:
swa: Asif Noorani katika blogu ya Dawn anasema:

eng: Mehdi Hassan is dead, but I am not sad.
swa: Mehdi Hassan amefariki, lakini sihuzuniki.

eng: Don’t curse me when I say I am relieved, for death has brought an end to his decade-long suffering. Watching him lie helpless and speechless, afflicted by so many ailments, not to speak of bedsores, was a heart-wrenching experience.
swa: Usinilaani kwa kuwa ninasema nimepata tulizo, kifo chake kimekuwa ni mwisho wa mateso aliyoyapata kwa miaka 10. kumshuhudia akiwa amelala, asiyejiweza wala kuongea, akiteseka kwa maumivu, achilia mbali ngozi yake iliyo na vidonda, ilikuwa ni hali isiyozoeleka

eng: Adil Omar (@Adil_Omar) tweets:
swa: Adil Omar (@Adil_Omar) katika ukurasa wake wa Twita anasema:

eng: @Adil_Omar:I won't pretend that I listened to his music, but I was well aware of his status and impact.
swa: @Adil_Omar:Siwezi kudanganya kuwa nilikuwa nausikiliza muziki wake, lakini nilikuwa nafahamu fika thamani na mchango wake.

eng: RIP Mehdi Hassan
swa: Pumzika kwa amani Mehdi Hassan.

eng: Singer Talat Aziz, who was trained by Mehdi Hassan describes how he feels:
swa: Mwimbaji Talat Aziz, anaelezea hisia zake:

eng: I feel a tremendous personal sense of loss.
swa: Ninajisikia mwenye huzuni kupita kiasi.

eng: I was his 'shagird' (apprentice), I spent a lot of time with him.
swa: Nilikuwa mwanafunzi wake, mara nyingi nilikuwa naye.

eng: For me he was a star.
swa: Kwangu mimi alikuwa ni nyota.

eng: I don't have words to describe his loss.
swa: Ninakosa cha kusema kufuatia kifo chake.

eng: He was a great asset to the world of Ghazal.
swa: Alikuwa hazina kubwa kwa ulimwengu wa Ghazal.

eng: Though he was not singing for quite sometime, but he will be missed.
swa: Pamaja na kuwa ni muda mrefu ulipita bila yeye kuimba, lakini atakumbukwa.

eng: There will never be another Mehdi Hassan.
swa: Hapatatokea tena Mehdi Hassan mwingine.

eng: Please check out Fawad's tribute to Mehdi Hassan, whom he terms as one of the greatest sub-continental singers of the post-partition era.
swa: Ipitie tanzia ya Fawad kwa Mehdi Hassan, ambaye anamchukulia kama mwimbaji wa enzi asiye na mfano katika Asia ya kusini.

eng: Unlike other countries in the region, Sudan is grossly underreported, and this was ever so evident during Friday and Saturday’s street demonstrations.
swa: Tofauti na nchi nyingine katika eneo lake, Sudani mara nyingi huwa haipati nafasi katika vyombo vikuu vya habari, na hili lilikuwa wazi zaidi wakati wa maandamano yaliyofanyika Ijumaa na Jumamosi.

eng: The Sudanese government keeps a tight grip on local media and bans journalists from reporting on issues of human rights and corruption.
swa: Sababu ni kwamba serikali ya Sudani imevibana mno vyombo vya ndani vya habari na kuwazuia waandishi kuripoti habari zinazohusu masuala ya haki za binadamu na ufisadi.

eng: This however does not justify the blatant lack of interest from international media outlets.
swa: Hali hii, hata hivyo haihalalishi tabia dhahiri ya vyombo vya habari vya nje ya kutotilia maanani .

eng: Al Jazeera, for instance, played a prominent role in reporting the uprisings in several Arab countries, but netizens say it seems to ignore the events currently unfolding in Sudan.
swa: Al Jazeera, kwa mfano, ilifanya wajibu wake kwa namna ya pekee katika kuripoti maandamano yaliyotokea katika nchi kadhaa za ki-Arabu, lakini watumiaji wa mtandao wanasema shirika hilo linaonekana kupuuza matukio yanayoendelea nchini Sudani.

eng: Sudanese women at the forefront of #SudanRevolts.
swa: Wanawake wa ki-Sudani wakiwa mstari wa mbele katika maandamano yanayoendelea Sudani.

eng: The media coverage of recent protests in Sudan was confined to articles in Al Arabiya and Al Jazeera, including some snippets on Al Jazeera’s English Channel.
swa: Habari za maandamano ya hivi karibuni nchini Sudani zilizopata nafasi kwenye vyombo vikuu vya habari, zilionekana tu kwenye makala zilizochapishwa kwenye mtandao wa Al Arabiya na Al Jazeera, kwa kujumuisha dondoo chache kwenye Idhaa ya Kiingereza ya Al Jazeera.

eng: Other news outlets to cover the protests include CNN, the Malaysian news outlet The Star, the New York Times, Yahoo News, ABC News, and the Chicago Tribune.
swa: Mashirika mengine ya habari yaliyoripoti maandamano hayo ni CNN, The Star shirika la habari la ki-Malaysia, New York Times, Yahoo News, ABC News, na Chicago Tribune.

eng: Nonetheless, this has not brought enough attention to the issues on the ground, as most of these news outlets don’t have much impact in the region, say netizens.
swa: Hata hivyo, habari hizi hazijafanya watu kujua vizuri kile kinachoendelea nchini humo, kwa kuwa, kwa mujibu wa watumiaji wa mitandao, vyombo hivi vya habari havina hadhira kubwa katika eneo hili.

eng: The protests kicked off after Friday prayers in a mosque in Wad Nubawi neighborhood in Omdurman.
swa: Maandamano yalianza baada ya swala ya Ijumaa katika msikiti wa mtaa wa Wad Nubawi huko Omdurman.

eng: A call for protests tagged as #SandstormFriday was made a day earlier.
swa: Wito wa maandamano ulitolewa kupitia alama habari ya #SandstormFriday siku moja kabla.

eng: The demonstrations were organized to protest against rising prices and the government’s new austerity plans that were announced by Sudanese president Omar Al-Bashir and implemented last week.
swa: Maandamano yaliratibiwa ili kupinga mfumuko wa bei na mpango wa serikali kubana matumizi ambao ulitangazwa na rais wa Sudan Omar Al-Bashir na kuanza kutekelezwa juma lililopita.

eng: Those who heard about the protest made their way there.
swa: Wale waliosikia habari za maandamano hayo walijitokeza kwenye eneo la tukio.

eng: Hamid was one of them; he tweeted : On my way to Al-Sayed Abdelrahman mosque in Wad Nubawi.
swa: Hamid alikuwa mmoja wao, na hapa alitwiti tweeted : Ninaelekea kwenye msikiti wa Al-Sayed Abdelrahman kwenye mtaa wa Wad Nubawi.

eng: After prayer, people gathered in front of the mosque and marched on one of the main roads in Wad Nubawi chanting anti-regime slogans.
swa: Baada ya swala, watu walikusanyika mbele ya msikiti na kuandamana kupitia barabara za mitaa ya Wad Nubawi wakiimba kauli mbiu za kupinga utawala wa nchi hiyo.

eng: This protest lasted a few hours before police dispersed the crowd with tear gas and plain clothed police men infiltrated the ranks of the protesters.
swa: Maandamano yalimalizika saa chache kabla ya polisi kuwatawanya waandamanaji kwa kutumia mabomu ya machozi na polisi waliokuwa wamevaa kiraia walijipenyeza kwenye makundi ya waandamanaji.

eng: After the protests were disbanded, Yousif Al Mahdi was on the scene and tweeted:
swa: Baada ya waandamanaji kutawanywa, Yousif Al Mahdi alikuwa kwenye eneo la tukio na kutwiti :

eng: Protest back on inside district, wad nubawi fighting back, police cars in sideroads & firing tear gas @ houses
swa: Maandamano yamerudi safari hii kwenye wilaya ya Wad Nubawi wakipambana, magari ya polisi yameegeshwa pembeni mwa barabara yanarusha mabomu ya machozi

eng: At the same time, similar protests started in Burri neighbourhood of Khartoum, and eventually in Al-Daim.
swa: Wakati huo huo, maandamano kama hayo yalianza kwenye mitaa ya Burri jijini Khartoum, na baadae kule Al-Daim.

eng: The protests in Burri were quickly suppressed by security personnel and police.
swa: Maandamano ya Burri yalidhibitiwa haraka sana na wanausalama wakishirikiana na polisi.

eng: Al-Daim however was too much for the authorities to handle.
swa: Yale ya Al-Daim hata hivyo yalikuwa makubwa mno kwa polisi kuweza kuyadhibiti.

eng: Ammar Mahdi tweets:
swa: Ammar Mahdi alitwiti :

eng: Hours ago from ‪#AlDaim district , ppl throwing police signs and step on them.
swa: Masaa machache yaliyopita kutoka ‪#AlDaim watu wanatupa alama za polisi na wanapanda juu ya alama hizo

eng: Moez Ali shares a photograph of a burning police car on Twitter The protests in Al-Daim went on into the night with several police trucks burnt by protesters.
swa: Picha iliyowekwa na Moezi Ali katika mtandao wa twita kuonyesha gari la polisi likiteketea kwa moto Maandamano ya Al-Daim yaliendelea mpaka usiku huku magari kadhaa ya polisi yakiteketezwa kwa moto na wanaandamanaji.

eng: Haitham Makkawi was on the ground and claimed that Al-Daim residents have taken over the scene:
swa: Haitham Makkawi alikuwa kwenye eneo la tukio na alidai kwamba wakaazi wa Al-Daim wamejaza eneo hilo:

eng: Al-Daim residents have completely taken over!
swa: Wakazi wa Al-Daim wamejazana eneo hili!

eng: Photos of burnt down police trucks were all over twitter showing the aftermath of the protests.
swa: Picha za kuteketea kwa magari ya polisi zimetawanyika kwenye mtandao wa twita kuonyesha athari ziliozletwa na waandamanaji.

eng: Later that night another protest started in Siteen Street, a main road in Khartoum next to Riyad neighbourhood; this photo shows protesters gathering around a burnt tyre in the middle of the road.
swa: Baadae usiku huo, maandamano mengine yalianza kwenye mtaa wa Siteen, barabara kuu mjini Khartoum, karibu na mtaa wa Riyad;Picha hii inaonyesha wanaandamanaji wakikusanyika kuzunguka tairi linaloungua moto katikati ya barabara.

eng: Girifna, a non-violent movement, used social media sites like Facebook and Twitter to convey information about the whereabouts of protests around the tri-state capital.
swa: Girifna, wanaharakati wa vuguvugu la amani, walitumia zana za habari za kiraia kama Facebook na Twita ili kutawanya habari kuhusu mahali walipo waandamanaji katika mji huo mkuu wenye majimbo matatu.

eng: In this tweet , Girifna directs people to the location of new protests in Omdurman: Girifna - Omdurman: Calling on the residents of Omdurman to head now to Al-Sabeel and Al-Doha roundabout
swa: Katika twiti hii, Girifna anaelekeza watu eneo la maandamano huko Omdurman: Girifna - Omdurman: Nawaalika wakazi wa Omdurman kuelekea Al-Sabeel na katika mzunguko wa Al-Doha

eng: Girifna’s efforts portray the advantages of citizen journalism in a country where free speech and reporting is suppressed.
swa: Jitihada za Girifna ni mfano dhahiri wa uandishi wa habari za kiraia katika nchi ambapo uhuru wa kujieleza na kuripoti habari umebinywa.

eng: The Sudanese online community was overjoyed by the events unfolding in the capital Khartoum; Hamid Murtada, who was at the heart of the protests, tweeted : Allah-u-Akbar and Al Hamdulillah ..
swa: Jamii ya wa-Sudani mtandaoni ilifurahishwa mno na matukio yanayoendelea katika mji mkuu wa Khartoum; Hamid Murtada, ambaye alikuwa kwenye maandamano hayo, alitwiti: الله أكبر ولله الحمد... البلد مولعة من كل جهة... قامت قامت!

eng: The country is on fire..
swa: Allah-u-Akbar na Al Hamdulillah …Nchi inawaka moto…na inaendelea kuwaka!

eng: It's on, it's on! Some of the Sudanese Twitter users likened the events happening in Khartoum to those in other countries in the region and maintained solidarity with those struggling with dictatorial regimes elsewhere.
swa: Baadhi ya watumiaji wa mtandao wa twita wa-Sudani walifurahishwa na matukio yanayotokea mjini Khartoum na yale yanayotokea kwenye nchi nyingine za eneo hilo na kuonyesha mshikamano na wale wanaohangaika kujikwamua na tawala za ki-dikteta duniani kote.

eng: Khalid Ewais, a journalist with Al Arabiya, tweeted : Salute to the revolutionaries of Syria who are supporting our revolution despite their circumstances, as for those who are mocking Sudan and its people we tell them: This is not our first revolution
swa: Khalid Ewais, mwandishi wa habari wa Al Arabiya, alitwiti: تحية لثوار سوريا الذين يناصرون ثورتنا الآن رغم ظروفهم، أما بعض الذين يسخرون من السودان وشعبه الآن نقول: ليست ثورتنا الأولى ‎ Ninawaheshimu wanamapinduzi wa Syria ambao wanaunga mkono mapinduzi yetu pamoja na hali yao ngumu, na wale wanaoikejeli Sudani na watu wake, kwao tunawaambia: Haya si mapinduzi yetu ya kwanza

eng: The Sudanese Diaspora were on standby for those who needed help on the ground giving tips on how to document the protests and possible use of social media sites in the advent of an internet shutdown.
swa: Raia wa Sudani wanaoishi nje ya nchi hiyo walikuwa tayari kwa wale waliohitaji msaada walioko eneo la tukio kwa kuwapa maelekezo ya namna ya kutangaza maandamano hayo na matumizi ya zana za uandishi wa kiraia ikitokea mtandao wa intaneti umekatwa.

eng: Nada, a Sudanese residing in Egypt, advised on how best to cover the demonstrations:
swa: Nada, m-Sudani anayeishi Misri, alishauri namna ya kutangaza vyema yanayoendelea kwenye maandamano:

eng: if u are an IPHONE user & are amongst the protesters in sudan, download USTREAM thru the app. world. ‪#SudanRevolts.
swa: Kama unatumia simu aina ya IPHONE na ni miongoni mwa waandamanaji nchini Sudani, shusha (download) programu ya USTREAM kupitia kitendea kazi kiitwacho world‪#SudanRevolts.

eng: The online Sudanese community seems optimistic about the course of the Sudanese revolution, where many promise that June 30, 2012 will be the ruling National Congress Party's final anniversary.
swa: Jamii ya mtandaoni ya wa-Sudani ina matumaini na mwelekeo wa mapinduzi ya Sudani, ambapo wengi wanajiapiza kwamba tarehe 30, Juni 2012 itakuwa siku ya mwisho ya chama kinachotawala nchi hiyo cha NCP (National Congress Party) kuadhimisha kuwapo kwake madarakani.

eng: Sudanese officials are repeating the all too familiar 'lies' Arab officials have been telling us since the beginning of the so-called Arab Spring in December 2010.
swa: Maafisa wa serikali ya Sudani wanaendelea kurudia ‘uongo’ uliozoeleka ambao watawala wa ki-Arabu wamekuwa wakiutumia tangu kuanza kwa yale yanayoitwa Mapinduzi ya Uarabuni yaliyoanza mwezi Desemba 2010.

eng: Protests are contained, they say, in citizens attacking policemen, who retaliate in self-defense, goes the story.
swa: Imekuwa kawaida kusikia kauli kama, ‘waandamanaji wamedhibitiwa wakati wakiwashambulia polisi, ambao nao walijihami kwa kushambulia’ na kuendelea.

eng: Sudan is the latest country to join the massive protest movement that saw the toppling of Zine Al Abedine Ben Ali of Tunisia in January 2011 and Hosni Mubarak of Egypt the following month.
swa: Sudani ni nchi iliyojiunga hivi karibuni kwenye vuguvugu kubwa la maandamano ya wananchi wanaotaka mabadiliko yaliyosababisha kuanguka kwa watawala wa muda mrefu kama Zine Al Abedine Ben Ali wa Tunisia mapema mwezi Januari 2011 na mwanzake Hosni Mubarak wa Misri mwezi uliofuata.

eng: Libya's Muammar Gaddafi was also captured and later on killed by an angry mob in October 2011.
swa: Muammar Gaddafi wa Libya naye alikamatwa na baadae kuuawa na kundi la wananchi wenye hasira mwezi Oktoba 2011.

eng: Arab governments are keen in limiting their loss to those three dictators by conducting a massive crackdown on political dissent and an unprecedented killing spree against their revolting people.
swa: Serikali za ki-Arabu zimekuwa na jitihada ya kuhakikisha idadi ya madikteta waliong’olewa haizidi hao watatu, kwa kufanya ukandamizaji mkubwa dhidi ya upinzani wa kisiasa na vile vile kuendesha vitendo vya mauaji yasiyokubalika ya watu wao wenyewe wanaoonekana 'kuwaasi'.

eng: Sudanese officials are now repeating the same lines we heard from all Arab officials, whose reigns are troubled by angry people they have continued to rule with an iron fist and oppress for decades.
swa: Maafisa wa Sudani sasa wanarudia yale yale tuliyoyasikia kwa watawala wote wa nchi za ki-Arabu ambao nchi zao zinasumbuliwa na wananchi wenye hasira ambao wamekuwa wakitawaliwa kidhalimu na kwa kukandamizwa kwa miongo kadhaa.

eng: Mimz reacts to how the official Sudanese News Agency (SUNA) covered the news.
swa: Mimz anaonyesha hisia zake juu ya jinsi ambavyo Shirika la Habari la Sudani (SUNA) lilitangaza habari hizo.

eng: @MimzicalMimz: SUNA says protests yesterday were 'limited'. Just the fact that protests were acknowledged conveys the magnitude of #SudanRevolts
swa: @MimzicalMimz: Shirika la habari SUNA linasema jana waandamanaji “walizuiwa’. ukweli kwamba shirika hilo limeandika kuhusu habari hiyo jambo hilo pekee ni ujumbe mahsusi kuhusu ukubwa wa maandamano hayo.

eng: Egyptian journalist Salma Elwardany, who is in Khartoum, sums up the coverage.
swa: Mwandishi wa habari wa ki-Misri Salma Elwardany, ambaye yuko Khartoum, anatoa muhtasari wa yanayotokea nchini humo.

eng: Nshima, the stodgy porridge-like substance cooked out of maize-meal, has divided families and triggered food riots in Zambia at one time or other.
swa: Nshima, aina ya ugali unaopikwa kwa unga wa mahindi, umewahi kuwa sababu ya migogoro ya kifamilia na kusababisha ghasia kadhaa zinazohusiana na chakula nchini Zambia katika nyakati tofauti.

eng: The production of maize — or corn as it is known in other parts of the world — is an even bigger issue in the mining region of the Copperbelt and metropolitan areas like the capital, Lusaka, where large working populations rely on the commercial supply of the product.
swa: Uzalishaji wa mahindi ni shughuli nyeti katika maeneo yanazalisha dhahabu kama Copperbelt pamoja na maeneo mengine muhimu kama mji mkuu, Lusaka, ambako idadi kubwa ya watu wanategemea sana mahindi.

eng: Accordingly, maize determines the political direction of the nation.
swa: Kwa sehemu kubwa, mahindi yanaongoza mustakabali wa kisiasa katika nchi hii.

eng: In May, the World Bank urged the Zambian government not to interfere in determining the floor prices of maize sold by farmers to the Food Reserve Agency and other interested parties in the agri-business chain.

eng: Despite such calls, the Ministry of Agriculture announced this year’s floor price of maize at K65,000 (about $13 USD) per 50 kilo bag.
swa: Pamoja na mwito huo, Waziri wa Kilimo alitangaza kwamba mwaka huu, bei ya unga wa mahindi itakuwa K65,000 (sawa na takribani Tsh. 20,000) kwa gunia la kilo 50.

eng: World Bank country director for Zambia, Malawi and Zimbabwe, Kundhavi Kadiresan criticized the decision and claimed that poor Zambian farmers were being exploited as some traders were buying maize from them in anticipation of re-selling it at a higher price to the state-run Food Reserve Agency.
swa: Mkurugenzi wa Benki ya Dunia kwa nchi za Zambia, Malawi na Zimbabwe, Bw. Kundhavi Kadiresan aliukosoa uamuzi huo na kudai kwamba wakulima masikini wa Zambia wananyonywa kwa sababu baadhi ya wafanyabiashara walikuwa wananunua mahindi kutoka kwa wakulima hao kwa ajili ya kuliuzia Shirika linaloendeshwa na serikali liitwalo Hifadhi ya Chakula kwa bei ya juu.

eng: Kadiresan also indicated that the World Bank is deeply concerned that not only does the government’s policy fail to ensure the long term sustainable growth of the agriculture sector, it also does very little to create jobs and reduce poverty.

swa: Sekta ya kilimo nchini Zambia inategemea sana mahindi, ukiachilia mbali mazao mengine na mifugo.

eng: The bulk of the maize is grown by peasant farmers who are faced with regular droughts during the rainy season, an unreliable and expensive supply of fertilizer, and difficulties transporting the commodity to markets.
swa: Sehemu kubwa ya mahindi inalimwa na wakulima wadogo ambao wanakabiliwa na hali ya ukame wa mara kwa mara hata nyakati za majira ya mvua, ugavi wa mbolea usioaminika na wenye gharama kubwa, na matatizo ya usafiri kati ya mashamba yao na yaliko masoko ya mahindi.

eng: In 1986, Zambians in the Copperbelt and Lusaka regions rioted because the price of maize increased several fold when incomes were stagnant.
swa: Mwaka 1986, wa_Zambia wanaoishi kwenye majimbo ya Copperbelt na Lusaka waligoma kwa sababu bei ya mahindi ilikuwa imeongezeka mara dufu wakati kipato walichokuwa wanakipata kilibaki vile kilivyokuwa.

eng: Four years later, unrest over price increases even sparked a coup attempt.
swa: Miaka minne baadae, ghasia zilizohusiana na bei ya mahindi ziliongezeka kiasi cha kusababisha jeshi kuingilia kati.

eng: Announcing the new maize floor price, agriculture and livestock minister Emmanuel Chenda said:
swa: Akitangaza habari hizo za bei mpya ya unga mahindi, waziri wa kilimo na mifugo Emmanuel Chandaalisema:

eng: We have taken this decision in order to protect the food security of the country and also to ensure that small-scale farmers are not discouraged from producing the crop in subsequent years… To ensure that Zambian maize is competitive on the international markets, the Government will ensure that production costs are reduced through, among other strategies, the provision of agricultural extension training and transportation for mobility to extension workers with a view to increasing productivity among the small-scale farmers.
swa: Tumechukua uamuzi ili kulinda usalama wa chakula katika nchi na pia kuhakikisha kwamba wakulima wadogo hawakatishwi tamaa kuzalisha mazao katika miaka ijayo…kuhakikisha mahindi yanayolimwa Zambia yanakuwa na ushindani vya kutosha katika soko la kimataifa. Serikali itahakikisha gharama za uzalishaji zinapungua kupitia, pamoja na mikakati mingine, mafunzo ya huduma za ugavi wa kilimo na usafiri kwa ajili ya wafanyakazi wa mafunzo hayo kwa mtazamo wa kuongeza uzalishaji miongoni mwa wakulima wadogo.

eng: Chenda also revealed that the Government was putting in place programs to build additional storage facilities as a long-term measure to avoid wastage under the Food Reserve Agency (FRA).
swa: Chenda pia aliweka wazi kwamba serikali ilikuwa inachukua hatua za kutayarisha mipango wa muda mrefu ywa kujenga maghala ili kuondoa tatizo la kupotea kwa chakula kingi chini ya Shirika la Hifadhi ya Chakula.

eng: A few days before the minister’s statement, the FRA had destroyed huge stocks of rotten maize in various districts of the country.
swa: Siku chache kabla ya tamko hilo la waziri, shirika la hifadhi ya chakula liliharibu kiasi kikubwa cha mahindi yaliyoharibika katika wilaya kadhaa za nchi hiyo.

eng: Said Chenda:
swa: Chenda alisema:

eng: I wish to inform the nation that most of the waste under the FRA we have been experiencing is due to inadequate and unsuitable storage facilities… In order to address this challenge, Government has begun to put in place programs to build additional storage facilities as a long-term measure.
swa: Ningependa kulijulisha taifa kwamba uharibifu wa vyakula kwenye shirika letu la hifadhi ya chakula kwa sehemu kubwa unatokana na vifaa duni vya kuhifadhia…Ili kukabiliana na changamoto hii, Serikali imeanza kutekeleza mipango ya kujenga vifaa vya kudumu vya kuhifadhia.

eng: This post and its translations to Spanish, Arabic and French were commissioned by the International Security Network (ISN) as part of a partnership to seek out citizen voices on international relations and security issues worldwide.Visit the ISN blog and see more related stories.
swa: Makala haya ni sehemu ya tafsiri ya ki-Hispania, ki-Arabu na ki-Faransa ambazo zilitolewa na Mtandao wa Usalama wa Kimataifa (ISN) kama sehemu ya ushirikiano wa kutafuta sauti za raia wa kawaida katika masuala ya mahusiano na usalama wa mataifa duniani. Tembelea blogu ya ISN ili kuona habari nyingine zinazofanana na hii.

eng: Featured image of Zambian maize by Choconancy1 on Flickr (CC BY-NC-SA 2.0).
swa: Picha inayoonekana ya mahindi yanayolimwa Zambia imewekwa na Choconancy1 kwenye mtandao wa Flickr (CC BY-NC-SA 2.0).

eng: If you are not used to reading success stories about education in Afghanistan, this one is for a change.
swa: Kama hujazoea kusoma habari za mafanikio ya kielimu katika nchi ya Afganistani, habari hii ni ya kukubadilisha mtazamo wako.

eng: On 30 June, 2012 the Center of Science in Kabul announced that Khalilullah Yaqubi, a high school student from Ghazni province, had independently discovered a mathematical formula that can be used to solve 'second-degree quadratic equations with one unknown'.
swa: Mnamo tarehe 30 Juni, 2012, Kituo cha Sayansi katika mji wa Kabul, kilitangaza kuwa Khalilullah Yaqubi, mwanafunzi wa shule ya sekondari kutoka katika Jimbo la Ghazni, kwa juhudi zake mwenyewe aligundua kanuni ya kimahesabu inayoweza kutumika katika kukokotoa milinganyo ya kwadratiki ya mtajo mmoja ya ukomo wa kipeo cha pili.

eng: Khalilullah is an eleventh-grade student at the Al-Beruni High School in Nawabad, on the outskirts of the city of Ghazni.
swa: Khalilullah ni mwanafunzi wa darasa la 11 (sawa na kidato cha tano Afrika Mashariki) katika shule ya sekondari ya Al-Beruni iliyo katika mitaa ya Nawabad nje kidogo ya jiji la Ghazni.

eng: Speaking about the formula, Khalilullah says:
swa: Akiongea kuhusu kanuni hiyo, Khalilullah anasema:

eng: I have not seen this formula before in any book.
swa: Sijawahi kuiona kanuni hii katika kitabu chochote.

eng: Neither I have used any source, nor cheated from Internet.
swa: Wala sijawahi kutumia chanzo chochote, au kufanya udanganyifu wowote kwa kutumia mtandao wa intaneti.

eng: This is all my efforts.
swa: Hizi ni kutokana na jitihada zangu mwenyewe.

eng: Through this formula we can solve the problems of degree of equations (sic).
swa: Kupitia kanuni hii, tunaweza kukokotoa maswali mbalimbali ya milinganyo (sic).

eng: Some Twitter users have welcomed the news as an indication of improvements in the Afghan education sector.
swa: Baadhi ya watumiaji wa Twita wamezipokea habari hizi kama ishara ya maendeleo ya sekta ya elimu nchini Afganistani.

eng: Mulex, for example, has tweeted:
swa: Kwa mfano, Mulex alitwiti:

eng: Wow!
swa: Loo!

eng: Amazing news from Afghanistan.
swa: Habari za kushangaza kutoka Afghanistani.

eng: Sign of progress in their education system.
swa: Ni ishara ya maendeleo kwa mfumo wa elimu yao.

eng: Another Twitter user, Jasur Ashurov ('A settled nomad from Central Asia'), wrote:
swa: Mtumiaji mwingine wa Twita, Jasur Ashurov (‘mkazi asiye mzawa kutoka Asia ya Kati aliandika:

eng: You don't always get positive news from #Afghanistan.
swa: Si rahisi sana kupata habari nzuri kutoka nchini Afghanistani.

eng: This why I've been so happy to read this.
swa: Ndio maana nimekuwa na furaha sana baada ya kusoma habari hii.

eng: Rephrasing a Russian scientist and poet, he added :
swa: Akifupisha maneno aliyowahi kuandika Jasur Ashurov, mwanasayansi na mshairi wa Kirusi ,Jasur Ashurov aliongeza :

eng: Our country Afghanistan is one of the countries where proper attention has not been paid to education sector.
swa: Nchi yetu ya Afghanistani ni miongoni mwa nchi ambazo sekta ya elimu haijapewa msisitizo stahiki.

eng: One of the basic reasons has been the continuous instability overwhelming the society.
swa: Moja ya sababu kubwa imekuwa ni mwendelezo wa kutokuwa na utulivu wa kisiasa, jambo linaloizidi uwezo jamii.

eng: The wars and conflicts - national, regional and international – that have been using Afghan land as their theater have made the development in social and educational fields suffocate to a large extent.
swa: Vita na migogoro -ya kitaifa, ya kikanda na hata kimataifa- ambayo imekuwa ikiitumia ardhi ya Afghanistani kama kiwanja cha vita imesababisha maendeleo kudorora kwa kiasi kikubwa katika nyaja za kijamii na za kielimu.

eng: Starting from Soviet invasion in 1979, one can count myriads of tussles and disturbances hampering the establishment of satisfactory education system.
swa: Kuanzia mapinduzi ya Kisovieti ya mwaka 1979, mtu anaweza kuhesabu maelfu ya mapigano na usumbufu uliozuia kuanzishwa kwa mfumo wa elimu wa kuridhisha.

eng: The problems, more basic in nature, have been the focal point of people's concentration rather than the education system.
swa: Matatizo, ambayo ni ya kiasili zaidi, yamekuwa ndio yanayozingatiwa sana na watu kuliko mfumo wa elimu.

eng: Despite all these difficulties, many Afghans succeed in becoming educated, sometimes even self-educated.
swa: Pamoja na changamoto zote hizi, watu wengi wa Afghanistan wamefanikiwa kupata elimu, na wakati mwingine wakijisomesha wenyewe.

eng: In December 2011, another talented resident of Ghazni, without any special training or tools, flew an aircraft he had built from bits of rickshaw and a secondhand Toyota car in his garden.
swa: Mwaka 2011, mkazi mwingine wa Ghazni aliye na kipaji, bila hata ya kupata mafunzo yoyote au vifaa maalum, alipaisha ndege aliyoiunda kwa kutumia mabaki ya mkokoteni wa matairi mawili unaokokotwa na binadamu na pia kwa kutumia mabaki ya gari aina ya Toyota iliyokuwepo katika bustani yake.

eng: Alexander Sodiqov has contributed to this post.
swa: Alexander Sodiqov pia alitoa mchango wake katika kuandaa makala hii.

eng: Open Society Foundation and Disability Right Initiative have formed an organization to cater specifically to the disabled African youth - African Youth With Disability Network.
swa: Open Society Foundation, Shirika la Uwazi katika Jamii wakishirikiana na Mpango wa Haki za Walemavu (Disability Right Initiative, DRI, wameungana kuunda shirika litakalowahudumia vijana wa ki-Afrika wenye ulemavu - Shirika litakaloitwa Mtandao wa Vijana wa ki-Afrika wenye Ulemavu.

eng: Through the network, African youths around the continent with disability received training on social media skills and how to work and portray themselves as journalists:
swa: Kupitia mtandao huo, vijana wenye ulemavu kutoka sehemu mbalimbali barani humu walipatiwa ujuzi wa kutumia zana za uandishi wa kijamii na jinsi ya kufanya kazi na kuonekana kama waandishi wa habar:

eng: for the promotion, adoption and ratification of the United Nations Convention on disabled people.
swa: kwa kutangazwa, kupitishwa na kuridhiwa kwa Mkataba wa Umoja wa Mataifa kuhusu haki za walemavu.

eng: The YI and DRI saw a dire need to set up a specifically African organization, which gave rise to the African Youth with Disabilities Network (AYWDN).
swa: YI na DRI (vifupisho vya majina) waliona haja kubwa ya kuunda shirika mahususi kabisa la kiafrika, iliyosababisha kuundwa kwa shirika hilo la kuwahudumia vijana walemavu wa ki-Afrika.

eng: This group was created as a way to bring together young Africans from across the continent with the aim of creating inclusive societies where people with disabilities can live better lives with dignity and contribute to and influence the internal political debates.
swa: Kundi hili liliundwa ili kuwaleta pamoja vijana kutoka barani barani kwa lengo la kuunda jamii zilizopamoja ambapo watu wenye ulemavu wanaweza kuishi maisha mazuri zaidi na yenye staha na kuchangia na hata kubadili mwelekeo wa mijadala ya ndani ya kisiasa

eng: Workshop participants (left to right): Boaz, Gladys and Medi.
swa: Washiriki wa Kongamano (kushoto kwenda kulia): Boaz, Gladys na Medi.

eng: Photo courtesy of Rebecca Wanjiku
swa: Picha kwa hisani ya Rebecca Wanjiku

eng: Earlier this month, a workshop was held in Dakar, Senegal and several countries including Uganda, Kenya, Senegal, Zambia, and Tunisia.
swa: Hapo awali, mwezini huu, kongamano jingine lilifanyika mjini Dakar, Senegali na nchi nyingi kama Uganda, Kenya, Zambia na Tunisia ziliwakilishwa.

eng: Persons with disability are not just covered in positive light but no light at all.
swa: Watu wenye ulemavu si tu hawapewi nafasi ya kutosha katika vyombo vikuu vya habari lakini hawapati nafasi kabisa.

eng: The workshop empowered persons with disability with techniques on how to handle and take over media especially the social media and included communication and writing techniques.
swa: Warsha hii iliwawezesha vijana hawa wenye ulemavu kwa kuwapatia ujuzi wa namna bora ya kufanya kazi na hata kuchukua usukani wa vyombo vya habari hasa vya kijamii pamoja na mbinu za mawasiliano na kuandika.

eng: Rebecca, an active Kenyan blogger, discusses the workshop on her blog:
swa: Rebecca, mwanablogu wa Kenya, anaandika haya kuhusu warsha hiyo:

eng: This week I had a fabulous week with a group of young people; training on media, whether new or old is never easy.
swa: Nimekuwa na juma jema pamoja na kikundi cha vijana; nikitoa mafunzo ya kutumia vyombo vya habari, viwe hivi vipya au vile vya zamani huwa si rahisi.

eng: The media in every country is almost guilty of similar things; they don’t cover our issues, they entrench prejudice and stereotypes in most cases never have time to write and air positive stories.
swa: Vyombo vya habari katika kila nchi kwa kawaida vina hatia ya mambo yanayofanana; havitangazi masuala yetu, vinaongeza chuki na ubaguzi na mara nyingi havina muda wa kuandika na kutangaza habari chanya.

eng: The workshop educated and trained the disabled so that they can in turn educate the public using tools such as Twitter and Facebook.
swa: Warsha iliwaelimisha na kuwafunza vijana wenye ulemavu kuwafanya hatimaye waweze kuwafunza wananchi wengine namna ya kutumia zana kama twita na Facebook.

eng: Rebecca writes:
swa: Rebecca anaandika:

eng: When you think new media training, you probably think I do all the sexy stuff like using infographics to make your website interactive or how to have a dancing or a fancy AVI on twitter.
swa: Wengine wenu mkifikiria mafunzo ya vyombo vipya vya habari, labda mnafikiria nafanya vitu vigumu kama kutumia picha zenye ujumbe kufanya mtandao uwe na maingiliano au jinsi ya kuwa na AVI inayocheza kwenye mtandao wa twita.

eng: No, think basics on how to set up a Facebook page, why it is important, why you should be on twitter, looking for other people in your country on twitter and seeing why they have so many followers and why or what you should do to get followers.
swa: La, fikiria vitu rahisi kama kufungua ukurasa katika mtandao wa Facebook, umuhimu wa kujiunga na mitandao ya twita na Facebook, namna ya kuwatafuta watu wengine wanaotumia mtandao wa Twita nchini kwako na kufahamu sababu ya kwa nini wanafuatiliwa na watu wengi na kwa nini na kipi cha kufanya ili upate wafuasi wengi.

eng: Think about growing up in rural Uganda, in a wheelchair, motivated by a mother who believes that you must get educated and achieve your potential no matter the circumstances, think about pushing a wheelchair through the muddy roads when it rains, but most of all, think about the village schoolmates in primary school who had to wake up two hours earlier so that they can help push you two miles to the primary school.
swa: hebu fikiria umekulia sehemu za vijijini nchini Uganda, ukiwa kwenye baiskeli ya walemavu, ukipewa motisha na mama ambaye anaamini kuwa lazima uelimika na kufikia uwezo wako bila kujali hali. Fikiria kusukuma baiskeli au kile kiti kinachotumiwa na walemavu kwenye matope wakati mvua ikinyesha, lakini zaidi ya yote fikiria wanafunzi wenzako unaosoma nao shule ya msingi walioamka masaa mawili kabla ili wakusukume maili hizo mbili hadi ufike shuleni kwako.

eng: A comment from a workshop participant, "My ignorance made me think social media was tough."
swa: Maoni ya mshiriki mmoja wa warsha hiyo, "Kutokujua kwangu kulinifanya nikaamini kuwa kutumia zana za habari za kijamii ni jambo ngumu."

eng: Photo courtesy of Rebecca Wanjiku
swa: Picha kwa hisani ya Rebecca Wanjiku

eng: Deputy Secretary General for Administration at Federation of Liberian Youth, Daintowon Pay-bayee ,says, “disability is not inability.”
swa: Naibu Katibu Mkuu wa Utawala katika Shirikisho la Vijana wa Liberia, Daintowon Pay-bayee, anasema, "Ulemavu sio kukosa uwezo."

eng: She then asks, "you have heard that before but what is your perception if you first meet a disabled person?"
swa: Kisha anaendelea kwa kuuliza, "umeyasikia maneno hayo kabla lakini mtazamo wako ni upi unapokutana na mlemavu kwa mara ya kwanza?"

eng: Ms Pay-bayee refuses to be judged because of what she is that's why she will keep working on her dream:
swa: Bi Pay-bayee anakataa kuhukumiwa kwa kuwa ni mlemavu ndiyo maana ataendelea kuitimiza ndoto yake:

eng: Disability is not inability.
swa: Ulemavu sio kukosa uwezo.

eng: To fight discrimination and change public perceptions, we need to begin talking about youth with disabilities in our homes, our neighborhoods, and on the national and international stage.Donors, governments, and the media need to give this issue urgent attention.
swa: Ili kupingana na ubaguzi na kubadilisha mtazamo wa watu, inatubidi tuanze kuongea kuhusu vijana wenye ulemavu majumbani mwetu, kwa majirani zetu, na hata kwa kiwango cha nchi na pia kote duniani. Wafadhili, serikali, na vyombo vya habari wanapaswa kuchukua hatua za haraka kushughulikiwa suala hili.

eng: Perceptions of people with disabilities are degrading.
swa: Mitazamo ya walemavu ni ya kudhalilisha.

eng: We need to encourage the potential in all of our young people.
swa: Tunahitaji kuwatia moyo vijana wote ili kile kilichomo ndani mwao kitimie.

eng: I will keep working for my dream of living in an inclusive society where I am judged not by my physical limitations but by my potential and my character.
swa: Nitaendelea kupigania ndoto yangu ya kuishi katika jamii yenye usawa ambapo sitakuhumiwa kwa kile nisichoweza kufanya kwa sababu ya ulemavu wa mwili bali kwa uwezo na tabia zangu.

eng: Daintowon Pay-bayee, an ardent campaigner of people living with disability in Liberia, remembers when she got disabled at the age of five.
swa: Daintowon Pay-bayee, mwanaharakati wa watu wanaoishi na ulemavu wa Liberia, anakumbuka alivyopata ulemavu wake akiwa na umri wa miaka tano.

eng: There are photos, posts and tweets about the workshop on OSIWA Facebook page, OSIWA Twitter page and AYWDN Facebook page.
swa: Habari zaidi kuhusu warsha hii zinapatikana kupitia Ukurasa wa OSIWA , katika mtandao wa FacebookUkurasa wa OSIWA katika mtandao wa Twita na Ukurasa wa facebook wa Shirika la Vijana wenye ulemavu AYWDN

eng: OSIWA Program Coordinator Kanja Sesay shared insights from the workshop on Twitter:
swa: Mratibu wa mpango ya OSIWA, Kanja Sesay alitoa maoni yake kuhusu warsha hii kwa kupitia mtandao wa twita:

eng: @MKSesay: "For the media, it is no longer politically correct to talk of blind people but of people living with a visual handicap" - Tidiane Kasse
swa: @MKSesay: " Kwenu vyombo vya habari, kisiasa si sahihi tena kuzungumzia vipofu bali watu wanaoishi na ulemavu wa macho" - Tidiane Kasse

eng: @MKSesay: "Young people all over the world are doing great things"...
swa: @MKSesay: "Vijana kote duniani wanafanya mambo makubwa"...

eng: Positive statement from disability rights activists meeting in Senegal.
swa: Taarifa chanya kutoka kwa wanaharakati wanaotetea haki za walemavu wanaoshiriki katika warsha nchini Senegali.

eng: @MKSesay: #African‬ states are lagging behind in promoting disability rights, youth need to hold governments accountable.
swa: @MKSesay: # Nchi za Afrika bado ziko nyuma katika kutetea haki za walemavu, vijana wanapaswa kuziwajibisha serikali zao.

eng: The 2012 Global Voices Summit has just opened in Nairobi, Kenya (July 2-3).
swa: Mkutano wa Global Voices (Sauti za Dunia) wa 2012 umeshafunguliwa muda mfupi uliopita katika jiji la Nairobi, nchini Kenya.

eng: We wish you could be with us there in person, but if you can't you can still watch the livestream and chat with the us live.
swa: Tungetamani sana ungeweza kujumuika nasi pale, lakini kama hilo haliwezekani, waweza pia ukatutazama moja kwa moja kupitia mtandao wa intaneti na pia tukaweza kujadiliana papo kwa hapo.

eng: It's a public event with 300 particpants from 60 countries, mostly bloggers and citizen media enthusiasts, ages 18-76.
swa: Ni tukio la wazi linalowajumuisha washiriki 300 kutoka nchi 60 duniani, zaidi wanablogu na waandishi wa vyombo vya habari vya kiraia wenye umri kati ya miaka 18 hadi 76.

eng: The goal of the Summit is to explore the range and importance of online citizen media around the world.
swa: Lengo la kongamano hili ni kujadili kuhusu upana na umuhimu wa vyombo vya habari za kiraia za mtandaoni ulimwenguni kote.

eng: Please check the Summit blog, program, Twitter hashtag #GV2012, and of course the video below.
swa: Tafadhali tembelea Blogu ya Mkutano, ratiba,katika alama ishara ya Twita, #GV2012, na pia kutazama video ifuatayo.

eng: Some parts of the program run on two tracks, and you can check the Summit website video page to chose between streams.
swa: Baadhi ya matukio yanaendeshwa kwa namna mbili, hivyo waweza kutembelea ukurasa maalumu wa video wa kongamano na kisha uchague kati ya namna hizo mbili.

eng: Watch live streaming video from globalvoices at livestream.com
swa: Sambaza taarifa hizi na kwa wengine!

eng: Oh, and we have great live photo updates on Flickr too:
swa: Pia tuna picha nzuri za moja kwa moja katika mtandao wa Flickr.

eng: This post is part of our International Relations & Security coverage.
swa: Makala haya ni sehemu ya habari zetu maalumu za Mahusiano na Usalama wa kimataifa

eng: Power lines over buildings in Cameroon, 2008.
swa: Mikondo ya umeme ikionekana juu ya majengo nchini Cameroon, 2008.

eng: Photo by Zzilch on Flickr (CC BY-NC-ND 2.0)
swa: Picha ya Zzilch kwenye mtandao wa Flickr (CC BY-NC-ND 2.0)

eng: After his reelection in November 2011, President Paul Biya of Cameroon announced that the country would soon become a giant “construction site”.
swa: Baada ya kuchaguliwa kwa mara nyingine mwezi Novemba 2011, Rais Paul Biya wa Cameroon alitangaza kwamba ndani ya muda mfupi, nchi yake ingeongoza kwa kuwa “eneo la ujenzi”.

eng: The goal for his new term is for Cameroon to reach emerging market status by 2035 through a series of “great achievements” in transport and energy infrastructure development .
swa: Lengo kubwa la awamu yake mpya ya urais kwa nchi ya Kameruni ni kufikia hadhi ya soko linaloibukia ifikapo 2035 kupitia hatua kwa hatua za “mafanikio makubwa” katika maendeleo ya miundo mbinu ya usafiri na nishati .

eng: It’s a deadline that fails to convince many commentators, if only because the challenges are so great.
swa: Kutimia kwa ndoto hii ndani ya muda uliopangwa kumeshindwa kuwashawishi wachambuzi wengi wa masuala ya kisiasa, kwa sababu tu changamoto zilizopo ni nyingi.

eng: Energy, and specifically electricity, is especially problematic.
swa: Nishati, na hususani umeme, ni sekta yenye matatazo mengi.

eng: Like many other African countries, Cameroon suffers from insufficient electricity supplies.
swa: Kama ilivyo katika nchi nyingi za Kiafrika, Cameroon inataabika na ugavi duni wa umeme nishati ya umeme.

eng: Journalist Leopold Nséké explains in an article published in Afrique Expansion Magazine:
swa: Mwandishi Leopold Nséké anaeleza katika makala yake iliyochapishwa kwenye jarida la Afrique Expansion Magazine:

eng: Underequipped, the African continent is awash in the obsolescence of its facilities and bore the brunt of poor management of available resources.
swa: Kule kuwa na nyenzo duni, bara la Afrika imefurikwa na nyenzo zilizopitwa na wakati pamoja na utawala duni na butu wa raslimali zilizopo.

eng: Representing 15% of the world population, Africa consumes paradoxically only 3% of the total world production of electricity.
swa: Ikiwa na takribani asilimia 15 ya idadi ya watu duniani, ni ajabu kabisa kwamba Afrika inatumia asilimia 3 tu ya umeme unaozalishwa duniani.

eng: There is no electricity in Mafa Kilda village, it's just passing by (and going from Ngong to Garoua).
swa: Hakuna umeme kwenye vijiji vya Mafa Kilda, umeme unapita tu kwa nguzo za umeme (ukitokea Ngong kwenda Garoua).

eng: By Philippe Semanaz on Flickr in 2006 (CC BY-SA 2.0)
swa: Picha ya Philippe Semanaz kwenye mtandao wa Flickr mwaka 2006 (CC BY-SA 2.0)

eng: According to some estimates (fr) only 20% of Cameroon’s population has a regular access to electricity supplies.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa makadirio (fr) yasiyorasmi, ni asilimia 20 tu ya idadi ya wa-Cameroon wameunganishwa na umeme.

eng: Indeed, those who have access to power tend to experience cuts in supply as often as every three days.
swa: Kwa hakika, pamoja na kuwa na umeme, watu hao hukumbana na kero ya kukatika kwa umeme takribani kila baada ya siku tatu. .

eng: Electricity is also increasingly expensive commodity for most of the country’s citizens.
swa: Umeme unaendelea kuwa bidhaa ghali kwa raia wengi kuweza kumudu bei yake.

eng: The privately-owned AES Sonel, for example, recently announced a 7% rise in prices starting from June 1, 2012.
swa: Kampuni binafsi ya AES Sonel, kwa mfano, hivi karibuni ilitangaza kupanda kwa bei ya umeme kwa asilimia 7 kuanzia tarehe 1 Juni, 2012.

eng: Limited access to electricity also represents a threat to the industrialization of Cameroon, which in turn could undermine Cameroon’s ambition of becoming emerging economy by 2035.
swa: Kutokuwepo kwa uhakika wa upatikanaji wa umeme pia kunaleta tishio kwa maendeleo ya viwanda nchini Cameroon, jambo ambalo litakwaza ndoto ya nchi hiyo kuwa nchi yenye uchumi imara ifikapo 2035.

eng: A study conducted by the Polytechnic National High School of Yaounde outlined that:
swa: Utafiti uliofanywa na Shule ya Sekondari ya Ufundi ya Younde ulibainisha kwamba:

eng: Production losses were estimated at EU91.5 million per year in industrial enterprises because of the difficulties in supplying electricity.
swa: Hasara za uzalishaji katika makampuni ya viwanda zilikadiriwa kuwa EU milioni 91.5 kwa mwaka kwa sababu ya matatizo ya ugawi wa umeme.

eng: These results indicate that inadequate and poor quality of electricity supply has slowed industrial development.
swa: Matokeo haya yalionyesha kwamba kiwango pungufu na kilicho duni cha ugawi wa umeme kimezorotesha maendeleo ya umeme.

eng: Yet unreliable electricity supplies are also a major concern for the wider population. Feowl is a new community-led initiative that aims to refine and provide currently absent data on the impact of poor electricity supply in Douala, the economic center of Cameroon.
swa: Aidha, ugavi wa umeme usioaminika unagusa maisha ya idadi kubwa ya watu nchini humo.Feowl ni mradi mpya unaotaribiwa na jamii unaolenga kukusanya, kusaili na hatimaye kutoa takwimu ambazo kwa sasa hazipatikani juu ya athari za ugavi duni wa umeme huko Douala, eneo linalosifika kwa shughuli za uchumi nchini humo.

eng: As Cameroon essentially relies on hydro-energy production, the Government also launched the construction of the Lom Pangar dam in the east of the country.
swa: Kwa vile Cameroon kimsingi inategemea, uzalishaji wa umeme utokanao na maji , serikali imezindua ujenzi wa bwawa la Lom Pangar lililo mashariki mwa nchi hiyo.

eng: The project – funded by the World Bank and other international organizations - is considered to be integral to Cameroon’s aspirations to become an emerging economy.
swa: Mradi huo -unaofadhiliwa na Benki ya Dunia na mashirika mengine ya kimataifa- unachukuliwa kuwa na umuhimu wa pekee katika kufikiwa kwa ndoto za nchi hiyo za kuwa na uchumi imara.

eng: The dam is expected to the increase energy production of Cameroon with a planned capacity of 7.250 billion cubic meters for a reservoir that will cover 610 km2.
swa: Bwawa hilo linalotazamiwa kuongeza uzalishaji wa nishati ya umeme nchi humo litakuwa na ukubwa wa mita za ujazo bilioni 7.250 litakalotunza maji kwa eneo lenye kilomita za mraba 610.

eng: Water supplies will also be held in reserve for the dry season at two damns further downstream of the Sanaga River, thereby enabling them to generate more electricity.
swa: Maji yatahifadhiwa kwa matumizi hasa wakati wa ukame katika mabwawa hayo yaliyopo kwenye mto wa Sanaa, hivyo kusaidia kuzalisha umeme zaidi.

eng: Christiane Badgley’s blog highlights some of the shortcomings of the project.
swa: Blogu ya Christiane Badgley inaangazia baadhi ya mapungufu ya mradi huo.

eng: She is concerned that the electricity produced will mainly prioritize the needs of Cameroon’s industries :
swa: (Mwanablogu huyo) anawasiwasi kwamba umeme utakaozalishwa unakusudiwa zaidi kutosheleza mahitaji ya umeme wa viwanda vya nchi hiyo:

eng: …the urban and rural poor do not appear to be the primary beneficiaries of the Lom Pangar project.
swa: …masikini wa mijini na vjijini hawaonekani kuwa wanufaika wa mradi wa Lom Pangar.

eng: Instead, the dam is designed to regulate the flow of the Sanaga River in order to increase energy production from existing and proposed downstream hydropower plants serving the southern electricity grid and the country’s single largest electricity consumer, the Alucam aluminum smelter.
swa: Badala yake, bwana limebuniwa kudhibiti maji ya mto Sanaga ili kuongeza uzalishaji wa umeme kwenye mashine za kufua umeme zilizopo tayari na zile zinazokusudiwa kujengwa ili kutosheleza mkondo wa umeme wa kusini pamoja na mgodi wa machimbo ya madini ya aluminiam wa Alucm unaotumia umeme zaidi nchini humo.

eng: Jointly owned by the government of Cameroon and the Canadian-based company Alcan, Alucam plans to more than double its production and needs new sources of cheap energy to do so.
swa: Mgodi huo wa Alucam unaomilikiwa kwa ubia wa serikali ya nchi hiyo na kampuni ya ki-Kanada iitwayo Alcan, unapanga kuongeza uzalishaji wake mara dufu na hivyo unahitaji vyanzo vipya nafuu vya nishati kufikia malengo hayo.

eng: This post and its translations to Spanish, Arabic and French were commissioned by the International Security Network (ISN) as part of a partnership to seek out citizen voices on international relations and security issues worldwide.
swa: Makala haya ni sehemu ya tafsiri ya ki-Hispania, ki-Arabu na ki-Faransa ambazo zilitolewa na Mtandao wa Usalama wa Kimataifa (ISN) kama sehemu ya ushirikiano wa kutafuta sauti za raia wa kawaida katika masuala ya mahusiano na usalama wa mataifa duniani.

eng: This post was first published on the ISN blog, see similar stories here.
swa: Tembelea blogu ya ISN ili kuona habari nyingine zinazofanana na hii.

eng: The Ladies in White (Las Damas de Blanco) are again top of mind with Cuban diaspora bloggers.
swa: Kikundi cha wanawake kijiitacho ‘wanawake wavaliao mavazi meupe’ (Ladies in White) kwa mara nyingine wametawala fikra za wanablogu wa Cuba waishio nje ya nchi.

eng: As one of the oldest and most respected opposition entities on the island, their peaceful protests - and regular arrests by state security forces - continue to attract attention.
swa: Maandamano ya amani ya kikundi hicho ambacho ni moja wapo ya vyombo vya upinzani vinavyoheshimika zaidi katika visiwa hivyo –pamoja na kukamatwa kwao mara kwa mara na vyombo vya dola –yanaendelea kuvuta hisia za watu.

eng: The most recent confrontation happened this past weekend as members of the group attempted to carry out two protests in Havana.
swa: Mapambano ya hivi karibuni yalitokea mwishoni mwa juma lililopita wakati ambapo wanachama wa kikundi hicho walipojaribu kufanya maandamano mara mbili mjini Havana.

eng: Pedazos de la Isla, which chronicled the events in photographs, noted that:
swa: Pedazos de la Isla, ambaye aliorodhesha matukio hayo hatua kwa hatua kwa kutumia picha , alibaini kwamba:

eng: Despite the government repression, more than 40 Ladies in White carried out their accustomed march to the Santa Rita Church in Havana this Sunday, June 17th, to celebrate Father’s Day.
swa: Pamoja na ukandamizaji uliofanywa na serikali, zaidi ya wanawake 40 wa kikundi hicho cha ‘Ladies in White’ walishiriki maandamano kuelekea kwenye kanisa liitwalo Santa Rita mjini Havana siku ya Jumapili, tarehe 17 Juni, kuadhimisha Siku ya Baba.

eng: When the mass concluded, these women decided to catch their oppressors off guard and marched for the second time in one day, this time from Infanta street to Neptune Street.
swa: Mara tu baada ya ibada kuhitimishwa, akina maana hawa waliamua kuwazidi werevu polisi na kuandamana kwa mara ya pili ndani ya siku moja, mara hii wakitokea mtaa wa Infanta kuelekea mtaa wa Neptune.

eng: The blog also posted two other entries about state action against members of the Ladies in White.
swa: Blogu hiyo pia iliweka posti mbili nyingine kuhusu hatua zilizochukuliwa na serikali dhidi ya wanachama wa kikundi hicho cha ’Ladies in White’.

eng: The first detailed how Caridad Caballero Batista, her husband and son were searched and detained:
swa: Posti ya kwanza iliweka taarifa nyingi kuhusu namna Caridad Caballero Batista, mume wake na mtoto wao wa kiume walivyopekuliwa na kuwekwa kizuizini:

eng: After visiting some relatives...they were intercepted by the political police upon arriving to the province of Holguin.
swa: Baada ya kuwatembelea ndugu kadhaa…walijikuta wakizungukwa na polisi wanaotumika kisiasa mara tu walipowasili kwenye jimbo la Holguin.

eng: According to Caballero, the police agent who intercepted the vehicle her family was traveling on...told the driver to hand him his documentation.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Cabellero, afisa wa polisi aliyelizuia gari ambalo familia yake ililitumia kusafiria…alimwamuru dereva kumkabidhi nyaraka zake.

eng: However, the activist explains that 'more than for the purpose of asking to see the driver’s documents, this action was intentionally aimed at searching my husband Esteban and the bag he was carrying, which was full of clothes'.
swa: Hata hivyo, wanaharakati wanaeleza kwamba ‘lengo lilikuwa zaidi ya kuomba kuona nyaraka za dereva, kitendo hicho kilipangwa kwa makusudi ya kumpekua mume wangu Esteban pamoja na begi alilokuwa amelibeba, lililokuwa limejaa nguo’.

eng: The agent ordered Esteban to get off the vehicle in order to search him, to which the dissident replied that he was not going to allow, considering that he 'is not a delinquent'.
swa: Afisa huyo wa jeshi alimwamuru Esteban kushuka garini ili afanyiwe upekuzi, kitendo ambacho Esteban alikipinga akisema asingeruhusu kufanyiwa hivyo, akisema kwamba ‘yeye si mhuni’.

eng: Caballero says that 'the agents were infuriated and told Esteban that he was committing a crime'.
swa: Caballero anasema kwamba ‘maafisa hao walipandwa na ghadhabu na kumwambia Esteban kwamba alikuwa anatenda kosa la jinai’.

eng: The response of the agents was to shove Esteban Sandez into a vehicle of the Operational Guard to take him to the Police Unit, where he’d be searched and detained.
swa: Matokeo yake maafisa hao wa polisi walimlazimisha Esteban Sandez kupanda gari la Polisi wamlete kituo cha polisi, ambako alipekuliwa na kushikiliwa.

eng: Upon seeing this, Caridad Caballero and her son Eric Sandez got off the car and began to protest against the arbitrariness, assuring the agents that if they were going to take Esteban, then they’d have to them too.
swa: Kwa kuona hayo, Caridad Caballero na mwanae Eric Sandez alishuka garini na kuanza kupingana na unyama huo, akiwaambia polisi hao kwamba kama wangemchukua Esteban, basi ingebidi wawachua na wao (yeye na mwanae) pia.

eng: In a matter of minutes, the three activists were taken to a police unit located on the outskirts of Holguin.
swa: Katika dakika chache, wanaharakati hao watatu walichukuliwa kwenda kituo cha polisi kilichopo nje ya mji wa Holguin.

eng: After a number of hours, the family was released, but upon arriving to their home in the city of Holguin they noticed that the political police had already set up the accustomed weekend operation in order to impede them from arriving to Sunday Mass.
swa: Baada ya masaa kadhaa, familia hiyo iliachiliwa huru, lakini mara tu baada ya kuwasili nyumbani kwao mjini Holguin walibaini kuwa polisi hao wanaotumika kisiasa walikuwa wamepanga kufanya operesheni ya kawaida ya mwisho wa juma ili kuwazuia kuhudhuria Ibada ya Jumapili.

eng: Obstruction from attending Holy Mass has been one of the tactics employed by state security to contain the activity of the group.
swa: Kitendo cha kuwazuia kuhudhuria Ibada Takatifu kilikuwa mojawapo ya mbinu zinazotumiwa na idara ya usalama wa nchi hiyo kuzibana harakati za kikundi hicho.

eng: The second post told of the arrest of an elderly member of the group:
swa: Posti ya pili ilisimulia kukamatwa kwa mwanachama ajuza wa kikundi hicho:

eng: This Father’s Day, Ladies in White throughout all of Cuba mobilized with the purpose of carrying out peaceful activities to celebrate the date.
swa: Katika Siku ya Baba mwaka huu, wanachama wa kikundi cha “Ladies in White” kote nchini Cuba walihamasika kufanya harakati za amani za kusherehekea siku hiyo.

eng: As a consequence, the regime’s police forces responded with a repressive operation which began days prior, resulting in the arrests of countless of these women throughout all of the island’s provinces.
swa: Matokeo yake, vikosi vya polisi vya nchi hiyo vilijibu mapigo kwa operesheni maalumu ya kikandamizi iliyoanza siku chache kabla, na kusababisha kukamatwa kwa idadi kubwa ya wanawake hawa katika majimbo yote ya kisiwa hicho.

eng: Among those arrested was 75 year-old Blanca Hernández Moya, who suffered physical attacks at the hands of police agents...
swa: Katika waliokamatwa alikuwepo Blanca Hernández Moya , ajuza wa miaka 75, aliyeteseka kwa kipigo cha kinyama akiwa mikononi mwa polisi…

eng: The elderly woman...was on her way from her home in Central Havana to the headquarters of the Ladies in White- the home of the fallen leader of the group, Laura Pollan, located on Neptuno Street- when she was violently intercepted by state police.
swa: Ajuza huyo…alikuwa akielekea yalipo makao makuu ya kikundi hicho cha Ladies in White akitokea nyumbani kwake mitaa ya Havana Kati –alikozaliwa kiongozi wa kikundi hicho aliyeuawa, Laura Pollan, mtaa wa Neptune –ambapo alibughudhiwa sana na polisi.

eng: They attacked me', said Moya, 'they shoved me into a vehicle, and a female agent twisted my arm and hit me'.
swa: ‘Walinishambulia’, anasema Moya, ‘walinilazimisha kuingia garini, na polisi mmoja wa kike alinikunja mkono wangu na kunipiga’.

eng: After some minutes, the vehicle which the Lady in White was in parked and she was kicked out, being left abandoned by a dam near the desolate area known as Penalver, on the outskirts of Cotorro.
swa: Baada ya dakika kadhaa, gari lililokuwa limembeba ajuza huyo liliegeshwa na alilazimishwa kutoka, akatelekezwa pembeni mwa bwawa karibu tu na eneo lisilo na watu liitwao Penalver, nje ya mtaa wa Cotorro.

eng: Capitol Hill Cubans also took notice of the weekend's arrests.
swa: Blogu ya Capitol Hill Cubans pia iliandika habari za ‘kamata kamata’ hiyo iliyofanyika mwisho wa juma.

eng: The thumbnail image used in this post is by dumplife (Mihai Romanciuc), used under an Attribution-NonCommercial 2.0 Generic (CC BY-NC 2.0) Creative Commons license.
swa: The Picha inayoonekana kwenye posti hii imepigwa na dumplife (Mihai Romanciuc), imetumiwa kwa leseni ya Creative Commons (CC BY-NC 2.0).

eng: Visit dumplife (Mihai Romanciuc)'s flickr photostream.
swa: Tembelea picha za dumplife (Mihai Romanciuc) kwenye mtandao wa Flickr.

eng: Hello World and jambo from Kenya!
swa: Salamu kutoka Kenya!

eng: Welcome to the Global Voices podcast.
swa: Karibuni katika matangazo ya sauti ya moja kwa moja (Podikasti) kutoka katika mkutano wa Sauti za Kimataifa.

eng: What is the future of online citizen media?
swa: Je, mwelekeo wa vyombo vya habari vya kiraia kwa siku zijazo ni upi?

eng: In this edition (and the next) you will hear from editors, authors, co-founders and other participants at the 2012 Global Voices Citizen Media Summit in Nairobi to discuss the future of how we all work together online.
swa: Kupitia toleo hili na yatakayofuatia mtaweza kuwasikia wahariri, waandishi, waanzilishi wenza na hata washiriki wengine wa Mkutano huo kutoka mjini Nairobi wakijadili mustakabali wa namna tunavyofanya kazi kwa pamoja mtandaoni.

eng: The Global Voices Summit takes place every two years and there are many topics on the agenda, possibly too many to fit into one podcast but certainly a lot of food for thought right here.
swa: Mkutano huu hufanyika kila baada ya miaka miwili na huwa kuna mada nyingi katika ajenda, labda hata nyingi kuweza kuenea katika podikasti moja lakini kwa hakika kuna mengi ya kutafakari.

eng: First, let's go way back, a long time in internet years and consider the origins of that thing we call Global Voices.
swa: Kwa kuanzia, hebu turudi nyuma, kwa siku za kitambo na tuangazie asili ya Sauti ya Dunia.

eng: Co-founder Ethan Zuckerman explains how Global Voices came to be, what happens at the Summits, and what he thinks the future holds.
swa: Mwanzilishi mwenzaEthan Zuckerman anaelezea namna Sauti za Dunia zilivyozaliwa, kile ambacho hufanyika katika mikutano hii, na kile anachofikiri kuwa mustakabali wa Jumuiya hii.

eng: The #GV2012 Summit is a place to meet and find out more about our authors, editors and contributors who travelled from all corners of the world.
swa: Mkutano wa Sauti za Dunia ni mahali pa kupatanika na kufahamu mengi zaidi kuhusu wahariri, waandishi na wachangiaji wengine waliosafiri kutoka kila kona ya dunia.

eng: Everyone was excited, but one of the most thrilled participants was Elaine Díaz from Havana, Cuba.
swa: Kila mtu alikuwa na msisimuko wa pekee, lakini mmoja wapo wa washiriki waliokuwa na furaha alikuwa Elaine Díaz anayetoka Havana, Cuba.

eng: Here she explains a little more about citizens online in Cuba.
swa: Hapa anaeleza kidogo zaidi kuhusu raia wa mtandaoni wa nchi yake ya Cuba.

eng: It wouldn’t be a Global Voices gathering without smart and vocal people from around the world.
swa: Kwa kweli mkusanyiko huu usingekuwa na maana hasa ya Sauti za Dunia bila ya kuwa na watu wenye sauti maridadi kutoka kote duniani.

eng: Andrea Arzaba is a journalist in Mexico and she collected some observations of the event, starting with her own reflections.
swa: Andrea Arzaba ni mwandishi wa habari nchini Mexico ambaye alikusanya utafiti mdogo kuhusu tukio hili, kwa kuanzia na fikra zake mwenyewe.

eng: Daudi Were is a Kenyan blogger who writes on Mentalacrobatics.
swa: Daudi Were ni mwanablogu wa Kenya anayeandika katika blogu ya Mentalacrobatics.

eng: He was also the very entertaining MC during the public Summit meeting attended by 300 people.
swa: Yeye ndiye aliyekuwa anaongoza ratiba katika mkutano huu wa umma uliohudhuriwa na watu 300.

eng: He explained his connection with Global Voices and how Kenyan technology continues to innovate, particularly in the area of mobile.
swa: Alieleza kuhusu uhusiano wake na Jumuiya ya Sauti za Dunia na jinsi teknolojia ya Kenya inavyozidi kuwa ya ubunifu, hasa katika sekta ya vifaa vya mkononi kama simu.

eng: A group photo from the Global Voices Summit in Nairobi, Kenya.
swa: Picha ya Pamoja ya wahudhuriaji wa Mkutano wa Nairobi, Kenya.

eng: The impact of citizen media
swa: Athari ya Vyombo vya habari vya kiraia

eng: Through Global Voices, many people who are sometimes overlooked are able to have their views and reports amplified.
swa: Kwa kupitia Sauti za Dunia, watu wengi ambao mara nyingi hupuuzwa na habari zao kutokupewa nafasi katika vyombo vikuu vya habari wanawweza kupata nafasi na hivyo maoni na habari zao kupewa kipaumbele.

eng: Leila Nashawati Rego is a Spanish and Syrian human rights activist.
swa: Leila Nashawati Rego ni mwanaharakati wa haki za binadamu mwenye asili ya Uhispania na Syria.

eng: She teaches communications at Carlos the Third University in Spain as well as write for a number of respected outlets.
swa: Ni muhadhiri wa stadi za mawasiliano katika Chuo Kikuu cha Carlos III, na pia anaandikia magazeti kadhaa yenye kuheshimika.

eng: We discussed the growth of online citizen media and the results of that expansion.
swa: Tulijadili kuhusu kukua kwa uandishi wa mtandaoni na matokeo ya kutanuka kwa uandishi huo.

eng: So long, but not goodbye
swa: Muda mrefu, lakini sio mwisho

eng: Some bitter-sweet news came out of the Global Voices Summit too.
swa: Habari zenye mchanganyiko wa huzuni na furaha zilitoka kwenye mkutano huu vile vile.

eng: Sami Ben Gharbia from Tunisia told us that he is stepping down from the position of Director of Global Voices Advocacy.
swa: Sami Ben Gharbia kutoka Tunisia alitueleza kuwa anajiuzulu nafasi ya Mkurugenzi wa Utetezi wa Sauti za Dunia, ama Global Voices Advocacy.

eng: So, naturally it was time to take a look at the work that he has done and find out what he will be up to next.
swa: Kama ilivyotarajiwa aliwaeleza washirika yale aliyokuwa ametimiza na yale anayotaka kufanya katika siku za usoni.

eng: As ever, thanks to all of our contributors, producers and music makers who help to make this happen.
swa: Kama ilivyo desturi, nawashukuru wachangiaji, wazalishaji na watunga nyimbo waliosaidia kufanya warsha ifaulu.

eng: You can find out more about the summit by checking the Twitter hashtag #GV2012 and by taking a look at the dedicated Summit pages.
swa: Unaweza kuangalia mihutasari mingine katika twita kupitia alama ishara ya #GV2012 na pia kwa kuangalia kurusa maalumu za Mkutano.

eng: The Global Voices Podcast.
swa: Podikasti ya Sauti za Dunia.

eng: The world is talking, I hope you’ve been listening.
swa: Dunia inaongea, natumaini umekuwa ukisikiza.

eng: Music credits
swa: Shukrani kwa watunga nyimbo

eng: In the podcast you can hear lots of lovely Creative Commons music.
swa: Katika podikasti hii unaweza kusikiliza nyimbo nyingi nzuri zilizochini ya Haki miliki ya Creative Commons.

eng: Thanks to Mark Cotton for his fantastic creations and thanks also to all of the wonderful voice over performances and clips that help to glue the podcast together. Podcast: Play in new window | Download Subscribe: iTunes | Android | RSS
swa: Shukrani kwa Mark Cotton kwa ubunifu wake na pia shukrani kwa sauti murua ajabu katika maonyesho ya moja kwa moja mkutanoni na pia zilizorekodiwa tayari ambazo zimetusaidia kutayarisha podikasti hii.

eng: Former Egyptian president Hosni Mubarak has died at least once every few weeks since the beginning of the Egyptian revolution, which toppled his 32-year reign.
swa: Rais wa zamani wa Misri Hosni Mubarak amewahi kufa angalau mara moja kwa kila baada ya majuma machache tangu kuanza kwa mapinduzi ya Misri, yaliyouangusha utawala wake uliodumu kwa miaka 32.

eng: Netizens react to the latest speculations regarding his health.
swa: Watumiaji wa mtandao wanaitikia tetesi za hivi karibuni kuhusu afya yake.

eng: Lubna F. reassured her readers that Mubarak's health status is a recurring news item.
swa: Lubna F. aliwahakikishia wasomaji wake kwamba hali ya afya ya Mubarak ni habari isiyokoma kujirudia-rudia.

eng: She wrote:
swa: Aliandika:

eng: @fatanil: Dear foreigners, sensing that many of you are confused.
swa: @fatanil: Wapendwa wahamiaji na wageni nchini humu, ninahisi kuwa wengi wenu mmechanganikiwa.

eng: So to clarify, Mubarak is dead/alive-ISH.
swa: Kwa hivyo kwa kufafanua tu, Mubarak amefariki na yu hai bado.

eng: Happens every few weeks, dont worry.
swa: Kifo chake hutokea kila baada ya majuma machache, wala msiogope.

eng: And Jonathan Moremi once tweeted a schedule for Mubarak's death:
swa: Na Jonathan Moremi alitwiti ratiba ya kifo cha Mubarak:

eng: @jonamorem: BREAKING: #Mubarak will die today at 11:57 AM and then again at 4:12 PM.
swa: @jonamorem: HABARI ZA HIVI PUNDE: #Mubarak atafariki dunia leo saa 5: 57 asubuhi na kwa mara nyingine saa 10:12 alasiri.

eng: Please show compassion.
swa: Tafadhali onyesha moyo wa huruma.

eng: Next show tomorrow at 7:48 AM and 3:44 PM
swa: Onyesho linalofuata ni kesho saa 1:48 asubuhi na 9:44 alasiri.

eng: However, on June 19, news of Mubarak's death seemed real.
swa: Hata hivyo, Tarehe 19 Juni, habari za kifo cha Mubarak zilionekana kuwa na ukweli.

eng: @Ekramibrahim: I think #Mubarak has officially died. #Egypt
swa: @HaYatElYaMaNi: Habari mpya: Imethibitika Mubarak amefariki #mubarak

eng: But once again, the Egyptian (and foreign journalists) fell pray to Mubarak's death rumors. An hour later, news came that Mubarak was still alive, or may be came back from death as Ms. Entropy tweeted:

eng: A protest was held in Cairo's Nasr City on July 4 by young Egyptians, both male and female, in order to send a message against harassment.
swa: Maandamano yalifanywa na vijana wadogo wa Misri, wasichana kwa wavulana katika mji mdogo wa Nasr jijini Cairo mnamo tarehe 4 Julai kwa lengo la kutuma ujumbe kupinga udhalilishaji wa kijinsia.

eng: Since the revolution took place, Egyptians both online and offline have been standing up against sexual harassment and gender-based violence.
swa: Tangu mapinduzi yalipofanyika, Wamisri wanaotumia mtandao wa intaneti na wasiotumia mtandao wa intaneti wamekuwa wakisimama imara kupinga udhalilishaji wa kijinsia pamoja na machafuko yatokanayo na kutokujali usawa wa binadamu.

eng: In June a march against sexual harassment was attacked.
swa: Mwezi Juni matembezi ya kupinga udhalilishaji wa kijinsia yalishambuliwa.

eng: Nevertheless, initiatives to combat harassment continue.
swa: Haikujalisha, harakati za kukabiliana na udhalilishaji huo zinaendelea.

eng: On a short series of posts, professor Carlos Serra writes about some of the reasons why Mozambique's blogsphere is fading away.
swa: Katika mfululizo mfupi wa makala zake, Profesa Carlos Serra anabainisha baadhi ya sababu zinazoeleza kwa nini blogu za Msumbiji zinaendelea kupungua siku hadi siku.

eng: One reader comments that blogging requires a load of work in order to ensure updates and quality.
swa: Msomaji mmoja anatoa maoni akidhani kwamba kublogu kunahitaji kazi kubwa katika kuhakikisha kuwa habari mpya zinaendelea kuwepo sambamba na kiwango cha habari hizo.

eng: Whereas Serra says that social media may need to be blamed, despite the pros of its usage.
swa: Wakati Serra anasema kwamba zana za uandishi wa kiraia (kama vile twita na facebook) zinaweza kulaumiwa kusababisha hali hii, pamoja na faida za matumizi ya zana hizo.

eng: On 3 July, 2012 the news channel Al Jazeera broadcast a documentary that investigated the mysterious death of Palestinian president Yasser Arafat.
swa: Mnamo tarehe 3 Julai, 2012 kituo cha televisheni cha Al Jazeera ilionesha makala ambayo yalihusu uchunguzi wa kifo cha kutatanisha cha Rais wa Palestina Yasser Arafat.

eng: He died in Paris on 11 November, 2004 and the documentary alleges that rather than dying of natural causes, Arafat was poisoned with polonium.
swa: Alifariki dunia Mjini Paris mnamo tarehe 11 Novemba, 2004 na makala hayo yaliashiria kwamba hakufariki kwa njia ya kawaida ila aliwekewa sumu ya poloni.

eng: Both during and after the airing of the documentary, many Palestinian Twitter users tweeted their thoughts and reactions regarding the evidence presented in it.
swa: Wakati na hata baada ya kuonyeshwa kwa makala hayo, wa-Paletistina wengi wanaotumia twita walitwiti kutoa maoni na miitikio yao kuhusu ushahidi uliotolewa.

eng: The majority were not surprised by the allegations that Arafat was poisoned, something that has long been claimed by many.
swa: Wengi wao hawakushangaa kuhusu madai ya kwamba Arafat aliwekewa sumu, jambo ambalo kwa muda limedaiwa na watu wengi.

eng: However the allegation that polonium was used was a new detail.
swa: Hata hivyo, madai ya kwamba sumu ya poloni ilitumiwa, huo ulikuwa ushahidi mpya wa kina.‏

eng: ‏Yasser Arafat at the World Economic Forum in Davos, January 2001.
swa: Yasser Arafat katika Mkutano wa Jukwaa la Uchumi wa dunia mjini Davos, Januari 2001.

eng: Image by Remy Steinegger (CC BY-SA 2.0).Twitter user This Is Gaza tweeted: Al Jazeera reveals new facts about Arafat's death after a nine-month investigation found high levels of the poisonous element polonium in the belongings of president Arafat.
swa: Picha ya Remy Steinegger (CC BY-SA 2.0) Mtumiaji twita, 'Maoni kutoka Gaza' alitwiti: Al Jazeera imefunua ukweli mpya kuhusu kifo cha Arafat baada ya uchunguzi wa miezi tisa, iligundua kiwango cha juu cha sumu ya poloni katika vifaa alivyokuwa akivitumia marehemu Rais Arafat

What's new is that evidence is provided, when at first there were just rumours. Many Palestinians questioned why the documentary was being broadcast now, and resorted to conspiracy theories as an explanation.
swa: Na mimi mwenyewe nikatoa maoni: Wapalestinia wengi waliuliza iweje makala hayo yatangazwe sasa, na wengine wakaoanisha habari hizo kuwa hila.

eng: Twitter user Majd responded: It is galling when those who have conspired for eight years to hide the truth of Yasser Arafat's assassination, then say when someone comes to reveal the truth, "Your timing is suspicious!"
