eng: S.B comments on the start of health workers' indefinite strike in Abidjan.
swa: S.B anatoa maoni juu ya kuanza kwa mgomo usio na ukomo unaoratibiwa na wafanyakazi wa taasisi za afya mjini Abidjan.

eng: On Connection Ivorienne, he states that:
swa: Katika mtandao wa Connection Ivorienne, anabainisha kwamba:

eng: From the total no-fees for healthcare initiated by the state of Côte d'Ivoire after the end of the post-electoral crisis to free selected healthcare services, employees of certain health institutions have yet to receive their salary in a regular manner.
swa: Kufuatia mabadiliko ya utolewaji wa huduma za afya ambazo zilitolewa bure kabisa baada tu ya kumalizika kwa mgogoro wa baada ya uchaguzi, sera iliyoanzishwa na serikali ya Côte d'Ivoire, ambayo sasa imeelekeza baadhi ya huduma tu ndizo zitakuwa bure, wafanyakazi wa taasisi kadhaa za afya hawajapata mishahara yao kwa wakati.

eng: What's worse is that their manager did not get any payments for the past 16 months.
swa: Kibaya zaidi ni kwamba wakubwa wao hawakupata fungu lolote kwa ajili hiyo kwa zaidi ya miezi kumi na sita.

eng: Le Potentiel writes that French president Hollande's assessment of Human Rights violations in DR of Congo were not taken lightly by the Congolese government as the Francophone Summit is set to take place in Kinshasa, DRC.
swa: Le Potentiel anaandika kwamba tathmini ya Uvunjaji wa Haki za Binadamu nchini DRC Kongo iliyofanywa na Rais wa Ufaransa Hollande haikuchukuliwa kijuu juu na serikali ya Kongo wakati ambapo Mkutano wa nchi zizungumzazo Kifaransa ndio kwanza umeanza mjini Kinshasa, DRC.

eng: The two governments seem to be at odds on the death of Human right activist Chebeya, the national electoral commission and the need for a human rights committee.
swa: SErikali hizi mbili zinaonekana kutofautiana sana kuhusu mambo kama kifo cha mtetezi wa Haki za Binadamu Ndg Chebeya, tume ya taifa ya uchaguzi na uhitaji wa kamati itakayosimamia masuala ya haki za binadamu.

eng: Betty Mould Iddrisu, jurist and Minister of Justice of Ghana, writes on pambazuka.org:
swa: Betty Mould Iddrisu, Jaji na Waziri wa Sheria wa Ghana, anaandika kwenye blogu ya pambazuka.org:

eng: To reach the upper level is rare, and once you have arrived there, you still have to face hostility and doubts about your abilities, because you are a woman.
swa: Kufikia ngazi za juu kabisa za utawala si rahisi, na hata unapopanda mpaka juu kabisa, bado unajikuta unakabiliwa na hisia za watu zenye uadui na watu wanakuwa na mashaka na uwezo wako, kwa sababu tu wewe ni mwanamke.

eng: A woman at the top works harder than a man to prove her skills, and yet she still must face entrenched prejudices and hostility, in her role as manager and leader, in a work environment largely dominated by males.
swa: Mwanamke akikamata madaraka ya juu humbidi kufanya kazi kwa bidii zidi kuliko mwanaume ili kuthibitisha uwezo wake, lakini bado hata akifanya hivyo anakumbana na uadui pamoja na mfumo unaomwona kuwa duni, iwe katika majukumu yake kama meneja na kiongozi, na hata katika mazingira yoyote ya kazi ambayo yanatawaliwa kwa kiasi kikubwa na wanaume.

eng: This post is part of our special coverage Indigenous Rights.
swa: Makala hii ni sehemu ya makala zetu maalumu kuhusiana na haki za wazawa .

eng: At least 7 civilians were killed, up to 32 were injured, and 35 were intoxicated on October 4, 2012, when combined armed forces violently removed demonstrators from Cuatro Caminos ("four roads"), a well-known intersection of roads that go to Quetzaltenango, Guatemala City, Huehuetenango and Totonicapán.
swa: Raia wasiopungua 7 wameuawa, takribani watu 32 wamejeruhiwa na 35 walidhuriwa na sumu mnamo tarehe 4, Oktoba, 2012 wakati majeshi ya muungano yalipotumia nguvu kuwatawanya waandamanaji kutoka katika njia panda maarufu inayoeleka Quetzaltenango, jiji la Guatemala City, Huehuetenango na Totonicapán.

eng: Demonstrators blocked the road to protest the rising price of electricity in the area.
swa: Waandamanaji walifunga barabara kupinga ongezeko la bei ya nishati ya umeme katika eneo lao.

eng: They also demand a dialogue with the government to discuss their objections to the education and constitutional reforms proposed by President Otto Pérez Molina.
swa: Pia, wanahitaji majadiliano na serikali ili kujadili pingamizi lao kuhusiana na mabadiliko ya elimu pamoja na ya katiba yaliyopendekezwa na Rais Otto Pérez Molina.

eng: The demonstrators were representatives from indigenous communities from Totonicapan, an exceptional, mostly indigenous (90%) community in the Guatemalan highlands.
swa: Waandamanaji walikuwa wawakilishi wa jamii za wazawa kutokaTotonicapan, kwa upekee kabisa, wazawa wengi ambao ni asilimia tisini(90%) ni wanajamii kutoka katika nyanda za juu za Guatemala.

eng: While demonstrations are common in the area, the number of persons killed and injured is highly unusual.
swa: Wakati maandamano yakiwa yanafanana katika eneo hilo, idadi ya watu waliouawa na kujeruhiwa si ya kawaida kabisa.

eng: There is evidence that members of the Guatemalan Army were carrying guns, although the Minister of Interior has denied it, arguing that the peasants killed each other, as Mario Rodríguez explains in his blog post "Declarations full of cynicism" .
swa: Kuna ushahidi kuwa wanachama wa jeshi la Guatemala walibeba bunduki, pamoja na kuwa Waziri wa Mambo ya Ndani hakukukubaliana na taarifa hii akisema kuwa wakulima waliuana wenyewe kwa wenyewe kama Mario Rodríguez anavyoelezea katika makala kwenye blogu yake " Matamko Yenye Ushawishi binafsi" .

eng: Cantons in Totonicapán.
swa: Mkoa wa Totonicapán.

eng: Photo by Sandra Sebastian from plazapublica.com.gt under a Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial license.
swa: Picha na Sandra Sebastian kutoka plazapublica.com.gt chini ya Creative Commons Attribution Ruhusa isiyo ya Kibiashara.

eng: Hard working and one of the most active environmentalist communities, the people in Totonicapán are dedicated to preserving the forest and their water sources, as described by Cultural Survival:
swa: Wakiwa ni wachapakazi wazuri na jamii ya wanamazingira, watu wa Totonicapán wanajulikana kwa utunzaji wa misitu na vyazo vyao vya maji, kama inavyofafanuliwa katika mtandao wa Masalio ya Kitamaduni (Cultural Survival):

eng: The forest has been preserved for generations, thanks to the work of people who have lived in harmony with the world around them, by means of ancestral knowledge of resource management and active participation of each community.
swa: Misitu imekuwa ikihifadhiwa kwa ajili ya vizazi, shukrani kwa juhudi za watu walioishi kwa amani na ulimwengu uwazungukao, hali iliyochangiwa na maarifa ya mababu zao ya umilikaji wa rasilimali pamoja na ushiriki hai wa kila jamii.

eng: For such level of care and management you need a well-organized community and active leaders seeking common good.
swa: Kwa hali hii ya kuthamini na usimamizi, unahitaji jamii iliyo na mshikamano na yenye viongozi wawajibikaji wanaotafuta maslahi ya umma.

eng: Totonicapán is one of the few territories where indigenous authorities exercise power, divided in 48 cantons, lead by community mayors and a President who serves as the mediator in case of conflicts and as the spokesperson when it is necessary to dialogue beyond the community.
swa: Totonicapán ni miongoni mwa maeneo machache ambayo mamlaka za wazawa zina nguvu, zilizogawanywa katika majimbo 48 yanayoongozwa na Mameya pamoja na Rais ambaye anafanya kazi kama mpatanishi endapo kutatokea migogoro na pia kama mzungumzaji mkuu endapo kutakuwa na majadiliano ya nje ya wanajamii.

eng: In 2011, for the first time in history, a single woman, law student María del Carmen Tacam, was elected President of the Cantons in Totonicapán.
swa: Mwaka 2011, meya wa kwanza katika historia, mwanamke mmoja ambaye ni mwanafunzi wa sheria, María del Carmen Tacam, alichaguliwa kuwa rais wa jimbo la Totonicapán.

eng: She explained in an interview that she follows the instructions of the consensus of all 48 local authorities.
swa: Katika mahojiano , mwanamke huyu alieleza kuwa anafuata maelekezo yaliyofikiwa na mamlaka zote 48 za mamlaka za vijiji.

eng: As reported by Voces Mayas , María del Carmen explained that while appealing to refrain from violent measures, the indigenous communities blocked the Cuatro Caminos intersection because the government and the corporations did not respond to their clear demands.
swa: Taarifa iliyotolewa na Voces Mayas , María del Carmen alieleza kuwa, wakati akisihi kuacha kutumia nguvu, jamii za watu wazawa walifunga njia panda ya Cuatro Caminos kufuatia serikali na mashirika kushindwa kusikiliza madai yao ya msingi.

eng: She also mentioned that the local hospital collapsed due to the number of people injured. The Constitutional Reform proposed by the President, which they disapprove.
swa: Pia alitanabaisha kuwa, hospitali ya mtaa ilizidiwa na wagonjwa kutokana na idadi kubwa ya watu waliojeruhiwa. marekebisho ya katiba yaliyopendekezwa na Rais ambayo wananchi hawajakubaliana nayo.

eng: Education reform, as they oppose the modifications to the requirements to become a school teacher. Rising cost of electricity because the company did not stick to their commitments.
swa: Mabadiliko ya elimu , kama wanavyopinga marekebisho ya vigezo vya mtu kuwa mwalimu katika shule fulani. kuongezeka kwa gharama za nishati ya umeme kwa kuwa kampuni haikuzingatia malengo iliyojiwekea.

eng: The community wants to keep the dialogue open and is waiting for clear responses from the government of Pérez Molina.
swa: Wanajamii wanataka majadiliano yawe ya wazi na wanasubiri majibu ya serekali ya Pérez Molina.

eng: During the previous government, the dialogue between the government and the communities was mediated by the Ombudsman, as documents show, but this time he was denied access.
swa: Wakati wa serikali iliyotangulia, majadiliano kati ya serikali na wanajamii yalipatanishwa na Ombudsman kama hati zinavyoonesha, lakini kwa kipindi hiki, alizuiwa kufanya hivyo.

eng: María del Carmen Tacám and the symbol of power.
swa: María del Carmen Tacám na ishara ya uongozi.

eng: Photo by Sandra Sebastian from plazapublica.com.gt under a Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial license.
swa: Picha na Sandra Sebastian kutoka plazapublica.com.gt chini ya Creative Commons Attribution Ruhusa isiyo ya Kibiashara.

eng: Furthermore, as early as March 2012, different voices raised their concerns about the rapidly growing size and role of the military in Guatemala and the presence of so-called "mega projects" like the Goldcorp mine.
swa: Kwa kuongezea zaidi, mapema mwezi Machi, 2012, watu tofauti waliweka bayana matakwa yao kuhusiana na ongezeko la haraka la idadi na kazi za kijeshi nchini Guatemala na uwepo wa kile kijulikanacho kama “miradi mikubwa” ("mega projects") kama vile mgodi wa Goldcorp.

eng: Cascadia solidaria comments about the increased militarized actions against civilians:
swa: Cascadia solidaria anaeleza kuhusiana na kuongezeka kwa matukio mengi ya kijeshi dhidi ya raia:

eng: The strategic use of roadblocks by indigenous and campesino organizations as form of political pressure and re-vindication is harshly contested by the state and powerful economic actors, especially the business lobby CACIF*, which has campaigned for the prohibition and repression of blockades as violations of the right to freedom of movement.
swa: Mkakati wa kufunga barabara unaotumiwa na wazawa na jumuiya za campesino kama namna ya hamasa za kisiasa na kama namna ya kuhamasisha utatuzi wa changamoto zao unapingwa vikali na taifa pamoja na mkundi yenye ushawishi mkubwa wa kiuchumi haswa haswa kundi la watu wafanyabiashara la CACIF*, ambalo limeshahamasisha kuwashikilia watu kama namna ya kukiuka haki ya watu kuwa na uhuru wa kutembea.

eng: The Pérez Molina administration has previously used violence to break up roadblocks and occupations by students, teachers, and parents protesting exclusionary education reforms; if today’s deaths are confirmed to be the responsibility of security forces, it will mark the first clear instance of mortal government repression against civilian protest under Mano Dura.
swa: Serikali ya Pérez Molina siku za hivi karibuni ilitumia nguvu kuwatawanya makundi ya wanafunzi, walimu na wazazi wanaoandamana kupinga mabadiliko ya elimu yaliyo ya kibaguzi; kama mauaji ya sasa yatathibitishwa kuwa yametokana na matumizi ya nguvu ya kijeshi, itakuwa ni kiashirio cha kwanza cha serikali kandamizi iliyo ya kiuaji dhidi ya raia wanaoandamana chini ya uangalizi waMano Dura.

eng: While community leaders have called for investigation of the deaths, if the administration follows the blueprint established by its response to social conflict and protest in Barillas, Huehuetenango, repressive measures such as arrests of protest leaders or declaration of a state of exception could be implemented instead.
swa: Wakati viongozi wa kijamii wanashinikiza uchunguzi kufuatia mauaji haya, kama uongozi unafuata mkakati ulioanzishwa kufuatia migogoro ya kijamii na maandamano ya Barillas, Huehuetenango, mbinu za kushikilia watu kama vile kuwaweka kizuizini viongozi wa maandamano au serekali kutoa tamko zingeweza kutumika.

eng: In an official statement, the President -who is the maximum authority and Commander in Chief of the Guatemalan Army- indicated that he has ordered an investigation into the violence and deaths from October 4.
swa: Katika tamko rasmi la serikali, Rais ambaye ndiye mwenye mamlaka ya mwisho na aliye amiri jeshi mkuu wa jeshi la Guatemala alitanabaisha kuwa ameshatoa amri ya kufanyika kwa uchunguzi kuhusiana na uonevu na mauaji toka Octoba 4.

eng: In the meantime, the communities are waiting for dialogue and responses.
swa: Wakati huohuo, wanajamii wanasubiria majadiliano pamoja na majibu ya kero zao.

eng: This post is part of our special coverage Indigenous Rights.
swa: Makala hii ni sehemu ya makala zetu maalumu kuhusiana na haki za wazawa .

eng: The Atomic Power Project in Koodankulam in the Tirunelveli district of the southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu has started operations last month amidst protests (see Global Voices report).
swa: Mradi wa Nguvu ya Atomiki wa Koodankulam katika wilaya ya Tirunelveli iliyoko katika jimbo la India ya Kaskazini lijulikanalo kama Tamil Nadu, tangu mwezi uliopita walikwisha anzisha maandamano miongoni mwao. (tazama taarifa za Mtandao wa Sauti za Dunia).

eng: The plant has started generating electricity but the situation is becoming worse as arrests are still being carried out and protesters remain in jail.
swa: Mtambo huu umeshaanza kuzalisha umeme lakini hali inaendelea kuwa mbaya kwani watu wanaendelea kuwekwa kizuizini na waandamanaji wanaendelea kushikiliwa magerezani.

eng: This week also marks a call for a fortnight of protests across India in solidarity with people’s struggle against the Nuclear Plant.
swa: Wiki hii pia ni mwanzo wa maandamano ya wiki mbili katika maeneo yote ya India kwa ushirikiano na watu wenye kupinga matumizi ya Mitambo ya Nyuklia.

eng: On Sunday, 14th of October, the revolutionary Democratic Front issued a statement condemning the illegal detention and, arrest on the members of an all-Indian fact finding team to Koodankulam nuclear plant in Tamil Nadu.
swa: Mapema Jumapili ya tarehe 14 Oktoba, Chama cha RDF (Revolutionary Democratic Front) kilitoa tamko linalolaani watu kushikiliwa na kuwekwa kizuizini kwa wanachama wote wa India wanaojaribu kuutafuta ukweli kuhusu mtambo wa nyuklia wa Koodankulam ulio katika jimbo la Tamil Nadu.

eng: The team was detained at Nanguneri on the 12th of October, 20 km away from Koodankulam on charges of “illegal assembly”.
swa: Kundi hilo lilishikiliwa huko Nanguneri mnamo tarehe 12 Oktoba, kilomita 20 kutoka Koodankulam kwa mashitaka ya kuitisha “mikutano isiyo ya halali”.

eng: After a daylong detention, the police charged them under different sections of Criminal Law Amendment Act.
swa: Baada ya kuzuiwa kwa takribani siku nzima, polisi waliwahukumu kwa kutumia vifungu tofauti tofauti vya sheria ya marekebisho ya makosa ya jinai.

eng: The team members have been taken to Palayamkottai prison.
swa: Wanakikundi hao hao wamepelekwa katika mahabusu ya Palayamkottai.

eng: According to Sanhati:
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Sanhati:

eng: “The people of Koodankulam have been bravely fighting against the nuclear power plant which has come up in their homes and hearths for months now.
swa: “Watu wa Koodankulam wamekuwa wakipinga mitambo ya nyuklia kwa ustadi mkubwa uliojengwa katika makazi yao na kusababisha uonevu kwa miezi kadhaa sasa.

eng: The government instead of responding to their just demands and concerns for the immense security risk and the environmental hazard that this plant can cause on the surrounding area, has responded with the most cruel repression on the protesting masses.
swa: Badala ya serikali kusikiliza matakwa yao na kuzingatia suala la kutokuwa na hali nzuri ya ulinzi pamoja na madhara ya uharibifu wa mazingira unaotokana na mitambo hii ya Nyuklia. serikali imewajibu waandamanaji kwa kutumia njia ya ukandamizaji wa kikatili kabisa.

eng: Their attempt to restrict and repress this fact-finding team also clearly shows how they do not want the people to speak out or even knows about the conditions in Koodankulam or about the valiant movement the people are fighting there.
swa: Jaribio la serikali la kuzuia na kulikandamiza kundi hili linalojaribu kuutafuta ukweli inaonesha kwa uwazi kabisa kuwa serikali haitaki watu wazungumzie wala kufahamu hali ilivyo huko Koodankulam au kuhusiana na juhudi ambazo watu wanazoziweka na mambo wanayoyapigania.

eng: The government is simply trying to intimidate and throttle all voices of solidarity and support to the people fighting against Koodankulam nuclear plant.
swa: Serikali inachokifanya ni kujaribu kuwaogopesha watu pamoja na kujaribu kuua sauti za mshikamano wa watu wanaowaunga mkono watu wanaopinga uwepo wa Mtambo wa Nyuklia wa Koodankulam.

eng: Protesters across the nation send in their signatures to kudankulam, India, in solidarity with the anti nuclear campaign.
swa: Waandamanaji nchini kote wanatuma saini zao huko Kudankulam, India, kama namna ya kuonesha mshikamano katika mkakati wa kutokubaliana na matumizi ya nguvu ya nyuklia.

eng: Image by Dipti Desai.
swa: Picha na Dipti Desai.

eng: Copyright Demotix (15/03/2012)
swa: Hati miliki Demotix (15/03/2012)

eng: Also on Sunday, the Socialist Janata (Democratic) Party in Kerala voiced support to people agitating against the proposed nuclear project at Koodankulam in Tamil Nadu.
swa: Pia, siku ya Jumapili, chama cha Kijamaa cha Janata (cha kidemokrasia) huko Kerala kilitoa tamko la kuonesha ushirikiano na watu wanaopinga mpango wa mradi wa Mitambo ya Nyuklia huko Koodankulam katika jimbo la Tamil Nadu.

eng: Women from the protests are still in prison.
swa: Wanawake kutoka miongoni mwa waandamanaji bado wangali gerezani.

eng: Anitha S. writes about them in a post titled 'Koodankulam women from prison: Tell everyone we are still here !:
swa: Anitha S. anaandika kukuhusiana na wanawake hao katika makala yenye kichwa cha habari Wanawake wa Koodankulam kutoka Gerezani: mwambie kila mmja kuwa bado tungali huku!:

eng: Xavieramma said, “We are here so that the world will not see any more nuclear power plants that are dangerous and uneconomic...
swa: Xavieramma anasema, “tupo hapa ili ulimwengu usiendelee zaidi kuona mitambo ya nyuklia iliyo hatari na isiyokuwa na manufaa….

eng: I saw that there are so many people in various parts of the country who are raising their protest.
swa: Nimeona kuwa kuna watu wengi sana katika maeneo mbalimbali nchini wanaoendelea na maandamano.

eng: It is not just about losing their land and sea, but it is about the creation of spaces where life itself is in danger.
swa: Sio tu kuhusu kupoteza ardhi na bahari yao, lakini ni kuhusiana na kujenga matabaka na huku ukichukulia maisha yenyewe yanavyokuwa katika hatari.

eng: Who would want to live in such places?”
swa: Nani angependa kuishi katika mazingira kama haya?”

eng: As another woman Selvi said, “It is only after being part of the struggle that we realized that trying to establish one’s right to live as one wishes, pursuing traditional livelihoods and also questioning activities that are being implemented without consulting the people is equivalent to crime and sedition.”
swa: Kama alivyosema mwanamke mmoja aitwaye Selvi, “hii ni mara tu baada ya kuwa miongoni mwa sehemu ya kujituma ndipo tulipogundua kuwa kujaribu kuweka misingi ya haki ya mtu ya kuishi kama mtu anavyotegemea, akiendeleza utamaduni wa kuishi kindugu na pia kuhoji mambo yanayotekelezwa bila hata ya kujadiliana na watu ni karibu sawa na kosa la jinai na uhaini”.

eng: As Sundari said, “We are here for a common cause- we are here for the world.
swa: Kama Sundari alivyosema, “Tupo hapa kwa ajili ya jambo moja tu- tupo hapa kwa ajili ya ulimwengu.

eng: They wanted to tell the world that they are here, inside, locked up only physically within concrete and iron.
swa: Walitaka kuuambia ulimwengu kuwa tupo hapa, ndani, tumezuiwa kimwili tu kwa kuta za matofali na chuma.

eng: “Tell everyone we are still here”.
swa: “Mwambie kila mmoja kuwa bado tuko hapa”.

eng: They are still in the Women’s Prison of Trichy, holding on to their vision of a world that is “free from one of the most toxic of human inventions".
swa: Bado wapo katika gereza la wanawake la Trichy, wakiwa bado wanashikilia msimamo wa dunia wa “kutokomeza moja ya silaha hatari sana duniani iliyogunduliwa na mwanadamu”.

eng: Former U.S. president Jimmy Carter is accepting questions on Facebook and Twitter (#CarterQA) as part of a commemoration of the Carter Center’s 30th anniversary of "waging peace and fighting disease worldwide".
swa: Rais wa zamani wa Marekani Jimmy Carter anapokea maswali kupitia mitandao ya kijamii ya Facebook na Twita (#CarterQA) kama sehemu ya kuadhimisha miaka 30 ya Kituo cha Carter (Carter Center) kinachojishughulisha na "kupigania masuala ya amani na kupambana na magonjwa duniani kote".

eng: President Carter will be answering by video on October 19, 2012.
swa: Rais Carter atakuwa anayajibu maswali hayo kwa njia ya video tarehe 19 Oktoba, 2012.

eng: Cambodia is mourning the death of King Father Norodom Sihanouk who died last October 15, 2012.
swa: Nchi ya Kambodia inaomboleza kifo cha baba Mfalme Norodom Sihanouk aliyefariki tarehe15 Ockoba, 2012.

eng: Sihanouk is known as a hero of the Kingdom of Cambodia for his achievements which include the peaceful claiming of the country's independence from the French colonization in 1953, for steering the country's road to prosperity during the Sangkum Reastr Niyum, for winning a case in the International Court of Justice in 1962 which recognized Cambodia's ownership of Preah Vihear Temple near the Thai border, and particularly his role in the Paris Peace Agreement in 1991 which marked the end of civil wars that brought peace to the country.
swa: Sihanouk anajulikana kama shujaa wa dola ya Kambodia kutokana na mafanikio yake ambayo ni pamoja na kuipatia uhuru nchi yake kwa njia ya amani kutoka kwa ukoloni wa Kifaransa mnamo mwaka 1953, kuiongoza nchi katika njia ya mafanikio wakati wa Sangkum Reastr Niyum kwa kushinda kesi katika Mahakama ya Kimataifa mnamo mwaka 1962 iliyoifanya Kambodia kupata umiliki halali wa hekalu la Preah Vihear karibu na mpaka wa Thai, na haswa haswa jukumu lake kubwa katika Mkataba wa Amani wa Paris mwaka 1991 uliohitimisha vita vya kiraia na hatimaye kuleta amani nchini Kambodia.

eng: “You are our hero, you will be missed” is the common message expressed by citizens and netizens who are all mourning the death of the King.
swa: “Wewe ni shujaa wetu, tutakukosa” ni ujumbe uliokuwa unatolewa na waombolezaji wote, raia wasio wa mtandaoni na wale wa mtandaoni kufuatia kifo cha mfalme wao.

eng: His body was brought back to the country from Beijing where he often went to seek medical treatment.
swa: Mwili wake ulirudishwa nchini kutoka Beijing mahali ambapo alipendelea kwenda kwa ajili ya matibabu.

eng: Cambodians waited in line along the Russian Boulevard near the Council of Ministers for the return of the late King Father Norodom Sihanouk.
swa: Watu wa Kambodia walijipanga katika misafara pembezoni mwa barabara pana ya Kirusi karibu na jengo la mikutano la Mawaziri wakisubiria kuupokea mwili wa Baba Mfalme Norodom Sihanouk.

eng: Photo by author
swa: Picha na mwandishi wa posti hii.

eng: On October 17, 2012, millions of people waited in line along the way from the international airport to the Royal Palace to pay respect to the King reminiscent of Sihanouk's historic return to Cambodia in November 1991 after being out of the country for 13 years.
swa: Mnamo Oktoba 17, 2012, mamilioni ya watu walijipanga katika misafara pembezoni mwa barabara itokayo uwanja wa ndege wa kimataifa kuelekea katika Kasri Tukufu ili kutoa heshima yao ya mwisho kwa Mfalme, tukio linalokumbusha tukio la kihistoria la kurudi nchini Kambodia kwa mfalme Sihanouk mwaka 1991 baada ya kuwa nje ya nchi kwa miaka 13.

eng: The news of Sihanouk's death broke out during the long holiday of Pchum Ben Festival.
swa: Habari za kifo cha Sihanouk zilianza kusambaa wakati wa likizo ndefu ya sherehe ya Pchum Ben.

eng: The mood suddenly changed in the internet as people started to send their tributes to the late King.
swa: Hali ilibadilika ghafla katika mitandao ya intaneti mara baada ya watu kuanza kutuma maneno ya kumkumbuka hayati mfalme wao.

eng: Cambodians used the twitter hashtag #RIPKingSihanouk to express their mourning: @Cambodian_VIPz #RIPKingSihanouk We're sad and we're crying, you were leaving us.
swa: Watu wa Kambodia walitumia kiungo habari#RIPKingSihanouk cha Twita katika kuomboleza:

eng: Father king of independence Norodom Sihanouk. pic.twitter.com/11x8wRXD ‏@lanycassie #RIPKingSihanouk My hero grandpa smile the best in this world <3 pic.twitter.com/fuD2ilqt
swa: ‏@lanycassie #Pumzika kwa amani Mfalme Sihanouk, babu yangu shujaa ameutumikia ulimwengu ipasavyo <3 pic.twitter.com/fuD2ilqt

eng: @Nida_CamELF Without him, Cambodia are now may still be the slave of French Colonization. #RIPKingSihanouk
swa: @Nida_CamELF Bila yeye, Kambodia inaweza tena kuwa mtumwa wa ukoloni wa Kifaransa. #RIPKingSihanouk

eng: @PinkyElevenShi Even It's Raining But Cambodian Still Stay in front of The Royal Palace This Made Me Crying #RIPKingSihanouk
swa: @PinkyElevenShi Hata kama mvua inanyesha, watu wa Kambodia bado wanaendelea kuwepo mbele ya Kasri Tukufu. Hali hii inanifanya nijisikie kulia. # Pumzika kwa amani mfalme Sihanouk

eng: There are also Facebook pages which were created in honor of the King Father:
swa: Pia kuna kurasa za Facebook zilizoanzishwa kwa kumbukumbu ya Baba Mfalme:

eng: Cambodians coming from various provinces and regions were united in mourning the death of King Norodom Sihanouk.
swa: Watu wa Kambodia kutoka katika majimbo na maeneo mbalimbali waliungana kuomboleza kifo cha Mfalme Norodom Sihanouk.

eng: Photo from the Facebook photo album of Rip Somdech Ta (King Norodom Sihanouk)
swa: Picha kutoka katika hifadhi ya picha za Facebook ya Somdech Ta (Mfalme Norodom Sihanouk)

eng: Khmerbird hopes to see Cambodian politicians to follow the teachings of the late King:
swa: Khmerbird Anategemea kuwaona wanasiasa wa Kambodia wakifuata mafundisho ya hayati mfalme:

eng: The King Father once said (Source):
swa: Baba Mfalme aliwahi kusema (chanzo):

eng: I want my country to be independent, always independent.
swa: Nahitaji nchi yangu kuwa huru, wakati wote kuwa huru.

eng: I have done my best, but as a human being I cannot be perfect, nobody is perfect.
swa: Nimefanya kwa kadiri ya uwezo wangu, lakini mimi kama binadamu, siwezi kuwa mkamilifu, hakuna aliye mkamilifu.

eng: I hope all Cambodian politician would follow this statement. The King Father accepted that he is not perfect but he has a clear vision to put his country independent.
swa: Ni matumaini yangu kuwa wanasiasa wote wa Kambodia watayafuata maelezo haya.Baba Mfalme alikiri kuwa yeye si mkamilifu, lakini alikuwa na maono thabiti ya kuifanya nchi yake kuwa huru.

eng: Khmerbird identifies the legacy of Sihanouk:
swa: Khmerbird anaainishaurithi ambao Sihanouk ameuacha:

eng: He built a very beautiful country and made Cambodia once as the most beautiful country in Asia.
swa: Aliijenga nchi nzuri na kuifanya nchi ya Kambodia kuwa nchi inayovutia sana katika bara la Asia.

eng: There’s one thing we know it is true is that he loves his country and he wants to bring happiness to his people.
swa: Kuna jambo moja tunalolifahamu fika kuwa (Sihanouk) aliipenda nchi yake na alitaka kuleta furaha kwa watu wake.

eng: The King's death inspired citizens like Koh Tha to contribute more for the progress of the country:
swa: Kifo cha Mfalme kiliwahamasisha raia kama vile raia huyuKoh Tha ambaye alihamasika kuchangia zaidi katika maendeleo ya nchi:

eng: I watched TVs broadcasted the ceremony and historical films and documents of my late great King.
swa: Nilifuatilia Televisheni zilizokuwa zinaonesha sherehe, picha za kihistoria na hati za hayati Mfalme wangu.

eng: I don’t know why my mind feel so mixed, sad and sorrow.
swa: Sifahamu ni kwa nini akili yangu inajisikia kuchanganyikiwa, yenye huzuni na masikitiko.

eng: My tear dropped silently.
swa: Chozi lilinitoka moyoni.

eng: I deeply feel that I myself as well as my country lost the great hero.
swa: Ninapata hisia kali kuwa mimi mwenyewe pia na nchi yangu tumempoteza shujaa mkubwa.

eng: Then, a very strong power come into my heart and talk my that “Kok Tha, there is something that you need to put more effort to help and develop your country”.
swa: Na ndipo nguvu kubwa ikaja katika moyo wangu na kujisemea “Kok Tha , kuna jambo ambalo unapaswa kuliwekea juhudi zaidi la kusaidia na kuijenga nchi yako”.

eng: I just feel that what I have done so far is not enough and even much less than my king.
swa: Nilijisikia kuwa, kile nilichokwisha kukifanya hadi sasa hakitoshi na ni kidogo sana ukilinganisha na kile alichokifanya Mfalme wangu.

eng: I need to continue my hard-work and my well-being to colleague, youth organizations, role models, my friends, youths, family and my love.
swa: Ninapaswa kuendelea kujituma na kujitolea kwa wenzangu, mashirika ya vijana, watu wa kupigiwa mfano, marafiki zangu, vijana, familia na mpenzi wangu.

eng: The National Mourning Ceremony for the King will take place until October 23, 2012. The public can pay their last respects by visiting the Royal Palace in the next three months.
swa: Hafla ya kitaifa ya maombolezo ya Mfalme itaendelea hadi tarehe 23 Oktoba, 2012. wananchi wanaweza kutoa heshima yao ya mwisho kwa kufika katika Kasri Tukufu kwa kipindi cha miezi mitatu ijayo.

eng: After this period, the King's body will be cremated according to Buddhism ritual.
swa: Baada ya muda huu, mwili wa Mfalme utachomwa hadi kuwa majivu kulingana na mila na desturi za Budha.

eng: Tear gas and stun grenades were used to disperse a protest in Kuwait against changes to the electoral law.
swa: Mabomu ya kutoa machozi na maguruneti ya kumfanya mtu kupoteza fahamu yalitumika kutawanya maandamano ya kupinga mabadiliko ya sheria ya uchaguzi nchini Kuwait.

eng: The call for the Karamat Watan (A Nation's Dignity) march, which took place on Sunday, was made on Twitter, and attracted about 150,000 out of the country's population of 3 million.
swa: Kuitishwa kwa matembezi ya Karamat Watan ( Heshima ya Taifa), yaliyofanyika siku ya Jumapili, yaliyoandaliwa katika mtandao wa Twita, yaliyowavutia takribani watu 150,000 kati ya watu milioni 3 ambao ndio idadi ya watu wa Kuwait.

eng: Media outlets considered this number to be the biggest in the small Gulf emirate's history.
swa: Taarifa za vyombo vya habari zinaichukulia idadi hii kuwa ni kubwa kabisa katika historia ya Falme za ghuba ndogo.

eng: The protest came in reaction to the Amir Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah decree to change the electoral law, making a citizen vote for one candidate instead of four, as it used to be in the elections of Kuwaiti parliament.
swa: Waandamanaji walipingana na amri ya Amir Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah ya kubadili sheria ya uchaguzi inayowataka raia wamchague mgombea mmoja badala ya wagombea wanne kama ilivyokuwa awali katika chaguzi za bunge la Kuwait.

eng: The protest was not only an objection for making such a change but more importantly to protest the change of a law without the parliament or the people having their say in it.
swa: Maandamano hayakulenga tu kupinga mabadiliko haya ya sheria ya uchaguzi, bali pia kupinga kubadili sheria hii bila ya kulishirikisha bunge na maoni ya wananchi.

eng: Since last June, Kuwaiti parliament has been frozen by the Amir and then dissolved by the constitutional court for 'wrong procedures' in dissolving the parliament before it.
swa: Tangu mwisho wa mwezi Juni, Bunge la Kuwait lilisimamishwa na Rais Amir na hatimaye kuvunjwa na mahakama ya kikatiba kwa ‘taratibu zisizo sahihi’ za kuvunja Bunge.

eng: The opposition has been protesting since but was never able to gather such a huge crowd; even the liberal "Tahalof" and Pan-Arabist "Manbar" took part in Sunday's demonstration despite their disagreement with the Islamist-Conservative opposition.
swa: Upinzani umekuwa ukilalamikia jambo hili kwa muda sasa lakini kamwe haukufanikiwa kuhamasisha idadi kubwa ya watu kama ilivyo sasa; hata chama cha kiliberali cha "Tahalof" na kile cha mkusanyiko wa Waarabu "Manbar" walijumuika katika maandamano ya jumapili pamoja na kuwa hawakubaliani na upinzani wa waisilamu wenye msimamo mkali.

eng: In a unique step, this demonstration was organized through Twitter.
swa: Katika hatua ya kipekee, maandamano haya yaliratibiwa kupitia mtandao wa Twita.

eng: The account @KarametWatan (which translates to A Nation's Dignity) was started to call for the protest.
swa: Akaunti ya Twita @KarametWatan (ambayo maana yake ni Heshima ya Taifa) ilianzishwa ili kuitisha maandamano.

eng: It suggested an orange avatar (in reference to the 2006 youth movement that changed the electoral law from 25 districts to 5), and organized the meeting points with the following map:
swa: Ilipendekeza picha ya rangi ya chungwa (kwa kurejea harakati za vijana za mwaka 2006 yaliyobadilisha sheria ya uchaguzi kutoka wilaya 25 hadi wilaya 5), na walipanga sehemu za mikutano kwa kutumia ramani ifuatayo:

eng: The protest route shared by @KarametWatan on Twitter
swa: Njia ya maandamano iliyowekwa na @KarametWatan katika mtandao wa Twita

eng: As usual, Kuwaitis used Twitter to post pictures and videos of the protest.
swa: Kama kawaida, watu wa Kuwait walitumia Twita kuweka picha na video za maandamano.

eng: Here are some of the pictures:
swa: Zifuatazo ni baadhi ya picha;

swa: Katika Twita, @NforNaser anasema kuwa polisi walimtaka aliangushe bango hili vinginevyo wangempiga.

eng: The sign reads: Believe in the people; disbelieve in the system.
swa: Bango linasomeka: waamini watu, usiuamini mfumo.

eng: Picture of the crowds marching posted by @nourah_ibrahim
swa: Picha ya makundi makubwa ya watu katika matembezi iliyowekwa na@nourah_ibrahim

swa: Muandamanaji akiwa amejeruhiwa kichwani (picha iliwekwa na @BuNaWaFF)

eng: Another injured protester with his feet cuffed (posted by @3asalaswad)
swa: Muandamanaji mwingine aliyejeruhiwa huku miguu yake ikiwa imefungiwa pingu (Imewekwa na @3asalaswad)

eng: Protesters running away from tear gas bombs (posted by @JanarlySpeaking)
swa: Waandamanaji wakikimbia kukwepa moshi wa mabomu ya machozi (imewekwa na @JanarlySpeaking)

swa: Ili kuonesha idadi, makundi makubwa ya waandamanaji na nyimbo zilizokuwa zikiimbwa mara kwa mara, video hii ilitumwa katika mtandao wa YouTube na Q8jo7a:

eng: On Monday , Sabr Online Newspaper reported that all detained protesters have been released:
swa: Siku ya Jumatatu , Gazeti la mtandaoni la Sabr lilitoa taarifa kuwa, waandamanaji waliokuwa wanashikiliwa walishaachiliwa:

eng: Urgent: All those arrested in the Nation's Dignity march have been released
swa: Muhimu: Wote waliokuwa wanashikiliwa katika matembezi ya Heshima ya Taifa wameshaachiliwa

eng: Lingua Project Global Voices in Malagasy
swa: Mradi wa Lingua wa Global Voices katika lugha ya Ki-Malagasi

eng: Lingua project Global Voices in Malagasy has just published its 5,000th post.
swa: Mradi wa Lingua wa Global Voices katika lugha ya ki-Malagasi umechapisha mtandaoni posti yake ya 5,000.

eng: The project was started on September 12, 2007 and was one of the first African lingua project.
swa: Mradi huo ulianza mwezi Septemba 12, 2007 ukiwa kati ya miradi ya mwanzo kabisa ya Mradi mkubwa wa Lugha za Kiafrika.

eng: There are currently 16 active Malagasy translators, among them is one of the youngest Global Voices translator, 16-year-old Radifera Felana Candy.
swa: Kwa sasa mradi huo unaendeshwa na watafsiri wa ki-Malagasi wapatao 16 miongoni mwao akiwamo mmoja wa watafsiri wadogo kabisa wa Global Voices , mwenye umri wa miaka 16 aitwaye Radifera Felana Candy.

eng: In an effort to include ordinary Singaporeans in the planning of the nation's future, the government has launched a "national conversation" that will last for about a year to gather people's views.
swa: Katika juhudi za kuwahusisha wananchi wa tabaka la chini katika kupangilia mustakabali wa Singapore, serikali ya nchi hiyo imezindua “mazungumzo ya kitaifa” yatakayodumu kwa mwaka mmoja ili kukusanya maoni ya watu.

eng: Led by the Our Singapore committee, the national conversation will take place online as well as in various dialogues and meetings.
swa: Ikiongozwa na kamati yetu ya Singapore, mazungumzo hayo ya kitaifa yatafanyikia mtandaoni na pia kwa njia ya mahojiano kadhaa na mikutano.

eng: Our Singapore Conversation has both a website and a Facebook page, and urges people to share their views on Twitter using the #oursgconv hashtag.
swa: Mazungumzo hayo ya Singapore tayari yanapatikana katika tovuti na pia ukurasa wa Facebook, na yanawataka watu watoe maoni yao katika mtandao wa twita kwa kutumia kiungo habari cha #oursgconv.

eng: The exercise has been met with positivity from some Singaporeans.
swa: Zoezi hili limeshapokewa vizuri na baadhi ya watu wa Singapore.

eng: Petunia Lee writes about her experience of attending a dialogue session:
swa: Petunia Lee anaandika kuhusiana na uzoefu wake wa kuhudhuria katika vipindi vya mazungumzo:

eng: From the Facebook page of Our SG Conversation
swa: Kutoka katika ukurasa wa facebook wa mazungumzo yetu ya SG

eng: I must say that my experience of the SG Conversation opened my eyes to other Singaporeans.
swa: Napaswa kusema kuwa, uzoefu wangu katika mazungumzo ya SG ulifungua macho yangu kwa wananchi wenzangu wa Singapore.

eng: For one, I didn't realize that the elderly in Singapore felt such a sense of dispossession and rejection until one elderly gentleman from my group said his piece.
swa: Jambo la kwanza, sikuweza kutambua namna wazee wa Singapore walivyojisikia kwa kunyimwa haki ya kumiliki na kutengwa hadi pale mzee mmoja mchangamfu kutoka katika kikundi changu alipotoa maoni yake.

eng: For another, I had had the wrong assumption that harmonious race relations are so much a part of us that we don't need to work at it.
swa: Jambo jingine ni kuwa, nilikuwa na mtizamo hasi kuwa mahusiano ya amani kati ya watu wa rangi tofauti ni sehemu ya maisha yetu kiasi kwamba hatuhitaji kulifuatilia kabisa.

eng: It was a Malay lady doctor who in her impassioned speech convinced me that race relations can cause today, as much rawness as in the 1960s.
swa: Alikuwa ni daktari mwanadada mtu wa Malaysia ambaye katika hotuba yake iliyojaa hamasa alinishawishi kuwa mahusiano kati ya watu wa rangi tofauti yanaweza kuleta madhara leo kama ilivyotokea katika miaka ya 1960.

eng: So yes... I think if, as explained by Mr Tan, the aim of the SG Conversation is to teach each of us some truths about our own country, then it did achieve that aim with me.
swa: Ndiyo.... nafikiri kwamba, kama jinsi ilivyoelezwa na ndugu Tan, dhumuni la mazungumzo ya SG ni kutufundisha ukweli fulani kuhusu nchi yetu, na kwangu mimi, lengo hili lilitimia.

eng: However, many others are wary of the exercise, seeing it as nothing more than a public relations endeavour.
swa: Hata hivyo, wapo watu wengi wanaotilia mashaka zoezi hili, wakiona kuwa si chochote zaidi ya jitihada za mahusiano ya umma.

eng: Molly Meek believes that the whole national conversation is simply a ploy to change the ruling party's image:
swa: Molly Meek anaamini kuwa mazungumzo yote ya kitaifa ni hila tu za kubadilisha taswira ya chama tawala:

eng: The PAP’s strategy is intelligent—one even wonders if they have consulted professionals on the matter before proceeding with their efforts—and one cannot helped but be impressed by their measurable success.
swa: Mbinu ya chama tawala (PAP) ni yenye kutumia akili sana—mtu anaweza kujiuliza kama waliwasiliana na wataalamu kuhusiana na jambo hili kabla ya kuendelea na juhudi zao hizi- mtu hawezi kusaidiwa bali kuridhishwa kwa mafanikio yao yanayopimika.

eng: The strategy employed is perhaps fairly simple—target a few citizens, including prominent ones and lesser-known ones, that are moderately against the PAP, give them a different impression, and let them spread the news that the PAP really is not what its detractors have made it out to be.
swa: Mbinu iliyotumika kwa hakina ni rahisi— imelenga raia wachache ikiwa ni pamoja na watu maarufu na wale wanaojulikana kidogo tu na kwa wastani, wale wanaokipinga chama tawala cha PAP, wakiwapa mawazo tofauti na kuwaacha wakisambaza taarifa kuwa chama tawala cha PAP sio kweli kuwa ndio wanaokikashifu.

eng: In fact, these do not even need to say anything—a mere talk with the PAP that leaves them with nothing to criticize will be effective enough for others who can still be convinced to support the PAP.
swa: Kwa hakika, mambo haya hayapaswi kuwa na maana yoyote, ni maneno matupu kwa chama cha PAP ambacho kinawaacha wakiwa hawana chochote cha kupinga itakuwa ni njia muafaka sana kwa wengine ambao bado wanaweza kushawishika kukiunga mkono chama cha PAP.

eng: An editorial at publichouse.sg points out that the conversation may not lead to real change:
swa: Mhariri katika gazeti la publichouse.sg anafafanua kuwa mazungumzo haya yanaweza yasiishie kwenye mabadiliko ya kweli:

eng: Even if it is assumed that the ministers leading the current initiative are of a keenly liberal bent, the older guards in the Cabinet remain likely to have a veto over the final product.
swa: Hata kama itafikiriwa kuwa mawaziri wanaoratibu mkakati huu wa sasa wanafanya udanganyifu makini wa wazi, waangalizi wa zamani katika baraza la mawaziri bado wanaweza kupiga kura ya turufu kuhusiana na matokeo ya mpango huo.

eng: It is instructive that a majority of the more liberal suggestions made by the Remaking Singapore Committee – such as for the government to define the out-of-bounds markers for political debate, creating an Economic Relief Scheme for the structurally unemployed and subsidising the MediShield premiums of low-income groups – went unheeded.
swa: Inaelekezwa kuwa, mengi ya mapendekezo huru na yaliyo makini yaliyoandaliwa na kamati teule ya Singapore- kama yale ya serikali kuweka bayana waundaji wasio na mipaka ya midahalo ya kisiasa, uanzishwaji wa mpango wa kuwasaidia kiuchumi watu wasio na ajira pamoja na kupunguza gharama za bidhaa kwa makundi ya watu wa kipato cha chini hayakutiliwa maanani.

eng: Join the Singapore Conversation' websiteHoward Lee, writing for The Online Citizen, commented on the perceived partisan bias in the conversation:
swa: jiunge na tovuti ya mazungumzo ya Singapore’ Howard Lee, anayeliandikia gazeti la The Online Citizen, alitoa maoni kwa mfuasi wa chama anayedhaniwa kupendelewa katika mazungumzo hayo:

eng: We simply do not want to see a Conversation that is dominated by people who might be sympathetic of the ruling party's position on national issues, and are hence more likely to be part of the ancient echo chamber.
swa: Hatutaki kuona mazungumzo yanayotawaliwa na watu wanaoonekana kuvumilia utendaji wa chama tawala katika mambo ya kitaifa, na ambao ndio wanaosadikiwa kuwa sehemu ya mwangwi wa kale wa chumba cha siri cha majaji.

eng: How would we look forward, if so?
swa: Tungewezaje kufikiria yajayo kama ndivyo?

eng: In other words, Wong and others like him need to realise that the ball is in the PAP's court to prove that they can be non-partisan, rather than lambast those who are raising the red flag on partisanship as 'politicised'.
swa: Kwa maneno mengine, Wong na wengine kama yeye wanatakiwa kutambua kuwa mpira kwa sasa upo katika mipaka ya chama tawala cha PAP ili kuthibitisha kuwa wanaweza wsiwe wafuasi wa chama, bali ni watu wanaokipinga chama kwa nguvu zote na ambao wanaipeperusha bendera nyekundu kwa ushirikiano wao wakiwa kama watu waliofundishwa siasa.

eng: Proof is in actions, not words.
swa: Kuthibitisha kupo kwenye matendo na si kwa maneno.

eng: We want diverse voices, even oppositional ones that sit at the far ends of the fence of logic and possibility, to get to the bottom of matters and stimulate a hearty, if not heart-felt, discussion, rather than another consensus building show-and-tell.
swa: Tunahitaji sauti kutoka sehemu tofauti tofauti, hata wale wapinzani walio mbali kabisa ya wigo wa mantiki na wasio na manufaa, wahusishwe kwa kila jambo na wahamasishe midahalo kwa moyo na kama sio kwa kuguswa, kuliko kujenga muafaka mwingine wa kuonesha na kusema.

eng: And Singaporeans have the right to expect the National Conversations to be like that.
swa: Na watu wa Singapore wana haki ya kutegemea mazungumzo ya kitaifa kuwa namna hiyo.

eng: While the conversation continues in dialogue sessions and on Facebook, the Twitter hashtag #oursgconv appears to have been hijacked by anti-opposition spam: @SGSilentMaj : Freedom of expression is bad for #Singapore #sgpolitics #sgelections http://bit.ly/REUBsd http://bit.ly/TJjDZX
swa: Wakati mazungumzo yanaendelea katika vikao vya maongezi na katika facebook, kiungo habari cha Twita, #oursgconv kinaonekana kuingiliwa bila idhini na jumbe za watu wanaopinga mpango huu:

eng: @SGLaoBaiXing : WP taking credit for PAP's work #sgpolitics #sgelections http://bit.ly/TcBoTM http://bit.ly/R4RV9G
swa: @SGSilentMaj : Uhuru wa kutoa maoni ni mbaya kwa #Singapore #sgpolitics #sgelections http://bit.ly/REUBsd http://bit.ly/TJjDZX

eng: As Kuwaitis embarked on their largest ever protest to denounce changes to the electoral law, passed by the country's hereditary ruler while the Parliament was dissolved, Egyptians kept themselves busy on Twitter, dishing advice to them on what to do and not to do.
swa: Wakati watu wa Kuwait walipoanzisha maandamano makubwa ambayo hayakuwahi kutokea ya kuonesha waziwazi kutokukubaliana na mabadiliko ya sheria ya uchaguzi yaliyopitishwa chini ya mtawala wa kurithi kufuatia kuvunjwa kwa bunge, watu wa Misri wametumia muda wao mwingi katika Twita wakitoa ushauri kwa watu wa Kuwait kuhusiana na yapi ya kufanya na yapi ya kutokufanya.

eng: Samah Anwar tackles the dress code of Kuwaiti men, who wear a long flowing gown called a thobe.
swa: Samah Anwar amejikita katika kujadili namna ya uvaaji ya wanaume wa Kuwait, ambao wanavaa namna fulani ya kanzu iitwayo thobe.

eng: @samahanwar: Wearing a thobe is not suitable for revolutions
swa: @samahanwar: Kuvaa kanzu aina ya thobe si vazi muafaka katika harakati za mapinduzi

eng: In another tweet, she uses reason:
swa: Katika ujumbe mwingine wa Twita, Samah Anwar anatoa sababu:

eng: @samahanwar: Don't destroy your country.
swa: @samahanwar: Usiiangamize nchi yako.

eng: You are living well.
swa: Unaishi vizuri.

eng: Thank God for your blessings.
swa: Mshukuru Mungu kwa kila unalojaaliwa.

eng: Other people aren't able to live
swa: Watu wengine wanashindwa kuishi.

eng: Many Egyptians echoed similar sentiments.
swa: Watu wengi wa Misri walikuwa na mawazo yanayofanana.

eng: Ebrahim Elkhadm writes :
swa: Ebrahim Elkhadm anaandika:

eng: @ebrahimelkhadm: You would be losers if you listen to us.
swa: @ebrahimelkhadm: Mtapotea kama mkitusikiliza sisi.

eng: We don't even know how to advice ourselves. Let's not be stupid

eng: On Tuesday 9 October, 1962, Uganda got its independence as the Union Jack flag of England was lowered, the Ugandan flag raised whilst jubilant Ugandans sang the Uganda National Anthem.
swa: Mnamo Jumanne ya Oktoba 9, 1962, Uganda ilijitwalia uhuru wake wakati bendera ya Uingereza iliposhushwa, na bendera ya Uganda kupandishwa wakati huo wa-Ganda wenye furaha na matumaini mapya wakiimba Wimbo wa Taifa la Uganda.

eng: On Tuesday 9 October, 2012, Uganda marked the Golden Jubilee of this historic event.
swa: Tarehe 9 Oktoba, 2012, Uganda ilitimiza miaka 50 ya dhahabu ya tukio hilo la kihistoria.

eng: Many occasions have taken place around the country to mark this special day, which started with the Kampala Carnival on Sunday 7 October.

eng: Uganda has had eight presidents since independence, namely, King Sir Edward Muteesa II, Apollo Milton Obote, Idi Amin Dada, Yusuf kironde Lule, Godfrey Lukongwa Binayiisa, Paulo Muwanga, Tito Okello Lutwa, and the current President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni.
swa: Uganda imewahi kuwa namarais nane tangu uhuru, kwa majina, Mfalme Edward Muteesa II, Apollo Milton Obote, Idi Amin Dada, Yusuf kironde Lule, Godfrey Lukongwa Binayiisa, Paulo Muwanga, Tito Okello Lutwa, na rais wa sasa Yoweri Kaguta Museveni.

eng: User @Racksonador calls for a stop to alarmist discussion:
swa: Mtumiaji wa mtandao wa twita @Racksonador anatoa wito wa kumaliza mijadala ya kishabiki:

eng: @Racksonador : And stop saying that people are going to get killed or that you are going to get killed and that you are leaving the country.
swa: @Racksonador : Acheni kusema kuwa watu watauawa au kwamba mtauwa na kwamba mtahama nchi.

eng: IT'S DONE #ElcomandanteSeQueda (The commander is staying)
swa: IMEKWISHA! #ElcomandanteSeQueda (The commander is staying)

eng: On the side of the opposition there is gratitude for Henrique Capriles and his campaign, criticism towards the President's opportunism, and allegations of serious irregularities that go back to the days of the campaign.
swa: Kwa upande wa upinzani kuna pongezi kwa Henrique Capriles na timu yake ya kampeni, kukosolewa kwa tabia ya rais kubahatisha fursa, na madai ya ukiukwaji mkubwa wa taratibu za uchaguzi zinazoanzia kipindi cha kampeni.

eng: Similarly, many also call fellow Capriles supporters to reflect on the results, to continue the fight, and to take into account that while victory was not achieved in this election, the leaders of the opposition now have an organized group that will allow for cohesive and more efficient work in the years to come.
swa: Vivyo hivyo, wengi wanatoa wito kwa wafuasi wenzao wa Henrique Capriles kutafakari matokeo hayo, kuendeleza mapambano, na kufahamu kuwa hata kama ushindi haukupatikana katika uchaguzi huu, viongozi wa upinzani sasa wameonekana kuwa imara hali inayowezesha kuwa na utendaji wa pamoja na uliobora kwa miaka mingi ijayo.

eng: Fedosy Santaella (@Fedosy) writes:
swa: Fedosy Santaella (@Fedosy) anaandika:

eng: @Fedosy : Capriles will continue serving, I will continue writing.
swa: @Fedosy : Capriles ataendelea kutumikia nchi hii, nami nitandelea kuandika.

eng: My country is my country.
swa: Nchi yangu ni nchi yangu.

eng: I am no less Venezuelan, and no less a writer.
swa: Mimi si m-Venezuela asiye na haki kama wengine, na si mwandishi asiye kama wengine.

eng: Moraima Guanipa (@haticos) says:
swa: Moraima Guanipa (@haticos) anasema:

eng: @haticos : I will recognize the victory of Hugo Rafael Chávez Frías but I will never applaud the opportunistic, abusive, and manipulative way in which it was imposed.
swa: @haticos : Nitautambua ushindi wa Hugo Rafael Chávez Frías lakini kamwe sitampongeza mtu huyu aliyepatikana kwa njia za ubabaishaji, matusi, na ubabe.

eng: User @upallove , meanwhile, expresses her disappointment in the results of this and of past presidential elections: @upallove : Cristina won in Argentina.
swa: Mtumiaji @upallove , wakati huo huo, anaonyesha kukatishwa tamaa na matokeo ya uchaguzi huu wa Urais na nyingine zilizopita:

eng: @DynamiteAndre: "LONG LIVE CHÁVEZ!" followed by the sound of shots in a row.
swa: @DynamiteAndre: "UISHI MAISHA MAREFU CHÁVEZ!" maneno yakifuatiwa na milio ya risasi.

eng: No, chavista friend.
swa: Hapana, rafiki wa chavista .

eng: You won't be able to convince me that this is OK.
swa: Hutaweza kunishawishi kwamba hiyo ni sahihi.

eng: After sifting through the numerous exchanges that took place during the night of the election, an idea seems to creep up as part of the debate: the need for mutual recognition to overcome the long separation of social classes, and the need for self-criticism from each of the players.
swa: Baada ya kupitia mijadala mbalimbali iliyotokea usiku wa uchaguzi, kuna wazo linaonekana kujitokeza kuwa sehemu ya mjadala: hitaji la kutambua kwa pamoja umuhimu wa kumaliza matabaka katika jamii, na hitaji la wadau wote kujichunguza wenyewe.

eng: Luis Carlos Díaz (@LuisCarlos) points to this need that stands out as a result of this election:
swa: Luis Carlos Díaz (@LuisCarlos) anabainisha hitaji hili ambalo linabaki kuwa matokeo ya uchaguzi:

eng: @LuisCarlos : The competition for the recognition of the other begins.
swa: @LuisCarlos : Mashindano ya kuwatambua wengine ndiyo kwanza yanaanza.

eng: Luis Carlos also highlighted a fact for reflection by all political tendencies:
swa: Luis Carlos pia anakazia ukweli unaotakiwa kuwa sehemu ya tafakuri za mienendo yote ya kisiasa:

eng: @LuisCarlos : President Chávez wins a presidential election for the fourth time and will have a 1999-2019 term.
swa: @LuisCarlos : Rais Chávez ameshinda uchaguzi wa rais kwa mara ya nne na atakuwa na muhula ulioanza 1999 mpaka 2019.

eng: From the side supporting Chávez, Gabriel López (@GaboVzla) says:
swa: Kutoka upande unaomwunga mkono Chávez, Gabriel López (@GaboVzla) anasema:

eng: @GaboVzla: The victory that we all already know about also deserves profound reflection, which will surely come.
swa: @GaboVzla: Ushindi ambao wote tayari tunaufahamu unahitaji tafakari ya kina, ambayo ni lazima iwepo.

eng: Today, let's celebrate and strengthen our democracy
swa: Leo, tusherehekee na kuimarisha demokrasia yetu

eng: Many questions remain unanswered and many more opinions will fill the discussion this week in the Venezuelan blogosphere.
swa: Maswali mengi yanabaki bila majibu na maoni mengine mengi yatajaza mjadala huo kwa juma hili katika ulimwengu wa blogu nchini Venezuela.

eng: Today, social networks in Venezuela show a country at the fringe.
swa: Leo, mitandao ya kijamii nchini Venezuela imekuwa ikitoa taswira ya nchi hiyo kuwa ukingoni mwa zoezi muhimu.

eng: Along with testimonies, information, rumors and recommendations, citizen media platforms like Twitter, Facebook and Flickr have shared photos that portray a massive participation to elect the next President of the Republic.
swa: Pamoja na shuhuda mbalimbali, taarifa, tetesi na mapendekezo, majukwaa ya vyombo vya habari vya kijamii kama vile Twita, Facebook na Flickr yameonyesha picha zinazoonyesha ushiriki mkubwa wa raia katika kumchagua Rais ajaye wa Jamhuri hiyo.

eng: According to some comments, some voting centers opened their doors to the first assistants on Saturday at midnight, and they continue welcoming citizens from inside the country and abroad.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa maoni kadhaa, baadhi ya vituo vya upigaji kura vilifunguliwa usiku wa manane wa siku ya Jumamosi, ambapo wasimamizi wasaidizi wa zoezi hilo waliruhusiwa kuingia, na kuwapa fursa raia kutoka ndani na nje ya nchi kupiga kura.

eng: Maritza Salazar (@MaritzaSalazar) shared this picture of voters waiting in queue since the night before:
swa: Maritza Salazar (@MaritzaSalazar) aliweka picha hii ya wapiga kura wakiwa katika foleni ndefu tangu usiku wa kuamkia uchaguzi:

eng: Photo shared by @maritzasalazar on Twitter
swa: Picha na @maritzasalazar kupitia mtandao wa Twita

eng: Fernando Rios (@FernandoRiosD) shared a photo of Carlos Urbaneja, a 94-year-old citizen whose identity number is 5 and who went to exercise his right to vote:
swa: Fernando Rios (@FernandoRiosD) aliweka picha ya Carlos Urbaneja, raia mwenye miaka 94 ambaye namba yake ya utambulisho ni 5 na ayekwenda kutumia haki yake ya kuchagua:

eng: Photo shared by @FernandoRiosD on Twitter
swa: Picha imewekwa na @FernandoRiosD kupitia mtandao wa Twita

eng: Under the hashtag #NoEsUnaColaEsUnCamino (it is not a queue, it is a road) that makes reference to Henrique Capriles' slogan "there's a road"; many Twitter users shared pictures of the voting centers, the long queues, cheering messages, and fingers painted in violet ink which confirms without doubt that someone voted.
swa: Kwa kupitia alama habari #NoEsUnaColaEsUnCamino (si foleni, ni barabara) inayorejea kauli mbiu ya Henrique Capriles "kuna barabara"; watumiaji wa mtandao wa twita wametuma mtandaoni picha za vituo vya upigaji kura, foleni ndefu, ujumbe wa matumaini, na vidole vilivyochonywa wino usiofutika unaothibitisha pasi na shaka kwamba mhusika amepiga kura.

eng: Carlos Garcia (@carlosgarciareq) and Mirian de Aristimuño (@MiriamJSdeA) presented their fingers painted in violet under the hashtag #yavote (I already voted):
swa: Carlos Garcia (@carlosgarciareq) na Mirian de Aristimuño (@MiriamJSdeA) walionyesha vidole vyao vilivyochonywa wino usiofutika kupitia alama habari #yavote (Nimeshapiga kura yangu):

eng: Photo shared by @MiriamJSdeA on Twitter
swa: Picha imewekwa na @MiriamJSdeA kupitia mtandao wa Twita

eng: Photo by @carlosgarciareq on Twitter
swa: Picha imewekwa na @carlosgarciareq kupitia mtandao wa Twita

eng: Also, Martha Evelyn Batres (@Tita_Batres) uploaded images that showed the large number of people that participated in the election:
swa: Vilevile, Martha Evelyn Batres (@Tita_Batres) alipandisha picha zilizoonyesha idadi kubwa ya watu wakishiriki uchaguzi huo:

eng: Photo shared by @Tita_Batres on Twitter
swa: Picha zimewekwa na @Tita_Batres kupitia mtandao wa Twita

eng: Furthremore, the blog The Devil's Excrement shared some pictures where we can see the long queues in Caracas and outside Venezuela:
swa: Zaidi ya hayo, blogu ya The Devil's Excrement iliweka picha kadhaa zinazoonyesha foleni ndefu za watu jijini Caracas na hata nje ya Venezuela:

eng: Andrés Bello School, photo shared on the blog The Devil's Excrement Jessica Carrillo collaborated in this post.
swa: Shule ya Andrés Bello, picha iliwekwa awali kwenye blogu ya The Devil's Excrement Jessica Carrillo alishiriki katika uandaaji wa posti hii.

eng: This post is part of our special coverage Venezuela Elections 2012. Portuguese photographer Eduardo Leal has published an online photographic gallery that aims to "give a voice to both sides, the supporters of Chávez and of ."
swa: Mpiga picha wa Kireno Eduardo Leal ameweka mkusanyiko wa picha mtandaoni ambao unakusudia “kupaza sauti za wafuasi wa pande zote, yaani wafuasi wa Chávez na wale wa ."

eng: In 'Faces and Voices of an Election', Eduardo captures the thoughts and feelings of the Venezuelan people as they explain who they will vote for in the presidential election on Sunday, October 7, 2012.
swa: Katika 'Sura na Sauti za Uchaguzi', Eduardo anavuta hisia na mawazo ya watu wa Venezuela anapowapa fursa ya kueleza ni mgombea yupi watamchagua katika uchaguzi wa rais uliofanyika Jumapili, Oktoba 7, 2012.

eng: He opens the introduction to his online gallery with a brief overview of the last 14 years under the government of President Hugo Chávez:
swa: Anafungua utangulizi wa mkusanyiko wa picha hizo za mtandaoni kwa maelezo mafupi ya siku 14 za mwisho za serikali ya Rais Hugo Chávez:

eng: With him in power a new socialism government change the face of the country, previously better known for beauty pageants and as the birthplace of Simón Bolivar, the Latin America liberator.
swa: Akiwa madarakani, serikali mpya ya kijamaa inabadilisha (ilibadilisha) uso wa nchi ambayo mwanzoni ilifahamika zaidi kama sehemu ya kihistoria nzuri na sehemu alipozaliwa mpigania uhuru wa Latini Amerika, Simón Bolivar.

eng: Social reforms were established, help to the poor increased in housing benefits and school programmes.
swa: Mabadiliko ya kijamii yalianzishwa, yaliyowasaidia watu masikini kuimarisha hali zao za kimaisha na mipango ya shule.

eng: A voice was given to the ones that never had it.
swa: Sauti za wale ambao hawakuwahi kuipata fursa hii ziliwezeshwa kusikika kwa mara ya kwanza.

eng: Copyright Eduardo Leal.
swa: Haki zote kwa Eduardo Leal.

eng: Eduardo continues explaining that, for many years, Chávez ruled with minimum opposition.
swa: Eduardo anaendelea kueleza kuwa, kwa miaka mingi,Chávez aliongoza bila kuwa na upinzani wa maana.

eng: This opposition was "usually composed by an elite class that for decades enjoyed the benefits of living in an oil-rich country," he says.
swa: Upinzani huu “mara nyingi uliundwa kwa tabaka la matajiri na wasomi ambao kwa miongo kadhaa wamekuwa wakila matunda ya kuishi katika nchi yenye hazina kubwa ya mafuta” anasema.

eng: But Eduardo also points out that, over the years, opposition to Chávez has grown as problems become more evident.
swa: Lakini pia, Eduardo anaonyesha kuwa, kwa miaka mingi, upinzani unaolekezwa kwa Chávez umeongezeka kadiri matatizo yanapoendelea kuwa dhahiri.

eng: Violence on the streets went to levels never seen, putting Caracas on the top of the list of the most dangerous cities in the world.
swa: Machafuko katika mitaa yamefikia kiwango ambacho hayakuwahi kushuhudiwa, yakiliweka jiji la Caracas katika nafasi ya juu kabisa kwa kuwa miongoni mwa majiji hatari kabisa duniani.

eng: Electricity and food shortages, raising inflation and inflammable speech’s from the President start to create new winds and opportunities to the opposition.
swa: Upungufu wa nishati ya umeme na chakula, ongezeko la bei za bidhaa na hotuba kali za Rais zinaanza kutengeneza uelekeo mpya na fursa nzuri kwa upinzani.

eng: Copyright Eduardo Leal.
swa: Haki zote kwa Eduardo Leal.

eng: Eduardo goes on to discuss the current division in Venezuelan society:
swa: Eduardo anaendelea kuujadili mgawanjiko ulioko hivi sasa miongoni mwa jamii ya Venezuela:

eng: The supporters of Chávez, known as Chavistas, in one side and on the other the opposition composed not only by the middle class and the elite as before, but also by common people that feels that the country needs a change.
swa: Wafuasi wa Chávez, wajulikanao kama Chavistas, kwa upande mmoja, na kwa upande mwingine, wale wa upinzani, sio tu unaundwa watu wa tabaka la kati na lile la juu linalojumuisha matajiri na wasomi kama ilivyokuwa awali, bali pia walalahoi wanaodhani nchi hiyo inahitaji mabadiliko.

eng: Copyright Eduardo Leal.
swa: Haki zote kwa Eduardo Leal.

eng: He refers to Henrique Capriles, Chávez's opponent, as the face of "the rise of the opposition" and "the one that for the first time can challenge President Hugo Chávez."
swa: Anachukulia mfano wa Henrique Capriles, ambaye ni mpinzani wa Chávez, kuwa ni sura ya “kukua kwa upinzani” na ambaye kwa mara ya kwanza anaweza kumpa changamoto ya kweli kweli Rais Hugo Chávez."

eng: Copyright Eduardo Leal.
swa: Haki zote kwa Eduardo Leal.

eng: With this project, Eduardo wants to "create a better understanding of what the Venezuelan people think about the changes and hopes for their country."
swa: Kwa mradi huu, Eduardo anataka "kutengeneza picha ya uelewa sawia juu ya kile ambacho watu wa Venezuela wanafikiri kuhusu mabadiliko na matuamaini yao kwa nchi yao.

eng: Visit his online gallery to see and read many more Venezuelan 'faces and voices'.
swa: Tembelea mkusanyiko wa picha zake mtandaoni na ujionee na kujisomea zaidi kuhusu ‘sura na sauti’ nyingine nyingi zaidi za Venezuela.

eng: You can also keep up with Eduardo and his work through Twitter (@Eduardoleal80), Facebook, and Tumblr.
swa: Unaweza pia kuendelea kumfuatilia kazi za Eduardo kupitia mtandao wa Twita (@Eduardoleal80), Facebook, na Tumblr.

eng: This post is part of our special coverage Venezuela Elections 2012. Note: We came across Eduardo's work through a post by Francisco Toro in the blog Caracas Chronicles.
swa: Kumbuka: Tuliweza kuifahamu kazi ya Eduardo kupitia makala ya Francisco Toro katika blogu ya Kumbukumbu ya Matukio ya Caracas ( Caracas Chronicles).

eng: This post is part of our special coverage Venezuela Elections 2012.
swa: POsti hii ni sehemu ya habari zetu maalumu za Uchaguzi wa Venezuela 2012.

eng: Emotions ran high on Sunday night after the official results of the October 7, 2012, presidential elections were released.
swa: Palikuwa na msimuko mkubwa siku ya Jumapili baada ya kutangazwa kwa matokeo rasmi yauchaguzi wa Rais tarehe 7 Oktoba, 2012.

eng: President Hugo Chávez was re-elected with 55.14% of the vote, while opposition candidate, Henrique Capriles, obtained 44.24%, as reported by Venezuela's National Electoral Council .
swa: Rais Hugo Chávez alichaguliwa kwa mara nyingine kwa asilimia 55.14 ya kura, wakati mgombea wa upinzani,Henrique Capriles, akipata asilimia 44.24, kwa mujibu wa Baraza la Uchaguzi la Nchi hiyo.

eng: Part of the country celebrated the continuation of the 'Bolivarian Revolution' under Chávez, while the other side lamented another electoral loss.
swa: Sehemu ya nchi hiyo ilisherehekea mwendelezo wa Mapinduzi ya Bolivia" chini ya Chávez, wakati upande mwingine ukilalamikia kupoteza uchaguzi kwa mara nyingine.

eng: Chávez supporters reflect
swa: Wafuasi wa Chávez wakitathmini

eng: Tamara Pearson in Venezuelan Analysis refers to Sunday's results as "an imperfect victory."
swa: Tamara Pearson katika blogu ya Venezuelan Analysis anayarejea matokeo hayo ya Jumapili kama "ushindi usiokamilika".

eng: She writes that despite the celebratory mood among Chávez supporters on Sunday night, she felt "a bit down":
swa: Anaandika kwmaba pamoja na hisia za kusherehekea ushindi walizonazo wafuasi wa Chavez usiku wa Jumapili, alionekana "mnyonge kidogo":

eng: because over six million people supported, by voting for Capriles, selfishness (he had focused his campaign on Venezuela ending its solidarity with other countries) and the destruction and sale of their country.
swa: kwa sababu zaidi ya watu milioni sita walimwunga mkono, kwa kumpigia kura Capriles, ubinafsi (alielekeza kampeni zake kwa kuitaka nchi hiyo kuachana na ushirikiano na nchi nyingine) na uharibifu na kuuzwa kwa nchi yao.

eng: She goes on to analyze why the gap between the opposition and Chávez is narrowing.
swa: Anaendelea zaidi kwa kuchambua kwa nini tofauti ya kura kati ya upizani na Chavez inaendelea kupungua.

eng: From her perspective, "the opposition will come out of these elections emboldened" so "the revolution can't lie down and relax":
swa: Kwa mtazamo wake, "upinzani umetoka kwenye uchaguzi huu ukiwa na nguvu mpya" kwa hiyo "mapinduzi hayatabaki bila tahayari":

eng: If we don’t beat corruption and bureaucracy in the next period, we could lose this revolution.
swa: Kama hatutaushinda ufisadi na urasimu katika kipindi kijacho, tunaweza kuyapoteza mapinduzi haya.

eng: Now that the presidential elections are over, we have two main questions: How will we deepen the revolution, and will it survive?
swa: Sasa wakati uchaguzi wa Rais umemalizika, tunayo maswali mawili makubwa: Tutaimarishaje mapinduzi, na je yataendelea kuwepo?

eng: Supporters of President Hugo Chavez during the presidential elections on October 7, 2012.
swa: Wafuasi wa Rais Hugo Chavez wakati uchaguzi wa rais tarehe 7 Oktoba, 2012.

eng: Photo by Alejandro Rustom.
swa: Picha ya Alejandro Rustom.

eng: Antonio Aponte, from the blog Un Grano de Maíz , congratulates fellow Chávez supporters for the victory, but also looks at future challenges for the Bolivarian Revolution.
swa: Antonio Aponte, wa blogu ya Un Grano de Maíz , anawapongeza wafuasi wenzake wa Chávez kwa ushindi huo, lakini vile vile anatazama changamoto za mbeleni zinazoyakabili Mapinduzi ya Venezuela.

eng: He also analyzes the narrowing distance between government supporters and the opposition:
swa: Anachambua pia kupungua kwa tofauti ya kura baina ya wafuasi wa serikali na wale wa upinzani:

eng: from a 26% difference in the presidential election of 2006 we have moved to a weak 10%.
swa: kutoka tofauti ya asilimia 26 katika uchaguzi wa rais wa mwaka 2006 sasa tumefikia katika tofauti ndogo ya asilimia 10.

eng: We lost almost 20% of our votes.
swa: Tumepoteza takribani asilimia 20 ya kura zetu.

eng: Preliminary analysis indicates that we lost in low-income sectors and didn't gain votes from middle class sectors.
swa: Uchambuzi wa awali unaonyesha kwamba tumepoteza katika sekta za watu wenye kipato kidogo na wala hatukujiongozea kura kutoka katika sekta za tabaka la kati.

eng: Why the decline?
swa: Kwa nini kura zimepungua?

eng: The answer lies in the essence of socialism, without understanding it we are destined to fail: Socialism is the essence of love, of fraternal relationships, of the sense of belonging to society.
swa: Jawabu liko kwenye umuhimu wa ujamaa, bila kuuelewa sisi ni wa kushindwa: Ujamaa ni msingi wa upendo, mahusiano ya kindugu, hisia za kuwa sehemu ya jamii.

eng: Capitalism has as its essence selfishness, individual solutions.
swa: Ubepari msingi wake ni ubinafsi, majawabu binafsi.

eng: That is the foundation of the battle, selfishness in a fierce fight against love, and that is where our efforts must be directed.
swa: Huo ndio msingi wa mapigano, ubinafsi katika mapigano dhidi ya upendo, na kwamba hapo ndipo juhudi zatu zapaswa kuelekezwa.

eng: He concludes that 'revolutionaries' must urgently acquire a 'culture of discussion': "A revolution that doesn't discuss, dies":
swa: Anahitimisha kwamba "wanamapinduzi" lazima wajijengee 'utamaduni wa mijadala': "Mapinduzi ambayo hayajadili, hufa":

eng: Study, discussion, must be the main tasks of society.
swa: Kusoma, kujadili, lazima viwe ndiyo majumu makuu ya jamii.

eng: Ignorance is counterrevolutionary.
swa: Ujinga ni kizuizi cha mapinduzi.

eng: ¡Long live Chávez!
swa: Uishi maisha marefu Chávez!

eng: Reflections from the opposition
swa: Tathmini za wapinzani

eng: Many opposition bloggers followed Capriles' campaign closely, with enthusiasm for what seemed to be the right moment for a change in Venezuela.
swa: Wanablogu wengi wa upinzani walifuatilia kwa karibu kampeni za Capriles, kwa hamasa ya kile kilichoonekana kuwa wakati muafaka wa mabadiliko nchini Venezuela.

eng: They quickly reacted to the results, sharing their sadness and disappointment, but also looking forward with self-criticism.
swa: Waliotoa maoni yao pindi tu matokeo yalipotangwa, wakiambizana namna wanavyojisikia huzuni na fadhaa, lakini vilevile wakitazama mbele kwa jicho la kujikosoa.

eng: Blogger Alex Boyd says he "never expected a different outcome".
swa: Mwanablogu Alex Boyd anasema "hajawahi kutegemea matokeo tofauti".

eng: He shares a map of the results and adds a note about electoral fraud:
swa: Anaweka ramani ya matokeo na kuongeza dokezo la wizi wa kura:

eng: Hugo Chavez trounced the opposition candidate again.
swa: Hugo Chavez amemwangusha mgombea wa upinzani kwa mara nyingine.

eng: Six years on, Chavez still is the choice of the majority of my countrymen.
swa: Miaka sita sasa, Chavez bado ni chaguo la raia walio wengi.

eng: And that's OK, I don't have a problem with that.
swa: Na hiyo ni sawa, sina tatizo na hilo.

eng: The good thing about it is that Henrique Capriles, Leopoldo Lopez, Ramon Guillermo Aveledo et al buried the phantom of electoral fraud in Venezuela.
swa: Uzuri wa hayo ni kwamba Henrique Capriles, Leopoldo Lopez, Ramon Guillermo Aveledo na wengine walilizika jinamizi la wizi wa kura nchini Venezuela.

eng: By claiming, repeatedly, that the system had been sufficiently audited, and that the opposition had managed to place witnesses in 100% of voting centres nationwide, there is no room for further entertaining the thought of fraud.
swa: Kwa kudai, mara kwa mara, kwamba mfumo ulikuwa umekaguliwa vya kutosha, na kwamba upinzani umeweza kuweka waangalizi katika asilimia 100 ya vituo vya upigaji kura, hakuna ten nafasi ya kuendekeza wazo la wizi wa kura.

eng: Manuel Silva from the blog No solo con la palabra thinks that one of the worst things the opposition has done throughout multiple electoral processes is not being prepared for a defeat.
swa: Manuel Silva wa blogu ya No solo con la palabra anadhani moja ya mambo mabaya kabisa ambayo upinzani umeyafanya katika michakato ya chaguzi hizi ni kutokuwa na maandalizi ya kushindwa.

eng: However, Silva argues that the opposition's loss is not a political loss:
swa: Hata hivyo, Silva anahoji kwamba kushindwa kwa upinzani si kushindwa kwa siasa:

eng: Here we lost because the majority of Venezuelans identify with this form of government .
swa: Hapa tumeshindwa kwa sababu wengi wa wa-Venezuela wanajitambulisha kwa serikali ya namna hii .

eng: We are willing to accept abuse and trampling as a way of life, we have made insecurity something natural, we have settled for misery, we have accepted gladly to live as we have done in recent years: hating each other.
swa: Tuko tayari kukubali kutukanwa na kufanyiwa dhihaka kama sehemu ya maisha, tumefanya kutokuwa na usalama kuwa kitu cha kawaida, tumeridhika na ufukara, tumekubali kuishi kwa furaha kama tulivyofanya katika miaka ya hivi karibuni: tukichukiana.

eng: Two young men, members of the indigenous Mapuche community from Southern Chile, were sentenced on August 13, 2012, to 541 days of prison for their responsibility in an attack against police officers during a clash on November 2, 2011, in the rural sector of the Ercilla commune.
swa: Vijana wawili wanaume, wazawa wa jamii ya Mapuche kutoka Chile ya Kusini, mnamo tarehe 13 Agusti, 2012 walihukumiwa siku 541 za kukaa gerezani kufuatia kuhusika na shambulio dhidi ya polisi katika machafuko yaliyotokea tarehe 2 Novemba, 2012 katika sehemu ya vijijini ya jamii ya Ercilla .

eng: Nineteen-year-old Paulino Levipán and eighteen-year-old Daniel Levinao started a hunger strike on August 27, 2012, along with Rodrigo Montoya Melinao and Eric Montoya Montoya to protest their detention.
swa: Paulino Levipán mwenye umri wa miaka 19 na Daniel Levinao mwenye umri wa miaka 18 walianzisha mgomo wa kutokula mnamo tarehe 27, wakishirikiana na Rodrigo Montoya Melinao na Eric Montoya Montoya ili kupinga kukamatwa kwao.

eng: The latter were accused of attempted murder of a policeman that was guarding ranch Centenario, in the same Ercilla community, on August 2011.
swa: Waliotangulia kutajwa walituhumiwa kwa kumuua polisi aliyekuwa aliyekuwa doria katika shamba la wanyama lijulikanalo kama Centenario katika eneo la jumuia hiyo ya Ercilla mapema mwezi Augusti 2011.

eng: They were still being processed in an oral trial.
swa: Watu hawa wamekuwa wakihojiwa mara kwa mara.

eng: Yesterday, October 25, the four mapuche prisoners decided to abandon their protest after the Chilean Supreme Court decided to comply with some of their demands.
swa: Jana, Oktoba 25, wafungwa wanne wa gereza la mapuche waliamua kusitisha kususia kula mara baada ya Mahakama Kuu ya Chile kukubaliana na baadhi ya matakwa yao.

eng: They are already at the prison's nurse station receiving food.
swa: Tayari wapo katika kituo cha matunzo cha gereza hilo wakipata mlo.

eng: Mapuche stencil, photo by Flickr user Paul Lowry (CC BY-NC-ND 2.0)

eng: The maximum Chilean court ruled to partially annul the trial that convicted them.
swa: Mahakama kuu ya Chile ilisimamia katika kuharakisha uchunguzi uliopelekea hukumu yao.

eng: In Daniel's case, a new trial was ordered because the first one lacked enough proof to reach a sentence. As for Paulino, the court changed his accusation to injuries based on "evident mistakes in the application of the law", therefore his sentence changed from 10 years in prison to 3 years in parole.
swa: Katika shauri laDaniel, uchunguzi mwingine uliagizwa kufanyika kwa kuwa ule wa kwanza ulikosa ushahidi wa kutosha ili kukamilisha hukumu.a. kama ilivyo kwa Paulino, mahakama ilibadilisha shitaka lake na kulifanya kuwa ni la kujeruhi kwa kuzingatia “makosa ya kiushahidi katika matumizi ya sheria”, hivyo hukumu yake ikabadilishwa kutoka miaka 10 gerezani hadi kifungo cha nje ya gereza kwa miaka 3.

swa: Umoja wa Mataifa umetangaza kuisherehekea tarehe 10 Novemba (Jumamosi) kama Siku ya Malala.

eng: People around the world celebrated Malala as a beacon for 32 million girls who can not go to school.
swa: Watu kote ulimwenguni walimshangilia Malala kama kielelezo cha wasichana wapato milioni 32 ambao hawana fursa ya kupata elimu.

eng: This day was celebrated in more than 100 countries across the globe.

eng: But in Malala's hometown open house events couldn't be organized out of fear of possible terrorist attacks.
