eng: The June 2012 riots in western Myanmar involving Rohingyas and Rakhine prompted several international Islamic organizations and countries to extend their offer of assistance to resolve the conflict and deliver aid to victims.
swa: Machafuko ya Juni 2012 huko magharibi mwa Myanmar yanayowahusisha Rohingya na Rakhine yaligusa mashirika ya kimataifa ya Kiislamu pamoja na nchi mbalimbali katika kujitolea kusaidia kutatua mgogoro huu pamoja na kutoa misaada kwa wahanga.

eng: The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), for instance, has proposed the establishment of a permanent office in Myanmar.
swa: Shirika la Ushirikiano wa Kiislam (OIC), kwa mfano, limependekeza kuanzishwa kwa ofisi yake ya kudumu nchini Myanmar.

eng: This initiative sparked phenomenal opposition across the country, especially in Yangon, Mandalay, Pakkoku, Sittwe and Phyar Pone. Online comments are also almost unanimous in opposing an OIC presence in the country.
swa: Hatua hii iliibua hali ya kupingwa nchini kote, haswa haswa huko Yangon, Mandalay, Pakkoku, Sittwe na Phyar Pone. maoni ya mtandaoni pia yanaonesha msimamo mmoja wa kupinga uwepo wa OIC nchini Myanmar.

eng: Many people in Myanmar believe that an OIC office is not necessary to help the Muslim minority in Myanmar.
swa: Watu wengi wa Myanmar wanaamini kuwa Shirika la Ushirikiano wa Kiislam (OIC) halina ulazima wa kuwepo ili iwasaidie waislam wachache nchini Myanmar.

eng: Dr. Aye Maung, a member of parliament and the president of the Rakhine Nationalities Development Party has argued that aid and donation can be delivered without setting up an OIC office in the country:
swa: Daktari Aye Maung ambaye ni mbunge na Rais wa chama cha Rakhine Nationalities Development alihoji kuwa utoaji wa misaada unaweza kufanyika bila ya kuweka Ofisi ya OIC nchini:

eng: OIC is mainly for religion purposes, an organisation with 57 countries which are cooperating with Islamic countries.
swa: Shirika la Ushirikiano wa Kiislam (OIC) ni mahususi kwa dini, shirika linalojumuisha nchi 57 zilizo na ushirika na nchi za kiislam.

eng: It's unlike ASEAN which is a regional and multi-religious association nor European Union. And therefore we can and should receive the donations through the government without opening an OIC office.
swa: Sio kama ASEAN ambayo ipo kikanda na yenye kujumuisha dini mbalimbali na wala siyo Umoja wa Ulaya. na hivyo tunaweza na tulipaswa kupokea misaada kupitia serikali bila ya kufungua ofisi ya OIC.

eng: Myo Set advised the OIC to communicate directly with other UN bodies and NGOs if they found the government machinery unreliable:
swa: Myo Set aliishauri Shirika la Ushirikiano wa Kiislam (OIC) kuwasiliana moja kwa moja na mashirika mengine ya Umoja wa Mataifa na mashirika mengine ya binafsi kama wameona kuwa kupitia serikalini sio njia muafaka:

eng: Burma has full cooperation with NGOs and UN which is why no more political coalition is needed if OIC's pure intention is to provide only food, shelter, health care service and security for Muslims.
swa: Burma ina ushirikiano mzuri na mashirika binafsi pamoja na Umoja wa mataifa na ndio sababu hakuna haja ya siasa za mseto kama lengo kuu la OIC ni kusaidia tu chakula, malazi, huduma za afya na ulinzi kwa Waislamu.

eng: Whatever they wish to supply can go through the UN if Burmese authorities are not reliable.
swa: Chochote watakachohitaji kukitoa kinaweza kupitia Umoja wa Mataifa kama wameona mamlaka za Barma si njia muafaka.

eng: Ko Htike wrote with the view that the riot was not a religious clash, thereby asserting that the OIC should not shape the situation to be one.
swa: Ko Htike aliandika akiwa na mtazamo kuwa fujo hazikutokana na vurugu za kidini, hivyo hali inajieleza wazi kuwa OIC haipaswi kubadili hali kuwa la uelekeo mmoja.

eng: The Rohingya issue is neither a religious clash nor ethnic clash.
swa: Jambo hili la Rohingya si mzozo wa kidini wala wa kikabila.

eng: It's just a problem between illegal immigrants and locals.
swa: Ni tatizo tu kati ya wahamiaji na wazawa.

eng: It is such an ordinary problem which usually occur in many countries across the world.
swa: Ni jambo la kawaida kabisa ambalo mara nyingi hutokea katika nchi mbalimbali duniani.

eng: Nothing more.
swa: Siyo zaidi ya hapo.

eng: I think OIC should not shape the situation to be a religious issue.
swa: Nadhani OIC isilifanye jambo hili kuwa la kidini.

eng: I respect the kindness to provide humanitarian aid.
swa: Ninaheshimu ukarimu wao wa kutoa misaada ya kibinadamu.

eng: If the intent is for humanitarian reason, other states and regions in Myanmar should be given assistance as well just like what other countries (e.g. Japan, US) are doing.
swa: Kama lengo ni misaada ya kibinadamu, basin a majimbo na mikoa mingine inapaswa pia ipewe misaada kama tu jinsi nchi nyingine (mfano. Japani, Amerika) wanavyofanya.

eng: Ko Htike echoed the popular domestic opinion in Myanmar, opposing the Rohingya's struggle for recognition as an ethnic minority in the country.
swa: Ko Htike anakumbushia maoni yaliyozoeleka yanayozungumzwa nchini Myanmar, yanayopinga juhudi za Rohingya ya kutambua kama yechoed the popular domestic opinion in Myanmar, opposing the Rohingya's struggle for recognition as an ethnic minority in the country.

eng: Opinion on the Rohingyas is divided; the global community consider them as among the most persecuted minorities in Asia.
swa: Maonin kuhusiana na Rohingyas yamegawanyika; jamii za kimataifathe zinawachukulia wao kama kikundi kidogo mno kinachodharauliwa sana barani Asia.

eng: For several weeks, there has been talk of a Memorandum of Understanding signed between the OIC and Myanmar's Ministry of Border Affairs, though there is little information about whether the agreement actually exists, and if so, what it comprises.
swa: Kwa wiki kadhaa kumekuwa na fununu kuhusu uwepo wa Hati ya Makubaliano iliyotiwa saini kati ya Shirika la Ushirikiano wa Kiislam (OIC) na Wizara inayoshughulika na mambo ya Mipaka ya Myanmar pamoja na kuwa kuna taarifa zisizo za kina sana kama kweli makubaliano hayo yapo, na kama ndivyo, inajumuisha mambo gani.

eng: When people started posting comments opposing the agreement, Hmuu Zaw from the president's office clarified that the OIC office would only be a temporary liaison office rather than an official representative office.
swa: Walipoanza kutuma maoni yao wakipinga makubaliano hayo, Hmuu Zaw kutoka ofisi ya Rais alifafanua kuwa, ofisi ya Oic itakuwa ni ya dharura tu itakayofanya kazi kama ofisi ya uwakilishi ya dharura na si kama ofisi ya kudumu ya uwakilishi.

eng: This explanation didn't convince many.
swa: Ufafanuzi huu haukuwashawishi watu wengi.

eng: Tyfone Athene questioned the possible duration of the temporary office:
swa: Tyfone Athene alihoji muda halisi wa uwepo wa ofisi hii ya dharura:

eng: Temporary liaison office? how long will it take? 60 or unlimited years?
swa: Ofisi ya uwakili ya dharura? Itachukua muda gani? Miaka 60 au miaka isiyo na kikomo?

eng: Poe Pwint Phyu thinks that if the government regarded the original incident a non-sectarian clash, then the agreement with the OIC should not have been signed:
swa: Poe Pwint Phyu anafikiri kuwa kama serikali ililitazama tukio la awali kuwa halikuwa la kidini, basi serikali isingepitisha makubaliano na OIC:

eng: Photo - CJ Myanmar Facebook Page
swa: Picha- CJ Ukurasa wa Facebook wa Myanmar

eng: My last question to Mr. President's advisers: Do you see this recent conflict as merely a religious riot (thus you allowed a temporary office for OIC) or urgent issue of neglect and violence which victimized Rakhine natives?
swa: swali langu la mwisho kwa washauri wa Mheshimiwa Rais: mnafikiri mgogoro wa hivi karibuni kuwa umesababishwa na vurugu za kidini ( na hivyo mkaruhusu ofisi ya dharura ya OIC)Do you see this recent conflict as merely a religious riot (thus you allowed a temporary office for OIC) au ni jambo muhimu la kutelekeza na uonevu lililowaacha wazawa wa Rakhine kuwa wahanga? or urgent issue of neglect and violence which victimized Rakhine natives?

eng: Others criticized the lack of transparency on procedures of government ministries.
swa: Wengine walikosoa kukosekana kwa uwazi kwa yale yanayofanywa na wizara za serikali.

eng: Ah Moe made this request :
swa: Ah Moe alitoa pendekezo lake:

eng: Be it a temporary liaison office or permanent branch office, what we are asking for now is to show a copy of that MOU to public, that's what we want mainly.
swa: Iwe ni ofisi ya uwakilishi ya dharura au ni tawi la ofisi ya kudumu, tunachokiomba kwa sasa ni kuwa ni kuiweka wazi nakala ya hati ya makubaliano, hilo ndilo haswa tunalolihitaji.

eng: The government attempted to dissuade people from joining the protests against the setting up of an OIC office; despite this, they were held October 15 in several cities across the country.
swa: Serekali ilijaribu kuwashawishi watu wasijihusishe na maandamano ya kupinga kuanzishwa kwa ofisi ya OIC; pamoja na ushawishi huu, maandamano yalifanyika Oktoba 15 katika majiji kadhaa nchini kote.

eng: Bowing to public pressure, the president's office announced on the same day that the government would not permit the setting up of an OIC liaison office in Myanmar.
swa: Kwa kuhofia msukumo wa watu, ofisi ya Rais ilitangaza siku hiyo hiyo kuwa serikali isingeruhusu kuanzishwa kwa ofisi ya uwakilishi ya dharura OIC nchini Myanmar.

eng: However, it didn't mention the content of the controversial MOU.
swa: Hata hivyo, haikutaja yaliyomo kwenye hati ya makubaliano iliyosababisha mkanganyiko.

eng: It was not clear if the government had informed the OIC of this decision.
swa: Haikueleweka wazi kama serikali ilishaitaarifu OIC kufuatia maamuzi haya.

eng: The government has assured the public that it would continue to accept humanitarian aid by coordinating closely with OIC and other international groups.
swa: Serikali imeihakikishia umma kuwa itaendelea kupokea misaada ya kibinadamu kwa ushirikiano wa karibu na OIC na makundi mengine ya kimataifa.

eng: Meanwhile, the OIC said they have yet to receive a formal notification from Myanmar government regarding a decision to disallow a liaison office.
swa: Wakati huohuo, OIC wanasema kuwa bado hawajapokea taarifa rasmi kutoka serikali ya Myanmar kufuatia maamuzi yaliyofikiwa ya kutoruhusu kuwepo kwa ofisi ya uwakilishi ya OIC.

eng: In related news, the Myanmar Red Cross Society issued a press release denying rumors that it is sponsoring a hidden OIC office inside its building.
swa: Katika habari zinazohusiana na hizi, Jumuia ya Msalaba Mwekundu ya Myanmar ilitoa tamko kupitia kwa waandishi wa habari ikikanusha uvumi kuwa inafadhili ofisi ya OIC iliyoanzishwa kinyemela katika jingo lao.

eng: This post is part of our special coverage Myanmar's Rohingya.
swa: Makala hii ni sehemu ya habari zetu maalum Rohingya ya Myanmar .

eng: After causing wide spread damage along the Atlantic Coast in United States, Super storm sandy is being labelled as the costliest storm ever.
swa: Baada ya kusababisha uharibifu mkubwa pembezoni mwa pwani ya atlantiki nchini Marekani, Kimbunga kikubwa sandy kinachukuliwa kama kimbunga kilichosababisha madhara makubwa ambayo hayakuwahi kutokea.

eng: With estimates running as high as $45 billion for reconstruction and rebuilding, the country prepares to cope with the losses.
swa: Kiasi cha fedha kinachokadiriwa kufikia dola za kimarekani milioni 45 zinahitajika ili kurekebisha na kujenga upya makazi na miundombinu, ambapo nchi inajiandaa kukabiliana na hasara hiyo.

eng: At least 33 people have been reported dead and scores displaced across the East Coast.
swa: Watu wasiopungua 33 inaelezwa kuwa wamepoteza maisha na idadi kubwa ya watu wameachwa bila makazi katika maeneo mbalimbali ya pwani ya Mashariki.

eng: Amidst the furor, Hafiz Mohammad Saeed, the founder of banned militant organization Lashkar e Taiba (LeT) and head of Jaamat ud Dawa (JuD) offered a considerable amount of humanitarian aid to the US to bear losses.
swa: Huku kimbunga hiki kikiendelea kuleta madhara, Hafiz Mohammad Saeed, mwanzilishi wa kundi la kijeshi lililofutwa, Lashkar e Taiba (LeT) na kiongozi wa Jaamat ud Dawa (JuD) alitoa msaada wa kibinadamu kwa nchi ya Marekani ili kuisaidia kufuatia uharibifu uliotokea.

eng: Hurricane Sandy wreaked havoc on the Rockaways and Breezy Point in Queens.
swa: Kimbunga Sandy kilichosababisha uharibifu mkubwa ulioenea sehemu za mwambao na pwani ya Queens.

eng: Many lost their homes, businesses and possessions.
swa: Wengi wamepoteza makazi yao, biashara na mali zao.

eng: Image by Kevin Downs.
swa: Picha na Kevin Downs.

eng: Pledging help of every kind, he said "Jamaat-ud-Dawa is ready to send its volunteers, doctors, food, medicines and other relief items on humanitarian grounds if the US government allows us.”
swa: Akiahidi kusaidia kwa hali na mali misaada ya kila aina, alisema, "Jamaat-ud-Dawa iko tayari kutuma watu wa kujitolea, madaktari, vyakula, madawa na vitu vingine vya kuwasaidia wahanga endapo serikali ya Marekani itaturuhusu”.

eng: Known as the mastermind behind the 2008 Mumbai attacks, the JuD founder also carries a $10million US bounty on his head.
swa: Akijulikana kama muongozaji mkuu wa mashambulizi ya Mumbai ya mwaka 2008, mwanzilishi wa JuD pia alitoa msaada wa dola milioni 10 za kimarekani .

eng: The American Embassy in Pakistani capital Islamabad however refused to accept help from Saeed.
swa: Hata hivyo, ubalozi wa Marekani katika mji mkuu wa Islamabad nchini Pakistani umekataa kupokea msaada kutoka kwa Saeed.

eng: Using their Twitter account, the embassy made it clear that while they appreciate the gesture of Muslims to help, they clearly did not take his offer seriously.
swa: Wakitumia ukurasa wao wa Twita, ubalozi huo umeweka bayana kuwa pamoja na kuwa wanathamini kitendo cha waislamu kutoa misaada, hawakutilia maanani kabisa msaada wa ndugu Saeed.

eng: @usembislamabad (US Embassy Islamabad): We respect the Islamic tradition of help to the needy, but we can’t take Hafiz Saeed’s offer seriously.
swa: @usembislamabad (Ubalozi wa Marekani Islamabad): Tunaheshimu utamaduni wa Waislamu wa kutoa misaada kwa wahitaji, lakini hatuwezi kutilia mkazo msaada wa Hafiz Saeed.

eng: Following the tweet, a spokesperson for JuD posted the following replies:
swa: Kufuatia maelezo hayo katika Twita, msemaji wa JuD alijibu kama ifuatavyo:

eng: @JuD_Official (Jamat 'ud' Da'wah): @usembislamabad Our offer was precisely due to the seriousness of the matter.
swa: @JuD_Official (Jamat 'ud' Da'wah): @usembislamabad Tulitoa msaada wetu wa dhati kutokana na hali halisi ya janga.

eng: We hope Muslims in #US will keep the tradition alive.
swa: Ni matarajio yetu kuwa Waislamu wanaoishi Marekani watauendeleza utamaduni huu.

eng: Inshallah
swa: Inshallah

eng: @JuD_Official (Jamat 'ud' Da'wah) @usembislamabad Our Help offer is for the American people, we will engage Muslims in US to be at forefront to help their fellow countrymen.
swa: @JuD_Official (Jamat 'ud' Da'wah) @usembislamabad Msaada wetu ni kwa ajili ya watu wa Marekani, tutawahusisha Waislamu wa Marekani kuwa mstari wa mbele katika kuwasaidia ndugu zao.

eng: The US embassy went as far as calling Saeed a suspect for his involvement in Mumbai attacks and also labelling his organization JuD as a ‘designated terrorist’ organization.
swa: Ubalozi wa Marekani ulienda mbali pale walipomuhusisha Saeed na tuhuma za kujihusisha na mashambulizi ya Mumbai na pia kuliita shirika lake JuD kuwa ni shirika lililo na mrengo wa kigaidi.

eng: @usembislamabad (US Embassy Islamabad ‏): Saaed is wanted for suspected involvement in the Mumbai attacks, which killed 166.
swa: @usembislamabad (US Embassy Islamabad ‏): Saaed anatafutwa kuhusishwa na mashambulizi ya Mumbai yaliyopelekea watu 166 kuuawa.

eng: The Twitter account for JuD was once more ready with a response.
swa: Ukurasa wa Twita wa JuD ulikuwa tayari kutoa majibu.

eng: @JuD_Official (Jamat 'ud' Da'wah): @usembislamabad US govt has conceded to the fact of inadmissible evidence against Hafiz Saeed.
swa: @JuD_Official (Jamat 'ud' Da'wah): @usembislamabad Serikali ya Marekani imekubali ukweli ambao haukudhibitishwa kuwa ni sahihi ndidi ya Hafiz Saeed.

eng: UNSCR hearing is pending.
swa: Kauli ya UNSCR bado inasubiriwa.

eng: Leaves nothing behind.
swa: Hakuna kinachoachwa.

eng: Reactions over this offer remain mixed.
swa: Maoni kuhusiana na msaada huu bado yanakanganya.

eng: While many term it as generous, some also see the irony behind it. @Rifaqat_Mir (Rifaqat A. Mir): In spite of the enmity the US poses to Hafiz Saeed he still has the generosity and benevolence to show compassion for his enemy
swa: @Rifaqat_Mir (Rifaqat A. Mir): pamoja na uadui unaowekwa na Marekani kwa Hafiz Saeed, bado ana nia ya dhati ya kutoa misaada katika kuendelea kuonesha kumjali adui yake.

eng: @humayusuf (Huma Yusuf): They say Muslims don't have a sense of humour, but Hafiz Saeed's offer to help #Sandy victims is HILARIOUS http://www.thenews.com.pk/Todays-News-13-18499-Hafiz-Saeed-offers-humanitarian-aid-to-US … @anDYRude (Anirudh Malladi): Just read that Hafiz Saeed, a dreaded terrorist, has offered "Help in the form of food, doctors etc" to victims of #HurricaneSandy.
swa: @anDYRude (Anirudh Malladi): Punde tu nimesoma kuwa, Hafiz Saeed, gaidi aliyeogopeka, amejitolea"kutoa msaada wa vyakula, madaktari, n.k " kwa wahanga wa kimbunga cha sandy.

eng: LMAO!
swa: LMAO!

swa: @nidak_ (Nida Khan): Kuvumilia jumbe za kashfa zinazoendelea kati ya Hafiz Saeed na ubalozi wa Marekani mjini Islamabad ni 1-1, ningeweza kusema. #Mzunguko unaofuata?

eng: @anamzehra86 (Anam Zehra): US Embassy's response to Hafiz Saeed's offer is their way of saying "we take your religion seriously,you should too"
swa: @anamzehra86 (Anam Zehra): Majibu ya Ubalozi wa Marekani kufuatia kujitolea kwa Hafiz Saeed ni namna yao ya kutaka kusema kuwa, "tunachukulia dini yako kwa uzito mkubwa sana, nawe ungalipaswa pia kufanya hivyo"

eng: Syrian photographers from around the country are revealing, sharing, and archiving Syria's uprising through photographs which showcase destruction.
swa: Wapiga picha wa Syria kutoka katika maeneo mbalimbali ya nchi wanafichua, kutuma sehemu mbalimbali na kuweka kumbukumbu ya machafuko katika picha zinazoonesha uharibifu uliotokea.

eng: Despite the limited media sources, what comes out from Syria shows the horrific reality Syrians on the ground face as they see their country being literally torn apart.
swa: Pamoja na ufinyu wa vitendea kazi vya utoaji habari, habari zinazotoka Syria zinaonesha hali ya kutisha inayowakabili wananchi wa tabaka la chini kabisa na huku wakishuhudia nchi yao inavyoraruliwa na kuachwa vipande vipande.

eng: Although there is no liable resources to confirm the locations of the photographs nor the number of victims, the next few pictures are just a sample to consider of how Syria's infrastructure and residential areas have been affected.
swa: Pamoja na kuwa hakuna nyenzo za kuweza kuonesha picha hizo zinapatikana wapi wala idadi ya wahanga, zifuatazo ni baadhi ya picha chache zinazoonesha namna miundo mbinu na makazi ya watu yalivyo athiriwa.

eng: If you are stuck for a few minutes at a traffic signal in the Bangladesh capital Dhaka, you will probably see children rushing up to the windows of your vehicle.
swa: Pale inapotokea umekwama kwa dakika chake katika taa za barabarani katika mji mkuu wa Bangladeshi Dhaka, bila shaka utaona watoto wakijazana kwenye madirisha ya gari lako.

eng: Some of these children carry flowers; some have a stack of books in the crook of their arms, some carry bundles of newspapers and some have candy for sale.
swa: Miongoni mwao kuna wale watakaokuwa wamebeba maua; wengine marundo ya vitabu, wengine magazeti na hata wapo wale wanaouza pipi.

eng: They try their best to earn sympathy from commuters to sell their goods.
swa: Wote wanafanya kila linalowezekana kuwavutia wasafiri barabarani ili wauze bidhaa zao.

eng: This painful scene is ubiquitous on the streets of Dhaka.
swa: Sura hii ya kuhuzunisha inatawala mitaa mingi ya jiji la Dhaka.

eng: These street children are known as Pothoshishu.
swa: Katika jiji hili watoto hao hujulikana kwa jina la Pothoshishu.

eng: The street is where they earn their living.
swa: Ni huko mitaani ndiko wanakojipatia riziki.

eng: The total number of street children in Bangladesh is estimated at 400,000.
swa: Jumla ya watoto hao wa mitaani nchini Bangladeshi inakadiriwa kuwa laki nne (karibu nusu milioni).

eng: Almost half of these children live in Dhaka city alone.
swa: Karibu nusu ya idadi hiyo wanaishi katika jiji la Dhaka peke yake.

eng: A very large percentage of these children are young girls.
swa: Miongoni mwao, walio wengi ni wasichana.

eng: These female street children are especially vulnerable to abuse and exploitation.
swa: Watoto hawa wa kike wanakabiliwa na unyanyasaji na vitendo vingine vya dhuluma dhidi yao.

eng: Street girls Mili and Brishti earn their living by selling flowers.
swa: Wasichana wa mitaani Mili na Brishti wanajitafutia riziki kwa kuuza maua.

swa: Hakimiliki Demotix (21/1/2012)

eng: On March, 2012 Unnayan Onneshan published a report titled “social connection of the street girls in the context of Dhaka city, Bangladesh” .
swa: Mwezi Machi, 2012 Unnayan Onneshan alichapisha ripoti iliyopewa kichwa cha habari “social connection of the street girls in the context of Dhaka city, Bangladesh” yaani 'Uhusiano wa kijamii wa wasichana wa mitaani katika muktadha wa jiji la Dhaka, Bangladeshi.

eng: The research shows that the majority of the street girls (37.50%) sell flowers for a living.
swa: Utafiti unaonyesha kwamba wengi kati ya wasichana hao wa mitaani (37.50%) hujipatia riziki kwa kuuza maua.

eng: 18.80% of these young girls are forced into prostitution, 6.25 % work in the clothing industry, 6.25% become beggars, 12.50% start as shopkeepers and 6.25% are paper-hawkers.
swa: Asilimia 18.80 kati yao hulazimishwa kujihusisha na ukahaba, asilimia 6.25 hufanya kazi katika viwanda vya nguo, asilimia 6.25 huwa ombaomba, asilimia 12.50 hufanya kazi za kuuza duka na asilimia 6.25 ni wachuuzi wa magazeti.

eng: Almost half of these girls have a measly daily income of Tk.
swa: Karibu nusu ya wasichana hawa wana kipato cha kujikimu tu kipatacho kama Tk.
101-299 (dola za Marekani 1.25 hadi 3.75, kama Tsh2,000 - Tsh5,000).

eng: The daily income of 43.75 % of the girls is Tk.
swa: Kipato cha kila siku cha asilimia 43.75 ya wasichaa ni Tk.

eng: 300 (US$3.75) and above.
swa: 300 (dola $3.75, sawa na Tsh5,000) na zaidi.

eng: But they seem to be the lucky ones, because 6.25 % of the street girls earn less than Tk.
swa: Lakini hao ni wale ambao wana bahati sana, kwa sababu asilimia 6.25 ya wasichana wa mitaani hupata chini ya Tk.
100 (dola 1.25, sawa na Sh2,000) kwa siku.

eng: Almost 45% of these girls do not receive any treatment from government medical facilities or clinics.
swa: Karibu asilimia 45 ya wasichana hawa hawapati hudma zozote za afya katika vituo vya afya vya serikali.

eng: 3 out of 10 of these girls have never been enrolled in any type of educational institution.
swa: Wasichan 3 kati ya 10 hawajawahi kupata elimu ya aina yoyote katika taasisi zinazohusika na elimu.

eng: Most women in Bangladesh are vulnerable to fall victim to abuse such as rape, murder, eve teasing, dowry and acid attacks.
swa: Wakawake wengi nchini Bangladeshi wako kwenye hatari ya kufanyiwa dhuluma kama vile ubakaji, kuuwawa, kuchezewa, mahari na hata kumwagiwa tindikali.

eng: But the street children who spend their childhood under the open skies of Dhaka face such risks on a daily basis.
swa: Lakini watoto wa mitaani wasio na makazi katika jiji la Dhaka wanakabiliana na hatari hizi kila siku.

eng: The New Patriotic Party (NPP), the strongest opposition party in Ghana has challenged the recent Presidential election results, claiming electoral fraud.
swa: Chama Kikuu cha Upinzani nchini Ghana, New Patriotic Party (NPP), kimeyapinga matokeo ya hivi karibuni ya Uchaguzi wa Rais, kikidai uchaguzi huo ulighubikwa na vitendo vya udanganyifu.

eng: Refusing to accept the results declared by the electoral commission, the NPP has decided to take the matter to the courts.
swa: Kikigoma kuyakubali matokeo yaliyotangazwa na Tume ya Uchaguzi, chama hicho kimeamua kulipeleka suala hilo katika vyombo vya sheria.

eng: According to Ghana Decides:
swa: Kwa mujibu wa blogu yaGhana Decides:

eng: The largest opposition party in Ghana, the New Patriotic Party (NPP) has challenged the results of the 2012 Presidential election, accusing the Electoral Commission of Ghana of colluding with the incumbent, National Democratic Congress (NDC) to steal votes.
swa: chama hicho kikuu cha upinzani NPP kimeyapinga matokeo ya uchaguzi wa rais mwaka 2012, kikiituhumu Tume ya uchaguzi kutumiwa na chama kilichoko madarakani, National Democratic Congress (NDC) kuiba kura.

eng: The Chairman of the Electoral Commission, Dr. Kwadwo Afari Gyan, has denied the allegations saying the the NPP can challenge the results in Ghana’s courts according to the electoral laws of the country.
swa: Mwenyekiti wa Tume ya Uchaguzi, Dr. Kwadwo Afari Gyan, amekanusha madai hayo akisema kwamba chama cha NPP wanayo haki ya kupinga matokeo hayo katika mahakama za Ghana kwa mujibu wa sheria za uchaguzi za nchi hiyo.

eng: The Chairman of the Electoral Commission, Dr. Kwadwo Afari Gyan, declared President Mahama winner by 50.70% of the votes, beating his main challenger Nana Akufo-Addo of the NPP who polled 47.7% of the votes.
swa: Mwenyekiti wa Tume ya Uchaguzi, Dr. Kwadwo Afari Gyan, alimtangaza Rais Mahama kuwa mshindi kwa kujipatia asimilia 50.7 ya kura, akimshinda mpinzani wake wa karibu Nana Akufo-Addo wa chama cha NPP aliyepata asimilia 47.7 ya kura.

eng: NPP's projected the results online.
swa: Ubashiri wa matokeo uliofanywa na chama cha NPP.

eng: NPP's projection on their Facebook page showed that they have won the elections according to the results they received from their polling agents.
swa: Ubashiri wa NPP katika ukurasa wao wa Facebook ulioneysha kwamba wameshinda uchaguzi huo kwa mujibu wa matokeo waliyoyapokea kutoka kwa mawakala wao wa uchaguzi.

eng: Party gurus of the NPP have been holding a crunch meeting over the matter whether to consider a court action.

eng: Ghana Decides reports:

eng: Following this, the NPP has resolved to take the issue to court and has vowed to use all available legal means to seek justice.

eng: Meanwhile, numerous supporters of the NPP have poured onto the streets of Circle, ostensibly to listen to party leaders who are assembling near the Kwame Nkrumah Circle to address the teeming crowd.

eng: Many observer and monitoring missions, including the African Union and CODEO have endorsed the results of the Electoral Commission and have called for calm.

eng: Inaccurate media descriptions of Africa are not a rare phenomenon - even if the comedy of errors has steadily declined over the last few years.
swa: Makadirio ya vyombo vya habari yasiyosahihi kuhusu Afrika ni hali iliyozoeleka - hata kama makosa yamekuwa yakipungua kwa miaka michache iliyopita.

eng: The misrepresentation of the continent in the media is not a trivial subject, as Professor Charles Moumouni explains :
swa: Tafsiri mbaya ya bara hili inayooneshwa na vyombo vya habari si jambo dogo, kama Profesa Charles Moumouni anavyoeleza :

eng: Poor representation of Africa in Western media is neither a new nor an exceptional phenomenon.
swa: Picha mbaya ya Afrika inayochorwa katika vyombovya habari vya Magharibi si jambo geni wala la ajabu.

eng: It was already a subject of concern during the 1970s, notably in the context of discussions about New World Information and Communication Order (NWICO).
swa: Limekuwa suala la mjadala tangu miaka ya 1970, hususani katika mikhtadha ya mijadala kuhusu Utaratibu wa Mawasiliano na Habari katika Dunia Mpya (New World Information and Communication Order, NWICO).

eng: But the image of Africa currently being propagated by Western media is all the more concerning as it adversely effects African development efforts.
swa: Lakini sura ya Afrika ambayo kwa sasa inaendelezwa na vyombo vya habari vya Magharibi ni suala linaleta wasiwasi kwa sababu inaathiri jitihada za maendeleo ya Afrika.

eng: African media itself, however, is certainly not immune from criticism of this sort.
swa: Vyombo vya habari vya Afrika vyenyewe, hata hivyo, kwa sasa havina kinga dhidi ya ukosoaji wa aina hii.

eng: Several initiatives have emerged, in recent years, to help improve the accuracy of African media.
swa: Kuna miradi kadhaa imeibuka, kwa miaka ya hivi karibuni, kusaidia kuboresha umakini wa vyombo vya habari vya Afrika.

eng: The African Media Initiative and Media Monitoring Africa are just two examples.
swa: African Media Initiative (Mradi wa Vyombo vya Habari vya ki-Afrika) na Media Monitoring Africa (Ufuatiaaji wa Vyombo vya Habari Afrika) ni mifano miwili.

eng: Here is a summary of the gems, errors and other inaccuracies in global media coverage of Africa and in the African media itself:
swa: Hapa ni muhtasari wa watu maarufu, makosa na kutokuwepo umakini katika habari zinazopewa nafasi katika vyombo vya habari vya dunia kuhusu Afrika na katika vyombo vya habari vya Afrika vyenyewe:

eng: Global media coverage of Africa
swa: Habari za Afrika katika vyombo vya habari vya Afrika

eng: Canada - RDC: "Stephen Harper enters Africa's heart of darkness"
swa: Kanada - RDC: "Stephen Harper aingia katika moyo wa giza la Afrika"

eng: Here is a perfect gift to salute the new year: our new e-book dedicated to Africa's Sub-Saharan region.

eng: African Voices of Hope and Change, gives you an intimate perspective into the stories and people of Sub-Saharan Africa through our best English-language posts from 2012.
swa: Sauti ya Kiafrika ya Matumaini na Mabadiliko, kinakupa mtazamano wa kipekee kuhusu watu na habari za eneo hilo la Afrika kupitia posti zetu zilizo bora zilizoandikwa kwa lugha ya Kiingereza kwa mwaka 2012.

eng: From a total of about 800 posts produced over the year from the region, we hand-picked 13 posts to feature from Senegal, Uganda, Mozambique, Guinea-Bissau, Ghana, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Mauritania, Kenya, Angola and other countries.
swa: Kutoka idadi ya takribani posti 800 zilizoandikwa kwa mwaka katika eneo hilo, tulichagua posti 13 zinazoangazia nchi kama Senegali, Uganda, Msumbiji, Guinea-Bissau, Ghana, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Mauritania, Kenya, Angola pamoja na nchi nyingine.

eng: You are welcome to download it here.
swa: Unakaribishwa kukipakua (download) hapa.

eng: You can even send a copy (in PDF, ePub or Mobipocket format) to your relatives or friends across the world, maybe as a present for their donation to GV.
swa: Unaweza hata kutuma nakala yake (katika mfumo wa PDF, ePub au Mobipocket) kwa ndugu ay marafiki zako kokote walipo duniani, labda kama zawadi ya mchango wao kwa GV.

swa: Kilicho muhimu zaidi, tafadhali sambaza ujumbe kwa watu wako, kupitia mitandao ya kijamii na namna yoyote unayoona inafaa!

eng: African Voices of Hope and Change is more evidence of the power of we', a collective effort focusing on places and people too often 'forgotten' by mainstream media worldwide, despite Africa’s diverse but promising growth in the upcoming years.
swa: Sauti ya Kiafrika ya Matumaini na Mabadiliko ni ushahidi zaidi wanguvu ya kufanya kazi pamoja', jitihada za pamoja zinazojielekeza kwa watu na mahali ambapo mara nyingi "husahauliwa" na vyombo vikuu vya habari duniani kote, ingawa ni kweli Afrika ni kubwa lakini bado kuna matumaini ya maendeleo katika miaka ijayo.

eng: As stated in the ebook introduction, "At the start of the new millennium, it felt as though the African continent was essentially written off by the international community... recent statistics suggest that nine of the fastest-growing economies in the world are in Sub-Saharan Africa."
swa: Kama ilivyosemwa katika utangulizi wa kitabu-pepe kicho, "Katika mwanzo wa mileniam mpya, ilionekana kama bara la Afrika lilikuwa limeachwa na jumuiya ya kimataifa.... takwimu za hivi karibuni zinaonyesha kuwa uchumi wa nchi nane unaokua kwa kasi zaidi duniani uko katika eneo la Kusini mwa Jangwa la Sahara."

eng: And while many experts actually believe that new technology's most lasting influence will be on a broadening field of education, "also important is the potential for leveraging technology towards a more general transparency and accountability, as shown by initiatives based on social and citizen media for monitoring local elections or making government data available on the Internet."
swa: Na wakati wataalamu wengi wakiamini kuwa athari chanya za muda mrefu zinazotokana na teknolojia mpya zitakuwa kwenye sekta ya elimu, 'pia lililo muhimu ni uwezo wa kuitumia teknolojia kwa faida katika maeneo kama uwazi wa jumla na uwajibikaji, kama inavyoonyeshwa na miradi inayojishughulisha na vyombo vya habari vya kijamii na kiraia kwa ajili ya kufuatilia chaguzi za mahali mahususi au kufanya takwimu za serikali kupatikana kwenye mtandao wa intaneti."

eng: Aimed at providing a larger context and fostering the Global Voices mission, this collection of 2012 posts will try to parse out such complex framework and open up the horizon for the upcoming year.
swa: Ikiwa imelengwa kupanua mukhtadha na kukuza malengo ya Global Voices, this mkusanyiko huu wa posti za mwaka 2012 utajaribu kuelezea muundo huo changamani na kufungua upeo kwa ajili ya mwaka ujao.

eng: These voices tell us about moving forward in hope and change, their accounts reveal a path infused with struggle and collaboration.
swa: Sauti hizi zinatuambia juu ya kusogea mbele kwa matumaini na mabadiliko, fikra za waandishi zinafunua njia iliyowezeshwa na jitihada na ushirikiano.

eng: Thanks to Mohamed Adel for technical support and to those who variously contributed to articles selected for this new e-book: Afef Abrougui, Ahmed Jedou, Anna Gueye, Eleanor Staniforth, Endalk, James Propa, Kofi Yeboah, Lova Rakotomalala, Nwachukwu Egbunike, Richard Wanjohi, Sara Gold, Sara Moreira, and Ndesanjo Macha.

eng: In an interview with Angolan television, at the beginning of January, the professor spoke about the situation in Guinea-Bissau after the death of President Malam Bacai Sanhá.
swa: Katika mahojiano na televisheni ya Angola, mwanzoni mwa mwezi Januari, Profesa huyo alizungumzia hali ya mambo nchini Guinea-Bissau baada ya kifo cha Rais Malam Bacai Sanhá.

eng: After this, Milocas Pereira said that she began to feel under great pressure .
swa: Baada ya hayo, Milocas Pereira alisema kwamba alianza kujisikia kuwa kwenye shinikizo kubwa .

eng: On last November 3, the Sindicato dos Jornalistas Angolanos (Union of Angolan Journalists) denounced that the Guinean journalist had been “terrorized” in Luanda:
swa: Mnamo NOvemba 3,Sindicato dos Jornalistas Angolanos (Umoja wa waandishi wa Angola) ulidai kwamba mwandishi wa Guinea "amefanyiwa ugaidi" jijini Luanda:

eng: Milocas Pereira was attacked in the beginning of the month of May by unknown people, before having communicated her intention to leave Angola to some people she had spoken with.
swa: Milocas Pereira alishambuliwa mwanzoni mwa mwezi Mei na watu wasiofahamika, baada ya kuwa aliwasiliana na watu wake wa karibu aliokuwa amezungumza nao kuhusiana na nia yake ya kuondoka Angola.

eng: She pointed to this attack as the cause for this decision.
swa: Alibainisha kuwa shambulio hilo lilikuwa ni sababu ya uamuzi huo.

eng: According to “Sol Mansi” Radio , the journalist had no doubts that the attack had strong political motivations:
swa: Kwa mujibu waRadio “Sol Mansi” , mwandishi huyo hakuwa na mashaka kuwa shambulio hilo lilikuwa na msukumo wa kisiasa:

eng: She was running the risk of losing her life, and the only solution that she had was to immediately leave Angola, and return to her country.
swa: Alikuwa akikimbia hatari ya kupoteza maisha yake, na ufumbuzi pekee aliokuwa nao ulikuwa ni kuondoka haraka Angola, na kurudi nchini mwake.

eng: Counselled by a friend to publicly denounce the attack, MP said she preferred not to.
swa: Akishauriwa na rafiki yake kutangaza kushambuliwa, mwandishi huyo alisema hakutaka kufanya hivyo.

eng: Further counselled to go to Portugal, MP said she did not trust the Portuguese and said she would feel better in Guinea-Bissau with those responsible for the transition.
swa: Baadaye akashauriwa kwenye Ureno, hata hivyo alisema hakuwa anawaamini Wareno na kusema alijisikia afadhali angeenda Guinea-Bissau kuwa na wale wanaohusika na wakati huo wa mpito.

eng: Last October, in statements to the same radio station, the Secretary of State for Communities in Guinea-Bissau, Idelfrides Gomes Fernandes confirmed the news about the possible disappearance of the journalist for the first time.
swa: Mwezi Oktoba uliopita, akitoa tamko katika kituo kile kile cha radio, Waziri wa Nchi kwa Masuala ya Jamii nchini GUinea-Bissau, Idelfrides Gomes Fernandes alithibitisha habari kuhusu uwezekano wa kutoweka kwa mwandishi kwa mara ya kwanza.

eng: Four months after her mysterious disappearance, the family decided to contact authorities, but the only response that they got was silence.
swa: Miezi Minne ya kutoweka kiajabu, familia iliamua kuwasiliana na mamlaka zinazohusika, lakini majibu pekee waliyoyapata ni kimya.

eng: In its November 2nd edition, the Novo Jornal (New Newspaper) (Angola) dedicated an entire page to the disappearance of the journalist.
swa: Katika toleo lake la 2 mwezi Novemba, the Novo Jornal (Gazeti Jipya) (Angola) lilitoa ukurasa mzima kwa habari za kupotea kwa mwandishi.

eng: Two months ago, Bartolomeu Capita of the National Movement of Cabinda wrote on the site of the organization Peace & collaborative development network that Milocas Pereira could have been ordered killed in Angola:
swa: Miezi miwili iliyopita, Bartolomeu Capita wa taasisis ya National Movement of Cabinda (Vuguvugu la Kitaifa la Cabinda) aliandika katika tovuti yao Peace & collaborative development network kwamba Milocas Pereira inawezekana iliamuriwa auawe nchini Angola:

eng: Nobody has seen Ms. Pereira or simply heard from her for almost a month now.
swa: Hakuna aliyemwona Mama Pereira wala kusikia kutoka kwake kwa zaidi ya mwezi sasa.

eng: Yet she was teaching at the independent University of Angola.
swa: Na alikuwa akifundisha katika Chuo Kikuu cha Angola.

eng: Concerns have arisen which must be addressed.
swa: Mashaka yamekuwa makubwa na yanahitaji kushughulikiwa.

eng: More and more fellow scholars are discreetly suggesting that she may have been murdered, for having sought to investigate certain matters related to the obscure links between Angola's criminal regime and Guinea-Bissau.
swa: Wanazuoni wenzake wanahofia kuwa huenda ameuawa, baada ya kuwa alionyesha nia ya kufanya uchunguzi wa masuala ya namna utawala dhalimu wa Angola unavyohusiana na nchini ya Guinea Bissau.

eng: News of the disappearance of the 58 year old journalist was made public at a time in which the family – that was trying not to complicate police investigations – began to lose hope that Milocas was still alive.
swa: Habari za kutoweka kwa mwandishi huyo mwenye umri wa miaka 58 zilikuwa hadharani wakati ambao familia yake -ambayo ilijaribu kurahisisha uchunguzi wa polisi- ilianza kupoteza matumaini kuwa Milocas alikuwa hai bado.

eng: The brother of the professor, Carlos Pereira, who lives in Lisbon, said to Voice of America :
swa: Kaka wa Mhadhiri huyo, Carolos Pereira, anayeishi Lisbon, aliiambia Sauti la Marekani :

eng: What comes to us is this, she has disappeared since the end of July.
swa: KInachotujia ni kuwa, alitoweka tangu mwishoni mwa mwezi Julai.

eng: We suspect a lot.
swa: Tunahisi mengi.

eng: That she could have run into many things and needed to flee, hide or had some could of retaliation.
swa: Kwamba huenda alikumbana na vingi na akaamua kuimbia nchi, akajificha au alifanyiwa vitendo vya kuliza kisasi.

eng: On the blog Rispito , the Guinean Samba Bari alleges that the disappearance is another challenge for the transitional authorities and that the situation could widen the fissure between the Guinean government not recognized by Luanda and the Angolan government.
swa: Kwenye blogu ya Rispito , raia wa Guinea Samba Bari anadhani kuwa kutoweka kwa mwandishi huyo ni changamoto nyingine kwa serikali ya mpito na kuwa hali hiyo inaweza kuongeza misuguano kati ya serikali ya Guinea isiyotambuliwa na Luanda na serikali ya Angola.

eng: It's Christmas in Bethlehem, in the West Bank, Palestine, the birth place of Jesus Christ.
swa: Ni sikukuu ya kuzaliwa Kristo mjini Betlehemu, katika ukanda wa Magharibi, Palestina, mahali alipozaliwa Kristo.

eng: What better way than to celebrate this occasion than by sharing photographs and reactions of netizens to this event, celebrated by billions worldwide.
swa: Ni namna ipi nzuri zaidi ya kusherehekea tukio hili kwa kuwashirikisha picha pamoja na mitazamo ya watumiaji wa intaneti kuhusiana na tukio hili linalosherehekewa na mabilioni ya watu duniani kote.

eng: Israeli journalist Joseph Dana was in Bethlehem to see the lighting of the Christmas tree and shares this photograph:
swa: Mwanahabari wa Israeli Joseph Dana alikuwa Betlehemu kuangalia mwanga wa miti ya Krismasi na alipakia mtandaoni picha ifuatayo:

eng: The lighting of the Xmas tree in Bethlehem.
swa: Mwanga wa mti wa Krismasi mjini Betlehemu.

eng: Photograph shared by @ibnezra on Twitter
swa: Picha iliwekwa na @ibnezra katika mtandao wa Twita

eng: Lauren Bohn offers a closer image of the tree, from the same celebration:
swa: Lauren Bohn aweka picha ya mti wa Krismasi aliyopigwa kwa ukaribu zaidi wakati wa sherehe hizi:

eng: Beautiful Christmas tree lighting in Bethlehem, comments @LaurenBohn on Twitter, as she shares this picture
swa: Mwanga mzuri wa mti wa Krismasi mjini Betlehemu, maoni @LaurenBohn katika Twita, wakati akiweka mtandaoni picha hii

eng: And Maath Musleh shares pictures of the lit up streets of Bethlehem, in preparation for Christmas:
swa: Na Maath Musleh aweka mtandaoni picha zinavyoonesha jinsi mitaa ya Bethlehemu ilivyoangazwa katika maandalizi ya sikuu ya kuzaliwa Kristo:

eng: Bethlehem streets lighting up for Christmas, tweets @MaathMusleh, who shares this image on Twitter
swa: Mitaa ya Betlehemu inavyoangazwa kwa mwanga wa taa za Krismasi, anatwiti @MaathMusleh, ambaye aliweka picha hii katika mtandao wa Twita

eng: Ahmed Aggour posts this photograph of the tree during the day:
swa: Ahmed Aggour, mchana wa leo aliweka picha hii ya mti:

eng: The most beautiful #Christmas tree ever, and right where it belongs.
swa: Mti mzuri wa Krismasi kuliko mwingine wowote ule unaopatikana mjini Betlehemu.

eng: Merry Christmas. #Bethlehem #Palestine, tweets @Psypherize
swa: Heri ya sikukuu ya kuzaliwa Kristo. #Betlehemu #Palestina, alitwiti @Psypherize

eng: Merry Christmas!
swa: Heri ya Sikukuu ya Noeli kusherehekea Kuzaliwa kwa Kristo!

eng: A screenshot of the Face the Balkans website.
swa: Picha ya mwonekano wa tovuti ya Balkans.

eng: Fifteen young journalists from six different countries have produced a series of personal stories about representatives of the minorities (in a broad sense) from Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Serbia, and Macedonia.
swa: Waandishi vijana kumi na watano kutoka katika nchi zipatazo sita tofauti wametengeneza mfululizo wa masimulizi binafsi kuhusu masuala ya namna jamii zenye watu wachache (kwa mapana yake) zinavyoweza kuwakilishwa kutoka Bosnia na Herzegovina, Kosovo, Serbia, na Macedonia.

eng: The stories are available in English, German, and French on the Face the Balkans website.
swa: Habari zinapatikana katika lugha za Kiingereza, Kijerumani, na Kifaransa katika mwonekano wa tovuti ya Balkans.

eng: A group of secondary school teachers broke into and entered the office of the Minister of Education in protest against the arbitrary transfer of 120 teachers to other schools.
swa: Kikundi cha walimu wa shule za sekondari kilivunja na kuingia katika ofisi ya Waziri wa Elimu wakipinga kuhamishwa holela kwawalimu 120 kwenda kwenye shule nyingine.

eng: The transfers were made to punish teachers who participated in last year's strikes demanding the improvement of the conditions of employees in the education sector.
swa: Walimu hao wamekuwa wakihamishwa kuwaadhibu wale wote walioshiriki katika mgomo wa mwaka uliopita kushinikiza kuboreshwa kwa mazingira ya kazi katika sekta ya elimu.

eng: The teachers considered this act a punishment for a strike they held to demand of their rights and also a violation of civil service law in Mauritania.
swa: Walimu walikichukulia kitendo hicho kama adhabu kufuatia hatua yao ya kugoma kudai haki zao na vilevile kupuuzwa kwa sheria za utumishi wa umma nchini Mauritania.

eng: For his part, Mohamed Ould Rabani, Secretary General of the independent syndicate of secondary education teachers, slammed the transfer as a dangerous precedent in the history of Mauritania and asked his colleagues not to conform to the ministry's orders.
swa: Kwa upande wake, Mohamed Ould Rabani, Katibu Mkuu wa baraza hru la walimu wa shule za sekondari, waliuponda uhamisho huo kama hatua ya hatari katika historia ya Mauratania na kuwaomba wenzake kutokutii amri ya Wizara.

eng: In the same context, another group of arbitrary transferred teachers, held a demonstration in front of the Education Minister Ahmed Ould Bah's office, denouncing the decision and demanding its immediate retreat.
swa: Katika mukhtadha huo huo, kikundi kingine cha walimu walihamishwa kiholela, walifanya maandamano mbele ya ofisi ya Waziri wa Elimu Ahmed Ould Bah, wakiupinga uamuzi huo na kudai kusitishwa mara moja hatua hiyo.

eng: Some of them also protested in front of the presidential palace in Nouakchott and threatened to resign from their posts in case the decision is not retracted.
swa: Baadhi yao vile vile waliandamana mbele yamakazi ya rai huko Nouakchott na wakatishia kuacha kazi ikiwa uamuzi hautabatilika.

eng: It is worth mentioning that the ministry had suspended the salaries of hundreds of teachers after their participation in the strikes organized by the syndicate.
swa: Ikumbukwe kuwa wizara imewasimamishia mishahara ya mamia ya walimu baada ya wao kushiriki maandamano yaliyoandaliwa na baraza hilo.

eng: Photograph of the protesting teachers posted on Twitter by @mejdmr
swa: Picha ya walimu wakiandamana iliyowekwa kwenye twita na @mejdmr

eng: The National Syndicate for Secondary Education issued a statement condemning the arbitrary transfer:
swa: Baraza la Taifa la Elimu ya Sekondari lilitoa tamko kulaani uhamisho holela:

eng: The Mauritanian Ministry of Education arbitrarily transferred dozens of secondary education teachers because of their participation in legitimate strikes which is considered a dangerous violation of the rights of syndicate members, especially the right to demonstrate, which is guaranteed by article 14 in the constitution and by the international agreements signed by our country, such as the the International Labor Convention number 87, which is related to syndicate freedoms.
swa: Wizata ya Elimu ya Mauritania imewahammisha kiholela makumi ya walimu wa sekondari kwa sababu ya ushiriki wao katika mgomo halali. hatua inayoonekana kuwa ni uvunjifu wa hatari wa haki za wanachama wa baraza hilo, hususani haki ya kuandamana, inayolindwa na ibara ya 14 ya katiba na pia inalindwa na mikataba ya kimataifa iliyotiwa saini na nchi yetu, kama Makubaliano ya Kimataifa ya Kazi namba 87, ambayo yanakuhusiana na haki za baraza.

eng: Tiguend blog posts a testimony of one the teachers effected by the transfers, entitled "This is why I deserve the sanction" where he speaks of the injustice of that decision:
swa: Blogu ya Tiguend iliweka shuhuda za walimu walioathirika na uhamisho huo, zilizopewa jina "Hii ndiyo sababu kwa nini ninastahili kutimuliwa kazi" ambapo walizungumzia kukiukwa kwa haki kwa uamuzi huo:

eng: I have been teaching for 10 years in Trarza region and never during those years have I got less then 17 points on my evaluation.
swa: Nimekuwa nikifundisha kwa miaka 10 katika mkoa wa Trarza na sijawahi katika kipindi chote hicho kupata chini ya alama 17 katika Tathmini ninayofanyiwa.

eng: I have worked with various directors and my salary has never been suspended except this time because of my participation in the strike.
swa: Nimefanya kazi na waratibu mbalimbali na mshahara wangu haujawahi kusimamishwa isipokuwa wakati huu kwa sababu ya kushiriki mgomo.

eng: I have no record of absence or slackening in my duties and everything is fine, thanks God, until the director Mohamed Ould el Talib came and sent a report to the Rousou School director to whom he reports, asking him to give me a 6/20 grade and to accuse me of snitching and gossip, which he has been bragging about since his illegal nomination as head of administration.
swa: Sina rekodi ya kukosa au kuzembea majukumu yangu na kila kitu kiko sawia, namshukuru Mungu, mpaka mratibu Mohamed Ould el Talib alikuja na kutuma ripoti kwa mratibu wa Rousou School ambaye ni mkubwa wake wa kazi, akimwomba anipe alama 6 kati ya 20 na kunituhumu kupiga umbeya na majungu, tabia ambayo amekuwa akijidai nayo tangu ameteuliwa kwa namna inayotia mashaka kuwa mtawala wa elimu.

eng: All this was a reason to transfer me arbitrarily along with 16 other teachers in Trarza whose only fault is to have taken part in the strike knowing that the law guarantees this right and the constitution protects it for a noble life and a more dignified education.
swa: Haya yote ndiyo yamekuwa sababu ya mimi kuhamishwa kienyeji pamoja na wenzangu 16 hapa Trarza ambao kosa letu pekee ni kushiriki mgomo tukijua kabisa kuwa sheria zinailinda haki hii na katiba ya nchi nayo inatulinda kwa ajili ya maisha na elimu ya kuheshimika.

eng: Mauritan.net says that the transfer is a result of a complaint, accusing the teachers of "inciting strikes and exercising politics":
swa: Tovuti ya Mauritan.net inasema kwamba uhamisho ni matokeo ya malalamiko, yakiwatuhumu walimu kwa "kulazimisha mgomo na kufanya siasa":

eng: The transfer of the teachers was based on directors reports via the governors and the letters of the governors' letters stated that they are inciting strikes and practicing politics.
swa: Uhamisho wa walimu ulizingatia taarifa za waratibu elimu kupitia kwa Magavana na barua za Magavana zilieleza kwamba walimu hao walifanya siasa kwa kushiriki mgomo huo batili.

eng: Dedda Cheikh Brahim criticizes the way the Mauritanian regime is dealing with teacher's protests:
swa: Dedda Cheikh Brahim anakosoa namna utawala wa Mauritania unavyoshughulikia maandamano hayo ya walimu:

eng: In the military democracy, protests are punishable and the teachers are now paying for it in a legal way
swa: Katika demokrasia ya Kijeshi, maandamano huadhibiwa na walimu sasa wanalipa gharama ya kwa mujibu wa sheria

eng: He adds:
swa: Anaongeza:

eng: The teachers were transferred after they decided to demand their rights.
swa: Walimu walihamishwa baada ya kuamua kudai haki zao.

eng: There is God oh Mauritanian
swa: Mungu yupo ewe Mmauritania

eng: Mauritanian journalist Mohamed Ould Salem also slammed the Minister of Education for creating a crisis in the education sector:
swa: Mwandishi Mohamed Ould Salem alimlaumu Waziri wa Elimu kwa kusababisha mzozo katika sekta ya elimu:

eng: Ould Bah doesn't breathe ordinary Oxygen but lives from making crises and injustice.
swa: Ould Bah havuti hewa iliyozoeleka bali huishi kwa kuminya haki za watu na kutengeneza mizozo.

eng: This is why he decided to punish 108 of the best teachers because they participated in legal strikes.
swa: Ndio maana aliamua kuwaadhibu walimu bora 108 kwa sababu tu walishiriki kwenye mgomo uliofuata sheria.

eng: He adds:
swa: Anaongeza:

eng: A new date with a year marked with a crisis in the education sector with 108 teachers refusing punitive transfer and education syndicates promising to make the decision fall and a minister who is very creative in making up crises and accumulating failure
swa: Tarehe mpya imeingia kwenye historia kwa mgogoro katika sekta ya elimu ambapo walimu 108 wamegomea uhamisho wa adhabu na baraza la elimu likiahidi kufutilia mbali uamuzi huo pamoja na waziri huyu mbunifu katika kutengeneza matatizo na kulimbikiza makosa

eng: Nasser Al Hachemi tweets:
swa: Nasser Al Hachemi alitwiti:

eng: It is humiliation and tyranny.
swa: Ni unyanyasaji na uimla.

eng: My heart with you oh you holders of the light
swa: Moyo wangu uko nanyi enyi wabeba taa

eng: Activist Mejdi Ahmed also had his word about the matter:
swa: Mwanaharakati Mejdi Ahmed pia alitia neno katika suala hili:

eng: The teachers protested yesterday in the Education Minister premises asking to renounce the decision of transferring them - a decision they judged unfair.
swa: Walimu waliandamana jana katika maeneo ya Wizara ya Elimu wakiiomba (Wizara) kubatilisha uamuzi wa kuwahamisha -uamuzi waliouchukulia kuwa haukuwa wa haki.

eng: Al Cheikh Ould Horma also tweeted:
swa: Al Cheikh Ould Horma alitwiti:

eng: In Mauritania the teachers insist to ideologize the conflict with minister who in turn insists of ideologizing the teachers demand
swa: Nchini Mauritania walimu wanasisitiza kuufanya mgogoro huu kuwa wa kiitikadi na waziri muhusika akijibu mapigo kwa kuyafanya madai yao kuwa ya kiitikadi

eng: The academic year is about to start in Mauritania and the battle starts again between the Minister and the syndicates.
swa: Mwaka wa masomo unakaribia kuanza nchini Mauritania na vita ndio kwanza vimeanza kwa mara nyingine baina ya Waziri na baraza la walimu.

eng: A dire war
swa: Ni vita hatari

eng: Once again an indigenous girl was killed after being brutally raped in Borodalupara village, Kawkhali Upazila of Rangamati district.
swa: Kwa mara nyingine tena msichana mzawa ameuliwa mara baada ya kufanyiwa ukatili kwa kubakwa katika kijiji cha Borodalupara, Kawkhali Upazila ya wilaya ya Rangamati.

eng: The victim, Khomaching Marma (14) was a student of class eight.
swa: Khomaching Marma (14) ambaye ni mhanga wa kitendo hiki, alikuwa ni mwanafunzi wa darasa la nane.

eng: Her dead body was found in the slopes of a mountain just 200-300 yards away from her home.
swa: Mwili wake ulikutwa katika miteremko ya milima takribani yadi 200 hadi 300 kutoka nyumbani kwake.

eng: She was last seen going to a nearby jungle to bring her family’s cattle back home.
swa: Mara ya mwisho alionekana akielekea kwenye msitu wa karibu na nyumbani kwake kuchukua mifugo ya familia yake kutoka malishoni.

eng: Rina Dewan posted on her Facebook wall regarding the reason behind this heinous crime:
swa: Rina Dewan aliandika katika ukurasa wake wa Facebook akieleza sababu za kufanyika kwa kitendo hiki cha kikatili:

eng: There is a settler village named Nallyachari Uttor Matha within half a kilometer of the place where Thomaching’s dead body was recovered.
swa: Kuna mlowezi mmoja katika kijiji ajulikanaye kwa jina la Nallyachari Uttor Matha aishie takribani umbali wa nusu ya kilometa kutoka sehemu ilipokutwa maiti ya Thomaching.

eng: During the early 1980s the government evicted the indigenous Marmas from their land and settled Bengalis there.
swa: Kwenye miaka ya 1980 hivi, serikali iliwaondoa wakazi wazawa wajulikanao kama Marmas kutoka kwenye ardhi yao na kisha kuwakaribisha watu wa Kutoka Bengali.

eng: Now those settlers claim a large portion of Borodalupara as theirs.
swa: Kwa sasa wahamiaji hao wanataka kujimilikisha sehemu kubwa ya Borodalupara.

eng: A few days ago, some Marma villagers planted ginger in their lands but the settlers destroyed their crops and created unrest.
swa: Siku chache zilizopita, baadhi ya wanavijiji wa Marma walipanda tangawizi kwenye mashamba yao lakini wahamiaji hao waliharibu mazao yao na kusababisha hali ya amani kupotea.

eng: It has been learnt that conflict exists for land between the maternal uncle of Thomaching Marma and the Bengali settlers.
swa: Imekwishafahamika kuwa kuna mgogoro wa ardhi uliopo kati ya mjomba wa Thomaching Marma na wahamiaji wa Bengali.

eng: So, it is suspected that she was raped and killed to avenge.
swa: Kwa hiyo, inadhaniwa kuwa alibakwa na kisha kuuliwa kama namna ya kulipiza kisasi.

eng: Violence against indigenous women has increased in recent times.
swa: Ukatili dhidi ya wanawake wazawa umeongezeka siku za hivi karibuni.

swa: Haki miliki Demotrix.

eng: Violence against indigenous women has increased in recent times.
swa: Ukatili dhidi ya wanawake wazawa umeongezeka siku za hivi karibuni.

eng: A few months ago, another indigenous girl was raped and killed. She was a student of class five.
swa: Miezi michache iliyopita, msichana mwingine alibakwa na kisha kuuliwa.Alikuwa ni mwanafunzi wa darasa la tano.

eng: Hari kishore Chakma, a journalist, provides some statistics on the rape of indigenous women in an article at daily Prothom Alo :
swa: Mwandishi wa habari Hari kishore Chakma, anatoa baadhi ya takwimu zinazoonesha matukio ya kubakwa kwa wanawake wazawa katika makala ya gazeti la kila siku la Prothom Alo :

eng: Up to November of this year, 20 indigenous girls and women were raped in three hill districts.
swa: Mpaka mwezi wa Novemba mwaka jana, wasichana na wanawake 20 wazawa walibakwa katika wilaya tatu za mlimani.

eng: Thomaching Marma’s name is now added to this ever-growing list.
swa: Na kwa sasa, jina la Thomaching Marma linajumuishwa kwenye orodha hii inayoendelea kukua.

eng: In 2011, 10 indigenous women were raped.
swa: Mwaka 2011, wanawake 10 wazawa walibakwa.

eng: Kapaeng, a human rights organization, reported this statistics.
swa: Kapaeng ambalo ni shirika la kutetea haki za binadamu lilitoa takwimu hizi.

eng: According to this organization, 51 indigenous women were the victims of violence during this year.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa shirika hili, wanawake wazawa 51 walikuwa wahanga wa matukio haya kwa mwaka huu.

eng: This number was 31 in 2011 and just 4 in 2008.
swa: Mwaka 2011 matukio kama haya yalikuwa 31 na manne tu mwaka 2008.

eng: This brutal rape and murder once again has spread anger and rage across the country.
swa: Ukatili huu wa ubakaji na mauaji kwa mara nyingine tena umeshaeneza hasira na vurugu nchini kote.

eng: Processions have been arranged in Dhaka, Chittagong and Sylhet.
swa: Mazungumzo yalikwisha kupangwa katika miji ya Dhaka, Chittagong na Sylhet.

eng: Netizen have also expressed their rage and protested.
swa: Raia wa mtandaoni nao wameshaonesha hasira yao na pia kuandamana.

eng: Protests in Dhaka against the rape and killing of an indigenous girl.
swa: Maandamano huko Dhaka ya kupinga ubakaji na mauaji ya msichana mzawa.

eng: Image by Firoz Ahmed.
swa: Picha na Firoz Ahmed.

eng: Copyright Demotix
swa: Haki miliki Demotix

eng: Mithun Chakma Jummo posted on Facebook:
swa: Mithun Chakma Jummo aliandika katika ukurasa wake wa Facebook:

eng: Just like the numb, cold body of our sister, have we also become numb?
swa: Kama tu jinsi ilivyo kwa mwili baridi wa dada yetu usioweza kufanya lolote, je, nasi pia tumekuwa hivyo?

swa: Mjini Imphal , watu walipaza sauti zao ili kutafuta haki dhidi ya unyanyasaji wa kijinsia wa msichana.

eng: What should be our protests?
swa: Maandamano yetu yawe kwa lengo gani?

eng: Only one procession?
swa: Kwa jambo moja tu?

eng: Then becoming quiet and numb again!
swa: Halafu tuwe kimya na tuliopooza tena!

swa: Serikali ya India ililazimishwa kuwatia nguvuni wahusika wa vitendo hivi vya kikatili.

swa: Siku za hivi karibuni, msichana mzawa alibakwa na kisha kuuliwa katika kijiji cha Borodalupara huko Kawkhali upazila katika wilaya ya Rangamati.

swa: Hata hivyo, Polisi wameshindwa hata kumtia nguvuni angalau mhusika mmoja.

swa: Kama ilivyo kwa tukio hili, mamia ya akina dada zetu na mama zetu wazawa wamebaki kuwa wahanga wa kubakwa na mauaji kwa muda mrefu.

swa: Ni jambo la kikatili kwa wabakaji na wauaji kufanya ukatili huu katika makazi yetu muda wote.

swa: Hakuna uhakika kuwa, miongoni mwao ghafla hawatajisahau na kasha kutoa misimamo yao.

swa: Ahmed Ismail ni mpiga picha za video ambaye aliuawa mjini Salambad mwaka jana (2011) wakati alipiga picha za maandamano.

swa: Alipigwa risasi kutoka kwenye gari la kiraia.

eng: On January 24, the official launch of Hadithi, a platform for hosting open access academic content will take place in Nairobi, Kenya.
swa: Januari 24, ni siku ambayo inategemewa kuwa ya kuzindua rasmi Hadithi, ambalo ni jukwaa la kuhifadhia zana za bure za kitaaluma mjini Nairobi, Kenya.

eng: Various scholars and digital players will get together to discuss digital open access in higher education in Kenya.
swa: Wasomi mbalimbali na wadau wa mitandao watakusanyika pamoja kujadili upatikanaji wa zana huru za kitaaluma katika elimu ya juu nchini Kenya.

eng: Hadithi will search, view and download articles from research institutions around the world.
swa: Hadithi itasaidia kutafuta, kuona na kushusha makala kutoka katika taasisi za kitafiti duniani kote.

eng: To register for this event, find Hadithi on Facebook and Eventbrite.
swa: Kujiandikisha kwa tukio hili, itafute Hadithi mtandaoni kupitia Facebook na tovuti ya Eventbrite.

eng: Gaurav Mishra analyzes the dynamics of grassroots change movements and how they work to make an impact in the mainstream using social media.
swa: Gaurav Mishra anachambua nguvu ya vuguvugu la mabadiliko linaloanzia kwa watu wa kawaida na namna inavyofanya kazi kuleta mabadiliko chanya katika utendaji wa vyombo vikuu vya habari kwa kutumia vyombo vya habari vya kiraia.

eng: As part of our collaboration with Syria Deeply we are cross-posting a series of articles that capture civilian voices caught in the crossfire, along with perspectives on the conflict from writers around the world.
swa: Kama sehemu ya ushirikiano wetu na Syria Deeply tuna mfululizo wa makala mbalimbali zinazogusa sauti za raia zilizopatikana katika machafuko sambamba na mitizamo ya waandishi kutoka ulimwenguni kote kuhusiana na mgogoro unaoendelea.

eng: Loubna Mrie paid a steep price for her place in Syria’s revolution.
swa: Loubna Mrie alipata pigo kubwa kutokana na msimamo wake kuhusiana na mapinduzi ya Syria.

eng: As an Alawite who took a stand against President Bashar Al Assad, she pitted herself against her community; many Alawites have remained staunchly behind Assad, as the leader of their sect and the protector of their privileged position of power.
swa: Kama mtu wa kikundi cha Alawite aliyeamua kuwa na msimamo tofauti dhidi ya Rais Bashar Al Assad, aliamua kujitenga moja kwa moja na jamii yake; watu wengine wa Alawite wameendelea kumtii Assad kama kiongozi wa dhehebu na mwangalizi wao kutokana na upendeleo wanaoupata kutoka kwa kiongozi wao akiwa kama Rais.

eng: From the start of the uprising, Loubna’s parents took opposite sides: her father and uncles stood with Assad, while Loubna and her mother supported the growing protests.
swa: Kuanzia mwanzo wa harakati za kuwa kinyume na mamlaka, wazazi wa Loubna walikuwa katika pande tofauti: baba yake na wajomba zake walikuwa upande wa Assad, wakati Loubna na mama yake walikuwa wakiunga mkono maandamano yaliyokuwa yakishamiri.

eng: It was a position Loubna’s father made it clear he wouldn’t tolerate: he demanded her loyalty to the Assad camp.
swa: Ulikuwa ni upande alipo baba yake na Loubna uliomfanya afikie msimamo wa kushindwa kuvumilia: baba yake alimtaka atii upande wa Assad.

eng: In August, Loubna left her hometown of Latakia, in western Syria, fleeing across the border to Turkey.
swa: Mwezi Agusti, Loubna aliondoka katika mji aliokulia wa Latakia, Magharibi mwa Syria na alisafiri kwa ndege hadi Uturuki.

eng: Her father kidnapped her mother and threatened to kill her as punishment.
swa: Baba yake alimshikilia mama yake na Loubna kama mateka na kutishia kumuua kama sehemu ya adhabu.

eng: When Loubna refused to return her father followed through on the threat.
swa: Loubna alipokataa kurudi, baba yake alitimiza adhabu aliyoipanga.

eng: Her father killed her mother, and cut her off from the life she had known before the uprising.
swa: Baba yake hatimaye alimuua mama yake na Loubna, alimkatisha maisha aliyoyajua kabla ya kuamua kuwa kinyume na mamlaka ya Syria..

eng: Loubna is now a filmmaker with Basma, a media activist group.
swa: Kwa sasa, Loubna ni mtayarishaji wa filamu wa Basma, kikundi cha uanaharakati wa vyombo vya habari.

eng: She travels around Syria with a camera, chronicling the revolution on film.
swa: Anasafiri maeneo mengi ya Syria na kamera yake akikusanya matukio ya mapinduzi ya Syria katika filamu.

eng: We met up with her in Gaziantep, Turkey, to talk about life and war in Syria.
swa: Tulikutana naye huko Gaziantep, Uturuki ili kuongea naye kuhusu maisha na vita nchini Syria.

eng: Below is a portion of that chat.
swa: Ifuatayo ni sehemu ya mazungumzo yetu naye.

eng: SD: What was it like in Latakia at the beginning of the revolution?
swa: SD: Latakia kulikuwaje wakati harakati za mapinduzi zilipoanza?

eng: Mrie: It started like every other city in Syria.
swa: Mrie: Ilianza kama ilivyo kwa kila jiji nchini Syria.

eng: The demonstrations just had the normal, peaceful slogans like, “we want better schools”, “we want better jobs”, “we want democracy”.
swa: Maandamano yalikuwa na misemo ya amani kabisa kama vile, “tunahitaji shule nzuri”, “tunahitaji kazi zilizo bora”, “tunahitaji demokrasia”.

eng: We didn’t even say the line “al shaab yureed isqat al nizam”—“the people want the regime to fall”.
swa: Na hata hatukusema “al shaab yureed isqat al nizam”—“ watu wanataka serikali itoke madarakani”.

eng: SD: Were there many Alawites protesting?
swa: SD: Kulikuwa na watu wengi wa Alawite walioandamana?

eng: Mrie: No.
swa: Mrie: Hapana.

eng: There were hardly any.
swa: Ilikuwa nadra sana kumuona mtu wa Alawite katika maandamano.

eng: Latakia is full of Alawites, and most of them were supporting the regime.
swa: Latakia kuna watu wa Alawite wengi sana na wengi wao walikuwa wanauunga mkono utawala ulioko madarakani.

eng: We had just a small slice of society that was against the regime, but they didn’t go to demonstrations because they were so afraid.
swa: Tulikuwa na kikundi kidogo sana cha wanajamii waliokuwa kinyume na serikali, lakini hawakwenda kwenye maandamano kwa kuwa walikuwa wakiogopa kupita kiasi.

eng: From day one, the regime was trying to convince people that this is not a revolution-it’s just terrorists or an Islamic movement against you.
swa: Tokea siku ya kwanza, utawala ulijaribu kuwashawishi watu kuwa haya hayakuwa mapinduzi, ni magaidi tu au harakati tu za kiislam dhidi yenu.

eng: SD: When did it all happen?
swa: SD: Haya yote yalitokea lini?

eng: When did your family fall apart?
swa: Ni wakati gani ambapo familia yako ilijitenga?

eng: Mrie: It happened last November.
swa: Mrie: Mwezi Novemba mwaka jana.

eng: It was so traumatic, I couldn’t even think about anything.
swa: Ilisikitisha sana, hata sikuweza hata kuwaza kuhusu jambo lolote.

eng: I felt guilt, huge guilt.
swa: Nilijisikia mwenye hatia, hatia kubwa.

eng: I kept crying for three days, but then I realized that my mom didn’t die just to see me crying in my bed the whole day. So I chose the other option: to grab my camera and go back to Syria.
swa: Nililia kwa siku tatu, lakini niligundua kuwa mama yangu hakunihurumia kabisa pamoja na kulia kwangu siku nzima chumbani mwangu, kwa hiyo, nilifanya maamuzi mengine: nilichukua kamera yangu haraka na kurudi Syria.

eng: SD: Did she speak to you in the final month?
swa: SD: Aliongea nawe katika ule mwezi wa misho??

eng: Loubna
swa: Loubna

eng: Mrie: No, they kidnapped her in the middle of August.
swa: Mrie: Hapana, walimteka katikati ya mwezi Agusti.

eng: I didn’t hear from her again since then.
swa: Baada ya hapo, hakuwahi kuwasiliana nami tena.

eng: Even my aunts and my grandma didn’t call me because they were so afraid that if the government found out they were in touch with me, they would harm them.
swa: Hata shangazi zangu na bibi yangu hawakutaka kuwasiliana nami tena kwa kuwa waliogopa sana kuwa kama serikali ingegundua kuwa walikuwa wanawasiliana nami, wangewadhuru.

eng: Even my neighborhood and my old friends didn’t talk with me at all.
swa: Hata majirani zangu na marafiki wa zamani hawakuwasiliana nami kabisa.

eng: They didn’t say we are sorry, we feel sad, we feel anything.
swa: Hawakunipa pole, hawakuonesha huzuni yao, wala kuonesha hali ya kutoguswa na lililotokea kabisa.

eng: They were saying that you deserve that.
swa: Ni kama vile walikuwa wanasema nilistahili.

eng: So it’s not only the loss of my mom that broke my heart, it’s also the attitude of the people that I was growing up with.
swa: Kwa hiyo, sio tu kifo cha mama yangu kilichonivunja moyo, lakini pia na mtazamo wa watu nilioishi nao toka utotoni.

eng: SD: What was your father’s argument?
swa: SD: Baba yako alikuwa na mtazamo gani?

eng: Mrie: I have no idea.
swa: Mrie: Sifahamu kabisa.

eng: But maybe they were just convinced by these stories that the regime has been telling them: that this is an Islamic movement and they will kill you, and that you will lose everything.
swa: Labda walikuwa wanashawishiwa tu na hadithi hizi kuwa serikali ilishawaambia: kuwa hizi ni harakati za kiislamu, na watakuua, na kuwa, utapoteza kila kitu.

eng: I think that for the big families- my family is one of them—they are so afraid.
swa: Nafikiri kwa familia kubwa—familia yangu ni miongoni mwao—wanaogopa sana.

eng: They know that when the regime will fall they will lose almost everything, because when the regime was in control they knew they could do anything and no one would punish them.
swa: Wanajua kuwa, kama utawala utaachia ngazi, watapoteza kila kitu, kwa sababu, serikali ilipokuwa na mamlaka yote ya kuongoza, walijua wangeweza kufanya lolote na kusingekuwa na yeyote wa kuwapa adhabu.

eng: They could do all the stealing, the cheating, the robberies.
swa: Wangeweza kuiba, kudanganya na unyang’anyi.

eng: For me, I understand the rich families or the families that are in power, but I don’t understand the poor families who support Assad.
swa: Kwa upande wangu, ninapata mantiki ya kinachofanyika kwa familia tajiri au familia zilizo madarakani, lakini sizielewi familia masikini zinazomuunga mkono Assad.

eng: I remember my neighbors…they were so poor.
swa: Ninawakumbuka majirani zangu… walikuwa masikini sana.

eng: I’d wonder, why are you supporting this regime?
swa: Nilishangaa, ni kwa nini mnaendelea kuunga mkono mfumo wa utawala?

eng: What did the regime do for you?
swa: Serikali imekufanyia nini?

eng: After a while we discovered it’s like a religious thing for them.
swa: Baada ya muda fulani, tuligundua kuwa, kwao, ilikuwa ni kama aina fulani hivi ya dini.

eng: In the last years, it was Hafez Al Assad, and now it's Bashar Al Assad The people worship these guys.
swa: Kwa miaka ya hivi karibuni, alikuwa ni Hafez Al Assad, na sasa ni Bashar Al Assad. Watu wanawaabudu hawa jamaa.

eng: Since the revolution began, I kept telling people that the protesters who are in the streets, the opposition, they are not monsters.
swa: Tangu mapinduzi yalipoanza, niliendelea kuwaambia watu kuwa, waandamanaji walioko mitaani, wapinzani, sio wakatili.

eng: I fled to Turkey with the help of the Free Syrian Army.
swa: Nilisafiri kwa ndege hadi Uturuki kwa msaada wa Jeshi Huru la Syria.

eng: They were so nice to me and they helped me.
swa: Walikuwa wakarimu kwangu na walinisaidia sana.

eng: They knew that I’m an Alawite, but they didn’t kill me as the government is always trying to say.
swa: Walifahamu kuwa mimi ni miongoni mwa watu wa Alawite, lakini hawakuniua kama jinsi ambayo serikali kila mara inavyojaribu kusema,

eng: SD: Do you think they are changing their opinion at all?
swa: SD: Unadhani wanabadili mitazamo yao?

eng: Do you think the community is changing its opinion at all?
swa: Unadhani jamii inabadili mtazamo wake?

eng: Mrie: Now they are stuck in the middle.
swa: Mrie: Kwa sasa wapo katikati.

eng: They are losing their children in battle.
swa: Wanapoteza watoto wao kwenye mapigano.

eng: They are losing their generation in the army.
swa: Wanapoteza uzao wao katika jeshi.

eng: So they know that the government is not making any good for them, but at the same time they are so afraid of the opposition.
swa: Kwa hiyo, wanatambua kuwa serikali haiwafanyii jambo lolote zuri, lakini, wakati huohuo, wanaogopa sana kuwa kinyume na serikali.

eng: We have Islamist elements in the revolution, and it makes them afraid.
swa: Tuna chembechembe za kiislam katika mapinduzi, na hizi zinawafanya wawe na hofu sana.

eng: They are in the middle. They know that the government is not helping them, but at the same time they are afraid of the opposition. I have been hearing stories about how, when the dead bodies come to the villages of the Alawites, all the village starts to curse Bashar Al Assad and curse his government because he’s not protecting them and they are sacrificing themselves for someone who is not making any efforts.
swa: Nimekuwa nikisikia habari za kwa vipi, na lini miili ya watu waliokufa ilivyoletwa katika vijiji vya watu wa Alawite, vijiji vyote vikaanza kumlaani Bashar Al Assad na Serikali yake kwa kuwa hawezi kuwalinda na wanajitolea kwa mtu asiyeweka juhudi yoyote.

eng: SD: From what we keep hearing, the regime has scared the Alawite community so much that they think it’s a battle for survival, life or their death.
swa: SD: Kwa kile tunachoendelea kukisikia, serikali imeiogopesha sana jamii ya Alawite kiasi kwamba wanafikiri kuwa ni mapigano ya kuokoa uhai, maisha au vifo vyao.

eng: How do you think that you can calm down those fears?
swa: Unafikiri ni kwa namna gani utaweza kuiondoa hofu hiyo?

eng: Mrie: The problem in this community is that they won’t understand.
swa: Mrie: Tatizo la jamii hii ni kuwa, hawataelewa.

eng: All they know is that if you were an Alawite and you were against the regime, your punishment will be doubled.
swa: Wanachokifahamu wao ni kuwa, kama ulikuwa mtu wa Alawite, na ulikuwa mpinzani wa serikali, adhabu yako itakuwa mara mbili.

eng: If they just saw the stories and just turned on the TV and heard the slogans, they would know that this is not a revolution against them.
swa: Laiti wangefuatilia habari na kutazama televisheni na wangezisikia kauli mbiu, wangejua kuwa haya si mapinduzi dhidi yao.

eng: SD: Right now in the Alawite community, if somebody stands up, like you, and supports the revolution, what happens? Mrie: They would kill his mom. SD: They say that?
swa: SD: Wakati huu katika jamii ya watu wa Alawite, kama mtu atasimama imara, kama ilivyo wewe, na akaunga mkono mapinduzi, kitu gani kitatokea?

eng: Mrie: No, but it happened to me.
swa: Mrie: Hapana, lakini ilinitokea mimi.

eng: I’m not a terrorist.
swa: Mimi siyo gaidi.

eng: I didn’t do anything wrong.
swa: Sikufanya jambo lolote baya.

eng: I just stepped out from my small community and said that I am with the revolution, I am with my people.
swa: Nilijiondoa tu kutoka kwenye jamii yangu ndogo na kusema kuwa nipo upande wa mapinduzi, nipo na watu wangu.

eng: I’m not going to witness all this bloodshed and keep quiet.
swa: Sitaweza kuendelea kushuhudia damu inavyomwagika halafu nikaa kimya.

eng: It’s not a political cause, it’s now a human cause…this is a revolution for us, for our children, for our grandchildren.
swa: Hali hii haisababishwi na siasa, kwa sasa inasababishwa na binadamu…haya ni mapinduzi kwa ajili yetu, kwa ajili ya watoto wetu, kwa ajili ya babu na bibi zetu.

eng: SD: The whole regime could change tomorrow.
swa: SD: Serikali yote inaweza kubadilika kesho.

eng: Whenever it happens, how is this community going to react?
swa: Vyovyote itakavyokuwa, unafikiri jamii hii italipokeaje hili?

eng: How is Syria going to change if you have so much fear within the Alawite community?
swa: Syria itabadilika vipi kama bado kuna hofu kubwa miongoni mwa jamii ya watu wa Alawite?

eng: Mrie: Right now we have liberated areas.
swa: Mrie: Hadi sasa tuna maeneo ambayo yapo huru.

eng: There are Alawites in those liberated areas, so you can see samples of a new Syria, how it’s going to be. not killing the Alawites, they are not kicking them out of their houses.
swa: Kuna watu wa Alawite katika maeneo hayo, kwa hiyo unaweza kuona mfano wa Syria mpya, jinsi itakavyokuwa. hauwaui watu wa jamii ya Alawite, hawawaondoi katika nyumba zao.

eng: We are all one.
swa: Sisi ni kitu kimoja.

eng: We are just a good community.
swa: Sisi ni jamii iliyo njema.

eng: Not because of Bashar Al Assad, because we are a peaceful people.
swa: Sio kwa sababu ya Bashar Al Assad, sababu ni kuwa, sisi ni watu wenye amani.

eng: SD: There are some Alawites in the coalition, in the opposition.
swa: SD: Wapo baadhi ya watu wa Alawite katika serikali ya mpito, kwa upande wa upinzani.

eng: Are they people that the larger Alawite community respects?
swa: Ni watu ambao wanaheshimika kwa jamii kubwa ya Alawite?

eng: Are they people that can be leaders and help the community?
swa: Ni watu ambao wanaweza kuja kuwa viongozi na wakaisaidia jamii?

eng: Mrie: The community hates the Alawites who are with Moaz al Khatib.
swa: Mrie: Jamii inawachukia hao watu wa Alawite ambao wako na Moaz al Khatib.

eng: They say these are not even Alawites—they are outcasts.
swa: Wanasema hawa wala sio watu wa jamii ya Alawite—ni watu waliojitenga.

eng: Loubna I’m living the same situation myself.
swa: Loubna Ninaishi maisha ya namna hii hii.

eng: They broke into my house.
swa: Waliingia nyumbani kwangu.

eng: They stole all my things.
swa: Waliiba vitu vyangu vyote.

eng: They stole my papers from my college.
swa: Waliiba karatasi zangu za chuoni.

eng: All I got from my Alawite community, who are supporters of the regime, was just bad words on Facebook.
swa: Yote haya yalifanywa na watu wa jamii yangu ya watu wa Alawite ambao wanaiunga mkono serikali, yalikuwa ni maneno mabaya tu katika ukurasa wa facebook.

eng: SD: What did they say?
swa: SD: Walisemaje?

eng: Mrie: That you deserved it and we wish that the same thing that happened to your mom will happen to you.
swa: Mrie: Kuwa ulistahili na tunaombea lililomtokea mama yako litokee na kwako.

eng: SD: There might always be some anger against the Alawites for standing behind Assad?
swa: SD: Yawezekana wakati wote kukawa na kiasi fulani cha hasira dhidi ya watu wa Alawite kwa kumuunga mkono Assad?

eng: What does that mean for Syria?
swa: Hii inamaanisha nini kwa nchi ya Syria?

eng: Mrie: In Syria the shelling is still going on and everyday we have more dead people.
swa: Mrie: Nchini Syria, mabomu bado yanaendelea kulipuliwa na kila siku watu wanaendelea kufa.

eng: So we can’t really decide now the shape of the future Syria.
swa: Kwa hiyo, kwa sasa hatuwezi kwa hakika, kuamua muonekano wa Syria ijayo.

eng: We know that revenge doesn’t build a country, doesn’t build democracy.
swa: Tunajua kuwa. Kulipiza kisasi hakujengi nchi wala demokrasia.

eng: We went in the streets and made sacrifices to make a new country; revenge will not help us to do this.
swa: Tuliingia mitaani na kujitoa sadaka ili kuijenga nchi mpya. Visasi havitatusaidia kulifanikisha hili.

eng: But we will punish the people who did make mistakes, who killed.
swa: Lakini tutawap adhabu watu waliofanya makosa, wale walioua.
