eng: (We) immediately asked the Myanmar Embassy in Malaysia about this issue at 5 pm and again at 8 pm via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
swa: Mara moja, tuliuuliza ubalozi wa Mynmar huko Malasia kuhusiana na tukio hilo mapema majira ya saa 11 jioni na tuliwauliza tena saa saa 2 usiku kupitia Wizara ya Mambo ya ndani.

eng: The Ambassador said the news was false.
swa: Balozi alituambia kuwa habari hizi zilikuwa ni za uongo

eng: A Myanmar national put 11 red roses in front of Malaysia's Embassy in Yangon in honor of Myanmar migrants killed in Malaysia.
swa: Raia wa Myanmar akiweka maua waridi ya rangi nyekundu 11 mbele ya Ubalozi wa Malasia hukoYangon kwa heshima ya raia wa Mynmar waliouawa huko Malasia.

eng: Photo - Ye Moe's Facebook.
swa: Picha – Ukurasa wa Facebook wa Ye Moe.

eng: Wai Lin Oo expressed his frustration with the Embassy's response:
swa: Wai Lin Oo alionesha kusikitishwa kwake na majibu ya Ubalozi:

eng: And they charge us extreme taxes.
swa: Ni dhahiri kuwa kuna matukio haya!

eng: I can't even mention in words how they often reprimand ( citizens who are seeking refuge in the Embassy). When can we depend on Myanmar government?
swa: Kama unataka kuthibitisha maneno ya ubalozi, andaa safari ya kwenda Mynmar kuchukua miili ya watu waliopoteza maisha.

eng: It's really discouraging.
swa: Fang Ran alikazia nilichotangulia kukisema.

eng: Myo Set compared how the governments of other countries are behaving when faced with a similar situation: When a Japanese was killed in 2007 in Myanmar, a Japan Minister came at once.
swa: Mjapani mmoja alipouawa nchini Mynmar mwaka 2007, waziri wa Japani aliiingilia kati mara moja.

eng: When Myanmar workers had issues with a Korean factory owner, the Korean Embassy suddenly became involved in the case.
swa: Pale wafanyakazi wa Mynmar walipokuwa na kutokuelewana na Mkorea mmoja ambaye alikuwa ni mmiliki wa kiwanda fulani, Ubalozi wa Korea mara moja uliingilia kati shauri hilo.

eng: North Korea cleared away the books about Kim Jong Ill from book shops in Myanmar.
swa: Korea ya Kaskazini waliviondoa vitabu vya Kim Jong wa III haraka sana kutoka katika maktaba mbalimbali nchini Myanmar.

eng: What a shame!
swa: Nni aibu gani hii!

eng: US came down to Myanmar once there were issues of Yettaw.
swa: Marekani walifika haraka Myanmar pale tu lilipotokea suala laYettaw.

eng: Our turn?
swa: Msimamo wetu?

eng: In Malaysia, the Ambassador's mouth got a stroke.
swa: Huko Malasia, mdomo wa Balozi ulipatwa na ganzi.

eng: Ministry of Information is crippled and Myanmar government is paralyzed.
swa: Wizara ya Mawasiliano imepatwa na kilema na serikali ya Myanmar imepooza.

eng: We are Burmese, a community page of Myanmar citizens around the world questioned the silence of NGOs and media regarding the abuses suffered by Buddhists in Malaysia:
swa: Sisi ni Raia wa Barma , ukurasa wa jumuia ya raia wa Myanmar waishio pande zote za dunia ulihoji ukimya wa mashirika binafsi na vyombo vya habari kufuatia udhalilishaji wanaokabiliana nao watu wa jamii ya budha nchini Malasia:

eng: When riots in Meikhtilar Township in Myanmar happened, (the global) media and international organizations (like the) UN, Human Rights Watch (reported) about it and some even exaggerated the (situation), labeling it ethnic cleansing, genocide, Muslims in Myanmar are being brutally massacred, or something like that....But why are they silent than normal about the current massacre in Malaysia targeting Myanmar Buddhists?
swa: Wakati vurugu zilipotokea huko katika mji wa Meikhtilar nchini Myanmar, vyombo vya habari vya kimataifa na mashirika ya kimataifa kama vile Umoja wa Kimataifa, shirika la Haki za Binadamu yaliripoti matukio haya na pia baadhi yao walipotosha hali halisi ya mambo, wengine wakisema ni mpango wa kufutilia mbali makabila fulani, mauaji ya halaiki, waislamu ya Myanmar wanauawa kikatili na mambo vyanayofanana na hayo..... lakini ni kwa nini kumekuwa na ukimya uliopitiliza kuhusiana na mauaji ya kikatili yaliyotokea nchini Malasia yanayowalenga wabudha wa Myanmar.

eng: How many lives must the Burmese Buddhists sacrifice further to put the (situation) on pages and screens?
swa: Wabudha wa Myanmar wajitoe mhanga kwa kiasi gani ili hali wanayokabiliana nayo ifahamike na kuchukuliwa hatua stahiki?

eng: Please show the so-called RIGHTS you all repeatedly use whenever you get every chance to make the Burmese Buddhists dishonorable in every page and every screen worldwide.
swa: Tafadhali onesha kile kinachofahamika kama HAKI ambacho kila mmoja wenu amekuwa akikitumia popote uonapo wabudha wa Myanmar wakifedheheshwa popote pale katika maandiko au kwa picha

eng: On June 4, when voices became louder and attacks became more serious, the Myanmar government issued an Aide Memoire to Malaysia's Ambassador in Myanmar urging the Malaysian government to investigate the issue immediately and take legal actions against responsible persons.
swa: Mapema Juni 4, kadiri hali hii ilivyozidi kupigiwa kelele, mashambulizi nayo ndivyo nayo yalivyozidi kushika kasi, Serikali ya Myanmar ilitoa tamko la kidiplomasia kwa balozi wa Malasia nchini Myanmar likiitaka serikali ya Malasia kufanyia uchunguzi matuko haya haraka iwezekanavyo na kuwachukulia hatua za kisheria watu wote watakaohusika na matukio haya.

eng: On June 6, Malaysia reported that 900 Myanmar nationals were detained during a security sweep.
swa: Manamo tarehe 6 Juni, serikali ya Malaysia ilitaarifu kuwa raia 900 wa Myanmar walishikiliwa wakati wa msako wa kiulinzi.

eng: Myanmar government is preparing to send a team of special representatives to Malaysia.
swa: Serikali ya Myanmar inajiandaa kupeleka jopo la wataalam nchini Malasia.

eng: Since some of the injured Myanmar migrants cannot afford the hospital bills, the Malaysia Kampung Free Funeral Service Social Team (Kampung FFSS) gave donation to the victims.
swa: Kwa kuwa baadhi ya wahamiaji wa Myanmar hawezi kumudu gharama za matibabu, Timu ya Huduma za bure za Mazishi ya Kampung nchini Malasia (Kampung FFSS) ilitoa msaada kwa wahanga.

eng: U Aung Ko Win, President of the Kanbawza Bank who also runs Myanmar Airways International (MAI) donated $50,000 US dollars and cut the MAI air ticket fees of the Malaysia-Myanmar route by 50% for the convenience of migrants who wish to go back to Myanmar.
swa: U Aung Ko Win, ambaye ni Rais wa Benki ya Kanbawza ambaye pia ni mmiliki wa Shirika la Ndege la Kimataifa la Myanmar (MAI) alichangia dola za Kimarekani 50,000 na kutoa tiketi za ndege kwa punguzo la asilimia 50 kwa safari ya Malasia-Myanmar ili kuwarahisishia wahamiaji wote wanaotaka kurudi nchini Myanmar.

eng: Another well-known wealthy personnel, U Zaw Zaw, who is President of Myanmar Football Federation announced that he will donate 1,000 air tickets for those who want to go back to Myanmar, plus additional $20,000 US dollars donation to Kampung FFSS.
swa: Tajiri mwingine mashuhuri sana, U Zaw Zaw, ambaye ni Rais wa Shirikisho la Soka la Myanmar alitangaza kuwa atachangia tiketi 1,000 za ndege kwa wote wanaohitaji kurudi nchini Myanmar, pamoja na kuchangia dola za kimarekani 20,000 Kampung FFSS.

eng: Many netizens on Facebook changed their profile pictures to black to grieve the deaths of Myanmar citizens in Malaysia.
swa: Watumiaji wengi wa mtandao katika mtandao wa Facebook walibadilisha picha zao na katika taarifa zao na kuweka picha nyeusi kuomboleza vifo ya raia wa Myanmar vilivyotokea huko Malasia.

eng: Iran Voices is created based on Ushahidi's successful project.
swa: Sauti za Iran ni mradi ulioundwa kwa kutumia mafanikio ya mradi wa Ushahidi.

eng: Iran Voices aims to report about Iranian small cities and villages and send by emailing people's requests and concerns to the authorities and MPs.
swa: Sauti za Iran inakusudia kuripoti habari kuhusu miji midogo na vijiji vya Iran na vile vile kukusanya maombi na matatizo ya wananchi na kuyatuma kwa serikali na wabunge.

eng: At the end of 2012, the Nigerian Ministry of Agriculture made public its plans to provide free mobile phones to rural farmers.
swa: Mwisho wa mwaka wa 2012, Wizara ya Kilimo ya Nigeria ilitangaza mipango yake ya kutoa Simu za Mkono bure kwa wakulima vijijini.

eng: According to this report:
swa: Kulingana na ripoti hii:

eng: Ibukun Idusote, Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Agriculture, was reported as saying that the Federal Ministry of Agriculture would procure ten million mobile phones, worth about N60 billion, from China and the US for free distribution to rural farmers across the country.
swa: Idusote Ibukun, Katibu Mkuu wa Wizara ya Kilimo katika serikali ya Shirikisho la Nigeria, aliripotiwa akisema kuwa Wizara hiyo lingetafuta fedha za kununua simu za Mkono zipatazo milioni kumi zenye thamani ya N60 bilioni, kutoka China na Marekani kwa ajili ya kuzisambaza bure kwa wakulima vijijini nchini kote.

eng: This triggered reverberations in the Nigerian blogosphere.
swa: Mpango huo uliibua gumzo katika ulimwengu wa blogu za Nigeria.

eng: Kikiowo Ileowo asks where the government got the statistics – that warrants 10 million mobile phones for 10 million farmers – from:
swa: Kikiowo Ileowo anauliza mahali ambapo serikali ilitoa takwimu - kwamba Simu za Mkono milioni 10 zilihitajika kwa wakulima milioni 10:

eng: The question… is where exactly are the 10million farmers?
swa: swali ni ... wakulima milioni 10 wako wapi hasa?

eng: Are they from the army of the unemployed 16, 074, 295 or from the already employed 51, 181, 884.
swa: Je, wao ni wale kutoka jeshi la Wanijeria 16, 074, 295 wasiokuwa na ajira au kutoka kwa 51, 181, 884 walioajiriwa.

eng: If their answer is the former, what exactly are they producing that Nigeria has not become a hub of everything food?
swa: Kama jibu ni wale wasiokuwa na ajira, ni nini hasa wanazalisha ambacho hakijaiifanya Nigeria kuwa kitovu cha uzalishaji wa chakula?

eng: Now, understand that a large portion of food production in Nigeria is done through mechanized farming which makes use of less manual labour.
swa: Sasa, elewa kwamba sehemu kubwa ya uzalishaji wa chakula nchini Nigeria hufanyika kwa njia ya kilimo kinachotumia mashine inayotumia idadi ndogo ya wafanya kazi.

eng: The 'farmers' Mr. President wants to provide handset for are subsistent farmers who produce what they mostly consume in their homes.
swa: Wakulima' ambao Mheshimiwa Rais anataka kutoa simu za Mkono kwao ni wakulima ambao huzalisha chakula kwa ajili ya kukidhi mahitaji ya chakula majumbani mwao.

eng: I have a garden at the back of my house; does that qualify me as a recipient of the 'Jona-phone'?
swa: Nina bustani nyuma ya nyumba yangu; je hiyo inanifanya nikidhi vigego vya kupokea 'Simu za Jonathani'?

eng: I see no reason why the president in conjunction with his minister of Agriculture would insult the collective intelligence of Nigerians by playing to the gallery with a noble idea that has revolutionised countries like Uganda, Kenya and India.
swa: Sioni sababu kwa nini rais kwa kushirikiana na waziri wake wa Kilimo wangeweza kutusi akili za Wanigeria wote kwa kufanyia maigizo wazo zuri kama hili ambalo limebadilisha nchi kama Uganda, Kenya na India.

eng: There has since been a correction on the real cost of the phones:
swa: Kumekuwa na marekebisho juu ya gharama halisi ya simu:

eng: …the Minister of Agriculture, Dr. Akinwunmi Adesina, has corrected the report that the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry, Mrs. Ibukun Odusote, said the phones would be bought by the government at the cost of N60 billion, his explanation that the phones will be supplied to farmers through Public/Private Sector partnership…
swa: Waziri wa Kilimo, Dk Akinwunmi Adesina, amesahihisha maelezo ya ripoti ya Katibu Mkuu wa Wizara, Bi Ibukun Odusote, iliyosema kuwa simu za Mkono zingeweza kununuliwa na serikali kwa gharama ya N60 bilioni, maelezo yake ni kwamba Simu za Mkono zitatolewa kwa wakulima kupitia ushirikiano wa Umma na Sekta Binafsi ...

eng: Dr. Akinwumi Adesina, Nigeria's Minister of Agriculture
swa: Dr. Akinwumi Adesina, Waziri wa Kilimo wa Nigeria

eng: Dr Adesina, the Minister of Agriculture rose up in defence of the project.
swa: Dk Adesina, Waziri wa Kilimo aliutetea mradi huo.

eng: In a press release he says:
swa: Katika taarifa yake kwa vyombo vya habari anasema:

eng: When I came on board as minister of agriculture in July of 2011, I found a corrupt and totally inefficient fertilizer sector. The government was spending huge amounts of money on direct procurement and distribution of subsidized fertilizer, but less than 11% of farmers got the fertilizers.
swa: Wakati mimi nilifika kwenye bodi ya Kilimo kama waziri wa kilimo mnamo Julai 2011, serikali ilikuwa inatumia kiasi kikubwa cha fedha kwenye manunuzi ya moja kwa moja na usambazaji wa mbolea ya ruzuku, lakini chini ya 11% ya wakulima waliipata hiyo mbolea.

eng: Some of the fertilizers paid for by government were never delivered to the warehouses.
swa: Kiasi fulani cha mbolea iliyolipiwa na serikali haikuwa ikifikishwa katika maghala.

eng: Some of the fertilizer delivered contained more sand than fertilizer while a large portion of the fertilizer subsidized by government found its way across our borders to neighbouring countries where it was sold at prevailing market prices.
swa: Kiasi fulani cha mbolea hiyo kilikuwa na mchanga mwingi kuliko mbolea wakati sehemu kubwa ya mbolea hiyo ya ruzuku ya serikali ilivushwa nje ya mipaka yetu na kupelekwa katika nchi jirani ambapo iliuuzwa kwa bei halisi ya soko.

eng: This technology-mediated solution, he asserts, ended the corruption associated with fertilizer distribution:
swa: Suluhisho hili la kiteknolojia, yeye anadai lilimaliza tatizo la rushwa kwenye usambazaji mbolea:

eng: We ended four decades of corruption in the fertilizer sector within 90 days of my assumption of office as minister.
swa: Tulimaliza ufisadi uliodumu kwa miongo minne katika sekta ya mbolea ndani ya siku 90 baada ya kuingia ofisini kama waziri.

eng: How did we do this?
swa: Tulifanikiwaje?

eng: We were able get subsidized high quality fertilizer and seeds to our rural farmers by introducing the GES (Growth Enhancement Support) scheme in April of 2012.
swa: Tuliweza kufanya mbolea na mbegu za ruzuku zenye viwango vya juu zipatikane kwa wakulima wetu wa vijijini na kuanzisha GES (Msaada wa Uwezeshaji wa Kuimarisha) mwezi Aprili ya 2012.

eng: The GES scheme delivers inputs (fertilizers and seeds) to farmers directly by using farmers' cell phones.
swa: Mpango wa GES huwezesha kupatikana kwa mbolea na mbegu kwa wakulima moja kwa moja kwa kutumia simu za Mkono za wakulima.

eng: We created an electronic platform (e-wallet) on which we registered farmers and agro dealers who own shops that sell farm inputs all over the country.
swa: Tumetengeneza jukwaa la kielektroniki (mkoba-pepe) ambako tuliwasajili wakulima na wafanyabiashara wa mazao ya kilimo wanaomiliki maduka yanayouza pembejeo za kilimo kote nchini.

eng: To date we have registered 4.2 million farmers and about 900 agro dealers.
swa: Hadi sasa tumeweza kuwasajili wakulima milioni 4.2 na pia wafanyabiashara wa mazao ya kilimo 900.

eng: The Minister thinks that although many Nigerian farmers are illiterate but are able to use mobile telephones:
swa: Waziri anadhani kwamba ingawa wakulima wengi Nigeria hawajui kusoma na kuandika lakini wana uwezo wa kutumia simu ya mkononi:

eng: Some people think that our farmers are uneducated and cannot use cell phones.
swa: Baadhi ya watu wanadhani kwamba wakulima wetu hawana elimu na hovyo hawawezi kutumia simu za mkononi.

eng: The evidence does not support that.
swa: Ushahidi haukubaliani na madai hayo.

eng: Under the GES scheme, we made it possible for farmers to transact business in their own local languages using their cell phones.
swa: Chini ya mpango wa GES, tuliwezesha wakulima kufanya miamala ya kibiashara kwa kutumia lugha zao za kiasili kwa kutumia simu za mkononi.

eng: From data we collected based on farmers’ use of cell phones to access fertilizers and seeds last year, we found that the total number of transactions done by phone with respect to the GES scheme was 4.9 million.
swa: Kutokana takwimu tulizozikusanya kwa kuangalia namna wakulima wanavyotumia simu za mkononi kupata mbolea na mbegu kwa mwaka jana, tuligundua kwamba idadi ya miamala iliyofanywa kwa njia ya simu katika mpango wa GES ilifikia 4,900,000.

eng: Of these, 1.2 million were in English, 620,000 were in Pidgin, 2.2 million were in Hausa, and 854,000 were in Yoruba and 344 were in Igbo.
swa: Kati ya hizi, milioni 1.2 ilikuwa katika Kiingereza, 620,000 ilikuwa katika ki-Pidgin, milioni 2.2 ilikuwa katika Kihausa, na 854,000 ilikuwa katika ki-Yoruba na 344 ilikuwa katika ki-Igbo.

eng: From this data, we have no doubt that our farmers are well able to use cell phones.
swa: Kutokana na takwimu hizi, hatuna shaka kwamba wakulima wetu wanao uwezo wa kutumia simu za mkononi.

eng: Technology, according to the Dr Adesina, aided his judgement that there would be no food crisis after floods swept through some parts of the country:
swa: Teknolojia, kwa mujibu wa Dk Adesina, imesaidia ubashiri wake kwamba hakutakuwa na ukosefu wa chakula hata baada ya mafuriko kukumba baadhi ya maeneo ya nchi:

eng: When the floods occurred, there was panic in the land... I was not moved.
swa: Wakati mafuriko yalipotokea, kulikuwa na taharuki katika nchi ... mimi sikubabaika kabisa.

eng: We used modern technology to guide our decision.
swa: Tulitumia teknolojia ya kisasa kuongoza uamuzi wetu.

eng: Using remote sensing and satellite imagery, we mapped out the extent of the flood and determined that no more than 1.17% of our total cultivated area was affected by the floods.
swa: Kwa kutumia teknolojia ya kujua maeneo na matumizi ya picha za satelaiti, tulichora picha za kiwango cha mafuriko na kufahamu kuwa si zaidi ya asilimia 1.17 ya eneo lililolimwa lilikuwa limeathirika na mafuriko.

eng: Our detractors wanted the world to believe the opposite, that food crisis was imminent.
swa: Wapinzani wetu walitaka dunia kuamini kinyume, kwamba ukosefu wa chakula usingekwepeka.

eng: They were wrong.
swa: Walikuwa wamekosa.

eng: Today, five months after the floods, we do not have a food crisis.
swa: Leo hii, miezi mitano baada ya mafuriko, hatuna ukosefu wa chakula.

eng: Nonetheless, some netizens still have unanswered questions.
swa: Hata hivyo, baadhi wana-mtandao bado wana maswali yasiyojibiwa.

eng: Olusola Adegbeti asks:
swa: Olusola Adegbeti anauliza:

eng: One must then poignantly ask, though it be a rhetorical question, if the purchase and distribution of GSM phones to hundreds of farmers spread across the length and breadth of a country so large as Nigeria is the most critical and challenging of issues bedevilling the Nigerian agricultural sector at the moment?
swa: Mtu anaweza kuuliza, ingawa ni swali lisilohitaji jibu, kama ununuzi na usambazaji wa Simu za Mkono za GSM kwa mamia ya wakulima walioenea katika urefu na upana wa nchi hiyo kubwa, ni muhimu zaidi kuliko changamoto ya masuala yanayoikumba sekta ya kilimo ya Nigeria wakati huu?

eng: Your guess is as good as mine.
swa: Hisia zako kuhusiana na suala hili ni nzuri kama langu.

eng: Running on the heels of the above, it is convenient to say that one does not need the wisdom of Solomon or the prophetic insight of Isaiah to be led in the direction of the myriad of issues that have since rendered the agricultural sector beggarly, issues such as lack of easy access to land for farming, absence of reliable and corruption-free financial institutions to empower farmers acquire the required modern machinery for mechanised and commercial farming that is usually the backbone of every nation, lack of easy access to requisite technology and agro-chemical support-structure for sustained annual and perennial farming as well as animal husbandry....
swa: Nikirejelea swala hili, ni rahisi kusema kwamba mtu hana haja ya hekima ya Solomoni au ufahamu unabii wa Isaya kwa kuongozwa katika mwelekeo kuwa kunayo masuala mengi ambayo tangu kitambo yameikumba sekta ya kilimo. Masuala kama vile kama ukosefu wa upatikanaji rahisi wa ardhi ya kilimo, ukosefu wa taasisi za kuaminika na zisizo na mianya ya rushwa ili kuwawezesha wakulima kupata mashine za kisasa zinazohitajika kwa ajili ya kilimo cha kibiashara ambacho kwa kawaida huwa ndio uti wa mgongo wa kila taifa, ukosefu wa upatikanaji rahisi wa teknolojia zinazohitajika katika kilimo na mfumo wa kuwezesha kupatikana kwa dawa za kilimo kwa ajili ya kilimo endelevu kwa mwaka mzima pamoja na ufugaji ....

eng: The Sun asks if farmers really need new mobile phones, when they already have one or have other sources of information?
swa: Jarida la Sun linauliza kama kweli wakulima wanahitaji Simu mpya za Mkono, wakati tayari wana namna moja au nyingine ya vyanzo vya habari?

eng: The telephone is also clearly not the best way to reach farmers who mostly live in the rural areas.
swa: Ni wazi pia kuwa Simu ya Mkono si njia bora ya kufikia wakulima ambao wengi wao wanaishi katika maeneo ya vijijini.

eng: Rural information centres, traditional communication models and the radio are much better channels.
swa: Vituo vya habari vya vijiji na redio ni njia bora zaidi.

eng: There are also many more direct initiatives through which the government can boost agricultural production in the country, than provision of telephones.
swa: Kuna njia ambazo serikali inaweza kukuza uzalishaji wa kilimo katika nchi, kuliko utoaji wa simu.

eng: More importantly, the government does not need to buy telephones for farmers because those among them who could use such phones, already have them.
swa: Muhimu zaidi, serikali haina haja ya kununua simu kwa ajili ya wakulima kwa sababu wale kati yao ambao wanaweza kutumia simu hizo, tayari wanazo.

eng: With handsets selling for as low as between N2000 and N3000 in the country, any farmer that is worth the name can afford to own one, and most likely has one already.
swa: Kwa vile Simu za Mkono huuzwa kwa bei ya chini kama kati ya N2000 na N3000 nchini Nigeria, mkulima yeyote anaitwa mkulima anaweza kumudu simu, na zaidi huenda anayo tayari.

eng: If they do not, what the government needs to do is to empower them to be able to afford such a basic tool.
swa: Kama hawana, kitu ambacho serikali inahitaji kufanya ni kuwapa uwezo wa kuweza kujimudu ili waweze kununua chombo hicho cha msingi.

eng: Disu Kimor thinks that it’s another white elephant project:
swa: Disu Kimor anadhani kwamba mradi huu una harufu ya ujanja ujanja:

eng: Such white elephant projects will only reinforce the perception of Nigeria as a laughing stock of the rest of the world where we like to teach the blind sign language.
swa: Miradi ya ujanja ujanja kama hii itaimarisha mtazamo wa uliosambaa duniani kote kuwa wa-Nigeria ni vichekesho tufundoshao kipofu lugha ya ishara.

eng: Any developing country such as Nigeria, wishing to develop its agricultural sector will focus direct government intervention to help farmers and boost food production on achieving steady supply of working capital, improve research and development, water supply, ensure low cost of fuel and labour, (corruption-free) subsidy on farming equipment and basic infrastructure.
swa: Nchi yoyote inayoendelea kama Naijeria inayotaka kuendeleza sekta ya kilimo, italenga kuifanya serikali iingilie kati kusaidia wakulima kuongeza uzalishaji wa chakula, kuboresha utafiti na maendeleo, maji, kuhakikisha gharama ya chini ya mafuta na kazi, ( bila rushwa) pia ruzuku kwa kilimo vifaa na miundombinu ya msingi.

eng: Disu concludes:
swa: Disu anahitimisha:

eng: One day, posterity will judge the quangos and political leaders of this country whose main pre-occupation is keeping the country on its knees or embezzle and waste much needed public funds.
swa: Siku moja, vizazi vijavyo vitahukumu vigogo na wanasiasa wa nchi hii ambao kazi kubwa ni kuitafuna nchi au kutumia vibaya fedha za umma zinazohitajika sana.

eng: The trial of Tunisian FEMEN activist Amina Tyler, who was arrested on May 19 after she graffitied the word FEMEN on the wall of cemetery in Kairouan, 184km from the capital Tunis, will resume on June 5.
swa: Kesi ya Amina Tyler, mwanaharakati wa FEMEN raia wa Tunisia, ambaye alikamatwa Mei 19 baada ya kuchora neno FEMEN kwenye ukuta wa makaburi ya Kairouan, kilomita 184 kutoka mji mkuu wa Tunis, itaendelea Juni 5.

eng: Amina's lawyers argued that she had the pepper spray for self-defense reasons, following the death threats she received last March, after she posted topless photographs of herself on Facebook.
swa: Wanasheria wa Amina walisema kwamba alikuwa na kifaa hicho kwa sababu ya kujilinda, kufuatia vitisho vya kuuawa alivyopata mwezi Machi, baada ya yeye kuwa ameweka picha inayomwonyesha bila nguo kifuani kwenye mtandao wa Facebook.

eng: Though she avoided a six-month jail-term for this charge, Amina remains in custody and now faces new charges: "undermining public morals", "desecrating a cemetery" and "belonging to a criminal organization" .
swa: Ingawa alikwepa kifungo cha miezi sita jela kwa mashtaka hayo, Amina bado yuko chini ya ulinzi na sasa anakabiliwa na mashtaka mapya: "kupuuza maadili ya jamii", "kudharu eneo la makaburi" na "kuwa mwanachama wa shirika la kihalifu" .

eng: These charges could land the 19-year-old in jail for several years.
swa: Madai haya yanaweza kumfunga jela kwa miaka kadhaa msichana huyu wa miaka 19.

eng: On 31 May, Amnesty International called upon the Tunisian authorities to release Amina.
swa: Tarehe 31 Mei, Shirika la Kimataifa la kutetea haki za binadamu la Amnesty International lilitoa wito kwa utawala wa Tunisia kumwachia Amina.

eng: The organization described the charges as "politically motivated and targeting her for her activism on women's rights".
swa: Shirika hilo liliyaelezea mashtaka hayo kama "masuala ya kisiasa yanayomlenga kwa sababu ya harakati zake za kutetea haki za wanawake".

eng: Silence of the so called "Democrats"?
swa: Kimya cha wanaojiita "Wanademokrasia"?

eng: The secular Tunisian opposition's lack of support to Amina, was met with criticism.
swa: Kukosekana kwa msaada kwa ajili ya Amina kutoka kwa Chama cha Upinzani kisicho cha kidini nchini Tunisia, kulikosolewa.

eng: Fearing to lose the future votes of the conservative electorate, it seems that leftist politicians have preferred to remain silent.
swa: Woga wa kupoteza kura za wapiga kura wahafidhina kwa siku za mbeleni, inaonekana kwamba wanasiasa wa mrengo wa kushoto waliona ni bora kubaki kimya.

eng: This is not the first time political parties from the left faced accusations of letting down their own "progressive" values.
swa: Hii si mara ya kwanza vyama vya siasa vya mrengo wa kushoto kukabiliwa na madai ya kudumaza tunu zake za kimaendeleo.

eng: For instance, they were also accused of adopting a weak stance on the case of Ghazi Beji and Jabeur Mejir, who were convicted to seven and half years in prison last year, over the publication of online content deemed offensive to Islam.
swa: Kwa mfano, pia walituhumiwa kwa kuchagua msimamo dhaifu kwenye kesi ya Ghazi Beji na Jabeur Mejir, ambao walipatikana na hatia na kufungwa kwa miaka saba na nusu jela mwaka jana, kwa uchapishaji wa maudhui mtandaoni yaliyoonyesha kukashifu Uislamu.

eng: In the Avaaz petition demanding the release of Amina, the support committee for the young FEMEN activist said :
swa: Katika hati ya Avaaz ya kushinikiza kuachiwa kwa Amina, kamati ya msaada kwa mwanaharakati huyo kijana wa FEMEN ilisema :

eng: Amina is back in prison!
swa: Amina amerudi gerezani!

eng: We were all deluded by the announcement that Amina was released over the possession of an incendiary object.
swa: Sisi wote tulipumbazwa na tangazo kwamba Amina aliachiliwa kwa mashitaka ya kumimiliki kifaa hatari.

eng: Amina is the prisoner of the Tunisian political hypocrisy and the silence of those claiming to be democrats but do not dare to take sides in this ongoing battle.
swa: Amina ni mfungwa wa unafiki wa kisiasa nchini Tunisia na kimya cha wale wanaojidai kuwa wanademokrasia lakini hawajaribu kuonyesha msimamo katika vita hivi vinavyoendelea.

eng: Tunisian writer Gilbert Naccache also criticized the proclaimed democrats' stance:
swa: Mwandishi wa Tunisia Gilbert Naccache pia alikosoa msimamo wa wanademokrasia uliotangazwa:

eng: It is really hard for democracy to make its way to our brains!
swa: Ni vigumu sana kwa demokrasia kupata nafasi kwenye akili zetu!

eng: Those claiming to be ready to fight until the end for freedom, (...) are denouncing an intolerable provocation when Amina expressed herself(...)
swa: Wale waliodai kuwa tayari kupambana mpaka mwisho kwa ajili ya uhuru, (...) wanakemea uchochezi usiovumilika wakati Amina alipojielezea (...)

eng: The pretexts used to condemn Amina, even by those who accused her of distracting attention away from the real problems or further dividing Tunisians, are in fact only finding a way not to assume their duty which is supporting Amina against slander and lies,(...) and supporting every individual's right to express him/herself in his/her own way.
swa: Hila zilizotumika kumhukumu Amina, pia kwa wale ambao walimtuhumu kwa kuhamisha usikivu kutoka kwenye matatizo halisi au kugawa zaidi wa-Tunisia, kwa kweli ni kutafuta njia tu si kubeba wajibu wao ambao ni kumsaidia Amina dhidi ya uzushi na uongo, (...) na kusaidia haki ya kila mtu kujieleza katika njia yake mwenyewe.

eng: Three other FEMEN activists, two French and one German are also set to stand trial on June 5.
swa: Wanaharakati wengine watatu wa FEMEN, Wafaransa wawili na Mjerumani mmoja pia wanatarajiwa kujibu mashtaka Juni 5.

eng: They each face a six-month imprisonment after they staged a topless protest outside a Tunis-based court on May 29 in support of Amina.
swa: Wanatarajiwa kufungwa kifungo cha miezi sita kwa kufanya maandamano wakiwa na vifua wazi nje ya makao ya mahakama ya Tunis mnamo Mei 29 kumuunga mkono Amina.

eng: Elia Saikaly's short movie catches the majestic beauty of Mount Everest at night in time-lapse.
swa: Sinema fupi za Elia Saikaly zimenasa uzuri mkuu wa Mlima Everesti nyakati za usiku kwa kila sekunde.

eng: He shares in his blog the experience of climbing to the summit of Mount Everest for the second time.
swa: Anasimulia kwenye blogu yake uzoefu wake wa kupanda hadi kilele cha Mlima Everest kwa mara ya pili.

eng: Two young Saudi men were arrested in the capital Riyadh by the Committee of the Promotion of Virtue and the Prevention of Vice (CPVPV) for allegedly insulting religion.
swa: Vijana wawili wa ki-Saudi walikamatwa katika mji mkuu wa Riyadh na Kamati ya Kukuza Maadili na Kuzuia Maovu (CPVPV) kwa madai ya kukashifu dini.

eng: Bader Al-Rasheed @BAlrasheed and Abdullah Al-Bilasi @3bdlla shared their story on Twitter.
swa: Bader Al-Rasheed @BAlrasheed na Abdullah Al-Bilasi @3bdlla walisimulia yaliyowapata kwenye mtandao wa twita.

eng: According to Al-Rasheed, they were sitting outside a cafe when a CPVPV's car passed by to call people to leave the area to perform evening prayers.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Al-Rasheed, walikuwa wamekaa nje ya mkahawa wakati gari la CPVPV lilipokuwa likipita kwa kuwaamuru watu kuondoka eneo hilo waende kwenye swala ya jioni.

eng: He said he argued with the CPVPV member whether sitting at public places at prayer times was illegal.
swa: Alisema yeye alibishana na mtumishi mmoja wa CPVPV kama kuketi katika maeneo ya umma wakati wa saa za swala ilikuwa kosa.

eng: Al-Rasheed later tweeted :
swa: Al-Rasheed baadaye alitwiti :

eng: @BAlrasheed: Because it was the first time I hear of this law and the heya’ (what CPVPV is informally referred to) acts arbitrarily sometimes, I went to their car and asked: is there a law that bans sitting in public places at prayer times?” 	@BAlrasheed: Kwa sababu ilikuwa ni mara ya kwanza mimi kusikia sheria hii na 'heya'(neno la mtaani wanalooitwa CPVPV) mambo holela wakati mwingine, nilikwenda katika gari lao na kuuliza: kuna sheria inayopiga marufuku kukaa katika maeneo ya umma wakati sala?"
The employee’s answer was that it’s haram (religiously forbidden), but Al-Rasheed interrupted saying:
swa: Jibu la mwajiriwa huyo lilikuwa kwamba ni haramu (imezuiliwa kidini), lakini Al-Rasheed aliingilia kati akisema:

eng: @BAlrasheed: Don't tell me what religion says, is there a law? 	@BAlrasheed: Usiniambie dini inavyosema, je kuna sheria?
Religion is a matter of personal choice.
swa: Dini ni suala la uamuzi binafsi.

eng: It's the law that I have to abide by."
swa: Ni sheria tu ndiyo ninalazimika kutii."

eng: According to Al-Rasheed, the employee was irritated and asked for his and his friend's identification cards.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Al-Rasheed, mtumishi huyo alikasirika na akadai kitambulisho chake na cha rafiki aliyekuwa naye.

eng: Then, the CPVPV member started threatening them and inciting the police official to take action against them.
swa: Kisha, mtumishi huyo wa CPVPV alianza kuwatishia na kuchochea maafisa wa polisi kuchukua hatua dhidi yao.

eng: Minutes later, another CPVPV car and a police car came to arrest them and took them to al-Sulaimaniyah police station.
swa: Dakika chache baadaye, gari lingine la CPVPV na gari la polisi lilikuja kuwakamata na kuwapeleka katika kituo cha polisi cha al-Sulaimaniyah.

eng: Al-Bilasi talked about the inhumane conditions in the cells: "It was small and overcrowded.
swa: Al-Bilasi alisimulia kuhusu hali ya mbaya na unyama katika selo:.. ".

eng: There weren't any beds or mattresses,” he says. “We slept on the floor.
swa: Hakukuwa na vitanda vyovyote au magodoro," alisema "Tulilala sakafuni.

eng: I asked an officer to let me sleep in the hallway but he just cursed me," he adds.
swa: Nilimwomba afisa magareza kuniruhusu nilale koridoni lakini yeye alinitukana tu, " anaongezea.

eng: The next morning, they were taken, handcuffed, to the Investigation and Prosecution Bureau.
swa: Asubuhi iliyofuata, walichukuliwa, wakiwa wamepigwa pingu mkononi, kupelekwa kwa Ofisi ya Upelelezi na Mashtaka.

eng: Upon arriving there, they were taken to a small room where they waited for hours before they were called separately for investigation.
swa: Baada ya kuwasili hapo, walipelekwa kwa chumba kidogo ambapo walisubiri kwa masaa kadhaa kabla ya wao kuitwa kivyao kwa ajili ya mahojiano.

eng: The investigator told Abdullah that CPVPV members and police officers are “not to be argued with but obeyed.”
swa: Mpelelezi alimwambia Abdullah kwamba mtumishi wa CPVPV na maafisa wa polisi "si watu wa kubishana nao bali kuwatii."

eng: Their nightmare came to an end when they were released after their parents bailed them out even though the investigator called what happened a "misunderstanding."
swa: Jinamizi lao lilifikia mwisho wakati walipoachiliwa baada ya wazazi wao kuwawekea dhamana ingawa mpelelezi aliliita tukio hilo kuwa ni "kutokuelewana."

eng: Religious police were not satisfied and demanded that the two men get tried.
swa: Polisi wa kidini hawakuridhishwa na kudai kwamba watu hao wawili washitakiwe.

eng: More absurdly, al-Bilasi and al-Rasheed reported a strange story about a Lebanese man they met in al-Sulaimaniyah police station who was arrested for a “religiously illegitimate smile”!
swa: Kichekesho zaidi, al-Bilasi na al-Rasheed waliripoti simulizi la mwaka kuhusu raia wa Lebanon waliyemkuta katika kituo cha polisi cha al-Sulaimaniyah ambaye alikamatwa kwa "tabasamu lisiloruhusiwa kidini"!

eng: @balrasheed: One of the more bizarre stories we came across during our detention was of a Lebanese salesman who was sentenced to five days imprisonment.
swa: @balrasheed: Moja ya mambo ya ajabu zaidi kukutana nayo selo ilikuwa ni mfanyabiashara wa Lebanon ambaye alihukumiwa kifungo cha siku tano.

eng: His crime: "A non-Sharia compliant smile."
swa: Kosa lake: "Tabasamu lisiloruhusiwa na Sharia."

eng: The incident happened on March 25, 2013.
swa: Tukio hilo lilitokea tarehe 25 Machi, 2013.

eng: Vachanalays (newspaper reading centres) are a familiar sight in most neighbourhoods in Bombay where locals read the papers and discuss the day’s news.
swa: Vachanalays (vituo vya kusoma magazeti) ni jambo la kawaida katika vitongoji vingi mjini Bombay ambapo wenyeji husoma magazeti na kujadili habari zilizotokea siku husika.

eng: Sans Serif reports how they are slowly going out of fashion.
swa: Sans Serif anaripoti jinsi vituo hivyo vinavyozidi kupitwa na wakati pole pole.

eng: The blog also highlights photoblogger M.S. Gopal's excellent photo essay on the subject at Mumbai Paused.
swa: Blogu hiyo pia inaonyesha picha nzuri inayojieleza ya mwanablogu wa picha M.S. Gopal juu ya maudhui hayo kwenye Mumbai Yasimamishwa.

eng: Francisco J. P. Chuquela, a collaborator of Global Voices' partner @Verdade Newspaper in Mozambique, reported this story for Global Voices
swa: Francisco J. P. Chuquela, anayefanya kazi na mshirika wa Global Voices @Verdade Newspaper nchini Msumbuji, aliripoti habari hii kwa ajili ya Global Voices

eng: Health professionals in Mozambique have been on strike for ten days leading to the halt of operations in many medical units throughout the country.
swa: Wafanyakazi wa sekta ya afya nchini Msumbiji wamekuwa katika mgomo uliodumu kwa siku kumi na kusababisha kusimama kwa huduma katika vitengo vingi vya kutoa huduma za afya kote nchini humo.

eng: The dispute with the government is based on demands for wage increase and standardisation, as well as the readjustment of the emergency room prices throughout the country's hospitals.
swa: Mgogoro wao na serikali umetokana na madai yao ya kuboreshewa maslahi na mazingira ya kazi pamoja na kurekebishwa kwa gharama za chumba cha wagonjwa mahututi katika mahospitali yote nchini humo.

eng: It is the second strike of the sector to take place in the country in 2013, only this time the protest of the doctors has expanded to more health professionals and has extended now for a second week.
swa: Huu ni mgomo wa pili katika sekta hiyo kufanyika nchini humo kwa mwaka 2013, isipokuwa tu wakati huu mgomo wa madaktari umepanua wigo wake na kujumuisha wataalamu zaidi wa afya na umeendelea kwa juma la pili sasa.

eng: Emotions peaked on Sunday night, May 26, 2013 when the President of Associação Médica de Moçambique, Dr. Jorge Arroz, was arrested by police under accusation of sedition (incitement of discontent or rebellion against a government).
swa: Hisia za hasira zilipanda Jumapili usiku, Mei 26, 2013 wakati Rais wa Associação Medica de Moçambique, Daktari Jorge Arroz, alipokamatwa na polisi akishitakiwa kwa makosa ya uchochezi (kitendo cha kuonyesha kutoridhika au uasi dhidi ya serikali).

eng: The release of Arroz a few hours later was fueled by massive popular mobilisation in front of the police station combined with the presence of mainstream media and the intervention of jurists.
swa: Kuachiliwa huru kwa Arroz saa chache baadaye kulichochewa kwa kiasi kikubwa na uhamasishaji mkubwa wa watu mbele ya kituo cha polisi ikichangiwa pia na kuwepo kwa vyombo vikuu vya habari na hatua ya wanasheria kuingilia kati.

eng: Tomás Queface, a student of sociology, summarised on his blog Política e Tecnologia how Mozambicans immediately questioned on social media the reasons behind Arroz's detention and commented on the lack of freedom of expression in the country.
swa: Tomás Queface, mwanafunzi wa sosholojia, alitoa muhtasari kwenye blogu yake aiitayo Política e tecnologia jinsi wananchi wa Msumbiji walipohoji haraka sana kwenye vyombo vya habari vya kijamii sababu ya Arroz kutiwa kizuizini na kutoa maoni juu ya ukosefu wa uhuru wa kujieleza nchini humo.

eng: On Monday morning, May 27, health professionals met at the Cineteatro Gilberto Mendes, holding empty plates on their hands.
swa: Siku ya Jumatatu asubuhi, Mei 27, wataalamu wa afya walikutana katika jengo la Cineteatro Gilberto Mendes, huku wameshika sahani tupu kwenye mikono yao.

eng: Photo by Canal Moz.
swa: Picha kwa hisani ya Canal Moz.

eng: Government's counter-information
swa: Serikali yadhibiti habari

eng: Analysts believe that the arrest of Arroz has increased the participation of health professionals in the strike.
swa: Wachambuzi wanaamini kwamba kukamatwa kwa Arroz kulichochea ushiriki wa wafanyakazi zaidi wa afya katika mgomo huo.

eng: Reports on the percentage of participating strikers range from 90 to five percent of the medical workforce, Aljazeera's The Stream reported on May 28.
swa: Taarifa kuhusu asilimia ya wafanyakazi walioshiriki mgomo ni kati ya asilimia 90 hadi 95 ya wafanyakazi wote wa afya", kipindi cha The stream cha Aljazeera kiliripoti tarehe 28 Mei.

eng: On May 28, a citizen reported that health professionals were meeting in Beira's Central Hospital.
swa: Mei 28, raia alitoa taarifa kwamba wataalamu wa afya walikuwa wanakutana katika Hospitali ya Beira ya kati.

eng: Throughout the first week of the strike, as the spokesman of the Ministry of Health said that all health units had returned to normality, citizen and independent reporters stated that there were many restrictions in some of the major medical units.
swa: Katika wiki ya kwanza ya mgomo, wakati msemaji wa Wizara ya Afya akisema kuwa vitengo vyote afya vilirejea hali ya kawaida, waandishi wa habari za kiraia na wale wa kujitegemea walisema kuwa kulikuwa vikwazo vingi katika baadhi ya vitengo vikubwa vya matibabu.

eng: Citizens and journalists in Maputo sent their reports from several hospitals and health unites: consultations were delayed, and patients were being received and screened by students, military doctors, foreigners and international organisations such as the Red Cross.
swa: Raia na waandishi wa habari mjini Maputo walituma ripoti zao kutoka hospitali kadhaa na vitengo vya afya: kulikuwa na kuchelewa kwa ushauri wa kitabibu, na wagonjwa walikuwa wanapokewa na kupimwa na wanafunzi, madaktari wa kijeshi, wageni na mashirika ya kimataifa kama vile Shirika la Msalaba Mwekundu.

eng: Other professionals, who usually occupy positions of leadership outside the units, were performing more specialized services.
swa: Wataalamu wengine, ambao kwa kawaida huchukua nafasi ya uongozi wa nje vitengo, walikuwa wanafanya huduma fulani mahususi.

eng: Acts of intimidation
swa: Vitendo vya vitisho

eng: Hospital directors tried to mobilize health professionals to work, but to no avail.
swa: Wakurugenzi wa hospitali walijaribu kuhamasisha wataalamu wa afya kufanya kazi, lakini hawakufanikiwa.

eng: An audio recording shared by the Medical Association of Mozambique on Facebook on May 21 revealed the Director of Mozambique's largest hospital threatening and intimidating healthcare professionals:
swa: Rekodi ya sauti iliyotumwa na Chama cha Madaktari cha Msumbiji katika Mtandao wa Facebook mnamo Mei 21 imefunua kitendo cha Mkurugenzi wa hospitali kubwa Msumbiji akiwatisha wataalamu wa afya:

eng: Thirty-six Azeri activists including one blogger, Kiaksar, were arrested on Thursday, 27 June in Urmia.
swa: Wanaharakati thelathini na sita wa Azeri akiwamo mwanablogu mmoja, Kiaksar, walikamatwa siku ya Alhamisi, 27 Juni katika eneo la Urmia.

eng: Security forces released 300 of these activists after a few hours of interrogation.
swa: Vikosi vya usalama viliwaachilia huru wanaharakati hao 300 baada ya kuwahoji kwa masaa kadhaa.

eng: Al Jazeera has come under fire in Egypt for what many describe as its "biased" reporting during and following the ousting of former Egyptian president Mohamed Morsi on July 4.
swa: Al Jazeera iko kwenye wakati mgumu nchini Misri kwa kile kinachoelezwa na wengi kuwa ni "upendeleo" wake katika kutangaza habari zake wakati na baada ya kuondolewa madarakani kwa rais wa zamani wa Misri Mohamed Morsi mnamo Julai 4.

eng: The Qatar-based channel is being accused of siding with the Muslim Brotherhood and being its mouthpiece.
swa: Kituo hicho cha televisheni kilichopo nchini Qatar kinatuhumiwa kuegemea upande wa wafuasi wa Muslim Brotherhood na kugeuka kuwa mdomo wa kikundi hicho.

eng: After Morsi was removed from office by the Army, Al Jazeera's Live Egypt service, Al Jazeera Mubasher, was immediately taken off air.
swa: Baada ya Morsi kuondolewa madarakani na Jehsi, matangazo ya moja kwa moja kutoka Misri ya kituo hicho cha Al Jazeera, yaitwayo Al Jazeera Mubasher, ghafla yalikatika.

eng: The network announced:
swa: Kituo hicho kilitangaza:

eng: Al Jazeera's live Egypt service have been taken off air along with several other TV channels.
swa: Matangazo ya moja kwa moja ya Al Jazeera kutoka Misri yameondolewa hewani pamoja na vituo vingine vya televisheni.

eng: Reports from our correspondents say this happened during a live broadcast when security forces stormed the building and arrested the presenter, guests and producers.
swa: Habari kutoka kwa waandishi wetu zinasema wakati matangazo ya moja kwa moja yakiendelea wanajeshi walivamia jengo na kumkamata mtangazaji, wageni waliokuwepo na watayarishaji wa kipindi hicho.

eng: Two days later, the Downtown Cairo prosecutor issued an arrest warrant for the channel's news director Abdel Fattah Fayed.
swa: Siku mbili baadae mwendesha mashitaka wa eneo la Downtown jijini Cairo alitoa hati ya kukamatwa kwa mkurugenzi wa habari wa kituo hicho Abdel Fattah Fayed.

eng: Fayed is being charged with "threatening public peace and national security through broadcasting incendiary news."
swa: Fayed anashitakiwa kwa "kuhatarisha amani miongoni mwa raia na usalama wa taifa kwa kutangaza habari za kichochezi."

eng: He was detained for two days and then released on bail.
swa: Alishikiliwa kwa siku mbili na baadae aliachiwa kwa dhamana.

eng: On 8 July, mass resignation of 22 staff members took place over what they claimed to be "coverage that was out of sync with real events in Egypt."
swa: Siku ya Julai 8, wafanyakazi 22 wa kituo hicho walijiuzulu kwa kile walichodai kuwa "matangazo yalikuwa hayaonyeshi matukio halisi ya hali ya mambo nchini Misri."

eng: Other reports say that 26 Egyptian employees have resigned, including four in the main Doha office.
swa: Habari nyingine zinasema wafanyakazi 26 raia wa Misri wamejiuzulu, wakiwemo wanne wanaofanya kazi kwenye ofisi kuu iliyoko Doha.

eng: One of the reporters, Wesam Fadhel reportedly resigned in a Facebook post .
swa: Mmoja wa watangazaji, Wesam Fadhel inasemekana kuwa aliacha kazi kupitia posti yake kwenye mtandao wa Facebook .

eng: The note reads:
swa: Ujumbe wake unasomeka:

eng: I resigned from Al Jazeera today.
swa: Ninaacha kazi Al Jazeera leo.

eng: It's lying openly.
swa: Kituo hiki kinadanganya mchana kweupe.

eng: They are showing old footage from an empty Tahrir and saying it was taken a short while ago and they are airing the scenes for hours.
swa: Wanaonyesha picha za video zilizopigwa zamani kutoka kwenye viwanja vya Tahrir na kusema eti zimepigwa muda mfupi uliopita na kuzirudia rudia kwa masaa kadhaa hewani.

eng: When I asked Ahmed Abu Al Mahasen for the reason he said that I should mind my own business.
swa: Nilipomwuliza Ahmed Abu Al Mahasen sababu ya kufanya hivyo alinijibu nisiingilie mambo yasiyonihusu.

eng: Al Jazeera cameras are in Tahrir live now.
swa: Kamera za Al Jazeera ziko Tahrir sasa hivi.

eng: Sadly I used to work in a place which I thought had credibility but its credibility is based on a despicable political stance.
swa: Nafadhaika, nimewahi kufanya kazi kwenye sehemu niliyodhani ina weledi lakini weledi wake unategemeana na hali ya kisiasa.

eng: On Twitter, Elijah Zarwan comments:
swa: Kwenye mtandao wa Twita, Elijah Zarwan anatoa maoni yafuatayo:

eng: @elijahzarwan: Al-Jazeera Egypt staff resign after ‘biased coverage’: Resigning June 1 wld have been courageous http://tinyurl.com/mjculx8
swa: @elijahzarwan: Mfanyakazi wa Al-Jazeera Misri ameacha kazi kwa sababu ya "habari za upendeleo": Angeacha kazi tarehe 1 June angekuwa ushujaa http://tinyurl.com/mjculx8

eng: And Nezar AlSayyad adds:
swa: Na Nezar AlSayyad anaongeza:

eng: @nezar: Al Jazeera Cable has recently become to Islamists in Egypt what Fox News has been to fundamentalist Republicans in the US for many years.
swa: @nezar: Kituo cha Jazeera kwa muda wa hivi karibuni kimekuwa cha Kiislamu kama ambavyo Fox News kimekuwa cha wahafidhina wa Republican nchini Marekani kwa miaka mingi.

eng: In another development, Rawya Rageh, Al Jazeera's reporter in Cairo, tweets photographs of threatening flyers dropped outside Al Jazeera's Cairo offices today: A threatening flyer dropped outside Al Jazeera's office in Cairo.
swa: Katika hali isiyoeleweka sawia, Rawya Rageh, mwandishi wa Al Jazeera jijini Cairo, anatwiti picha za vipeperushi vya kutishia vilivyotupwa nje ya ofisi za Al Jazeera jijini Cairo leo:

eng: @RawyaRageh: Threatening leaflets dropped near AlJazeera's offices in Cairo - bloodied hand & line 'lies & other lies' #Egypt A lying camera kills a nation reads a flyer thrown outside Al Jazeera office in Cairo.
swa: Kipeperushi cha vitisho kilichotupwa nje ya ofisi ya Al Jazeera, Cairo.

eng: Photograph shared by @RawyaRageh on Twitter
swa: Picha imewekwa kwenye mtandao wa twita na @RawyaRageh

eng: @RawyaRageh: 'A bullet may kill a person, a lying camera kills a nation' on flyer dropped near AlJazeera's offices #Egypt
swa: @RawyaRageh: 'Risasi yaweza kumwua mtu, lakini kamera iliyojaa uwongo ni maafa kwa taifa' kinasema kipeperushi kimoja karibu na ofisi za Al Jazeera #Misri

eng: More than 400 Chinese citizens signed an open letter on July 23, 2013, calling on Chinese authorities to release Xu Zhiyong, a prominent lawyer and rights campaigner who was detained on July 16 after calling for the release of activists and campaigning against government abuses.
swa: Mnamo Julai 23, 2013, zaidi ya raia 400 wa China wamesaini barua ya kushinikiza serikali ya China kumuachia huru Xu Zhiyong, ambaye ni mwanasheria mashuhuri na mpigania haki aliyekamatwa mnamo Julai 16 baada ya kushinikiza kuachiwa kwa wanaharakati pamoja na kuratibu kampeni dhidi ya uovu unaofanywa na serikali.

eng: CHINA MEDIA PROJECT has translated the letter into English.
swa: MRADI WA VYOMBO VYA MAWASILIANO WA CHINA (CHINA MEDIA PROJECT) ulitafsiri barua hii kwenda katika lugha ya Kiingereza.

eng: Operation Djakpata, launched in April 2013 by the Benin Ministry of the Interior, Public Security and Religion, intends to track all criminals engaged in illegal activities which could disturb the Benin people.
swa: Kampeni ya Djakpata, iliyozinduliwa mapema mwezi April 2013 na Wizara ya mambo ya ndani, Ulinzi na Dini ya Benin, inadhamiria kuwasaka wahalifu wote wanaojihusisha na shughuli zote zisizo halali na ambazo zinaweza kuleta usumbufu kwa watu wa Benin.

eng: However, for the past few days, public opinion of this project has been extremely divided.
swa: Un processus salué par la population béninoise, car vivre dans la sécurité viens la décharger des gouffres de la misère.

eng: Safety in Benin by Felix Krohn on Flickr CC-BY-NC
swa: Kuanzia sasa, usiku unabaki kuwa ni wa jeshi la Benini.

eng: On his blog, Illassa Benoit quoted Charles Toko, a business owner from Benin:
swa: Matumaini yaliyopo ni kuwa, kampeni hii itakuwa endelevu na kusambaa katika miji mingine yote.

eng: @LaTeam_229: Les USA ont Les Experts Manhattan, Les Experts Miami nous #AuBénin on a #DJAKPATA
swa: Na hivyo daima amani itakuwa ni rafiki wa watu wa Benini, ni mfano wa demokrasia nchini Benini na ulimwenguni kote

eng: @LaTeam_229: The US have the Manhattan Experts, the Miami Experts #AuBénin {in Benin] we have #DJAKPATA
swa: Benin: Benoit Degla akiizindua kampeni ya Djakpata na actubenin Katika mitandao ya kijamii, watu wa Benini hawaoneshi kuiunga mkono kampeni hii.

eng: China has put into effect a new law this week requiring grown children to visit their parents “frequently”.
swa: Wiki hii China imeanza kutumia sheria mpya inayowataka watoto waliokwishafikia umri wa kujitegemea kuwatembelea wazazi wao "mara kwa mara".

eng: It is strong tradition in China to respect the elderly and take care of parents as they get older, but modern lifestyles has meant that young people leave home for their own love and career.
swa: Ni utaratibu wa lazima kabisa kwa nchi ya China kuheshimiwa watu wazima na kuwatunza wazazi kwa kadiri ya umri wao unavyosogea, lakini aina mpya ya maisha imewalazimu vijana wadogo huondoka nyumbani kwenda kutafuta maisha yao.

eng: The new law says adults should care about their parents "spiritual needs" and "never neglect elderly people", but it doesn't specify how often they need to visit the parents or what punishment they will receive if they fail to abide.
swa: Sheria mpya inawataka vijana kujali “mahitaji ya kiroho” na “kutowapuuza wazee” lakini sheria hii haijaweka bayana ni mara ngapi vijana wanapaswa kuwatembelea wazazi wao au ni adhabu gani watakabiliana nayo endapo watashindwa kuitii sheria hii.

eng: The law is designed as China's population ages rapidly due to the one-child policy.
swa: Sheria hii imeanzishwa kufuatia idadi kubwa ya watu wa China kuonekana kuwa na umri mkubwa na hii inatokana na sera ya kuzaa mtoto mmoja tu.

eng: The journal reported that more than 14 percent of China’s population, or 194 million people, are over 60 years old, according to the most recent figures from the National Bureau of Statistics.
swa: The journal liliripoti kuwa, zaidi ya asilimia 14 ya watu wa China ambao ni watu milioni 194 wana umri wa zaidi ya miaka 60, hii ni kwa mujibu wa taarifa za hivi karibuni za Shirika la Taifa la Takwimu.

eng: By 2030, that figure will double.
swa: Hadi mwaka 2030, ididi hii itakuwa mara dufu.

eng: Moreover, since 2012, China’s pension system has been in crisis with a shortfall of 2.9 trillion US dollars.
swa: Kwa nyongeza, tangu mwaka 2012, mfumo wa malipo ya uzeeni wa China umekuwa katika mgogoro kwani umekabiliwa na upungufu wa kiasi cha fedha cha Dola za Marekani trilioni 2.9.

eng: Young Chinese are worried that they are being asked to support government retirees.
swa: Vijana wadogo wa China wana mashaka kuwa, wanalazimishwa kuisaidia katika kuwatunza wastaafu wa serikali.

eng: The new law has triggered ridicule on China's most popular microblogging website Sina Weibo, with many quipping that the enforcement of the law is questionable and visiting parents should be a moral issue to be encouraged rather than a law that should be enforced.
swa: Katika tovuti ya jukwaa maarufu la kublogu la nchini China, Sina Weibo, sheria hii mpya imeonekana kudhihakiwa ambapo wengi wanakejeli kwa kusema kuwa utekelezaji wa sheria hii una walakini kwani kuwatembelea wazazi lilipaswa kuwa jambo la kijamii lililohitaji uhamasishaji wa kawaida badala ya kushurutishwa kwa sheria.

eng: Some complained that they can't get enough time off from work to visit their parents even if they wanted to, while others thought that the law was introduced to make up for China's brewing pension issue.
swa: Baadhi ya watu walilalama kuwa, hawawezi kupata muda wa kutosha kutoka kazini na kwenda kuwatembelea wazazi wao hata kama wangekuwa tayari kufanya hivyo, wakati wengine wanafikiri kuwa, sheria hiyo ilianzishwa kwa lengo la kuimarisha hali mbaya iliyopo ya mfumo wa posho ya uzeeni nchini China.

eng: Online personality “Zhuomo Xiansheng” wrote sarcastically:
swa: Mtumiaji wa mtandao wa intaneti “Zhuomo Xiansheng” aliandika kwa kejeli:

eng: Family bonds should be based on spontaneous emotions.
swa: Ukaribu wa Kifamilia unapaswa kuwa ni wa hisia za hiari.

eng: It's funny to make it part of a law; it's like requiring couples to have a harmonious sex life after marriage.
swa: Ni jambo la ajabu kulifanya kuwa sehemu ya sheria, yaani ni kama kuwaomba wapenzi waishi maisha ya kimahusiano ya usawa mara baada ya kuoana.

eng: Lawyer Yang Lei echoed the same sentiment: The question is how to enforce the law? For example, give the parents a fingerprint attendance machine?
swa: Mwanaasheria Yang Lei alisisitiza mtazamo uliotangulia kusemwa:

eng: Yu linfeng speculated China's unfair social security is one of the reasons for introducing the law: Social security is mostly for the civil servants, most ordinary people don't have any much pension to rely on.
swa: Hifadhi ya jamii ipo zaidi kwa wafanyakazi wa umma, watu wengi wa kawaida hawana kiinua mgongo wanachoweza kukitegemea.

eng: TV host Cao Baoying thought that the law is a way for the government to avoid its own responsibility :
swa: Mtangazaji wa Runinga, Cao Baoying anafikiri kuwa sheria hii imeanzishwa kama namna ya serikali ya kukwepa wajibu wake:

eng: By introducing the law, emphasizing the one-sided civic duty, while weakening the government responsibilties.
swa: Kwa kuanzisha sheria hii, serikali inasisitiza uwajibikaji wa upande mmoja, yaani jukumu la wananchi, lakini kwa upande mwingine inadumaza majukumu ya serikali.

eng: An ifeng news commentary piece concluded :
swa: Sehemu ya maoni ya ifeng newskilihitimisha :

eng: Introducing the law to promote filial piety can be effective in forcing children to visit their parents, but if their external pressure can not be reduced, how meaningful is the helpless "filial piety"?
swa: Kuanzishwa kwa sheria hii inayolenga kuhamasisha watoto kuwatii wazazi wao inaweza kuwa muafaka katika kuwalazimisha watoto kuwatembelea wazazi wao, lakini kama hawatasaidiwa katikakukabiliana na changamoto nyingine wanazokabiliana nazo, sheria hii ya “watoto kuwatii wazazi wao” itakuwa na msaada gani?

eng: How are we supposed to feel about the dignity of the law?
swa: Ni kwa jinsi gani tunapaswa kuona umuhimu wa sheria hii?

eng: Global Voices and the North American Congress on Latin America (NACLA) have launched a new partnership that will combine Global Voices’ focus on citizen media and NACLA’s analysis and expertise to bring our readers original, in-depth coverage about the region.
swa: Global Voices na Shirika la Marekani Kaskazini Linaloshughulika na Amerika Kusini (NACLA) kwa pamoja wameanzisha ushirikiano ambao utaunganisha dira ya ‘Sauti za Dunia’ ya uanahabari wa kiraia pamoja na ile ya NACLA ya uchambuzi na utoaji wa elimu, lengo likiwa ni kuwaletea wasomaji wetu habari halisi na za kina kutoka katika eneo hili la Latini Amerika.

eng: NACLA, founded in 1966, is an independent, nonprofit organization that seeks to “foster knowledge beyond borders” by providing information and analysis on Latin America and its complex relationship with the United States:
swa: NACLA, lililoanzishwa mwaka 1966, ni shirika huru, lisilo la kimaslahi lililo na lengo la “kuendeleza maarifa bila mipaka” kwa njia ya kutoa taarifa na uchambuzi kuhusu Latini Amerika pamoja na hali tete ya ushirikiano kati yake na Marekani:

eng: “We believe that knowledge is essential for change, so we use a unique combination of information/media activism and popular education to provide people the tools they need to understand the world in order to change it”
swa: “tunaamini kuwa maarifa ni muhimu sana katika mabadiliko, kwa hiyo, tunatumia muunganiko wa kipekee kabisa wa taarifa/uanaharakati wa vyombo vya habari na elimu ya kawaida ili kuwapatia watu vitu wanavyovihitaji ili kuweza kuuelewa vizuri ulimwengu na kisha kuwa na uwezo wa kuubadili”

eng: Every month, GV and NACLA authors will work together to provide content related to a specific topic.
swa: Kila mwezi, waandishi wa GV(Sauti za Dunia) na NACLA watakuwa wanafanya kazi kwa pamoja ili kutoa habari zitakazokuwa zinazungumzia mada moja.

eng: A podcast with interviews, analysis, and additional reporting on the issues analyzed in the posts will be available at the end of the month.
swa: Podikasti yenye mahojiano, uchambuzi na taarifa za ziada kuhusiana na mambo yaliyojadiliwa kwenye makala mbalimbali zitapatikana kila mwisho wa mwezi.

eng: Migrant Journeys
swa: Safari za Wahamiaji

eng: We begin our partnership with the theme “Migrant Journeys.”
swa: Tunaanza ushirikiano wetu kwa kuanza na mada ya “Safari za Wahamiaji”.

eng: In July we will be covering a wide range of issues related to migration: from the immigration bill that is currently being discussed in the United States Congress, to the human stories behind migrants’ dangerous trek north through Central America and Mexico.
swa: Mwezi Julai tutakua tukizungumzia kwa mapana kabisa mambo yanayohusiana na uhamiaji: kutoka kwenye Mswada wa Uhamiaji ambao kwa sasa unajadiliwa katika bunge la Marekani, hadi kwenye habari kuhusu safari ngumu na ndefu za wahamiaji kutoka Kaskazini mwa Amerika kupitia Amerika ya Kati hadi nchini Mexico.

eng: Simukai Tinhu, a political analyst based in London, asks, "Are Zimbabwe's relations with the West warming as elections approach?"
swa: Simukai Tinhu, mchambuzi wa masuala ya siasa anayeishi London, anauliza, "Je, mahusiano ya Zimbabwe na nchi za kimagharibi yanaimarika kadri uchaguzi unavyokaribia?"

eng: Murray Hunter of the University Malaysia Perlis discusses the situation of Muslim-majority societies in Southeast Asia as well as the issues associated with the rise of Islam in the region.
swa: Murray Hunter wa Chuo Kikuu cha Malaysia Perlis anajadili hali ya jamii ya Kiislamu katika Asia ya Kusini pamoja na masuala yanayohusiana na kukua kwa Uislamu katika eneo hilo.

eng: Poverty, literacy, education, displacement, feudalism, unemployment, suppression, and control is dispossessing Muslims within ASEAN.
swa: Umaskini, kujua kusoma na kuandika, elimu, kuhamishwa, ukabaila, ukosefu wa ajira, ukandamizaji, na udhibiti ni mambo yanayowaonea Waislamu ndani ya ASEAN.

eng: Government and Ulama are trying to develop theocracies based little social and economic research and knowledge, and promote ritualized conformity instead.
swa: Serikali pamoja na Ulama wanajaribu kukuza utawala wa kidini kwa msingi mdogo wa utafiti wa kijamii na kiuchumi pamoja na maarifa, na badala yake kujaribu kukuza mila zinazolingana.

eng: Islamic interpretations are patterned into rigid thinking and ideas where new interpretations are frowned upon.
swa: Tafsiri za Kiislamu zimejikita katika fikra na mawazo yasiyobadilika ambapo tafsiri mpya zapaswa kujengwa kwazo.

eng: Twenty-two children between four and 12 years old at a public primary school in the Indian state of Bihar are dead after eating contaminated mid-day meals on July 16, 2013.
swa: Mnamo tarehe 16 Julai, 2013, watoto 22 walio na umri kati ya miaka minne na 12 katika shule moja ya msingi ya serikali katika jimbo la Bihar nchini India, walipoteza maisha mara baada ya kula chakula cha mchana kinachoamikiwa kuwa kilikuwa na sumu.

eng: Many more in the poor, rural village of Chapra were hospitalized in serious condition.
swa: Wengi wao wakiwa ni wakazi wa kijiji masikini cha Chapra, walilazwa hospitalini kufuatia hali zao kuwa mbaya sana.

eng: The food is believed to have been poisoned by pesticides.
swa: Chakula walichokula kinaaminika kuwa kilikuwa na dawa ya kuulia wadudu.

eng: The tragedy was the worst incident in a rash of apparently tainted school lunches.
swa: Janga hili limekuwa tukio baya kabisa lililotokana na uzembe wa wazi kwa chakula cha mchana cha wanafunzi hao kuchanganyikana na sumu.

eng: In a separate incident in Bihar's Madhubani district, 15 students fell ill after eating mid-day meals.
swa: Katika tukio lingine huko Bihar katika wilaya ya Madhubani, wanafunzi 15 waliugua mara baada ya kula chakula cha mchana.

eng: In Gaya-Bihar, one student was killed after eating school lunch there.
swa: Huko Gaya-Bihar, mwanafunzi mmoja alipoteza maisha baada ya kula chakula cha mchana.

eng: And in another separate incident in Dhule in the district of Maharashtra, 31 children were hospitalized after having their mid-day meals.
swa: Na katika tukio jingine huko Dhule katika wilaya ya Maharashtra, watoto 31 walilazwa hospitalini mara baada ya kupata chakula cha mchana.

eng: A student at a government-funded Hindi school in outskirts of Mumbai, India, 2011.
swa: Mwanafunzi wa shule ya Kihindi inayofadhiliwa na serikali nje kidogo ya Mumbai, India, 2012.

eng: The mid-day meal scheme, which began in the 1960's, is one of India's oldest and aims to encourage marginalized classes to send their children to schools.
swa: Utaratibu wa chakula cha mchana, ulioanza miaka ya 1960, ni miongoni mwa taratibu za siku nyingi sana nchini India ulio na lengo la kuwapa moyo familia masikini kuwapeleka watoto wao shuleni.

eng: Besides the education, a meal for every student is given as an incentive for enrollment.
swa: Mbali na elimu, kutolewa kwa chakula kwa kila mwanafunzi, imekuwa kama hamasa kwa ajili ya kuwavutia wanafunzi kuandikishwa mashuleni.

eng: However, ever since the start of the scheme, reports of embezzlement of food meant for children have consistently surfaced.
swa: Hata hivyo, tangu kuanza kwa utaratibu huu, kumekuwa na taarifa za wazi za ubadhirifu wa chakula kilichokusudiwa kwa wanafunzi.

eng: A 2006 news report found that students of a primary school in Darjeeling were deprived of their meals for 18 months.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa taarifa za habari za mwaka 2006, ilionekana kuwa, wanafunzi wa shule za misingi za Darjeeling walikabiliana na upungufu wa chakula kwa muda wa miezi 18.

eng: The issue has, as expected, taken a political twist.
swa: Kama ilivyotarajiwa, jambo hili limechukuliwa kisiasa.

eng: The political party in power has alleged that the opposition has indulged in a conspiracy to frame them.
swa: Chama kilichopo madarakani kilidai kuwa upinzani umejihusisha katika njama za kuwateka watu kimtizamo.

eng: The school principal's husband is reported to be a political figure who was responsible for supplying food to the school.
swa: Mume wa mkuu wa shule anaelezwa kuwa na ushawishi mkubwa wa kisiasa na ndiye aliyekuwa msambazaji wa chakula shuleni hapo.

eng: The negligence on the part of the government angered many on social networking sites.
swa: Serikali kushindwa kutilia mkazo tukio hili, umewaghadhabisha watu wengi katika mitandao mbalimbali ya kijamii.

eng: India-based Twitter user Vikram Singh (@cynicalvs) wrote:
swa: Mtumiaji wa Twita aliye na makazi yake nchini India, Vikram Singh (@cynicalvs) aliandika:

eng: @cynicalvs: How can kids die of eating a midday meal?
swa: @cynicalvs: watoto wanawezaje kufariki baada ya kula chakula cha mchana?

eng: It is food.
swa: Ni chakula.

eng: Somebody needs to be tried for murder. #chappra
swa: Kunamtu anapaswa kushitakiwa kwa kosa la mauaji. #chappra

eng: As soon as journalists began reaching hospitals to report on the situation, more mismanagement came to surface.
swa: Mara baada ya waandishi wa habari kuanza kutembea mahospitalini kwa ajili ya kutoa taarifa za tukio hili, matumizi mabaya ya madaraka yaliendelea kujitokeza.

eng: The streamed video images showed surviving children laid next to each other crammed on a desk and saline water being administered.
swa: Picha katika mfumo wa video za mtandaoni ziliwaonesha watoto walionusurika wakiwa mamelala kila mmoja karibu na mwenzakeAs soon as journalists began reaching hospitals to report on the situation, more mismanagement came to surface.

eng: Milind Khandekar, the managing editor of ABP News (@milindkhandekar), observed:
swa: Milind Khandekar, ambaye ni mhariri mkuu wa kampuni ya uhabarishaji ya the managing editor of ABP News (@milindkhandekar), alitoa maoni yake:

eng: @milindkhandekar: Pictures from Chappra shows relatives using paper fan for children admitted in the hospital.
swa: @milindkhandekar: picha kutoka Chappra zinawaonesha ndugu wa watoto waliolazwa hospitali wakiwapepea watoto wao kwa makaratasi.

eng: Is this ' Bihar model of development?
swa: Huu ndio ‘mfano mzuri wa maendeleo ya Bihar’?

eng: This incident, soon enough, prompted users on social media to discuss negligence and arrogance of Indian politicians.
swa: Mapema kabisa, tukio hili liliwapelekea watumiaji wa mitandao ya kijamii kujadili hali ya dharau na kiburi iliyooneshwa na wanasiasa wa India.

eng: Abhijit Majumder, a journalist from Delhi (@abhijitmajumder), tweeted:
swa: Abhijit Majumder, ambaye ni mwandishi wa habari kutoka Delhi (@abhijitmajumder), alitwiti:

eng: @abhijitmajumder: Our politicians don't discriminate.
swa: @abhijitmajumder: Wanasiasa wetu hawabagui.

eng: 2G for the better-off or NREGA, Mid-day meal for the poorest, all are robbed with equal relish. #Chhapra
swa: 2G kwa wale wanaojiweza au NREGA, chakula cha adhuhuri kwa mafukara, wote wanadanganywa kwa mvuto sawa. #Chhapra

eng: Students of a Hindi school in the outskirts of Mumbai eat on the ground with no seating or plates.
swa: Wanafunzi wa shule ya Kihindi nje kidogo ya Mumbai wakipata chakula wakiwa wamekaa chini pasipo kuwa na viti wala bakuli.

eng: Another student shows a tiffin box and complains about the quality of the food.
swa: Mwanafunzi mwingine akionesha kibobo chenye chakula cha adhuhuri huku akilalamika kuhusu ubora wa chakula hicho.

eng: Majumder, was making a reference to recent scams such as 2G and NREGA, which have run into billions of dollars and planted grave mistrust towards the way Indian government functions.
swa: Majumder, alirejelea matukio ya udanganyifu yaliyotokea hivi karibuni, kama yale ya2G na NREGA, ambayo yaligharimu mabilioni ya dola na kupandikiza hali ya kukosa imani kubwa kwa namna serikali ya India inavyotimiza majukumu yake.

eng: Another Delhi-based journalist, Raghavendra Verma (@r_verma), made a commentary on the general attitude of the teachers at these government run schools:
swa: Mwandishi mwingine wa habari ambaye makazi yake ni Delhi, Raghavendra Verma (@r_verma), alitoa maoni yake kuhusu namna ambavyo walimu wanavyozichukulia shule zinazomilikiwa na serikali.:

eng: @r_verma: School teachers serve mid day meal to children as if they are doing some big personal favour to them. #Chhapra
swa: @r_verma: walimu huwapatia watoto chakula cha adhuhuri kana kwamba wamejitolea sana na kwa upendeleo mkubwa. #Chhapra

eng: Fazal Abbas (@fazlabas), a Mumbai-based Twitter user, brought some historical perspective to the ongoing discourse:
swa: Fazal Abbas (@fazlabas), ambaye ni mtumiaji wa Twita aishiye Mumbai, alitoa historia kuhusiana na tukio hili:

eng: @fazlabas: Chhapra is same as our first president Dr. Rajendra Prasad left half century back.
swa: @fazlabas: Chhapra ni kama ilivyokuwa kwa Rais wetu wa kwanza Dk.

eng: Children are dying for education.
swa: Watoto wanafariki kwa ajili ya elimu.

eng: Kiran Bedi (@thekiranbedi), a former police officer from Delhi who is recognized for her philanthropic activities and anti-corruption crusade in India, tweeted:
swa: Kiran Bedi (@thekiranbedi), ambaye ni askari mstaafu kutoka Delhi, ambaye anajulikana kwa utendaji kazi uliotukuka na mmoja wa wapinga rushwa nchini India, alitwiti:

eng: @thekiranbedi: Mid-day meals, at places r a scandal and un-hygienic.
swa: @thekiranbedi: Mlo wa adhuhuri, ni wenye majungu na usio katika hali ya usafi.

eng: Teachers too r wasting time cooking!Why not serve fruits and nuts?
swa: Pia, walimu wanapoteza tu muda wao kupika chakula hicho! Kwa nini wasiwagawie matunda na njugu?

eng: Bedi's narrative corroborates with the above photographic evidence.
swa: Maelezo ya Bedi yanaunga mkono ushahidi wa picha uliotangulia kutolewa.

eng: Not just Bihar, government run schools, across India, may have bigger stories of negligence and mismanagement to tell.
swa: Sio tu Bihar, miongoni mwa shule zinazomilikiwa na serikali nchini India zilizoweza kuwa na mengi ya kujadiliwa kuhusiana na kutotilia maanani mambo na usimamizi mbovu.

eng: As far as this case is concerned, the Indian government was quick to announce a compensation of 2 lakhs (about 3,367 US dollars) to the victims family.
swa: Kwa jinsi shauri hili lilivyo, serikali ya India ilipaswa haraka sana itangaze fidia ya lakhs 2 (takribani dola za kimarekani 3,367) kwa familia za wahanga.

eng: The exact cause of how the food became contaminated is being studied - in short, a long bureaucratic process follows.
swa: Uchunguzi wa ni kwa namna gani chakula hiki kilichanganyika na sumu bado unaendelea-kwa ufupi, mchakato mrefu wa kiuchunguzi unafuata.

eng: Will those guilty be held accountable?
swa: Je, waliohusika watawajibishwa.

eng: A key was the symbol for Rouhani's campaign.
swa: Alama ya kampeni za Rouhani ilikuwa ni Ufunguo.

eng: Photo via Mashreghnews
swa: Picha kupitia Mashreghnews

eng: The campaign symbol of president-elect Hassan Rouhani was a key.
swa: Alama ya Rais mteule Hassan Rouhani ilikuwa ni ufunguo.

eng: Now, Iranian netizens are discussing whether Rouhani will actually be able to open any locks.
swa: Kwa sasa, raia wa mtandaoni wa Iran wanajadili kama Rouhani ataweza kufungua kila kufuli.

eng: Rouhani promised a government of “hope and prudence”, and thousands of Iranians celebrated his victory hoping for a better future.
swa: Rouhani aliahidi kuleta serikali “yenye tumaini na iliyo makini” na hivyo, maelfu ya watu wa Iran walisherehekea ushindi wake wakitegemea mustakabali mzuri wa maisha ya baadae.

eng: In Omid Dana's blog we read:
swa: Kwenye blogu ya Omid Danaameandika:

eng: Which lock will Rouhani's key open?
swa: Ufunguo la Rouhani utafungua kufuli gani?

eng: Mostafa Tajzadeh says releasing political prisoners is not in the hands of Rouhani.
swa: Mostafa Tajzadeh anasema kuwa, kuwaachilia huru wafungwa wa kisiasa ni jambo ambalo halipo mikononi mwa Rouhani.

eng: Doesn't Khatami say that we should lower our expectations?
swa: Khatami hakusema kuwa tupunguze kiwango cha matarajio yetu?

eng: People often say, with good reason, that the key to nuclear negotiations, relations with the US, and the Syria crisis are in the hands of the Supreme Leader... With all this said, Rouhani's only keys are those to his house or his office.
swa: Mara nyingi watu wanasema, kwa malengo mazuri, namna ya kuelekea kwenye muafaka wa matumizi ya nyuklia, uhusiano na Marekani pamoja na mgogoro wa Syria vipo ndani ya uwezo wa Rais... pamoja na yote haya kusemwa, funguo za Rouhani ni za kufungulia milango ya nyumba yake au ofisi yake tu.

eng: Jaleboon writes:
swa: Jaleboon anaandika:

eng: Some, like Omid Dana, ask which locks Rouhani can open.
swa: Baadhi ya watu, kama ilivyo kwa Omid Dana, anauliza ni makufuli gani anavyoweza kuyafungua Rouhani.

eng: The answer is that he already opened the lock of the election that had become illegitimate with the 2009 crisis.
swa: Jibu ni kuwa, ameshafungua kufuli la uchaguzi uliokuwa batili kufuatia mgogoro wa mwaka 2009.

eng: Several netizens metion problems and locks that Rouhani's key might open.
swa: Watumiaji kadhaa wa mtandao wa intaneti wametaja matatizo ambayo wanafikiri kuwa ufunguo wa Rouhani unaweza kuyafungua.

eng: Mahsa tweeted:
swa: Mahsa tweeted:

eng: I don't want freedom to wear the veil or not, I want the day to come when inflation and unemployment rates are lowered and marginalized people do not need to sell drugs.
swa: Bila kujali uhuru umefichwa au la, ninachohitaji ni kuona siku moja kuwa mfumuko wa bei za bidhaa na kukosekana kwa ajira vinapungua ikiwa ni pamoja na kuhakikisha kuwa watu wa hali ya chini hawajihusishi na uuzaji wa madawa ya kulevya..

eng: Negar Mortazavi tweeted:
swa: Negar Mortazavi alitwiti:

eng: Sources close to #Rouhani say he is planning to send special envoys to some countries to repair broken ties & start a new chapter with Tehran. 	Vyanzo vya habari vilivyo karibu na #Rouhani vinasema kuwa, Rais huyu mteule amepanga kutuma wawakilishi maalum katika nchi kadhaa kwa lengo la kurejesha uhusiano mzuri pamoja na kuanzisha ukurasa mpya na nchi ya Tehran.
In the meantime several campaigns also asked Rouhani to fix the Iranian internet and end filtering.
swa: Wakati huohuo, kampeni kadhaa zinamtaka Rouhani kuboresha mtandao wa intaneti wa Iran ikiwa ni pamoja na kukomesha uchujaji wa taarifa katika mtandao wa intaneti.

eng: A Facebook campaign asked Rouhani to end the filtering of Facebook, and a group of bloggers and cyber activists wrote a letter to the President-elect asking him to increase Internet speeds.
swa: Kampeni ya Facebook ilimtaka Rouhani kukomesha uchujaji wa taarifa katika mtandao wa Facebook, na kikundi cha wanablogu na wanaharakati wa sayansi ya mfumo wa mawasiliano na udhibiti wake walimwandikia barua Rais mteule wakimtaka aongeze kasi ya mtandao wa intaneti.

eng: They also complain about filtering and remind Rouhani that he himself used the Internet to promote his campaign.
swa: Pia, walilalamikia kuchujwa kwa taarifa za mtandaoni na pia walimkumbusha Rouhani kuwa alitumia mtandao wa intaneti katika kufanikisha kampeni yake.

eng: US President Barack Obama finished his six-day tour of three African countries, Senegal, South Africa and Tanzania, on July 2, 2013.
swa: Rais wa Marekani Barack Obama amemaliza ziara yake ya siku sita katika nchi tatu za Kiafrika, Senegali, Afrika Kusini na Tanzania, mnamo Julai 2, 2013.

eng: The global public opinion about the importance and impact of his tour is sharply divided.
swa: Maoni ya watu duniani kote kuhusiana na umuhimu na matokeo ya ziara hiyo, yameonyesha kugawanyika mno.

eng: During his visit, Obama announced a new initiative, "Power Africa", to double access to electricity in Sub-Saharan Africa.
swa: Wakati wa ziara yake, Obama alitangaza mradi mpya, "Umeme kwa Afrika", kwa lengo la kukuza matumizi ya umeme mara dufu katika nchi zilizo kusini mwa Jangwa la Sahara.

eng: Through this initiative, the US is committing seven billion US dollars while private sector companies have committed more than nine billion.
swa: Kupitia mradi huu, Marekani inaahidi kutoa Dola za Kimarekani bilioni saba wakati makampuni ya sekta binafsi yanatoa zaidi ya bilioni tisa kwa mradi huo.

eng: According to the White House blog, nearly 70 percent of Africans lack access to electricity.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa blogu ya Ikulu ya Marekani, karibu asilimia 70 ya Waafrika hawajafikiwa na huduma ya umeme.

eng: Image of President Barack Obama on a billboard welcoming him in Dar Es Salaam.
swa: Picha ya Rais Barack Obama katika bango kubwa barabarani kumkaribisha jijini Dar Es Salaam.

eng: Photo courtesy of Instagrammer Sandy Temu.
swa: Picha ya mtumiaji wa Instagram Sandy Temu.

eng: Commenting about the initiative, Bright Simmons at African Argument commended this new idea for strategic engagement with Africa:
swa: Akitoa maoni yake kuhusu mradi huo wa umeme, Bright Simmons wa mtandao wa African Argumentalipongeza wazo hili jipya la ushirikiano wa kimkakati baina ya Marekani na bara la Afrika:

eng: As one of the people who have in the past complained about the seeming lack of new ideas for a “strategic engagement with Africa” from the Obama White House, I welcome renewed energy towards that direction.
swa: Kama mmoja wa watu waliolalamika sana siku za nyuma kuhusu kilichoonekana kuwa kukosekana kwa mawazo mapya ya "ushirikiano wa kimkakati na Afrika" kutoka Ikulu ya Obama, ninauona mpango wa nishati kuwa na mwelekeo sahihi.

eng: The issue selected – Africa’s electricity challenge – is clearly a vital one.
swa: Jambo lenyewe lililochaguliwa -changamoto ya umeme barani Afrika- linao umuhimu mkubwa.

eng: The World Bank for instance says that all sub-Saharan African countries, minus South Africa, combined do not generate more electricity than Argentina.
swa: Benki ya Dunia kwa mfano inasema kwamba nchi zote za Kusini mwa Jangwa la Sahara, ukiiacha Afrika Kusini, kwa pamoja hazizalishi umeme wenye mkondo mkubwa kuliko nchi moja tu ya Argentina.

eng: Including South Africa, they produce only as much as Spain.
swa: Ukiijumuisha na Afrika Kusini, kiasi cha umeme kinachozalishwa kinafikia kile cha Uhispania.

eng: It is commendable that the White House is pledging up to $7 billion in additional funding from two of its overseas-focussed agencies – EXIM and OPIC – for this cause.
swa: Ni jambo la kupongezwa kwamba Ikulu ya Marekani inaahidi mpaka Dola za Marekani bilioni 7 kama msaada wa nyongeza kutoka kwenye mashirika yake yenye mrengo wa kusaidia nchi za nje -EXIM na OPIC - kwa sababu hii.
