swa: Ma-Laza anahoji kuwa suala kuu si hasa nani atakuwa waziri mkuu bali atakuwa ana ajenda gani akikabidhiwa ofisi :

eng: (The prime minister should be) a person with outstanding technical know-how, a uniter who is able to carry out the policy of the President of the Republic.
swa: (waziri mkuu lazima awe) mtu mwenye wasifu wa weledi, mtu atakayewaunganisha watu na mwenye uwezo wa kushughulikia sera za Rais wa Jamhuri.

eng: In theory, the Prime Minister should not belong to any political movement.
swa: Kinadharia, Waziri Mkuu lazima asiwe sehemu ya harakati za siasa.

eng: He will not be against Rajoelina, nor against Ravalomanana (the two last presidents).
swa: Hatakuwa kinyume na Rajoelina, wala Ravalomanana (marais wawili waliopita).

eng: In short, he will have to be that rare person who will inspire the trust of the investors.
swa: Kwa kifupi, lazima awe mtu nadra atakayewafanya wawekezaji wavutiwe kuja.

eng: The question is: does this person even exist?
swa: Swali ni: hivi mtu wa namna hii yupo kweli?

eng: Venezuela is going through an economic, political and social crisis which brought about thousands of citizens taking the streets to express their discontent.
swa: Venezuela inapitia katika mgogoro wa ikuchumi, kisiasa na kijamii ambao umewafanya maelfu ya raia kuingia mitaani kuonyesha kutokuridhika kwao na hali ya mambo.

eng: For more than a week, Venezuelans have been involved in mass protests that, until now, have caused eight deaths, hundreds of injuries and hundreds of arrests.
swa: Kwa zaidi ya juma moja, wa-Venezuela wamekuwa wakishiriki maandamano ambayo, mpaka sasa, yamesababisha vifo nane, mamia ya majerhi na mamia wakiwekwa kizuizini.

eng: In this edition of GV Face, our Latin America editor Silvia Viñas and I talk to Global Voices author and digital rights lawyer Marianne Díaz Hernández who has been tracking citizen media and web censorship amidst a government-imposed media blackout in Venezuela.
swa: Katika toleo hili la Majadiliano ya GV, mahariri wetu wa Amerika ya Kusini Silvia Viñas na mimi tutafanya mazungumzo na mwandishi wa Global Voices na mwansheria wa haki za mtandaoni Marianne Díaz Hernández ambaye anafuatilia kwa karibu vitendo vya kufuatiliwa vyombo vya habari za kiraia na mtandao wakati huu ambapo vyombo vikuu vya habari vimefungiwa kutimiza wajibu wake nchini Venezuela.

eng: Marianne talks about everyday life in Venezuela - how shortages of food and medicine affect people, and how newspapers in the country have been reduced to as few as four pages because of lack of paper.
swa: Marianne anazungumzia kuhusiana na maisha ya kawaida nchini Venezuela -namna upungufu vya chakula na madawa unavyoathirir watu, na jinsi magazeti nchini humo yalivyopunguza kurasa na kubaki na kurasa chache mpaka nne hivi kutokana na ukosefu wa karatasi.

eng: She recommends alternative online news sources that focus on fact-checking, including Elperiodistacivico.com, at a moment when disinformation and propaganda is confounding those trying to make sense of events.
swa: Anapendekeza vyanzo mbadala vya mtandaoni kwa minajili ya kuchunguza taarifa, ikiwa ni pamoja na Elperiodistacivico.com, wakati huu ambao kuna upotoshwaji wa taarifa na propaganda zinawakwamisha wale wanaojaribu kuelewa hali halisi ya matukio yanayoendelea.

eng: It has been called South Korea's "greatest export."
swa: Umekuwa ukiitwa "bidhaa kuu ya mauzo nje" ya taifa la Korea Kusini.

eng: PSY's K-pop song Gangnam style is the most watched video on YouTube.
swa: Wimbo wa PSY ulio katika mahadhi ya Pop ndio wimbo uliotazamwa zaidi kwenye mtandao wa YouTube.

eng: But behind the glamorous facades and big paychecks, it's not all fun and romance until South Korea's censors have done their work.
swa: Lakini nyuma ya hali hii inayoonekana kijuu juu kuwa ni kupendwa na malipo makubwa kadhalika, muziki huu hauwezi kuwa mzuri wala wa kuvutia mashabiki wake mpaka kwanza wakaguzi wa kazi za sanaa nchini Korea Kusini hawajakamilisha kazi yao.

eng: Our managing editor Solana Larsen talks to our Korean language editor Yoo Eun Lee on the growing popularity of K-pop worldwide.
swa: Mhariri wetu mtendaji Our Solana Larsen anazungumza na mhariri wetu wa lugha ya Kikorea Yoo Eun Lee kuhusu ukuaji wa umaarufu wa muziki wa miondoko ya K-pop duniani kote.

eng: Yoo Eun is also the creator of the website K-pop Decoder.
swa: Yoo Eun pia ni mwandilishi wa tovuti ya K-pop Decoder.

eng: We ask her what she thinks makes K-pop special?
swa: Tunamwuliza anafikiri nini kinaufanya muziki wa K-pop uwe wa pekee?

eng: What has the impact of K-pop been on culture, fashion and music in South Korea?
swa: Je, muziki huo wa K-pop umekuwa na athari gani kwenye utamaduni, mitindo na muziki wa Korea Kusini?

eng: And whether she thinks K-pop's global success would have been possible without social media and YouTube.
swa: Na ikiwa anafikiri mafanikio ya muziki huo wa Kikorea duniani kote yangewezekana pasipo mitandao ya kiraia na YouTube.

eng: Feel free to ask more questions below. ﻿
swa: Jisikie huru kuuliza maswali zaidi hapa chini. ﻿

eng: Maldivian blogger Hani Amir writes about the traditional fishing methods of the reef fishermen of Maldives which include catching tons of fish with their hands, instead of nets or rods.
swa: Mwanablogu wa MaldiviHani Amir anaandika kuhusu mbinu za uvuvi asilia ikiwa ni pamoja na kukamata mamia ya samaki kwa mikono yao, badala ya kutumia nyavu au fimbo.

eng: The bloggers also sheds light on how they are being exploited by greedy resort owners who tries to exploit them by not paying what they deserve.
swa: Mwanablogu huyo pia anatoa mwangaza kuhusu namna wanavyonnyonywa na wamiliki walafi wa hoteli wnaojaribu kuwaibia kwa kutokuwalipa kile wanachostahili.

eng: His name is Djamel Ghanem, and he's a young Algerian cartoonist.
swa: Jina lake ni Djamel Ghanem, na mchora katuni kijana wa Kialjeria.

eng: His job is no fun in a country where censorship and prosecution await those who dare to speak their minds.
swa: Kazi yake si ya kujifurahisha tu kwenye nchi ambako ufuatiliaji na kushitakiwa ni kawaida kuwangojea wote wale wanaothubutu kusema wazi wazi kile wanachofikiri.

eng: Ghanem faces 18 months in prison for an unpublished caricature of Algeria's President Abdelaziz Bouteflika that was deemed offensive by the authorities.
swa: Ghanem anakabiliwa na kifungo cha miezi 18 jela kwa kosa la kuchora kikaragosi ambacho hata hivyo hakikuchapishwa cha Rais wa Algeria Abdelaziz Bouteflika kilichohesabiwa na mamlaka za dola nchini humo kuwa ni matusi that was deemed offensive.

eng: Djamel Ghanem via Algérie Focus.
swa: Djamel Ghanem kupitia jarida la Algérie Focus.

eng: Used with permission
swa: Imetumiwa kwa ruhusa

eng: In fact, President Bouteflika is not represented or even directly mentioned in the unpublished cartoon.
swa: Kwa hakika, Rais Bouteflika hakutajwa wazi wazi katika katuni hiyo ambayo hata hivyo haikuwa imechapishwa.

eng: The drawing portrays two citizens mocking the fourth term the current president is seeking after ruling Algeria for 15 years.
swa: Mchoro huo unawaonyesha raia wawili wakidhihaki kipindi cha nne ambacho rais wa sasa anakitafuta baada ya kuwa ameitawala Aljeria kwa miaka 15 mfulizo.

eng: The caricature compares the fourth mandate to baby diapers.
swa: Katuni hiyo inakifananisha kipindi cha nne na nepi za mtoto.

eng: With the drawing, Ghanem wanted to convey the idea that Algerians are treated like children.
swa: Kwa mchoro huo, Ghanem alitaka kutuma ujumbe kuwa Wa-Aljeria wamefanywa kama watoto.

eng: For that, he was taken to court and threatened with imprisonment.
swa: Kwa hilo pekee, alichusimamishwa kizimbani na kutishiwa kifungo.

eng: The district attorney of Oran, the second largest city in Algeria, located 400 kilometers northwest of the capital Algiers, wanted the cartoonist to admit that he had the intention of insulting the president.
swa: Mwanasheria wa wilaya ya Oran, mji wa pili kwa ukubwa nchini Aljeria, alimtaka mchoraji huyo kukiri kuwa alikuwa na lengo la kumdhihaki rais.

eng: But Ghanem categorically denied that he had such intention.
swa: Lakini Ghanem kwa ujasiri kabisa alikana kuwa na nia hiyo.

eng: Neither Bouteflika nor his advisers filed the suit against Ghanem.
swa: Si Bouteflika wala washauri wake walifungua mashitaka dhidi ya Ghanem.

eng: It was Ghanem's former employer, La Voix de l'Oranie (Voice of Oran), a daily newspaper known for its pro-regime editorial line, who sued him for the cartoon which was never published in the media.
swa: Alikuwa ni mwajiri wa zamani wa Ghanem, La Voix de l'Oranie (Sauti Oran), gazeti la kila siku linalofahamika kwa tahariri zenye mrengo wa kuipamba serikali, ndilo lililomshitaki kwa katuni yake hiyo ambayo hata hivyo haijawahi kuchapishwa kwenye vyombo vya habari.

eng: Sued by his own newspaper, Ghanem saw all the doors of Algerian media closing in his face.
swa: Akiwa ameshitakiwa na gazeti lake mwenyewe, Ghanem alijikuta mpweke asiye na msaada wowote wa chombo chochote cha habari nchini Aljeria.

eng: Interviewed by Algerie-Focus, Ghanem explained that he has had difficulties finding a lawyer to defend his cause along with other challenges:
swa: Akihojiwa na Algerie-Focus, Ghanem alieleza kuwa pamoja na changamoto nyingine, ilikuwa vigumu kumpata mwanasheria wa kumtetea dhidi ya mashitaka hayo:

eng: the director of another newspaper was advised to not hire me.
swa: mkurugenzi wa gazeti jingine alishauriwa kutokuniajiri.

eng: I became persona non-grata. Through me, they want to thwart the opposition who is fighting against a fourth term for the president.
swa: Nikawa mkiwa asiye na rafiki, Kupitia mimi, walitaka kuwatisha wapinzani wa mpango huo wa kutafuta kuchaguliwa kwa kipindi cha nne cha uraist.

eng: After the case's first hearing, the judges requested an 18-month prison sentence against Ghanem.
swa: Baada ya kusikilizwa kwa mshitaka hayo kwa mara ya kwanza, majaji walipendekeza kifungo cha miezi 18 dhidi ya Ghanem.

eng: The final ruling is expected next month on March 4.
swa: Hukumu ya mwisho inatazamiwa kusikilizwa mwezi ujao tarehe 4 Machi.

eng: Meanwhile, netizens are voicing their support for and solidarity with Ghanem.
swa: Wakati huo huo, watumiaji wa mtandao wameendelea kupaza sauti zao kumwuunga mkono na kuungana kumsaidia Ghanem.

eng: An online petition demands that Ghanem be let go:
swa: Kuna tamko la mtandaoni linalotaka Ghanem aachiliwe huru:

eng: If the media and the opinion keep quiet on this infringement of freedom of expression and the violation of a citizen's rights, then tomorrow any court can charge a journalist for criticizing the president of the republic, an army official, a minister or a deputy.
swa: Kama vyombo vya habari na maoni huru ya watu yanabaki kimya kulaani uvunjifu huu wa uhuru wa kujieleza na uvunjifu wa haki za binadamu, basi kesho mahakama yoyote inaweza kumshitaki mwandishi kwa kumkosoa rais wa jamuhuri, au afisa wa jeshi, waziri au hata naibu waziri.

eng: With this petition, we demand an end to the prosecution against Djamel Ghanem.
swa: Kwa hati hii ya kudai kuachiliwa huru kwa Ghanem, tunadai kusitishwa kwa mashitaka dhidi ya Djamel Ghanem.

eng: By shielding the president against any criticism, the administration is trying to impose a totalitarian ideology upon its citizens.
swa: Kwa kumkinga rais dhidi ya ukosoaji wa aina yoyote, utawala wa nchi hiyo unajaribu kuimarisha sera ya uimla dhidi ya raia wa nchi hiyo.

eng: Freedom of expression is at risk in Algeria.
swa: Uhuru wa maoni uko shakani Algeria.

eng: Ghanem's case is a typical example of how dire the situation is for cartoonists and other people willing to speak up.
swa: Kesi ya Ghanem ni mfano hai wa namna hali ilivyo ngumu kwa wachora katuni na watu wengine wasioficha maoni yao.

eng: Interim president Adly Mansour issued a presidential decree promoting General Abdel Fattah El-Sissi, minister of defence, to the rank of field marshal.
swa: Rais wa serikali ya mpito ya Misri, Adly Mansour atoa amri ya Rais ya kumpandisha cheo Jenerali Abdel Fattah El-Sissi, ambaye ni waziri wa ulinzi kuwa Jemadari Mkuu.

eng: It is the highest rank in the Egyptian military.
swa: Hii ni nafasi ya juu kabisa katika jeshi la Misri

eng: The promotion has created a buzz online, with many wondering whether it paves the way for Sissi to run for presidency in elections penciled in for the end of April.
swa: Upandishwaji cheo huu umezua mjadala mkubwa katika mitandao ya intaneti ambapo watu wengi wanajiuliza kama ndio njia ya Sissi kugombea urais unaotarijiwa kufanyika mwisho wa mwezi Aprili.

eng: Adam Makary tweets:
swa: Adam Makary katika ukurasa wa Twita aandika:

eng: Reminder - Sisi was #Egypt's first defence minister not to hold the top rank of Field Marshal.
swa: Reminder - Sisi #Egypt's alikuwa ni waziri wa ulinzi wa kwanza ambaye hakustahili kupewa nafasi kuu kabisa ya Jemadari Mkuu.

eng: Louisa Loveluck notes:
swa: Louisa Loveluck atoa angalizo:

eng: And Ahmed Abrass explains what the title Field Marshal means :
swa: Pia, Ahmed Abrass anafafanua maana ya cheo cha Jemadari Mkuu :

eng: Field Marshal in English means someone who has led troops on the field battle and have obtained scintillating victories
swa: Kwa kiingereza, Jemadari Mkuu ina maana kuwa mtu Fulani aliyewangoza wanajeshi vitani na akapata ushindi mkubwa .

eng: This isn't the case for El Sissi.
swa: Kwa El Siss, hili si jambo la yeye kulitilia maanani.

eng: However, it seems that this is not a prerequisite in the Egyptian army and that the former general had all the necessary qualifications to become a Field Marshal.
swa: Hata hivyo, inaonekana kuwa kuwa Jemadari Mkuu siyo kigezo cha muhimu katika jeshi la Misri na hata hivyo Meja Jenerali huyu mstaafu alikuwa na vigezo vyote vya kumfanya kuwa Jemadari Mkuu .

eng: Nervana Mahmoud explains:
swa: Nervana Mahmoud afafanua:

eng: Bel Trew confirms:
swa: Bel Trew athibitisha kuwa:

eng: And Egyptian Streets says:
swa: Na Egyptian Streets asema:

eng: Many netizens seem puzzled and clearly annoyed by the news.
swa: Watumiaji wengi wa mtandao wameonesha kushangazwa na waziwazi kuchukizwa na habari hii.

eng: On Facebook, Mina Labib asks :
swa: Katika mtandao wa kijamii wa Facebook, Mina Labib auliza :

eng: What is he being honoured for?
swa: Anatunukiwa hasa kwa lipi alilolifanya?

eng: The explosions?
swa: Kuhusu milipuko iliyotokea?

eng: Egypt woke up on January 24 to a series of four explosions, which left six dead and over 70 wounded in Cairo.
swa: Januari 24, Misri ilikabiliwa na mfululizo wa milipuko iliyoua watu sita na wengine 70 walijeruhiwa huko Cairo.

eng: Some suggest that this promotion is a fast-track to Sissi's presidential bid.
swa: Baadhi ya watu wanaona kuwa, kupandishwa cheo huku ni namna ya ya haraka ya Sissi kuelekea kugombea Urais.

eng: Nervana Mahmoud writes:
swa: Nervana Mahmoud aandika:

eng: Promotion of general Sisi is a sign of imminent resignation.
swa: Kupandishwa cheo kwa Sisi ni ishara ya karibu sana ya kuachia madaraka.

eng: Egyptian Streets adds:
swa: Egyptian Streets adds:

eng: BREAKING: Reports indicate Al-Sisi meeting with military leaders to plan his nomination for Presidency, likely to resign. #Egypt — Egyptian Streets (@EgyptianStreets) January 27, 2014 And journalist Patrick Kingsley explains: Just spoke to a senior military source who claimed #Sisi wd have to resign if he ran.
swa: Ni punde tu niliongea na afisa mkubwa wa jeshi ambaye alitanabaisha kuwa #Sisi angepaswa kuachia ngazi kama atagombea Urais.

eng: It seems that the presidential bid isn't the only reason for this promotion.
swa: Inaonekana kuwa kugombea Urais siyo sababu pekee ya kupandishwa cheo hiki.

eng: Tarik Salama tweets:
swa: Tarik Salama atwiti:

eng: Sisi promoted as Marshal is a salary necessity.
swa: Sisi kupandishwa cheo kama Jemadari Mkuu ni kwa minajili ya kuongezewa mshahara.

eng: And Basil Al Dabh adds:
swa: Basil Al Dabh anaongeza:

eng: While Gr33ndata shares this cartoon:
swa: Gr33ndata akiweka kikaragosi:

eng: Génesis Carmona, Venezuelan beauty queen, another victim of the political crisis.
swa: Génesis Carmona, mwanamitindo wa Venezuela, mwathirika mwingine wa vurugu za kisiasa.

eng: Génesis Carmona, a young Venezuelan beauty queen and student, died on the 19th of February from a bullet wound to the head that she received the previous day during the anti-government protests.
swa: Génesis Carmona, mrembo wa Venezuela na mwanafunzi, ameuawa mnamo Februari 19 kwa jereha lililotokana na risasi ya kichwani iliyompata jana wakati wa maandamano ya kuipinga serikali.

eng: This is how they transported the student Génesis Carmona who was shot in the head while protesting in Valencia.
swa: Hivi ndivyo walivyomsafirisha Génesis Carmona aliyepigwa risasi ya kichwa wakati akiandamana jijini Valencia.

eng: @pabloaure in the Guerra Mendez clinic talking with the mother and another family member of Genesis Carmona who has a bullet wound to the head.
swa: @pabloaure akiwa kwenye kliniki ya Guerra Mendez akizungumza na mama na mwanafamilia mwingine wa Genesis Carmona mwenye jeraha la risasi kichwani.

eng: According to the specialists who treated her at the Dr. Rafael Guerra Méndez Clinic in the city of Valencia, Miss Tourism Carabobo 2013 was hit by the projectile in the right-hand side of the occipital lobe, which hosts the brain's visual centre.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa madaktari bingwa waliomtibu kwneye kiliniki hiyo ya Dk. Rafael Guerra Méndez iliyopo jijini Valencia, Mrembo huyo ambaye ni Miss Tourism wa Carabobo kwa mwaka 2013 alipigwa risasi kutoka upande wake wa kulia wa fuvu, linalobeba sehemu ya ubongo inayohusika na kuona.

eng: There was speculation that she would have lost her vision even if she had been able to recover.
swa: Kulikuwa na tetesi kuwa angepoteza uwezo wake wa kuona hata kama angeweza kupona.

eng: Genesis Carmona (23) wounded by a bullet at the protest in Valencia comes out of the operating theatre, is now in intensive care.
swa: Genesis Carmona (23) amejeruhiwa na risasi akiwa kwenye maandamano jijini Valencia ametoka kwenye chumba cha upasuaji, na sasa yu katika chumba cha wagonjwa mahututi.

eng: A Caracas newspaper has published a collection of tweets from the user Héctor Rotunda (@Hecalo), who narrates the events from the moment Génesis Carmona received the gunshot wound until her death.
swa: Gazeti la Caracas lilichapisha mkusanyiko wa twiti kutoka kwa mtumiaji wa mtandao wa twita aitwaye Héctor Rotunda (@Hecalo), anayeelezea mfululizo wa matukio tangu Génesis Carmona alipopigwa risasi mpaka alipopoteza maisha yake.

eng: Rotunda was in the same part of the protest as the late beauty queen.
swa: Rotunda alikuwa karibu na mrembo huyo wakati wa maandamano hayo.

eng: We were at the march in front of the Cedeño subway station.
swa: Tulikuwa tukiandamana mbele ya kituo cha basi cha Cedeño.

eng: We heard a burst of gunfire and threw ourselves to the ground...
swa: Tulisikia mlio wa risasi na wote tukalala chini...

eng: On Twitter the reactions of anguish and accusations continue.
swa: Kwenye mtandao wa twita miitikio ya tukio hilo pamoja na lawama zinaendelea kumiminika.

eng: The Governor of the State of Carabobo, Francisco Ameliach, has been singled out as the main instigator of the attack on the protest in Valencia.
swa: Gavana wa Jimbo la Carabobo, Francisco Ameliach, ametwajwa kuwa mtu aliye nyuma ya shambulizi hilo kwenye maandamano jijini Valencia.

eng: A few days ago the Governor sent messages over Twitter that the protestors are now using to accuse him of inciting violence .
swa: Siku chache zilizopita Gavana huyo alituma twiti kwenye mtandao wa twita kwamba waandamanaji sasa wamezoea kumtuhumu kwa kuanzisha mapigano .

eng: In the following tweet, for example, he mentions the UBCH , the Bolívar - Chávez Battle Units (Unidades de Batalla Bolívar - Chávez) of the United Socialist Party of Venezuela (PSUV - Partido Socialista Unido de Venezuela), the country's governing party.
swa: Katika twiti ifuatayo, kwa mfano, anataja UBCH , kifupi cha Kikosi cha Vita cha Bolívar - Chávez (Unidades de Batalla Bolívar - Chávez) cha Chama cha Kisoshalisti cha Venezuela (PSUV - Partido Socialista Unido de Venezuela), ambacho ndicho kinachotawala nchini humo.

eng: UBCH get ready for the forceful counter-attack.
swa: UBCH muwe tayari kwa kujibu mapigano.

eng: Diosdado will give the order.
swa: Diosdado atatoa amri.

eng: Diosdado Cabello is currently President of the National Assembly (Venezuelan Parliament).
swa: Diosdado Cabello ndiye Rais wa Bunge la Taifa hilo Venezuela.

eng: Meanwhile the Member of Parliament Francisco Soteldo made a statement to the media asking for justice for the death of Carmona:
swa: Wakati huo huo, mbunge Francisco Soteldo alitoa kauli kwenye vyombo vya habari akidai haki itendeke kufuatia kifo cha Carmona:

eng: Soteldo: "We demand justice for the death of Génesis Carmona"
swa: Soteldo: "Tunadai haki kwa kifo cha Génesis Carmona"

eng: Thus Carmona has become the fourth fatality in the protests that have been taking place in Venezuela.
swa: Kwa kifo hicho, Carmona anakuwa mtu wa nne kupoteza maisha katika maandamano ambayo yamekuwa yakiendelea nchini Venezuela.

eng: One of China's top journalists and TV anchors, Chai Jing, has caused a stir online after she gave birth in the US, with some netizens calling her a "traitor" or a "liberal hypocrisy".
swa: Mmoja kwa waandishi wa wanaoheshimika nchini China na mgwiji wa televisheni, Chai Jing, amesababisha moto mkali mtandaoni baada ya kujifungulia Marekani, huku watumiaji wengine wa mtandao wakimwita "msaliti" au "mnafiki".

eng: After pictures of Chai holding a newborn baby at an airport were published online, reports surfaced that she had given birth to a daughter in the US in October 2013.
swa: Baada ya picha za Chai akiwa amembeba mwanae mchanga uwanja wa ndege kuchapishwa mtandaoni, taarifa zilisambaa kwamba alikuwa amejifungua mtoto wa kike nchini Marekani mwezi Oktoba 2013.

eng: Obviously, the benefit is that the child becomes a US citizen.
swa: Ilivyo, faida ni kwamba mtoto huyo anakuwa raia wa Marekani.

eng: A highly respected reporter in China, Chai is known for her sharpness, persistence and her direct, cut-to-the point interview technique.
swa: Mtangazaji huyo anayeheshimika sana nchini China, Chai anafahamika kwa weledi wake, ufuatiliaji na mbinu yake ya kuhoji bila kona, na kujielekeza kwenye hoja moja kwa moja.

eng: She made her name for covering the SARS epidemic in 2003 and the Sichuan earthquake in 2008.
swa: Amejitengenezea jina kwa kutangaza habari za mlipuko wa mafua ya ndege (SARS) mwaka 2003 na tetemeko la Sichua mwaka 2008.

eng: Chai Jing holding a newborn baby at an airport.
swa: Chai Jing akiwa amembeba mwanae alipokuwa uwanja wa ndege.

eng: Photo from Sina Weibo
swa: Picha ya Sina Weibo

eng: Chai giving birth in the US has disappointed a lot of her fans, with many calling her hypocritical.
swa: Kitendo cha Chai kujifungulia nchini Marekani kimewakatisha tamaa mashabiki wake wengi, huku wengi wakimwita mnafiki.

eng: Netizen “Tan” wrote:
swa: Mtumiaji wa mtandao ajiitaye “Tan” aliandika:

eng: We should understand that these public figures attack or criticize their home country, not because they love this country but one day have the capability to embrace the United States, Europe and other countries.
swa: Tufike mahali tuelewe kuwa hawa watu maarufu wana tabia ya kushambulia na hata kuzikosoa nchi zao walikozaliwa, si kwa sababu wanaipenda nchi hii lakini kwa sababu siku moja wanaweza kujikuta wakihamia Marekani, Ulaya na hata kwenye nchi nyinginezo.

eng: Which kind of people who criticize this country are more sincere?
swa: Watu gani wanaoikosoa nchi hii wanamaanisha?

eng: Only those who will always be Chinese.
swa: Ni wale tu ambao siku zote watabaki kuwa wa-China.

eng: However, a large number of people also expressed their support.
swa: Hata hivyo, idadi kubwa ya watu waliunga mkono kitendo hicho.

eng: Some were sad about the emigration trend among China’s middle class, calling for reflection among Chinese top leaders:
swa: Wengine wakisikitishwa na tabia inayoshika kasi ya kuhama nchi miongoni mwa watu wa tabaka la kati, wakitoa mwito kwa viongozi waandamizi nchini China kutafakari:

eng: Very realistic, higher-ups should reflect on why things like this happen.
swa: Ni ukweli kabisa, kwamba vigogo wajitafakari kwa nini mambo yamekuwa hivi.

eng: When thinking about the future, she has the ability to select a country with a more fair, equal and sound system for his child.
swa: Tunapotafakari siku za mbeleni, (Chai) anaweza kuchagua nchi yenye mfumo wa haki, usawa na unaoeleweka kwa ajili ya mwanae.

eng: It’s not for anyone else to comment on.
swa: Hili si suala la mtu yeyote kulitolea maoni.

eng: If you have the ability, would you become a US citizen?
swa: Kama una uwezo, je ungependa kuwa raia wa Marekani?

eng: Think about it and you will understand.
swa: Tafakari sana na utaelewa.

eng: We ourselves cannot change the status quo in this country, we do not have the votes, why can’t we make a change for our children?
swa: Sisi wenyewe hatuwezi kubadilisha hali ya mambo tuliyoizoea nchini humu, hatuna kura, sasa kwa nini tusifanye mabadiliko kwa watoto wetu?

eng: It’s Chai Jing’s own freedom and personal matter to decide where her child should be born.
swa: Ni uhuru wa Chai Jing na ni juu yake mwenyewe kuamua wapi mwanae azaliwe.

eng: Commentator Liu Xuesong wrote :
swa: Mchambuzi Liu Xuesong aliandika :

eng: Whether one is patriotic or not, the most important thing is not to find out where the child was born, but to see his role as a citizen in this country, and how many good deeds he has done.
swa: Ikiwa ni uzalendo au sivyo, jambo la muhimu si kujua wapi mtoto alizaliwa, lakini muhimu ni kutazama wajibu wake kama raia wa nchi hii, na vingapi vizuri amevifanya kwa ajili ya nchi hii.

eng: Whether if it is worth it to love this country has something to do with the collective consciousness of this country, whether it shows love, harmony, friendliness and generosity and whether it focuses on the prosperity, justice and civilization.
swa: Kwamba ni muhimu kuipenda nchi hii ni suala la dhamira ya jumla ya watu wa nci hii, kwamba inaonyesha upendo, ushirika, urafiki na ukarimu na ikiwa lengo ni mafanikio, haki na ustaarabu.

eng: Another netizen wrote :
swa: Mtumiaji mwingine wa mtandaoni aliandika :

eng: Some netizens said that she only wants the child to have a more normal lifestyle, which has nothing to do with patriotism.
swa: Baadhi ya watu walisema kwamba anataka mwanae awe na mtindo wa kawaida wa maisha, kitu ambacho hakina uhusiano na uzalendo.

eng: Perhaps, this is the problem the government should reflect on.
swa: Labda, hili ndilo tatizo ambalo serikali yapaswa kulitafakari.

eng: Mexican authorities have confirmed the murder of Gregorio Jiménez de la Cruz, aka “Goyo”.
swa: Maafisa wa serikali nchini Mexico wamethibitisha kuuawa kwa Gregorio Jiménez de la Cruz, ajulikanaye pia kwa jina la “Goyo”.

eng: The lifeless body of Jiménez de la Cruz was found in a clandestine grave on February 11, 2014, according to reports in El Universal and La Jornada.
swa: Mwili wa Jiménez de la Cruz ulikutwa katika makaburi la siri tarehe 11, Februari, 2014, hii ni kwa mujibu wa taarifa kutoka El Universal na La Jornada.

eng: The electronic version of the weekly Proceso had previously reported the disappearance of the reporter, demanding answers from the authorities.
swa: Gazeti la kielekroniki la kila wiki la Proceso mapema lilitoa taarifa ya kupotea kwa mwandishi huyu wa habari huku likihitaji majibu kutoka serikalini.

eng: On Twitter, the hashtag #HastaQueAparezcaGoyo was used to express support for the family and colleagues of Jiménez de la Cruz during the darkest hours.
swa: Katika ukurasa wa Twita, kiungo habari #HastaQueAparezcaGoyo kilitumika kama namna ya kuiunga mkono familia na marafiki wa Jiménez de la Cruz wakati wa kipindi kigumu walichopitia.

eng: The journalist Paola Rojas was one of the first to spread the word on Twitter:
swa: Mwandishi wa habari, Paola Rojas ndiye aliyekuwa wa kwanza kusambaza habari katika kupitia ukurasa wa Twita:

eng: The Special Prosecutor of Veracruz has confirmed that journalist Gregorio Jiménez was murdered.
swa: Mpelelezi maalum wa shitaka la Veracruz amethibitisha kuwa mwandishi wa habari Gregorio Jiménez aliuawa

eng: The activist Jesús Robles Maloof asked for the resignation of the governor in Veracruz, where Gregorio Jiménez de la Cruz practiced his profession as a journalist:
swa: Mwanaharakati, Jesús Robles Maloof alimtaka Gavana wa jimbo la Veracruz kujiuzulu, mahali ambapo Gregorio Jiménez de la Cruz alifanyia shughuli zake kama mwandishi wa habari:

eng: It's time that Javier Duarte is removed from the government.
swa: Ni muda muafaka wa Javier Duarte aondolewe katika serikali.

eng: On the morning of February 11, the activist shared this photo:
swa: Asubuhi ya Februari 11, mwanaharakati mmoja aliweka picha hii katika ukurasa wa Twita:

eng: Mexican Journalists demostration against violence in #Veracruz. #HastaQueAparezcaGoyo . pic.twitter.com/1zPd1w8heb — Jesús Robles Maloof (@roblesmaloof) February 11, 2014
swa: Waandishi wa habari wa Mexico waandamana kupinga ukatili huko #Veracruz. #HastaQueAparezcaGoyo . pic.twitter.com/1zPd1w8heb — Jesús Robles Maloof (@roblesmaloof) February 11, 2014

eng: Twitter user Másdel131 also shared a photo from the same protest:
swa: Pia, mtumiaji wa Twita, Másdel131 aliweka picha iliyopigwa kutoka kwenye maandamano hayo:

eng: From the Veracruz' government's representation in the Federal District, journalists protest
swa: Kutoka makao makuu ya serikali ya Veracruz, waandishi wa habari waandamana

eng: While Pertaesus asked:
swa: Pertaesus aliuliza:

eng: The demand raised in the hashtag #HastaQueAparezcaGoyo raises another equally painful question-how long until we get our country back?
swa: Hitaji lao lililowekwa katika kiungo habari #HastaQueAparezcaGoyo laibua swali jingine lenye kuibua maumivu- itachukua muda gani hadi kuirudisha nchi yetu?

eng: Mexico is one of the world’s most dangerous countries for journalists, according to Reporters Without Borders. The organization adds that “more than 80 have been killed in the past decade, and 17 have disappeared”.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Waandishi wa Habari Wasio na Mipaka, "Mexico ni moja ya nchi hatari sana duniani kwa maisha ya waandishi wa habari”, Umoja huu unaongeza kuwa, “Zaidi ya waandishi wa habari 80 wameshauawa katika kipindi cha muongo mmoja uliopita, 17 hawajulikani walipo” Kifo cha Gregorio Jiménez de la Cruz lazima kijumuishwe katika idadi hii.

eng: In Mexico there is an atmosphere of uncontrolled war and violence, ever since the previous President, Felipe Calderón, launched an attack on drugs in 2006. Judging by the death of Gregorio Jiménez de la Cruz, the violence in the country continues under the administration of Enrique Peña Nieto.
swa: Nchini Mexico, kuna hali ya vita iliyoshindikana na machafuko, hii ni tokea Rais aliyepita, Felipe Calderón, kuanzisha mkakati wa kukabiliana na madawa ya kulevya mnamo mwaka 2006. kwa kuzingatia kifo cha Gregorio Jiménez de la Cruz, machafuko nchini Mexico yanaendelea chini ya uangalizi wa Enrique Peña Nieto.

eng: As questions began to emerge over Zambian President Michael Sata's commitment to following through on a campaign promise for a new constitution, the leader stunned with a comment mocking calls for a "people-driven" constitution by asking if any country had ever passed an animal-driven one.
swa: Wakati maswali yakianza kuibuka kuhoji utashi wa kisiasa wa Rais wa Zambia Michael Sata kufuatia ahadi ya kampeni kusimamia mchakato wa kupatikana kwa katiba mpya, kiongozi huyo amekuja na mzaha akikejeli "kelele" za wanaotaka katiba "inayotokana na watu" na kuwauliza kama ipo nchi yoyote duniani imewahi kupitisha katiba iliyotokana na wanyama.

eng: During a swearing in ceremony of constitution office holders, the only time Sata publicly addresses the nation on television, he said:
swa: Wakati wa sherehe za kuapishwa kwa maafisa wa masuala ya katiba, wakati pekee ambapo Sata amewahi kulihutubia taifa kwa njia ya runinga, alisema:

eng: And for all of you here, ask the most learned woman here, Madam Chibesakunda.
swa: Na kwenu nyote mlioko hapa, hebu mwulizeni mwanawake aliyesoma kuliko wote hapa, Mheshimiwa Chibesakunda.

eng: You are always saying people-driven constitution, people-driven constitution.
swa: Siku zote nawasikia mnasema katiba inayotokana na watu, katiba inayotokana na watu.

eng: Madam, where do you have an animal-driven constitution?
swa: Mheshimiwa, wapi tutapata katiba inayotokana na wanyama?

eng: Have you ever seen an animal-driven constitution, which country because everybody is talking of people driven constitution, so once you produce the animal driven one, let’s ask Mr Phiri, once you produce the animal driven constitution, we compare the two constitutions, what we have and then we shall look at that.
swa: Umewahi kuiona katiba inayotokana na wanyama, nchi gani kwa sababu kila mtu anazungumzia katiba iliyotokana na watu, ili ukishatengeneza ile iliyotokana na mnyama, labda tumwulize Bw. Phiri, tukishatengeneza katiba iliyotokana na wanyama, tuweze kuzilinganisha katiba hizo mbili, kile kilichomo ili sasa tuweze kutazama cha kufanya..

eng: As an opposition party, Zambia’s now-ruling party the Patriotic Front defeated the then-ruling Movement for Multiparty Democracy (MMD) in 2011 with a promise that when elected into office in elections later that year, it would pass a new constitution within 90 days of taking office.
swa: Kama chama cha upinzani, sasa kikiwa chama tawala nchini Zambia, chama cha Patriotic Front kilikishinda kilichokuwa chama tawala cha Movement for Multiparty Democracy (MMD) mwaka 2011 kwa ahadi kuwa kikichaguliwa kuingia ikulu baadae mwaka huo, kingepitisha katiba mpya ndani ya siku 90 baada ya kutwaa madaraka.

eng: A few weeks into office, President Sata appointed a technical committee to look into the previous constitutional making processes to come up with a new document.
swa: Wiki kadhaa baada ya kushika madaraka, Rais Sata aliteua kamati ya ufundi ili kutazama michakato iliyotumika kutengeneza katiba zilizopita ili kuja na rasimu ya katiba mpya.

eng: The promised landmark difference with the previous processes was to be that the draft constitution was going to be simultaneously released to both the government and the public and a referendum held.
swa: Pendekezo hilo ambalo ni la pekee lilikuwa kwamba rasimu hiyo ya katiba ingetolewa kwa wakati mmoja kwenda serikalini na kwa wananchi na wakati huo huo kura ya maoni ingefanyika.

eng: People holding a banner demanding that President Sata releases the draft constitution.
swa: Watu wakiwa wamebeba bango wakidai kwamba Rais sata aitoe rasimu ya katiba.

eng: Photo used with permission of The Zambian Voice.
swa: Picha imetumiwa kwa ruhusa ya The Zambian Voice.

eng: With shifting deadlines and the constitution making process running into two years, the government changed its approach and asked the technical committee to only print ten copies of the draft constitution, which the cabinet was to study first.
swa: Huku kukiwa na tarehe za mwisho zinazobadilika badilika na hatimaye mchakato wa kutengeneza katiba ukiendelea kwa mwaka wa pili sasa, serikali ilibadilisha mbinu yake na kuiomba kamati ya ufundi kuchapisha nakala kumi pekee za rasimu ya katiba, ili baraza la mawaziri lipate fursa ya kuiptia kwanza.

eng: The draft constitution was later leaked via Zambian Watchdog and is now known as the "eleventh copy".
swa: Rasimu hiyo ya katiba baadae ilivuja kupitia blogu ya Zambian Watchdog na sasa inafahamika kama "nakala ya kumi na moja".

eng: Some started to cast doubt on Sata’s commitment to enacting a new constitution when he said that the country did not need a fresh document altogether but only amendments to certain clauses.
swa: Baadhi ya watu walianza kuwa na wasiwasi na utashi wa kisiasa wa Rais Sata katika kuleta katiba mpya pale alinukuliwa akisema, nchi hii haikuhitaji katiba mpya kabisa bali mabadiliko ya hapa na pale.

eng: At another time, Sata said the current constitution was still good because six elections had been held under it.
swa: Wakati mwingine, Sata alisema katiba ya sasa ilikuwa bado ni nzuri kwa sababu chaguzi sita zilishafanyika kwa kuitumia katiba hiyo hiyo.

eng: Nyalubinge Ngwende on his Brutal Journal blog wrote:
swa: Nyalubinge Ngwende katika blogu yake inayojulikana kama Brutal Journal aliandika:

eng: hen it comes to the constitution, President Sata will not fool us.
swa: Linapokuja suala la katiba, Rais sata asitufanye wajinga.

eng: The building of roads, universities, more schools and health facilities come to mean nothing if the citizens are enslaved by political tyranny that refuses to hand them a constitution meant to unleash their full liberties and broaden opportunities for citizens, regardless of their geographical position on the global map.
swa: Ujenzi wa barabara, vyuo vikuu, shule zaidi na huduma za afya hazitakuwa na maana yoyote kama raia wanakuwa mateka wa utawala wa kisiasa unaokataa kuwapatia yenye maana ya kuwapatia uhuru wao kamili na fursa pana kwa raia, bila kujali waliko kijiografia katika ramani ya dunia.

eng: A people driven constitution is our choice and not that of PF!
swa: Katiba inayotokana na watu ni chaguo letu na sio chaguo la PF!

eng: Ngwende goes on to explain what is meant by a people-driven constitution in a country where Cabinet with the President as the head has a played a bigger role in the enactment of constitutions by excluding clauses that people had recommended and infusing those favouring the rulers:
swa: Ngwende anaendelea kuelea kile kinachomaanishwa na katiba inayotokana na watu katika nchi ambayo Baraza la Mawaziri linaloongozwa na rais limefanya wajibu wake vya kutosha katika kutengeneza katiba kwa njia ya kutoa vipengele ambavyo wananchi walivipendekeza na kuviondoa vile vinavyowapendelea watawala:

eng: When civil society activists are talking of a people driven constitution, they mean a good document that will stand the test of time; with statutes that meet the aspirations of the people and one that the people themselves will agree to.
swa: Wakati wanaharakati wa asasi za kiraia wanazungumzia katiba iliyotokana na watu, wanamaanisha katiba nzuri itakayodumu kwa muda mrefu; yenye sheria zinazojibu matakwa ya watu na ile ambayo watu wenyewe wataikubali.

eng: Joining a chorus of other opposition politicians and civil society organisations, MMD President Nevers Mumba commented:
swa: Akiungana na wanasiasa wengine wa upinzani na asasi za kiraia, rais wa MMD Nevers Mumba alikuwa na maoni haya:

eng: I think that God has allowed him to lose his way because I can’t imagine a President making such comments.
swa: Ninafikiri kuwa Mungu amemruhusu apoteze mwelekeo kwa sababu siwezi kuamini Rais akitoa matamshi ya aina ile.

eng: What Zambians are saying is that look, we want a better constitution in which we participate in its formulation For him to make such comments shows arrogance of the highest level.
swa: Kile ambacho Wazambia wanakisema ni kwamba tazama, tunahitaji katiba bora ambayo tutashiriki katika kuitengeneza Kitendo chake kutoa matamshi ya aina ile yanaonyesha kiburi cha hali ya juu sana.

eng: I appeal to the President to be presidential about this matter. We are determined to have a new constitution, with or without him anyway.
swa: Ninamwomba rais kuwa na hadhi ya ki-Rais katika suala hili. tumekusudia kupata katiba mpya, iwe akiwepo yeye au vinginevyo.

eng: Sata ordered government officials not to respond to the constitution debate.
swa: Sata aliwaamuru maafisa wa serikali kutokujibu lolote linalohusiana na mjadala wa katiba.

eng: However, his Justice Minister and PF Secretary General Wynter Kabimba during a visit to Malawi probably gave away the biggest fear his government had in the draft document—50 percent plus one threshold for election to the office of the president and a presidential running mate for the office of vice president.
swa: Hata hivyo, Waziri wake wa Sheria na Katibu Mkuu wa PF Wynter Kabimba akiwa kwenye ziara nchini Malawi huenda alipuuzia woga wa serikali wa serikali yake kwenye rasimu ya katiba - kufikiwa kwa asilimia 50 ya kura zote jumlisha kura moja kwa uchaguzi wa rais na mgombea mwenza wake wa nafasi ya umakamu wa Rais.

eng: Kabimba said:
swa: Kabimba alisema:

eng: There are all these demands about 50 percent plus one constitutional provision, running mate constitutional provision without taking into account that where these provisions obtain they have caused more problems than the solutions they should have brought about to society.
swa: Kuna madai yote haya kuhusu hitaji la kikatiba la asilimia 50 jumlisha kura moja na hitaji la mgombea mwenza bila kuzingatia kuwa mambo haya yanapokuwa kwenye katiba yamesababisha matatizo mengine zaidi kuliko majibu ambayo vingetoa kwa jamii.

eng: We can learn from others.
swa: Tunaweza kujifunza kwa wengine.

eng: We don’t have to make the same mistakes that others have made in order to do the right thing.
swa: Hatulazimiki kufanya makosa yale yale ambayo wengine wameyafanya nia kufanya jambo jema zaidi.

eng: Zimbabwe's former Finance Minister Tendai Biti.
swa: Waziri wa zamani wa Fedha wa Zimbabwe Tendai Biti.

eng: Photo released under Creative Commons by Chatham House.
swa: Picha imetolewa chini ya leseni ya Creative Commons na Chatham House.

eng: Zimbabwe's former Finance Minister Tendai Biti's home was reportedly bombed in the early morning February 25, 2014, Twitter users and other media houses announced. He is one of the key members of the opposition Movement for Democratic Change and a staunch critic of President Robert Mugabe.
swa: Nyumba ya Waziri wa zamani wa Fedha wa Zimbabwe Tendai Biti ilidaiwa kulipuliwa alfajiri ya Februari 25, 2014, watumiaji wa Twita na vyombo vingine vya habari vilitangaza. ni mmoja wa wanachama tegemeo wa chama cha Upinzani cha MDC na mkosoaji mkubwa wa Rais Robert Mugabe.

eng: Biti is the secretary general for Movement for Democratic Change, led by former Prime Minister Morgan Tsvangirai.
swa: Biti ni katibu mkuu wa MDC, kinachoongozwa na Waziri Mkuu wa zamani wa nchi hiyo, Morgan Tsvangirai.

eng: His home was first bombed in 2011.
swa: Nyumba yake ililipuliwa mwaka 2011.

eng: No suspects have been arrested so far.
swa: Hakuna watuhumiwa walikamatwa mpaka sasa.

eng: Tendai Biti's house has reportedly been bombed ... again — Nqaba Matshazi (@nqabamatshazi) February 25, 2014
swa: Nyumba ya Tendai Biti inasemekana kulipuliwa...kwa mara nyingine

eng: @freedomtrapped @lanceguma Sad bad and mad, all of it.
swa: Inahuzunisha vibaya na ni ukichaa, vyote kwa pamoja.

eng: I take no sides.
swa: Sina upande wa kutetea.

eng: Bob's eating popcorn and making jokes about political violence. — Conor Walsh (@ConorMWalsh) February 25, 2014
swa: Bob anakula bata na kufanya utani kuhusu ghasia hizi za kisiasa

eng: @ConorMWalsh @LanceGuma they may find traces of a familiar birthday cake on the bottles & canisters used to make the bombs — Webster Madanhi (@FreedomTrapped) February 25, 2014
swa: Wanaweza kukuta mabaki ya keki maarufu ya kusherehekea siku ya kuzaliwa kwenye chupa za vikopo vilivyotumika kutenengeneza mabomu

eng: Our opposition parties have their fair share of hooligans, but petrol bombs are the domain of the state security agencies. — Lance Guma (@LanceGuma) February 25, 2014
swa: Vyama vyetu vya upinzani haviwezi kukwepa lawama kwa kuwa na vikundi vya wahuni, lakini mabomu ya petroli hayawezi kutoka kwingine kokote isipokuwa kwneye vyombo vya usalama vya dola.

eng: Although many people seem to suspect the government, one Twitter user, tinashe chirape, suggested that it was the work of the opposition Movement for Democratic Change (MDC):
swa: Inagwa watu wengi wanaonekana kuitilia mashaka serikali, mtumiaji mmoja wa mtandao wa Twita, tinashe chirape, alipendekeza kuwa ilikuwa ni kazi ya chama cha upinzani cha MDC chenyewe:

eng: Is violence taking its course in the MDC ?
swa: Hivi ghasia ndio zimeanza ndani ya MDC ?

eng: Another user said the news of the bombing is fake:
swa: Another user said the news of the bombing is fake:

eng: Fake!
swa: Uongo!

eng: Its a bottle thrown at gate by passing street kid>"@kwirirayi: Tendai Biti's house bombed http://t.co/uzmbq9VUWY #3mobzw #twimbos" — Rufaz~wa~Mavhure (@Mavhure) February 25, 2014
swa: Ni chupa tu imetupiwa getini na mtoto wa mtaani aliyekuwa anapita

eng: In the blog Panfleto Negro , John Manuel Silva and Emiliana Duarte are keeping a list of confirmed deaths from the ongoing protests taking place in Venezuela.
swa: Katika blogu ya Panfleto Negro , John Manuel Silva na Emiliana Duarte wanafuatilia orodha ya vifo vilivyotokea kufuatia maandamano yanayoendelea nchini Venezuela.

eng: A day after a tiny news items titled, "Saudi Arabia 'seeking Pakistani arms for Syrian rebels" appeared in Pakistani newspapers, political blogger Ahsan Butt posts a provocative piece warning Pakistan's foreign policymakers against tiptoeing into Syria's affairs.
swa: Siku moja baada ya dondoo ndogo ya habari yenye kichwa cha habari, "Saudi Arabia 'inatafuta uungwaji mkono kwa waasi wa" ilipoonekana kwenye magazeti ya Pakistani, mwanablogu wa siasa Ahsan Butt aliposti tahadhari kali kwa watunga sera ya mambo ya Kimataifa wa nchi ya Pakstani kuachana na mambo ya ndani ya Syria.

eng: In "This is not our war (Syria Edition)" on the Five Rupees Blog, Ahsan writes:
swa: Katika makala ya "Hii siyo vita yetu (Toleo la Syria)" kwenye blogu ya Five Rupees, Ahsan anaandika:

eng: What Pakistan is doing vis-a-vis Syria is one of the dumbest things Pakistan has done in a long time, and that’s really saying something.
swa: Kile ambacho Pakistani inakifanya kinyume cha Syria ni moja wapo ya mambo ya kijinga kabisa kuwahi kufanywa na Pakistani kwa muda mrefu, na ambalo linatuma ujumbe muhimu.

eng: The Syrian civil war, tragic as it is, has nothing to do with Pakistan.
swa: Vita vya wenyewe kwa wenyewe Syria, hatika hali mbaya ilivyo, haihusu Pakistani kwa vyovyote vile.

eng: Pakistan has no interests in that conflict.
swa: Pakistani haina maslahi yoyote kwenye mgogoro huo.

eng: None.
swa: Hakuna.

eng: Saudi Arabia is in talks with Pakistan to provide Pakistan-made anti-aircraft and anti-tank rockets.
swa: Saudi Arabia iko kwenye mazungumzo na Pakistani ili kutoa ndege na roketi za kivita zilizotengenezwa Pakistani.

eng: Ahsan warns:
swa: Ahsan anaonya:

eng: Is it wise and advisable to wade into a sectarian civil war two thousand miles away?
swa: Hivi ni busara na inashauriwa kweli kujiingiza kwenye vita vya ndani ya nchi iliyo kwenye umbali wa maili elfu mbili?

eng: Just examine the trajectory of sectarian violence over the last decade.
swa: Hebu saili mwenendo wa ghasia hizi katika muongo uliopita.

eng: He explains that any interference in Syria will force the Pakistani state to pay attention to rising sectarian violence in the country:
swa: Anaeleza kuwa hatua yoyote ya kuingilia mambo ya Syria itailazimisha serikali ya Pakistani kuanza kutazama kwa makini kukua kwa ghasia za kidini ndani ya nchi:

eng: What are the possible ramifications for such a policy on sectarian violence in Pakistan?
swa: Yepi ni madhara yanayowezekana kutokana na sera za aina hiyo linapokuja suala la ghasia za kidini nchini Pakistani?

eng: Is it likely to exacerbate and make more deadly sectarian cleavages or the opposite?
swa: Je, inawezekana ikachochea misuguano ya kidini au kinyume chake?

eng: Ahsan lists four more provocative questions which you can read here.
swa: Ahsan anaorodhesha maswali manne ya kufikirisha zaidi ambayo unaweza kuyasoma hapa.

eng: Demonstration in Valencia, Venezuela, on February 13, 2014.
swa: Maandamano jijini Valencia, Venezuela, mnamo Februari 13, 2014.

eng: Photo by Luis Turinese, copyright Demotix.
swa: Picha ya Luis Turinese, haki miliki Demotix.

eng: In various Venezuelan cities the demonstrations led and organized mostly by students have not ceased.
swa: Katika majiji mbalimbali nchini Venezuela maandamano yanayoongozwa na yaliyoandaliwa kwa kiasi kikubwa na wanafunzi hayajakoma.

eng: Protesters are demanding the release of students arrested by Venezuelan security forces.
swa: Waandamanaji wanadai kuachiliwa huru kwa wanafunzi waliokamatwa na vikosi vya usalama vya Venezuela.

eng: They have received the support of a group of citizens and opposition leaders, who also demand solutions to many socio-economic problems affecting the population.
swa: Wanafunzi hao wameungwa mkono na kikundi cha raia na hata viongozi wa upinzania, ambao nao wanadai ufumbuzi wa matatizo ya kijamii na kiuchumi yanayowaathiri sana walio wengi.

eng: Since early February the capitals of some Andean states in the country have been the epicenter of student demonstrations which, at the beginning, called for more security in universities.
swa: Tangu mwanzoni mwa mwezi Februari makao makuu ya majimbo ya nchi hiyo yamekuwa vituo vya maandamano ya wanafunzi ambayo, mwanzoni, yalikuwa na wito wa kudai usalama zaidi katika vyuo vikuu.

eng: Additionally, national political personalities were promoting street assemblies , also known as #LaSalida (the exit), aiming to “promote debate and dialogue to attain a democratic exit to some of the problems affecting our nation”.
swa: Kwa nyongeza, wanasiasa maarufu wa kitaifa walikuwa wakitangaza mikutano ya mitaani , inayofahamika kwa jina la #LaSalida (pa kutokea), iliyokuwa imelenga "kukuza majadiliano na midahalo ili kupata demokrasia ya kuwaokoa raia na matatizo yanayolikabili taifa”.

eng: By February 12, these political leaders decided to convene a national day of protests, enlisting the support of thousands of students and citizens across the country.
swa: Ilipofika Februari 2, wanasiasa hawa waliamua kuandaa siku rasmi ya maadamano ya kitaifa, wakiwaunga mkono maelfu ya wanafunzi na raia nchini kote.

eng: The consequences of that day have led to extending the popular demonstrations.
swa: Matokeo ya siku hiyo yamesababisha maandamano yaliyopata umaarufu mkubwa.

eng: Cities across the country are joining the call to protest, even though many of these demonstrations have resulted in violent clashes between protesters and law enforcement.
swa: Majiji kote nchini humo yanaitikia mwito wa maandamano, hata ingawa mengi ya maandamano haya yameshasababisha vurugu baina ya waandamanaji na vikosi vya ulinzi.

eng: Social networks, specially Twitter, have been flooded with photos documenting the protests in each region, taking the place of the regular mass media in Venezuela, which is going through a blackout due to the government's threats to fine media who cover the protests.
swa: Mitandao ya kijamii, hususani twita, imefurika picha za maandamano hayo katika kila mkoa, ikichukua nafasi ya vyombo vikuu vya habari nchini Venezuela, ambavyo kwa sasa vimefungiwa kufuatia tishio la serikali kuvipiga faini vyombo vya habari vitakavyotangaza ama kuandika habari za maandamano hayo.

eng: During Thursday's night, on February 13, user @yirli4ny_ shared an image of a 180-meter flag being hoisted in an important highway in Puerto Ordaz, in the Guayana region:

swa: Mwisho, El Periodista Cívico (mwandishi wa haki za raia) amekuwa akiandika habari kuhusu maandamano hayo ya kitaifa, akiweka habari mpya kuhusu waandamanaji waliokuwa wamewekwa kizuizini katika mikoa mbalimbali ya nchi hiyo.

eng: For the first time Costa Ricans living abroad are allowed to vote in a presidential election. From around the world, Costa Ricans have been using Twitter to report about their vote.

eng: This time, we, the 15,000 Costa Ricans living abroad, are key, our votes might avoid a run-off.
swa: Kipindi hiki, sisi raia 15,000 tunaoishi nje ya nchi, ni ufunguo, kura zetu lazima zizuie kufungana katika kura.

eng: From Costa Ricans living in Australia, the first ones to cast their vote, to the ones based in Japan, France, the United States and elsewhere, citizens are reporting about their vote with expressions full of excitement.
swa: Kutoka kwa Raia wa Costa Rica wanaoishi nchini Australia, ambao ndio waliokuwa wa kwanza kupiga kura, wakifuatiwa na wale wanaoishi Japan, Ufaransa, Marekani na kwingineko, raia wanaota taarifa huku wakionesha hisia zilizojaa hamaki.

eng: Timed with the start of President Park Geun-hye's second year in office, about 40 thousand South Koreans (police estimate 15 thousand) held protests across the country.
swa: Huku ukiwa umepangiliwa ufanyike mwanzo wa kipindi cha pili cha Rais Park Geun-hye madarakani, takribani wa-Korea elfu 40 (polisi wanadai ni elfu 15) walifanya mgomo nchini kote.

eng: The demonstration, spearheaded by Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, calls halt to a clampdown on labor groups, the government's move towards privatization of public sector and cover-up of the presidential election manipulation scandal.
swa: Mgomo huo, ulipangwa na Shirikisho la Vyama vya Wafanyakazi nchini Korea, ukiwa na wito wa kusitishwa kwa kudhibitiwa kwa vyama vya wafanyakazi, hatua ya serikali kubinafsisha sekta ya umma na kufunikwa skandali ya wizi wa kura katika uchaguzi wa rais.

eng: Prominent citizen journalist Media Mongu tweeted a photo of the protest (embedded below).
swa: Mwandishi wa habari za kiraia anayeheshimika Mongu alitwiti picha ya maandamano (imewekwa hapa chini).

eng: Thousands of Venezuelans that now live outside of their home country have organised demonstrations to support the actions on the streets in the South American country.
swa: Maelfu ya Wavenezuela wanaoishi ng'ambo wameandaa maandamano kuwaunga mkono wenzao wanaoandamana mitaani katika nchi yao ya Bara la Amerika ya Kusini.

eng: The images of these gatherings have been shared widely on social networks.
swa: Picha ya mikusanyiko hiyo zimekuwa zikisambaa kwenye mitandao ya kijamii.

eng: On Facebook the page SOS Venezuela collects a large number of photos, which are also published with the tags #iamyourvoicevenezuela #SOSVenezuela and #PrayForVenezuela on Twitter and Instagram.
swa: Kwenye ukurasa wa Facebook uitwao SOS Venezuela picha nyingi zinakusanywa, ambazo pia zinachapishwa kwa alama habari ya #iamyourvoicevenezuela #SOSVenezuela na #PrayForVenezuela kwenye mtandao wa Twita na Instagram.

eng: My cousin sent me this photos of Venezuelans and foreigners protesting today in Malta.
swa: Mpwa wangu amenitumia picha hii ya Wavenezuela na wageni wanaoandamana leo mjini Malta.

eng: Some Venezuelans abroad took advantage of the protests to deliver documents to international organisations or to the Parliaments of the countries where they live.
swa: Baadhi ya Wavenezuela ng'ambo walitumia fursa ya maandamano hayo kupeleka nyaraka kwa mashirika ya kimataifa au mabunge ya nchi hizo wanakoishi.

eng: This was the case with a group of citizens who demonstrated in The Hague.

swa: Tulipeleka nyaraka kwenye Bunge.

swa: Tulilaani vitendo vya uvunjifu wa haki za binadamu nchini Venezuela

swa: Gaby Silva aliweka video kwneye mtandao wa Instagram inayoonyesha maandamano yaliyofanywa na kikundi cha Wavenezuela jijini Madrid.

eng: The video shows citizens calling for justice, peace and dialogue.
swa: Video hiyo inawaonyesha wananchi hao wakitoa mwito wa haki, amani na majadiliano.

swa: Gazeti la TalCual lilisambaza picha ya waandamanaji kwneye viwanja vya Times Square jijini New York.

eng: Meanwhile, in Venezuela the opposition leader Leopoldo López turned himself in to the authorities and President Nicolás Maduro assured that he will faces charges of sedition and "unawareness of the Constitution".
swa: Wakati huo huo, nchini Venezuela kiongozi wa upinzani Leopoldo López alitekeleza ahadi yake kwa kujisalimisha mwenyewe kwa mamlaka za serikali na Rais Nicolás Maduro alitangaza kwamba atakabiliwa na mashitaka ya uchochezi na "kutokuelewa Katiba".

eng: Nepal’s Parliament has elected Mr. Sushil Koirala (75), the president of the party Nepali Congress, as the new Nepali Prime Minister.
swa: Bunge la Nepal limemchagua Bw. Sushil Koirala (75), rais wa chama cha Nepali Congress, kuwa Waziri Mkuu wa Nepal.

eng: Nepali diaspora blogger Indra congratulates the new Prime Minister and thinks that "the gift Mr. Koirala has for empowering others with his humility and sincerity will go a long way".
swa: Mwanablogu wa NNepali aishiye ughaibuni Indra anampongeza Waziri Mkuu mpya na anafikiri kwamba "zawadi aliyonayo Bw. Koirala kwa kuwawezesha wengine kwa unyenyekevu na ukweli haitaondoka wa haraka".

eng: One of the Taliban negotiators pulled out during a recent talk with the Pakistan government demanding that the agenda includes the strict imposition of Sharia law.
swa: Mmoja wa msemaji wa Taliban alijitoa kwenye majadiliano ya hivi karibuni na serikali ya Pakistan na kudai kuwa ajenda ni pamoja na kuanzishwa kwa sharia kali.

eng: Pakistani Blogger and Journalist Beena Sarwar highlights a protest note posted in Facebook titled '10 reasons why I do not want Shariah in Pakistan' by communities The Traitors of Pakistan (Liberal/Secular Pakistanis against oppression, discrimination, extremism and intolerance) and Pakistan Votes (activist community).
swa: Mwanablogu wa Pakistan na Mwandishi wa Habari Beena Sarwar alipinga wazo hilo kupitia tamko aliloliweka katika mtandao wa Facebook lenye kichwa cha habari 'sababu 10 kwa nini sitaki Shariah nchini Pakistan' na linapatikana katika mitandao mingine ya kijamii kamaKusitisha Udini Pakistan, harakati za kupinga ukandamizaji, ubaguzi, kuvuka mipaka na uvumilivu na Uchaguzi wa Pakistani linaloendeshwa na Asasi za Kiraia.

eng: Here are some gems:
swa: Hapa ni baadhi ya sababu:

eng: Religion and how I choose to practice it is my business and not that of the State.
swa: Dini na ninavyochagua kuishi ni biashara yangu na ni suala lisiloihusu Serikali.

eng: Enforcing Shariah will not make me a better Muslim nor will it make Pakistan a welfare state.
swa: Kutekeleza Shariah hakutanifanya kuwa muislamu bora wala kuboresha hali ya mambo nchini Pakistan.

eng: The world’s welfare states are all governed by secular governments.
swa: Mataifa yote yaliyoendelea yanatawaliwa na serikali zisizo za kidini.

eng: I reject the idea that Shariah in any form can be enforced by those who have raped and plundered my country, blown up schools and mosques and beheaded soldiers.
swa: Kukataa wazo kwamba Shariah kwa namna yoyote inaweza kutekelezwa na wale ambao wamebaka na kupora nchi yangu, kulipua shule na misikiti na kukata askari vichwa.

eng: I will not give these criminals the right to dictate to me.
swa: Sitawapa wahalifu hawa haki ya kuniamrisha.

eng: I will not give up my civil rights, including freedom of thought and expression, under the guise of Shariah.
swa: Sitasalimisha haki yangu ya kiraia, ikiwa ni pamoja na uhuru wa mawazo na kujieleza, chini ya kivuli cha Shariah..

eng: Activists John Bosco, (handcuffs) and Bisi Alimi (sign) in prison uniforms protesting in London against anti-gay legislation in Uganda on December 10, 2012.
swa: Wanaharakati John Bosco, (mwenye pingu mkononi) na Bisi Alimi (mwenye bango) wakiwa na mavazi ya kifungwa wakiandamana jijini London kupinga sheria mpya ya kupinga ushoga nchini Uganda tarehe 10, Decemba, 2012.

eng: Photo by Reporter#20299.
swa: Picha kwa hisani ya Reporter#20299.

eng: Uganda's President Yoweri Museveni signed a controversial anti-gay bill into law on January 24, 2014 that punishes homosexual acts with life in prison in some cases.
swa: Rais wa Uganda Yoweri Museveni amesaini muswada unaopiga marufuku ushoga na kuufanya kuwa sheria tangu Januari 24, 2014. Sheria hiyo mpya itaadhibu vitendo vya ushoga kwa kifungo cha maisha jela katika baadhi ya masuala.

eng: The parliament of Uganda overwhelmingly passed the bill on December 20, 2013.
swa: Bunge la Uganda kwa kishindo kabisa lilipitisha muswada huo mnamo Desemba 20, 2013.

eng: It also provides for prison sentences for anyone who does not report gay people to authorities and punishes the use of Facebook and Twitter accounts to fight for gay rights a crime with a maximum of seven years in jail.
swa: Sheria hiyo inatoa adhabu ya kifungo jela kwa yeyote ambaye hatatoa taarifa za kuwapo kwa raia anayefanya vitendo vya kishoga kwa mamlaka za kiserikali na vile vile sheria hiyo inatoa hukumu kwa mtu yeyote kutumia mitandao ya kijamii kama Facebook na Twita kwa minajili ya kupigania haki za mashoga kitendo kinachotafsiriwa na sheria hiyo kuwa ni cha jinai na hukumu yake ni kifungo kisichozidi miaka saba jela.

eng: US President Barack Obama and other leaders around the world have warned President Museveni that the law is an abuse of human rights.
swa: Rais wa Marekani Barack Obama na viongozi wengine duniani walimuonya Rais Museveni kuwa sheria hiyo ni uvunjifu wa haki za binadamu.

eng: Ugandan LGBT activists say that the law makes Uganda one of the worst places to be gay in the world.
swa: Wanaharakati wa asasi ya Uganda inayotetea haki za mashoga na wasagaji (LGBT) wanasema kuwa sheria hiyo inaifanya Uganda kuwa sehemu hatari zaidi kwa mashoga duniani.

eng: Many people have taken to social media to discuss it, some in support while others adamantly against.
swa: Watu wengi wamejadili suala hili kwenye mitandao ya kijamii, wengine wakiunga mkono hatua hiyo na wengine wakiipinga vikali.

eng: My twitter & facebook are Illegal,the fine of five thousand currency points or imprisonment of a min. of 5 years & a maxi of 7 years or both — Dr. Frank Mugisha (@frankmugisha) February 24, 2014
swa: Akaunti ya Twita na ya Facebook ni kinyume cha sheria, faini ya sarafu 5,000 au kifungo jela hadi miaka mitano na kisichozidi miaka saba au vyote viwili kwa pamoja

swa: Marekani, sasa mnaweza kuishukia Uganda na kufanya chochote mnachotaka, muswada sasa umekuwa sheria

swa: Nyie manaopiga kelele za kuutukuza ushoga, mkafie kuzimu.

swa: Mtandelea kuzungumzia haki zenu za kijinga za binadamu wakati mkipumzika na ibilisi huko

eng: Social Researchers at L’Institut supérieur des sciences de la population (High Institute of Population Science) in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso published a report entitled "Grossesses non désirées et avortements au Burkina : causes et conséquences" (The causes and consequences of Unintended Pregnancies and Abortions in Burkina Faso).

eng: The report highlights a few important statistics :

eng: -A third of all pregnancies are unintended, and one third of these unintended pregnancies result in an abortion.
swa: -Theluthi ya mimba zote hazikutarajiwa, na theluthi ya mimba hizi husababisha utoaji wa mimba.

eng: -The size of the desired family is on average of 6 children in rural areas, against 3 in Ouagadougou.

eng: -Between half and two thirds of women who seek abortions are going to traditional practitioners who do not have the required medical skills.
swa: -Kati ya nusu na theluthi mbili ya wanawake wanaotafuta huduma za kutoa mbimba huenda kwa waganga wa kienyeji wasio na ujuzi wa kitabibu unaotakikana.

eng: Back then in Peru, terror and fear was part of our daily lives.

eng: I had just graduated from law school in Lima. It was late 1993 and my beloved Peru was recovering from 12 years of internal conflict which had claimed tens of thousands of lives.
swa: ndio nilikuwa nimemaliza elimu yangu ya sheria jijini Lima. ilikuwa ni mwaka 1993 na ambapo wakati huo Peru yangu niipendayo ndiyo ilikuwa inajijenga mara baada ya miaka 12 ya machafuko ya wenyewe kwa wenyewe yaliyogharimu maisha ya makumi elfu ya watu.

eng: Christmas was coming and I decided it was time for my first journey abroad to visit a dear aunt.
swa: Krismasi ilikuwa inakaribia na kwa mara ya kwanza niliamua kumtembelea shangazi yangu kipenzi.

eng: My mother's elder sister moved to Venezuela in the late 1950s. She got married in Caracas and settled there with her husband and two sons. After my younger cousin died in a car accident, my mother and her sister strengthened their bond and never let distance deter them from staying in touch.
swa: Dada mkubwa wa mama yangu alihamia Venezuela miaka ya 1950. aliolewa huko Caracas na aliishi huko na mumewe pamoja na watot wao wawili wa kiume. mara baada ya binamu wangu mdogo kufariki katika ajali ya gari, mama yangu na dada yake waliimarisha ukaribu wao, na kamwe hawakuruhusu umbali uwatenganishe.

eng: When I stepped foot outside Simón Bolívar International Airport in Maiquetía, I was instantly struck by how different everything looked, compared with Lima.
swa: Nilipofika Simón Bolívar International Airport Maiquetía, haraka nilishangazwa na namna ambavyo mambo yalivyokuwa tofauti, haswa nilipolinganisha na Lima.

eng: Caracas was a shiny modern city, with high-rises, highways, flyovers, and recently repaved roads.
swa: Caracas ulikuwa ni mji uliokuwa unapendeza, wenye majengo marefu, barabara kuu, barabara za kupandana, na barabara zilizokuwa zimefanyiwa ukarabati siku za karibuni.

eng: All the cars looked like they had just rolled off the factory assembly line, glossy and splendid. New cars was something we were just starting to get used to in Peru, after out-of-control hyperinflation had made all of us billionaires with little purchasing power.
swa: magari yote yalionekana kana kwamba ndio yametolewa kiwandani, yenye kung'aa na ya kifahari; Magari mapya ni jambo tililokuwa tumeanza kulizoea Peru, baada ya mfumuko wa bei usiozuilika uliotuacha wengi wetu kama mabilionea tusiokuwa na uwezo wa kununua chochote.

eng: The road signs looked like they had been painted the day before.
swa: alama z barabarani zilionekana kana kwamba ndio ziliandikwa jana tu.

eng: I could feel progress everywhere I looked, and this was just on the way from the airport to my aunt's house.
swa: niliweza kuhisi maendeleo kila nilipopatazama, na hiii ilikuwa ni katika safari yangu ya kutoka uwanja wa ndege kulekea nyumbani kwa shangazi yangu.

eng: Rain welcomed me on this adventure, something we Limeans are not used to at all.
swa: Katika safari hii, mvua ilinikaribisha, kitu ambacho sisi watu wa Lima hatukukizoea kabisa.

eng: The next day I started my tour of the city. I didn't feel like a total outsider.
swa: siku iliyofuata nilianza kulitembelea jiji. sikujiona kama mgeni kabisa.

eng: My generation grew up watching Venezuelan soap operas on TV, so some popular areas were familiar to me: Chacao, Chacaíto, the Virgen of Chiquingirá. So was the rhythmic speaking that I noticed was following me everywhere.
swa: Jamii yangu ilikua ikiangaliaMy generation grew up watching Venezuelan soap operas on TV, kwa hiyo baadhi ya maeneo maarufu yalikuwa siyo mageni kwangu: Chacao, Chacaíto, Bikira wa Chiquingirá. kwa hiyo, yalikuwa ni maongezi ya mahadhi niliyoyagundua yaliyokuwa yakinifuata kila nilipokuwepo, baada ya siku chache.

eng: During a visit to one museum, I saw a guy looking at a list of battles fought by Simón Bolívar, the liberator of Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Perú and Bolivia. There were the names of the battles with no indication of the where they'd been fought, and I stood by next to this tourist and started with a lesson learnt long ago at school: Carabobo, Venezuela; Boyacá, Bogotá, Pichincha, Ecuador; and Junín and Ayacucho, Perú (country of yours truly).
swa: katika kutembelea nyumba fulani ya maonesho, nilimuona jamaa mmoja akitazama orodha ya mapambano yaliyopiganwa na Simón Bolívar, ambaye ni mpigania uhuru wa Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Perú and Bolivia. kulikuwa na majina ya mapambano pasipo kuwa na kiashiria cha mahali ambapo mapambano hayo yalipofanyikia, na nilisimama pembeni mwa mtalii huyu na kisha nilianza na somo nililojifunza shuleni miaka mingi iliyopita: Carabobo, Venezuela; Boyacá, Bogotá, Pichincha, Ecuador; na Junín na Ayacucho, Perú (nchi yako kwa hakika).

eng: On that trip, during a visit to a beach whose name I have forgotten, my toes first felt the waters of the Atlantic, I owe that to Venezuela too.
swa: katika safari hiyo, wakati wa matembezi katika pwani ya bahari ambayo jina lake nimelisahau, vidole vyangu vilihisi maji ya bahari ya Atlantic, hali inayonikumbusha pia Venezuela.

eng: But what impressed me above all was the freedom people had, simply living their lives. We could enter any building and there was no military officer waiting to check our bags and belongings.
swa: Lakini kilichonifurahisha zaidi kilikuwa ni uhuru waliokuw nao watu, walikuwa wakiishi maisha waliyoyataka. tuliweza kuingia katika jengo lolote na bila ya kukutana na askari yeyote aliyekuwa akisubiri kutukagua na mali zetu.

eng: There were no metal detectors or special machines that we had to pass through at the entrance of shopping centers or museums or anywhere for that matter.
swa: Hakukuwa na vifaa vya kutafuatia vitu vya chuma alivyobeba mtu wala uwepo wa mashine maalum ambazo tulipaswa kupita kwanza katika milango ya maduka, katika majumba ya maonesho na mambo mengine yanayohusiana na hayo.

eng: I even walked in front of government buildings and ministries, as if that was the most normal thing to do. No one stopped me from being there, no one checked my documents, and no one made me feel like there was something to fear.
swa: Pia nilipita katika majengo ya serikali na ya wizara mbalimbali, kana kwamba hilo lilikuwa ni jambo la kawaida kabisa. hakuna aliyenikataza kuwepo maeneo yale, hakuna aliyetaka kuangalia taarifa zangu, na hakuna yeyote aliyetaka kunifanya nihisi kuwa kulikuw na jambo la kuogopa.

eng: That is why I have been overwhelmed with sadness, as the recent stories and images have been trickling out of Venezuela.
swa: Hii ndio sababu inayonifanya nigubikwe na huzuni, kufuatia habari za hivi karibuni pamoja na picha zinazotumwa kutoka Venezuela

eng: Brothers are fighting brothers.

eng: If you look at these stories, the local media is highlighting the "Facebook" part of the story as the ‘news’, but undermine the social, cultural, and political factors leading to those sad incidents.

eng: The live video streaming platform Ustream is offering citizen journalists the opportunity to apply for free pro accounts and publicity for any innovative use of video for breaking news, activism, and social good.

eng: Ustream has recently supported three live channels broadcasting from Ukraine's #EuroMaidan protests, including the popular channel Spilno.tv.

eng: “We created Ustream for Change to recognize the efforts of these inspiring citizen broadcasters, and we hope to encourage others to think beyond four walls and harness the power of live video,” says Brad Hunstable, Ustream’s CEO and founder.
swa: “Tulitengeneza Ustream kwa Mabadiliko kutambua jitihada za watengenezaji hawa mahiri wa video za kijamii, na tunatumaini kuwatia moyo wengine kufikiri nje ya kuta na kukuza nguvu ya video za moja kwa moja,” anasema Brad Hunstable, Mkurugenzi Mtendaji na Mwanzilishi wa Ustream.

eng: “Ustream is an enthusiastic supporter of Internet freedom, stable societies, and emerging democracies.
swa: “Ustream inaunga mkono kwa dhati kabisa uhuru wa Mtandaoni, jamii zilizo imara na demokrasia changa.

eng: Our technology offers a means of achieving transparency on both sides of the camera, and we fully intend to support those who are leading movements for positive change,” he says.
swa: Teknolojia yetu inatoa namna ya kuufikia uwazi kwa pende zote za kamera, na tunatarajia kuunga mkono kwa dhati wale wanaoongoza harakati za kuleta mabadiliko chanya,” anasema.

swa: Kabla ya kuanza kwa Mashindano ya Sochi ya Majira ya Baridi takribani majuma mawili yaliyopita, mwandishi aliyejitambulisha kama wako mkweli (yours truly) aliliambia shirika la Habari za Kimataifa la Marekani kwamba gahsia zinazoendelea nchini Ukraini zingeweza kubadili uelekeo wa ufuatiliaji wa mashindano ya Olimpiki kwa Warusi wanaotumia Intaneti.

eng: Today, after a relative lull, violence returned to Kiev’s streets, causing a dramatic shift in RuNet activity.
swa: Leo, baada ya ghasia na vurugu kuanza tena kwenye mitaa ya Kiev, na kugeuza kabisa upepo wa habari katika mitandao ya kiRusi.

eng: Indeed, the images coming out of Ukraine depict something like a civil war.
swa: Kwa hakika, picha zinazokuja kutoka Ukraini zinachora taswira ya kitu kinachofanana na vita vya wenyewe kwa wenyewe.

eng: While the news from Kiev is making headlines globally, comparative Twitter analytics demonstrate that today’s events in Ukraine galvanize Russian speakers to a degree distinct from the rest of the world.
swa: Wakati habari kutoka Kiev zikigonga vichwa vya habari duniani kote, uchambuzi wa matumizi ya mtandao wa Twita yanaonyesha kwamba matukio yanayoendelea leo nchini Ukraine yamekamata hisia za wazungumzaji wa Kirusi kuliko sehemu nyingine yoyote duniani.

eng: Indeed, in the last 24 hours on Twitter, Russian users’ interest in Ukraine has surpassed their attention on the Olympics.
swa: Kwa hakika, katika masaa 24 yaliyopita kwenye mtandao wa Twita, hamasa ya watumiaji wa Twita wa Ki-Rusi katika kufuatialia hali ya mambo nchini Ukraini imezidi bashasha ya kufuatilia mashindano ya Olimpiki.

eng: This reverses a trend in place since January 25, 2014, weeks before even the opening ceremony, when Russians last tweeted more about Kiev than Sochi.
swa: Hali hii inabadili mwelekeo uliokuwepo tangu Januari 25, 2014, majuma kadhaa kabla ya kufunguliwa rasmi kwa mashindano hayo, ambapo wa-Rusi wali-twiti zaidi kuhusu Kiev kuliko Sochi, mahali yanakofanyikia mashindano ya Olimpiki.

eng: The trend among Anglophone Twitter users over the last month is similar, but interest in Sochi has always dominated.
swa: Takwimu za watumiaji wa Twita baina ya wazungumzaji wa Kiingereza kwa zaidi ya mwezi uliopita zinaonyesha hali hiyo hiyo, lakini hamasa ya kujua kinachoendelea Sochi imekuwa juu siku zote.

eng: Even today, with Ukraine in flames, English-language tweets about Kiev are just over half the more than 200 thousand about the Winter Games.
swa: Hata leo, Ukraine ikiwa inawaka moto, twiti za Kiingereza kuhusu Kiev zimezidi kidogo nusu ya zaidi ya twiti laki mbili kuhusu Mashindano ya Olimpiki.

eng: While it’s no surprise that Internet users are drawn to the revolutionary display in Kiev, it is remarkable that the host of the Winter Olympics seems to have lost its home audience to a foreign event.
swa: Wakati haishangazi kwamba watumiaji wa Intaneti wamevutwa na harakati za kimpinduzi huko Kiev, inashangaza kwamba wenyeji wa mashindano ya Olimpiki wamepoteza hadhira yao kwa tukio la nje ya nchi hiyo.
