eng: Several digital rights international organizations sent the Mexican Congress a letter expressing international support for the defense of the freedom of expression and Internet freedom in Mexico.
swa: Mashirika kadhaa ya kimataifa ya haki za digitali zilitumia kongamano la Mexico barua kuonyesha msaada wa kimataifa kwa ajili ya kutetea uhuru wa kujieleza na uhuru kwenye mtandao nchini Mexico.

eng: The letter is signed by Electronic Frontier Foundation, Vía Libre, Digital Rights NGO, among other academics and experts.
swa: Barua imetiwa sahihi na Electronic Frontier Foundation, Vía Libre, Digital Rights NGO, miongoni mwa wasomi wengine na wataalam.

eng: According to the signers, each regulation refered to telecommunications and broadcastiong approved by Mexican Congress should comply constitutional regulations and international rules about human rights signed by Mexico.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa waliotia sahihi, kila kanuni inakusudia kulazimisha kanuni za mawasiliano ya simu na utangazaji zilizopitishwa na kongamano la Mexico kuzingatia kanuni za kikatiba na sheria za kimataifa kuhusu haki za binadamu iliyotiwa saini na Mexico.

eng: They also issued a call for the observance of the UN resolution about right to privacy in the digital era on the complimentary law on telecommunicatons, the joint declaration about surveillance programs and their impact in freedom of expresson and the 13 principles about human rights, in order to ensure the respect of human rights in the internet.
swa: Pia walitoa wito kwa maadhimisho ya azimio la Umoja wa Mataifa kuhusu haki ya faragha katika zama za digitali juu ya sheria ya lazima ya mawasiliano ya simu, tamko la pamoja juu ya mipango ya ufuatiliaji na athari zake katika uhuru wa kujieleza kanuni 13 kuhusu haki za binadamu , ili kuhakikisha heshima ya haki za binadamu katika mtandao inakuwepo.

eng: This week's GV Face comes to you live from São Paulo, Brazil where government, civil society and corporate representatives from around the world gathered this week at NETMundial to hash out a "roadmap" for global Internet governance in a post-Snowden world.
swa: Mazungumzo ya GV juma hili yanakujia moja kwa moja kutoka São Paulo, Brazil mahali ambapo wawakilishi wa serikali, vyama vya kiraia na mashirika wamekusanyika kutoka duniani kote wiki hii katika kituo cha mkutano cha NETMundial ili kutengeneza 'mwongozo' wa utawala wa kidunia wa mtandao wa intaneti katika kipindi hiki cha baada ya sakata la Snowden.

eng: Ellery Biddle of Global Voices Advocacy is joined by Marianne Diaz and Ben Wagner.
swa: Ellery Biddle wa Global Voices Utetezi anaungana na Marianne Diaz na Ben Wagner.

eng: A secret US plan to support regime change in Cuba with a Twitter-like messaging service called ZunZuneo has now come under the spotlight with news reports that thousands of Cubans were duped into signing up for the service under false pretenses.
swa: Mpango wa siri wa Marekani wa kubadili utawala nchini Cuba wenye huduma ya ujumbe inayofanana na Twita iitwayo ZunZuneo sasa unaangaliwa kwa mashaka baada ya kuwepo kwa taarifa kuwa maelfu ya wa-Cuba walidanganyika kujisajili kupata huduma hizo.

eng: Will there be consequences for digital activists worldwide?
swa: Je, kutakuwa na madhara kwa wanaharakati wa kidijitali duniani kote?

eng: Some worry it will lead to even more distrust and censorship of the internet and social media in their countries.
swa: Wengine wana mashaka gatua hiyo inaweza kusababisha hali ya kutokuaminiana na kufuatiliwa kwa mtandao wa intaneti na mitandao ya kijamii katika nchi zao.

eng: A spirited discussion with: Sana Saleem, Ivan Sigal and Solana Larsen.﻿
swa: Majadiliano ya kina na: Sana Saleem, Ivan Sigal na Solana Larsen.﻿

eng: In the early days of blogging, Iran's reformist bloggers were widely celebrated in international media.
swa: Katika siku za mwanzo za kublogu, wanablogu wataka mabadiliko wa Iran walikuwa maarufu sana kwenye vyonbo vya habari vya kimataifa.

eng: The country was youthful, internet savvy and early to innovate with online political dialogue.
swa: Nchi ilikuwa changa, watu wakiwa na uelewa wa mtandao wa intaneti na ilikuwa ya kwanza kufanya mijadala ya kisiasa mtandaoni.

eng: Lately, things are more quiet.
swa: Hivi karibuni, mambo yamekuwa kimya.

eng: Iran is famously heavy handed when it comes to censorship and repression.
swa: Iran inafamika kwa ubabe wake linapokuja suala la kufuatilia na kudhibiti yanayoandikwa mtandaoni.

eng: Have Persian bloggers been silenced?
swa: Je, wanalogu hao wamenyamazishwa?

eng: Or is what appears to be a gradual decline in blogging simply because of social media and changing norms?
swa: Au hiki kinachoonekana kuwa kushuka kwa kublogu ni kwa sababu ya kubadilika kwa utamaduni na uandishi wa kiraia?

eng: Writers of a new report by the Annenberg School’s Iran Media Program, “Whither Blogestan: Evaluating Shifts in Persian Cyberspace” (PDF) join Global Voices on GV Face this week to discuss their findings.
swa: Waandishi wa taarifa mpya iliyoandaliwa na Mpango wa Vyombo vya Habari vya Iran wa Shule Kuu ya Annenberg, “Hali ya Blogu za Mashariki ya Kati: Tathmini ya Mabadiliko ya Mitando ya Mashariki ya Kati” (PDF) wanaungana na Global Voices kwenye mazungumzo ya GVwiki hii kujadili matokeo ya utafiti wao.

eng: Arash Kamangir and Laurent Giacobino talk to Solana Larsen.
swa: Arash Kamangir na Laurent Giacobino wanazungumza na Solana Larsen.

eng: While neighboring Rwanda is making news with the commemoration of the 1994 genocide and the increased tension with France, Burundi is marred in an overlooked political crisis and surge of violence that opposes, again, Hutus and Tutsis.
swa: Wakati nchi jirani ya Rwanda inagonga vichwa vya habari na maadhimisho ya mauaji ya kimbari ya mwaka wa 1994 na kuongezeka kwa mvutano na Ufaransa, Burundi imeharibiwa katika kupuuzwa kwa mgogoro wa kisiasa na dalili za vurugu zinazoweza kusababisha mapigano mapya ya Wahutu na Watutsi.

eng: Tshitenge Lubabu in Burundi opines that the roots of the crisis are the current political leaders:
swa: Tshitenge Lubabu nchini Burundi anatoa maoni kwamba mzizi hasa wa mgogoro ni viongozi wa sasa wa kisiasa:

eng: Most of our leaders, properly elected or not, despite long years in power, stand out by their incompetence Any lies are good to seize or stay in power.
swa: Wengi wa viongozi wetu, waliochaguliwa vyema au sivyo, licha ya kukaa muda mrefu madarakani, ni wazembe uongo wowote ni mzuri kumfanya akwae madaraka.

eng: When their mandates come to an end as stipulated in the Constitution, their overzealous entourage, never sated, beg them not to leave power.
swa: Wakati majukumu yao yanafikia mwisho kama ilivyoainishwa katika Katiba, wasaidizi wao wenye bidii, wasioridhika kamwe, huwaomba wasiachie madaraka.

eng: As if without them, the sun might not rise tomorrow.
swa: Ni kama wanafikiri bila wao, jua halitawaka kesho.

eng: Global Voices Meetups are back in 2014.
swa: Mikutano ya Global Voices imeanza kwa mwaka 2014.

eng: Following a successful round of gatherings in six cities around the world in 2013, members of our community are working to organize opportunities for our readers and others interested to learn more about our work and to become involved in our mission.
swa: Kufuatia mafanikio ya mikutano kwenye majiji sita duniani kote mwaka 2013, wanafamilia wa Global Voices wanafanya juhudi za kuandaa fursa kwa wasomaji wetu na wengine wote wanapenda kujifunza zaidi kuhusu kazi zetu kuhusika na shughuli zetu.

eng: We are pleased to announce the next Global Voices Meetup is scheduled for Thursday, April 17 in Lagos, Nigeria.
swa: Tunayo furaha kubwa kutangaza mkutano wetu mdogo unaopagwa kufanyika Alhamisi ya Aprili 17 jijini Lagos, Naijeria.

eng: The meetup will be hosted by Global Voices community member Nwachukwu Egbunike (@feathersproject) in conjunction with the School of Media and Communication at Pan-Atlantic University in Victoria Island, Lagos beginning at 9:00 a.m.
swa: Mwenyeji wa mkutano huo atakuwa ni mwanafamilia ya Global Voices Nwachukwu Egbunike (@feathersproject) akishirikiana na Shule Kuu ya Mawasiliano ya Umma ya Chuo Kikuu cha Pan-Atlantic katika kisiwa cha Victoria, Lagos kuanzia saa 3:00 asubuhi.

eng: Registration is required (see below for more information).
swa: Usajili unahitajika (tazama hapa chini kwa taaarifa zaidi).

eng: The Meetup will be an opportunity for students, bloggers, and others working in the field of citizen media to share experiences and to learn about the work of one another. In addition, the event will focus on: Providing an overview of the work that we do at Global Voices, including Rising Voices, Advox, and Lingua Sharing ways that the wider community can get involved with Global Voices Networking activities so that participants can share information about their own digital projects or ideas for projects Discussions about how to validate news on social media
swa: Mkutano huo utakuwa ni fursa kwa wanafunzai, wanablogu, na wengine wanaofanya kazi katika tasnia ya uandishi wa kiraia kushirikiana uzoefu wao na kujifunza zaidi kazi za wengine. kwa nyongeza, tukio litakuwa na malengo yafuatayo: Kutoa picha ya kazi ambazo tunazifanya kwenye Global Voices, ikiwa ni pamoja na miradi maalumu ya Rising Voices, Advox, na Lingua Kushirikiana njia ambazo jamii kwa upana wake inaweza kuhusika na Global Voices Kutengeneza mtandao ili washiriki waweza kushirikiana taarifa kuhusu miradi yao ya kidijitali au hata mawazo waliyonayo kwa miradi ijayo Majadiliano kuhusu namna ya kuthibitisha habari kwenye mitandao ya kijamii

eng: If you are interested in taking part, please fill out the following registration form.
swa: Kama ungependa kushiriki, tafadhali jaza fomu ifauatayo ya usajili.

eng: You will receive a confirmation email regarding your participation.
swa: Utapokea uthibitisho wa barua pepe kuhusu ushiriki wako.

eng: The event is free to attend, but space is limited.
swa: Tukio hili ni bure, ingawa nafasi ni chache.

eng: You can also send an email to: rising globalvoicesonline.org for more information.
swa: Unaweza kutuma barua pepe kwa: rising globalvoicesonline.org kwa ajili ya taarifa zaidi.

eng: Please follow the hashtag #GVMeetup for this and other meetups from around the world.
swa: Tafadhali fuatilia alama habari ya #GVMeetup kwa ajili ya kujua zaidi kuhusu mikutano hii na mingineyo ijayo duniani kote.

eng: Lauri writes about a project in South Africa, FunDza Literacy Trust, that takes advantage of mobile phone technology to encourage reading among kids:
swa: Lauri anaandika kuhusu mradi uliopo Afrika Kusini, Mfuko wa Usomaji wa FunDza, unaotumia teknolojia ya simu za mkononi kuhamasisha tabia ya kusoma kwa watoto:

eng: What I find lovely, though, is when Africans sort out innovative solutions to their problems.
swa: Kinachofurahisha, hata hivyo, ni pale Waafrika wanapopata majibu ya kiubinifu kwa matatizo yao.

eng: FunDza Literacy Trust is one such solution.
swa: Mradi wa FunDza ni mfano moja wapo.

eng: Cellphones have taken off big in Southern Africa and FunDza has latched on to that to get kids reading.
swa: Simu za mkononi zimeenea sana nchini Afrika Kusini na FunDza wanalenga kuwasaidia watoto wapende kusoma.

eng: I'm proud to be writing regularly for them.
swa: Ninajisikia fahari kuandika mara kwa mara kwa ajili yao.

eng: How it works is a story begins on a Friday.
swa: Namna inavyofanya kazi ni kwamba hadithi inaanza Ijumaa.

eng: Each story has seven chapters and one chapter goes out on the kids' cellphones each day.
swa: Kila hadithi ina sura saba na sura moja inatumwa kwenda kwennda kwenye simu za watoto kila siku.

eng: Here is my author's page with all of the stories I've written at FunDza.
swa: Hapa ni ukurasa wa mwandishi wenye hadithi zote nilizoandika kwenye mradi wa FUnDza.

eng: Click on any story and see the comments the readers leave.
swa: Bofy kwenye hadithi yangu kuona maoni yanayoanhwa na wasomaji.

eng: The kids are reading and seriously engaging with the stories!
swa: Watoto wanasoma na kuhusika na hadithi!

eng: I think this is wonderful!
swa: Ninadhani hatua hii ni kubwa!

eng: Gershom Ndhlovu argues that Africa leaders are making a mistake by blaming the West for Africa's problem:
swa: Gershom Ndhlovu anasema kuwa viongozi wa Afrika wanafanya kosa kuzilaumu nchi za Magharibi kwa matatizo ya Afrika:

eng: At the last EU-Africa Summit held in Belgium, Zambia's president Michael Chilufya Sata reiterated what other African leaders had said in the past about the West contributing to wars on the continent through the sale of guns and other military hardware.
swa: Kwenye mkutano wa hivi karibuni wa Umoja wa Ulaya ulifanyika nchini Ubeligiji, rais wa Zambia Michael Chilufya Sata alijibu mapigo kwa kile kile ambacho viongozi wengine wa Afrika walikisema huko nyuma kuhusu Nchi za Magharibi kuchangia vita barani humu kupitia biashara ya sialaha na vifaa vingine vya kivita.

eng: Quoted by Eil D’Afrique, Sata told the gathering that Africa had no gun factory that fuels conflict and that Europe was responsible for conflicts on the continent because weapons used in conflicts are manufactured in Western countries.
swa: Akinukuliwa na Eil D’Afrique, Sata aliuambia mkutano huo kuwa Afrika haikuwa na kiwanda cha silaha zinazochochea migogoro na kwamba Ulaya inahusika moja kwa moja na migogoro inayotokea barani humu kwa sababu silaha zinazotumika kwenye migogoro zimezalishwa kwenye viwanda vilivyoko kwenye nchi za Magharibi.

eng:
Most poor child soldiers involved in conflicts in Africa carry guns manufactured in Europe that cost thousands of dollars. 	“Askari wengi watoto na masikini wanaohusika na migogoro hii barani Afrika wanabeba silaha zilizozalishwa Ulaya zenye kugarimu maelfu ya dola.
These poor children could not have money to buy these weapons, said Sata.
swa: Watoto hawa masikini hawawezi kuwa na fedha za kununulia silaha hizi,” alisema Sata.

eng: In its post-independence existence, Africa has had its fair share of coups and counter-coups and civil wars.
swa: Katika kipindi cha baada ya uhuru, Afrika imekuwa na mchango wake wa kutosha kwenye mapinduzi na visasi vya kupindua waliopindua pamoja na vita vya wenyewe kwa wenyewe.

eng: Of course, most of these were brewed in smoky backrooms where Western diplomats met military officers while sipping on expensive wines and spirits, enticing them with not only the control of national resources if they kicked out an anti-Western radical leader but also the support of their capital.
swa: Ni kweli, kuwa mapinduzi mengi yalipangwa kwenye vyumba vya faragha ambapo wanadiplomasia wa nchi za Magharibi walikutana na maafisa wa kijeshi huku wakigida mvinyo na pombe ghali, wakiwafanya si tu wawe na tamaa ya kudhibiti raslimali za taifa kama watang’oa viongozi wenye misimamo mikali dhidi ya nchi za Magharibi lakini pia kuwafadhili mtaji.

eng: This is how megalomaniac tyrants like Mobutu Sese Seko rose to power and maintained a hold on it.
swa: Hivi ndivyo madikteta kama Mobutu Sese Seko walivyoweza kupanda na kung’ang’ania madarakani.

eng: But to blame all or most of the recent conflicts in Africa on Western countries and European gun factories is being disingenuous and burying heads in the sand, ostrich-like.
swa: Lakini kuzilaumu nchi za Magharibi na viwanda vya silaha barani Ulaya kwa migogoro yote au mingi ya migogoro hiyo ya hivi karibuni ni kutokuwa wakweli na kwa hakika ni sawa na kuficha vichwa mchangani, kama afanyavyo mbuni.

eng: It is pathetic that African countries still blame their former colonial masters today for their economic failures clearly caused by corruption, mismanagement and sheer incompetence
swa: Ni aibu kuwa leo bado nchi za Afrika zinawalaumu mabwana zao wakoloni wa zamani kwa uchumi uliozorota ambao kwa hakika kabisa kunasababishwa na ufisadi, udhibiti mbovu wa raslimali na kukosa uwezo.

eng: Iranian blogger Siamak Mehr was arrested in 2010 and is serving a 4-year sentence
swa: Mwanablogu wa Iran Siamak Mehr aliwekwa kizuizini mwaka 2010 na kwa sasa anatumikia kifungo cha miaka minne jela

eng: Mohammad Reza Pourshajari, a jailed blogger known by his pen name Siamak Mehr, wrote an open letter from prison where he spoke of torture and extremely difficult conditions in prison.
swa: Mohammad Reza Pourshajari, mwanablogu aliyefungwa hela anayefahamika kwa jina lake la kalamu Siamak Mehr, aliandika barua ya wazi kutoka jela ambapo alizungumzia vitendo vya utesaji na hali ngumu anayokabiliana nayo gerezani.

eng: The letter, dated March 6, 2014 was widely republished by many websites at the end of March.
swa: Barua hiyo, yenye tarehe Machi 6, 2014 ilichapishwa kwenye tovuti nyingi mwisho wa mwezi Machi.

eng: The 52-year old blogger is serving a 4-year sentence in Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj, which is north-west of Tehran.
swa: Mwanablogu huyo mwenye miaka 52 anatumikia kifungo chake cha miaka minne kwenye gereza la Ghezel Hesar mjini Karaj, ulioko kaskazini magharibi mwa Tehran.

eng: He was arrested on September 12, 2010 on charges of insulting the Prophet and enmity towards God in his blog posts.
swa: Alikamatwa Sepatemba 12, 2010 kwa mashtaka ya kumkashfu Mtume Muhammad na kumkufuru Mungu kwenye makala alizokuwa anaziweka kwenye blogu yake.

eng: In the letter, Pourshajari wrote:
swa: Kwenye barua hiyo, Pourshajari aliandika:

eng: ... as soon as I was arrested in my apartment by security forces, I was tortured, beaten and threatened to be executed...
swa: ... mara tu nilipowekwa chini ya ulinzi nyumbani kwangu na vyombo vya usalama, niliteswa, nilipigwa na kutishiwa kifo...mimi ni mhanga wa unyanyasaji wa utawala huu wa Kiislamu.

eng: At the end of the letter, he invites the international community and governments who care for human rights to help Iranian people win their rights and freedom.
swa: Mwisho wa barua hiyo, anawakaribisha jumuiya na serikali za Kimataifa zinazojali haki za binadamu kuwasaidia wananchi wa Iran kupata haki zao na uhuru.

eng: She said:
swa: Alisema:

eng: The authorities are refusing the transfer of Mr. Pourshajari to a medical facility and are depriving him of all his medications, in the hope that he will soon die.
swa: Serikali inakataa kumsafirisha Bw. Pourshajari kwenda kupata huduma za matibabu na wanamnyima huduma hiyo, ili apoteze maisha.

eng: To , the doctors' opinions are of no importance; they completely ignore them.... All Iranians are forced to obey and do whatever pleases the system.
swa: Kwa , ushauri wa daktari hauna maana; wanapuuza ushauri....Raia wa Iran wanalazimika kuheshimu na kufanya lolote ili kupendezesha mfumo wa serikali.

eng: A Facebook page has been launched to support the jailed blogger, with a copies of his letters and updates on his situation.
swa: Ukurasa wa Facebook umeanzishwa ili kumwunga mkono mwanablogu huyo aliyefungwa, ukiwa na nakala ya barua zake na habari mpya zinazohusiana na hali yake.

eng: Here is a video, uploaded in December 2011, showing Siamak Mehr in chains, apparently on his way to court.
swa: Hapa chini ni video, iliyowekwa mtandaoni Desemba 2011, ikimwonyesha Siamak Mehr akiwa amefungwa minyororo, akielekea mahakamani.

eng: Syrian father Wael Zain claims his British son, aged five, is stranded in Syria and that the British Foreign Office is not helping reunite them.
swa: Mzazi wa Kisyria Wael Zain anadai mwanae wa kiume mwenye uraia wa Uingereza, mwenye miaka mitano, amekwama Syria na kwamba Ubalozi wa Uingereza haujamsaidia kukutana nae.

eng: Photograph shared on Twitter.
swa: Picha imewekwa kwenye mtandao wa Twita.

eng: Wael Zain, a Syrian living and working in London, has turned to Twitter to draw attention to the plight of his five-year-old son, Maudh, who holds a British nationality, and who has been stranded in Syria for three years.
swa: Wael Zain, Msyria anaishi na kufanya kazi jijini Londoa, ameingia kwenye mtandao wa Twita kutafuta kusikilizwa kufuatia tatizo la mwanae mwenye umri wa miaka mitano, Maudh, mwenye uraia wa Uingereza, ambaye amekwama na kubaki Syria kwa miaka mitatu.

eng: In a series of tweets, Zain explains that his son, whom he claims was recently shot at, is with his mother in a village in Deraa, and needs medical attention.
swa: Katika mfululizo wa twiti zake, Zain anaeleza kwamba mwanae huyo, anayedai kuwa alipigwa risasi, anaishi na mama yake kwenye kijiji fulani eneo la Deraa, na anahitaji matibabu kuokoa maisha yake.

eng: He also claims that the British Foreign Office has turned a deaf ear to his ordeal.
swa: Anadai kwamba Ubalozi wa Uingereza umekuwa kiziwi kila alipofanya jitihada za kuwasilisha maombi yake.

eng: Originally from Deraa, Syria, Zain tweets:
swa: Akiandika mwenyewe kutoka Deraa, Syria, Zain anatwiti:

eng: He explains:
swa: Anaeleza:

eng: @bbclysedoucet with his mother in a village near Nawa in Deraa.
swa: Kwa sasa yuko na mama yake kijijini karibu na eneo la Nawa huko Seraa.

eng: Has been there for over 3 years.
swa: Amekuwa huko kwa miaka mitatu.

eng: 2 weeks ago he was shot at..
swa: Wiki mbili zilizopita alipigwa risasi.

eng: In other tweets, addressed to British Foreign Secretary William Hague, Zain appeals:
swa: Katika twiti nyinginezo, alizozielekeza kwa Waziri wa Mambo ya Kigeni wa Ungereza William Hague, Zain anaomba:

eng: He further adds:
swa: Anaongeza:

eng: Chengdu Living teaches readers how to rent an apartment in China without going through the agent by giving a 5 step-to-step guide.
swa: Chengdu Living anawafundisha wasomaji wake namna ya kutafuta chumba cha kupanga nchini China bila kwenda kwa dalali kwa kutoa mwongozo wa hatua tano.

eng: Yellow ribbons tied along a Seoul street in the hope of miracles following the Sewol ferry disaster.
swa: Utepe wa njano ukiwa umefungwa katika mtaa wa Seoul kwa matarajio ya muujiza wa janga la kivuko cha Sewol.

eng: Photo by Lee Yoo Eun.
swa: Picha na Lee Yoo Eun.

eng: It's been 14 days since a South Korean ferry capsized with several hundred people on board.
swa: Zimetimia siku 14 tangu kivuko cha Korea Kusini kizame kikiwa na abiria mamia kadhaa.

eng: Now, 205 people are confirmed dead, with 97 people still missing.
swa: Mpaka sasa, watu wapatao 205 wamethibitishwa kupoteza maisha, na wnegine 97 bado hawajulikani walipo.

eng: The captain and entire crew of the ferry have since been arrested.
swa: Nahodha na wafanyakazi wote wa kivuko wote wamewekwa ndani.

eng: Prime Minister Chung Hong-won has resigned amid criticism of the government's delayed response to the disaster.
swa: Waziri Mkuu Chung Hong-won tayari amejiuzulu kufuatia serikali kushutumiwa kuwa ilichelewa kuchukua hatua kukabiliana na janga hilo.

eng: Three people from the Korea Shipping Association's Incheon office have been arrested and accused of destroying evidence.
swa: Watu watatu kutoka kwenye ofisi ya Incheon ya Chama cha Usafiri wa Majini cha Korea nao wamekamatwa kwa tuhuma za kuharibu ushahidi.

eng: As details of the South Korean government's botched handling of the sinking were revealed, anger has grown.
swa: Wakati taarifa zaidi kuhusu uzembe wa serikali ya Korea Kusini katika kushughulikia ajali hiyo zimepatikana, hasira za wananchi zimeendelea kuongezeka.

eng: Online, users have taken aim at authorities and mainstream conservative media for merely parroting the government's excuses:
swa: Kwenye mtandao, watumiaji wa intaneti wamezilaumu mamlaka za serikali na vyombo vya habari kwa kuendelea 'kuimba' visingizio vinavyotolewa na serikali:

eng: The government's abysmal risk management skills, their incompetence and lies, and the media that keeps lying non-stop... All of this has enraged the victims' families.
swa: Mbinu mbovu za kukabiliana na majanga, udhaifu na uongo, na vyombo vya habari vinavyoendelea kudanganya mfululizo...Yote haya yameziumiza familia.

eng: In the wake of the Sewol ferry disaster, this country's rock bottom has been revealed.
swa: Katika ajali hii ya kivuko cha Sewol, udhaifu wa serikali hii umefunuliwa.

eng: The president has vanished from the news.
swa: Rais haonekani kwenye taarifa za habari.

eng: The concerned government authorities' gaffes and numerous mistakes and other failures have disappeared from media reports.
swa: Madudu ya idara za serikali na makosa mengi na kushindwa kwa serikali havionekani kwenye taarifa za habari.

eng: Just like how in the sinking ferry Sewol, the ship's captain escaped first.
swa: Kama ilivyotokea kwenye kuzama kwa kivuko cha Sewol, nahodha wa meli alikimbia.

eng: The media shows footage of devices deployed at the Sewol shipwreck scene and clips of experts during the rescue operation.
swa: Vyombo vya habari vinaonyesha video inayoonesha vifaa vilivyookolewa kutoka kwenye eneo la ajali ya kivuko hicho na vipande vya video zilizotengenezwa na wataalamu wakati wa zoezi la ukoaji.

eng: It seems like the operation is actively under way - if we only look at the media.
swa: Inaonekana zoezi hilo linaendelea kwa ufanisi -kama tunategemea kupata habari kupitia vyombo vya habari pekee.

eng: However, there are no additional survivors besides those initially rescued at the accident scene.
swa: Hata hivyo, hakuna wahanga wengine ukiacha wale waliokuwa wameokolewa katika eneo la ajali.

eng: There is no progress, but the media keep blabbing.
swa: Hakuna maendeleo, lakini vyombo vya habari vinaendelea kupiga porojo.

eng: The real scene is totally different than what the media shows.
swa: Eneo hasa ilikotokea ajali ni tofauti na lile linaloonyeshwa na vyombo vya habari.

eng: Outrage has further been stoked by politicians taking advantage of the calamity.
swa: Hasira imechochewa zaidi na wanasiasa wanaoonekana kutumia tukio hilo kisiasa.

eng: A governing Saeunri party lawmaker is under fire for wrongfully accusing a victim's parent of being an outsider "who wants to stir up turmoil and grudges against the government".
swa: Mbunge wa chama tawala cha Saeunri yuko kikaangoni kwa kumtuhumu kimakosa mzazi wa mmoja wa wahanga wa ajali hiyo kuwa mtu asiyehusika 'anayetaka kuchochea tu hasira dhidi ya serikali'.

eng: The lawmaker later explained that she was misled by fake images shared online.
swa: Mbunge huyo baadae alieleza kwamba alikuwa amepotoshwa na picha bandia zilizokuwa zinasambaa mtandaoni.

eng: And police are now investigating a writer who wrote on Facebook that the "Sewol ferry disaster is a scene directed by Pro-North Korean sympathizers who want to spread confusion and chaos in South Korean society."
swa: Polizi hivi sasa wanamchunguza mwandishi aliyeandika kwenye mtandao wa Facebook kwamba "Janga la kivuko cha Sewol ni tukio lililotengenezwa na vibaraka wa Korea Kaskazini wanaotaka kutengeneza mazingira ya hali ya sintofahamu na tahayaruki katika jamii ya Korea Kusini. "

eng: Now the tactic of branding people "red commies" and "Pro-North " has become a daily thing.
swa: Sasa mbinu za kuwaita watu "wakomusnisti wekundu" na "Vibaraka wa Kaskazini" limekuwa jambo la kawaida siku hizi.

eng: How outrageous is this situation?
swa: Hali hii inaudhi sana.

eng: If we cant change the leadership which covers up every flaw with the "Pro-North" tactic, we have no answer.

eng: Balik Cina is a new website which compiles some of the hilarious and notorious quotes made by Malaysian politicians.
swa: Balik Cina ni tovuti mpya ambayo hukusanya baadhi ya nukuu za kuchekesha na za ajabu zinazotolewa na wanasiasa wa Kimalysia.

eng: Most of the quotes featured on the site were submitted by netizens.
swa: Nukuu nyingi zinazowekwa kwenye mtandao huo huwa zinatumwa na watumiaji wa mtandao.

eng: The quotes are linked to a news source which provides details and context of a particular issue.
swa: Nukuu huunganishwa na kungo cha chanzo cha habari kinachotoa undani na mukhtadha wa suala husika.

eng: Balik Cina is actually an infamous quote in Malaysia.
swa: Balik Cina kwa hakika ni maarufu sana nchini Malaysia.

eng: Here’s the reason why the website is named Balik Cina:
swa: Hapa unaweza kuona sababu za kwa nini tovuti hiyo imeitwa Balik Cina:

eng: Balik Cina literally means 'go back to China' in Bahasa Malaysia.
swa: Balik Cina ina maana 'rudi China' kwa lugha ya Kibahasa Malaysia.

eng: The term Balik Cina was first popularized by the principal of a Shah Alam high school in July 2013.
swa: Neno Balik Cina lilikuzwa na mkuu wa shule ya sekondari ya Shah Alam mwezi Julai 2013.

eng: This term and other phrases of similar sophistication has since been trending in Malaysia.
swa: Neno hilo na yanayofanana nayo yamekuwa yakitawala mijadala ya mtandaoni nchini Malaysia.

eng: Inspired by the outstanding quality of public discourse perpetuated by Malaysian politicians, we started BalikCina.com to keep track of all exciting developments in our political landscape.
swa: Tukiwa tumehamishwa na ubora wa matamshi yanayotolewa na wanasiasa wa Malaysia, tulianzisha tovuti ya BalikCina.com kuweka kumbukumbu sawa ya maendeleo ya siasa zetu.

eng: Balik Cina aspires to be the finest collection of all beautiful and inspirational quotes by Malaysian politicians and public figures.
swa: Balik Cina inahamasisha kukusanywa kwa nukuu zote nzuri na zenye hamasa zinazotolewa na wanasiasa wa Malaysia na watu maarufu wa nchi hii.

eng: Aizyl Azlee of The New Forward reviews the website and confirms that Malaysian politicians often spew out ridiculous statements:

eng: Malaysian politicians say ridiculous stuff so often that most of us can barely keep up.
swa: Wanasiasa wa Malaysia husema mambo ya kijinga mara nyingi kiasi kwamba hatuwezi hata kuyashika yote wanayoyasema.

eng: Before we’re done laughing at one quote, there’s already another one going viral on the internet.
swa: Kabla hatujamaliza kucheka kwa ujinga mmoja, ujinga mwingine tayari unakuwa umeshasemwa na unasambaa mtandaoni.

eng: So much so that we aren’t exactly able to remember half of what we’ve laughed at.
swa: Ni ujinga mwingi kiasi kwamba hatutaweza kabisa kukumbuka hata nusu tu ya yale tuliyoyacheka.

swa: Serikali imejibu mapigo.

swa: Mbunge anataka kufuatilia matumizi ya mtandao ili kuwafurahisha ndugu wa wahanga wa ndege iliyopotea ya Malaysia ya MH370.

eng: Zimbabwe's President Robert Mugabe has angered Nigeria with comments made on March 15, 2014 during his 90th birthday luncheon that Nigeria and its citizens are corrupt.
swa: Rais wa Zimbabwe Robert Mugabe ameikasirisha Naijeria kwa matamshi aliyoyatoa Machi 15, 2014 wakati wa sherehe ya kuzaliwa kwake kuwa Naijeria na raia wake ni mafisadi.

eng: Mugabe asked, "Are we now like Nigeria where you have to reach into your pocket to get anything done?
swa: Mugabe aliuliza, "Hivi tumekuwa kama Naijeria nchi ambayo ni lazima upapase mfuko ili kupewa huduma yoyote?

eng: You see, we used to go to Nigeria and every time we went there we had to carry extra cash in our pockets to corruptly pay for everything.
swa: Unajua, tumekuwa tukienda Naijeria na kila wakati tukienda kule ilitubidi kubeba pesa za ziada mifukoni mwetu ili kutoa rushwa kwa kila tulichotaka kukifanya.

eng: You get into a plane in Nigeria and you sit there and the crew keeps dilly dulling without taking off as they wait for you to pay them to fly the plane."
swa: Unapanda ndege nchini Naijeria na unakaa kwenye siti na wafanyakazi wa ndege wanabaki kujibaraguza na ndege haiondoki utadhani wanasubiri uwalipe ili ndege ipae."

eng: The Nigerian government summoned Zimbabwe's envoy last week over Mugabe's remarks.
swa: Serikali ya Naijeria imemwandikia balizi wa Zimbabwe wiki iliyopita kupata ufafanuzi wa matamshi hayo ya Mugabe.

eng: However, the Coalition Against Corrupt Leaders (CACOL) in Nigeria has asked the federal government to deal with the message and not the messenger.
swa: Hata hivyo, Umoja wa Kupambana na Watawala Mafisadi (CACOL) nchini Naijeria umeitaka serikali ya shirikisho kufanyia kazi ujumbe huo na sio aliyeutoa ujumbe huo.

eng: The 2013 Transparency International Corruption Index shows the level of perceived corruption to be higher in Zimbabwe than in Nigeria.
swa: Kipimo cha Ufisadi kwa mwaka 2013 cha taasisi ya Transparency kinaonyesha kiwango cha ufisadi unaoonekana kiko juu zaidi nchini Zimbabwe kuliko ilivyo Naijeria.

eng: Mugabe's comments have received mixed reactions on Twitter.

eng: What Mugabe said about Nigeria is true but he said it to the wrong people. — Macharia Mucheru (@MashRomeo) April 12, 2014
swa: Kile Mugabe alichosema kuhusu Naijeria ni ukweli ila aliyasema hayo kwa watu wasio sahihi

eng: For God's sake, why should Robert Mugabe fabricate a tissue of lies against Nigeria.
swa: Kwa jina la Mwenyezi Mungu, kwa nini Robert Mugabe anaipaka matope Naijeria.

eng: Is it true that Nigerians are corrupt? — IaM►DeMal (@Dmalan_D) April 12, 2014
swa: Ni kweli kuwa Wanaijeria ni wananuka rushwa?

eng: Mugabe says "all Nigerians are corrupt" while world bank reveals that "Nigeria's the most poorest country in Africa" #poverty = corruption — OurLeadersHaveSoldUs (@Worldworth_Saro) April 14, 2014
swa: Mugabe anasema "Wanaijeria wote ni wala rushwa" wakati benki ya dunia imeonesha kuwa "Naijeria ni nchi masikini zaidi barani Afrika" Umasikini = ufisadi

swa: Ufisadi ni tatizo kubwa Naijeria.

swa: Watawala wetu ni mafisadi kupindukia.

eng: Nigeria summons Zimbabwean envoy over Mugabe’s comments.

eng: I am Nigerian but I do not see any wrong in calling a spade a spade. — Almustapha Zubairu. (@mustybnzubair) April 11, 2014

swa: Kama Mugabe anaweza kufungua mdomo wake kuuita Naijeria kuwa inanuka rushwa....basi ni wazi tunalo tatizo kubwa...tena kubwa sana!

eng: The Friedrich Ebert Foundation has published a research report on the use of social media in Cameroon:
swa: Shirika la Friedrich Ebert limechapisha ripoti ya utafiti kwenye matumizi ya mitandao ya kijamii nchini Cameroon:

eng: To what extent, for what purposes and by whom are social media like Twitter, Facebook, Blogs, Linkedin, etc. used in the country?
swa: Kwa kiwango kipi, kwa malengo yapi na kwa akina nani basi mitandao ya kijamii kama Twita, Facebook, Blogu, Linkedin, nk. inatumika nchini humo?

eng: To find answers to these questions, the Friedrich-Ebert-Foundation has commissioned a research report on the use of social media in Cameroon...
swa: Kujua majibu ya maswali hayo, Shirika la Friedrich Ebert limetoa taarifa ya matumuzi ya mitandao ya kijamii nchini Cameroon...

eng: In terms of the popularity of social media, as elsewhere, Facebook is the single most popular social media tool in Cameroon.
swa: Kwa upande wa umaarufu wa mitandao ya kijamii, kama ilivyo kwingineko, Facebook ndiyo zana maarufu zaidi nchini Cameroon.

eng: Some Cameroonian Facebook groups have up to 20.000 followers and more.
swa: Baadhi ya makundi ya Ki-Camerron yana hadi wafuasi 20.000 na zaidi.

eng: More surprising is the strong popularity of Linkedin.
swa: Na kwa hali ya kushangaza ni umaarufu wa mtandao wa Linkedin.

eng: Close to 4 Cameroonian internet users out of ten have subscribed to the service, compared to only 3% in neighbouring Nigeria.
swa: Karibu watumiaji wanne kati ya watano wa mtandao wa intaneti nchini Cameroon wamejiunga na huduma hiyo, ikilinganishwa na asilimia tatu tu kwenye nchi jirani ya Naijeria.

eng: The search for jobs and employment opportunities may explain at least parts of this puzzle.
swa: Utafutaji wa kazi na fursa za ajira inaweza kuwa sehemu ya majibu ya hali hii.

eng: A quickly increasingly popular social media site is the microblogging service Twitter.
swa: Mtandao mwingine unaopata umaarufu nchini humo ni Twita.

eng: Cameroon is now among the top-ten African countries in terms of the tweeted volumes, though Tweeting is heavily concentrated on Douala and Yaoundé.
swa: Cameroon kwa sasa ni kati ya nchi kumi maarufu za kiafrika zenye ujazo mkubwa wa twiti, ingawa twiti nyingi zinatokea kwenye miji ya Douala na Yaoundé.

eng: By comparison, blogging is still in an infant stage, given its exceedingly higher demands on time and content.
swa: Kwa kulinganisha, bado kuna uchanga wa kublogu, kwa kuangalia mahitaji makubwa ya muda na maudhui.

eng: However, for what Cameroonian bloggers may lack in numbers, they more than make up for in terms of quality.
swa: Hata hivyo, ingawa wanablogu wa Cameroon ni wachache kwa idadi, wana uwezo mkubwa kimaudhui na viwango.

eng: Some of Africa’s best blogs come from Cameroon, some of whom are organized in the “Collectif des Blogueurs Camerounais."
swa: Baadhi ya blogu maarufu zaidi barani Afrika zinatoka Cameroon, baadhi zikiwa zinaratibiwa na na muungano wa wanablogu uitwao “Collectif des Blogueurs Camerounais."

eng: In addition, a number of innovations have already emerged that will no doubt accelerate the spread of social media, including the emergence of mobile money which now enables commercial activities.
swa: Kwa nyongeza, tayari jitihada za kiubunifu zimefanyika na haina shaka kuwa jitahada hizo zitaongeza kuenea kwa mitandao ya kijamii, ikiwa ni pamoja na kuanzishwa kwa huduma za kifedha kwa njia ya simu za mkononi ambayo kwa sasa inasaidia kukuza shughuli za kiuchumi.

eng: New parents everywhere face a common problem: getting their babies to sleep.
swa: Wazazi wapya duniani kote hukabiliana na tatizo linalofanana: kuwafanya watoto wao wapate usingizi.

eng: And there's a common solution: a lullaby.
swa: Na kwa bahati njema, kuna ufumbuzi unaofanana: wimbo wa kulalia!

eng: But it turns out lullabies don't just help babies relax, they help adults, as well, explains author Kathy Henderson, who collected lullabies from across the globe for her children's book, Hush, Baby, Hush.
swa: Lakini inaonekana kuwa si tu kwamba nyimbo la kulalia zinawasaidia watoto kupumzika, lakini pia zinawasaidia watu wazima, hali kadhalika, anaeleza mwandishi Kathy Henderson, aliyekusanya nyimbo za aina hiyo kutoka kila kona ya dunia alipokuwa akiandaa kitabu chake cha watoto kiitwacho, Hush, Baby, Hush .

eng: She says lullabies help parents "deal with the situation in which they are being wound up by a child, or they are failing to get them to sleep, or they are feeling really, really tired themselves."
swa: Anasema nyimbo hizo tulivu zinawasaidia wazazi "kukabiliana na hali ya kusumbuka na watoto, au wanapojikuta hawawezi kuwafanya walale, au hata katika nyakati ambazo wao wenyewe wamechoka."

eng: The title of Henderson's book comes from a Jamaican lullaby called "Hush Baby Hush," with a version recorded by The Kitchen Sisters.
swa: Jina la kitabu cha Henderson kimetokana na wimbo wa ijamaika iitwao "Hush Baby Hush," ambao toleo lake limerekodiwa na studio ya The Kitchen Sisters.

eng: The author says lullabies share certain traits.
swa: Mwandishi anasema nyimbo hizi zina sifa inayofanana.

eng: They almost always have both music and words.
swa: Zote zina muziki na maneno.

eng: The music has to have a "soothing rhythm" and a rather narrow musical range.
swa: Muziki una "ala nyororo" sambamba na mapigo ya taratibu.

eng: But the lyrics, she says, can be about anything — and cover a wide spectrum of human emotion and mood.
swa: Lakini mashairi, anasema, yanaweza kuhusu chochote -na yanabeba ujumbe wa aina mbalimbali za kihisia na mwonekano.

eng: There are lullabies about anger, frustration, and humor.
swa: Kuna nyimbo za hasira, kukatishwa tamaa, na ucheshi.

eng: Henderson points out there are lullabies about "food, families, monsters, children being naughty" and many other things.
swa: Henderson anabainisha kuwa zipo nyimbo kuhusu "chakula, familia, majinamizi, watoto wasumbufu" na mambo mengine mengi.

eng: Lullabies are also sung in all sorts of situations, not just when a baby is in bed. For example, mothers sometimes sing them while they work, so their children will settle down and let them keep on working.
swa: Nyimbo za aina hii huimbwa katika hali za aina zote, si tu wakati mtoto anatafuta usingizi. kwa mfano, akina mama wakati mwingine wanaimba wakiwa wakifanya kazi, ili kuwafanya watoto wao watulie na kuwapa nafasi ya kufanya kazi.

eng: Henderson reckons the oldest lullaby is from well before the common era and says researchers have found lullabies in the oldest-known literature.
swa: Henderson anakumbuka wimbo wa zamani kabisa una historia ndefu na kusema watafiti wamegundua nyimbo za aina hiyo kupitia fasihi za kale zinazofahamika.

eng: Egyptian blogger Nadia El Awady wrote a blog post in which she questions if women wearing Hijab face discrimination in western countries or not.
swa: Mwanablogu wa Mirsi Nadia El Awady anaandika posti ya blogu yake ambapo anahoji kama wanawake wanaovaa Hijabu wanabaduliwa kwenye nchi za magharibi ama la.

eng: Nadia, as an Egyptian who grew up in the US and lived prolonged periods in Europe, adds from her personal experience in regards to reactions she received in both Eastern and Western countries when it comes to wearing the Hijab or even taking it off.
swa: Nadia, kama Mmisri alikulia Marekani na ameishi kwa kipindi kirefu Ulaya, anaelezea uzoefu wake kuhusu mwitikio alioupata kwenye nchi za Mashariki na Magharibi linapokuja suala la kuvaa Hijab au hata kuivua.

eng: She writes:
swa: Anaandika:

eng: During all those years, I have been without the hijab, with the hijab, wearing a very long hijab (called a khimar), wearing a face veil (called a niqab), back to wearing a shorter hijab and finally, now, no hijab at all.
swa: Kwa miaka yote hiyo, nimekuwa sivai Hijab, nikivaa hijab, nikivaa hijab ndefu sana (inayoitwa khimar), nikivaa kitambaa cha kufunika uso (kinachoitwa niqab), baadae nikaanza kuvaa hijab fupi na hivi sasa, sivai kabisa.

eng: I’ve done it all.
swa: Nimeyafanya yote hayo.

eng: I’ve seen all the reactions.
swa: Nimeona mwitikio.

eng: The way I have dressed over the years may have been accepted by some in my inner circles and criticized by others; this is true.
swa: Namna nilivyovaa kwa miaka yote hiyo imekuwa ikikubaliwa na baadhi ya marafiki wangu wa karibu na kukosolewa na wengine; hii ni kweli.

eng: How a woman dresses is a highly contentious subject no matter where you are in the world.
swa: Namna mwanamke anavyovaa ni mada yenye mjadala mkali bila kujali uko wapi duniani humu.

eng: When I donned the face veil, my own father was against it.
swa: Nilipoacha kuvaa kitambaa cha kufunika uso, baba yangu mzazi alikuwa kinyume.

eng: When I took off my hijab, I lost at least one good friend and was tsk tsked by many others.
swa: Niliachana na Hijab, nilimpoteza angalau rafiki yangu mmoja wa karibu na wengi walinishangaa.

eng: These are normal reactions and they are to be expected.
swa: Hii ni miitikio ya kawaida na inatarajiwa.

eng: I do not categorize these reactions as discrimination.
swa: Siwezi kuiweka kwenye kundi la unyanyasaji.

eng: Friends and family have definite ideas of how they expect me to live my life.
swa: Marafiki na familia wanajua wanachokitarajia kwa maisha yangu.

eng: They believe they know what is best for me.
swa: Wanaamini wanajua kile kilicho bora kwangu.

eng: A group of students at Iran's Amirkabir University in Tehran chanted pro-opposition slogans, held placards and waved the Iranian flag during a speech by failed conservative presidential candidate and former top nuclear negotiator Saeed Jalili on 14 April 2014.
swa: Kikundi cha wanafunzi wa Chuo Kikuu cha Amirkabir kilichopo Tehran nchini Iran, kiliimba kauli mbiu za kuunga mkono Upinzani, huku wakibeba mabango na kupeperusha bendera ya Iran wakati wa hotuba ya mgombea aliyeshindwa mhafidhina ambaye alikuwa mpatanishi mkuu wa nguvu za nyuklia Saeed Jalili mnamo Aprili 14, 2014.

eng: The shouted slogans supported Mir Hussein Mousavi and Mehdi Karroubi, leaders of the Green Movement protests that rocked the country following President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's reelection in 2009 by a landslide.
swa: Nyimbo hizo zenye maneno yanayotumiwa na wapinzani zilikuwa zinamwuunga mkono Mir Hussein Mousavi na Mehdi Karroubi, ambao ni viongozi wa maandamano ya Green Movement yalifanikiwa sana nchini humo kufuatia kuchaguliwa kwa mara nyingine kwa kishindo kwa Rais Mahmoud Ahmadinejad mwaka 2009.

eng: Protesters considered the elections results fraudulent, and millions rallied for Ahmadinejad's removal.
swa: Waandamanaji waliyachukulia matokeo hayo kuwa ya kuchakachuliwa, na mamiliano waliandamana kumtaka Ahmadinejad aachie madaraka.

eng: But authorities began a widespread crackdown on the movement in early 2010, and Mousavi and Karroubi, both former presidential candidates, as well as Mousavi's wife Zahra Rahnavard were placed under house arrest on 14 February 2011.
swa: Hata hivyo, vyombo vya dola vilianza kupambana kwa nguvu na vuguvugu hili mapema mwaka 2010, na Mousavi pamoja na Karroubi, ambao wote ni wagombea wa urais, ikiwa ni pamoja na mke wa Mousavi aitwaye Zahra Rahnavard ambao kwa pamoja waliwekwa chini ya ulinzi na kuzuiliwa kutoka nyumbani kuanzia Februari 14, 2011.

eng: Students at Amirkabir University chanted, "Our vote is for imam's prime minister," a reference to Mousavi, who was prime minister from 1980 to 1988 when Ruhollah Khomeini was in power as the country's supreme leader.
swa: Wanafunzi wa Chuo Kikuu cha Amirkabir waliimba, "Kura zetu tunampa Waziri Mkuu wa Imam," wakimaanisha Mousavi, ambaye alikuwa waziri mkuu kuanzia mwaka 1980 mpaka 1988 wakati ambao Ruhollah Khomeini alikuwa madarakani kama kiongozi mkuu wa nchi hiyo.
