eng: Rwanda’s top musicians King James, Miss Jojo, Riderman, Tom Close, and Urban Boyz join the fight against malnutrition in Rwanda with a YouTube music video.
swa: Wanamuziki maarufu wa Rwanda King James, Miss Jojo, Riderman, Tom Close, and Urban Boyz walijiunga na mapambano dhidi ya utapiamlo nchini Rwanda kupitia video ya muziki kwenye mtandao wa YouTube.

eng: The video is also available with Swahili subtitles.
swa: Video hiyo pia inapatikana kwa maandishi ya Kiswahili .

eng: Screenshots of some of the participant videos from the Indigenous Language Challenge
swa: Picha mnato za video za washiriki wa Shindano la Lugha za Asili

eng: Love it or hate it, the online buzz surrounding the Ice Bucket Challenge earlier this year brought more awareness to the disease amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).
swa: Soga la mtandaoni la Love it or hate it , kuhusu Zoezi la Mabonge ya Barafu mapema mwaka huu lilikuza uelewa wa ugonjwa unaofahamika kama amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.

eng: Participants filmed themselves dumping cold water on their heads and challenging another person to do the same or donate money toward research for a cure.
swa: Washiriki walijipiga picha wakijiwekea mabonge ya barafu vichwani mwao na kumtaka mtu mwingine kufanya vile vile na akishindwa alipaswa kutoa fedha kwa ajili ya matibabu ya ugonjwa uliotajwa.

eng: Now a similar concept aimed at awareness for indigenous languages is making its way around the internet.
swa: Sasa wazo kama hilo linalolenga kukuza uelewa kwa lugha za asili limepamba moto mtandaoni.

eng: In the Indigenous Language Challenge, the one who accepts the challenge must record a video speaking an indigenous language and tap someone else to do the same.
swa: Katika zoezi la Lugha ya Asili, yeyote anayekubali zoezi hilo lazima arekodi video akiongea lugha yake ya asili na kumtaka mtu mwingine aongee vile alivyoongea yeye.

eng: The outcome has been a wide range of people around the world who are producing videos, some for the first time, as a way to proudly share their language online and encouraging more to do the same.
swa: Matokeo yake watu wengi kutoka sehemu mbalimbali duniani wanatengeneza video, wengine kwa mara ya kwanza, kama njia ya kutangaza lugha zao mtandaoni na kuwafanya watu wengine kuitambua na kuitumia.

eng: A Facebook group was created to collect links to the videos, where people could share their motivations and connect with others taking part in the Challenge.
swa: Kundi la mtandao wa Facebook lilianzishwa kukusanya viungo vya video hizo zinazoingizwa, na kwenye ukurasa huo washiriki wanaweza kutuma kazi zao na kuungana na wengine wanaoshiriki Zoezi hilo.

eng: Many chose to upload their videos directly to Facebook where one can hear North American languages like Kwak'wala and Lakota, as well as the Miriwoong language from Australia, for example.
swa: Wengi huchagua kupandisha video zao moja kwa moja kwenye mtandao wa Facebook na huko husikia lugha zinazozungumzwa kwenye bara za Amerika Kaskazini kama vile Kwak'wala na Lakota, vile vile lugha ya Miriwoong kutoka Australia, kwa mfano.

eng: Efforts to pinpoint the origin of this challenge are ongoing, but according to the group administrator, one of the first participants was James Gensaw, speaking words in the Yurok language.
swa: Jitihada za kuweka kumbukumbu sawa kuhusu asili ya Zoezi hili zinaendelea, lakini kwa mujibu wa kiongozi wa kundi hilo, mmoja wa washiriki wa mwanzo kabisa alikuwa James Gensaw, aliyekuwa anayezungumza maneno ya lugha ya Yurok.

eng: Who are some of the participants?
swa: Akina nani ni washiriki?

eng: And why is this activity so important?
swa: Na kwa nini zoezi hili ni la muhimu?

eng: Colleen Fitzgerald, Director of the Native American Languages Lab at The University of Texas at Arlington, shares her thoughts on her blog post at the Huffington Post:
swa: Colleen Fitzgerald, Mkurugenzi wa Maabara ya Lugha za Asili za Amerika Kaskazini kwenye Chuo Kikuu cha Texas mjini Arlington, anatoa maoni yake kupitia posti yake kwenye blogu yake kwenye makala ya Huffington:

eng: Many of these videos come from adults who are second language learners.
swa: Video nyingi kama hizi zimetoka kwa watu wazima wanaojifunza lugha ya pili.

eng: For many years, government-run boarding schools in both the U.S. and Canada took children from Native families.
swa: Kwa miaka mingi, shule za bweni zinazoendeshwa na serikali nchini Marekani na Kanada ziliwachukua watoto kutoka familia za wenyeji.

eng: This had an immense effect on Native language acquisition.
swa: Hatua hii ilikuwa na matokeo makubwa kwenye kujifunza lugha za asili.

eng: Children lost priceless years of daily home environments with parents and grandparents communicating to them in their language.
swa: Watoto waliopoteza bure miaka mingi ya kukosa mazingira muafaka 'ya nyumba' na wazazi wao waliweza kuwasiliana kwa lugha zao za asili.

eng: Home is where children's language development thrives and grows, and where children acquire the many different speech forms that express the human experience.
swa: Nyumba ni mahali ambapo maendeleo ya lugha za watoto huongezeka na kukua, na ndipo watoto hujifunza lugha nyingine tofauti zinazowafanya wawasiliane.

eng: What gets lost?
swa: Kinachopotea ni nini?

eng: So much, from the everyday language of instructions, telling jokes, or a recipe, to the ritual language of prayers, ceremonial speeches, or sharing stories of the ancestors.
swa: Vingi, kuanzia lugha ya kila siku ya mawasiliano, kutaniana, mbinu na hata lugha za namna ya kuomba, hotuba za kwenye sherehe, au hata kusimuliana hadithi za kale.

eng: Here are two examples of participants in this Challenge, who uploaded their videos to YouTube.
swa: Hapa kuna mifano miwili ya washiriki wa zoezi hili, walioweka video kwenye mtandao YouTube.

eng: Jackelyn Seitcher speaking in the Nuu-chah-nulth language shares words after accepting the challenge.
swa: Jackelyn Seitcher akizungumza kwa lugha ya Nuu-chah-nulth anasema maneno ya kukubali kuingia kwenye shindano.

eng: Monica Peters takes the opportunity for the challenge to show the translations of works in Kanienkeha.
swa: Monica Peters anachukua fursa ya kushiriki zoezi hili kwa kuonesha tafsiri za kazi zake kwenye Kanienkeha.

eng: She then goes onto challenge members of the "Keeping the Kanienkeha Language Strong" Facebook group, community leaders and teachers, and students that are just starting out to speak the language.
swa: Kisha anakwenda kwenye ukurasa wa Facebook wa washiriki wa zoezi hili unaoitwa "Kutunza Uimara wa Lugha ya Kanienkeha ", linaloundwa na viongozi na walimu, na wanafunzi ambao ndio kwanza wameanza kuzungumza lugha hiyo.

eng: There are other videos collected on the blog News From Native California.
swa: Zipo video nyingine zilizokusanywa kwenye blogu ya Habari Kutoka California ya Asili.

eng: Konwennenhon Marion Delaronde also posted her video in the group speaking Kanien'keha (Mohawk).
swa: Konwennenhon Marion Delaronde vile vile alichapisha video yake kwenye kundi linalozungumza lugha ya Kanien'keha (Mohawk).

eng: After being challenged by Kehte Deer, she enthusiastically took part and shared her reflections after uploading her video:
swa: Baada ya kupata changamoto na Kehte Deer, alihamasika kushiriki na kutoa maoni yake baada ya kupandisha video yake:

eng: Already I think I heard all the languages from different nations.
swa: Tayari ninadhani nimesikiliza lugha zote kutoka mataifa mbalimbali.

eng: I have to tell you all that all your languages are so beautiful.
swa: Ni lazima nikwambie kwamba lugha zote ni tamu.

eng: Always speak your own languages if you can.
swa: Zungumza lugha yako kama unaweza.

eng: It’s hopeful.
swa: Inaleta matumaini.

eng: I want to encourage all of you to continue to learn, continue to teach other and to really put your life into it, speaking.
swa: Ninataka kuwahamasisha nyote kuendelea kujifunza, kuendelea kuwafundisha wengine na kwa hakika kuyaanza mapya mapya kwenye lugha mpya, kwa kuizungumza.

eng: I’m so happy that I can speak Mohawk.
swa: Ninafuraha sana ninaweza kusema kwa lugha ya Mohawk.

eng: I’m not fluent, a lot is still missing, but I want to thank everyone who has recorded themselves for this challenge, because you inspired me.
swa: Sijafuzu na kuiongea kwa ufasaha, bado kuna ninayohitaji kujifunza, lakini ningependa kumshukuru kila mmoja aliyejirekodi kwa ajili ya Shindano hili, kwa sababu mmenihamasisha.

eng: Pan African Vision's Ajong Mbapndah talks to Gershom Ndhlovu about the politics around the sickness and death of Zambia's president Michael Sata:
swa: Ajong Mbapndah wa Pan African Vision anazungumza na Gershom Ndhlovu kuhusu siasa zinazozunguka ugonjwa na kifo cha Rais wa Zambia Michael Sata:

eng: President Michael Sata recently passed away in London and it appears his health and medical condition where shrouded in secrecy, why were Zambians not notified of the Presidents failing health?
swa: Rais Michael Sata siku za hivi karibuni amefariki dunia jijini London na inaonekana afya yake na huduma za tiba alizopatiwa ziligobikwa na usiri, kwa nini wananchi wa Zambia hawakupewa taarifa za kuzorota kwa afya ya Rais?

eng: : An online publication, Zambian Watchdog, alerted the nation to President Michael Sata’s failing health more than two years before he passed on.
swa: : Tovuti ya habari, Zambian Watchdog, iliwajulisha wananchi kuhusiana na kuzorota kwa afya ya rais Michael Sata kwa zaidi ya miaka miwili kabla ya kifo chake.

eng: It is the same publication that could expose the secretive treatments abroad that he used to take.
swa: Tovuti hiyo hiyo iliweza kuweka wazi matibabu ya siri aliyokuwa akipatiwa huko ughaibuni.

eng: Both senior government officials and ruling party cadres were not happy with the publication for keenly following and exposing Mr Sata’s condition and there were many attempts to shut down the online publication which was at times blocked for access to people in Zambia.
swa: Maafisa waandamizi wa serikali na makada wa chama tawala hawakufurahishwa na habari hizo zilizokuwa zikifuatilia kwa makini na kuweka wazi hali ya Mhe Sata na kulikuwa na majaribio mengi ya kuifungia tovuti hiyo ambayo kwa nyakati kadhaa ilizuiwa kuifanya isipatikane kwa wasomaji wanaoishi Zambia.

eng: On the question of why, obviously the government and the party wanted to show that the President was healthy and discharging his functions.
swa: Kuhusu swali la kwa nini ilikuwa hivyo, ni dhahiri serikali na chama tawala kilitaka kuonesha kwamba Rais alikuwa yu na afya njema na akiendelea na kazi zake.

eng: They probably did not want to admit the fact because of a constitutional clause which calls for the removal of the office holder, once declared unfit by a medical board if called by Cabinet.
swa: Huenda hawakutaka kukiri ukweli kwa sababu katiba inataka kuondolewa madarakani kwa kiongozi, ikithibitishwa na baraza la madaktari kwa ombi la baraza la mawaziri, kwamba afya yake ina matatizo.

eng: In fact, one citizen attempted to compel Cabinet to call for such a board through the High Court but his application was dismissed.
swa: Kwa hakika, raia mmoja alijaribu kulishinikiza Baraza la Mawaziri liitake bodi ya madaktari kuchunguza afya ya rais kupitia Mahakama Kuu lakini ombi lake lilitupiliwa mbali.

eng: #swazijustice is a campaign calling for the release of Bheki Makhubu, editor of the Nation magazine and Thulani Maseko, a human rights lawyer, who were jailed in Swaziland for two years for writing an article critical of the judiciary in the country.
swa: #swazijustice ni kampeni inayotoa wito wa kuachiliwa huru kwa Bheki Makhubu, mhariri wa gazeti la Taifa na Thulani Maseko, mwanasheria wa haki za binadamu, ambao walifungwa jela nchini Swaziland kwa miaka miwili kwa sababu ya kuandika makala kukosoa mfumo wa mahakama nchini humo.

eng: The two were arrested on 17 March, 2014 and sentenced to two years in prison on July 25, 2014.
swa: Wawili hao walikamatwa tarehe 17 Machi 2014 na kuhukumiwa kifungo cha jela cha miaka miwili mnamo Julai 25, 2014.

eng: #DistrictThai demonstration in London, via the District Thai Facebook page.
swa: Maandamano ya #DistrictThai jijini London, Picha kupitia ukurasa wa Facebook wa District Thai.

eng: A group of Thai citizens gathered outside London's Odeon Cinema in Leicester Square on Monday, November 10, as the theater hosted the international premiere of "The Hunger Games: Mockingjay Part 1," to draw attention to the real-life threats to democracy, the freedom of expression, and the rule of law in Thailand.
swa: Kikundi cha raia wa Thailand kilikusanyika nje ya Ukumbi wa Sinema wa Odeon uliopo kwenye viwanja vya Leicester jijini London siku ya Jumatatu, Novemba 10, wakati wa kuonesha kwa mara ya kwanza kwa filamu maarufu ya "The Hunger Games: Mockingjay Sehemu ya 1," kama jitihada za kufanya dunia iangazie uwepo wa hali inayotishia demokrasia, uhuru wa kujieleza, na utawala wa sheria nchini Thailand.

eng: The film is significant for many Thais.
swa: Filamu hiyo ina umuhimu mkubwa kwa wa-Thai wengi.

eng: Indeed, opponents of Thailand's recent coup, which displaced the democratically-elected government of Yingluck Shinawatra, have even adopted the movie's famous three-finger salute.
swa: Kwa hakika, wapinzani wa mapinduzi ya kijeshi hivi majuzi nchini Thailand, yaliyoiong'oa madarakani serikali iliyokuwa imechaguliwa kidemokrasia iliyokuwa ikiongozwa na Yingluck Shinawatra, na waliweza kuiga alama ya vidole maarufu ya vitatu inayoonekana kwenye filamu hiyo.

eng: The gesture has become so popular that the country's military junta actually banned it, along with several other forms of political dissent.
swa: Alama hiyo imekuwa maarufu sana kiasi kwamba jeshi la nchi hiyo limeipiga marufuku, ikiwa ni pamoja na upinzani mwingineo wa kisiasa.

eng: Hundreds of Thais recently used the salute at the cremation ceremony for former Deputy House Speaker Apiwan Wiriyachai, greeting Yingluck Shinawatra with the three fingers, when she arrived to pay her respects.
swa: Mamia ya wa-Thai hivi karibuni yalitumia salamu hiyo kwenye mazishi ya Naibu spika wa zamani Apiwan Wiriyachai, kwa kumsalimia Yingluck Shinawatra kwa ishara hiyo, alipowasili kutoa heshima zake za mwisho.

eng: Many of the activists in London this week wore masks, for fear of reprisals against their friends and families still in Thailand.
swa: Katika kusanyiko hilo juma hili jijini London, wengi wa wanaharakati hao walilazimika kuvaa magamba ya kuficha nyuso zao, kwa hofu ya kuwasababishia matatizo ndugu na jamaa zao walioko nchini Thailand.

eng: The activists set up a Facebook page and a Twitter account to coordinate their efforts, using the hashtag #DistrictThai.
swa: Wanaharakati hao walifungua ukurasa wa Facebook na akaunti ya Twita katika kuratibu jitihada zao, kwa kutumia alama ishara #DistrictThai.

eng: District is a reference to the plot of "The Hunger Games," where a centralized, authoritarian dictatorship rules different geographic areas ("districts").
swa: District inaaminisha mkakati ulioitwa "The Hunger Games," ambapo udikteta wa kiimla unaoanzia mahali fulani hutawala maeneo mengine ya kijiografia yanayoitwa wilaya ("districts").

eng: Most of the districts are impoverished and enslaved to the "Capital."
swa: Maeneo haya yamefukarishwa na kutumikishwa na "Makao Makuu."

eng: Activists' social media accounts are maintained in Thai and in English, serving audiences both at home in Thailand and around the world.
swa: Anuani hizo za mitandao ya kijamii zinaendeshwa kwa lugha za ki-Thai na Kiingereza, kwa ajili ya hadhira ya nyumbani huko Thailand na duniani kote.

eng: The group's Facebook page was popular, attracting more than 1,000 "likes" in a single weekend.
swa: Ukurasa wa Facebook wa kundi hilo ulikuwa maarufu, ukivutia watu 1,000 kuupenda ndani ya mwisho wa juma moja pekee.

swa: Picha kutoka kwenye ukurasa wa Facebook wa Yingluck Shinawatra.

eng: Thai politics became even more chaotic today when the country's former prime minister was impeached by a legislative body, which was appointed by a military-backed government.
swa: Siasa za Thailand zimechukua sura mpya leo baada ya waziri mkuu wa zamani wa nchi hiyo kupigiwa kura ya kutokuwa na imani nae na bunge la nchi hiyo, lililoteuliwa na serikali inayoongozwa na kijeshi.

eng: The National Legislative Assembly (NLA) went through the motions of a secret ballot to impeach former Prime Minister Yingluck Shinawatra over corruption related to a rice pledging scheme intended for small farmers that she supervised.
swa: Bunge la nchi hiyo lilisimamia mchakato wa kupiga kura ya siri kumwondoa waziri mkuu huyo wa zamani Yingluck Shinawatra kwa tuhuma zinazohusina na mpango wa kununua mchele uliokusudiwa kuwasaidia wakulima wadogo, mpango ambao aliusimamia yeye.

eng: The program involved the government buying the rice output of local farmers at high a price before reselling the rice to the global market.
swa: Katika mpango huo serikali ilinunua mchele kwa wakulima wadogo kwa bei ya juu na kuuza katika soko la dunia.

eng: But critics saw the rice subsidy program as a disastrous populist policy that was implemented to benefit the support base of Yingluck's party in the north part of the country.
swa: Lakini wakosoaji wake wanasema mpango huo ulikuwa na malengo ya kumpa umaarufu na ulitekelezwa ili kukisaidia chama cha Yingluck katika sehemu ya kaskazini mwa nchi hiyo.

eng: Yingluck is the first female prime minister of the kingdom, and whose Pheu Thai party-led coalition won the election in 2011.
swa: Yingluck ni waziri mkuu wa kwanza mwanamke katika utawala wa kifalme wa nchi hiyo, kupitia muungano wa kisiasa unaoongozwa na chama cha Pheu Thai ulioshinda katika uchaguzi wa 2011.

eng: However the military has ruled Thailand since May 2014.
swa: Hata hivyo, jeshi la nchi hiyo limetawala Thailand tangu Mei 2014.

eng: The military has drafted a new constitution and appointed several bodies to rule the country and implement electoral and political reforms as part of the normalization process.
swa: Jeshi limeandika katiba mpya na kuteua vyombo kadhaa ili kutekeleza mabadiliko ya uchaguzi na kisiasa kama sehemu ya kurejea kwenye utawala wa kiraia.

eng: The NLA is one of the institutions created by the military to oversee the country's transition.
swa: Bunge ni moja ya taasisi zilizoundwa na jeshi kwa malengo ya kuratibu kipindi cha mpito.

eng: The impeachment reflected the desire of the military to block Yingluck's return to politics.
swa: Kura hiyo ya kutokuwa na imani na waziri mkuu ni picha ya sauti ya jeshi kutaka kumzuia Yingluck kurejea kwenye siasa za nchi hiyo.

eng: Security forces were on a state of alert around the parliament during the assembly.
swa: Vikosi vya kijeshi vilikuwa kwenye hali ya tahadhari kuzunguka viunga vya bunge hilo wakati wa kikao hicho

eng: RECAP: After being barred from talking to the press by the #ThaiJunta, Yingluck issues statement on Facebook https://t.co/3Dv3g7DPF4 — Saksith Saiyasombut (@Saksith) January 23, 2015
swa: Saa 2 asubuhi mbele ya bunge kulikuwa na idadi kubwa ya wanajeshi na polisi kuwadhibiti wapinzani. Maandamano yalipigwa marufuku Yingluck amepinga uamuzi wa bunge, unaomzuia kuchaguliwa kushika madaraka yoyote ya umma kwa miaka mitano.

eng: NCPO & police at SC Park Hotel.
swa: Kadhalika, anakabiliwa na mashitaka kadhaa ya jina (yanayohusiana na kashfa za ufisadi) yanayoweza kumfanya afungwe jela kwa miaka isiyozidi miaka kumi.

eng: A translated copy of her statement, as reported on by the Pheu Thai party website, highlights:
swa: Yingluck ametoa tamko rasmi kwenye mtandao wake wa Facebook, baada ya kufuta mpango wake wa kuongea na waandishi wa habari jijini Bangkok kama ilivyoagizwa na vyombo vya dola.

eng: I would like to reaffirm that I am innocent.
swa: Ningepedna kusisitiza kwamba sina hatia.

eng: I would like to thank the minority that voted against the impeachment.
swa: Ningependa kuwashukuru walio wachache bungeni kwa kupiga kura ya kupinga hatua ya kuniondoa madarakani.

eng: I praise you for your strength in upholding the principle of justice.
swa: Ninawapongeza kwa ushujaa wenu katika kuendeleza kanuni haki.

eng: Despite the fact that the process to impeach me was rushed and due process was ignored to the extent it stripped me my basic rights which every Thai citizen is entitled to, I believed that I did my best to present my case.
swa: Pamoja na ukweli kwamba mchakato wa kupiga kura ya kutokuwa na imani na mimi ulikimbizwa na haki haikufuatwa kiasi kwamba haki zangu za msingi zilipuuzwa, haki ambazo raia wote wa Thailand wanastahili, ninaamini kwamba nilifanya kila nililoweza kujitetea.

eng: I insist that the Rice Pledging Scheme is beneficial for the farmers and the country, and the scheme did not incur losses as alleged.
swa: Ninasisitiza kwamba Mpango wa Uuzaji wa Mchele una manufaa kwa wakulima na nchi kwa ujumla, na mpango huo haukuleta hasara kama inavyodaiwa.

eng: Any figures on the losses from the scheme have all been manipulated with bias towards me and with a hidden agenda used to eliminate a political opponent.
swa: Takwimu zozote kuyapa uzito madai ya mpango huo kulisababishia hasara taifa zimepikwa ili kufanya nionekane nina hatia na zina ajenda ya siri ya kuondoa upinzani wa kisiasa.

eng: Worst of all, the rice farmers’ lives have become a political tool.
swa: Mbaya zaidi, maisha ya wakulima wa mchele yamefanywa kuwa karata ya kisiasa.

eng: In the matter of the charges filed by the Attorney General, the former prime minister also said,
swa: Kuhusu mashitaka yaliyofunguliwa na Mwanasheria wa Serikali, waziri huyo mkuu wa zamani alisema,

eng: It is regrettable that the many so called coincidences that I spoke of yesterday happened once again today.
swa: Inasikitisha kwamba vingi nilivyovizungumza jana vimetokea leo tena.

eng: Just an hour before the NLA vote on impeachment, the Office of the Attorney General decided to file criminal charges against me for negligence of duty.
swa: Saa moja kabla ya Bunge kupiga kura ya kuniondoa, ofisi ya Mwanasheria Mkuu wa Serikali iliamua kufungua mashitaka ya jinai dhidi yangu kwa kuzembea kazini.

eng: This is in conflict with the comments made by the head of prosecuting team that there is not yet enough probable cause.
swa: Mashitaka hayo yanapingana na matamshi ya kiongozi wa mashitaka kwamba hakuna ushahidi wa kutosha.

eng: The Office of the Attorney General is an institution that has long played a key role in ensuring justice.
swa: Ofisi ya Mwanasheria Mkuu wa Serikali ni taasisi ambayo kwa muda mrefu imekuwa ikitimiza wajibu wake kuhakikisha kwamba haki inatendeka.

eng: Yet their actions on this issue are deemed to be questionable.
swa: Lakini bado, vitendo vyao katika suala hili vinaibua maswali mengi kuliko majibu.

eng: In her statement, she decried what she called the absence of democracy and the rule of law, particularly for the farmers.
swa: Katika tamko lake, alilia na kile alichokiita kukosekana kwa demokrasia na utawala wa sheria, hususani kwa wakulima.

eng: While the impeachment did not come as a surprise, some provided their analysis of the situation.
swa: Wakati kura ya kumng'oa waziri mkuu haukuja bila kutarajiwa, baadhi walifanya uchambuzi wa hali hiyo.

swa: Kadri mgongano mkubwa wa maslahi unavyozidi kuwa wazi, ndivyo watu zaidi wanavyozidi kuamka

swa: Kung'olewa kwa Yingluck ni maigizo zaidi ya kuwa mchakato wa haki na unaokubalika Ungejisikiaje kama unaamka siku moja, unajikuta ulikuwa unaishi kwenye nchi ya 'mazombi' inayoendeshwa na jeshi bila kuongozwa na sheria wala haki na uhuru wa kiraia

eng: Troubled times are brewing, and as long as the country is under martial law, without public participation in governance and accountability, the purge of political opponents will continue.
swa: Nyakati ngumu zinanukia, na kadri nchi inavyozidi kuwa chini ya jeshi, bila kuwa na ushiriki wa raia kwenye utawala na uwajibikaji, upinzani hautakoma.

eng: Former NATO Assistant Secretary General for Public Diplomacy Kolinda Grabar Kitarović has been elected Croatia's first woman president, defeating the incumbent president in the first presidential elections since the small southeastern European country joined the European Union last year.
swa: Aliyekuwa Katibu mkuu wa NATO wa masuala ya uhusiano wa kimataifa Kolinda Grabar Kitarović amechaguliwa kuwa Rais wa kwanza mwanamke wa nchi ya Croatia, kwa kumshinda Rais aliyemaliza muda wake katika uchaguzi wa kwanza kabisa mara baada ya nchi hii ndogo ya Ulaya ya Kusini kujiunga na Jumuia ya Umoja wa Ulaya mapema mwaka jana.

eng: Grabar Kitarović won in a tight race against incumbent President Ivo Jospović in the runoff in January 2015, netting 50.74% of the votes, according to preliminary results.
swa: Grabar Kitarović alipata ushindi katika mazingira ya upinzani mkali kutoka kwa Rais aliyemaliza muda wake, katika duru ya pili ya uchaguzi uliofanyika January 2015, akijizolea asilimia 50.74 ya kura zote, kwa mujibu wa taarifa za matokeo ya awali.

eng: She will be inaugurated on February 18, 2015.
swa: Ataapishwa rasmi tarehe 18 Februari, 2015.

eng: As Croatia's first woman president, and the country's fourth elected president since independence, she will undoubtedly leave her mark on both the country and region.
swa: Kama Rais wa kwanza mwanamke nchini Croatia, na Rais wa nne wa kuchaguliwa tangu nchi hii ijipatie uhuru wake, bila shaka yoyote ataweka historia kwa nchi yake na ukanda wa Jumuia ya Ulaya.

eng: But despite her historic win, many citizens who would have preferred a different political representative are worried as to how their views and needs will be represented with her at the helm.
swa: Pamoja na ushindi wake wa kihistoria, raia wengi ambao wangalipendelea Rais tofauti na yeye, wanaonesha hofu yao ni kwa namna gani mawazo na mahitaji yao yatatekelezwa na Rais huyu katika kipindi cha uongozi wake.

eng: Teacher, the test is over, but Bosnia is still writing!This meme has widely circulated following Croatia's presidential runoff.
swa: Mwalimu, mtihani umemalizika, lakini Bosnia anaendelea kuandika! ujumbe huu umesambaa kwa kiasi kukubwa kufuatia duru ya pili ya uchaguzi.

eng: The diaspora is often called out for favoring right-wing political parties, while not living and paying taxes in Croatia.
swa: Jumuia ya watu wanaoishi nje ya nchi mara nyingi hutakiwa kupigia kura vyama vya mrengo wa kulia, pamoja na kuwa watu hawa hawaishi nchini Crotia na wala kutozwa kodi.

eng: A member of the Croatian Democratic Union, the party instrumental in Croatia gaining independence in 1992, Grabar Kitarović is eager to bring what she has called "the Croatian spirit" back, as well as re-enforce "traditional" values.
swa: Grabar Kitarović ambaye ni mwanachama wa chama cha Umoja wa Demokrasia ya Raia wa Crotia, chama kilichosimamia kupatikana kwa uhuru wa nchi hii mwaka 1992, amenuia kurudisha kile alichokiita "Hulka ya Watu wa Crotia", pamoja na kusisitiza mambo ya "kiutamaduni".

eng: The country is highly divided between the available center-left and center-right political options, and she only defeated Josipović by only a few thousand votes.
swa: Nchi hii ina mpasuko mkubwa miongoni mwa makundi mawili ya siasa za kati-kushoto na kati-kulia, na alifanikiwa kumshinda mpinzani wake, Josipović kwa tofauti ya elfu kadhaa tu za kura.

eng: Josipović becomes the first Croatian president since the country's independence who didn't win reelection for a second term, as both Franjo Tuđman, Croatia's first president, and Stjepan Mesić were both reelected for two full terms each.
swa: Josipović anakuwa Rais wa kwanza tangu Croatia ipate uhuru kwa kushidwa kuchaguliwa kama Rais kwa awamu ya pili ya uongozi tofauti na maRais wengine kama Franjo Tuđman, Rais wa kwanza wa Croatia, pamoja na Stjepan Mesić ambao wote waliongoza kwa vipindi vyote viwili.

eng: In the eyes of many voters, Josipović hasn't done much for Croatians during his mandate as president.
swa: Kwa mtazamo wa wapiga kura wengi, Josipović alipokuwa Rais, hakuweza kutimiza mambo mengi waliyoyataka watu wa Crotia.

eng: The road to a runoff
swa: Kuelekea duru ya pili ya uchaguzi

eng: The race seems to have been dirty and expensive.
swa: Harakati za uchaguzi zinaonekana kuwa ziligubikwa na udanganyifu na matumizi makubwa ya fedha.

eng: The first round of elections was held on December 28, 2014, with four candidates for its presidency: Ivan Vilibor Sinčić, a young political activist, who was the biggest surprise and managed to take 16.42% of the vote; Milan Kujundžić, a right-wing politician, who won only 6.30% votes; Grabar Kitarović, representing the center-right Croatian Democratic Union, who took 37.88%; and incumbent President Josipović, who won 38.48% votes.
swa: Duru ya kwanza ya uchaguzi ilifanyika tarehe 28 December, 2014, ukiwa na wagombea wanne wa uRais: Ivan Vilibor Sinčić, mwanaharakati mdogo wa kisiasa, ambaye aliwashangaza wengi kwa kupata asilimia 16.42 ya kura zote; Milan Kujundžić, mwanasiasa wa mrengo wa kulia alipata asilimia 6.30 ya kura zote; Grabar Kitarović, anayewakilisha mrengo wa kati-kulia wa chama cha Umoja wa Kidemokrasia wa Chrotia, aliyejizolea asilimia 37.88; na Rais aliyekuwa madarakani Josipović, aliyepata asilisia 38.48% ya kura zote.

eng: The president can't be elected unless he or she secures more than 50% of the votes.
swa: Rais hawezi kutangazwa hadi pale mgombea atakapopata zaidi ya asilimia 50 ya kura zote.

eng: Because none of the four managed to surpass the 50% threshold (only 47.14% of the total electorate voted in first round), Grabar Kitarović and Josipović went head to head on January 11.
swa: Kwa kuwa, hakuna hata mmoja wao aliyefanikiwa kupata zaidi ya asilimia 50 nya kura zote (asilimia 47.14 tu ya wapiga kura wote ndio tu waliopiga kura katika duru ya kwanza ya uchaguzi), Grabar Kitarović na Josipović ndio walioelekea kwenye duru ya pili ya uchaguzi iliyofanyika January 11.

eng: During the campaign, the candidates offered up many plans for the country, still struggling with a troubled economy, high unemployment, low GDP and corruption.
swa: Wakati wa kampeni, wagombea walieleza mikakati mingi kwa ajili ya nchi yao, ambayo hadi sasa inakabiliwa na changamoto ya mdororo wa uchumi, kukosekana kwa ajira, kushuka kwa pato la taifa na rushwa.

eng: However, despite the amount of money poured into the elections, presidential power is actually very limited within the Croatian government, with the president mainly acting as a representative within the country and abroad and performing ceremonial duties such as awarding important individuals.
swa: Hata hivyo, pamoja na kiasi kikubwa cha fedha kutumiwa kwenye kampeni, madaraka ya uRais kwa hakika ni machache katika serikali ya Crotia, ambapo Rais kimsingi anakuwa kama muwakilishi ndani na nje ya nchi pamoja na kushughulikia mambo ya sherehe kama vile kuwatunuku watu mashuhuri.

eng: No matter how divided we are in these or future electoral percentages, the bad economical percentages are the same for everyone #izboriprh (#electionscroatia)
swa: Bila kujali ni kwa kiasi gani tunatofautiana katika asilimia za kura katika chaguzi hizi au zijazo, asilimia mbaya za kiwango cha uchumi zitaendelea kuwa zilezile kwa kila mmoja wetu.#izboriprh (#electionscroatia)

eng: Nevertheless, candidates sought votes through television debates, which often left the average voter wanting for a concrete reason to give either candidate their vote.
swa: Mbali na hali hii, wagombea waliwashawishi wapiga kura pia kupitia midahalo iliyorushwa kwenye vituo vya televisheni, midahalo iliyomfanya mpiga kura wa kawaida kutaka kupata sababu za msingi za kwa nini ampigie kura mgombea mmojawapo.

eng: Debates did, however generate some humorous tweets from Croatian social media users under the hashtags #izboriprh (#electionscroatia), #izbori2014 (#elections2014), #debataRTL (#debateRTL), and #HRTizbori (#HRTelections).
swa: Hata hivyo, midahalo hii iliibua twits za kufurahisha kutoka kwa watumiaji wa mitandao ya kijamii wa Crotia kupitia viungo habari #izboriprh (#electionscroatia), #izbori2014 (#elections2014), #debataRTL (#debateRTL), na #HRTizbori (#HRTelections).

eng: Between Ivo Josipovića and Kolinda Grabar Kitarović I can only choose an invalid voting ballot. #izboriprh #izbori2014
swa: Kati ya Ivo Josipovića na Kolinda Grabar Kitarović ninaweza tu kuchagua karatasi kura zisizo sahihi. #izboriprh #izbori2014

eng: One tweet summed up the general sentiment: What is saddest is that this historical event, in a patriarchal state, is probably not seen as a victory by any feminist. #izboriprh
swa: Kinachosikitisha zaidi ni kuwa tukio hili la kihistoria, katika nchi yenye misingi ya mfumo dume, bila shaka halichukuliwi kama ushindi kwa yeyote awateteao wanawake. #izboriprh

eng: Libela.org, an independent portal on gender, sex and democracy in Croatia, asked whether Grabar Kitarović is capable of uniting the nation and working in favor of women's rights, despite the fact she did not play the "female card" during the elections.
swa: Libela.org, jarida linalojitegemea la masuala ya usawa wa jinsia, jinsia pamoja na demokrasia nchini Crotia, ilihoji kama Grabar ana uwezo wa kuliunganisha taifa ikiwa ni pamoja na Kitarović is capable of uniting the nation and working kutoa kipau mbele kwa haki za binadamu, pamoja na kuwa hakucheza "female card" wakati wa uchaguzi.

eng: A nation is made of people, and the people of Croatia have chosen Kolinda Grabar Kitarović to be their next president, as is supposed to happen in a democracy.
swa: Taifa linajengwa na watu, na watu wa Crotia wameshamchagua Kolinda Grabar Kitarović kama Rais wao anayefuata, na kama jinsi inavyopaswa kufanyika katika nchi yenye demokrasia.

eng: Time will tell how much good the people's choice will bring the country.
swa: Wakati ndio utakaosema kiwango cha umahiri wa chaguo la watu katika kuijenga nchi ya Croatia.

eng: Human rights groups were blocked by the police from getting near the pope motorcade.
swa: Makundi ya haki za kijamii yalizuiwa na Polisi kuukaribia msafara wa Papa Francis.

eng: Image from Facebook page of Kathy Yamzon
swa: Picha kutoka kwenye ukurasa wa facebook wa Kathy Yamzon

eng: Not everyone in the Philippines was able to see Pope Francis when he began his current visit to the Philippines.
swa: Fursa ya kumwona kumwona Papa Francis alipoanza ziara yake ya ki-Papa nchini Ufilipino haikuwa kwa wazi kwa kila m-Filipino aliyetaka.

eng: A group activists carrying signs for social justice says the police prevented it from staging a demonstration in sight of the Pope's motorcade.
swa: Kikundi cha wanaharakati kilichokuwa na mabango yanayopinga hali mbaya ya haki za kijamii nchini humo kinasema polisi waliwazuia kufanya maandamano mbele ya msafara wa Papa.

eng: There are also reports that law enforcement officers detained several street children during the Pope's public procession.
swa: Kadhalika, kuna taarifa kwamba maafisa wa polisi waliwakamata na kuwaweka kizuizini baadhi ya watoto wa mtaani wakati wa ziara hiyo ya Papa.

eng: Pope Francis will tour the Philippines from January 15 to January 19.
swa: Papa Francis alizuru Ufilipino kuanzia Januari 15 mpaka 19.

eng: The visit, themed "mercy and compassion," takes Pope Francis to the largest Catholic-dominated nation in Asia.
swa: Ziara hiyo, iliyokuwa na kauli mbiu ya "rehema na huruma," ilimfikisha Papa Francis katika taifa hilo linaloongoza kwa idadi kubwa ya wa-Katoliki nchini Asia.

eng: Some 2,000 activists gathered in Manila to greet the Pope by unfurling banners that highlight some of the issues that affect the nation's poor, such as hunger, landlessness, and injustice.
swa: Kiasi cha wanaharakati 2,000 walikusanyika jijini Manila 'kumsalimia' Papa kwa mabango yaliyokuwa na ujumbe wa masuala kadhaa yanayowaathiri masikini wa taifa hilo, kama vile njaa, ukosefu wa ardhi, na uvunjifu wa haki.

eng: Police blocked the march from getting near the motorcade, however.
swa: Polisi hata hivyo waliwazuia kuukaribia msafara wa Papa.

eng: Activist leader Nato Reyes criticized the government for stopping various groups from trying to tell the Pope about the Philippines' "real situation":
swa: Kiongozi wa wanaharakati hao Nato Reyes aliikosoa vikali serikali kwa kuyazuia makundi mbalimbali yaliyotaka kujaribu kumweleza Papa kuhusu "hali halisi" ya mambo nchini Ufilipino. :

eng: From Day 1, there has been a conscious effort to regulate what the Pope can see and hear.
swa: Kuanzia Siku ya 1, kumekuwa na jitihada za makusudi kujaribu kudhibiti kile ambacho Papa anatakiwa kukiona na kukisikia.

eng: It is monumentally ironic since the Pope did not come here to see only ” true, the good and the beautiful”.
swa: Hilo liko wazi kwa sababu Papa hakuja nchini humu kuona kile kinachoitwa "ukweli, mema na mazuri" pekee.

eng: The Pope came here to hear about the problems of the poor and marginalized.
swa: Papa amekuja hapa kusikia matatizo ya watu masikini na wanaotengwa.

eng: Police barred a group of activists from marching near the Pope's motorcade.
swa: Polisi wakiwazuia wanaharakati kadhaa kuandamana karibu na msafara wa Papa.

eng: Photo from Facebook page of Southern Tagalog Exposure.
swa: Picha kutoka ukurasa wa Facebook wa Southern Tagalog Exposure.

eng: Photo from Facebook page of the group.
swa: Picha kutoka ukursa wa Facebook wa kikundi hicho.

eng: Members of the police confiscate an activist's flag.
swa: Polisi wakirarua bendera ya mwanaharakati.

eng: Police said only "greeting streamers" were permitted.
swa: Polisi wamesema 'watu waliokuwa wakimshangilia' Papa tu ndio tu waliruhusiwa.

eng: Photo from Facebook page of Southern Tagalog Exposure.
swa: Picha kutoka ukurasa wa Facebook wa Southern Tagalog Exposure.

eng: Some political prisoners were able to hang a banner outside their cell.
swa: Baadhi ya wafungwa wa kisiasa waliweza kuning'iniza mabango nje ya vyumba vyao vya magereza.

eng: They urged the Pope to look into the worsening human rights situation in the country.
swa: Walimwomba Papa kutazama hali ya haki za binadamu yanayozidi kuwa mbaya nchini humo.

eng: Photo from Facebook page of Kathy Yamzon.
swa: Picha kutoka ukurasa wa Facebook wa Kathy Yamzon.

eng: In addition to interfering with protesters, the government also reportedly “detained” and “caged” street children a few days before the Pope's arrival.
swa: Zaidi ya kuwaingilia waandamanaji, serikali pia inadaiwa 'kuwakamata" na "kuwaweka kizuizini" watoto wa mtaani siku chache baada ya Papa kuwasili.

eng: Manila Standard Today, a major daily newspaper, questioned the wisdom of this policy, saying it amounts to a Potemkin-Village approach.
swa: Jarida maarufu la kila siku la Manila Standard Today, lilihoji busara ya sera hii, likisema inamwelekeo unaokaribiana na sera ya Potemkin-Village.

eng: The government has denied detaining street children during the Pope’s visit.
swa: Serikali imekanusha kuwakamata watoto wa mtaani wakati wa ziara ya Papa.

eng: Meanwhile, officials erected a green wall along the Pope's motorcade route, preventing him and other motorists from seeing the urban poor who live beyond the barrier.
swa: Wakati huo huo, maafisa wa serikali walitengeneza kwa haraka ukuta wa kijani pembezoni mwa barabara ambazo msafara wa Papa Francis ungepita, kwa lengo la kumzuia Papa na watu wengine waliokuwa kwenye msafara huo kuo mitaa wanayoishi maskini pembezoni mwa kizuizi.

eng: Another “barrier” separating the Pope from the people was the heavy security.
swa: Kizuizi kingine kinachomtenga Papa na watu kilikuwa usalama mkali.

eng: Many said the deployment of police and placement of metal barriers throughout the city was excessive, making it difficult for people even to glimpse the nation's special guest.
swa: Wengi walisema kumwagwa kwa polisi na kuwekwa kwa vizuizi vya chuma jijini humo kulizidi kiwango, na kuwafanya watu washindwe kumwona mgeni huyo maalum wa taifa.

eng: Several disgruntled Filipino Internet users pointed to the Pope’s recent visit to Sri Lanka, where he was seen touching and blessing the hands of the faithful along the road.
swa: Baadhi ya watumiaji wa mtandao wa intaneti wa ki-Filipino walifananisha ziara ya hivi majuzi ya Papa nchini Sri Lanka, ambapo alionekana akigusa na kubariki mikono ya waumini waliokuwa wamesimama barabarani kumlaki.

eng: Overkill police deployment?
swa: Polisi walizidi kiwango?

eng: Aquino is president of the Philippines.
swa: Aquino ni rais wa Ufilipino.

eng: Image from Facebook page of labor center Kilusang Mayo Uno (May First Movement).
swa: Picha kutoka ukurasa wa Facebook wa kituo cha kazi cha Kilusang Mayo Uno (Vuguvugu la Mei Mosi).

eng: Pope Francis!
swa: Papa Francis!

eng: Quirino Ave cor Taft Ave on his way to MOA Arena around 5pm @gmanews pic.twitter.com/LKXJYY3NBA — Bam Alegre (@BamAlegre) January 16, 2015
swa: Quirino Ave cor Taft Ave akiwa njiani kwenda kwenye uwanja wa MOA Arena majira ya saa 11 jioni @gmanews pic.twitter.com/LKXJYY3NBA — Bam Alegre (@BamAlegre) January 16, 2015

eng: Pope Francis waving as he passed by Quirino Ave cor.
swa: Papa Francis!

eng: The government says the strict security detail is a necessary precaution.
swa: Papa Francis akipunga mono alipokuwa akipita akiwa kwenye gari la Quirino.

eng: Still, many continue to urge authorities to respect the wishes of the faithful and let them closer to the Pope:
swa: Hata hivyo, wengi wanaendelea kuhoji kwa nini serikali haikuheshimu matakwa ya waumini na kuwaruhusu kumkaribia Papa:

eng: Sure it's for security purposes but I think the Pope would really like to reach out to the people hidden by hundreds of security personnel. — Kat De Castro⭐♎ (@KatDeCastro) January 16, 2015
swa: Ni kweli kwamba hali hiyo ilikuwa ya lazima kwa usalama lakini ninadhani Papa angependa kuwafikia watu waliokuwa wamefichwa na mamia ya wana usalama.

eng: Nonoy Oplas criticized the “militarized security system” adopted by the government:
swa: Nonoy Oplas alikosoa vikali "mfumo wa kiusalama wa kijeshi" unaotumiwa na serikali:

eng: Seeing him on the road is the closest thing (the people) can get and see the Pope.
swa: Kumwona barabarani ni jambo la fahari zaidi ambalo watu wangejisikia kuweza kumwona Papa.

eng: And the paranoid security system tried hard to make the public's view of the Pope as short as possible, as far as possible.
swa: Na mfumo unakera wa usalama ulijaribu kufanya iwe vigumu kwa watu kumwona Papa kwa karibu kadri inavyowezekana.

eng: Many are hoping the government will rethink its security arrangements in the days ahead, to allow more people to lay eyes on Pope Francis, before he departs on January 19.
swa: Wengi wanatarajia kwamba Serikali itafikiria upya utaratibu wake wa kiusalama katika siku zilizobaki, ili kuwaruhusu watu zaidi kumwona Papa Francis, kabla hajaondoka Januari 19.

eng: Nigerian pastor Esther Ibanga joined with Muslim leaders in the city of Jos to call for the return of Chibok girls who were kidnapped by the extremist group Boko Haram.
swa: Mchungaji wa ki-Naijeria Esther Ibanga akiwa na viongozi wa Kiislam mjini Jos kutoa mwito wa kurudishwa kwa wasichana wa Chibok waliokuwa wametekwa na kikundi cha kigaidi kiitwacho Boko Haram.

eng: Credit: Women Without Walls Initiative (Willie Abok).
swa: Picha: Women Without Walls Initiative (Willie Abok).

eng: Published with PRI's permission
swa: Imechapishwa kwa ruhusa ya PRI

eng: This article and a radio report by Joyce Hackel for The World originally appeared on PRI.org on January 14, 2015 and is republished as part of a content-sharing agreement.
swa: Makala haya na taarifa ya redio ya Joyce Hackel wa Kipindi cha The World yalichapishwa kwa mara ya kwanza kwenye mtandao wa PRI.org mnamo Januari 14, 2015 na yamechapishw atena kama sehemu ya makubaliano ya kubadilishana maudhui.

eng: With all eyes turned on France last week, a massacre perpetrated by religious extremists in a northeastern Nigerian town called Baga barely registered around the globe.
swa: Wakati macho yote yakiwa yameelekezwa Ufaransa juma lililopita, shambulio la kigaidi lililofanywa na magaidi wa kidini na kukatisha maisha ya watu wengi katika mji wa kaskazini mashariki mwa Naijeria uitwao Baga halikupata kutangazwa na vyombo vingi vya habari duniani.

eng: That disparity in news coverage jumps out, especially to Nigerians.
swa: Kukosekana kwa habari kwa makusudi namna hiyo hakukubaliki kwa wa-Naijeria.

eng: Esther Ibanga, a pastor in the town of Jos and a founder of a group called Women Without Walls, says she would have hoped the world would have paid more attention to the Boko Haram assault that took hundreds, perhaps thousands of Nigerian lives.
swa: Esther Ibanga, mchungaji wa mji wa Jos na mwanzilishi wa kikundi kiitwacho Wanawake Wasio na Mipaka, anasema alitegemea dunia ingetazama kwa uzito ugaidi unaofanywa na kikundi cha Boko Haram kinachochukua mamia, na pengine maelfu ya maisha ya wa-Naijeria.

eng: I was angry in my heart. 	Nilikasirika sana moyoni mwangu.
But my anger was toward my government," says Ibanga, the pastor of Jos Christian Missions.
swa: Lakini hasira yangu ilikuwa dhidi ya serikali yangu," anasema Ibanga, mchungaji wa kanisa la Jos Christian Missions.

eng: Because my government and my rulers have to value their own people. 	Kwa sabbau serikali yangu na watawala wake wanapaswa kuthamini watu wao wenyewe.
If you don't value your own people first, why would you expect someone else to value them?"
swa: Kama huthamini watu wako mwenyewe kwanza, kwa nini utarajie mtu mwingine awathamini?"

eng: Jos is the capital of Plateau State in Nigeria's Middle Belt.
swa: Jos ni mjini kuu wa Jimbo la Plateau kwenye ukanda wa kati wa Naijeria.

eng: It lies hundreds of miles south of Boko Haram strongholds in Borno State in Nigeria's northeast.
swa: Uko mamia ya maili kusini mwa ngome ya Boko Haram kwenye Jimbo la Borno kaskazini mashariki mwa Naijeria.

eng: Religious tensions in the Middle Belt pre-date Boko Haram and began most recently in the mid-1990s.
swa: Misuguano ya kidini katika uakdna wa kati imeanza siku nyingi kabla ya kufahamika kwa Boko Haram katika miaka ya 1990.

eng: It's unfortunate, but over the years we sort of got used to it, that Christians and Muslims don't get on well together, Ibanga says.
swa: Ni bahati mbaya sana, lakini kwa miaka kadhaa sasa ni kama tumeanza kuzoea, kwamba wa-Kristo na wa-Islam hawapatani, anasema Ibanga.

eng: Even after the tensions had become commonplace, the severity of a 2010 massacre in the town of Dogo-Nahawa turned Ibanga and other local women into vocal activists.
swa: Hata baada ya misuguano hiyo kuzoeleka, kiwango cha mauaji ya mwaka 2010 kwenye mji wa Dogo-Nahawa kulimfanya Ibanga na wanawake wengine wa sehemu hiyo kuwa wanaharakati wanaopaza sauti.

eng: The war was taken into the bedrooms, she says.
swa: Vita imeenea mpaka kwenye vyumba vya kulala, anasema.

eng: The village that was attacked, they actually went right into their bedroom at night when they were sleeping and started killing them.
swa: Kijiji kilichoshambuliwa, washambuliaji walienda mpaka vyumbani walikolala watu usiku na kuanza kuwaua.

eng: In response, Ibgana organized 100,000 women, mainly Christians, in a march through Jos.
swa: Matokeo yake, Ibgana aliwaratibu wanawake 100,000, wengi wao wakiwa wa-Kristo, kuandamana katika mji wa Jos.

eng: The idea, she recalls, was "to let the government know the women on the plateau were not going to keep quiet any more."
swa: Wazo, anakumbuka, lilikuwa "kuifanya serikali ijue kwamba wanawake kwenye Jimbo hilo hawakuwa tayari kuendelea kunyamazia vitendo hivyo"

eng: But in the weeks that followed, Ibanga and others discovered that the extremist violence in Dogo-Nahawa was in fact a reprisal attack — in response to an earlier assault in the region by Christian militants.
swa: Lakini katika majuma yaliyofuata, Ibanga na wengine waligundua kwamba ghasia hizo za kigaidi katika eneo la Dogo-Nahawa zilikuwa kwa hakika mashambulio ya kulipiza kusasi -kujibu shambulio la awali lililofanywa na wanamgambo wa ki-Kristo.

eng: The Muslim women now reacted and said, 'Hey, wait a minute, our own people were killed as well,' she recalls.
swa: Wanawake wa ki-Islam waliitikia na kusema, 'Jamani, subiri kidogo, mbona watu wetu wenyewe wanauawa pia,' anakumbuka.

eng: So Muslim women in Jos held their own, separate rally.
swa: Kw ahiyo wanawake wa Kiislam mjini Jos waliamua kufanya mkutano wao wenyewe.

eng: But even after the Christian and the Muslim demonstrations, the violent clashes continued.
swa: Lakini hata baada ya maandamano ya wa-Kristo na wa-Islam, mapigano yameendelea.

eng: At that point, Ibanga reached out to a local Muslim religious leader, Khadija Hawaja.
swa: Hali ilipofikia hapo, Ibanga aliamua kukutana na kingozi wa dini ya ki-Islam wa eneo hilo, Khadija Hawaja.

eng: That's when I realized the issue is really not religion, the issue was politics. 	Hapo ndipo nilipotambua kwmaba suala halikuwa dini, bali siasa.
But religion was used as a very powerful tool," she says.
swa: Lakini dini ilitumiwa kama silaha yenye nguvu," anasema.

eng: I reached out to her and I said, 'Hey listen, you know we're not each other's problems. 	Nilimfuata na kusema, 'Hebu sikia, unajua sisi hatuwezi kuwa tatizo la mwenzake.
It's not about you being a Muslim and me being a Christian.
swa: Wala suala sio wewe kuwa Muislamu au mimi kuwa Mkristo.

eng: These politicians are knocking our heads together.
swa: Hawa wanasiasa wanatugonganisha vichwa vyetu.

eng: And it's all about them maintaining power.'"
swa: Na nia yao ni kuendelea kubaki madarakani.'"

eng: Because Jos was so politically polarized, the women met on "neutral ground" — in a restaurant.
swa: Kwa sababu Jos ilikuwa imeathirika sana kisiasa, wanawake hao walikutana katika 'eneo lisilo na upande' — hotelini.

eng: She could have been killed, Ibanga says.
swa: Angeuawa, Ibanga anasema.

eng: And I could have been killed also, going into a Muslim community.
swa: Na ningeuawa pia, kwa kwenda tu kwenye jamii ya ki-Islam.

eng: After months of collaboration, Ibanga and Hawaja founded the Women Without Walls Initiative.
swa: Baada ya miezi ya kushirikiana, Ibanga na Hawaja walianzisha Mradi wa Wanawake Wasio na Mipaka.

eng: We want to do away with the walls that divide and separate us, whether it's the walls of social class or the wall of ethnicity or the walls of religion, she says.
swa: Tunataka kuachana na mipaka inayotutenga na kutugawanya, iwe ni mipaka ya matabaka ya kijamii au mipaka ya kidini, alisema.

eng: We really cannot join the politicians in this fight. 	Hatuwezi kuungana na wanasiasa kwenye vita hii.
We are mothers.
swa: Sisi ni akina mama.

eng: We are life givers and we are solution bearers.
swa: Sisi tunatengeneza uhai na tunatafuta majibu.

eng: And we think that we should bring solutions to the table, rather than dwell on the problem."
swa: Na tunadhani kwmaba lazima tuje na majibu ya matatizo, badala ya kuishi kwenye matatizo."

eng: On January 19, Congolese police in Kinshasa violently dispersed protesters opposed to the revision of the electoral law that would allow Joseph Kabila to remain in power.
swa: Mnamo Januari 19, Polisi wa Kongo jijini Kinshasa walitumia nguvu kubwa kuwatawanya waandamanaji waliokuwa wanapinga kubadilishwa kwa sheria ya uchaguzi itakayomruhusu Joseph Kabila kubaki madarakani.

eng: 35 protesters, most of them students, and 1 policeman were killed.
swa: Waandamanaji 35, wengi wao wakiwa wanafunzi na polisi mmoja waliuawa.

eng: The city of Goma was also affected by clashes that saw the arrest of many among the thousands of protesters.
swa: Jiji la Goma liliathiriwa na mapigano yaliyosababisha kukamatwa kwa watu wengi miongoni mwa maelfu ya waandamanaji.

eng: Kabila seeks to indirectly extend his term, which is coming to an end next year, by organizing a census that would take 3 years to complete.
swa: Kabila anaonekana kutumia mbinu zisizo za moja kwa moja kutafuta kugombea muhula mwingine wa Urais katika uchaguzi wa unaotarajiwa kufanyika mwakani, kwa kuandaa sensa ambayo kwa kawaida huchukua miaka mitatu kukamilika.

eng: Kabila is barred by the constitution from seeking a third term, however his term would be automatically prolonged until the census is completed.
swa: Kabila anazuiwa na katiba ya nchi hiyo kugombea kwa kipindi cha tatu, ingawa kwa kampeni ya sasa itabidi andelee kutawala mpaka sensa itakapokamilika.

eng: Shortly after the protests, mobile internet and texting were shut down briefly as well as most schools in the city.
swa: Muda mfupi baada ya maandamano, mtandao wa intaneti na huduma ya ujumbe mfupi wa maandishi kwenye simu vilizimwa pamoja na shule nyingi zilizopo jijini kufungwa.

eng: Some dormitories were set ablaze during the clashes.
swa: Baadhi ya mabweni yalichomwa moto wakati wa ghasia.

eng: The Kabila administration argues that a census is necessary prior to issuing the electoral lists for the presidential and parliamentary elections of 2016.
swa: Utawala wa Kabila unadai kwamba sensa ni zoezi muhimu na linalostahili kupewa kipaumbele ili kuhakikisha kwamba orodha ya wapiga kura inaandaliwa vyema kwa ajili ya uchaguzi ujao wa Rais na wabunge unaotarajiwa kufanyika 2016.

eng: The very influential Catholic Church has backed the opposition request to forego any revision to the planned electoral calendar.
swa: Kanisa Katoliki lenye ushawishi mkubwa nchini humo limeunga mkono madai ya upinzani ya kusimamisha shughuli yoyote ya kupitia upya ratiba ya uchaguzi.

eng: The proposed revision is currently under review at the Senate.
swa: Mabadiliko yanayopendekezwa yanafanywa na Baraza la Seneti.
