swa: Video ifuatayo ya kijamii iliyopigwa na Kininfos Januari 19 inayoonesha sehemu ndogo ya ghasia kwenye mji huo mkuu wakati waandamanaji waijaribu kufunga mitaa:

eng: Paul Nsapu, secretary general for Africa of the International Federation for Human Rights in Kinshasa, is appalled by the excessive measures taken by the government:
swa: Paul Nsapu, katibu mkuu wa Muungano wa Kimataifa wa Haki za Binadamu Barani Afrika unaofanya kazi zake Kinshasa, anashangazwa na hatua kali zilizochukuliwa na serikali:

eng: For the most part these people were killed while they were advancing to protest.
swa: Kwa kiasi kikubwa watu hawa waliuawa wakati wakielekea kuandamana.

eng: We didn't expect the government to act in the same way as a rebel group.
swa: Hatukutarajia serikali iwafayie hivyo utafikiri ni kikundi cha waasi.

eng: The following video provides a recap of the events over the past week :
swa: Video ifuatayo inatoa muhtasari wa matukio katika juma lililopita:

eng: Ida Sawyer, DR Congo Researcher for Human Rights Watch, adds that the repression is in contradiction with the rights of citizens to express themselves:
swa: Ida Sawyer, Mtafiti wa Kongo DRC wa Shirika la Kutetea Haki za Binadamu la Human Rights Watch, anaongeza kwamba vitendo vya kuzima maandamano vinapingana na haki za raia ambao lengo lao ni kujieleza:

eng: Congolese security forces have fired into crowds of demonstrators with deadly results.
swa: Vikosi vya usalama nchini Kongo vimerusha risasi za moto kwa makundi ya waandamanaji na matokeo yake ni wengi kuuawa.

eng: People should be allowed to express their views and peacefully protest without the fear of being killed or arrested
swa: Watu lazima waruhusiwe kusema maoni yao na hata kuandamana kwa amani bila hofu ya kuuawa wala kukamatwa

eng: CPJ's Africa Program Coordinator, Sue Valentine argues that shutting down internet and SMS communication in the country is an infringement on basic Congolese rights:
swa: Mratibu wa programu wa Afrika wa CPJ, Sue Valentine anasema kuzima mtandao wa intaneti na mawasiliano ya simu katika nchi hiyo ni kukiukwa kwa haki za msingi za wa-Kongo:

eng: By shutting down internet and messaging services and blocking websites, Congolese authorities are denying citizens their fundamental right to communicate and to receive and impart information
swa: Kwa kuzima mtandao wa intaneti na huduma za ujumbe mfupi wa maandishi na kufunga tovuti, serikali ya Kongo inawanyima raia haki zao za msingi za kuwasiliana na kupokea na kusambaza taarifa

eng: Jason Stearns explains why these protests have a different feel on his Congo Siasa blog:
swa: Jason Stearns anaeleza kwa nini waandamanaji wana hisia kali kwenye blogu yake ya Congo Siasa:

eng: Students are now playing a much more important role than in 2011.
swa: Waandamanaji sasa wanatimiza wajibu wao muhimu kuliko ilivyokuwa mwaka 2011.

eng: The epicenter of the protests has been at the University of Kinshasa (UNIKIN), which has been stormed by presidential guards and police.
swa: Maandamano yameanzia kwenye Chuo Kikuu cha Kinshasa (UNIKIN), kichovamiwa na watu wa usalama wa taifa pamoja na Polisi.

eng: There are over 30,000 students at the university, and hundreds of thousands of students across the country.
swa: Kuna wanafunzi 30,000 wa Chuo Kikuu, na mamia ya maelfu ya wanafunzi nchini kote.

eng: In Bukavu, too, university students were at the forefront of demonstrations organized yesterday.
swa: Mjini Bukavu, hali kadhalika, wanafunzi wa Chuo Kikuu walikuwa mstari wa mbele kwenye maandamano yaliyoandaliwa jana.

eng: In the past, the political fervor of university campuses has often been tempered when student bodies have been co-opted by political elites.
swa: Siku za nyuma, mijadala ya kisiasa katika Vyuo Vikuu mbalimbali nchini humo ilizimwa kirahisi kwa sababu vyama vya wanafunzi viliingiliwa na wanasiasa.

eng: This time that seems to be different.
swa: Safari hii mambo yalikuwa tofauti.

eng: Joseph Kabila took power in 2001 following the assassination of his father Laurent Kabila.
swa: Joseph Kabila alitwaa madaraka mwaka 2001 kufuatia kuuawa kwa baba yake Laurent Kabila.

eng: Under Congolese law, the Congolese National Police are responsible for providing security and ensuring public order during demonstrations.
swa: Chini ya Sheria ya Kongo, Polisi wanawajibu wa kutoa ulinzi na kuhakikisha umma unafanya maandamano kwa utulivu.

eng: The national police chief can call on the regular Congolese army to provide assistance if police forces are overwhelmed.
swa: Mkuu wa Polisi nchini humo ana mamlaka ya kuwaita wanajeshi wa nchi hiyo kutoa msaada kama polisi wanazidiwa.

eng: Wekesa Sylvanus hopes that 2015 will be a year of free and fair elections in Africa:
swa: Wekesa Sylvanus anataraji kwamba 2015 utakuwa mwaka wa chaguzi huru na haki barani Afrika:

eng: https://wekesasylvanus.wordpress.com/2015/02/18/will-2015-be-a-year-of-free-and-fair-elections-in-africa/
swa: https://wekesasylvanus.wordpress.com/2015/02/18/will-2015-be-a-year-of-free-and-fair-elections-in-africa/

eng: Since the advent of multi party democracy in Africa, electoral contests have become a do or die affair in majority of African countries.
swa: Tangu kurejeshwa kwa mfumo wa demokrasia ya vyama vingi barani Afrika, ushindani nyakati za uchaguzi umekuwa suala la kufa na kupona kwenye nchi nyingi za ki-Afrika.

eng: Elections in Africa are a high risk affair and in the recent times, they have been a trigger of conflicts.
swa: Chaguzi barani Afrika ni suala lenye hatari zake na katika nyakati za hivi karibuni, chaguzi zimekuwa kichocheo cha migogoro.

eng: Kenya and Ivory Coast are good examples of how mismanaged elections can plunge a country into a conflict.
swa: Kenya na Ivory Coast ni mifano mizuri ya namna kutokusekana kwa utaratibu mzuri wa uchaguzi kunavyoweza kuiingiza nchi kwenye machafuko.

eng: Half a century after gaining independence, majority of African states have not got it right in terms of conducting and managing free and fair elections.
swa: Karibu nusu karne baada ya uhuru, nchi nyingi za ki-Afrika hazijaweza kuwa na taratibu sahihi kufanya chaguzi zilizo huru na haki.

eng: The year 2015 will see a host of African countries go through elections.
swa: Mwaka 2015 utashuhudia nchi nyingi zikiingia kwenye uchaguzi.

eng: Presidential elections and/or legislative elections will be held in Nigeria, Sudan, Ethiopia, Burundi, Tanzania, Zambia, Togo, Ivory Coast, Mauritius, Central Africa Republic, Burkina Faso, Niger, Guinea, Chad, and Egypt and may be South Sudan depending on the peace deal to be signed.
swa: Chaguzi za Rais na/au wabunge zitafanyika kwenye nchi za Naijeria, Sudan, Ethiopia, Burundi, Tanzania, Zambia, Togo, Ivory Coast, Mauritius, Jamhuri ya Afrika ya Kati, Burkina Faso, Naija, Guinea, Chadi, na Misri na labda Sudani Kusini kutegemeana na makubaliano ya amani yanayotarajiwa kuwekewa saini.

eng: Most of these countries have struggled to institute the practice of democracy in recent times.
swa: Nyingi za nchi hizi zimepambana kutaasisisha utendaji wa kidemokrasia katka siku za hivi karibuni.

eng: 2015 therefore presents a great opportunity for them to show the world that they have matured democratically.
swa: Mwaka 2015 unaleta fursa kubwa kwa nchi hizi kuionesha dunia kwamba sasa zimekomaa kidemokrasia.

eng: Uganda's parliament in session.
swa: Bunge la Uganda likiendelea na kikao.

eng: Photo used with permission from parliament Watch Uganda.
swa: Picha imetumiwa kwa ruhusa ya Taasisi ya Parliament Watch Uganda.

eng: Ugandans are taking advantage of social media to bridge the gap between citizens and legislators, thanks to Parliament Watch Uganda, a virtual tracker that monitors the Parliament of Uganda on a regular basis and provides both relevant data and expert analysis.
swa: Wananchi wa Uganda wanatumia vizuri mitandao ya kijamii kuwasiliana na wabunge wao, kwa msaada wa Parliament Watch Uganda, taasisi inayofuatilia shughuli za Bunge la Uganda na kisha kutoa takwimu zinazohitajika pamoja na uchambuzi wa kitaalam.

eng: On 26 February, 2015, the initiative organized the #MPsEngage Twitter chat with women members of Parliament (MPs) to discuss the topic 'Making Women Count in Legislative Processes'.
swa: Mnamo Februari 26, 2015, taasisi hiyo iliandaa Mjadala ulioitwa #MPsEngage na kufanyika kwenye mtandao wa Twita ili kuwapa fursa wabunge wanawake kuzungumzia mada iliyoitwa, "Kuwafanya Wanawake Wathaminike kwenye Mchakato wa Kibunge'.

eng: Three audiences participated in the chat in real time: the people of Gulu in Northern Uganda, female members of parliament and Uganda's social media audience.
swa: Wahudhuriaji walikuwa wa aina tatu na kwa wakati ule ule: Watu wa Gulu kaskazini mwa Uganda, wabunge wanawake wa Uganda na watumiaji wa mitandao ya kijamii nchini Uganda.

eng: Gulu is a post conflict district in Northern Uganda.
swa: Gulu ni wilaya iliyokuwa na misuguano Kaskazini mwa Uganda.

eng: It was the center of conflict between the government of Uganda and the Lord’s Resistance Army (LRA).
swa: Kilikuwa ni kitovu cha mgogoro kati ya serikali ya Uganda na waasi wa Lord’s Resistance Army (LRA).

eng: Women in the area face many challenges inherited from the war and the general neglect of the central government.
swa: Wanawake wa eneo hilo wanakabiliwa na changamoto nyingi ambazo ni athari za vita na kupuuzwa na serikali kuu.

eng: Members of the audience in Gulu asked questions via microphones, which were tweeted to the MPs by a social media expert in the audience.
swa: Wahudhuriaji kutoka Gulu waliuliza maswali kupitia vinasa sauti, na wataalamu wa mitandao ya kijamii walitwiti maswali hayo kwa wabunge.

eng: During the chat, the female MPs were tasked to take stock of their achievements and challenges that they've faced during their term in office.
swa: Wakati wa majadiliano hayo, wabunge wanawake walitakiwa kuelezea mafanikio na changamoto walizokabiliana nazo wakati wote wa kipindi cha uongozi wao.

eng: Ugandan social media users took it upon themselves to comment, quote and direct the attention of their followers to #MPsEngage.
swa: Watumiaji wa mitandao ya kijamii walitoa maoni, kunukuu na kuwaelekeza wafuatiaji wao kwenye alama ishara ya majadiiano hayo ambayo ilikuwa ni #MPsEngage.

eng: Do women in Uganda have full access to participation in all political process and decision making in UG? #MPsEngage pic.twitter.com/8Oz5PlWDk1 — Parliament Watch (@pwatchug) February 25, 2015
swa: Je, wanawake nchini Uganda wanapata ushiriki katika katika michakato yote ya kisiasa na kufanya maamuzi nchini Uganda?

eng: Ugandan journalist and blogger Raymond Qatahar observed:
swa: Mwandishi wa Uganda, ambaye pia ni mwanablogu Raymond Qatahar alikuwa na haya ya kuchangia:

eng: Taking an observatory eye into the #MPsEngage .
swa: Ninafuatilia majadiliano ya #MPsEngage.

eng: Glad that finally, a technological solution has been found to connect legislators to p'ple — Qatahar Raymond (@qataharraymond) February 26, 2015
swa: Nina furaha kwamba hatimaye, suluhisho ya kiteknolojia limepatikana na kuwaunganisha wabunge na wananchi

eng: Jackie Asiimwe, a Ugandan lawyer, asked:
swa: Jackie Asiimwe, Mwanasheria ya Uganda, aliuliza:

eng: When will we ever ask male MPs how they are advancing the cause of women, because they too are voted by and represent women. #MPsEngage — Jacqueline Asiimwe (@asiimwe4justice) February 26, 2015
swa: Ni lini tutapata fursa ya kuwauliza wabunge wanaume namna wanavyoshughulikia masuala ya wanawake, kwa sababu na wao pia walichaguliwa na wanawawakilisha wanawake

eng: Kollin Rukundo brought up the issue of the marriage and divorce bill.
swa: Kollin Rukundo aliibua suala la muswada wa ndoa na talaka .

eng: The bill, among other things, makes asset-sharing mandatory in a divorce, provides cohabiting partners with property rights and makes marital rape illegal:
swa: Muswada huo, pamoja na mambo mengine, unawalazimisha wanandoa kuwa na umiliki sawa wa mali zao, na kuwafanya wenzi wanaoishi pamoja bila ndoa kuwa na haki za kumiliki mali na pia unafanya ubakaji unaofanyika kati ya wanandoa kuwa kosa la jinai:

eng: Referring to Marriage & Divorce Bill "How can an MP pick one clause(divorce) and use it demonise the entire bill?"- Miria Matembe #MPsEngage — Kollin Rukundo T (@kollinsayz) February 26, 2015
swa: Kwa kurejea muswada wa Ndoa na Talaka, "Namna gani Mbunge anaweza kuchukua kipengele kimoja (talaka) na kukitumia kupinga muswada mzima?

eng: Quoting Miria Matembe, a former minster of ethics and integrity, Jackie Asiimwe said:
swa: Akimnukuu Miria Matembe, waziri wa zamani wa maadili na uadilifu, Jackie Asiimwe alisema:

eng: MPs don't use their power properly.
swa: Wabunge hawatumii mamlaka yao ipasavyo.

eng: Instead they do the work of the Executive - building schools, supplying medicines - Matembe #MPsEngage — Jacqueline Asiimwe (@asiimwe4justice) February 26, 2015
swa: Badala yake wanafanya kazi za Serikali -kujenga shule, kununua madawa - Matembe

eng: Daniel Turitwenka, a social media consultant, shared a photo of a participant in Gulu, northern Uganda, in a live phone conversation during the chat:
swa: Daniel Turitwenka, mshauri mwelekezi wa mitandao ya kijamii, aliweka picha ya mshiriki wa Gulu, kaskazini mwa Uganda, akishiriki moja kwa moja kwa njia ya simu wakati wa mjadala huo:

eng: #Gulu had a live phone conversation with @UWOPA chair Betty Amongi - answering and directly #MPsEngage pic.twitter.com/R5IvjNyy46 — Danny T (@DannyT_UG) February 26, 2015
swa: Wakazi wa Gulu walikuwa na majadiliano ya moja kwa moja kwa njia ya simu na Mwenyekiti wa Asasi ya UWOPA, Betty Among - maswali yalijibiwa na moja kwa moja

eng: He quoted one of the participants:
swa: Alimnukuu mmoja wa washiriki:

eng: #Gulu Mr Okello says separation of children and parents is an issue and urges @pwatchug to keep bringing the MPs to answer qns #MPsEngage — Danny T (@DannyT_UG) February 26, 2015
swa: Bw Okello anasema kutengana kwa watoto na wazazi ni suala gumu na aliwasihi @pwatchug kuendelea kuwaleta wabunge wajibu maswali

eng: Gulu residents made their needs known:
swa: Wakazi wa Gulu walijitahidi kufanya mahitaji yao yafahamike:

eng: #Gulu everyone should have access to reproductive health. still a lot of women lack this! #MPsEngage pic.twitter.com/DzYSvJNHyj — Parliament Watch (@pwatchug) February 26, 2015
swa: Hapa Gulu kila mmoja lazima apate huduma za afya ya uzazi. Bado wanawake wengi hawana huduma hizi

eng: They decried poor service delivery:
swa: Suala la huduma duni za ukunga lililalamikiwa:

eng: #Gulu "our women die every day and night because of lack of midwives!
swa: Wanawake wetu wengi wanapoteza maisha mchana na usiku kwa sababu ya kukosekana kwa wakunga!

eng: Although the chat took place on Twitter, Denis R Tumusiime noted that female MPs have not yet embraced social media:
swa: Ingawa mazungumzo hayo yalifanyika kwenye mtandao wa Twita, Denis R Tumusiime alibaini kwamba wabunge wanawake bado hawajaweza kutumia vizuri mitandao ya kijamii kufanya shughuli zao:

eng: @deejahn @she_infinite I am yet to see a tweet from a female mp. #MPsEngage — Dennis R. Tusiime (@drwatooro) February 26, 2015
swa: Bado sijaona twiti kutoka kwa mbunge mwanamke

eng: As the debate drew to a close, Jackie Asiimwe, the lawyer, noted that engagement should not be a one-off:
swa: Wakati mjadala huo ukielekea ukingoni, Jackie Asiimwe, ambaye ni mwanasheria, alishauri kwamba ushiriki huo usiishie hapo:

eng: Our time here is coming to an end, but the conversation continues.
swa: Muda wetu unakaribia kuisha, lakini mazungumzo yaendelee.

eng: We must all engage our MPs all the time. #MPsEngage — Jacqueline Asiimwe (@asiimwe4justice) February 26, 2015
swa: Lazima tuwasiliane na wabunge wetu muda wote

eng: Uganda's president Yoweri Museveni.
swa: Rais wa Uganda Yoweri Museveni.

eng: Photo released under Creative Commons by Russell Watkins/Department for International Development UK).
swa: Picha imetolewa chini ya leseni ya Creative Commons na Russell Watkins/Idara ya Maendeleo ya Kimataifa Uingereza).

eng: Seventy percent of Ugandans are under the age of 29.
swa: Asilimia sabini ya wa-Ganda wana umri chini ya miaka 29.

eng: That means they have seen only one president since they were born.
swa: Ndio kusema tangu wazaliwe wamemwona rais mmoja tu.

eng: On 26 January, 2015, Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni and his National Resistance Movement (NRM) celebrated 29 years in power.
swa: Januari 26, 2015, Rais wa Uganda Yoweri Museveni na chama chake cha National Resistance Movement (NRM) walisherehekea miaka 29 madarakani.

eng: This day was set apart as the liberation day to mark the day NRM took over power after a five-year armed struggle against repressive governments.
swa: Siku hiyo imetengwa kuwa siku ya ukombozi kuadhimisha siku ambayo chama cha NRM kilitwaa madaraka baada ya mapambano ya miaka mitano msituni kuiondoa serikali kandamizi madarakani.

eng: President Museveni is already seeking a sixth presidential term.
swa: Rais Museveni tayari anatafuta kuchaguliwa kwa kipindi cha sita cha Urais.

eng: Billboards erected by his party supporting his intention to continue ruling the country are all over the capital city Kampala.
swa: Mabango yaliyotengenezwa na chama chake kuunga mkono nia yake ya kuendelea kuitawala nchi hiyo yameenea kwenye jiji la Kampala, makao makuu ya nchi hiyo.

eng: To gather public support for his intention to run again, Museveni has been seen handing out brown envelopes of money to poor people during public gatherings, something he has also done in the past.
swa: Ili adhima yake hiyo iungwe mkono na wananchi, Museveni amekuwa akionekana hadharani akikabidhi bahasha za kaki zenye pesa kwa raia maskini awapo kwenye mikusanyiko ya watu. Amekuwa na mazoea hayo hata siku za nyuma.

eng: He has come under public criticism for treating the national treasury as his Automatic Teller Machine (ATM).
swa: Hata hivyp, amekosolewa na wananchi kwa kuifanya hazina ya nchi hiyo kama Mashine binafsi ya Kutoa Fedha (ATM).

eng: For many Ugandans, the celebration of the liberation day was a moment to take stock of the governance of the NRM and the promises the the NRM made when they came into power.
swa: Kwa wa-Ganda wengi, sherehe za siku ya ukombozi ulikuwa ni wakati wa kutathimini utawala wa NRM na ahadi zake ambazo chama hicho kilizitoa kilipokuwa kinaingia madarakani.

eng: George Ayittey, a Ghanaian economics professor and president of Free Africa Foundation in Washington, DC, reminded the rest of the world what Museveni said when he became president of Uganda in 1986:
swa: George Ayittey, prefesa wa uchumi wa Ghana na rais wa Mfuko wa Uhuru wa Afrika (FAF) jijini Washington, DC, aliukumbusha ulimwengu kile ambacho Museveni alikisema mwaka 1986 alipokuwa rais wa Uganda:

eng: In 1986, President Museveni told us, "No African president should be power for more than 10 years."
swa: Mwaka 1986, Rais Museveni alituambia, "Hakuna Rais wa Afrika anapaswa kubaki madarakani kwa zaidi ya miaka kumi."

eng: He himself is still there 29 years later — George Ayittey (@ayittey) January 4, 2015
swa: Yeye mwenyewe bado yuko madarakani kwa miaka 29 baadae

eng: Ugandan journalist Benjamin Rukwenge is tired of Twitter users complaining instead of doing something about the situation:
swa: Mwandishi wa Uganda, Benjamin Rukwenge amechoshwa na watumiaji wa mtandao wa Twita wanaolalamika badala ya kuchukua hatua kukabili hali hiyo:

eng: Whatever your sentiments, you can't argue with history. #NRM has lots of +ves to its 29yrs.
swa: Haijalishi hisia zako zikoje, huwezi kupambana na historia.

eng: While Edgar Mwine, an unemployed graduate of economics, quoted lawyer, policy analyst and social entrepreneur Godber Tumushabe:
swa: Wakati Edgar Mwine, mhitimu wa uchumi asiye na ajira, alimnukuu mwanasheria, mchambuzi wa sera na mjasiria mali wa kijamii Godber Tumushabe:

eng: It's insulting to the intelligence of Ugandans to say that 29 years of Museveni Rule is a success @godbertumushabe #HotSeat — Mwine (@mwineedgar) January 28, 2015
swa:
Ni kutukana akili za wa-Ganda kusema kwamba miaka 29 ya utawala wa Museveni ni mafanikio
Museveni said in a speech that he said he will never give power to the opposition, whom he called wolves, because he has the support of the army. 	Museveni alisema kwenye hotuba yake kwamba kamwe hataachia madaraka kwa upinzani, anaouita mbwa mwitu, kwa sababu anaungwa mkono na jeshi.
Commenting on an article about the speech on the Daily Monitor website, Kabindist" wrote:
column3: Akitoa maoni kuhusu hotuba hiyo kwenye tovuti ya Daily Monitor website, "Kabindist" aliandika:

eng: So its official.There is no democracy in Uganda.Its about Museveni and his Army.So,all these years when he said he needed more time to professionalize the Army,he meant brain wash it to do his bidding.Term limits,age limits and all the above are but play things for Kaguta.He believes his day will not come.With his NRM wolves the country is already torn apart and like a greedy wolf he wont let go.Who is he lying to?
swa: Museveni na Jeshi lake ndio kila kitu. Kw ahiyo, miaka yote hii aliposema alihitaji muda zaidi kulifanya jeshi liwe la kisasa, alimaanisha kulipumbaza akili lifanye anachotaka yeye. Ukomo wa madaraka, ukomo wa umri na yote hayo yapo lakini ni kama mchezo tu kwa Kaguta.

eng: Commenting on the same story, Bishanga Paul warned Museveni:
swa: Akitoa maoni kwenye makala hiyo hiyo, Bishanga Paul alimuonya Museveni:

eng: Gadafi had a strong Army and was csupported by the people who later got disgusted and dragged him through the city to see him off the country of Libya forever.
swa: Gadafi alikuwa na Jeshi imara na aliungwa mkono na watu ambao baadae walichoshwa na kumfukuza jijini kuhakikisha hatawali nchi hiyo milele.

eng: And to drive the point home, the Daily Monitor illustrated:
swa: Na ili kuihusisha hoja hiyo na hali ya mambo nchini, Daily Monitor lilionesha kwa mchoro:

eng: CARTOON: Today, marks 29 years since the NRM assumed power. @chrisatuk #NRM29 pic.twitter.com/Kf2ivmpDzz — Daily Monitor (@DailyMonitor) January 26, 2015
swa: KATUNI: Leo tunatimiza miaka 29 tangu NRM itwae madaraka

eng: In his criticism of Museveni, Charles Onyango Obbo, Mail & Guardian Africa editor, compared Museveni to Lords Resistance Army leader Joseph Kony:
swa: Akimkosoa Museveni, Charles Onyango Obbo, mhariri wa Mail & Guardian Africa, alimfananisha Museveni na kiongozi wa waasi wa Lords Resistance Army Joseph Kony:

eng: To begin with, Kony and Museveni are the longest serving post-1986 leaders of their respective organisations.
swa: Kwa kuanzia, Kony na Museveni ni viongozi waliotawala kwa muda mrefu baada ya mwaka 1986 taasisi zao.

eng: Counting from when he came to power, Museveni has been leader of NRM, president and commander-in-chief for 29 years.
swa: Kwa kuhesabu kuanzia alipochukua madaraka, Museveni amekuwa kiongozi wa NRM, rais na amiri jeshi mkuu kwa miaka 29.

eng: Kony effectively became leader of the LRA in 1988, after cobbling it together from the remnants and other dregs of Alice Lakwena’s defeated Holy Spirit Movement.
swa: Kony alikuwa kiongozi rasmi wa waasi wa LRA mwaka 1988, baada ya kuwaunganisha masalia ya chama kilichokufa cha Alice Lakwena kiitwacho Holy Spirit Movement.

eng: Kony has, therefore, led LRA for 26 years, the only rebel leader of the Museveni era who comes close to The Chief.
swa: Kony, kwa hiyo, ameiongoza LRA kwa miaka 26, kiongozi pekee wa waasi katika kipindi cha Museveni anayemkaribia Chifu mwenyewe (Museveni).

eng: When it comes to military and political survival, therefore, Museveni and Kony are in a class of their own.
swa: Linapokuja suala la kudumu jeshini na kisiasa, kwa hiyo, Museveni na Kony wako kwenye kundi la aina yake.

eng: I think Museveni will outlast Kony, but strange things happen in our neck of the woods so I wouldn’t place a bet on it.
swa: Ninadhani Museveni atadumu zaidi ya Kony, lakini wakati mwingine mambo yasiyo ya kawaida hutokea kwenye maisha haya yasiyotabirika kwa hiyo sitajiapiza kwa hilo.

eng: In December last year, the Daily Monitor quoted Museveni saying that Ugandans do not want him to leave.
swa: Mwezi Desemba mwaka jana, jarida laDaily Monitor lilimnukuu Museveni akisema kwamba wa-Ganda hawataki aondoke madarakani.

eng: He blamed his clinging to power to Ugandans who keeps re-electing him.
swa: Aliwabebesha lawama wa-Ganda kwa kuendelea kumchagua na hivyo kumfanya abaki madarakani.

eng: Northern Cameroon border, where Boko Haram operates
swa: Mpaka wa Cameroon Kaskazini, ambako where Boko Haram hufanya kazi zao

eng: On February 4, Boko Haram conducted a particularly gruesome attack on the town of Fotokol in Northern Cameroon, right across the Nigerian border.
swa: Mnamo Februari 4, Boko Haram walifanya shambulio baya kwenye mji wa Fotokol Kaskazini mwa Cameroon, baada tu ya kuvuka mpaka wa Naijeria.

eng: Hundred of civilians are feared dead, 81 confirmed so far by the Minister of Defense.
swa: Mamia wa raia wanahofiwa kupoteza maisha 81 wamethibitika kufa na Wizara ya Ulinzi.

eng: Local Human Rights Organization believes that close to 370 civilians were killed.
swa: Shirika la Haki za Binadamu nchini humo linaamini kwamba karibu watu 370 wameuawa.

eng: Local testimonies mention scores of bodies in the streets with their throats slit.
swa: Mashuhuda wa tukio hilo wanasema kwamba miili kadhaa ilipatikana kwenye mitaa ikiwa imechinjwa makoromeo.

eng: The town of Fotokol has been subjected to battles between Boko Haram and Camerronian and Chadian armed forces recently: March 2014, August 2014 and October 2014.
swa: Mji wa Fotokol umekuwa ukikabiliwa na vita kati ya Boko Haram na majeshi ya Cameroon na Chadi kwa siku za hivi karibuni: Machi 2014, Agosti 2014 na Oktoba 2014.

eng: Cameroonian Blogger Noelle Lafortune reports that the attack signals that Boko Haram might be losing ground in the region:
swa: Mwanablogu wa Cameroon Noelle Lafortune anaripoti kwamba shambulio hilo linaonesha kwamba Boko Haram inaweza kuwa inaanza kupoteza nguvu katika eneo hilo:

eng: On the frontline, doubt might be switching sides.
swa: Kwenye mstari wa mbele, wasiwasi unakumba pande zote.

eng: The emergence of the Chadian army in support of the Cameroonian and Nigerian military appears to be decisive, given the panic moves that has seemingly gripped Boko Haram.
swa: Kujitokeza kwa jeshi la Chadi uunganisha nguvu na majeshi ya Camerron na Naijeria kuonekana kuwa na maamuzi sasa, imeleta hali ya tahayaruki kwa kikundi hicho cha kigaidi cha Boko Haram.

eng: The firepower of the coalition forces routed Shekau (head of Boko Haram) and his gang.
swa: Mapigano ya majeshi hayo ya pamoja yalimng'oa Shekau (kiongozi wa Boko Haram) na genge lake.

eng: I hope you realize that if they deploy the fried mozzarella cheese sticks, I'm switching teams. tweeted by Twitter user @LibyaLiberty
swa: Ninatumaini unajua kwamba kama wanapanga mishikaki ya siagi za kukaanga, ninabadili washirika. anatwiti mtumiaji wa mtandao wa twita @LibyaLiberty

eng: This week The Intercept revealed a rating system that the US government encourages social workers, teachers and law enforcement workers to use to detect potential terrorists.
swa: Juma hili, The Intercept ilibaini mfumo wa maswali kwamba serikali ya Marekani inawahamasisha watu wa ustawi wa jamii, walimu na polisi kutumia maswali fulani fulani ili kuwabaini magaidi.

eng: The ranking system is "supposed to alert US government officials to individuals at risk of turning to radical violence, and to families or communities at risk of incubating extremist ideologies."
swa: Mfumo huo unatarajiwa "kuwaweka maafisa wa serikali ya Marekani katika hali ya tahadhari kwa watu wenye hatari ya kugeuka kuwa watu wa ghasia, na familia au jamii zilizo kwenye uwezekano wa kukumbatia itikadi za kikaidi."

eng: The system detailed in a 36-page internal government document obtained by the digital magazine was put together by the National Counterterrorism Center and is part of a wider government strategy for Countering Violent Extremism, which calls for local community and religious leaders to work together with law enforcement and government agencies.
swa: Maswali hayo yaliyochambuliwa kwenye karabrasha la ndani ya serikali lenye kurasa 36 lilipatikana kupitia jarida moja la mtandaoni na lilipangiliwa na Kituo cha Taifa cha Kupambana na Ugaidi ni sehemu ya mkakati mpana wa serikali wa Kupambana na Itikadi Kali, unatoa mwito kwa jamii na viongozi wa dini wa kila mahali kufanya kazi na mashirika ya kiserikali na kusimamia sheria .

eng: The White House is currently hosting an international 3-day summit on Countering Violent Extremism with representatives from over 60 countries.
swa: Ikulu ya Marekani hivi sasa ni mwenyeji wa mkutano wa kimataifa wa siku tatu kuhusu Kupambana na Itikadi kali ukiwa na wawakilishi kutoka kwenye nchi zaidi ya 60.

eng: Under categories like “Expressions of Hopelessness, Futility,” “Talk of Harming Self or Others,” and “Connection to Group Identity (Race, Nationality, Religion, Ethnicity)," the ranking system asks teachers, social workers and police officers to rank individuals from 1 to 5.
swa: Kwenye kipengele kama "Kuonesha Kukata tamaa, Kutokujiamini," "Kuzungumizia Kujidhuru au Kuwadhuru wengine," na "Kujitambulisha na Makundi (Rangi, Utaifa, Dini, Kabila)," maswali hayo yanawaomba walimu, ustawi wa jamii na maafisa wa polisi kuwapa alama watu kati za 1 na 5.

eng: While reading the document at Global Voices, we couldn't help but laugh out loud because of the reductive approach of the survey.
swa: Wakati tukizoma karabrasha hilo, hatukujizuia isipokuwa kucheka kwa sauti kwa sababu ya mtindo wa kupunguza mambo unaotumika kwenye utafiti huo.

eng: We decided to make our own quiz based on the simplistic assumptions the National Counterterrorism Center made, in its ranking system.
swa: Tuliamua kutengeneza chemsha bongo yetu wenyewe kwa kutumia bashiri nyepesi zilizofanywa na Kituo cha Taifa cha Kupambana na Ugaidi kwenye kutunga maswali yake.

eng: Take our satirical quiz.
swa: Shiriki Chemshabongo yetu ya Kukuchekesha.

eng: This Quiz was created by Taisa Sganzerla, Elizabeth Rivera, Amira Alhussaini and Sahar Habib Ghazi.
swa: Chemshabongo hii imeandaliwa na Taisa Sganzerla, Elizabeth Rivera, Amira Alhussaini naSahar Habib Ghazi.

eng: The Art of Ama Ata Aidoo is a film by filmmaker Yaba Badoe:
swa: The Art of Ama Ata Aidoo ni filamu iliyotayarishwa na mtayarishaji wa filamu Yaba Badoe:

eng: The Art of Ama Ata Aidoo, explores the artistic contribution of one of Africa's foremost women writers, a trailblazer for an entire generation of exciting new talent.
swa: The Art of Ama Ata Aidoo, inasaili mchango wa kisanii wa mmoja wa waandishi wanawake mashuhuri barani Afrika, anayeongoza kizazi hiki kwa kipaji kipya cha pekee.

eng: This feature-length documentary charts Ama Ata Aidoo's creative journey in a life that spans 7 decades from colonial Ghana, through the tumultuous era of independence, to a more sober present day Africa where nurturing women's creative talent remains as hard as ever.
swa: Dokumentari hii inasaili safari ya ubunifu ya Ama Ata Aidoo ya miongo saba kuanzia enzi za Ghana inayotawaliwa na wakoloni, kupitia nyakati za uhuru, mpaka Afrika ya leo ambako ubunifu wa vipaji vya wanawake hauonekani kiwepesi.

eng: The Art of Ama Ata Aidoo (Teaser) from Big Heart Media on Vimeo.
swa: The Art of Ama Ata Aidoo (Teaser) from Big Heart Media kwenye mtandao wa Vimeo.

eng: Yemen is in political limbo, without a president and government, since the Houthi militias took over government institutions and the presidential palace in capital city Sanaa.
swa: Yemen iko kwenye mzozo wa kisiasa, bila kuwa na rais wala serikali, tangu waasi wa Houthi kuangusha taasisi za kiserikali na kuteka ikulu kwenye mji mkuu wa Sanaa.

eng: On February 8, they released a document with a Ministry of Interior logo banning all protests in Yemen.
swa: Februari 8, waasi hao walitoa waraka kupitia Wizara ya Mambo ya ndani kupiga marufuku maandamano yoyote nchini Yemen.

eng: New decisions at Houthi-land: Protests are no longer allowed #Yemen welcome to the new democracy pic.twitter.com/mNi7HfWKSU — Baraa Shiban (@BShtwtr) February 9, 2015
swa: Maamuzi ya nchi ya Hauthi: Maandamano hayaruhusiwi tena nchini Yemen. Karibu kwenye demokrasia mpya

eng: With the announcement of the "Constitutional Declaration" by the Houthis, a new power shift is taking place.
swa: Kwa tangazo la "Azimio la Kikatiba" lilifanywa na wanamgambo hao wa Houthi, mabadiliko mapya ya kimadaraka yanatokea.

eng: What do Yemenis think?
swa: Wa-Yemeni wanafikiri nini?

eng: How do they perceive the transitional period under Houthis rule and what are their main concerns?
swa: Wanakielewaje kipindi hiki cha mpito chini ya utawala wa wanamgambo wa Houthi na yepi ni matatizo yao makubwa?

eng: We speak to activists from Yemen Baraa Shiban (@BShtwtr), Osama Abdullah (@PoliticsYemen), and @NoonArabia in this episode of GVFace.
swa: Tunaongea na wanaharakati kutoka Yemen We Baraa Shiban (@BShtwtr), Osama Abdullah (@PoliticsYemen), na@NoonArabia kwenye toleo hili la GVFace.

eng: Amira Alhussaini, our MENA editor, moderated the discussion along with me.
swa: Amira Alhussaini, mhariri wetu wa Afrika Kaskazini na Uarabuni, aliongoza majadiliano hayo akiwa nami.

eng: Many apologies for some of the technical and audio trouble we had in this Hangout.
swa: Tunasikitika kwa matatizo kadhaa ya kiteknolojia na usikivu usioridhisha wa sauti kwenye mazungumzo haya.

eng: Houthi activist Hussaini Bukhaiti (@HussainBukhaiti) was supposed to join us as well.
swa: Mwanaharakati wa Houthi Hussaini Bukhaiti (@HussainBukhaiti) alipaswa kuungana nasi pia.

eng: We have invited Bukhaiti, Osama and Baraa to write pieces on Global Voices to help us dig deeper into the issues that Yemen faces and their hope for the future.
swa: Tulimkaribisha Bukhaiti, Osama na Baraa kuandika kwenye tovuti ya Global Voices kutusaidia kuelewa undani wa masuala yanayoikabili Yemen na matumaini yaliyopo kwa siku za usoni.

eng: Déjà Vu?
swa: Hofu ya Yaliyotokea?

eng: President Edgar Lungu on a helicopter ride viewing the South Luangwa National Park during a holiday he took two weeks into office.
swa: Rais Edgar Lungu akiwa kwenye helikopta akiangalia Hifadhi ya Wanyama ya Luangwa Kusini wakati wa likizo yake aliyoichukua majuma mawili tu baada ya kushika madaraka.

eng: Picture used with permission of Salim Henry/SHENPA.
swa: Picha imetumiwa kwa ruhusa ya Salim Henry/SHENPA.

eng: Just after winning the election to replace Sata, Lungu underwent medical tests at Lusaka Trust Hospital and Maina Soko Military Hospital, both of which are within a short distance from the presidential palace in the Woodlands district of the capital city.
swa: Kabla ya kushinda uchaguzi na kumrithi Sata, Lungu alifanya uchunguzi wa afya kwenye hospitali ya Lusaka Trust pamoja na Hospitali ya Kijeshi ya Maina Soko, zote zikiwa umbali mdogo tu kutoka yalipo makazi ya rais, ikulu, wilaya ya Woodlands jijini Lusaka.

eng: Departing from his predecessor’s practice of not announcing his health-related matters, Lungu’s press aide Amos Chanda said in a statement:
swa: Akijaribu kuachana na utaratibu wa mtangulizi wake wa kuficha taarifa zake zinazohusiana na afya, msaidizi wake wa habari Amos Chanda alisema kwenye taarifa yake:

eng: His Excellency Mr. Edgar Chagwa Lungu, President of the Republic of Zambia has today undergone two medical examinations at Maina Soko Military Hospital and Lusaka Trust Hospital respectively.
swa: Mheshimiwa Edgar Chagwa Lungu, Rais wa Jamhuri ya Zambia amechunguzwa afya yake mara mbili kwenye Hospitali ya Kijeshi ya Maina Soko na Hospitali ya Lusaka Trust.

eng: President Lungu undertook a Baseline Health Parameters routine check-up at Maina Soko and attended the dentistry at Lusaka Trust Hospital.
swa: Rais Lungu alifanyiwa uchunguzi wa kina kwenye Hospitali ya Maina Soko na kisha kuchunguzwa kinywa kwenye Hospitali ya Lusaka Trust.

eng: Doctors have given him a clean bill of health.
swa: Madaktari wamemthibitishia kwamba afya yake iko imara.

eng: Nevertheless, his holiday, which began after his first international assignment on a trip to the African Union (AU) summit in the Ethiopian capital, Addis Ababa, raised eyebrows.
swa: Hata hivyo, likizo yake hiyo, iliyoanza baada ya shughuli yake ya kwanza kimataifa ya kuhudhuria Mkutano wa Umoja wa Afrika (AU) Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, iliwastua watu.

eng: Lawyer-turned-politician Lungu, who went to the South Luangwa National Park, one of Zambia’s prime tourist destinations, had not finished picking his Cabinet at the time.
swa: Lungu, mwanasiasa ambaye kitaaluma ni mwanasheria, alikwenda kwenye hifadhi ya wanyama za Luangwa Kusini, moja wapo ya vivutio vikuu vya watalii nchini Zambia, akiwa hata hajamaliza kuteua Baraza lake la Mawaziri wakati huo.

eng: President Lungu, quoted in The Post, defended his decision to go on what he called a retreat:
swa: Rais Lungu, alinukuliwa na jarida la The Post, akitetea uamuzi wake wa kwenda kwenye kile alichokiita mapumziko :

eng: I told you that I will have no honeymoon.
swa: Nimekwambia kwamba sitakuwa na siku za fungate.

eng: There is a difference between a holiday and a retreat, I was looking at the dictionary this morning and I said, ‘do these people know?’
swa: Kuna tofauti kati ya likizo na mapumziko, nilikuwa nachungulia kamusi yangu asubuhi hii na ninajiuliza, 'hawa watu wanajua tofauti hii?'

eng: I am going for a retreat, I am not on holiday.
swa: Ninaenda mapumzikono, sina likizo.

eng: You don’t go on holiday with the full complement of office staff.
swa: Huendi likizo ukiwa umeambatana na watumishi wote wa ofisi yako.

eng: The Secretary to the Cabinet is going and some of my ministers and State House officials are not going to nurse me, but help me think through the appointments I am making.
swa: Katibu wa Baraza la Mawaziri naye anaambatana na mimi na hata baadhi ya Mawaziri na maafisa wa ikulu hawaendi kuniliwaza, ila kunisaidia kufikiri uteuzi ninaoufanya.

eng: He added:
swa: Aliongeza:

eng: I know my priorities; some cheeky fellows are saying ‘Lungu doesn’t know his priorities’.
swa: Ninavijua vipaumbele vyangu; baadhi ya watu wanasema, 'Lungu hajui vipaumbele vyake'.

eng: My priority is the people of Zambia.
swa: Kipaumbele changu ni watu wa Zambia.

eng: How I treat my work is not anybody’s prerogative, it is mine.
swa: Namna gani ninafanya kazi yangu si shughuli ya mtu mwingine yeyote kujua, ni yangu.

eng: In the run-up to the January 20 election, Opposition United Party for National Development Vice President Canicius Banda, a medical doctor, said that the burden of proof lay with ruling Patriotic Front President Lungu to convince the nation that he was well because a medical report his party had seen indicated that the now head of state allegedly suffered from a kidney problem.
swa: Wakati wa kuelekea kwenye uchaguzi wa Januari 20, Makamu wa Rais wa Chama cha Upinzani cha UPND, Canicius Banda, daktari wa tiba, alisema chama kinachotawala cha PF anakotoka Rais Lungu kina kazi ya kulishawishi taifa kwamba hana matatizo ya kiafya kwa sababu cheti cha uchunguzi wa afya ambacho chama chake kimekiona kinaonesha kwamba mkuu huyo wa sasa wa nchi anaugua maradhi ya figo.

eng: Banda later recanted his claim about seeing Lungu’s medical report.
swa: Banda baadaealikanusha madai yake kwamba aliona cheti cha uchunguzi wa afya ya Lungu.

eng: Blogger Elias Munshya Munshya, in response to Banda’s claims of having seen Lungu’s medical report, wrote:
swa: Mwanablogu Elias Munshya Munshya, alijibu madai ya Banda kwamba aliona cheti cha uchunguzi wa afya ya Lungu aliandika:

eng: I do see why some Zambians should be concerned about the health of presidential candidates.
swa: Ninaweza kuona kwa nini baadhi ya Wazambia wana sababu ya kuwa na wasiwasi na afya ya wagombea urais.

eng: But demanding medicals for candidates is as ridiculous as demanding that candidates be of a certain level of education.
swa: Lakini kudai tarifa za kiafya za wagonbea ni upuuzi kama ilivyo kutaka wagombea wawe na kiwango fulani cha elimu.

eng: If indeed we should be caring about medical reports, then the next questions to deal with would be: where are we going to draw the line?
swa: Kama tunahitaji kweli kujali vyeti vya uchunguzi wa afya, basi maswali yanayofuata yanayohitaji majibu: tutaishia wapi?

eng: Does evidence of a disease of the lung affect a person’s ability to rule?
swa: Hivi ushahidi kwamba mtu anaugua maradhi ya mapafu unaatiri uwezo wake kutawala?

eng: This is why our constitution only states that one should not lead if they are “incapacitated”.
swa: Hii ndio sababu katiba yetu inataka tu kwamba mtu hawezi kutawala kama 'hali yake ni mbaya'.

eng: It does not say that one must not rule if they are sick, for such a requirement would be impossible to meet by mere mortals.
swa: Haisemi kwamba mtu hatatawala kwa sababu tu ni mgonjwa, kwa sababu kusema hivyo kusingetekelezeka. .

eng: It is understandable why Zambians are concerned with the health of their presidents or those aspiring to be presidents.
swa: Inaeleweka kwa nini Wazambia wana wasiwasi na afya ya marais wao au wale wanaotaka kuwa marais.

eng: Former President Frederick Chiluba, who served as the country's second president, died in Zambia following a series of trips to South Africa for treatment and check-ups for heart-related complications.
swa: Rais wa zamani Frederick Chiluba, rais wa pili kutawala nchi hiyo, alifariki nchini Zambia baada ya safari nyingi kwenda Afrika Kusini kwa matibabu na uchunguzi wa afya kwa matatizo yanayohusiana na moyo.

eng: Lungu beat 10 other candidates, scraping by just 1.66 per cent over the nearest rival, opposition UPND’s Hakainde Hichilema, to become Zambia’s sixth president since independence from Britain in 1964.
swa: Lungu aliwashinda wagombea wengine 10, akishinda kwa asilimia 1.66 mbele ya mpinzani wake mkuu, Hakainde Hichilema wa chama cha Upinzani cha UPND, na kuwa Rais wa sita wa Zambia tangu uhuru kutoka kwa Uingereza mwaka 1964.

eng: The main opposition candidate General (Rtd) Muhammadu Buhari speaking at African Diaspora Conference in London.
swa: Mgombea Urais wa upinzani, Jenerali (Mstaafu) Muhammadu Buhari akiongea kwenye Kongamano la Raia wa Afrika wanaoishi Ughaibuni lililofanyika katika jiji la London.

eng: Some political observers believe that the postponement is a political strategy meant to favour the ruling party.
swa: Baadhi ya wafuatiliaji wa masuala ya kisiasa wanaamini kuwa kuahirishwa kwa uchaguzi ni mbinu za kisiasa zilizo na lengo la kukipendelea chama tawala.

eng: Photo by Michael Tubi, copyright © Demotix (5 April, 2013)
swa: Picha na Michael Tubi, copyright © Demotix (5 April, 2013)

eng: The Nigerian Independent National Election Commission (INEC) announced on February 7, 2015, that presidential election due on February 14 would be pushed back by six weeks because of security concerns in areas held by militant group Boko Haram.
swa: Tume huru ya uchaguzi ya Nigeria (INEC) mnamo tarehe 7 Januari, 2015 ilitangaza kuwa, uchaguzi mkuu uliopangwa kufanyika tarehe 14 Februari ungesogezwa mbele kwa muda wa wiki sita kwa sababu ya masuala ya kiusalama hususani katika maeneo yanayoshikiliwa na wanamgambo wa kundi la Boko Haram.

eng: The group has increased its campaign of violence in northern Nigeria.
swa: Kundi la Boko Haram linaendeleza harakati zake za machafuko Kaskazini mwa Nigeria.

eng: Recently, it conducted what Amnesty International described as the group’s “deadliest massacre in recent history” in Baga, a town in the north-eastern state of Borno.
swa: Siku za hivi karibuni, kundi la Boko Haram lilitekeleza kile kinachoelezewa na shirika la kutetea haki za binadamu, Amnesty International, kuwa ni "moja ya mauaji ya halaiki ambayo hayakuwahi kufanywa na kundi hili" katika mji wa Baga ulio Kaskazini Mashariki mwa Jiji la Borno.

eng: The chairman of the election commission Attahiru Jega said that security forces would be conducting a six-week special operation against Boko Haram so "they would rather not be distracted by the elections." The government has vowed to finish off the group in six weeks.
swa: Mwenyekiti wa tume ya uchaguzi, Attahiru Jega alisema kuwa jeshi litaendesha operesheni ya wiki sita dhidi ya Boko Haram ili "kuepusha kuingiliwa na masuala ya uchaguzi" Serikaliimejinadi kulifutilia mbali kundi hili ndani ya wiki sita.

eng: This is the first time in Nigeria’s history that the presidential election is being postponed.
swa: Katika historia ya Naijeria, hii ni mara ya kwanza kwa uchaguzi mkuu wa Rais kuahirishwa.

eng: However, this is not the first time a national election will postponed in Nigeria.
swa: Hata hivyo, hii haitakuwa mara ya kwanza kwa uchaguzi wa Kitaifa kuahirishwa nchini Nigeria.

eng: In 2011, we reported the reaction of Nigerian netizens to the rescheduling of the national parliamentary elections.
swa: Mwaka 2011, tulitaarifu kuhusu malalamiko ya watumiaji wa Mtandao wa intaneti wa Nigeria kuhusiana na mabadiliko ya tarehe za chaguzi za Taifa za kibunge.

eng: Since the announcement, there has been many speculations as to the real reasons for the postponement.
swa: Tangu kutangazwa kuahirishwa kwa uchaguzi, kumekuwa na ufuatiliaji wa karibu wa kutaka kujua hasa sababu za msingi zilizopekea kuahirishwa kwa uchaguzi mkuu wa Rais.

eng: For example, 'Gbénga Sèsan, the director for Paradigm Initiative Nigeria, thinks that the electoral commission was forced to postpone the election:
swa: Kwa mfano, 'Gbénga Sèsan, mkurugenzi wa Paradigm Initiative Nigeria, anafikiri kuwa tume ya uchaguzi ilishinikizwa kuahirisha uchaguzi:

eng: It is clear that this postponement decision, by @inecnigeria, was forced.
swa: Ni dhahiri kuwa uamuzi huu wa kuahirisha uchaguzi na @inecnigeria, ulilazimishwa.

eng: This has a lot of implications regarding #NigeriaDecides — 'Gbénga Sèsan (@gbengasesan) February 7, 2015
swa: Hili lina matazamio makubwa ikizingatiwa #NigeriaDecides — 'Gbénga Sèsan (@gbengasesan) February 7, 2015

eng: Henrik Angerbrandt, a PhD candidate in political science and researcher at the Nordic Africa Institute, believes the postponement has more to do with politics than security.
swa: Henrik Angerbrandt, ambaye ni mwanafunzi wa Shahada ya uzamivu (PhD) katika masuala ya Sayansi ya Siasa na mtafiti katika taasisi ya Nordic Africa, anaamini kuwa kuahirishwa huku kwa uchaguzi kumechagizwa na sababu za kisiasa zaidi kuliko za kiusalama.

eng: He wonders why the offensive against an insurgency that has lasted for six years coincides with the date of the presidential election.
swa: Anashangaa ni kwa nini operesheni dhidi ya magaidi hawa waliokuwepo kwa miaka sita sasa inafanyika katika kipindi cha tarehe za uchaguzi wa Rais.

eng: Less than three weeks ago, the national security advisor to the president called for the elections to be postponed.
swa: Takribani wiki tatu zilizopita, mshauri wa Rais wa masuala ya usalama wa taifa alipendekeza kuahirishwa kwa uchaguzi.

eng: However, this was not because the security agents were unprepared but because of slow distribution of voters’ cards.
swa: Hata hivyo, uamuzi huu haukutokana na sababu kuwa, vyombo vya usalama havikuwa vimejiandaa, lakini ni kwa sababu ya usambazaji wa polepole wa kadi za wapiga kura.

eng: INEC, the responsible authority, replied there was no reason for postponement.
swa: Tume ya Taifa ya Uchaguzi (INEC), ambayo ndiyo mamlaka husika, ilitoa taarifa yake kuwa hakukuwa na sababu ya kuahirishwa kwa uchaguzi.

eng: Hence, it looks like a last resort has been to return to the security argument, first articulated in September by the PDP Senate President.
swa: Hivyo, inaonekana kuwa, kilichosalia ilikuwa ni kurejea kwenye kigezo cha masuala ya usalama ambacho, hapo awali, mwezi Septemba kilitolewa ufafanuzi na mwenyekiti wa Seneti ya Chama cha PDP.

eng: There are different theories on what PDP benefits from the postponement.
swa: Kuna nadharia tofauti za namna ambavyo chama tawala cha PDP kinavyofaidika na kuahirishwa kwa uchaguzi wa Rais.

eng: As the election has come closer, opinion polls have shown growing dissatisfaction with Jonathan’s government and Buhari has emerged as a possible winner of the election.
swa: Kadiri siku za kupiga kura zilivyokaribia, kura za maoni zimeonesha ongezeko la wananchi waliokosa imani na sserikali ya Rais Goodluck Jonathan na hivyo Mwanajeshi mstaafu Muhamudu Buhari ameonekana kuwa anaweza kushinda kwenye uchaguzi huo.

eng: A postponement would provide an opportunity for Jonathan to recover some lost grounds.
swa: Kuahirishwa kwa uchaguzi kunaweza kutoa mwanya kwa Jonathan kurekebisha baadhi ya makosa aliyokwisha kuyafanya.

eng: As incumbent party, PDP is furthermore believed to benefit from more resources than APC, making an extended campaign phase seem preferable.
swa: Kama chama kilicho madarakani, PDP kinadhaniwa kuwa ni chama kinachoweza kusaidiwa zaidi na serikali kuliko APC, hali inayochangia kupelekwa mbele kwa muda wa uchaguzi kwa manufaa ya chama tawala.

eng: Another possible advantage is that despite long resistance from Jonathan, neighbouring countries are increasingly present in the combat of Boko Haram and some extra weeks may halt the loss of territory to the insurgents.
swa: Pamoja na kuwa Rais Goodluck Jonathan hakutaka nchi jirani kuisadia nchi yake kupambana na Boko Haram, ushirika wao katika wiki chache unaweza kuisaidia Naijeria kusitisha harakati za magaidi hawa za kutaka kuitawala nchi hii, jambo ambalo linaweza kuchukuliwa kuwa ni moja ya manufaa itakayopata chama tawala kutokana na kuahirishwa jwa uchaguzi.

eng: That would make Jonathan have something to show the many critics that have questioned both his capability and commitment to respond to Boko Haram.
swa: Hali ambayo Kuahirishwa kwa uchaguzi kunaweza kutoa mwanya kwa Uwezekano mwingine wa chama tawala kufaidika na kuahirishwa kwa uchaguzi. Hili litamfanya Jonathan arudishe imani kwa wale wapinzani wake wanaohoji uwezo wake na utayari wake wa kukabiliana na Boko Haram.

eng: He notes that the postponement has been met with widespread disappointment and suspicion.
swa: Anatanabaisha kuwa kuahirishwa kwa uchaguzi kumegubikwa na hali ya watu kuonesha kukatishwa tamaa pamoja na ni uamuzi wa mashaka tele.

eng: He wonders what will happen if the objectives of the special operation are not met after six weeks:
swa: Anajiuliza ni nini kitatokea ikiwa malengo ya operesheni hii maaalum hayatafikiwa mara baada ya wiki sita kumalizika:

eng: The initial responses to the postponement express widespread disappointment and suspicion.
swa: Mwitikio wa awali wa kuahirishwa kwa uchaguzi unaonesha kuwa watu wamevunjika moyo na wana mashaka na uamuzi huu.

eng: The opposition candidate, Muhammadu Buhari, and major actors in civil society have appealed for calm, but the decision triggers major discontent.
swa: Mgombea u-Rais wa upinzani, Muhammadu Buhari, pamoja na washikadau wakuu wa asasi za kiraia wamewataka watu kuwa watulivu, lakini uamuzi huu umechochea hali ya watu kutokuridhika na hali ilivyo.

eng: Ahead of the decision, Nigerians gathered for protests in the streets in Lagos and Abuja.
swa: Mara baada ya kutolewa kwa uamuzi huu, raia wa Naijeria walikusanyika kwenye mitaa ya jiji la Lagos na Abuja kwa ajili ya kufanya maandamano.

eng: If there would be nationwide demonstrations, there are many places in which there is a high risk for violence.
swa: Kama yangalitokea maandamano ya nchi nzima, kuna maeneo mengi sana ambayo kungeweza kutokea machafuko.

eng: The special operation that the military commences is scheduled for six weeks.
swa: Operesheni hii maalum iliyoanzishwa na jeshi imepangwa kudumu kwa wiki sita.

eng: The record of the military’s operations in the north east in the last six years offers few indications that the situation will have improved significantly in these weeks.
swa: Kumbukumbu ya harakati za kijeshi katika eneo la Kaskazini Mashariki mwa Naijeria kwa miaka sita iliyopita inaonesha uwezekano mdogo kuwa hakutakuwa na mafanikio yatakayoonekana kwa muda huu wa kipindi cha wiki sita.

eng: The question is what will happen if the objectives of the operation are deemed not to have been accomplished at this time.
swa: Jambo la kujiuliza ni kuwa, nini kitatokea ikiwa malengo ya operesheni hii hayatakuwa yamekamilika mara baada ya wiki sita kuisha.

eng: Will the military call for postponement for another month?
swa: Jeshi litaomba tena liongezewe mwezi mmoja zaidi?

eng: The end of April is the upper limit according to the constitutional requirements for when elections must hold.
swa: Mwisho wa mwezi Aprili ndio kikomo kwa mujibu wa katiba, hivyo italazimika kwa uchaguzi kufanyika.

eng: Or, even worse, will there be a suggestion for an interim government?
swa: Au, hata kama haitakuwa vizuri, labda kutakuwa na mapendekezo ya kuundwa kwa serikali ya mpito?

eng: Moyosore Ayodele also wonders how Boko Haram can be defeated in six weeks after terrorising the country for six years:
swa: Moyosore Ayodele anajiuliza ni kwa namna gani Boko Haram wanaweza kudhibitiwa ndani ya wiki sita ikiwa ni baaada ya kuendesha matukio ya kigaidi kwa miaka sita:

eng: 6yrs, Boko haram couldn't be won, but we want to win it within 6weeks because of election.
swa: Kwa miaka 6 haikuwezekana kuwakabili Boko haram, lakini tunataka kuwashinda kwa wiki sita kwa sababu ya uchaguzi.

swa: Ni dhahiri PDP=Boko haram. #nigeriaelection — Moyosore Ayodele (@mohyur) February 8, 2015

swa: Uchaguzi ulipangwa kufanyika Machi 28 ni ukiukwaji wa wazi kabisa wa vifungu vya sheria vilivyomo kwenye Katiba ya Nigeria.

swa: Anza mapema, kusanya fedha za kutosha ili tuzifuje.

swa: Zinapokaribia tu kuisha, ahirisha (Uchaguzi).

eng: The cover photo from Masih Alinejad's Facebook page "My Stealthy Freedom"
swa: Picha kuu kutoka kwenye ukurasa wa Facebook wa Masih Alinejad uitwao "My Stealthy Freedom"

eng: London based Iranian journalist Masih Alinejad won the 2015 Women's Rights Award at the Geneva Summit for Human Rights and Democracy for her Facebook page "My Stealthy Freedom" this past week.
swa: Mwandishi raia wa Iran anayeishi London Masih Alinejad ameshinda Tuzo ya Haki za Wanawake kwa mwaka 2015 kwenye Mkutano wa Geneva wa Haki za Binadamu na Demokrasia kutokana na kampeni yake kwenye mtandao wa Facebook iitwayo "My Stealthy Freedom"juma lililopita.

eng: The page invites Iranian women to post pictures of themselves without a Hijab, in defiance of Iran's Islamic laws that enforce compulsory hijab.
swa: Ukurasa huo unawakaribisha wanawake wa ki-Iran kuweka picha zao humo wakiwa wamevalia Hijab, kupinga sheria ya ki-Islam ya Iran inayolazimisha mavazi hayo.

eng: With over 750, 000 followers, this page has been considered something of social media movement for Iranian women.
swa: Ukurasa huo wenye wafuasi 750, 000, umeonekana kuwa na sura ya harakati za mtandaoni kwa ajili ya wanawake.

eng: Below is a video from her acceptance speech at the Summit:
swa: Hapa chini kuna video iliyowekwa kwenye ukurasa wake kuonesha hotuba yake ya kupokea tuzo hiyo kwenye Mkutano huo siku ya Jumanne iliyopita:

eng: Organised by Africa is a Country blog, White History month 2015 is coming next month:
swa: Likiwa limeandaliwa na blogu ya Africa is a Country , tukio la Mwezi wa Historia Nyeupe linajongea mwezi ujao:

eng: Last March was the inaugural White History Month here on Africa is a Country, and without tooting too loudly on our own vuvuzela, it was kind of brilliant.
swa: Mwezi Machi mwaka jana ndio ulikuwa mwezi wa uzinduzi wa zoezi hilo kwenye blogu hii, na bila kupuliza sana mavuvuzela yetu kw akujisifu, ule kwa hakika ulikuwa ni mwezi mzuri.

eng: So we’re going to do it again.
swa: Tunaahidi kufanya kama tulivyofanya kipindi hicho.

eng: We featured stuff like Kathleen Bomani’s Leather from Human Skin in 1880s Philadelphia and pulled together a wide range of material, from Britain’s mass torture regime in 1950s Kenya to that time the South African government sent a delegation to the USA to find out how “reservations” worked.
swa: Tutakuwa na mambo kama ngozi ya Kathleen Bomani kutoka Human Skin, Filadefia ya miaka ya 1880 na tutakuwa na mambo mengi, kama vile utawala wa kikatili wa Uingereza kwenye miaka ya 1950 nchini Kenya na hata wakati ule serikali ya Afrika Kusini ilipotuma ujumbe kwenda Marekani kutafuta kujua namna "kuweka nafasi za mahotelini/ndege" kunavyofanyika.

eng: If you would like to participate, you should:
swa: Kama ungependa kushiriki, unatakiwa:

eng: Get in touch using editorial africasacountry com and let us know what you want to write about.
swa: Wasiliana nasi kwa editorial africasacountry com na tufahamishe kile unachotaka tukiandikie.

eng: Take a look at what was featured last year to get an idea of what we’re looking for.
swa: Angalia kile tulichokiandika mwaka jana kupata wazo la kile tunachokitafuta.

eng: Perhaps we weren't visible from space, like the Great Wall of China.
swa: Pengine hatukuweza kuonekana kutokea angani, kama ilivyo kwa Ukuta Mkubwa wa China.

eng: But fortunately the drone-mounted camera that filmed us in front of Cebu City’s grand Provincial Capitol building on the afternoon of January 25, 2015 hovered only a few hundred feet above us, a fraction of the Global Voices community assembled into a very respectable-looking—considering how quickly we did it—column-and-circle formation representing the 10 years of our existence.
swa: Lakini kwa bahati nzuri kifaa mithili ya eropleni kilichofungwa kamera kiliweza kutuchukua picha za video tukiwa mbele ya Jengo la Provincial Capital la Mamlaka ya Jiji la Cebu majira ya mchana wa Januari 25, 2015, kikiwa umbali wa mamia kadhaa ya futi tokea ardhini, tukiwa ni sehemu tu ya wanajamii wa Global Voices tuliokuwa tumekusanyika katika muonekano wa kipekee kabisa-na ikizingatiwa namna tulivyokusanyika hivyo kwa haraka-mpangilio wa mstari mmoja na mduara uliowakilisha miaka 10 ya kuwepo kwetu.

eng: We turned 10 in December, so the sixth Global Media Citizen Summit in January in Cebu City, Philippines, was another moment to celebrate, our only regret being that we weren’t able to do it with the entire 800-plus active members of the community present.
swa: Tulifikisha miaka 10 mwezi Disemba, kwa hiyo Mkutano Wa Dunia wa Uanahabari wa Kiraia wa sita uliofanyika mwezi Januari huko katika jiji la Cebu, nchini Ufilipino, ulikuwa ni fursa nyingine ya kusherehekea, hata hivyo, ni masikitiko yetu kuwa hatukuweza kuadhimisha siku hii tukiwa na wanajamii wote hai zaidi ya 800 waliopo hadi sasa.

eng: As the only times our virtual community gets to meet face to face, our biennial Summits are extremely important for the development of the organisation.
swa: Ikiwa ndio wakati pekee wa jamii yetu hai kukutana ana kwa ana, Mikutano yetu ifanyikayo kila baada ya miaka miwili ni ya muhimu sana kwa maendeleo ya jumuia yetu.

eng: The 2015 Summit included four days of internal meetings, and culminated in a public conference at the Cebu Provincial Capitol on the theme of The Open Internet: Local Perspectives, Global Rights.
swa: Mkutano wa mwaka 2015 ulihusisha siku nne za mikutano ya ndani, na ulihitimishwa kwa kongamano la wazi lililofanyika katika jengo la Provincial Capitol la Mamlaka ya Jiji la Cebu lililojadili dhana kuu ya Uhuru wa Mtandao wa intaneti.

eng: The proceedings opened, movingly and appropriately, with a statement read by Global Voices members calling for the release of jailed online media workers and activists.
swa: Kongamano lilifunguliwa kwa namna mahsusi iliyowagusa watu kwa wanajamii wa Global Voices kusoma tamko la kushinikiza kuachiwa huru kwa wanahabari wa mtandaoni na wanaharakati waliofungwa jela.

eng: Also announced at the Summit were the winners of the essay competition supported by Google.
swa: Pia, katika kongamano hilo, walitangazwa washindi wa shindano la kuandika insha lililofadhiliwa na Google.

eng: We have many to thank for helping making our 2015 Summit such a success:
swa: Tuna wengi wa kuwashukuru kwa kufanya mkutano wetu wa mwaka 2015 kuwa wa mafanikio:

eng: Our speakers, for generously sharing your expertise during the Summit sessions (see reports and videos on the Summit site).
swa: Wawasilishaji mada wetu, kwa kutushirikisha ujuzi wenu bila hiana katika mafunzo wakati wa mkutano (fuatilia taarifa na video kwenye tovuti ya Mkutano).

eng: Our attendees, who came from near and far within the Philippines, and from other parts of the world, to be part of the event.
swa: Shukrani za dhati kwa Wawakilishi, ambao walikuja kutoka katika maeneo ya karibu na ya mbali katika nchi ya Ufilipino, na pia wote waliokuja kutoka katika maeneo mengine Duniani kwa lengo la kushiriki mkutano huu.

eng: Our international sponsors: Ford Foundation, MacArthur Foundation, Google, Open Society Foundations, Knight Foundation, Yahoo! and Automattic.
swa: Shukrani za dhati kwa Wafadhili wetu wa kimataifa: Ford Foundation, MacArthur Foundation, Google, Open Society Foundations, Knight Foundation, Yahoo! na Automattic.

eng: And the Summit would not have been the success it was without the tremendous support we received from our host location.
swa: Na pia, mkutano wetu usingeweza kufikia mafanikio haya bila ya ushirikiano wa kipekee tulioupata kutoka kwa wenyeji wa tulipofanyia mkutano.

eng: Our heartfelt gratitude to our media sponsor SunStar Publishing, and our tech sponsors Globe Telecom and Smart Communications.
swa: Shukrani zetu za dhati kabisa ziwaendee wafadhili wetu wa masuala ya habari SunStar Publishing, pamoja na wafadhili wetu wa mawasiliano Globe Telecom na Smart Communications.

eng: To the Province of Cebu for letting us have the run of their grand Provincial Capitol Building for two whole days.
swa: Pia, shukrani zetu za dhati ziiendee Mamlaka ya Jiji la Cebu kwa kuturuhusu kutumia jengo lao tukufu la Provincial Capitol kwa muda wa siku mbili.

eng: To the Philippine Department of Tourism for the warm Filipino welcome and the epic closing party at the Museo Sugbo.
swa: Pia, tunatoa shukrani za kipekee kwa Idara ya Utalii ya Ufilipino kwa ukaribisho mwanana wa maadhi ya Kifilipino na kwa sherehe iliyofana ya kuhitimisha mkutano, iliyofanyika Museo Sugbo.

eng: And to Doris Isubal-Mongaya and her team at PRWorks for their extraordinary organisational skills and expert touches that made our time in Cebu special in so many ways—and for the gift of the drone video.
swa: Shukrani za kipekee pia ziwaendee Doris Isubal-Mongaya na timu yake ya PRWorks kwa kutumia maarifa na ujuzi wao wa hali ya juu uliofanya maisha yetu ya Cebu, kwa namna kadha wa kadha, kuwa ya kipekee sana-pia tunashukuru sana kwa zawadi ya video iliyochukuliwa kutokea angani.

eng: And onward and upward we go.
swa: Na tunasonga Mbele na Juu Zaidi kwa Mafanikio.

eng: Photo from Papuan Voices, used with permission.
swa: Picha kutoka Kwenye Video ya "Sauti za wa-Papua, imetumiwa kwa rushusa.

eng: Papuan Voices is a video-production advocacy initiative that allows West Papua activists to make their own short films that tell their stories and describe their everyday struggles.
swa: Sauti za wa-Papua ni mkakati wa utetezi kupitia uandaaji wa video unaowawezesha wanaharakati wa Papua ya Magharibi kutengeneza filamu fupi zinazosimulia habari zao pamoja na kuelezea harakati za maisha yao ya kila siku.

eng: The mainstream media rarely reports anything about life in West Papua, a province of Indonesia.
swa: Vyombo vikuu vya habari ni nadra sana kuzungumzia lolote kuhusiana na maisha ya watu wa Papua ya Magharibi, moja ya majimbo ya Indonesia.

eng: When reporters do turn to the region, it's usually to focus on the political conflict between the Indonesian government and West Papua's independence movement.
swa: Waandishi wa habari wanapolitupia jicho eneo hili, mara nyingi wamekuwa wakizungumzia mgogoro wa kisiasa uliopo kati ya serikali ya Indonesia na harakati za uhuru wa Papua ya Magharibi.

eng: Papuan Voices introduces readers to other aspects of Papuan culture and history:
swa: Mradi wa Sauti za wa-Papua unawajulisha wasomaji mambo mengine yanayohusu utamaduni na historia ya watu wa Papua:

eng: These stories are not just framed around West Papua’s political struggle for independence; they are not the stories of conflict that are more often circulated.
swa: Simulizi hizi hazina uhusiano wa moja kwa moja na harakati za Papua ya Magharibi za kujitafutia uhuru; siyo habari za mgogoro ambazo kwa kiasi kikubwa ndizo zimekuwa zikisambazwa.

eng: Rather, they are the stories behind the conflict: the struggles for education, the environment, equality and dignity.
swa: Hizi ni habari tofauti na mgogoro wa kisiasa unaoendelea: Ni kuhusu juhudi katika elimu, mazingira, usawa na utu.

eng: Papuan Voices is a collaboration between EngageMedia and Justice, Peace, and the Integrity of Creation.
swa: Mradi wa Sauti za wa-Papua ni ushirikiano kati ya EngageMedia na Haki, Amani, na Uaminifu wa Ubunifu.

eng: The project works with local organizations in Jayapura and Merauke in West Papua, where local activists attended multimedia workshops, and learned to narrate West Papua's complex story through videos.
swa: Mradi huu unafanya kazi na mashirika ya wazawa katika maeneo ya Jayapura na Merauke huko Papua ya Magharibi, ambapo wanaharakati wazawa walihudhuria warsha ya njia za upashanaji habari na kujifunza namna ya kuelezea kupitia video habari ambazo si rahisi kufikiwa.

eng: The result was a two-volume video featuring various local filmmakers and unique stories about the social, cultural, and political situation in West Papua.
swa: Hii imepelekea kuandaliwa kwa matoleo mawili ya video yaliyowahusisha waandaaji kadhaa wa filamu ambao ni wazawa na pia, zikiwa zimesheheni habari za kipekee za kijamii, kitamaduni, pamoja na hali ya kisiasa ya Papua ya Magharibi.

eng: The project's organizers hope “these stories will inspire others to learn and act, so that the voices of West Papua are brought to the forefront.”
swa: Waandaji wa mradi huu wanategemea kuwa “habari hizi zitawapa watu wengine hamasa ya kujifunza na kuchukua hatua, na hivyo kupelekea sauti za watu wa Papua Magharibi kusikika.”

eng: Some of the videos have been screened already in other parts of Indonesia.
swa: Tayari kuna picha zilizopigwa kutoka katika baadhi ya video hizo katika maeneo mengine ya Indonesia.

eng: One of the popular films is Mutiara Dalam Noken (Pearl in the Noken), which tells the story of Dr. Mia, “a Papuan woman who has devoted her life to treating the sick and tending to the disenfranchised in very remote areas in West Papua.”
swa: Moja ya filamu maarufu ni ile ya Mutiara Dalam Noken (Lulu ndani ya Noken), inayozungumzia habari ya daktari Mia, “Mwanamke wa Papua aliyejitolea kuwatibu wagonjwa pamoja na wale wanaoelekea kukosa haki zao za kiraia katika maeneo ya ndani sana ya Papua ya Magharibi.”

swa: Picha kutoka kwenye video ya "Sauti za wa-Paupa."

eng: Screen capture from "Papuan Voices."
swa: Picha kutoka kwenye video ya "Sauti za wa-Paupa."

eng: In a testimony, Wetipo lamented that violence against women is not adequately reported.
swa: Katika kutoa maoni yake, Wetipo alilalamikia suala la ukatili dhidi ya wanawake kutokuripotiwa ipaswavyo.

eng: Media mostly cover political and military violence.
swa: Vyombo vya habari vinazungumzia tu masuala ya siasa pamoja na ukatili wa wanajeshi.

eng: And yet no one looks at the violence that occurs to women.
swa: Hakuna hata mmoja anayezungumzia ukatili dhidi ya wanawake.

eng: Wetipo's video is intended to expose the poor conditions of women in Papua:
swa: Video ya Wetipo's inategemewa kuonesha hali ngumu ya maisha inayowakabili wanawake wa Papua:

eng: I want to show the world the lives of Papuan women.
swa: Ninataka kuuonesha ulimwengu kuhusu maisha ya wanawake wa Papua.

eng: They work so hard and receive no help from their family members.
swa: Wanafanya kazi kwa bidii sana na bila ya kupata usaidizi wowote kutoka kwa wanafamilia wenzao.

eng: Their husbands don’t even help them carry goods to the market.
swa: Hata waume wao huwa hawawasaidii kubeba mizigo pindi wanapoelekea sokoni.

eng: We hope that people will see these films and be inspired to bring change to their lives.
swa: Ni mategemeo yetu kuwa watu wataona filamu hizi na na kupata hamasa ya kuwasaidia kubadili maisha yao.

eng: Screen capture from "Papuan Voices."
swa: Picha kutoka kwenye video ya "Sauti za wa-Paupa."

eng: The name Wamena itself comes from the word ‘Wam’, which means swine, and ‘Ena’, which means to tame.
swa: Jina lenyewe, Wamena linatokana na neno ‘Wam’, likiwa na maana ya nguruwe, na ‘Ena’, likiwa na maana kufuga.

eng: Every rite of passage is symbolized by the presenting of pigs, and a family’s wealth is measured by the number of pigs they own.
swa: Kila maadhimisho ya hatua fulani ya maisha huambatana na kukabidhiwa nguruwe, na pia, utajiri wa familia hupimwa kwa wingi wa nguruwe katika familia.

eng: Pigs are also the symbol of peace among the tribes in the central highlands.
swa: Nguruwe pia ni ishara ya amani miongoni mwa makabila ya watu wanaoishi maeneo ya kati ya uwanda wa juu.

eng: An epidemic of pig deaths would therefore present a serious economic setback for the people of Wamena.
swa: Hii inamaanisha kuwa, panapotokea ugonjwa unaosababisha vifo vya nguruwe wengi, ni dhahiri kuwa pia kutakuwa na anguko kubwa lamkiuchumi miongoni mwa jamii ya watu wa Wamena.

eng: The video shows the close relationship between the community's pigs and people, and the social impact of an epidemic that killed large numbers of pigs:
swa: Video hii inaonesha uhusiano wa karibu kati ya nguruwe na watu pamoja na madhara kwa jamii kutokana na nguruwe wengi kufa kwa ugonjwa:

eng: Screen capture from "Papuan Voices."
swa: Picha kutoka kwenye video ya "Sauti za wa-Paupa."

eng: Jordan's Ministry of Awqaf and Islamic Affairs has called for a funeral prayer in absentia to be held in all of the kingdom's mosques on February 4, while Jordan's churches tolled their bells mourning their fallen hero.

eng: Image of protesters from the first march of part-time and freelance workers in Macedonia, December 2014.
swa: Picha ya maandamano yaliyohusu kazi za mikataba ya muda na wale walio na ajira zaidi ya moja nchini Makedonia, tarehe 24, Desemba.
