eng: Almost 1,000 people in Macedonia have signed on to participate in a second protest of part-time workers and freelancers, scheduled for February 6.
swa: Takribani, watu 1,000 nchini Macedonia wameshatia saini ya kukubali kushiriki kwa mara nyingine kwenye maandamano ya kuwatetea wafanyakazi walio na mikataba ya muda pamoja na wale walioajiriwa na mwajiri zaidi ya mmoja ,yanayotarajiwa kufanyika tarehe 6 Februari.

eng: In the first protest in December 2014, several thousand people took to the streets of Skopje, marching against additional taxes and fees imposed by new government regulations, effective as of January 1, 2015.
swa: Katika maandamano ya awali, yaliyofanyika Desemba 2014, maelfu ya watu walijitokeza kwenye mitaa ya Skopje wakipinga ongezeko la kodi pamoja na ada inayotozwa kwa mujibu wa taratibu mpya za serikali zilizoanza kutumika rasmi tarehe 1 Januari, 2015.

eng: Due to ambiguities in the new regulation and lack of coordination between government agencies in implementing the new law, payment of fees for part-time and freelance work for certain categories of workers were blocked in the last days of January.
swa: Kutokana na sintofahamu iliyopo katika sheria hii mpya na kukosekana kwa mawasiliano mazuri miongoni mwa vyombo husika vya serikali katika kutekeleza sheria hii, malipo ya ada ya kufanya kazi isiyo ya mkataba wa kudumu pamoja na baadhi ya wafanyakazi walio na mwajiri zaidi ya mmoja walizuiwa katika tarehe za mwisho za mwezi Januari.

eng: META.mk news agency recently reported:
swa: META.mk ambalo ni wakala wa habari, siku za hivi karibuni lilitaarifu kuwa:

eng: In the longest month of the year, freelancers who have fees higher than 9,590 denars will be left without income.
swa: Katika mwezi mrefu wa mwaka, wafanyakazi walio na mwajiri zaidi ya mmoja na ambao hutoa ada zaidi ya denari 9,590 (sawa na dola za kimarekani 178) hawatapata hawatalipwa.

eng: Copyright agency “Berin” said that they received a notice from Pension and Disability Insurance Fund (PIOM) asking them not to pay fees higher than 9,590 denars until information on how the calculations would be made is not published on the website.
swa: Wakala wa hati miliki “Berin” walisema kuwa walipokea taarifa kutoka Mfuko wa Pensheni na Bima ya Ulemavu (PIOM) ikiwataka kutokutoa ada zaidi ya denari 9,590 mpaka pale taarifa ya namna ya ukokotoaji unavyofanyika itakapositishwa kuwekwa kwenye tovuti.

eng: As stated in the notice, the reason for this is the lack of coordination of the Ministry of Labor and Social Policy, PIOM and PRO regarding the new law, which provides freelancers to also pay pension and disability insurance.
swa: Kama ilivyoelezwa katika taarifa hiyo, sababu kubwa ya kushindikana kutekelezwa kwa sheria hii mpya ni kukosekana kwa mawasiliano mazuri kati ya Wizara ya Kazi na Sera ya Kijamii, PIOM na PRO, sheria inayowataka wafanyakazi walioajiriwa na mwajiri zaidi ya mmoja kutoa mchango wa pensheni pamoja na bima ya ulemavu.

eng: What sets this new organized protest apart from others is that it uses innovative tactics: participants are preparing to ask the Ministry of Labor and Social Policy about the law's ambiguities using Freedom of Information Act (FOI) requests.
swa: Kinachopelekea kuratibiwa kwa maandamano haya mapya ikilinganishwa na maandamano mengine ni matumizi ya mbinu mpya: washiriki wanajiandaa kuiuliza Wizara ya kazi na Sera ya jamii kuhusiana na utata wa kisheria kwa kuzingatia matakwa ya Kanuni ya Uhuru wa Kupata Taarifa.

eng: By submitting requests for access to information as to the reasons for the delay in payments, protesters aim to show the bureaucratic inefficiency of the ministry under what many say is an absurd pretext and absurd regulations.
swa: Kwa kutumia kigezo kuwa maombi ya kupata taarifa ndio sababu kubwa ya kuchelewesha malipo, waandamanaji wana lengo la kuonesha mapungufu ya utaratibu huu wa wizara ambao wengi wanaamini kuwa urasimu huu ni visingizio na kanuni zisizo na maana yoyote.

eng: Come on freelancers, let's go to the Ministry of Labor and Social Policy and demand the answers they owe us.
swa: Jitokezeni wafanyakazi mlio na mwajiri zaidi ya mmoja, twendeni Wizara ya Kazi na Sera za Jamii ili tupate majibu ya maswali yetu.

eng: Many of us didn't receive pay during January, let's ask them why!
swa: Wengi wetu hatukulipwa mwezi Januari, watuambie kwa nini hawakutulipa!

eng: Some of us had our contracts discontinued, let's ask them why!
swa: Baadhi yetu mikataba yetu ilisitishwa, tuwaulize kwa nini waliisitisha!

eng: They didn't ask us when they decided to change five laws last summer, let us ask them now!
swa: Hawakutushirikisha wakati walipoamua kubadilisha sheria zote tano wakati wa kipindi cha majira ya joto, ni muda muafaka wa kuwauliza!

eng: Friday, February 6 at 11:00 p.m.
swa: Ijumaa, tarehe 6 Februari majira ya 11:00 p.m.

eng: Ministry for Labor and Social Policy.
swa: Wizara ya Kazi na Sera ya Jamii.

eng: Use the forms enclosed.
swa: Tumia fomu zilizoambatanishwa.

eng: We have the right to answers.
swa: Tuna haki ya kupata majibu.

eng: EVENT DETAILS
swa: UNDANI WA TUKIO

eng: Each freelancer will submit a FOI request to the ministry and then join the rest who will stand in front of the ministry.
swa: Kila mfanyakazi aliyeajiriwa na mwajiri zaidi ya mmoja, atawasilisha wizarani maombi ya Uhuru wa Kupata Taarifa (FOI) na kisha kujiunga na wengine watakaokuwa wamekusanyika mbele ya jengo la wizara.

eng: The submission process will take about two hours.
swa: Mchakato wa uwasilishaji wa maombi utachukua takribani masaa mawili.

eng: The template for the request is enclosed within the comments of this event .
swa: Fomu ya maombi imeambatanishwa kwenye maoni ya tukio hili .

eng: You can choose your own questions or copy some of the list which is also enclosed.
swa: Unaweza kujichagulia maswali au kunakili baadhi kutoka kwenye orodha iliyoambatanishwa.

eng: According to Macedonia's Law on Freedom of Access to Information of Public Character, state bodies are under obligation to respond to written FOI requests within 30 days.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Sheria ya Macedonia ya Uhuru wa Kupata Taarifa ya Kanuni ya Umma, mamlaka za serikali zinalazimika kutolea majibu ya maombi ya Uhuru wa Kupata Taarifa (FOI) ndani ya siku 30.

eng: Those who submit the request in person orally should receive responses within five days.
swa: Kwa wale waliowasilisha maombi kwa kutamka wanapaswa kupokea majibu ndani ya siku tano.

eng: More information about the FOI law is available on the website of Commission for Protection of the Right to Free Access to Public Information and the informative civil society portal "Right to Know."
swa: Taariza zaidi kuhusu sheria ya Uhuru wa Kupata Taarifa inapatikana katika tovuti ya Tume ya kulinda Haki ya Kupata Taarifa za Umma na Jukwaa la umoja wa upashanaji habari za Kiraia "Haki ya Kujua."

eng: Several hundred, if not more, FOI requests are expected to be directed at Macedonia's government through this protest.
swa: Mamia kadhaa, pengine na zaidi ya maombi ya Uhuru wa Kupata Taarifa (FOI) yanategemewa kuwasilishwa kwenye serikali ya Macedonia kuptia maandamano haya.

eng: Image tweeted by @Nav_urov.
swa: Picha twiti ya @Nav_urov.

eng: Photo from a drone flying above the massive December 10 student protests.
swa: Picha ya kamera iliyokuwa ikipaa juu ya kundi la wanafunzi waliokuwa wakiandamana Desemba 10.

eng: The Republic of Macedonia has issued a new regulation banning the use of drones up to 500 meters from government buildings, public gatherings and protests.
swa: Jamhuri ya Masedonia imetunga kanuni mpya kuzuia matumizi ya kamera za anga kwa umbali wa mita 500 kutoka kwenye majengo ya serikali, mikusanyiko ya watu na maandamano.

eng: The pro-government Dnevnik daily wrote a report about the new regulation, which has been in effect since January 31, but has yet to be posted online on any relevant government website.
swa: Gazeti linalounga mkono misimamo ya serikali Dnevnik daily liliandika ripoti kuhusu kanuni mpya, ambayo imekuwa ikitenda kazi tangu Januari 31, lakini ikiwa bado haichapishwa mtandaoni kwenye tovuti yoyote muhimu ya serikali.

eng: It is not allowed to operate unmanned aircraft under 150 meters above any inhabited are, under 50 meters of distance from any person, ship, vehicle or infrastructure, the regulation reads.
swa: Hairuhusiwi kutumia kijindege cha kamera kisichoruhusiwa katika umbali wa mita 150 juu ya eneo la makazi, mita 50 kutoka kwa mtu, gari, au jengo, kanuni hiyo inasomeka.

eng: It also forbids pointing the drone towards persons, animals or gatherings of people.
swa: Kadhalika, kanuni hiyo inazuia kuelekeza kamera inayopaa kwa mtu, mnyama au mkusanyiko wa watu.

eng: According to the regulation: "It is not allowed to fly unmanned aircraft in a radius of 500 meters from building related to security, buildings of state bodies and critical masses of people, such as the buildings of Ministry of Defense and the Army of Republic of Macedonia, buildings of the Ministry of Interior, the Government, the Assembly, the residence of the President of the state, embassies, sport competitions of high risk, and big gatherings of people (protests)."
swa: Kwa mujibu wa kanuni hiyo: "Hairuhusiwi kurusha kamera kwenye kipenyo cha mita 500 kutoka kwenye jengo linalohusika na usalama, majengo ya vyombo vya serikali na mkusanyiko muhimu wa watu, kama vile majengo ya Wizara ya Ulinzi na Jeshi la Jamhuri ya Masedonia, majengo ya Wizara ya Mambo ya Ndani, serikali, Bunge, makazi ya Rais wa nchi, majengo ya Ubalozi, mashindano ya michezo yenye hatari kubwa, na mkusanyiko mkubwa wa watu (wanaoandamana)."

eng: Student Plenum, the organizers of the December 10 protest claim that a drone camera operator was detained by the police.
swa: Mkutano wa wanafunzi, ulioandaa maandamano ya Desemba 10 unadai kwamba mwongozaji wa kamera hiyo ya kupaa angani alikamatwa na polisi.

eng: There is no public record for how long or on what charges.
swa: Hakuna taarifa zilizotolewa hadharani kuhusiana na na kukamatwa kwae wala mashitaka yake.

eng: The boy with the drone has been detained in the Karposh police station.
swa: Kijana mwenye kamera hiyo amekamatwa kwenye kituo cha Polisi cha Karposh.

eng: The pressure continues but they won't stop us.
swa: Shinikizo linaendelea lakini hawawezi kutuzuia.

eng: This is just the beginning!
swa: Huu ni mwanzo tu!

eng: Two years ago, tens of thousands of Macedonians took to the streets to protest against poverty and corruption in their country of two-million.
swa: Miaka miwili iliyopita, makumi ya maelfu ya wa-Masedonia yaliingia mtaani kuandamana dhidi ya umasikini na ufisadi kwenye nchi hiyo yenye idadi ya watu milioni mbili.

eng: Since then, different groups of people - students, teachers, residents and workers - have come out to protest, demanding better conditions and rights.
swa: Tangu wakati huo, makundi mbalimbali ya watu - wanafunzi, walimu, wakazi na wafanyakazi - wamejitokeza kuandamana, kudai mazingira bora na haki.

eng: The government has used various tactics to discourage media coverage of protests, including intimidating journalists.
swa: Serikali imetumia mbinu mbalimbali kukatisha tamaa kutangazwa kwa habari za maandamano hayo, ikiwa ni pamoja na kuwatisha waandishi wa habari.

eng: Tweet bird Image by Id-iom and used under a CC BY-NC 2.0 Creative Commons license.
swa: Picha ya ndege wa Twita na Id-iom na imetumiwa chini ya leseni za Ubunifu ya CC BY-NC 2.0.

eng: Of the approximately 7,000 languages spoken around the world, only a small fraction are found on the Internet.
swa: Katika lugha karibu 7,000 zinazozungumzwa duniani, ni lugha chache sana zinaweza kupatikana mtandaoni.

eng: On the platform Twitter, 85% of the tweets are written in one of just eight languages, according to one study - not exactly an accurate reflection of the planet's cultural and linguistic diversity.
swa: Kwenye mtandao wa twita kwa mfano, asilimia 85 ya twiti zinaandikwa kwa lugha nane pekee, kwa mujibu wa utafiti mmoja - hata hivyo, utafiti huo unaweza usitoe picha halisi ya wingi wa lugha na tamaduni za dunia kwenye mtandao wa intaneti.

eng: Even though more and more communities are beginning to discover the possibilities of sharing their language online, much more can be done to raise awareness and highlight these efforts.
swa: Ingawa jamii zaidi na zaidi zinaanza kugundua uwezekano wa kuweka lugha zao mtandaoni, hatua zaidi na zaidi zinahitajika kufanyika ili kujaribu kukuza uelewa na kutangaza juhudi hizi.

eng: For International Mother Language Day on February 21, Rising Voices, along with our organizing partners the Living Tongues Institute, Endangered Languages Project, and Indigenous Tweets, as well as a wide range of participating partners, are coming together to launch the campaign “Tweet in Your #MotherLanguage.”
swa: Kwa malengo ya Siku ya Kimataifa za Lugha Asili mnamo Februari 21, Rising Voices, kwa kushirikiana na washirika wetu katika maandalizi Taasisi ya Living Tongues , Mradi wa lugha zilizo hatarini kutoweka, na Indigenous Tweets, ikiwa ni pamoja na washirika wengi washiriki, tunaungana kuzindua kampeni ya “Twiti kwa #LughaAsili.”

eng: Through this online campaign, we want to recognize and encourage Internet users who are sharing their language on Twitter with a special focus on indigenous, endangered and minority languages, all of which may not be as well represented online.
swa: Kwa kupitia kampeni hii ya mtandaoni, tunahitaji kuwatambua na kuwahamasisha watumiaji wa mtandao wa intaneti wanaotumia lugha zao za asili kwenye mtandao wa Twita hususani kwenye lugha za wenyeji, zilizo kwenye hatari ya kutoweka na zinazozungumzwa na watu wachache, zote zikiwa hazijawakilishwa ipasavyo mtandaoni.

eng: It's easy to get involved:
swa: Ni rahisi kushiriki kampeni hii:

eng: Step 1 – Tweet in Your Mother Language
swa: Hatua ya 1 – Twiti kwa Lugha yako ya Asili (kilugha)

eng: Tweet using your mother language throughout the day Share “Why is it important to use your language on the Internet?”
swa: Twiti kwa kutumia lugha yako ya asili siku nzima Jadili "Kwa nini ni muhimu kutumia lugha yako kwenye mtandao wa intaneti?"

eng: Tweet greetings or your favorite words/phrases in your language Tweet a translation to encourage speakers of other indigenous and minority language communities
swa: Twiti salamu au maneno/misemo yako uipendayo kwa lugha yako Twiti tafsiri yake kuwahamasisha wazungumzaji wa jamii nyinginezo za lugha za wenyeji na wachache

eng: Step 2 – Add Hashtags
swa: Hatua ya 2 – Ongeza Alama habari

eng: Add the hashtag #MotherLanguage Add the hashtag of the language (i.e. #Lakota, #Yoruba)
swa: Ongeza alama habari #MotherLanguage Ongeza alama habari ya lugha husika (mfano #Kichaga, #Kisukuma)

eng: Step 3 – Join the Conversation!
swa: Hatua ya 3 – Jiunge na Mazungumzo!

eng: Find others using the #MotherLanguage hashtag and retweet them Search for the hashtag of your mother language and follow others tweeting in it Connect with other people celebrating language diversity
swa: Watafute watu wengine kwa kutumia alama habari ya #MotherLanguage na sambaza twiti zao Tafuta alama habari ya lugha yako ya asili na wafuatilie wengine wanao-twiti kwa lugha hiyo Ungana na watu wengine wanaosherehekea wingi wa lugha

eng: For more details on how to take part, take a look at the campaign website.
swa: Kwa taarifa zaidi kuhusu namna ya kushiriki, pitia tovuti ya kampeni hiyo.

eng: Why Tweet in Your #MotherLanguage?
swa: Kwa nini Utwiti kwa #LughaAsili?

eng: Despite the increase in the number of languages being used online, many communities still face ongoing challenges when trying to communicate through social media.
swa: Pamoja na kuongezeka kwa idadi ya lugha zinazotumiwa mtandaoni, jamii nyingi bado zinakabiliana na changamoto zinapojaribu kuwasiliana kupitia mitandao za kijamii.

eng: Some languages lack a keyboard that allows users to write in their language, and many parts of the world still lack adequate connectivity, excluding them from the online conversation.
swa: Baadhi za lugha zinakosa herufi za kompyuta zinazowasaidia watumiaji kuandika kwa lugha zao, na sehemu nyingine za dunia bado hazina mtandao wa intaneti, hali inayowafanya watengwe na mazungumzo ya mtandaoni.

eng: However, Internet communication has proven to be an important part of language preservation and revitalization.
swa: Hata hivyo, mawasiliano ya mtandao yamethibitisha kuwa sehemu za muhimu ya utunzaji na uhuishaji wa lugha.

eng: Easy-to-use digital tools allow for more people to create content in their language, and the Internet for speakers of these languages to connect, regardless of geographic distances.
swa: Zana za kidijitali zilizorahisi kutumia zinasaidia watu kutengeneza maudhui kwa lugha zao, na kusaidia upatikanaji wa mtandao wa wazungumzaji wa lugha hizi, bila kujali sehemu za kijiografia.

eng: This campaign will highlight the work of many individuals and groups committed to using their languages on the Internet, many of whom may be considered "language digital activists" for their role in bridging this divide and encouraging a new generation of speakers.
swa: Kampeni hii itamulika kazi za watu mbalimbali na makundi yaliyojitoa kutumia lugha zao kwenye mtandao wa intaneti, wengi wanaoweza kutambuliwa kama "wanaharakati wa kidijitali wa lugha" kwa nafasi zao katika kuunganisha pengo hili na kuhamasisha kizazi kipya cha wazungumzaji.

eng: We are fortunate to count the participation of "ambassadors" such as Rodrigo Pérez (@ISF_MX) from Mexico, who regularly tweets in the Zapotec language and Ignacio Tomichá Chuve (@MonkoxBesiro) from Bolivia, who regularly tweets in the Bésiro (Chiquitano) language, who created these videos extending an invitation to participate in the campaign.
swa: Tunayo bahati kupata uungwaji mkono na "mabalozi" kama Rodrigo Pérez (@ISF_MX) kutoka Mexico, ambaye hu-twiti kwa lugha ya ki-Zapoteki na Ignacio Tomichá Chuve (@MonkoxBesiro) kutoka Bolivia, anaye-twiti kwa lugha ya Bésiro (Chiquitano), ambao walitenegeza video hizi kualika washiriki katika kampeni hii.

eng: More ambassador videos are on their way and will be added to the playlist:
swa: Mabalozi wengine wataongezwa kwenye orodha:

eng: Thanks to help of many people around the world, the campaign website has already been translated in more than 25 languages, including Odia, Sena, and Lezgian.
swa: Shukrani nyingi kwa msaada wa watu wengi duniani kote, na tovuti ya kampeni tayari imetafsiriwa kwenye lugha zipatazo 25, ikiwa ni pamoja na Odia, Sena, na ki-Lezgia.

eng: Many of these translations came from members of the Global Voices' Lingua Project, a community of volunteer translators.
swa: Nyingi za tafsiri hizi zimefanywa na wanachama wa Mradi wa Lingua wa Global Voices, Jamii ya watafsiri wanaojitolea.

eng: With your help, we can pave the way for a more multilingual Internet where different languages are celebrated, not excluded.
swa: Kwa msaada wako, tunaweza kufanya mtandao uwe na lugha nyingi kadri iwezekanavyo wenye kushamiri lugha tofauti tofauti, na sio kubagua baadhi ya lugha.

eng: All it takes is a tweet or retweet!
swa: Kinachohitajika tu ni kutwiti au kutangaza twiti za wengine!

eng: Five companies are said to have misappropriated funds for fighting Ebola in Sierra Leone:
swa: Makampuni matano nchini Sierra Leone yanasemekana kutumia fedha zilizokusudiwa kupambana na Ebola kwa njia za kifisadi:

eng: Here are the 5 companies who were awarded the biggest contracts to provide goods and services to Sierra Leone’s ebola response as listed in the Ebola Funds Audit Report covering the period from May – October 2014.
swa: Haya hapa makampuni matano yaliyokuwa yameingia mikataba mikubwa ya kusambaza vifaa na kutoa huduma katika kupambana na ugonjwa wa Ebola nchini Sierra Leone kama yalivyoorodheshwa kwenye Taarifa ya Ukaguzi ya Fedha za Kupambana na Ebola kwa kipindi cha kuanzia Mei - Oktoba 2014.

eng: The following contracts did not meet the country’s procurement laws and policies and documentation to support the awarding of these contracts were missing, and unaccounted for.
swa: Mikataba ifuatayo hakukidhi sheria na sera za manunuzi za nchi na nyaraka za kuthibitisha namna yalivyoshinda tenda hizo hazionekani, na hakuna anayeweza kutoa maelezo.

eng: This makes it possible for fraud, waste, and misappropriation of funds to occur therefore crippling the nation’s ability to quickly respond to the crisis.
swa: Hali hii inafanya uwepo uwezekano wa kutokea vitendo vya kifisadi, upotevu na hata matumizi mabaya ya fedha na hivyo kuzorotesha uwezo wa taifa hilo kupambana na janga hilo.

eng: Young men in Niger - CC-BY-2.0
swa: Vijana huko Niger - CC-BY-2.0

eng: For the first time, Boko Haram conducted an assault on Niger's territory and the youth of Niger will not stand for it.
swa: Kwa mara ya kwanza, Boko Haram kimetekeleza shambulio kwenye mpaka na Naija na vijana wa ki-Naija hakuweza kuvumilia.

eng: Boko Haram assaulted Bosso and Diffa, two towns in southeast Niger at the border with Nigeria but was repelled by Niger and Chad's army.
swa: Boko Haram walishambulia Bosso na Diffa, miji miwili iliyo kusini mashariki mwa Naija kwenye mpaka wa nchi hiyo na Naijeria lakini walirudishwa nyuma na majeshi ya Chad na Naija.

eng: Boko Haram lost an estimated 100 combatants in the clash but a suicide bomber detonated explosives in the city a few hours later, killing 5 civilians.
swa: Boko Haram imepoteza zaidi ya wnaamgambo 100 kwenye mapigano hayo lakini mtu aliyejitolea mhanga alijilipua mjini masaa machache baadae, na kuua watu wasiopungua watano.

eng: The youth of Niger was prompt to react to the attacks.
swa: Kijana mmoja wa Naija alisukumwa kujibu mapigo.

eng: Niamey (Niger's capital) High school students got together to condemn the attacks on their country and express in Hausa their support to their troops fighting at the border: Post by El Grintcho Billo.
swa: Wanafunzi wa shule za sekondari jijini Niamey (mji mkuu wa Naija) walikusanyika pamoja na kulaani shambulio hilo nchini mwao, na kwa kutumia lugha ya ki-Hausa, waliunga mkono vikosi vyao vinavyopambana mpakani: Imewekwa na El Grintcho Billo.

eng: Jennifer Sefa-Boakye highlights 10 of Golden Baobab Prize for African Illustrators’ finalists:
swa: Jennifer Sefa-Boakye anasaili orodha ya washindani 10 bora zaidi wa tuzo ya Golden Baobab kwa Wachoraji wa Kiafrika:

eng: Late last year Ghana-based pan-African literary organization Golden Baobab introduced us to a shortlist of talented illustrators, whose work ranged from 3-D Ashanti folktales to intricately drawn Moroccan cityscapes and African barbershop-inspired murals in Durban.
swa: Mwaka jana shirika la Afrika lenye makazi yake nchini Ghana, Golden Baobab, liliwatambulisha wachoraji kadhaa wenye vipaji, ambao kazi zao ni kama vile masimulizi ya Ashanti yaliyosukwa kutoka miji ya Moroko na hata wapiga rangi wa ki-Afrika katika vyumba vya kunyolea jijini Durban.

eng: Awarded in November, the inaugural Golden Baobab Prize for African Illustrators was one of the foundation’s six prizes recognizing the year’s best African writers and illustrators of children’s stories.
swa: Uzinduzi wa tuzo hizo za Glolden Baobab kwa wachoraji wa ki-Afrika ulifanyika mwezi Novemba, na ni moja ya tuzo sita zinazotambua waandishi na wachoraji bora wa ki-Afrika wa vitabu vya watoto wa mwaka.

eng: Filipinos Ask 'Where Is the President?'
swa: Wafilipino Wauliza 'Rais Yuko Wapi?'

eng: RETWEET if you think PNoy should've attended the arrival of honors instead of that Car Plant event. #NasaanAngPangulo tweets @BobOngWords.
swa: TWITI TENA kama unadhani PNoy alipaswa kuhudhuria mapokezi ya heshima badala ya tukio la Kiwanda cha Magari. #NasaanAngPangulo alitwiti @BobOngWords.

eng: The hashtag #NasaanAngPangulo, which means “where is the president” in Tagalog, became the top trending topic on Twitter worldwide as Filipinos expressed their outrage at President Noynoy Aquino for skipping the arrival honors for elite policemen killed in a special operation.
swa: Alama habari #NasaanAngPangulo, yenye maaana 'Rais yuko wapi' katika lugha ya Kitagalog, ilikuwa mada maarufu zaidi kwenye mtandao wa Twita duniani wakati Wafilipino walipokuwa wakionesha hasira zao kwa Rais Noynoy Aquino kufuatia kukosekana kwake kwenye mapokezi ya heshima ya miili ya polisi waliouawa wakiwa kwenye operesheni maalum.

eng: Aquino graced the opening of Mitsubishi Motor Corporation’s new car factory in Laguna (province south of Manila) rather than attend the police ceremony.
swa: Aquino alihudhuria kuzinduliwa kwa kiwanda kipya cha magari cha kampuni ya Mitsubishi huko Laguna (jimbo lililo kusini mwa Manila) badala ya kuhudhuria mapokezi ya miili ya polisi.

eng: The coffins carrying the remains of the dead policemen arrived at Villamor Airbase after being flown all the way from the southern Philippine town of Mamasapano, Maguindanao.
swa: Majeneza yaliyobeba mabaki ya miili ya polisi hao yaliwasili kwenye uwanja wa ndege wa Villamor baada ya kusafirishwa kutoka Mamasapano, mji ulio kusini mwa Ufilipino, Maguindanao.

eng: Forty-four members of the Philippine National Police-Special Action Force (PNP-SAF) were killed in a botched-up counter-terror operation which became an 11th-hour pitched battle between state forces and Moro secessionist rebels operating in the Mamasapano area.
swa: Askari arobaini na wanne wa Jeshi la Polisi la Ufilipino - Kikosi Maalum (PNP-SAF) waliuawa kwenye operesheni ya kupambana na ugaidi mapambano yaliyochukua masaa 11 kati ya vikosi vya serikali na waasi wa Moro wanaotaka kujitenga na wanaofanya shughuli zao kwenye eneo la Mamasapano.

eng: They were part of a 400-member police operation sent to capture the alleged mastermind of the 2002 Bali bombings who was said to be hiding in the area.
swa: Marehemu hao walikuwa sehemu ya askari 400 waliokuwa wametumwa kumkamata mtu anayedaiwa kupanga matukio ya milipuko ya mabomu ya Bali mwaka 2002 anayesemekana kujificha eneo hilo.

eng: The US government has placed a $5-million bounty on suspect Zulkifli bin Hir alias Marwan.
swa: Serikali ya Marekani ilitoa kiasi cha dola za Marekani milioni tano kama zawadi kwa atakayetoa taarifa zitakazowezesha kumkamata mtuhumiwa Zulkifli bin Hir alias Marwan.

eng: A series of memes ridiculing President Aquino’s absence from the arrival ceremony were widely circulated on social networking sites like Facebook and Twitter.
swa: Mfululizo wa ujumbe uliokuwa ukienea kwa kasi kudhihaki kukosekana kwa Rais Aquino kwenye mapokezi hayo ulizunguka kwenye mitandao ya kijamii kama Facebook na Twita.

eng: Filipino netizens recalled how President Aquino was quick to looking after big corporations and attending celebrity events while being absent in many of the big tragedies that befell the nation.
swa: Wafilipino watumiao mitandao walikumbushana namna Rais Aquino alivyokuwa mwepesi kutoa muda wake kuhudhuria shughuli za zinazoandaliwa na makampuni makubwa wakati akikosekana kwenye majanga mengi makubwa yaliyoliathiri taifa.

eng: When the bodies of the MH17 crash victims arrived in The Netherlands, the Dutch King Willem-Alexander and Queen Maxima, and the rest of the Dutch royal family, along with government officials sat and watched and cried and mourned with nation as the coffins were brought from planes to hearses.
swa: Wakati miili ya waathirika wa ndege ya MH17 ilipowasili nchini Uholanzi, Mfalme wa nchi hiyo Willem-Alexander na Malkia Maxima, na pamoja na familia karibu yote ya kifalme, wakiambatana na maafisa wa serikali walikaa na kutazama na kulia na kuomboleza na taifa wakati majeneza yaliposhushwa kutoka kwenye ndege.

eng: Nothing was more important than that ritual for the dead.
swa: Hakuna kilichokuwa muhimu zaidi ya kuwaenzi marehemu hao.

eng: President Aquino gave a speech during the necrological services for the slain policemen a day after their coffins arrived.
swa: Rais Aquino alitoa hotuba wakati ibada ya mazishi ya polisi waliouawa siku moja baada ya majeneza kuwasili.

eng: But the president was again put on the spot for being late and thus putting the rites on hold to wait for his arrival.
swa: Lakini wakati huo kwa mara nyingine alisemekana kuchelewa na kufanya shughuli zingoje mpaka atakapowasili.

eng: Aquino’s speech during the service also became the butt of online jokes for being more about himself than the fallen cops.
swa: Hotuba ya Aquino wakati wa ibada hiyo iligeuka kuwa kituko mtandaoni kwa kusemekana kuzungumzia mambo yake binafsi kuliko marehemu.

eng: A meme pointed out how Aquino always begins his speech in the vein of George Lucas’ Star Wars.
swa: Utani uliokuwa ukisambaa mtandaoni ulionesha namna Aquino huanza hotuba yake kwa maneno ya George Lucas wa Star Wars.

eng: From the Facebook page of Jason Valenzuela.
swa: Kutoka kwenye ukurasa wa Facebook wa Jason Valenzuela.

eng: The president’s spokesman has defended his absence from the arrival honors for the dead policemen, saying this was not part of his schedule.
swa: Msemaji wa rais ametetea kutokuwepo kwa rais katika mapokezi ya miili ya polisi, akisema kwamba hiyo haikuwa sehemu ya ratiba yake.

eng: He also belittled criticisms by netizens in a Palace briefing, pointing out that this was not the majority view.
swa: Pia alikejeli wakosoaji wake mtandao kwenye taarifa yake Ikulu, akisema kwamba ukosoaji huo ni mtazamo usiowakilisha maoni ya wengi.

eng: School children in Arusha, Tanzania.
swa: Watoto wa shule mkoani Arusha, Tanzania.

eng: Photo released under Creative Commons by Flickr user Colin J. McMechan.
swa: Picha imetolewa na mtumiaji wa mtandao wa Flickr Colin J. McMechan kwa leseni ya Creative Commons.

eng: Tanzania is set to make a historic shift away from English and replace it with Swahili as the language of instruction in the country’s schools.
swa: Tanzania iko tayari sasa kufanya mabadiliko ya historia kwa kuachana na lugha ya Kiingereza na kuanza kutumia rasmi Kiswahili kama lugha ya kujifunzia na kufundishia katika shule za nchi hiyo.

eng: The new education system launched by President Jakaya Kikwete on February 13, 2015, in line with National Vision 2025 will also extend basic education from seven years to 11 years, provide free education at primary and education levels and abolish national examinations for primary school levers.
swa: Sera mpya ya elimu iliyozinduliwa na Rais Jakaya Kikwete mnamo Februari 13, 2015, inayokwenda sambamba na Mpango wa Taifa Kuelekea 2025 inarefusha elimu za msingi kutoka miaka saba ya sasa mpaka miaka 11, na kuifanya elimu hiyo kuwa bure ikiwa ni pamoja na kuondoa mtihani wa taifa kwa wahitimu wa elimu ya msingi kuingia sekondari.

eng: This appears to be one of the first times that a country in Africa will teach students at all levels in an African language instead of a foreign language.
swa: Hatua hii inaonekana kuwa mojawapo ya maamuzi ya kwanza kwamba nchi ya Afrika inaamua kufundisha wanafunzi wake kwa ngazi zote kwa kutumia lugha ya ki-Afrika badala ya lugha za kigeni.

eng: Commenting on the language shift, Atetaulwa Ngatara, the assistant director for policy at the Ministry of Education and Vocational Training, said English will still be taught as a language, but for students to learn English it's not necessary that all their subjects be taught in it.
swa: Akitoa maoni yake kuhusu mabadiliko ya lugha, Atetaulwa Ngatara, naibu mkurugenzi wa sera katika Wizara ya Elimu na Mafunzo ya Ufundi, alisema Kiingereza kitaendelea kufundishwa kama lugha, na kwamba wanafunzi kujifunza Kiingereza haitamaanisha kuwa ni lazima masomo yote yafundishwe kwa lugha hiyo.

eng: An article about the policy shift posted on Facebook by Oliver Stegen, a Swahili speaker of German origin and a linguistic advisor at language development non-profit SIL International, elicited mixed responses.
swa: Makala kuhusu mabadiliko hayo ya sera iliyowekwa kwenye mtandao wa Facebook naOliver Stegen, ambaye ni mzungumzaji wa Kiswahili mwenye asili ya Ujerumani na mshauri wa lugha wa shirika lisilo la kibiashara linaloshughulika na ukuzaji wa lugha SIL International, iliibua hisia mchanganyiko.

eng: Nancy Petruzzi Maurer joked:
swa: Nancy Petruzzi Maurer alitania kwa salamu ya Kiingereza iliyokosewa:

eng: Goood mauning teacha!
swa: Goood mauning teacha!

eng: No more
swa: Hakuna zaidi

eng: Paul A Kijuu commented in Swahili saying that English has turned the educated class into robots:
swa: Paul A Kijuu alitoa maoni kwa Kiswahili akisema kwamba Kiingereza kimegeuza tabaka la wasomi kuwa maroboti:

eng: On my side, Oliver Stegen I see this as the right move.
swa: Kwa upande wangu, Oliver Stegen mimi naona hii ni hatua nzuri sana.

eng: Our problem is complaining.
swa: Shida yetu ni kulalamika.

eng: Education has to be given using the language that the user understands.
swa: Elimu inapaswa itolewe kwa lugha inayoeleweka kwa mtumiaji.

eng: English does not help us apart from turning us into robots.
swa: Kiingereza hakitusaidii zaidi ya kutufanya maroboti.

eng: Our educated elites do not think independently because they do not understand what they studied.
swa: Wasomi wetu hawafikiri kwa kujitegemea kwa sababu hakuna walichojifunza wanachokielewa.

eng: Vera Wilhelmsen noted that not everyone needs to go to university but everyone deserves a good basic education:
swa: Vera Wilhelmsen alibainisha kwamba ingawa si kila mtu anahitaji kufika Chuo Kikuu lakini kila mmoja anastahili elimu bora ya msingi:

eng: I think it is important to consider what kind of basic education will benefit the most people.
swa: Ninadhani ni muhimu kutafakari aina gani ya elimu ya msingi itawanufaisha watu wengi.

eng: It is clear that per today not very many people make it to secondary school, and even fewer graduate from it.
swa: Ni bayana kwamba mpaka leo hii si watu wengi wanafanikiwa kufika sekondari, na ni wachache sana wanahitimu elimu hiyo.

eng: There is a problem when neither students not teachers are equipped to make the switch from Swahili to English in secondary school.
swa: Kuna tatizo pale ambapo si wanafunzi wala walimu wameandaliwa kubadilika kutoka Kiswahili kwenda Kiingereza katika shule ya Sekondari.

eng: Of course we have to watch for the effects, but I also do think it is a good step forward.
swa: Ni kweli, tunapaswa kutazama athari zake, lakini ninaamini hii ni hatua nzuri ya mafanikio.

eng: Not everyone needs to go to university, but everyone deserves a good basic education!
swa: Si lazima kila mmoja afike Chuo Kikuu, lakini raia wote wanastahili elimu bora ya msingi!

eng: However, not everyone was in support of the new education system.
swa: Hata hivyo, si kila mmoja aliafiki mfumo huo mpya wa elimu.

eng: Steve Nicolle pointed out one possible effect of the new policy:
swa: Steve Nicolle alibainisha uwezekano wa athari ya sera hiyo mpya ya elimu:

eng: I suspect one effect of this legislation will be an increase in enrollments in private schools that continue to offer tuition in English.
swa: Ninahisi athari ya sera hii itakuwa kuongezeka kwa uandikishaji wa wanafunzi katika shule binafsi ambazo zinaendelea kufundisha kwa Kiingereza.

eng: Keep an eye open for politicians opening new English medium schools in the near future!
swa: Chunguzeni sana mtaona wanasiasa wakifungua shule mpya zinazofundisha kwa Kiingereza katika siku za hivi karibuni!

eng: Elly Gudo agreed with Steve Nicole, arguing that politicians will be the main beneficiaries of the policy:
swa: Elly Gudo alikubaliana na Steve Nicole, akidhani kwamba wanasiasa watakuwa wanufaika wakuu wa sera hii:

eng: I totally agree with Steve Nicolle.
swa: Ninakubaliana na wewe kabisa Steve Nicolle.

eng: Having lived in Tanzania, I can tell you for sure that politicians are the highest beneficiaries of this new policy.
swa: Kwa kuishi hapa Tanzania, ninaweza kukuambia kwa hakika kwamba wanasiasa watakuwa ndio wanufaika wakuu wa sera hii ya elimu.

eng: Majority of Tanzanian middle and all upper classes who have identified with the global village will do anything to take their children to English Medium Schools.
swa: Wengi wa wa-Tanzania wa tabaka la kati na la juu ambao wanahusudu utandawazi watafanya kila wanaloweza kuwapeleka watoto wao kwenye shule zinazofundisha Kiingereza.

eng: The common man's child will then be highly disadvantaged when it comes to University admission and by extension job acquisition.
swa: Mtoto wa masikini ndiye atakayekuwa mwathirika mkuu utakapokuja wakati wa kujiunga na Chuo Kikuu na hata pale anapoanza kutafuta kazi.

eng: After 2 decades, the country will be highly classified.
swa: Baada ya miongo miwili, nchi itakuwa na matabaka yaliyo wazi.

eng: Tanzania needs a French-type Revolution in many facets.
swa: Tanzania inahitaji mapinduzi kama yale ya Ufaransa katika sura nyingi.

eng: Opposing the policy, Muddyb Mwanaharakati said the following in Swahili:
swa: Akipinga sera hiyo, Muddyb Mwanaharakati alisema yafuatayo kwa Kiswahili:

eng: Oliver Stegen do not make me laugh.
swa: Oliver Stegen usichekelee.

eng: They have politicised the issue.
swa: Wametia siasa ndani yake.

eng: Their children go to international schools .
swa: Watoto zao wanasoma international schools .

eng: We, the poor ones, will continue with going to under performing and poorly equipped schools and continue with our English of ya, ya, yes no yes no.
swa: Sisi akina kajamba nani tutasoma zilezile S.t vichochoroni ili tubaki na Kiingereza chetu cha ya, ya, yes no yes no.

eng: At the same time their children are speaking English fluently.
swa: Wakati watoto wao wanamwaga ngeli ya maana.

eng: We are still very far, Oliver, even public notices and government information in many places are still in English.
swa: Kwetu bado sana Oliver hata matangazo na sehemu nyingi ya masuala ya serikali yapo Kiingereza.

eng: Josephat Rugemalira observed that the new policy is not as radical as people think:
swa: Josephat Rugemalira alibaini kwamba sera mpya haina mabadiliko makubwa kinyume na watu wanavyofikiri:

eng: You need to read carefully what the policy says: it says Swahili will be used at all levels and ALSO says English will be used at all levels (that means including primary level).
swa: Unahitaji kusoma kwa makini sera inavyosema: Inasema Kiswahili kitafundishwa katika ngazi zote na PIA inasema Kiingereza kitaendelea kutumika katika ngazi zote (maana yake ni pamoja na shule ya msingi).

eng: So my interpretation is that the only NEW thing made possible by such statements is that it is possible now for some people to establish Swahili medium secondary schools, and it is now official that local government authorities can convert existing primary schools to become English medium.
swa: Kwa hiyo tafsiri yangu ni kwamba jambo pekee jipya linalowezekana kupitia kauli kama hizi ni kuwepo kwa uwezekano kwamba sasa baadhi ya watu wanaweza kuanzisha Shule za Sekondari zinazofundisha kwa Kiswahili, na kwamba sasa ni rasmi mamlaka za serikali za mitaa zinaweza kugeuza shule za msingi zilizopo kuwa za Kiingereza.

eng: Reacting to the same article posted on Trending Kenya, Margaret Njeru explained that the new system does not kick out foreign or second languages but put them in their appropriate places in the learning process:
swa: Akijibu makala hiyo hiyo iliyochapishwa kwenye mtandao wa Trending Kenya, Margaret Njeru alieleza kwamba mfumo huo mpya wa elimu haipigi teke lugha za kigeni bali kuziweka katika nafasi sahihi katika mafunzo:

eng: Indeed, bold and in the right direction.
swa: Kwa hakika, hatua hii ni ya kijasiri na ni mwelekeo sahihi.

eng: Education is about development, and that development can only come through a language a people make sense of.
swa: Elimu ni maendeleo, na maendeleo yanaweza kuja tu kupitia lugha inayoeleweka vizuri kwa watu.

eng: The world over, none of the so-called developed economies operates in a foreign language, and the use of the former colonial languages in many African countries has definitely contributed to the marginalization of the majority in the development process.
swa: Duniani kote, hakuna nchi zinazosemekana kuwa zimeendelea zinazotumia lugha za kigeni. Matumizi ya lugha za wakoloni waliotawala nchi nyingi za Afrika yamechangia kubaguliwa kwa wananchi wengi katika mchakato wa maendeleo.

eng: If we have to define "our" development path, then the language choice must go hand-in-hand with it.
swa: Kama tunapaswa kutafsiri njia ya maendeleo 'yetu', basi uchaguzi wa lugha lazima uende sambamba na njia hiyo.

eng: And this does not in any way mean kicking out the foreign (or second languages), rather putting them in their appropriate place in the learning process.
swa: Na hii haimaanishi kwa vyovyote kuzipiga teke lugha za kigeni (au zile tunzojifunza ukubwani), badala yake ni kuziweka katika nafasi inayozifaa katika ufundishaji na ujifunzaji.

eng: Kwame Aboagye said it is time Africans used their languages:
swa: Kwame Aboagye alisema ni wakati sasa wa-Afrika watumie lugha zao wenyewe:

eng: It is about time that our African countries should speak our own dialects such as Twi, Yoruba, Swahili and Mandingo.
swa: Wakati umewadia nchi zetu za ki-Afrika ziongee lugha zetu wenyewe kama vile ki-Twi, ki-Yoruba, ki-Swahili na ki-Mandingo.

eng: English wasn't our original language in the first place and we need to wake-up and go back to our principals with pride.
swa: Kiingereza hakikuwa lugha yetu ya asili na tunahitaji kuamka na kurejea misingi yetu wenyewe kwa fahari.

eng: The shift is monumental but it comes with significant challenges, noted Christina Higgins:
swa: Mabadiliko hayo ni ya kihistoria lakini yanakuja na changamoto kadhaa, kama alivyobainisha Christina Higgins:

eng: What good news indeed.
swa: Habari njema kabisa.

eng: Now the big test will be how to transition to Swahili in terms of materials, exams, and more.
swa: Sasa jaribio kubwa litakuwa namna ya kutafsiri kwa Kiswahili vitabu, mitihani na zaidi.

eng: Despite challenges, this shift is truly monumental.
swa: Pamoja na changamoto zake, mabadiliko haya ni ya kihistoria.

eng: Children in Tripoli in August 2011.
swa: Watoto wakiwa huko Tripoli, Agusti, 2011.

eng: Photo by MITSUYOSHI IWASHIGE.
swa: Picha na MITSUYOSHI IWASHIGE.

eng: Copyright Demotix
swa: Haki miliki Demotix

eng: This article and radio report by Shirin Jaafari for The World originally appeared on PRI.org on February 26, 2015, and is republished as part of a content-sharing agreement.
swa: Makala na taarifa hii ya habari iliyoandaliwa na Shirin Jaafari kwa ajili ya kipindi cha redio kiitwacho The World kwa mara ya kwanza ilionekana kwenye tovuti ya PRI.org siku ya tarehe 26 Februari 2015, inachapishwa tena chini ya makubaliano ya ushirikiano wa maudhui.

eng: As Libya was torn apart by a revolution in 2011, Haifa El-Zahawi left the country for the United States.
swa: Katika kipindi ambacho Libya ilikuwa ikiharibiwa vibaya kutokana na mapinduzi yaliyotokea mwaka 2011, ndicho kipindi hicho hicho Haifa El-Zahawi aliondoka kuelekea Marekani.

eng: Now a dentist, she's looking for jobs.
swa: Kwa sasa anatafuta kazi akiwa kama daktari wa afya ya kinywa.

eng: But she's also devoting herself to a different project: Teaching kids back in Libya.
swa: Lakini pia, anautumia muda wake katika mradi mwingine tofauti: Anafundisha watoto nchini Libya.

eng: The volatile security situation there has kept kids out of school since October.
swa: Hali tete ya kiusalama nchini Libya imewafanya watoto washindwe kwenda shule tangu mwezi Oktoba.

eng: So if kids can't get to their classrooms, El-Zahawi thought, why not bring the classroom to them?
swa: Kwa kuwa watoto hawawezi tena kuhudhuria masomo katika shule zao, El-Zahawi aliwaza ni kwa nini asisogeze madarasa karibu na huko walipo?

eng: The Benghazi Skype School was born.
swa: Na hapa ndipo Shule ya Skype ya Benghazi ilipozaliwa rasmi.

eng: We started with a personal account and a Skype, says El-Zahawi from New York.
swa: Tulianza na akaunti ya mtu binafsi pamoja na Skype, anasema El-Zahawi akiwa mjini New York.

eng: She posted about her project on social media, asking Libyans if they were able to help.
swa: Aliweka taarifa za mradi wake huu katika mitandao ya kijamii akiwaomba raia wa Libya kumsaidia.

eng: Within a week, she was receiving "a really huge and positive response."
swa: Katika muda wa wiki moja amepata "matokeo makubwa na ya kutia moyo kabisa."

eng: She even heard from an IT company in Libya that wanted to sponsor her project.
swa: Pia alipata habari kuwa kuna kampuni moja ya Teknolojia ya Mawasiliano ilitaka kumfadhili.

eng: Of course, Internet classrooms have their own problems.
swa: Hata hivyo, masomo kupitia mtandao wa intaneti yana changamoto zake.

eng: Patchy Internet connections are a major hurdle, as are the frequent power outages that Libyans face.
swa: Upatikanaji wa mtandao wa intaneti usiotabirika ni kikwazo kikubwa kinachochangiwa na tatizo la kukatika kwa umeme mara kwa mara linalowakabili raia wa Libya.

eng: We try and make live as much as we can, but due to the problems ... we try to record the lessons and post them online, El-Zahawi says.
swa: Tunajaribu kwa kadiri tuwezavyo kuhakikisha wanafunzi wanapata masomo papo kwa hapo, lakini kutokana na changamoto zilizopo ... tunajaribu kurekodi masomo na kisha kuyapakia mtandaoni, El-Zahawi anasema.

eng: But despite the challenges, the Benghazi Skype School has been a success so far.
swa: Lakini, pamoja na changamoto hizi, Shule ya Skype ya Benghazi hadi sasa imekuwa na mafanikio makubwa.

eng: Families send us pictures of the students doing their homework, El-Zahawi says.
swa: Familia zimetutumia picha zinazoonesha wanafunzi wakifanya kazi wanazopewa na mwalimu wao, El-Zahawi anasema.

eng: They're even wearing their school uniforms.
swa: Pia, wanavaa sare zao za shule.

eng: The bigger idea behind the school, El-Zahawi says, is to bring hope to the families and kids who "really need it."
swa: Wazo kuu la kuanzisha shule hii, El-Zahawi anasema ni kurudisha matumaini kwa familia na watoto "wanaohitaji elimu."

eng: She's worried about news like the recent beheading of a group of men in Libya at the hands of ISIS, and she hopes that educating Libyan children will help stop the spread of radicalization.
swa: Anaogopeshwa na habari kama hii ya hivi karibuni ya kuchinjwa kwa watu kadhaa nchini Libya na kundi la ISIS, na anaamini kuwa kwa kuwaelimisha watoto wa Libya kutasaidia kukomesha kuenea kwa ukatili huu.

eng: We have to educate our kids, she says, "Only by learning, we can fight."
swa: Tunahitaji kuwapatia elimu watoto wetu, anasema, "elimu tu ndiyo itakayotusaida kupambana na hali hii."

eng: Do you know Kenyan technology companies that got funded in 2014?
swa: Je, unayajua makampuni ya teknolojia nchini Kenya yaliyopata ufadhili kwa mwaka 2014?

eng: Child labor exploitation is worsening in the Philippines.
swa: Hali ya utumikishaji wa watoto nchini Ufilipino inazidi kushamiri.

eng: In 2011, the Philippine National Statistics Office reported that there were 5.5 million working children in the country, 2.9 million of whom were working in hazardous industries such as mining and plantations.
swa: Mwaka 2011, Ofisi ya Takwimu ya Ufilipino ilitaarifu kuwa kulikuwa na watoto milioni 5.5 waliokuwa wakitu mikishwa, miongoni mwao, milioni 2.9 walikuwa wakifanya kazi kwenye viwanda vilivyo hatari kwa afya yao kama vile vya migodi na mashamba makubwa.

eng: The agency added that 900,000 children have stopped attending school in order to work.
swa: Taasisi hii ya serikali iliongeza kuwa, watoto 900,000 walisitisha msomo kwa ajili ya kwenda kufanya kazi.

eng: These alarming numbers highlight the poor conditions experienced by many Filipino children, who lack key social services and access to welfare.
swa: Idadi hii inaashiria hali tete inayowakabili watoto wengi wa Ufilipino, ambao wanakosa mahitaji muhimu ya kijamii pamoja na kukosa kuthaminiwa.

eng: The Philippines is a signatory to the Convention on the Rights of the Child and other international instruments that aim to promote the welfare of children.
swa: Ufilipino ni moja ya nchi iliyoingia mkataba wa Makubaliano kuhusu Haki za Mtoto pamoja na kwenye t mashirika mengie ya kimataifa yaliyo na malengo ya kulinda mustakabali wa watoto.

eng: There is also a popular initiative to build child-friendly government, especially at local level.
swa: Pia, kuna mkakati maarufu wa kuwa na serikali inayowajali watoto, husani kwa maeneo ya vijijini.

eng: But these laws and programs have not succeeded in eliminating the various forms of abuse, poverty and deprivation experienced by many children.
swa: Hata hivyo, sheria hizi pamoja na mikakati hii bado haijafanikiwa kutokomeza aina mbalimbali za uonevu, umasikini na hali ya kukosa malazi na chakula kunakowakabili watoto wengi.

eng: Last month, the Ecumenical Institute for Labor Education Research (EILER) published a baseline study which confirmed the prevalence of child labor in mines and plantations in various parts of the country.
swa: Mwezi uliopita, Taasisi ya Kidini ya Tafiti za Elimu ya Ajira(EILER) ilitoa taarifa ya utafiti msingi ambao ulithibitisha kuendelea kuwepo kwa utumikishwaji wa watoto migodini pamoja na kwenye mashamba makubwa katika maeneo mbalimbali nchini Ufilipino.

eng: In plantation communities, about 22.5 percent of households have child workers.
swa: Kwenye jamii za watu wanaohusika na mahsmba makubwa, takribani asilimia 22.5 ya makazi ya watu yana watoto wanaofanya kazi katika mashamba hayo.

eng: In mining towns, child labor incidence was 14 percent.
swa: Kwenye maeneo ya migodi, matukio ya watoto kufanyishwa kazi yalionekana kwa asilimia 14.

eng: Child laborers in oil palm fields often serve as fruiters, harvesters, haulers, loaders, and uprooters.
swa: Kwenye mashamba ya miti ya mafuta ya michikichi, mara nyingi watoto hufanyishwa kazi za kupanda, kuvuna, kupakua, kupakia pamoja na kung’oa mimea.

eng: Meanwhile, child labourers in sugarcane estates work weeding, harvesting and fetching water.
swa: Kwa upande mwingine, watoto wanaotumikishwa katika mashamba ya miwa hufanya kazi za palizi, kuvuna pamoja na kuchota maji.

eng: In mines, child labourers usually fetch water, carry sacks of rocks, load the thick logs used to support the underground tunnels, or become errand boys for regular workers.
swa: Kwenye migodi, watoto hutumikiswa kwenye kazi kama vile za kuchota maji, kubeba viroba vya udongo, au kukusanya magogo manene kwa ajili ya kuimarisha njia za ardhini, au wanaweza kuwa wajakazi wa wafanyakazi wazoefu wa mgodini.

eng: They are also reserve workers and 'relievers', whenever regular miners cannot come to work.
swa: Pia, watoto huwa ni wafanyakazi wa ziada na “wapokezi” hususani pale wachimbaji madini wa kudumu hawatafika kazini.

eng: Girls in mines work in gold panning or providing services to miners such as doing their laundry or cooking meals.
swa: Watoto wa kike kwenye migodi hufanya kazi ya kuchambua dhahabu au kutoa huduma anuai kwa wachimbaji madini kama vile kuwafulia nguo au kuwapikia chakula.

eng: EILER observed that child workers are exposed to extreme weather conditions, long working hours and a difficult environment while using substandard tools and equipment.
swa: EILER iligundua kuwa, watoto wanaotumikishwa hufanyishwa kazi kwenye hali mbaya ya hewa, kufanya kazi kwa muda mrefu sana na kwenye mazingira magumu huku wakitumia zana na vifaa vya kufanyia kazi ambavyo ni duni.

eng: In plantations, trucks pick children up from their homes and bring them to makeshift tents located in nearby provinces to stay and work for periods lasting from two weeks to a month without their parents.
swa: Kwenye mashamba makubwa, magari huwachukua watoto kutoka majumbani kwao na kuwapeleka kujenga mahema karibu na maeneo ya miji na kasha huishi humo wakifanya kazi kwa vipindi vya kati ya wiki mbili hadi mwezi mmoja na bila ya kuwa na wazazi wao.

eng: Since most plantations use harmful agro-chemicals, the children working on them are directly exposed to these threats.
swa: Kwwa kuwa mashamba mengi makubwa hutumia viuatilifu, watoto wanaofanya kazi katika mashamba haya huwa katika hatari kubwa ya kuathiriwa na viuatilifu hivi.

eng: Their counterparts working in mines, meanwhile, are handling dangerous tools and are made to work without protective equipment for long hours.
swa: Wenzao wanaofanya kazi kwenye migodi, wakati huo huo, huwa wanatumia vifaa ambavyo ni hatari na wanafanyishwa kazi kwa muda mrefu na bila ya kuwa na vitu vya kuwakinga na hatari mbalimbali.

eng: Social hazards such as the use of illegal drugs to keep children inside the tunnels awake for hours are also a regular feature of the country's mines.
swa: Matumizi ya vitu hatarishi kwa jamii kama vile madawa ya kulevya ya kuwafanya watoto waingie migodini na kufanya kazi kwa muda mrefu ni mambo ya kawaida kwenye migodi.

eng: Pitang holding a placard which reads: "I am a child labourer".
swa: Mtoto akiwa amebeba bango linalosomeka: "Mimi ni mtoto inayefanyiPitang holding a placard which reads: "I am a child labourer".

eng: Photo from the Facebook page of Jhona Ignilan Stokes
swa: Picha kutoka Ukurasa wa Facebook wa Jhona Ignilan Stokes

eng: A former child worker from Mindanao, Pitang, shares her experience in the plantations during a recent public forum organized by EILER:
swa: Pitang, kutoka Mindanao, ambaye ni mmoja wa watoto waliokuwa wakitumikishwa aelezea uzoefu wake wa kufanya kazi kwenye mashamba makubwa wakati wa mijadala ya wazi iliyoandaliwa na EILER:

eng: I was ten years old when I stopped going to school.
swa: Niliacha kwenda shule nikiwa na umri wa miaka 10.

eng: I have lost hope that I might still go back to school, and I thought to myself that I would be a singer instead.
swa: Nilishapoteza tumaini la kuwa siku moja nitarudi tena shuleni, na nilifikiri kuwa mwimbaji badala yake.

eng: I usually sing to endure and forget the feeling of pain and fatigue from working in plantation.
swa: Mara nyingi huwa napenda kuimba kama namna ya kukabiliana na kusahau hisia za maumivu na uchovu niliokuwa nikiupata katika mashamba makubwa.

eng: It has been four years since I stopped schooling.
swa: Ni miaka mine sasa imepita tangu nilipoacha shule.

eng: I only reached the sixth grade level and then had to stop so I could work.
swa: Niliweza kufika darasa la sita peke yake na hapo nililazimiaka kuachana na masomo ili nikafanye kazi.

eng: Fortunately, there are groups like EILER which are campaigning for the elimination of the worst forms of child labor in the country.
swa: Kwa bahati nzuri, yamekuwepo makundi kama vile EILER yanayoendesha kampeni ya kukemea aina mbalimbali za utumikishwaji wa watoto nchini Philippenes.

eng: One of their programs is Balik-Eskuwela (Return to School) which seeks to bring child workers back to school.
swa: Moja ya miradi yao ni Balik-Eskuwela (Rudi shuleni) ambao una lengo la kuwarudisha mashuleni watoto wanaotumikishwa.

eng: The European Union is one of EILER's partners on this project.
swa: Umoja wa Ulaya ni moja ya washirika wa EILER katika mradi huu.

eng: Child workers return to school.
swa: Watoto wanaofatumikishwa kazi warudi shuleni.

eng: Photo from the Facebook page of Balik-eskuwela *All photos by EILER, used with permission
swa: Picha kutoka ukurasa wa Facebook wa Balik-eskuwela *Picha zote kutoka EILER, na zimetumiwa kwa ruhusa

eng: A shooting in a restaurant in Bamako, capital city of Mali, claimed the lives of five people on Friday night, March, 6.
swa: Shambuliko la kigaidi lilitekelezwa kwenye mgahawa jijini Bamako, makao makuu ya Mali, limechukua maisha ya watu watano usiku wa siku ya Ijumaa mnamo Machi, 6.

eng: The attack took place around midnight in a restaurant called La Terrasse in Downtown Bamako and a dozen people are seriously injured.
swa: Shambulio hilo lilifanyika usiku wa maneno kwenye mkahawa unaoitwa took Terrasse kwenye mitaa ya Bamako na watu zaidi ya kumi wamejeruhiwa vibaya.

eng: Two suspects are in detention and are being interrogated by security forces.
swa: Washukuiwa wawili wamekamatwa na wanaendelea kuhojiwa na vyombo vya ulinzi na usalama.

eng: A local officer reports that the two individuals were armed and hooded.
swa: Afisa wa polisi aliripoti kwamba watu hao wawili walikuwa na silaha kali pamoja na mavazi ya kijeshi.

eng: One burst into the restaurant and opened fire.
swa: Mtu mmoja alilipua bomu kwenye mkahawa.

eng: Three Malians, one French and one Belgian were killed.
swa: Raia wawili wa watatu, Mfaransa mmoja na raia mwingine wa Ubelgiji waliuawa.

eng: A local blogger posted a video of police forces as they come to investigate the crime scene:
swa: Mwanablogu mmoja aliweka video inayoonesha vikosi vya polisi waliokuwa wakifanya uchunguzi kwenye eneo la tukio:

eng: Global Voices contributor Marc- André Boisvert wrote on Twitter that such an attack was inevitable, given that Mali is still trying to re-establish peace in the northern region:
swa: Mchangiaji wa Global Voices Marc- André Boisvert aliandika kwenye mtandao wa twita kwamba shambulio kama hilo halikuwa linaepukika, kwa sababu Mali bado inajitahidi kurudisha hali ya amani kwenye ukanda huo wa Kaskazini:

eng: We all knew it would happen in #Bamako.
swa: Sote tulijua tukio hili lingetokea mjini Bamako.

eng: We all knew that the rue du #BlaBla would be a target.
swa: Sote tunajua shabaha ilikuwa kuwalenga wapiga kelele.

eng: Philippe Paoletta, a resident of Bamako, agrees with Marc-André:
swa: Philippe Paoletta, mkazi wa Bamako, anakubaliana na Marc-André:

eng: Everyone always thought this was bound to happen at some point in #bamako.
swa: Kila moja alijua yaliyotokea yangetokea wakati fulani hapa Bamako.

eng: Doesn't make it any less shocking or horrifying.
swa: Hata hivyo hiyo haifanyi hali hiyo isiwe ya kushangaza.

eng: All our thoughts are with the victims of the attack.
swa: Tunawatakia majeruhi wa shambulio kupona kwa haraka.

eng: A screenshot of a YouTube video posted by Ren TV showing an attack on an Ethiopian national.
swa: Picha ya video ya You tube iliyowekwa na A Ren TV ikionesha kushambuliwa kwa raia wa Ethiopia.

eng: Recent violence in Kwa-Zulu Natal and Durban is being attributed to comments made by the Zulu King Goodwill Zwelithini, who allegedly told foreigners to go home.
swa: Mashambulizi ya hivi karibuni huko Kwa-Zulu Natal na Durban yanahusishwa na kauli iliyotolewa na mfalme wa Zulu Goodwill Zwelithini. Inasemekana kuwa aliwataka wahamiaji warudi makwao.

eng: The attacks involved beatings, killings, and burning and looting shops and property owned by foreigners.
swa: Mashambulizi hayo yalihusisha watu kupigwa, kuuawa, kuchomwa moto, wizi madukani pamoja na wizi wa mali za wahamiaji.

eng: Five people have been killed, including a 14-year-old boy who was shot on Monday.
swa: Watu watano wameshauawa, miongoni mwao akiwamo mvulana wa miaka 14 aliyeuawa siku ya jumatatu.

eng: Over 1,000 foreigners have fled their homes.
swa: Zaidi ya wahamiaji 1,000 wameyakimbia makazi yao.

eng: Some South Africans accuse foreigners of taking away jobs, businesses, and engaging in criminal activities.
swa: Baadhi ya watu wa Afrika Kusini wanawatuhumu wahamiaji kuwachukulia nafasi zao za kazi, biashara, pamoja na kujihusisha na uhalifu.

eng: Between 2000 and 2008, at least 67 people died in xenophobic attacks.
swa: Kati ya mwaka 2000 na 2008, takribani watu 67 walipoteza maishakwenye shambulio dhidi ya wahamiaji.

eng: In May 2008, a series of riots left 60 people dead.
swa: Mnamo Mei 2008, mfululizo wa machafuko ulisababisha watu 60 kupoteza maisha.

eng: In January this year, four people were killed in Johannesburg in similar attacks.
swa: Mapema mwezi wa Januari mwaka huu, watu wanne walipoteza maisha huko Johannesburg kutokana na matukio ya aina hii.

eng: Using the hashtags #XenophobicSA and #AfrophobicSA South Africans and non-South Africans immediately took to Twitter to express their disgust and shock at the brutality displayed by South Africans and lack of action from the South African government.
swa: Kwa kutumia viungo habari#XenophobicSA na #AfrophobicSA raia wa Afrika Kusini na wale wasio wa Afrika Kusini kwa haraka kupitia mtandao wa Twitter walionesha kuchukizwa na kushtushwa na ukatili uliofanywa na raia wa Afrika Kusini pamoja na Serikali ya Afrika Kusini kushindwa kuchukua hatua kufuatia tukio hili.

swa: Ni dhahiri kuwa nilikuwa najidanganya. #XenophobicSA — Nyawira Njoroge (@NyawiraNjoroge) April 11, 2015

swa: Njia rahisi kabisa ya kupata kazi ifanywayo na mhamiaji ni kwenda shule na siyo kuchukua silaha. #XenophobicSA #xenophobicattacks — Abi Mwachi M.D (@abimwachi) April 10, 2015

swa: Nkt — Joan mumbua (@Joangor25) April 10, 2015

swa: Kitendo cha kuondoa sanamu za kikoloni kimefuatiwa na watu wa Afrika Kusini kuwaondosha waafrika wenzao siku iliyofuata #XenophobicSA — Ashley Mendelowitz (@AshMendelo) April 11, 2015

swa: Wakati kinachotokea Afrika ya Kusini kinasikitisha, kuwa mwangalifu katika kusambaza picha za zamani za machafuko nchini Afrika Kusini& wakizifanya kama vile ni za hivi karibuni. #XenophobicSA — larry kwirirayi (@kwirirayi) April 15, 2015

swa: Mashambulizi dhidi ya wahamiaji hayahusiani na watu wanaovuka mpaka wa nchi kinyume na utaratibu, kinachotkea ni kulazimishwa kuwachukia Waafrika wenzetu. #XenophobicSA — Thapelo (@mokhathi) April 11, 2015

swa: Ndugu wakiwa kwenye foleni kwenye sehemu itoayo huduma za mazishi jijini Nairobi kwa ajili ya kuwatambua marehemu waliouawa katika shambulio ya Chuo Kikuu Kishiriki cha Garissa kilicho kaskazini mwa Kenya.

eng: Photo by Boniface Muthoni.
swa: Picha na Boniface Muthoni.

eng: Al-Shabaab militants attacked Garissa University College in Kenya on 2 April 2015, killing at least 147 people, mostly students, and injuring 79.
swa: Wanamgambo wa Al-Shabaab walishambulia Chuo Kikuu kishiriki cha Garissa nchini Kenya mnamo Aprili 2 2015, na kuwaua watu wasiopungua 147, wengi wao wakiwa ni wanafunzi, na kuwajeruhi wengine 79.

eng: More than eight times as many people were cut down by the violence than were killed during the Charlie Hebdo shooting in France, which left 17 dead, yet the Garissa tragedy hasn't prompted anywhere near the same level of international solidarity as the Paris attack.
swa: Idadi hii ni mara nane ya watu waliouawa wakati wa shambulio la Charlie Hebdo nchini Ufaransa, liliua watu wapatao 17, lakini inashangaza kwamba tukio baya kabisa la Garissa halijaonekana kuifanya dunia itoe mshikamano kwa kiwango kile kile kama ilivyokuwa kwenye shambulio la Paris.

eng: There was a similar criticism after the Baga massacre in Nigeria, which occurred around the same time as the Charlie Hebdo killings.
swa: Hali kama hiyo ilijitokeza baada ya mauaji ya Baga nchini Naijeria, yaliyotokea karibu wakati huo huo wa mauaji ya Charlie Hebdo.

swa: Wakati tukio la Charlie hebdo lilivuta hisia za hisia za watu wengi huku zaidi ya wakuu 40 wa nchi walishiriki kwenye mkutano wa mshikamano wa kitaifa, tukio la Mauaji ya Baga halikupewa uzito unaostahili.

eng: Observers criticised what coverage Western media did give the attack, as well.
swa: Wachunguzi walikosoa kile kilichokuwa kikitangazwa na vyombo vya habari vya ki-Magharibi na walishambulia, hali kadhalika.

eng: After CNN wrongly placed Tanzania in Uganda and Nairobi in Nigeria on a map of East Africa, the Africa is a Country blog suggested that people switch off television news to make sense of the attack:
swa: Baada ya CNN kukosea na kuiweka Tanzania kwenye eneo la Uganda na Nairobi kuonekana iko Nigeria kwenye ramani ya Afrika Mashariki, Blogu ya Africa is a Country blog ilishauri kwamba watu wazime televisheni zao ili waweze kuelewa shambulio hili:

eng: To make sense of the attack by Al Shabaab on Garissa University near Kenya’s border with Somalia (official count of fatalities are 148; others say closer to 200), you may want to switch off television news.
swa: Ili kuelewa shambulio hili lililofanywa na Al Shabaab kwenye Chuo Kikuu cha Garissa karibu na mpaka wa Kenya na Somalia (takwimu rasmi ni vifo 148; wengine wanasema 200), pengine utahitaji kzima taarifa za habari kwenye televisheni.

eng: Especially since CNN is moving Nairobi to Nigeria and Tanzania to Uganda.
swa: Hasa kwa sababu CNN imeihamishia Nairobi kwenda Naijeria na Tanzania kwenda Uganda.

eng: Crucial will be how these attacks will be framed in the next few hours and especially how the Kenyan state will respond (already they’ve blamed the judiciary and in the past they’ve round up Somalis despite little evidence).
swa: Tusichokijua ni namna gani mashambulizi haya yataelezewa ndani ya masaa machache yajayo na namna gani serikali ya Kenya itashughulikia janga hili (tayari wanalaumu mahakama na siku za nyuma waliwahusisha wa-Somali pamoja na kuwa na ushahidi mdogo).

eng: Equally important is public opinion.
swa: Kilichomuhimu ni maoni ya umma.

eng: So, like we did at the time of the attack by Al Shabaab on the Westgate Mall in Kenya’s capital Nairobi, we’ve compiled a bunch of links, including some twitter accounts, we suggest you read or follow.
swa: Kwa hiyo, kama tulivyofanya wakati wa shambulio lililopangwa na Al Shabaab kwenye jengo la kibiashara la Westgate kwenye mji mkuu wa Kenya, Nairobi, tumekusanya viungo vingi, ikiwa ni pamoja na anuani za mtandao wa twita, tunapendekeza uzisome au kuzifuatilia.

eng: Idriss Ali Nassah stressed the need for Africa to tell its own stories:
swa: Idriss Ali Nassah alisisitiza uhitaji wa Afrika kutangaza habari zake yenyewe:

eng: BBC is broadcasting a debate, CNN is fixated on the Iran nuclear deal.
swa: BBC wanatangaza mdahalo, CNN haina habari na mambo mengine ziadi ya mpango wa nyuklia wa Iran.

eng: Africa needs own media houses to tell our stories #GarrisaAttack — Idriss Ali Nassah (@mynassah) April 2, 2015
swa: Afrika inahitaji vyombo vyake vya hbari kusimuliza habari zake yenyewe

eng: KiGossip.Com wondered why a CNN journalist would ask a survivor if he/she was scared:
swa: Mtandao wa KiGossip.Com uishangaa kwa nini mwandishi wa habari wa CNN alimwuliza mtu aliyenusurika kifo kama ameogopa:

eng: So, a CNN Journalist asked a survivor from the Garrisa Attack: 'WERE YOU SCARED'?
swa: Kwa hiyo, mwandishi wa habari wa CNN alimwuliza mtu aliyenusurika kifo kwenye shambulio la Garissa: "HIVI ULIOGOPA'?

eng: Absolute MADNESS...
swa: Huu ni UPUUZI...kwa nini hajafukuzwa?

eng: However, a few users noted that even local media houses are not doing a good job:
swa: Hata hivyo, watumiaji wachache wa mtandao wa twita walibaini kwamba hata vyombo vya ndani ya bara la Afrika havifanyi kazi nzuri:

eng: Let's just agree that local media did/has done a shoddy job in covering #GarrisaAttack.
swa: Tukubaliane kwamba vyombo vya ndani navyo vimefanya kazi mbaya katika kutangaza habari za shambulio la Garissa.

eng: Bait headlines and shallow reporting. — PluckyAdage (@PluckyAdage) April 5, 2015
swa: Vichwa vya habari vya kidaku na kutoa habari zisizojitosheleza

eng: As @StandardKenya runs pictures of families in pain but quotes from politicians.
swa: Gazeti la @StandardKenya limechapisha picha za familia zinazoomboleza lakini likinukuu wanasiasa.

eng: Africans blaming the West from moving on so fast from the #GarrisaAttack yet our own media moved on first. — AyoBrayo (@iOceanBrayo) April 6, 2015
swa: Waafrika wanazilaumu nchi za Magharibi kwa kuachana na habari za Shambulio la Garissa mapema lakini hata vyombo vyenu navyo viliachana na habari hizo mapema

eng: JuwelsM argued that Africans should drive their own narrative:
swa: JuwelsM alihoji kwamba Waafrika waanze kuamua mambo gani yana uzito kwao:

eng: @mynassah We r all terribly guilty of undervaluing ourselves.Perhaps it's time we stop waiting 4 the West 2 decide 4 us what's important. — JuwelsM. (@JuwelsM) April 5, 2015
swa: Sote tuna hatia kwa kujipuuza wenyewe. Labda tuanze kuachana na kasumba ya kusubiri nchi za Magharibi ziamue nini kina umuhimu kwetu.

eng: Last week a leading private university in Pakistan was forced to cancel an academic discussion on human rights in its southwestern province Balochistan “due to state intervention“.
swa: Juma lililopita Chuo Kikuu maarufu cha binafsi nchini Pakistani kililazimika kuahirisha mjadala wa kitaaluma kuhusu haki za binadamu kwenye jimbo la kusini magharibi la Balochistan “kwa sababu ya kuingiliwa na serikali“.

eng: Balochistan, Pakistan's largest, least populated and poorest province is witnessing its fifth separatist movement since 1947.
swa: Balochistani, jimbo kubwa zaidi nchini Pakistani, lenye idadi ndogo zaidi ya watu na lenye umasikini mkubwa linashuhudia vuguvugu la tano la kujitenga tangu mwaka 1947.

eng: Public discussions on Balochistan's war are rare.
swa: Majadiliano kuhusu vita vinavyoendelea Balochistani ni nadra.

eng: Nationalists think silence on Balochistan is their patriotic duty, others self-censor out of fear of Pakistan's powerful military.
swa: Watetezi wa utaifa wa nchi hiyo wanadhani kwamba kimya kwa hali ya mambo jimboni Balochistani ni wajibu wao, wengine wanajihadhari kwa hofu ya nguvu kubwa ya kijeshi iliyopo Pakistani.

eng: But few really understand what is going on in the province, because media coverage and reporting from there is thin.
swa: Lakini wachache wanaelewa kile kinachoendelea kwenye jimbo hilo, kwa sababu habari zinazoandikwa kutoka kwenye jimbo hilo ni chache mno.

eng: In this episode of GV Face, we break the silence on Balochistan by talking to Pakistani and Baloch activists and journalists who dare to speak out and report on human rights abuses in the province.
swa: Katika toleo hili la GV Face, tunavunja ukimya kuhusu jimbo la Balochistani kwa kuzungumza na wanaharakati na wanandishi wa Kipakistani na Kibalochi wanaothubutu kuzungumza na kuripoti kuhusu uvunjifu wa haki la binadamu kwenye jimbo hilo.

eng: Theses activists and journalists walk a thin dangerous line.
swa: Wanaharakati hawa na waandishi hawa wanafanya kazi kwenye mazingira yenye hatari.

eng: Mir Mohammad Ali Talpur (@mmtalpur), a veteran human rights activists who was a part of the cancelled LUMS talk will join us.
swa: Mir Mohammad Ali Talpur (@mmtalpur), mwanaharakati mkongwe wa haki za binadamu alikuwa sehemu ya mjadala wa kitaaluma uliofutwa ataungana nasi.

eng: We will also have Fahad Desmukh (@desmukh), who heads PakVoices, a news site that reports on communities in Balochistan's coastal areas, Adnan Aamir (@iadnanaamir), who heads the online publication Balochistan Point, and Ali Arqam (@aliarqam), an activist and reporter with Newsline magazine.
swa: Tutakuwa na Fahad Desmukh (@desmukh), anayeongoza PakVoices, tovuti ya habari inayoripoti kuhusu jamii zinazoishi kwenye maeneo ya pwani ya jimbo la Balochistani, Adnan Amir (@iadnanamir), anayeongoza chapisho la mtandaoni liitwalo Balochistan Point, na Ali Arqam (@aliarqam), mwanaharakati na mwandishi wa gazeti la Newsline

eng: Backstory
swa: Historia ya hali ya mambo

eng: Facts about the Balochistan conflict are hard to verify.
swa: Habari za kweli kuhusu mgogoro wa Balochistani ni ngumu kuthibitika.

eng: What we do know is that Baloch nationalists are seeking independence from Pakistan, and Pakistan's armed intelligence operatives are trying to suppress them, sometimes through extrajudicial “forced disappearances”.
swa: Kile tusichokijua ni kwamba wananchi wanaodai uhuru wa Balochistani kutoka Pakistani, na shughuli za kiintelejensia za kijeshi nchini humo zinajaribu kupunguza harakati hizi, wakati mwingine kupitia "kupotea kwa watu" kwa njia zilizo nje ya taratibu za kisheria.

eng: According to the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan, since 2010, the bodies of hundreds of Balochistan’s “missing people” have turned up dead bearing torture marks.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Tume ya Haki za Binadamu nchini Pakistani, tangu mwaka 2010, miili ya mamia ya Wabalochistani "waliopotea" wanasemekana kupoteza maisha wakiwa na majeraha ya kuteswa.

eng: In 2013 alone, 116 bodies were found across the province, 87 of which were identified by families who accused Pakistan’s security agencies of abducting their loved ones.
swa: Mwaka 2013 pekee, miili 116 ilipatikana kwenye jimbo hilo, kati ya hiyo 87 ilitambuliwa na familia zilizotuhumu vyombo vya usalama nchini Pakistani kwa kuwaua wapendwa wao.

eng: The government maintains that separatists are funded by “outside forces”.
swa: Serikali inasema kwamba watu wanaotaka kujitenga wanalipwa na “vikosi vya nje ya nchi hiyo”.

eng: Various sectarian and Islamist militias also use the area for recruitment training to fight wars in Iran and Afghanistan, both of which border Balochistan.
swa: Wanamgambo mbalimbali wa kidini na Kiislamu pia wanatumia eneo hilo kwa kuendesha mafunzo kwa ajili ya kuandaa wapiganaji wa vita nchini Irani na Afghanistani, nchi zote zikiwa kwenye mpaka wa Balochistan.

eng: These groups also launch attacks within Pakistan.
swa: Makundi haya pia yameanzisha mashambulizi ndani ya Pakistani.

eng: Sometimes these groups join forces in pursuit of money and resources.
swa: Wakati mwingine vikundi hivi vinaunganisha nguvu katika jitihada za kutafuta fedha na raslimali nyingine.

eng: The result is the people living in Balochistan have to protect themselves from several different dangerous ideologies.
swa: Matokeo yake ni watu wanaoishi Balochistani kujilinda wenyewe dhidi ya itikadi mbalimbali za hatari.

eng: Since 2001, thousands of ethnic Shia Hazaras, Balochistan's largest minority, have been killed by militant groups.
swa: Tangu mwaka 2001, maelfu ya kabila la Shia Hazara, ambalo ni kubwa katika makabila madogo yanayopatikana kwenye jimbo la Balochistani, wameuawa na vikundi vya wanamgambo.

eng: Many more have been forced to leave a province they've called home for generations.
swa: Wengi zaidi wamelazimisha kulihama jimbo hilo ambalo kwa vizazi vingi limekuwa ndiyo makazi yao.

eng: Some Baloch nationalist groups are trying to drive all non-Baloch and the Pakistan military out of the province.
swa: Baadhi ya makundi ya Wabalochi yanayopigania taifa lao yanajaribu kuwafukuza raia wasio Wabalochi pamoja na vikosi vya kijeshi vya Pakistani nje ya jimbo.

eng: Military convoys are bombed.
swa: Yapo matukio ya wanajeshi wanapigwa mabomu.

eng: Punjabi families who have lived in Balochistan for decades are now branded by some groups as unwanted “settlers”, hundreds have been killed in attacks and thousands forced to flee the violence.
swa: Familia za Punjabi zinazoishi kwenye jimbo la Balochistani kwa miongo mingi kwa sasa wamepachikwa majina ya vikundi vingine kama “walowezi” wasiohitajika, mamia wakiwa wameshauawa kwenye mashambulio na maelfu wakiwa wamelazimika kuyakimbia makazi yao kwa sababu ya ghasia.

eng: This text is part of the 46th #LunesDeBlogsGV (#MondayBlogsOnGlobalVoices) on March 23, 2015.
swa: Makala haya ni sehemu ya 46 ya #LunesDeBlogsGV (#JumatatuYaBloguGlobalVoices) siku ya Machi 23, 2015.

eng: On #LunesDeBlogsGV (#MondayOfBlogsOnGlobalVoices), we work to preserve blogs as an "endangered species", confronting the challenges that threaten their existence in today's digital jungle.
swa: Kwenye #LunesDeBlogsGV (#JumatatuyaBloguGlobalVoices), tunajitahidi kuzitunza blogu mithili ya "viumbe wanaoelekea kutoweka", kwa kushughulikia changamto zinazokabili uwepo wa blogu kwenye ulimwengu wa kidijitali.

eng: In a similar effort, the blogger Iván Lasso compiles stories about the future of blogging and the problems bloggers face today, when their content runs the risk of being lost in the abundance of different types and quality levels of information on the Internet.
swa: Jitihada kama hizi zinamfanya mwanablogu Iván Lasso kuchambua mustakabali wa kublogu na matatizo yanayowakabili wanablogu leo, wakati ambao maudhui yao yanakuwa kwenye hatari kubwa ya kupotea kufuatia wingi wa aina na ubora wa viwango vya taarifa zinazopatikana kwenye mtandao wa intaneti.

eng: The situation bloggers increasingly find online, Lasso argues, is approaching a "David and Goliath" situation.
swa: Hali wanayoendelea kukumbana nayo wanablogu mtandao, Lasso anasema, inakaribiana na ile ya "Daudi na Goliathi".

eng: Lasso says of the biggest issues for bloggers today:
swa: Lasso anazungumzia suala kubwa kwa wanablogu leo:

eng: In recent years, following the popularity of the Web, there is a much larger audience available.
swa: Katika miaka ya hivi karibuni, kutokana na kuongezeka kwa matumizi makubwa ya Mtandao, kuna hadhira kubwa ya wasomaji inayofikika.

eng: But I suspect that much of this audience will never be yours.
swa: Lakini nina wasiwasi kwamba hadhira hii inaweza isimsaidie mwanablogu.

eng: Its's an audience that comes to the Net looking for simple entertainment and when they want more "hard" information, they go to the traditional mainstream media which is also on the Web.
swa: Sababu ni kwamba hii ni hadhira inayokuja mtandaoni kutafuta habari nyepesi za burudani na wanapohitaji taarifa 'muhimu', wanazitafuta kwenye vyombo vikuu vya habari ambavyo navyo vinapatikana mtandaoni.

eng: Lasso also offers some solutions for the challenges bloggers face:
swa: Lasso anatoa ufumbuzi kwa changamoto hizi wanazokabiliana nazo wanablogu:

eng: Nowadays, for an independent blog to have a certain degree of success (recognition, reputation, and views), you must become a laser beam focused on what readers want:
swa: Siku za leo, kwa blogu huru kuwa na mafanikio ya kiasi fulani (kutambuliwa, heshima, na hata kutembelewa), lazima ujifunze kujua wasomaji wanahitaji nini na ukizingatie:

eng: You want to report news?
swa: Unataka kutoa habari kupitia blogu yako?

eng: You must give it them as soon as possible, faster than anyone.
swa: Zitoe mapema kadri inavyowezekana, mapema kabla hazijaonekana kwingineko.

eng: You want to offer analysis and points of view?
swa: Unataka kufanya uchambuzi na kutoa maoni yako?

eng: You must go deeper than anyone.
swa: Nenda ndani zaidi kuliko wengine.

eng: You want to be instructional?
swa: Unataka kutoa elimu?

eng: You have to explain things better than anyone.
swa: Elezea mambo kwa ufasaha kuliko wengine.

eng: And be more specific than anyone.
swa: Na zungumzia masuala mahususi yanayowagusa watu.

eng: Continue reading Ivan Lasso's post here, and follow him on Twitter.
swa: Endelea kusoma makala ya Ivan Lasso hapa, na mfuatilie kwenye mtandao wa Twita.

eng: This text is part of the 46th #LunesDeBlogsGV (#MondayOfBlogsOnGlobalVoices) on March 23, 2015.
swa: Hii ni sehemu ya 46 ya #LunesDeBlogsGV (#JumatatuYaBloguGlobalVoices) mnamo Machi 23, 2015.

eng: Voters line up at a polling station in Nyendo Masaka, Uganda, on February 18, 2011.
swa: Wapiga kura wakiwa wamejipanga kwenye kituo cha kupigia kura huko Nyendo Masaka, Uganda, mnamo Februari 18, 2011.

eng: Photo by Peter Beier.
swa: Picha na Peter Beier.

eng: Copyright Demotix
swa: Haki miliki Demotix

eng: American think tank International Republican Institute (IRI) released the results of an opinion poll at the end of March, which revealed that a majority of Ugandans are generally satisfied with government performance.
swa: Shirika la Kimarekani liitwalo International Republican Institute (IRI) lilitoa matokeo ya utafiti wake mwisho wa mwezi Machi, yaliyoonesha kwamba Waganda wengi wameridhishwa na utendaji wa serikali yao.

eng: Over two-thirds of respondents (69 percent) said the country is headed in the right direction.
swa: Zaidi ya theluthi mbili ya waliohojiwa (asilimia 69) walisema kwamba kwamba serikali iko kwenye njia sahihi katika kutekeleza majukumu yake.

eng: In particular, those polled thought the government was performing well or very well in managing the economy, reducing crime and delivering basic services in terms of health, clean water, roads and education.
