swa: Kwa mujibu wa matokeo hayo, wale waliotoa maoni yao wanadhani serikali ilikuwa inafanya vizuri au vizuri sana kwenye kusimamia uchumi, kupunguza uhalifu na kutoa huduma za msingi za jamii kama vile afya, maji safi, barabara na elimu.

eng: However, the government did register poor marks on fighting corruption, with 69 percent of respondents thinking that authorities were handling corruption badly or very badly.
swa: Hata hivyo, serikali ilionekana kufanya vibaya kwenye eneo la kupambana na ufisadi, huku asilimia 69 ya waliohojiwa wakifikiri kwamba mamlaka zinazohusika hazikuwa zikishughulikia tatizo la ufisadi inavyotakiwa.

eng: The findings prompted a lively debate in social networks and on mainstream media, with many commenters questioning how so many Ugandans could think the country, where President Yoweri Museveni has ruled for nearly three decades, was headed in the right direction.
swa: Matokeo haya yaliibua mjadala mzito kwenye mitandao ya kijamii na kwenye vyombo vikuu vya habari, na wachambuzi wengi walihoji iweje Waganda wengi wafikiri nchi yao, iliyotawaliwa na Rais Yoweri Museveni kwa karibu miongo mitatu, ilikuwa kwenye mwelekeo sahihi wa kimaendeleo.

eng: According to the 2013 Millennium Development Goals Report for Uganda, the country under Museveni has succeeded in "halving the number of people living in absolute poverty and achieving debt sustainability" – and was on track to achieve another eight of its targets.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Taarifa ya Malengo ya Maendeleo ya Mileniamu ya 2013 nchini Uganda , nchi hiyo chini ya Museveni imefanikiwa "kupunguza nusu ya idadi ya watu wanaoishi kwenye ufukara uliokithiri na kupunguza madeni yake" – na ilikuwa inafanya vizuri katika kutimiza malengo mengine nane.

eng: The country registered real gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 5.2 percent in 2013 due to strong exports and public investment, and was expected to continue growing even more in 2014 and 2015, according to African Development Bank data (although severe drought may have changed this forecast).
swa: Nchi hiyo ina ukuaji wa wastani wa pato la ndani (GDP) wa asilimia 5.2 kwa 2013 kwa sababu ya kuuza zaidi bidhaa nje ya nchi na kukua kwa uwekezaji, na ilitarajiwa kuendelea kukua hata kwa mwaka 2014 na 2015, kwa mujibu wa takwimu za Benki ya Maendeleo ya Afrika (ingawa ukame mkubwa unaweza kuwa umebadili utabiri huu).

eng: However, international organizations have over the years denounced human right abuses and attacks on freedom of expression in Uganda, where the regime uses ready-made laws to target activists and opposition leaders.
swa: Hata hivyo, mashirika ya kimataifa yamekuwa yakilaani matendo ya ukiukwaji wa haki za binadamu na kubanwa kwa uhuru wa kujieleza nchini Uganda, ambapo utawala wa nchi hiyo umetumia sheria mpya kuwalenga wanaharakati na viongozi wa upinzani.

eng: In October 2014, Amnesty International expressed concerns that Ugandan people were "unable to challenge their political rulers, speak freely and dispute a group of new human rights-denying laws."
swa: Mwezi oktoba 2014, Shirika la Kutetea Haki za Binadamu la Amnesty International lilionesha kwamba wananchi wa Uganda "hawakuwa na uwezo wa kuwapinga watawala wao wa kisiasa, kuongea kwa uhuru na kulaani sheria kadhaa zinazopingana na haki za binadamu. "

eng: Human Right Watch lists similar concerns, including the "deaths of at least 49 people during protests in 2009 and 2011."
swa: Shirika la Human Right Watch linaorodhesha masuala yayo hayo, ikiwa ni pamoja na "vifo vya watu wasiopungua 49 wakati wa maandamano ya mwaka 2009 na 2011."

eng: People DO NOT grow to love and cherish dictatorships'
swa: Watu hawakui ili waupende na kuuenzi udikteta'

eng: Readers commented widely on an analysis of the poll results published on the website of the Uganda's Monitor, a highly respected private daily.
swa: Wasomaji waitoa maoni mengi wakichambua matokeo hayo ya kura ya maoni yaliyochapishwa kwenye tovuti ya gazeti binafsi linaloheshimika nchini Uganda na linalochapishwa kila siku liitwalo Monitor.

eng: SagInc, taking examples of dictators laundering, wrote:
swa: SagInc, akitolea mfano wa madikteta wanaofahamika, aliandika:

eng: The question is who requested for and subsequently paid for the research to be carried out?
swa: Swali ni nani aliomba na kufadhili utafiti huu ufanyike?

eng: You will be surprised how much money has exchanged hands and from whom.
swa: Utashangazwa na kiasi cha pesa kilichotumika na nani hasa walizitoa fedha hizo.

eng: Former dictators: Ben Ali of Tunisia, Suharto of Indonesia, Yakubu Gowan of Nigeria, Nicolae Ceaușescu of Romania all engaged in social-engineering at the height of their dictatorships to try and conceal the true state of affairs but all in vain.
swa: Madikteta wa zamani kama Ben Ali wa Tunisia, Suharto wa Indonesia, Yakubu Gowan na Nigeria, Nicolae Ceaușescu wa Romania wote walishiriki kuchakachua mitazamo ya jamii ili kupalilia udikteta wao na kujaribu kuficha hali halisi ya mambo na hata hivyo hawakuweza.

eng: History tells us that people DO NOT grow to love and cherish dictatorships but rather the opposite.
swa: Historia inatuambia kwamba watu hawakui kuupenda na kuuenzi udikteta isipokuwa kinyume chake.

eng: IRI says the poll was conducted in December 2014 and funded by the foreign aid arm of the United States, the US Agency for International Development.
swa: IRI inasema kura hiyo ya maoni ilifanyika kati ya Desemba 2014 na ilifadhiliwa na shirika la misaada la Marekani, wakala wa Marekani kwa Maendeleo ya Kimataifa.

eng: Ugandans have reason to be skeptical.
swa: Waganda wana kila sababu ya kuwa na wasiwasi.

eng: A few days after the poll results were released, Ugandan media revealed that the government had reportedly paid a US public relations firm 614 million Ugandan shillings ($206,000, 174,000 euros) "to prop up Uganda's image" after it took a hit internationally thanks to a law that criminalized same-sex relations with life in prison in some cases.
swa: Siku chache baada ya matokeo hayo kutandazwa, vyombo vya habari nchini humo viligundua kwamba serikali inasemekana ililipa shirika moja la mahusiano ya umma lenye makazi yake nchini Marekani shilingi milioni 614 za Uganda (sawa na $206,000, au euros 174,000) "kuitengeneza vizuri taswira ya Uganda" baada ya mtafaruku ulioenea duniani kote kufuatia sheria inayofanya mahusiano ya mapenzi ya jinsia moja kuwa kosa la jinai linaloadhibiwa kwa kifungo jela kwa baadhi ya mazingira.

eng: The Anti-Homosexuality Act was struck down by the country's Constitutional Court in August 2014.
swa: Sheria hiyo ya kupambana na ushoga ilibatilishwa na mahakama ya katiba ya nchi hiyo mwezi augusti 2014.

eng: Infographic courtesy International Republican Institute.
swa: Habari picha haki miliki ya International Republican Institute.

eng: In Uganda, 65 percent of respondents in this poll support the respect of term limits, an issue that grows more relevant by the day.
swa: Nchini Uganda, asilimia 65 wa watu walioshiriki utafiti huu wanaunga mkono ukomo wa madaraka, suala ambalo linaendelea kubeba umuhimu kila uchao.

eng: In January 2015, Museveni said he is not ready to hand over power to the opposition leaders, calling them "wolves lurking to tear Uganda apart."
swa: Mwezi Januari 2015, Museveni alisema hayuko tayari kukabidhi madaraka kwa viongozi wa upinzani, akiwaaita "mbwa mwitu wanaotaka kuisambaratisha Uganda."

eng: James commented:
swa: James alikuwa na maoni haya:

eng: Election reform and terms limit reflect the views of many.
swa: Uchaguzi na ukomo wa awamu ya uongozi ndio mtazamo wa wengi.

eng: The rest of the survey is pure fuzzy maths.
swa: Takwimu zilizobaki ni uchakatuzi tu.

eng: Dictatorship, murders, lies'
swa: Udikteta, mauaji, uongo'

eng: On the same site, commenter Jomo wondered if the respondents were informed enough:
swa: Kwenye tovuti hiyo hiyo, mchambuzi Jomo alijiuliza kama washiriki wa utafiti huo walikuwa na taarifa za kutosha:

eng: I don't know whether the researchers took into account the fact that a large number of Ugandans (un-researched street wisdom!), both urban and rural, are largely uninformed, and depend on either here-say, or information handed down by government agents/representatives, to form their opinions.
swa: Sijui kama watafiti walizingatia ukweli kwamba wananchi wengi wa Uganda (hii ni busara ya mtaani isiyohitaji usomi), mjini na vijijini, hawana uelewa wa mambo, na wanategemea tetesi, au taarifa zinazotolewa na taasisi za serikali, ili wawe na mtazamo fulani.

eng: Augustus Karube thought the poll provides useful information for political parties and wondered how their leaders are going to use it:
swa: Augustus Karube alifikiri utafiti huo unatoa taarifa muhimu kwa vyama vya siasa na alifikiri namna viongozi wa vyama vya siasa wanaweza kutumia utafiti huu:

eng: What really matters most, to opposition parties is, how best they can use this information, to prepare themselves, to develop strategy, to address and focus on key issues, which were sited in this quick/short poll.
swa: Kilicho muhimu zaidi, kwa upinzani ni, namna ipi nzuri ya kutumia taarifa hizi, kujiandaa, kujenga mikakati, kwa lengo la kushughulikia masuala muhimu, yaliyoguswa kwenye utafiti huu mdogo.

eng: They should take a particular note of respondents disagreements or dismay or disapproval, but not to read too much into it.
swa: Vyama vya siasa vichunguze masuala ambayo washiriki wnegi hawakuyakubali au waliyapinga au walishangazwa nayo, hata hivyo wasiyazingatie sana.

eng: Never the less, do not dismiss it all together, as rubbish.
swa: Lakini pia wasiyapuuze na kuyaona ni takataka.

eng: At least, it is a document, which provides a sort of overview of the political, economic and social issues, under this regime, as seen through the lives and experiences of voters, minus the untold truth.
swa: Angalau, utafiti huu ni waraka tu, unaotoa mwelekeo wa hali ya kisiasa, kiuchumi na kijamii, chini ya utawala huu, kama yanavyotazamwa kupitia maisha na uzoefu wa wapiga kura wenyewe, ukiacha ukweli ambao hauwezi kusemwa.

eng: Use it wisely.
swa: Tumieni utafiti huu kwa busara.

eng: Nothing out of it, should be taken for granted, to be or not to be the absolute truth.
swa: Chochote kisipuuzwe na kuchukuliwa kijuu juu, na pia tusichukulie kila kilichosemwa kuwa ni uongo au ukweli.

eng: What is your view?
swa: Una maoni gani?

eng: If you were to be asked, but you were not?
swa: Kama ungeulizwa na hukuulizwa?

eng: Uganda's opposition parties have threatened to boycott presidential and parliamentary elections due in February 2016, arguing that the Electoral Commission is biased in favor of Museveni and his ruling party and demanding it be replaced.
swa: Vyma vya upinzani nchini Uganda vimetishia kugomea uchaguzi wa rais na wabunge utakaofanyika mwezi Februari 2016, kwa hoja kwamba Tume ya Uchaguzi una upendeleo kwa Museveni na chama chake kinachotawala na wanadai ibadilishwe.

eng: An analysis by Moses Khisa, a PhD candidate in political science at Northwestern University in Illinois, USA, on Uganda's Observer criticizing the poll results as "self-deception" received a lot of comments from netizens. mungu wrote:
swa: Uchambuzi uliofanywa na Moses Khisa, mwanafunzi wa Shahada ya Uzamivu ya sayansi ya siasa ya Chuo Kikuu cha Northwest huko Illinois, Marekani kwenye gazeti la Observer la nchini Uganda akikosoa matokeo hayo ya utafiti na kuyaita kuwa "uwongo mtupu" ulipokelewa kwa hisia tofauti na raia. Msomaji ajiitae mungu aliandika:

eng: MK you also have to concede that your concept of 'right direction' vastly differs from that of most Ugandans.
swa: MK lazima na wewe ukubali kwamba dhana yako ya 'mwelekeo sahihi' inatofautiana sana na ile ya wananchi wa Uganda.

eng: For them all those failures of M7 regime are in fact sweet music and the right direction.
swa: Kwa Waganda mapungufu yote ya utawala wa M7 kwa kweli ni kama muziki mtamu na welekeo sahihi wa mambo.

eng: In my village they will tell you he has actually helped reduce the dust on their roads because ever since he came to power none of their children has excelled academically, got a well paying job and bought a car.
swa: Kijijini kwangu watakwambia alisaidia kupunguza vumbi kwenye barabara zao kwa sababu tangu aingie madarakani hakuna mtoto wao aliwahi kufaulu kimasomo, na kupata kazi inayolipa kumwezesha kununua hata gari.

eng: So they are not interested in a tarred road either.
swa: Kwa hiyo hata barabara ya lami inayojengwa kijijini kwao hawana kazi nayo.

eng: A resistance to Western civilization may be?
swa: Ni kukataa ustaarabu wa kimagharibi labda?

eng: Think about it
swa: Fikiria zaidi

eng: Francis, another reader, wrote:
swa: Francis, msomaji mwingine, aliandika:

eng: What can you write home about M7/NRM/NRMO other than Dictatorship, Murders, Lies, Nepotism, Cronyism, Land grabbing, Coercion, Militarism, Robberies, Thefts, Impunity, domineering, Threats, Poverty, Rotten Education system, Tribalism, sectarianism, deception.
swa: Unaweza kuandika nini kuhusu M7/NRM/NRMO na National Resistance Movement/National Resistance Movement Organisation] kuliko Udikteta, Mauaji, Uongo, Undugu, Urafiki, Unyang'anyi wa ardhi, Ghasia, Matumizi ya Jeshi, Ujambazi, Wizi, Ufisadi, Utawala wa kiimla, Vitisho, Umasikini, mfumo mbovu wa elimu, Ukabila, udini, udanganyifu.

eng: Among the readers of that daily newspaper, Peter was the only one to express a positive comment:
swa: Miongoni mwa wasomaji wa gazeti hilo la kila siku, Peter ni mtu pekee aliyeotoa maoni chanya:

eng: If the country is going in the right direction and Museveni achieves high marks, the logic is there is no problem.
swa: Kama nchi inaelekea kwenye mwelekeo sahihi na Museveni anafanikiwa kwa alama za juu, mantiki ni kwamba hakuna tatizo.

eng: Other problems created does not arise, they have no base.
swa: Matatizo mengine yanayotengenezwa hayapo, na hayana msingi.

eng: Let those who want to come to power wait for 2016, to see Uganda continuing in aright direction.
swa: Wale wanaotaka kuingia madarakani wasubiri mwaka 2016, ili kuiona Uganda ikisonga mbele kwenye uelekeo sahihi.

eng: Bambalazaabwe Ssemakula represented the opinion of many readers:
swa: Bambalazaabwe Ssemakula aliwakilisha maoni ya wengi:

eng: Survey or no survey, nothing is gonna change as those in leadership do not see this as credible information as long as it does not wholly suit NRM
swa: Kuwe na utafiti au usiwe na utafiti, hakuna kitakachobadilika maadam wale walio madarakani hawaoni kwamba taarifa hizi kuwa za kutiliwa maanani kwa sababu haziipendezi NRM

eng: Ugandans went to Twitter, too, to comment on the results, with hashtag #IRIUgandaPolls.
swa: Waganda kwenye mtandao wa Twita, nao kadhalika, walikuwa na maoni kuhusiana na matokeo hayo, kwa utumia alama habari ya #IRIUgandaPolls.

eng: Twitter user T.Ddumba and journalism student kemigisa jacky pointed out unrealistic promises from politicians:
swa: Watumiaji wa twita T.Ddumba pamoja na mwanafunzi wa uandishi wa habari Kemigisa Jacky waligusia ahadi hewa za wanasiasa:

eng: @tomddumba Many promises no action, many visions, no work on ground, but 69% of Ugandans believe the country is going in the right direction — kemigisa jacky (@JackyKemigisa) March 21, 2015
swa: Ahadi nyingi lakini hakuna maono mengi, hakuna kinachofanyika katika hali halisi, lakini asilimia 69 ya Waganda wanaamini nchi yao iko kwenye uelekeo sahihi wa kimaendeleo

eng: Water and sanitation specialist Fredrick Tumusiime, based in Kampala, responded to their tweets, saying:
swa: Mtaalam wa maji na usafi Fredrick Tumusiime, anayeishi Kampala, alijibu twiti hizi, akisema:

eng: @JackyKemigisa If right direction means going to bed and waking up the next day, the country is on course.
swa: Kama mwelekeo sahihi maana yake kuweza kulala na kuamka siku ya pili, basi nchi iko pahala pake.

eng: Expectations are low. @tomddumba — Fredrick Tumusiime (@tufre80) March 21, 2015
swa: Wananchi hawana matarajio makubwa

eng: MozFestEA will take place from July 17th - 19th 2015, at Victoria University, Kampala, Uganda under the theme,“Building solutions for Africa's challenges, together on the web”:
swa: MozFestEA ni tukio litakalofanyika kuanzia Julai 17 - 19, 2015 kwenye Chuo Kikuu cha Victoria, Kampala, Uganda likiwa na maudhui makuu, "Kutafuta Majibu ya Changamoto za Afrika, kwa pamoja mtandaoni":

eng: MozFest East Africa is an annual event that brings together educators, innovators, learners and makers from East Africa and beyond to share experiences and build the web together laying a foundation for growth of the internet and information technology in Africa.
swa: MozFest Afrika Mashariki ni tukio la kila mwaka linalowaleta pamoja wataalam wa elmu, wabunifu, wasomi na mafundi wa Afrika Mashariki kujaribu kujadili namna ya kujenga mtandao kwa pamoja kwa kuweka msingi wa ukuaji wa mtandao wa intaneti na teknolojia ya habari barani Afrika.

eng: The event is exponentially spreading across Africa to help address the technological challenges faced in the African continent through meaningful collaborations.
swa: Tukio hili limeenea Afrika nzima kusaidia kukabili changamoto za teknolojia zinazolikabili bara la Afrika kwa kutumia mifumo mizuri ya ushirikiano.

eng: Window with a view towards Sucre.
swa: Dirisha lenye madhari inayoelekea Sucre.

eng: Image by Erika Ordosgoitti.
swa: Picha na Erika Ordosgoitti.

eng: The nude, one of the oldest and most recurrent subjects in the art world, has led to the suspension of many Facebook accounts over the years.
swa: Michoro ya uchi, moja wapo ya mada za muda mrefu zaidi na zinazoendelea kuwa na umaarufu katika ulimwengu wa sanaa, imesababisha kusimamishwa kwa akaunti nyingi za mtandao wa facebook katika kipindi cha miaka kadhaa.

eng: One recent and widely reported example was the account of Jerry Saltz, an art critic from New York Magazine.
swa: Mfano wa hivi karibuni na uliotangazwa kwa kiasi kikubwa ni ule wa akaunti ya Jerry Saltz, msanii anayetumia sanaa kukosoa kupitia Jarida la New York.

eng: Last month, his account was suspended because he shared images deemed inappropriate, according to the network's terms of service.
swa: Mwezi uliopita, akaunti yake ilifungiwa kwa sababu aliweka michoro inayosemekana kuwa haina maadili, kwa mujibu wa vigezo na masharti ya mtandao huo.

eng: On digital media, inappropriate often means naked.
swa: Kwenye mitandao ya kidijitali, 'kutokuwa na maadili' mara nyingi humaanisha uchi au ngono.

eng: In Saltz's case, the images were provocative and deemed to be pornographic, according to the New York Times' ArtsBeat blog.
swa: Kwa kilichomkuta Saltz, michoro ilisemekana kuwa na taswira ya ngono, kwa mujibu wa blogu ya New York Times inayoitwa ArtsBeat.

eng: But the same criteria has been applied to a broad range of images, from breastfeeding mothers to artists whose works reveal nipples, penises, and in particular, vaginas.
swa: Lakinikigezo hicho hicho kimetumika kuhakiki aina mbalimbali za michoro na picha, kuanzia ile ya akina mama wanaoonekana kunyonyesha mpaka kwa wasanii ambao kazi zao zinaonesha chuchu, sehemu za siri za kiume, na hata zile za kike.

eng: The female reproductive organ seems all but banned from social networks, even in the case of a reproduction of Gustave Courbet's famous 1866 painting The Origin of the World.
swa: Via vya kike vinaonekana kuwa ndiyo michoro inayoongoza kupigwa marufuku kwenye mitandao ya kijamii, hata kwenye sanaa ya mchoro maarufu wa Gustave Courbet wa mwaka 1866 unaojulikana kama The Origin of the World. .

eng: Venezuelan performance artist Erika Ordosgoitti, whose art focuses primarily on the female body, is another example of a person who has faced numerous challenges due to her publishing nude works on social media.
swa: Msanii wa sanaa za maonesho wa Venezuela Erika Ordosgoitti, ambaye kazi zake zinajikita zaidi kwenye maeneo ya mwili wa mwanamke, ni mfano mwingine wa mtu aliyekumbana na changamoto nyingi kwa sababu ya kuchapisha kazi zake za sanaa zenye kuonesha sehemu za siri kwenye mitandao ya kijamii.

eng: Among other works, Facebook has censored a portrait of her naked body five times in a row.
swa: Miongoni mwa kazi nyingine, Facebook imefuatilia mchoro wa mwili wake mwenyewe ukiwa uchi kwa mara tano sasa.

eng: Screenshot of a report on pornographic content in Facebook saying that Erika's photo has been reported and therefore, deleted.
swa: Picha ya taarifa kuhusu maudhui ya kingono kwenye mtandao wa Facebook ikisema kwamba picha ya Erika imelalamikiwa na hivyo, imefutwa.

eng: Shared by Erika Ordosgoitti.
swa: Imewekwa kwenye mtandao na Erika Ordosgoitti.

eng: The above text, explaining Facebook's reasons for deleting the photo reads: "We have reviewed the photo reported on the basis of nudity or pornography.
swa: Maandishi hayo hapo juu, yanaeleza sababu za Fecebook kufuta picha hiyo na yanasomeka hivi: "Tumeikagua picha iliyolalamikiwa kwa kuonesha utupu au kuwa na maudhui ya kingono.

eng: As it infringes our Terms of Service, it was removed.
swa: Kwa sababu inakiuka Msharti na Vigezo vyetu, picha hiyo imeondolewa.

eng: Thanks for reporting.
swa: Asante sana kwa kutujulisha.

eng: We already told Erika Ordos that we deleted her photo, but we did not tell her who filed the complaint.
swa: Tumemjulisha Erika Ordos kwamba tumefuta picha yake, lakini hatukumfahamisha nani aliwasilisha malalamiko.

eng: Facebook never discloses the identity of the person filling the report."
swa: Facebook haina utaratibu wa kuweka wazi jina la mtu anayelalamikia maudhui."

eng: Global Voices asked Ordosgoitti to tell us about her experience with censorship on social media platforms.
swa: Global Voices ilimwuliza Ordosgoitti atusimulie uzoefu wake kuhusu kufuatiliwa kwa kazi zake kwenye majukwaa ya mitandao ya kijamii kwa lengo la kumdhibiti.

eng: From there, we started to think about how both users and system administrators facilitate censorship.
swa: Kuanzia hapo, tumeanza kufikiri namna watumiaji na wasimamizi wa mifumo ya mtandao wanavyoweza kuwezesha ufuatiliaji huu.

eng: This post will be the first in a series of publications that will address the different ways of dealing with art censorship, based on the stories of Erika Ordosgoitti and other artists who have been restrained by social networks' terms of service and by social conventions.
swa: Makala hii itakuwa ya kwanza katika mfululizo wa machapisho yatakayojadili namna mbalimbali za kushughulikia suala la kudhibitiwa kwa sanaa hii, kwa kutumia masimulizi ya Erika Ordosgoitti na wasanii wnegine waliobanwa na masharti na vigezo vya mitandao ya kijamii ikiwa ni pamoja na makubaliano ya kijamii.

eng: Ordosgoitti's latest exhibition, titled Comida de moscas (Food for Flies), comments on the censorship that she has experienced and managed to document.
swa: Maonesho ya hivi karibuni ya Ordosgoitti, yaliyokuwa na jina la Comida de moscas (Chakula cha Nzi), yalikuwa ni mtazamo kuhusu ufuatiliwaji aliokumbana nao na namna alivyoweza kufanya kazi zake.

eng: Warning: The photograph shown below contains graphic language.
swa: Tahadhari: Picha inayooneshwa hapa chini ina maudhui yenye lugha kali.

eng: In the first years, the page went viral online.
swa: Katika mwaka wa kwanza, ukurasa wangu ulikuwa maarufu mno mtandaoni.

eng: They continually closed my account, blocking me, and warning me, and I kept on deliberately posting my work.
swa: Kila mara waliufunga ukurasa wangu, kunizuia kuitumia akaunti yangu na wakati mwingine kunionya, lakini bado niliendelea na kazi zangu kwa makusudi.

eng: I received many insults and a few death threats.
swa: Nilitukanwa sana na hata wakati mwingine kupata vitisho vya kuuawa.

eng: Video installation with insulting comments received by Ordosgoitti from users in Internet.
swa: Video ikiwa na maneno yenye matusi aliyoyapata Ordosgoitti kutoka kwa watumiaji wa mtandao wa intaneti.

eng: Shared image by the artist and published with permission.
swa: Picha iliyotumiwa ni ya msanii na imechapishwa kwa ruhusa.

eng: Venezuelan artist Eliseo Solis Mora found himself in a similar situation not long ago.
swa: Msanii wa Venezuela Eliseo Solis Mora alijikuta kwenye hali kama hiyo si muda mrefu uliopita.

eng: He was blocked by Facebook for publishing a self-portrait—a frontal nude that is part of a performance art piece.
swa: Alifungiwa na Facebook kwa kuchapisha mchoro wenye sura yake—ukionesha sehemu za mbele za uchi wake ambao ni sehemu ya kazi zake za sanaa ya maonesho.

eng: He writes:
swa: Anaandika:

eng: Networks are nowdays a complex medium.
swa: Mitandao ya kijamii siku hizi imekuwa jukwaa gumu kulitumia.

eng: I have been banned for my photos.
swa: Nimefungiwa kwa sababu ya picha zangu.

eng: On Facebook, I posted a picture of Esther Ferrer and they blocked me.
swa: Kwenye mtandao wa Facebook, niliweka picha za Esther Ferrer na wakanifungia.

eng: It happened again with a nude that I later dedicated to Ai Weiwei.
swa: Imetokea tena kwa mchoro niliokuwa nimeuchapisha kwa heshima ya Ai Weiwei.

eng: On Instagram, they automatically erased an image that was reported.
swa: Kwenye mtandao wa Instagram, picha yoyote inayolalamikiwa hufutwa mara moja.

eng: Complainants remain anonymous
swa: Walalamikaji habaki kuwa siri

eng: Ordosgoitti says artists are usually blocked or censored because of complaints filed by other users with access to their accounts.
swa: Ordosgoitti anasema wasanii hufungiwa au kufuatiliwa shauri ya malalamiko yanayotoka kwa watumiaji wengine wa mtandao wanaoona mashapisho yao.

eng: I've had about seven different Facebook accounts.
swa: Nimewahi kuwa na akaunti kama saba tofauti za mtandao wa facebook.

eng: Currently I have two Facebook accounts: an official account and an alternative one, and usually one of them is blocked, so I use the other to bypass this.
swa: Kwa sasa nina akaunti mbili: moja rasmi na nyingine ni mbadala, na mara nyingi moja wapo hufungiwa, kwa hiyo ninatumia nyingine kukabiliana na hali hiyo.

eng: The artist says the criteria for censorship are applied loosely and unequally.
swa: Msanii huyo anasema vigezo vya kufuatiliwa havizingatiwi sana na havitumiki kwa usawa.

eng: She also notes that users who file unreasonable complaints face no penalties:
swa: Anabainisha kwamba watumiaji wanaotoa malalamiko yasiyo na maana hawaadhibiwi:

eng: Facebook is the first to be blamed on this form of censorship because their policy promotes anonymous reporting.
swa: Mtandao wa Facebook ndio wa kwanza kabisa kulaumiwa kwa mtindo huu wa kufuatilia watumiaji wake kwa sababu sera zao zinalinda malalamiko yanayoficha jina la mlalamikaji.

eng: I believe this policy is unfair, because it doesn't give me the opportunity to know who is denouncing me and why .
swa: Ninaamini sera hii haina haki, kwa sababu hainipi fursa ya kujua nani ananiharibia na kwa sababu gani .

eng: They thank the user who's complaining, without even knowing if the report is valid.
swa: Wao humshukuru mtumiaji anayelalamika, bila hata kujua kama alichokilalamikia kina mantiki.

eng: Although the terms of use are clear enough, the reasons for censorship are not, because nowadays (and it was not always like this) it is assumed that their intention is to exclude pornography or sexually explicit images, a policy that can thereby extend to exempting scientific and artistic images.
swa: Ingawa masharti ya kutumia yako wazi sana, sababu zinazoweza kutumiwa kwa ufuatiliaji haziko wazi, kwa sababu siku hizi (na imekuwa hivi siku zote) inaaminiwa kwamba nia kufuta kabisa picha za ngono au zenye maudhui ya kimapenzi, sera ambazo inaweza kuhusisha hata picha za kisayansi au za sanaa.

eng: But how do you differentiate pornographic or vulgar images from artistic ones?
swa: Lakini unawezaje kutofautisha picha za ngono na zile za sanaa?

eng: Facebook's decision to protect the identity of those who denounce images reflects an intention to keep these situations from instigating conflict between users.
swa: Uamuzi wa mtandao wa Facebook kuficha utambulisho wa wale wanaolalamikia picha unatoa taswira ya kufanya mambo haya kuleta migogoro kwa watumiaji wa mtandao huo.

eng: But it also presents new challenges, as the artists indicate.
swa: Lakini pia inaleta changamoto mpya, kama wasanii wanavyoonesha.

eng: Solís Mora, whose body images online have also encountered censorship, considers the criteria for censoring artistic images on digital media undemocratic:
swa: Solís Mora, ambaye picha za mwili wake zimekuwa zikifuatiliwa kwa lengo la kudhibiti kazi zake, anaona vigezo vya kufuatilia picha za sanaa kwenye mitandao ya kidigitali haikuzi demokrasia:

eng: ...celebrities have more freedom.
swa: ...watu maarufu wana uhuru zaiidi.

eng: Proof of this is the famous wallpaper with Kim Kardashian showing her butt that went viral through social networks.
swa: Ushahidi wa hili ni picha inayomwonesha Kim Kardashian akionesha makalio yake iliyosambaa sana kwenye mitandao ya kijamii.

eng: There is something interesting that you notice when you open Instagram: there are sexist images published everyday with thousands of 'likes' while there are works of art that are automatically blocked ...
swa: Kuna jambo la kufikirisha unapofungua mtandao wa Instagram: kuna picha za kingono zinazochapishwa kila siku zenye maelfu ya watu wanaoweka alama ya kuvutiwa nazo wakati kazi za sanaa zikizuiwa bila mjadala...

eng: Solís Mora recently published a warning—or rather a manifesto—on his Facebook wall:
swa: Hivi karibuni Solís Mora alichapisha tahadhari —au ilani—kwenye ukurasa wake wa Facebook:

eng: If on this account, which is largely handled as a working tool, I show my naked body and if you, dear reader, don't like it, just turn the page ... I recommend then, that if you're my friend or virtual friend, try to understand that I am an artist with total creative freedom and that what I show here is art.
swa: Kama kwenye akaunti hii, ambayo inatumika kama zana ya kazi zaidi, ninaonesha mwili wangu ukiwa uchi na kama wewe, mpendwa msomaji wangu, usingependa kuona picha hizo, funga ukurasa…ninashauri, kwamba kama wewe ni rafiki yangu au mtu tunayewasiliana mtandaoni, jaribu kuelewa kwamba mimi ni msanii mwenye uhuru kamili w akiubunifu na kwmaba ninachokionesha hapa ni sanaa.

eng: Like Ordosgoitti, Mora has been bullied and even received death threats because of his work.
swa: Kama ilivyo kwa Ordosgoitti, Mora amekuwa akidhalilishwa na hata kupata vitisho vya kifo kwa sababu ya kazi zake.

eng: For him, censorship from cultural institutions has always been something he's had to deal with, but the constraints on his online artistic freedom, he says, are growing:
swa: Kwake, ufuatiliaji unaofanywa kwa lengo la kudhibiti kazi zake kutoka kwenye taasisi za utamaduni limekuwa ni jambo ambalo amejifunza kushughulika nalo, lakini vikwazo kwa uhuru wa kazi zake za sanaa mtandaoni, anasema, vinaendelea kuongezeka:

eng: The problem goes beyond reporting—the real problem is the lack of freedom.
swa: Tatizo ni zaidi ya kulalamikiwa—tatizo halisi ni kukosekana kwa uhuru.

eng: However, I like to hear people talking about nude, even though it is the oldest subject in the art world...
swa: Hata hivyo, ninapenda kusikia watu wakizungumzia sanaa ya uchi, hata kama ni mada ya zamani sana kwenye ulimwengu wa sanaa...

eng: Editor's note: This post started a team discussion on nude art on our page.
swa: Maelezo ya Mhariri: Makala haya yalianzisha mjadala wa pamoja kuhusiana na sanaa ya uchi kwneye ukurasa wetu.

eng: While some team members wanted to include the works subjected to censorship, others were reluctant.
swa: Wakati wenzetu walitaka kuambatanisha kazi zinazozungumziwa hapa, wengine walikuwa wazito.

eng: Thus, based on these conversations, we opened the discussion in our community blog.
swa: Kwa hiyo, kwa kutumia mazungumzo hayo, tulifungua mjadala kwenye blogu ya jamii yetu.

eng: You can see the discussion here and add your thoughts in the comments.
swa: Unaweza kuona mjadala hapa na kuongeza mawazo yako kwenye kisanduku cha maoni.

eng: Twitter users show support for Garissa victims via Arnaud Seroy on twitter
swa: Watumiaji wa Twita waonesha mshikamano wao na wahanga wa tukio la Garisa kupitia Arnaud Seroy katika Twita

eng: On April 2, 2015, at least 147 people were killed by gunmen on the campus of Garissa University in Kenya, according to Kenya's National Disaster Operation Centre (KRCS).
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Kituo cha Kitaifa cha Kukabiliana na Majanga cha nchini Kenya (KRCS), mnamo Aprili 2, 2015, watu wasiopungua 147 waliuawa kwa kufyatuliwa risasi katika chuo kikuu cha Garissa nchini Kenya.

eng: The center also reports that 79 people were injured and 587 people were evacuated at this stage.
swa: Kituo hicho pia kilitaarifu kuwa watu 79 walijeruhiwa na wengine 587 walifanikiwa kutolewa kutoka katika eneo la tukio.

eng: The suspected mastermind of the massacre is the Somalia-based Al-Shabaab militant group, which claimed responsibility for the attack.
swa: Mtuhumiwa mkubwa wa mauaji haya ya halaiki ni kikundi cha wanamgambo wa Al-Shabaab kilicho na maskani yake nchini Somalia kilichotangaza kuhusika na shambulizi hilo.

eng: The tragic accounts of the shooting by survivors triggered a show of solidarity worldwide.
swa: Maelezo kutoka kwa wahanga wa tukio hili zilichochea watu kuonesha mshikamano wao kutoka katika maeneo mbalimbali duniani kote.

eng: The francophone world, still weary after the Charlie Hebdo attack, responded by showing solidarity with the Garissa victims on social networks with the hashtag #JesuisKenyan (to mirror the hashtag #JesuisCharlie).
swa: Jamii ya wazungumzaji wa lugha ya Kifaransa, bado wakiwa na kumbukumbu ya shambulizi la Charlie Hebdo, walionesha mshikamano wao na wahanga wa shambulizi la Garissa kupitia mitandao ya kijamii katika kiungo habari #JesuisKenyan (kama taswira ya kiungo habari cha hashtag #JesuisCharlie).

eng: It was the second most trending topics on Twitter in France on April 3.
swa: Hii ilikuwa ndio mada ya pili kwa mvuto kuliko nyingine yoyote katika Twita nchini Ufaransa mnamo Aprili 3.

eng: Here are a few of those posts:
swa: Yafuatayo ni baadhi tu ya machapisho hayo:

eng: #JeSuisKenyan — #BPM Nouveau single (@TEAMBEOZEDZED) abril 2, 2015
swa: #JeSuisKenyan — #BPM Nouveau single (@TEAMBEOZEDZED) Tarehe 2 Aprili, 2015

eng: 147 died in the horrific #terrorist attack against education and our future.
swa: Watu 147 wamepoteza maisha katika shambulizi la kutisha la kigaidi dhidi ya wanachuo vijana wa taifa la kesho.

eng: Let's show solidarity #JesuisKenyan
swa: Tuoneshe mshikamano wetu#JesuisKenyan

eng: Not enough talk in the media about the terrorist attack at the university in Kenya, are 147 dead not enough ?!
swa: Haitoshi kuzungumzia shambulio hili la kigaidi lililotokea katika chuo kikuu cha Kenya kwenye mitandao ya kijamii, watu 147 ni wachache?!

eng: HORRIBLE #JesuisKenyan
swa: Inatisha sana #JesuisKenyan

eng: Desireé Lozano, blogging for Voces Visibles, urges attention be paid to the extremely high rate of teenage pregnancies in Venezuela, where 25% of the pregnancies are among young people, and the lack of an appropriate public policy to counter this phenomenon and its repercussions.
swa: Desireé Lozano, anayeblogu kwenye blogu ya Voces Visibles, anatoa mwito kwa ongezeko kubwa la mimba za utotoni nchini Venezuela, ambapo asilimia 25 ya mimba ni za vijana, na kukosekana kwa sera sahihi za kudhibiti tatizo hili na matokeo yake.

eng: Venezuelan statistics are the highest in South America and remains in first place from two years ago.
swa: Takwimu za Venezuela zinaonesha kwamba nchi hiyo ina idadi kubwa ya mimba za utotoni barani Amerika ya Kusini na imekua ya kwanza kwa miaka miwili iliyopita.

eng: Maternal mortality is an issue directly related to teen pregnancy.
swa: Vifo vya watoto ni suala kuu linalohusiana moja kwa moja na mimba za utotoni.

eng: Desiree cited Venezuelan deputy Dinorah Figuera, president of the Family Committee of the Venezuelan National Assembly, who said the state's responsibility is to provide prevention:
swa: Desiree anamtolea mfano Dinorah Figuera, makamu wa rais wa Kamati ya Bunge inayoshughulika na Familia aliyesema kwamba wajibu wa serikali ni kuzuia mimba hizo:

eng: One consequence of teen mothers is woman lose development opportunities from a professional viewpoint, take any job in order to make some income. 	Matokeo moja wapo ya kuwa mama katika kipindi cha utoto ni mwanamke kukosa fursa za kujiendeleza kitaaluma, na hivyo kujikuta akifanya kazi yoyote ile kujipatia kipato.
For this reason, the state should mount a massive campaign to prevent teenage pregnancy," the Venezuelan deputy says.
swa: Kwa sababu hii, serikali lazima ifanye kamepni kuba kuzuia mimba za utotoni," alisema.

eng: Additionally, teenage pregnancy contributes to an already established trend, the feminization of poverty.
swa: Kwa nyongeza, mimba za utotoni zinachangia kuongezeka kwa umasikini wa kipato kwa wanawake.

eng: Furthermore, the phenomenon embodies a risk for the mother’s health, running a greater danger than the average.
swa: Zaidi, hali hii inaleta hatari kwa afya ya mama, hatari kubwa kuliko kawaida.

eng: In her article, the writer collects interesting expert statements on the subject providing an overview of the problem.
swa: Kwenye makala yake, mwandishi anakusanya matamshi mbalimbali ya wataalamu kuhusu suala hilo na hivyo kutoa mwanga kuhusiana na tatizo hilo.

eng: Continue reading Desireé Lozano's and Voces Visibles' work here or on Twitter.
swa: Endele kusoma kazi za Desireé Lozano na Voces Visibles hapa au kwenye mtandao wa Twita.

eng: This post was part of the 46th #LunesDeBlogsGV (Monday of blogs on GV) on April 13, 2015.
swa: Makala haya ni ya 46 kwenye mfulululizo wetu wa #LunesDeBlogsGV (Jumatatu ya Blogu GV) mnamo Aprili 13, 2015.

eng: Sunset illuminates a crucifix.
swa: Mchweo nyuma ya msalaba.

eng: Image courtesy Flickr user Sharon.
swa: Picha na mtumiaji wa Flickr Sharon.

eng: In terms of number of followers, Christianity is often considered a major world religion.
swa: Kwa idadi ya waumini, Ukristo mara nyingi huonekana na dini kuu duniani.

eng: However, there are very few Christians in Japan, where less than 1% of the population observes the Christian faith.
swa: Hata hivyo, kuna Wakristo wachache sana nchini Japani, ambako chini ya asilimia moja ya idadi wa watu ni waumini wa imani ya Kikristo.

eng: In Japan, spirituality as it is understood and practiced in the West or in the Judeo-Christian tradition is not common.
swa: Nchini Japani, imani kama inavyoeleweka na kuenziwa katika nchi za Kimagharibi au kwenye utamaduni wa Kiyahudi ni nadra sana.

eng: For the average Japanese person, Christianity is associated mainly with getting married in a faux chapel with a faux priest.
swa: Kwa Mjapan wa kawaida, Ukristo unahusishwa zaidi na ndoa inafungwa na kasisi kanisani.

eng: What an awesome chapel wedding (／_;)/
swa: Jengo zuri la kufungia ndoa(／_;)/

eng: Using pseudonyms, some Japanese people are going online to profess their Christian faith.
swa: Kwa kutumia majina ya bandia, baadhi ya wa-Japan huingia mtandaoni kutangaza imani yao ya Kikristo.

eng: One blog post in particular has prompted dozens of comments about Christianity in Japan.
swa: Makala moja ya blogu ilivutia maoni mengi kuhusu imani ya Ukristo nchini Japani.

eng: In the blog post, an anonymous blogger in Japan describes his relationship with Christianity:
swa: Kwenye makala hiyo ya blogu, mwanablogu wa Kijapani asiyetumia jina lake, anaelezea kwa nini ni Mkristo:

eng: I have an inferiority complex: why is it that the people around me are so successful, yet I can accomplish nothing?
swa: Mimi sijiamini na najihisi kuwa mtu duni: kwa nini watu wanaonizunguka wawe na mafanikio, wakati mimi sina kitu?

eng: So when others around me are cold to me, I feel like crying with sorrow and rage, and wonder why it is that I alone must suffer like this.
swa: Kwa hiyo wakati wengine hawanichangamkii, ninajisikia kuumia na hasira, na kushangaa kwa nini niteseke peke yangu namna hii.

eng: It's often said that if you want to change the world, then you must change yourself.
swa: Mara nyingi inasemekana kwamba kama unataka kuubadili ulimwengu, basi lazima ujibadili mweyewe.

eng: And it came to me in a flash.
swa: Na hilo lilinijia mawazoni.

eng: Maybe all that I can do is accept that there's some sort of divine being who loves me.
swa: Labda ninachoweza kukifanya ni kukubali kuwa kuna aina fulani ya Mungu anayenipenda.

eng: Speaking truthfully, however, I don't believe that God exists, and so it is hard for me to say that I have faith.
swa: Nikiongea kwa ukweli kabisa, hata hivyo, siamini kwamba Mungu yupo, na ni vigumu sana kwangu kusema kwamba nina imani ya kidini.

eng: But I tried assuming God exists and imagined myself loved by that kind of existence, which led me to thank him for his abundant love.
swa: Lakini nimejaribu kujiaminisha wakati mwingine kwamba huenda Mungu yupo na nimejichukulia kama mtu anayependwa na uwepo huo, hali inayonifanya nimshukuru kwa upendo wake mwingi kwangu.

eng: I never experienced something better than this thankfulness.
swa: Sijawahi kujisikia vizuri zaidi ya kushukuru namna hii.

eng: I am ashamed to say that made me realise how I had been unthankful to others.
swa: Ninajisikia aibu kusema kwamba hali hiyo imenifanya nigundue namna gani siku za nyuma sikuwa mtu wa shukrani kwa wengine.

eng: The blogger here is conflicted; he wants to have Christian faith, but is unsure if God even exists.
swa: Mwanablogu huyo alijichanganya kidogo hapa; akisema anataka kuwa na imani ya Ukristo, lakini wakati huo huo akiwa hana uhakika kama Mungu yupo.

eng: However, it seems religious devotion brought the blogger bewilderment as well as joy.
swa: Hata hivyo, inaonekana ibada za kidini zimemfanya mwanablogu huyu kujisikia kuchanganyikiwa kwa upande mmoja pamoja na kujisikia furaha kwa upande mwingine.

eng: Oh, but wait, isn’t this a typical pattern of involvement with a religion?
swa: Ah, ngoja, hii si namna ya kawaida kabisa ya kujihusisha na dini?

eng: Or am I already involved with it?
swa: Au tayari nina dini?

eng: I cannot expel something that has made an impression on my heart.
swa: Siwezi kuachana na kitu ambacho kimegusa moyo wangu.

eng: It is too late to think it over anyway.
swa: Haiwezekani tena kufikiri upya hata hivyo.

eng: The doctrine teaches me to how to live life as a human and it all sounds very decent to me.
swa: Mafundisho ya dini yananielekeza namna ya kuishi kama binadamu na kwangu hilo linafaa.

eng: I am inclined to listen to it, and live a spiritually rich life by coming closer, but I cannot make up my mind because it is a religion.
swa: Nimejiweka sawa kusikiliza, na ninaishi maisha yaliyojaa imani kwa kuendelea kuwa karibu, lakini siwezi kuamua kwa sababu dini.

eng: I guess my parents would not like me believing in religion.
swa: Ninadhani wazazi wangu wasingenipenda niwe na dini.

eng: Oh well, since they contradict me no matter what I do, what I do makes little difference.
swa: Na kweli, kwa sababu inanichanganya hata nifanyeje, kile ninachokifanya haleti tofauti.

eng: I must keep this feeling secret.
swa: Lazima nifanye hisia hizi ziwe siri.

eng: Many commenters responded negatively to the post.
swa: Many commenters responded negatively to the post.

eng: Commenter takass32 denied the existence of a god.
swa: Mtoa maoni ajiitaye takass32 alikana uwepo wa Mungu.

eng: I suppose the ability to imagine or believe in a non-existent person who is honorable and tolerant of yourself is the essence of religious devotion.
swa: Nadhani uwezo wa kufikiri au kuamini mtu asiyekuwepo na anayeheshimiwa utafikiri yupo na kuwa na uvumilivu ndio umuhimu wa ibada za kidini.

eng: honeybe, another commenter on the blog post, had a more positive opinion about having faith, but also made it a point to highlight the negative aspects of religion.
swa: honeybe, mtoa maoni mwingine kwenye blogu hiyo, alikuwa na maoni chanya kuhusu kuwa na imani, lakini alisaili matatizo ya dini.

eng: There is nothing wrong with getting involved with a religion unless you generate a negative effect on people around you, such evangelising persistently, trying to sell religious tracts, or imposing religious ideas.
swa: Si vibaya kuwa na dini labda kama kufanya hivyo kunaleta madhara hasi kwa watu wanaokuzunguka, kama vile kuwahubiria wengine kwa nguvu, kujaribu kueneza vipeperushi vya dini, au kuaminisha watu imani zako.

eng: Commenter ketudan considered the possibility that the blogger may be in danger of joining a cult.
swa: Msomaji mwingine ketudan aliona uwezekano wa mwanablogu huyo kujikuta katika hatari ya kujiunga na vikundi vya dini.

eng: Unfortunately, there are tons of cults and new religions that define themselves as "Christian", so I advise you to Google the name of that church or the religion.
swa: Kwa bahati mbaya, kuna vikundi vingi vya dini mpya vinavyojitangaza kama "Wakristo", kwa hiyo ninakushauri utumie mtandao wa google kupata jina la kanisa au dini ya kujiunga nayo.

eng: I had a homework assignment once to attend a service in the past so I visited "a decent church” in the neighborhood, but what I found there was a kooky cult in which someone pretending to be a minister played the guitar in a Japanese-style room.
swa: Niliwahi kufanya kazi ya ziada wakati fulani kuhudhuria ibada siku za nyuma na baadae ninatembela "kanisa zuri" hapa jirani, lakini nilichokikuta ni kikanisa cha kijinga kikiwa na mtu anayejifanya mhubiri akipiga gitaa kwenye chumba chenye madhari ya ki-Japani.

eng: gohankun felt sympathy for the sheer difficulty of having a religious faith in Japan.
swa: gohankun alipatwa na huruma kwa ugumu wa kukutana na imani za kidini nchini Japani.

eng: It sure is tiring to have a particular religion in Japan.
swa: Kwa kweli inachosha kupata dini fulani nchini Japani.

eng: I have undergone hardships because I come from a Christian family and I am a Christian, too.
swa: Nimekutana na ugumu kwa sababu ninatoka kwenye familia ya Kikristo na mimi ni Mkristo, pia.

eng: I still suffer sometimes.
swa: Ninateseka wakati mwingine.

eng: There are times when I wish I had been born in the West.
swa: Kuna nyakati ninatamani ningekuwa nimezaliwa kwenye nchi za Magharibi.

eng: Life would be much easier then.
swa: Maisha yangekuwa rahisi.

eng: Commenter nows_s came to the conclusion that religion is just another way to get through life.
swa: Msomaji mwingine ajiitaye nows_s alihitimisha kwamba dini ni namna nyingine ya kufurahia maisha.

eng: Life is too much for one person to confront, so we submit to the gods, rely on a country, or become addicted to love affairs, two-dimensional characters, nicotine, or alcohol.
swa: Maisha ni mafupi sana kwa mtu kuhangaika, kwa hiyo tunajikabidhi kwa miungo, kwa kweli ni kutegemea, au kulowea kwenye tabia za mapenzi, tabia mbovu, madawa ya kulevya, au pombe.

eng: If that somehow enables us to live an easy life, then, what's the problem?
swa: Kama lolote kati ya hayo linakufanya uishi maisha ya amani, tatizo nini?

eng: Kayhan reacts on its Thursday, April 23, 2015 front page to the end of Saudi airstrikes. Two prominent hardline newspapers published front pages boasting of a Saudi Arabian defeat today.
swa: Magazeti mawili yenye umaarufu mkubwa leo katika kurasa za mbele yalihanikizwa kwa habari za kushindwa kwa Saudi Arabia.

eng: This is not a complete analysis of Iran's media landscape. Looking at a hardline news sources such as Kayhan or Vatan Emrooz in Iran can be likened to looking at Fox News in the United States.
swa: Habari zili zimetokana na tangazo la Saudi Arabia la kusitisha mashambulizi ya anga dhidi ya Yemen mapema Jumanne hii.

eng: Kayhan, a newspaper associated with Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei's office, published their frontpage with the photo of a young Houthi Yemeni boy sitting on what seems to be rocket that remains from the Saudi Arabian airstrikes against Houthi fighters.
swa: Kayhan, gazeti lililo na uhusiano na kiongozi mkuu wa Kidini, Ayatollah Khamenei, katika ukurasa wake wa mbele lilichapisha picha ya kijana wa Yemen wa Kihouthi akiwa amekalia kitu ambacho kilionekana kama mabaki ya roketi yaliyotokana na mashambuli ya anga ya ndege za kivita za Saudi Arabia dhidi ya wapiganaji wa Houthi.

eng: The title reads, "Yemen's Ansar Hezbollah humiliate Israel and America."
swa: Kichwa cha habari kinasomeka, "Wapiganaji wa Yemen wa Ansar Hezbollah waidhalilisha Israel na Marekani."

eng: The Houthi's are often identified as "Yemen's Ansar Hezbollah" inside Iran.
swa: Nchini Iran, Wahouthi wa Yemen kwa kawaida hujulikana kwa jina la Ansar Hezbollah".

eng: Vatan Emrooz, another hardline newspaper tied to the Peydari Front, a political party associated with the Revolutionary Guards and Basij forces, published a front page cover depicting a framed portrait of the Saudi king fallen across the rubble of destroyed building with the exclamation, "Saudi's air dies!".
swa: Vatan Emrooz, gazeti jingine lenye msimamo mkali lilikisimamia kidete chama cha 'Peydari Front,' ambacho ni chama cha kisiasa kilicho na uhusiano na walinzi wa kiuanamapinduzi na majeshi ya Basij katika ukurasa wake wa mbele lilichapisha picha ya kutengenezwa iliyokuwa inamuonesha Mfalme wa Saudi Arabia akiwa ameanguka kwenye kifusi cha jengo lililoharibiwa na ikiwa na maneno, "Pumzi ya Saudi imekufa!".

eng: Describing someone's air as 'dying' is a popular Persian idiom for someone's defeat.
swa: Unaposema pumzi ya mtu imekufa, huu ni msemo maarufu wa kiajemi unaoonesha kushindwa kwa mtu.

eng: A sub-caption states, "Operation 'Hurricane Certainty' ends after 27 days of crime and infanticide without achieving any of its goals."
swa: Maelezo ya chini yanasema, "Kampeni ya 'Kimbunga Yakinifu' yamalizika mara baada ya siku 27 za uhalifu na mauaji ya vichanga na bila ya kufikia hata moja ya matazamio yake"

eng: Vatan Emrooz reactons on its Thursday, April 23, 2015 front page to the end of Saudi airstrikes.
swa: Gazeti la Vatan Emrooz likiwa na maoni yake ukurasa wake wa mbele wa tarehe 23 Aprili, 2015 kufuatia Saudi Arabia kutangaza kusitisha mashambulizi ya anga nchini yemen.

eng: Follow Global Voice's Yemen coverage here.
swa: Fuatilia habari za Yemen katika Global Voice hapa.

eng: Participants wrote messages and sealed them in envelopes for the families of the Garissa victims.
swa: Washiriki wa ibada hiyo waliandika ujumbe na kuufunga kwenye bahasha kwa ajili ya familia za wahanga wa mauaji ya Garissa.

eng: Photo by Filip Noubel
swa: Picha na Filip Noubel

eng: A group of students, mostly from Kenya, gathered in Beijing on April 18 to hold an unofficial candlelight vigil to honor the memory of the 147 people killed at Garissa University College on April 2 in northern Kenya.
swa: Kikundi cha wanafunzi, wengi wao wakiwa Wakenya, walikusanyika jijini Beijing mnamo Aprili 18 kufanya ibada isiyorasmi ya kuwakumbuka watu 147 waliouawa kwenye Chuo Kikuu Kishiriki cha Garissa mnamo Aprili 2 kaskazini mwa Kenya.

eng: While the global media, including Chinese media, initially covered the news of Garissa massacre widely, the interest rapidly faded.
swa: Wakati vyombo vya habari vya kimataifa, ikiwa ni pamoja na vile vya China, vilianza kwa kuandika mno habari za Garissa, baada ya muda mfupi, hakuna kilichoendelea.

eng: As many pointed out, worldwide reactions have generally been much less noticeable in comparison to recent incidents of similarly large losses of lives.
swa: Kama wengi walivyoonesha, mwitikio wa dunia kwa ujumla umekuwa mdogo kwa kulinganisha na matukio ya watu wengi kupoteza maisha yao kwa wakati mmoja hivi karibuni.

eng: This combined lack of visibility in the news landscape prompted Kenyan and other African students to react in Beijing, despite being thousands of kilometers away from their home countries.
swa: Hali hii ya kukosekana kwa taarifa zilizohusiana na shambulio la Garissa liliwafanya wanafunzi wa Kiafrika wanaosoma jijini Beijing kuchukua hatua, pamoja na kuwa maelfu ya kilometa mbali na nchi walizotoka.

eng: Thus, on April 18 a vigil was organized in Chaoyang park in central Beijing to pay tribute to the victims and their families.
swa: Kwa sababu hiyo, mnamo Aprili 18 ibada ya kuwaombea marehemu iliandiliwa kwenye bustani ya Chaoyang katikati ya Beijing kuwaenzi marehemu, waathirika pamoja na familia zao.

eng: A vigil in a city that forbids protest
swa: Ibada kwenye jiji linalozuia maandamano

eng: Beijing is home to one of the largest communities of African students, who often live in dorms on campuses and create their own tight-knit communities that cross countries of origin and language.
swa: Beijing ni makazi ya jamii kubwa za wanafunzi wa Afrika, wengi wao wakiishi mabwenini kwenye kampasi za vyuo na huunda familia zenye udugu wa karibu unaowaunganisha raia wa nchi na lugha mbalimbali.

eng: The idea of holding a vigil for Kenyan victims came from Brand South Africa country manager for China Tebogo Lefifi.
swa: Wazo la kufanya ibada hiyo kwa ajili ya wahanga wa Kenya lilianzishwa na tovuti ya Brand South Africa inayoratibiwa na Tebogo Lefifi, kwa eneo la nchi ya China .

eng: The site is set up to promote that country's image.
swa: Tovuti hiyo ilianzishwa kutangaza taswira ya nchi hiyo.

eng: Lefifi tells Global Voices that she was inspired "by many people posting on WeChat complaining that the world is not taking a stand on the 147."
swa: Lefifi anaiambia Global Voices kwamba alihamasishwa na watu wengi kutangaza kwenye mtandao wa WeChat kulalamika kwamba dunia haijaonesha msimamo kuhusiana na shambulio hilo lililopoteza maisha ya watu 147."

eng: In addition, she says an email from Africa2.0 Kenya Chapter, a foundation for African initiatives, commenting on the Garissa violence reminded her that she belongs to the generation that Africa has been waiting for to implement positive change.
swa: Kwa nyongeza, anasema barua pepe kutoka kwa Africa2.0 Kenya Chapter, taasisi kwa ajili ya miradi ya Kiafrika, ikichambua shambulio la Garissa lilimkumbusha kwamba anatokana na kizazi ambacho Afrika imekuwa ikikingoja kwa ajili ya kutekeleza mabadiliko chanya.

eng: She is not satisfied with the Twitter-based awareness campaign #147isnotjustanumber, as she says the naming of victims is inadequate to bring about a positive outcome.
swa: Hajaridhishwa na kampeni ya kuelimisha watu iliyokuwa ikifanyika kwenye mtandao wa Twita iliyokuwa na jina la #147isnotjustanumber , akisema kuwataja kwa majina wahnga hakutoshi kuleta mabadiliko chanya.

eng: She believes it is more important to organize the African communities to voice support for their Kenya friends.
swa: Anaamini ni muhimu sana kuziratibu jamii za Waafrika kupaza sauti kuwaunga mkono rafiki zao wa Kenya.

eng: In the end, the vigil was organized by Lefifi and three other Kenyan female students.
swa: Hatimaye, ibada ya mkesha iliandaliwa na Lefifi na wanafunzi wengine watatu wa kike raia wa Kenya.

eng: One of them, Tina Kinuthia, explains how the idea eventually took shape:
swa: Mmoja wao, Tina Kinuthia, anaeleza namna wazo lilivyozaliwa na kufanyiwa kazi:

eng: We think African and Kenyan lives matter, this cannot fall into oblivion so we created a WeChat group where very rapidly we had about 100 people who also shared the poster we made for the vigil in their own circles.
swa: Tunadhani maisha ya Waafrika na Wakenya yana thamani kubwa, hili haliwezi kusahaulika kiwepesi, kwa hiyo tulianzisha kundi la soga kwenye mtandao wa WeChat ambapo ndani ya muda mfupi tulifikia watu 100 tuliokuwa pia tukisambaza tangazo tulilokuwa tumelitengeneza kwa ajili ya ibada yetu ya mkesha kwa watu tuliokuwa tukiwafahamu.

eng: Some even used the WeChat to send messages to be later written on paper cards and sent to the families of the victims.
swa: Wengine walitumia mtandao wa WeChat kutuma ujumbe ambao baadae ungeandikwa kwenye kadi za karatasi na kuwatumia wanafamilia wa wahanga.

eng: But we had also a lot of people trying to sabotage the event, saying we shouldn't do something that has no official permission.
swa: Lakini pia tulikuwa na watu wengi waliokuwa wakijaribu kuhujumu tukio hilo, wakisema tusijaribu kuandaa tukio ambalo halina ruhusa rasmi.

eng: We had no money, no sponsor so we decide to organize ourselves limit to one hour to avoid problems and went for it.
swa: Hatukuwa na fedha, wala mfadhili na hivyo tuliamua kuandaa tukio la saa moja tu ili kukwepa matatizo na tukadhamiria.

eng: While organizing a public vigil may sound like a rather simple idea to implement, there is very little tolerance for manifestations of public sentiment, even grief, in China's public space without a long and complicated process of securing official authorizations.
swa: Wakati kuandaa ibada hiyo ya wazi kulionekana kama ni wazo jepesi tu la kutekeleza, kwa mazingira ya China, ni kama hakuna uvumilivu wa aina yoyote kwa yeyote anayeonesha hisia hadharani, ikiwa ni pamoja na maombolezo, bila kulazimika kupitia mchakato mrefu na mgumu wa kupata idhini rasmi ya kiusalama.

eng: In this case, the students decided to be creative and design an event that would allow for their feelings and concerns to be expressed without causing unnecessary trouble for the participants.
swa: Kwa sababu hiyo, wanafunzi waliamua kuwa wabunifu na kupanga tukio abalo lingewawezesha kuonesha hisia na wasiwasi wao bila kuwaingiza matatizoni washiriki wake.

eng: Poster for Garissa vigil in Beijing.
swa: Bango la ibada ya kumbukumbu ya Garissa jijini Beijing.

eng: Photo by Filip Noubel
swa: Picha na Filip Noubel

eng: The organizers spread the word on WeChat and through offline conversations for people to gather discreetly in Chaoyang park, one of the largest in the business part of Beijing.
swa: Waandaaji walisambaza ujumbe kwenye mtandao wa WeChat na kutumia majadiliano ya ana kwa ana na watu ili kujikusanya kwenye viwanja vya Chaoyang, moja wapo ya sehemu kubwa zaidi za kibiashara jijini Beijing.

eng: Technically, gatherings of less than 500 people do not need a permit in that park, while having a vigil even in front of the Kenyan embassy or in another commercial place would require cumbersome bureaucracy.
swa: Kiutaratibu, kukusanyika watu wasiozidi 500 kwenye viwanja hivyo hakuhitaji ruhusa, wakati kuwa na ibada ya kumbukumbu hata mbele ya ubalozi wa Kenya au kwenye eneo lolote la kibiashara kunahitaji kufuata urasimu mkubwa.

eng: One of the instructions shared on the WeChat group says:
swa: Moja wapo ya maelekezo yaliyotolewa kwenye kundi la mtandao wa WeChat yanasema:

eng: The optics should look like a normal picnic in a park.
swa: Tukio lionekane kama mtoko wa kawaida wa nje kwenye bustani hiyo.

eng: Bring some blankets.
swa: Mlete mablanketi.

eng: Another participant reminded that:
swa: Mshiriki mwingine alikumbushia kwamba:

eng: There is usually a gathering of 50 yoga practitionners in the park, and they don't have a permit.
swa: Kwa kawaida huwa kuna mkusanyiko wa watu wanaofikia 50 wanaofanya tahajudi kwenye bustani hiyo, na huwa hawalazimiki kupata ruhusa.

eng: As Tina Kinuthia explains:
swa: Tina Kinuthia anaeleza zaidi:

eng: We wanted a gathering in an open space, because this is also where vigils were organized in Garissa and Nairobi and we wanted something spontaneous.
swa: Tulitaka kuwa na mkusanyiko kwenye eneo la wazi, kwa sababu ibada za maombolezo kama hizi zilikuwa zinaandaliwa Garissa na Nairobi na tulitaka kuwa na matukio yanayotokea kwa wakati mmoja.

eng: The event included a reading of original poetry, a candlelight mini-memorial with a minute of silence and also the creation of cards addressed to the families of the 147 victims to be mailed to Kenya later.
swa: Tukio hilo lilihusisha kusomwa kwa mashairi yaliyotungwa na washiriki wenyewe, kuwasha mishumaa ya maombolezo inayoambatana na dakika moja ya kukaa kimya na pia kutengeneza kadi za pole zilizoandikwa kwa anuani za familia za wahanga 147 ambazo zingetumwa nchini Kenya baadae.

eng: The vigil's impact
swa: Matokeo ya Ibada Hiyo

eng: Around 70 African students gather near an entrance of the park to join the vigil.
swa: Wanafunzi wapatao 70 wa Kiafrika walikusanyika karibu na lango la bustani hiyo kuhudhuria ibada hiyo.

eng: Photo by Filip Noubel
swa: Picha na Filip Noubel

eng: Fortunately, the weather was good on April 18 in the late afternoon, as the students started to gather at one entrance of Chaoyang park to commemorate the victims.
swa: Kwa bahati nzuri, hali ya hewa ilikuwa murua alasiri ya Aprili 18, wanafunzi walipoanza kujikusanya kwenye moja wapo ya malango ya kuingilia bustani ya Chaoyang ili kuwakumbuka marehemu wa shambulizi hilo la Garissa.

eng: Nearly 70 people, including students from Africa and China, sat in a remote corner of the park in front of a make-shift altar with candles.
swa: Karibu watu 70, ikiwa ni pamoja na wanafunzi kutoka Afrika na China, walikaa kwenye kona ya mbali ya viwanja hivyo mbele ya picha maalum ya maombolezo wakiwa na mishumaa yao.

eng: Soon, Kenyan students began to deliver short speeches expressing grief but also concern at the future of Kenyan society.
swa: Kisha, wanafunzi wa Kenya walianza kutoa hotuba zao fupi kuonesha masikitiko yao lakini pia wasiwasi wao kuhusu mustakabali wa jamii ya Wakenya.

eng: Several speakers insisted that Kenya must overcome its differences and learn to live together despite differences in culture, ethnicity and religion.
swa: Wasemaji kadhaa walisisitiza kwamba Kenya lazima ishinde tofauti zilizopo na ijifunze kuishi pamoja bila kujali tofauti za utamaduni, makabila na dini.

eng: This was followed by a reading of several poems written in English specifically for the vigil.
swa: Sehemu hiyo ilifuatiwa na kusomwa kwa tenzi kadhaa zilizokuwa zimeandikwa kwa lugha ya Kiingereza mahususi kwa ajili ya ibada hiyo.

eng: One poem by Amina Jarso, a Kenyan student based in Beijing, reads:
swa: Utenzi mmoja uliotungwa na Amina Jarso, mwanafunzi wa Kenya anayeishi Beijing, unasomeka kama ifuatavyo:

eng: Her soul wanted to speak,
swa: Roho yake ilitaka kuzungumza,

eng: To ask of her accused crime,
swa: Kuulizia makosa anayotuhumiwa nayo,

eng: She wanted to reason with him,
swa: Alitaka kujadiliana naye,

eng: If only he'd give her more time.
swa: Ikiwa tu angempa muda zaidi.

eng: His eyes bloodshot with anger,
swa: Macho yake yalikodoa kwa hasira,

eng: Her eyes teary with fear,
swa: Macho yake yalibubujikwa na machozi,

eng: He fights to silence his conscience,
swa: anapambana kunyamazisha nafsi yake,

eng: She struggles not to shed a tear.
swa: anahangaika afanyeje machozi yasitiririke.

eng: They pause and inhale together,
swa: Walitulia kimya kuvuta pumzi pamoja,

eng: Two heartbeats synchronizing ,
swa: Mapigo ya moyo yakienda pamoja,

eng: the gun between has no pulse,
swa: Risasi kati yao haikutulia,

eng: An intruder in their first meeting.
swa: Imeingilia mkutano wao wa kwanza.

eng: Let's listen much more closely,
swa: Hebu na tusikilize zaidi kwa ukaribu,

eng: To the gaps of words unsaid,
swa: Kwa yale ambayo maneno hayakuyasema,

eng: And give the 147 back their names,
swa: Na tuwape wale 147 majina yao,

eng: So their memories won't just fade.
swa: Ili kumbukumbu zao zisipotee kirahisi.

eng: While another poem said:
swa: Utenzi mwingine ulisema:

eng: Face down helplessly I stand,
swa: Ninasimama nikiinama chini,

eng: Tears hitting hard the unarmed ground,
swa: Machozi yakidondoka kwa nguvu kwenye ardhi isiyo na silaha,

eng: 147 the number lingering in my mind,
swa: Tarakimu ya 147 ikiizonga fikra yangu,

eng: Remembering they will they will not be around.
swa: Nikikumbuka hatutawaona tena

eng: At this point of the vigil, a security officer for the park came to announce that all candles should be blown out and that the people should vacate the corner of the park.
swa: Katika hatua hii ya ibada, afisa mmoja wa usalama pale bustanini alifika na kutangaza kwamba mishumaa yote izimwe na watu wote watawanyike kuondoka kwenye sehemu hiyo.

eng: One student tried to negotiate and buy some time to allow for the completion of the vigil, but the guard remained standing by, informing her superiors by walkie-talkie and urging everyone to leave.
swa: Mwanafunzi mmoja alijaribu kujadiliana naye kumwomba asubiri kwa muda mfupi ili wamalize ibada, lakini mlinzi huyo alishikilia msimamo wake na kumjulisha mkuu wake huku akiwaamuru watu wote kutawanyika.

eng: Chinese perceptions of Garissa and the vigil
swa: Mtazamo wa Wachima kuhusu shambulio la Garissa na ibada hiyo ya kumbukumbu

eng: There were around 10 Chinese participants at the vigil, a mix of students, professors and friends of Kenya.
swa: Kulikuwa na washiriki 10 wa Kichina kwenye ibada hiyo, mchanganyiko wa wanafunzi, ma-Profesa na marafiki wa Kenya.

eng: Tina Kinuthia explains how some got involved:
swa: Tina Kinuthia anaeleza namna walivyopata taarifa na kuamua kushiriki:

eng: We got great support.
swa: Tulipata msaada mkubwa.

eng: A person who runs a travel agency saw a posting in Jinru Feizhou, volunteered to translate the poster and shared in her community, this is how we got Chinese people coming.
swa: Mtu anayeendesha kampuni ya usafiri aliona bango kwenye eneo la Jinru Feizhou, akajitolea kulitafsiri na kulisambaza kwenye jamii yake, hivyo ndivyo tulivyowapata baadhi ya washiriki wenzetu wa Kichina.

eng: One participant is a former student of Nairobi who still remembers a few words of Swahili and said she came because she felt that:
swa: Mshiriki mmoja alikuwa mwanafunzi jijini Nairobi na anakumbuka maneno kadhaa ya Kiswahili na akasema alikuja kwa sababu alijisikia kuwa:

eng: Nairobi is part of my home, and I care about Kenya.
swa: Nairobi ni sehemu ya nyumbani kwetu, na ninaijali sana Kenya.

eng: Another Chinese participant explained that:
swa: Mshiriki mwingine wa Kichina alieleza kwamba:

eng: Most of the people around me are shocked, we even had a discussion in our class on how to avoid such things happening, and what should be the role of government, universities and students?
swa: Watu wengi wanaonizunguka walishangaa, na tulikuwa na mjadala darasani kwetu namna gani tunaweza kuzuia matukio kama haya, na serikali, vyuo vikuu na wanafunzi kila mmoja kwa nafasi yake afanye nini?

eng: As one of the African organizers points out:
swa: Muandaaji mmoja wa Kiafrika alibainisha:

eng: Chinese people seem well aware, but without a platform to mourn and support Africa, there is no place for them to express themselves.
swa: Wachina wanaonekana kujua kinachoendelea, lakini bila jukwaa la kuomboleza wala kuiunga mkono Afrika, hakuna namna wanayoweza kuitumia kujieleza.

eng: While the WeChat group is still active, the event is also taking on a second life in the offline world.
swa: Wakati kikundi cha soga kwenye mtandao wa WeChat bado kipp, tukio hilo linafanyika wakati mwingine nje ya mtandao.

eng: The Africa 2.0 Kenya office will distribute the cards to the families of the victims and has requested the framed picture used for the makeshift altar to hang in their Nairobi office as a tangible sign of worldwide solidarity.
swa: Ofisi za Africa 2.0 Kenya office zitasambaza kadi kwa familia za wahanga na zimeomba picha iliyotumika kwenye ibada hiyo iwekwe kwenye ofisi za Nairobi kama alama ya mshikamo wa kidunia.

eng: Tree of Ténéré in 1961.
swa: Mti wa Ténéré mwaka 1961.

eng: CC-BY-SA 2.0.
swa: CC-BY-SA 2.0.

eng: The conflict with Boko Haram in southwest Niger currently monopolizes the country's news.
swa: Kwa sasa, mgogoro na Boko Haram huko Kusini Magharibi mwa Niger ndio unaotawala vichwa vya habari vya nchi hiyo.

eng: On March 3, Boko Haram killed 19 civilians in an attack on two villages, Kiu Keleha and Toubu Buka, situated on the Nigerien banks of Lake Chad.
swa: Mapema Machi 3, Boko Haram waliwaua raia 19 katika shambulizi lililotokea katika vijiji viwili vya, Kiu Keleha na Toubu Buka, vilivyopo pembezoni mwa ukanda wa mto Chad uliopita nchini Nigeria.

eng: In response, Nigerien armed forces have joined neighboring military groups to collaborate a counterattack on Boko Haram.
swa: Kufutia tukio hili, wanajeshi wa Nigeria waliungana na majeshi ya nchi nyingine za jirani katika kukabiliana na kundi la Boko Haram.

eng: Despite these efforts, however, Niger's southwest remains isolated and vulnerable.
swa: Hata hivyo, pamoja na juhudi zote hizi, sehemu ya Kusini Magharibi mwa Niger bado ni sehemu hatari na iliyotengwa.

eng: A new initiative by Nigerien bloggers, Mapping for Niger, is helping to increase national awareness by mapping the country’s towns, revealing a side of Niger that many living there didn't know existed.
swa: Mkakati mpya wa wanablogu wa Nigeria, Mapping for Niger, unasaidia kulitambulisha taifa kwa kuonesha maeneo mbalimbali ya miji, wameanza kuliweka katika ramani eneo la Niger ambalo watu wengi wanaoishi huko hawakuwahi kulifahamu.

eng: The East: an isolated region and home to the Little Prince
swa: Magharibi: Eneo lililotengwa na mahali palipo na mtoto mdogo wa mfalme

eng: Just like the Tree of Ténéré (which was for a long time the most isolated tree in the world, until it was destroyed by a negligent driver), east Niger is partially isolated from the rest of the country.
swa: Kama ilivyo kwa Mti wa Ténéré (ambao kwa muda mrefu umekuwa mti uliojitenga kuliko mwingine wowote ule duniani, ambao kipindi fulani uliharibiwa na dereva ambaye hakuwa makini), Niger ya Magharibi kwa kiasi fulani imetengwa ukilinganisha na sehemu nyingine yoyote ya nchi hii.

eng: This isolation makes it more difficult to coordinate efforts to combat Boko Haram, exposing it to assaults by the rebels.
swa: Kutengwa huku kwa Niger ya magharibi kunafanya mikakati ya kukabiliana na Boko Haram kuwa migumu, na hivyo kulifanya eneo hili kushambuliwa kwa urahisi na magaidi.

eng: The history of the region, and more specifically the Tree of Ténéré, however, is quite unique.
swa: Hata vivyo, historia ya eneo hili, hususani mti wa Ténéré, ni wa kipekee sana.

eng: The legendary Tree of Ténéré was an acacia, isolated in the middle of the desert, the only tree for 400 kilometers (250 miles) around.
swa: Mti wa kihistoria wa Ténéré ulikuwa ni wa jamii ya acacia, uliojitenga katikati mwa jangwa, mti wa pekee ulio katika kipenyo cha jangwa cha kilomita 400 sawa na maili 250.

eng: It was the only tree in the world to be so isolated, serving as a landmark for the caravan routes crossing the Sahel, but also inspired many poets, who fell in love with the desert, as shown in these videos by A. Décotte:
swa: Ulikuwa ni mti wa pekee duniani uliokuwa umejitenga, uliokuwa unatumiwa kama alama na safari za watu waliosafiri kwa magari kupitia Sahel, lakini pia ni mti uliopendwa sana na washairi, waliotokea kulipenda jangwa hili kama inavyooneshwa katika video hizi zilizowekwa na A. Décotte:

eng: and B. Hofmans:
swa: na B. Hofmans:

eng: On Google Maps and Google Earth, the location of the Tree of Ténéré is marked by a stunning photo of the tree overlaid with a phrase from "The Little Prince" (shared by Pierre Destruel):
swa: Katika picha za Google pamoja na picha za ardhini za Google, mahali palipo na mti wa Ténéré kunaoneshwa kwa picha ya kuvutia ya mti huu iliyoambatana na maneno ya"The Little Prince" (imewekwa na Pierre Destruel):

eng: The Little Prince is Back: What makes the desert beautiful is that somewhere it hides a well.
swa:
Mtoto mdogo wa Mfalme amerejea: Kinacholifanya jangwa kuvutia ni kuwa kuna sehemu katika jangwa hili kuna chemmchem.
Photo composition by Pierre Destruel.	Picha na Pierre Destruel.
P. Destruel has added the following caption to explain the image he has made between the tree and The Little Prince, quoting a passage from the book by Antoine de Saint-Exupéry: 	P. Destruel ameweka picha ifuatayo katika kuelezea taswara aliyoijenga kati ya mti na mtoto mdogo wa mfalme, akitumia kifungu cha maneno kutoka kwenye kitabu cha Antoine de Saint-Exupéry:
Look at it carefully so that you will be sure to recognise it in case you travel some day to the African desert.	Iangalie kwa makini ili baade uweze kuitambua vizuri endapo siku moja utasafiri katika jangwa hili.
And, if you should come upon this spot, please do not hurry on. 	Kama utafika mahali hapa, tafadhali, usiwe na haraka.
Wait for a time, exactly under the star. 	Subiri kwa muda, sawia chini ya jua.
Then, if a little man appears who laughs, who has golden hair and who refuses to answer questions, you will know who he is. 	Kama atatokea kijana mdogo akicheka, aliye na nywele za rangi ya dhahabu na akataaye kujibu swali lolote, hapo utakuwa umeshamtambua yeye ni nani.
If this should happen, please comfort me. 	Kama hili litatokea, tafadhali, unifariji.
Send me word that he has come back.	Nitumie ujumbe kuwa tayari amesharejea.
The Project— Mapping for Niger	Mradi— Kuchora ramani za kufuatilia matukio nchini Niger
This project is being run collectively by the geography department of the Abdou Moumouni University in Niamey, its students, Open Street Map, and Rising Voices. 	Mradi huu unaendeshwa kwa ushirikiano na idara ya Jiografia ya Chuo Kikuu cha Abdou Moumouni kilichopo Niamey, wanafunzi wake, Open Street Map, pamoja na Rising Voices.
The project trains students and the rest of the team in the skills they need to participate in a collaborative open-source mapping project.	Mradi huu unatoa mafunzo stahiki kwa ajili ya mradi huu kwa wanafunzi pamoja na washiriki wengine wote.
Armed with these news skills in mapping and citizen journalism, participants have been going out into the surrounding rural villages to map key sites, such as schools, roads, and hospitals. 	Wakiwa tayari na ujuzi wa maarifa haya mapya ya uboreshaji wa ramani pamoja na uanahabari wa kiraia, washiriki wamekuwa wakitembelea vijiji vya karibu ili kuboresha katika ramani taarifa za maeneo muhimu kama vile shule, barabara pamoja na hospitali.
They have also used their skills to link the maps created directly with the needs of the local communities.	Wameweza pia kutumia maarifa waliyojifunza kwa kuunganisha ramani walizoziandaa na mahitaji muhimu ya jamii.
On International Women’s Day, for example, the contribution of female participants was recognised and celebrated at a training workshop with the organisations ITECH CENTER, Fada Tech, and Femmes & Tic Niger (an association created by Fatima Alher, a member of the Mapping for Niger project): 	Kwa mfano, kwenye Siku ya Wanawake Duniani, mchango wa washiriki wanawake ulitambuliwa na kusherehekewa katika katika kituo cha mafunzo na mashirika ya ITECH CENTER, Fada Tech, na Femmes & Tic Niger (Umoja ulioanzishwa na Fatima Alher, ambaye ni mmoja wa wanachama wa Mradi wa Kuiweka Niger katika Ramani):
OpenStreetMap Mapping workshop with Femmes & TIC Niger (created by Fatima Alher), via Mapping for Niger on Facebook. 	Mafunzo ya OpenStreetMap ya uwekaji ramani na Femmes & TIC Niger (Iliyoanzishwa na Fatima Alher).
So far, the project has helped improve and enrich maps of Madaoua, Niamey, Dosso, Zinder, Kolmane, and Guidan Toudo. 	Hadi sasa, mradi huu umesaidia kuongeza na kuboresha ramani za Madaoua, Niamey, Dosso, Zinder, Kolmane, na Guidan Toudo.
The project will also expand gradually to other regions of Niger.	Mradi huu pia utazidi kupanuka taratibu katika maeneo mengine ya Niger.
Other organisations, such as Search for Common Ground, will collaborate with these initiatives to strengthen the communities in vulnerable areas. 	Mashirika mengine kama vile Search for Common Ground nalo litashiriki katika miradi kama hii ili kuboresha hali za wanajamii walio katika maeneo hatarishi.
Although this is still an informal collaboration, Search for Common Ground is involved in several other important projects, including efforts to strengthen social cohesion and advance the peace process, particularly among young people of Zinder: 	Pamoja na kuwa, katika hatua hii bado ni ushirikiano ambao siyo rasmi, Search for Common Ground linashiriki katika miradi mingine muhimu, ukiwemo wa jitihada za kuleta hali ya umoja katika jamii na kuendeleza harakati za kuleta amani, hususani miongoni mwa vijana wadogo wa jamii ya Zinder:
We succeeded in training 172 youth, including more than 40 young women. 	Tulifanikiwa kuwapatia mafunzo vijana 172, wakiwemo wanawake zaidi ya 40.
Participants came from various socioeconomic backgrounds, ranging from university students to illiterate gang members, and were of different ethnicities, ages, and institutional affiliations. 	Washiriki walitoka katika matabaka tofauti ya kijamii, kuanzia wanafunzi wa vyuo hadi vijana wa magenge na wasiokuwa na elimu, na pia waliotokea katika makabila tofauti, marika tofauti na waliotoka katika taasisi mbalimbali.
Another 806 young people, 10% of them women, shared their thoughts on new concepts and discovered how to apply them in their own context. 	Vijana wengine 806, asilimia 10 wakiwa ni wanawake, walitoa mawazo yao kuhusiana na maarifa waliyojifunza na pia kutambua namna ya kutumia maarifa waliyoyapata katika mazingira yao.
After our training, a reformed gang leader requested an extra restitution session for the students of a vocational school in Zinder. 	Mara baada ya mafunzo yetu, kiongozi wa kundi la vijana lililozaliwa upya aliomba kurudiwa kwa mafunzo hayo kwa ajili ya wanafunzi wa shule ya ufundi iliyopo Zinder.
	
From the Facebook page of Zunar Kartunis	Kutoka kwenye ukurasa wa Facebook wa Zunar Kartunis
A Malaysian cartoonist facing several sedition charges has vowed to keep on using his pen to criticize government corruption, human rights violations, and abuses of power. 	Mchora katuni wa Malaysia anayekabiliwa na mashtaka ya uchochezi ameapa kuendelea kutumia penseli yake kuikosoa serikali kwa ufisadi, ukiukwaji wa haki za binadamu, na matumizi mabaya ya madaraka.
Zulkiflee Sm Anwar Ulhaque, more popularly known as Zunar in Malaysia, is a political cartoonist who has been arrested twice for alleged violations of the Sedition Act, a colonial-era law. 	Zulkiflee Sm Anwar Ulhaque, anayefahamika zaidia kama Zunar nchini Malaysia, ni mchoraji w akatuni ambaye amewahi kuwekwa ndani mara mbli kwa mashtaka ya kuvunja sheria ya Uchochezi, iliyotungwa na wakoloni.
Zunar, who was arrested earlier this month, was charged with nine counts of sedition. 	Zunar, ambaye alikamatwa mapema mwezi huu, alishtakiwa kwa makosa tisa ya uchochezi.
If found guilty, he can be detained for a maximum of 43 years. 	Akipatwa na hatia, anaweza kufungwa kwa miaka isiyozidi 43.
He is currently out on bail.	Hivi sasa yuko nje kwa dhamana.
Zunar has been critical of the ruling coalition which has been in power since the 1950s.	Zunar amekuwa mkosoaji mkubwa wa chama kinachotawala tangu miaka ya 1950.
Because of his activism, five of his cartoon compilations are banned in Malaysia. 	Kwa sababu ya harakati zake, vitabu vitano ya katuni zake vimepigwa marufuku nchini Malaysia.
Even those who print, distribute, and sell these books are harassed by the government. 	Hata wale wanachapisha, kutawanya na kuuza vitabu hivi wanapata bughudha ya serikali.
Instead of backing down, Zunar refuses to be intimidated. 	Badala ya kurudi nyuma, Zunar amegoma kutishika.
He once said that “as the regime sharpens their iron fists, my pen gets sharper!” 	Aliwahi kusema kwamba kadri utawala unavyonoa ngumi zake za chuma, ndivyo penseli yangu inavyozidi kuwa na makali!"

eng: He added:
swa: Aliongeza:

eng: Talent is not a gift, but a responsibility.
swa: Kipaji si zawadi, bali wajibu.

eng: So I will use it as a tool to convey people’s voice through art and to push for total reform for a better Malaysia.
swa: Kw ahiyo nitakitumia kama zana ya kupaza sauti ya watu kupitia sanaa na kushinikiza mabadiliko kwa maslahi ya Malaysia.

eng: I will not keep quiet.
swa: Sitanyamaza.

eng: How can I be neutral, even my pen has a stand!
