swa: Kwa nini nisioneshe upande, wakati hata penseli yangu huwa na upande nikiitumia?

eng: From the Facebook page of Zunar Kartunis
swa: Kutoka kwenye ukurasa wa Facebook wa Zunar Kartunis

eng: Asked about his technique, Zunar explained that it’s important for an artist to 'take a stand' and convey the right message to the reading public:
swa: Alipoulizwa kuhusu mbinu yake, Zunar alieleza kwamba ni muhimu kwa msanii 'kuwa na msimamo unaoeleweka' na kutoa ujumbe sahihi kwa hadhira yake:

eng: My ideas are based on current issues, especially politics.
swa: Mawazo yangu hutokana na masuala yanayotokea, hususani siasa.

eng: When an issue arises, the first step is to understand the issue from different sources and perspectives.

eng: This is Uganda (ThisIs256) is a platform of talented writers from Uganda who are determined to write positive stories about their country, banishing stories about poverty porn, hunger, Ebola, and tribalism, among others.
swa: This is Uganda (ThisIs256) ni jukwaa la waandishi waliobobea kutoka Uganda walio na utayari wa kuandika habari makini za kuihusu nchi yao, wakilenga kutokomeza uanahabari uchwara, njaa, Ebola, ukabila, pamoja na mambo mengine.

eng: They seek to represent an authentic, reflective, honest, and objectively balanced study about Uganda that you will never find anywhere else in mainstream western media.
swa: Wanachojaribu kukifanya ni kuanzisha aina ya utafiti kuihusu Uganda ambao ni halisi, makini, wa kweli na usio wa kiupendeleo ambao kamwe usingalikuwa rahisi kuuona kwenye vyombo vikuu vya habari vya magharibi.

eng: Their latest story is about Victor Ochen, a former internally displaced person who was nominated by the American Friends Service Committee (AFSC), a Quaker social justice organisation, for the Nobel Peace Prize.
swa: Habari yao ya hivi karibuni ni ya kumhusu Victor Ochen,aliyekuwa mmoja wa wakimbizi wa ndani, aliyependekezwa na American Friends Service Committee (AFSC), ambayo ni taasisi ya utetezi wa haki za kiraia, kushindania Tuzo ya Amani ya Nobeli.

eng: In the past, AFSC nominated Desmond Tutu, Martin Luther King Jr., and US President Jimmy Carter, who all became winners.
swa: Kwa kipindi cha nyuma, AFSC iliwapendekeza akina Desmond Tutu, Martin Luther King Jr., na Rais wa Marekani, Jimmy Carter, ambao wote walifanikiwa kushinda tuzo hii.

eng: The organisation unsuccessfully nominated Mahatma Gandhi, who never won the Nobel Peace Prize, although he was nominated five times between 1937 and 1948.
swa: Taasisi hii mara kadhaa ilimpendekeza Mahatma Gandhi, ambaye hata mara moja hakufanikiwa kutangazwa mshindi wa tuzo ya amani ya Nobeli, pamoja na kupendekezwa kuigombea mara tano kati ya miaka ya 1937 na 1948.

eng: Ochen, 33, founded the African Youth Initiative Network, based in Lira, Uganda, in 2005, which works in medical rehabilitation of victims of burnings, mutilations of all kinds, rape, and psychological torture as well as promotes youth leadership.
swa: Ochen, mwenye umri wa miaka 33, alianzisha taasisi ya African Youth Initiative Network, mnamo mwaka 2005 iliyo na mskani yake huko Lira, Uganda, taasisi iliyo na jukumu la kuwasaidia watu kurudia katika hali yao ya awali wakiwemo wale walioungua kwa moto, ukeketaji wa namna mbalimbali, ubakaji, pamoja na unyanyasaji wa kisaikolojia ikiwa ni pamoja na kuwahamasisha vijana katika masuala ya uongozi.

eng: It has grown to become an international network of medical professionals who help victims rebuild their homes and livelihoods.
swa: Hadi sasa taasisi hii imeshapanuka kiasi cha kuwa mtandao wa kimataifa wa wataalamu wa tiba ambao jukumu lao ni kuwasaidia wahanga kujenga upya makazi yao na maisha yao.

eng: According to This is Uganda:
swa: Kwa mujibu wa This is Uganda:

eng: What Victor did out of sheer compassion added him to this prestigious list.
swa: Kwa kile Victor alichokifanya kwa moyo wake wa dhati wa kujitolea, ndicho kilichomfanya kuwa mmoja wa watu waliopendekezwa kuwania tuzo hii iliyo ya heshima ya hali yajuu.

eng: As a teenager in Abia camp that was home of over 40,000 people, he formed a peace club with his peers in the camp.
swa: Akiwa kijana mdogo katika kambi ya Abia iliyokuwa na watu zaidi ya 40,000, kambini hapo, aliweza kuanzisha kikundi cha amani akiwa na wenzake.

eng: This initiative angered the elders “Why are you talking about peace that you have never seen?”
swa: Mkakati huu uliwakasirisha wazee kiasi cha kumuuliza “Kwa nini unaongelea amani ambayo hujawahi kuiona?”

eng: He was enterprising; he risked his life to burn charcoal to raise his school fees.
swa: Alijitolea; alihatarisha maisha yake kwa kuchoma mkaa ili apate ada ya shule.

eng: Then later he joined secondary school and could barely afford time to do his charcoal business so he became a cobbler, he used to repair shoes of kids at school.
swa: Baadae alijiunga na elimu ya sekondari ambapo ni mara chache sana alipata muda wa kufanya biashara yake ya mkaa, hivyo alilazimika kuwa fundi viatu, alikuwa akirekebisha viatu vya watoto shuleni.

eng: One day he landed a big job of mending the shoes of the school football team, unfortunately that money was stolen.
swa: Wakati fulani Victor alijipatia kazi nzuri ya kufanya maboresho ya viatu vya timu ya shule ya mpira wa miguu, kwa bahati mbaya fedha aliyoipata iliibwa.

eng: His hard work and favor from the teachers saw him through high school.
swa: Kusoma kwake kwa bidii na kupendwa kwake na walimu kulimuwezesha kusoma elimu ya upili.

eng: Victor’s heart was home even when he worked with straight talk foundation in Kampala, interacting with the people in the field made him realize that the people of northern Uganda wanted more than hand outs but wanted and deserved more.
swa: Victor alionesha uzalendo wa kweli kwa nchi yake hata pale alipokuwa akifanya kazi na taasisi ya straight talk foundation ya Kampala, alipokuwa akikutana na watu katika shughuli zake aligundua kuwa watu wa Kaskazini mwa Uganda kuna mengine zaidi walistahili na walihitaji mbali na vipeperushi.

eng: That is when he left his job and started the African youth initiative Network.
swa: Na hili ndilo lililomfanya akaacha kazi yake na kuanzisha Mradi wa Mtandao wa Vijana wa Kiafrika (African youth initiative Network).

eng: This initiative mobilizes communities especially the youth to pursue peace and human rights, reconciliation.
swa: Mradi huu unazikutanisha jamii na hususani vijana ili waweze kudumisha amani pamoja na kulinda haki za binadamu na kuleta maridhiano.

eng: They offer psychosocial support to the former victims of conflict, most of who suffer severe emotional pain and struggle with forgiveness, they have also supported over 5000 people with reconstructive surgeries especially the women whose lips were cut off, the initiative also supports income generating activities, have formed 100 peace clubs in schools and universities in northern Uganda and over 6000 young people have gone through the peace building and transitional justice programme.
swa: Wanatoa msaada wa saikolojia ya inayohusiana na matatizo ya kijamii, wanatoa msaaada kwa wahanga wa migogoro iliyotokea kipindi cha nyuma, wengi wao wakiwa ni wale walio na maumivu makali ya kihisia na wanaohangaika kupata msamaha, pia wameshasaidia zaidi ya watu 5000 waliokuwa wanahitaji upasuaji wa kurekebisha sehemu za mwili hususani kwa wanawake ambao midomo yao ilikatwa. Mradi huu ambao pia unawawezesha vijana katika shughuli mbalimbali za kuwapatia kipato, umesaidia pia kuaanzishwa kwa klabu 100 amani kaitka mashule na kwenye vyuo vikuu Kaskazini mwa Uganda na zaidi ya vijana 6000 wameshahudhuria mafunzo ya kuimarisha amani na upatikanaji wa waki.

eng: Tokyo Metropolitan Police arrested Igarashi in July 2014 for allegedly emailing crowd-funders of her art project links to a webpage, where they could download 3D data that could be used to create vulva-shaped kayaks based on the shape of her genitals.
swa: Polisi wa Jiji la Tokyo walimkamata Igarashi mwezi Julai 2014 kwa kudaiwa kuwatuma viungo vya mtandao kwa njia ya barua pepe kwa wafadhili wa mradi wake ili waweze kupakua (download) data zenye taswira halisi ambazo zingeweza kutumika kutengeneza kayak zenye sura ya uke inayotokana na sehemu zake za siri.

eng: Igarashi was again arrested several months later for displaying another artwork based on the shape of her genitalia in a Tokyo sex shop—a clear case of police harassment, according to her lawyer.
swa: Igarashi alikamatwa tena mara kadhaa kwa kuonesha kazi yake ya sanaa iliyokuwa na sura ya sehemu zake za siri kwenye duka moja la ngono jijini Tokyo -kitendo cha kidhalilishaji kilichofanywa na Polisi, kwa mujibu wa mawanasheria wake.

eng: For several months prior to her arrest in July 2014, Igarashi, who also goes by the pseudonym 'Rokudenashiko" ( ろくでなし子 or "good-for-nothing girl"), had gained notoriety for creating and displaying a variety of works of art based on the shape of her genitals.
swa: Kwa miezi kadhaa kabla ya kukamatwa kwake mwezi Julai, Igarashi, anayetumia jina la 'Rokudenashiko" ( ろくでなし子 yaani "msichana wa hovyo"), alipata umaarufu kwa kutengeneza aina mbalimbali za kazi ya sanaa kwa kutumia sura ya sehemu zake za siri.

eng: Megumi Igarashi, aka Rokudenaishiko, is the Tokyo artist accused of obscenity.
swa: Megumi Igarashi, kwa jina jingine Rokudenaishiko, ni msanii wa Tokyo anayetuhumiwa kukiuka maadili.

swa: Hebu tuangalie baadhi ya kazi zake za sanaa.

eng: In Japan, media portraying either the male or female genitalia are illegal under Article 175 of the penal code.
swa: Nchini Japan, vyombo vya habari kuonesha sehemu za siri ni kosa la jinai chini ya Kifungu cha 175 cha makosa ya jinai.

eng: The prohibition dates back to the Meiji Period, when Japan adopted Western practices and institutions in the latter half of the 19th Century.
swa: Zuio hilo lilianza enzi za Meiji, wakati Japani ikianza kukubaliana na utamaduni na taasisi za kimagharibi kwenye nusu ya pili ya karne ya 19.

eng: Interestingly, Article 175 offers no clear guidance to police or courts about what constitutes obscenity in these cases:
swa: Hata hivyo, ibara ya 175 haina mwongozo uliowazi kwa polisi au mahakama kuhusu kile kinachoweza kuitwa kukosa maadili katika kesi kama hizi::

eng: ...There is not a clause in this article, which defines the term "obscenity" and "neither government administrators nor the courts were legally compelled to specify what constituted "obscene material".
swa: ...Hakuna kifungu kwenye ibara hii, kinachotafsiri neno "ukosefu wa maadili" na "si watawala wa serikali wala mahakama zililazimishwa kufafanua kile kinachoitwa "vitu visivyo vya kimaadili".

eng: It is little wonder that multiple interpretations have been given to this article with regards to its application.
swa: Inashangaza kidogo kwamba tafsiri nyingi zimekuwa zikitolewa kwenye ibara hii kuhusiana na namna inavyoweza kutumika.

eng: If we consider visual material such as manga or cinema, the law has interpreted the term obscenity in this article as the exposure of pubic hair, the adult genitals and the sexual act.
swa: Kama tunachukulia vifaa vinavyoonekana kama vile manga au sinema, sheria imetafsiri neno ukosefu wa maadili kwenye ibara hii kama kuonesha vinyweleo vya sehemu za siri, sehemu za siri za watu wazima na tendo la ngono.

eng: Thus, if this should happen the exposed parts in any kind of visual material should be hidden with what in Japan is called bokashi (blurring or fogging) or with a digital mosaic.
swa: Kwa hiyo, kama hili ndivyo lilivyo basi maana yake kifaa chochote kinachoonesha sehemu hizi lazima kifichwe kwa kile Japani inachokiita bokashi (giza giza/kivuli) au kwa ukungu wa kidijitali.

eng: This extremely vague definition of obscenity has created numerous inconsistencies in court decisions, which are central to the current debate on freedom of speech in Japan.
swa: Tafsiri hii ya uvunjifu wa maadili isiyo na maana inayoeleweka imesababisha kutokufanana kwa maamuzi mengi ya mahakama, ambavyo ni sehemu ya mjadala wa uhuru wa kujieleza nchini Japani.

eng: Japanese culture also has a strong taboo about discussing or even acknowledging vaginas (although Holland-based Metroplis TV, the publisher of the informative clip below, has no problem with using the term "Pussy Boat" to describe Igarashi's vulva-shaped kayak):
swa: Utamaduni wa Japani pia una mwiko mkali kuhusu kujadili au hata kuonesha kuwa kuna kiungo kinaitwa uke (ingawa Metroplis TV yenye Kidachi, mchapishaji wa kipande hiki kinachoelimisha hapa chini, haina tatizo na kutumia maneno kama "Mtumbwi wa uke" kuelezea kayak za Igarashi zenye sura ya uke):

eng: However, the cyber crime bill is new, and the version posted online (not the final version) caused debate instantly.
swa: Hata hivyo, muswada wa makosa ya mtandao ni mpya, na toleo lake lililowekwa mtandaoni (na si toleo lililofanyiwa marekebisho bungeni) lilisababisha mjadala mkali ndani ya muda mfupi.

eng: As in many other countries, online fraud and financial scams indeed are a persistent threat in Tanzania.
swa: Kama ilivyo kwenye nchi nyingine, makosa ya mtandaoni na uhalifu wa kifedha kwa hakika ni tishio la muda mrefu kwa Tanzania.

eng: But the bill covers much more than this.
swa: Lakini muswada huu unashughulikia mambo mengi zaidi ya uhalifu huu.

eng: And it has now passed the parliament despite criticism from opposition politicians, social media practitioners and human rights activists.
swa: Na kwa sasa muswada huu umepitishwa na bunge pamoja na kukosolewa vikali na wanasiasa wa upinzani, wadau wa mitandao ya kijamii na wanaharakati wa haki za binadamu.

eng: Leading opponents of the legislation from civil society say they will take the government to court if the president signs the bill into law.
swa: Wakosoaji wakuu wa muswada huu kutoka kwenye asasi za kiraia wanasema wataipeleka serikali mahakamani kama rais atauidhinisha muswada huu kuwa sheria.

eng: The Citizen, a local newspaper, has identified several of the most concerning areas of the bill for Internet users.
swa: Gazeti linalochapishwa nchini Tanzania, The Citizen, limebainisha maeneo kadhaa makuu kwenye muswada huo yatakayowaathiri watumiaji wa mtandao wa intaneti.

eng: In an analysis for CIPESA, a regional ICT policy group, Ugandan journalist and analyst Juliet Nanfuka writes that the primary aim of cyber crime bill should be to safeguard citizens' rights on the Internet.
swa: Katika uchambuzi uliofanywa na CIPESA, kikundi cha sera za teknolojia ya habari na mawasiliano, Mwandishi na mchambuzi wa Uganda Juliet Nanfuka anaandika kwamba lengo kuu la muswada huo wa makosa ya jinai linapaswa kuwa kulinda haki za raia wawapo mtandaoni.

eng: Instead, she says, it shows an "overt disregard for press freedom and freedom of expression, excessive powers to police, and protections afforded to ordinary citizens."
swa: Badala yake, anasema, muswada huo unaonesha “kupuuza uhuru wa habari na kujieleza, mamlaka makubwa kwa polisi, na ulinzi unaotarajiwa kwa wananchi wa kawaida.”

eng: The bill outlaws the publication of "misleading, deceptive or false" information, a measure that Nanfuka noted presents a clear threat to free and open expression online.
swa: Muswada huu unazuia kuchapishwa kwa “taarifa zinazopotosha, zenye udanganyifu au zisizo na ukweli”, kipimo ambacho Nanfuka anasema kinaleta tishio la wazi kwa haki ya kujieleza kwa uhuru na uwazi mtandaoni.

eng: It gives police wide ranging ability to search the homes of suspected violators of the law, seize their electronic hardware, and demand their data from online service providers.
swa: Muswada huo unawapa polisi mamlaka makubwa ya kupekua nyumba za watu wanaohisiwa kuvunja sheria hiyo, kukamata vifaa vyao vya kieletroniki, na hata kudai data zao kutoka kwa makampuni yanayotoa huduma za mtandao.

eng: Aidan Eyakuze and Ben Taylor, both of whom work for the independent East African initiative Twaweza, argued that the bill gives too much power to police without meaningful oversight:
swa: Aidan Eyakuze na Ben Taylor, wote wawili wakifanya kazi kwenye asasi huru inayofanya kazi zake Afrika Mashariki iitwayo Twaweza, walikuwa na hoja kwamba muswada huo unatoa nguvu nyingi mno kwa polisi bila namna nzuri ya kuwadhibiti:

eng: ...the bill gives even very junior police officers the power to search and/or seize any computer equipment or data, including the content of messages, with no meaningful justification required or oversight provided.
swa: ...muswada unampa mamlaka hata afisa mdogo kabisa wa polisi kupekua na/au kumnyang’anya raia kifaa cha kompyuta au data, ikiwa ni pamoja na maudhui ya ujumbe, bila sababu au usimamizi unaoeleweka.

eng: This includes demanding information from internet service providers and mobile phone networks.
swa: Hii ni pamoja na kudai taarifa za mtumiaji kutoka kwenye makampuni yanayotoa huduma za intaneti na mitandao ya simu za mkononi.

eng: Tanzanian blogger Thinklessactmore noted that police could use the law to "harass online activists in the name of suspicion of cyber bullying without due of the law."
swa: Mwanablogu wa ki-TanzaniaThinklessactmore alibainisha kwamba polisi wanaweza kutumia sheria hii “kuwabughudhi wanaharakati wa mtandaoni kwa kisingizio cha kuwa na mashaka na udhalilishaji wa mtandaoni bila kufuata utaratibu wa kisheria."

eng: Twitter user Sultan Rajab, a tax and financial consultant in Tanzania, said he thought well of the bill, but was concerned about the powers it bestows upon police:
swa: Mtumiaji wa mtandao wa Twita Sultan Rajab, ambaye ni mshauri mwelekezi wa masuala ya kodi na kifedha nchini Tanzania, alisema alifikiri muswada ni mzuri, lakini alikuwa na wasiwasi na mamlaka waliyopewa polisi:

eng: @JMakamba it is a good bill/law.
swa: Ni muswada/sheria nzuri.

eng: I am worried about the power given to our police.
swa: Nina wasiwasi na mamlaka waliyopewa polisi.

eng: Ignorant & low income earners might suffer. — Sultan Rajab (@SultanKipupwe) April 1, 2015
swa: Wananchi wasio na elimu na wenye kipato kidogo wanaweza kupata msukosuko mkubwa.

eng: The bill also criminalizes the sending of information "without prior solicitation" by electronic means.
swa: Muswada huu pia unaeleza kwamba kutuma taarifa “bila idhini ya anayetumiwa” kwa njia za kieletroniki ni kosa la jinai.

eng: While this section is intended to address spam and phishing attacks, it could be interpreted quite broadly.
swa: Wakati kipengele hiki kikikusudia kudhibiti vitendo vya usambazaji wa ujumbe wenye madhara kwa anayeupokea, bado kinaweza kutafsiriwa kwa upana.

eng: Maria Sarungi Tsehai, a communications expert and founder of the organisation Change Tanzania, asked:
swa: Maria Sarungi Tsehai, mtaalam wa mawasiliano na muasisi wa taasisi ya Change Tanzania , aliuliza:

eng:
@jpb4rretto: @MariaSTsehai How is any message transmitted with solicitation? 	Inawezekanaje ujumbe wowote kutumwa kwa idhini ya anayeupokea?
Call me and ask me to write you and email? #CyberCrimeBill — Maria Sarungi Tsehai (@MariaSTsehai) April 2, 2015
swa: Kwa kunipigia na kuniomba nikuandikie barua pepe?

eng: But unlike the Cyber Crime Bill, none of these three bills have been shared with the public in their current versions.
swa: Lakini tofauti na Muswada wa Makosa ya Mtandaoni, miswada hiyo mitatu haikuonekana hadharani katika matoleo yao ya hivi sasa.

eng: Commenters on social media and journalists are sharing opinions on why they think the Tanzanian government has an interest in keeping these bills from the public, while at the same time rushing the process.
swa: Wachambuzi kwenye mitandao ya kijamii na waandishi wa habari wanajadiliana namna gani wanafikiri serikali inaweza kuwa na maslahi fulani kwa kuzuia miswada hii isionekane hadharani, wakati huo huo ikiharakisha mchakato.

eng: Some question if it is due to the fact that Tanzania is preparing for elections in late October 2015.
swa: Baadhi wanahoji ikiwa ni kwa ajili ya maandalizi ya uchaguzi utakaofanyika mwishoni mwa mwezi Oktoba mwaka huu nchini Tanzania.

eng: Tanzania's ruling party, Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM), over the past few years increasingly has confronted the growing influence of opposition parties.
swa: Chama kinachotawala nchini Tanzania, Chama cha Mapinduzii (CCM), kwa miaka kadhaa iliyopita kimekuwa kikipata ushindani unaoendelea kukua siku kwa siku kutoka kwenye vyama vya Upinzani nchini humo.

eng: At the same time, journalists and media have also faced threats and violence.
swa: Wakati huo huo, waandishi wa habari na vyombo vya habari vimekuwa vikipata misukosuko na kutishwa.

eng: Writing on Washington Post blog, Keith Weghorst and Ruth Carlitz argue that fast-tracking the bills is "consistent with the behavior of a ruling party willing to hold onto power at all costs." They write, "The more that the government can weaken the legitimacy of opposition criticism—by monopolizing the flow of public information—the better they are positioned to prevent scandals and poor performance from hurting them at the polls."
swa: Wakiandika kwenye blogu ya Washington Post, Keith Weghorst na Ruth Carlitz wanadhani kwamba kuharakishwa kwa miswada hiyo “kunaendana na tabia ya chama hicho kinachotawala ya kutaka kung’ang’ania madaraka kwa gharama yoyote.” wanaandika, "kadri serikali inavyodhoofisha uhalali wa mashambulizi ya upinzani –kwa kuhodhi upatikanaji wa taarifa za umma –ndivyo inavyokuwa kwenye nafasi nzuri ya kuzuia kashfa na utendaji duni zisiwadhuru kwenye uchaguzi.”

eng: Thinklessandactmore was impressed that Tanzania has realized the need to regulate the Internet use, but said the bill was rushed into parliament:
swa: Thinklessandactmore alifurahishwa kwamba Tanzania imetambua uhitaji wa kudhibiti matumizi ya mtandao, lakini akasema muswada huo uliwahishwa mno kupelekwa bungeni:

eng: It’s important to have law that would regulate online activities and the use of internet but it should be done in a right way.
swa: Ni muhimu kuwa na sheria ambayo itadhibiti shughuli za mtandaoni na watumiaji wa mtandao wa intaneti lakini hilo lifanyike kwa namna sahihi.

eng: There is no hurry in having such law; there was none in the past 53 years of independence.
swa: Hakuna uharaka wa kuw ana sheria hiyo; haikuwepo kwa miaka 53 tangu tupate uhuru.

eng: If it takes one or two years to have a better cyber-crime law be it so, let’s conduct enough research on the issues; collect different opinions about the bill before it is present in the parliament.
swa: Kama itachukua mwaka au miaka miwili kuwa na sheria bora ya makosa ya mtandaoni, iwe hivyo. Tufanye utafiti wa kutosha kuhusu suala hili; tukusanye maoni tofauti kabla ya kupeleka muswada huo bungeni.

eng: Lwanda Magere, a software engineer, accused its authors of using a "copy-paste" strategy:
swa: Lwanda Magere, injia wa program za kompyuta, aliwatuhumu waandishi wa muswada huo kutumia mbinu ya “kunukuu bila marekebisho”:

eng: Cyber Crime Bill Tanzania: copied and pasted, almost zero ability to implement. — Lwanda Magere (@nndekindo) April 7, 2015
swa: Muswada wa Makosa ya Mtandaoni Tanzania: Umenukuliwa mahali bila marekebisho yoyote, hivyo hakuna uwezekano wa kutekelezeka

eng: Tanzanian blogger PATO jokingly shared a photo showing the number of members of parliament who passed the bill:
swa: Mwanablogu wa Tanzania PATO kwa utani alituma picha inayowaonesha wabunge kadhaa waliopitisha muswada huo:

eng: These are your MPs that passed the #CyberCrimeBill y'day!
swa: Hawa ndio wabunge wenu waliopitisha Muswada wa Makosa ya Mtandaoni jana!

eng: Vote wisely in October fellas! pic.twitter.com/pEScSHYYPZ — PATO♠️ (@PatNanyaro) April 2, 2015
swa: Pigeni kura kwa busara mwezi Oktoba jamani!

eng: He had probably thought it would be easy to steal some shampoo from the owner of a store in Peru, but things went bad for this thief.
swa: Labda alidhani ingekuwa vyepesi kuiba shampoo mali ya mmiliki wa duka nchini Peru, lakini mambo yalimwendea mrama mwizi huyu.

eng: The man and his accomplice entered a store in the Peruvian city of Huancayo, saying they were buying some liquor, and when the owner was distracted, they took a box of shampoo.
swa: Mtu mmoja akiwa ameongozana na mwenzake waliingia kwenye duka lililoko kwenye jiji la Huancayo nchini Peru, wakisema walikuwa wanataka kununua pombe, na mmiliki alipokuwa amepumbazwa kidogo, jamaa walibeba boksi la shampoo.

eng: The owner noticed what had happened and asked for help from security guards.
swa: Mmiliki aligundua mchezo wao na kuwaarifu walinzi.

eng: To prevent the situation from escalating, one of the thieves knelt down to ask for forgiveness.
swa: Ili kuzuia tukio hilo lisifike mbali, mmoja wa wezi hao alipiga magoti na kuomba msamaha.

eng: The owner, a woman, was so moved by this reaction that she didn't press charges.
swa: Mmiliki wa duka, aliyekuwa mwanamke, aliguswa na kitendo hicho na akaamua kuachana na mpango wa kuwachukulia hatua.

eng: The accomplice also benefited, although he didn't ask for forgiveness.
swa: Mwenzake na mwizi huyo aliyeomba msamaha naye alinufaika na msamaha huo, ingawa hakuwa ameomba msamaha.

eng: The guy claimed he will never again commit an act like this one.
swa: Jamaa huyo alidai hatarudia tena kufanya kitendo kama hicho.

eng: The blog Noticias Huancayo Perú summed it up:
swa: Blogu ya Noticias Huancayo Perú ilisimulia mhutasari wa tukio hilo:

eng: He knelt down and begged the old lady for forgiveness, claiming it would be the last time he'd steal.
swa: Lipiga mgoti na kumwomba mwanamke wa umri wa makamo amsamehe, akimsihi kwamba hiyo ndiyo itakuwa mara yake ya mwisho kuiba.

eng: The affected lady while accepting the thief's pleas, refused to report the incident.
swa: Mama huyo kwa kukubali ombi la mwizi wake, aliamua kuachana na mpango wa kutoa taarifa ya tukio hilo.

eng: User KDNA15TV posted a video with the events:
swa: Mtumiaji KDNA15TV aliweka video zinazozungumzia tukio hilo:

eng: Thief got forgiveness after kneeling down for stealing a box of shampoo.
swa: Mwizi apata msamaha baada ya kupiga magoti kuomba msamaha kwa kuiba boksi la shampoo.

eng: Along with his accomplice...
swa: Alikuwa na rafiki yake waliyekuwa wameambatana...

eng: Jianjay Potter and Grace Zardon in Monrovia, Liberia.
swa: Jianjay Potter akiwa na Grace Zardon mjini Monrovia, Liberia.

eng: Credit: Marc Campos.
swa: Picha: Marc Campos.

eng: Published with PRI's permission.
swa: Imechapishwa kwa ruhusa ya PRI.

eng: This article and radio report by Andrea Crossan for The World originally appeared on PRI.org on April 7, 2015, and is republished here as part of a content-sharing agreement.
swa: Makala haya na taarifa ya habari kwa njia ya redio vimeandaliwa na Andrea Crossan maalum kwa ajili ya kipindi cha The World awali kilionekana kwenye mtandao wa PRI.org mnamo Aprili 7, 2015, na kushapishwa tena hapa kama sehemu ya makubaliano ya kubadilishana maudhui.

eng: The West African country of Liberia has been devastated over the past year by an Ebola outbreak that has killed thousands of people.
swa: Liberia, nchi iliyoko Afrika Magharibi imekuwa na mlipuko wa Ebola kwa mwaka mzima ambao umeua maelfu ya watu.

eng: And for those in hospitals suffering, all they see are masks and robot-looking suits of doctors and nurses caring for them.
swa: Na kwa wale walio mahospitalini wakiteseka, wanachoweza kukiona ni sura za madaktari na manesi waliovalia mavazi kama roboti wakijaribu kuwahudumia.

eng: The medics must wear those protective suits to stop them from coming in contact with a patient.
swa: Watumishi wa afya lazima wavae mavazi haya maalum kuwakinga na maambukizi yanayoweza kutokea kwa wagonjwa wao.

eng: But some humanity is stripped away with the intimidating get-up.
swa: Lakini hali hiyo inakuwa kama inadhalilisha utu wa mwanadamu.

eng: Until now.
swa: Mpaka sasa.

eng: Los Angeles-based artist Mary Beth Heffernan saw the Ebola suits on news reports.
swa: Msanii anayeishi Los Angeles Mary Beth Heffernan aliona mavazi ya kujikinga na Ebola kwenye taarifa za habari.

eng: She thought about how isolating it was for the patients.
swa: Alifikiri namna gani mavazi ya jinsi hii yanaleta hisia za kutengwa na kubaguliwa kwa wagonjwa.

eng: And she came up with the idea of taking photos of health workers that could be attached to their protective clothing.
swa: Na kuanzia hapo akapa wazo la kuwapiga picha watumishi wa afya na kuziweka kwenye mavazi hayo ya kujilinda na maambukizi.

eng: In late February, Heffernan travelled to Monrovia, Liberia to do just that.
swa: Mwishoni mwa mwezi Februari, Heffernan alisafiri kwenda Monrovia, Liberia kufanya kazi hiyo ya kupiga picha.

eng: She brought cameras, six printers, ink cartridges and sticky labels to print the photos on.
swa: Alinunua kamera, mashine sita za kuchapisha, wino na karatasi maalum za kuchapishia picha.

eng: Mary Beth Heffernan taking photograph of health worker Morris Zolu.
swa: Mary Beth Heffernan akipiga picha za mhudumu wa Morris Zolu.

eng: Credit: Marc Campos.
swa: Picha: Marc Campos.

eng: “I invited the healthcare workers to offer the expression that the wished they could have given their patient if they weren’t covered up with these suits,” says Heffernan.
swa: “Niliwakaribisha wahudumu wa afya kuniambia maneno ambayo wangependa kuwaambia wagonjwa wao kama wasingekuwa wamefunikwa na mavazi hayo," anasema Heffernan.

eng: Most chose to smile warmly for the camera and that is what the patients see in this head shot photograph.” 	Wengi waliamua kutabasamu nikiwapiga picha na hicho ndicho wagonjwa wao wanachokiona kwenye picha zao kubwa wanazozibadika kwenye mavazi yao.”
Health workers Morris Zolu, Kaifouba Kamara, and Joseph Walatee wearing their portraits.
swa: Mhudumu wa afya Morris Zolu, Kaifouba Kamara, akiwa na Joseph Walatee wakiwa wamevaa picha zao.

eng: Credit: Marco Campos.
swa: Picha: Marc Campos.

eng: The portraits were attached to the safety suits and then thrown out at the end of each work day.
swa: Picha hizo zilibandikwa kwenye mavazi hayo ya kujikinga na zilitupwa kila siku inapomalizika.

eng: “One of the challenges was that photographs are kind of hard to come by in Liberia and they are expensive to print.”
swa: “Moja wapo ya changamoto ilikuwa ni kwamba ni vigumu kupata picha nchini Liberia na ilikuwa gharama kubwa kuzichapisha."

eng: So Heffernan gave staff members a copy of their portrait to keep.
swa: Kwa hiyo Heffernan aliwapa watumishi hao nakala moja ya picha zao kwa ajili ya matumizi yao binafsi.

eng: A photo label on the back of an iPad Credit: Marc Campos.
swa: Alama ya picha nyuma ya iPad. Picha: Marc Campos.

eng: Heffernan says that it’s better than just having health workers wear name tags.
swa: Heffernan anasema kwamba ni vizuri zaidi wahudumu wa afya kuvaa picha hizo kuliko kuvaa vitambulisho vyenye majina yao.

eng: “An ID is tiny, it’s laminated, and it’s also about authority.
swa: “Kitambulisho ni kidogo, kimejadaliwa utepe mwembamba, na kinaleta picha ya mamlaka.

eng: It’s about differentiating classes of people with power, and what I wanted was to make the patient more powerful.”
swa: Kinatofautisha makundi ya watu wenye mamlaka, na kile nilichotaka ni kuwafanya wagonjwa wajisikie kuwa na mamlaka zaidi.”

eng: Selina, a Monrovia healthcare worker, wearing her portrait.
swa: Selina, mhudumu wa afya wa Monrovia, akiwa kavaa picha yake.

eng: Credit: Marc Campos.
swa: Picha: Marc Campos.

eng: And for the workers, it helped them to better relate to each other and their patients.
swa: Na kwa wahudumu hao, kufanya hivyo kuliwasaidia kuhusiana vyema wao kwa wao pamoja na wagonjwa wao.

eng: Health care workers told Heffernan, "we no longer look like scary ninjas.”
swa: Wahudumu hao wa afya walimwambia Heffernan, " hatuonekani kama watu wanaotisha.”

eng: Health worker in Monrovia donning gloves.
swa: Wahudumu wa afya jijini Monrovia wakivaa glovu.

eng: Credit: Marc Campos.
swa: Picha: Marc Campos.

eng: If all works out, perhaps the medics won't have to wear the photographs on their clothing much longer.
swa: Kama juhudi zitaendelea, huenda watumishi wa afya hawatahitajika kubandika picha zao kwenye nguo zao kwa muda mrefu.

eng: The Ebola outbreak has been tapering in recent months and there are hopes that the country could soon be declared free of the disease.
swa: Mlipuko wa Ebola umekuwa ukipungua katika miezi ya karibuni na kuna matumaini kwamba nchi hiyo inaweza kutangazwa kuwa haina maambukizi ya ugonjwa huo.

eng: Morris Zolu, Hygienist, entering Red Zone.
swa: Morris Zolu, bwana afya, akiingia kwenye eneo lenye hatari.

eng: Credit: Marc Campos.
swa: Picha: Marc Campos.

eng: Pedro Muller reflects on the lapse of the school system, an institution he says meant for a different historical context.
swa: Pedro Muller anatafakari kuhusu matatizo yanayoukabili mfumo wa shule, taasisi anayosema ilimaanisha mazingira tofauti ya kihistoria.

eng: In this regard, he notes the importance of two similar, but at the same time different, concepts: "to study" and "to be educated":
swa: Kwa kusema hayo, anabainisha umuhimu wa dhana hizi mbili zinazofanana lakini zikimaanisha nyakati mbili tofauti: "Kusoma" na "kuelimika":

eng: To be educated goes beyond memorizing a couple of names and forgetting them the next day.
swa: TKuelimika kunaenda mbali zaidi ya kukariri majina kadhaa na kuyasahau siku inayofuata.

eng: It is about having an inquisitive mind and wondering about what hides behind the obvious, it is to acquire skills, to exercise your lateral thinking, a divergent thinking that many call "thinking outside of the box".
swa: Kuelimika ni kuwa na udadisi na kuhoji yale yaliyofichika nyuma ya kinachoonekana kuwa mazoea, ni kuwa na ujuzi, kuutumia uwezo wa kufikiri tofauti, fikra mbadala tunazoweza kuziita "kufikiri nje ya boksi".

eng: To be educated is also about learning to be creative and innovative.
swa: Kuelimika ni kujifunza kuwa mbunifu na mgunduzi.

eng: We learn better in groups; it is part of our nature to discuss, think and reflect on a specific topic and draw conclusions.
swa: Tunajifunza vizuri kwenye makundi; ni sehemu ya asili yetu kujadili, kufikiri na kutafakari mada mahususi na kufanya mahitimisho.

eng: It is said that the best way to became educated is to learn.
swa: Inasemekana kwamba namna nzuri ya kuelimika ni kujifunza.

eng: Muller invites readers to watch the following English-language video, wherein Logan LaPlante talks about the concept of ​​"hacking education" or "hackschooling", which refers to the process of learning as a group experience, based on trial and error and, above all, the importance of creativity.
swa: Muller anawakaribisha wasomaji wake kutazama video ifuatayo iliyo katika Kiingereza, ambako Logan LaPlante anazungumzia dhana ya "kuidua elimu" au "dukuaelimu", anayosema ni mchakato wa kujifunza kwa kikundi, kwa mtindo wa kujaribu na, zaidi, umuhimu wa ubunifu.

eng: Continue reading Muller's post here, or follow him on Twitter.
swa: Endelea kusoma makala ya Muller hapa, au mfuatilie kwenye mtandao wa Twita.

swa: Makala haya ni sehemu ya 46 ya #LunesDeBlogsGV (JUmatatu ya blogu ya GV) mnamo Machi 23, 2015.

swa: Kikosi cha Uokoaji Topos México Tlatelolco kimeanza kampeni ya kuomba michango ili kuweza kuungana na jitihada za uokoaji zinazoendelea baada ya tetemeko lenye ukubwa wa 7.8 kuitikisa Nepal Jumamosi iliyopita, na kukatisha maisha ya watu zaidi ya 4,000 na wengine 7,000 wakijeruhiwa.

eng: The group was born when volunteers spontaneously showed up to help in the aftermath of 1985 Mexico City earthquake.
swa: Kundi hili lilizaliwa wakati watu wanaojitolea kujitokeza kusaidia baada ya tetemeko lililoikumba Mexico mwaka 1985.

eng: The group was formally organized as a civil association in February 1986 and for more than three decades, they have assisted rescue and recovery efforts in the Mexican states of Tabasco, Chiapas, Oaxaca, State of Mexico, Veracruz and Mexico City, and in countries all over the world including Haiti, Indonesia, El Salvador and Chile.
swa: Kundi hilo zamani lilikuwa likiratibiwa na asasi ya kiraia kwa zaidi ya miongo mitatu tangu mwezi Februari 1986, na kimesaidia jitihada za uokoaji kwenye majimbo ya Tabasco, Chiapas, Oaxaca, Jimbo la Mexico, Veracruz na Mexico City, yote yakiwa nchini Mexico na kwenye nchi nyinginezo duniani ikiwa ni pamoja na Haiti, Indonesia, El Salvador na Chile.

eng: Topos México doesn't receive any payment for their work since it is entirely based on volunteers.

eng: Most of the time, local authorities or Mexico's federal government cover their travel expenses and the countries they go give them visas and access to the disaster zones.

eng: On March 5, 2015, the European Union Court of Justice ruled that the reduced value-added tax (VAT) established for printed books should not apply to digital books, considering everything distributed or delivered electronically or via Internet as a service.

eng: Amalia Lopez questions the resolution on the Blog Sinerrata Editores:
swa: Amalia Lopez anahoji hukumu hiyo kwenye blogu ya Sinerrata Editores:

eng: What struck me was that they used the format as an argument to reinforce their decision, which maybe could have made sense at some point in the past, but nowadays, I find it completely absurd.
swa: Kinachonishangaza ni kwamba walitumia mfumo wa kitabu kama hoja ya kufanyia maamuzi yao, jambo linaloweza kuwa na mantiki kwa kipindi cha nyuma, lakini leo, ninaona huu ni sawa na upuuzi.

eng: It is true, an e-book is a file and not an object, but does it make a book less of a book if I keep it on my computer or my e-reader rather than on the book shelf?
swa: Ni kweli, kitabu cha kidijitali ni faili tu na sio kitu, lakini je nikikiweka kitabu kwenye kompyuta yangu au kifaa kingine cha kukisomea badala ya kukiweka kwenye kabati, hiyo inakifanya kisiwe na hadhi ya kitabu?

eng: When I read a digital book, is the cultural experience lesser than when a read the book on paper?
swa: Ninapokisoma kitabu kilicho kwenye mfumo wa kidijitali, uzoefu wa kitamaduni ninaoupata unakuwa pungufu ya ule ninaoupata nikiwa nakisoma kitabu kwenye karatasi?

eng: That is to say, what this court has ruled (or, at least, that's my interpretation) is that what makes a book a cultural product, thus deserving reduced tax (and a lower cost to its consumers), is the paper on which is printed.
swa: Ndio kusema, kilichoamuliwa na mahakama (au, angalau, hiyo ni tafsiri yangu tu) ni kwamba kinachofanya kitabu kiwe zao la utamaduni, na hivyo kustahili kupata punguzo la kodi (na hiyo maana yake ni punguzo la bei kwa wateja), ni karatasi linalotumiwa kuchapishia kitabu hicho.

eng: The sentence includes books downloaded or viewed online and encompasses electronic formats for computers, smartphones, e-readers or any reading devices.

eng: The United States of America formally dropped Cuba from its state sponsors of terrorism list Friday, a designation reserved for nations that, according to the US government, repeatedly provide support for international acts of premeditated, politically motivated violence against non-combatants.
swa: Marekani imeiondoa Cuba kwenye orodha ya nchi zinazofadhili ugaidi siku ya Ijumaa, hadhi zinazopewa nchi, kwa mujibu wa Marekani, ambazo zina kawaida ya kuwezesha vitendo vya ngazi ya kimataifa vilivyopangwa, na vyenye lengo la kupambana kisiasa na raia wasio na silaha.

eng: According to the US State Department:
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Wizara ya Mambo ya Nchi ya Marekani:

eng: In December 2014, the President instructed the Secretary of State to immediately launch a review of Cuba’s designation as a State Sponsor of Terrorism, and provide a report to him within six months regarding Cuba’s support for international terrorism.
swa: Mnamo Desemba 2014, Rais alimwagiza Waziri wa Nchi kupitia upya haraka hadhi ya Cuba kama Nchi Inayofadhili Ugaidi, na kutoa taarifa kwake ndani ya miezi sita kuhusu ufadhili wa Cuba kwa vitendo vya kimataifa vya ugaidi.

eng: On April 8, 2015, the Secretary of State completed that review and recommended to the President that Cuba no longer be designated as a State Sponsor of Terrorism.
swa: Mnamo Aprili 8, 2015, Waziri wa Nchi alikamisha kazi hiyo na kumshauri Rais kwamba Cuba haina sifa tena ya kuwa Nchi Zinazofadhili Ugaidi.

eng: Accordingly, on April 14, the President submitted to Congress the statutorily required report indicating the Administration’s intent to rescind Cuba’s State Sponsor of Terrorism designation, including the certification that Cuba has not provided any support for international terrorism during the previous six-months; and that Cuba has provided assurances that it will not support acts of international terrorism in the future.
swa: Hivyo, mnamo Aprili 14, Rais alitoa hoja kwenye Bunge kuomba taarifa inayoonesha nia ya Utawala wake kuiondoa Cuba kwenye orodha ya Nchi Zinazofadhili Ugaidi, ikiwa ni pamoja na uthibitisho kwamba Cuba haijatoa ushirikiano wowote kuwezesha Ugaidi wa kimataifa katika kipindi cha miezi sita; na kwamba Cuba imetoa uhakikisho kwamba haitawezesha vitendo vya ugaidi wa kimataifa katika siku zijazo.

eng: The 45-day Congressional pre-notification period has expired, and the Secretary of State has made the final decision to rescind Cuba’s designation as a State Sponsor of Terrorism, effective today, May 29, 2015.
swa: Kipindi cha siku 45 ilizopewa Bunge kutafakari taarifa hiyo kimekwisha, na Waziri wa Nchi ametoa uamuzi wa mwisho wa kuiondoa Cuba kwenye orodha ya Nchi Zinazofadhili Ugaidi kuanzia leo, Mei 29, 2015.

eng: The rescission of Cuba’s designation as a State Sponsor of Terrorism reflects our assessment that Cuba meets the statutory criteria for rescission.
swa: Kuondolewa kwa Cuba kwenye orodha ya Nchi Zinazofadhili Ugaidi kunaonesha tathimini yetu kwamba Cuba ina sifa za kuondolewa kwenye orodha hiyo.

eng: While the United States has significant concerns and disagreements with a wide range of Cuba’s policies and actions, these fall outside the criteria relevant to the rescission of a State Sponsor of Terrorism designation.
swa: Wakati Marekani ina wasiwasi na haikubaliani na sera na mienendo mingi ya Cuba, bado inaamini kwamba hazina uhusiano na kufadhili vitendo vya ugaidi.

eng: Residents of the city of Medellín, Colombia, are asking themselves if the metro is the place to talk about abortion, stemming from an ad by the #ladecisiónestuya (the decision is yours) campaign that's running in the public transit system's cars, as shared by user Jaime Andrés (@JAIM3_ANDR3S): The Decision Is Yours pic.twitter.com/Nbaq2zJHXn — Jaime Andrés (@JAIM3_ANDR3S) May 26, 2015
swa: Wakazi wa jiji la Medellín, Colombia, wanajiuliza kama treni inaweza kuwa eneo la kuzungumzia masuala ya utoaji mimba, kutokana na tangazo la kampeni ya #ladecisiónestuya (uamuzi ni wako) inayoendeshwa kwa mifumo mbalimbali ndani ya vyombo vya usafiri wa umma, hasa magari, kama inavyosimuliwa na mtumiaji wa twita aitwaye Jaime Andrés (@JAIM3_ANDR3S):

eng: The campaign is being spearheaded by a non-profit organization offering sexual and reproductive healthcare services, carrying the message: "398,000 abortions should not be illegal."
swa: Kampeni hiyo inaendeshwa na shirika lisilo na kiserikali linalotoa huduma za afya ya uzazi, ikiwa na ujumbe "kutolewa kwa mimba 3980,000 isiwe kosa la jinai."

eng: Under the hashtag #Abortonoesculturametro (Abortion Is Not Metro Culture) referring to the set of rules governing Medellín's Metro called "Cultura Metro" (Metro Culture), people have been sharing their opinions for and against abortion, in the same way that the mass transit system installations' cars are used on a daily basis to post messages using other graphic material.
swa: Kwa kutumia alama ishara ya #Abortonoesculturametro (Utoaji Mimba si Utamaduni wa Ndani ya Treni) kwa kurejea sheria mbalimbali zinazoongoza treni za Medellín zinazoitwa "Cultura Metro" (Utamaduni wa Metro), watu wamekuwa wakiadili maoni kuunga mkono au kupinga utoaji mimba, kwa namna ile ile kama mifumo ya sauti kwenye magari inavyotumika kila siku kutuma ujumbe na habari nyingine za picha.

eng: Don Osborne discusses a news feature on the Olivet Nazarene University website showing a map of "The Second Most Spoken Languages Around the World."
swa: Don Osborne anajadili habari iliyowekwa kwenye tovuti ya Chuo Kikuu cha Olivet Nazarene ikionesha ramani ya "Lugha za pili kuzungumzwa zaidi duniani."

eng: He points out key problems from the map:
swa: Anaeleza matatizo makuu kutokana na habari hiyo:

eng: The first issue is assuming that "The most spoken language in any country is often obvious; usually, it’s the official language of the country."
swa: Suala la kwanza ni kudhani kwamba "lugha inayozungumzwa zaidi kwenye nchi yoyote huwa wazi; mara nyingi, ni lugha ya taifa husika."

eng: In Africa this often is not the case, if by "most spoken" one counts number of speakers.
swa: Barani Afrika hali ni tofauti, kama kusema "lugha inayozungumzwa zaidi" maana yake ni kuhesabu idadi ya wazungumzaji.

eng: An example is Mali, whose linguistic profile was explored on this blog in discussing the long-tail of languages - Bambara is certainly more used than the official French.
swa: Kwa mfano nchini Mali, ambapo hali ya lugha iliangaziwa kwenye blogu hii katika kutazama uzungumzaji wa lugha - Kibambara kinaonekana kuwa lugha maarufu kuliko hata lugha rasmi ya Kifaransa.

eng: Official language is a category that doesn't lend itself to ranking use of languages in Africa, beyond the (admittedly important) context of official use and its spillover to popular use.
swa: Lugha rasmi si kigezo kinachoaminika katika kupima umaarufu wa lugha barani Afrika, zaidi ya mukhtadha (muhimu) wa matumizi rasmi na umaarufu wake.

eng: In the case of two countries at least, this runs into additional problems:
swa: Kwa mifano ya nchi hizo mbili, kuna masuala mawili yanajitokeza:

eng: •South Africa has 11 official languages (the Olivet site incorrectly lists only one of them - Zulu - as official).
swa: •Afrika Kusini inazo lugha 11 rasmi (tovuti ya Olivet imetaja Kizulu pekee kuwa lugha rasmi).

eng: So one of the official languages will be second most spoken.
swa: Kwa hiyo moja wapo ya lugha rasmi inakuwa lugha ya pili kuzungumzwa.

eng: Perhaps that is Xhosa as indicated, but the model focusing on official languages hasn't worked here.
swa: Pengine lugha hiyo inaweza kuwa ki-Xhosa kama inavyooneshwa, lakini mtazamo wa kutumia lugha rasmi kama kigezo hauonekani kufanya kazi katika mazingira haya.

eng: •Rwanda has three official languages (Kinyarwanda, French, and English), and Central African Republic two (Sango and French).
swa: •Rwanda ina lugha tatu rasmi (Kinyarwanda, Kifaransa, na Kiingereza), na Jamhuri ya Afrika ya kati inazo mbili (Ki-Sango na Kifaransa).

eng: Since the site doesn't consider these official languages in discussing second most widely spoken, it is reduced to stating that Swahili is "second" most used in Rwanda, and that indigenous languages are used in CAR - which doesn't tell us much.
swa: Kwa sababu tovuti haijazingatia lugha hizi rasmi katika kujadili lugha za pili zinazozunguzwa zaidi, imejikuta ikidai kwamba Kiswahili ni lugha ya pili kuzungumzwa zaidi nchini Rwanda, na kwamba lugha za asili ndizo zinazotumika zaidi nchini Jamhuri ya Afrika ya Kati - jambo ambalo halitoi taswira halisi.

eng: Read part 2 of his discussion here.
swa: Soma sehemu ya pili ya hoja zake hapa.

eng: Pregnant 11-year-old who refused to abort creates controversy.
swa: Kugoma kwa mjamzito wa miaka 11 kutoa mimba kumesababisha utata.

eng: We wrote recently about about a 10-year-old pregnant girl from Paraguay who was allegedly raped by her stepfather and who was unable to have an abortion because of legal limitations in the country.
swa: Hivi karibuniTuliandika kuhusu msichana wa miaka 10 aliyekuwa mjamzito nchini Paraguay kwa kudaiwa kubakwa na baba yake wa kambo na namna alivyoshindwa kutoa mimba hiyo kwa sababu sheria za nchi hiyo zinazuia utoaji wa mimba.

eng: Now, in Uruguay, where abortion is legal in the first 12 weeks of pregnancy, the case of a pregnant 11-year-old who refused to have one has shocked the country.
swa: Sasa, nchini Uruguay, ambako utoaji wa mimba unaruhusiwa ndani ya majuma 12 ya mwanzo ya ujauzito, tukio la msichana wa miaka 11 aliyegoma kutoa mimba limeishangaza nchi.

eng: This girl, who has been said to have an intellectual disability, was raped by the 41-year-old grandfather of her half-sister.
swa: Msichana huyu, anayesemekana kuwa na ulemavu wa akili, alibakwa na babu wa dada yake wa kambo mwenye miaka 41.

eng: This man is now in custody and will be prosecuted for rape, Uruguayan officials told Agence France-Presse.
swa: Mwanaume huyu kwa sasa yuko kizuizini na anashitakiwa kwa makosa ya ubakaji, wanasema maafisa wa Uruguay walipozungumza na Agence France-Presse.

eng: Family members, doctors, social organizations, and the media have encouraged the girl to terminate the pregnancy.
swa: Wanafamilia, madaktari, mashirika ya kijamii, na vyombo vya habari vimemshawishi msichana huyu kuitoa mimba hiyo.

eng: They have even pressured the government to try and force her to go through with it, according to Pangea Today.
swa: Wameishinikiza serikali kujaribu kumlazimisha kufanya hivyo, kwa mujibu wa jarida la Pangea Today.

eng: The response was, however, not favorable to them:
swa: Majibu, hata hivyo, hayajawaridhisha:

eng: “There is no risk for the life of the child or baby, so we cannot force her to have an abortion,” the director of INAU, Monica Silva, said.
swa: “Hakuna hatari yoyote kwa maisha yake wala mtoto, kwa hiyo hatuwezi kumlazimisha kutoa ujauzito huo," mkurugenzi wa INAU, Monica Silva, alisema.

eng: Atnaf Berhane, member of the Zone 9 Bloggers, was jailed for blogging about human right violations in Ethiopia.
swa: Atnaf Berhane, mmoja wa wanablogu wanaounda kundi la wanablogu wa Zone 9, amefungwa gerezani kwa sababu ya kublogu kuhusiana na ukiukwaji wa haki za binadamu nchini Ethiopia.

eng: (Image Credit: digital drawing by Melody Sundberg.
swa: (Hisani ya picha: Mchoro wa kidigitali na Melody Sundberg.

eng: Image used with her permission)
swa: Picha imetumiwa kwa ruhusa yake)

eng: In April 2014, nine bloggers and journalists were arrested in Ethiopia.
swa: Mnamo mwezi wa Aprili, wanablogu tisa pamoja na waandishi wa habari walikamatwa nchini Ethiopia.

eng: Several of these men and women had worked with Zone9, a collective blog that covered social and political issues in Ethiopia and promoted human rights and government accountability.
swa: Baadhi ya wanaume na wanawake hawa walikuwa wakifanya kazi na Zone9, blogu ya ushirika iliyokuwa inazungumzia masuala ya kijamii na ya kisiasa nchini Ethiopia ikiwa ni pamoja na kuhamasisha uzingatiaji wa haki za binadamu na uwajibikaji wa serikali.

eng: And four of them were Global Voices authors.
swa: Miongoni mwao, wanablogu wanne walikuwa ni waandishi wa Global Voices.

eng: They have been behind bars ever since, their trial postponed time and again.
swa: Tangu wakati huo, wameendelea kuwepo gerezani, huku shitaka lao likiwa linaahirishwa mara kwa mara.

eng: Last week, we featured our debut post from a series - "They Have Names" - that hopes to highlight the individual bloggers who are currently in jail.
swa: Wiki iliyopita, tuliweka makala yetu ya kwanza kutoka kwenye mfululizo wa makala- "Wanayo Majina" - iliyo na tumaimi la kuwazungumzia wanablogu ambao hadi sasa wapo gerezani.

eng: We wish to humanize them, to tell their particular and peculiar stories.
swa: Tunataka kutambua utu wao, tunataka kuelezea habari zao za kipekee na mahususi kabisa.

eng: This week, Ghanaian author, Kofi Yeboah, writes about the youngest of the Zone9ers, Atnaf Berahane.
swa: Wiki hii, mwandishi kutoka Ghana, Kofi Yeboah, aandika kuhusu mwanablogu mdogo kabisa wa Zone9, Atnaf Berahane.

eng: Atnaf Berahane, 26 years old, is the youngest of the Zone9 bloggers.
swa: Atnaf Berahane, aliye na umri wa miaka 26, ndiye mwanablogu wa Zone9 aliye mdogo kuliko wengine wote.

eng: He was arrested in Ethiopia on April 25 and 26, 2014 alongside Abel Wabela, Befeqadu Hailu, Mahlet Fantahun, Zelalem Kibret, and Natnael Feleke (all members of the Zone 9 blogging collective) and journalists Asmamaw Hailegeorgis, Tesfalem Waldyes and Edom Kassaye.
swa: Alitiwa kizuizini nchini Ethiopia mnamo tarehe 25 April, 2014 akiwa na wenzake Abel Wabela, Befeqadu Hailu, Mahlet Fantahun, Zelalem Kibret, na Natnael Feleke (wote wakiwa katika ushirika wa kublogu wa Zone 9) pamoja na waandishi wa habari, Asmamaw Hailegeorgis, Tesfalem Waldyes na Edom Kassaye.

eng: Ethiopia is a country where freedom of expression is repressed by the government.
swa: Ethiopia ni nchi ambayo uhuru wa kujieleza unaminywa na serikali.

eng: There is strict media regulation in the country, especially when it comes to discussions of politics and human rights.
swa: Nchini Ethiopia, kuna sheria kali dhidi ya uanahabari, hususani pale linapokuja suala la kujadili kuhusu siasa na haki za binadamu.

eng: As a result, citizens read news mostly from the Internet.
swa: Hii inapelekea raia kutegemea kupata habari kupitia mtandao wa intaneti.

eng: Atnaf's passion for civic engagement and interest in disseminating information to citizens to understand what the constitution says about their right and freedom led him to co-found the Zone9 Blog: his passion for human rights activism ignited the interest to co-found the organisation.
swa: Hamasa ya Atnaf ya kujihusisha na uelimishaji wa jamii na kuvutiwa kwake kusambaza taarifa kwa raia ili kuwafahamisha kile katiba ya nchi inachokizungumzia kuhusiana ha haki na uhuru wao ilimfanya yeye kuwa mmoja wa waanzilishi wa blogu ya zone9: Hamasa yake ya kuwa mwanaharakati wa haki za binadamu ilichochea yeye kuwa mmoja wa waanzilishi wa asasi ya Zone9.

eng: But his passion for human rights and freedoms left him in chains.
swa: Hata hivyo, hamasa yake ya kutetea haki za binadamu imempelekea kupokonywa uhuru wake.

eng: In real life, Atnaf is an ICT specialist who works with Addis Ababa city administration at Bole sub-city.
swa: Katika maisha yake ya kawaida, Atnaf ni mtaalamu wa masuala ya TEHAMA anayefanya kazi na mamlaka ya Jiji la Addis Ababa katika mji wa Bole.

eng: The trailtrackerblog, where supporters post regular updates about the case and the bloggers' condition, describes him as a young Ethiopian who is "known for his use of Twitter handle for hyper local updates."
swa: Blogu ya trailtracker, ambayo marafiki wa wanablogu na waandishi hawa wamekuwa wakiitumia kuweka mara kwa mara taarifa za maendeleo ya kesi yao pamoja na hali yao, wanamwelezea Atnaf kama Mhabeshi ambaye "anafahamika kwa umahiri wake wa kutumia twita kusambaza kwa haraka habari motomoto za nchi yake".

eng: Atnaf also runs his own blog and is a digital security expert.
swa: Pia, Atnaf anamiliki blogu yake na pia ni mtaalamu wa masuala ya usalama wa kidigitali.

eng: The sad reality of the muffled aspirations of one so young as Atnaf is best captured by this post:
swa: Ukweli unaoumiza wa ndoto izimwayo ya kijana mdogo kama Atnaf unafafanuliwa vizuri kwenye makala hii:

eng: Is it the “Federal Republic of Ethiopia” or the “Republic of Dystopia” (police state)?
swa: Hii ni “Shirikisho la Jamhuri ya Ethiopia” au ni “Jamhuri ya Daistopia” (Taifa la polisi)?

eng: Has Ethiopia crossed into the Twilight Zone, the Fifth Dimension?...
swa: Je, Ethiopia imevuka mipaka, kwa kiwango cha tano?...

eng: Ethiopia today might as well be called the “Republic of Dystopia”.
swa: Ethiopia ya leo inaweza pia kuitwa “Jamhuri ya Daistopia”.

eng: Young men and women barely in their 20s are arrested and jailed for “terrorism” merely for blogging on Facebook and speaking their minds on other social media.
swa: Vijana wadogo wa miaka 20 wanakamatwa na kufungwa gerezani kwa "ugaidi" kwa kisa tu cha kuelimisha watu kupitia mtandao wa Facebook pamoja na kutoa maoni yao kupitia mitandao ya kijamii.

eng: Atnaf, together with other incarcerated Zone 9 bloggers, deserve praise and not a jail sentence.
swa: Atnaf, pamoja na wanablogu wengine walioko gerezani wanapaswa kupongezwa na siyo kifungo gerezani.

eng: It is not only the future of Atnaf that is on trial but that of every aspiring young man/woman who dares take a repressive government to task on free speech.
swa: Siyo tu mustakabali wa Atnaf unaowekwa rehani, bali pia ni kwa kila kijana mwenye ari na aliyenuia kuiwajibisha serikali kandamizi kwenye uhuru wa kujieleza.

eng: Playwright Aizzah Fatima plays a character she calls a "hijabi feminist."
swa: Mwandishi wa michezo ya kuigiza Aizzah Fatima aliigiza uhusika anaouita "mwanaharakati haki za wanawake anayevaa hijabi."

eng: Credit: Courtesy Aizzah Fatima.
swa: Picha: Haki miliki ya Aizzah Fatima.

eng: Published with PRI's permission
swa: Imechapishwa kwa ruhusa ya PRI

eng: This article and radio report by Joyce Hackel for The World originally appeared on PRI.org on May 28, 2015, and is republished here as part of a content-sharing agreement.
swa: Makala haya na taarifa ya redio iliyoandikwa na Joyce Hackel kwa ajili ya kipindi cha redio kiitwacho The World kilichoonekana kwanza kwenye tovuti ya PRI.org mnamo Mei 28, 2015, na kimechapishwa hapa kama sehemu ya makubaliano ya ushirikiano wa kimaudhui.

eng: Aizzah Fatima used to worry that the title of her one-woman play, "Dirty Paki Lingerie," would offend her fellow South Asians.
swa: Aizzah Fatima amekuwa akiogopa kwamba jina la igizo lake linalochezwa na mhusika mmoja, "Dirty Paki Lingerie," (Vazi lisilofaa kuvaliwa hadharani), lingeweza kuwaudhi ndugu zake wa-Asia ya Kusini.

eng: But after nearly five years of staging the production from Toronto to Turkmenistan, the Pakistani American actress is less concerned when the ethnic slur raises eyebrows.
swa: Lakini baada ya takribani miaka mitano ya kuigiza akiwa Toronto na baadae Turkmenistan, mwigizaji huyo Mmarekani mwenye asili ya Pakistani hajali kama jina hilo linaleta karaha.

eng: It was a big challenge when I first started doing this play to get the Muslim American community to support it, she says.
swa: Ilikuwa ni changamoto kubwa nilipoanza kuigiza onesho hili kupata ushirikiano wa jamii ya Waislamu wa Kimarekani, anasema.

eng: That's really changed.
swa: Mambo yamebadilika sana.

eng: The monologues in 'Lingerie' explore issues of identity, sexuality and religion from the perspective of six Pakistani Americans.
swa: Lengo hasa kwenye igizo hilo ni kusaili masuala ya kujitambua, ujinsia na dini kwa mtaamo wa Wamerekani sita wenye asili ya Kipakistani.

eng: In recent weeks, Fatima and director Erica Gould have taken the production to Luton, Bradford, Glasgow and London where they've engaged with local Muslim communities through "talk-backs" after the show.
swa: Katika majuma ya hivi karibuni, Fatima na mwongozaji wake Erica Gould wamepanua kazi zao mpaka Luton, Bradford, Glasgow na London ambako wanawashirikisha Waislamu wa maeneo hayo kwenye majadiliano kupitia "mazungumzo ya mrejesho" baada ya onesho.

eng: I've had theaters book the show, and then drop it because they were worried, she says.
swa: Nimewahi kukutana na matukio ya baadhi ya kumbi za maonesho kuomba nikaoneshe onesho langu kwao, na baadae kuniarifu kwamba wameghairi kwa sababu ya woga, anasema.

eng: We were in Bradford, which I think is one of the poorest cities and the largest concentrations of Pakistani people in the UK, and there were definitely people in the audience who had an issue with it. 	Kuna wakati tulikuwa Bradford, ninakodhani ni moja wapo ya miji masikini zaidi na yenye watu wengi zaidi wenye asili ya pakistani nchini Uingereza, na kulikuwa na watu kwenye hadhira yangu waliokerwa na onesho hilo.
And they were vocal about it, yet they still came."
swa: Na walisema wazi wazi, na bado alikuja."

eng: The phrase "Paki" is especially derogatory in Britain, where it was first used by tabloids in the 1960s to refer to all South Asians, including Indians, Afghans and Bangladeshis.
swa: Neno "Paki" ni tusi nchini Uingereza, ambako lilitumika awali kwenye magazeti miaka ya 1960 kuwatambulisha Waasia Kusini, ikiwa ni pamoja na Wahindi, waafghani na Wabangladeshi.

eng: Fatima says she decided to write the show to offer a more nuanced view of the Pakistani-American experience in the US, and because she was frustrated by being told she wasn't "trashy enough" to portray the roles typically offered to South Asian Muslim actresses.
swa: Fatima anasema aliamua kuanza kuandika onesho hilo kujaribu kuonesha mtazamo usiozoeleka wa maisha halisi ya Wamarekani wenye asili ya Pakistani wanaoishi Marekani, na kwa sababu alikuwa ameumizwa kihisia kuambiwa kwamba hakuwa anafaa kuvaa uhusika wa waigiziji wa ki-Islamu wenye asili ya Asia Kusini.

eng: There was a human side to this experience of being a Muslim American woman that was completely missing in the media, completely missing in the types of characters we see in film, TV, theater, she says.
swa: Kuna mtazamo wa kibinadamu kwenye uzoefu huu wa kuwa mwanamke wa Kiislamu (tena) Mmarekani aliyekuwa anakosekana kwenye vyombo vya habari, aliyekosekana kabisa miongoni mwa wahusika tunaowaona kwenye filamu, runinga, kumbi za maonesho, anasema.

eng: I wanted to portray Muslim women, especially women who cover their hair, the way I know them to be, as activists and feminists and very outspoken go-getters.
swa: Nilitaka kumwonesha mwanamke wa Kiislamu, hususani wanawake wanaofunika nywele zao, kwa namna ninavyowafahamu, wanaharakati na watetezi wa haki za wanawake na wapaza sauti wakubwa wa kushinikiza mambo.

eng: Fatima says the South Asian stereotypes will be shattered in coming decades.
swa: Fatima anasema mtazamo hasi na wa jumla kwa Waasia wa Kusini utakoma katika miongo ijayo.

eng: I really hope in my lifetime, 30 years down the road, we're able to look back at this time and say, 'Hey, now we're beyond it,' she says.
swa: Ninatumaini kwenye maisha yangu, miaka 30 ijayo, tutaweza kutazama nyuma kuona nyakati hizi na kusema, 'Tumevuka kipindi hicho, anasema.

eng: We've moved on.
swa: Tumepiga hatua.

eng: Who will be next?
swa: Nani atafuata? michoro ya wanablogu wa Bangladesh waliouawa.

eng: Sketch of deceased Bangladesh bloggers by MadhuMondol.
swa: Kwa hisani ya MadhuMondol.

eng: The Global Voices community calls for international attention to the alarming situation of bloggers in Bangladesh.
swa: Jumuia ya Global Voices yaitaka jamii ya kimataifa kutupia jicho hali tete ya usalama inayowakabili wanablogu wa Bangladeshi.

eng: Bloggers have been killed, and many more have been attacked, subjected to death threats and ostracized by religious hardliners for their writing.
swa: Wanablogu wameshauawa, na wengine wengi wamesha shambuliwa, wakijikuta kwenye vitisho vya kuuawa na pia kutengwa na wahafidhina kutokana na mambao wanayoaandika.

eng: This year alone, three bloggers have been assassinated in public.
swa: Kwa mwaka huu peke yake, wanablogu watatu waliuawa mbele ya hadhara.

eng: The names of these bloggers and others under threat appeared on a list of 84 people submitted to a special government committee by a group of conservative Muslim clerics who accused the bloggers of “atheism” and writing against Islam.
swa: Majina ya wanablogu hawa pamoja na wengine walio katika hatari hii yalionekana kwenye listi ya watu 84 iliyowasilishwa kwenye kamati maalum ya serikali na kikundi cha viongozi wa Kiislam kilichowatuhumu wanablogu hawa kwa kujihusisha na "upagani" pamoja na kuandika mambo yanayopingana na Uislam.

eng: Government officials responded by blocking critical websites and making arrests, of bloggers and leaders from the religious right, at the height of #shahbag protests in 2013.
swa: Kufuatia tuhuma hizi kwa wanablogu hawa, Serikali iliamuru kufungwa kwa tovuti makini na kukamatwa kwa wanablogu pamoja na viongozi kwa kutumia sheria ya dini wakati ambapo maandamano ya #shahbag ya 2013 yalipokuwa wameshika hatamu.

eng: Some media outlets, including prominent right-wing blogs, have even propagated the idea that all bloggers are atheists who “hurt the feelings” of religious Bangladeshis.
swa: Baadhi ya vyombo vya habari, zikiwemo blogu maarufu za mrengo wa kulia, zimediriki hata kusambaza maneno kuwa wanablogu wote ni wapagani ambao “wamekuwa wakipotosha imani” ya waumini wa dini nchini Bangladesh.

eng: Atheists have the same rights as other citizens in Bangladesh.
swa: Wapagani wana haki sawa na raia wengine wa nchini Bangladesh.

eng: Under national law, any person who has a “deliberate” or “malicious” intention of “hurting religious sentiments” can be prosecuted.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa sheria ya nchi, mtu yeyote aliye na madhumuni “thabiti” au “kushukiwa” “kudhuru hisia za kiimani” anaweza kuhukumiwa.

eng: But vigilante violence and murder for alleged insults is a horrendous response and egregious violation of the laws of Bangladesh.
swa: Lakini machafuko yatokanayo na kujichukulia sheria mkononi pamoja na mauaji kunakotokana na tuhuma za kukashifu ni jambo lisilovumilika kabisa na ni dhahiri kuwa ni ukiukwaji wa sheria za Bangladesh.

eng: Despite this, Bangladesh’s secular government has done little to discourage the attacks or bring the killers to justice.
swa: Hata hivyo, serikali ya kidini ya Bangladesh hadi sasa imeweka juhudi hafifu sana za kukemea mashambulizi haya au kuwafikisha wauaji kwenye vyombo vya sheria.

eng: These bloggers were neither advocating nor perpetrating such violence.
swa: Wanablogu hawa hawakuwa wakiunga mkono au kujihusisha kwenye machafuko hayo.

eng: They were writing about the complex, often tendentious political climate in Bangladesh and the importance of upholding human rights.
swa: Walikuwa wakiandika kwa maoni yao kuhusiana na hali tete ya kisiasa ya Bangladesh pamoja na umuhimu wa kuweka kipau mbele haki za binadamu.

eng: They were exercising their right to free expression, enshrined by their nation’s constitution and international human rights doctrine to which Bangladesh is party.
swa: Walikuwa wakitumia haki yao ya uhuru wa kujieleza, whuku wakilindwa na katiba ya taifa lao pamoja na Sheria ya kimataifa ya haki za binadamu ambayo Bangladesh ni mwanachama.

eng: Global Voices is a community bloggers, activists, writers, and translators from 137 countries.
swa: Global Voices ni jumuia ya wanablogu, wanaharakati, waandishi, na watafisi kutoka katika nchi 137.

eng: The universal human right to free expression is fundamental to our mission.
swa: Haki ya binadamu ya kimataifa ya uhuru wa kujieleza ndiyo kipau mbele chetu katika dira yetu.

eng: We tell underreported stories from around the world and defend the rights of everyone to speak freely and without fear.
swa: Tunasambaza habari zisizopewa kipaumbele kutoka katika katika pande zote za dunia pamoja na kutetea haki ya kila mmoja ya kujieleza kwa uhuru bila ya hofu.

eng: Among those the 84 individuals on this list are friends and collaborators of the Global Voices community.
swa: Miongoni mwa wanablogu hao, watu 84 katika listi hii ni marafiki na wachangiaji wa jumuia ya Global Voices.

eng: There are also bloggers and online activists who are not in the list, but are in peril because of their writing and activism.
swa: Pia, wapo wanablogu pamoja na wanaharakati wa mtandaoni ambao hawapo katika listi hiyo, lakini wapo katika hali hatarishi kutokana na uandishi na uanaharakati wao.

eng: We are deeply concerned for the safety of Bangladeshi bloggers both in and outside the country.
swa: Kwa kila hali, tunahusika moja kwenye usalama wa wanablogu wa Bangladesh waliopo ndani na nje ya nchi hii.

eng: We condemn the murders of bloggers Ananta Bijoy Das, Ahmed Rajib Haider, Washiqur Rahman and Avijit Roy and call on authorities to ensure that those responsible for these killings are brought to justice.
swa: Tunawalaani waliofanya mauaji ya Ananta Bijoy Das, Ahmed Rajib Haider, Washiqur Rahman na Avijit Roy na pia tunazitaka mamlaka husika kuwachchukulia hatua za kisheria wale wote waliohusika kutimiza mauaji hayo.

eng: And we ask our allies in the international human rights community to join us in our call, and in helping to ensure safety for those in peril.
swa: Na pia, tunawaomba washirika wetu wote wa jamii ya kimataifa ya kutetea haki za binadamu kutuunga mkono ikiwa ni pamoja na kusaidia kuimarisha usalama wa watu wote walio katika mazingira hatarishi.

eng: Following incumbent Burundi President Nkurunziza's candidacy for a third term, General Godefroid Niyombare announced that he has dismissed the current administration and that he is taking over until further notice.
swa: Kufuatia nia ya kugombea urais kwa kipindi cha tatu ya Rais wa Burundi aliye madarakani Nkurunziza, Jenerali Godefroid Niyombare alitangaza kwamba utawala uliopo umeangushwa rasmi na kwamba anatwaa madaraka mpaka itakapotangazwa vinginevyo.

eng: The government denies such coup has taken place and calls it a "farce".
swa: Serikali ilikanusha mapinduzi hayo kutokea na iliyaita "upuuzi".

swa: Rais Nkurunziza haikuwa nchini wakati mapinduzi yakitangazwa (lakini hakuna anayejua ikiwa amerudi au bado) : Rais alikuwa akihudhuria Mkutano wa Wakuu wa Nchi za Afrika Mashariki wakati mapinduzi hayo yakitangazwa.

eng: He has tried to fly back to the capital city but it is unclear whether he has succeeded.
swa: Amejaribu kureje kwa ndege jijini Bujumbura lakini haijulikani kama alifanikiwa.

eng: This is not (just) about ethnic conflicts :
swa: Huu si mgogoro (tu) wa kikabila :

eng: Nkurunziza and General Niyombare are both former Hutu rebel leaders.
swa: Nkurunziza na Jenerali Niyombare wote walikuwa viongozi wa waasi wa Ki-Hutu.

eng: They also belong to the same governing party, and Niyombare was both Ambassador to Kenya and intelligence chief, a post he was dismissed from earlier this year.
swa: Zote wako kwenye serikali ya chama hicho hicho, na Niyombare alikuwa balozi wa Kenya na mkuu wa ujasusi, nafasi ambayo alinyang'anywa mwaka huu.

eng: Like in Burkina Faso earlier this year, public opinion in Burundi seems to be in support of the coup as a way to oppose African life rulers:
swa: Kama ilivyokuwa kwa Burkina Faso mapema mwaka huu, maoni ya wananchi nchini Burundi yanaonekana kuunga mkono mapinduzi ya kijeshi kama namna moja ya kupinga watawala wa Kiafrika wanaotaka kutawala milele:

eng: What’s happening today in Burundi is reminiscent of what took place late last year in Burkina Faso, when long-time head of state Blaise Compaore was deposed by the military after declaring his intention to run for yet another term.
swa: Kiel kinacotokea leo Burundi ni mapaki ya kile kilichotokea mwishoni mwa mwaka jana nchini Burkina Faso, wakati mkuu wa nchi aliyetawala muda mrefu Blaise Compaore alipong'olewa madarakani na jeshi baada ya kutangaza dhamira yake ya kugombea tena kipindi kingine cha utawala.

eng: While the situation in Burkina Faso is still in flux, it was a key moment, as the public massively supported the coup, fed up with Compaore’s decades-long rule (..)but The situation in Burundi is also different, particularly given the protracted civil war which ended in 2005.
swa: Wakati hali nchini Burkina Faso bado haijatengemaa, hatua hiyo ilikuwa ya muhimu, kwa sababu wananchi waliunga mkono mapinduzi hayo, kwa sababu ya kuchoka utawala wa miongo kadhaa wa Compaore(..)lakini hali nchini Burundi ni tofauti kidogo, hususani kwa kurejea historia ya vita ya wenyewe kwa wenyewe nchini humo iliyokwisha mwaka 2005.

eng: Despite the recent arrests of FIFA officials due to indictments laid by the US Department of Justice, the world football governing body has said that its elections, which it calls the 65th FIFA Congress, will continue as scheduled today.
swa: Pamoja na kutiwa nguvuni kwa maafisa kadhaa wa FIFA kufuatia mashitaka yaliyofunguliwa na Wizara ya Sheria ya Marekani, chombo hicho kinachosimamia kandanda duniani kimesema kwamba uchaguzi wake, ambao utaunda baraza la 65 la FIFA, utaendelea kama ulivyopangwa hivi leo.

eng: Current FIFA president Sepp Blatter, who headed the organisation while the two-decade siege of corruption, bribery and money laundering was allegedly taking place, is seeking a fifth term at today's congress.
swa: Rais wa FIFA aliye madarakani Sepp Blatter, ambaye ameongoza chombo hicho katika kipindi cha miongo miwili inayodaiwa kugubikwa na ufisadi, rushwa na fedha haramu, anatafuta kuchaguliwa kwa muhula wa tano kwenye baraza la leo.

eng: Blatter has refused to resign amidst the scandal, despite several calls for him to step down.
swa: Blatter amegoma kujiuzulu pamoja na kuzungukwa na tuhuma, pamoja na mashinikizo yanayomtaka aachie ngazi.

swa: Unaweza kufuatilia matangazo ya moja kwa moja ya uchaguzi wa FIFA hapa.

eng: The ISIS, an Al Qaeda off-shoot has come to occupy large swathes of Syria and Iraq, leaving behind a trail of horror and destruction in a few months.
swa: Kundi la ISIS, ambalo ni tawi la Al Qaeda limedhibiti sehemu kubwa ya Syria na Iraq, na kusababisha taharuki kubwa na kusababisha uharibifu mkubwa ndani ya kipindi cha miezi michache.

eng: Areas captured by the fanatic group which insists on wiping out all sites of "heresy" and "apostasy" include the Cradle of Civilisation, an area rich in history since ancient times.
swa: Maeneo yaliyodhibitiwa na kikundi hicho kinachosisitiza kutokomeza maeneo yote ya "tetesi" na "kidini" ni pamoja na lile linaloitwa Cradle of Civilisation, eneo lenye historia kubwa tangu nyakati za zamani.

eng: The United Nations Education, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO) has a dedicated page entitled Safeguarding Syrian Cultural Heritage just to track the damage the Syrian conflict, now in its fourth year, has brought to the country's history.
swa: Shirika la Umoja wa Mataifa linaloshughulikia Elimu, Sayansi na Utamaduni (UNESCO) lina ukurasa maalum kwa ajili ya Kulinda Urithi wa Kiutamaduni wa Syria kwa lengo la kufuatilia uharibifu uliosababishwa na mapigano nchini humo, yanayokaribia miaka minne sasa, na athari zake kwenye historia yanchi hiyo.

eng: According to UNESCO:
swa: Kwa mujibu wa UNESCO:

eng: Illegal excavations and looting have exponentially increased since the beginning of the conflict in Syria.
swa: Uchimbaji na uvunjaji haramu kwa pamoja vimeongezeka tangu kuanza kwa vita nchini Syria.

eng: These actions have damaged many historical sites and museums, and important Syrian cultural property has disappeared from the country to end up on the black market and/or in private collections.
swa: Matukio haya yameharibu maeneo mengi ya kihistoria na makumbusho, na utajiri mkubwa wa kiutamaduni nchini humo umetoweka nchini na kuishia kwenye minada haramu na/au kuhifadhiwa na watu binafsi.

eng: Numerous archaeological sites in Syria are being systematically targeted for clandestine excavations by well-organized and often armed groups.
swa: Maeneo mengi ya kihistoria nchini Syria yamekuwa yakilengwa katika mashambulizi yanayofanywa na wanamgambo ambao mara nyingi huwa na silaha.

eng: Excavated archaeological objects of cultural significance make a lucrative trade for unscrupulous dealers operating both locally and internationally.
swa: Mali za kihistoria zinazoibwa zina umuhimu mkubwa wa kihistoria na kuwaletea faida kubwa wafanyabiashara hao wa kimagendo nchini humo na kimataifa.

eng: Sites situated near the borders are, in general, more susceptible to being targeted by looters who take advantage of their location to quickly and illegally export artefacts out of Syria.
swa: Maeneo hayo yaliyo karibu na mipaka, kwa ujumla, yamekuwa yakilengwa na wahalifu hao wanaotumia fursa ya kuwa karibu na maeneo hayo kuisafirisha utajiri huo nje ya nchi kwa urahisi kwa kutumia njia haramu.

eng: On the condition of museums, the damage assessment of museums page notes:
swa: Kuhusu hali ya makumbusho, ukurasa unaozungumzia tathmini ya uharibifu unabainisha:

eng: Most of the damage to museums in Syria has occurred in the north-western region of the country, where there have been incidents of looting of valuable cultural property, and many works of art are currently unaccounted for.
swa: Uharibufu mkubwa kwenye makubusho hayo nchini Syria umetokea kwenye eneo la kaskazini magharibi mwanchi hiyo, ambapo kumekuwa na matukio ya kuibwa kwa utajiri mkubwa wa kiutamaduni, na kazi nyingi za sanaa hazijulikani ziliko.

eng: A large number of museums have also had their infrastructure damaged as a result of being caught in the armed conflict.
swa: Idadi kubwa ya majengo ya makumbusho yameharibiwa vibaya ikiwa ni matokeo ya mapigano yanayoendelea kwa kutumia silaha nzito.
