eng: In April 2014, nine bloggers and journalists were arrested in Ethiopia.
swa: Mnamo mwezi wa Aprili, wanablogu tisa pamoja na waandishi wa habari walikamatwa nchini Ethiopia.

eng: Several of these men and women had worked with Zone9, a collective blog that covered social and political issues in Ethiopia and promoted human rights and government accountability.
swa: Baadhi ya wanaume na wanawake hawa walikuwa wakifanya kazi na Zone9, blogu ya ushirika iliyokuwa inazungumzia masuala ya kijamii na ya kisiasa nchini Ethiopia ikiwa ni pamoja na kuhamasisha uzingatiaji wa haki za binadamu na uwajibikaji wa serikali.

eng: Four of them were Global Voices authors.
swa: Miongoni mwao, wanablogu wanne walikuwa ni waandishi wa Global Voices.

eng: In July, they were charged under the country’s Anti-Terrorism Proclamation.
swa: Mapema mwezi Julai, walishitakiwa chini ya tamko la wazi la nchi dhidi ya ugaidi.

eng: They have been behind bars ever since and their trial has only recently begun.
swa: Wamekuwa gerezani tangu wakati huo na kesi yao hivi karibuni ndio imeanza kusikilizwa.

eng: This marks the sixth post in our series – “They Have Names” – that seeks to highlight the individual bloggers who are currently in jail.
swa: Makala hii ni ya tatu katika matoleo ya makala zetu za – “Wanayo Majina” – iliyo na madhumuni ya kuwazungumzia wanablogu ambao hadi sasa wapo gerezani.

eng: We wish to humanize them, to tell their particular and peculiar stories.
swa: Tunataka kutambua utu wao, tunataka kuelezea habari zao za kipekee na mahususi kabisa.

eng: This week, Swedish blogger and artist Melody Sundberg writes about Abel Wabela, a member of Zone9 and the manager of Global Voices' Amharic site.
swa: Wiki hii, mwanablogu wa Swideni na msanii, Melody Sundberg aandika kuhusu Abel Wabela, mmoja wa wanakikundi cha Zone9 na msimamizi wa jukwaa la Global Voices' katika Lugha ya Kihabeshi.

eng: I have never been to Ethiopia, but I have followed the never-ending trials of the bloggers closely through social media and conversations.
swa: Sikuwahi kufika Ethiopia, lakini nimefuatilia kwa ukaribu kupitia mitandao ya kijamii pamoja na kwenye majadiliano mashitaka ya wanablogu hawa yasiyoisha.

eng: A name often mentioned is that of Abel Wabela, a 28-year-old blogger, author and translator for Global Voices.
swa: Jina ambalo limekuwa likitanjwa mara nyingi ni la Abel Wabela, mwanablogu mwenye umri wa miaka 28, mwandinshi na mtafsiri wa Global Voices.

eng: During the first three months of the bloggers' detention in Maekelawi*, Abel refused to sign a prepared confession paper in which he, together with the other bloggers, were incriminated.
swa: Katika kipindi cha miezi mitatu ya kushikiliwa kwa mwanablogu huyu huko Maekelawi*, Abel alikataa kutia saini hati ya kiapo ambayo ingewaweka hatarini yeye pamoja na wanablogu wenzake.

eng: For this, Abel underwent extreme torture.
swa: Kufutia kukaa huku, Abel aliteswa isivyo mithilika.

eng: According to the Ethiopian Human Rights Project (EHRP), he was beaten by a person using a stick, and his feet were whipped by someone using a computer plug cable.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Mradi wa Haki za Binadamu wa Ethiopia (EHRP), Abel alipigwa na mtu kwa kutumia fimbo na mwingine aliichapa miguu yake mara kwa mara kwa kutumia waya wa kuchajia ngamizi.

eng: He was forced to lay on the floor while interrogators stomped on his back, neck and face.
swa: Alilazimishwa kulala sakafuni huku waliokuwa wakimhoji wakimkanyaga mgongoni mwake, kwenye shingo na usoni.

eng: Since then, he has had to use a hearing aid as a result of worsened hearing impairment.
swa: Tangu hapo, amekuwa akitumia vifaa vya kumsaidia kusikia kutokana na kusababishiwa tatizo la kiwango cha juu la kutokusikia.

eng: According to Endalk Chala, co-founder of the blogging group, Abel had suffered poor treatment even before his arrest.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Endalk Chala, mmoja wa aanzilishi wa kundi hili la ku-blogu, Abel amekuwa akipata tendwa visivyo hata kabla ya kukamatwa kwake.

eng: One day, three weeks before the arrest, Abel was beaten as he was walking home from work.
swa: Siku moja, wiki moja kabla ya kukamatwa kwake, Abel alivamiwa na kupigwa wakati akielekea nyumbani alipokuwa akitoka kazini.

eng: Several people appeared and beat him so severely that he lost his consciousness, and they took his cell phone and laptop.
swa: Watu kadhaa walijotkeza na kumpiga vibay sana kiasi cha kupoteza fahamu na pia walichukua simu yake ya mkononi pamoja na ngamizi mpakato yake.

eng: He feared beating was a threat, intended to make him stop blogging.
swa: Alihisi kuwa kwa kumpiga ilikuwa kama onyo, lililokuwa na lengo la kumfanya asiendelee kublogu.

eng: But Abel continued his work.
swa: Hata hivyo, abel aliendelea na kazi yake.

eng: Abel Wabela.
swa: Abel Wabela.

eng: Photo courtesy of family.
swa: Picha kwa idhini ya familia.

eng: I wanted to know more about Abel, so I asked some of those close to him to describe their friend.
swa: Nilitaka kufahamu zaidi kuhusu Abel, kwa hiyo niliwaomba wale marafiki zake wa karibu kumzungumzia Abel.

eng: Endalk Chala describes Abel as the most kindhearted and wonderful soul.
swa: Endalk Chala anamzungunzia Abel kama mtu mwenye kujali sana na wa kipekee kabisa.

eng: Abel is a man of knowledge and a great conversationalist, and he believes in open and honest discussions.
swa: Abel ni mtu mweledi sana na amminiye katika masikilizano, na anayeami katika majadiliano ya wazi na ya kweli..

eng: Jomanex Kasaye describes Abel as being straight forward and knowing what he stands for. At the same time, he is very humble.
swa: Jomanex Kasaye anamuelezea Abel kama mtu asiyepindisha maneno na anayefahamu fika kile anachokisimamia. na wakati huo huo, Abel ni mnyenyekevu sana.

eng: Abel is always hungry for more knowledge.
swa: Mara zote Abel anakuwa na uchu wa kutaka kujua.

eng: He likes to spend his time in discussions with historians, university lecturers and authors. His faith is important to him.
swa: Mara nyingi anapenda sana kutumia muda wake kujadili na wanahistoria, wahadhiri wa vyuo vikuu na waandishi. imani yake ni moja ya vipau mbele vyake.

eng: He loves attending in church.
swa: Anapenda kuhudhia ibada kanisani.

eng: He often visited prisoners, having the country and its people in his heart.
swa: Mara kwa mara alikuwa akiwatembelea wafungwa, akiwa na upendo wa dhati kwa nchi yake na watu wake.

eng: He always thinks of others rather than himself.
swa: Mara nyingi alikuwa akiwafikiria wengine kuliko anavyojifikiria yeye.

eng: The heartless treatment of Abel continued after his detention in Maekelawi.
swa: Matukio yasiyo nya utu dhidi ya Abel yaliendelea hata mara baada ya kushiliwa Maekelawi.

eng: Following one of the trials in February, prison officials had forgotten to handcuff him on the bus heading back to the prison.
swa: Kufuatia shitaka lake la mwezi Februari, maafisa wa polisi walisahau kumfunga pingu wakati wakimrudisha gerezani.

eng: For this, Abel was punished.
swa: Kwa sababu hii, Abel aliadhibiwa.

eng: They tied him up with dog chains for the whole day, and took away his hearing aid.
swa: Walimfunga kwa mnyororo wa mbwa kwa siku nzima na pia kumnyang'anya kifaa chake cha kumsaidia kusikia.

eng: During a trial in May, Abel was once again punished for using his right to expression.
swa: Wakati wa shitaka lake la mwezi Mei, kwa mara nyingine tena Abel aliadhibiwa kwa kutumia haki yake ya kujieleza.

eng: Abel questioned the judges for not letting the detainees speak.
swa: Abel aliwauliza majaji ni kwa nini hawakutoa ruhusa kwa washitakiwa kujieleza.

eng: For this, he was sentenced to four months for contempt of court.
swa: Kwa sababu hii, Abel alihukumiwa kifungo cha miezi minne kwa kuibeza mahakama.

eng: The kind of treatment Abel has been put through could break anyone.
swa: Aina ya matukio yasiyo ya utu alyokwishakabiliana nayo Abel yangeliweza kumkatisha tamaa mtu mwingine.

eng: Still, Abel has kept showing resistance.
swa: Lakini, abel ameendelea kuwa na msimamo.

eng: I ask myself: What is it that makes someone risk being jailed, beaten and tortured?
swa: Ninajiuliza: Ni nin haswa kinachomsukuma mtu hata kuweka reahani maisha yake kwa kufungwa jela, kupigwa na kuteswa?

eng: Reading Abel's latest letter, I find the answer:
swa: Kusoma Reading barua, ya hivi karibuni ya Abel kumenifanya nipate jibu:

eng: My purpose is to communicate.
swa: Lengo langu ni kufanya mawasiliano.

eng: My aim is to learn.
swa: Lengo langu ni kujifunza.

eng: My reason is to engage in a deep insightful intuitive understanding of life and fight bystander apathy.
swa: Sababu yangu kubwa ni kujihusisha kupata ufahamu wa kimaono na wa kina kabisa wa maisha na kupambana na hali ya kutokuchukua hatua na kutojali.

eng: This is my mission as a human.
swa: Hii ndio nia yangu mimi kama mwanadamu.

eng: It is not a task I was given from a stranger.
swa: Hii siyo kazi niliyopewa na mtu asiyefahamika.

eng: I will not allow anyone to trample on this basic right.
swa: Sitaruhusu yeyote yule kuminya haki hii ya msingi.

eng: I will not bargain with anyone whether they are people of political power, individuals, institutions or even a society to give away my basic speech right.
swa: Sitakubaliana na yeyote yule hata kama akiwa ni mwanasiasa, mtu binafsi, taasisi hata na jamii inayotaka kunipokonya haki yangu ya kujieleza.

eng: I practice my free speech rights in a public sphere, in my own private space, on social media, in prison, in a court room, in a police interrogation rooms.
swa: Ninatumia uhuru wangu wa kujieleza kwa watu kwa nafasi yangu binafsi, kwenye mitandao ya kijamii, gerezani, kwenye chumba cha mahakama, na hata kwenye vyumba vya polisi vya mahojiano.

eng: I use my free speech rights responsibly without hindering other peoples’ rights and I want to practice it everywhere.
swa: Ninatumia haki zangu za kujieleza ipasavyo bila la kuingilia haki za wengine, na hili ninataka kulionesha popote pale.

eng: In hindsight warnings, intimidations, arrest and torture have not stopped me from exercising my free speech rights neither they do in the future.
swa: Kwa kuweza kung'amua maangalizo, vitisho, kukamatwa na kuteswa hakujanifanya niache kutumia haki zangu za kujieleza na hata wakifanya hivi kwa siku zijazo.

eng: To fight bystander apathy... 	Kupambana na hali ya kutokuchukua hatua na kutojali...
This is my mission as a human."
swa: Hii ndio nia yangu mimi kama mwanadamu."

eng: The sentences form a simple answer to a difficult question.
swa: Sentensi hizi zinatoa jibu rahisi kwa swali gumu.

eng: The reason Abel keeps using his freedom of expression is because it is a basic right that can be exercised everywhere in every situation.
swa: Sababu inayomfanya Abel aendelee kutumia haki yake ya msingi ya uhuru wa kujieleza ni kwa kuwa ni haki ya msingi ambayo inaweza kutumiwa kila mahali na kwa kila hali.

eng: He has made the choice to use this right, because speaking out against injustice is to fight bystander apathy.
swa: Ameafanya uamuzi wa kuitumia haki hii, kwa kuwa kuzungumza dhidi ya ukandamizaji ndio kupambana na hali ya kutokujali na kutochukua hatua.

eng: I am more than certain that he will continue defending this right for the rest of his life.
swa: Nina uhakika zaidi ya asilimia mia kuwa ataendelea kutetea haki yake hadi mwisho wa maisha yake.

eng: We live in a world where some label the use of freedom of expression as an act of terrorism.
swa: Tunaishi kwenye ulimwengu ambao kuna baadhi ya watu wanaouchora uhuru wa kujieleza kama kitendo cha ugaidi.

eng: We also live in a world where others are sacrificing their freedom while defending our right to speak our minds.
swa: Pia tunaishi kwenye ulimwengu ambao baadhi ya watu wanatoa sadaka uhuru wao katika kutetea uhuru wetu wa kujieleza.

eng: The Zone9 Bloggers defended human rights.
swa: Wanablogu wa Zone9 walitetea haki za binadamu.

eng: They chose to stand up against injustice.
swa: Wameamua kusimamia kidete dhidi ya ukiukwaji wa haki.

eng: They chose to speak the truth.
swa: Wameamua kuusema ukweli.

eng: For this, they were robbed of their freedom.
swa: Kwa minajili hii, walipokonywa uhuru wao.They chose to stand up against injustice.

eng: I do not know Abel today, but I look forward to the day I will.
swa: Hadi sasa, simfahamu Abel, lakini nina imani siku moja nitamfahamu.

eng: * Following their arrest, the bloggers and journalists were jailed in Maekelawi.
swa: * Kufuatia kukamatw kwao, wanablogu na waandishi hawa walifungwa gerezani huko Maekelawi.

eng: Maekelawi is the Federal Police Crime Investigation Sector in Addis Ababa.
swa: Maekelawi ni Sekta ya Polisi ya Shirikisho la Upelelezi wa Matukio lililopo Addis Ababa.

eng: Political prisoners, journalists, bloggers, protest organizers among others are held there before proceeding to prison.
swa: Wafungwa wa kisiasa, waandishi wa habari, wanablogu, waratibu wa maandamano na wngine wengi huwekwa kizuizini huko kabla ya kupelekwa jela.

eng: Human Rights Watch has reported about torture, coercive interrogation methods and poor detention conditions taking place there.
swa: Waangalizi wa haki za binadaPolitical prisoners, journalists, bloggers, protest organizers among others are held there before proceeding to prison.

eng: Soccer fans holding vuvuzelas watching the opening game of the World Cup.
swa: Mashabiki wa soka waliobeba mavuvuzela wakitazama mchezo wa ufunguzi wa Kombe la dunia.

eng: Photo by Marcello Casal Jr.
swa: Picha ya Marcello Casal Jr.

eng: Published by Agência Brasil under Creative Commons.
swa: Imechapishwa na Agência Brasil kwa leseni ya Creative Commons.

swa: Miaka mitano iliyopita mnamo Juni 11, mashindano ya 19 ya Kombe la Dunia la FIFA yalianza Afrika Kusini.

eng: It was the first time the tournament had ever taken place on African soil.
swa: Ilikuwa ni mara ya kwanza kwa mashindano hayo kufanyika kwenye ardhi ya Afrika.

eng: Using the hashtag #2010Memories, South Africans on Twitter remembered the day Vuvuzelas took over the soccer world.
swa: Kwa kutumia alama habari ya #2010Memories , Waafrika Kusini kwenye mtandao wa twita walikumbuka siku ambayo mavuvuzela yalitawala ulimwengu wa kandanda.

eng: Vha Musanda shared a photo of the moment that sent South Africa into tears.
swa: Vha Musanda aliweka picha mtandaoni iliyoonesha dakika muhimu iliyoitoa mchozi ya furaha Afrika Kusini.

eng: It was the first goal of the tournament by South African striker Tshabalala in the match against Mexico, which ended 1-1:
swa: Lilikuwa ni goli la kwanza kwenye mashindano hayo lililofungwa na mshambuliaji wa Afrika Kusini Tshabalala kwenye mchezo dhidi ya Mexico, uliomalizika kwa bao 1-1:

eng: The moment that brought tears to SA'ns.
swa: Dakika iliyowatoa machozi mashabiki wa Afrika Kusini.

eng: We were United.
swa: Tuliunganishwa.

eng: S/O to my government for that dispora donation #2010memories pic.twitter.com/muGzcdQSLv — Vha Musanda (@freedom_ride) June 11, 2015
swa: Shukrani kwa serikali kwa mchango wa raia waishio ughaibuni

eng: The YouTube video below shows Shakira singing Waka Waka, the song for 2010 World Cup during the opening ceremony:

eng: While everyone was crazy about the tournament, Khulekani Mathe remembers that he was crazy about something else:
swa: Wakati kila mmoja alikuwa na 'kichaa' cha mashindano, Khulekani Mathe anakumbuka alivyochanganyikiwa kwa jambo jingine kabisa:

swa: Siku kama ya leo 2010 nilikuwa India.

swa: Wakati kila mmoja akifuatilia mechi ya ufunguzi, nilikuwa nimechanganyikiwa nisijue wapi nikatazame mchezo huo

eng: Twitter user King Billy never felt so safe in the streets of Johannesburg, which is considered one of the most violent cities in the world:
swa: Mtumiaji wa twita King Billy anasema hakuwahi kujisikia salama kwenye mitaa ya Johannesburg, inayosemekana kuwa moja wapo ya mitaa hatari zaidi duniani:

eng: Vuma Augustus said he'd never seen people so united in all his life:

swa: Sikuwa kuwaona watu walioungana kiasi kwenye maisha yangu, nimekumbuka nyakati hizi sana

eng: Few South Africans appear to be overly distraught by the allegations that the country paid a $10-million bribe to win its World Cup bid.
swa: Baadhi ya Waafrika Kusini wanaoonekana kushangazwa na madai kwamba nchi hiyo ilitoa rushwa ya dola za Marekani milioni 10 ili kupewa nafasi ya kuandaa mashindano hayo.

eng: Twitter user Yang and Reckless said the scandal doesn't bother him:
swa: Mtumiaji wa Twita 'Yang and Reckless' alisema kashfa hiyo haimsumbui:

swa: Nilikuwepo kushuhudia nchi nzuri iliyoungana.

eng: Bribe or no bride the 2010 World Cup Legacy lives on pic.twitter.com/UH7g2t9z1B — Yang and Reckless (@CosteMayang) June 11, 2015
swa: Rushwa iwepo au isiwepo Kumbukumbu ya Kombe la Dunia la 2010 itaendelea kuwepo

eng: Other people online are event more indifferent:
swa: Watu wengine mtandaoni hawakuwa tofauti sana:

eng: #2010memories#FIFAscandal WTF***k who cares there was a bribe or not..we got beautiful stadiums..tourists ar still coming so wht — Lucky 1Xap sentence. (@LuckylLucky) June 11, 2015
swa: Nani anajali kama rushwa ilitolewa au haikutolewa...tulipata viwanja vizuri...watalii bado wanakuja...sasa nini

swa: Nchi nyingine, anasema Nkateko Baloi, zina wivu wa maendeleo ya Afrika Kusini mwaka 2010:

swa: Kwa nini tubaki kukumbuka mambo ya zamani wakati nchi nyingine zina wivu wa namna mashindano yalivyokuwa mazuri

eng: According to Kabwe Songolo, the conduct of the South African government and FIFA shouldn't detract from the fun of the sporting event itself:
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Kabwe Songolo, vitendo vya serikali ya Afrika Kusini na FIFA havipaswi kutupotezea mwelekeo wa kufurahia kandanda lenyewe:

swa: Achacheni nao!

eng: Some Internet users addressed US federal investigators, who are responsible for the recent high-profile arrests in Switzerland.
swa: Baadhi ya watumiaji wa mtandao walielekeza maoni yao kwa wapepelezi wa Serikali ya Marekani, ambao ndio waliohusika kuwakamata wakubwa wa FIFA nchini Uswisi.

eng: But one things the FBI cannot take away from #SouthAfrica is the pride and #2010memories! — King Billy⭐ (@itsmissbilly_) June 11, 2015
swa: Lakini kimoja ambacho FBI hawawezi kukichukua kutoka Afrika Kusini, ni fahari na kumbukumbu ya 2010!

eng: However, Charlie Langa's memories are not as positive as many South Africans on Twitter:
swa: Hata hivyo, kumbukumbu za Charlie Langa hazikuwa chanya kama ilivyo kwa wa-Afrika Kusini wengine kwenye mtandao wa Twita:

eng: The legacy of Corruption.
swa: Kumbukumbu ya Ufisadi.

eng: Bribery, Racketeering, Money Laundering, Tax evasion.The list is too long=783. #2010memories. — Charlie Langa (@CharlieLanga) June 11, 2015
swa: Rushwa, mipango ya wizi, Uhamishaji wa Fedha haramu, Ukwepaji wa kodi. Orodha ni ndefu

eng: While Tom Moultrie wonders how much innocence South Africans have lost since the World Cup:
swa: Wakati Tom Moultrie akishangaa kiasi gani cha uungwana walichokipoteza Waafrika Kusini tangu kumalizika kwa Kombe la Dunia:

eng: #2010memories all over my social media today.
swa: Kumbukumbu za 2010 zimetamalaki kwenye mitandao yangu yote ya kijamii leo.

eng: How much innocence have we lost in the last 1826 days? — Tom Moultrie (@tomtom_m) June 11, 2015
swa: Tumepoteza uungwana kiasi gani katika siku 1826 zilizopita?

eng: Protests in Niamey, Niger via Abdoulaye Hamidou on twitter (with his permission)
swa: Maandamano mjini Niamey, Naija kupitia kwenye ukurasa wa Abdoulaye Hamidou kwenye mtandao wa Twita (kwa ruhusa yake)

eng: 20,000 Nigeriens took to the streets in Niamey, Niger on June, 6.
swa: Wanaija 20,000 wameingia mitaani mjini Niamey, Naija mnamo Juni, 6.

eng: There are multiple causes for the protests: endemic poverty, mediocre governance and restricted free speech are among the main grievances from Nigerien civil society.
swa: Kuna ababu nyingi za maandamano hayo: umaskini uliokithiri, utawala mbovu na kubanwa kwa uhuru wa kujieleza yakiwa ni moja wapo ya malalamiko ya asasi za kiraia nchini humo.

eng: These protests come on the hill of similar uprisings in Burkina Faso, Burundi and Togo.
swa: Maandamano kama haya yalitokea katika nchi za Burkina Faso, Burundi na Togo.

eng: The government resigned in Burkina Faso while elections are postponed in Burundi.
swa: Serikali iliachia ngazi nchini Burkina Faso wakati uchaguzi ukiahirishwa nchini Burundi.

eng: In May, citizens in Lome protested presidential election results that saw Togolese president Faure Gnassingbe won a third term.
swa: Mwezi Mei, wananchi wa Lome waliandamana kupinga matokeo ya urais yaliyompa ushindi rais Faure Gnassingbe aliyeshinda kwa muhula wa tatu.

eng: Photo from the Facebook Page of #myfriend campaign.
swa: Picha kutoka kwenye ukurasa wa Facebook wa kampeni ya #myfriend.

eng: A selfie campaign in Myanmar promotes tolerance and friendship amid rising cases of hate speech, discrimination, and communal violence accross the country.
swa: Kampeni ya kujipiga picha nchini Myanmar imeonekana kukuza kuvumiliana na kuongeza urafiki wakati ambapo kuna ongezeko la matukio ya watu kutukanana, kubaguana na ghasia za kijamii katika maeneo mengi ya nchi hiyo.

eng: The Facebook campaign is led by young people from Yangon, the country's biggest city, and it launched last April by asking the public to pose for selfies with their friends who belong to a different ethnic groups or religions.
swa: Kampeni ya mtandao wa facebook inayoongozwa na vijana kutoka jiji kubwa zaidi nchini humo, Yangon, na ilianza mwezi April kwa kuwaomba watu kujipiga picha wakiwa na marafiki zao wenye dini au kabila tofauti na wao na kuzituma picha hizo kwenye mtandao huo.

eng: The campaign uses the hashtags #myfriend and #friendship_has_no_boundaries.
swa: Kampeni hiyo inatumia alama habari za #myfriend na #friendship_has_no_boundaries.

eng: Since 2012, there have been intermittent clashes between some Buddhists and minority Muslims in central, western, and northern areas of Myanmar, including in Meikhtila in central Myanmar, where the houses of both Buddhist and Muslim communities were burned down and thousands of people were displaced.
swa: Tangu mwaka 2012, kumekuwa na ghasia kubwa kati ya baadhi ya waumini wa dini ya ki-Budha na Waislamu walio wachache katika maeneo ya kati, magharibi,na kaskazini mwa Myanmar, ikiwa ni pamoja na Meikhtila lililo katikati ya Myanmar, ambako nyumba za watu wa jamii za ki-Budha na ki-Islam zilichomwa na maelefu ya watu wakiachwa bila makazi.

eng: The most serious communal violence took place in October 2012 in the Rakhine state of western Myanmar, where Rohingya Muslims have been living in refugee camps near the city of Sittwe.
swa: Vurugu kubwa zaidi ni zile zilizotokea mwezi Oktoba 2012 katika jimba la Rakhine magharibi mwa Myanmar, ambako wa-Islamu wa Rohingya Muslims wamekuwa wakiishi kwenye makambi ya wakimbizi karibu na jiji la Sittwe.

eng: The Myanmar government considers the Rohingya to be illegal immigrants.
swa: Serikali ya Myanmar inawachukulia watu wa jamii ya Rohingya kuwa wahamiaji haramu.

eng: At the same time, online hate speech and harassment has been widespread on Myanmar's social media, creating an atmosphere intolerance and racism.
swa: Wakati huo huo, kuna matukio ya kusambaa kwa maneno ya kashfa na kutukanana sambamba na unyanyasaji kwenye mitandao ya kijamii nchini humo, hali inayofanya kuwepo kwa mazingira ya kutokuvumiliana pamoja na ubaguzi wa rangi.

eng: Below are some photos from the #MyFriend campaign to prove that people in Myanmar, especially the young, are determined to end hate by showing respect and friendship.
swa: Hapa chini unaweza kuona picha za kampeni ya #MyFriend kuthibitisha kwamba watu nchini Myanmar, hususani vijana, wamekusudia kumaliza chuki kwa kuonesha wanavyoheshimiana na kupendana.

eng: Han Seth Lu, a Buddhist, uploads a photo with his Muslim friend:
swa: Han Seth Lu, Mwislamu, aliweka picha hii akiwana rafiki yake Mbudha:

swa: Mimi ni Mbudha na Rafiki yangu ni Mwislam.

eng: I'm a Boy and She is a Girl.
swa: Mie mvulana yeye ni Msichana.

eng: We are different but we accept each other.
swa: Tunaonekana tofauti lakini tunakubaliana.

eng: Life is not permanent, enjoy yourself right now.
swa: Maisha hayadumu, furahia sasa.

eng: Because friendship has no boundaries. #MyFriend #Friendship_has_no_boundaries - looking for peace with May Khin
swa: Kwa sababu urafiki hauna mipaka. #MyFriend #Friendship_has_no_boundaries - tunatafuta amani tukiwa na May Khin

eng: Rody Din, a Christian, shares a photo with his Buddhist friend from Thailand:
swa: Rody Din, Mkristo, anaweka picha akiwa na rafiki yake Mbudha kutoka Thailand:

eng: He is a Sikh and I'm a Muslim.
swa: Huyu ni Msikh na mie Mwislam.

eng: But we are friends.
swa: Bado tu marafiki.

eng: Although we have diversities,we share our own opinions and beliefs, we accept and respect our different identities. #Myfriend #Friendship_has_no_boundaries
swa: Ingawa tuna tofauti zetu, bado tunazungumzia maoni na imani zetu, tumezikubali na kuziheshimu tofauti zetu. #Myfriend #Friendship_has_no_boundaries

eng: Professor Pierre de Vos weighs in on the debate about assisted dying in South Africa after a South African High Court ruled that a dying person is entitled to be assisted by a qualified medical doctor to end his or her life:
swa: Profesa Pierre de Vos anaingia rasmi kwenye mjadala mkali kuhusu uwezekano wa kumsaidia mtu kufa nchini Afrika Kusini baada ya Mahakama Kuu nchini humo kuamua kwamba mtu anayekufa ana haki ya kusaidiwa kufa na daktari ili aweze kuyahitimisha maisha yake:

eng: It is important to note that the ruling does not force any person to end his or her life or to assist anyone else to do so.
swa: Ni muhimu kuona kwamba hukumu hii haimlazimishi mtu kuyakatisha maisha yake au kumsaidia mtu kufanya hivyo.

eng: It remains a personal choice.
swa: Hilo bado linabaki kuwa uamuzi wa mtu binafsi.

eng: The judgment thus confirms that the criminal law (or, I would add, the ethical rules of the HPCSA ) cannot be used to enforce the moral, religious or ethical beliefs of some on everyone.
swa: Hukumu hii inaweka msisitizo wa sheria ya makosa ya jinai (au, ningeongeza, sheria ya maadili ya Baraza la Watumishi wa Sekta ya Afya Afrika Kusini kwamba haiwezekani kutekeleza jambo lolote lililo kinyume na misimamo ya kidini au kimaadili kwa mtu yeyote.

eng: However, this does not force those who hold such moral, religious or ethical beliefs to act in breach of their beliefs.
swa: Hata hivyo, hayo haiwalazimishi wale wenye imani hizo kuweza kuvunja imani zao wenyewe.

eng: Moreover, if the Constitutional Court confirms the judgment it would be desirable for Parliament to pass legislation to establish a system with minimum safeguards in order to protect patients.
swa: Zaidi, kama Mahakama ya Katiba itapitisha hukumu hiyo basi itafaa kwa Bunge kupitisha mfumo utakaowalinda wagonjwa.

eng: In the absence of such legislation a patient would have to approach a court for permission to be legally assisted to die.
swa: Bila sheria hizo mgonjwa atapaswa kwenda mahakamani kupata ruhusa ya kusaidiwa kufa.

eng: Today is June 4, the 26th anniversary of the Tiananmen Square pro-democracy protests of 1989.
swa: Leo ni Juni 4, maadhimisho ya 26 ya maandamano ya kudai demokrasia ya Tiananmen mwaka 1989.

eng: In recent years, some numbers have gone missing on the Chinese Internet because of censorship.
swa: Katika miaka ya hivi karibuni, baadhi ya tarakimu zimepotea kwenye mtandao wa Intaneti nchini China kwa sababu ya udhibiti wa taarifa.

eng: They are all unsearchable on mainland Chinese search engines and cannot appear in public timelines on social media.
swa: Tarakimu hizo hazitafutiki kwenye tovuti za kutafutia taarifa na haziwezi kuonekana kwenye mitandao ya kijamii.

eng: Political cartoonist Biantailajiao highlighted such ridiculous way of erasing history on Twitter:
swa: Mchora katuni za kisiasa Biantailajiao, kupitia mtandao wa twita, alionesha namna hiyo ya kijinga ya kujaribu kufuta historia:

eng: If possible, they would delete this particular date from the calendar.
swa: Kama inawezekana, wanaweza kuifuta kabisa tarehe hii kwenye kalenda.

eng: A date none of us will forget, sketched on a wall in Pokhara.
swa: Siku ambayo kamwe sote hatutaweza kuisahau, iliyochorwa kwenye ukuta huko Pokhara.

eng: The quake spared Pokhara, but aftershocks have hit in the form of cancelled bookings and empty hotel rooms.
swa: The quake spared Pokhara, but aftershocks have hit in the form of cancelled bookings and empty hotel rooms.

eng: Photo by @paavan11 via Nepal Photo Project.
swa: Picha na @paavan11 kupitia Mradi wa Picha wa Nepal.

eng: Used with permission
swa: Imetumiwa kwa ruhusa

eng: More than 8,000 people have been killed, twice as many are injured, 2 million people have been displaced, and an estimated total of 8 million have been affected in some way.
swa: Zaidi ya watu 8,000 wameuawa, mara mbili zaidi ya idadi hii wakiwa majeruhi, watu milioni 2 wakiwa wameachwa bila makazi, na watu wanaokadiriwa kufikia milioni 8 wakisadikiwa kuathiriwa kwa namna moja ama nyingine.

eng: (For more information, see Global Voices' special coverage page.)
swa: (Kwa taarifa zaidi, fuatiliaGlobal Voices' ukurasa wa habari maalum .)

eng: The Nepal Photo Project is working to capture this historic catastrophe in pictures.
swa: Mradi wa Picha wa Nepali unafanya kazi ya kukusanya picha za dhoruba hii ya kihistoria.

eng: The project belongs to a team of ten photographers in and around Kathmandu, led by photographer Sumit Dayal and writer Tara Bedi, who launched the initiative shortly after the April 25 earthquake.
swa: Mradi huu unamilikiwa na kundi la wapiga picha 10 wanaotoka nje pamoja na wale wa Kathmandu, linaloongozwa na mpiga picha Sumit Dayal na mwandishi Tara Bedi, ambaye alizindua mradi huu siku chache mara baada ya kutokea kwa tetemeko la ardhi la tarehe 25 Aprili.

eng: So far, it has more than 61,400 followers in Instagram and more than 7,600 followers on Facebook.
swa: Hadi sasa, mradi huu una zaidi ya wafuatiliaji 61,400 katika Instagram na zaidi ya wafuatiliaji 7,600 kwenye Facebook.

eng: Using crowdsourced photos, contributing photographers retell the story of life after the earthquakes: the devastation, rescue, relief, reconstruction, and the rays of hope for the future.
swa: Wakitumia mtindo wa ukusanyaji wa picha kutoka katika maeneo tofauti, wapiga picha katika mradi huu wanasimulia simulizi za maisha ya baada ya kutokea kwa tetemeko la ardhi: uharibifu, uokozi, misaada, ujenzi mpya, pamoja na miale ya matumaini kwa nyakati zijazo.

eng: The increasing popularity of the project is due primarily to its simplicity: contributors merely add a hashtag to their images, writing #nepalphotoproject, and include a short caption about the photo's context and characters.
swa: Umaarufu wa haraka wa mradi huu unatokana haswa na urahisi wake: wachangiaji wanaweka tu kiungo habari katika picha zao na kuandika #nepalphotoproject, na kisha kujumuisha na maelezo kidogo yanayohusiana muktadha wa picha pamoja na wahusika katika picha ile.

eng: Organizers want to keep it more functional and personal in nature.
swa: Wanaoratibu mradi huu wanalenga kuufanya mradi huu kuwa na ufanisi mzuri na ulio ndani ya uwezo wa mtu binafsi.

eng: The project's recent posts show how life in Nepal is returning to normal and how people are rebuilding.
swa: Makala za hivi karibuni za mradi huu zinaonesha jinsi maisha nchini Nepali yanavyorejea katika hali ya kawaida na namna watu wanavyojiimarisha tena.

eng: This is Manju Gurung.
swa: Hii ni Manju Gurung.

eng: Whenever I try to take her picture, she giggles and runs away.

eng: She and her family have been living together with two more families in a chicken shed since April 25. At least the school is on for her and she is happy to be with her friends.

eng: In April 2014, nine bloggers and journalists were arrested in Ethiopia.
swa: Mnamo mwezi wa Aprili, wanablogu tisa pamoja na waandishi wa habari walikamatwa nchini Ethiopia.

eng: Several of these men and women had worked with Zone9, a collective blog that covered social and political issues in Ethiopia and promoted human rights and government accountability.
swa: Baadhi ya wanaume na wanawake hawa walikuwa wakifanya kazi na Zone9, blogu ya ushirika iliyokuwa inazungumzia masuala ya kijamii na ya kisiasa nchini Ethiopia ikiwa ni pamoja na kuhamasisha uzingatiaji wa haki za binadamu na uwajibikaji wa serikali.

eng: And four of them were Global Voices authors.
swa: Miongoni mwao, wanablogu wanne walikuwa ni waandishi wa Global Voices.

eng: They have been behind bars ever since, their trial postponed time and again.
swa: Tangu wakati huo, wameendelea kuwepo gerezani, huku shitaka lao likiwa linaahirishwa mara kwa mara.

eng: This marks the third post in our series – “They Have Names” – that seeks to highlight the individual bloggers who are currently in jail.
swa: Makala hii ni ya tatu katika matoleo ya makala zetu za - "Wanayo Majina" - iliyo na madhumuni ya kuwazungumzia wanablogu ambao hadi sasa wapo gerezani.

eng: We wish to humanize them, to tell their particular and peculiar stories.
swa: Tunataka kutambua utu wao, tunataka kuelezea habari zao za kipekee na mahususi kabisa.

eng: This story comes from Endalk Chala, a founding member of the Zone9 collective who was spared arrest on account of being in the United States, where he is pursuing a PhD.
swa: Simulizi hii inatoka kwa Endalk Chala, mmoja wa waanzilishi wa umoja wa Zone9 ambaye alisalimika kwa kutofungwa gerezani kwa kile kinachoelezwa kuwa alikuwa nchini Marekani, anaposomea shahada yake ya Uzamivu.

eng: I met Zelalem Kiberet in 2012.
swa: Kwa mara ya kwanza nilikutana na Zelalem Kiberet mwaka 2012.

eng: I had come to know him through his blog, where he wrote about curious and inspiring literary pieces, art, politics, history and philosophy.
swa: Nilimfahamu kupitia blogu yake, ambapo alikuwa akiandika kwa kiudadisi na kwa mvuto makala kuhusiana na sanaa, siasa, historia na falsafa.

eng: For me, reading his posts on philosophy and chatting with him occasionally on Facebook was never intimate enough, so I decided to meet him in person.
swa: kwangu mimi, kwa kusoma makala zake zilizohusiana na falsafa pamoja na kupiga soga naye mara kwa mara kupitia Facebook, kamwe hakukuniridhisha, hadi pale nilipoamua kuonana naye ana kwa ana.

eng: At that time, I always longed to meet my online friends.
swa: Kwa kipindi hicho, nilikuwa nikitamani sana kukutana na rafiki zangu wa mtandaoni.

eng: This is what eventually led to us forming Zone9.
swa: Hili ndilo haswa hatimaye lililotupelekea kuanzisha Zone9.

eng: That day it was Befeqadu, who is the dynamo of the collective, who organized our meeting.
swa: Siku hiyo, alikuwa niBefeqadu ambaye ndiye aliyekuwa mshika dau mkubwa wa umoja huu, aliratibu mkutano wetu.

eng: We met in a café called Pizza, at the heart of Addis Ababa.
swa: Tulikutana kwenye mgahawa uliojulikana kwa jina la Pizza, katikati mwa jiji la Addis Ababa.

eng: Befeqadu and I arrived first and then Zelalem joined us.
swa: Befeqadu na mimi tuliwasili wa kwanza, na baadae Zelalem alijumuika nasi.

eng: He greeted us warmly.
swa: Alitusalimu kwa bashasha.

eng: We were sitting at table near the door.
swa: Tulikuwa tumekaa kwenye meza iliyokuwa karibu na mlango.

eng: He ordered a cup of macchiato and then we had one of our best conversations.
swa: Aliagiza kikombe kimoja cha macchiato na kisha tukafanya moja ya mazungumzo mazuri kabisa.

eng: Zelalem was a graduate student at the School of Law of Addis Ababa University, and also taught law at Ambo University.
swa: Zelalem alikuwa mhitimu katika Kitivo cha Sheria katika Chuo Kikuu cha Addis Ababa na pia alikuwa akifundisha masual ya sheria katika Chuo Kikuu cha Ambo.

eng: I consider myself very lucky to have worked with Zelalem.
swa: Nilijiona mwenye bahati sana kwa kutokea kufanya kazi na Zelalem.

eng: Because of his wit, humorous writings and uncompromising digs on religion, his friends tweaked Zelalem’s name into the name of the imminent French writer Zola, whom Zelalem himself read with great enthusiasm.
swa: Kutokana na upeo wake mkubwa, uandishi wa kuvutia, na maaandiko yake yaliyokuwa na mvuto na msimamo wake wa kuidadafua dini, marafiki zake walibadilisha kidogo jina la Zelalem na kuwa jina la mwandishi mashuhuri wa Ufaransa, Zola, ambaye hata Zelalem mwenyewe amekuwa akimsoma kwa shauku kubwa.

eng: Our Zola’s love for philosophy and art is so visible that he made the banner of his blog the famous painting of Jacques-Louis David’s "The Death of Socrates".
swa: Upendo wa Zola wetu katika masuala ya falsafa na sanaa unajidhihirisha kwake haswa pale alipolifanya tangazo la utambulisho wa blogu yake kuwa ni picha maarufu ya "Kifo cha Socrates" iliyoandaliwa na Jacques-Louis David.

eng: The Death of Socrates, by Jacques-Louis David.
swa: Kifo cha Socrates, na Jacques-Louis David. ilitolewa Released to public domain.

eng: Released to public domain. Image via Wikimedia.
swa: Picha kupitia Wikimedia.

eng: Zola’s hit tweets were so illustrious among his peers that I would dare to say that at the time of his arrest, Zola was becoming the most commonly read Ethiopian on Twitter.
swa: Twita za Zola zilizopata umaarufu mkubwa zilitosha sana kumuelezea vizuri miongoni mwa wenzake kiasi kwamba ninadiriki kusema kwamba hadi wakati anatiwa kizuizini, Zola tayari alishakuwa Mhabeshi aliyekuwa akisomwa sana katika mtandao wa Twitter.

eng: His humorous and witty tweets established him as a rising literary talent to watch.
swa: Ukarimu wake na Twiti zake za hekima ya hali ya juu vilimfanya kuwa mtu ambaye ilikuwa lazima kumfuatilia.

eng: Zola can also write longer moving pieces.
swa: Zola anaweza pia kuandika makala zinazodumu kwa kipindi kirefu.

eng: In one of his blog posts he mocked a subject which mainstream newspapers from inside Ethiopia haven’t dared to acknowledge.
swa: Katika moja ya makala zake za blogu, alitoa dhihaka dhidi ya watu fulani ambao kamwe magazeti ya nchini Ethiopia hayakuthubutu kukanusha.

eng: In his blog post, titled “How to create your own religion? – An Ethiopian guide", he wrote a long satire on how state-run outlets broadcast programs in an effort to create a cult personality of the late former president Meles Zenawi.
swa: Katika malaka moja ya blogu, iliyokuwa na kichwa cha habari “Namna unavyoweza Kuvumbua Dini yako Mwenyewe – Mwangozo wa Kihabeshi", aliandika makala ndefu ya dhihaka ya namna ambavyo vipindi kwenye vyombo vya habari vinavyomilikiwa na serikali na harakati zao za kujaribu kupenyeza mfumo wa kidini wa aliyekuwa Rais wa Ethiopia hayati Meles Zenawi.

eng: These kinds of his writings put Zola on the radar of the Ethiopian government.
swa: Aina hii ya maandiko yake ulimuweka Zola katika ungalizi wa karibu uliokuwa unafanywa na serikali ya Ethiopia.

eng: Today, after over a year in prison, he is facing trumped-up terrorism charges for being a true intellectual, and one who uses humor to communicate his critiques.
swa: Hadi wakati huu, takribani mwaka mmoja akiwa gerezani, Zola anakabiliwa na mashitaka ya kutengenezwa yanayomhusisha na ugaidi ati kwa kuwa tu ni mwanazuoni halisi atumiaye unyenyekevu wake katika ukosoaji.

eng: On the banner of his blog, Zola has written ‘Let Freedom Ring’.
swa: Katika bango la blogu yake, Zola aliandika ‘Acha Uhuru Uvume’.

eng: For as long as he is behind bars, we must carry out this wish on his behalf.
swa: Kwa kuwa bado yupo gerezani, hatuna budi kudumisha matarajio haya kwa niaba yake.

eng: Burundian president Pierre Nkuruzinza.
swa: Rais wa Burundi Pierre Nkuruzinza.

eng: Photo released under Creative Commons by the World Economic Forum.
swa: Picha imetolewa chini ya leseni ya Creative Commons na World Economic Forum.

eng: New research by Afrobarometer, a project that measures public attitudes in Sub Saharan Africa, suggests that most Africans support two-term presidential term limits for their presidents.
swa: Utafiti mpya uliofanywa na Afrobarometer, mradi unaopima mitazamo ya wananchi katika nchi za kusini mwa Jangwa la Sahara, unaonesha kwamba wa-Afrika wengi wanaunga mkono ukomo wa vipindi viwili tu kwa marais wao.

eng: The report, based on surveys in 34 African countries, says:
swa: Taarifa hiyo, inayojumuisha tafiti katika nchi 34 za Afrika, inasema:

eng: This is true even in those countries that have never had term limits and those that have removed them in the past 15 years.
swa: haya yameonekana hata kwenye nchi zile ambazo hazijawahi kuwa na ukomo wa vipindi vya urais na hata kwenye nchi zile zilizoondoa ukomo huo katika kipindi cha miaka 15 iliyopita.

eng: Continuing efforts to dispense with term limits thus reveal a major disconnect between African leaders and African citizens on this issue, underlining the lingering legacy of big-man rule on the continent and highlighting the fragility of African democracies.
swa: Juhudi zinazoendelea za kuondoa ukomo wa madaraka zinaonesha tofauti kubwa kati ya matakwa ya watawala wa Afrika dhidi ya matakwa ya wananchi wanaowongoza, hali inayoonesha kuendelea kuwepo kwa hulka ya udikteta barani humo na hivyo kuonesha dalili mbaya kwa demokrasia ya Afrika.

eng: The report discusses the term limit extension phenomenon in African politics:
swa: Taarifa inajadili dhana ya kuongeza ukomo wa mihula ya utawala katika siasa za Afrika:

eng: At the end of the 20th century, many African countries adopted presidential term limits aspart (sic) of a broader set of constitutional rules that accompanied the transition from personal and authoritarian rule to pluralistic modes of governance.
swa: Mwishoni mwa karne ya 20 , nchi nyingi za Afrika ziliweka ukomo wa mihula ya urais kama sehemu ya sheria pana za kikatiba zilizoenda sambamba na mabadiliko kutoka kwenye utawala binafsi na wa kiimla kwenda kwenye mfumo wa utawala unaoheshimu matakwa ya walio wengi.

eng: While term limits were widely embraced by the larger African public, these rules have in recent years come under increasing attack from incumbent presidents seeking to extend their tenures.
swa: Wakati takwa la ukomo wa mihula ya urais lilipokelewa vizuri na wananchi wengi wa Afrika, bado sheria hizi katika miaka ya hivi karibuni zimekuwa zikishambuliwa na marais walioko madarakani wanaotafuta kuendelea kutawala .

eng: In the first six months of 2015 alone, the presidents of Burundi, Benin, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and Rwanda have either personally or through their supporters expressed the intention to dispense with or circumvent term limits in order to seek additional terms of office.
swa: Katika miezi sita ya kwanza ya 2015 pekee, marais wa Burundi, Benin, Congo (DRC), na Rwanda wamejaribu ama wao wenyewe au kwa kuwatumia wafuasi wao, kuonesha nia ya kuondoa ukomo wa mihula ya utawala ili kuwawezesha kupata muhula mwingine madarakani.

eng: These quests are often couched in language that portrays a leader’s desire for more time in office as a response to popular demands.
swa: Majaribio haya mara nyingi hufanyika kwa lugha inaonesha kuwa nia ya watawala hawa kuendelea kubaki madarakani ni kuitikia mwito wa wananchi.

eng: A striking example was Blaise Compaoré’s 2014 attempt to seek a third term in Burkina Faso, which was stopped by popular protests that forced the president not just to back off, but to leave the country.
swa: Mfano wa karibu ni ule wa jaribio la mwaka 2014 la Blaise Compaoré kutafuta muhula wa tatu nchini Burkina Faso, ambalo lilisitishwa na maandamano makubwa nchini humo kumlazimisha rais si tu kuachana na wazo hilo, lakini kuihama nchi.

eng: But other leaders have been more successful in their efforts to avoid relinquishing power.
swa: Lakini wapo watawala wengine ambao jitihada zao za kukwepa kuondoka madarakani zilifanikiwa.

eng: David Shinn, the former US ambassador to Burkina Faso and Ethiopia, says the track record on term limits in African politics is "mixed":
swa: David Shinn, balozi wa zamani wa Marekani nchini Burkina Faso na Ethiopia, anasema rekodi ya ukomo wa mihula ya urais katika siasa za Afrika ina mkanganyiko:

eng: Early in 2008, thirty-three of sub-Saharan Africa’s forty-eight countries had constitutions that contained term limit provisions.
swa: Mapema mwaka 2008, nchi thelathini na tatu kati ya arobaini na nane zilizo kusini mwa jangwa la Sahara zilikuwa na katiba zenye ukomo wa vipindi vya urais.

eng: Some African leaders have willingly turned over power in compliance with these constitutional requirements.
swa: Baadhi ya watawala wa Afrika kwa hiari yao wamekubaliana na matakwa haya ya katiba.

eng: They include recent, former leaders of Botswana, Benin, Cape Verde, Mali, Mozambique, Säo Tomé e Principe and Tanzania.
swa: Hawa ni pamoja na watawala wa zamani wa Botswana, Benin, Cape Verde, Mali, Mozambique, Säo Tomé e Principe na Tanzania.

eng: Nelson Mandela in South Africa stepped down after one term.
swa: Nelson Mandela wa Afrika Kusini aling'atuka baada ya muhula mmoja tu wa urais.

eng: Jerry Rawlings of Ghana and Daniel arap Moi of Kenya complied with constitutional term limits under duress.
swa: Jerry Rawlings wa Ghana na Daniel arap Moi wa Kenya walikubaliana na matakwa ya katiba zao zilizoweka ukomo wa urais.

eng: Several African leaders tried but failed to change the term limit provision of their constitution so that they could run again.
swa: Watawala wengine wa Afrika walijaribu kubadili masharti yaliyoweka ukomo wa madaraka kwenye katiba ili waendelee kutawala na wakashindwa.

eng: Zambia’s Frederick Chiluba, Malawi’s Bakili Muluzi and Nigeria’s Olusegun Obasanjo ultimately bowed to the will of the political system and accepted term limits.
swa: Kuna Frederick Chiluba wa Zambia, Bakili Muluzi wa Malawi na Olusegun Obasanjo wa Naijeria ambao hatimaye ilibidi kukubaliana na matakwa ya mfumo wa kisiasa yanayodai kuwepo kwa ukomo wa madaraka.

eng: Other African incumbents managed to change the constitution so that they could have at least one additional term.
swa: Hata hivyo, wapo watawala wa Afrika waliofanikiwa kubadili katiba zao ili kupata angalau muhula mwingine wa kugombea.

eng: Current or recent leaders in Burkina Faso, Chad, Gabon, Guinea, Namibia, Togo, Uganda and Algeria are among those who successfully changed term limit requirements in order to prolong their time in office.
swa: Watawala wa sasa au wa hivi karibuni nchini Burkina Faso, Chad, Gabon, Guinea, Namibia, Togo, Uganda na Aljeria ni miongoni mwa wale walifanikiwa kuondoa ukomo wa madaraka ili kuwawezesha kuendelea kuwa madarakani.

eng: In 2008, Cameroon’s parliament eliminated the two-term (seven years per term) limit for Paul Biya.
swa: Mwaka 2008, bunge la Cameroon liliondoa ukomo wa madaraka (ambao ni miaka saba kwa muhula) kwa ajili ya Paul Biya.

eng: I served at the U.S. embassy in Yaounde when Biya first became president in 1982.
swa: Nilifanya kazi kwneye ubalozi wa Marekani jijini Yaounde wakati ambao Biya aliingia madarakani mwaka 1982.

eng: He will be able to run again in 2011 after twenty-eight years as president.
swa: Ataweza kugombea tena mwaka 2011 baada ya kutawala kwa miaka ishirini na nane akiwa rais.

eng: The president of Niger is currently trying to change the constitution so that he can run for a third term.
swa: Rais wa Naija hivi sasa anaendelea na jitihada zake za kubadili katiba ili aweze kugombea tena kwa muhula wa tatu.

eng: In total, 18 African countries do not have presidential term limits.
swa: Kwa ujumla, nchi 18 za Afrika hazina masharti ya ukomo wa urais.

eng: Sudan presents a unique case; although President Bashir has been in power since 1989, his reelection earlier this year—when he carried 94 percent of the vote—is technically only his second term in office, following the secession of South Sudan in 2011 after a national referendum.
swa: Sudani ni mfano tofauti kidogo; ingawa Rais Bashir amekuwa madarakani tangu mwaka 1989, kuchaguliwa kwake tena mapema mwaka huu -huku akipata asilimia 94 ya kura - ndio muhula wake wa pili pekee unaoweza kusema amekuwa madarakani, kufuatia kujitenga kwa Sudani Kusini mwaka 2011 baada ya kura ya maoni.

eng: During the Economic Community Of West African States (ECOWAS) meeting last month in Accra, Ghana, West African leaders dropped the idea of instituting a two-term limit on the presidency across the region, after The Gambia and Togo, the only member states without term limits, opposed the move.
swa: Wakati wa mkutano wa Jumuiya ya Kiuchumi ya Nchi za Afrika Magharibi (ECOWAS) mwezi uliopita jijini Accra, Ghana, watawala wa Afrika Magharibi walikubaliana kuachana na wazo kuheshimu ukomo wa mihula miwili tu ya urais katika eneo hilo, baada ya Gambia na Togo, nchi wanachama pekee zisizo na ukomo wa madaraka, kupinga hatua hiyo.

eng: Internet users in West Africa were widely critical of the decision.
swa: Watuamiaji wa intaneti katika eneo la Afrika Magharibi walipinga vikali uamuzi huo.

eng: A conflict in Burundi continues today, sparked by President Pierre Nkurunziza's bid for a third term.
swa: Mgogoro wa Burundi unaendelea leo, umechochewa na Rais Pierre Nkurunziza wa nchi hiyo kutaka kugombea tena kwa muhula wa tatu.

eng: Riots have spread throughout the country in protest.
swa: Ghasia zimeenea nchini kote kwa maandamano.

eng: The UN Secretary General Ban Kimoon has even called on Ugandan President Museveni to intervene.
swa: Katibu Mkuu wa Umoja wa Mataifa Ban Kimoon amemwomba Rais wa Uganda Museveni kuingilia kati suala hilo.

eng: At an impromptu East African Community (EAC) meeting, former army general Godefroid Niyombare (who'd been suspended just a few months earlier) staged a coup in an attempt to oust Nkurunziza.
swa: Kwenye mkutano wa dharura wa Jumuiya ya Afrika Mashariki, Jenerali wa zamani wa jeshi Godefroid Niyombare (ambaye alikuwa amesimamishwa miezi kadhaa iliyopita) aliongoza jaribio la mapinduzi kutaka kumng'oa Nkurunziza.

eng: The events in Burundi and in other countries such as the Democratic Republic of Congo, Burkina Faso, and Rwanda have sustained a growing debate among Africans about term limits.
swa: Matukio nchini Burundi na nchi nyingine kama Kongo (DRC), Burkina Faso, na Rwanda zimeendeleza mijadala inayoendelea miongoni mwa wa-Afrika kuhusu ukomo wa madaraka.

swa: Kwa hiyo kama Wanyarwanda wanaomba awaongeze kwa zaidi ya mihula miwili, hiyo sio demokrasia?

eng: Kenyan blogger Ken Opalo noted that the record suggests presidents trying to extend their limits are more likely to succeed:
swa: Mwanablogu wa Kenya Ken Opalo alibainisha kwamba taarifa zinaoonesa kwamba marais wanaojaribu kuongeza kipindi cha urais wana nafasi kubwa ya kufanikiwa:

eng: So what we see in the existing data is that conditional on *overtly* trying to scrap term limits African Heads of State are more likely to succeed than not (9 successes, 6 failures).
swa: Kile tunachokiona kwenye takwimu nikwamba wale wanaojaribu kuondoa ukomo kwa Wakuu wa Nchi za Afrika wana uwezekano mkubwa wa kufanikiwa kuliko kinyume chake (tisa wamefanikiwa, sita wameshindwa).

eng: However, this observation doesn’t tell us anything about the presidents who did not formally consider term limit extensions.
swa: Hata hivyo, hali hii haituambii chochote kuhusu marais ambao hawakuonesha rasmi kutaka kujiongezea muhula madarakani.

eng: For instance, in Kenya (Moi) and Ghana (Rawlings), presidents did not initiate formal debate on the subject but were widely rumored to have tried to do so.
swa: Kwa mfano, nchini Kenya (Moi) na Ghana (Rawlings) marais hawakuanzisha mjadala rasmi wa kujiongezea muhula wa urais lakini kulikuwa na tetesi nyingi kwamba walijaribu.

eng: So it’s probably the case that presidents who are more likely to succeed self-select into formally initiating public debate on the subject of term limit extension, thereby tilting the balance.
swa: Kwa hiyo huenda ni kweli kwamba marais wanaweza kufanikiwa kwa kuamua kuanzisa mjadala wa wazi wa suala la kujiongezea muhula wa kutawala, na hivyo kuweka uwiano.

eng: And if you factor in the countries that have had more than one episode of term-limited presidents stepping down, suddenly the odds look pretty good for the consolidation of the norm of term limits in Sub Saharan Africa.
swa: Na kama ukiingiza na nchi ambazo zimewahi kuwa na zaidi ya tukio moja la marais waliolazimishwa na katiba kuachia madaraka na wakafanya hivyo, hali inaonekana kuwa nzuri kwa kuwa na ukomo wa madaraka katika eneo la Kusini mwa Jangwa la Sahara.

eng: He concluded on an optimistic note:
swa: Anahitimisha kwa hoja yenye matumaini:

eng: I wouldn’t rule out, in the next decade or so, the adoption of an African Union resolution (akin to the one against coups) that sanctions Heads of State who violate constitutional term limits.
swa: Siwezi kujua kwa hakika, lakini kuna uwezekano kuwa kwenye kipindi cha muongo ujao, Umoja wa afrika utakuwa na azimio (kama lile linalopinga mapinduzi) linalowawekea vikwazo Wakuu wa Nchi wasioheshimu ukomo wa kuwa madarakani.
