eng: A new film follows one Syrian family through five years of upheaval.
swa: Filamu mpya yaonesha mwenendo wa familia moja ya Syria kwa kipindi cha miaka mitano ya vurugu za kisiasa.

eng: Credit: Filmmaker Sean McAllister.
swa: Picha kwa hisani ya: Mtayarisha Filamu Sean McAllister.

eng: This article and radio report by Leo Hornak for The World originally appeared on PRI.org on September 24, 2015, and is republished here as part of a content-sharing agreement.
swa: Makala hii pamoja na ripoti ya rediao iliyoandaliwa na Leo Hornak wa The World, kwa mara ya kwanza iliwekwa PRI.org mnamo tarehe 24 Septemba, 2015, na inachapishwa tena hapa kwa makubaliano ya kushirikiana kwenye maudhui.

eng: The scale of the Syrian tragedy is difficult to comprehend: more than 200,000 dead, 6 million internally displaced, 3 million more living as refugees.
swa: Kiwango cha janga la vita vya Syria ni vigumu kulielezea: zaidi ya watu 200,000 wamepoteza maisha, milioni 6 wakiwa wakimbizi wa ndani, na milioni 3 na zaidi wakiishi kama wakimbizi.

eng: Now an award-winning new film is seeking to bring home the personal consequences of the war for ordinary people.
swa: Kwa sasa, filamu mpya iliyojipatia tuzo inatazamia kuelezea madhara ya mtu mmoja mmoja ya raia wa kawaida yatokanayo na vita vya nchini Syria.

eng: Since 2009, before the start of the current conflict, the British film-maker Sean McAllister has been filming the daily lives of one family based in Damascus.
swa: Tangu mwaka 2009, kabla ya kuanza kwa mgogoro wa hivi sasa, mtayarishaji wa filamu wa kiingereza, Sean McAllister alikuwa akichukua filamu ya maisha ya kila siku ya familia moja iliyo na maskani yake huko Damascus.

eng: Amer Daoud and his wife Raghda Hassan first met and fell in love as political prisoners in the cells of a Syrian prison 15 years ago.
swa: Amer Daoud pamoja na mke wake Raghda Hassan kwa mara ya kwanza walikutana na kuwa wapenzi wakiwa kama wafungwa wa kiasiasa kwenye seli za magereza ya Syria takribani miaka 15 iliyopita.

eng: After their release they married and had a family. McAllister’s camera has been with them and their children through every step of Syria’s revolution, its civil war and the family’s final exile in Europe. The resulting documentary is called "A Syrian Love Story."
swa: Kamera ya McAllister imekuwa ikiwafuatilia wao pamoja na familia yao kwa kila hatua ya mapinduzi ya Syria, vita vya wenyewe kwa wenyewe, pamoja na maisha ya uhamishoni ya familia hii huko ulaya. simulizi hii imepewa jina la "Simulizi ya Kimapenzi ya Syria."

eng: McAllister says that he had already begun filming the family when the revolution began.
swa: McAllister anasema kuwa alianza kuchukua filamu ya familia hii tangu mapinduzi yalipoanza.

eng: “I got a call saying ‘Do you know what?
swa: “Nilipigiwa simu na kuambiwa, ‘Unajua nini?

eng: It’s starting in Syria!’ — and the first people on the streets were Amer and his son Kaka, and they had both been arrested.”
swa: Hali imechafuka tena nchini Syria!’ — na watu wakwanza kabisa kuingia mitaani walikuwa ni Amer pamoja na mtoto wake wa kiume, Kaka, na wote walikamatwa na kutiwa kizuizini.”

eng: Eventually the family is freed, but Sean himself is arrested and held in a Syrian jail for a week.
swa: Hatimaye familia ipo huru, lakini Sean yeye alikamatwa na na kushikiliwa kwenye gereza moja nchini Syria kwa muda wa wiki moja.

eng: As a result, the authorities discover who he has been filming, and Amer, Raghda and the children are forced into exile for their own safety.
swa: Kilichofuatia, serikali ilitambua mtu aliyekuwa akichukua filamu, na pia Amer, Raghda na walilazimika kwenda kuishi uhamishoni kwa ajili ya usalama wao.

eng: As the family tries to adapt to new countries and new environments, the strain begins to wear on the Amer and Raghda’s marriage.
swa: Kadiri familia inavyozidi kuzoea nchi za kigeni pamoja na mazingira mapya, hali ya kukosa amani inajitokeza katika familia ya Amer na Raghda.

eng: In spite of the suffering it shows, McAllister still sees his film as ultimately optimistic: “I think the message of hope is in the defiance — the defiance of one family, who have all pulled through.”
swa: Pamoja na madhila yaonekanayo katika filamu hii, McAllister bado anaitazama filamu hii kama yenye kuleta matumainin makubwa: “Nafikiri ujumbe wa matumaini upo kwenye ujasiri usio na kificho— ujasiri ulio dhahiri wa familia moja, ambao kila mwanafamilia ameupitia.”

eng: He believes that films that humanize migrants and refugees are more important than ever.
swa: Anaamini kuwa filamu zinazotambua utu wa wahamiaji na wakimbizi ndizo zilizo za muhimu kabisa.

eng: “We see on the television people washed up on the seashore.
swa: “Tunaona kwenye televisheni watu wakiwa wamesombwa na maji na kuletwa pembezoni mwa ukingo wa bahari.

eng: Amer and Raghda give a voice to all these people you see on the news.”
swa: Amer na Raghda wanawatetea watu wote hawa ambao kila siku tunawaona kwenye habari.”

eng: Tanzania has had four presidents since gaining independence from Britain in 1961.

eng: The first, Julius Kambarage Nyerere, mostly referred to by his honoric title Mwalimu Nyerere, is the most respected and loved statesman in Tanzanian history.
swa: Rais wa kwanza, Julius Kambarage Nyerere, anayefahamika zaidi kwa jina la heshima Mwalimu Nyerere, amekuwa mzalendo anayeheshimika na kupendwa zaidi katika historia ya Tanzania.

eng: He was a strong supporter of the liberation movement on the continent and anti imperialist-movement around the world.
swa: Nyerere alikuwa mstari wa mbele katika harakati za ukombozi barani humo na aliunga mkono harakati za kupambana na ubeberu duniani kote.

eng: It is no wonder that political organisations such as FRELIMO of Mozambique, the ANC and PAC of South Africa, ZANU and ZAPU of Zimbabwe, the MPLA of Angola and SWAPO of Namibia all had offices and training camps in Tanzania.

eng: In addition, the country gave safe haven to US civil-rights activists, Black Panther party members such as Pete O'Neal and Geronimo, and Vietnam War resisters.
swa: Kwa nyongeza, nchi hiyo ilikuwa kimbilio la wanaharakati wa kimarekani wa haki za kiraia, wanachama wa chama cha Black Panther kama vile Pete O'Neal na Geronimo, pamoja na wapinzani wa vita vya Vietnam.

eng: Oplan Bayanihan pushes Lumads to evacuate their lands, but also paves the way for corporations to take hold of the land, and use the Armed Forces of the Philippines as their own security force as they plunder and suck the Earth of its natural elements. Image and caption by Anakbayan USA.Reacting to reports that paramilitary activities and mining operations are displacing Lumad tribes, many Filipinos have called for urgent government action to stop the violence against the indigenous peoples.
swa: Oplan Bayanihan yapelekea jamii ya Lumad kuziacha ardhi zao, lakini pia wanaweka mazingira ya makampuni kumiliki ardhi na pia wanatumia majeshi ya Ufilipino kama ulinzi wao huku wakipora na kujizolea maliasili ya madini.Picha kwa hisani ya Anakbayan USA.Akizungumizia habari kuwa shughuli zifananazo za kijeshi pamoja na zile za uchimbaji madini zinachochea kuondosha makabila ya Lumad kwenye maeneo yao, raia wengi wa Ufilipino wameita sserikali kuchukua hatua mapema iwezekanavyo ili kukomesha ukatili dhidi ya wazawa.

eng: Lumad is a collective term referring to the indigenous tribes in Mindanao, the Philippines’ second biggest island located in the southern part of the country.
swa: Lumad ni neno linalotumika kutambulisha makabila ya wazawa wa Mindanao, kisiwa cha pili kwa ukubwa nchini Ufilipino kilichopo upande wa kusini wa nchi hii.

eng: Lumad leaders from Surigao province reported that paramilitary groups have attacked their schools and communities, forcing more than 2,000 people to leave their homes in the mountains and seek shelter in the city center.
swa: Viongozi wa Lumad kutoka kwenye jimbo la Surigao walitaarifu kuwa vikundi vya wanamgambo vilivamia shule zao pamoja na wanajamii, hali iliyolazimu zaidi ya watu 2,000 kuyakimbia makazi yao maeneo ya milimani na kutafuta hifadhi katika maeneo ya jiji.

eng: Many came from Lumad communities which have actively resisted the entry of mining companies.
swa: Wengi wao walikuwa watu wa jamii ya Lumad ambao walipinga vikali uvamizi wa makampuni ya uchimbaji madini.

eng: The National Commission for Culture and the Arts (NCCA), a government agency, described the violence against the Lumad as an attack on Philippine culture:

eng: The NCCA recognizes these indigenous peoples and their leaders as the core and the backbone of the country’s intangible cultural heritage.
swa: Tume ya Taifa ya Utamaduni na Sanaa (NCCA) inawatambua raia hawa wazawapamoja na viongozi wao kama kiini na tegemeo la urithi wa kiutamaduni wa nchi ya Ufilipino.

eng: They are the bearers of our unique artistic traditions.
swa: Uvamizi huu ni kikwazo dhidi ya utamaduni wetu wa kipekee wa kisanaa.

eng: Their murder is the murder of our peoples’ soul.
swa: Ukatili wao ni ukatili dhidi ya utu wa watu wetu.

eng: As the living transmitters of time-tested knowledge systems, skills and practices, to wound them is to damage the cultural basis for the sustainable development of our nation.
swa: Kama watoa elimu wa kipindi kirefu, maarifa na utendaji, kuwajeruhi ni kuharibu msingi wa utamaduni ambao ndio tegemeo la maendeleo endelevu ya nchi yetu.

eng: ‪The United Nations Special Rapporteurs on the rights of indigenous peoples, Victoria Tauli-Corpuz, and on the situation of human rights defenders, Michel Forst urged the military to end its occupation of some tribal schools:‬
swa: ‪Muwakilishi maalum wa umoja wa Maifa wa kuratibu haki za raia wazawa, Victoria Tauli-Corpuz, na mtetezi wa haki za binadamu, Michel Forst walilitaka jeshi kuacha kuzishikilia baadhi ya shule za kiutamaduni:‬

eng: Military occupation of civilian institutions and killing of civilians, particularly in places such as schools which should remain safe havens for children from this type of violence, are unacceptable, deplorable and contrary to international human rights and international humanitarian standards
swa: Hali ya majeshi kushikilia taasisi za kiraia pamoja na kuwaua raia, hususani maeneo kama shule ambazo zilipaswa kuwa sehemu salama kwa ajili ya watoto wa maeneo haya yaliyo na machafuko, ni mambo yasiyokubalika, wala kuvumilika na ni kinyume kabisa na haki za kimataifa za binadamu na pia ni kinyume na viwango vya kimataifa vya utoaji huduma za kijamii

eng: For its part, the military has denied that it organized paramilitary groups to harass the Lumad communities.
swa: Hata hivyo, jeshi limekanusha kuwa liliratibu makundi mithili ya jeshi kwa ajili ya kuzidhalilisha jamii za watu wa Lumad.

eng: It insisted that tribal war was the cause of violence in the Lumad areas.
swa: Jeshi lilisisitiza kuwa, vita vya kimakabila ndivyo vilivyokuwa chanzo cha machafuko katika maeneo ya Lumad.

eng: But the governor of the province disputed this and accused the military of creating and arming the paramilitary groups.
swa: Lakini, Gavana wa jimbo alitupilia mbali madai haya na kulitupia jeshi lawama kwa kuasisi na kutoa silaha kwa makundi haya mithili ya jeshi.

eng: The Philippines senate has committed to investigating the issue.
swa: Seneta wa Ufilipino ameahidi kulifanyia uchunguzi suala hili.

eng: The FreeBassel poster from @freebassel on Twitter.
swa: Bango la FreeBassel kutoka kwenye anuani ya mtandao wa Twita @freebassel.

eng: Bassel Safadi has been imprisoned in Syria for almost four years and friends and activists fear for his life after he was transferred from his prison today to an unknown location
swa: Mfungwa huyo amewekwa ndani nchini Syria kwa miaka minne na marafiki na wanaharakati wana wasiwasi na maisha yake baada ya kuhamishwa leo kutoka kwenye gereza alilokuwemo kwenda mahali kusikojulikana

eng: Activists are calling upon the Syrian government to immediately release imprisoned Syrian-Palestinian software engineer Bassel Khartabil, also known as Bassel Safadi, after he was moved from his prison to an unknown location earlier today.
swa: Wanaharakati wanaitaka serikali ya Syria kumwachilia huru mara moja mfungwa ambaye ni mhandisi wa programu za kompyuta mwenye asili ya Syria na Palestina Bassel Khartabil, anayefahamika pia kama Bassel Safadi, baada ya kuhamishiwa kutoka kwenye gereza lake kwenda mahali pasipojulika mapema leo.

eng: Safadi, who has been in prison for almost four years, is also a well-known open-source software developer.
swa: Safadi, ambaye amekuwa gerezani kwa zaidi ya miaka minne, anafahamika sana kama mtengenezaji wa zana huria za mtandaoni.

eng: He is a Creative Commons leader in Syria and active in projects like Mozilla Firefox and Wikipedia, and is credited with opening up the Syrian Internet and extending online access and knowledge to the public.
swa: Ni kiongozi wa taasisi ya Creative Commons nchini Syria na anafanya kazi bila kuchoka kwenye miradi kama Mozilla Firefox na Wikipedia, na amejizolea sifa kwa kufungua mtandao wa intaneti nchini Syria na kupanua upatikanaji na uelewa wa mtandao kwa wananchi.

eng: According to the European Parliament, his detention is part of Syrian government efforts to restrict access to online communities and stifle freedom of expression in the country.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Bunge la Ulaya, kukamatwa kwake ni sehemu ya jitihada za serikali ya Syria kujaribu kuzuia upatikanaji wa mtandao kwa jamii ya mtandaoni na hata kuminya uhuru wa kujieleza nchini humo.

eng: According to a Facebook page set up by supporters calling for his release:
swa: Kwa mujibu wa ukurasa wa Facebook ulioanzishwa na watetezi wake wakidai kuachiliwa kwake:

eng: Bassel was transferred from Adra prison to an unknown location after a patrol, whose affiliation is not known, came to him and asked him to gather his things.
swa: Bassel alihamishwa kutoka gereza la Adra kwenda kusikojulikana baada ya walinzi wasiojulikana wanahusiana na nani, walipokuja na kumtaka akusanye vitu vyake.

eng: It is expected that he has been transferred to the civil court headquarters at the Military Police in Al Qaboun area.
swa: Inatarajiwa kwamba atakuwa amehamishiwa kwenye makao makuu ya mahakama ya kiraia kwenye eneo la Jeshi la Polisi huko Al Qaboun.

eng: We are worried and fear for Bassel after his whereabouts are unknown again
swa: Tuna wasiwasi na maisha yake baada ya kutokujulikana amepelekwa wapi baada ya hapo.

eng: Khartabil was arrested on March 15, 2012, on the first anniversary of the start of the Syrian revolution.
swa: Khartabil alikamatwa mnamo Machi 15, 2012, siku ya kukumbuka mwaka mmoja tangu kuanza kwa mapinduzi ya Syria.

eng: He was interrogated and tortured for five days by Military Branch 215.
swa: Alihojiwa na kuteswa kwa siku tano na kikosi cha usalama cha Military Branch 215.

eng: He was then transferred to the Interrogation Division Branch 248 and detained incommunicado for nine months.
swa: Alihamishwa kwenye kwenye kitengo cha mahojiano namba 248 na hakuruhusiwa kuonana na watu kwa miezi tisa.

eng: On December 9, 2012, Khartabil was brought before a military prosecutor without an attorney present, and charged with "spying for an enemy State".
swa: Mnamo Desemba 9, 2012, Khartabil alipelekwa mbele ya mwendesha mashtaka wa jeshi bila kuwa na mwanasheria, na alishitakiwa kwa "kufanya upelelezi kwa ajili ya nchi adui".

eng: He was then sent to the Adra Prison in Damascus, where he has been held, until today.
swa: Alipelekwa kwenye gereza la Adra jijini Damascus, ambako amekuwa anashikiliwa, mpaka leo.

eng: The Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) notes that:
swa: Taasisi ya Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) inasema:

eng: It was Bassel's visibility as a technologist and activist that made him a target for detention.
swa: Bassel alijikuta akikamatwa kwa sababu ya kuonekana kwake kama mtaalam wa teknolojia na mwanaharakati.

eng: An online petition, initiated by friend and campaigner Mohamed Najem, is available at Change.org calling for Khartabil's immediate release.
swa: Tamko la mtandaoni, lililoanzishwa na rafiki yake na mwanaharakati Mohamed Najem, linapatikana kwenye tovuti ya Change.org kudai Khartabil aachiliwe huru.

eng: Please click the link to sign it.
swa: Tafadhali bofya kiungo hiki ili kutia saini.

eng: Friend and freedom of speech campaigner Jillian C. York, who is also EFF Director for International Freedom of Expression, lends her support to the drive.
swa: Rafiki na mwanaharakti wa uhuru wa mtandaoni Jillian C. York, ambye pia ni Mkurugenzi wa EFF kwa ajili ya kutetea uhuru wa kujieleza kimataifa, anamwunga mkono.

eng: She tweets:
swa: Alitwiti:

eng: My friend Bassel Safadi has been transferred from Adra prison in Syria, we don't know where-Please sign our petition https://t.co/sER4lWTXjB — jillian c. york (@jilliancyork) October 3, 2015
swa: Rafiki yangu Bassel Safadi amehamishwa kutoka gereza la Adra nchini Syria, na hatujui aliko. Tafadhali tia saini tamko hili

eng: We know petitions won't convince Syria (or anyone) but it's all we've got.
swa: Tunajua matamko hayataishawishi serikali ya Syria (au yeyote) lakini ndicho tunachoweza kukifanya.

eng: Please help get the word out so Bassel stays safe. — jillian c. york (@jilliancyork) October 3, 2015
swa: Tafadhali tusaidie kueneza ujumbe huu ili Bassel awe salama.

eng: The Global Voices community demands justice for seven free expression advocates who are facing trial in Morocco due to their advocacy.
swa: Jumuia ya Global Voices yataka haki kutendeka kwa watetezi saba wa uhuru wa kujieleza walioshitakiwa kutokana na wajibu wao wa utetezi.

eng: The seven advocates have sought to defend human rights, hold authorities accountable to the public, and uphold rule of law in their country.
swa: Watetezi hawa saba wamekuwa wakitetea haki za binadamu, kuweka bayana maovu ya maafisa wa serikali pamoja na kudai utawala wa sheria nchini mwao.

eng: Five have been charged with "threatening the internal security of the State" and two face charges of "receiving foreign funding without notifying the General Secretariat of the government."
swa: Watano kati yao wameshitakiwa kwa kosa la "kuhatarisha usalama wa ndani wa Taifa" na wawili wengine wameshitakiwa kwa kosa la "kupokea ufadhili wa fedha bila ya kushirikisha sekretarieti ya serikali".

eng: We call on the Moroccan government to stand by its commitments to international human rights agreements and drop all charges against these seven individuals.
swa: Tunaitaka serikali ya Morocco kusimamia makubaliano ya haki za binadamu za kimataifa na hivyo kufuta mashitaka iliyofungua dhidi ya watu hawa saba.

eng: Hisham Almiraat at the Global Voices Summit in Nairobi, 2012.
swa: Hisham Almiraat akiwa kwenye mkutano wa Global Voices jijini Nairobi mwaka 2012.

eng: Among those charged is Hisham Almiraat, a medical doctor and long-time member of our community.
swa: Miongoni mwa walioshitakiwa ni Hisham Almiraat, ambaye ni mtabibu na kwa muda mrefu amekuwa mmoja wa wachangiaji wa jumuia yetu.

eng: We cannot remain silent in the face of this threat to our friend.
swa: Hatuwezi kuwa kimya katika mazingira hatari anayokabiliana nayo ndugu yetu.

eng: Hisham has had a leading voice in Morocco’s blogosphere for nearly a decade.
swa: Hisham amekuwa mstari wa mbele kabisa katika ulimwengu wa kublogu nchini Morocco kwa takribani miaka kumi.

eng: He co-founded citizen media projects Talk Morocco and Mamfakinch, and served as Global Voices’ advocacy director.
swa: Alikuwa mwanzilishi wa miradi kadhaa ya Uanahabari wa kiraia ikiwemo Talk Morocco na Mamfakinch, na pia alifanya kazi kama mkurugenzi wa kitengo cha utetezi cha Global Voices.

eng: Balancing profession and passion, Hisham has spent many years working to improve the lives and well-being of Moroccans, both as a civil society advocate and as a medical doctor.
swa: Akimudu vizuri kati ya kazi zake za kitaaluma na kufanya kazi za kujitolea, Hisham ametumia miaka yake mingi kujibidisha kuboresha maisha na uhai wa jamii ya watu wa Morocco akiwa kama mtetezi wa jumuia za kiraia na pia kama mtabibu.

eng: Like other media and human rights groups around the world, we fear that this case represents an attempt by the Moroccan government to silence those who are critical of its policies and practices.
swa: Kama ilivyo kwa vyombo vingine vya habari na makundi ya haki za binadamu ulimwenguni, tuna hofu kuwa mashitaka haya ni jaribio la serikali ya Morocco la kuwanyamazisha wote wanaojaribu kuhoji kuhusu sera na utendaji wa serikali.

eng: We see this not only as a threat to our friend and colleague, but also to our broader mission.
swa: Hatulitazami hili kama ni hatari tu kwa rafiki na mwenzetu, bali pia ni hatari kwa malengo yetu mapana.

eng: As a community of bloggers and activists from over 160 countries, we invoke the universal human right to free expression each day, as we tell stories from underrepresented communities around the world.
swa: Kama jumuia ya wanablogu na wanaharakati kutoka nchi zaidi ya 160, kila uchao tunatetea na kusihi haki ya msingi ya binadamu ya uhuru wa kujieleza, kwani tumekuwa tukiandika na kusambaza habari kutoka kwenye jamii ya watu wasioweza kusikika na wala kusikilizwa kwa urahisi kutoka ulimwenguni kote.

eng: We call on allies to support our message, and on foreign governments to hold the Moroccan government to account on its actions and principles. #Justice4Morocco
swa: Tunawaomba washirika wetu wote kuunga mkono ujumbe wetu, pamoja na serikali kutoka nchi mbalimbali kuishinikiza serikali ya Morocco kuwajibika kwa matendo na mwenendo wake. #Justice4Morocco

eng: SUPPORT OUR CALL
swa: UUNGE MKONO WITO WETU

eng: Sign this open statement from our community
swa: Thibitisha tamko la wazi kutoka kwenye jumuia yetu

eng: Support the campaign on social media using the hashtag #Justice4Morocco
swa: Unga mkono kampeni hii kupitia mitandao ya kijamii kwa kutumia kiungo habari #Justice4Morocco

eng: Read and share stories about the case:
swa: Soma na sambaza habari kuhusu kesi hii:

eng: Global Voices’ Hisham Almiraat Faces Trial in Morocco, Global Voices International appeal to the Moroccan authorities to drop charges against human rights defenders, Free Press Unlimited Morocco’s Smiling Face and Heavy Hand, Human Rights Watch Amid wave of defamation cases, CPJ joins call for Morocco to drop charges against press, Committee to Protect Journalists
swa: Hisham Almiraat wa Global Voices Ashitakiwa nchini Morocco, Global Voices Jamii ya Kimataifa Yaitaka Serikali ya Morocco Kufuta Mashitaka dhidi ya Watetezi wa Haki za Binadamu, Free Press Unlimited Uso wa Morocco Wenye Furaha na Mkono Mzito, Human Rights Watch Katikati ya Kesi za Kukashifiana, CPJ yaunga mkono kampeni ya kufuata mashtaka dhidi ya Vyombo vya habari, Kamati ya Kutetea Waandishi wa Habari

eng: Read and share Hisham’s past coverage for Global Voices
swa: soma na sambaza makala za Global Voices zilizoandikwa na Hisham.

eng: Some bodies are global, but most bodies remain local, regional, "ethnic."'
swa: Kwa nini maiti nyingine ni mali ya dunia nzima, wakati maiti nyingine ni za maeneo husika pekee?'

eng: In this episode of GV Face, the Global Voices Hangout series, Joey Ayoub, a Lebanese blogger and Global Voices contributor, Lova Rakotomalala, our Paris-based French language editor and Laura Vidal, our Paris-based Latin America community manager talk about race, the politics of death and the unequal reactions to tragedies around the world.
swa: Katika toleo hili la mazungumzo ya GV, mfululizo wa soga za Global Voices, Joey Ayoub, mwanablogu wa ki-Lebanoni na mwandishi wa Global Voices, Lova Rakotomalala, mhariri wa lugha ya Kifaransa anayeishi Paris na Laura Vidal, kiongozi wa jumuiya ya Amerika Kusini anayeishi Paris watazungumzia rangi, siasa za vifo na miitikio isiyo na usawa yanapotokea majanga duniani kote.

eng: Global Voices is a border-less, largely volunteer community of more than 1400 writers, analysts, online media experts and translators.
swa: Global Voices ni jamii isiyo na mipaka, kwa sehemu kubwa jumuiya ya watu wanaojitolea yenye waandishi, wachambuzi, wataalamu wa uandishi wa mtandaoni na wafasiri wapatao 1400.

eng: We set a news agenda that builds bridges, global understanding and friendship across borders.
swa: Tunaanzisha mijadala ya kihabari inayojenga madaraja, uelewa wa masuala ya kidunia na mahusiano ya kirafiki.

eng: We focus on telling stories from marginalized and misrepresented communities.
swa: Tunalenga kusimulia habari za jamii zinazopuuzwa na zinazopuuzwa.

eng: Our translators render these stories into more than 35 languages.
swa: Watafsiri wetu wanahakikisha kwamba habari hizo zinapatika katika lugha 35.

eng: Many of our community members speak multiple languages and call more than one city and country their home.
swa: Wengi wa wanachama wetu wanazungumza luga zaidi ya moja na wanaishi zaidi ya mji au nchi moja.

eng: After the Paris attacks on November 13, Joey wrote a post titled, "The Streets of Paris Are as Familiar to Me as the Streets of Beirut", which went viral:
swa: Baada ya mashambulio ya Paris mnamo Novemba 13, Joey ameandika makala yenye kichwa cha habari, "Mitaa ya Paris Inavyonikumbusha Mitaa ya Beirut ", ambayo imesomwa sana mtandaoni:

eng: I come from a privileged Francophone community in Lebanon.
swa: Ninatoka katika jamii iliyoendelea kidogo pale Lebanon.

eng: This has meant that I have always seen France as my second home.
swa: Kwa kuwa lugha yetu ni Kifaransa, nimejikuta nikiiona nchi ya Ufaransa kama nyumbani kwetu.

eng: The streets of Paris are as familiar to me as the streets of Beirut.
swa: Mitaa ya Ufaransa ninaifahamu sana kama ninavyoifahamu Beirut.

eng: I was just in Paris a few days ago.
swa: Nilikuwa Paris siku chache tu zilizopita.

eng: These have been two horrible nights of violence.
swa: Siku mbili hizi zimekuwa za kutisha sana.

eng: The first took the lives of over 40 in Beirut; the second took the lives of over 120 people and counting in Paris.
swa: Siku ya kwanza ilishuhudia vifo vya watu zaidi ya 40 mjini Beirut; usiku wa siku ya pili maisha ya zaidi ya watu 120 jijini Paris yalikatishwa.

eng: It also seems clear to me that to the world, my people’s deaths in Beirut do not matter as much as my other people’s deaths in Paris.
swa: Kwangu, inaonekana wazi kwamba kwa dunia yetu, vifo vya watu mjini Beirut havijagusa hisia za watu kama ilivyotokea kwa vifo vilivyotokea jijini Paris.

eng: We do not get a “safe” button on Facebook.
swa: Hatujapata kile kitufe cha ‘salama’ kwenye mtandao wa Facebook.

eng: We do not get late night statements from the most powerful men and women alive and millions of online users.
swa: Hatujapata salamu za pole zilizotolewa usiku wa manane kutoka kwa watu maarufu zaidi duniani pamoja na mamilioni ya watumiaji wa mtandao.

eng: We do not change policies which will affect the lives of countless innocent refugees.
swa: Hatukubadilisha sera zitakazoathiri maisha ya wakimbizi wasio na hatia ambao idadi yao haifahamiki.

eng: This could not be clearer.
swa: Hali hii haieleweki kabisa.

eng: I say this with no resentment whatsoever, just sadness.
swa: Ninayasema haya bila chuki wala hasira yoyote, isipokuwa huzuni.

eng: Laura Vidal was a block away at a bar when the first attack took place at a restaurant on November 13 in Paris.
swa: Laura Vidal alikuwa baa mtaa wa pili na eneo ambalo mashambulizi yalitokea.

eng: Laura moved to Paris seven years ago from Venezuela as a student.
swa: Laura alihamia Paris miaka saba iliyopita akitokea Venezueelza kama mwanafunzi.

eng: In, "After the Paris Attacks: For It to Be Unity, It Can't Be Partial", she reflects:
swa: Kwenye makala ya, "Baada ya Mashambuzi la Paris: Ili Uwe Mshikamano Kweli, Haupaswi Kuwa Nusunusu ", anaandika:

eng: Since I arrived in Paris I’ve followed the endless discussions on origins, skin colours, backgrounds and religious faiths.
swa: Tangu nimefika Paris, nimefutilia mijadala mingi sana kuhusiana na masuala ya asili ya mtu, rangi ya ngozi, historia ya mtu na imani za kidini.

eng: Part of my research work is based on—of all subjects—intercultural sensitivity.
swa: Sehemu ya utafiti wangu imejikita kwenye -mada ya ajabu kabisa- uelewa wa tamaduni za wengine.

eng: These conversations are emotional, and therefore uncomfortable. But they’re necessary.
swa: Mazungumzo haya yamejaa hisia, kwa hiyo wakati mwingine yanafanya watu wajisikie vibaya. hata hivyo, mijadala hiyo ni ya muhimu.

eng: And I say this because it seems that dividing the world between “us” and “them” isn’t useful.
swa: Na nayasema haya kwa sababu inavyoonekana kuigawa dunia kwa maneno kama "sisi" na "wao" hayatusaidii.

eng: And it never has been.
swa: Na haiwezi kuwa hivyo.

eng: In fact, the artificial creation of difference is what fuels all of this.
swa: Kwa hakika, tofauti hizi zinazotengenezwa ndizo zinazoharibu mambo.

eng: And this is how we learn to see “ourselves” and “others”, and this is the lens through which we have studied history and watch the news.
swa: Na hivyo ndivyo tunavyojifunza kujiona kama "sisi" na "wengine", na tunajifunza historia na kutazama taarifa za habari kwa jicho hili.

eng: “Us” and “them”.
swa: Sisi na "wao".

eng: “Here” and “far away”.
swa: Hapa na "mbali".

eng: I don’t think we can afford to keep this view of the world anymore—assuming we ever could—and maintain this denial of reality.
swa: Sidhani kama tunaweza kuendeleza mtazamo kama huu kwa muda mrefu -labda tuliweza kabla- na kuendea kuukana ukweli wa mambo.

eng: Lova's essay, "Creating a Media of Empathy One Letter at a Time", published after the Charlie Hebdo attacks, co-authored with Global Voices Nigeria contributor Nwachukwu Egbunike:
swa: Andiko la Lova, "Kujenga Uandishi wa Kujali Wengine Moja Baada ya Nyingine", iliyochapishwa baada ya shambuzi la Charlie Hebdo, aliyoiandika kwa kushirkiana na mwandishi wa Naijeria Nwachukwu Egbunike:

eng: The time to have a global discussion on terror attacks, free speech, empathy and Islamophobia is not when tragedy strikes but beforehand and when cooler heads prevail.
swa: Wakati wa kufanya mijadala ya maana kidunia kuhusu mashambulizi ya kigaidi, uhuru wa kujieleza, kujali wengine na Hofu ya Uislamu sio pale majanga yanapotokea lakini kabla, tena yapaswa kuwa wakati vichwa vyetu vimetulia.

eng: Yet, whether we like it or not, the public thirst to make sense of the world is highest when such sad events occur.
swa: Hata hivyo, tupende tusipende, kiu ya umma kujaribu kuulewa ulimwengu ni kubwa pale matukio mabaya yanapotokea.

eng: The timing might not be ideal, but we have the opportunity as media contributors to reframe the conversation for thousand of readers all over the world, while they are paying attention.
swa: Wakati muafaka unaweza usiwepo, lakini tunayo fursa, kama waandishi wa habari kutengeneza aina ya mijadala yenye tija kwa maelfu ya wasomaji wetu duniani kote, hasa pale wanapokuwa wanafuatilia kwa makini.

eng: Pictures of Afghan children at a school run by a local mosque for Afghan orphans & refugees in Shiraz, Iran.
swa: Picha ya watoto wa ki-Afraghani wakiwa katika shule ya watoto yatima wakimbizi inayoendeshwa na msikiti wa sehemu hiyo Shiraz, Iran.

eng: Photo by Simon Monk (CC BY-NC-ND 2.0).
swa: Picha na Simon Monk (CC BY-NC-ND 2.0).

eng: In an announcement from the United Nation mission in Iran, the Iranian government will include all of its registered refugees into its Salamat Insurance Scheme.
swa: Katika tangazo lililotolewa na mpango wa Umoja wa Mataifa nchini Iran, serikali ya Iran itawaingiza wakimbizi wote walioandikishwa kwenye Mpango wake wa Bima ya Salamat.

eng: This is a collaboration between the Ministry of Interior, responsible for immigrant affairs, the Iranian Health Insurance Organization and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).
swa: Mpango huu ni ushirikiano kati ya Wizara ya Mambo ya ndani, inayoshughulika na masuala ya wahamiaji, Shirika la Bima ya Afya la Irani na Shirika la Umoja wa Mataifa linaloshughulikia Wakimbizi (UNHCR).

eng: This plan is targeted at Iran's Afghan and Iraqi refugee population.
swa: Mpango huu unawalenga wakimbizi wote raia wa Afrghastani na Iraq wanaoishi Irani.

eng: Iran's English daily Tehran Times, part of the Mehr News Agency owned by the Islamic Ideology Dissemination Organisation, described the "gratitude" of Sivanka Dhanapala, the UNHCR Representative in Iran, for the program:
swa: Gazeti la kila siku la Kiingereza nchini Iran Tehran Times, ambalo ni sehemu Shirika la Habari la Mehr linalomilikiwa na Shirika la Kueneza Itikadi ya Kiislamu , lilieleza shukrani za Sivanka Dhanapala, ambaye ni mwakilishi wa UNHCR nchini humo, kwa mradi huo:

eng: UNHCR’s Representative in Iran acknowledged the Iranian Government’s contribution, expressed UNHCR’s gratitude towards the Government of the Islamic Republic of Iran for all the services it has rendered to the largest protracted urban refugee population in the world for over three decades, and inclusion of the refugees in this Universal Insurance Scheme which is exemplary not only regionally but also globally, and added that such a services haven’t been provided before and I sincerely hope other countries will follow this example.
swa: Mwailishi wa UNHCR nchini Iran akiushukuru mchango wa serikali ya Irani, alionesha shukrani za UNHCR kwa serikali ya Jamhuri ya Kiislam ya Irani kwa huduma zote ilizozitoa kwa wakimbizi wanaoishi mijini nchini humo, ambao ni idadi kubwa zaidi duniani, katika kipindi cha miongo mitatu, na kuwaingiza wakimbizi kwenye Mpango wa Bima ya Afya, ambao ni mfano mzuri duniani, na kuongeza kwambahuduma kama hizo hazijatolewa kabla na ninaamini kwa dhati kwamba nchi nyingine zitafuata mfano huu.

eng: Half of the coverage for the program will come from the Iranian government, while the UNHCR will contribute with US $8.3 million.
swa: Nusu ya gharama za mpango huo zitatoka kwa serikali ya Irani, wakati UNHCR itachangia dola za ki-Marekani milioni 8.3.

eng: The program will be available to all registered refugees, who will receive access to a health insurance package for "hospitalization and temporary hospitalization", as available to Iranian nationals.
swa: Mpango huu utawanufaisha wakimbizi zote walioandikishwa, ambao watapata huduma za bima ya afya kwa 'kulazwa na matibabu', kama ilivyo kwa raia wa nchi hiyo.

eng: According to the UNHCR website, Iran is home to one of "the world's largest and most protracted refugee populations."
swa: Kwa mujibu wa tovuti ya UNHCR, Irani inahifadhi idadi kubwa zaidi ya wakimbizi duniani.

eng: Iran's Afghan refugee population nears 1 million, with an additional estimated 1.4 to 2 million unregistered refugees living and working in the country.
swa: Wakimbizi wenye asili ya Afghanistani inakaribia milioni 1, huku ikiaminika kwamba kuna wakimbizi wasioandikishwa wanaokadiriwa kuwa kati ya milioni 1.4 na 2 wanaoishi na kufanya kazi zao nchini humo.

eng: Iran's treatment of this demographic has been subject to past criticism, however, most notable in the 2013 Human Rights Watch report that detailed the mistreatment and sometimes abuse Afghans faced from both Iranian society and the government.
swa: Hatua ya serikali ya Irani kutoa huduma hizi kwa wakimbizi imekosolewa sana, hata hivyo, ripoti ya mwaka 2013 Shirika la Haki za Binadamu iliyoonesha kwamba wakimbizi wa Afghanistani walikuwa wakitendewa uonevu na wakati mwingine kunyanyaswa na wananchi wa Irani na serikali.

eng: For their 2015 projection, the UNHCR detailed their expectations for Iran's intake for mostly Afghan, Iraqi and Pakistani refugees as outlined in the image below.
swa: Kwa makadirio ya 2015, Shirika la UNHCR lilionesha matarajio yake kwa mpango huo mahsusi kwa wakimbizi wa Afghani, Iraq na Pakistani kama inavyooneshwa kwenye picha ifuatayo.

eng: Chart from UNHCR country operations profile.
swa: Mchoro kutoka kwenye shughuli za UNHCR nchini humo.

eng: Iran has been criticized for not taking in any Syrian refugees throughout the civil war there.
swa: Irani imekuwa ikikosolewa kwa kutokuwapokea wakimbizi wa Syria wakati wote wa vita vya wenyewe kwa wenyewe.

eng: This reproach comes amidst the fact that it is heavily involved in the Syrian conflict as an ally and supporter of the Syrian President Bashar Al-Assad.
swa: Haya yanatokea wakati ambao nchi hiyo inajihusisha mno na mgogoro wa Syria kama mshirika na mwuungaji mkono mkuu wa Rais wa Syria Rais Bashar Al-Assad.

eng: Indeed, this development in instating universal public healthcare for refugee populations is a notable milestone for both Iran and the region.
swa: Kwa hakika, maendeleo haya katika kuboresha huduma za afya kwa wakimbizi ni mafanikio makubwa kwa nchi ya Irani na eneo hilo zima.

eng: Iran can, however, still improve its image in bolstering its role in alleviating the neighbouring Syrian refugee crisis.
swa: Irani inaweza, hata hivyo, kuboresha taswira yake katika kuchukua hatua za kushughulikia mgogoro wa wakimbizi wa nchi jirani ya Syria.

eng: Lumad leaders display banner calling for the protection of their communities as they march towards Manila.
swa: Viongozi wa Lumad wakionesha bango linaloshinikiza kulindwa kwa jamii yao walipokuwa katika matembezi ya kuelekea jijini Manila.

eng: Photo from the Facebook page of ST Exposure
swa: PIcha kutoka Ukurasa wa Facebook wa ST Exposure

eng: Over 700 Lumad (indigenous peoples from the southern Philippine island of Mindanao) traveled thousands of kilometers and set up protest camps in the nation's capital of Manila in October 2015 to demand the removal of troops and paramilitary forces from their communities.
swa: Mnamo Oktoba, 2015, zaidi ya watu 700 wa jamii ya Lumad (Raia wazawa kutoka katika kisiwa cha Mindanao kilichopo kusini mwa nchi ya Ufilipino) walisafiri maelfu ya kilomita ikiwa ni pamoja na kuweka kambi katika jiji la manila kwa lengo la kushinikiza kuondolewa kwa wanajeshi pamoja na kusitisha matumizi ya nguvu za kijeshi katika jamii zao.

eng: Dubbed the Manilakbayan 2015, the people’s caravan also seeks public support to end the human rights abuses committed by state forces against the Lumad.
swa: Ukijulikana kama Manilakbayan 2015, msafara wa watu ambao pia una lengo la kutafuta kuungwa mkono na jamii ya kimataifa katika kukomesha ukiukwaji wa haki za bianadamu unaofanywa na majeshi ya nchi dhidi ya jamii ya Lumad.

eng: Testimonies from some of the Lumad were shared on Facebook by multimedia group Southern Tagalog Exposure.
swa: Shuhuda kutoka kwa baadhi ya jamii ya watu wa Lumad zilisambazwa kupia mtandao wa Facebook na kikundi cha Southern Tagalog Exposure.

eng: The hashtag #StopLumadKillings trended in the Philippines after the gruesome murders of Lumad community school head Emerito Samarca and two indigenous leaders Dionel Campos and Bello Sinzo last September 1, 2015.
swa: Kiungo habari #StopLumadKillings kilipata umaarufu nchini Ufilipino mara baada ya kutokea kwa mauaji ya kutisha ya Emerito Samarca ambaye ni mkuu wa shule ya jamii ya watu wa Lumad pamoja na mauaji ya raia wazawa Dionel Campos na Bello Sinzo, mauaji yaliyotokea mwezi Septemba 1, 2015.

eng: This was the most high-profile case in what activists claim is a systematic campaign of repression against indigenous peoples in Mindanao, including the targeting of their leaders for assassinations, the closing of indigenous schools, and the military occupation of their homelands.
swa: Hili ni moja ya tukio la aina yake ambalo wanaharakati wanaliona kuwa ni kampeni ya kimkakati ya ukandamizaji dhidi ya raia wazawa wa Mindanao, ikies ni pamoja na kuwalenga viongozi wao na kuwaua, ufungaji wa shule za raia wazawa, pamoja na ardhi yao kukaliwa na wanajeshi.

eng: Lumad organizations explain that they are being targeted at the behest of large-scale mining, plantations, and other companies salivating over the resource-rich Lumad lands.
swa: Mashirika ya Lumad yanaelezea kuwa yanalengwa chini ya mwavuli wa organizations explain that they are being targeted at the behest of Uchimbaji madini mkubwa, mashamba makubwa ya kilimo, pamoja na makampuni mengine yaliyo na uchu wa wa ardhi yenye rutuba ya jamii ya watu wa Lumad.

eng: The armed forces of the Philippines is also accused of arming and training Lumad paramilitaries to fight their own kin.
swa: Majeshi ya Ufilipino yanatuhumiwa pia kwa kuweka wanajeshi na kutoa mafunzo ya kijeshi kwa watu wa jamii ya Lumad kwa ajili ya kukabiliana na ndugu zao wenyewe.

eng: The militarization of indigenous communities has led to massive evacuations of thousands of Lumad across Mindanao.
swa: Utoaji wa mafunzo ya kijeshi kwa baadhi ya jamii ya watu wazawa imepelekea kuhama kwa maelfu ya watu wa Lumad kutoka Mindanao.

eng: These brief statements gathered by Southern Tagalog Exposure bear witness to the intense militarization of indigenous communities and plunder of their ancestral lands.
swa: Taarifa hizi fupi zilizokusanywa na Southern Tagalog Exposure yatoa ushuhuda kuhusiana na utoaji wa mafunzo ya kijaeshi kwa jamii ya wazawa pamoja na uporaji wa ardhi za urithi za wazawa.

eng: Our ancestral lands are being forcibly taken from us. 	Ardhi zetu za urithi zinachukuliwa kwa nguvu.
We want to drive the soldiers away and dismantle the paramilitary groups dividing the ranks of us Lumad.
swa: Tunahitaji kuwaondosha wanajaeshi na kuharibu kabisa makundi ya watu waliopokea mafunzo ya kijeshi na ambao ndio wanatuvunjia heshima jamii ya Lumad.

eng: We want to live in peace."
swa: Tunahitaji kuishi kwa amani."

eng: Bai Bibiaon Ligkaian Bigkal, Woman Warrior of Tala-ingod, Davao del Norte
swa: Bai Bibiaon Ligkaian Bigkal, Mwanamke mpambanaji wa Tala-ingod, Davao del Norte

eng: “Soldiers massacred our tribe.
swa: “Wanajeshi wameangamiza kabila letu.

eng: The government and corporations prioritize personal interests, not the interests of the people.
swa: Serikali pamoja na mashirika yameweka mbele maslahi yao pekee, na siyo maslahi ya jamii nzima.

eng: The people are not important to them.
swa: Watu siyo wa muhimu kwao.

eng: When we defend our ancestral land and culture, they accuse us of being part of New People's Army to justify abductions or murders.”
swa: Tunapojaribu kulinda aridhi zetu za urithi pamoja na na utamaduni wetu, wanatutuhumu kuwa sisi ni sehemu ya , yaani jeshi jipya la watu kama namna ya kuhalalisha kuwaondosha watu kutoka katika makazi yao au kutekeleza mauaji.”

eng: Kaylo, Manobo of Talaingod, Davao del Norte
swa: Kaylo, Manobo wa Talaingod, Davao del Norte

eng: Because of the repression of the soldiers, we were forced to evacuate and leave our land. 	Kutokana na uonevu wa wanajeshi, tulilazimika kuondoka na kuiacha ardhi yetu.
To be displaced is difficult, with the heat and no water.
swa: Kuachwa bila makazi ni kugumu sana, kukiwana joto kali na bila ya maji.

eng: We want to return to our land.
swa: Tunahitaji kurudi kwenye maeneo yetu.

eng: I vowed to myself as a Lumad since childhood to continue our fight until I die."
swa: Tokea nikiwa mdogo, mimi kama raia wa Lumad niliapa kuendelea kudai haki yetu hadi siku nitakayokufa."

eng: Krstina Lantao, Southern Mindanao Region
swa: Krstina Lantao, Eneo la Kusini mwa Mindanao

eng: “The Philippine Army destroyed our school.
swa: “Jeshi la Ufilipino liliharibu shule yetu.

eng: They even burned our agricultural cooperative.
swa: Pia, lilichoma majengo ya ushirika wetu wa kilimo.

eng: I experienced getting jailed and now face trumped-up charges of kidnapping.
swa: Nilijikuta nimefungwa gerezani na sasa nimeshitakiwa kwa kusingiziwa kosa la utekaji.

eng: We miss our ancestral land.
swa: Tuna hamu ya kuipata tena ardhi yetu tuliyoirithi kwa mababu zetu.

eng: Wherever we go, we yearn for it.
swa: Popote tutakapokuwa, tutaipigania.

eng: This is where we live and grew up.
swa: Huku ndipo tunapoishi na tulipokulia.

eng: If it is taken from us, our culture will die with the next generation.”
swa: Kama tutaporwa ardhi yetu, utamaduni wetu utapotea sambamba na kizazi kijacho.”

eng: Datu Isidro, Kitaotao, Bukidnon
swa: Datu Isidro, Kitaotao, Bukidnon

eng: “The helicopter of the soldiers arrived at our place.
swa: “Chopa ya wanajeshi iliwasili katika makazi yetu.

eng: They burned our house. Only the clothes we wore were saved. According to the soldiers, the Lumad are not allowed to study.
swa: Walichoma nyumba yetu. tulibakiwa tu na nguo tulizokuwa tumevaa. wanajeshi walidai kuwa, watu jamii ya Lumad hawapaswi kwenda shule.

eng: When I grow up, I want to be a teacher to prove them wrong.”
swa: Nikiwa mkubwa, nitapenda kuwa mwalimu ili kuwaonesha kuwa mawazo yao siyo sahihi. .”

eng: Kimkim Baliti, 13-year-old Manobo, Talaingod, Davao del Norte
swa: Kimkim Baliti, 13-year-old Manobo, Talaingod, Davao del Norte

eng: “"We will not die in the jungles, but instead will die from the open pit mining.
swa: “"Hatutafia kwenye mapambano, bali tutafia kwenye mashimo ya wazi ya uchimbaji madini.

eng: We should be the ones benefiting from the wealth of Mindanao. The soldiers say we are New People's Army to justify our displacement and murder.
swa: Sisi ndio tunaopaswa kunufaika na utajiri wa Mindanao.Wanajeshi wanatutuhumu kuwa sisi ni , yaani jeshi jipya la watu kama namna ya kuhalalisha kuwaondosha watu kutoka katika makazi yao au kutekeleza mauaji.

eng: They should be the ones who must go because they are outsiders to our ancestral land.”
swa: Wao ndio wanaopaswa kuondoka kwa kuwa wao ndio wavamizi wa ardhi yetu ya tokea enzi za mababu.”

eng: Jean Derong, Manobo, Davao Oriental
swa: Jean Derong, Manobo, Davao Oriental

eng: “The role of women in the struggle of the native Lumad is important.
swa: “Jukumu la wanawake katika harakati za kuilinda jamii halisi ya Lumad ni la muhimu.

eng: Our respect for each other is high.
swa: Heshima iliyopo miongoni mwetu ni ya hali ya juu sana.

eng: We need to collectively defend our human rights and our ancestral land.”
swa: Kwa pamoja, tunahitaji kulinda haki zetu pamoja na ardhi yetu tuliyoirithi kutoka kwa mababu zetu.”

eng: Bai Aida Seiza, Manobo, Paquibato, Davao City
swa: Bai Aida Seiza, Manobo, Paquibato, Davao City

eng: Amin Anvary's mother Farah Bakhshi in a protest for her son's release.
swa: Mama yake Amin Anvary Farah Bakhshi akidai kuachiwa huru kwa mwanae.

eng: Image from ICHRI.
swa: Picha: ICHRI.

eng: Student activist Amin Anvari, 21, who received a suspended prison sentence earlier this year for Facebook postings promoting basic civil liberties, has been arrested and held without charge at Evin Prison’s Ward 2-A by Iran’s Revolutionary Guards since 4 October, 2015.
swa: Mwanaharakati mwanafunzi Amin Anvari, 21, aliyesamehewa kifungo cha awali mapema mwaka huu kwa sababu ya maandishi yake kwenye mtandao wa Facebook yanayopigania uhuru wa kiraia, amekamatwa tena bila kushtakiwa kwenye gereza la Evin, kitendo kilichofanywa na Walinzi wa Mapinduzi ya Irani tangu Oktoba 4, 2015.

eng: According to a family member, he has been under intense pressure to make false confessions.
swa: Kwa mujibu nwa mwanafamilia, kijana huyo amekuwa akishinikizwa kukiri uongo.

eng: “They are threatening us and harassing us just to put pressure on Amin in prison.
swa: “Wanatutisha na kutubughudhi kama mbinu ya kumshinikiza Amin huko jela.

eng: I’m sure of that.
swa: Nina uhakika na hilo.

eng: They want him to agree to confess to lies,” Amin Anvari’s mother, Farah Bakhshi, told the International Campaign for Human Rights in Iran.
swa: Wanataka akubali kukiri uongo,” mama wa Amin Anvari, Farah Bakhshi, aliuambia Mtandao wa Kimataifa wa Kutetea Haki za Binadamu nchini Irani.

eng: Amin Anvari was first arrested on 30 December, 2014, because of his Facebook posts on basic civil rights.
swa: Amin Anvari alimatwa kwa mara ya kwanza Desemba 30, 2014, kwa sababu ya kuandika masuala yanayohusu haki za msingi za raia kwenye mtandao wa Facebook.

eng: He was released the same day on a 300 million-rial (approximately USD $10,000) bond.
swa: Aliachiliwa huru siku hiyo hiyo kwa dhamana ya riali milioni 300 (sawa na dola za Marekani 10,000).

eng: In July 2015, he was tried at Branch 26 of the Islamic Revolutionary Court presided by Judge Ahmadzadeh and sentenced to two and a half years in prison for “propaganda against the state,” “insulting the Supreme Leader,” and “insulting Mohammad Taghi Mesbagh Yazdi”, who is a member of the Council of Experts.
swa: Mwezi Julai, 2015, alisomewa mashitaka kwenye Mahakama ya Kimapinduzi ya Kiislamu iliyokuwa inaongozwa na Jaji Ahmadzadeh na kuhukumiwa kifungo cha miaka miwili na nusu jela kwa "kuendesha propaganda dhidi ya serikali," "kumtukana Kiongozi Mkuu wa nchi," na "Kumtukana Mohammad Taghi Mesbagh Yazdi”, ambaye ni mwanachama wa Baraza la Wataalam.

eng: But his sentence was suspended for five years.
swa: Hata hivyo, hukumu hiyo iliahirishwa kwa miaka mitano.

eng: Ms. Bakhshi recalled that her son Amin was arrested again on 4 October by ten men who stormed into their home without showing identification or warrants and confiscated his personal computers.
swa: Bi. Bakhshi anakumbuka kwamba kijana wake huyo Amin alikamatwa tena mnamo Oktoba 4 na watu wanne waliovamia nyumba yake bila kuonesha vitambulisho wala hati yoyote na kuchukua kompyuta za kijana huyo.

eng: Since then she has only been able to have three brief phone conversations with him.
swa: Tangu wakati huo mama huyo ameweza kuongea na kijana wake mara nne tu kwa simu.

eng: She, her husband, and her younger son have been harassed and warned not to give interviews about Amin’s arrest.
swa: Yeye, mume wake, na mtoto wao mdogo wamekuwa wakisumbuliwa na kuonywa wasithubutu kuongea na waandishi kuhusiana na kukamatwa kwa Amin.

eng: “Anything that happens to my two children, myself and my husband will be the responsibility of the Revolutionary Guards.
swa: “Chochote kitakachowakuta wanangu hawa wawili, mimi na mume wangu kitahusiana moja kwa moja na Walinzi wa Mapinduzi.

eng: They are threatening us so that I don’t protest or give interviews.
swa: Wanatutisha sana ili tusipinge jambo hilo wala kukubali kuhojiwa na waandishi.

eng: But I have no other choice.
swa: Lakini sina jinsi.

eng: You want me not to give interviews?
swa: Mnataka nisihojiwe?

eng: For God’s sake release my son and then I’ll be quiet,” Ms. Bakhshi said.
swa: Nawaombeni kwa jina la Mwenyezi Mungu mwachieni mwanangu na nitakaa kimya,” alisema Bi.

eng: Ms. Bakhshi relayed to the Campaign how an official at Evin Prison tried to pressure her not to speak with media:
swa: Bi. Bakhshi aliuambia mtandao huo namna afisa mmoja wa serikali kwenye gereza la Evin alivyojaribu kumwekea shinikizo la kutokuongea na vyombo vya habari:

eng: He told me he would let me see my son if I promised not to give interviews or join protests.
swa: Aliniambia ataniruhusu kumwona kijana wangu kama nitamhakikishia kuwa sitaongea na waandishi wala kuandamana.

eng: I said I would agree, if he promised to release my son.
swa: Nikamwambia ningekubali, kama angeniahidi kumwachia mwanangu.

eng: He said no, and I said 'well, then I will continue to do what I’m doing.'
swa: Alikataa, na nikamwambia, 'kama ni hivyo, nitaendelea kufanya kile ninachokifanya.'

eng: Amin Anvari’s mother added that she was silent for two weeks after her son’s arrest.
swa: Mama wa Amin Anvari aliongeza kwamba amekuwa kimya kwa majuma mawili baada ya kukamatwa kwa kijana wake.

eng: But on 19 October, she joined a protest gathering by a group of prisoners’ families.
swa: Lakini ilipofika Oktoba 19, alishiriki maandamano yaliyoratibiwa na kikundi cha familia za wafungwa.

eng: “That same day Amin phoned our home and spoke to his father and said he was well and said ‘Tell mother not to give interviews because it will cause problems ’.”
swa:
Siku hiyo hiyo Amin alitupigia simu nyumbani na kuongea na baba yake akamwambia alikuwa mzima na kusema, 'Mwambie mama asiongee na waandishi kwa sababu itaniletea matatizo [kwenye kesi yake'.”
Ms. Bakhshi said during this summer’s annual family visit to Turkey they discovered that some of Amin’s friends had been arrested.	Bi. Bakhshi alisema wakati wa ziara ya kifamilia ya majira ya joto walioifanya nchini Uturuki waligundua kwamba baadhi ya marafiki wa Amin walikuwa wamekamatwa.
She told him not to return to Iran if he thought there might be a problem.	Alimwambia asirudi Irani kama alihisi angepata matatizo.
But he said he had done nothing wrong and wanted to return to his university studies, Ms. Bakhshi added. 	Lakini anasema hakufanya makosa yoyote na alitaka kurudi kuendelea na masomo yake ya Chuo Kikuu, Bi.
“My plea to the judicial officials is that they should not arrest youths and pass heavy judgments against them every time they criticize.	“Wito wangu kwa maafisa wa mahakama ni kwamba wasiwakamate vijana na kuwapa hukumu kubwa kila wanapokosoa.
My son should be sitting in class and studying right now.”	Kijana wangu alitakiwa awe darasani anasoma hivi sasa.

eng: Land Grab.
swa: Ukwapuaji wa Ardhi.

eng: Federico Boyd Sulapas Dominguez uploaded this painting in time for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit which will be held in the Philippines.
swa: Federico Boyd Sulapas Dominguez alipakia mchoro huu wakati wa kuelelekea kwenye kongamano la Ushirika wa Kiuchumi la Asia-Pacific linalotarajiwa kufanyika nchini Ufilipino.

eng: Reposted with permission
swa: Imerudiwa kuchapishwa kwa ruhusa

eng: Over the past 40 years, Filipino artist Federico Boyd Sulapas Dominguez has been painting the efforts of indigenous peoples to combat destructive mining, development aggression, and militarization.
swa: Kwa kipindi cha miaka 40 iliyopita, msanii wa Kifilipino Federico Boyd Sulapas Dominguez amekuwa akiandaa picha zinazoonesha harakati za wazawa katika kukomesha uchimbaji madini wa uharibifu, utafutaji maendeleo usiojali haki, pamoja na matumizi ya nguvu za kijeshi.

eng: His aim is to enlighten the public about the situation of ethnic groups in the Philippines and their campaign for the protection of their ancestral lands.
swa: Lengo lake ni kuifahamisha jamii kuhususiana na masaibu yaikumbayo jamii ya watu waishio Ufilipino pamoja na harakati zao za kulinda ardhi waliyorithishwa na mababu zao.

eng: The Philippines has more 14 million indigenous peoples belonging to 110 ethno-linguistic groups.
swa: Ufilipino ina zaidi ya wakazi wazawa milioni 14 ambao huzungumza lugha zaidi ya 110 za kikabila.

eng: However, the unique heritage of these tribes is threatened by rapid urbanization, commercialization, and encroachment of their lands by state-approved activities such as agribusiness ventures, logging, and mining.
swa: Hata hivyo, urithi huu wa aina yake unahatarishwa na ongezeko la haraka la miji, harakati za kibiashara pamoja na uporaji wa ardhi yao kupitia shughuli zinazopewa baraka zote na serikali zikiwamo zile za kilimo, uvunaji miti na uchimbaji wa madini.

eng: In Mindanao Island, located in the southern part of the country, the collective term for ethnic groups is Lumad.
swa: Katika kisiwa cha Mindanao, kilichopo kaskazini mwa Ufilipino, jamii ya watu wa huko hujulikana kwa jina la lumad.

eng: Various lumad groups which are resisting the entry of mining firms into their communities has been in the news during September and October 2015 after they were attacked by paramilitary groups.
swa: Makundi anuai ya Lumad ambayo yanapinga kuingiliwa na makampuni ya uchimbaji madini yamejitokeza kwenye vyombo vya habari kati ya miezi ya Septemba na Oktoba 2015 mara baada ya kushambuliwa na makundi ya watu mithili ya wanajeshi.

eng: About 700 Lumad members have set up camps in Manila, the nation’s capital, to demand the pull-out of troops from their homes.
swa: Takribani watu 700 wa jamii ya Lumad wameweka kambi jijini Manila, mji mkuu wa Ufilipino, kwa ajili ya kushinikiza kuondolewa kwa wanajeshi kwenye makazi yao.

eng: The plight of the Lumad is reflected in many of Federico's artworks.
swa: Malalamiko ya Lumad yanaonekana sana kwenye kazi nyingi za Federico.

eng: He has also been uploading copies of his old paintings on Facebook which he thinks are still relevant because of the attacks on Lumad communities and the continued plunder of natural resources in the ancestral domains of ethnic tribes.
swa: Amekuwa pia akipakia nakala ya kazi zake za zamani katika ukurasa wake wa Facebook ambazo anaziona kama bado zina manufaa kufuatia kuvamiwa kwa jamii ya Lumad na matukio ya mfululizo ya kurubuni mali asili zilizopo kwenye maeneo ya urithi ya makabila haya.

eng: Some of his paintings have been widely shared on social media by activists, scholars, and heritage advocates who are seeking to inspire the public to support the Lumad’s right to self-determination.
swa: Baadhi ya michoro yake tayari imeshasambazwa kwa kiasi kikubwa kwenye mitandao ya kijamii na wanaharakati, wanazuoni pamoja na watetezi wa masuala ya urithi ambao wanalenga kuhamasisha jamii kusaidia jamii ya lumad kupata haki yao.

eng: Federico, who is a Mandaya (Lumad indigenous people from the eastern part of Mindanao), encourages younger artists to enrich their knowledge of Philippine culture by integrating with ethnic communities.
swa: Federico, ambaye ni wa kabila la Mandaya (Jamii ya wazawa wa lumad kutoka Mashariki ya Mindanao), anawahamashisha wasanii wachanga kuongeza maaarifa yao kuhusu utamaduni wa Ufilipino kwa kujumuika na jamii za wazawa.

eng: Memes widely shared in solidarity with the victims of the Paris attacks.
swa: Picha zinazozunguka mitandaoni kuwafariji wahanga wa shambulio la Paris.

eng: I come from a privileged Francophone community in Lebanon.
swa: Ninatoka katika jamii iliyoendelea kidogo pale Lebanon.

eng: This has meant that I have always seen France as my second home.
swa: Kwa kuwa lugha yetu ni Kifaransa, nimejikuta nikiiona nchi ya Ufaransa kama nyumbani kwetu.

eng: The streets of Paris are as familiar to me as the streets of Beirut.
swa: Mitaa ya Ufaransa ninaifahamu sana kama ninavyoifahamu Beirut.

eng: I was just in Paris a few days ago.
swa: Nilikuwa Paris siku chache tu zilizopita.

eng: These have been two horrible nights of violence.
swa: Siku mbili hizi zimekuwa za kutisha sana.

eng: The first took the lives of over 40 in Beirut; the second took the lives of over 120 people and counting in Paris.
swa: Siku ya kwanza ilishuhudia vifo vya watu zaidi ya 40 mjini Beirut; usiku wa siku ya pili maisha ya zaidi ya watu 120 jijini Paris yalikatishwa.

eng: It also seems clear to me that to the world, my people’s deaths in Beirut do not matter as much as my other people’s deaths in Paris.
swa: Kwangu, inaonekana wazi kwamba kwa dunia yetu, vifo vya watu mjini Beirut havijagusa hisia za watu kama ilivyotokea kwa vifo vilivyotokea jijini Paris.

eng: We do not get a "safe" button on Facebook.
swa: Hatujapata kile kitufe cha 'salama' kwenye mtandao wa Facebook.

eng: We do not get late night statements from the most powerful men and women alive and millions of online users.
swa: Hatujapata salamu za pole zilizotolewa usiku wa manane kutoka kwa watu maarufu zaidi duniani pamoja na mamilioni ya watumiaji wa mtandao.

eng: We do not change policies which will affect the lives of countless innocent refugees.
swa: Hatukubadilisha sera zitakazoathiri maisha ya wakimbizi wasio na hatia ambao idadi yao haifahamiki.

eng: This could not be clearer.
swa: Hali hii haieleweki kabisa.

eng: I say this with no resentment whatsoever, just sadness.
swa: Ninayasema haya bila chuki wala hasira yoyote, isipokuwa huzuni.

eng: It is a hard thing to realize that for all that was said, for all the progressive rhetoric we have managed to create as a seemingly united human voice, most of us members of this curious species are still excluded from the dominant concerns of the "world".
swa: Ni vigumu kuelewa kwamba kwa yote yaliyosemwa, kwa maneno matupu tuliyoweza kuyatamka kwa jina la 'mshikamano na wahanga', wengi wetu tulio binadamu kama wengine tunatengwa na kelele hizi hewa za mshikamano wa kile kinachoitwa 'dunia'.

eng: And I know that by "world", I am myself excluding most of the world.
swa: Natambua kwa kutumia neno 'dunia', mimi mwenyewe ninabagua sehemu kubwa sana ya dunia.

eng: Because that’s how power structures work.
swa: Kwa sababu huo ndio muundo wa wenye nguvu unavyofanya kazi.

eng: I do not matter.
swa: Sina thamani.

eng: My "body" does not matter to the "world".
swa: Mwili' wangu hauna thamani kwa 'dunia'.

eng: If I die, it will not make a difference.
swa: Nikifa, hakuna anayejali.

eng: Again, I say this with no resentment.
swa: Narudia, siyasemi haya kwa chuki na hasira.

eng: That statement is merely a fact.
swa: Sentensi hii ni ukweli uliodhahiri.

eng: It is a political fact, true, but a fact nonetheless.
swa: Ni ukweli wa kisiasa, uhalisia, lakini ndio ukweli wenyewe.

eng: Maybe I should have some resentment in me, but I am too tired.
swa: Labda nijikaze niwe na hisia fulani ndani yangu, lakini nimechoka.

eng: It is a heavy thing to realize.
swa: Ni jambo zito sana kulitambua.

eng: I know that I am fortunate enough that when I do die, I will be remembered by friends and loved ones.
swa: Ninafahamu kwamba nina bahati sana kwamba nikifa, nitakumbukwa na marafiki na wapendwa wangu.

eng: Maybe my blog and an online presence might even gather some thoughts by people around the world.
swa: Huenda blogu yangu na ninayoyaandika mitandaoni yanaweza kuwafanya baadhi ya watu wakatafakari maneno yangu.

eng: That is the beauty of the internet.
swa: Huo ndio uzuri wa mtandao wa intaneti.

eng: And even that is out of reach to too many.
swa: Lakini mtandao unatumika na wachache sana.

eng: Never so clearly as now have I understood what Ta-Nehisi Coates wrote about when he spoke of the Black Body in America.
swa: Sikuwahi kuelewa vizuri Ta-Nehisi Coates alimaanisha nini alipoandika kuhusu Mwili Mweusi nchini Marekani .

eng: I think there is a story to be told of the Arab Body as well.
swa: Nadhani tunaweza kupanua simulizi hiyo na kuwa Mwili wa Kiarabu pia.

eng: The Native American Body.
swa: Mwili wa Mmarekani Mzawa.

eng: The Indigenous Body.
swa: Mwili wa Mhindi Mwekundu.

eng: The Latin American Body.
swa: Mwili wa Mwamerika Kusini.

eng: The Indian Body.
swa: Mwili wa Mhindi.

eng: The Kurdish Body.
swa: Mwili wa Mkurdi.

eng: The Pakistani Body.
swa: Mwili wa Mpakistani.

eng: The Chinese Body.
swa: Mwili wa Mchina.

eng: And so many other bodies.
swa: Na miili mingine mingi.

eng: The Human Body is not one.
swa: Mwili wa Binadamu unatofautiana.

eng: It sure feels that it should be by now.
swa: Kwa hakika inaonekana hivyo kwa sasa.

eng: Maybe that in itself is an illusion.
swa: Labda kufanana kwa miili ni ndoto.

eng: But maybe it is an illusion worth preserving because without even that vague aspiration towards oneness on the part of some part of the body, I am not sure what sort of world we would be living in now.
swa: Lakini huenda ni ndoto inayohitaji kutunzwa kwa sababu bila hata hisia hizi hewa za mshikamano kwa sehemu ya viungo vya mwili, sina hakika ni dunia ya aina gani tungekuwa tunaishi sasa hivi.

eng: Some bodies are global, but most bodies remain local, regional, "ethnic".
swa: Miili mingine ni ya kidunia, lakini miili mingine inayahusu maeneo husika, nchi husika, na baadhi ya makabila pekee.

eng: My thoughts are with all the victims of today’s and yesterday's horrific attacks, and my thoughts are with all those who will suffer serious discrimination as a result of the actions of a few mass murderers and the general failure of humanity’s imagination to see itself as a unified entity.
swa: Ninasikitika sana pamoja na wahanga wa mashambulio ya kinyama ya leo na jana, na ninasikitika na wale wote wanaathirika na ubaguzi mbaya sana unaotokana na matendo ya wauaji wa halaiki na kushindwa kwa sisi wanadamu kujiona kwa utambulisho mmoja.

eng: My only hope is that we can be strong enough to generate the opposite response to what these criminals intended.
swa: Tumaini langu pekee ni kwamba tunaweza kuwa imara kiasi cha kutoa majibu yaliyo kinyume na yale yaliyotarajiwa na wahalifu wa mashambulizi haya.

eng: I want to be optimistic enough to say that we are getting there, wherever "there" might be.
swa: Nina matumaini mengi kiasi cha kusema kwamba tunaelekea huko, bila kujali 'huko' ni wapi.

eng: We need to talk about these things.
swa: Tunahitaji kuzungumzia masuala haya.

eng: We need to talk about Race.
swa: Tunahitaji kuzungumzia kuhusu rangi za watu.

eng: We just have to.
swa: Tunalazimika.

eng: This article and radio report by April Peavey for The World originally appeared on PRI.org on November 5, 2015, and is republished here as part of a content-sharing agreement.
swa: Makala haya na taarifa ya habari ya radio iliyoandaliwa na April Peavey kwa ajili ya kipindi cha The World kilionekana kwa mara ya kwanza kwenye tovuti ya PRI.org mnamo Novemba 5, 2015, na kimechapishwa tena hapa kama sehemu ya makubaliano ya kushirikiana maudhui.

eng: Tritha Sinha is a woman who's always known exactly what she wants.
swa: Tritha Sinha ni mwanamke ambaye siku zote anafahamu kile anachokitaka.

eng: I always wanted to be free and not depend on my father for pocket money or eventually my boyfriends or brother and that sort of thing, she says.
swa: Nimekuwa nikitaka kuwa huru na kuacha kumtegemea baba yangu kwa fedha za kujikimu au kuwategemea rafiki zangu wa kiume au kaka na watu kama hao, anasema.

eng: Sinha is the driving force behind the New Delhi- and Paris-based band Tritha Electric.
swa: Sinha ni nguzo inayotengemeza bendi yenye makazi yake jijini New Delhi na Paris iitwayo Tritha Electric.

eng: She grew up in Kolkata and says, in India, the women around her weren't all that happy.
swa: Alikulia eneo la Kolkata na anasema, nchini India, wanawake waliomzunguka hawakuwa watu wenye furaha.

eng: They were stifled.
swa: Walikuwa wakiishi katika maisha ya ugandamizi.

eng: I had seen tears on faces of my aunts or mother, or just teachers randomly at school — and that made me feel that something is just not right.
swa: Nimeshuhudia mama yangu pamoja na shangazi zangu wakilia, wakati mwingine hata walimu katika shule nilizosoma -na hali hiyo ilinifanya nijisikie kwamba kuna mambo hayaendi ipasavyo.

eng: Music, Tritha Sinha says, was her way out — a ticket to financial independence and liberation.
swa: Muziki, Tritha Sinha anasema, ulikuwa njia ya kutokea -tiketi ya kuelekea kwenye uhuru wa kifedha na kujitegemea.

eng: That independent streak started at a very young age.
swa: Uhuru huo ulianza tangu akiwa mdogo.

eng: Tritha Sinha was only 5 when she started singing.
swa: Tritha Sinha alianza kuimba akiwa na miaka mitano tu.

eng: Credit: April Peavey.
swa: Picha: April Peavey.

eng: She paid her way through college by singing in Bollywood movies.
swa: Alijilipia ada ya chuo kwa kuimba kwenye filamu za ki-Hindi.

eng: But singing songs written by other people wasn't enough.
swa: Lakini kuimba nyimbo zilizoandikwa na wengine halikuwa jambo linalomtosheleza.

eng: Oh no, she needed to write her own songs and front her own band.
swa: Ah, hapana, alihitaji kuandika nyimbo zake mwenyewe nakumiliki bendi yake mwenyewe.

eng: That's where Tritha Electric comes in.
swa: Hapo ndipo bendi ya Tritha Electric inaanza.

eng: Sinha calls it ethno-punk music.
swa: Sinha anaiita muziki wa ethno-punk .

eng: The ethno part is a nod to her classical Indian musical roots and the punk, she says, helps her express the struggles of being an independent woman in India today.
swa: Sehemu ya ethno ni kuendeleza asili yake ya muziki wa ki-Hindi na punk, anasema, inamsaidia kuelezea mapambano ya kuwa mwanamke anayejitegemea nchini India leo.

eng: Tritha Electric's latest album is called Pagli.
swa: Albamu mpya ya bendi ya Tritha Electric inaitwa Pagli.

eng: That means "crazy woman" in Bengali.
swa: Maana yake ni 'mwanamke mtukutu' kwa lugha ya ki-Bengali.

eng: And the songs on it tell the story of a woman who feels confined by tradition.
swa: Na nyimbo zote kwenye albamu hiyo zinasimulia hadithi ya mwanamke anayejisikia kufungwa na mila.

eng: But she breaks the rules and finds freedom.
swa: Lakini anavunja mila hiyo na kujipatia uhuru.

eng: Much like Tritha Sinha herself.
swa: Ni kama Tritha Sinha mwenyewe.

eng: She says, "To discover freedom sometimes we need to go through very crazy moments or insanity sometimes to just realize what is freedom or how important freedom can be for our individual deep inner selves.
swa: Anasema, "Kuugundua uhuru wakati mwingine tunahitaji kupitia nyakati ngumu au hata ukichaa wakati mwingine ili kuelewa nini maana ya uhuru na kwa jinsi gani uhuru waweza kuwa muhimu kwa utu wetu wa ndani.

eng: And that really opened the door of my independent musical life."
swa: Na hiyo ndiyo iliyofungua mlango wa mafanikio yangu kimziki."
