eng: On November 6, the Republic of Congo's President Denis Sassou-Nguesso claimed victory in a referendum staged to allow him to stand for election once again, anticipating moves by colleagues in Rwanda, Burundi and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where long-serving presidents are all trying to change constitutions to extend their respective stays in power.
swa: Mnamo Novemba 6, Rais wa Jamhuri ya ki-demokrasia ya Kongo, Denis Sassou-Nguesso alijipatia ushindi katika kura ya maoni iliyokuwa iamue ikiwa angeweza kugombea Urais kwa mara nyingine, kufuata nyayo za watawala wenzake wa Rwanda, Burundi na Jamhuri ya ki-Demokrasia ya Kongo (DRC), ambapo ma-Rais waliodumu madarakani kwa muda mrefu wanajaribu kubadili katiba zao ili kujiongea muda wa kubaki madarakani.

eng: The call for the referendum was strongly contested by the political opposition, leading to several deaths at various protests in the streets of the capital, Brazzaville, during the week of the October 25 referendum.
swa: Kura hiyo ya maoni ilipigwa vikali na vyama vya upinzani nchini humo na kusababisha vifo kadhaa katika maandamano yaliyoendelea kwenye baadhi ya mitaa ya makao makuu ya nchi hiyo, Brazzaville, wakati wa juma la kuelekea kura hiyo iliyofanyika Oktoba 25.

eng: Sassou-Nguesso was president of the People's Republic of Congo between 1979 and 1992 and has held the office in the renamed Republic of Congo from 1997.
swa: Sassou-Nguesso alikuwa rais wa Jamhuri ya Watu wa Kongo kati ya 1979 na 1992 na aliendelea kushikilia madaraka hata baada ya nchi hiyo kubadili jina na kuitwa Jamhuri ya Kongo kuanzia mwaka 1997.

eng: #Sassoudegage protests via kabolokongo.com
swa: Maandamano ya #Sassoudegage.

eng: Violent clashes at anti-referendum protests
swa: Mapigano wakati wa maandamano ya kupinga kura hiyo ya maoni

eng: The constitution of the Republic of Congo (also known as Congo-Brazzaville) limits the number of presidential terms to two, and sets the maximum age to stand for office at 70.
swa: Katiba ya Jamhuri ya Kongo (nchi inayofahamika pia kama Kongo-Brazzaville) inamzuia rais kutawala zaidi ya vipindi viwili, na imeweka umri wa mwisho wa rais kuwa madarakani ambao ni miaka 70.

eng: In early 2015, Sassou-Nguesso organised a series of consultations with some of the country's major political players to look into the possibility of modifying a constitution that has been in place since 2002.
swa: Mwanzoni mwa 2015, Sassou-Nguesso aliandaa mfululizo wa mashauriano na baadhi ya watu muhimu kisiasa nchini humo ili kuangalia uwezekano wa kurekebisha katiba ambayo imekuwa ikitumika tangu mwaka 2002.

eng: This manoeuvre was the subject of severe criticism from a section of the opposition, who saw it as an attempt by the current president to stand for office a third time.
swa: Mpango huo ulikosolewa vikali na wapinzani wake, walioutafsiri kama mchezo wa rais aliyepo madarakani kufanya jaribio la kutaka kugombea kwa muhula wa tatu.

eng: Sassou-Nguesso, nonetheless, went ahead with the referendum, asking the Congolese people if they would grant the amendments necessary for him to hold onto power.
swa: Sassou-Nguesso, hata hivyo, aliendelea na mpango wake na kuitisha kura ya maoni, akiwauliza wananchi wa Kongo kama wanaweza kubariki marekebisho yanayoweza kumwezesha kubaki madarakani.

eng: Prior to the vote, the opposition called for a general boycott, and protests broke out against the president in several cities, notably Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire.
swa: Kabla ya kupigwa kura hiyo, vyama vya upinzani vilitangaza kususia zoezi hilo, na maandamano yalilipuka kumpinga rais katika miji kadhaa, hususani Brazzaville na Pointe-Noire.

eng: The authorities said four died and 10 were injured in violence during referendum week, as hashtags such as #Sassoufit (a play on words with the President's surname and the French for 'that's enough') and #Sassoudegage (Sassou out) trended on social media.
swa: Mamlaka zinasema watu wanne walipoteza maisha na 10 wengine walijeruhiwa katika mapigano wakati wa juma la kura hiyo ya maoni kama alama habari za #Sassoufit (inayochezea jina la ukoo la rais huyo na kulichanganya na neno la Kifaransa lenye maana 'imetosha') na #Sassoudegage (Sassou nje) zikitumika sana kwneye mitandao ya kijamii.

eng: Despite a low turnout of 10% the referendum nevertheless returned a 'yes' victory, paving the way for Sassou-Nguesso's wished-for constitutional change.
swa: Pamoja na watu kujitokeza kwa kiwango kidogo cha asilimia 10 kura hiyo ya maoni hata hivyo iliidhinisha ushindi wa 'ndio', na hivyo kutengenezea njia ya mabadiliko ya katiba aliyoyataka mhe. Sassou-Nguesso.

eng: #sassoufit slogans at protests against Nguesso via canalfrance info
swa: kauli mbio za #sassoufit kwenye maandamano yanayompinga Nguesso. Picha kupitia canalfrance info

eng: What does the future hold for Congo-Brazzaville?
swa: Nini Mustakabali wa Kongo-Brazzaville?

eng: For the opposition the low turnout signalled the population's opposition to the constitutional reform.
swa: Kwa vyama vya upinzani, idadi ndogo ya waliojitokeza kupiga kura ni ishara ya ushindi na umaarufu wake kuhusu suala hilo la mabadiliko ya katiba.

eng: Ismaël Bowend Nabole, a reporter at Brazzaville's Omega FM, noted that the Congolese opposition rejected the result:
swa: Ismaël Bowend Nabole, mwandishi wa Omega FM iliyopo jijini Brazzaville, anasema kwamba vyama vya upinzani nchini humo viliyakataa matokeo hayo:

eng: One of the opposition's two major outlets has called the referendum a "constitutional coup" because the poll was neither free, fair, impartial nor transparent" and took place "under siege conditions".
swa: Vyombo viwili vikuu vya habari vinavyomilikiwa na vyama vya upinzani vimeita kura hiyo ya maoni "Mapinduzi ya kikatiba" kwa sababu kura hiyo haikuwa huru, wala haki, ilijaa upendeleo bila uwazi" na ilifanyika "katika mazingira ya utekaji".

eng: The international community and electoral observers were also sceptical of the results.
swa: Jumuiya ya kimataifa na waangalizi wa uchaguzi wamekuwa na wasiwasi na matokeo hayo.

eng: Michel Taube, Director of the French-language current affairs website "l'Opinion Internationale" explained the position of the French government on the poll:
swa: Michel Taube, Mkurugenzi wa tovuti ya habari inayotumia lugha ya Kifaransa "l'Opinion Internationale" alielezea upinzani wa serikali ya Ufaransa kuhusu uchaguzi huo:

eng: François Hollande, the French President, has distanced himself from Sassou-Nguesso.
swa: François Hollande, Rais wa Ufaransa, amejitenga na Sassou-Nguesso.

eng: After causing disappointment all over Africa with remarks made to the media the day before, the Elysée released a tardy statement saying that it "condemned any violence and supports freedom of expression. points out his speech in Dakar on the 29th November 2014 where he expressed his wish for all constitutions to be respected and for consultation of the electorate to take place under conditions of undisputed transparency."
swa: Baada ya kusababisha mshangao kote barani Afrika kwa matamshi aliyoyatoa mbele ya vyombo vya habari siku moja kablda, Elysée ilisema "inalaani ghasia zozote na inaunga mkono uhuru wa kujieleza. anatoa mfano wa hotuba yake aliyoitoa jijini Dakar mnamo Novemba 29, 2014 alizungumzia matarajio yake kwa katiba zote kuheshimiwa na zoezi la kuwasikiliza wapiga kura kufanyika katika mazingira yenye uwazi wa kutosha."

eng: Now it is clear from Sunday's constitutional referendum that Denis Sassou-Nguesso, doesn't respect the constitution nor can he offer undisputed transparency.
swa: Sasa ni wazi baada ya kura ya maoni ya Jumapili kwamba Denis Sassou-Nguesso, haheshimu katiba wala kuweka uwazi usio na shaka.

eng: Taube added that this position will force government and opposition to dig their heels in as a political crisis continues to simmer in the country:
swa: Taube aliongeza kwamba upinzani utailazimisha serikali na vyama vya upinzani kuchukua tahadhari kwa sababu mgogoro wa kisiasa unaendelea kufuka nchini humo:

eng: Let's not forget: some hours before being ousted, Ben Ali of Tunisia and Blaise Compaoré of Burkina Faso did not suspect that democracy would triumph over an all-powerful statesman.
swa: Tusisahau: masaa kadhaa kabla ya kung'olewa, Ben Ali wa Tunisia na Blaise Compaoré wa Burkina Faso hawakuwa na habari kuwa demokrasia ingeshinda dhidi ya watawala wanaojiona wana nguvu zote.

eng: Young people in the Republic of Congo remain hopeful for the future, if deeply distrustful of the various political interests at play in the country.
swa: Vijana wa nchini hiyo wana matumaini na mustakabali wao, lakini hata hivyo wana wasiwasi mkubwa kwa maslahi ya kisiasa yanayotishia ustawi wa nchi yao.

eng: A trio of students, Josué Mfutila Kiangata, Aaron Malu Mukeba and Martin Nomapungu gave African news portal Waza Online their views on events in the country.
swa: Wanafunzi watatu, Josué Mfutila Kiangata, Aaron Malu Mukeba na Martin Nomapungu walitoa maoni yao kwenye tovuti ya habari za Afrika inayoitwa Waza Online kuhusu hali yamaono inavyoendelea nchini humo.

eng: Martin:
swa: Martin:

eng: Some candidates proclaim victory before the elections; they imply that the heads of the institutions which run the elections are obedient.
swa: Baadhi ya wagombea wanadai wameshinda kabla ya uchaguzi; wana maana kwamba wakuu wa taasisi zinazoendesha uchaguzi ni vibaraka wao.

eng: Yet these institutions should be neutral and independent.
swa: Lakini taasisi hizi hazikupaswa kuwa na upande na zilitakiwa kuwa huru.

eng: They are bodies made up of politicians; they come with their political allegiances.
swa: Ni vyombo vilivyoundwa na wanasiasa; vinakuwa na maslahi fulani ya kisiasa.

eng: Aaron:
swa: Aaron:

eng: I think that democratic principles are universal and that we are supposed to abide by them.
swa: Ninadhani misingi ya kidemokrasia inafanana duniani kote na kwamba tunapswa kuiheshimu.

eng: I am not with those people who think that the African hereditary system of the olden days was a good system.
swa: Sikubaliani na wale wanaofikiri mfumo wa zamani wa ki-Afrika kurithishana ulikuwa mfumo mzuri.

eng: Josué:
swa: Josué:

eng: Literature teaches us that we should organise elections against a peaceful backdrop.
swa: Fasihi inatufundisha kwamba lazima tuandae uchaguzi kubadilisha mambo.

eng: But here in Africa it doesn't work like that.
swa: Lakini hapa Afrika mambo hayaendi namna hiyo.

eng: Why?
swa: Kwa nini?

eng: Because it is a borrowed culture, a culture for Westerners that people have come to impose on Africa.
swa: Kwa sababu ni utamaduni ulioazimwa, utamaduni wa wa-Magharibi ulioletwa Afrika bila kuangalia mazingira halisi.

eng: Zone9 bloggers, together after their release.
swa: Wanablogu wa Zone9, wakiwa pamoja mara baada ya kuachiwa huru.

eng: Photo via Zone9 Facebook page.
swa: Picha kutoka ukurasa wa Facebook wa Zone9.

eng: In the wake of their acquittal and release from prison, Ethiopia's Zone9 bloggers reflect on their experience and thank their supporters.
swa: Mara baada ya kukutwa bila ya hatia na kisha kuachiwa huru kutoka gerezani, Wanablogu wa Zone9 kutoka Ethiopia wametoa tathmini kwa yale yaliyowakuta pamoja na kuwashukuru wote waliowaunga mkono.

eng: The bloggers were arrested in April of 2014 and prosecuted under Ethiopia's Anti-Terrorism Act.
swa: Wanablogu hawa waliwekwa kizuizini April, 2014 na kisha kushtakiwa chini ya sheria ya nchini Ethiopia ya kupambana na ugaidi.

eng: Five members of the group were released in July of 2015 and the remaining four were acquitted and released during the week of October 19, 2015.
swa: Wanablogu watano wa Zone9 waliachiwa huru mwezi Julai, 2015 na wengine wanne waliokuwa wamesalia hawakukutwa na kesi ya kujibu na hivyo kuachiwa huru wiki ya tarehe 19, Oktoba, 2015.

eng: Learn more about their case.
swa: Jifunze zaidi kuhusu shitaka lao.

eng: This post was collectively written by Zone9 and translated from Amharic to English by Endalk Chala.
swa: Mkala hii iliandikwa kwa ushirikiano wa Zone9 na kutafsiriwa na Endalk Chala kutoka lugha ya Kihabeshi kwenda katika lugha ya Kiingereza.

eng: Our release was as surprising as our detention.
swa: Kuachiwa kwetu huru kulikuwa kwa kushangaza kama ilivyokuwa kushikiliwa kwetu.

eng: Five of us were released after our charges were "withdrawn" in July.
swa: Watano miongoni mwetu waliachawa huru mara baada ya mashtaka yao "kufutwa" mapema mwezi Julai.

eng: The remaining four of us were released in October because we were acquitted (save for the appeal against our acquittal).
swa: Wanne tuliosalia tualiachiwa huru mapema mwezi Oktoba kwa kuwa hatukukutwa na kesi ya kujibu (hali iliyotuwezesha kukosekana kwa ushahidi dhidi yetu).

eng: Still one member of our group, Befeqadu, was released on bail and must defend himself later this year in December.
swa: Bado kuna mmoja wetu, Befeqadu, ambaye aliachiwa kwa dhamana na anapaswa kuwasilisha utetezi wake mwaka huu mwezi Disemba.

eng: Even though we were released in different circumstances, one thing makes all of us similar – our strong belief that we didn’t deserve even a single day of arrest.
swa: Pamoja na kuwa tuliachiwa huru kwa sababu tofauti tofauti, kuna jambo moja linalotufanya tushabihiane- Imani yetu thabiti kwamba, hatukustahili kutiwa kizuizini hata mara moja.

eng: Yes, it is good to be released, but we were arrested undeservedly.
swa: Ndio, ni vizuri kuachiliwa huru, lakini hatukustahili kutiwa kizuizini.

eng: All we did was write and strive for the rule of law because we want to see the improvement of our country and the lives of its citizens.
swa: Tulichokifanya kilikuwa ni kuandika na kupigania utawala wa sheria kwa kuwa tunahitaji uboreshwaji wa nchi pamoja na maisha bora kwa raia.

eng: However, writing and dreaming for the better of our nation got us detained, harassed, tortured and exiled.
swa: Hata hivyo, kuandika na kuwa na ndoto ya Taifa bora ilitupelekea kutiwa kizuizini, kudhalilishwa, kuteswa na kuishi mbali na nyumbani.

eng: Undeservedly.
swa: Haikustahili.

eng: ...writing and dreaming for the better of our nation got us detained, harassed, tortured and exiled.
swa: ...kuandika na kuwa na ndoto ya Taifa bora ilitupelekea kutiwa kizuizini, kudhalilishwa, kuteswa na kuishi mbali na nyumbani.

eng: Undeservedly.
swa: Haikustahili.

eng: It makes us happy when we hear people say they are inspired by our story.
swa: Tunafurahi pale tunaposikia kuwa watu wanatiwa hamasa kwa kupata habari zinazotuhusu.

eng: But it also makes us sad when we learn people are scared to write because they have seen what we have gone through for our writings.
swa: Hata vivyo, tunajisikia vibaya pale tunapotambua kuwa watu wanaogopa kuandika kwa kuwa wameshuhudia masahibu tuliyopitia kwa sababu ya kuandika kwetu.

eng: Our incarceration makes us experience happiness and grief at the same time.
swa: Kufungwa gerezani kumetufanya tuwe na furaha pamoja na hofu kuu kwa wakati mmoja.

eng: The bottom line is that it is good to know we have inspired people while it is saddening that people have left the public discourse as a result of our detention.
swa: Jambo la muhimu kabisa ni kuwa, ni vizuri kufahamu kuwa tumewapa watu hamasa na kwa upande mwingine inahuzunisha kuwa watu wameacha gumzo kubwa miongoni mwa raia kufuatia kushikiliwa kwetu gerezani.

eng: It is sad to know that our detention has had a chilling effect on public discourse.
swa: Inahuzunisha kufahamu kuwa kushikiliwa kwetu kulipelekea hali kukata tamaa miongoni mwa raia.

eng: We are victims of institutionalized misconduct.
swa: Sisi ni wahanga wa kukosekana kwa uwajibikaji wa makusudi.

eng: But this does not lie not beyond our ability to forgive.
swa: Lakini hili halipo mbali na uwezo wetu wa kusamehe.

eng: To our incarcerators who gave us those ordeals, even if you are not asking us for forgiveness, here we are.
swa: Kwa wale waliotufunga gerezani na ambao walitusababishia madhila haya, hata kama hautuombi msamaha, sisi hatuna kinyongo.

eng: Our incarceration made us feel our lives pass by us.
swa: Kushikiliwa gerezani kulitufanya kujisikia kuwa maisha yetu hayakuathiriwa.

eng: It is true we have missed and lost things.
swa: Nni kweli kuwa tulikosa vingi na kupoteza vingi.

eng: But we also have increased our learning curve.
swa: Lakini pia, tumeongeza wigo wetu wa kujifunza.

eng: We have learned a lot.
swa: Tumejifunza mengi sana.

eng: Our detention tells a broader story of our country.
swa: Kushikiliwa kwetu gerezani kumetupa simulizi pana sana kuihusu nchi yetu.

eng: We were able to witness the price of freedom of expression is dearly expensive.
swa: Tumeweza kushuhudia gharama ya uhuru wa kujieleza kwa namna iliyotugharimu kupita kiasi.

eng: We are firsthand witnesses of injustice.
swa: Sisi ni mashuhuda halisi wa kunyimwa haki.

eng: More than anything, we have learned that a nation which is rampant with injustice is the foremost enemy of its law abiding citizens.
swa: Kubwa kuliko yote, tumejifunza kuwa taifa lililo kithiri kwa uminywaji wa haki ndilo adui nambari moja kwa raia wanaofuata sheria.

eng: We are victims of institutionalized misconduct.
swa: Sisi ni wahanga wa kukosekana kwa uwajibikaji wa makusudi.

eng: But this does not lie not beyond our ability to forgive.
swa: Lakini hili halipo mbali na uwezo wetu wa kusamehe.

eng: To our incarcerators who gave us those ordeals, even if you are not asking us for our forgiveness, here we are.
swa: Kwa wale waliotufunga gerezani na ambao walitusababishia madhila haya, hata kama hautuombi msamaha, sisi hatuna kinyongo.

eng: And please forgive us, for we are law abiding citizens who refuse to live on your terms.
swa: Tunawaomba mtusamehe, kwa kuwa, sisi ni raia tunaofuata sheria na ambao tunakataa kuishi kwa kufuata matakwa yako.

eng: For all people who were with us both in good times and in bad times, those of you who stood by us not only in our successes but also in our failures, YOU are awesome! You are our friends, you are our family, you were our lawyers, you campaigned for us, and you defended our cause.
swa: Kwa watu wote ambao walikuwa nasi wakati wa shida na raha, wale waliokuwa nasi wakati wote siyo tu wa mafanikio bali hata pale tuliposhindwa, NINYI ni watu wazuri!Ninyi ni marafiki wetu, ninyi ni familia yetu, mlikuwa wanasheria wetu, mlitupigania, na mlitulinda.

eng: Thank you!
swa: Tunashukuru!

eng: Thank you!
swa: Tunashukuru!

eng: You all deserve our heartfelt gratitude for your actions reduced the length of our prison time and eased our boredom while we were in prison.
swa: Nyote mnastahili pongezi za dhati kabisa kwa kila mlilolifanya kwani lilipunguza muda wetu wa kukaa gerezani pamoja na kutupunguzia hali ya kukata tamaa katika kipindi tulichokuwa gerezani.

swa: Leo ni #JumanneyaKutoa, siku maalum kwa kuonesha ukarimu wa kila namna duniani kote.

eng: An article written by our Lebanese community member Joey Ayoub hours after the Paris attacks reminds us of this, and of why we at Global Voices do the work we do.
swa: Makala iliyoandikwa na mwanachama wa familia ya Global Voices mwenye asili ya Lebanoni Joey Ayoub masaa machache baada ya shambulio la Paris inatukumbusha jambo hili, na sababu ya sisi wa Global Voices kufafanya kile tunachokifanya.

eng: In The Streets of Paris Are as Familiar to Me as the Streets of Beirut, Joey writes movingly about "the general failure of humanity’s imagination to see itself as a unified entity."
swa: Katika makala ya Mitaa ya Paris Inavyonikumbusha Mitaa ya Beirut, Joey anaandika kwa ustadi kuhusu "kushindwa kwa sisi binadamu kujitazama kwa sura ya usawa."

eng: He adds:

eng: It is a hard thing to realize that for all that was said, for all the progressive rhetoric we have managed to create as a seemingly united human voice, most of us members of this curious species are still excluded from the dominant concerns of the 'world'.
swa: Ni vigumu kuelewa kwamba kwa yote yaliyosemwa, kwa maneno matupu tuliyoweza kuyatamka kwa jina la ‘mshikamano na wahanga’, wengi wetu tulio binadamu kama wengine tunatengwa na kelele hizi hewa za mshikamano wa kile kinachoitwa ‘dunia’

swa: Kila siku katika Global Voices wahariri na waandishi pamoja na watafsiri wetu wa kujitolea wanafanya kazi kuvuka mipaka ya nchi zao, saa za mahali waliko na kuvuka viambaza vya lugha kukuletea habari zinazotokana na sauti za wananchi wa kawaida ambazo kwa kawaida hazithaminiwi sana vyombo vikuu vya habari, kukuleta taarifa za uhuru wa kujieleza mtaoni na kuwaunga mkono wale wote wanaoungana na majadiliano haya ya mtandaoni.

eng: Your donations help cover the cost of server space, administrative expenses, our microgrant programs and Global Voices staff.
swa: Mchango wako utatusaidia kulipia gharama za kuwa mtandaoni, gharama za uendeshaji, miradi midogo ya ufadhili na wafanyakazi wa Global Voices.

eng: Afghan school children in Iran have been the subject of abuse and mistreatment.
swa: Watoto wa Afghanistan wanaosoma nchini Iran wanakabiliwa na udhalilishwaji na unyanyaswaji.

eng: Photo from ICHRI and used with permission.
swa: Picha kutoka ICHRI na imetumiwa kwa ruhusa.

eng: On January 5, 2016 Shargh newspaper reported that the principal of a school in Damavand beat five young Afghan students with a hose and left marks on their faces and bodies, telling them, “You Afghans have to leave.
swa: Mnamo Januari 5, 2016 gazeti la Shargh lilitaarifu kuwa, mkuu wa shule huko Damavand aliwapiga wanafunzi wadogo raia wa Afghanistan kwa kutumia mpira wa kupitishia vitu kama maji na kuacha alama kwenye nyuso na miili yao, huku akiwaambia, "Ninyi raia wa Afghanistani, mnatakiwa kuondoka.

eng: There are too many of you.” Afghan students are being subjected to physical punishment and discrimination in Iranian schools, according to media reports in Iran that the government has tried to suppress.
swa: Mpo wengi sana" Wanafunzi wa Afghanistan wanakabiliana na udhalilishaji kimwili pamoja na kunyanyapaliwa katika shule nyingi za nchini Iran, hii ni kwa mujibu wa vyombo vya habari vya Iran na kwamba serikali imekuwa ikijaribu kuficha matukio haya.

eng: “News about abused students in general, and Afghan students in particular, only pop up in the media by accident because the monitoring agencies and the Education Ministry try to suppress these incidents,” Shirzad Abdollahi, an expert in Iranian educational affairs, told the International Campaign for Human Rights in Iran.
swa: “Kwa ujumla, habari kuhusu kuonewa kwa wanafunzi, na hususani wanafunzi raia wa Afghanistan, huwa zinaonekana kwa bahati sana kwenye vyombo vya habari kwa kuwa mamlaka za ufuatiliaji na Wizara ya Elimu imejaribu kufifisha matukio haya,” Shirzad Abdollahi, ambaye ni mtaalam wa masuala ya elimu nchini Iran aliiambia asasi ya Kimataifa ya Kutetea Haki za Binadamu ya nchini Iran.

eng: Iran is host to one of the largest refugee populations in the world, with 950,000 Afghans registered in 2015, according to the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).
swa: Nchini Iran kuna kambi ya wakimbizi inayoaminika kuwa ni moja ya kambi zenye idadi kubwa ya wakimbizi ambapo raia 950, 000 wa Afghanistan walijiandikisha kwa mwaka 2015, hii ni kwa mujibu wa Kamishana wa Umoja wa Mataifa anayeshughulikia wakimbizi (UNHCR).

eng: The mistreatment of Iranian children in schools, whether it is bodily punishment or verbal abuse and humiliation, is common in Iran, according to Abdollahi, but it is worse for Afghan children because they have fewer protections.
swa: Uonevu dhidi ya watoto wa Afghanistan mashuleni, bila kujali kama ni wa kudhuru mwili, maneno ya uonevu au udhalilishaji, kwa mujibu wa Abdollahi, mambo haya yamezoeleka nchini Iran, hata hivyo, hali ni mbaya sana kwa raia wa afghanistan ambao wana watu wachache wa kuwatetea.

eng: The educational system tends to deal with these incidents without punishing abusive staff, and they try to hide it from the press, he told the Campaign.
swa: Wakati wa Kampeni ya kutetea haki za binadamu, Abdollahi aliweka bayana kuwa mamlaka za elimu zinajaribu kufuatilia matukio haya bila ya kuwawajibisha wahusika, na pia wanajaribu kuficha matukio haya yasiandikwe au kutangazwa kwenye vyombo vya habari.

eng: Many undocumented Afghan children also face bureaucratic obstacles that prevent them from attending school, a violation of international law that guarantees the right to education.
swa: Watoto wengi wa Afghanistan wasiofahamika pia wanakabiliwa na vikwazo vya kiukiritimba vinavyowakosesha fursa ya kupata elimu, jambo ambalo ni kinyume na haki ya Kimataifa ya kuhakikisha kila mtu anapata elimu.

eng: An Afghan student from the city of Pakdasht was beaten and expelled from school for not paying tuition, according to the most recent report appearing January 16, 2016 in the Vaghaye Ettefaghiehnewspaper.
swa: Mwanafunzi wa Afghanistan kutoka katika jiji la Pakdasht alipigwa na kufukuzwa shule kwa kushindwa kulipa ada ya masomo, hii ni kwa mujibu wa taarifa ya hivi karibuni iliyotolewa mapema tarehe 16 Januari 2016 kwenye gazeti la Vaghaye Ettefaghieh.

eng: The parents were only able to afford one million rials (about $33) of the 2.3 million rials ($76) demanded by the school.
swa: Wazazi walikuwa na uwezo wa kutoa fedha za Iran, riali milioni moja (sawa na dola za Marekani 33) kati ya riali milioni 2.3 (sawa na dola za Marekani 76) zilizopaswa kulipwa shuleni hapo.

eng: The student was told not to come back to school until tuition was paid in full.
swa: Mwanafunzi huyu aliambiwa asirudi shuleni hadi hapo kiasi chote cha fedha kitakapolipwa.

eng: Following the January incident in Damavand, one of the parents told Sharg newspaper,
swa: Kufuatia tukio la Damavand la mwezi Januari, mmoja wa wazazi alizungumza na gazeti la Sharg na kusema,

eng: We went and complained to the district’s school administration and they sent an investigator to the school.
swa: Tulipeleka malalamiko yetu kwa uongozi wa elimu hali iliyopelekea kutumwa kwa mtu wa kuchunguza shule iliyohusika.

eng: But after all that, the school’s headmaster told us it was better not to drag things out further...He said our kids were being rowdy and they caused the principal to get angry.
swa: Hata hivyo, pamoja na juhudi hizi, mkuu wa shule alitueleza kuwa haikuwa vyema kuchukua hatua za juu namna ile... Alisema kuwa, watoto wetu walikuwa wakipiga kelele kiasi cha kumfanya mkuu wa shule kujawa na hasira.

eng: Last year a teacher from another school in Pakdasht punished four Afghan elementary students by forcing them to put their hands inside a toilet, according to a February 10, 2015 report from Tabnaknews.
swa: Mwaka uliopita, mwalimu mmoja wa shule moja iliyopo Pakdasht aliwaadhibu watoto wanne raia wa Afghanistan waliokuwa wakisoma shule ya msingi kwa kuwalazimisha kushika uchafu chooni, hii ni kwa mujibu wa ripoti ya Februari 10, 2015 ya gazeti la Tabnak.

eng: “The mistreatment of Afghan students is not systematic within the educational system but rather it’s at the school level, depending on the personal beliefs of the headmasters, principals or teachers,” Abdollahi told the Campaign.
swa: Kwenye kampeni ya kutetea haki za binadamu, Abdollahi alisema, “Udhalilishaji wa wanafunzi raia wa Afghanistan siyo wa mfumo mzima wa elimu, bali umekithiri mashuleni kulingana na mtazamo binafsi wa wakuu wa shule na walimu”.

eng: Teachers and administrators are not sufficiently trained about children’s rights, he added.
swa: Abdollahi aliongeza kuwa, walimu na viongozi hawana mafunzo ya kutosha kuhusiana na haki za watoto.

eng: In the short-term, there should be better monitoring of headmasters and teachers and any violations should be countered with greater firmness..Honorable teachers, who are more than a few, should stand up to colleagues who are abusive...The media should also raise awareness about the rights of children and make society more sensitive towards the mistreatment of students.
swa: Kwa sasa, kunahitajika ufuatiliaji wa karibu wa wakuu wa shule na walimu na pia, ukiukwaji wowote wa haki za watoto ushughulikiwe barabara. Walimu waungwana ambao ni wachache sana wasiwavumilie walimu wanaoendekeza unyanyasaji. Vyombo vya habari pia havina budi kuimarisha uelewa wa watu kuhusu haki za watoto na pia kuifanya jamii kuwa na uelewa zaidi kuhusu uonevu dhidi ya wanafunzi.

eng: “There’s no official directive condoning physical violence against Afghan students.
swa: “Hakuna matamko rasmi ya serikali yanayokemea uonevu dhidi ya wanafunzi wa Afghanistan.

eng: The problem is society’s views,” Abdollahi told the Campaign.
swa: Tatizo ni mtazamo walionao wanajamii,” Abdollahi aliweka bayana wakati wa kampeni.

eng: “A few years ago a group of families in Tehran’s Kan district rallied in front of their neighborhood school to stop Afghan students from enrolling there,” he said.
swa: “Miaka michache iliyopita, kundi la familia kadhaa katika halmashauri ya Kan, Tehran, waliandamana mbele ya shule iliyopo jirani na makazi yao wakishinikiza wanafunzi wa Afghanistan wasijiunge na shule hiyo” Abdollahi alisema.

eng: In addition to physical abuse and discrimination, Afghan students are also financially more vulnerable because their parents, most of whom are refugees, often earn less than average Iranians.
swa: Mbali na uonevu wa kimwili na udhalilishaji, wanafunzi raia wa Afghanistan wanakabiliwa pia na hatari ya kukosa mahitaji ya msingi kwani wazazi wao, wengi wao wakiwa ni wakimbizi, kwa kawaida hupata ujira mdogo kuliko raia wa kawaida wa Iran.

eng: “Since last year, the tuition issue has been somewhat resolved and schools are no longer required to demand tuition from Afghan students,” said Abdollahi.
swa: “Tangu mwaka jana, suala la ada ya shule kwa kiasi fulani lilitatuliwa kwani shule haziwatozi tena ada wanafunzi raia wa Afghanistan,” alisema Abdollahi.

eng: “They may be asked to make voluntary contributions for certain school expenses, but it’s not clear what’s voluntary and what’s not.”
swa: “Wanaweza kuombwa kuchangia michango ya hiari kwa ajili ya matumizi fulani ya shule, lakini hata hivyo, haijawekwa wazi ni michango gani ni ya lazima na ipi isiyo ya lazima.”

eng: “Nevertheless, regulations state that Afghan students have the same rights as their Iranian classmates and no one has the right to mistreat them,” he said.
swa: “Hata hivyo, kanuni zinasema kuwa Wanafunzi raia wa Afghanistan wana haki sawa na wanafunzi wenzao wa Iran na hakuna yeyote aliye na mamlaka ya kuwadhalilisha,” alisema Abdollahi.

eng: In 2011, the Education Ministry’s international affairs deputy announced that foreign students were banned from enrolling in special schools for the gifted, as well as in exemplary public schools and vocational schools, a violation of the internationally guaranteed right to higher education.
swa: Mwaka 2011, Naibu Waziri wa elimu, Masuala ya Kimataifa, alitangaza kuwa, wanafunzi wa kigeni wamezuiwa kujiunga na shule za vipaji maalum, pamoja na shule za serikali za kupigiwa mfano na shule za ufundi, hali ambayo ni ukiukwaji wa haki ya kimataifa ya kupata elimu ya juu.

eng: “Educational policies should not be subject to seasonal changes in taste or governments.
swa: “Sera za elimu hazipaswi kubadilishwa mara kwa mara kwa kuzingatia matakwa ya mtu binafsi au uongozi ulipo madarakani.

eng: Education is a recognized children’s right regardless of nationality, ethnicity, residency status or financial means,” Abdollahi told the Campaign.
swa: Elimu ni haki ya mtoto inayotambuliwa bila kujali uraia, ukabila, sehemu unayoishi au uwezo wa kifedha,” Abdollahi alitanabaisha wakati wa kampeni.

eng: “This right must be completely respected without any impact from changing governments and policies,” he said.
swa: “Haki hii haina budi kuheshimiwa kwa dhati kabisa bila ya kikwazo chochote kutokana na kubadilishwa kwa serikali au sera,” alisema Abdollahi.

eng: Abdullah Hassan, known as Fish, lived at the Dadaab refugee camp in Kenya for 23 years.
swa: Abdullah Hassan, anayefahamika kama Fish, aliishi katika kambi ya wakimbizi ya Dadaab nchini Kenya kwa miaka 23.

eng: Credit: Abdullah Hassan/Courtesy
swa: Picha kwa hisani ya: Abdullah Hassan/Courtesy

eng: This article by Rachel Gotbaum for The World originally appeared on PRI.org on February 18, 2016, and is republished here as part of a content-sharing agreement.
swa: Makala hii iliyoandaliwa na Rachel Gotbaum kwa ajili ya The World kwa mara ya kwanza ilichapishwa kwenye tovuti ya PRI.org tarehe 18 Februari, 2016, na inarudiwa kuchapishwa hapa kwa makubaliano ya kushirikiana maudhui.

eng: Abdullah Hassan, whose nickname is Fish, was 7 years old when his father was murdered by militants in Somalia.
swa: Abdullah Hassan, ambaye jina lake la utani ni Fish alikuwa na umri wa miaka 7 pale baba yake alipouawa na wanamgambo nchini Somalia.

eng: He then left Somalia and traveled to Kenya, to the Dadaab refugee camp.
swa: Na ndipo aliposafiri kuelekea kwenye kambi ya wakimbizi ya Dadaab.

eng: Along the way two of Hassan's brothers and his sister died of malnutrition.
swa: Wakiwa njiani, kaka wawili na dada yake Hassan walipoteza maisha kwa ugonjwa wa utapia mlo.

eng: When he and his mother arrived at the camp the conditions there weren't much better.
swa: Yeye na mama yake walipowasili kambini hapo, mazingira ya kambi hayakuwa yakuridhisha.

eng: The camp was created in 1992 to house 90,000 Somalis escaping their civil war.
swa: Kambi hii ilianzishwa mwaka 1992 kwa ajili ya kuwahifadhi wakimbizi 90,000 wa Somalia waliokuwa wakikimbia vita vya kiraia nchini humo.

eng: To this day, there is little plumbing or running water, and the UN Refugee Agency often cuts the already minimal food rations.
swa: Hadi sasa, kuna miundo mbinu hafifu sana ya maji au maji yanayotiririka, na pia shirika linaloshughulika na wakimbizi limepunguza sana ugawaji wa vyakula kambini hapo.

eng: Many refugees have died of hunger.
swa: Wakimbizi wengi wameshafariki kwa sababu ya kukosa chakula.

eng: There are also cholera outbreaks because of massive flooding and little sanitation.
swa: Kumekuwa pia na mlipuko wa ugonjwa wa kipindupindu kwa sababu ya idadi kubwa ya wakimbizi pamoja na mfumo hafifu wa uwekaji safi mazingira.

eng: Fish's wife died of an ulcer due to lack of proper medical care.
swa: Mke wa Fish alifariki kwa vidonda vya tumbo kutokana na kukosa matibabu stahiki.

eng: Fish's work with the Danish Refugee Council is considered volunteerism due to his refugee status.
swa: Fish kufanya kazi na Baraza la Wakimbizi la Kidenishi inachukuliwa kuwa ni kujitolea kutokana na hali ya yeye kuwa ni mkimbizi.

eng: Credit: Abdullah Hassan/Courtesy
swa: Picha kwa hisani ya: Abdullah Hassan/Courtesy

eng: The refugees are not allowed to work and very few are allowed to leave.
swa: Wakimbizi hawaruhusiwi kufanya kazi na wachache sana huruhusiwa kuondoka kambini.

eng: Fish works for the Danish Refugee Council, but it's not a job in the traditional sense: the agency provides Fish with a stipend, and considers him a volunteer.
swa: Fish anafanya kazi na Baraza la Wakimbizi la Kidenishi, lakini katika hali ya kawaida, hii siyo kazi haswa ya kumuingizia kipato: Baraza hili linampatia Fish hela ya kujikumu tu na hivyo kuchukuliwa kama mtu anayejitolea.

eng: The Dadaab camp now houses 500,000 people and is a ramshackle city the size of New Orleans.
swa: Hadi sasa, kambi ya Dadaab inawahifadhi wakimbizi 500,000 ikiwa na miundombinu chakavu sana na ukubwa wake unalinganishwa na ukubwa wa jiji la New Orleans.

eng: Recently the militant group Al Shabaab has penetrated the camp.
swa: Hivi karibuni, kikundi cha wanamgambo wa Al Shabaab kilivamia kambi hii.

eng: We experienced severe violent activities, kidnappings, shootings, killings, there were a lot of vehicles bombed, says Hassan.
swa: Tulipata mateso makali sana, kutekwa, kupigwa risasi, magari mengi yalilipuliwa Hassan anasimulia.

eng: My colleagues in the community were killed.
swa: Baadhi ya wenzangu katika jamii ile waliuawa.

eng: Fish was also targeted and had to leave for Nairobi, where he is now living illegally.
swa: Fish alikuwa ni mmoja wa watu waliokuwa wanalengwa na ilimlazimu kwenda Nairobi, ambapo anaishi hadi sasa bila ya kuwa na kibali.

eng: He is often stopped by police and must offer them bribes to avoid arrest.
swa: Mara kwa mara amekuwa akikaguliwa na polisi na amekuwa akiwapa hongo ili asikamatwe.

eng: After feeling trapped at Dadaab and in Kenya for 23 years, Fish hopes to resettle somewhere less hostile with his daughters, who still live at the camp.
swa: Baada ya kukaa kwenye kambi ya Dadaab nchini Kenya kwa miaka 23, Fish ana matumaini ya kupata mahali pengine palipo na auheni pa kuishi yeye pamoja na watoto wake wa kike ambao bado wanaishi kambini hapo.

eng: He hopes to make a new life.
swa: Anayo matumaini ya kuanza maisha mapya.

eng: “I’m optimistic that I may go out of this country Kenya and get resettled," he says.
swa: “Ninaamini kuwa ninaweza kuimaha Kenya na kupata utulivu mpya" anafafanua.

eng: It’s just about time that God has a solution for me.” 	Ni kusubiria muda tu, Mungu anajibu juu yangu.”
Fish is profiled in the new book "City of Thorns" by Ben Rawlence.
swa: Maisha ya Fish yanajumuishwa kwenye kitabu kipya "City of Thorns" cha Ben Rawlence.

eng: Read more about it here.
swa: Soma zaidi kuhusu kitabu hiki hapa.

eng: Blogging is bad for your back .. in Saudi Arabia.
swa: Kublogu kunahatarisha migongo na makalio ya watu ...nchini Saudi Arabia.

eng: Image used as part of an Amnesty International campaign to draw attention to the plight of Saudi blogger Raif Badawi, sentenced to 10 years in prison and 1,000 lashes in Saudi Arabia in 2014 for setting up a "liberal" website
swa: Picha imetumiwa kama sehemu ya kampeni ya Shirika la Amnesty International kutangaza uonevu aliokumbana nao mwanablogu wa ki-Saudia Raif Badawi, aliyehukumiwa kifungo cha miaka 10 jela sambamba na viboko 2,000 nchini Saudi Arabia mwaka 2014 kwa kosa la kutengeneza tovuti ya 'mambo ya kijinga'

eng: Saudi Arabia has sentenced a Twitter user to 10 years in prison in addition to 2,000 lashes for publishing 600 tweets "which spread atheism" on the micro-blogging site.
swa: Saudi Arabia imemhukumu mtumiaji wa mtandao wa Twita kifungo cha miaka 10 jela pamoja na viboko 2,000 kwa kuandika twiti 600 "zinazoeneza imani ya kutokutambua uwepo wa Mungu" mtandaoni.

eng: According to Saudi daily Al Watan the Twitter user, whose name was not disclosed, was sentenced by a court in Medina which found him guilty of denying the existence of God and holy scriptures, accusing prophets of lying and also ridiculing the Holy Quran.
swa: Kwa mujibu jarida la kila siku nchini humo liitwalo Al Watan mtumiaji huyo wa mtandao wa Twita, ambaye jina lake limehifadhiwa, alihukumiwa na mahakama moja mjini Medina iliyompata na hatia ya kukana uwepo wa Mungu na kuidhihaki Kurani Tukufu, kumtuhumu mtume kwa kudanganya watu.

eng: He was also fined 20,000 Riyals (5,300 US dollars).
swa: Kadhalika, amepigwa faini ya Rayali 20,000 (sawa na Dola za Marekani 5,300).

eng: The man was arrested after the Information Crimes Prevention Unit at the Committee for the Promotion of Virtue and Prevention of Vice or Saudi Arabia's religious police started monitoring his Twitter account.
swa: Mtu huyo alikamatwa baada ya kazi ya kufuatilia anayoyaandika kwenye mtandao wa twita kufanywa na Kitengo cha Kuzuia Makosa ya Habari kinachoundwa na Kamati ya Kukuza Maadili na Kuzuia Maovu au Polisi wa Kidini nchini Saudi Arabia.

eng: The newspaper adds that the man, aged 28, confessed his atheist beliefs in court and refused all attempts to make him repent, citing his right to freedom of speech.
swa: Gazeti hilo linasema kwamba mtu huyo, mwenye umri wa miaka 28, alitangaza hadharani imani yake ya kukana uwepo wa Mungu mahakamani na kukataa kata kata jaribio la kumshawishi atubu madhambi yake, kwa kutumia kisingizio cha uhuru wake wa kujieleza.

eng: He added that he was previously a Muslim, and has now renounced all religions after communicating with websites which spread atheism on the Internet.
swa: Aliongeza kwamba awali aliwahi kuwa Mwislamu na kwa sasa ameachana na dini zote baada ya kufanya mawasiliano na tovuti zinazoeneza imani ya kukana uwepo wa Mungu kupitia mtandao wa Intaneti.

eng: The court, added the newspaper, proved the accusations against the man based on his confessions and the testimony of four men who said they found the Twitter account on the man's mobile phone, and it was proved that the service operating the phone was under his name.
swa: Mahakama, linaoneza gazeti, ilithibitisha mashitaka hayo dhahiri dhidi ya mtu huyo kwa kutumia ushahidi wa aliyoyakiri mahakamani pamoja na ushahidi wa watu wanne waliosema walikutana na akaunti ya Twita kwenye simu yake, na kwamba ilithibitika kuwa yaliyokuwa yakifanyika kwa kutumia simu hiyo yalifanyika kwa jina lake.

eng: The sentence was met by a muted response online, with many just exchanging links to news stories without much commentary on it.
swa: Hukumu hiyo haikupata mwitikio mkubwa mtandaoni, isipokuwa baadhi ya watumiaji kubadilishana viungo vya habari zinazohusiana na tukio hilo bila kutolea maoni yoyote.

eng: Abdulrahman, from Egypt, warns Saudi Twitter users:
swa: Abdulrahman, anayeishi Misri, anawaonya watumiaji wa Twita wanaoishi Saudi Arabia:

eng: This is Saudi Arabia.
swa: Hii ndiyo Saudi Arabia.

eng: A 28-year-old Saudi man has been sentenced to 10 years in prison, 2,000 lashes and a 20,000 Riyal fine for atheism on Twitter.
swa: Kijana wa miaka 28 wa ki-Saudi amehukumiwa miaka 10 jela, viboko 2,000 na kuamuriwa kulipa faini ya Riyali 20,000 kwa kosa la kutokuamini uwepo wa Mungu kwenye mtandao wa Twita.

eng: Users of social media in Saudi Arabia should be careful.
swa: Watumiaji wa mitandao ya kijamii nchini Saudi Arabia lazima muwe waangalifu.

eng: You are being watched, persecuted and threatened.
swa: Mnafuatiliwa, mtaadhibiwa na kutishwa.

eng: A simple tweet could threaten your life.
swa: Twiti moja nyepesi inaweza kutishia maisha yako.

eng: What a society of ignorance and backwardness!
swa: Jamii iliyojaa ujinga na ujima kiasi gani!

eng: According to a 2001 Saudi law, "anything contravening a fundamental principle or legislation, or infringing the sanctity of Islam and its benevolent Shari’ah, or breaching public decency" is punishable by law.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Sheria ya Saudi ya 2001, "chochote kile kinachopingana na kanuni ya msingi au sheria, au kisichoonesha adabu kwa imani ya Uislamu na Shaaria, au kinachokwenda kinyume na maadili yanayokubalika" kitaadhibiwa kwa mujibu wa sheria.

eng: In 2014, the conservative kingdom, issued drastic laws which, according to Human Rights Watch, criminalises "virtually all dissident thought or expression as terrorism."
swa: Mwaka 2014, ufalme wa nchi hiyo, uliidhinisha sheria ambazo, kwa mujibu wa shirika la Human Rights Watch, zinatafsiri "kitendo chochote cha kutoa maoni yoyote huru kuwa ni ugaidi" na kutoa adhabu kali.

eng: Article 1 of the law describes as terrorism those:
swa: Ibara ya 1 ya sheria hiyo inatoa tafsiri sahihi ya maana ya ugaidi:

eng: “Calling for atheist thought in any form, or calling into question the fundamentals of the Islamic religion on which this country is based.”
swa: “Kutangaza kwa namna yoyote ile mawazo yenye kukana uwepo wa Mungu, au kuhoji hadharani misingi ya dini ya ki-Islam ambayo ndiyo nguzo ya nchi hii.”

eng: In May 2014, a criminal court in Jeddah sentenced blogger Raif Badawi to 10 years in prison and 1,000 lashes for “insulting Islam”.
swa: Mwezi Mei 2014, mahakama ya jinai mjini Jeddah ilimhukumu mwanablogu Raif Badawi kifungo cha miaka 10 jela na viboko 1,000 kwa 'kukashifu Uislamu".

eng: Badawi was prosecuted for developing “Saudi Arabian Liberals”, an online forum he launched in 2008 debating the role of religion in the country.
swa: Badawi alihukumiwa kwa kujaribu kujenga jamii wa "Wasaudi Arabia Wanaoshabikia Mabadiliko", jukwaa la mtandaoni lililoanzishwa mwaka 2008 kuendesha mijadala ya nafasi ya dini nchini humo.

eng: The then 32-year-old was also ordered to pay a one million riyals fine (approximately US$266,600).
swa: Badawi akiwa na umri wa miaka 32 wakati huo aliamuriwa kulipa faini ya Riyali milioni moja (takribani dola za kimarekani 266,600).

eng: Despite an international campaign calling for his release, Badawi is still in prison today.
swa: Pamoja na kampeni ya kimataifa inayodai kuachiwa huru kwake, Badawi bado anasota jela hadi leo.

eng: In January 2015, he was flogged 50 out of the scheduled 1,000 lashes.
swa: Mwezi Januari 2015, alichapwa viboko 50 kati ya 1,000 alivyohukumiwa.

eng: His second flogging has been postponed due to Badawi's poor health.
swa: Awamu ya pili ya zoezi la kumchapa imeahirishwa kwa muda ufuatia kuzorota kwa afya ya Badawi.

eng: Michael Niyitegeka, a respected authority on social media in Uganda.
swa: Michael Niyitegeka, mtaalam wa mitandao ya kijamii nchini Uganda.

eng: Photo from his official Twitter account, @niyimic
swa: Picha kutoka kwenye ukurasa wake wa Twitter. @niyimic

eng: On February 18, Uganda goes to the polls.
swa: Tarehe 18 Februari mwaka huu, nchi ya Uganda itafanya chaguzi.

eng: Like many countries around the world, social media has become part and parcel of political communication and conversation in Uganda.
swa: Kama ilivyo kwa nchi nyingine duniani, mitandao ya kijamii imekuwa sehemu muhimu ya mawasiliano ya kisiasa na majibizano nchini Uganda.

eng: For example, social media played a significant role during the first ever presidential debate on January 15.
swa: Kwa mfano, mitandao ya kijamii ilibeba jukumu muhimu sana wakati wa mdahalo wa aina yake kuwahi kutokea wa mapema Januari 15.

eng: The hashtag #UGDebate16 trended throughout the debate.
swa: Kiungo habari #UGDecides16 kilishika kasi wakati wote wa mdahalo.

eng: Ugandans like never before use social media tools to engage in election-related chatter.
swa: Watu wa Uganda, wanatumia sana mitandao ya kijamii pengine kuliko wakati mwingine wowote kama sehemu ya ushiriki wao kwenye mambo yanayohusu chaguzi.

eng: According to the Uganda Communication Commission, Uganda had over 11 million Internet users as of March 2015 and 1.8 million Facebook subscribers in the country of over 37 million as of Novembers 2015, while mobile subscriptions are estimated to be 19 million.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Tume ya Mawasiliano ya Uganda, hadi mwezi Machi 2015, Uganda ilikuwa na zaidi ya watumiaji wa intaneti milioni 11 na pia hadi mwezi Novemba 2015 kulikuwa na watumiaji wa mtandao wa Facebook zaidi ya milioni 37, huku watumiaji wa simu za mkononi walikadiriwa kufikia milioni 19.

eng: I spoke with Michael Niyitegeka, an accreditation consultant and an authority on social media in Uganda, to discuss the role that social media has played in this election season.
swa: Nilikutana na Michael Niyitegeka, ambaye ni mshauri mhakiki na mtaalam wa mitandao ya kijamii nchini Uganda ili kujadili mchango wa mitandao hii katika kipindi hiki cha uchaguzi.

eng: Prudence Nyamishana (PN): What has the role of social media been in this year's election in Uganda?
swa: Prudence Nyamishana (PN): Mitandao ya kijamii imekuwa na mchango gani kwenye chaguzi za mwaka huu nchini Uganda?

eng: Michael Niyitegeka (MN): Social media has taken a role that nobody anticipated it would have.
swa: Michael Niyitegeka (MN): Mitandao ya kijamii imefanya kazi kubwa sana ambayo hakuna yeyote ambaye alitegemea.

eng: Out of the blue, there is a lot of attention from all the political actors and players.
swa: Bila kutarajiwa, kumekuwa na hamasa kubwa kutoka kwa wanasiasa na wafuatiliaji wa siasa.

eng: It's like they have woken up to the reality that social media is not something that they can take for granted.
swa: Ni kama vile wamegundua kuhusu ukweli kwamba mitandao ya kijamii ni kitu ambacho hakiwezi kuchukuliwa kirahisi.

eng: And so there has been a lot of investment, a lot of people hired to run social media campaigns and candidates’ pages.
swa: Na kwa hiyo, kumekuwa na uwekezaji mkubwa, idadi kubwa ya watu wameajiriwa ili kusimamia kampeni kupitia mitandao ya kijamii pamoja na kurasa za wagombea.

eng: Therefore, the relevance and importance of social media in Uganda has gone to a different level.
swa: Kwa hiyo, umuhimu wa mitandao ya kijamii nchini Uganda umeongezeka kwa kiasi kikubwa kabisa.

eng: On the other hand, there has been what I can call amateurism because the people who hired and were hired to conduct social media campaign did not come up with clear strategies at the beginning of the campaign.
swa: Hata hivyo, kumekuwepo na kile ninachoweza kukiita kufanya kazi bila weledi kwa kuwa watu waliopewa jukumu la kuendesha kampeni za mtandaoni hawakuwa na mikakati madhubuti katika hatua za mwanzo za kampeni.

eng: As a result, some started strong and died out, others gained momentum as a the campaigns went on, but if they had planned in advance the aspirants would have had better mileage on social media.
swa: Matokeo yake, baadhi yao walianza wakiwa imara sana, na mara wakapotea, wengine walizidi kushika kasi kadiri kampeni zilivyokuwa zikiendelea, , lakini kama wangekuwa wamejipanga vizuri mapema, wafuasi wao wangalinufaika zaidi kupitia mitandao ya kijamii.

eng: Social media users in Uganda have also evolved and the number has increased.
swa: Watumiaji wa mitandao ya kijamii nchini Uganda wamechipukia na idadi yao imeongezeka.

eng: For example the number of people that have just joined Twitter during the campaign season is massive.
swa: Kwa mfano, idadi ya watumiaji wa Twittter waliojisajili hivi karibuni wakati wa kipindi cha uchaguzi ni wengi mno.

eng: Social media has claimed a position that it didn’t have in the beginning- it has become more important and more critical.
swa: Mitandao ya Kijamii imejiweka mahali ambapo hapo awali haikuwepo-imekuwa yenye umuhimu mkubwa na inayohitajika.

eng: People share real-time photos that caused some camps to 'Photoshop' crowds to give the impression to voters that they have support.
swa: Watu wanatuma mitandaoni picha halisi ambazo zinapelekea baadhi ya makundi “kughushi picha” za mikusanyiko ya watu ili kuwaonesha wapiga kura kuwa wanaungwa mkono na wengi.

eng: Social media has elevated some political personalities and events such as the presidential debate, which was closely followed and intensely debated by Ugandans because of social media.
swa: Mitandao ya kijamii imewapa nafasi wanasiasa wengi pamoja na matukio anuai ya kisiasa kama ilivyokuwa kwa mdahalo wa Urais ambao ulifuatiliwa kwa ukaribu na kujadiliwa kwa mapana sana na watu wa Uganda kupitia mitandao ya kijamii.

eng: PN: Do you think Ugandans have successfully engaged with the presidential candidates on social media?
swa: PN: Unafikiri watu wa Uganda wamefanikiwa kukutana na kuchangamana na wagombea wa kiti cha Urais kupitia mitandao ya kijamii?

eng: MN: From my observation, I think one or two presidential candidates are tweeting for themselves, the rest have hired social media teams.
swa: MN: Nionavyo mimi, kati ya mwanasiasa mmoja au wawili ndio wanaoweka taarifa kupitia Twitter wao wenyewe, wengine wote wameajiri watu wa kuwapigia kampeni kupitia mitandao ya kijamii.

eng: The candidates come up with a social media team, who come up with a Twitter handle and a Facebook page.
swa: Wagombea walitafuta watu wa kupiga kampeni kupitia mitandao ya kijamii, na watu hao ndio wakabuni kurasa za Twitter na Facebook.

eng: They basically run the campaigns on behalf of the candidate.
swa: Kimsingi, wanaendesha kampeni kwa niaba ya wagombea.

eng: You don’t get the feel of the natural person, the actual candidate behind the Twitter handle but more of a robot tweeting on what the candidate is doing.
swa: Ni vigumu kupata ladha ya mgombea halisi, ni utaratibu wa mgombea halisi kupitia Twitter, yaani ni kama roboti linalotwiti yale ayafanyayo mgombea.

eng: Have we been able to engage the camps from a machinery perspective?
swa: Tumefanikiwa kuzikutanisha kambi za kisiasa kwa mtazamo wa taratibu za kivyama?

eng: National Resistance Movement, the ruling party, has tried to organise Twitter chats but it’s also not consistent and people are not paying attention to them in terms of engagements.
swa: Chama tawala, National Resistance Movement, kimejaribu kuwa na utaratibu wa kupiga soga kupitia Twitter, hata hivyo utaratibu huu haujakuwa wa kudumu na umepelekea watu kukosa hamasa kwa sababu ya kukosekana kwa ushirikiano.

eng: For instance, when the party hosted Hon Rebecca Kadaga, the first female Speaker of Parliament in Uganda, people were just tweeting what Kadaga was saying but it would have made more sense if Kadaga was the one tweeting and having a conversation with social media users.
swa: Kwa mfano, kipindi ambacho chama kilimualika Mh. Rebecca Kadaga, ambaye ni spika wa kwanza Mwanamke nchini Uganda, watu walikuwa wakituma jumbe kupitia Twitter kuhusu kile alichokuwa akikijadili Kadaga, hata hivyo, ingekuwa na maana sana kama Kadaga mwenyewe angekuwa anapiga soga na watumiaji wa mitandao ya kijamii.

eng: I am sure this would have been different.
swa: Nina uhakika kuwa utaratibu huu ungeleta utofauti mkubwa sana.

eng: So social media engagement is something that political camps jumped on, but I don’t think that it is something that they seriously made strategies for.
swa: Kwa hiyo, matumizi ya mitandao ya kijamii ni jambo ambalo kambi za kisiasa zimelikurupukia tu, sifikiri kuwa ni jambo ambao waliliwekea mikakati ya kutosha.

eng: A screenshot of the official Twitter page for Uganda Presidential Debate.
swa: Picha kutoka kwenye ukurasa rasmi wa Twitter wa Mdahalo wa Wagombea Urais wa Uganda.

eng: The event was one of the most tweeted election-related event in Uganda's political history.
swa: Tukio hili ni moja ya matukio ya uchaguzi yaliyowahi kusambazwa kwa kiasi kibubwa kabisa kupitia Twitter katika historia ya chaguzi nchini Uganda.

eng: PN: What has been the place of social media as a propaganda tool in this election season?
swa: PN: Ni kwa kiasi gani mitandao ya kijamii imekuwa kama chombo cha kusambaza propaganda katika kipindi hiki cha uchaguzi?

eng: MN: Freedom of expression comes with responsibility to it.
swa: MN: Uhuru wa kujieleza unaambatana na wajibu wake.

eng: There are instances of irresponsible reporting and commenting on social media.
swa: Kuna wakati upotoshaji hutokea wakati wa kutoa taarifa na katika kuchangia maoni kupitia mitandao ya kijami.

eng: Candidates have an obligation to be mature and responsible enough when saying things because they are not just communicating to their supporters, but to wider audiences.
swa: Wagombea wana wajibu wa kuonesha ukomavu na kuwajibika ipasavyo pale wanapotakiwa kuzungungumza, kwa kuwa, siyo tu wanaongea na mashabiki wao, bali pia ni kwa jamii nzima.

eng: So different political parties should be responsible when putting out information, For example, when the ruling party secretary was recorded saying that those that cause confusion would have their children killed, people recorded the message and shared it widely.
swa: Kwa hiyo, vyama vya siasa vinapaswa kuwa makini vinapotoa taarifa kwa umma. Kwa mfano, Katibu wa chama tawala alikaririwa akisema kuwa, kwa yeyote ambae angesababisha mitafaruku watoto wao wangeuawa , watu walirekodi ujumbe ule na kisha kuusambaza kwa kasi.

eng: We, the users, should also be responsible and verify information before sharing it because unverified information can easily lead to chaos and political violence.
swa: Sisi watumiaji wa mitandao pia tunawajibika na kudhibitisha taarifa kabla ya kuzisambaza kwa kuwa taarifa zisizo na udhibitisho zinaweza kuwa chanzo cha vurugu na machafuko ya kisiasa.

eng: PN: How do we score in terms of freedom of expression online?
swa: PN: Tupo kwenye nafasi gani kwenye suala la uhuru wa kujieleza mtandaoni?

eng: MN: I think Ugandans still enjoy, to a greater extent, freedom of expression online.
swa: MN: Ninaona kuwa, jamii ya watu wa Uganda bado wanafurahia kwa kisasi kikubwa uhuru wa kujieleza kupitia mtandao.

eng: And I believe we cannot reach the levels of countries like Thailand that suppress media freedom online.
swa: Na pia, ninaamini kuwa hatuwezi kufikia kiwango walichofikia nchi kamaThailand ambayo inakandamiza uhuru wa habari wa mtandaoni.

eng: With the amount of liberty and freedom Ugandans enjoy on social media have, nipping it up would be a difficult task.
swa: Kwa kuzingatia haki na uhuru wanaoufurahia watu wa Uganda kwenye mitandao ya kijamii, kukandamiza uhuru huu itakuwa vigumu sana.

eng: You would just have to have shut down the Internet.
swa: Labda mtu mwenyewe aamue kuzima mtandao wa intaneti.

eng: PN: What role is social media going to play in terms of monitoring and observation on election day?
swa: PN: Mitandao ya kijamii itakuwa na mchango gani kwenye uangalizi na ufuatiliaji siku ya uchaguzi?

eng: MN: There is a side of me that thinks that the Internet is going to slow down.
swa: MN: Ninafikiri kuwa kasi ya mtandao itapungua.

eng: That’s just me.
swa: Haya ni maoni yangu.

eng: Because you see if you are the person in charge and things are not going on as expected, a couple of things might happen.
swa: Unajua nini, kama wewe ndiye msimamizi na unaona mambo yanaenda mrama, unaweza kuamua lolote.

eng: But with this wide-spread Internet, it is going to be difficult to do anything stupid.
swa: Lakini kwa jinsi mtandao wa intaneti ulivyosambaa, itakuwa vigumu sana kwa mtu kufanya jambo la kijinga kama hili.

eng: For instance there is a police truck in Mbale, a town in eastern Uganda, that was ferrying ruling party supporters, I don’t think in their wildest imagination they would have taken a photo and shared it as netizens did.
swa: Kwa mfano, kuna gari la polisi huko Mbale, mjini ulio Mashariki mwa Uganda, lilionekana kusafirisha wafuasi wa chama tawala, sidhani kuwa kwa kuzingatia kiwango chao kikubwa cha kufikiri wangeweza kupiga picha na kuisambaza kwenye mitandao ya kijamii kama walivyofanya watumiaji wa mtandao wa intaneti.

eng: There was another incident when someone from the ruling party was trying to claim on Twitter that the opposition Forum for Democratic Change ferries people to its rallies but people came out and blasted him.
swa: Kulikuwa pia na tukio jingine pale mtu mmoja kutoka chama tawala kupitia Twitter alidai kuwa chama cha upinzani, Forum for Democratic Change, kilikuwa kikisafirisha watu ili kuhudhuria mikutano yao, hata hivyo watu walijitokeza na kumpinga.

eng: To counter his claim, social media users displayed multiple shots of the incident which showed that there were in fact cows in the truck.
swa: Ili kubatilisha madai yake, watumiaji wa mitandao ya kijamii waliweka picha kadhaa za tukio hilo ambazo zilionesha katika magari hayo kulikuwa na ng’ombe.

eng: So anybody who is participating in this election has to be extremely careful.
swa: Kwa hiyo, yeyote anayehusika na uchaguzi huu, anapaswa kuwa makini.

eng: PN: What do you think will be the role of social media post-election, in terms of civic engagement?
swa: PN: Unafikiri mitandao ya kijamii itakuwa na wajibu upi mara baada ya uchaguzi, kwa kuzingatia ushiriki wa jamii?

eng: MN: Social media is going to continue growing; the space is going to continue growing more than it was in the past five years.
swa: MN: Mitandao ya kijamii itazidi kuimarika; jukwaa hili litazidi kukua ukilinganisha na miaka mitano iliyopita.

eng: We are going to have more leaders being held accountable though online activism, more people will pay attention to citizens' sentiments and concerns expressed online.
swa: Tutashuhudia viongozi wakiwajibishwa kupitia uanaharakati wa mtandaoni, watu wengi zaidi watatilia maanani hisia na mahitaji ya wananchi wanayoyaweka bayana kupitia mtandao wa intaneti.

eng: So social media is going to be an accountability tool.
swa: Kwa hiyo, mitandao ya kijamii inaenda kuwa chombo cha kuwajibisha.

eng: I will see somebody doing something and I will take a photo and share knowing it will be picked up by many other concerned citizens.
swa: Nikiona mtu anafanya jambo fulani, nitapiga piga na kuisambaza nikiwa na imani kuwa itaonwa na wengine wengi na watachukua hatua.

eng: PN: Do you have any final thoughts?
swa: PN: Una lolote la kumalizia?

eng: MN: As Ugandans on social media, we need to go beyond the semantics of followers, the semantics of the number of likes, we need to start digging deeper and deal with real issues in a more realist way and that is going to require much more than just having likes or followers.
swa: MN: Waganda kwenye mitandao ya kijamii, tunahitaji kuachana na kasumba ya kubweteka na wingi watu wanaokufuatilia, au utaratibu wa kuwa na watu wengi waliopendezwa na kile ulichokichapisha kwenye mtandao wa kijamii, tunatakiwa tufanye uchunguzi wa kina na kufanya mambo yenye tija na ambayo yatawafanya watu wasiishie tu kupendezwa au kuwa na wafuatiliaji wengi.

eng: It is important for us to look at analytics, collaborations, create valuable content for our followers.
swa: Itakuwa vizuri kama tutakuwa tunachanganua, tunashirikiana na kuandaa vitu vyenye tija kwa ajili ya wale wanaotufuatilia.

eng: We know governments, businesses and brands pay attention to social media.
swa: Tunafahamu kuwa kwa sasa, serikali, wafanyabiashara na kampuni mbalimbali zinatoa kipau mbele kikubwa sana kwenye mitandao ya kijamii.

eng: Hogwarts headmaster Professor Dumbledore reacts to the news saying "Bring it on!"
swa: Mkuu wa Hogwarts, Profesa Dumbledore avijibu vyombo vya habari kwa kusema "Uwekeni bayana!"

eng: Photo source: Hummus for Thought Facebook page
swa: Chanzo cha picha: Ukurasa wa wa Facebook wa Hummus for Thought

eng: Saudi Arabia's notorious religious police intend to give Professor Albus Dumbledore, the headmaster of Hogwarts, a run for his money.
swa: Polisi watukutu wa nchini Saudi Arabia wanatarajia kupata utaalam wa masuala ya uchawi kama ule alionao Profesa Albus Dumbledore, ambaye ni mkuu wa shule ya Hogwarts.

eng: Thirty members of the Commission for the Protection of Virtue and Prevention of Vice have just completed a five-day course which will enable to them to fight black magic, identify sorcerers and even break their spells.
swa: Wajumbe thelathini wa Tume ya Kusimamia Maadili na Kukabiliana na Maovu wamehitimu mafunzo ya siku tano ambayo yanatarajiwa kuwawezesha kukabiliana na uchawi, kuwatambua walozi na hata kuvunja laana zao.

eng: Needless to say, practicing magic is strictly prohibited in the deeply conservative kingdom, where those convicted of witchcraft and sorcery are executed.
swa: Bila hata kusemwa, kujihusisha na uchawi ni jambo linalopingwa vikali kwenye Falme za Wahafidhina halisi, ambapo yeyote atakayekutwa na hatia ya kujihusisha na uganga na ulozi ananyongwa.

eng: From the UAE, commentator Sultan Al Qassemi quips:
swa: Kutoka Umoja wa Falme za Kiarabu,UAE, mchambuzi Sultan Al Qassemi anasema:

eng: @jk_rowling Harry Potter and the Dark Kingdom.
swa: @jk_rowling Harry Potter na Ufalme Uliojificha.

eng: Please make it happen.
swa: Tafadhali hakikisha hili linatokea.

eng: But Hassan Cha says training the religious police is a "twisted version of Harry Potter":
swa: Pia, Hassan Cha anasema kuwa kuwapatia mafunzo haya polisi wa kidini ni "toleo la Harry Potter lililosanifiwa":

eng: Harry Potter aside, it seems that such training programmes have been ongoing for a while.
swa: Ukiweka pembeni Harry Potter, inaonekana kuwa programu kama hizi zilishaanza kitambo.

eng: One user on Facebook shares a post from 2013 for a similar workshop.
swa: Mtumiaji mmoja wa Facebook alichapisha makala iliyoandikwa mwaka 2013 iliyokuwa inazungumzia mafunzo yanayofanana na haya.

eng: In fact, combating sorcery is one of five main areas religious police should focus on in doing their work.
swa: Kiuhaliasia, kupambana na ulozi ni moja ya maeneo muhimu matano ambayo polisi wa kidini wanapaswa kuyashughulikia wawapo kwenye majukumu yao.

eng: The other four are: "preserving Islam, preventing blackmail, fighting human trafficking, and ensuring that no one disobeys the country’s rulers."
swa: Mambo mengine manne ni: "kuulinda Uislam, kuzuia kushurutisha mtu kutoa taarifa zake, kupambana na usafirishaji haramu wa binadamu pamoja na kuhakikisha kuwa hakuna yeyote anayekaidi kuwatii watawala."

eng: Zimbabwe's President Robert Mugabe turned 92 this month.
swa: Rais wa Zimbabwe Robert Mugabe atimiza miaka 92 mwezi huu.

eng: Public domain photo by the U.S. Air Force.
swa: Picha ya Wazi na U.S. Air Force.

eng: Zimbabwe's President Robert Mugabe, nicknamed 'Uncle Bob', turned 92 on February 21.
swa: Rais wa Zimbambwe Robert Mugabe, akifahamika kwa jina la utani 'Anko Bob', alitimiza miaka 92 tarehe 21 Februari mwaka huu.

eng: He is the world's oldest president, holding office since 1987.
swa: Yeye ndiye Rais aliyekula chumvi nyingi kuliko Marais wengine wote duniani , na amekuwa madarakani tangu mwaka 1987.

eng: His time in the upper echelons of Zimbabwe's government isn't limited to his 30-year stint as president; he also was Zimbabwe's prime minister from 1980 to 1987.
swa: Muda wake wa kutumikia nyadhifa za juu serikalini haukomei tu kwenye miaka 30 akiwa kama Rais. Aliwahi pia kuwa waziri mkuu wa Zimbabwe kati ya mwaka 1980 na 1987.

eng: According to human rights organisations such as Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch Mugabe's government regularly mistreats opposition politicians and their supporters, journalists, civil society activists and human rights defenders.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa mashirika ya kutetea haki za binadamu ya Amnesty International na Human Rights Watch, Serikali ya Mugabe mara kwa mara imekuwa ikiwatendea isivyo wapinzani na wafuasi wao, waandishi wa habari, mashirika ya kiraia pamoja na wanaharakati wa haki za binadamu.

eng: Human Rights Watch's World Report 2015 pointed out that, "The government of President Robert Mugabe continued to violate human rights in 2014 without regard to protections in the country’s new constitution.
swa: Taarifa ya kimataifa ya shirika la Human Rights Watch ya mwaka 2015 ilibainisha kuwa , "Serikali ya Rais Robert Mugabe ilibobea katika kukiuka haki za binadamu katika kipindi cha mwaka 2014 bila kujali kifungu cha sheria kwenye katiba mpya ya Zimbabwe kinacholinda haki za raia.

eng: An expected legislative framework and new or amended laws to improve human rights in line with the constitution never materialized."
swa: Serikali ya Mugabe haijawahi kusimamia utekelezaji wa kisheria uliotarajiwa sambamba na sheria mpya au zilizoboreshwa kwa minajili ya kusimamia haki za binadamu kulingana na matakwa ya katiba."

eng: Mugabe is also accused by Zimbabwe's opposition and the international community of systemic electoral fraud.
swa: Kadhalika, Mugabe analaumiwa na wapinzani wa nchi hiyo pamoja na Jamii za Kimataifa kwa mwendelezo wa Udanganyifu wa Kimfumo wakati wa Chaguzi za Kisiasa.

eng: Online, Twitter users have been sharing facts about and quotes from a man known for his oratory skills, brashness, sense of humor, homophobia and hatred for the West.
swa: Kwenye mitandao ya kijamii, watumiaji wa Twitter wamekuwa wakisambaza taarifa na nukuu za Mhe Mugabe anayeulikana sana kwa uwezo wa kuzungumza, hasira, vichekesho, chuki dhidi ya wapenzi wa jinsia moja na utamaduni wa ki-Magaharibi.

eng: I have died many times. 	Nimeshafariki mara nyingi sana.
I have actually beaten Jesus Christ because he only died once."
swa: Na kwa kweli, nimemshinda hata Yesu Kristo kwa kuwa yeye alikufa mara moja tu."

swa: Robert Mugabe.

swa: Heri ya siku ya kuzaliwa mjomba — Sammy Netsh (@Sammy_Livhu) Februari 21, 2016

swa: Mugabe alitoa kauli hii wakati wa sherehe yake ya kukumbuka miaka 88 ya kuzaliwa, kufuatia kuzushiwa kifo mara kwa mara.

swa: Hatukuwafukuza wazungu, tulichokifanya ni kuchukua ardhi yetu Rais Robert Mugabe — Sivuyile Fanatic (@MndaweSivuyile) February 21, 2016

eng: Mugabe chased white Zimbabwean farmers from the country from the year 2000 as part of his land reform and black empowerment program.
swa: Mugabe aliwafukuza wakulima wazungu raia wa Zimbabwe waliokuwa wakihodhi ardhi nchini humo mwaka 2000 ikiwa ni mpango wake wa mageuzi ya ardhi na utoaji fursa kwa raia weusi.

eng: A total of 4,000 white farmers lost their farms.
swa: Jumla ya wakulima wazungu 4,000 walipoteza mashamba yao.

eng: Mugabe made the observation after the United Nations chief Ban Ki-moon urged African leaders not to cling to power.
swa: Mugabe hakukosa cha kusema kujibu kauli ya Katibu Mkuu wa Umoja wa Mataifa Ban Ki-moon ya kuwataka Marais wa Afrika kuacha kung'ang'ania madaraka.

eng: “Let me marry you first, if you want me to accept homosexuality in my country.”
swa: “Ngoja nianze kukuoa wewe kwanza ndio niruhusu mahusiano ya jinsia moja nchini mwangu.”

swa: Robert Mugabe alipomjibu Barak Obama. — IG: AdvBarryRoux (@Barry_Roux) Februari 21, 2016

eng: Mugabe is reported to have made the statement after US President Barack Obama called on African governments to give gay men and women equal marriage rights.
swa: Imetaarifiwa kuwa, Mugabe alitoa kauli hii kufuatia Rais wa Marekani Barack Obama kuwataka viongozi Afrika kutoa haki sawa kwa wanaume na wanawake wanaoshiriki mapenzi ya jinsia moja.

eng: In 2011, Mugabe referred to gay people as being "worse than dogs and pigs."
swa: Mwaka 2011, Mugabe aliwaelezea watu wanaoshiriki mapenzi ya jinsia moja kuwa ni "wa hovyo kuliko hata mbwa na nguruwe."

eng: ‘The white man is here as a second citizen.
swa: ‘Mzungu yupo hapa kama raia mbadala.

eng: The only man you can trust is a dead white man.’ ~Robert Mugabe — AFRICAN HISTORY (@africanarchives) February 21, 2016
swa: Mzungu pekee unayeweza kumwamini ni yule aliyekwisha fariki.’ ~Robert Mugabe — AFRICAN HISTORY (@africanarchives) February 21, 2016

eng: The quote is widely attributed to him by many sources online including a 2015 article by the Mayor of London Boris Johnson.
swa: Vyanzo vingi vya mtandaoni ikiwa ni pamoja na Makala ya 2015 iliyoandikwa na Meya wa London Boris Johnson, vinamuhusisha Rais Mugabe na msemo huu.

eng: Speaking at the opening of the annual African Union summit in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, last month, Mugabe said the UN’s headquarters in New York should be in a more populous country, such as China, India, or in Africa.
swa: Akiongea kwenye mkutano wa kila mwaka wa Umoja wa Afrika huko Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, mwezi uliopita, Mugabe alisema makao makuu ya Umoja wa Mataifa uliopo New York yalipaswa yajengwe kwenye nchi zilizo na idadi kubwa zaidi ya watu kama vile China, India au barani Afrika.

swa: Tumewasamehe, lakini pengine hatujajitendea haki...

swa: Mliunda ICC , nasi hatuna budi kuanzisha mahakama yetu ya kuwashitaki wazungu, kuwashitaki akina Bush na Blair."

eng: Fun fact: When Robert Mugabe was born the Ottoman Caliphate still existed.
swa: Ukweli unaofurahisha: Kipindi Robert Mugabe alipozaliwa, Milki ya Khalifa ya Uturuki bado ilikuwepo.

swa: Pia, amekuwa madarakani kwa miaka 6 zaidi ya miaka aliyoishi Steve Biko. — Imran Garda (@ImranGarda) Februari 21, 2016

eng: The Ottoman Caliphate was the last Sunni Islamic caliphate of the late medieval and the early modern era.
swa: Milki ya Kahalifa ya Uturuki ilikuwa ndio Milki ya Khalifa ya mwisho ya Kiislam ya dhehebu la Sunni ya kipindi cha mwisho za zama za kati na kipindi cha mapema cha zama mpya.

eng: The Turkish National Assembly abolished the Ottoman Caliphate on March 3, 1924.
swa: Bunge la Uturuki lilikomesha milki ya Khalifa ya Uturuki mnamo tarehe 3 Machi, 1924.

eng: Steve Biko was an anti-apartheid activist in South Africa who died in 1977 at the age of 30.
swa: Steve Biko alikuwa ni mwanaharakati wa kupinga ubaguzi wa rangi nchini Afrika ya Kusini ambaye alifariki mwaka 1977 akiwa na umri wa miaka 30.

eng: Robert Mugabe is the most academically honored President in the world.
swa: Robert Mugabe ndiye Rais aliyesoma zaidi kuliko Marais wengine wote duniani.

eng: No other president has more university degrees than him. #factcheck — p.Brobbey (@PrinceBaaRCa) February 21, 2016
swa: Hakuna Rais mwingine aliye na idadi kubwa ya shahada za vyuo vikuu kama yeye. #factcheck — p.Brobbey (@PrinceBaaRCa) February 21, 2016 Robert Mugabe ndiye Rais aliyesoma zaidi kuliko Marais wengine wote duniani.

eng: Mugabe has got seven degrees.
swa: Mugabe ana shahada saba.

eng: He graduated with a bachelor of arts degree from the University of Fort Hare, South Africa, before getting four bachelor's degrees and two master's degrees through distance learning.
swa: Alihitimu shahada ya sanaa katika chuo kikuu cha Fort Hare, Afrika Kusini kabla ya kuhitimu tena shahada nne na shahada mbili za umahiri kwa njia ya elimu kwa masafa.

eng: American journalist Anna Therese Day was arrested in Bahrain for covering protests to mark the fifth anniversary of Arab Spring-like protests which still continue.
swa: Mwanahabari wa Marekani, Anna Therese Day alitiwa nguvuni nchini Bahrain alipokuwa akiripoti maandamano ya kumbukumbu ya miaka mitano ya maandamano ya mageuzi ya Uarabu mpya yanayozidi kushamiri.

eng: Photograph shared on social media after Day's arrest (Photo source: frontlinefreelance.org)
swa: Picha iliyopakiwa kwenye mitandao ya kijamii mara baada ya Day kukamatwa(Chanzo cha picha: frontlinefreelance.org)

eng: American award winning journalist Anna Therese Day was arrested in Bahrain, along with three of her crew members, also American, for covering protests to mark the country's fifth anniversary of Arab Spring-like protests, which still continue today.
swa: Mwanahabari wa Marekani aliyejizolea tuzo Anna Therese Day alishikiliwa nchini Bahrain akiwa na wenzake watatu ambao pia ni raia wa Marekani kwa sababu ya kuripoti maandamano ya kumbukumbu ya miaka mitano ya maandamano ya mageuzi ya Uarabu mpya nchini Bahrain.

eng: She was deported on February 16, along with her crew, after spending a day in detention.
swa: Mapema tarehe 16 Februari, Day na wenzake walilazimishwa kurudi nchini mwao mara baada ya kushikiliwa kwa siku moja.

eng: The team was arrested during a demonstration in Sitra, and charged with taking part in an illegal protest and entering the country under a false pretext.
swa: Wanahabari hawa walishikiliwa wakati wa maandamano ya huko Sitra na kutuhumiwa kwa kushiriki maandamo yasiyo rasmi pamoja na kuingia nchini Bahrain kwa udanganyifu.

eng: In a series of tweets, the Bahraini Ministry of Interior accuses Day and her crew of taking part in "illegal" protests:
swa: Kwa mfululizo wa jumbe za Twitter, Wizara ya Mambo ya Ndani ya Bahrain inamtuhumu Day pamoja na wenzake kwa kushiriki kwenye maandamano “yasiyo halali”:

eng: Four Americans have been arrested after one of them was caught with his face covered during his participation with rioters in Sitra
swa: Raia wanne wa Marekani wanashikiliwa mara baada ya mmoja wao kukutwa akishiriki kwenye maandamano pamoja na waandamanaji na akiwa amejifunika uso wake huko Sitra

eng: The rest were arrested at a police checkpoint in the same area
swa: Waliobaki walikamatwa katika kituo cha uangalizi cha polisi katika eneo hilo la Sitra

eng: Those arrested entered Bahrain on February 11 and 12 and presented wrong information to the concerned authorities claiming that they came to Bahrain for tourism
swa: Waliokamatwa waliingia nchini Bahrain kati ya Februari 11 na 12 na kutoa taarifa za uongo kwa mamlaka husika wakidai kuwa walifika nchini Bahrain kwa ajili ya kutalii

eng: Those arrested worked in media without a permit in addition to committing acts which break the law.
swa: Walioshikiliwa walikuwa wakijihusisha na uandishi wa habari bila ya kibali na pia kufanya mambo ambayo ni kinyume na sheria.

eng: Legal action has been taken against them and they have been referred to the public prosecutor.
swa: Taratibu za kisheria zimeshachukuliwa dhidi yao na wameshafikishwa kwa mwendesha mashtaka wa serikali.

eng: Accusing journalists of breaking the law for covering news is not new to Bahrain.
swa: Mashitaka dhidi ya waandishi wa habari ya kuvunja sheria kwa sababu ya kukusanya habari siyo jambo geni nchini Bahrain.

eng: More recently, photojournalist Ahmed Al Fardan was sentenced to three months in prison for taking photographs of protests.
swa: Hivi karibuni, mwnahabari mpiga picha Ahmed Al Fardan alihukumiwa kwenda jela miezi mitatu kwa kupiga picha maandamano.

eng: He was charged with "intent" to protest.
swa: Alituhumiwa kwa kosa la "kutaka" kuandamana.

eng: Accusing journalists of taking part in protests was not lost on activists and friends who raised the alarm after Day's arrest.
swa: Kuwatuhumu waandishi wa habari kushiriki kwenye maandamano ni jambo ambalo halikuachwa nyuma na wanaharakati na marafiki waliopaza sauti zao mara baada ya kushikiliwa kwa Day.

eng: On Twitter, journalist C. Robert Gibson appealed to his followers to make noise:
swa: Kupitia Twitter, mwandishi wa habari C. Robert Gibson aliwaomba marafiki wake wasikae kimya kuhusu tukio hili:

swa: Bahrain imemshikilia rafiki na mfanyakazi mwenzangu @ATDLive kwa kosa la kutimiza wajibu wake kama mwandishi wa habari.

swa: Sambaza habari hizi kwa marefu na mapana: https://t.co/bZbN5m5qXz #FreeAnnaDay — C. Robert Gibson (@crgibs) Tarehe 16 Februari, 2016

swa: Uandishi wa habari nchini Bahrain ni kosa la jinai.

swa: Mwandishi wa habari wa Bahrain Nazeeha Saeed anafahamu.

swa: Siyo tu kwamba walimfanyia ukatili kutokana na kutimiza wajibu wake, lakini waliomfanyia ukatili walionekana hawakuwa na hatia.

eng: Just like this.
swa: Hivyo tu.

swa: Kupigwa ngumi, mateke akiwa amefunikwa macho. Simulizi ya ukatili dhidi ya Nazeeha ni moja ya matukio mengi nchini #Bahrain: https://t.co/MgHKJCqwiD pic.twitter.com/ltdqybS5Xf — Amnesty Bahrain (@aibahrain) Tarehe 15 Februari, 2016

eng: James Lynch, deputy director of the Middle East and North Africa Programme, said:

eng: Today in Bahrain, anyone who dares to criticize the authorities – whether a human rights defender or political activist – risks punishment Despite pledges from the authorities to prosecute security forces responsible for human rights violations in 2011, the Bahraini people are still waiting for justice.
swa: Kwa hali ilivyo sasa nchini Bahrain, kwa yeyote anayejaribu kuikosoa serikali- ama iwe ni mwanaharakati wa haki za binadamu au mwanasiasa-anajitakia mateso Mbali na serikali kuahidi kuvishitaki vyombo vya dola vilivyohusika na vitendo vya uvunjaji wa haki za binadamu mwaka 2011, watu wa Bahrain bado wanatumaini kuwa haki itatendeka.

eng: Institutions set up to protect human rights have not only failed to independently investigate or hold perpetrators to account, but now increasingly appear to be used to whitewash continuing abuses.
swa: Taasisi zinazojitokeza kutetea haki za binadamu siyo tu zimeshindwa kufanya uchunguzi huru, au hata kuwawajibisha wahusika, kwa sasa baadhi ya taasisi hizi zinaonekana kutumika kufunika maovu yanayoendelea kutendeka.

eng: Five years on, demonstrations continue, but are smaller and quieter.
swa: Miaka mitano sasa, maandamano yanaendelea, lakini ni ya wastani na ya ukimya .

eng: Today, protesting, or rather “gathering”, is criminalized by law and villages are under day-and-night security watch.

eng: On February 18, Ugandans voted in presidential, parliamentary and local elections tainted by violence, protests, arrests and reports of rigging.
