eng: Also, many trained journalists also contribute, which increases their skills and online exposure.
swa: Pia, waandishi wengi kitaaluma wamekuwa wakichangia katika tovuti hii hivyo kuongeza na kuukuza ujuzi wao na kuwaongezea wigo mpana na uzoefu wa masuala ya mtandaoni.

eng: Write a 200-words news story (or submit a new photo with a short description) answering the questions: What event?
swa: Andika habari yenye maneno 200 (au tuma picha mpya ikiwa na maelezo machache) ukijibu maswali yafuatayo: Ni tukio gani hilo?

eng: Where and when did it happen?
swa: Limetokea wapi na lini?

eng: Who was involved?
swa: Ni nani mhusika au wahusika wa tukio hilo?

eng: How did the event occur?
swa: Tukio hilo lilitokeaje?

eng: Why is it noteworthy?
swa: Kwa nini inastahili kupewa kipaumbele?

eng: The site has identified three examples of good local stories for new writers.
swa: Wavuti hii imeonesha mifano mitatu ya habari nzuri za wenyeji kutoka kwa waandishi wapya.

eng: One of the stories is about a Kenyan man, Lawrence Gekonge, who buried his wife in the kitchen after she passed away because she used to spend most of her time there.The man says that he should be buried in the sitting room of the main house when he dies.
swa: Moja kati ya habari hizo ni ile inayohusu mwanaume mmoja wa Kenya Lawrence Gekonge, aliyemzika mkewe jikoni baada ya kuaga dunia; kwa sababu, mkewe alipenda kutumia muda wake mwingi akiwa jikoni. Mwanaume huyo ameusia kuwa naye pia akiaga dunia angependa azikwe katika sebule ya nyumba yake kubwa.

eng: The second story is about citizen reporter, Dickens Luvanda, who has managed to consistently publish over 50 stories a week.
swa: Habari ya pili ni kuhusu mwandishi mzawa, Dickens Luvanda, aliyeweza kuandika kwa mfululizo na kwa bidii kubwa habari zipatazo 50 kwa wiki.

eng: The third one is about 1,200 title deeds lying uncollected at the Lands Registry.
swa: Na habari ya tatu ilihusu hati miliki za ardhi zipatazo 1,200 zilizorundikwa na kuachwa bila kuchukuliwa na wenyewe katika ofisi za Usajili wa Ardhi huko Thika.

eng: The project's lead editor Enoch Nyariki told Global Voices in an email conversation that the site has so far published 61,000 stories.
swa: Mhariri Kiongozi wa mradi ndugu Enoch Nyariki aliiambia Global Voices kupitia mahojiano yaliyofanyika kwa njia ya email kuwa; tovuti hii imeshachapisha habari na makala zipatayo 61,000.

eng: He said that one of the main challenges the project is facing is having citizen reporters take advantage of free HiviSasa Academy they have set up to empower reporters with basic news writing skills. The YouTube video below is an introduction to the academy in Sheng, a mixture of Swahili and English:
swa: Alisema kuwa moja kati ya kichocheo kikubwa walicho nacho katika mradi huu ni waandishi wa kiraia kuchangamkia fursa ya bure ya Chuo cha HiviSasa kilichoanzishwa kwa ajili ya kuwawezesha waandishi kuwa na ujuzi na msingi wa awali katika uandishi wa habari.

eng: The academy offers various free lessons such as How To Interview, How to Report Court Stories, Writing Lawfully - Plagiarism/Accreditation, Writing Lawfully - Defamation/Libel, Hate Speech, etc.
swa: Chuo kinatoa masomo kadhaa bure kama vile Jinsi ya Kufanya Mahojiano, Jinsi ya Kuripoti Habari kutoka Mahakamani, Uandishi wa Kisheria- Wizi wa Maandishi, Uandishi wa Kisheria- Maandishi ya Kukashifu/Maandishi ya Kutweza, Makala za Chuki, n.k.

eng: Piloted in 2012 with the support of 88mph, which invests in start-ups, the project was launched in January 2014.
swa: Mradi huu ulianzishwa kwa majaribio mwaka 2012 kwa hisani na ushirikiano wa 88mph, ambao iwaliwekeza kwa kuanzia na mradi ulizinduliwa rasmi Januari 2014.

eng: Other investors in the project are Omidyar Network and Novastar Ventures.
swa: Wawekezaji wengine katika mradi huu ni pamoja na Omidyar Network na Novastar Ventures.

eng: Editor's note: Global Voices also receives support from Omidyar Network.
swa: Nyongeza ya Mhariri: Global Voices pia hupokea msaada kutoka Omidyar Network.

eng: Oops!
swa: Du!

eng: Facebook joined Filipinos in celebrating the Philippine Independence Day.
swa: Facebook iliungana na wa-Filipino kusherehekea Siku ya Uhuru wa Ufilipino.

eng: However, it unintentionally inverted the country's flag.
swa: Hata hivyo, ilifanya kosa la kutokukusudia kwa kugeuza bendera ya nchi hiyo.

eng: June 12 is Independence Day in the Philippines.
swa: Juni 12 ni Siku ya Uhuru nchini Ufilipino.

eng: The Philippines declared independence from Spain on June 12, 1898 after more than 300 years of colonial rule.
swa: Ufilipino ilijitwalia uhuru wake kutoka nchi ya Uhispania mnamo Juni 12, 1898 baada ya zaidi ya miaka 300 ya ukoloni.

eng: In honor of this special day, Facebook greeted Filipinos by displaying the Philippine flag.
swa: Katika kuenzi siku hiyo muhimu, Facebook iliwasalimu wa-Filipino kwa kuonesha bendera ya nchi yao.

eng: However, the flag was inverted which is only done when the country is at war.
swa: Hata hivyo, bendera hiyo ilikuwa imegeuzwa, kitendo ambacho kuashiria nchi hiyo iko vitani.

eng: Philippine Star newspaper quickly noticed the mistake:
swa: Gazeti la Star nchini humo lilibaini haraka kosa hilo:

eng: LOOK: In honor of Philippine Independence Day, Facebook's home page greets Filipino netizens with a banner of the Philippine flag—except that it's displayed with the red part at the top and the blue at the bottom, signifying the country is in a state of war.
swa: TAZAMA: Katika kuenzi Siku ya Uhuru wa Ufilipino, Ukurasa wa kwanza wa Facebook unawasalimu watumiaji wa mtandao wa Ufilipino kwa tangazo lenye bendera ya Ufilipino -bahati mbaya tu ni kwamba sehemu nyekundu ya bendera hiyo iko juu na bluu iko chini, kuonesha kwamba nchi iko vitani.

eng: Filipino Facebook users are laughing over this mistake although majority are grateful Facebook remembered to send its Independence Day greetings.
swa: Kufuatia kosa hili, watumiaji wa mtandao wa Facebook nchini Ufilipino wanacheka ingawa wengi wanaishukuru Facebook kwa kuwatumia salamu za Siku ya Uhuru.

eng: However, there are also netizens who criticized Facebook for incorrectly displaying the Philippine flag.
swa: Hata hivyo, kuna watumiaji wa mtandao wanaoikosoa Facebook kwa kuweka bendera ya nchi yao kimakosa.

eng: Below are some reactions on Facebook and Twitter:
swa: Hapa chini ni baadhi tu ya miitikio kwenye mtandao wa Facebook na Twita:

eng: Facebook user Berniemack Arellano asks if the error is a movie marketing ploy:
swa: Mtumiaji wa Facebook, Berniemack Arellano aliuliza kama kosa hilo ni ujanja wa kutangaza filamu:

eng: Dear Facebook,
swa: Wapendwa Facebook,

eng: Has the President and the Congress declared war on some country?
swa: Je, Rais na Bunge limetangaza tunaingia kwenye vita na nchi fulani?

eng: Ano to, marketing ng Independence Day: Resurgence?
swa: Mmefanya nini, mnatangaza Filamu ya Siku ya Uhuru?

eng: Has the President and the Congress declared war on some country?
swa: Je, Rais na Bunge limetangaza tunaingia kwenye vita na nchi fulani?

eng: Facebook says we're at war.
swa: Facebook inasema tuko vitani.

eng: Happy Independence Day, Philippines.
swa: Heri ya Siku ya Uhuru, Ufilipino.

eng: Dear @facebook: It's not a happy Independence Day if our flag is like this.
swa: Facebook: Bendera ionekane hivi na iwe Siku ya Uhuru.

eng: This is the correct way to display the Philippine flag.
swa: Hii ni namna sahihi ya kuonesha bendera ya Ufilipino.

eng: In the country’s history, the red banner was last displayed at the top during the Second World War in 1941 to 1945.
swa: Katika historia ya nchi hiyo, sehemu nyekundu ilionekana juu ya bluu wakati wa Vita Vikuu vya Pili vya Dunia mwaka 1941 mpaka 1945.

eng: Philippine flag.
swa: Bendera ya Ufilipino.

eng: Image from the official website of the Philippine government
swa: Picha kutoka tovuti ya serikali ya Ufilipino

eng: Je suis pineapple, or I am pineapple.
swa: Nanasi la Je suis, au mimi ni nanasi.

eng: Via Mirana (with permission)
swa: Picha ya Mirana (imetumiwa kwa ruhusa)

eng: When it comes to memes, pineapple is the new orange, at least in Madagascar.
swa: Linapokuja suala la mzaha mtandaoni, basi nanasi limekuwa kama chungwa jipya, angalau kwa nchi ya Madagaska.

eng: Social media in Madagascar has become quite pineapple-flavored over the past few days.
swa: Mitandao ya kijamii nchini Madagaska imejawa na mzaha wenye kibwagizo cha nanasi kwa siku kadhaa sasa.

eng: Why the sudden fervor for the spiky fruit?
swa: Kwa nini tunda hili lenye miiba miiba limekuwa na umaarufu wa haraka hivyo?

eng: Here is a bit of context on the current social situation on the Red Island.
swa: Hii ni sehemu tu ya hali halisi katika jamii hiyo iliyo ndani ya kisiwa hicho Chekundu.

eng: Madagascar came up as the world's poorest country in one of the poverty indices published by the World Bank (and reported by media outlets such as Radio France Internationale).
swa: Madagaska inaonekana kuwa kati ya nchi masikini zaidi duniani baada ya Benki ya Dunia kuchapisha takwimu zake na (kuripotiwa na vyombo vya habari kama vile Radio France Internationale).

eng: The criticism of the economic status of the country did not sit well with the president of Madagascar.
swa: Ukosoaji juu ya hali ya uchumi wa nchi haukumpendeza sana Rais wa Madagaska.

eng: He challenged observers, local media and citizens to "provide evidence that the country was getting poorer."
swa: Aliwaomba wachambuzi, vyombo vya habari na wananchi " kutoa ushahidi unaoonesha kuwa nchi hiyo inaendelea kuwa masikini zaidi."

eng: Malagasy netizens quickly obliged in a biting manner:
swa: Watumiaji wa mitandao ya kijamii wa ki-Malagasiharaka walilitazama suala hilo kwa namna rahisi:

eng: Is this graph here not enough evidence Mr President ? #Madagascar #WASH
swa: Je takwimu hizi si ushahidi unaojitosheleza Mheshimiwa Rais? #Madagascar #WASH

eng: Koolsaina, a Malagasy community blog, posted the following photo on its website:
swa: Koolsaina, Blogu ya kijamii ya Malagasi ilibandika picha ifuatayokatika tovuti yake:

eng: Malagasy citizens going through trash pile ups in Antananarivo.
swa: Wananchi wa Malagasi wakipekua vitu katika marundo ya takataka katika jalala huko mjini Antananarivo.

eng: Via Koolsaina
swa: Picha ya Koolsaina

eng: Following that first tense exchange between the president and Malagasy netizens, another Malagasy community website, Tananews, posted a photo of First Lady Voahangy Rajaonarimampianina wearing a a green dress with a pineapple motif on the front:
swa: Kufuatia majibizano makali yaliyotokea baina ya Rais na mitandao ya kijamii ya Malagasi, tovuti nyingine ya kijamii, Tananews, ilibandika picha ya mke wa Rais Voahangy Rajaonarimampianina akiwa amevaa nguo ya kijani ikiwa na urembo wenye picha ya nanasi kwa mbele:

eng: The Malagasy president and the first lady at an independence day ceremony.
swa: Rais wa Malagasi akiwa na mkewe katika sherehe za siku ya Uhuru.

eng: Via Tananews
swa: Picha na Tananews

eng: Tananews added a link and a comment with a hint of sarcasm that said, "Indeed, not everyone is poor in Madagascar."
swa: Tananews waliweka ukurasa mwingine ukiwa na maneno ya mzaha yaliyosema, "Hakika, sio kila mtu ni maskini hapa Madagaska."

eng: The link showed that the dress was probably designed by high-end clothing brand Dolce & Gabana that sold for US $7,745 on the website of department store Nieman Marcus (it is unclear whether that is the actually cost of the dress that the first lady was wearing).
swa: Katika ukurasa huo walionesha gauni alilovaa mke wa Rais lililobuniwa na kampuni kubwa ya ubunifu wa mavazi ya Dolce & Gabana na linauzwa dola $7,745 katika tovuti ya idara ya mauzo Nieman Marcus (hakuna uhakika kama hiyo ndio bei halisi ya gauni hilo alilovaa mke wa Rais).

eng: The outrage was swift on the Malagasy web.
swa: Kulitokea ghadhabu ya ghafla katika mitandao wa intaneti nchini humo.

eng: A flurry of memes with the hashtag #mananasy (pineapple) appeared within days on various Malagasy websites and social media.
swa: Mafuriko ya utani huo wenye alama ishara ya #mananasi yameendelea kwa siku kadhaa ndani ya tovuti mbalimbali na mitandao ya kijamii ya Malagasi.

eng: Here are a few memes that were widely shared:
swa: Hii ni baadhi tu ya mizaha iliyotumiwa na kuenezwa kwa wingi:

eng: Spoof of Facebook founder Marc Zuckerberg's profile wondering about pineapples in Madagascar.
swa: Kibonzo cha Marc Zuckerberg mwanzilishi wa Facebook akishangaaa kuhusu mananasi huko Madagaska.

eng: The meme reads, " Do you know how to wear Pineapple as they do in Antananarivo ? (play on word with a traditional folk song)" Used with permission.
swa: Kibonzo kinasomeka hivi, Je unajua jinsi ya kuvaa nanasi kama wafanyavyo huko Antananarivo ? (Cheza na maneno kwa kutumia nyimbo za asili)" Imetumika kwa ruhusa.

eng: Beggar: "Can I have US $7,000 please?"
swa: Ombaomba: "Tafadhali, je naweza kupata dola 7,000?"

eng: First lady: "I have no pineapple for you."
swa: Mke wa Rais: "Sina nanasi kwa ajili yako."

eng: Via the POV Facebook page
swa: Picha imechukuliwa kwenye ukurasa wa Facebook wa POV

eng: New pineapple haircut because I want to be famous too.
swa: Mtindo mpya wa kunyoa nanasi kwa sababu nataka kuwa maarufu pia.

eng: Via Rivo Francis on Facebook
swa: Picha ya Rivo Francis kwenye mtandao wa Facebook

eng: Did you know that the brand Dolce & Ananas was all the rage in Madagascar?
swa: Je ulifahamu kuwa brandi ya Dolce & Ananas ndio chanzo cha ghasia na hasira hapa Madagaska?

eng: Anana means pineapple in French.
swa: Anana ikimaanisha nanasi kwa Kifaransa.

eng: Via Aina Rakotoson on Facebook
swa: Picha yaAina Rakotoson kwenye Facebook

eng: Tragically, all the jokes about pineapple came a few days after tragedy struck the country's independence day ceremony. A grenade exploded into the crowd watching the military parade in the national stadium, killing three people and injuring 91.
swa: Kwa bahati mbaya, mizaha yote iliyohusu nanasi ilikuja baada kutokea tukio la kutisha katika sherehe za siku ya Uhuru wa nchi hiyo; ambapo, bomu la kurushwa kwa mkono lililipuka wakati wananchi wakiangalia gwaride la kijeshi katika uwanja wa Taifa,na kuua watu watatu na wengine 91 walijeruhiwa.

eng: Here is a video of the aftermath:
swa: Hii ni video ya tukio hilo

eng: The whole conversation on "Pineapple-Gate" comes at a time when a major bill on freedom of speech and ethics online is being prepared by Malagasy authorities.
swa: Majadiliano yote ndani ya "Pineapple-Gate" yamekuja katika kipindi muhimu ambapo muswada wa sheria ya uhuru wa kujieleza na maadili mtandaoni unaandaliwa na mamlaka za Malagasi.

eng: The early returns from insiders on how the bill will shape up hint that it will severely restrict free expression online and will include heavy fines for any materials deemed to be libel.
swa: Wakizungumzia hilo vyanzo vya ndani vinatonya na kuzungumzia jinsi muswada huu utakavyobana uhuru wa kujieleza mtandaoni na utakuwa na faini kubwa kwa makala au taarifa zozote zitakazoonekana kuwa ni za uongo.

eng: The bill should be submitted to the parliament for approval in the coming weeks.
swa: Muswada huo utakabidhiwa bungeni wiki chache zijazo kwa ajili ya kupitishwa.

eng: Global Voices in Malagasy editor Andriamifidisoa Zo aka Jentilisa has contributed to this story with links and emails to the bloggers mentioned in this article.
swa: Mhariri wa Global Voices kwa ki-Malagasi Andriamifidisoa Zo kwa jina la utani Jentilisa amechangia habari hii kwa viungo na barua pepe kwa wanablogu waliotajwa kwenye makala haya.

eng: The Week That Was podcast takes a look at some of the stories that we’ve published recently on Global Voices.
swa: Matangazo ya Sauti ya ‘Wiki Ilivyokwenda’ Global Voices: inaangazia baadhi ya habari ambazo tumezichapisha kwenye tovuti ya Global Voices.

eng: This week, we take you to Bosnia and Herzegovina, Japan and Myanmar.
swa: Wiki hii, tunakuchukua mpaka Bosnia na Herzegovina, Japan na Myanmar.

eng: We also speak with Global Voices Brazil editor Taisa Sganzerla about a heinous rape case that has Brazil and other parts of the world in uproar and with Global Voices contributor Leila Nachawati Rego about her new novel that pays homage to the anonymous people who are living, loving and resisting for Syria.
swa: Aidha, tunazungumza na mhariri wa Global Voices Brazil,m Taisa Sganzerla kuhusu kesi ya ubakaji ambayo imeifanya Brazil na sehemu nyingine za dunia kupiga kelele na pia tutazungumza na mwandishi wetu Leila Nachawati Rego kuhusu riwaya yake inayoangazia maisha ya watu wanaoishi, wanaoipenda na kupambana kwa ajili ya Syria.

eng: This episode features stories by Filip Stojanovski, Nevin Thompson, Mong Palatino, Fernanda Canofre and Taisa Sganzerla, and Firuzeh Shokooh Valle.
swa: Kipidni cha leo kina habari zilizoandikwa na Filip Stojanovski, Nevin Thompson, Mong Palatino, Fernanda Canofre na Taisa Sganzerla, na Firuzeh Shokooh Valle.

eng: We also feature Creative Commons licensed music from the Free Music Archive, including Please Listen Carefully by Jahzaar; Machine Elves by Alan Singley; Looking For That Moment When Time Stands Still by Will Bangs; All My Light by Cory Gray; Shamon’s Roar by Sergey Cheremisinov; and A Storm At Eilean Mor by Jon Luc Hefferman.
swa: Kadhalika, tunakuburudisha na muziki wenye leseni ya Creative Commons kutoka maktaba ya matandaoni ya Free Music, ikiwemo Please Listen Carefully wa Jahzaar; Machine Elves wa Alan Singley; Looking For That Moment When Time Stands Still wa Will Bangs; All My Light wa Cory Gray; Shamon’s Roar wa Sergey Cheremisinov; na A Storm At Eilean Mor wa Jon Luc Hefferman.

eng: Expect to hear our voices again in two weeks.
swa: Tarajia kusikia sauti zetu kwa mara nyingine katika kipindi cha majuma mawili.

eng: Happy listening!
swa: Tunakutakia usikilizaji mwema!

eng: Image in SoundCloud thumbnail is by Filip Stojanovski, CC BY.
swa: Picha kwenye alama ya SoundCloud imepigwa na Filip Stojanovski, CC BY.

eng: This week we take you to Russia, India, and Madagascar.
swa: Wiki hii tunakupeleka hadi Urusi, India, na Madagascar.

eng: We also speak with Global Voices contributor Kirsten Han about recent actions of the Singapore police against activists over their Facebook posts.
swa: Tumeongea pia na mwakilishi wa Global Voices, Kirsten Han kuhusu matukio ya hivi karibuni ya polisi wa Singapore dhidi ya wanaharakati na machapisho yao kwenye mtandao wa Facebook.

eng: Later we chat with Global Voices contributor Marianne Diaz Hernandez about how electrical shortages are limiting basic communication and hindering free expression in Venezuela.
swa: Pia, tunaongea na mwakilishi wa Global Voices, Marianne Diaz Hernandez kuhusu namna tatizo la umeme linavyotatiza mawasiliano na kukwamisha uhuru wa kujieleza nchini Venezuela.

eng: This episode features stories by Kevin Rothrock ,Rezwan, Lova Rakotomalala, Kirsten Han and Marianne Diaz Hernandez.
swa: Makala haya yanahusisha simulizi zilizoandaliwa na Kevin Rothrock ,Rezwan, Lova Rakotomalala, Kirsten Han na Marianne Diaz Hernandez.

eng: In this episode of the Week that Was at Global Voices, we featured Creative Commons licensed music from the Free Music Archive, including Please Listen Carefully by Jahzzar; Cloud Burst by Kai Engel, Indian Spice by Podington Bear; Masculine by David Szesztay and The Fresh Monday by Dexter Britain.
swa: Katika Makala haya ya Wiki hii kwenye matangazo ya sauti ya Global Voices, tulijadili kuhusu muziki wenye leseni ya Creative Commons kutoka kenye Hifadhi huru za Muziki, ikiwa ni pamoja na Please Listen Carefully ulioimbwa na Jahzzar; Cloud Burst ulioimbwa na Kai Engel, Indian Spice ulioimbwa na Podington Bear; Masculine na David Szesztay pamoja na The Fresh Monday ulioimbwa na Dexter Britain.

eng: Image used in Soundcloud thumbnail is by Edu Alarcón from Flickr.
swa: Picha iliyotumiwa kwenye Soundcloud ni kwa hisani ya Edu Alarcón kutoka Flickr.

eng: Published under Creative Commons license (CC BY 2.0).
swa: Imechapishwa kwa mujibu wa leseni ya Creative Commons (CC BY 2.0).

eng: Renna Ramadan prepared an iftar meal for her family, Syrians from Idlib who hoped to reach Northern Europe but instead are living in the passenger waiting area at Piraeus Port Terminal 1 in Athens, Greece.
swa: Renna Ramadan akiandaa futari kwa ajili ya familia yake, wa-Syria kutoka Idlib waliokuwa na matumaini ya kufikia Kaskazini mwa Ulaya lakini kinyume chake wamekuwa wakiishi katika eneo maalum kwa ajili ya abiria kusubiria katika bandari ya Piraeus huko Athens, ugiriki.

eng: Several hundred refugees and migrants remain at Piraeus, long after Greek authorities vowed to move the people to other camps.
swa: Mamia mengine ya wakimbizi na wahamiaji wamesalia huko Piraeus, kwa muda mrefu baada ya mamlaka za Ugiriki kuapa kuwapeleka watu wengine katika kambi zingine.

eng: Credit: Jodi Hilton/Pulitzer Center
swa: Picha: Jodi Hilton/Kituo cha Pulitzer

eng: This article by Jeanne Carstensen originally appeared on PRI.org on June 10, 2016, and is republished here as part of a content-sharing agreement.
swa: Makala haya ya Jeanne Carstensen yalichapishwa awali kwenye tovuti ya PRI.org mnamo Juni 10, 2016, na yanachapishwa kwa mara nyingine hapa kama sehemu ya makubaliano ya kushirikiana maudhui.

eng: On the first night of Ramadan, residents of the informal tent camp at Piraeus port in Athens line up for special meals to break their fast.
swa: Katika usiku wa kwanza wa mfungo wa Ramadhan, wakazi wa kambi isiyo rasmi ya mahema katika bandari ya Piraeus jijini Athens walijipanga kwenye foleni kupokea futari ya kufuturia.

eng: As the sun sets behind the massive ferries that take travelers to the Greek islands, hundreds of hot, tired refugees line up in front of a trailer in a vast parking lot.
swa: Wakati jua linapozama nyuma ya vivuko vingi vinavyosafirisha wasafiri kwenda katika visiwa vya Ugiriki, mamia ya wakimbizi waliochoka na kutweta jasho jingi, wamepanga mstari mbele ya behewa kubwa lililowekwa katika viwanja vikubwa vya maegesho.

eng: They haven’t eaten or had a drink of water since about 4 a.m.
swa: Hawajala au kunywa maji tangu saa kumi alfajiri.

eng: It’s clear the Greek government is trying to support the refugees during Ramadan.
swa: Ni wazi kuwa serikali ya Ugiriki inajaribu kuwasaidia wakimbizi hawa katika kipindi hiki cha mfungo wa Ramadhani.

eng: But even so, conditions at Piraeus are abysmal.
swa: Pamoja na hivyo, hali ya hapa Piraeus inakatisha tamaa kabisa.

eng: Hedda Grew, a volunteer with the NGO Team Sweden, says the Ramadan fasting is only increasing tensions among people who are already desperate about their circumstances.
swa: Hedda Grew, ambaye anajitolea pamoja na wanafanyakazi wa Asasi Isiyo ya Kiserikali ya Sweden, anasema kuwa; mfungo wa Ramadhani unaongeza kadhia kwa watu ambao tayari wana mfadhahiko mkubwa wa hali ya sasa.

eng: They can't drink, they can't eat, they're just sitting in their hot tents all day, and it's a combination between the Ramadan and the waiting, she says.
swa: Hawawezi kula, hawawezi kunywa chochote, yaani wamekaa tu ndani ya mahema yao yaliyo na joto kali kwa siku nzima; na huu ni mchanganyiko wa Ramadhani na kusubiri  ndivyo alisikika akisema.

eng: And there’s an awful lot of waiting.
swa: Na kuna msururu wa kusubiri unaokera.

eng: I walk to a quieter area of the camp where I meet Amal Herh, a beautiful young mother of four from Aleppo.
swa: Ninatembea katika eneo lililo kimya katika kambi ambapo ninakutana na Amal Herh, ambaye ni mama wa watoto wanne ni mrembo na kijana bado anayetokea Aleppo.

eng: Her name means "Hope" in English.
swa: Jina lake linamaanisha "Tumaini" kwa Kiswahili.

eng: I have a lot of hope, she says. "But now I must be strong, more strong, for my family."
swa: Nina matumaini makubwa alisema, "Lakini sasa lazima niwe jasiri na imara kwa ajili ya familia yangu"

eng: Amal is putting on a positive face, but I can see the distress in her eyes.
swa: Amal ana uso uliojaa bashasha, lakini hata hivyo unaweza kuona fadhaa katika macho yake.

eng: She tells me that Ramadan makes her long for home.
swa: Ananiambia kuwa mfungo huu wa Ramadhani unamfanya akumbuke sana nyumbani.

eng: I want to go to Aleppo for Ramadan, with cooking and some cold water and a good place, not this, she says.
swa: Nataka kwenda Aleppo kwa ajili ya Ramadhani, ambapo kuna mapishi ya kila aina na maji baridi na mahali pazuri pa kukaa, sio kama hivi.

eng:
Some good fruit, not orange every day. 	Matunda mazuri ya aina tofauti na sio haya machungwa ya kila siku.
You don't love the same food every day, yes?
swa: Huwezi kula chakula hicho hicho kila siku ukakipenda, sivyo?" alisema Amal.

eng: I tell her I understand.
swa: Nilimwambia kuwa ninamuelewa sana.

eng: That people tell me that Ramadan is a very happy time of year, with family, and special food.
swa: Watu hao waliniambia kuwa Ramadhani ni kipindi cha furaha sana kwa mwaka ukiwa na familia yako huku mkishirikiana vyakula maalum.

eng: Yes, she says. "But I don't say what I can say to you, because I am very sad now, because I remember my house."
swa: Ndio alisema, "Ila siwezi kusema hili nilisemalo kwako kwa sasa kwa sababu nina huzuni sana, kwa sababu nimeikumbuka nyumba yangu"

eng: The next night I accept an invitation to a very different Iftar meal with Anna Stamou, a Greek woman who converted to Islam, and her husband, Naim el Ghandour, president of the Muslim Association of Greece.
swa: Usiku uliofuata nilikubali mualiko wa kula futari iliyokuwa na utofauti kidogo na ile ya jana iliyokuwa nyumbani kwa Anna Stamou, mwanamke wa Kigiriki aliyebadili dini na kuwa Muislam, na mume wake Naim el Ghandour, Rais wa Jumuiya ya Kiislam huko Ugiriki.

eng: Naim was born in Egypt.
swa: Naim alizaliwa Misri.

eng: The Ramadan app on his phone signals sundown with a recording of a call to prayer.
swa: Picha katika simu yake kwa Ramadhani hii inaonesha ishara ya jua kuzama ikiwa na muito wa adhana.

eng: At the table, there's playful banter about whether the salad is Egyptian or Greek.
swa: Katika meza kulikuwa na utani kuhusu saladi iliyoandaliwa kuwa ilikuwa ya Kimisri au ni ya Kigiriki?

eng: Over Iftar dinner Anna translates for Naim as he speaks Greek.
swa: Baada ya futari Anna alimtafsiria Naim wakati akiongea Kigiriki.

eng: He’s sad for the thousands of Muslim refugee having to celebrate Ramadan in the camps.
swa: Anahuzunika kwa ajili ya maelfu ya wakimbizi wa Kiislamu wanaosherehekea Ramadhani ndani ya kambi.

eng: But he tells me he’s glad to see Yannis Mouzalas, the Greek minister of migration, is making an effort to show support during Ramadan.
swa: Lakini alisema kuwa anafarijika kuona Yannis Mouzalas, waziri wa Uhamiaji nchini Ugiriki akifanya jitihada za kuwasaidia wakimbizi hao wakati huu wa Ramadhani.

eng: It's very encouraging for us, he says.
swa: Inatutia moyo sana alisema Naim.

eng: The refugees are in a terrible situation in Greece.
swa: Wakimbizi wapo katika hali mbaya sana hapa Ugiriki.

eng: But Naim, who fled his native Egypt in 1967, is grateful that they are at least away from the violence.
swa: Lakini Naim aliyekimbia asili yake ambayo ni Misri mwaka 1967, anashukuru kuwa wakimbizi hao angalau wako mbali na vurugu.

eng: They are way better than if they were there and maybe a bomb would be in their heads right now and they would celebrate no Ramadan, no nothing, he says.
swa: Aliendelea kusema kuwa; "hapa wako na unafuu zaidi kuliko wangekuwa kule na labda bomu lingeshawaangukia sasa hivi na wasingeweza kusherehekea Ramadhani, wala chochote.

eng: But the best Ramadan blessing would be to end the fighting.
swa: Lakini baraka na zawadi bora kabisa kwa ajili ya Ramadhani ingekuwa kumaliza mapigano.

eng: I wish there would be a solution with Europe to stop the war, he says. "Because this is the issue — to stop the war.
swa: Natamani kungekuwa na suluhisho kwa Ulaya kumaliza vita kwa sababu imeshakuwa ngumu kumaliza hivyo vita.

eng: All of them want to go back.
swa: Wote wanataka kurudi nyumbani kwao.

eng: We certainly wish that next Ramadan will find us without war."
swa: Tunawaombea kwa hakika kuwa Ramadhani ijayo itukute hatuna vita kati yetu.

eng: Later I keep thinking about Amal in her tent back in Piraeus.
swa: Baadaye niliendelea kuwaza kuhusu Amal akiwa kule kwenye hema lake kule Piraeus.

eng: It’s not easy to feel your dignity slipping away, especially during the holidays.
swa: Sio rahisi kuuona utu wako ukipotea hivi hivi hasa katika kipindi cha mapumziko.

eng: I wish I could bring her cool water and freshly peeled oranges from Aleppo for Ramadan.
swa: Ninatamani ningeweza kumletea maji baridi na machungwa yaliyochumwa na kumwenywa muda huo huo kutoka Aleppo kwa ajili ya Ramadhan.

eng: Jeanne Carstensen and Jodi Hilton are covering the refugee crisis in Greece with support from the Pulitzer Center.
swa: Jeanne Carstensen na Jodi Hilton wanaandika habari za janga la wakimbizi nchini Ugiriki kwa msaada wa kituo cha Pulitzer.

eng: Poster for the African Conference of Bloggers and Vloggers via Armelle.
swa: Bango la Tamasha la WanaBlogu na WanaVilogu kutoka kwa Armelle.

eng: Used with her permission
swa: Imetumiwa kwa ruhusa yake

eng: Armelle Nina Sitchoma reported on the first African Bloggers and Vloggers’ Festival (FABY, for its initials in French), which took place 3-5 June 2016 at La Place du Souvenir in Dakar, Senegal.
swa: Armelle Nina Sitchoma aliripoti katika tamasha la kwanza la Waafrika wanao miliki Blogu na Vilogu lililofanyika tarehe 3-5 Juni 2016 (FABY, ikiwa ni kifupisho chake katika lugha ya Kifaransa), lililofanyika huko Place du Souvenir mjini Dakar, Senegal.

eng: The blogger, who is from Douala, Cameroon, wrote on her website that the two-day festival attracted 36 of the "best" bloggers and vloggers from around Africa as well as other digital figures.
swa: Mwanablogu kutoka Douala, Cameroon, aliandika katika tovuti yake kuwa tamasha hilo la siku mbili lilivutia wanablogu na vilogu wa viwango vya juu kabisa wapatao 36 na wadau wengine wa masuala ya mitandao kutoka pande zote za Afrika.

eng: They gave presentations on African digital content and the economic opportunities to be found on the African web.
swa: Wataalam hawa wa masuala ya mitandao walitoa mada mbalimbali zinazohusu masuala ya mtandao barani Afrika na fursa za kiuchumi zinazopatikana katika mitandao hiyo ya Afrika.

eng: She continued:
swa: Aliendelea kueleza kuwa:

eng: The two days of discussions were arranged around two panel discussions: “Big Data: What place is there for African content?” moderated by web 2.0 consultant Aboubacar Sadikh Ndiaye, and “The Future of Video in Africa” moderated by Mountaga Cissé from Senegal.
swa: Zilikuwa siku mbili za majadiliano zilizoandaliwa katika makundi mawili ya majadiliano: “Data Kubwa: Bara la Afrika lina nafasi gani? Kundi hili liliongozwa na mshauri wa Web 2.0 Aboubacar Sadikh Ndiaye, na Kundi lingine lilijadili mada, "Hatima ya Video Barani Afrika” liliongozwa na Mountaga Cissé kutoka Senegal.

eng: The panels included well-known bloggers and vloggers such as Edith Brou from Ivory Coast, Yassine Massouath from Morocco, and Mountaga Cissé from Senegal, who spoke on the theme of “How to succeed on the internet: Job opportunities in an IT world.”
swa: Makundi haya ya majadiliano yalikuwa yameundwa na wanablogu na vilogu wengi maarufu kama vile Edith Brou wa Ivory Coast, Yassine Massouath kutoka Morocco, na Mountaga Cissé kutoka Senegal.

eng: Whilst Annie Payep from Cameroon, Ameyaw from Ghana, and Alexandre Lette and NK Thiat from Senegal led a workshop on “Ensuring quality content”.
swa: Mountaga Cisse aliongelea mada iliyokuwa na kichwa cha somo "jinsi ya kufanikiwa kupitia mtandao wa Intaneti: Nafasi za kazi katika Ulimwengu wa Teknolojia" Wakati huo huo Annie Payep kutoka Cameroon, Ameyaw kutoka Ghana, Alexandre Lette na NK Thiat kutoka Senegal waliongoza warsha iliyobeba dhima ya "Udhibiti Viwango" Masimulizi ya kufanikiwa kwa Waafrika kama ile ya Aisha Dème wa wavuti ya Agendakar, yalijadiliwa na kushirikishwa kwa hadhira.

eng: African success stories, such as that of Aisha Dème of the website Agendakar, were shared with the audience.
swa: Pia kulikuwa na maonesho ya mitindo na upambaji kutoka kwa Sylvia Njoki wa Kenya na Mode & Beauté kutoka kwa Aba wa Senegal.

eng: There were also exhibition stands featuring make up – Fashion from Sylvia Njoki (Kenya) and Mode & Beauté from Aba of Senegal – and cooking, video games, education and comedy were also covered and the first African Bloggers & Vloggers’ Festival
swa: Shughuli za mapishi, michezo, mijadala ya elimu pamoja na sanaa za vichekesho navyo pia vilipata nafasi katika tamasha hilo kubwa la kwanza Barani Afrika lililowashirikisha Wanablogu na Wanavilogu hao waliotoka sehemu mbalimbali humu Barani.

eng: Image shared on Twitter by Tanzanian Member of Parliament Zitto Kabwe Ruyagwa. (@zittokabwe)
swa: Picha iliwekwa kwenye mtandao wa Twita na Mbunge wa Tanzania Zitto Kabwe Ruyagwa. (@zittokabwe)

eng: Tanzanian citizen Isaac Abakuki Emily was convicted of insulting Tanzanian President John Magufuli on his Facebook page by the Arusha Resident Magistrate’s Court.
swa: Raia wa Tanzania Isaac Abakuki Emily alipatwa na hatia ya kumtukana Rais wa Tanzania John Magufuli kwenye ukurasa wake wa Facebook na Hakimu Mkazi wa Mahakama ya Arusha.

eng: Emily first appeared in court on April 15, 2016 on charges of "insulting" the country's president, John Magufuli, allegedly contrary to Section 16 of Tanzania's Cybercrime Act No. 14 of 2015, which says:
swa: Emily alisimama mbele ya mahakama kwa mara ya kwanza mnamo Aprili 15, 2016 kujibu mashtaka y 'kumtukana' rais wa nchi, John Magufuli, ikidaiwa kuwa alikwenda kinyume na Ibara ya 16 ya Sheria ya Makosa ya Jinai ya Tanzania Na. 14 ya 2015, inayosema:

eng: Any person who publishes information, data or facts presented in a picture, text, symbol or any other form in a computer system where such information, data or fact is false, deceptive, misleading or inaccurate commits an offence, and shall on conviction be liable to a fine not less than three million shillings or to imprisonment for a term not less than six months or to both.
swa: Mtu yeyote anayechapisha taarifa, takwimu au habari katika picha, maandishi, alama au kwa namna nyingine yoyote katika mfumo wa kompyuta ambapo taarifa hizo, takwimu au habari hizo ni za uongo, zenye udanganyifu, zenye kupotosha ukweli au zisizo sahihi atakuwa anatenda kosa, na akitiwa hatiani atatakiwa kulipa fidia ya si chini ya shilingi milioni tatu kifungo jela kisichopungua miezi sita jela au vyote viwili kwa pamoja

eng: He was accused of posting the controversial Facebook message, written in Swahili, on March 17, 2015, despite knowing that posting false or misleading statements about the country's president is against the law.
swa: Emily anadaiwa kuweka ujumbe wenye utata kwenye ukurasa wake wa Facebook, ulioandikwa kwa Kiswahili, mnamo Machi 17, 2016, wakati akijua kuwa kuchapisha kauli za uongo au zinazopotosha ukweli kuhusu rais wa nchi ni kinyume cha sheria.

eng: His comment was in reference to President Magufuli's surprise live call to 360, a current affairs program on Clouds TV.
swa: Maoni yake hayo yalihusiana na hatua ya Rais Magufuli kupiga simu isiyotarajiwa kwa kipindi cha 360, kinachohusiana na mambo yanayotokea kwenye kituo cha televisheni cha Clouds TV.

eng: While on the air, the president thanked the presenters and expressed his admiration for the show.
swa: Wangali hewani, rais aliwashukuru watangazaji na kuonesha alivyoshabiki wa kipindi hicho.

eng: Neither Emily's personal Facebook page, nor the discussion page on which he is reported to have posted the comment, have come up in searches, but his Facebook comment allegedly read:
swa: Emily anadaiwa kuchapisha ujumbe wenye utata kwenye mtandao wa Facebook kwa lugha ya Kiswahili mnamo Machi 17, 2015, hali akijua kwamba kumkosoa rais wa nchi ni kinyume cha sheria.

eng: Theatrics in politics , how come you compare this imbecile to Nyerere ?
swa: Hizi siasa za maigizo, halafu mnamfananisha huyu bwege and Nyerere wapi buana.

eng: His conviction comes against the backdrop of Tanzania's relatively new cybercrime bill, which the Parliament passed on April 1, 2015, to address cybercrime issues such as child pornography, cyberbullying, online impersonation, electronic production of racist and xenophobic content, spam, illegal interception of communications, and the publication of false information.
swa: Hukumu yake imekuja wakati muswada mpya wa makosa ya uhalifu wa kimtandao, uliopitishwa mnamo april 1, 2015, ulipotungwa kushughulikia masuala ya kimtandao kama vile picha za ngono za watoto, udhalilishaji wa kimtandao, matumizi ya taarifa za watu isivyosahihi, uzalishaji wa maudhui yanayochochea ubaguzi wa rangi na ubaguzi wa wageni, ujumbe unaoutumwa bila ruhusa yake, udukuzi wa mawasiliano kinyume na sheria, na kuchapishwa kwa taarifa za uongo.

eng: Despite widespread opposition from politicians, social media experts, and human rights activists, the bill was pushed through parliament with relatively little discussion or debate.
swa: Pamoja na upinzani mkubwa kutoka kwa wanasiasa, wataalam wa mitandao ya kijamii, na wanaharakati wa haki za binadamu, muswada huo ulipelekwa haraka bungeni baada ya majadiliano au mdahalo wa kiwango cha chini.

eng: Former president Jakaya Kikwete signed it into law in May 2015.
swa: Rais mstaafu Jakaya Kikwete aliusaini muswada huo mnamo Mei 2015 kuwa sheria.

eng: They have also cautioned that police or the state could use their power to harass online activists or social media users.
swa: Wanaonya kwamba polisi au dola inaweza kutumia mamlaka hayo kuwabughudhi wanaharakati wa mtandnaoni au watumiaji wa mitandao ya kijamii.

eng: That same month, another netizen, Sospiter Jonas, was arraigned in a primary court in Dodoma Region and charged with “misuse of the Internet” after he posted a message on Facebook saying that Tanzanian Prime Minister Mizengo Pinda “will only become a gospel preacher.”
swa: Mwezi huo huo, mtumiaji mwingine wa mtandao, Sospiter Jonas, alisimamishwa kizimbani kwenye mahakama ya mwanzo mkoani Dodoma kwa kosa la 'kutumia vibaya mtandao' baada ya kubandika ujumbe kwenye mtandao wa Facebook akisema Waziri Mkuu wa Tanzania Mizengo Pinda “atakuwa mhubiri wa dini.”

eng: The four appeared before a Magistrate's court in Dar Es Salaam on November 6, 2015.
swa: Wanne haoa walisimamishwa mbele ya Hakimu Mkazi jijini Dar Es Salaam mnamo Novemba 6, 2015.

eng: Public prosecutors alleged that the accused published audio information on a WhatsApp group called the "Soka Group", that was intended to mislead the public during the October 2015 Tanzanian general elections, which were plagued by accusations of vote-rigging.
swa: Mwendesha mashtaka wa serikali alidai kwamba watuhumiwa hao walichapisha taarifa ya sauti kwenye kundi la WhatsApp linaloitwa "Soka Group", ambayo ilikusudia kupotosha umma wakati wa uchaguzi mkuu wa Oktoba 2015 nchini Tanzania , ambao uligubikwa na madai ya wizi wa kura.

eng: A screenshot of Samson Tusiime's Facebook post.
swa: Picha ya posti ya ukurasa wa Facebook wa Samson Tusiime

eng: Twitter in Uganda was buzzing on Sunday, 29 May with the hashtag #FreeSamwyiri.
swa: Kuanzia jumapili ya tarehe 29 Mei katika mtandao wa Twitter nchini Uganda kumekuwa na mzizimo wa kampeni zenye hastag #mfungulieniSamwyiri.

eng: The Twitter campaign followed the arrest of a Ugandan man named Samson Tusiime allegedly for wearing and distributing T-shirts bearing the photo of Ugandan opposition leader Kizza Besigye.
swa: Kampeni hizi zimefuatia kukamatwa kwa mwanaume wa Kiganda anayeitwa Samson Tusiime aliyekamatwa kwa kuvaa na kugawa tisheti zenye picha za kiongozi wa chama cha upinzani wa huko Uganda Kizza Besigye.

eng: Police allege that he was organizing "illegal" demonstrations and had plans of distributing similar T-shirts countrywide.
swa: Polisi nchini Uganda wanadai kuwa mwanaume huyo alikuwa anaandaa maandamano haramu na alikuwa na mpango wa kuzigawa tisheti hizo nchi nzima.

eng: According to Uganda's Independent newspaper, two other Ugandans, Ismail Muyinda and Asia Nanyanzi, were also arrested.
swa: Gazeti la Uhuru la Uganda, linasema kuwa Waganda wengine wawili ambao walifahamika kwa majina ya Ismail Muyinda na Asia Nanyanzi, nao pia walikamatwa.

eng: Tusiime had posted a message on Facebook on 28 May wearing the T-shirt in question, saying he was looking for his friend Ysmyl Muyinda (presumed to be the same Ismail Muyinda reported as arrested above), whose company produced and printed them.
swa: Tarehe 28 Mei Tusiime aliweka ujumbe katika ukurasa wake wa Facebook unaosema kuwa anamtafuta rafiki yake Ysmyl Muyinda akiwa amevaa tisheti hiyo anayoshutumiwa nayo (Inasadikiwa kuwa ndie Ismail Muyinda aliyetajwa hapo juu kuwa alikamatwa) Ismail ndie mmiliki wa kampuni iliyozalisha na kuchapisha tisheti hizo.

eng: He wrote that he had gone to different police stations looking for his friend.
swa: Tusiime aliandika kuwa ameenda katika vituo mbalimbai vya polisi akimtafuta rafiki yake.

eng: When friends noticed that Tusiime himself had gone missing, they started a hashtag #FreeSamwyiri.
swa: Baada ya marafiki wengine kugundua kuwa hata Tusiime naye haonekani pia, walianzisha hashtag #MfungueniSamwyiri.

eng: Police later confirmed that he was arrested.
swa: Baadae polisi walithibitisha kuwa alikuwa amekamatwa.

eng: The case has agitated many Ugandans, who are in shock that a T-shirt could be enough to arrest someone.
swa: Kesi hii imewashtua watu wengi nchini Uganda na wengi wameshangaa kuwa kumbe hata tisheti tu inaweza kumfanya mtu akamatwe na kuwekwa rumande!?

eng: Joel Nevender, a Ugandan blogger, asked the police:
swa: Mwana Blogu mmoja wa huko Uganda aitwae Joel Nevender amewauliza polisi kuwa;

eng: You're arresting @Samwyri for exercising his freedom of expression?
swa: Mnamkamata @Samwyri kwa sabau ameutumia uhuru wake wa kujieleza?

eng: Because of t-shirts?
swa: Kwa sababu ya Tisheti?

eng: T-shirts? #FreeSamwyri — Joel B Ntwatwa (@nevender) May 29, 2016
swa: Tisheti? #MfungueniSamwyri — Joel B Ntwatwa (@nevender) Mei 29, 2016

eng: While Ogutu Daudi tweeted:
swa: Wakati Ogutu Daudi alitwiti kwamba:

eng: Can we come out and stop calling this a democracy because it isn't.
swa: Je tunaweza kutoka na kusema kwa sauti kuwa hii sio demokrasia kwa sababu sio?

eng: Bloody tshirts.
swa: Tisheti Upuuzi gani!?

eng: Put us in yellow jumpsuits why don't you. #freesamwyri — iamogutudaudi (@iamogutudaudi) May 29, 2016
swa: Kwa nini msituweke wote kwenye maovaroli ya njano sasa? #mfungulienisamwyri — iamogutudaudi (@iamogutudaudi) Mei 29, 2016

eng: In recent months, Ugandan authorities have been especially intolerant of criticism.
swa: Miezi ya hivi karibuni mamlaka nchini Uganda imeshindwa kabisa kuvumilia kukosolewa.

eng: President Yoweri Museveni won a controversial fifth term in office in February 2016 in an election that the country's political opposition claims was rigged.
swa: Mwezi wa pili mwaka huu 2016 Raisi Yoweri Museveni alishinda uchaguzi na kurudi madarakani kwa muhula wa tano. Uchaguzi huo uliokuwa na sintofahamu nyingi ambapo vyama vya upinzani nchini humo vimekuwa vikilalamikia matokeo ya uchaguzi huo kupindishwa au kuchakachuliwa.

eng: Opposition members and other activists have been challenging Museveni's victory with a series of protests they've dubbed the “defiance campaign.”
swa: Viongozi wa upinzani na wanaharakati wengine nchini Uganda wamekuwa wakikosoa na kupinga ushindi wa Museveni kupitia maandamano mbalimbali.... “kampeni za kususia”

eng: Since the February election, authorities have arrested Kizza Besigye and other opposition figures multiple times as well as blocked social media twice in the interest of "national security".
swa: Tangu uchaguzi uishe mwezi Februari, mamlaka imemkamata na kumsweka rumande mara kadhaa Kizza Besigye na viongozi wengine wa upinzani pamoja na kufungia mitandao ya kijamii mara mbili kwa masilahi ya "usalama wa taifa".

eng: After Tusiime's arrest, Josephine Karungi wondered:
swa: Baada ya kukamatwa kwaTusiime, Josephine Karungi alishangaa na kusema :

eng: Some things are terribly hard to spin...ati now we arrested him because why...you can't really say it was the tee shirt can you? — Josephine Karungi (@jkkarungi) May 30, 2016
swa: Kuna vitu havijakaa sawa kabisa...ati tumemweka rumande sasa kisa ni nini........kweli hamuwezi kusema eti kisa ni tisheti tu...mnaweza kusema ndivyo? — Josephine Karungi (@jkkarungi) Mei 30, 2016

eng: Patoraking, a university student, thought that this act was worse than the days of Idi Amin, the Ugandan dictator who ruled Uganda from 1971 until 1979:
swa: Patoraking, yeye ni mwanafunzi wa Chuo Kikuu alisema kuwa hiki kitendo ni kibaya kuliko enzi za dikteta Idi Amini aliyeitawala Uganda tangu mwaka 1971 hadi 1979.

eng: Our parents can nolonger even tell us "During Amin's time, ....." because this time we r in is even worse than Amin's time #FreeSamwyri — Patoranking (@pyepar) May 29, 2016
swa: Wazazi wetu hawawezi hata kutuambia tena "enzi za Idi Amini..........." kwa sababu kipindi hiki tuko katika nyakati mbaya zaidi kuliko hata zile za Idi Amini. #MfungulieniSamwyri — Patoranking (@pyepar) Mei 29, 2016

eng: Chapter Four Uganda, a legal aid organisation, responded to the outcry by sending their legal team to the police station:
swa: Shirika la msaada wa kisheria liitwalo Chapter Four Uganda, liliitikia vuguvugu la kampeni hiyo kwa kupeleka timu ya wanasheria katika kituo cha polisi:

eng: Our officer is at SIU Kireka to obtain a statement from @Samwyri for appropriate legal action #FreeSamwyri — Chapter Four Uganda (@chapter4uganda) May 30, 2016
swa: Afisa wetu yuko SIU Kireka kuchukua maelezo kutoka kwa @Samwyri ili hatua stahiki za kisheria ziweze kuchukuliwa #MfungulieniSamwyri — Chapter Four Uganda (@chapter4uganda) Mei 30, 2016

eng: SIU Kireka stands for Special Investigation Unit at Kireka in the capital Kampala.
swa: Afisa wetu yuko SIU Kireka kuchukua maelezo kutoka kwa @Samwyri ili hatua stahiki za kisheria ziweze kuchukuliwa

eng: It is not yet known which exact charges will be laid against him.
swa: SIU Kireka ni kifupi cha (Special Investigation Unit at Kireka) yaani ni Kitengo Maalum cha Upelelezi katika eneo la Kireka katika mji mkuu wa Kampala.

eng: However, Qatahar Raymond, a Ugandan journalist who has been following Tusiime's case since he was arrested, speculated that he might be charged for inciting violence.
swa: Haijajulikana ni mashataka yapi hasa yamefunguliwa dhidi yake; hata hivyo, mwandishi wa habari wa Uganda Qatahar Raymond amekuwa akiifuatilia kwa ukaribu kabisa kesi hii ya Tusiime tangu akamatwe na anadhani kuwa Tusiime anaweza kushtakiwa kwa kosa la kuchochea vurugu.

eng: We learn that @Samwyri and his friend will likely be charged with 'inciting violence' if they are charged, that is. — Qatahar Raymond (@qataharraymond) May 30, 2016
swa: Tumegundua kuwa @Samwyri na marafiki zake wanaweza kushtakiwa kwa kosa la " uchochezi" — Qatahar Raymond (@qataharraymond) Mei 30, 2016

eng: A single blog post changed the life of this Somali mother of 8. Photo by Somali Faces (Donia and Mohammed).
swa: Blogu moja imebadilisha maisha ya mama huyu wa ki-Somali mwenye watoto nane Picha na Somali Faces (Donia na Mohammed).

eng: Used with permission.
swa: Imetumiwa kwa ruhusa.

eng: On May 1, Somali Faces covered a story about a poor Somali mother who is an Internally Displaced Person (IDP) and has eight small children, none of whom were attending school.
swa: Mnamo Mei 1, blogu ya Somali Faces iliandika habari kuhusu mama mmoja maskini wa ki-Somali anayeishi kama mkimbizi licha ya kuwa na watoto nane wadogo, ambao kati yao hakuna anayekwenda shule.

eng: She was facing abuse for belonging to a minority Somali clan and because of her dark skin.
swa: Alikuwa akikabiliana na vitendo vya ubaguzi kutoka kwa majirani zake kwa sababu ya kutoka kwenye ukoo mdogo wa kabila lisilofahamika sana ki-Somali na kwa sababu ya rangi yake nyeusi.

eng: She was contemplating suicide.
swa: Alijaribu kujinyonga.

eng: Sometimes I’m treated like a foreigner in my own country, like I don’t belong here.
swa: Wakati mwingine ninatendewa kama mgeni ndani ya nchi yangu mwenyewe, kama vile si mwenyeji wa hapa.

eng: I’m a single mother of 8 and none of my children are at school.
swa: Mimi ni mama asiye na mume mwenye watoto nane na hakuna hata mtoto wangu mmoja anayekwenda shule.

eng: I clean houses whilst carrying the child I’m carrying now.
swa: Ninasafisha nyumba nikiwa nimembeba mtoto huyu niliyembeba sasa hivi.

eng: The rest of my children look for any type of work that they can find.
swa: Watoto wangu wengine waliobaki hutafuta vibarua vyovyote wanavyoweza kuvipata.

eng: I know it’s a hard life and it’s not easy but what makes it so much harder and at times unbearable is how people treat me and my children.
swa: Ninafahamu ni maisha magumu na si rahisi lakini kinachonifanya nione maisha yawe magumu na yasiyovumilika ni namna watu wanavyotendea mimi na watu wangu.

eng: I sometimes feel like I’m in an ocean of people whose hearts are made of stone.
swa: Wakati mwingine najisikia kama niko kwenye bahari ya watu wenye mioyo ya mawe.

eng: Many discriminate against me because of my very dark skin colour.
swa: Wengi wananibagua kwa sababu ya kuwa na ngozi nyeusi.

eng: I tell them, that’s how God created me and I can’t change it.
swa: Ninawaambia, hivi ndivyo Mungu alivyoniumba na sina uwezi wa kujibadilisha.

eng: Either they reject me because I’m from a minority clan or because of my skin colour.
swa: Wananinyanyapaa ama kwa sababu ya kutoka uko mdogo au kwa sababu ya rangi yangu nyeusi.

eng: Sometimes, I contemplate whether death is better for us than living in a wretched life.
swa: Wakati mwingine ninafikiri kifo ni unafuu kwetu kuliko kuishi maisha ya namna hii.

eng: Readers were moved by her story, and began a fundraiser for her.
swa: wasomaji waliguswa na habari hiyo, na kuanza kuchanga fedha kwa ajili ya kumsaidia.

eng: A total of $4,000 was raised in 21 hours.
swa: Jumla ya Dola za Marekani 4,000 zilichangwa ndani ya kipindi cha saa 21.

eng: After the donations, Somali Faces reported:
swa: Baada ya michango hiyo, blogu ya Somali Faces ilitoa taarifa:

eng: Your donations changed her family’s life.
swa: Michango yenu imebadili maisha ya familia ya mama yule.

eng: Because of you, she will have her own shop, her house will be repaired and she told us that with the money she will be making, she can easily pay for her children’s education.
swa: Kwa sababu yenu, sasa ataweza kumiliki duka lake mwenyewe, nyumba yake itakarabatiwa na alituambia wamba kwa fedha atakazokuwa akizipata kwa biashara ya duka, sasa ataweza kulipa ada za watoto wake wapate elimu.

eng: You couldn’t conceal her smile and happiness, at times; she had difficulty getting the words out.
swa: Uso wake umejaa tabasamu na furaha wakati huu; alikosa kabisa maneno sahihi.

eng: Never in a million years did she imagine that she would receive this amount of money.
swa: Hakuwa kufikiri kwamba siku moja angepokea kiasi kikubwa fedha kiasi hiki.

eng: A week ago, she was discriminated against, hopeless and penniless and now, she has a continuous source of income for her family.
swa: Wiki moja lililopita, alikuwa akibaguliwa, alijiona hana matumaini na hakuwa hata na senti moja na sasa, ana chanzo endelevu cha mapato kumwezesha kutunza familia yake.

eng: We thank each every one of you for your unrelenting generosity and efforts to change this mother’s life.
swa: Tunamshukuru kila mmoja wenu kwa ukarimu na jitihada za kubadili maisha ya mama huyu.

eng: Somali Faces made sure that every dollar you sent was spent towards her family and we were involved every step when it came to the materials and how the money will be managed.
swa: Blogu ya Somali Faces ilihakikisha kwamba kila dola mliyoituma ilitumika kuboresha maisha ya familia hiyo na tulihusika kwa karibu kwa kila hatua katika kufuatilia matumizi ya kilichopatikana.

eng: We would like to thank Tadamun Social Society (TAAS) for their tremendous help.
swa: Tunapenda kuishukuru Chama cha Jamii cha Tadamun (TAAS) kwa msaada wao wa kipekee.

eng: We will be monitoring her progress and will provide you with a video update 3 to 6 months from now on how her and her beautiful children are doing.
swa: Tutakuwa tukifuatilia maendeleo na tutawapa video ya kinachoendelea katika kipindi cha kati ya miezi mitatu hadi sita kuanzia sasa kuhusu namna yeye na watoto wake wazuri wanavyoendelea.

eng: Somali Faces is an online project that shares everyday stories of ordinary Somali people from around the world.
swa: Somali Faces ni mradi wa mtandaoni unaoeneza habari za kila siku za maisha ya watu wa kawaida wa Somalia kutoka duniani kote.

eng: The idea was the brainchild of the creative duo of Donia Jamal Adam, a storyteller, human rights advocate and campaigner; and Mohammed Ibrahim Shire, an author and history enthusiast.
swa: Wazo la kuanzisha mradi huo lilikuwa ubunifu wa Donia Jamal Adam, mwanahabari, mtetezi na mpiganiaji wa haki za binadamu; na Mohammed Ibrahim Shire, mhariri na mpenzi wa historia.

eng: Statement of offence shared on Twitter by @samirasawlani.
swa: Hati ya mashitaka iliyowekwa kwenye mtandao wa Twita na @samirasawlani.

eng: Tanzanian citizen Leonard Mulokozi was charged on June 22 under Tanzania's Electronic and Postal Communications Act over a WhatsApp message that authorities say is "abusive" to Tanzanias president, John Magufuli.
swa: Raia wa Tanzania Leonard Mulokozi amesimamishwa kizimbani mnamo Juni 22 chini ya Sheria ya nchi hiyo ya Mawasiliano ya Kieletroniki na Posta kwa kosa la ujumbe wa WhatsApp ambao mamlaka zinasema ulikusudia 'kumtukana' rais wa nchi hiyo, John Magufuli.

eng: Mulokozi denied the charge at the Kisutu Resident Magistrate's Court and was released on bail.
swa: Mulokozi amekana mashtaka yake kwneye mahakama ya Hakimu Mkazi ya Kisutu na tuko nje kwa dhamana.

eng: The case will come up for mention on July 18.
swa: Kesi iyo itatajwa tena Julai 18.

eng: It is alleged that on June 2 Mulokozi posted the following message, in Swahili, on WhatsApp:
swa: Inadaiwa kwamba mnamo Juni 2 Mulokozi alituma ujumbe ufuatao kwenye mtandao wa WhatsApp:

eng: Does it mean this Pombe Magufuli doesn't have advisers?
swa: Hivi huyu Pombe nd'o kwamba hana washauri?

eng: Is he unadvisable?
swa: Hashauriki?

eng: Or is he just a fool?
swa: Au ni zuzu?

eng: He's real foolish, this fellow: he doesn't consider the applicable laws before opening his mouth; or does he also suffer from an illness like that of Mnyika?
swa: Bwege sana huyu jamaa; he doesn't consider the law in the place before opening his mouth au na yeye anaumwa ugonjwa wa Mnyika? (Maneno ya Kiingereza yanasema): haheshimu sheria zilizopo kabla ya kufungua mdomo wake

eng: Mulokozi is the latest victim of Tanzania's relatively new Cybercrime Law, which the Parliament passed in April 2015 to address issues such as child pornography, cyberbullying, online impersonation, illegal interception of communications, and the publication of false information.
swa: Mulokozi ni mhanga wa hivi karibuni zaidi wa Sheria ya Makosa ya Mtandao nchini humo, iliyopitishwa na Bunge Aprili 2015 kushugulikia masuala kama picha za ngono kwa watoto, udhalilishwaji wa mtandaoni, matumizi mabaya ya taarifa za watu, kuingilia mawasiliano ya watu isiyo halali, na kuchapisha taarifa za uongo.

eng: Despite widespread opposition from politicians, social media experts, and human rights activists, the bill was pushed through parliament with relatively little discussion or debate.
swa: Pamoja na upinzani mkubwa kutoka kwa wanasiasa, wataalam wa mitandao ya kijamii, na wanaharakati wa haki za binadamu, muswada huo ulipelekwa haraka bungeni baada ya majadiliano au mdahalo wa kiwango cha chini.

eng: Former president Jakaya Kikwete signed it into law in May 2015.
swa: Rais mstaafu Jakaya Kikwete aliusaini muswada huo mnamo Mei 2015 kuwa sheria.

eng: They have also cautioned that police or the state could use their power to harass online activists or social media users.
swa: Wanaonya kwamba polisi au dola inaweza kutumia mamlaka hayo kuwabughudhi wanaharakati wa mtandnaoni au watumiaji wa mitandao ya kijamii.

eng: Tanzanian citizen Isaac Abakuki Emily was convicted this month of insulting Tanzanian President John Magufuli on his Facebook page by the Arusha Resident Magistrate’s Court.
swa: Mwananchi mwingine wa Tanzania Isaac Abakuki Emily alihukumiwa mwezi huu kwa kosa la kumtukana Rais wa Tanzania John Magufuli kwenye ukurasa wake wa Facebook na Mahakama ya Hakimu Mkazi mjini Arusha.

eng: Emily may serve three years in prison, or alternatively pay a fine of five million shillings (US $2300), a steep sum in Tanzania, where the GDP per capita amounts to just under US $1000 per year.
swa: Emily anaweza kwenda jela miaka mitatu, au kulipa faini ya shilingi milioni tano za Tanzania (Dola za Marekani $2300), ambacho ni kiasi kikubwa sana nchini Tanzania, ambapo Wastani wa Pato la Mwananchi ni chini ya Dola za Marekani $1000 .

eng: This was reduced from seven million upon appeal by his lawyer, according to local news site The Citizen.
swa: Kiasi hiki kilipunguzwa kutoka milioni saba kwa rufaa ya mwanasheria wake, kwa mujibu wa tovuti ya habari nchini humo iitwayo The Citizen.

eng: He must pay the fine by August 8, or serve the prison term.
swa: Lazima alipe faini hiyo ifikapo mwezi Agosti 8, vinginevyo atalazimika kutumikia kifungo.

eng: The four appeared before a Magistrate's court in Dar Es Salaam on November 6, 2015.
swa: Wanne haoa walisimamishwa mbele ya Hakimu Mkazi jijini Dar Es Salaam mnamo Novemba 6, 2015.

eng: Public prosecutors alleged that the accused published audio information on a WhatsApp group called the "Soka Group", that was intended to mislead the public during the October 2015 Tanzanian general elections, which were plagued by accusations of vote-rigging.
swa: Mwendesha mashtaka wa serikali alidai kwamba watuhumiwa hao walichapisha taarifa ya sauti kwenye kundi la WhatsApp linaloitwa "Soka Group", ambayo ilikusudia kupotosha umma wakati wa uchaguzi mkuu wa Oktoba 2015 nchini Tanzania , ambao uligubikwa na madai ya wizi wa kura.

eng: A few weeks ago, Masonga Kitanda Olivier, a 23-year-old from the Democratic Republic of Congo, was beaten to death by three men in South Delhi’s Vasant Kunj area.
swa: Majuma machache yaliyopita, Masonga Kitanda Olivier, mwenye miaka 23 kutoka Kongo (DRC) aliuawa kwa kupigwa na wanaume watatu kwenye eneo la Vasant Kunj Kusini mwa Delhi.

eng: Olivier had moved to India for university studies and had recently started teaching French in a private institute.
swa: Olivier alihamia India kwa ajili ya masomo ya chuo kikuu na alikuwa ameanza kufundisha Kifaransa kwenye taasisi moja binafsi.

eng: His attackers allegedly used racial slurs as they assaulted him.
swa: Watu hao waliompiga wanadaiwa kusukumwa na hisia za ubaguzi wa rangi kwa sababu walimtukana.

eng: It was far from being the only recent case of violence against African people in India.
swa: Hili halikuwa tukio la kwanza la ukatili dhidi ya Waafrika wanaoishi nchini India.

eng: On May 25, a Nigerian student, 26-year-old Bamilola Kazim, was hit with an iron rod after an altercation over a parking issue with a local in the city of Hyderabad.
swa: Mnamo Mei 25, mwanafunzi wa Naijeria, Bamilola Kazim mwenye miaka 26, alipigwa kwa nondo baada ya kutokea kutokuelewana kuhusiana na eneo la maegesho kwenye jiji la Hyderabad.

eng: He was treated at a local hospital and released.
swa: Alitibiwa kwenye hospitali moja na kuruhusiwa.

eng: And in January, a 21-year-old Tanzanian woman studying in India was beaten, stripped and paraded naked in the streets of the city of Bangalore by a mob because they incorrectly thought her car had run over and killed a local woman.
swa: Mwezi Januari, mwanamke wa ki-Tanzania mwenye miaka 21 anayesoma India alipigwa, kuvuliwa nguo na kutembezwa akiwa uchi kwenye mitaa ya jiji la Bangalore na wahuni kwa sababu walidhani gari lake lilikuwa limemgonga na kumwua mwanamke mmoja.

eng: Three of her friends were also assaulted and the car they were traveling in was set on fire.
swa: Marafiki zake watatu nao walidhalilishwa na gari walilokuwa nalo liliteketezwa kwa moto.

eng: After they were done, the enraged horde went to houses where African students live and harassed them.
swa: Baada ya hayo, wahuni hao walikwenda kwenye nyumba ambazo wanafunzi wa ki-Afrika huishi na kuwafanyia vurugu.

eng: Throughout the last years, similar attacks targeting African nationals and people of African descent have continually made headlines.
swa: Katika kipindi chote cha miaka ya hivi karibuni, mashambulio kama hayo yakiwalenga raia wa ki-Afrika na watu wenye asili ya Afrika yameendela kugonga vichwa vya habari.

eng: So does that mean India has a problem with racism against Africans?
swa: Je, matukio hayo yanamaanisha India inalo tatizo la ubaguzi wa rangi dhidi ya wa-Afrika?

eng: Not if you ask India's Minister of External Affairs Sushma Swaraj, who was reluctant to categorize the Masonga Kitanda Olivier's killing as racist.
swa: Jibu ni hapana kama utamwuuliza waziri wa Mambo ya Kigeni wa India Sushma Swaraj, ambaye alikataa kukubali kuwa mauaji ya Masonga Kitanda Olivier yalisukumwa na hisia za ubaguzi wa rangi.

eng: Swaraj assured that the assault was carried out by anti-social elements and argued that giving the case a racial tinge would be unfair to the people of India, who generally believe in harmonious cohabitation.
swa: Swaraj alisisitiza kuwa udhalilishaji huo ulikuwa na chembechembe za kimatabaka na kudai kwamba kusema suala hilo lilikuwa ni ubaguzi wa rangi isingekuwa haki kwa wa-Hindi, ambao kwa ujumla wanaamini katika undugu na umoja.

eng: I would like to assure African students in India that this an unfortunate and painful incident involving local goons. — Sushma Swaraj (@SushmaSwaraj) 25 May 2016
swa: Ningependa niwahakikishie wanafunzi wa ki-Afrika kwamba tukio hili baya na lisilotarajiwa limesababishwa na wahuni wa eneo husika

eng: Swaraj took to Twitter to urge Indians to tell Africans that India loves them and shake their hand.
swa: Swaraj aingia kwenye mtandao wa Twita kuwasihi wa-Hindi kuwaambia wa-Afrika kuwa India inawapenda na wawashike mikono.

eng: However, many found it naive or hypocritical, in the face of recent violence against Africans as well as the discrimination that persists in other sectors of Indian society.
swa: Hata hivyo, watu wengi walichukulia matamshi hayo kama kutokuelewa hali halisi au basi unafiki, kwa kuangalia matukio ya udhalilishaji wa hivi karibuni uliofanywa dhidi ya wa-Afrika pamoja na ubaguzi unaoendelea kwenye sekta nyinginezo katika jamii ya wa-Hindi.

eng: Even after 70 years of Independence, we can't even make the Indians love each other, and they want us to tell Africans that we love them. — Mr. Tippler (@MrTippler) June 2, 2016
swa: Hata baada ya miaka 70 ya Uhuru, hatuwezi kuwafanya wa-Hindi wapendane, na wanatutaka tuwaambie wa-Afrika eti tunawapenda

eng: @SushmaSwaraj Maybe we shd work on better awareness and not superficial steps.
swa: Labda tuangalie namna bora ya kuongeza uelewa wa jambo hili na sio kutazama mambo kujuu juu.

eng: Besides, rights shd not depend on love. #AfricaIsNotACountry — Mihira Sood (@mihira_sood) 2 June 2016
swa: Wasihi wa-Hindi wenzako wasiwe wabaguzi wa rangi na wasichukie wageni.

eng: me: India loves you
swa: Hebu tubadilishe utambulisho wetu

eng: African citizen: Africa isn't a country https://t.co/UQbY0tPLmR — fluffy (@curiousgawker) 2 de junio de 2016
swa: Nimejaribu kwa jamaa mmoja wa ki-Kenya na alifurahi...aliniambia namna gani wa-Hindi wengi wanafanya akzi Kenya na namna wanavyoheshimiwa na nikajisikia vizuri

eng: @SushmaSwaraj Better still.
swa: Kwa ndugu zangu wa-Afrika,

eng: Urge fellow Indians to not be racist and xenophobic.
swa: Mabaki ya Imani za Kikoloni kwa wa-Afrika' bado Yangalipo

eng: Let's truly change who we are. @apercevoir — Harish Subramanian (@HarishSub) 2 June 2016
swa: Wa-afrika na serikali zao hawajabaki kimya kufuatia mashambulio ya hivi karibuni.

eng: Say "India loves you," then, to Muslims, Dalits, Africans, seculars...and go right back to kicking them in the face? https://t.co/sGXaArGadM — Nehr-who? (@threeinchfooll) 2 June 2016
swa: Al Jazeera iliripoti kwamba kikundi cha mabalozi wa ki-Afrika kimeungana na kutoa kauli ya pamoja kwa niaba ya wananchi wao waishio India, ambao wanaamini wanaishi kwenye "Mazingira ya hofu na kukosekana usalama" baada ya mashambulio hayo dhidi ya wa-Afrika.

eng: However, a minority of Twitter users seemed to think this was a good idea.
swa: Hii si mara ya kwanza kwa suala hili kuwasumbua wanadiplomasia wa Afrika, hata hivyo.

eng: @SushmaSwaraj tried it the kenyan guy was so happy...told me how so many indians work in kenya and how much they are respected there felt gd — Bharathsnayanar (@Bharathsnayana1) 5 June 2016
swa: Mwaka 2015, kabla ya mkutano wa tatu wa Jukwaa la Ushirikiano wa India na Afrika, mabalozi wa ki-Afrika jijini Delhi walidaiwa kutaka kususia maadhimisho ya Siku ya Afrika, ilikuwa imeandaliwana Baraza la Mahusiano ya Kiutamaduni la India jijini Delhi, kwa madai ya chuki dhidi ya wageni wanaoyokabiliana nayo raia wa Afrika wanaoishi India.

eng: 40 envoys almost boycott Africa Day
swa: Mabalozi 40 nusra wasusie Siku ya Afrika

eng: Africans go on camera recounting racism in India.
swa: Waafrika wameenda kwenye vyombo vya habari kulaani ubaguzi wa rangi unaofanywa India

eng: And minister blames media.
swa: Na waziri analaumu vyombo vya habari

eng: Some Africans have recounted their experiences with racism to various media outlets.
swa: Baadhi ya wa-Afrika wameandika kuhusu visa vya ubaguzi wa rangi unaofanyika kwenye vyombo vya habari.

eng: In a June 4 article for Scroll.in, a South African student of South Asian origin talked about subtle forms of racial and cultural stereotypes that exist in India:
swa: Katika makala ya Juni 4 iliyoandikwa kwenye tovuti ya Scroll.in, mwanafunzi wa Afrika Kusini mwenye asili ya Asia Kusini alizungumzia namna moja ya imani za kibaguzi na kiutamaduni zinazoonekana nchini India:

eng: It was also not uncommon for many students to have conversations with me, which they assumed were progressive, about Africa and Africans that were based on crude colonial stereotypes of Africans as being close to nature, having a good sense of rhythm or even, and possibly the most colonial, having big penises.
swa: Ni kawaida kwa wanafunzi wengi hapa kuzungumza na mimi, mazungumzo ambayo wao huyachukulia kwa uzito, kuhusu Afrika na wa-Afrika, hujikita kwenye imani za kikoloni kwa wa-Afrika kama watu wanaothamini asili, wanaoongea kwa bashasha au hata, kwamtazamo wa jumla, kuwa ni watu wenye uume mkubwa.

eng: While many of the students at JNU had an impressively extensive knowledge of their own colonial, independence and post-independence cultural, political, social and religious, and regional histories, as well as knowledge of western theory and philosophy, and were committed to an idea of Left politics that took ideas like South-South solidarity seriously, their knowledge of African social, political and cultural histories as well as present realities was limited.
swa: Wakati wanafunzi wengi chuoni kwangu wanaonekana kuwa na uelewa mkubwa wa historia yao ya ukoloni, uhuru, utamaduni wa baada ya uhuru, siasa, masuala ya kijamii na kidini, pamoja na uelewa wa nadharia na falsafa za kimagharibi, na wengi huwa na mitazamo ya siasa za mrengo wa kushoto kama zile zinazothamini sana umoja wa Kusini-Kusini, lakini uelewa wao wa historia ya Afrika kijamii, kisiasa na kiutamaduni pamoja na hali halisi ya sasa ulikuwa mdogo.

eng: There have been protests too.
swa: Kumekuwa na maadamano pia.

eng: For example, after the killing of Obodo Uzoma Simeon, a 36-year-old Nigerian citizen, outside an African restaurant in Parra in the state of Goa in 2013, more than 50 Nigerians blocked the highway.
swa: Kwa mfano, baada ya mauaji ya Obodo Uzoma Simeon, raia wa Naijeria mwenye miaka 36, nje ya mgahawa wa ki-Afrika jimboni Goa mwaka 2013, zaidi ya wa-Naijeria 50 walifunga barabara kuu.

eng: They stopped the hearse carrying Simeon and dragged his body on the road as a way to draw attention to the case and prevent a cover-up of the murder.
swa: Walisimamisha msafara wa msiba uliokuwa unasafirisha mwili wa Simeon na kuburuta mwili wake barabarani kama namna ya kuvuta hisia za watu kwa suala hilo na kuzuia kufichwa kwa mauaji hayo.

eng: Authorities, however, answered their protest by cracking down on undocumented Nigerians, a campaign that seemed to only make anti-African sentiment worse.
swa: Mamlaka za serikali, hata hivyo, zilijibu maandamano hayo kwa kuendesha zoezi la kuwafukuza wa-Naijeria waliokuwa wakiishi bila kufuata taratibu, zoezi ambalo lilionekana kama kukuza na kufanya hisia za ubaguzi dhidi ya wa-Afrika zionekane wazi zaidi.

eng: The negativity continued after Masonga Kitanda Olivier's murder.
swa: Hisia mbaya ziliendelea baada ya mauaji ya Masonga Kitanda Olivier.

eng: In response to an alleged rape case involving a Nigerian national, Goa's tourism minister publicly accused Nigerians of committing crime on purpose to prolong their stays in India.
swa: Akijibu madai ya tuhuma za ubakaji unaodaiwa kufanywa na raia wa Naijeria, waziri wa utalii wa jimbo la Goa aliwatuhumu wa-Naijeria hadharani kwa kufanya vitendo vya kiuhalisi kwa lengo ya kuongeza muda wa kuishi nchini India.

eng: We should have a strict law where we can deport them. 	Lazima tuwe makini kusimamia sheria ili tuweze kuwafukuza.
But unfortunately there is no such law in India at the moment," he said.
swa: Lakini ni bahati mbaya hatuna sheria kama hiyo nchini India kwa sasa," alisema.

eng: There is little doubt that the series of attacks on African individuals have disgraced India in front of the international community and has strained its ties with African countries.
swa: Upo wasiwasi kwamba mwendelezo wa mashambulizi kwa wa-Afrika umeichafua sifa ya India mbele ya jumuiya ya kimataifa na umetikisa uhusiano wa nchi hiyo na nchi za ki-Afrika.

eng: In an effort to reverse the dismal situation, Sushma Swaraj has sought to provide assurances to African ambassadors and individuals in India alike.
swa: Katika jitihada za kusafisha sura hiyo, Sushma Swaraj has amewahakikishia mabalozi wa ki-Afrika na watu wengine nchini India kuwa hatua stahiki zitachukuliwa.

eng: A group of African students called off a demonstration in the national capital as a result.
swa: Kundi la wanafunzi wa ki-afrika liliahirisha maandano kwenye mji mkuu wa nchi hiyo kuitikia wito huo.

eng: Hopefully, the country will soon be on the path to peace and security for Africans as well as for all marginalized communities in India.
swa: Huenda, nchi hiyo itarudi mapema kwenye njia ya kuwahihikishia amani na usalama wa-Afrika na jamii nyingine za wageni nchini India.

eng: Belarusian Internet users stripped in their workplaces to respond to the President's call to put more effort into their work.
swa: Watumiaji wa mtandao wa intaneti wa ki-Belarusi waliamua kuvua nguo zao wakiwa kazini kutii wito wa Rais wa kuongeza bidii kwa kazi zao.

eng: Image from Instagram.
swa: Picha kutoka mtandao wa Instagram.

eng: Belarusian citizens are not usually known to enthusiastically heed the commands of their long-time president Alyaksandr Lukashenka.
swa: Wananchi wa Belarusia hawana kawaida ya kutii amri za rais wao aliyedumu madarakani kwa kuda mrefu, Alyaksandr Lukashenka.

eng: In fact, his authoritarian monopoly on ruling Belarus is frowned upon.
swa: Kwa hakika, utawala wake wa kiimla nchini humo unaokosolewa sana.

eng: But as it turns out, there are exceptions to every rule.
swa: Lakini inavyoonekana, kila sheria ina mazingira fulani ya kukiukwa.

eng: On June 22, Lukashenka spoke at the All-Belarusian people's meeting, and, ending his speech, issued a call to Belarusians seeking a better life.
swa: Mnamo Juni 22, Lukashenka alizungumza kwenye mkutano unaofahamika kama 'Wa-Belarusi Wote', na alimalizia hotuba yake kwa kuwataka wananchi wote kujibidiisha katika kujitafutia maisha bora.

eng: Our life is about simple things.
swa: Maisha yetu yanahusu mambo rahisi na ya kawaida.

eng: We must get undressed and get to work.
swa: Lazima tuvue nguo tuchape kazi.

eng: Work till we sweat.
swa: Tuchape kazi hata jasho litutoke.

eng: If we don't, we'll perish.
swa: Tusipofanya hivyo, ndugu zangu tutapotea.

eng: The video of Lukashenka's speech made the rounds on social media, with disbelieving users trying to confirm that he had indeed used the word "to strip" (раздеваться) and not the similar-sounding "to develop " (развиваться).
swa: Video ya hotuba ya Lukashenka imesambaa sana kwenye mitandao ya kijamii, huku watumiaji wa mitandao hiyo wasioamini kama kwenye Rais aliyatamka maneno hayo na kujaribu kuthibitisha kama kweli Rais alitumia neno "kuvua nguo" (раздеваться) na sio neno jingine lenye matamshi kama hayo lenye maana ya "kuendeleza" (развиваться).

eng: But the transcript of the speech on the presidential website confirmed it.
swa: Lakinihotuba iliyoandikwa na kuwekwa kwenye tovuti ya ikulu ya nchi hiyo inathibitisha kwamba kweli Rais alimaanisha wananchi wavue nguo.

eng: And so the Belarusians took to the task with gusto.
swa: Kwa hiyo wananchi wakaamua kweli kutekeleza agizo hilo.

eng: Soon, social media were flooded with photos and videos of (mostly young) Belarusians in their offices and workplaces, stark naked, strategically covering themselves with binders, office tables, laptops, and going about their workday.
swa: Punde, mitandao ya kijamii ikafurika picha na video (nyingi zikiwa za vijana) wa ki-Belarusi wakiwa maofisini na makazini, uchi, huku wakifunika kidogo sehemu zao za siri kwa meza, kompyuta mpakato, na vifaa vingine na kuonekana wakiendelea na kazi zao.

eng: Belarusian urban news website CityDog collected the best specimens of the social network flashmob.
swa: Tovuti ya habari nchini humo iitwayo CityDog ilikusanya baadhi ya picha hizo kwenye mitandao ya kijamii.

eng: Batka (Lukashenko's nickname) said we should get naked and work, so we got naked and are working.
swa: Batka (jina la utani la Lukashenko) alisema tuvue nguo tufanye kazi, kwa hiyo tumeamua kubaki uchi tuchape kazi.

eng: We'll follow the advice as well))
swa: Tunazingatia ushauri wa Rais))

eng: Anything to prop up the country's economy.
swa: Tunafanya lolote liwezekanalo kukuza uchumi wa nchi.

eng: Thousands of Belarusians have been posting pictures on Instagram, Facebook, and Twitter using the hashtag #раздеватьсяиработать (#getnakedandwork).
swa: Maelfu ya wa-Belarusi wameweka picha kwenye mitandao ya Instagram, Facebook, na Twitter kwa kutumia alama ishara ya #раздеватьсяиработать (#vuanguofanyakazi).

eng: I weeded the strawberries today.
swa: Nilichuma matunda leo.

eng: And how have you fulfilled the state's command?
swa: Nikajiuliza nawezaje kutekeleza amri ya Rais?

eng: The flashmob became so popular that even users from other countries on the RuNet and beyond joined in.
swa: Vituko vya picha hizo vilishika kasi kiasi cha kuwavutia watumiaji wa mtandao katika nchi nyingine Urusi kushiriki.

eng: Supporting the Belarusian flashmob!
swa: Tunaunga mkono harakati za wa-Belarusi!

eng: Japan is experiencing a bit of a love affair with the capybara, the large, hamster-like rodent with a gentle disposition and a preference for hot spring baths.
swa: Inaonekana,kwa kiasi fulani, nchi ya Japan ina mapenzi na kapibara, wanyama wakubwa wenye sura kama ya panya buku wanaopenda kuogolea kwenye maji ya moto.

eng: The video "scratching many capybaras" has so far racked up more the 1.2 million views:
swa: Video ya "namna ya kuwasugua kapibara" imetazamwa mara milioni 1.2:

eng: The main attraction of the website is a "capybara navigator" that shows where to find the hamster-like rodent in prefectures all over Japan.
swa: Kivutio kikuu cha tovuti hiyo ni "ramani ya kapibara" inaonesha wapi unaweza kumpata mnyama huyo mwenye sura kama panya buku kote nchini Japani.

eng: The page's Twitter account has some amusing images as well:
swa: Akaunti ya ukurasa wa Twita ina picha nyingine:

eng: I went and saw the capybaras at Reoma Resort (in Kagawa on the island of Shikoku), and I'll be flying back home today.
swa: Nilikwenda kuwaona kapibara pale kwenye Mgahawa wa Reoma (eneo la Kagawa kwenye kisiwa cha Shikoku), na nitasafiri kwa ndege kurudi nyumbani leo.

eng: I'll provide an update on my blog.
swa: Nitawapa habari zaidi kwenye blogu yangu.

eng: The most popular video on the YouTube channel shows a capybara jumping from a pool:
swa: Video maarufu kwenye chaneli ya YouTube inamwonesha kapibara akirukia kwenye bwawa la kuogelea:

eng: Capybaras, which are native to South America, are well-known in Japan thanks to the popular cartoon character Kapibara-san.
swa: Kapibara wana asili ya Marekani ya Kusini, wanafahamika sana nchini Japani shauri ya katuni mmoja maarufu aitwaye Kapibara-san.

eng: From TRYWORKS: Kapibara-san is collaborating with LINE Pokopan in a hit new game!
swa: Kutoka tovuti ya TRYWORKS: Kapibara-san anashirikana na LINE Pokopan katika mchezo mpya mkali!

eng: Kapibara-san ranks against other animals and friends for loads of fun.
swa: Kapibara-san ni mkali kwa wanyama wote na ni rafiki mwenye mengi ya kuvutia.

eng: Details here: https://t.co/MSX5rqFzkY pic.twitter.com/lJKJqCJ6kt
swa: Habari zaidi hapa: https://t.co/MSX5rqFzkY pic.twitter.com/lJKJqCJ6kt

eng: The love for capybaras is not limited to Japanese people.
swa: Mapenzi ya kapibara hayapo Japani pekee.

eng: Umami Dearest, a member of American online community MetaFilter, has also created a guide to animal cafes in Japan, and her website includes where to see capybaras in that country. Capybaras are big at Japanese animal-petting spots #capybara #gianthamster #wetcapybara http://t.co/8Re8C0LM49 pic.twitter.com/1lNZpHtFVC — Animal Cafes (@AnimalCafes) August 7, 2015
swa: Umami Dearest, mwanachama wa jumuiya ya mtandaoni ya MetaFilter, ametengeneza mwongozo wa kwenda kwenye migahawa ya wanyama nchini Japani, na tovuti yake ina maelezo ya wapi unaweza kumwona kapibara nchini humo.

eng: For those who are interested, Umami Dearest has also posted some handy FAQ's about animal cafes in Japan.
swa: Kwa wale wanaopenda, Umami Dearest amechapisha baadhi ya Maswali Yanayoulizwa Mara kwa Mara kuhusu mikahawa ya wanyama nchini Japani.

eng: Donald Trump's presidential campaign has always advocated “getting tough on Iran,” but the rhetoric escalated ever so slightly last week, when retired Lieutenant General Michael T. Flynn, one of Trump's chief military advisors and a former director of the Defense Intelligence Agency, demanded that Ayatollah Khomeini—a man who's been dead for more than a quarter of a century—condemn the attack on July 14 in Nice, France.
swa: Kampeni ya Urais ya Donald Trump imekuwa ikipigania "kuchukuliwa kwa hatua kali dhidi ya Iran," lakini propaganda imeenea juma lililopita, kudai kuwa Luteni Jenerali Mstaafu Michael T. Flynn, mmoja wa washauri wakuu wa Trump wa masuala ya kijeshi na mkurugenzi wa zamani wa Shirika la Upelelezi wa Kiusalam (DIA), alimtoa wito kwa Ayatollah Khomeini—mtu ambaye alifariki zaidi ya robo karne iliyopita—kulaani shambulio lililofanyika Julai 14, mjini Nice, nchini Ufaransa.

eng: Michael Flynn, former director of the Defense Intelligence Agency, calls on a man dead 27 years to condemn extremism pic.twitter.com/qhtxOYeHce — Samuel Oakford (@samueloakford) July 15, 2016
