swa: Michael Flynn, mkurugenzi wa zamani wa Shirika la Upelelezi wa Kusalam, alitoa wito kwa mtu aliyekufa miaka 27 iliyopita kulaani msimamo mkali wa kidini

eng: Appearing on Fox News with Megyn Kelly, Flynn said angrily, “I want the Imam, or Khomeini, to stand up and be counted and to talk about this radical form of ideology in their bloodstream, in their DNA."
swa: Akiongea kwenye Kituo cha Televisheni cha Fox News akiwa na Megyn Kelly, Flynn alisema kwa hasira, “Ninamtaka Imam, au Khomeini, atoke hadharani na kuzungumzia itikadi hii kali ya kidini isiyojitenga na damu na nasaba za dini yao."

eng: Ayatollah Sayyid Ruhollah Khomeini died in 1989 after establishing the Islamic Republic of Iran, the first modern-day theocracy, following the Islamic Revolution in 1979.
swa: Ayatollah Sayyid Ruhollah Khomeini alikufa 1989 baada ya kuasisi Taifa ya Kiislamu la Iran, nchi ya kwanza ya kidini, kufuatia Mapinduzi ya Kiislam mwaka 1979.

eng: Flynn either confused the name “Khomeini” with Iran's current supreme leader, Ayatollah Sayyed Ali Hosseini Khamenei, or he is unaware that Ayatollah Khomeini died 27 years ago.
swa: Inaonekana Flynn ama alichanganya jina “Khomeini” na jina la Kiongozi Mkuu wa sasa, Ayatollah Sayyed Ali Hosseini Khamenei, au basi hakuwa anafahamu kuwa Ayatollah Khomeini alikufa miaka 27 iliyopita.

eng: Whether the mistake was confusion or ignorance, Flynn appeared on Fox News again the following day, on July 15, and said Khomeini again, insisting that the long-dead man denounce the attacks in Nice.
swa: Iwe kwamba kosa hilo limetokana na kuchanganya mambo au basi tu kutokujua, Flynn alionekana Fox News kwa mara nyingine kesho yake, mnamo Julai 15, na kumtaka Khomeini, akisisitiza kwamba mtu huyo aliyefariki zamani alaani mashambulio ya mjini Nice.

eng: Internet users both in Iran and the US have shared a few thoughts about Flynn's curious interest in “the Imam Khomeini."
swa: Watumiaji wa mtandao wa Intaneti nchini Irani na Marekani walisema machache kuhusiana na shauku hiyo ya Flynn kwa “Imam Khomeini."

eng: Iranian Twitter user Ameneh Mousavi tweeted:
swa: Mtumiaji wa Twita Ameneh Mousavi alitwiti:

eng: Wise people, can this be right?
swa: Watu wenye hekima, hivi hili linaweza kuwa sawa?

eng: General Michael Flynn, Donald Trump's military advisor, wants "Ayatollah Khomeini," the leader of Iran, to condemn the Nice terrorist attacks.
swa: Jenerali Michael Flynn, mshauri wa jeshi wa Donald Trump anamtaka "Ayatollah Khomeini," kiongozi wa Iran, kulaani mashambulio ya kigaidi ya Nice.

eng: Iranian-American journalist Saman Arbabi wrote:
swa: Mwandishi wa ki-Iran mwenye asili ya Marekani Saman Arbabi aliandika:

eng: On foreign policy #Trump team makes Bush team look like Nobel Laureate winners. https://t.co/AwQkXcLIeg — Saman Arbabi (@SamanArbabi) July 15, 2016
swa: Kuhusu sera ya mamabo ya nje, timu ya Trump inamfanya timu Bush ionekane kama mshindi wa Tuzo ya Amani ya Nobel

eng: American Internet users took an interest in the story, as well, after the Huffington Post wrote about it:
swa: Watumiaji wa mtandao wa intaneti walitazama suala kuu la habari hiyo, kadhalika, baada ya Huffington Post kuliandika suala hilo:

eng: Flynn’s offer to list Muslim leaders was undermined by the fact that his top example had been dead for 30 years https://t.co/8thyQRxdbQ — Christina Wilkie (@christinawilkie) July 15, 2016
swa: Maneno ya Flynn kuwahusisha viongozi wa Kiislam hayana maana kwa sababu anayemtaja amekufa miaka 30 iliyopita

eng: Cool, let's give the codes to ppl who cant tell diff bet. living ppl and really dead ones COME ON https://t.co/MRhPsxayug via @HuffPostPol — Maude Snuggs (@MillCunningham) July 15, 2016
swa: Sawa, eti tuwape madaraka watu ambao hawawezi hata kutofautisha watu waliokufa na wale walio hai

eng: A parody account satirizing the Russian foreign minister, Sergei Lavrov, also had some thoughts:
swa: Akaunti ya mashabiki wanaomkejeli waziri wa Mashauri ya Kigeni wa Urusi, Sergei Lavrov, ilikuwa na maoni yafuatayo:

eng: Wonder if he knows that Gorbachev isn't president of Russia.
swa: Inawezekana huyu jamaa anajua Gorbachev bado ni rais wa Urusi.

eng: Trump adviser wants Khomeini to denounce Nice attack https://t.co/hR30iNCypp — Soviet Sergey (@SovietSergey) July 18, 2016
swa: Mshauri wa Trump anamtaka Khomeini alaani shambulio la kigaidi la Nice

eng: As if by magic, Google Maps changed some town names in Crimea overnight.
swa: Kama vile ni miujiza, Ramani za Google zilibadili ghafla baadhi ya majina ya miji kwenye pwani ya Crimea.

eng: Images edited by Tetyana Lokot.
swa: Picha zimehaririwa na Tetyana Lokot.

eng: On July 27 Internet giant Google renamed a number of towns, villages, and settlements in Crimea—a peninsula in Ukraine that has been under Russian control since early 2014—on their Google Maps service.
swa: Mnamo Julai 27, Google ambao ndio mtandao mkubwa zaidi kwenye intaneti ilibadili majina ya baadhi ya miji, vijiji na mitaa ya Crimea -peninsula ya Ukraine ambayo imekuwa ikitawaliwa na Urusi tangu mapema 2014 —kwa kutumia huduma yake ya Ramani za Google.

eng: The change came after the Ukrainian parliament altered the names of 70 geographic locations in Crimea in accordance with its “decommunization” campaign in May 2016.
swa: Mabadiliko hayo yalikuja baada ya bunge la Ukraine kubadili majina ya maeneo ya kijiografia yapatayo 70 kwa mujibu wa kampeni ya "kupambana na ukomunisti" mwezi Mei 2016.

eng: Users of the Russian and Ukrainian versions of Google Maps noticed the differences immediately.
swa: Watumiaji wa Ramani za Google kwa ki-Rusi na ki-Ukraine waligundua mabadiliko hayo mara moja.

eng: For instance, according to a report by Meduza news website, the town of Krasnoperekopsk became “Yany Kapu,” Sovetskoe turned into “Ichki,” and Kirovskoe was changed to “Islyam-Terek.”
swa: Kwa mfano, kwa mujibu wa taarifa iliyoandikwa na tovuti ya habari ya Meduza, mji wa Krasnoperekopsk ulibadilika kuwa “Yany Kapu,” Sovetskoe ukawa “Ichki,” na Kirovskoe ulibadilishwa kuwa “Islyam-Terek.”

eng: Many of the new names have Crimean Tatar origin or other historic roots, replacing the Soviet-era variants.
swa: Majina mengi mapya yalikuwa na asili ya lugha ya ki-Crimea Tatari na historia nyinginezo, na kuodnoa majina yaliyokuwa na asili ya ki- Soviet.

eng: The change on Google Maps immediately provoked a backlash from Russian and Crimean officials.
swa: Mabadiliko ya Ramani za Google yalichokoza hasira za maafisa wa Urusi na Crimea.

eng: The head of annexed Crimea Sergey Aksyonov accused Google in a Facebook post of "producing a propagandistic product" and of "trying to create their own reality."
swa: Mkuu wa Crimea Sergey Aksyonov aliituhumu Google kwa bandiko la facebook "lililotengenezwa na wafanya propaganda" na kwa "kujaribu kutengeneza ukweli wanaouona wao."

eng: Russian communications minister Nikolay Nikiforov also joined in the criticism, saying that if Google didn't stick to Russian laws and the Russian names of towns and villages (in Crimea), it would "prevent the company from doing effective business in Russia."
swa: Waziri wa mawasiliano nchini urusi Nikolay Nikiforov pia aliungana na Sergey kukosoa mabadiliko hayo, akisema kwamba kama Google haitaheshimu sheria za Urusi na majina ya Urusi kwa miji na vijiji (huko Crimea), basi "ingeizuia kampuni hiyo kufanya biashara nchini Urusi."

eng: Ukrainian foreign minister Pavlo Klimkin reacted to the backlash on Twitter, referring to what Ukraine believes to be illegal occupation of Crimea by Russia:
swa: Waziri wa mambo ya kigeni wa Ukraine Pavlo Klimkin alijibu maneno hayo kwneye mtandao wa twita, akirejea kile ambacho Ukraine inakiamini kuwa kukaliwa isivyo halali kwa Crimea na Urusi:

eng: Renaming the stolen is a house of cards: it is bound to collapse under the weight of truth. #CrimeaIsUkraine — Pavlo Klimkin (@PavloKlimkin) July 28, 2016
swa: Kubadili majina ya sehemu zilizoibwa ni kucheza bahati nasibu: hatua hiyo itashindwa na ukweli

eng: On July 28, a spokesperson for Google told RBC news website that they were aware of the changes made in accordance with Ukraine's "decommunization" law and of Russia's displeasure.
swa: Mnamo Julai 28, msemaji wa Google aliiambia tovuti ya habari ya RBC kwamba walikuwa wanafahamu kwamba mabadiliko ya majina hayo yalifanyika kwamujibu wa sheria ya "kuachana na ukomunisti" ya Ukraine na hatua ambayo Urusi hawaifurahii.

eng: Google told RBC they were "actively working to restore the previous version of the names on the Russian version of Google Maps."
swa: Google iliiambia RBC kwmaba walikuwa "wanafanya kazi kwa bidii kurudisha majina ya zamani kwenye toleo la Ramani za Google kwa ki-Rusi."

eng: The Ukrainian government lost control of the Crimean peninsula in the spring of 2014, following a disputed referendum on seceding from Ukraine and joining the Russian Federation.
swa: Serikali ya Ukraine imepoteza udhibiti wa peninsula ya Crimea kwenye msimu wa masika ya 2014, kufuatia kura ya maoni iliyoamua kujitenga kwa eneo hilo kutoka Ukraine na kujiunga na Shirikisho la Urusi.

eng: Most of the world does not recognize Russia's subsequent annexation of the territory of Crimea.
swa: Jumuiya ya Kimataifa haiitambui hatua hiyo ya Urusi kuichukua Crimea.

eng: Source: Facebook
swa: Chanzo: Facebook

eng: After the Department of Justice in the United States filed lawsuits accusing Malaysian officials and their associates for laundering more than one billion US dollars through American institutions, Malaysians are wondering if ‘Malaysian Official 1,’ who is cited 36 times in the 136-page lawsuit, is actually their Prime Minister Najib Razak.
swa: Baada ya Wizara ya Sheria ya Marekani kufungua mashitaka mashtaka wakiwatuhumu maafisa wa Malayasia na wasaidizi wao kwa kutakatisha zaidi ya dola bilioni moja za marekani kupitia taasisi za ki-Marekani, wa-Malaysia wanahoji kama mtu aliyepachikwa jina la ‘Afisa wa Malaysia 1,’ anayeonekana mara 36 kwenye hati ya mashitaka yenye kurasa 136, ni waziri mkuu Najib Razak.

eng: The prime minister controls the 1Malaysian Development Berhad (1MDB) investment firm, which is at the centre of the lawsuit.
swa: Waziri Mkuu anaendesha Mradi wa kampuni ya uwekezaji wa Kimaendeleo ya 1Malaysian Berhad (1MDB), ambao ndio hasa kiini cha shitaka hilo.

eng: His stepson is also one of the accused.
swa: Mtoto wake wa kambo ni moja wapo wa watuhumiwa.

eng: The lawsuit aims to recover 17 assets in the US, which have allegedly been acquired through 1MDB funds.
swa: Mashataka hayo yanalenga kunyang'anywa mali zipatazo 17 nchini Marekani, ambazo zinadaiwa kupatikana kwa fedha za mradi wa 1MDB.

eng: The lawsuits claims 1MDB funds were spent on hotels, fine art, luxury real estate in New York, Los Angeles, and London, and even on the 2013 Hollywood film “The Wolf of Wall Street.”
swa: Shitaka hilo linadai fedha hizo zilitumiwa na mradi huo kwa ajili ya hoteli, sanaa, makazi ya kifahari kwenye majiji ya New York, Los Angeles, na London, na hata kwenye filamu ya 2013 ya Hollywood iitwayo “The Wolf of Wall Street.”

eng: This is not the first time that Najib Razak's name has been implicated in a corruption scandal.
swa: Hii si mara ya kwanza kwa jina la Najib Razak kuhusishwa na kashfa za ufisadi.

eng: Previously, he has been accused of pocketing more than 600 million dollars through anomalous transactions.
swa: Kipindi cha nyuma, waziri mkuu alituhumiwa kujipatia fedha zaidi ya dola milioni 600 kupitia miamala isiyoeleweka.

eng: After he was linked to several large dollar bank accounts, he claimed the funds were a political donation from a royal family in Saudi Arabia.
swa: Baada ya kuhusishwa na akaunti kadhaa kubwa zenye kutumia dola, alidai fedha hizo zilikuwa michango ya kisiasa kutoka kwenye familia ya ki-Falme nchini Saudi Arabia.

eng: US officials said the lawsuit is the “largest single action ever brought under the Kleptocracy Asset Recovery Initiative.”
swa: Maafisa wa Marekani walisema shtaka hilo ni "hatua kubwa zaidi kuwahi kuchukuliwa chini ya Mpango wa Kuokoa Mali wa Kleptocracy.”

eng: They vowed to return the funds to the Malaysian people:
swa: Waliapa kurudisha fedha hizo kwa watu wa Malaysia:

eng: The Department of Justice will not allow the American financial system to be used as a conduit for corruption.
swa: Idara ya ya Sheria haitaruhusu mfumo wa fedha wa Marekani utumike kufanya vitendo vya kifisadi.

eng: With this action, we are seeking to forfeit and recover funds that were intended to grow the Malaysian economy and support the Malaysian people.
swa: Kwa hatua hizi, tunatafuta kunyang'anya na kurudisha fedha hizo zilizokuwa zimelengwa kukuza uchumi wa Malyasia na kuwaidia watu wa Malaysia.

eng: Instead, they were stolen, laundered through American financial institutions and used to enrich a few officials and their associates.
swa: Badala yake, wameibiwa, kutapeliwa kupitia taasisi za ki-Marekani na kuwawezesha vigogo wachache kujitajirisha na marafiki zao.

eng: Many Malaysians believe the text of the lawsuit provides enough evidence against Najib.
swa: raia wengi wa Malaysia wanaamini maandishi yanayoonekana kwenye shitaka hiyo ni ushahidi tosha dhidi ya Najib.

eng: I don't see how MALAYSIAN OFFICIAL 1 could be anyone other than Najib in US DOJ case against 1MDB pic.twitter.com/z6xPE9OCh8 — Khairil Yusof (@kaerumy) July 20, 2016 #MalaysianOfficial1 Why is it so hard to find this guy? pic.twitter.com/v67tTpNHZa — David Teoh (@dteoh) July 22, 2016
swa: Sioni namna gani huyu anayeitwa AFISA WA MALAYSIA1 anaweza kuwa mtu mwingine zaidi ya Najib kwenye shitaka hili la Wizara ya Sheria ya Marekani kwenye kashafa hii

eng: DOJ stands for the US Department of Justice.
swa: Kwa nini ni vigumu kumpata mtu huyu?

eng: Former Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, who is calling for the resignation of Najib, urged the US to name Najib in the lawsuit:
swa: Waziri Mkuu wa Zamani Mahathir Mohamad, anayemtaka Najib ajiuzulu, aliiomba Marekani kumtaja Najib kwenye sitaka hilo:

eng: If the US really believes in eradicating corruption and money laundering which involves their country, they should not be shy about naming names and letting due process to take place.
swa: Kama Marekani inaamini kwa dhati kabisa katika kuukomesha ufisadi na utakatishaji wa fedha haramu unaoihusisha nchi yao, lazima wawe majasiri na kutaja majina ya wahusika na kuruhusu taratibu za kisheria kufanyika.

eng: When the thief is in charge of the police and the prosecuting agency, only foreign intervention can bring about justice.
swa: Mwizi anapokuwa mkuu wa polisi na idara za mashataka, hapo tunahitaji msaada wa nchi za kigeni kuhakikisha haki inapatikana.

eng: Let me clearly and formally declare that I am not the “Malaysian Official 1.” Will the Prime Minister, Datuk Seri Najib Razak similarly state his position – to formally deny it or confirm whether he is referred to as “Malaysian Official 1” and if the latter, what he proposes to do about the DOJ action.
swa: Naomba rasmi nitangaze wazi kwamba mimi sio "Afisa wa Malaysia1.” je, Waziri Mkuu, Datuk Seri Najib Razak atasema msimamo wake – kukanusha rasmi au kuthibitisha kwamba yeye ndiye anayetajwa kwa jina la “Afisa wa Malaysia 1” na kama ni kweli, anapendekeza hatua gani zichukuliwe.

eng: Najib’s camp is insisting that the name of the prime minister is not part of the lawsuit, which means there’s no basis in accusing him of corruption in relation to the 1MDB scandal.
swa: Kambi ya Najib inasisitiza kwamba jina la waziri mkuu halipo kwenye mashtaka hayo, ikiwa na maana kwamba hakuna msingi wa kumtuhumu waziri mkuu kwa ufisadi unaotajwa kwenye kashfa hiyo ya 1MDB.

eng: Some supporters of Najib are partly admitting that “Malaysian Official 1” could be referring to the prime minister, but they claim that the information presented by the US government is incorrect.
swa: Wanaomwunga mkono Najib kwa sehemu wanakiri kwamba “Afisa wa Malaysia1” anaweza kuwa waziri mkuu lakini wanadai taarifa zinazotolewa na serikali ya Marekani si sahihi.

eng: The hashtag #MalaysianOfficial1 trended after netizens reacted to the US DOJ report.
swa: ALama ishara ya #MalaysianOfficial1 imekuwa maarufu baada ya watumiaji wa mtandao kupata habari za taarifa ya Wizara ya Sheria ya marekani.

eng: Some even launched a campaign calling Internet users to search for the real ‘Malaysian Official 1’.
swa: Baadhi ya watumiaji wa mtandao wameanzisha kampeni ya kuwaomba watumiaji wengine wa mtandao kumtafuta 'Afisa wa Malaysia1’ halisi.

eng: I respect the position of PM but I've lost my respect for the man currently holding the position... #MalaysianOfficial1 @Malaysia_Gov — Nelson Pung (@NelsonPung) July 23, 2016
swa: Ninaheshimu nafasi ya Waziri Mkuu lakini nimepoteza heshima yangu kwa mtu aliyeshikilia madaraka hayo kwa sasa

eng: I'm angry that the money is used like a personal bank account.
swa: Nina hasira kwamba fedha za wananchi zinatumiwa kama vile ni za mtu binafsi.

eng: Front cover of the newspaper Canal de Moçambique.
swa: Ukurasa wa mbele wa gazeti la Canal de Moçambique.

eng: Photo: Dércio Tsandzana
swa: Picha: Dércio Tsandzana

eng: According to one of Mozambique's most trusted newspapers, Canal de Moçambique, the government has begun installing 450 security cameras in the cities of Maputo and Matola, as part of the “National Ordonnance on Intercepting Information” project, which reportedly includes plans to wiretap the general public.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa moja wapo ya magazeti yanayoaminika zaidi nchini Msumbiji, Canal de Moçambique, serikali imeanza kufunga kamera 450 za usalama kwenye miji ya Maputo na Matola, kama sehemu ya mradi wa “Mpango wa Taifa wa Kufuatilia Habari”, ambao unadaiwa kuwa na mipango ya kufuatilia nyendo za wananchi wa kawaida.

eng: (Earlier this year in May, Global Voices wrote about Mozambique's controversial plan.)
swa: (Mapema mwaka huu mwezi Mei, Global Voices iliandika kuhusu mpango huu wa Msumbiji wenye utata.)

eng: According to Canal de Moçambique, the government contracted “Msumbiji Investment Limited” to carry out the massive installation, without receiving any alternative offers for the procurement order.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Canal de Moçambique, serikali imeingia mkataba na “Kampuni ya Uwekezaji ya Msumbiji” kufunga kamera hizo, bila ushindani wa zabuni.

eng: The company, moreover, belongs to former President Armando Guebuza's son, who subcontracted the Chinese firm “ZTE” to perform the actual work, says the newspaper.
swa: Kampuni hiyo, hata hivyo, inamilikiwa na mtoto wa Rais wa zamani Armando Guebuza, aliyetoa kazi hiyo kwa kampuni ya ki-China "ZTE" kufanya kazi hiyo, linasema gazeti.

eng: Egídio Vaz, a prominent analyst and social media activist, was indignant about the situation:
swa: Egídio Vaz, mchambuzi maarufu na mwanaharakati wa mitandaoni, alionesha wasiwasi wake kwa hali hiyo:

eng: For more than two months, we have seen news of the big deals of these industrious sons of the fatherland’s hero.
swa: Kwa zaidi ya miezi miwili, tumesoma habari za miradi mikubwa ya watoto wakubwa wa nchi hii.

eng: My mood has worsened.
swa: Nimejisikia vibaya.

eng: This is bad.
swa: Hii si sahihi hata kidogo.

eng: But there is a cure for me.
swa: Lakini kuna tiba ya hali hii kwangu.

eng: TO FORGET.
swa: KUSAHAU.

eng: Schauque Spirou addressed the possible consequences of installing surveillance cameras throughout Maputo and Matola, recalling what happened in Brazil:
swa: Schauque Spirou alizungumzia uwezekano wa matokeo ya kufungwa kwa kamera hizo za usalama kwenye miji yote ya Maputo na Matola, akijaribu kukumbuka kile kilichotokea Brazil:

eng: We are slowly waking up, or we are sleeping and unaware… but there is no doubt that Big Brother is in action… the information given by Canal de Moçambique on the security cameras—I think that it should not be taken lightly: except the “tendering” of that kind… In Brazil, there is already talk of a “fines industry”, since the security cameras in the streets of São Paulo are used to catch “Formula 1 drivers”… but the money generated by these fines is causing mistrust among the most aware.
swa: Tunaamka taratibu, au tunalala bila kujua...lakini hakuna mashaka kuwa Mkubwa yuko kazini...taarifa zilizoandikwa na Canal de Moçambique kuhusu kamera za usalama -nadhani zisichukuliwe kirahisi: isipokuwa "utoaji wa zabuni" wa namna hiyo... Nchini Brazil, kuna mazungumzo ya “biashara ya kupiga faini”, kwa sababu kamera za usalama zilizofungwa kwenye mitaa ya São Paulo inatumika kuwamata “Madereva Formula 1 ”… lakini pesa zinazoingizwa kwa faini hizi zinasababisha hali ya kutokuaminika.

eng: According to Canal de Moçambique, however, the government might have legal grounds for awarding the surveillance contract without a public competition, given that the country's procurement law treats certain national-security concerns as an exception.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Canal de Moçambique, hata hivyo, serikali inaweza kuwa na uwezo wa kisheria kuingia mkataba na kampuni yoyote bila ushindani za kizabuni, kwa sababu sheria ya manunuzi ya nchi hiyo inaweka mwanya huo kwa masuala yanayohusu usalama wa taifa.

eng: But this still wouldn't justify the decision to award the contract to Guebuza’s son, given the possible conflict of interest.
swa: Lakini bado, hata hivyo, sheria hiyo haihallaishi uamuzi huu wa kutoa tenda kwa mtoto wa Guebuza, kwa kuzingatia uwezekano wa mgongano wa maslahi.

eng: Screen shot from "How the Cossacks Rescued Their Fiances" (1973).
swa: Picha iliyopigwa kwenye filamu ya "Namna Wakulima wa Kirusi Walivyowanusuru Wachumba Zao" (1973).

eng: Traditional' bondage in Mauritania; forced prostitution in Europe; and bride kidnapping in Kyrgyzstan.
swa: Kwa mfano kuna taarifa za utumwa wa 'kimila' nchini Mauritania; ukahaba wa kulazimishwa barani Ulaya; na vitendo vya utekeaji wa mabibi arusi nchini Kyrgyzstan.

eng: In 2016, an estimated 45.8 million were subjected to some form of slavery in 167 countries, according to the Global Slavery Index.
swa: Mwaka 2016, inakadiriwa watu milioni 45.8 walikuwa wahanga wa namna fulani ya utumwa katika nchi 167, kwa mujibu wa Kipimo cha Utumwa duniani.

eng: Even though slavery continues to plague us, discussions about human trafficking or slavery are seldom part of mainstream public discourse, and rarely do these conversations cater to children.
swa: Ingawa vitendo vya utumwa vinaendelea kuzisumbua jamii nyingi duniani, majadiliano kuhusu usafirishwaji wa binadamu na namna mbalimbali za utumwa hayaonekani kupea nafasi kwenye mijadala ya wazi, na mazungumzo haya hayapewi nafasi wazazi wanapozungumza na watoto.

eng: But an episode from a classic Ukrainian cartoon series broke taboos around addressing human trafficking as early as 1973.
swa: Lakini kipande kilichopo kwenye mfululizo wa katuni maarufu ya Ukraini kinaonekana kuvunja mwiko wa kutokuzungumzia masuala haya ya utumwa na usafirishaji wa binadamu tangu mwaka 1973 katuni hizo zilipoanza kuoneshwa.

eng: And now thanks to YouTube, almost half a century later, "How the Cossacks Rescued Their Fiancees" (Как казаки невест выручали), from the "How the Cossacks.." series, is making a global comeback.
swa: Hivi sasa kwapitia mtandao wa YouTube, takribani nusu karne baadae, katuni ya, "Namna Wakulima wa Kirusi Walivyowanusuru Wachumba Zao" (How the Cossacks Rescued Their Fiancees"), iliyo kwenye mfululizo uuitwao "Namna Wakulima wa Kirusi..", zinaonekana kurudia umaarufu wake wa awali.

eng: Single episodes of the series, uploaded to the video streaming site, have received as many as a million views.
swa: Kipande kimoja cha mfululizo huo, kilichowekwa kwenye tovuti ya video, kimetazamwa mara milioni moja.

eng: The episode on human trafficking has been viewed more than 500K times and intertwines folklore and social commentary in a way that can be used as a conversation starter about the broad area of kidnapping and slavery.
swa: Kipande kinachohusu usafirishwaji wa binadamu kimetazamwa zaidi ya mara 500,000 na kinaweka mchanganyiko wa masimulizi ya kale na mazungumzo ya kawaida ya kijamii kwa namna ambayo inaweza kutumiwa kuanzisha mazungumzo kuhusu suala zito la utekaji nyara na utumwa.

eng: This episode is a little over 17 minutes long, but well worth your time, as the director Vladimir Dahno combined classic animation techniques with a hilarious storyline and an excellent musical score.
swa: Kipande hiki kina urefu wa dakika kama 17 hivi, lakini kinafaa kutazamwa, kwa sababu mwongozaji wake Vladimir Dahno amechanganya mbinu za kutumia katuni na ucheshi sambamba na muziki mzuri.

eng: This episode follows three Cossacks who pursues a gang of girl-kidnapping pirates through various countries, which include satirically stereotyped depictions of Greece, Egypt and India.
swa: Kipande hiki kinasumulia namna Wakulima watatu wa Kirusi wanaojaribu kuwafuatilia wahuni wanaoteka watoto katika nchi mbalimbali, ikiwa ni pamoja na zile zinazoaminika kuongoza kwa vitendo hivi yaani, Ugiriki, Misri na India.

eng: The use of dialogue is minimal, making this episode accessible to worldwide audiences of all ages.
swa: Maongezi hayajapewa nafasi zaidi ya vitendo, kufanya iweze kuwafaa watazamaji wa nchi zote na umri wowote.

eng: If you liked this episode you might want to check out this list from UA Post: 10 Ukrainian cartoons that will make your children smarter.
swa: Kama unapenda kipande hiki basi wawezi kutazama kwa kutumia orodha iliyopo kwenye tovuti ya UA Post: katuni 10 za ki-Ukraini zinazoweza kuwafanya wanao wakawa werevu zaidi.

eng: Jefferson Krua fled Liberia as a refugee at age 5, and eventually settled in Boston, MA.
swa: Jefferson Krua aliondoka nchini Liberia akiwa na miaka mitano, na kisha kupata makazi ya kudumu huko Boston, MA.

eng: Recently, he's moved back to Liberia to help with re-building the country's infrastructure.
swa: Hivi karibuni alirejea nchini Liberia kwa ajili ya kusaidia kwenye ujenzi mpya wa nchi yake.

eng: Credit: Heidi Shin
swa: Picha kwa hisani ya Heidi Shin

eng: This article by Heidi Shin originally appeared on PRI.org on July 12, 2016, and is republished here as part of a content-sharing agreement.
swa: Makala haya yaliyoandikwa na Heidi Shin kwa mara ya kwanza yalichapishwa PRI.org mnamo tarehe 12 Julai 2016 na yanachapishwa tena hapa kwa makubaliano ya kushirikiana maudhui.

eng: Mercy Krua and her son Jefferson are having a disagreement.
swa: Mercy Krua na mtoto wake Jefferson wanashindwa kuafikiana.

eng: It’s about whether he should move back home.
swa: Sababu kuu ni ikiwa ni sahihi kwa Jefferson kurudi nyumbani.

eng: We’re sitting on her living room couch in Boston, where she’s eager to show off his childhood photos.
swa: Tunakaa kwenye kochi la chumba anachoishi huko Boston, na kisha anakuwa na mshawasha wa kutuonesha picha za utoto wake.

eng: This one’s from graduation, another one’s from the refugee camps in Ghana.
swa: Picha hii ni ya wakati wa mahafali, nah ii ni ya wakati nikiwa kwenye kambi za wakimbizi nchini Ghana.

eng: She’s reminded of what life was like before they fled Liberia, in the midst of its bloody civil wars.
swa: Anakumbushia maisha yalivyokuwa kabla ya kutoka nchi Liberia, kipindi ambacho vita ya wenyewe kwa wenyewe ilipokuwa imeshamiri.

eng: Jefferson was just a small child then, and when he was hungry or tired, she couldn’t offer something as simple as a snack.
swa: Kwa wakati huo, Jefferson alikuwa bado ni kijana mdogo, na pale alipopatwa na njaa au kuchoka, mama yake hakuweza kumpatia hata kifungua kinywa.

eng: Tears would follow, and she would panic, for fear of being discovered: “So you need to make sure the kids don’t cry, to bring like, to raise awareness that people or civilians are in the area.
swa: Machozi yalikuwa yakimtoka, na alikuwa mwenye hofu kuu kwa kuwa angeweza kugundulika: “Kwa hiyo inakupasa kuhakikisha kuwa mtoto halii, ni kama vile kumfahamisha kuwa kulikuwa na watu au raia katika eneo lile.

eng: Cause they didn’t really care, they were killing everybody.
swa: Hii ni kwa sababu watu wale hawakuwa wanajali, walikuwa wakimuua kila mmoja.

eng: So it was difficult, terrible.”
swa: Kwa kweli, ilikuwa hali tete sana, iliogopesha haswa.”

eng: But Jefferson remembers it differently.
swa: Hata hivyo, Jefferson ana kumbukumbu ya tofauti.

eng: He was just 5 years old when they left, and it all felt like an adventure.
swa: Wakati wanaondoka, yeye alikuwa na miaka mitano tu, na yeye alijisikia kama vile ni safari ya mapumziko.

eng: Hiding in the back of a UN food truck to gain safe passage out of Liberia, escaping through the jungles of Côte d’Ivoire, before landing in the refugee camps of Ghana, where they spent seven years.
swa: Kujificha nyuma ya gari la misaada ya chakula la Umoja wa Mataifa (UN) ili kupata mwanya wa kuondoka Liberia kupitia kwenye misitu ya Ivory Coast na kabla ya kufikia kwenye kambi za wakimbizi nchini Ghana, ambapo waliishi kwa miaka saba.

eng: Jefferson says when they eventually arrived in the US, that’s when he remembers that life got hard.
swa: Jefferson anasema kuwa, mara baada ya kuwasili nchini Marekani, ndipo alipogundua kuwa maisha haya kuwa yakimwendea vizuri hapo awali.

eng: It was the 1990s, and he was about to start middle school.
swa: Hii ilikuwa ni kwenye miaka ya 1990, ambapo alikuwa karibu kuanza shule ya sekondari.

eng: He takes me back to the housing projects in Boston where he spent most of his teen years.
swa: Ananichukua hadi kwenye miradi ya nyumba huko Boston mahali ambapo aliishi kwa kipindi chote cha ujana wake.

eng: He reminds me to lock the car door, and points to the street corner where he was jumped and his cousin was mugged, all while the school crossing guard looked on.
swa: Ananikumbusha kufunga mlango wa gari na kisha kunionesha kwenye kona ya barabara, mahali ambapo yeye na mpwa wake walishambuliwa huku mlinzi wa shule akishuhudia.

eng: We hear the sounds of squeaking swings, and kids shouting in Cape Verdean and Creole, so they can be heard over the blaring of the police sirens and ambulances driving by.
swa: Tunasikia sauti nyembamba za bembea, na watoto wanapiga kelele kwa lafudhi za kikepverde na lafudhi ya waafrika waliozaliwa Marekani. Kiasi kwamba wanaweza kusikika hata kwenye sauti ya juu ya ving’ora vya polisi na vya magari ya wagonjwa yanayopita karibu.

eng: When Jefferson was a kid here, he tells me, he was allowed to go from home to school to church, and that was it.
swa: Jefferson alipokuwa mtoto, alikuwa akiruhusiwa kutoka tu nyumbani na kenda shule na kanisani, basi.

eng: He kept his head in the books, and made it to college — to Cornell University, where he met other Africans, who weren’t refugees, but wealthy international students.
swa: Alizingatia sana kwenye masomo hadi akafanikiwa kufika chuo-Chuo Kikuu cha Cornell, ambapo alikutana na Waafrika wengine ambao hawakuwa wakimbizi, lakini wanafunzi wa kutoka mataifa mengine.

eng: Here it was cool to be African.
swa: Hapa alijisikia kuwa ilikuwa fahari kuwa Mwafrika.

eng: The university housed a rare collection of journals, where he learned about Liberia from scholars.
swa: Chuo hiki kilikuwa na mkusanyiko wa majarida adhimu, ambapo katika majirida haya aliweza kujisomea mambo anuai kuhusu Liberia.

eng: He admits the irony of having come to America, to a remote place like Ithaca, New York, to learn about his family’s roots.
swa: Anaukubali utani wa kuja Marekani, kwenye maeneo ya ndani kama ya Ithaca, New York, ili kujifunza kuhusu chimbuko la familia yake.

eng: He learned to speak the language again, studied civil engineering, and set his sights on going back to Liberia.
swa: Alijiufnza tena kuzungumza lugha ya kwao, alisomea uandisi wa majengo huku akitafakari kuhusu kurudi Liberia.

eng: He’d heard of other young Africans– who went to school abroad—and were returning to the Continent.
swa: Alipata habari za vijana wengine wa kiafrika-ambao walisoma nchi za nje-na kisha kurejea barani Afrika.

eng: So Jefferson moved back to Liberia last summer, just after the Ebola crisis had ended.
swa: Kwa hiyo, wakati wa kipindi cha kiangazi kilichopita, Jefferson alirejea nchini Liberia, mara tu baada ya kutokomezwa kwa ugonjwa wa Ebola.

eng: He remembers what it was like, when first arriving.
swa: Ananakumbuka halia aliyokuw anayo wakati wa kuwasili.

eng: “Man, I wanted to kiss the ground.
swa: “Ndugu, nilitamani kuibusu ardhi.

eng: I was so excited,” he says.
swa: Nilistaajabishwa sana,” anasema.

eng: “It’s like everybody talks like how you talk in your home, and it’s just a nice feeling to not be the other.”
swa: “ Ni kama vile kila mmoja anaongea kama unapokuwa kwako, ni hisia nzuri sana kutokujisikia vinginevyo.”

eng: Jefferson launched a digital news outlet in Liberia called the Bush Chicken.
swa: Jefferson alizindua chombo cha habari cha kidigitali nchini Liberia alichokipa jina la Bush Chicken.

eng: Here is a photo he took while on assignment, covering a student protest against proposed tuition hikes at the University of Liberia.
swa: Hii ni picha aliyoichukua wakati akiwa kwenye ukusanyaji wa taarifa, alipokuwa akikusanya habari kuhusu mgomo wa wanafunzi dhidi ya pendekezo la ongezeko la ada ya Chuo Kikuu cha Liberia.

eng: Credit: Photo courtesy of Jefferson Krua
swa: Picha kwa hisani ya Jefferson Krua

eng: He launched a digital news outlet called the Bush Chicken, which trains journalists to report with accuracy.
swa: Alizindua chombo cha habari cha kidigitali kinachofahamika kwa jina la Bush Chicken, ambacho kinatoa mafunzo kwa waandishi wa habari kuhusu namna ya kuripoti habari kwa usahihi. which trains journalists to report with accuracy.

eng: He’s also working on a start-up to bring a bike share program to Monrovia, where it can take hours for kids to get to school.
swa: Pia anatazamia kuanzisha mradi wa kushirikiana baiskeli katika jiji la Monrovia, ambapo utawasaidia watoto kutumia mda mchache kufika shuleni.

eng: But his mother worries for Jefferson’s safety, and says all she can do is pray.
swa: Hata hivyo, mama yake ana hofu kuhusu usalama wa mtoto Jefferson’s, kiasi kwamba anasema anachoweza kufanya ni kumuomba tu Mungu.

eng: They no longer have family to look out for Jefferson in Liberia, and the fruit trees, where they ate mangos and avocados from daily — all of these were gone as well.
swa: Hawana tena ndugu wa kumuangalia Jefferson huko Liberia, na hata miti ya matunda, waliyokuwa wakiitegemea kwa maembe na machungwa — haipo tena.

eng: The land isn’t theirs anymore, and so for her, home has vanished, too.
swa: Ardhi ile siyo ya kwao tena, hata na kwake, nyumbani pia kumepotea.

eng: For his mother Mercy, America is the place that’s provided opportunities.
swa: Kwa mtazamo wa Mercy, mama yake na Jefferson, Marekani ndiyo sehemu iliyompatia mafanikio.

eng: In the refugee camps, there were no jobs to be had.
swa: Kwenye kambi za wakimbizi, hakukuwa na kazi yayote ya kufanya.

eng: But here she worked long hours as a nanny, caring for someone else’s kids, so she would have enough to care for her own.
swa: Lakini, hapa Marekani, siku nzima anafanya kazi ya kuwatunza watoto, kuwa mwangalizi wa watoto wa watu wengine, kwa hiyo, anaweza kupata kiasi cha fedha cha kuwaangali na watoto wake.

eng: She saved enough to finish nursing school, and now works as a registered nurse.
swa: Aliweza kutumia fedha zake vizuri na kusomea uuguzi, na kwa sasa anafany kazi kama muuguzi aliyesajiliwa.

eng: “Honestly, I’m from Liberia,” she says.
swa: “Bila hiana, mimi ni raia kutoka Liberia,” anasema.

eng: “But wherever I am right now I consider it to be home.
swa: “Lakini kwa hapa nilipo sasa ndipo ninapopaona kama nyumbani.

eng: Wherever you are, where you see that you can make a day-to-day living, I consider it home for me.”
swa: Popote ulipo, panapokupatia riziki yako, kwa maoni yangu, ndipo ninapopachukulia kuwa ni nyumbani.”

eng: Mercy Krua, and her son Jefferson Krua, on her living room couch in Boston, MA.
swa: Mercy Krua akiwa na mtoto wake Jefferson Krua, wakiwa wamekaa kwenye kochi la chumba chake huko Boston, MA.

eng: Credit: Heidi Shin
swa: Picha kwa hisani ya Heidi Shin

eng: She doesn’t want to talk about Liberia anymore — the memories make her sad, she says.
swa: Hapendi tena kuzuizungumzia Liberia kabisa — kumbukumbu alizonazo zinamfanya ajisikie vvibaya sana.

eng: Instead, she proudly shows me a picture of US President Barack Obama and the late civil rights activist Martin Luther King, Jr. hanging on her living room wall of the home she now owns.
swa: Kinyume chake, ananionesha picha ya Rais wa Marekani, barack Obama na ya Mwanaharakati wa masuala ya kijamii hayati Martin Luther King, Jr ambazo amezitundika kwenye ukuta wa chumba chake cha kulala kwenye nyumba anayoimiliki.

eng: But Jefferson tells me this story about a run-in he had with the police, just in front of his mother’s house in Boston, when visiting not too long ago.
swa: Pamoja na haya, Jefferson ananisimmulia habari ya purukushani aliyokabiliana nayo na polisi, mbele ya nyumba ya mama yake huko Boston, pale alipomtembelea siku za hivi karibuni.

eng: “They’re questioning me, but one of them is so aggressive,” Jefferson says.
swa: “Wananiuliza maswali, lakini mmoja wao anakuwa mkali kweli kweli,” anasema Jefferson.

eng: The policeman shouts at him, as Jefferson searches for his license: “Why are you taking so long? Don’t you know it’s cold out here?”
swa: Askari anamfokea wakati Jefferson akiendelea kutafuta leseni yake: “Kwa nini unachukua muda mrefu hivyo?, Hufahamu kuwa kuna baridi kali sana?”

eng: Jefferson admits, “And as a black male in America, I am just scared.”
swa: Jefferson anakiri, “Nikijiangalia kuwa mimi ni mtu mweusi nchini Marekani, ninaogopa sana.”

eng: He continues, “So with something like that, it’s really hard to call America home.
swa: Anaendelea, “kwa hiyo, kwa mambo kama haya, ni vigumu sana kusema Marekani ni nyumbani.

eng: No matter how much money I can make in this country, whatever, I’m always going to be a black man in America.”
swa: Bila kujali ni kiasi gani cha fedha ninakipata katika nchi hii, kwa vyovyote, nitaendelea kuw amtu mweusi nchini Marekani.”

eng: But in Liberia Jefferson is the 1 percent.
swa: Lakini nchini Liberia, Jefferson ni asilimia moja tu.

eng: He shows me photos of the resorts he frequents, the press badge he flashes that gives him access.
swa: Alinionesha picha za maeneo mbalimbali aliyoyatembelea, kitambulisho cha uandishi wa habari alichokuwa akikionesha na kupata ruhusa.

eng: He can even put on an American accent whenever he needs it — something that affords you respect in Liberia.
swa: Angaliweza pia kutumia lafudhi ya kimarekani kama angependa— kitu ambacho kinaweza kukupa kutaminiwa nchini Liberia.

eng: He dreams of becoming Minister of Transportation, and he’s chosen not to become a US citizen, so he can be poised to enter politics there.
swa: Ana ndoto ya kuwa Waziri wa Uchukuzi na anapendelea kutokuwa raia wa Marekani, ili ajiahakikishie kuingia kwenye siasa huko Liberia.

eng: “All my dreams, everything, all my goals in life they’re focused on Liberia,” says Jefferson.
swa: “Ndoto zangu zote, kila kitu, mikakati yangu yote kwenye maisha, inailenga Liberia,” anasema Jefferson.

eng: He continues, “I have these nightmares where, I wake up and I’d just be sweating, and it’s basically Liberia got into another war again.
swa: Anaendelea kusema, “huwa ninakuwa na ndoto za majinamizi, yani ninaamka na kujikuta ninatokwa jasho, kwamba Liberia imeangukia kwenye vita kwa mara nyingine.

eng: And that’s a fear for me, because I don’t know what I would do.”
swa: Hii ndio hofu kubwa niliyonayo, kwa kuwa sijui nitafanya nini.”

eng: But for now, he’s embraced the opportunities his new home has given him, and he’s committed to helping rebuild the country, so that he says, “things like war aren’t so likely to happen again.”
swa: Lakini, kwa sasa anajivunia kwa neema ambazo anazipata awapo kwenye makazi yake mapya, na pia anawajibika kuijenga upya nchi yake, na hapa anasema, “mambo kama ya vita sidhani kama yatatokea tena.”

eng: This story was produced with the support of the Images and Voices of Hope's Restorative Narrative Fellowship.
swa: Habari hii iliandaliwa kwa ushirikiano na Kongamano la Uponyaji na Masimulizi la Picha na Sauti za Matumaini.

eng: Chinese graduates at a job exhibition in 2007.
swa: Wahitimu wa shahada wakiwa kwenye Kongamano la Ajira mwaka 2007.

eng: Photo from state news agency Xinhua.
swa: Picha kutoka shirika la habari la Taifa Xinhua.

eng: Once again, more than 7 million students in China graduated from university in May.
swa: Kwa mara nyingine, zaidi ya wanfunzi milioni 7 nchini China wamehitimu shahada zao kutoka vyuo mbalimbali mwezi wa Mei.

eng: If you add in the 300,000 overseas graduates and previous years' graduates who are still looking for jobs, that means more than 15 million young people were reportedly seeking their fortunes at the same time this year.
swa: Ikiwa utawajumuisha wanafunzi 300, 0000 kutoka vyuo vya nje pamoja na wale waliohitimu miaka iliyopita na ambao bado wanatafuta ajira, hii ina maana kuwa, zaidi ya vijana milioni 15 wanadhaniwa kuwa wanatafuta ajira kwa mwaka huu.

eng: As a newly rising economy power, China is considered to have a huge job market.
swa: Kama Taifa linaloibuka kwa kasi kiuchumi, China inachukuliwa kuwa na nafasi nyingi za ajira.

eng: Indeed, when you google “find a job in China”, millions of results pop up.
swa: Kwa kweli, kama utaamua kutafuta kwenye google "tafuta ajira nchini China", utapata mamilioni ya majibu.

eng: But the reality is many graduates struggle to find work after finishing their studies.
swa: Lakini ukweli ni kwamba, wahitimu wengi wa vyuo vikuu wanahangaika kutafuta ajira.

eng: In fact, a popular saying that has arisen in recent years holds that "graduation equals unemployment."
swa: Kwa hakika, kuna ule msemo ulioibuka miaka ya hivi karibuni kwamba "kuhitimu ni sawa na kukosa ajira".

eng: In 2013, the unemployment rate of graduates from colleges and universities two months after graduating was 17.6 percent, according to Times Higher Education; for those in rural areas, it was 30.5 percent.
swa: Mwaka 2013, kiwango cha ukosekanaji wa ajira kwa wahitimu wa vyuo vya kati na vyuo vikuu miezi miwili baada ya kuhitimu ilikuwa asilimia 17.6, hii ni kwa mujibu wa Times Higher Education; kwa wale wa vijijini, kiwangocha ukosekanaji wa ajira kilikuwa ni asilimia 30.5.

eng: That's higher than the general unemployment rate (or at least what's thought to be the unemployment rate, since data out of China is unreliable).
swa: Kiasi hiki ni kikubwa kuliko kiwango cha ujumla cha kukosekana kwa ajira, (au angalao kile kinachofikiriwa kuwa kiwango cha ukosekanaji wa ajira, kwani taarifa kutoka nje ya China hazina uhakika).

eng: As China's economy has slowed down in the past two years, the graduate unemployment problem only has worsened.
swa: Kwa kuwa uchumi wa China umekuwa ukishuka kwa miaka miwili iliyopita, hali ya kukosekana kwa ajira miongoni mwa wahitimu imezidi kuwa mbaya.

eng: The frustration of China's younger generations is reflected in a number of widely circulated social media and mobile text messages, such as the following:
swa: Mihemko ya kizazi cha vijana nchini China imeonekana kwenye mitandao mbalimbali ya kijamii na kupitia ujumbe mfupi wa simu za mkononi, kama inavyoonekana hapa:

eng: When we were born, the infant formula was toxic; when our bodies were in development, we could only consume junk food; when we attended kindergarten, the school fee was out of control; when we graduated from university, we were unemployed; when we tried to earn our living via the stock market, it collapsed; when we tried hard to fall in love, we found out all handsome guys were gay; when we started chasing after the mainstream , they were no longer mainstream.
swa: Wakati tunazaliwa, mlo wa mtoto machanga ulikuwa na sumu, wakati miili yetu ikiwa inaendelea kukua, tulikuwa tunatumia mlo usio kamili; tulipoanza shule ya awali, ada ilikuwa kubwa isivyomithilika, tulipohitimu vyuo vikuu, hatukuajiriwa, tulipojaribu kujikimu kupitia soko la ndani, lilianguka, tulipojaribu kuingia kwenye mapenzi, tuligundua kuwa kila kijana mzuri alikuwa ni shoga; tulipojaribu kufuata miiko , wala haikuwepo tena ile miiko.

eng: What university means: management is like prison, the quality is for hooligans. learn how to kiss in public, consume like a white-collar worker, daydream in class.
swa: Nini maana ya chuo kikuu: utawala ni kama jela, ubora ni kwa ajili ya wahuni. wanajifunza namna ya kubusiana hadharani, matumizi yao ni kama mfanyakazi wa kigeni na ndoto za alinacha darasani.

eng: Skipping classes is common, dormitories are like internet cafes.
swa: Kutokuhudhuria masomo ni jambo la kawaida, mambweni ni kama sehemu za huduma za intaneti.

eng: Taking exams becomes a profession, only the aristocracy can afford school fees.
swa: Kufanya mitihani kumekuwa ni utaalam, wanaomudu ada ya shule ni wale walio na uwezo tu.

eng: Thesis looks like Baidu search results.
swa: Andiko la utafiti linaonekana kama matokeo ya utafutaji kupitia Baidu.

eng: Everyone gets short-sighted.
swa: Kila mtu anajengewa matarajio yasiyo na tija.

eng: The food in school canteens is for feeding animals.
swa: Chakula kwenye migahawa ya shule ni ya kulishia wanyama.

eng: Having a job is like a dream.
swa: Kupata kazi ni kama ndoto.

eng: Graduation equals unemployment.
swa: Kuhitimu masomo ni sawa na kukosa kazi.

eng: Jobs on the market are for rural-to-urban migrants.
swa: Ajira zilizopo ni kwa wahamiaji kutoka vijijini kuja mjini.

eng: Many believe that part of the problem of unemployment for recent university graduates is related to the policy of higher education expansion since 1999.
swa: Watu wengi wanaamini kwamba moja ya mambo yanayochangia tatizo la ukosefu wa ajira miongoni mwa wahitimu wa vyuo vikuu wa hivi karibuni ni sera ya mwaka 1999 ya kuongeza udahili vyuo vikuu.

eng: Back then, only about 35 percent of high school graduates entered post-high school education including colleges, technical schools and universities.
swa: Kabla ya hapo takribani asilimia 35 tu ya wahitimu wa shule za upili ndio waliopata nafasi ya kusoma kwenye vyuo vya kati, vyuo vya ufundi ana vyuo vikuu.

eng: But in 2015, the percent was more than 80 percent, and about 40 percent became undergraduates at universities.
swa: Lakini, kwa mwaka 2015, asilimia hii ilikuwa ni zaidi ya asilimia 80, na pia takribani asilimia 40 walijiunga na shahada ya kwanza kwenye vyuo vikuu.

eng: For big cities like Beijing, the number of students entering university was more than 70 percent.
swa: Kwa majiji makubwa kama vile Beijing, kiasi cha wanfunzi waliojiunga na vyuo vikuu kilikuwa zaidi ya asilimia 70.

eng: Some argue there aren't enough jobs for so many university-educated people.
swa: Baadhi ya watu wanaona kuwa, hakuna ajira za kutosha kwa idadi iliyopo ya vijana wengi wanaohitimu elimu ya chuo kikuu.

eng: On popular social media site Weibo, Lydia commented on the over-supply of graduates:
swa: Kwenye mtandao maarufu wa kijamii wa Weibo, Lydia alitoa maoni kuhusu vyuo kutoa idadi kubwa sana ya wahitimu:

eng: Graduates are everywhere, and college students are not worth anything now.
swa: Wahitimu wapo kila mahali, na pia wahitimu wa vyuo vya kati kwa sasa hawathaminiwi kabisa.

eng: How could you tell the difference?
swa: Unawezaje kuleleza tofauti?

eng: Another Weibo user, "Nomadic hero", wrote that a side effect of expansion is a drop in the quality of graduates in general:
swa: Mtumiaji mwingine wa Weibo, "Nomadic hero", aliandika kwamba moja ya madahara ya kuongeza wigo wa udahili ni kushuka kwa ubora wa wahitimu kwa ujumla:

eng: The fight for educational justice to make sure the majority of people have the chance to go to school is good.
swa: Vita dhidi ya upatikanaji wa usawa ili kila mmoja apate fursa ya kwenda shule ni jambo jema.

eng: But it is true that the quality of students is getting worse.
swa: Hata hivyo, ni ukweli mtupu kwamba ubora wa wanafunzi unazidi kupotea.

eng: It is the university, rather than students, that lose value.
swa: Ni chuo kinachopoteza thamani kuliko hata wanafunzi.

eng: Ling Yan San Chi lamented:
swa: Ling Yan San Chi alitoa lawama:

eng: Graduated for two years already, but I am still working on how to find a job!! Why is my life so miserable?
swa: Nimehitimu miaka miwili iliyopita, lakini bado ninafanya kazi ya kutafuta ajira!!, kwa nini maisha yangu yananiendea kombo namna hii?

eng: HaiDe XiaTian even chose to carry on his studies in postgraduate school:
swa: HaiDe XiaTian kwa mfano, anafikiria kuendelea na masomo ya uzamili:

eng: I feel regret , but there is no other way and I have to carry on down this path.
swa: Ninajisikia kukata tamaa , lakini hakuna namna nyingine, na ninapaswa kuendelea na njia hii hii.

eng: Going to postgraduate school will be my last chance to enter an ideal university.
swa: Kujiunga na masomo ya uzamili kutanipa fursa ya kupata chuo kikuu halisi.

eng: The graduation ceremony is called commencement, which should stand for a new beginning for graduates, but many see it like an individual struggle, such as Weibo user UsedToBe5:
swa: Sherehe ya kuhitimu huitwa kuanza, ikiwa na maana ya mwanzo mpya kwa wahitimu, lakini wengi wanachukulia hali hii kama juhudi za mtu binafsi, kama ilivyo kwa mtumiaji wa Weibo UsedToBe5:

eng: Finding a job is a tough thing because you have to fall down and get up again and again.
swa: Kupata ajira ni kazi ngumu sana kwa kuwa yakupasa kuanguka na kuinuka tena mara nyingi iwezekanavyo..

eng: Of course, I have no one to blame since I choose it myself.
swa: Kwa kweli, sina yeyote wa kumlaumu kwani haya yalikuwa ni maamuzi yangu mwenyewe.

eng: Not everyone is gloomy about the situation.
swa: Hata hivyo, siyo kila mmoja amepoteza imani na hali hii.

eng: A hashtag on Weibo called #graduation doesn’t mean unemployment# gives the topic a positive twist, and messages try to offer support, tips and personal experiences.
swa: Kiungo habari kwenye Weibo kinachojulikana kama #kuhitimu hakumaanishi kukosa ajira# kinaupa mjadala huu sura tofauti, na pia jumbe zinajaribu kutoa hamasa, ushauri na uzoefu binafsi.

eng: The latest status with the above hashtag was published on July 12 by Weibo user "WanAn Xin XinYu," who was one of the 7 million newly graduated young people in 2016:
swa: Chapisho la mwisho kuhusiana na kiungo habari hapo juu lilichapishwa Julai 12 kwenye Weibo na mtumiaji"WanAn Xin XinYu," ambaye alikuwa miongoni mwa wahitimu wapya milioni 7 wa mwaka 2016:

eng: I am going to have another interview today, and I wish I could start working tomorrow. #graduation doesn’t mean unemployment# Add oil !
swa: Leo nitahudhuria usaili mwingine, na pia ninatamani kuanza kazi hata kesho. #kuhitimu hakumaanishi kukosa ajira# Add oil !

eng: Although I have been unemployed for a month.
swa: Pamoja na kuwa ni mwezi sasa umepita sijapata ajira.

eng: Photo posted on the Facebook page of Myanmar Meme by Htet Myat Lynn.
swa: Picha ilitumwa katika ukurasa wa Facebook wa kitamaduni wa Myanma kwa hisani ya Htet Myat Lynn.

eng: This is an example of memes reflecting the rivalry between the Yangon Chief Minister Phyo Min Thein (Kwee Phyo) and Wirathu, the leader of a radical Buddhist group.
swa: Huu ni mfano wa mawazo yanayoonesha uhasama uliopo baina ya Waziri Kiongozi wa Yangon; Phyo Min Thein (Kwee Phyo) na Wirathu, kiongozi wa kikundi cha ki-Budhha chenye msimamo mkali.

eng: Phyo Min Thei, the chief minister of Myanmar’s Yangon City, made a daring statement last week when he declared that the radical Buddhist nationalist group Ma-Ba-Tha (Association of Race and Religion Protection) is “no longer needed” since the Sangha Maha Nayaka Committee of the government is already overseeing the country's Buddhist affairs.
swa: Phyo Min Thei Waziri Kiongozi wa mji wa Yangon huko Myanma, ametoa kauli yenye uthubutu wiki iliyopita wakati alipotangaza kuwa kundi la ki-Buddha lenye msimamo mkali Ma-Ba-Tha (Chama cha Ulinzi wa Kikabila na Dini)“halihitajiki tena” kwa kuwa kamati ya Kiserikali ya Sangha Maha Nayaka tayari inayashughulikia masuala ya Wabuddha nchini.

eng: Wirathu, the influential leader of Ma-Ba-Tha, has threatened to hold a nationwide protest if the government will not take action against Phyo Min Thein.
swa: Wirathu, kiongozi wa Ma-Ba-Tha mwenye ushawishi mkubwa,ameitathreatened maandamano kwa nchi nzima kama serikali haitamchukulia hatua Phyo Min Thein.

eng: But Internet users have launched a campaign in support of the minister.
swa: Lakini watumiaji wengi wa mtandao wa intaneti wamezindua kampeni ya kumwunga mkono Waziri huyo.

eng: Established in 2013, Ma-Ba-Tha is a civil-religious group composed of Buddhist monks and their supporters whose avowed aim is to protect Buddhism, Buddhists and Myanmar from the so-called “danger of Muslim expansion.”
swa: Kikundi cha Ma-Ba-Tha kilichoundwa mwaka 2013, ni kikundi chenye mrengo wa kidini na kiraia na kimeundwa na watawa wa ki-Buddha na wafuasi wao ambao wamekula kiapo cha kulinda u-Buddha, wa-Buddha na Myanma dhidi ya kinachoitwa “hatari ya kuongezeka na kupanuka kwa Uislam.”

eng: Myanmar has a Buddhist majority population, although it has more than 100 ethnic minority groups.
swa: Asilimia kubwa ya wananchi wa Myanma ni wa-Buddha, ingawa ina zaidi ya vikundi vingine vidogo vidogo vipatavyo 100 vya madhehebu mengine

eng: Ma-Ba-Tha has gained notoriety because of its anti-Muslim statements and activities.
swa: Ma-Ba-Tha imejipatiaumaarufu kwa sababu ya kauli zake na vitendo vya kuupinga Uislam.

eng: In particular, it has been a strong force behind the attacks against the Rohingya people, a Muslim ethnic group living in the western part of Myanmar.
swa: Kwa hakika, kimekuwa chanzo na nguvu kubwa nyuma ya mashambulizi yanayofanywa dhidi ya watu wa Rohingya ambayo ni kikundi cha jamii ya Kiislam inayoishi Magharibi mwa Myanma.

eng: Supporters of the ideology of Ma-Ba-Tha and its leaders have been producing a hate-speech narrative that demands the government to expel the Rohingya, whom they are accusing of being illegal immigrants and terrorists.
swa: Wafuasi wa itikadi hiyo ya Ma-Ba-Tha pamoja na viongozi wake, wamekuwa wakitoa kauli za chuki zikiishurutisha serikali kuwafukuza wa-Rohingya, kwa kuwatuhumu ni wahamiaji haramu na pia ni magaidi.

eng: Many human rights groups consider the Rohingya to be one of the most persecuted minorities in the world.
swa: Makundi mengi ya haki za binadamyanadhania kuwa jamii hiyo ya Rohingya ni moja ya vikundi vidogo vya kijamii vinavyoonewa zaidi ulimwenguni.

eng: Phyo Min Thein, known by his supporters as Kwee Phyo, is part of the new ruling party National League for Democracy (NLD), which is led by Nobel Laureate Aung San Suu Kyi.
swa: Phyo Min Thein anayejulikana kama Kwee Phyo na wafuasi wake, ni sehemu ya chama kipya kinachotawala cha National League for Democracy (NLD), na kinaongozwa na mshndi wa tuzo ya Nobel Aung San Suu Kyi.

eng: The NLD came to power in February 2016 after defeating the military-backed party during the general elections.
swa: Chama hicho cha NLD kiliingia madarakani Februari 2016 baada yadefeating jeshi kushindwa na chama katika uchaguzi mkuu.

eng: The military had ruled Myanmar from 1962 until early this year.
swa: Jeshi limekuwa likiingoza nchi tangu 1962 hadi mapema mwaka huu

eng: As Yangon’s chief minister, Phyo Min Thein has made a name for himself instituting several contentious reforms, like a building regulation he imposed during the annual water festival in April.
swa: Kama Waziri Kiongozi wa Yangon Phyo Min Thein amejijengea jina miongoni mwa jamii na kuanzisha mijadala migumu kadhaa reforms, kama ule wa udhibiti wa majengo aliouanzisha wakati wa maadhimisho ya juma la maji ambalo hufanyika kila mwaka Aprili.

eng: But he sparked an even bigger controversy last week by publicly speaking against the powerful Ma-Ba-Tha.
swa: Lakini wiki hii ameanzisha mada moto zaidi baada ya wiki iliyopita kuongea hadharani akikishutumu kikundi chenye nguvu cha Ma-Ba-Tha.

eng: Fortunately, Phyo Min Thein received support from many Internet users. The hashtag #NoMaBaTha was endorsed on Facebook as part of the campaign to defend the chief minister against the online supporters of the radical Buddhist group.
swa: Bahati nzuri Phyo Min Thein ameungwa mkono na watumiaji wa mitandao na Hashtag #hapanaMaBaTha iliwekwa kwenye kurasa za Facebook kama sehemu ya kampeni za kumtetea na kumuunga mkono waziri dhidi ya watu wanaunga mkono kikundi cha wa-Buddha wenye msimamo mkali

eng: Some Facebook users are adopting this image on their profile page in support of the chief minister:
swa: Watumiaji hao hao wa Facebook wanatumia picha hii kwenye kurasa zao kumuunga mkono Waziri Kiongozi:

eng: Here are some reactions to the #‎NOMaBaTha‬ hashtag.
swa: Hii ni sehemu ya majibizano kwa hashtag #‎NOMaBaTha.

eng: Htin Linn Aye distinguished the Ma-Ba-Tha from the rest of Buddhist monks in the country:
swa: Htin Linn Aye iliyowatofautisha Ma-Ba-Tha na watawa wengine wa kiBuddha nchini kote:

eng: I revere the sons of Buddha who abide by his doctrine
swa: Ninawasalimu wote wana wa Buddha mnaofata mafundisho yake

eng: but... #‎NOMaBaTha‬
swa: Lakini... #‎hakunaMaBaTha‬

eng: Below is a Facebook post which went viral:
swa: Hapo chini ni chapisho lililosambaa sana huko facebook:

eng: To those who are saying we will become dogs if Ma-Ba-Tha no longer exists, now let me ask have we always been dogs many years before Ma-Ba-Tha came? :p:p:p:p:p
swa: Kwa wote wanaosema tutakuwa mbwa kama Ma-Ba-Tha haitakuwepo tena, nataka kuwauliza; je tumekuwa mbwa kipindi chote ambacho Ma-Ba-Tha hawakuwepo? :p:p:p:p:p

eng: credit ‪#‎NOMaBaTha‬
swa: credit ‪#‎NOMaBaTha‬

eng: Moe Kaung San thinks Ma-Ba-Tha's actions are tainting the image of Buddhism:
swa: Moe Kaung San nafikiri vitendo vya Ma-Ba-Tha vinaichafua taswira ya u-Buddha:

eng: Because the organization called Ma-Ba-Tha is
swa: Kwa sababu taasisi hii inayoitwa Ma-Ba-Tha ina

eng: getting involved in politics and making the country unstable by
swa: jishughulisha na siasa na kuifanya nchi ikose amani kwa

eng: creating racial hatred and religious discrimination in the name of race and religion protection
swa: kutengeneza chuki za kikabila na ubaguzi wa kidini kwa jina la kulinda dini na kabila/asili

eng: and is putting a bad image of Buddhism
swa: na wanauwekea v-Buddha picha mbaya

eng: #nodesireforMaBaTha #‎NoMaBaTha‬
swa: #hatuitamaniMaBaTha #‎HakunaMaBaTha‬

eng: A Google form was also created to gather more support for the statement issued by the Yangon chief minister about the Ma-Ba-Tha.
swa: Piailitengenezwa fomu maalum huko Google kwa ajili ya uungwaji mkono wa kauli ya Waziri Kiongozi wa Yangon aliyoitoa dhidi ya Ma-Ba-Tha.

eng: This week we take you to Indian-administered Kashmir, Nepal and China.
swa: Juma hili tunakupeleka hadi Kasmir, Jimbo linalotawaliwa na India , Nepal na China.

eng: We also speak with Global Voices contributor Angel Carrion about Puerto Rican opposition to a US fiscal control board, and we chat with Global Voices author Thant Sin about an outpouring of support for an official in Myanmar who dared to speak out against a radical Buddhist nationalist group.
swa: Tutaongea na mwandishi wa Global Voices Angel Carrion kuhusu hatua ya Puerto Rican kupinga bodi ya Marekani kudhibiti fedha, na tutaongea na mwandishi wa Global Voices Thant Sin kuhusu kuungwa mkono kwa afisa mmoja nchini Myanmar aliyeamua kuvunja kimya kwa kukemea ubaguzi unaofanywa na kikundi cha kidini cha Kibudha.

eng: This episode features stories by Kisholoy Mukherjee, Vishal Manve, Sanjib Choudhary, Oiwan Lam, Angel Carrion and Thant Sin.
swa: Kipindi hiki kina habari ziliandikwa na Kisholoy Mukherjee, Vishal Manve, Sanjib Choudhary, Oiwan Lam, Angel Carrion na Thant Sin.

eng: In this episode of the Week that Was at Global Voices, we featured Creative Commons licensed music from the Free Music Archive, including Please Listen Carefully by Jahzzar; The Universal Fluff Theory by Krackatoa; Anamorphic Orchestra by Alan Singley; Origami 1726 by the Blue Dot Sessions; Driving me backwards by Phil Reavis; and Carcrashlander Instrumentals by Cory Gray.
swa: Kwenye matangazo haya ya "Wiki Ilivyokwenda hapa Global Voices", tunasindikizwa na muziki wenye leseni ya Creative Commons kutoka Maktaba ya mtandaoni ya Free Music Archive, ikiwa ni pamoja na Please Listen Carefully wa Jahzzar; The Universal Fluff Theory wa Krackatoa; Anamorphic Orchestra wa Alan Singley; Origami 1726 wa the Blue Dot Sessions; Driving me backwards wa Phil Reavis; and Carcrashlander Instrumentals wa Cory Gray.

swa: Imewekwa kwenye mtandao wa Flickr.

eng: A photo posted on Facebook by Presidential Press Secretary Don Wanyama showing Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni speaking on the phone by the roadside.
swa: Picha iliyowekwa kwenye mtandao wa facebook na Mwandishi wa Habari wa Rais Don Wanyama ikimwonesha Rais wa Uganda Yoweri Museveni akiongea na simu pembeni mwa barabara.

eng: Twitter has exploded with funny memes after a photo appeared online showing Uganda's President Yoweri Museveni sitting on a chair by the roadside to make a call.
swa: Watumiaji wa mtandao wa Twita walitumiana picha za kuchekeshana baada ya kuonekana kwa picha inayomwonesha Rais wa Uganda Yoweri Museveni akiwa amekaa kwenye kiti chake pembeni mwa barabara akiongea na simu.

eng: His motorcade, which was on the way to a public event, stopped for about 30 minutes for him to make the call.
swa: Msafara wake, ambao ulikuwa ukielekea kwenye shughuli ya kikazi, ulisimama kwa takribani dakika 30 kumsubiri apige simu.

eng: Presidential Press Secretary Don Wanyama posted the photo on his Facebook page with the following message:
swa: Mwandishi wa Habari wa Rais Don Wanyama aliweka picha hiyo kwenye ukurasa wake wa facebook ikiwa na maelezo yafuatayo:

eng: On the way from Isingiro District yesterday where he'd presided over the World Population Day celebrations, President Museveni stopped at Kyeirumba Village to make a phone call.
swa: Njiani kutoka Wilaya ya Isingiro jana ambapo alishiriki maadhimisho ya Siku ya Idadi ya Watu Duniani, Rais Museveni alisimama kwenye kijiji cha Kyeirumba ili aweze kupiga simu.

eng: Curious residents gathered to look at the President, who after 30 minutes on phone, briefly interacted with them.
swa: Wakazi wa eneo hilo waliokuwa wakijiuliza nini kinaendelea walikusanyika kumwona Rais, ambaye baada ya dakika 30 za kuzungumza na simu, alijichanganya nao kwa muda mfupi.

eng: It's extraordinary how much a place can change in 50 years. For example, Dhaka, the capital of Bangladesh, is one of the most populous megacities of the world, but you wouldn't believe it from looking at old photos of it.

eng: In the 1960s, British photographer Roger Gwynn came to Bangladesh as a volunteer for the non-governmental Service Civil International.

eng: He visited various parts of the country, which was then East Pakistan, and took photographs.
swa: Aliweza kutembelea maeneo mbalimbali ya Bangladesh, ambayo kwa wakati huo ilijulikana kama Pakistani ya Mashariki na kuweza kupiga picha mbalimbali.

eng: Recently, some of his photos of were republished on a Facebook page called Bangladesh Old Photo Archive and went viral among Bangladeshi users.
swa: Hivi karibuni, picha zake zilichapishwa kwenye ukurasa wa Facebook ulijulikan kama Hifadhi ya Picha za Zamani ya Bangladesh na kisha kusambaa sana miongoni mwa watumiaji wa matandao nchini Bangladesh.

eng: Launched on 24 August 2011, the page has more than 171,000 fans.
swa: Ukurasa huu uliofunguliwa mnamo Agosti 24, 2011, una wafuatiliaji zaidi ya 171, 000.

eng: When you look at these archived photos, you get a glimpse of history, tradition and the lives of Bangladeshis over the past century.
swa: Pindi unapoangalia hifadhi ya picha hizi, unapata kidokezo cha historia, tamaduni na maisha ya raia wa Bangladesh kwa kipindi cha karne moja iliyopita.
