Photo: Timor Post, July 13 edition
swa: Picha na: Timor Post, Toleo la Julai 13

eng: The board of the Fatumeta Basic School, in Dili, has decided to start enforcing a rule against students speaking any language but Portuguese, including Tetum, while on school grounds.
swa: Bodi ya Shule ya Msingi Fatumeta katika kitongoji cha Dili imeamua kuweka sheria zitakazo wabana wanafunzi watakaoongea lugha nyingine tofauti na Kireno ikiwemo Kitetumi wawapo katika mazingira ya shuleni.

eng: According to the newspaper Timor Post, the director of the school, Fernanda Belo, argues that students should only speak Portuguese.
swa: Kutoka kwa gazeti la Timor Post, mkurugenzi wa shule hiyo Fernanda Belo, anasema kuwa wanafunzi ni lazima waongee Kireno pekee wawapo shuleni.

eng: Those "who do not speak the language,” she says, are better off “remaining silent.”
swa: Wanafunzi mbao "hawataweza kuongea lugha hiyo" watalazimika kukaa kimya.

eng: According to the newspaper, students caught speaking any language other than Portuguese are “fined.”
swa: Kwa mujibu wa gazeti hilo, mwanafunzi akikamatwa akizungumza lugha tofauti na Kireno "atapigwa faini".

eng: Written in Tetum, the Timor Post quotes Belo as saying:
swa: Ikiwa imeandikwa Kitetumi, gazeti la Timor Post limemnukuu Belo akisema kuwa:

eng: We have communicated this rule to the parents and established that they cannot speak Tetum; everyone has to speak Portuguese.
swa: Tumeeleza hii sheria kwa wazazi na tumeweka msimamo kuwa wanafunzi hawataongea Kitetumi, kila mmoja lazima aongee Kireno.

eng: If they speak Tetum, they get a $1 fine.
swa: Kama mwanafunzi ataongea Kitetumi atapigwa faini ya dola moja.

eng: The school director emphasizes that the "parents agreed to the rule" and justifies imposing the fine in order to help students to speak more Portuguese.
swa: Mkurugenzi wa shule hiyo anasisitiza kuwa "wazazi wamekubaliana na sheria hiyo" na kuafiki kupitisha faini hiyo ili kuwasaidia wanafunzi waweze kuongea Kireno zaidi.

eng: After gaining independence from Indonesia in 2002, Timor-Leste adopted Portuguese and Tetum as the country's official languages.
swa: Baada ya kupata Uhuru wake kutoka kwa Indonesia mwaka 2002, Timor-Leste iliamua kutumia Kireno na Kitetumi kama lugha rasmi ya Taifa.

eng: A decade later, however, studies indicated that only 15 percent of the population spoke Portuguese:
swa: Muongo mmoja baadaye, tafiti zinaonesha kuwa ni asilimia 15% pekee ya watundio wanaoongea Kireno:

eng: Despite being part of the CPLP, Timor-Leste is one of the countries with lower penetration of the Portuguese language.
swa: Pamoja na kuwa sehemu ya CPLP, Timor-Leste ni moja ya nchi ambazo Kireno kinapenya kwa kiwango cha chini kabisa.

eng: Throughout the country, about 20 different languages and dialects are spoken, in addition to Indonesian.
swa: Kwa nchi nzima kuna karibu lugha 20 tofauti zinazozungumzwa ukijumuisha na Kiindonesia.

eng: Only 15 percent of the population speaks Portuguese.
swa: Asilimia 15% tu ya watu ndio wanaozungumza Kireno.

eng: The Fatumeta Basic School's rules, however, appear to violate the country's laws on teaching.
swa: Pamoja na hayo, inaonesha kuwa sheria za shule ya Msingi ya Fatumeta zinavunja sheria za nchi katika ufundishaji.

eng: The President of the Alola Foundation and the goodwill ambassador for Educational Affairs, Kirsty Sword Gusmao, told Global Voices that the school's policy of fining Tetum speakers is being reviewed:
swa: Raisi wa Alola Foundation na balozi wa matumaini mema kwa ajili ya masuala ya elimu Kirsty Sword Gusmao,ameiambia Global Voices kuwa taratibu za kuwapiga faini wanafunzi wanaoongea Kitetumi zimepitiwa:

eng: I will refer this matter to Mrs. Deputy Minister for Basic Education because this rule/sanction does not correspond with the Law for Basic Education Curriculum .
swa: Nitalipeleka jambo hilo kwa Naibu Waziri wa Elimu ya Msingi kwa sababu sheria hii haiendani na sheria za Mtaala wa Elimu ya Msingi .

eng: Kirsty Sword Gusmão. Photo in public domain.
swa: Picha ya Kirsty Sword Gusmão.

eng: Gusmão explained:
swa: Gusmão anaelezea kuwa:

eng: The Fatumeta School Director is the one that should be fined for violating Law-Decree 4/2015 of the Basic Education Curriculum, which requires (a) the learning process has to start orally, and then reading followed by writing; (b) the progression from Tetum to Portuguese (begins with the teaching of Tetum literacy) (article 11-2); (c) the hours of Tetum and Portuguese literacy in the first cycle is not equal (Tetum will be higher) and in the second cycle it will become equal; and (d) in order to end the learning of the literacy component, it will need to first establish the basis of the two official languages (article 11-2) (no need to teach other maternal or national languages).
swa: Mkurugenzi wa shule ya Msingi Fatumeta ndie anayetakiwa kupigwa faini kwa kuvunja sheria iliyopitishwa 4/2015 ya Mitaala ya Elimu Msingi iliyohitaji yafuatayo (a) Hatua za kujifunza zitaanza kwa kuongea na kisha kusoma na kuandika kutafuata (b) Muendelezo wa kutoka Kitetumi kwenda Kireno ( utaanza kwa kutoa elimu ya Kitetumi) kifungu cha 11-2); (c) Masaa ya kujifunza Kitetumi na Kireno kwa mzunguko wa kwanza hayalingani ( ya Kitetumi yatakuwa juu kidogo) na katika mzunguko wa pili masaa yatalingana (d) ili kumalizia muundo wa mafunzo itahitaji kwanza kuwekwa kwa msingi wa lugha hizi mbili rasmi (kifungu 11-2) (hakuna haja ya kufundisha lugha mama au lugha nyingine ya Taifa).

eng: Long live the Tetum language!
swa: Iishi milele lugha ya Kitetumi!

eng: Global Voices also spoke to João Paulo Esperança, a Portuguese linguist who has lived in Dili for many years.
swa: Pia Global Voices tulizungumza na João Paulo Esperança, mtaalamu wa lugha ya Kireno ambaye ameishi Dili kwa miaka mingi.

eng: Esperança says the situation at the school needs to be confirmed, and then a response may or may not be necessary:
swa: Esperança anasema kuwa hali katika shule inahitaji kuthibitishwa na kisha mrejesho unaweza kuhitajika au usihitajike inategemea kama kuna umuhimu:

eng: First, we must confirm the true situation at this school, but I personally do not agree with school policies that prohibit students from speaking the language they want to use on the school grounds, outside of class.
swa: Kwanza kabisa tunatakiwa tuthibitishe hali halisi katika shule hii, lakini mimi binafsi sihafikiani na taratibu za shule zinazozuia wanafunzi kuzungumza lugha wanayotaka kuitumia katika mazingira ya shule, nje ya darasa.

eng: And there may also be families without financial means to pay these fines.
swa: Na zinaweza kuwepo familia ambazo hazina namna ya kulipia faini hizo.

eng: But I think it is not with an evil intent that some principals and teachers try to implement these measures.
swa: Lakini nadhani sio kwa nia mbaya Mkuu wa Shule na waalimu wanapojaribu kutekeleza sheria hiyo.

eng: Previously, schools in Timor often used corporal punishment, the teaching language was Portuguese (and, after the invasion, it was Indonesian), and students were punished physically for speaking other languages.
swa: Hapo nyuma shule za Timori zilitumia adhabu kali, na lugha ya kufundishia ilikuwa ni Kireno ( na baada ya uvamizi wa Indonesia, ilikuwa ni Kiindonesia)na wanafunzi waliadhibiwa vikali kwa kuongea lugha nyingine.

eng: This was most people's personal experience, but modern pedagogy refuses such measures from the past, so some teachers try to use these fines as an alternative punishment.
swa: Hii ilikuwa kitu wengi walipitia lakini Mtaala wa kisasa unakataa hatua hizo za kizamani hivyo baadhi ya waalim wanajaribu kutumia hizo faini kama njia mbadala ya kuadhibu.

eng: As for the attempt to create an immersion school in Portuguese, it will probably have to do with the fact that schools, seen as model in Timor like the Portuguese School, the Reference Schools and the mythic Externato S. José are committed to everyone speaking Portuguese inside the classroom .
swa: Kwa kuangalia jaribio hili la kuanzisha shule maalum zinazotumia Kireno kisichotumiwa kabisa na wenyeji, labda sababu ni kwamba shule, kama ile inayoonekana kuwa mfano bora kule Timor inayoendeshwa sawa sawa na shule za Kireno, Shule zenye Ubora ambao hata hivyo haupo kama vile Externato S. José zinambana kila mtoto aongee Kireno anapokuwa darasani .

eng: And this, lately, has led to a trend that should make us think.
swa: Na hili, katika siku za karibuni, limesababisha mtindo mpya unaotufanya tutafakari kulikoni.

eng: Many parents of Dili's upper-middle class, whose children cannot gain admittance to these immersion schools in Portuguese, are putting them in Filipino immersion schools of English, instead.
swa: Matokeo yake wazazi wengi wenye kipato cha juu kidogo kwenye kitongoji cha Dili, ambao watoto wao hawawezi kupokelewa kwenye shule hizi zinazofundisha kwa lugha ya kigeni ya Kireno, wanaamua kuwapeleka kwenye shule zinazofundisha ki-Filipino.

eng: Estanislau Saldanha, the president of the Permanent Council of the Board of Directors of DIT - Dili Institute of Technology, also believes the strict language policy is illegal:
swa: Estanislau Saldanha, Rais wa kamati ya kudumu ya bodi ya wakurugenzi wa DIT - Chuo cha Teknolojia cha Dili , anaamini kuwa sio halali kuwa na sheria kali katika matumizi ya lugha:

eng: This decision violates the RDTL Constitution in relation to the official language and also violates the basic law of education regarding the language of instruction at school.
swa: Uamuzi huu unavunja katiba ya RDTL kuhusiana na masuala ya lugha rasmi na pia inavunja sheria ya msingi ya elimu ikizingatia lugha ya kufundishia shuleni.

eng: Therefore, it violates the right that students have to express themselves and learn in an easier language that supports them to learn science materials in a faster way.
swa: Kwa hiyo, inavunja haki ya wanafunzi ya kujieleza na kujifunza kwa urahisi lugha inayowasaidia kujifunza masuala ya kisayansi kwa njia iliyo rahisi.

eng: Virgilio da Silva Guterres, the president of Timor-Leste's Press Council, says the interests of teaching science should prevail:
swa: Nae Rais wa Baraza la Habari la Timor-Lestè ndugu Virgilio da Silva Guterres anasema kuwa mapendekezo ya kufundisha sayansi lazima yajitokeze:

eng: The School of Fatumeta is meant to be a Portuguese language school?
swa: Je, shule ya Fatumeta ilikusudiwa kuwa shule ya lugha ya Kireno?

eng: The aim of the school is to teach science.
swa: Lengo la shule hiyo ni kufundisha sayansi.

eng: Using Portuguese or English language as a means or instrument to learn it, the goal is not the language itself .
swa: Matumizi ya lugha ya Kiingereza au Kireno kama njia au zana ya kujifunzia, lengo sio lugha yenyewe.

eng: We can not use children for retaliatory aims with rules that once applied.
swa: Hatuwezi kuwatumia au kuwahusisha watoto na taratibu ambazo zilishatumika kabla.

eng: The rules of the school Soibada, Maliana and College Ossu were valid and applicable in his time not for all time .
swa: Sheria za shule ya Soibada, Maliana na chuo cha Ossu zilikuwa sahihi na zinazotekelezeka kwa wakati huu (lakini) sio kwa kipindi chote (kwa leo).

eng: I ask the school principal to revoke this rule.
swa: Nimemwagiza mkuu wa shule kuiondoa sheria hii.

eng: Kashogy Junior, whose younger brothers study in a primary school in Dili, wrote on Facebook:
swa: Kashogy Junior, ambaye mdogo wake wa kiume anasoma shule ya msingi huko Dili aliandika katika ukurasa wake wa Facebook kuwa:

eng: Sometimes students are afraid to raise these questions because they fear being expelled from school.
swa: Wakati mwingine wanafunzi wanaogopa kuuliza maswali haya kwa sababu wanaogopa kufukuzwa shuleni.

eng: They are afraid of being transferred to schools they don't want to attend, as well.
swa: Wanaogopa kuhamishiwa katika shule ambazo hawapendi kwenda pia.

eng: So concerns “go up in smoke,” though there are many stories.
swa: Kwa hiyo "moshi nenda juu" ingawa kuna hadithi nyingi.

eng: Students think twice before they complain about anything.
swa: Wanafunzi hufikiria mara mbili kabla hawajalalamika kuhusu jambo lolote.

eng: Some students play ironic jokes with the situation when they are sanctioned.
swa: Wanafunzi wengine hulifanyia jambo mzaha likishathibitishwa.

eng: The Timor Post's report has had a profound impact on Timorese society.
swa: Taarifa hizi za Timor Post zimekuwa za manufaa sana kwa jamii ya wa-Timor.

eng: Fining students for speaking Tetum has produced particular shock among the public because Tetum is one of the country's official languages.
swa: Kuwapiga wanafunzi faini kwa sababu ya kuongea Kitetumi imeleta mshtuko mkubwa miongoni mwa jamii kwa sababu Kitetumi ni moja kati ya lugha rasmi nchini.

eng: A public school in Uganda.
swa: Shule ya umma nchini Uganda.

eng: Tweeps argue that taxpayers money need to bail out schools like this one.
swa: Watumiji wanasema fedha za walipa kodi zinahitaji kunusuru shule kama hizi.

eng: Image released under Creative Commons by The Sustainable Sanitation Alliance.
swa: Picha ya Creative Common na The Sustainable Sanitation Alliance.

eng: When news broke that the government of Uganda intends to use 1 trillion shillings (US$300 million) of taxpayer money to bail out defaulting businesses, Ugandans on Twitter called the move a 'scam" and suggested the bailout money go towards Uganda's neglected public schools instead.
swa: Pale habari zilipoenea kwamba serikali ya Uganda inakusudia kutumia kiasi cha shilingi za Uganda Trilioni moja (Dola za Kimarekani milioni 300) za walipa kodi kwa ajili ya kunusu biashara kubwa, wa-Ganda walio kwenye mtandao wa Twita waliuita mpango huo kama 'ufisadi' na kupendekeza kwamba fedha hizo zingetumika kunusuru shule za umma zilizotelekezwa.

eng: The companies that the government wants to rescue accumulated debt from loans they privately acquired from various banks in Uganda.
swa: Makampuni ambayo serikali inataka kuyanusuru na mzigo wa madeni makubwa yaliyotokana na mikopo iliyochukuliwa kutoka kwenye mabenki mbalimbali nchini Uganda.

eng: Many of the businesses are run by powerful well-connected tycoons.
swa: Biashara nyingi zinaendeshwa na wafanyabiashara wakubwa wenye nguvu.

eng: Some central bank and ministry of finance officials are against the bailout plan.
swa: Baadhi ya maafisa wa benki kuu na wizara ya fedha wamepinga mpango huo.

eng: David Mpanga, a Ugandan lawyer, called the plan "socialisation of loss":
swa: David Mpanga, mwanasheria wa Uganda, aliuita mpango huo kuwa ni 'kuwafanya wananchi walipe hasara':

eng: The privatisation of profit and socialisation of loss.
swa: Kubinafsisha faida na kuchangia hasara.

eng: Must we all pay for business failure when we didn't all share in the profits made? — David F.K. Mpanga (@dfkm1970) July 22, 2016
swa: Lazima wote tugharamie hasara ya biashara za matajiri lakini lini tulichangia faida wanayopata?

eng: Allan Ssenyonga was surprised to find out that one of the enlisted businesses is a discotheque:
swa: Allan Ssenyonga alishangazwa nkufahamu kwamba mmoja wa makampuni yaliyoorodheshwa kuingia kwenye mpango huo ni biashara ya manyoya:

eng: Club Silk is one of the companies in need of a bail out.
swa: Club Silk ni moja wapo ya makampuni yanayohitaji kunusuriwa.

eng: Is this really a priority for Uganda?? #ScamBailOuts — Allan Ssenyonga (@ssojo81) July 22, 2016
swa: Hivi kweli hiki ni kipaumbele kwa Uganda?

eng: Fredrick Tumusiime suggested:
swa: Fredrick Tumusiime alipendekeza:

eng: For any #bailout, the public must acquire a stake in the firm(s).
swa: Ili hatua zozote za kutoa ruzuku kwa makampuni zifanyike, lazima wananchi wawe na hisa kwenye kampuni husika.

eng: No public money for private sins. #ScamBailOuts https://t.co/kQ95Ky2cqB — Fredrick Tumusiime (@tufre80) July 22, 2016
swa: Fedha za umma zisitumike kugharamia dhambi za watu binafsi

eng: Ugandans questioned the rationale of plans to help well-connected and powerful tycoons in a country with little investment into infrastructure, and dilapidated schools and hospitals.
swa: Wa-Ganda walihoji umuhimu wa mipango hiyo ya kuwasaidia wafanyabiashara wakubwa wenye uhusiano na wanasiasa nchini humo wakati serikali ikiwekeza kidogo sana kwenye miundombinu, shule na huduma za afya.

eng: Sarah Bireete suggested that the government bail out poor schools:
swa: Sarah Bireete alipendekeza kwamba serikali inusuru shule za umma zenye hali mbaya:

eng: Poor Ugandans can't continue to subsidise the rich #ScamBailOuts Bailout schools with no classrooms, books &latrines pic.twitter.com/YkNYlFEQd1 — Bireete Sarah (@SarahBireete) July 23, 2016
swa: Wa-Ganda masikini wanaendelea kutoa ruzuku kwa matajiri. Kwa nini tusiziokoe shule zisizokuwa na madarasa, vitabu na vyoo?

eng: Jeff shared a photo of a company that the government should be helping out:
swa: Jeff aliweka picha ya kampuni moja ambayo alifikiri serikali ingeweza kuisaidia kumaliza madeni yake:

eng: A photo representing the companies that need bail out by the Government using taxpayers money #ScamBailOuts pic.twitter.com/nZuldcEzBH — Jeff 4.7.1™ (@andsjeff) July 23, 2016
swa: Picha inaonesha 'kampuni' ambayo inahitaji sana kupata msaada wa fedha za walipa kodi

eng: And another photo of a dilapidated public school:
swa: Picha nyingine ya shule ya umma yenye hali mbaya:

eng: Karungu Seed School,Buhweju District.
swa: Shule ya Msingi Karungu, Wilaya ya Buhweju.

eng: Does it need a BailOut?
swa: Hivi shule hii haihitaji msaada?

eng: NO,Bailout companies that don't pay Tax #ScamBailOuts pic.twitter.com/giwY9J1zXa — Jeff 4.7.1™ (@andsjeff) July 23, 2016
swa: Hapana, tusaidie makampuni ambay0 hata hivyo yanakwepa kodi

eng: While Samwise Gamgee advised:
swa: Wakati huo huo Samwise Gamgee alishauri:

eng: If Bailing them out is a matter of National Importance, sharing their profits should be a matter of National Importance too. #ScamBailouts — Samwise Gamgee (@Sambannz) July 22, 2016
swa: Kama kutoa msaada kwa makampuni haya ni suala lenye Maslahi ya Taifa, kutoa faida yanayopata makampuni hayo ni suala lenye Maslahi ya Taifa pia

eng: With conflict and insecurity plaguing North and West Africa and civil war lingering in Syria, people continue to risk their lives crossing the Mediterranean Sea on makeshift boats to seek sanctuary in Europe.
swa: Hali ya migogoro na kukosekana kwa amani kunakozisumbua nchi za Kaskazini na Magharibi mwa Afrika pamoja na vita vya wenyewe kwa wenyewe vinavyoendelea huko Syria, watu wanaendelea kuhatarisha maisha yao kwa kuvuka bahari ya Mediterranean kwa kutumia boti zisizofaa kwa ajili ya kutafuta hifadhi kwenye mataifa ya Ulaya.

eng: The human cost of these passages has been dramatically high.
swa: Njia hizi zimegharimu kwa kiasi kikubwa kabisa maisha ya watu.

eng: In 2015, more than one million people were estimated to have entered European Union countries by sea, five times more than the year before.
swa: Mwaka 2015, zaidi ya watu milioni moja walikadiriwa kuwa waliingia kwenye mataifa ya nchi za Ulaya kwa njia ya bahari, mara tano zaidi ya mwaka uliopita.

eng: So far in 2016, the figure stands at more than 240,000.
swa: Hadi sasa, mwaka 2016, idadi hii imefikia zaidi ya watu 240,000.

eng: According to the UN Refugee Agency, about 3,500 people who tried to immigrate to Europe died or went missing in the Mediterranean Sea in 2014.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa Shirika la Wakimbizi la UN , mwaka 2014, takribani watu 3,500 waliojaribu kuhamia Ulaya walipoteza maisha, ama hawakujulikana walipo kwenye bahari ya Mediterranean.

eng: In 2015, the number rose to 3,771.
swa: Mwaka 2015, idadi hii ilipanda na kufikia watu 3,771.

eng: This year has already seen 2,944 people perish.
swa: Mwaka huu, watu 2, 944 wameshateketea.

eng: This is where SOS Méditerranée comes in.
swa: Na hapa ndipo nafasi ya SOS Méditerranée inapoonekana.

eng: SOS Mediterranée is an organization aiming to provide assistance to any person in distress at sea, whether they are men, women or children, migrants or refugees, who find themselves in mortal danger while crossing the Mediterranean.
swa: SOS Mediterranée ni taasisi inayolenga kutoa msaada kwa mtu yeyote anayepatwa na matatizo baharini, ikiwa ni wanaume, wanawake au watoto, wahamiaji au wakimbizi wanaojikuta katika hali ya hatari pindi wanapojaribu kuvuka bahari ya Mediterranean.

eng: The project is financed by private donations and public funding.
swa: Mradi huu unafadhiliwa na wafadhili binafsi na misaada kutoka serikalini.

eng: The funds raised go toward renting the boat and the daily costs of maintenance and rescue.
swa: Fedha zinazopatikana zinatumika kwa ajili ya kukodisha boti pamoja na gharama za kila siku za matengenezo na uokozi.

eng: The MS Aquarius in Cuxhaven, 2012.
swa: MS Aquarius huko Cuxhaven, 2012.

eng: CC BY-SA 3.0
swa: CC BY-SA 3.0

eng: The ship used for the operation is the Aquarius.
swa: Meli inayotumika kwenye kampeni hii ni Aquarius.

eng: SOS Mediterranée was started by German merchant marine captain Klaus Vogel and Sophie Beau of France, who has experience in humanitarian programs.
swa: SOS Mediterranée ilianzishwa na Baharia mfanyabiashara wa Ujerumani kapteni Klaus Vogel na Sophie Beau wa Ufaransa walio na uzoefu wa programu za utoaji wa misaada ya kibinadamu.

eng: The project was created after the end of the Italian navy's Operation Mare Nostrum, which also aimed to rescue migrants in distress at sea.
swa: Mradi huu ulianzishwa mara baada ya Operation Mare Nostrum ya jeshi la majini la Italia, mradi uliolenga pia kuwaokoa wahamiaji waliopatwa na misukosuko baharini.

eng: SOS Mediterranée's blog includes several accounts from those who have made the perilous journey.
swa: Blogu ya SOS Mediterranée imeweka maelezo ya baadhi ya watu waliosafiri katika safari hizi za hatari.

eng: These are a few of their stories.
swa: Zifuatazo ni baadhi tu ya simulizi zao.

eng: Kebba is a 22-year-old welder from Gambia.
swa: Kebba ni kijana wa miaka 22 na ni fundi wa kuchomea vyuma kutoka nchini Gambia.

eng: He fled his country because of the reigning dictator and lack of work:
swa: Aliondoka nchini mwake kwa sababu ya uongozi wa kidikteta na pia kutokana na kukosekana kwa ajira:

eng: The only way to get ahead is to become a soldier, and I didn't want to do that.
swa: Namna pekee ya kusonga mbele ni kuwa mwanajeshi, na mimi sikuhitaji kufanya hivyo.

eng: I lost my father and had to support my mother and my young sisters, so I went looking for work elsewhere.
swa: Nilimpoteza baba yangu na hivyo nilichukua jukumu la kumwangalia mama yangu pamoja na dada zangu wadogo, kwa hiyo ilinilazimu nitoke kutafuta fedha.

eng: In Libya, I was kidnapped.
swa: Nikiwa nchini Libya, nilitekwa.

eng: I was held in a camp for two months.
swa: Nilishikiliwa kwenye kambi kwa muda wa miezi miwili.

eng: There was virtually no food, no water, nowhere to sleep.
swa: Kwa ujumla, hakukuwa na chakula, wala maji na hata sehemu ya kulala.

eng: They killed six people I know in the camps.
swa: Kambini pale, waliwaua watu sita niliokuwa ninawafahamu.

eng: They would say, "Give me your money or we'll kill you," and they kept their word.
swa: Walikuwa wakisema, “Nipe fedha uliyonayo, vinginevyo, ninakuua”, na hatimaye walitekeleza walichosema.

eng: I wanted to go back home, but I had no way of getting there.
swa: Nilifikia hatua ya kutaka kurudi nyumbani, hata hivyo sikuwa na namna ya kuondoka.

eng: So I decided to take a risk and go to Europe.
swa: Kwa hiyo, niliamua kujaribu kuelekea Ulaya.

eng: The smugglers kept us in another camp for two or three weeks.
swa: Wavushaji walituweka kwenye kambi nyingine kwa muda wa kati ya wiki mbili au tatu.

eng: When the day came, they stuffed us onto the rubber boat.
swa: Siku ilipowadia, walitushindilia kwenye boti ya mpira.

eng: There was no captain, just the will of God.
swa: Hakukuwa na mwongoza boti, ilikuwa ni kudra za mwenyezi Mungu tu.

eng: I have two dreams: to become an underwater welder and to write a book about this journey.
swa: Nina ndoto mbili: yakwanza ni kuwa mchomeleaji wa vyuma wa majini na pia kuandika kitabu kuhusu safari hii.

eng: But if life gives me nothing else, I hope to at least be able to live in peace.
swa: Hata hivyo, kama maisha hayata nitunuku jambo jingine, angalao nina matumaini ya kuishi kwa amani.

eng: Cyrill is a Cameroonian executive who fled the brutality of the militant group Boko Haram in the northern part of the country.
swa: Cyrill ni afisa wa Cameroon aliyekimbia ukatili wa wanamgambo wa kundi la Boko Haram huko Kaskazini mwa nchi yake.

eng: He spoke of torture houses, robberies and violence he witnessed in Libya, a launching point for many of the boats headed to Europe:
swa: Aliongelea kuhusu nyumba za mateso, unyang’anyi pamoja na machafuko aliyoyashuhudia nchini Libya, ambayo ndio sehemu ya pekee ya watu kuondoka kwa boti zinazoelekea Ulaya:

eng: Libya is in another world—it is a country that has lost all sense of morality.
swa: Libya ni nchi iliyo kwenye ulimwengu mwingine- ni nchi iliyopoteza kabisa thamani ya utu.

eng: A world that has returned to an animalistic state.
swa: Ni chi iliyorudi kwenye zama za unyama.

eng: There are kids who are trained to shoot at black people in the streets, rob them by putting a blade to their throat, or learn to torture migrants as their parents watch.
swa: Mitaani kuna watoto wanaofundishwa kuua watu weusi kwa risasi, kunyang’anya mali kwa kuwatishia watu kuwa wangewakata makoo kwa nyembe, au wanajifunza kuwatesa wahamiaji ilihali wakitazamwa na wazazi wao.

eng: They talk about the systematic rape of women in the streets, the ruthless smugglers and guards who beat them and spit on them and tell them that they're not worth the bread they're giving them.
swa: Wanaongea kuhusu utaratibu wa kuwabaka wanawake mitaani, wavushaji binadamu wasio na utu pamoja na walinzi wanawapiga na kuwatemea mate na kisha kuwatukana kuwa hawana thamani kama ilivyo kwa mikate wanayowapatia.

eng: Gode Mosle is a 22-year-old Syrian who lived in Damascus.
swa: Gode Mosle ni kijana wa miaka 22 kutoka nchini Syria aliyekuwa anaishi Damascus.

eng: He is now in Sweden but remains traumatized by his memories of his escape:
swa: Kwa sasa yupo nchini Swiden lakini huwa anasongwa sana na hali ya kuweweseka pindi akumbukapo namna alivyoweza kujiokoa:

eng: I told my friends in Syria to not take these boats.
swa: Niliwaambia rafiki zangu walioko Syria kuwa wasithubutu kutumia boti hizi.

eng: They should go through Turkey and Greece, even though it costs a lot more.
swa: Ni vyema wapitie Uturuki na Ugiriki pamoja na kuwa ni gharama zaidi.

eng: There were about 700 of us in the boat but there wasn't even room for half of us.
swa: Kwenye boti, tulikuwemo takribani watu 700 lakini nafasi iliyokuwepo haikuwa ya kutosheleza hata nusu yetu.

eng: Those smugglers are animals.
swa: Wavushaji wale ni wanyama.

eng: They scream at people, steal from them and hit them when they get on board.
swa: Wanawakaripia watu, wanawaibia na kuwapiga watu wanapopanda kwenye boti.

eng: It was a kind of psychological torture that started even before the boat.
swa: Ilikuwa ni namna ya kuwaathiri watu kisaikolojia hata kabla ya kupanda kenye boti.

eng: Two Africans died in the hold.
swa: Waafrika wawili walipoteza maisha wakiwa kwenye sehemu ya kuwekea mizigo.

eng: They suffocated; they couldn't breathe because of the exhaust from the engine.
swa: Waliishiwa pumzi; hawakuweza kupumua kwa sababu ya hewa chafu kutoka kwenye injini.

eng: It was so rickety, we couldn't stand or move.
swa: Hali ilikuwa tete sana, hatukuweza kusimama wala kusogea.

eng: As soon as someone did, the boat threatened to capsize.
swa: Pale tu mtu alipojaribu kujisogeza, kulikuwa na hatari ya boti kupinduka.

eng: There was a lot of screaming.
swa: Kulikuwa na mayoye ya mara kwa mara.

eng: I wouldn't make that voyage again.
swa: Sitakaa tena kurudia safari ya namna hiyo.

eng: I can't forget what I saw.

eng: A Nigerian citizen named his dog after the Nigerian president Muhammadu Buhari.
swa: Raia wa Nigeria alimpatia mbwa wake jina lifanananalo na la Rais wa nchi hiyo Muhammadu Buhari.

eng: Creative Commons photo by Erfan Kouchari in Tasnim News Agency.
swa: Picha kwa hisani ya Erfan Kouchari wa Shirika la habari la Tasnim na imetumiwa kwa masharti ya Creative Commons .

eng: A trader named Joe Fortemose Chinakwe has been arrested by the Nigerian police for naming his pet dog "Buhari," which happens to be the surname of the country's president, in a case that touches on Nigeria's long history of ethnic tensions.
swa: Mfanyabiashara ajulikaye kwa jina la Joe Fortemose Chinakwe amekamatwa na maafisa wa polisi wa Nigeria baada ya kumwita mtoto wa mbwa wake jina la "Buhari," ambalo ni jina la ubini la Rais wa Nigeria, tukio amnbalo linahusisha historia ndefu ya mivutano ya kimakabila nchini Nigeria.

eng: The canine was named after a man called Alhaji Buhari, who is Chinakwe's neighbour.
swa: Mbwa huyo alipewa jina la mtu aliyefahamika kwa jina la Alhaji Buhari, ambaye ni jirani yake na ndugu Chinakwe.

eng: However, a different neighbour reported him over the matter, and many have since misconstrued the name as coming from President Muhammadu Buhari (PMB).
swa: Hata hivyo, jirani mweingine alitoa taarifa ya tukio hilo, na watu wengi wametafsiri kuwa jina hilo limetokana na jina la Rais Muhammadu Buhari (PMB).

eng: The dog was named after a different Buhari.
swa: Jina la mbwa huyo lilitokana na Buhari mwingine.

eng: Not Pmb.
swa: Siyo Rais Buhari.

eng: Case has nothing to do with PMB https://t.co/TgoapGJ0vm — ZahrahMusa (@Zahrahmusa) August 21, 2016
swa: Jambo hili halina uhusiano na Rais Buhari https://t.co/TgoapGJ0vm — ZahrahMusa (@Zahrahmusa) Agusti 21, 2016

eng: Authorities said Chinakwe would be charged with "conduct likely to cause a breach of peace," according to the Vanguard newspaper in an August 17 report.
swa: Mamlaka zilitaarifu kuwa Chinakwe angeshitakiwa kwa "kosa la kutaka kuvunja amani," hii ni kwa mujibu wa Gazeti la Vanguard kwenye taarifa yake ya tarehe 17.

eng: You know an average Northerner will feel bad over such a thing.
swa: Unajua raia wa kawaida wa Kaskazini atajihisi vibaya kwa jambo kama hili.

eng: It can cause serious ethnic crisis or religious confrontation because when you are relegating such a name to a certain person, you are indirectly insulting him.
swa: Linaweza kusababisha ugomvi mbaya sana au mvutano wa kidini kwani kwa kumpatatia mtu mwingine jina hilo ni kama vile unamdhalilisha kwa namna fulani.

eng: Nigeria is an ethnic fault-line state with over 250 ethnic groups and a history of violent tensions.
swa: Nigeria ni taifa la mrengo wa makabila likiwa na zaidi ya makabila 250 sambamba na historia ya mivutano mibaya .

eng: The three major ethnic groups are the Hausas and Fulani in the north, the Yorubas in the west and the Igbos in the east.
swa: Makabila makubwa matatu ni Hausa na Fulani kwa upande wa Kaskazini, WaYoruba kwa upande wa Magharibi na WaIgbo kwa upande wa Mashariki.

eng: The country still bears the scars of years of distrust, bickering and pervasive cleavages that have been further exacerbated by religious fundamentalism.
swa: Nigeria bado inayavumilia makovu ya miaka mingi ya hali ya kutokuaminiana, The country still bears the scars of years of distrust, mabishano na mipasuko iliyotapakaa kila kona ya nchi na ambayo imendelea kukuzwa vibaya na ukereketwa wa kidini. .

eng: The Nigerian Civil War, which lasted from 1967 to 1970, the numerous and unresolved root causes of ethno-religious crisis have dominated the country's socio-political space since independence in 1960 have not helped matters.
swa: Vita vya wenyewe kwa wenyewe vya nchini Nigeria , vilivyoanaza mwaka 1967 hadi 1970, vyanzo vikuu vya mgogoro vya mrengo wa kikabila na kidini na ambavyo bado havijatatuliwa vimechukua nafasi kubwa kwenye masuala ya kijamii na kisiasa nchini Nigeria tangu wakati wa uhuru mnamo mwaka 1960 havijaweza kusaidia kutatua changamoto hii.

eng: As though these were not enough, the perpetrators of these crimes targeting certain ethnicities go unpunished and a culture of impunity prevails.
swa: Kana kwamba haya hayakutosha, wahamasishaji wa makosa yanayowalenga watu wa makabila fulani hawaadhibiwi na utamaduni huu wa kutokuadhibiwa unaendelea kushamiri.

eng: According to media reports, Chinakwe had inscribed the name on both sides of the dog's body and walked the animal through his Hausa-dominated neighbourhood.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa vyombo vya habari, Chinakwe alimwandika mbwa wake kweye pande zote za ubavu na kisha kumpitisha mbwa huyo kwenye maeneo ya majirani zake ambao weingi wao ni wa kabial la Hausa.

eng: Hausas are a minority in the southwestern state of Ogun, where Chinakwe resides.
swa: Kwa kawaida, kabila la Hausa ni wachache Kusini Magharibi mwa jiji la Osan, ambapo ndipo yalipo makazi ya Chinakwe.

eng: President Muhammadu Buhari, for his part, is ethnic Fulani.
swa: Rais Muhammadu Buhari kwa upande wake, yeye ni wa kabila la Fulani.

eng: Naturally, the news of Chinakwe's arrest and the reason given by the police did not go down well with Nigerians.
swa: Katika hali ya kawaida, habari za kukamatwa kwa Chinakwe na sababu za kukamatwa kwake hazikupokelewa vizuri na raia wa Nigeria.

eng: Abimbola Adedokun, a newspaper columnist, warned of the danger in allowing divisions along ethnic or religious lines to exist:
swa: Abimbola Adedokun, mwandishi wa magazeti, alionesha madhara kuruhusu kuwepo kwa mipasuko ya kimakabila au ya kidini:

eng: History has taught us that whenever the “average northerner” says he “feels bad over a thing”, the rest of us are supposed to hurriedly rearrange our manners.
swa: Historia imetufundisha kuwa, pale “raia wa kawaida wa kutoka kaskazini” anaposema “hafurahishwi na jambo fulani”, wengine wote hatuna budi kujisahihisha na kubadili mienendo yetu haraka sana.

eng: We are told to take heed of invisible limits that “infidels” are not permitted to cross.
swa: Tuanaambiwa tuchukue tahadhari ya vikwazo visivyoonekana na ambavyo wale wasio na imani hawaruhusiwi kuvivuka.

eng: Alarmingly, a number of us have restricted ourselves to this emasculating avoidance of wrath.
swa: Kwa hali ilivyo, wengi wetu tumejiwekea vikwazo dhidi ya hali ya kujizuia kujiingiza kwenye chuki hii.

eng: We have mapped out “no-go areas” of public discussion that we trespass at grievous risks to ourselves.
swa: Tumeainisha “maeneo tusiyopaswa kupita” ya mijadala ya wazi ambayo tunajipitia huku kukiwa tumejiweka kwenye hatari kubwa kabisa.

eng: We have seen the repercussions of trespassing these bounds and they are not pleasant.
swa: Tumeshajionea matokeo ya kuvuka mipaka hii na matokeo yake si mazuri.

eng: From Gideon Akaluka’s killings to the Reinhard Bonnke crusade violence, the Miss World riots, the Danish cartoons saga, and many other instances of unwarranted violence that have occurred, we have long realised we are dealing with a short-tempered evil spirit who demands a sacrifice of our collective dignity so he can let us live.
swa: Kutokea kwenye mauaji ya Gideon Akaluka hadi kwenye machafuko ya kampeni ya kidini ya Reinhard Bonnke, vurugu za mashindano ya Mlimbwende wa Dunia, suala la katuni za kidenishi pamoja na matukio mengine mengi yaliyotokea na kupelekea machafuko ambayo hayakutarajiwa, kwa muda sasa tumegundua kuwa tunakabiliana na mzimu aliyejeruhiwa na mwenye hasira ambaye anahitaji sisi tutoe utu wetu sadaka ili atuache tuendelee kuishi.

eng: Gideon Akaluka was a Christian Igbo trader in Nigeria who was beheaded by a mob in 1994 for allegedly desecrating the Koran.
swa: Gideon Akaluka alikuwa ni mfanyabiashara wa Nigeria kutoka kabila la Igbo ambaye alikatwa kichwa hadi kufa na kundi la watu mnamo mwaka 1994 kwa kile kinachodhaniwa kuwa alikashifu Koran.

eng: A 1991 visit by German evangelist Christian Reinhard Bonnke sparked deadly riots in the northern city of Kano after he reportedly converted some Muslims to Christianity.
swa: Mwaka 1991 Nigeria ilitembelewa na mwingilisti wa kikatoliki, Mjerumani Reinhard Bonnke yaliibuka machafuko mabaya huko Kusini mwa jimbo la Kano mara baada ya kuripotiwa kuwa aliwabadili dini baadhi ya Waislamu na kuwa Wakristu.

eng: In 2002, more than 200 people were killed and dozens of churches attacked during three days of rioting in the north over Nigeria's hosting of the Miss World beauty pageant.
swa: Mwaka 2002, zaidi ya watu 200 waliuawa na makumi mawili ya makanisa kushambuliwa wakati wa machafuko ya siku tatu mfululizo huko kaskazini kufuatia Nigeria kuwa mwenyeji wa shindano la kumpata mlimbwende wa Dunia .

eng: And in 2005, a Danish newspaper's publication of several editorial cartoons depicting the Prophet Muhammad led to protests in various countries, including Nigeria.
swa: Na mwaka 2005, gazeti la Kidenishi lililochapisha katuni zilizokuwa zikimzungumzia Nabii Muhammad ziliibua maandamano kwenye nchi mbalimbali, Nigeria ikiwa miongoni.

eng: Adedokun continued:
swa: Adedokun aliendelea:

eng: The trouble is that this evil spirit of violence who has a chokehold on our society is implacable.
swa: Tatizo nni kuwa hii laana ya machafuko inayoikaba jamii yetu ni vigumu sana kuipunguzaThe trouble is that this evil spirit of violence who has a chokehold on our society is implacable.

eng: He has tasted vats of blood of the innocent and assumed a proprietary right over our lives.
swa: Laana hii imegharimu maisha ya watu wengi wasio na hatia na kujihakikishia umiliki halali wa maisha yetu.

eng: Violence in Nigeria happens, not because of intrepid and insensitive people who say things that make others feel bad.
swa: Machafuko nchini Nigeria, yanatokea siyo kwa sababu ya watu wasio na hofu wala kujali ambao wanasema mambo yanayowafanya watu wengine wajisikie vibaya.

eng: Rather, they stem from a cultivated attitude of those who think others’ lives are theirs to take, and they have no regard for any law that attempts to restrain their execution of mindless violence.
swa: Kinyume chake, wanatokana na mitazamo iliyojengeka ya wale wanaofikiri kuwa maisha ya watu wengine ni halali yao, na hawana hofu yoyote ya sharia inayowakataza kutekeleza uhalifu.

eng: There is no legal basis for a trial of Chinakwe, according to Monday Ubani, the incoming second national vice president of the Nigeria Bar Association:
swa: Hakuna msingi wowote wa sharia dhidi ya shtaka la Chinakwe, hii ni kwa mujibu wa Monday Ubani, ambaye ni Makamu wa pili ajae wa Jumuia ya Kitaifa ya Wanasheria wa Nigeria:

eng: In the eye of the law, it is not criminal for somebody to name his or her dog after another person.
swa: Kwa maujibu wa sharia, siyo kosa la jinai kwa mtu fulani kumpatia jina la mtu fulani mbwa wake.

eng: It may be offensive by examining the circumstances under which the incident happened.
swa: Inaweza kuwa ni uonevu kufuatilia mazingira ya u tukio hilo.

eng: Nigerian Twitter users have condemned Chinakwe's incarceration.
swa: Watumiaji wa Twita nchini Nigeria wamelaumu kwa tukio la Chinakwe kutiwa nguvuni.

eng: Nigerian musician Seun Anikulapo Kuti, the son of the legendary Fela Kuti, said:
swa: Mwanamuziki wa Nigeria Seun Anikulapo Kuti, the son of the legendary Fela Kuti, alisema:

swa: Wanasheria wetu wa haki za binadamu wako wapi?

eng: This is serious injustice, why did the government not arrest OBJ who named his chimpanzee Patience?
swa: Hapa haki haijatendeka kabisa, kwa nini serikali haikumkamata OBJ aliyempa Sokwe wake jina la Patience?

eng: OBJ stands for former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo, who once owned a pet chimpanzee named Patience, supposedly after Patience Jonathan, the wife of another former president, Goodluck Jonathan.
swa: OBJ ni kifupisho cha Rais aliyepita wa Nigeria Olusegun Obasanjo, ambaye hapoa awali alikuwa na mtoto wa sokwe aliyempa jina la Patience, linalodaiwa kuwa ni jina la Patience Jonathan, mke wa Rais mwingine mstaafu, Goodluck Jonathan.

eng: Obasanjo campaigned against Jonathan in Nigeria's 2015 presidential election, which current President Muhammadu Buhari won.
swa: Obasanjo alikataa kumpigia kampeni Jonathan kwenye uchanguzi mkuu wa mwa Nigeria wa mweaka 2015, ambapo Rais wa sasa, Muhammadu Buhari alishinda.

eng: Reno Omokiri, new media spokesman of former President Jonathan, argued in a tweet that more should have heeded his words:
swa: Reno Omokiri, msemaji mpya wa Rais mstaafu Jonathan, wa kupitia vyombo vya habari, alitanabaisha kuptia ukurasa wake wa Twita kuwa ilikuwa vyema kwa watu kutilia maanani maoni yake:

swa: Unakumbuka niliposema hili Nilidhihakiwa na kupuuzwa, hata hivyo wakati umesema ukweli. pic.twitter.com/JGvjpwej7m — Reno Omokri (@renoomokri) Agusti 22, 2016

eng: Omokiri was referring to his August 11 tweet: "If you want to know whether there is change in Nigeria, insult PMB the way you insulted GEJ and you will know the true meaning of 'change'!"
swa: Omokiri amerejea Makala yake ya Twita ya tarehe 11 Agusti : "Kama unataka kufahamu kama kuna mabadiliko nchini Nigeria, mtukane PMB namna ulivyokuwa unamtukana GEJ na hapo ndipo utakapojua haswa nini maana ya 'badiliko'!"

eng: Buhari ran on a platform of "change" against Jonathan in last year's vote.
swa: Buhari alishiriki kwenye mdahalo mrefu wa jukwaa la "mabadiliko" dhidi ya Jonathan kwenye uchaguzi mkuu wa mwaka jana.

eng: Twitter user MaziNze chided the police for double standards:
swa: Mtumiaji wa Twita, MaziNze aliwalaumu polisi kwa kuwa na ubaguzi kwenye matumizi ya sheria:

swa: Viongozi wa kutoka kabila la Fulani hawapo gerezani, wale walioua kwa sababu ya ukashifuji dini wanaranda tu mtaani.

eng: it is the buhari dog owner that is in jail
swa: Bali, yule aliyempa mbwa wake jina ndiye aliyefungwa. i

swa: Habari za asubuhi Nigeria — maziNze™ (@hand2ome) Agosti 24, 2016

eng: A similar fate was visited on another lady in July, who was hacked to death in the nations capital, Abuja by suspected Muslim fanatics.
swa: Vingozi wa jamii ya wafugaji wa kabila la Fulani walituhumiwa kwa kosa la kuvamia jamii za wakulima nchini Nigeria na na kuwaacha kifo kikiwanyemelea .

eng: Kemi shared this photographs of Ali Baba, a Nigerian comedian, and his dogs which were named after world celebrities and leaders:
swa: Na mwezi Juni, mwanamke mmoja aliuawa na kundi la watu huko Kano kwa kosa lililodhaniwa la kumkashifu Nabii Mohammed.

eng: Meet Ali Baba &his dogs, OBJ, IBB, Obama, Abacha, Thatcher&Chaka
swa: Tukio kama hilo lilitokea kwa mwanamke mwingine mezi wa Julai, ambaye alikatwakatwa hadi kufa katika mji mkuu wa Nigeria, tukio linalodhaniwa kufanywa na Waislam wenye msimamo mkali.

eng: Those using ethnicity, religion and political sentiments to obfuscate this case should know that Nigeria is a country of laws.
swa: Kwa wale wanaotumia ukabila, dini na mrengo wa kisiasa ili kulikuza kupita kiasi shauri hili, wanapaswa kufahamu kuwa Nigeria ni nchi ya sheria.

eng: The human rights community will never sit back and watch innocent citizens being traumatised and dehumanized.
swa: Jumuia ya wasimamizi wa haki za binadamu hawataweza kukaa kimya na kutazama raia wasio na hatia wakifadhaishwa na kudhalilishwa.

eng: The fact that the two persons who donated this money are from the North and the South West, respectively, shows that the bonds of brotherhood and egalitarianism among patriotic Nigerians are superior to the whimsical and repulsive commentaries of the ethnic and religious bigots.
swa: Kwa kuwa watu wawili waliochangia fedha wanatokea Kaskazini na Kusini Magharibi inaonesha kuwa nguvu ya undugu na usawa miongoni mwa waNigeria wazalendo ni zaidi ya watu wa mzaha na walio na ushawishi hasi wa ukabila na udini.

swa: Kama bado hujausikiliza, huu hapa ndio wimbo mzuri wa kujivunia umoja na uhuru wa Nepali.

swa: Na hii ni tafsiri ya Kiingereza ya wimbo wa Taifa la Nepali iliyofanywa na Sushma Joshi.

eng: Hundreds of flower bouquets, we are one garland of Nepalis
swa: Mamia ya mashada ya maua, sisi ni shada moja la raia wa Nepali.

eng: Sovereign, spread from Mechi to Mahakali.

eng: This comes on the heels of an Internet shutdown that took place early in the morning on August 2, when Internet access in a commercial area of Dhaka was cut off for 3.5 hours as part of a government-enforced “drill” to test the capabilities of telecommunications agencies in the country.
swa: Hili linajitokeza katika mkanganyiko wa kufungiwa kwa mtandao wa internet kulikofanyika asubuhi ya tarehe 2 Agosti, wakati mtandao wa internet ulipokatwa katika mji wa kibiashara wa Dhaka kwa masaa matatu na nusu kama sehemu ya serikali kutekeleza mpango wa kujaribu uwezo wa mashirika ya simu nchini.

eng: The national telecommunications agency indicated that it was part of a series of test shutdowns that will soon take place across the country.
swa: Shirika la mawasiliano ya simu nchini lilionesha kuwa ilikuwa sehem ya mlolongo wa majaribio ya kuzima ambayo yatafanyika hivi karibuni nchini pote.

eng: The “Internet shutdown drill” was announced on August 1 and presented as a security measure.
swa: Mpango wa kuzima internet ulitangazwa Agosti 1 na kuwasilishwa kama mkakati wa kiusalama.

eng: This comes following the brutal attack in early July at the Holey Artisan Bakery, where 20 hostages were murdered as part of a terrorist attack that came at a time when violence is increasing in the country.
swa: Hili linafanyika kufuatia uvamizi wa kikatili uliofanyika mapema Julai katika enei la kuokea mikate la Holey Artisan, ambapo mateka wapatao 20 waliuawakama sehemu ya shambulio la kigaidi lililokuja katika kipindi ambacho vurugu zinaongezeka nchini .

eng: In addition to the Internet, other services were also cut.
swa: Pamoja na mtandao wa intaneti huduma nyingine pia zilikatwa.

eng: Mobile phone operators reportedly tested their ability to shut down voice calls and ISPs were also asked to block certain web pages.
swa: Makampuni ya uendeshaji wa simu za mikononi yaliripotiwa kupimwa uwezo wao kuzima miito ya sauti na ISPs pia waliambiwa wafungie baadhi ya tovuti.

eng: It is unclear whether these are the same sites that were ordered blocked on August 4.
swa: Haijaeleweka vizuri kama tovuti hizi ndio zile zile zilizoamriwa kufungiwa hapo Agosti 4.

eng: The Chairman of the Bangladesh Telecom Regulatory Commission (BTRC), Shahjahan Mahmood, clarified on August 3 that this exercise was the first in a series of temporary Internet shutdowns, saying “As part of the ongoing exercise, all sorts of Internet connections will be suspended for a short period anytime at any place in the country,”
swa: Mwenyekiti wa Tume ya Udhibiti wa Mawasiliano ya Simu nchini Bangladeshi (BTRC), Shahjahan Mahmood, kuwa hili zoezi lilikuwa la kwanza kati ya mfululizo wa kuzima kwa muda kwa mitandao ya internet, anasema “Kama sehemu ya zoezi linaloendelea, aina zote za mitandao ya internet itasimamishwa kwa kipindi kifupi kwa muda wowote na mahali popote hapa nchini,”

eng: Ahsan Habib Khan, vice-chairman of BTRC added that these future blackouts are likely to take place during the night, and on holidays.
swa: Ahsan Habib Khan, makamu mwenyekiti wa BTRC aliongezea kuzimwa huko kwa mitandao hiyo mara nyingi itakuwa inafanyika wakati wa usiku na siku za mapumziko.

eng: Citizens are struggling to see how these shutdowns might have a positive impact on public safety, but the pitfalls of this strategy seem self-evident.
swa: Wananchi wanapambana kuona jinsi kuzimwa huko kwa mitandao kutakavyokuwa na matokeo chanya katika usalama wao, lakini changamoto zimeonesha kukwama kwa mkakati huo.

eng: Bangladeshi citizens expressed dismay and anger on social media, with one Facebook user writing:
swa: Wananchi wa Bangladeshi wameeleza masikitiko yao na hasira zao kupitia mitandao ya kijamii kwa mtumiaji mmoja wa mtandao wa Facebook kuandika:

eng: And wtf is this??
swa: Na hiki ni nini??

eng: Without any prior notice or with such a short notice??
swa: Bila hata ya taarifa kabla au kwa taarifa ya muda mfupi hivyo??

eng: Do they have any idea how people work and how it may affect their work??
swa: Wanajua jinsi watu wqnavyofanya kazi kweli au kujua jinsi jambo hilo linavyoweza kuathiri kazi zao??

eng: Imagine the situation - an area suddenly went offline around the most critical time and most of the people don't even know about it and you can't even use your cell phone data to communicate with someone to inform about the situation cause your entire area is f**ed up!
swa: Fikiria kuhusu hali hiyo-mtandao unazimika katika eneo ghafla tena katika nyakati muhimu ambapo watu karibia wote hawajui kuhusu hilo na huwezi kutumia mtandao katika simu yako ya kiganjani kufanya mawasiliano na mtu mwingine kumpa taarifa kuhusu hali mbaya iliyosababishwa katika eneo zima.

eng: On Twitter, digital rights group Access Now called these actions “misguided”, as part of their global campaign against internet shutdowns, #KeepItOn.
swa: Huko Twitter, kundi la haki za kiteknolojia Access Now ziliita vitendo hivi kuwa "potofu" kama sehemu ya kampeni yao ya kimataifa kupinga kuzimwa kwa huduma ya internet, #ziwasheni.

eng: BREAKING: Today Bangladesh announced an internet shutdown "drill".
swa: YA KUSHTUKIZA: Leo Bangladesh imetangaza "mpango" wa kuzimwa kwa mtandao wa internet.

eng: Here's our take. #KeepitOn pic.twitter.com/0gVp1ndX8I — Access Now (@accessnow) August 1, 2016
swa: Huu ndio mtazamo wetu. #Usizimwe pic.twitter.com/0gVp1ndX8I — Access Now (@accessnow) Agosti 1, 2016

eng: This is not the first time networks have been deliberately shut down in Bangladesh.
swa: Hii sio mara ya kwanza mitandao kuzimwa kwa makusudi nchini Bangladeshi.

eng: In November 2015, the Bangladeshi government blocked social media sites including Facebook, Viber and Whatsapp for almost four weeks.
swa: Novemba 2015, serikali ya Bangladeshi ilifungia kurasa za mitandao ya kijamii ikiwemo Facebook, Viber na Whatsapp kwa kipindi cha karibu wiki nne. .

eng: On the first day of that ban, Internet access was cut to the entire country for roughly 75 minutes.
swa: Siku ya kwanza ya marufuku hiyo, huduma za internet zilikatwa nchi nzima kwa muda unaokadiriwa ni dakika 75.

eng: Immediately afterwards, Mahmood said it had been a mistake and the shutdown was the result of a “misunderstanding.”
swa: Mara moja baadaye, Mahmood alisema kuwa kuna makosa yalijitokeza na kuzimwa kwa mitandao hiyo ilikuwa ni matokeo ya "kutokuelewana"

eng: This new push to curtail citizens’ Internet access is extremely worrying, particularly in Bangladesh where freedom of expression is increasingly under threat, both online and in everyday life.
swa: Msukumo huu mpya wa kuwaondoshea wananchi mtandao wa interneti unatia hofu sana, hasa kwa Bangladesh ambapo uhuru wa kujieleza unaendelea kuwa chini ya vitisho , kote mitandaoni na katika maisha ya kila siku.

eng: In 2011, the United Nations declared Internet access to be a fundamental human right.
swa: Mwaka 2011, Umoja wa mataifa ulitangaza kuwa upatikanaji wa huduma za Internet kuwa haki ya msingi katika haki za binadamu. .

eng: Just four weeks ago, the United Nations Human Rights Council on Friday passed a nonbinding resolution condemning countries that prevent or disrupt access to the internet.
swa: Ni wiki nne tu zimepita, Baraza la Umoja wa Mataifa linalosimamia Haki za Binadamu ijumaa lilipitisha azimio lisilo la kisheria likilaani nchi zinazozuia au kukwamisha upatikanaji wa huduma za Interneti.

eng: Despite these repeated violations of digital rights, the government’s claims of moving towards a "Digital Bangladesh" continue.
swa: Licha ya kujirudia kwa ukiukwaji huu wa haki za kiteknolojia, madai ya serikali kuwa inasonga mbele kuelekea " Bangladeshi ya Kitenolojia" yameendelea.

eng: Protest in Ethiopia from Abdi Lemessa's Facebook page.
swa: Waandamanaji katika picha kutoka katika ukurasa wa Facebook wa Abdi Lemessa.

eng: Used with permission.
swa: Imetumiwa kwa ruhusa.

eng: As hundreds of protesters took to the streets over the weekend in Oromia and Amhara, two of Ethiopia’s largest administrative regions, security forces violently disbanded demonstrators with live bullets.
swa: Wakati mamia ya waandamanaji wakiingia mitaani mwishoni mwa juma huko Oromia na Amhara, ambayo ni mikoa miwili mikubwa ya kiutawala nchini Ethiopia, vikosi vya ulinzi vilimimina risasi za moto kwa waandamanaji.

eng: According to news sites and social media reports, about 100 protesters were killed.
swa: Kwa mujibu wa taarifa za tovuti na mitandao ya kijamii, waandamanaji wapatao 100 waliuawa.

eng: The protests in Oromia and Amhara started at different times and for different reasons, but they both stem from identity politics.
swa: Maandamano ndani ya Oromia na Amhara yalianza kwa nyakati tofauti na kwa sababu tofauti, lakini iliyo kubwa ni madai ya kisiasa.

eng: The distribution of wealth and power among Ethiopia's 100 million citizens falls suspiciously along ethnic lines.
swa: Mgawanyo wa mali na madaraka kati ya wa-Ethiopia wapatao milioni 100 unafanywa kwa upendeleo wa kikabila.

eng: The Tigray make up 6% of the population but dominate the ranks of the military and government.
swa: Wa-Tigrai ni asilimia 6 ya raia wa Ethiopia lakini ndio wanaoshikilia nafasi za juu katika jeshi na serikali.

eng: At 34%, the Oromos are the largest ethnic group in Ethiopia, but they have only a nominal federal representation in their country.
swa: Kwa 34%, Wa-Oromo ambao ni asilimia 34 ya watu wote nchini humo, ndilo kabila kubwa nchini Ethiopia, lakini hata hivyo wana uwakilishi wa jina tu katika serikali.

eng: The Amhara represent 27% of the country's population.
swa: Na Wa-Amhara wanawakilisha asilimia 27 nyingine ya watu nchini.

eng: Details of the exact number of fatalities were hard to come by before Monday because the government blocked internet services and telephone services in Oromia and parts of the Amhara region.
swa: Undani wa idadi halisi ya vifo ilikuwa ngumu kupatikana kabla ya Jumatatu kwa sababu serikaliilifunga huduma ya intaneti pamoja na huduma ya simu katika mkoa wa Oromia na baadhi ya sehemu za mkoa wa Amhara.

eng: Funerals of the dead took place on Monday and Tuesday in Bahir Dar and numerous towns across Oromia.
swa: Mazishi ya waliouawa yalifanyika siku za Jumatatu na Jumanne katika mji wa Bahir Dar na vitongoji kadhaa vyaOromia.

eng: Despite the government’s willingness to use lethal force, calls for more protests in Oromia and Amhara regions are already taking place on Facebook.
swa: Licha ya serikali kuwa na nia ya kutumia nguvu za kijeshi, wito wa maandamano zaidi katika mikoa ya Oromia na Amhara ulishachukua nafasi katika mtandao waFacebook.

eng: Activists, inside Ethiopia and abroad, claim that protests will not subside unless the government is open to an inclusive political solution in Oromia and Amhara.
swa: Wanaharakati wa ndani ya Ethiopia na nje ya nchi, wanadai kuwa maandamano hayatapungua labda serikali ifungue mlango wa siasa za umoja huko Oromia na Amhara.

eng: A weekend of killing in Amhara and Oromia
swa: Mwisho wa wiki wa mauaji katika Amhara na Oromia

eng: The Amhara regional state capital, Bahir Dar, saw the heaviest causalities in decades on Saturday as the residents took to the streets in protest, defying authorities who killed at least 20 protesters in a nearby historical city of Gonder two weeks before. According to Amnesty International, at least 30 people were killed in one day in Bahir Dar.
swa: Katika Makao makuu ya mkoa wa Amhara, Bahir Dar, yameshuhudiwa maandamano makubwa ambayo hayajaonekana kwa miongo mingi hapo Jumamosi baada ya wakazi wa mji huo kuingia mitaani kuandamana, wakipinga mamlaka iliyoua waandamanaji karibu 20 karibia na mji wa kihistoria wa Gonder wiki mbili kablaKulingana na taarifa za shirika la Kutetea Haki za Binadamu (Amnesty International), watu wapatao 30 waliuawa kwa siku moja huko Bahir Dar.

eng: Similarly, in Oromia at least 50 people were killed and hundreds were arrested.
swa: Vile vile, huko Oromia watu wapatao 50 waliuawa na mamia wengine walikamatwa.

eng: In the capital, Addis Ababa, hundreds of protesters tried to gather at Meskel Square, but were quickly and violently dispersed by security forces.
swa: Katika mji mkuu Addis Ababa, mamia ya waandamanaji walijaribu kujikusanya katika viwanja vya Meskel, lakini walitawanywa kwa haraka na kwa nguvu kubwa na vyombo vya usalama.

eng: On Tuesday afternoon a 1:40 second video posted on EthioTube shows security forces brutally beating demonstrators.
swa: Siku ya Jumanne adhuhuri saa saba na dakika arobaini video ya pili iliwekwa katika tovuti ya EthioTube ikionesha vyombo vya usalama vikiwapiga waandamanaji kikatili.

eng: CLICK TO WATCH
swa: KUANGALIA CLICK

eng: The Amhara protests
swa: Waandamanaji wa Amhara

eng: The protests in Amhara began on July 12, 2016 when security forces attempted to arrest a leader of the Wolqait Identity and Self-Determination Committee, Colonel Demeka Zewdu, on alleged terrorism charges.
swa: Maandamano ya Amhara yalianza Julai 12, 2016 wakati vyombo vya usalama vilipojaribu kumkamata kiongozi wa Kundi la Wolqait Linalodai Kutambuliwa, Kanali Demeka Zewdu, kwa tuhuma za ugaidi.

eng: The protestors in Amhara and their leaders are demanding the repositioning of the provinces of Welkait-Tegede community into the Amhara region from adjacent Tigray Regional State.
swa: Waandamanaji wa Amhara na viongozi wao wanadai kurejeshwa kwa jimbo la Welkait-Tegede katika mkoa wa Amhara kutoka kwa mamlaka ya mkoa wa karibu wa Tigrai.

eng: News reports and social media reports show that grievances among Welkait-Tegede community members have been building for some time over what activists say is the annexation of their land and forceful assimilation of their identity into Tigray region.
swa: Taarifa za habari na taarifa za mitandao ya kijamii zinaonesha kero za wanajamii ya Welkait-Tegede zimejengeka kwa muda sasa hasa kuhusu kile wanaharakati walichosema katika uhalalishaji wa ardhi yao na kuingiza utambulisho wao kwa nguvu katika jimbo la Tigrai.

eng: Remarkably, disproportionate political, economic and military power is vested in the elites hailing from Tigray region.
swa: Inashangaza, siasa, uchumi na nguvu za kijeshi zisizowiana, zimeachwa kwa kundi la wasomi wachache wanoibukia kutoka mkoa wa Tigrai.

eng: Pro-government commentators, however, play down the power of the Tigrayan elites instead blame opposition groups for blowing the question of Welkait-Tegede community assimilation out of proportion.
swa: Hata hivyo watoa maoni wa upande wa serikali walipuuzia nguvu ya wasomi wa Ki-Tigrari na badala yake walilaumu makundi pinzani kwa kulipigia debe swala la jamii ya watu wa Welkait-Tegede bila kuzingatia uwiano.

eng: The Oromia protests
swa: Waandamanaji wa Oromia

eng: The demonstrations in Oromia are the continuation of protests that have become a daily occurrence since November 2015.
swa: Maandamano ndani ya Oromia ni muendelezo wa maandamano ambayo yamekuwa sehemu ya maisha ya kila siku tangu Novemba 2015.

eng: Initially, the protest started in Oromia when students asked the government to stop its plan to expand the capital city Addis Ababa into surrounding farm lands of Oromia.
swa: Awali, maandamano yalianzia Oromia pale wanafunzi walipoidai serikali kuacha mpango wake wa kuupanua mji mkuu wa Addis Ababa kuelekea katika sehemu za mashamba ya Oromia.

eng: The students argued that the controversial plan to expand Addis Ababa into Oromia state would result in mass evictions of farmers mostly from the Oromo ethnic group.
swa: Wanafunzi walisema kuwa mpango huo tata wa kuupanua mji wa Addis Ababa kuelekea Oromia kutasababisha kufukuzwa kwa wakulima wengi hasa wenye asili ya Ki-Oromo.

eng: The government rejected the accusation, claiming that the expansion was intended only to facilitate the development of infrastructure such as transportation, utilities, and recreation centers.
swa: Serikali iliyakataa mashitaka hayo, ikidai kuwa upanuzi huo ulilenga tu kuwezesha maendeleo ya miundo mbinu kama vile barabara, maboresho mengine pamoja na sehemu za burudani.

eng: Although the government has scrapped the plan to expand Addis Ababa, the move has fallen far short of the demands of the protesters, which include greater questions of self-rule, freedom and identity.
swa: Ingawa serikali ilifuta mpango wa upanuzi wa Addis Ababa, hatua hiyo inaonekana kukwamishwa na madai ya waandamanaji yanayojumuisha suala kubwa la utawala huru, uhuru na utambulisho.

eng: For example, the students are demanding that Oromo become a federal language.
swa: Kwa mfano, wanafunzi wanadai kuwa ki-Oromo kiwe lugha ya taifa.

eng: Oromo, the language of the Oromo people, is the most widely spoken language in Ethiopia and the fourth largest African language.
swa: Ki-Oromo, lugha ya watu wa Oromo ndio lugha inayozungumzwa zaidi nchini Ethiopia na lugha ya nne kwa ukubwa barani Afrika.

eng: However, it is not the working language of the federal government.
swa: Pamoja na hayo, hiyo sio lugha rasmi kwa serikali ya shirikisho.

eng: In May 2014, the government suspended the plan to expand the capital city in order to abate the students protests that saw at least 12 students were killed and hundreds of ethnic Oromo students were imprisoned.
swa: Hapo Mei 2014, serikali ilifuta mpango wa upanuzi wa mji mkuu ili kupunguza maandamano ya wanafunzi yaliyopelekea wanafunzi 12 kuuwawa na mamia wenye asili ya ki-Oromo kufungwa jela.

eng: But in November 2015, the government decided to resume plans to expand the capital.
swa: Lakini Novemba 2015, serikali iliamua kuufufua mpango wa upanuzi wa mji mkuu.

eng: It is not clear if the government will revive the plan again.
swa: Kwa sasa hatuna uhakika kama serikali itaufufua mpango huo tena.

eng: Demands of self-rule in other regions
swa: Madai ya utawala huru katika mikoa mingine

eng: The arrest of numerous prominent opposition leaders such as Bekele Gerba and Yonatan Tesfaye, the suppression of journalists and bloggers and the brutal crackdown on protesters by security forces, in which at least 500 people have died according to Human Rights Watch have served only to ignite fresh protests in Oromia.
swa: Kukamatwa kwa viongozi maarufu kadhaa wa upinzani kama vile Bekele Gerba na Yonatan Tesfaye, ukandamizwaji wa waandishi wa habari na wanablogu na utawanywaji wa kikatili kwa waandamanaji kunakofanywa na vyombo vya usalama, watu wapatao 500 wameshakufa na taarifa hii ni kwa mujibu wa shirika la Human Rights Watch kumechochea maandamano mapya huko Oromia.

eng: The Ethiopian government spokesperson Getachew Reda frequently says there is no political solution as the government won the latest parliamentary election in May 2015 by 100%.
swa: Msemaji wa serikali ya Ethiopia Getachew Reda mara kwa maraanasema kuwa hakuna suluhu ya kisiasa kwa kuwa serikali ilishinda uchaguzi wa bunge uliofanyika karibuni hapo Mei 2015 kwa asilimia 100.

eng: Observers say that this is the most serious challenge the Ethiopian government has faced since they came to power in 1991.
swa: Waangalizi wanasema kuwa hii ni changamoto kubwa sana ambayo serikali ya Ethiopia inakumbana nayo tangu iwepo madarakani mwaka 1991.

eng: The closest was in 2005 when Ethiopia had its only truly contested election.
swa: Ya karibuni ilikuwa ni mwaka 2005 wakati Ethiopia ilipofanya uchaguzi pekee wenye ushindani wa kweli.

eng: But lately questions of self-rule and identity have become one of the sources of political violence.
swa: Lakini baadayemaswali kuhusu kujitawala na utambulisho vimekuwa moja ya vyanzo vya misuguano ya kisiasa.

eng: In April there were instances of violent demonstrations demanding self-rule in Southern Regional State, particularly in Konso area.
swa: Hapo Aprili kulikuwa na mifano ya maandamano ya vurugu waandamanaji wakidai utawala huru katika ukanda wa Kusini mwa nchi, hasa katika eneo la Konso.

eng: There were also similar conflicts in the South Western State of Gambela in January 2016.
swa: Pia kulikuwa na mgogoro wa kufanana na huo katika ukanda wa Kusini Magharibi mwa jimbo la Gambela hapo Januari 2016.

eng: Twitter user Awol echoed similar sentiments saying this is the most significant political mass action since the death of the late Prime Minister Meles Zenawi:
swa: Mtumiaji wa mtandao wa Twita, Awol alitoa maoni yanayofanana na hayo akisema, hii ni hatua muhimu sana ya kisiasa baada ya wananchi wengi kuchukua hatua tangu kifo cha Waziri Mkuu Meles Zenawi:

swa: Kufuatia uchaguzi wa mwaka 2005 serikali iliwapiga risasi waandamanaji wapatao mia tatu baada ya Waziri Mkuu wa kipindi hicho, Meles Zenawi, kutangaza hali ya hatari wakati watu waliokuwa wanawaunga mkono wapinzani kuamua kuingia mtaani kupinga matokeo ya uchaguzi huo.

swa: Tafadhali endelezeni ustaarabu mliouonesha kwa kipindi chote, msiguse raia wala mali zao.

swa: Kwa kasi hii ya kuondoa utawala na kushughulikia Ethiopia huru na ya haki iko karibu.

eng: I urge activists to focus on constructively helping the ongoing struggle aiming at creating free and fair Ethiopia that we are going to have sooner.
swa: Nawaomba wanaharakati kusimamia na kusaidia kujenga mapambano yenye kusudi la kutengeneza Ethiopia huru na ya haki ambayo tutakuwa nayo hivi karibuni.

eng: Sanyiikoo Oromoo pointed out the peaceful nature of the protestors:
swa: Sanyiikoo Oromoo alijaribu kuonesha utulivu wa waandamanaji:

swa: Watu wa Oromo ni wapenda amani.

eng: We are not aggressors.
swa: Sisi sio wachokozi.

eng: The people marched with religions books and green tree leaves to indicate that their rally is not designed for confrontation.
swa: Watu walitembea wakiwa wamebeba vitabu vya dini na matawi mabichi ya miti kuonesha kuwa maandano yao hayakuandaliwa kwa ajili ya mapambano.

eng: Yet they were savagely attacked.
swa: Lakini bado walishambuliwa kinyama.

eng: This week we speak with Global Voices editors Oiwan Lam, Mahsa Alimardani and Nevin Thompson about how politics and censorship are affecting Pokémon Go in Iran, Japan and China.
swa: Juma hili tunazungumza na wahariri wa Global Voices Oiwan Lam, Mahsa Alimardani na Nevin Thompson kuhusiana na siasa na vitendo vya kudhibiti mitandao vinavyoiathiri Pokémon Go katika nchi za Iran, Japan na China.

eng: We also take a look at two stories related to free expression in Timor-Leste and Mexico.
swa: Tunaangazia habari mbili zinazohusiana na uhuru wa habari huko Timor-Leste na Mexico.

eng: This episode features stories by Dalia Kiakilir, Giovanna Salazar, Nevin Thompson, Mahsa Alimardani and Oiwan Lam. Many thanks to all our authors, translators and editors who helped make this possible.
swa: Sehemu hii imewashirikisha Dalia Kiakilir, Giovanna Salazar, Nevin Thompson, Mahsa Alimardani na Oiwan Lam. shukrani nyingi kwa waandishi wetu, watafisri na wahariri waliowezesha kipindi hiki kwenda hewani.

eng: In this episode of The Week That Was at Global Voices, we featured Creative Commons licensed music from the Free Music Archive, including Please Listen Carefully by Jahzzar; Parade Shoes by Blue Dot Sessions; Mobile also by Blue Dot Sessions; Falcon Hood by Podington Bear; and Another Brick in the Wall (live) by Montana Skies.
swa: Katika kipidni hiki cha Yaliyotokea Wiki Hii Global Voices, tunakupatia muziki wenye leseni ya Creative Commons kutoka Maktaba ya mtandaoni ya Free Music, ikiwa ni pamoja na Please Listen Carefully wa Jahzzar; Parade Shoes wa Blue Dot Sessions; Mobile wa Blue Dot Sessions; Falcon Hood wa Podington Bear; and Another Brick in the Wall (uliorekodiwa moja kwa moja) na Montana Skies.

eng: Biblioburros, a mobile library in Colombia.
swa: Biblioburros, Maktaba tembezi nchini Colombia.

swa: Image: Acción Visual / Diana Arias / Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 3.0).

eng: What would the world be without the wit and inventiveness of all those who see what goes on and wonder what can they do to improve it?
swa: Dunia ingekuwaje kama kusingekuwa na hali ya utayari na ubunifu miongoni mwa wale wanaoona mambo yanavyokwenda na kisha kutafakari wanaweza kufanya nini ili kuboresha?

eng: What would the world be without teachers?
swa: Ulimwengu ungekuwaje kama kusingekuwa na walimu?

eng: Luis Soriano, a Colombian elementary school teacher born in Nueva Granada, understands the value of education.
swa: Luis Soriano, mwalimu wa shule ya sekondari na raia wa Colombia aliyezaliwa huko Nueva Granada, anatambua thamani ya elimu.

eng: He was raised in a community in the municipality of La Gloria, in the department of Cesar.
swa: Amekulia kwenye jamii ya manispaa ya La Gloria, wilaya ya Cesar.

eng: Soriano graduated with a diploma in Spanish literature, thanks to a professor who visited his village twice a month.
swa: Soriano alipata elimu ya stashahada ya Fasihi ya Lugha ya Kihispania, shukrani zimwendee Profesa aliyekuwa akizuru kijijini kwake kila baada ya miezi miwili.

eng: Personally aware of reading's importance, Soriano is doing what he can to make sure books reach children where they might not otherwise.
swa: Akiwa anatambua umuhimu wa kujisomea, Soriano anafanya kila juhudi ili kuhakikisha kuwa vitabu vinawafikia watoto hata pale ambapo katika hali ya kawaida wasingeweza kuvipata.

eng: “Biblioburros” (literally “Donkey Library”) is a mobile library that distributes books around Northern Colombia on the back of two donkeys named Alfa and Beto, whose names together form the word alfabeto, or “alphabet” in Spanish.
swa: “Biblioburros” (kwa maana nyingine “Punda Maktaba”) ni maktaba tembezi inayosambaza vitabu katika maeneo mbalimbali ya Kaskazini mwa Colombia kwa punda kuvibeba migongoni mwao, punda wanaojulikana kwa majina ya Alfa na Beto, ambapo majina yao kwa pamoja yanaunda neno alfabeto, au “herufi” kwa lugha ya Kihispania.

eng: And one more thing: they are the “wisest donkeys in the world,” according to blog Narrative Journalism in Latin America:
swa: Na jambo jingine zaidi: hawa ndio “ punda walio na akili kuliko wengine wote duniani,” kwa mujibu wa blogu ya Narrative Journalism ya Marekani ya Kusini:

eng: In 1997, had an idea that many considered wonderful, but for others was simply crazy: he decided on his own to load the back of two donkeys with 70 math, literature, geography, and history books.
swa: Mwaka 1997, alikuwa na wazo ambalo wengi walilifurahia pamoja na kuwa kuna baadhi waliona kama ni uwendawazimu: kwa utashi wake aliamua kuwabebesha punda wawili vitabu 70 vya hisabati, fasihi, Jiografia, na historia.

eng: His goal?
swa: Lengo lake lilikuwa nini?

eng: Take them to several poor children located in remote areas of his township.
swa: Lengo lilikuwa kuwafikishia vitabu watoto masikini wanaoishi maeneo ya mbali sana na mji.

eng: Luis Soriano has enjoyed reading since childhood—a passion he says he owes to his aunt, with whom he discovered a memorable poem by the Nicaraguan poet Rubén Darío:
swa: Luis Soriano amekuwa akifurahia kujisomea tangu alipokuwa mdogo-tabia aliyoipata kutoka kwa shangazi yake, ambaye kupitia yeye alifahamu kuhusu shairi la kihistoria lililoandikwa na mtunzi wa mashairi raia wa Nicaragua Rubén Darío:

eng: No doubt about it, Soriano is a Colombian Quixote who went crazy, just as the Knight of the Sad Figure, with books.
swa: Hakuna shaka katika hili, Soriano ni mfalme wa riwaya aliye na mapenzi yaliyopitiliza, ni kama ilivyo kwa Don Quixote, kwa usomaji wa vitabu.

eng: When his aunt read him "Margarita how sad the sea is," he couldn't sleep for eight days.
swa: Wakati shangazi yake alipomsomea "Margarita,namna bahari ilivyotulia," hakuweza kulala kwa siku nane.

eng: He was four years old and if he couldn't foresee it by then, at least he intuited his life would be intimately linked to literature.
swa: Kwa wakati huo alikuwa na umri wa miaka minne na kama kwa wakati huo hakuweza kuona kipaji chake, angalao aliweza kuwa na utambuzi kuwa katika siku zijazo angalijikita kwenye fasihi.

eng: Soriano recently spoke to CCN.com, listing some of the motivations for his Biblioburros project.
swa: Hivi karibuni, Soriano aliongea na tovuti ya CCN.com, huku akitaja baadhi ya mambo yanayomhamasisha kwenye mradi wake wa Punda Maktaba.

eng: According to the website:
swa: Kwa mujibu wa tovuti hii:

eng: In regions, a child must walk or ride a donkey for up to 40 minutes to reach the closest schools.
swa: Maeneo ya vijijini, mtoto ni lazima atembee au apande punda kwa takribani dakika 40 ili kufika katika shule ya karibu.

eng: The children have very few opportunities to go to secondary school.
swa: Watoto wana nafasi ndogo sana ya kuendelea na masomo ya sekondari. .

eng: There are teachers that would like to teach in the countryside.
swa: Pia, ni walimu wachache sana ambao wangependa kufundisha katika maeneo haya ya vijijini.

eng: While crusading against illiteracy in a war-weary hinterland, Soriano is keen to expand his meager English-language book collection.
swa: Akiwa katika jitihada yake ya kufa na kupona ya kufuta ujinga katika maeneo ya vijijini, Soriano anatazamia kukuza zaidi mradi wa vitabu vya kiingereza ambavyo kwa sasa ni vichache mno.

eng: Understanding the importance of bilingualism in a country that increasingly is connected to the outside world through digital and print, he feels passionately that rural children should have greater access to words written in the world’s most widely-spoken language.
swa: Kwa kutambua umuhimu wa kufahamu lugha zaidi ya moja kwenye nchi ambayo siku hadi siku inazidi kuunganishwa na mataifa mengine kupitia njia za kidigitali na machapisho, anaona ni muhimu sana kwa watoto wa vijijini kujisomea maandiko yaliyo katika lugha inayotumika kwa kiasi kikubwa kabisa duniani.

eng: The video below shows Luis Soriano in action, highlighting the difficulties of obtaining books in some areas.
swa: Video hapa chini inamuonesha Luis Soriano akiwa kazini, akibainisha ugumu anaokabiliana nao wa kupata vitabu katika maeneo mbalimbali.

eng: That, of course, is where he and his donkeys come in.
swa: Hata hivyo, hapa ndipo umuhimu wake na punda wake unapoonekana.

eng: I have 3,480 books stored in boxes, stuck in shelves, in boxes, and in small boxes.
swa: Nina vitabu 3,480 vilivyohifadhiwa kwenye maboksi, kupangwa kwenye rafu ana kwenye viboksi vidogo.

eng: I also have them at my friends' places, otherwise there wouldn't be any space for me, or for the books.
swa: Vingine nimeviombea kwa rafiki zangu, vinginevyo, kusingalipatikana nafasi ya ziada kwa ajili yangu wala ya vitabu.

eng: Alfa is actually the one carrying all the library, we have 120 titles in these bookshelves for rural areas for children to enjoy.
swa: Alfa ndiye punda anayebeba vitabu vyote, tuna takribani vitabu 120 kwa ajili ya watoto wa vijijini kujisomea.

eng: We do tours of 3, 4, 5, even 11 hours.
swa: Tunafunga safari kwa masaa 3, 4, 5, na hata masaa 11.

eng: That's 8 hours riding a donkey.
swa: Hii ina maana kuwa, kuna masaa 8 ya kupanda punda.

eng: This is lifetime commitment—to feel useful to the society to which I belong.
swa: Hili ni jukumu langu la kudumu na la manufaa la kuitumikia jamii yangu.

swa: Siku moja, Mwalimu Luis aliamua kuwatwika vitabu punda wake, Alfa na Beto na kisha kuvipeleka vitabu hivyo hadi maeneo ya vijijini kwa ajili ya watoto ambao hawakuwa na uwezo wa kuvipata vitabu hivyo.

eng: Since then, he's gone through the country with his mobile library.
swa: Tangu wakati huo, amekuwa akipita maeneo mbalimbali ya nchi na maktaba yake tembezi.

swa: Vyungu vyenye miguu mitatu vinavyotumika zaidi Botswana.
