eng: At least 65 civil society organizations (CSOs) and non-government organizations (NGOs) from across the world have already signed a unity statement urging the Cambodian government to release land rights activist Tep Vanny, who has been in detention for the past 12 months.
swa: Angalau Asasi za kiraia 65 (CSOs) na mashirika yasiyo ya kiserikali (NGOs) kutoka duniani kote yametia saini tamko la pamoja likiitaka serikali ya Cambodia kumwachia huru mwanaharakati wa haki za ardhi Tep Vanny, ambaye amekuwa kizuizini kwa miezi 12.

eng: Tep Vanny is a prominent human rights activist who has been campaigning on behalf of marginalized farmers and displaced small landholders in Cambodia.
swa: Tep Vanny ni mwanaharakati wa haki za binadamu maarufu ambaye amekuwa akifanya kampeni kwa niaba ya wakulima wadogo na wamiliki wa ardhi waliondolewa katika maeneo yao nchini Cambodia.

eng: She was arrested last August 2016 for leading the ‘Black Monday’ protest which was organized to call for the release of five human rights defenders accused of interfering in a government case involving an opposition leader.
swa: Alikamatwa Agosti 2016 kwa kuongoza maandamano ya ‘Jumatatu Nyeusi’ yaliyoandaliwa kwa ajili ya kudai kuachiliwa huru kwa wanaharakati wa haki za binadamu watano wanaotuhumiwa kwa kuingilia kesi ya serikali inayowahusu viongozi wa upinzani.

eng: The court convicted Tep Vanny of “insulting a public official” and sentenced her to six days in prison.
swa: Mahakama ilimuhukumu Tep Vanny kwa kosa la “kutukana viongozi wa umma” kifungo cha siku sita gerezani.

eng: But during her detention, the government revived a 2013 case against her when she led a protest in front of the prime minister’s house over the eviction of Boeung Kak Lake residents.
swa: Lakini akiwa kifungoni serikali ilifufua kesi yake ya 2013 alipoongoza maandamano mbele ya nyumba ya waziri mkuu akipinga kuondolewa kwa wakazi wa ziwa Boeung Kak.

eng: A government reclamation project in Boeung Kak Lake, located in the capital city of Phnom Penh, has displaced thousands of residents living around the area.
swa: Mradi wa serikali wa kuendeleza eneo la ziwa Boeung Kak, lililo katika mji wa Phnom Penh, umewahamisha maelfu ya wakazi waliokuwa wanaishi katika eneo hilo.

eng: On February 23, 2017, Tep Vanny was found guilty of committing “intentional violence with aggravating circumstances” during the 2013 protest, and she received a prison sentence of two years and six months.
swa: Hapo Februari 23, 2017, Tep Vanny alikutwa na hatia kwa kufanya “kosa kwa kukusudia la kuchochea hali hiyo” wakati wa maandamano ya 2013 na amehukumiwa kifungo cha miaka miwili na miezi sita gerezani.

eng: On August 8, 2017, the court affirmed the decision to convict Tep Vanny.
swa: Hapo Agosti 8, 2017, mahakama ilithibitisha uamuzi wa kumtia hatiani Tep Vanny.

eng: It was also reported that Tep Vanny could face a third trial for another revived case related to a 2011 protest in a Boeung Kak Lake community.
swa: Pia iliripotiwa kuwa Tep Vanny anaweza kukutana na shtaka la tatu kwa kufufuliwa kwa kesi nyingine inayohusiana na maandamano ya jamii ya Ziwa Boeung Kak hapo 2011.

eng: “Even though I am in jail, I am handcuffed and I am wearing prison uniform, the reality is that I am forever innocent.” #FreeTepVanny https://t.co/PCXixwZSFR — Lorenzo Urbinati (@LorUrb) August 15, 2017
swa: “Hata kama niko gerezani, nimefungwa pingu na ninavaa sare ya gerezani, ukweli ni kwamba sina makosa milele” #FreeTepVanny https://t.co/PCXixwZSFR — Lorenzo Urbinati (@LorUrb) August 15, 2017

eng: Tep Vanny’s prolonged detention is seen by some activists as part of a government plan to silence the opposition and spread fear among the people in time for the 2018 general elections.
swa: Kuongezeka kwa muda wa Tep Vanny kuwa kizuizini kunaonwa na baadhi ya wanaharakati kama sehemu ya mpango wa serikali kunyamazisha wapinzani na kueneza hofu miongoni mwa watu kuelekea uchaguzi mkuu hapo 2018.

eng: Cambodia’s ruling party has been in power for the past three decades, but it lost a significant number of seats in the 2013 elections.
swa: Chama tawala cha Cambodia kimekuwa madarakani kwa miongo mitatu sasa, lakini kilipoteza idadi kubwa ya viti katika uchaguzi wa 2013.

eng: The joint statement signed by 65 CSOs and NGOs warned that Tep Vanny’s detention “contributes to creating an atmosphere of fear for human rights defenders throughout Cambodia.”
swa: Tamko la pamoja lililosainiwa na asasi za kiraia na mashirika yasiyo ya kiserikali (CSOs naNGOs) limeonya kuwa kizuizi cha Tep Vanny “kimechangia hali ya hofu kwa wanaharakati wa haki za binadamu Cambodia yote.”

eng: It also emphasized that dissent and peaceful activism should not be criminalized:
swa: Pia limesisitiza kuwa upinzani na harakati za amani zisifanywe kuwa ni uhalifu:

eng: As a result of her imprisonment, Tep Vanny is prevented from carrying out her peaceful and valuable work as a woman human rights defender.
swa: Kama matokeo ya kufungwa kwake, Tep Vanny anazuiwa kufanya kazi yake ya amani na ya thamani kama mwanamke mpigania haki za binadamu.

eng: Peaceful protest and expressions of dissent are not a crime, and human rights defenders should not be penalized for the exercise of their human rights.
swa: Maandamano ya amani na matamko ya upinzani sio uhalifu, na wapigania haki za binadamu wasifungwe kwa kutumia haki zao za binadamu.

eng: The Asian Forum for Human Rights and Development noted that Tep Vanny’s trial violated international norms:
swa: Jukwaa la Haki za Binadamu na Maendeleo la Asia limekumbusha kuwa mashtaka ya Tep Vanny yamekiuka taratibu za kimataifa:

eng: The fabricated charges against Tep Vanny and her arbitrary detention are politically motivated attempts to silence and restrict her activism as a human rights defender.
swa: Mashtaka yaliyotengenezwa dhidi ya Tep Vanny na kizuizi holela ni majaribio yaliyochochewa kisiasa kunyamazisha na kumzuia harakati zake kama mpigania haki za binadamu.

eng: The trial itself did not meet international standards for a fair trial.
swa: Kesi yenyewe haikufikia vigezo vya kimataifa vya mashtaka ya haki.

eng: Aside from local human rights groups, activists and residents in Boeung Kak Lake have been petitioning the offices of UN agencies and various embassies in Cambodia to seek help in pressuring the Cambodian government to release Tep Vanny.
swa: Pamoja na vikundi vya haki za binadamu vya nyumbani, wanaharakati na wakazi wa ziwa Boeung Kak wamekuwa wakiomba ofisi za mashirika ya Umoja wa Mataifa na balozi mbalimbali nchini Cambodia kuishurutisha serikali imwachie huru Tep Vanny.

eng: Cambodian social media users are also encouraged to replace their profile photos with icons of the campaign.
swa: Watumiaji wa mitandao ya jamii nchini Cambodia pia wamehamasishwa kuweka picha za alama ya kampeni katika kurasa zao mtandaoni. .

eng: A table showing the new Kazakh alphabet, as published on the presidential website.
swa: A table showing the new Kazakh alphabet, as published on the presidential website.

eng: A website in Kazakhstan is showing users how their names will look in a new Latin alphabet expected to come into force by 2022.
swa: Tovuti ya kikazakhstan inaonyesha watumiaji jinsi majina yao yataonekana kwa alfabeti mpya za kilatini ambazo zitaanzakutumika mwaka 2022.

eng: Many have reacted with dismay after finding their names laced with apostrophes.
swa: Wengi wameshangazwa baada ya majina yao kuwa na apostrofi.

eng: As an article in the Economist explained, there were reasons for avoiding other, less punctuated versions of the Latin alphabet, such as the one initially floated: Delighted critics pointed out that the rendering of the Kazakh word for carrot in that alphabet would have been saebiz, which looks a bit like a transliteration of the Russian for “f**k off”.
swa: Wakosoaji wanadai kwamba kutumia neno Kazakh kumaanisha karoti isingekuwa sahihi, kwa sababu inaonekana kufanana na neno la ki-Rusi lenye kumaanisha matusi.

eng: The Russian government-run outlet Sputnik noted that even in the latest iteration, there are plenty of words that might look rude to people with a knowledge of Russian.
swa: Serikali ya kirusi imeeleza kuwa mabadiliko haya yatakua na maneno ambayo yanaweza kuwakwaza watu wengi wenye ujuzi wa kirusi.

eng: Such quirks are perhaps inevitable, and Cyrillic will still be the alphabet of choice for millions of Russian-speakers across the country.
swa: Pengine baadhi ya mabadiliko hayo hayakwepeki, na alfabeti za Kicyril zitabakia kama chaguo la mamilioni ya waongeaji wa kirusi nchini humo.

eng: But the issue of apostrophe proliferation in Kazakh remains pertinent.
swa: Lakini suala la uenezi wa apostrofi kwa kikazagh linafaa kubakia.

eng: So Nazarbayev said it’s time to accept latest version of Latin KZ alphabet.
swa: Kwa jiyo Nazarbayev alisema ni wakati wa kukubaliana na toleo jipya la alfabeti za KZ.

eng: To get an idea of what is bothering Kazakhs, Global Voices ran ourselves through the Latin-Cyrillic-Kazakh Latin alphabet treadmill to see how we looked when we came out the other side.
swa: Haijakaa vizuri na ina apostrofi. Ili kupata wazo la kinachowatisha wakazakh, Global Voices tukajiingiza kwenye kilatini-kicyril-kikazakh kilatini alfabeti ili kuona jinsi kama tungetokea kwenye upande mwingine.

eng: The methodology is simple.
swa: Njia ni rahisi.

eng: First imagine how your current name would have appeared on a birth certificate if you had been born in Kazakhstan, which was part of the Soviet Union before 1991.
swa: Kwanza fikiria jina lako litaonekanaje kwenye cheti chako cha kuzaliwa kama ungezaliwa Kazakhstan, ambayo ni sehemu ya muungano wa kisoveti kabla ya mwaka 1991.

eng: To do this, use a Latin to Cyrillic converter such as the one available on the Lexilogos "multilingual keyboard".
swa: Kufanya hivyo, tumia kibadikishaji cha kilatini kwenda kicyril kama kinachopatikana kwenye kibodi ya lugha nyingi. Kisha tumia kibadilishi cha Lexilogos "multilingual keyboard".

eng: Then use the Cyrillic to Kazakh Latin converter in order to find out how many apostrophes your name collects.
swa: Then use the Cyrillic kicyril kwenda kilatini cha kikazakh ili kujua jina lako litakua na apostrofi ngapi. Juan Tadeo, mwenye mamlaka ya mambo yote yanayotokea Mexico atakua Хуан Тадео kwa kicyril.

eng: Juan Tadeo, our authority on all things Mexico would be Хуан Тадео in Cyrillic.
swa: Lakini kwa kilatini cha kikazakh atakua Hy'an Tadeo, apostrofi moja kama ladha ya kichina.

eng: But in Kazakh Latin his name becomes Hy'an Tadeo, a single apostrophe effort with a somewhat Chinese flavour.
swa: Apostrofi zikapata mashiko pale ambapo Mkurugenzi Mtendaji wa Global Voices Georgia Popplewell, au Djordji'i'a Poppely'ell alipojiunga.

eng: The apostrophes begin to really take over when Global Voices Managing Director Georgia Popplewell, or Djordji'i'a Poppely'ell gets involved.
swa: Na zikafika hadi Uganda kwaPrudence Nyamishana (Pry'dence Ni'ami's'ana).

eng: And they go through the roof for our Uganda hand Prudence Nyamishana (Pry'dence Ni'ami's'ana). Curiously, however, our Global Voices Lingua director Mohamed ElGohary comes through the Alphabet Soup completely unscathed.
swa: Ukiwa na maswali, hata hivyo, Mkurugenzi wetu wa Lingua wa Global Voices Mohamed ElGohary Hata hivyo cha ajabu, Mkrugenzi wa Global Voices Lingua Mohamed ElGohary nae akaingia kwenye supu ya alfabeti bila kujitambua.

eng: It seems he is our translations chief for a reason...
swa: Inaonekana kuna sababu ya yeye kuwa mkuu wetu wa tafsiri...

eng: Murdered Mexican Journalist Cándido Ríos: 'Our Weapons Do Not Shoot Bullets.
swa: Mwanahabari wa Mexico Aliyeuawa Cándido Ríos: 'Silaha Zetu Hazirushi Risasi.

eng: Cándido Ríos Vázquez.
swa: Cándido Ríos Vázquez.

eng: Photo widely shared in Twitter.
swa: Picha iliyotumiwa kwa wingi huko Twitter.

eng: Mexican journalist Cándido Ríos, also known by locals and colleagues as “Pavuche,” was murdered on August 22, 2017, in a gun attack in Hueyapan de Ocampo, Veracruz, on Mexico's east coast, according to local sources.
swa: Mwanahabari wa Mexico Cándido Ríos, ambaye anafahamika kwa wenzake na watu wa kwao kama “Pavuche,” aliuawa hapo Agosti 22, 2017, katika shambulio la risasi huko Hueyapan de Ocampo, Veracruz, katika pwani ya mashariki ya Mexico, kulingana na vyanzo vya nyumbani.

eng: Independent news outlet Animal Político gave more details about his death:
swa: Chazo huru cha habari Animal Político kilitoa taarifa zaidi kuhusu kifo chake:

eng: Ríos, known as "Pavuche" among his colleagues, died while being transported to the hospital after having been wounded with a firearm of high caliber, sources familiar with the case told AFP.
swa: Ríos, anayefahamika kama "Pavuche" miongoni mwa wenzake, amefariki wakati akisafirishwa kwenda hospitali baada ya kujeruhiwa kwa risasi AFP.

eng: Ríos' name joins the list of journalists who have been murdered in Mexico this year, which includes Salvador Adame, Miroslava Breach and Javier Valdez.
swa: Jina la Ríos linaungana na orodha ya wanahabari ambao wameshauawa nchini Mexico mwaka huu ambayo ni pamoja na Salvador Adame, Miroslava Breach na Javier Valdez.

eng: According to freedom of expression advocacy group Article 19, Ríos is the ninth journalist assassinated in the country in 2017.
swa: Kulingana na kikundi cha kutetea uhuru wa kujieleza Article 19, Ríos ni mwanahabari wa tisa aliyeuawa nchini kwa mwaka 2017.

eng: Ríos was the founder of the weekly newspaper La Voz de Hueyapan and had reported for local newspaper Diario Acayucan for over 10 years.
swa: Ríos alikuwa mwanzilishi wa gazeti la kila juma La Voz de Hueyapan na alikuwa akiripotia gazeti la nyumbani Diario Acayucan kwa miaka kumi.

eng: His work included coverage of corruption and police.
swa: Kazi yake ilikuwa inajumuisha kuandika habari za polisi na rushwa.

eng: Animal Político pointed out:
swa: Animal Político walitaarifu:

eng: The journalist was known for his career as a crime reporter and for having conflicts with some former town mayors in the region due to his work.
swa: Mwanahabari huyu alifahamika katika kazi yake kama mwandishi wa habari za uhalifu na kwa kuwa na migogoro na baadhi ya mameya waliopita wa mji katika ukanda huo kutokana na kazi yake.

eng: Here’s to remember Cándido Ríos: "Our weapons don't shoot bullets, they shoot truth."
swa: Hii ni kwa kumkumbuka Cándido Ríos: "Silaha zetu hazirushi risasi, zinarusha ukweli."

eng: Journalist who was shot to death in Veracruz.
swa: Wanahabari waliouawa kwa risasi huko Veracruz.

eng: Shockingly, Ríos was under the local authorities' protection after he had received threats to his life over to his journalistic work.
swa: Cha kushitua ni kwamba Ríos alikuwa chini ya ulinzi wa mamlaka za mji baada ya kupokea vitisho dhidi ya maisha yake kwa kazi yake ya uhabarishaji.

eng: Newspaper La Jornada reported:
swa: Gazeti La Jornada limeripoti:

eng: Jorge Morales, from the State’s Commission to Serve and Protect Journalists, reported that Cándido Ríos had filed several complaints against some of the region's political figures for aggressions against his person.
swa: Jorge Morales, kutoka Tume ya Kulinda Wanahabari aliripoti kuwa Cándido Ríos alitoa malalamiko kadhaa dhidi ya wanasiasa wa ukanda huo kwa kutishia maisha yake.

eng: News site Huffington Post elaborated:
swa: Kituo cha Habari Huffington Post kilielezea:

eng: His tireless efforts to denounce injustice brought him popularity among readers, but also enemies like the former mayor of Ríos' hometown Hueyapan, who threatened him with death several times, said his former colleague Cecilio Perez, director of Diario de Acayucan.
swa: Jitihada zake zisizokoma kukemea udhalimu vilimletea umaarufu miongoni mwa wasomaji, lakini pia maadui kama vile Meya wa zamani wa Hueyapanal, mji wa nyumbani kwao Ríos' ambaye alimtishia kumuua mara kadhaa alisema mfanyakazi mwenza wa zamani Cecilio Perez, mkurugenzi wa Diario de Acayucan.

eng: Meanwhile, news portal MX Politico shared his picture on Twitter:
swa: Wakati huo huo, chanzo cha habari MX Politico kilishea picha zake huko Twitter:

eng: Cándido Ríos, the journalist who was murdered in Veracruz, warned everyone that he was going to be assassinated
swa: Cándido Ríos, mwanahabari aliyeuawa huko Veracruz alimweleza kila mmoja kuwa ataenda kuuawa

eng: Traditional media outlets in the country have provided minimal coverage to Ríos’ murder.
swa: Vyombo vya habari nchini viliripoti kidogo sana kuhusu mauaji ya Ríos’.

eng: Some have published different versions about the reasons behind his assassination.
swa: Vingine vilitoa taarifa zenye matoleo tofauti tofauti ya sababu za kuuawa kwakwe.

eng: Online national news outlet Milenio highlighted a comment from a Mexican government official who stated that Ríos was not the target of the attack in which he died:
swa: Chanzo cha habari za mitandaoni Milenio kilionesha maoni kutoka kwa afisa wa serikali ya Mexico aliyesema kuwa Ríos hakuwa mlengwa katika tukio alilouawa:

eng: Journalist Cándido Ríos Vázquez was not the target of the attack in which he and two other people died at a gas station in Hueyapan de Ocampo, Veracruz, said Roberto Campa Cifrian, deputy secretary of the Human Rights of Secretariat of the Interior.
swa: Mwanahabari Cándido Ríos Vázquez hakuwa mlengwa wa shambulio ambalo yeye na watu wengine wawili waliuawa katika kituo cha mafuta huko Hueyapan de Ocampo, Veracruz, alisema Roberto Campa Cifrian, Naibu Katibu wa Sekretarieti ya Mambo ya Ndani na Haki za Binadamu.

eng: Jaqueline Dorantes shared the following message among her followers:
swa: Jaqueline Dorantes alishirikisha ujumbe ufuatao kwa mashabiki wake:

eng: Cándido Ríos was the only journalist in Hueyapan
swa: Cándido Ríos alikuwa ndiye mwanahabari pekee Hueyapan

eng: Mexico has become an incredibly dangerous place to work for journalists, who are often threatened or assaulted for doing their job.
swa: Mexico imekuwa sehemu hatari zaidi kwa wanahabari kufanya kazi, ambapo hutishiwa au kukamatwa wakifanya kazi zao.

eng: Follow our special coverage about the several crimes against journalism in Mexico, and the impunity that surrounds these cases.
swa: Fuatilia taarifa yetu maalum kuhusu matukio kadhaa ya uhalifu dhidi ya wanahabari nchini Mexico na ukatili uliuzingira matukio haya.

eng: What Happens at Maekelawi?
swa: Kipi Kinajiri Maekelawi?

eng: All members of Zone9 in Addis Ababa, 2012.
swa: Wanachama wote wa Zone9 wakiwa Addis Ababa, 2012.

eng: From left to right: Natnael, Abel, Befeqadu, Mahlet, Zelalem and Atnaf.
swa: Kutoka kushoto kwenda kulia: Natnael, Abel, Befeqadu, Mahlet, Zelalem na Atnaf.

eng: This week, Ethiopian Prime Minister Hailemariam Desalegn announced that Maekelawi, one of the country's most famous detention centers, will soon close.
swa: Wiki hii, Waziri Mkuu wa Ethiopia, Hailemariam Desalegn alitangaza kuwa Maekelawi, ambacho ni moja ya vituo maarufu vya kushikilia watuhumiwa wa makosa mbalimbali, hivi karibuni kitaweza kufungwa.

eng: This brought a mix of emotions to the many Ethiopians who have survived the notoriously brutal interrogation practices used at Maekelawi.
swa: Hatua hii imeibua hisia mbalimbali miongoni mwa raia wengi wa Ethiopia walioshuhudia vitendo vya mahojiano yanayoambatana na mateso makali walivyovishuhudia walipokuwepo Maekelawi.

eng: Among them is Global Voices author and human rights blogger Befeqadu Hailu.
swa: Miongoni mwao ni mwandishi wa Global Voices na mwanablogu wa haki za binadamu Befeqadu Hailu.

eng: In 2014, Befeqadu was arrested along with eight of his blogger and journalist colleagues, all due to their participation in a collective blog known as Zone9, where they wrote about their government's obligations to human rights and constitutional law.
swa: Mwaka 2014, Befeqadu alikamatwa sambamba na waandishi na wanablogu wenzake kwa sababu ya ushiriki wao wa pamoja wa kuendesha blogu inayofahamika kama Zone9, jukwaa walilolitumia kuandika maoni yao kuhusu wajibu wa serikali kwenye haki za binadamu na utawala wa sheria.

eng: The nine writers were detained and held in Maekelawi without charge for nearly twelve weeks in 2014, before being charged under the country's Anti-Terrorism Proclamation.
swa: Waandishi hawa tisa walishikiliwa huko Maekelawi bila ya kufunguliwa mashitaka yoyote kwa takribani wiki 12 mwaka 2014, kabla ya kushitakiwa kwa sheria ya nchi ya kukabiliana na Ugaidi.

eng: Befeqadu later wrote a first-hand account of his experience in the detention center, which we share here in an effort to shed light on the harsh reality of Maekelawi under Ethiopia's current government.
swa: Baadae Befeqadu aliandika alitoa maelezo yake mwenyewe ya uzoefu wa kushikiliwa kwenye kituo hiki, maelezo tunayoyaweka hapa kama namna ya kutupia jicho hali ya ukweli wa mateso ya Maekelewi, kituo kinachoendeshwa na serikali ya sasa ya Ethiopia.

eng: In an August 2014 letter delivered to Global Voices by the bloggers' lawyers, Befeqadu wrote:
swa: Mapema mwezi Agosti 2014 barua iliyowasilishwa Global Voices na wanasheria wa mwanablogu huyu, Befeqadu aliandika:

eng: The idea of setting a foot in the compound of the ill-famed Maekelawi detention center gives a cold shiver to anyone who knows its history.
swa: Wazo la kutia mguu kwenye eneo la mateso makali la Kituo cha Ushikiliaji cha Maekelewi kinaweza kusababisha homa ya baridi kali kwa yeyote anayefahamu historia yake.

eng: But my sheer optimism and trust that the brutal and inhumane treatment of people was a distant memory saved me from trembling as I was escorted into the compound.
swa: Hata hivyo, imani yangu thabiti na ukweli kuwa mateso makali na udhalilishaji wa utu wa watu ilikuwa ni kumbukumbu ya muda mrefu iliyonisaidia kutokuogopa pale nilipokuwa nikisindikizwa katika viunga vya Maekelawi.

eng: The same was true of my friends, I suppose.
swa: Hali ilikuwa vivyohivyo hata kwa marafiki zangu, bila shaka.

eng: What is more, we had nothing to be scared of, because we are neither undercover agents nor members of armed forces.
swa: Kingine ni kuwa, hatukuwa na cha kuogopa, kwa kuwa hatukuwa mashushushu wala wanajeshi.

eng: We are just writers.
swa: Tulikuwa waandishi tu.

eng: But as soon as I arrived at Maekelawi, detainees informed me that I had been placed in one of the notorious sections of the detention center, known as “Siberia”.
swa: Hata hivyo, mara tu baada ya kuwasili Maekelawi, watu wengine walioshikiliwa walinitaarifu kuwa nimepangwa kwenye moja ya vitengo vyenye utatili mbaya sana wa kituo hiki, kitengo kinachojulikana kama “Siberia”.

eng: In less than a week, I felt like I was living in the middle of an account from the 2013 Human Rights Watch report entitled “They Want a Confession”.
swa: Kwa kipindi cha chini ya wiki moja, nilijisikia kuwa nilikuwa ninayaishi sawia mambo yaliyoelezwa kwenye Ripoti ya Human Rights Watch iliyokuwa na kichwa cha habari, “Wanahitaji Kukiri”.

eng: “They Want a Confession” documents serious human rights abuses, unlawful interrogation tactics, and poor detention conditions in Addis Ababa’s Maekelawi detention center, drawing from interviews with former Maekelawi detainees and their family members. Those detained in Maekelawi include scores of opposition politicians, journalists, protest organizers, and alleged supporters of ethnic insurgencies.
swa: “Wanahitaji Kukiri” inaelezea matukio mabaya ana ya uvunjifu wa haki za binadamu, mbinu sisizo za kisheria za mahojiano, pamoja na mazingira mabaya ya kituo cha kushikilia wahalifu cha Maekelawi kilichopo jijini Adis Ababa, matukio yaliyopatikana kwa kufanya mahojiano na watu waliokuwa wameshikiliwa Maekelawi pamoja na ndugu wa familia zao. dWaliokuwa wanashikiliwa Maekelawi ni pamoja na wanasiasa wa upinzani, waandishi wa habari, waratibu wa maandamano na wale wanaodhaniwa kuwa ni watu wanaounga mkono vitendo vya ugaidi.

eng: Befeqadu described the interrogation methods at Maekelawi as being "more about dominance and submission than confidence or creativity."
swa: Befeqadu alielezea njia za mahojiano huko Maekelawi ni zaidi ya"kutawaliwa na kujishusha kuliko kujiamini na ubunifu."

eng: If they cannot successfully extract information from you in this way, they force confessions by punching, beating, extended physical exercise and flogging, he wrote.
swa:
Kama watashindwa kupata taarifa kutoka kwako kulingana na matarajio yako, wanalazimisha mtu akiri kwa kupigwa ngumi, kuchapwa, kumpatia mtu mazoezi ya muda mrefu sana, anaandika.
I spoke with some detainees who had undergone even more wicked procedures that were clear violations of their privacy.
column3:
Niliongea pia na baadhi ya watu waliokuwa wameshikiliwa na ambao walikabiliana na mambo mabaya sana ambayo dhahiri yalikiuka uhuru wao wa faragha.
Some detainees were forced to strip naked and asked to stand or perform sit-ups until dawn.
column4: Baadhi ya washikiliwa walilazimishwa kuvua nguo zote na kuamrishwa kusimama au kusimama na kuchuchumaa hadi kulipokucha."

eng: He continued, describing how he and his colleagues were forced to confess:
swa: Aliendelea kuelezea namna yeye na wenzake walivyolazimishwa kukiri:

eng: In our case, finally we were made to plead guilty.
swa: Kwenye shauri letu, hatimaye tulilazimishwa kukiri makosa yetu.

eng: We confessed under duress.
swa: Tulikiri kutokana na nguvu kali iliyotumiwa.

eng: We could not bear the ceaseless brutal and psychologically degrading pressure.
swa: Hatukuweza kuvumilia ukatili na kuathiriwa vikali kisaikolojia.

eng: We could not carry on surviving the hell of Maeklawi. We ended up telling our interrogators what they wanted to hear.
swa: Tuliishia kuwaeleza kile walichohitaji kukisikia kutoka kwetu.

eng: To their delight, we added as many self-incriminating phrases as possible.
swa: Kwa faida yao, tuliongeza maneno ya kuonesha makosa yetu kwa kadiri ya ilivyowezekana.

eng: But phrases like “yes, we wanted to incite violence” never pleased them.
swa: Hata hivyo, misemo kama vile "ndio, tulitaka kuhamasisha machafuko", haikuwabariki kabisa.

eng: So they rewrote our confessions to fit their frame.
swa: Kwa hiyo waliandika upya maelezo yetu ili yaendane na matakwa yao.

eng: Some of us tried to explain. Others had to endure beatings.
swa: Baadhi yetu tulijaribu kutoa maelezo na wengine walijaribu kuvumilia vipigo.

eng: But at last we succumbed to the pressure and signed the carefully scripted confession pages, with the exception of our colleague Abel, who refused to sign at that time.
swa: Hatimaye, tulisaliti amri(isipokuwa Abel ambaye kwa wakati huo aligoma kabisa) na kuweka saini kurasa za maelezo zilizoandaliwa kwa umahiri mkubwa.

eng: He has survived the pain he has endured since, and his confession, when finally extracted, is completely untrue, to say nothing of ours.
swa: Alivumilia mateso yote tangu awali, na maelezo yake ambayo hatimaye aliyoyatoa, hayakuwa na ukweli wowote wa kuthibitisha lolote kuhusu sisi.

eng: Now we know that torture is the part of the Maekelawi ceremony that reveals the “truth” of a crime.
swa: Kwa sasa tunafahamu kuwa mateso ni sehemu ya sherehe ya Maekelawi inayotumiwa kufichua "ukweli" wa makosa aliyotuhumiwa nayo mtu.

eng: I had long thought police interrogations were complex, involving sophisticated skills, knowledge and psychological tactics to establish facts.
swa: Kwa kipindi kirefu nilikuwa nikifahamu kuwa mahojiano ya kipolisi ni mchakato mrefu unaohusisha weledi, maarifa na mbinu za kisaikolojia katika kubaini ukweli.

eng: I now know that police interrogations in Maekelawi are not so elaborate.
swa: Kwa sasa nimeelwa kuwa mahojino ya polisi huko Maekelawi hayapo hivi.

eng: In fact they are simple.
swa: Kwanza, polisi wa Maekelawi wapo kawaida kabisa.

eng: They are like machines that produce guilt in the detainees.
swa: Wao ni kama mashine zinazowajengea makosa watu watuhumiwa.

eng: At Maekelawi, the driving principle of police interrogations is that you are guilty unless proven otherwise.
swa: Kwa Maekelawi, msingi mkuu wa mahojiano ya kipolisi ni kuwa una makosa hadi pale itakapothibitishwa vinginevyo.

eng: Your pleas for innocence – or even for explanation – fall on deaf ears.
swa: Unataka kuonesha kuwa huna hatia - au kuomba kutoa ufafanuzi - hakuna anayekusikiliza hasilani.

eng: Befeqadu spent 18 months detained in Ethiopian prisons along his colleagues before they walked free in October 2015.
swa: Befeqadu na wenzake walishikiliwa gerezani kwa miezi 18 kwenye magereza nchini Ethiopia kabla ya kuachiwa huru mapema mwezi Oktoba 2015.

eng: He and his colleagues were acquitted without ever testifying in court.
swa: Yeye pamoja na wenzake walionekana hawakuwa na hatia bila hata ya kupelekwa mahakamani.

eng: Zone9 members rejoiced at the release of Befeqadu Hailu (second from left, in scarf) in October 2015.
swa: Wanablogu wa Zone9 wakifurahia mara baada ya kuachiwa kwa Befeqadu Hailu (wa pili kutoka kushoto aliyevaa skafu) mapema mwezi Oktoba 2015.

eng: Befeqadu also described accounts he had heard from fellow prisoners, who had been brought to Maekelawi after suffering through even worse ordeals at other detention centers in the country.
swa: Pia Befeqadu alielezea maelezo aliyoyasikia kutoka kwa wafungwa wenzake, ambao waliletwa Maekelawi ambao walipitia mateso mengine makali walipokuwa kwenye vituo vingine vya kushikilia watuhumiwa nchini Ethiopia.

eng: These detainees suffered from diabolical barbarity such as forcible extraction of their nails from their fingers, flogging, and hooding, he wrote.
swa: Wahikiliwa hawa walikabiliana na vitendo vibaya sana na vya kidhalimu kama vile kung'olewa kucha, kupigwa, na kufunikwa vichwa, aliandika.

eng: The information extracted from detainees in the unnamed detention center is then verified through more interrogation at the pre-trial detention center. Detainees never know where they were taken for this brutal investigation because they are hooded throughout.
swa: Taarifa zilizopatikana kwa watu wanaoshikiliwa kutoka kwenye vituo vya kushikilia visivyofahamika huhakikiwa kwa kukabiliana na mahojiano zaidi kwenye kituo cha kushikilia cha awali cha Kusikiliza maishauri. watu waliokuwa wanashikiliwa hawakuwa wanafahamu wapi wanapelekwa kwa ajili ya kufanyiwa uchunguzi wa kikatili wa namna hii kwa kuwa wakati wote nyuso zao zilikuwa zinafunikwa.

eng: The unnamed detention centers are like black holes.
swa: Vituo vya kushikiliwa watu visivyofahamika ni kama vile mashimo meusi.

eng: Referencing human rights violations under Derg regime, which Ethiopia's current government is now seeking to distance itself from, Befeqadu compared these experiences to those of the past.
swa: Akirejelea uvunjwaji wa haki za binadamu chini ya Serikali ya Kijeshi, ambayo serikali ya Ethiopia kwa sasa inajitahidi kuepukana nayo, Befeqadu alifananisha uzoefu huu na kipindi kilichopita.

eng: It turns out that the anguish of Ethiopian prisoners, something that appeared to be so distant in memory, is not that far off after all, he said.
swa: Imefahamika kwamba hofu ya wafungwa nchini Ethiopia, kitu ambacho kilishakaribia kufutika kwenye kumbukumbu za watu, kumbe ni nkumbukumbu iliyokaribu kabisa anasema.

eng: Responding to this week's news, Befeqadu wrote on Twitter:
swa: Akitolea ufafanuzi kuhusu habari ya wiki hii, Befeqadu aliandika kwenye Twitter:

eng: PM Hailemariam said, "Maekelawi was a torture house in Derg regime"; it is disappointing.
swa: PM Hailemariam said, "Maekelawi ilikuwa ni nyumba ya mateso wakati wa serikali ya kijeshi; inakatisha tamaa kabisa.

eng: I'm a living victim of that torture chamber under his rule.
swa: Mimi ni mhanga ninayeishi wa niliyepitia mateso kutoka sehemu hii.

eng: Back then, I wished to commit sucide instead of seeing interrogators the next day.
swa: Wakati ule nilitamani hata kujiua badala ya kukutana watu waliokuwa wanatuhoji.

eng: These guys make it difficult to forgive. — BefeQadu Z. Hailu (@befeqe) January 3, 2018
swa: Watu hawa si wa kuwasamehe kabisa. — BefeQadu Z. Hailu (@befeqe) January 3, 2018

eng: Befeqadu and two of his colleagues Atnaf and Natnael are not really free, in the purest sense of the word.
swa: Befeqadu na wenzake wawili Atnaf na Natnael hawapo huru moja kwa moja.

eng: Although their terrorism charges were reversed, they are awaiting decisions on other charges, all of which have been triggered by their peaceful criticism of the ruling government.
swa: Pamoja na kuwa makosa yao ya ugaidi yalifutwa, bado wanasubiria maamuzi kwenye mashtaka yao mengine, ambayo yote yalitokana ukosoaji wao wa serikali kwa njia ya amani

eng: Read More:
swa: Soma zaidi:

eng: Befeqadu's unabridged account of his experience in Maekelawi
swa: Maelezo halisi ya Befeqadu kuhusu mambo aliyokabiliana nayo alipokuwa ameshikiliwa Maekelawi

eng: Global Voices' full coverage of the case of the Zone9 bloggers
swa: Ufuatiliaji wa Kina wa Global Voices kuhusu kesi ya wanablogu wa Zone9

eng: Photo by Lens Young Halabi showing a wall in 2013 with the sentence "we are alive and staying; for the dream we stay".
swa: Picha na Lens Young Halabi ikionesha ukuta mwaka 2013 ukiwa na sentensi "tuko hai na tunabaki; kwa ajili ya ndoto zetu tunabaki".

eng: To all those who will inhabit the places we left….
swa: Kwa wote watakaoishi mahali tulipopaacha....

eng: We once had a revolution there.
swa: Tulishawahi kuwa na mapinduzi hapa.

eng: I never resided in those neighborhoods, but was a visitor, a stranger, with all my little rituals, such as greeting the neighbor on the staircase in the morning, my frantic searches for products that were not customarily sold there, my long, obsessive conversations with taxi drivers in order to gauge their political leanings and their views on checkpoints.
swa: Sijawahi kuishi maeneo hayo ila nilikuwa nayatembelea, mgeni na desturi zangu ndogo dogo kama vile kusalimia majirani kwenye ngazi asubuhi, kutafuta vitu ambavyo haviuzwi hapa kwa kawaida, mazungumzo yangu marefu na madereva taksi, ili kufahamu mlengo wao wa kisiasa na mitazamo yao juu ya vizuizi vya ukaguzi barabarani.

eng: We still have a revolution there, in Bustan Al Qasr.
swa: Bado tuna mapinduzi pale ndani ya Bustan Al Qasr.

eng: There you will see—unless the Barbarians have erased it—a childish sketch of a soldier and a bearded man with a hammer above them and the phrase: “a revolution that will crack heads”.
swa: Pale utayaona—labda kama mafedhuli watakuwa wameyafuta picha ya kitoto ya askari na mwanaume mwenye ndevu na nyundo juu yao na maneno yaliyosema: "Mapinduzi yatakayo vunja vichwa".

eng: This marked the beginning of our second revolution, one against those trying to confiscate our rights by force of weapon or religion.
swa: Huu ulikuwa mwanzo wa mapinduzi yetu ya pili, haya yakiwa dhidi ya wale wanaotaka kubinafsisha haki zetu kwa nguvu ya silaha au dini.

eng: But you probably don’t know about the many revolutions we have had there, painted by Abu Maryam.
swa: Lakini labda haufahamu kuhusu mapinduzi mengi tuliyofanya yaliyochorwa na Abu Maryam.

eng: You would probably not hear our voices as we tell you who Abu Maryam is.
swa: Pengine usingeweza kusikia sauti zetu pale tunapokuambia Abu Maryam ni nani.

eng: We have a revolution there.
swa: Tulikuwa na mapinduzi pale.

eng: They were protesting to open the checkpoint for civilians.
swa: Walikuwa wakiandamana ili kituo kifunguliwe kwa ajili ya raia.

eng: We have a revolution there.
swa: Tulikuwa na mapinduzi pale.

eng: We have a revolution there.
swa: Tulikuwa na mapinduzi pale.

eng: The closest of whom to me was Mustafa.
swa: Wa karibu sana kwangu alikuwa Mustafa.

eng: We opened a school there that held his name.
swa: Tulifungua shule pale iliyopewa jina lake.

eng: It is there too.
swa: Iko pale pia.

eng: The school gave us a reason to go on; we believed we were paying our debts.
swa: Shule ilitupa sababu ya kusonga mbele, tuliamini tulikuwa tunalipa deni letu.

eng: Mustafa’s grave and his school are yours now.
swa: Kaburi la Mustafa na shule yake vimekuwa vyenu sasa.

eng: If you ever pass by them, treat them with dignity, for this man was a wellspring of love, giving and devotion.
swa: Kama mkipita maeneo hayo basi mvitendee kwa heshima kwa sababu mtu huyu alikuwa amejaa upendo, kujitoa na ibada.

eng: We were part of his vision, and we failed.
swa: Tulikuwa sehemu ya maono yake na tumeshindwa.

eng: We have a revolution there.
swa: Tulikuwa na mapinduzi pale.

eng: We often laughed at his faulty grammar.
swa: Mara zote tulicheka ubovu wa sarufi yake.

eng: And when the outbreak of Leishmania occurred, and some of us carried out spraying campaigns, we had our own graffiti which said: “Leishmania over”.
swa: Na vita ilipotokea huko Leishmania na baadhi yetu tulikuwa na kampeni za kunyunyiza, tulikuwa na michoro yetu wenyewe katika kuta ikisema: “Leishmania imekwisha”.

eng: That was how we adapted, that was how we looked for solutions.
swa: Hivyo ndivyo tulivyokabiliana, hivyo ndivyo tulivyotafuta suluhisho.

eng: That is why you will find our schools and our hospitals in basements.
swa: Hiyo ndiyo sababu utakuta shule zetu na hospitali zikiwa kwenye mahandaki.

eng: We were adapting to the bombings.
swa: Tunakabiliana na mabomu.

eng: We were trying to resist.
swa: Tulikuwa tunajaribu kupinga.

eng: We had a revolution there….
swa: Tulikuwa na mapinduzi pale….

eng: The Eye Hospital!
swa: Hospitali ya macho!

eng: There we protested over and over against Sharia Courts.
swa: Pale tuliandamana tena na tena kupinga mahakama za sharia.

eng: There, ISIS murdered 35 of us.
swa: Pale ISIS ilipowaua wenzetu 35.

eng: There, our protests erupted to expel them.
swa: Pale, maandamano yetu yalipolipukuwa ya kuwafukuza.

eng: There I was jailed—don’t swear yet—for there was also where I was released, because we have a revolution there.
swa: Pale, niipofungwa gerezani usilaani kwanza, kwani pale pia ndipo nilipoachiliwa huru kwa sababu tulifanya mapinduzi pale

eng: Turn it back into a hospital.
swa: Rudi pale hospitali.

eng: Not like our underground hospitals, but one for all people.
swa: Sio kama hospitali zetu za kwenye handaki ila moja kwa watu wote.

eng: The place is teeming with spirits that will look after the ill.
swa: Mahali hapa panaungana na roho zitakazowaangalia wagonjwa.

eng: Old Aleppo was our resting place.
swa: Aleppo ya zamani palikuwa mahali pa amani.

eng: There I used to go to sing; we the evil terrorists loved to sing, to love, to cook and at “Falafel House” to eat everything but falafel.
swa: Pale nilizoea kwenda na kuimba, sisi magaidi wadhalimu tulipenda kuimba, kupendana, kupika na kula kila kitu katika “Nyumba ya Falafel ” isipokuwa falafel.

eng: You would be amazed at the piles of rocks.
swa: Ungeshangazwa na mafungu ya mawe.

eng: These were the houses of families, houses that were probably all they had.
swa: Hizi zilikuwa nyumba za familia, nyumba ambazo labda ndicho kitu pekee walikuwa nacho.

eng: They were forced to leave.
swa: Walilazimishwa kuondoka.

eng: Take some time to shed a tear in memory of their memories.
swa: Chukua muda kidogo kuomboleza kwa ajili ya kumbukumbu zao.

eng: You would not recognize it.
swa: Hautautambua tena.

eng: I used to leave for months, but could never get used to the magnitude of the destruction whenever I came back.
swa: Nilizoea kuondoka kwa miezi kadhaa lakini sikuuzoea ukubwa wa uharibifu kila niliporejea.

eng: That was what your neighbors faced, so shedding some tears would do no harm.
swa: Hicho ndicho majirani zako walichopitia hivyo kuomboleza kwa ajili yao haitakuwa na madhara.

eng: You would find, if they allowed, countless bodies under the rubble.
swa: Ungekuta, kama wangeruhusu miili isiyohesabika kwenye vifusi.

eng: It was not our intention to leave our bodies like that without a proper burial.
swa: Haikuwa dhamira yetu kuiacha miili yetu namna ile bila maziko stahiki.

eng: It wasn’t that we were negligent, but the jets were targeting all groups, and it became impossible in the last months to move the vehicles.
swa: Sio kwamba tulipuuzia, lakini ndege za vita zililenga makundi yote na ikawa sio rahisi kwa miezi kadhaa kuendesha gari.

eng: Give them, if you’re ever allowed, a proper burial.
swa: Wapeni maziko stahiki kama mtaruhusiwa.

eng: You will not be allowed to find out their names, for sure, but please don’t just give them random numbers.
swa: Hamtaruhusiwa kuyafahamu majina yao hakika, lakini tafadhali msiwape namba kwa kubahatisha.

eng: Use your imagination and bury them together.
swa: Tumieni hisia zenu na wazikeni pamoja.

eng: Syrian families have been scattered enough, and nobody likes to be buried alone.
swa: Familia za wa-Syria zimetawanyika vya kutosha na hakuna anayependa kuzikwa peke yake.

eng: We have a revolution there.
swa: Tulikuwa na mapinduzi pale.

eng: Curse it, or mourn it.
swa: Waweza kuyalaani au kuyaomboleza.

eng: It is there, in the rocks, in the graves, in the earth and above in the air.
swa: Ni pale katika miamba, ndani ya makaburi, katika ardhi na juu ya anga.

eng: On the wall of a graveyard we once wrote: “We are alive, we will keep going, and the dream will be realized”.
swa: Katika kuta za makaburi tulishawahi kuandika: "Tuko hai, tutaendelea kusonga mbele,na ndoto yetu itaonekana".

eng: Take whatever is left of us and keep on dreaming.
swa: Chukueni kila kilichosalia kwetu na endeleeni kuota.

eng: Soon everything else of yours will be confiscated.
swa: Muda mfupi ujao kila kilicho chenu kitataifishwa

eng: Screenshot of the Radio Garden, an online platform that, since 2016, is enabling listeners to access thousands of radio stations from across the globe.
swa: Picha kificho ya Radio Garden, jukwaa la mtandaoni, ambalo tangu mwka 2016 limekuwa likiwawezesha watu kusikiliza radio mbalimbali kutoka sehemu tofauti ulimwenguni.

eng: There’s a world of sounds out there to explore, and one online project out of the Netherlands lets you do just that.
swa: Kuna sauti za kila namna unazoweza kuzisikiliza duniani kote, na moja wapo ni mradi wa mtandaoni unaopatikana Uholanzi unaokuwezesha kufanya hivyo.

eng: Since late 2016, Radio Garden has since been connecting listeners to an ever-growing list of broadcasts from across the globe.
swa: Tangu mwishoni mwa mwaka 2016, Radio Garden imekuwa ikiwaunganisha wasikilizaji kwenye orodha ya vituo vya redio vinavyoongezeka kwa kasi kutoka sehemu mbalimbali ulimwenguni.

eng: The interface is as simple as its vision: an interactive map composed of green dots that represent different cities.
swa: Usanifu wake ni wa kawaida sana kama unavyoonekana. Ni ramani shirikishi yenye vidoti vya kijani vinavyowakilisha miji mbalimbali.

eng: Click on it, and you'll be tuned into one of the chosen area's radio stations.
swa: Ukibonyeza kwenye kidoti unakuwa umebonyeza kwenye mojawapo ya kituo kati ya vituo vya redio vilivyochaguliwa katika mji huo.

eng: You might stumble upon a news bulletin stream from Tonga; a traditional tune that's soothing its Iranian audience into slumber during the late hours of the night; or one of the few radio stations that continue to fill the airwaves in the Syrian city of Aleppo.
swa: Kwa bahati unaweza ukapata taarifa rasmi ya habari mpya kutoka redio Tonga. Ni redio ya zamani ya Iran inayoburudisha hadhira wakati wa masaa ya usiku ikiwa wamelala. Au unaweza kubahatika kusikiliza moja ya vituo vichache vya redio vinavyoendelea kujaza mawimbi ya sauti katika mji wa Siria wa Aleppo.

eng: Click on the "History" option on Radio Garden to be transported to an important part of a country's radio broadcasting history.
swa: Bofya kwenye sehemu ya "Kumbukumbu" kwenye Radio garden ili upelekwe kwenye sehemu muhimu ya kumbukumbu ya matangazo ya radio ya nchi husika.

eng: Other noteworthy features include a "History" function which showcases a country's traditional music and historic broadcasts; a "Jingles" section that, as its name suggests, offers a glimpse of a city's iconic radio jingles; and a "Story" option that offers first-hand accounts of people's involvement with community radio.
swa: Sifa nyingine nzuri ya redio hii ni pamoja na uwepo wa kipengele cha mziki wa zamani na matangazo ya sauti ya kihistoria; Sehemu ya “sauti za asili” kama jina linavyotanabaisha, inakupa matangazo ya asili ya radio maarufu za jiji, na sehemu ya “simulizi” inayokupa maelezo ya moja kwa moja ya namna watu wanavyojihusisha na radio za jamii.

eng: Once again, all of these will take you to a different part of the world, be it the Taiwanese capital of Taipei or the down-under metropolis that is Sydney, Australia.
swa: Kwa mara nyingine haya yote yatakupeleka sehemu tofauti ulimwenguni, inaweza kuwa ni mji mkuu wa Taiwan wa Taipel au mji mkuu wa Australia, yaani Sydney.

eng: Here's a YouTube video that showcases the Radio.Garden in action:
swa: Hii hapa ni video ya Youtube inayoielezea Radio Garden na namna inavyofanya kazi:

eng: The initiative was masterminded by the Institute for Sound and Vision in the Netherlands, under the direction of Golo Föllmer of the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg.
swa: Mpango huu ulibuniwa na Taasisi ya Matangazo ya Sauti na Picha ya nchini Uholanzi chini ya usimamizi wa Golo Föllmer wa Chuo Kikuu cha Martin Luther cha Halle-Wittenberg.

eng: It relied on the expertise of two local design companies, Studio Puckey and Moniker, who decided that the best way to tackle the task was to create a comprehensive map without borders or city names.
swa: Ubunifu huu ulizingatia utaalam wa makampuni mawili ya nchini humo ambayo ni Studio ya Puckey na Moniker, ambao walikubaliana kuwa namna nzuri ya kufanikisha kazi hii ilikuwa ni kuunda ramani iliyosheni isiyo na mipaka wala kuonesha majina ya miji.

eng: When it originally launch, Radio Garden garnered widespread attention on social media.
swa: Mara tu baada ya kuanzishwa rasmi kwa Radio garden, ilipata umaarufu mkubwa kweye mitandao ya kijamii.

eng: One of its designers, Jonathan Puckey, told The Guardian he was pleasantly surprised by the discussions he had seen about this project:
swa: Mmoja wa wasanifu wake, Jonathan Puckey aliliambia The Guardian kuwa alifurahishwa sana na majadiliano aliyoyashuhudia kuhusiana na mradi huu.

eng: On Reddit, it prompted a really sweet discussion, with people talking about their first contact with radio, or grandparents who had worked in radio during the second world war.
swa: Kwenye mtandao wa Reddit, radio hii iliibua mjadala mzuri sana, ambapo watu waliongelea uzoefu wao walipokutana na radio, au mababu zao waliofanya kazi radioni wakati wa vita ya pili ya dunia.

eng: The project's own Facebook page is also filled with words of encouragement and support, with users from all walks of life giving it rave reviews.
swa: Katika Ukurasa wa Facebook wa mradi huu, kumekuwa pia na maoni ya kutia moyo sana na uungwaji mkono, kwani watumiaji kutoka maeneo mbalimbali wamekuwa wakiweka mapitio yenye kupongeza na kusifia.

eng: Aside from the website, Radio Garden has an app for iOS and Android devices, enabling users to listen to their selected broadcasts at their convenience – even if their smartphones drop into sleep/idle mode.
swa: Mbali na kuwepo kwa tovuti, Radio Garden ina kitumizi cha mfumo endeshi wa iOS na wa fivaa vyaAndroid, hali inayowawezesha watumiaji wake kusikiliza matangazo ya radio kwa uhuru wao- hata kama simu janja zao zitakuwa kwenye hali ya kuzimika kiasi.

eng: A man stands in the street in Stone Town, Zanzibar, checking his phone.
swa: Mwanaume akiwa amesimama katika mtaa wa Mji Mkongwe, Zanzibar, akiperuzi simu yake ya kiganjani.

eng: Photo by Pernille Bærendtsen, used with permission.
swa: Picha ilipigwa na Pernille Bærendtsen na kutumiwa kwa ruhusa yake.

eng: Blogging has been popular in Tanzania for more than a decade, enabling writers and independent journalists to express views and report news that might not otherwise appear in mainstream media.
swa: Kwa zaidi ya muongo mmoja uliopita blogu zimekuwa maarufu nchini Tanzania, zikiwawezesha waandishi na wanahabari wa kujitegemea kutoa maoni yao na kuchapisha habari ambazo, kwa kawaida, zisingeweza kupata nafasi katika vyombo vikuu vya habari.

eng: But as of last month, this kind of work will come with a price tag.
swa: Lakini mpaka kufikia mwezi uliopita, shughuli ya kublogu zitaanza kuambatana na gharama.

eng: On March 16, 2018, the United Republic of Tanzania issued the Electronic and Postal Communications (Online Content) Regulations demanding that bloggers must register and pay over USD $900 per year to publish online.
swa: Tarehe 16 Machi 2018, Jamhuri ya Muungano wa Tanzania ilitangaza Kanuni za Mawasiliano ya Kielektroniki na Posta (Maudhui ya habari za mtandaoni) zinazowataka wanablogu wote kujiandikisha na kulipa zaidi ya dola za Kimarekani 900 ili kuweza kuchapisha habari mtandaoni.

eng: Application 2. These Regulations shall apply to online content including: (a) application services licensees; (b) bloggers; (c) internet cafes; (d) online content hosts; (e) online forums; (f) online radio or television; (g) social media; (h) subscribers and users of online content; and (i) any other related online content.
swa: Kanuni hizi zitahusu maudhui ya habari za mtandaoni pamoja na : (a) maombi ya leseni ya kutoa huduma; (b) Wanablogu; (c) maduka ya kutolea huduma za intaneti; (d) Wamiliki wa maudhui ya habari za mtandaoni; (e) Majukwaa mtandaoni; (f) Matangazo Redio au runinga za mtandaoni; (g) Vyombo vya habari; (h) Wateja na watumiaji wa maudhui ya habari za mtandaoni na; (i) Maudhui yoyote yanayohusu maudhui ya habari za mtandaoni.

eng: The new regulations have far-reaching implications for freedom of expression and human rights.
swa: Kanuni hii mpya ina athari kubwa kwa uhuru wa kujieleza pamoja na haki za binadamu.

eng: Bloggers must fill out official regulatory forms and avoid publishing prohibited content including nudity, hate speech, explicit sex acts, extreme violence, "content that causes annoyance", fake news, and "bad language" among other restrictions.
swa: Wanablogu wanalazimika kujaza fomu rasmi za kutoa huduma na kutakiwa kuepuka kuchapisha maudhui yaliyokatazwa ikiwa ni pamoja na picha za uchi, matamshi ya chuki, picha za ngono, vurugu, "madhui yanayosababisha maudhi", habari za uongo na, "lugha chafu" miongoni mwa makatazo mengine.

eng: The new regulations grant unrestrained power to the Tanzanian Communications Regulatory Authority (TCRA) to prescribe and proscribe.
swa: Sheria mpya inaipa nguvu Mamlaka ya Mawasiliano Tanzania (TCRA) kuruhusu na kufunga huduma.

eng: Under Part II, Number 4, TCRA then has the authority:
swa: Chini ya SEHEMU YA II, Namba 4, TCRA ina mamlaka pia ya:

eng: (a) to keep register of bloggers, online forums, online radio and online television; (b) to take action against non-compliance to these Regulations, including to order removal of prohibited content
swa: (a) kutunza orodha ya wanablogu, majukwaa mtandaoni, Redio na television mtandaoni;(b) Kuchukua hatua dhidi ya wanaovunja sheria hii, pamoja na kuamuru kuondolewa kwa maudhui yaliyokatazwa

eng: iAfrikan News further explains:
swa: iAfrikan News inaeleza zaidi:

eng: Online content publishers (blogs, podcasts, videos) will apply for a license at a fee of 100,000 Tanzanian Shillings (44 USD) pay an initial license fee of 1,000,000 Tanzanian Shillings (440 USD) and an annual license fee of 1,000,000 Tanzanian Shillings (440 USD).
swa: Wachapishaji wa maudhui ya habari za mtandaoni (blogu, matangazo ya sauti, video,) sasa wataomba leseni kwa ada ya shilingi za Kitanzania 100,000, kulipa ada ya awali ya leseni sh. 1,000,000 (sawa ya dola za kimarekani 440) na ada ya mwaka ya leseni kiasi cha sh.

eng: This means to run something as simple as a personal blog (text) if you live in Tanzania, you’d have to spend an initial (approximately) $900 (USD) in license fees.
swa: 1,000,000 (sawa ya dola za kimarekani 440). Hii ina maana kuwa kuendesha blogu binafsi ya kawaida tu ukiwa unaishi Tanzania inakuhitaji kutumia Dola za Kimarekani 900 kwa ajili ya kulipia ada za leseni.

eng: One immediate public concern regarding the new regulations is their ambiguity.
swa: Mojawapo ya mambo yanayoleta wasiwasi kuhusu kanuni hizi mpya ni utata wa tafsiri zake.

eng: In his latest post, blogger Ben Taylor analyzed the content of the regulations, taking note of a lack of clear definitions:
swa: Katika makala ya hivi karibuni, mwanablogu Ben Taylor alichambua maudhui ya kanuni hizi, akibainisha kukosekana kwa fasili iliyowazi:

eng: The first thing to note is that these regulations are very unclear on several important points.
swa: Kitu cha kwanza cha kuzingatia ni kwamba sheria hii haipo wazi kwa baadhi ya vifungu muhimu.

eng: Some terms – such as 'online content provider' and 'online content service provider' – are never defined.
swa: Baadhi ya maneno - kama vile 'mtoaji wa maudhui ya mtandaoni' na 'mtoaji wa huduma ya maudhui ya mtandaoni' -kamwe hayafafanuliwa.

eng: Are these the same thing?
swa: Je, hivyo ni vitu vinavyofanana?

eng: In other places, the title given to a section of the regulations bears no relation to its content – section 7, for example, has 'bloggers' in the title but nothing relevant to bloggers in the content.
swa: Katika maeneo mengine, kichwa cha habari kilichopo kwenye vifungu vya sheria hakina uhusiano na maudhui yake. Kwa mfano sehemu ya saba ina kichwa cha habari mwanablogu lakini hakuna maudhui yanayohusu blogu.

eng: There are spelling and grammatical errors throughout.
swa: Pia, sheria ina makosa ya tahajia za maneno na sarufi.

eng: And perhaps most bizarrely, the main section on applications for online content service licenses – section 14 – doesn’t even require that applicants must submit their application – only that they must 'fill in an application form' – or say where it should be submitted.
swa: Na labda kioja zaidi ni kifungu cha 14 cha matumizi ya leseni za huduma za maudhui ya habari za mtandaoni ambacho hakiwahitaji waombaji kutuma maombi yao wala hakitaji mahali pa kutuma isipokuwa wanatakiwa kujaza fomu ya maombi.

eng: Taylor raises essential questions throughout his analysis.
swa: Ndugu Taylor ana hoja muhimu katika uchambuzi wake.

eng: No one yet knows how these regulations will be interpreted by the Tanzanian Communications Regulatory Authority (TCRA), the police or the courts.
swa: Hakuna anayejua jinsi sheria hii itakavyotafsiriwa na Mamlaka ya Mawasiliano Tanzania (TCRA), mahakama au polisi.

eng: What is clear is that breaches of the new law will be punishable with a fine of "not less than five million Tanzanian shillings” (around USD $2,500), or imprisonment for “not less than 12 months or both."
swa: Kilicho wazi ni kwamba kuvunjwa kwa sheria hii mpya kunasababisha adhabu ya faini isiyopungua shilingi za kitanzania milioni tano” (Karibu dola za kimarekani 2,500), “au kifungo kisichopungua miezi kumi na mbili au vyote kwa pamoja”.

eng: The Collaboration on International ICT Policy for East and Southern Africa (CIPESA) issued a policy brief on the new regulation, warning against its ambiguity in certain sections:
swa: Umoja wa Sera ya Teknolojia ya Kimataifa ya Habari katika Afrika Mashariki ulitoa muhtasari wa sera tahadhari juu ya utata wa baadhi ya vifungu vya sheria mpya:

eng: ... regulations should be reviewed and amended to have clear, unambiguous definitions and wording, and quash the requirement for registration of bloggers and users of similar online platforms.
swa: Kanuni zinapaswa kurudiwa na kurekebishwa ili kuwa wazi, fasili tata na tahajia za maneno na kubatilisha masharti yanayofanana ya blogu kujisajili na watumiaji wenye majukwaa mtandaoni kujisajili pia.

eng: It is also essential that not too much power is vested in TCRA with regards to content take-downs and that diversity in content availability online is promoted.
swa: Ni muhimu pia TCRA isipewe nguvu kubwa kuondoa maudhui ya habari za mtandaoni, isipokuwa upatikanaji wa maudhui mbalimbali ya habari za mtandaoni uimarishwe.

eng: The obligations set out should not turn content service providers and publishers into monitors, by handing them responsibility such as use of moderating tools to filter content, conducting content review before publication, and undertaking mechanisms to identify sources of content.
swa: Wajibu uliowekwa usiwafanye watoa huduma na wachapishaji maudhui ya habari za mtandaoni kuwa viranja kwa kuwatwisha majukumu kama ya kurekebisha na kuchuja maudhui, kupitia upya maudhui kabla ya kuchapishwa na kuwa na utaratibu wa kutambua vyanzo vilivyochapisha maudhui.

eng: Blogging as alternative news in Tanzania
swa: Kublogu kama fursa mbadala ya habari Tanzania

eng: Blogging emerged in Tanzania around 2007 and became popular as an alternative news platform with educated, middle-class people, as well as politicians and political parties.
swa: Nchini Tanzania blogu zilianza miaka ya 2007 na zimejichukulia umaarufu kuwa majukwaa mbadala ya kupashana habari miongoni mwa wasomi, tabaka la watu wa kati, wanasiasa na vyama vya siasa.

eng: In Tanzania, where media historically holds strong ties to government interests, blogging opened up possibilities for individuals to establish private news outlets that proved immensely powerful in terms of reach and readership.
swa: Nchini Tanzania, ambapo kihistoria, vyombo vya habari vimekuwa na ukaribu mkubwa na maslahi ya serikali, blogu zilifungua mlango kwa watu binafsi kuanzisha majukwaa binafsi ya kupasha habari ambayo yameonekana kuwa na nguvu sana kwa sababu ya urahisi wake kupatikana na usomaji.

eng: Before the rise of mobile apps, access to a stable Internet connection and laptop were imperative for bloggers.
swa: Kabla ya vitumizi vya simu za kiganjani, upatikanaji wa mtandao wa intaneti ya uhakika na kompyuta mpakato yalikuwa ni mahitaji ya lazima sana kwa wanablogu.

eng: This set a relatively high barrier to participation for people with limited income.
swa: Hii inazuia kwa kiwango kikubwa watu kushiriki ikiwa wana kipato kidogo.

eng: Michuzi blog, launched in 2005 by Issa Michuzi, who is known as the 'father of all Swahili blogs', was one of the earliest and most widely read blogs in Tanzania, often reporting on politics and news, with thousands of readers per day.
swa: Blogu ya Michuzi, ilianzishwa mwaka 2005 na Issa Michuzi ambaye anajulikana pia kama 'mwazilishi wa blogu za kiswahili', ilikuwa ni moja ya blogu ya kwanza ambayo ilisomwa na maelfu ya wasomaji kwa siku katika Tanzania, mara nyingi ilihabarisha juu ya siasa na habari za kawida.

eng: Michuzi was the first in Tanzania to see blogging as a business.
swa: Michuzi alikuwa wa kwanza kuona kublogu kama biashara.

eng: He managed to keep his content free and accessible yet clearly capitalized on the power of ads to generate income.
swa: Aliweza kufanya maudhui yake yapatikane kwa uhuru na lakini alibaini pia nguvu kubwa ya matangazo yanayomwongezea kipato.

eng: Although Tanzania's poverty rate fell from 60 percent in 2007 to an estimated 47 percent in 2016, nearly 12 million Tanzanians still live in extreme poverty.
swa: Ingawa kiwango cha umaskini Tanzania ni asilimia 60 mwaka 2007 na inakadiriwa mwaka 2016 ilikuwa asilimia 47, karibia watanzania milioni 12 bado wanaishi katika umaskini uliokithiri.

eng: Internet access remains low at approximately 45 percent as of 2017.
swa: Wanaopata mtandao wa intaneti bado ni idadi ndogo inayokaribia asilimia 45 kwa takwimu za mwaka 2017.

eng: With a population of about 60 million people and 31 percent residing in urban areas, blogging is still out of reach for most.
swa: Na idadi ya watu inakaribia milioni 60 na asilimia 31 wanaishi maeneo ya mjini, hata hivyo blogu hazjaweza kuwafikia walio wengi.

eng: According to Tanzania Bloggers Network Secretary-General Krantz Mwantepele, as quoted in The Citizen, many Tanzanian bloggers cannot afford these fees because the "license applications and annual subscriptions are way beyond earnings of many bloggers."
swa: Kutokana na makala ya Katibu Mkuu wa Mtandao wa Wanablogu Tanzania ndugu Krantz Mwantepele, kama alivyonukuliwa katika gazeti la Citizen, wanablogu wengi wa kitanzania hawawezi kumudu ada hizo kwa sababu “maombi ya leseni na malipo ya mwaka ni makubwa zaidi ya pato la wanablogu waliowengi”.

eng: Will Tanzanian bloggers push back or pay up in a tense political climate?
swa: Je wanablogu wa ki-Tanzania watagemea au watalipa gharama katika hali hii tete ya kisiasa?

eng: Blogging continues to be a 'new frontier' for young Africans seeking new platforms to connect, discuss and analyze.
swa: Kublogu kunaendelea kuwa 'mbinu mpya' kwa vijana wa ki-Afrika wakisaka majukwaa mapya ili kujadili na kuchambua habari.

eng: With the rise of mobile apps, Tanzanian youth are online more than ever with nearly 60 percent on Facebook alone in 2017.
swa: Uwepo wa simu za kiganjani, umewafanya vijana wa ki-Tanzania kutumia mtandao zaidi mwaka 2017 takribani asilimia 60 ya vijana walitumia mtandao wa Facebook.

eng: Yet restrictions on freedom of expression pose a real challenge to social media users in Tanzania.
swa: Masharti juu ya uhuru wa kujieleza yanaleta changamoto hasa kwa watumiaji wa mitandao ya kijamii nchini Tanzania.

eng: While the constitution allows for freedom of speech, it does not guarantee press freedom.
swa: Wakati Katiba inaruhusu uhuru wa kujieleza, haitoi uhakikisho kuhusu uhuru wa vyombo vya habari.

eng: A set of media regulations provide Tanzanian authorities with the capacity to restrict media based on arguments of national security.
swa: Kanuni nyingi za vyombo vya habari huzipa mamlaka za Tanzania uwezo wa kuzuia vyombo vya habari kwa hoja ya kulinda usalama wa taifa.

eng: Authorities have become increasingly reliant on these rules as political tensions have risen over the past three years.
swa: Mamlaka zimeendelea kutegemea sheria hizi tangu uwepo wa hali ya mvutano wa kisiasa zaidi ya miaka mitatu iliyopita.

eng: Since the presidential elections in 2015, Tanzania's opposition has been restricted by a ban on opposition rallies and the stifling of independent media, sanctions, intimidation, and punishment of citizens for criticising President John P. Magufuli of the ruling Chama cha Mapinduzi (CCM, Swahili for 'Revolutionary Party').
swa: Tangu uchaguzi wa Rais wa mwaka 2015, upinzani Tanzania umekatazwa kufanya maandamano na vyombo vya habari vya kujitegemea vimefungiwa, kumekuwa na vikwazo, vitisho, na wananchi kuadhibiwa pale wanapomkosoa Rais John P. Magufuli wa Chama kilichoshika dola, Chama cha Mapinduzi (CCM).

eng: In December 2016, Tanzanian police arrested Maxence Melo, founder and director of Jamii Forums, a hugely popular Tanzanian online community, for refusing to disclose information on its members, a demand made under the Cybercrimes Act.
swa: Desemba 2016, m-Tanzania Maxence Melo ambaye ni mwanzilishi na Mkurugenzi wa Jamii Forums mtandao wa kijamii wenye umaarufu mkubwa Tanzania alikamatwa na polisi. Sababu ya kukamatwa kwake ni kukakataa kutoa taarifa za wanachama wake. Madai hayo yalifanywa kwa kutumia Sheria ya Makosa ya mMtandaoni.

eng: Melo was released after five days, but his arrest revealed disturbing implications for anyone writing and speaking actively online in forums and blogs in Tanzania.
swa: Melo aliachiwa baada ya siku tano, lakini kukamatwa kwake kulileta wasiwasi kwa kila mtumiaji wa mtandao huo Tanzania.

eng: Most recently, Chama cha Demokrasia na Maendelo (CHADEMA, Swahili for 'Party for Democracy and Progress'), Tanzania's largest opposition party, requested international intervention in the increasingly tense political situation characterized by the arrests of prominent opposition leaders.
swa: Hivi karibuni, Chama cha Demokrasia na Maendeleo (CHADEMA) ambacho ni chama kikuu cha upinzani, kiliomba Umoja wa Mataifa kuingilia kati kutokana na kuongezeka vitendo vya kukamatwa viongozi wakuu wa vyama vya upinzani.

eng: On February 16, 2018, a young student was killed allegedly by a stray-bullet, and several others were injured as the police dispersed an opposition rally in Dar es Salaam.
swa: Tarehe 16 Februari, 2018, mwanafunzi kijana aliuawa kwa kupigwa na kitu kilichosadikiwa kuwa ni risasi, na watu kadhaa walijeruhiwa wakati polisi ikiwatawanya wafuasi wa vyama vya upinzani waliokuwa wanaandamana jijini Dar es Salaam.

eng: These new regulations appear to be less about taxation but rather a convenient tool and part of a wider process to limit freedom of speech and participatory multiparty politics in Tanzania.
swa: Kanuni hizi hazionekani kulenga kukusanya kodi bali ni zana muafaka na sehemu ya zoezi pana la kuminya uhuru wa kujieleza na ushiriki wa siasa za vyama vingi Tanzania.

eng: Wadi Rum, Jordan.
swa: Chumba cha Wadi, Jordan.

eng: Photo by: TreksJo.
swa: Picha imepigwa na Treksjo.

eng: Jordan is the world’s second water-poorest country.
swa: Jordan ni nchi ya pili kwa uhaba wa maji duniani .

eng: One of its major surface water resources, the Jordan River, is shared with Israel, and another one, the Yarmouk River, is shared with Syria—both of which leave a fairly small share of water for Jordan.
swa: Mto Jordan ni moja ya vyanzo vyake vikuu vya maji ya juu ya ardhi, na ambao unatumiwa pia na nchi ya Israel.

eng: When it comes to the 12 identified groundwater basins countrywide, sustainability is a concern as some are exploited to their maximum capacity, and others are overexploited, threatening their future use.
swa: Chanzo kingine cha maji ni Mto Yarmouk,ambao pia unatumiwa na nchi ya Syria,hali inayopelekea nchi ya Jordan kuwa na mgao wa maji wa chini ya kiwango kinachohitajika

eng: The situation has been exasperated by the 1.4 million additional people residing in Jordan and relying on its finite water resources, due to the Syrian war.
swa: Hali ya uhaba wa maji umezidishwa na uwapo wa watu milioni 1.4 zaidi waliokimbia vita Syria na wanaishi Jordani wakitegemea vyanzo vyake vichache vya maji

eng: And looking to the future, climate change only threatens to make it worse.
swa: Na ukiangalia siku za mbeleni, mabadiliko ya tabia nchi yanafanya hali kuwa ngumu zaidi.

eng: Scientists from Stanford University predict that by the end of the century, Jordan could be 4°C hotter, with about a third less rain.
swa: Wanasayansi kutoka chuo kikuu cha Stanford wanatabiri kuwa mwishoni mwa karne, Joto nchini Jordani litapanda kufikia nyuzi joto la 4°C, na kutakuwa na upungufu mara tatu wa mvuap.

eng: Thus, it is threatened with absolute scarcity, as droughts and their duration are expected to double between 2071 and 2100.
swa: Kwahiyo, Jordani, inatishiwa na ukosefu kabisa wa maji, wakati kiwango cha ukame kinatarajiwa kuwa mara mbili zaidi kati ya mwaka 2071 na 2100.

eng: Although the struggle is undeniable, the 9,903,877 citizens of Jordan do not all feel it equally.
swa: Japokuwa jitihada za wananchi ziko wazi, ila raia 9,903,877 wa Jordani, hawabebi mzigo sawa.

eng: The government’s failure to provide water for some places can often be linked to the area’s social status.
swa: Serikali kushindwa kupeleka maji baadhi ya maeneo mara nyingi kunahusishwa na hali ya kijamii ya eneo husika.

eng: Sara Bader, a former resident of Amman's Al-Yasmine neighborhood (a rather crowded and less than average neighborhood) talked to Global Voices about her experience when she moved to Abdoun (an area considered to be for the elite classes):
swa: Sara Bader, mkazi wa zamani wa Amman eneo jirani la Al-Yasmine (eneo lenye wakazi wengi kupita kiasi) aliongea na Global Voices kuhusu uzoefu wake alipohamia Abdoun (eneo ambalo ni la watu wa hadhi ya juu):

eng: We would get water two times a week , sometimes in the summer that is barely enough to get us through the week, so we would time doing the laundry and other water-consuming activities with the day the water would get pumped.
swa: tulikuwa tunapata maji mara mbili kwa wiki , wakati mwingine kipindi cha kiangazi yalikuwa hayatufikishi hata mwisho wa juma, kwahiyo tulikuwa tunafua na kutumia maji kwa matumizi mengine siku ambayo maji yalikuwa yanatoka.

eng: We would always be very cautious when it came to water consumption.
swa: Tulikuwa makini sana na matumizi ya maji.

eng: Now , the water is pumped daily, and my mother does not care what day of the week it is for her to do laundry.
swa: Hapa , maji yanatoka kila siku, na mama yangu hatengi tena ni siku gani afue kwa juma.

eng: It may seem unfair for an area to have 24/7 water pumping while another only gets it twice a week, but the truth is that getting water pumped twice a week is a privilege that many Jordanians in the less fortunate places dream of.
swa: Inaweza ikaonekana sio sawa kwa baadhi ya maeneo maji kutoka kila siku huku kuna maeneo wanapata maji mara mbili kwa juma, ila ukweli ni kuwa kupata maji mara mbili kwa juma ni kama upendeleo ambao watu wa maeneo duni huutamani.

eng: In the poorer areas of Amman, in the provinces, and most importantly in the villages, water is pumped every 20 days, and sometimes not at all.
swa: Kwenye maeneo masikini ya Amman, kwenye vitongoji, na hasahasa vijijini maji yanatoka baada ya siku 20, na kuna wakati hayatoki kabisa.

eng: In a letter sent to the government to complain about the water issue, a citizen residing in the Jerash province stated:
swa: Kwenye barua iliyotumwa serikalini kulalamikia swala la maji, wananchi waishio katika kitongoji cha Jerash walisema:

eng: I am delivering the struggle of hundreds of people to you—people whom have not had water pumped to them in 30 or 20 or 19 days.
swa: Ninawasilisha malalamiko ya mamia ya watu kwako-watu ambao maeneo yao maji hayajatoka kwa siku 30 au 20 au 19.

eng: He continued:
swa: Akaendelea:

eng: I have proof that some water pipes have not held water for over a year because city hall has not been pumping water to these places, not even once a month.
swa: Nina ushahidi kuwa baadhi ya mabomba hayajawahi kutoa maji zaidi ya mwaka kwakuwa mamlaka ya waji haijawahi kupeleka maji kwenye maeneo hayo hata mara moja kwa mwezi.

eng: The comments on the letter by his fellow Jordanians indicate that the problem is shared by others.
swa: Maoni ya wananchi wenzake wa Jordani yanaonesha kuwa tatizo linawakumba watu wengi.

eng: Many advised him to move to a house “next to a government representative” or “to a better neighborhood” so that he gets better water service, as infrequent pumping is “unnoticeable” in the “elite” neighborhoods.
swa: Wengi walimshauri ahamie kwenye nyumba iliyokaribu na mwakilishi wa serikali au kwenye maeneo wanaoishi watu wenye hadhi ya juu ili aweze kupata huduma bora ya maji, kwakuwa maeneo hayo maji huwa hayakatiki.

eng: A huge issue in the provinces is that families there often have more members, and that a large amount of these citizens are farmers who desperately need the water for their crops as well.
swa: Swala kwenye kitongoji hiki nikuwa kaya zina watu wengi, na wakaazi wengi ni wakulima wanaohitaji maji ili wamwagilie mazao yao

eng: Not to mention that the government bills people for water service whether the citizens actually receive the service or not.
swa: Jambo la kushangaza Serikali huwapelekea watu ankara za maji bila kujali kama watu hao walipata maji au la.

eng: In the case that they don’t, they have to buy water that is delivered by non-government-owned water services (or “water tanks”, as they are colloquially known).
swa: Kipindi ambacho hawapati maji inawalazimu kununua maji kwenye malori yanayotoa huduma za binafsi za maji.

eng: Thus, they have to pay two bills: one issued by the government, and one by whoever you hire to fill your tanks.
swa: Kwahiyo, wanalazimika kulipa ankara mbili za maji: ile iliyotolewa na serikali na ile ambayo unamlipa mtu binafsi akuletee maji.

eng: The price set by the government for these water tanks is 4 Jordanian dinars (6 US dollars per meter), already an amount that many people can't afford, but some of these services exploit citizens in their time of need, charging 5 dinars.
swa: Bei elekezi iliyopangwa na serikali kwa wauzaji maji kwa malori ni dinari 4 za Jordani (dola 6 za kimarekani kwa mita), ni kiwango ambacho wananchi wengi hawakimudu, kuna baadhi ya watoa huduma hizo huwapandishia bei wananchi wakati wa uhaba wa maji hadi dinari 5.

eng: What is the reason behind the government's apparent neglect of the provinces when it come to their supply of water?
swa: Ni sababu gani zinazofanya serikali kuyatelekeza baadhi ya maeneo lipokuja swala la huduma ya maji?

eng: An employee in the Water and Irrigation Ministry who spoke with GV and who preferred to remain anonymous said:
swa: Mfanyakazi wa wizara ya maji na umwagiliaji akiongea na GV kwa mashariti ya kutotajwa jina lake alisema:

eng: The reality is different than most people’s assumptions: it is not that the ministry is biased in the schedule, it is simply that the poorer areas have weak infrastructure and pipes which cannot stand continuous pumping as they already leak 2/3 of the water pumped through them.
swa: Uhalisia ni tafauti na watu wengi wanavyofikiria: sio kuwa wizara ina upendeleo katika kugawa maji, ila maeneo duni yana miundo mbinu dhaifu na mabomba hayawezi kuhimili maji kutoka kila siku, mabomba mengi yametoboka na 2/3 ya maji hupotea kabla ya kufika eneo husika.

eng: That is why these places do not have a non-stop supply of water, because the ministry cannot afford losing that much water on a daily basis, thus the water is pumped every week or every two weeks, and most of it is not delivered because of the leaks.
swa: Hiyo ndio sababu inayopelekea maeneo hayo kutopata maji muda wote, kwasababu wizara haiwezi kupoteza maji mengi kiasi hicho kila siku, kwahiyo maji hufunguliwa kila juma au baada ya majuma mawili, na mengi hayawafikii wananchi kwa sababu yanapotea njiani.

eng: When asked why the ministry does not fix the leaks in the pipes or replace them all together, he simply commented that the budget cannot currently prioritize that.
swa: Alipoulizwa kwanini wizara haikarabati na kujiziba mabomba yanayovuja au kuyabadilisha kabisa, alisema kwasasa bajeti haiwezi kufanya hilo kipaumbele.

eng: However, the government promises a fairer distribution of water this year and that the provinces' supply of water is secured for the summer.
swa: Hats hivyo, serikali imeahidi mgao sawa wa maji mwaka huu na kuwa wakati wote wa majira ya kiangazi majiya uhakika yatapatikana.

swa: Hata hivyo, kuandaa michoro ya utupu na kuionesha hadharani ni jambo linalohitaji ujasiri nchini Nepali.

eng: Traditional gender roles in Nepali society see men as the caretakers of their families, which means they should be muscular and tough.
swa: Kiasili, mwanaume wa nchini Nepali ana wajibu wa kulea familia, jambo linaarishia kuwa mwanaumea anapaswa kuwa nguvu na mjasiri.

eng: As in other parts of the world, this "macho" expectation means that men in Nepal aren’t always comfortable with vulnerability or talking about their bodies or sexuality.
swa: Kama ilivyo sehemu nyingine duniani, hali hii ya "uanaume" inaashiria kuwa wanaume wa Nepali hawajisikii vizuri sana uanaume wao kuzungunziwa au kujadili kuhusu miili yao au jinsia yao.
