eng: Join the Global Voices Sub-Saharan Africa team (@gvssafrica) for a multilingual tweetathon demanding an end to the taxation of social media in Uganda.
swa: Ungana na Waandishi wa Global Voices ukanda wa Afrika Kusini mwa Jangwa la Sahara (@gvssafrica) kushiriki majadiliano yatakayofanyika kwa lugha mbalimbali kushinikiza kusitishwa kwa kodi ya mitandao ya kijamii nchini Uganda.

eng: On July 1, the Ugandan government began enforcing a new law that imposes a 200 shilling daily levy on people using internet messaging platforms, despite protests from local and international online free speech advocates.
swa: Mnamo Julai 1, serikali ya Uganda ilianza kutekeleza sheria mpya inayotoza kodi ya shilingi 200 za Uganda kila siku kwa watu wanaotumia majukwaa ya mtandaoni, pamoja na upinzani mkubwa kutoka watetezi wa uhuru wa kujieleza ndani na nje ya nchi hiyo.

eng: This move, according to Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni, has the dual purpose of strengthening the national budget and also curtailing "gossip" by Ugandans on social media.
swa: Hatua hiyo, kwa mujibu wa Rais wa Uganda Yoweri Museveni, inalenga kuimarisha bajeti ya taifa na kudhibiti "tabia ya umbeya" inayoendekezwa na wa-Ganda kwenye mitandao ya kijamii.

eng: It was also popular among local telecom providers, who do not directly benefit from the use of foreign-based “over-the-top” services such as Facebook, Twitter, and WhatsApp.
swa: Kodi hiyo pia inaonekana kukubalika kwa makampuni yanayotoa huduma za simu, ambayo hapo awali hayakuwa yanapata faida moja kwa moja kwa matumizi ya “mitandao ya nje” kama vile Facebook, Twitter, na WhatsApp.

eng: The policy was preceded with an order to register all new mobile SIM cards with the National Biometric Data Centre.
swa: Jeshi la polisi limepewa nguvu ya kusajili SIM kadi zote kwa msaada wa Kituo cha Taifa cha Takwimu za Kidijitali.

eng: The measure also forces Ugandans to only use mobile money accounts in order to recharge their SIM cards and makes it mandatory to pay a one percent levy on the total value of transaction on any mobile money transaction.
swa: Hatua hiyo pia inawalazimisha wa-Ganda kutumia akaunti zao za huduma ya fedha kwa njia ya simu ili kuongeza salio na hivyo kufanya iwe lazima kulipa kodi ya asilimia moja ya kiasi kinachohamishwa kwa kila muamala unaofanyika.

eng: These new policies make it more costly for Ugandans — especially those living in poverty — to communicate and perform everyday tasks using their mobile devices.
swa: Sera hizi mpya zinafanya iwe gharama kwa wa-Ganda -hususani wale wanaoishi kwenye umasikini - kuwasiliana na kufanya shughuli zozote kwa kutumia simu au vifaa vinavyofanana na hivyo.

eng: On July 2, civil society and legal advocates in Uganda filed a court challenge against the law, arguing that it violates the country's constitution.
swa: Mnamo Julai 2, asasi za kiraia na mawakili wa kisheria nchini Uganda walifungua kesi mahakamani kupinga sheria hiyo, wakisema inapingana na katiba ya nchi.

eng: A protester demonstrates his opposition to Uganda's social media tax at a gathering on July 6, 2018.
swa: Mwandamanaji akionesha upinzani wake sheria ya mitandao ya kijamii nchini Uganda kwenye mkusanyiko uliofanyika mnamo Julai 6, 2018.

eng: On July 6, concerned citizens and civil society advocates issued a joint press statement calling on Ugandans to avoid paying the tax by using alternate methods to exchange money and access social media, and to join a "National Day of Peaceful Protest Against Unfair Taxation" on Wednesday, July 11, 2018.
swa: Mnamo Julai 6, raia walioguswa na mwenendo huo na mambo kwa kushirikiana na mawakili wa asasi za kiraia walitoa tamko la pamoja kwa vyombo vya habari wakizungumzia masuala kadhaa ikiwemo kuwataka wa-Ganda kuepuka kulipa kodi hiyo; kutumia mbinu mbadala za kufanya miamala ya fedha pamoja na kuunganishwa na mitandao ya kijamii; na kuunga mkono "Siku ya Taifa ya Maandamano Dhidi ya Kodi ya Dhuluma" mnamo Jumatano, Julai 11, 2018.

eng: The Global Voices community and our network of friends and allies wish to support this and other efforts to demand an end to the tax.
swa: Jumuiya ya Global Voices na mtandao wetu wa marafiki na washirika tumeona vyema kuunga mkono juhudi hizi na nyingine zinazolenga kudai kusitishwa kwa kodi hii.

eng: We believe that this tax is simply a ploy to censor Ugandans and gag dissenting voices.
swa: Tunaamini kwamba kodi hii ni mpango wa kuwadhibiti wa-Ganda na kunyamazisha sauti zao.

eng: We believe social media should be freely accessible for all people, including Ugandans.
swa: Tunaamini mitandao ya kijamii inapaswa kupatikana kwa uhuru kwa watu wote, wakiwemo wa-Ganda.

eng: The Ugandan social media tax must go!
swa: Sheria ya kodi ya mitandao ya kijamii nchini Uganda lazima ikomeshwe!

eng: On Monday, July 9, beginning at 14:00 East Africa Time, we plan to tweet at community leaders, government and diplomatic actors, and media influencers to increase awareness and draw public attention to the issue.
swa: Kwa maana hiyo siku ya Jumatatu, Julai 9, kuanzia saa 8:00 mchana kwa Saa za Afrika Mashariki, tunapanga ku-twiti tukiwalenga viongozi wetu wa jamii, serikali na wanadiplomasia, watumiaji mashuhuri wa mitandao ya kijamii kwa madhumuni ya kuongeza uelewa wa watu kuhusu suala hili.

eng: We especially encourage fellow bloggers and social media users all over the world to join us.
swa: Tunawaomba wanablogu na watumiaji wa mitandao ya kijamii duniani kote kuungana nasi.

eng: JOINT PRESS STATEMENT ON THE AMENDMENT TO THE EXCISE DUTY ACT TO LEVY TAXES ON SOCIAL MEDIA USE AND MOBILE MONEY TRANSACTIONS
swa: TAMKO LA PAMOJA KWA VYOMBO VYA HABARI KUHUSU MAREKEBISHO YA SHERIA KWA MINAJILI YA KUTOZA KODI MATUMIZI YA MITANDAO YA KIJAMII NA MIAMALA YA FEDHA KWA NJIA YA SIMU ZA KIGANJANI

eng: Convened on Friday, 6 July, 2018 at 2.00PM
swa: Imetolewa mnamo Ijumaa,Julai 6, 2018 saa 8.00 alasiri.

eng: On Tuesday, 3 July, 2018, we young people and youth leaders from various student guild governments, musicians and artistes, Small and Medium-sized Enterprises and the Parliament of Uganda held a Press Conference at which we expressed our serious reservations and grave concerns about the amendment to the Excise Duty (Amendment) Act which levies a tax on social media access and an extortionist one per cent (1%) charge on Mobile Money transactions.
swa: Mnamo Jumanne, Julai 3, 2018, sisi vijana na viongozi vijana kutoka serikali mbalimbali za wanafunzi, wanamuziki, wasanii, wafanyabiashara wadogo na wa kati na Bunge la Uganda tulifanya mkutano na waandishi wa habari ambapo tulionesha masikitiko yetu makubwa kuhusu mabadiliko ya sheria ya Sheria ya Kodi inayoelekeza kutozwa kodi kwa matumizi ya mitandao ya kijamii na kulipwa kwa tozo ya asilimia moja kwa kila muamala unaofanyika kupitia huduma za fedha kwa njia ya simu za kiganjani.

eng: We implored the Speaker to recall Parliament from recess and asked the Leader of Government Business to table a motion to repeal the amendment by Friday, 6 July, 2018.
swa: Tulimwomba Spika wa Bunge kukatisha kikao cha Bunge na kumwelekeza Kiongozi wa shughuli za Serikali bungeni kuwasilisha hoja ya kusitisha marekebisho hayo Ijumaa, Julai 6, 2018.

eng: The deadline elapsed a few hours ago and we are here to announce the way forward:
swa: Muda tuliokuwa tumempa umeisha masaa kadhaa yaliyopita na tuko hapa kutangaza hatua tunazochukua:

eng: i) We invite citizens and subscribers to stop transacting via any of the Mobile Money services and as an alternative, rely on physical payment methods so as to avoid paying the unfortunate tax;
swa: i) Tunatoa wito kwa raia na watoaji wa huduma kuacha kufanya miamala yoyote kwa hutumia huduma za fedha kwa njia ya simu na ikibidi kufanya miamala kutumia njia mbadala zisizopitia kwenye simu zao ili kukwepa kulipa kodi hiyo;

eng: ii) We further encourage citizens to use available options to stay online without paying the daily two hundred Uganda shillings (200/-) per day to access social media sites;
swa: ii) Tunawahamasisha wananchi kutumia mbinu mbadala zilizopo kuwawezesha kuendelea kuwepo mtandaoni bila kulazimika kulipa shilingi za Uganda 200 kila siku ili kupata huduma za mitandao ya kijamii;

eng: iii) We also call upon Members of Parliament to expedite the process of recalling the House but also to conduct consultations in their constituencies regarding this matter;
swa: iii) Tunawaomba Wabunge wa Bunge la Uganda kuharakisha mchakato wa kuliomba bunge kuchukua hatua lakini pia kufanya mashauriano na wapigakura wao kuhusu suala hili;

eng: iiii) Finally, we are declaring Wednesday, 11 July, 2018 as a National Day of Peaceful Protest against Unfair Taxation.
swa: iiii) Mwisho, tunatangaza kuwa Jumatano, Julai 11, 2018 kuwa Siku ya Taifa ya Maandamano ya Amani Kupinga Kodi hiyo ya Dhuluma.

eng: In this regard, we invite citizens to deliver petitions to their Members of Parliament and to dress up in red coloured attire as they go about their daily business.
swa: Kwa mukhtadha huu, tunawaomba wananchi kuwasilisha saini zao kuonesha kupinga kodi hii kwa wabunge wao na wavae nguo nyekundu wanapokwenda kwenye shughuli zao.

eng: We have already notified the Uganda Police Force and a copy of the notification is available.
swa: Tumelijulisha Jeshi la Polisi Uganda na nakala ya taarifa tuliyowapa inapatikana.

eng: We will continue engaging our respective constituencies and leaders to protest, reject and continue the boycott until the poorly thought-out taxes are rescinded.
swa: Tutaendelea kuyashirikisha majimbo yetu na viongozi katika kupinga, kukataa na kuendelea kugomea mpaka kodi hiyo iliyoanzishwa bila kufikiriwa vizuri itakapoondolewa.

eng: As young leaders, we have undertaken research and consultations and are willing to suggest better avenues and models of taxation that are sustainable and beneficial to both the citizen and the state.
swa: Kama viongozi vijana, tumefanya utafiti na mashauriano na tuko tayari kushauri maeneo muafaka zaidi ya mifumo sahihi zaidi ya kodi ambayo itakuwa endelevu na yenye manufaa kwa wananchi na serikali.

eng: STEERING COMMITTEE
swa: KAMATI KUU

eng: NATIONAL CITIZENS’ ACTION AGAINST UNFAIR TAXATION
swa: HARAKATI ZA KITAIFA ZINAZOENDESHWA NA WANANCHI KUPINGA KODI YA DHULUMA

eng: Global Voices coverage of social media regulation in Uganda:
swa: Makala mbalimbali za Global Voices kuhusu mitandao ya kijamii nchini Uganda:

eng: Ugandan Government Plans to Tax Social Media Users for Too Much Gossip Netizen Report: Uganda’s ‘WhatsApp tax’ and SIM card regulations will make it harder to stay connected Ugandans Are Finally Back on Social Media After Days-Long Blackout Netizen Report: Facebook and Twitter Disappear in Uganda Amid Election Tensions Social Media Blocked in Uganda Ahead of President Museveni's Inauguration Netizen Report: Uganda and Nigeria Seek Stricter Controls for Social Media
swa: Serikali ya Uganda Inalenga Kuwatoza Kodi Watumiaji wa Mitandao ya Kijamii Kukomesha Umbeya Ripoti ya Mitandaoni: 'Kodi ya WhatsApp' na Sheria za SIM kadi Zitafanya Matumizi ya Mtandao yawe Magumu Wa-Ganda Warudi Tena kwenye Mitandao ya Kijamii Baada ya Kutokupatikana kwa Siku Kadhaa Ripoti ya Mitandaoni: Facebook na Twita Zimepotea Uganda Wakati Joto la Uchaguzi Likiendelea Kupanda Mitandao ya Kijamii Imefungwa nchini Uganda Wakati Rais Museveni Anaelekea Kuapishwa Ripoti ya Mitandaoni: Uganda na Nigeria Zinatafuta Mbinu ya Kudhibiti Zaidi Mitandao ya Kijami

eng: Malagasy children by Yves Picq - CC-BY-SA-3.0
swa: picha ya watoto wa Madagaskar na Yves Picq - CC-BY-SA-3.0

eng: Since the Convention on the Rights of the Child was signed in 1991, Madagascar has been multiplying its efforts to implement policies that protect child rights and created more than 750 child protection networks within the country since 2004.
swa: Tangu mkataba wa haki za mtoto ambao ulisainiwa mwaka 1991, Madagaska imeongeza jitihada za kutekeleza sera zinazolinda haki za mtoto na ilianzisha ndani ya nchi zaidi ya vituo vya mtandao 750 vya kuwalinda watoto tangu mwaka 2004.

eng: Despite this progress, abuse, violence, sexual exploitation and forced labor are still a tragic reality which silently occurs behind closed doors.
swa: Pamoja na maendeleo haya, unyanyasaji, matumizi ya nguvu, unyanyasaji wa kingono na kazi za lazima bado ndiyo ukweli wa kutisha ambao hufanyika ndani nyumba.

eng: According to a report released by the Malagasy State and UNICEF, every second young Malagasy claims to have been the victim of violence at school, and nine kids out of ten have been beaten by their family.
swa: Kutokana na taarifa iliiyotolewa na nchi ya Madagaskar na UNICEF, kila sekunde mtoto wa Madagaskar hudai kufanyiwa unyanyasaji shuleni, na watoto tisa kati ya kumi wanakuwa wamepigwa na familia zao.

eng: An alarming report by UNICEF
swa: Ripoti ya kutisha ya UNICEF

eng: Following a request by the Malagasy government, UNICEF carried out a study on violence perpetrated against children in the country.
swa: Kutokana na ombi la serikali ya Madagaska, UNICEF ilifanya utafiti juu ya unyanyasaji dhidi ya watoto katika nchi hiyo.

eng: The result of the study is beyond alarming:
swa: Matokeo ya utafiti huo yanatisha zaidi:

eng: 89% of children report having suffered from physical domestic abuse at least once.
swa: Asilimia 89 ya watoto wanadai kuwahi kuteswa nyumbani kwa kunyanyaswa kimwili angalau mara moja.

eng: Nonetheless, 72% of them say they feel safe at home.
swa: Katika hao, asilimia 72 wanasema hawajisikii amani wakiwa nyumbani.

eng: Globally, the report highlights that violence is very often rooted in traditional practices which are very difficult to challenge.
swa: Ripoti inaonesha unyanyasaji duniani umejikita katika mila za jadi ambazo ni vigumu kuzihoji.

eng: Rajae Sbihi, a child psychiatrist who partook to the study, explains:
swa: Rajae Sbihi, ambaye ni mtaalamu wa saikolojia ya watoto alishiriki katika utafiti, alieleza:

eng: Violence is considered as a means of education, whether it is at home or at school.
swa: Unyanyasaji unachukuliwa kama njia ya kuwaelimisha wakiwa shuleni au nyumbani.

eng: Young Malagasy girls by Hery Zo Rakotondramana on FlickR - CC BY-SA 2.0
swa: Picha ya wasichana vijana wa mMadagaskar iliyopigwa na Hery Zo Rakotondramana on FlickR - CC BY-SA 2.0

eng: According to Sbihi, children in rural communities are even more at risk to violence, explaining that almost 20% of Malagasy children are not registered at birth – particularly in remote districts – which increases their vulnerability.
swa: Kutokana na Sbihi, watoto katika jamii za vijijini wapo katika hatari zaidi ya kunyanyaswa, alisema kwamba karibu asimilia 20 ya watoto wa madagaska hawakusajiliwa wakati wamezaliwa – hasa wanaoishi wilaya zilizopo mbali– hiyo huongeza unyanyasaji wao.

eng: Public powers are indeed often one of the only safeguards for child victims of violence, even more, if it happens at home.
swa: Nguvu ya umma kiukweli ndiyo mara nyingi ni moja ya walinzi wa watoto waathirika wa unyanyasaji, na hasa inapotokea nyumbani.

eng: This type of violence leads to severe wounds, trauma, physical and emotional development troubles, risky behaviors or even dropping out of school altogether.
swa: Aina hii ya unyanyasaji hupelekea vidonda vya kudumu, kiwewe, matatizo ya ukuaji wa mwili na kifikra, tabia hatarishi au kuacha kwenda shule pia.

eng: Different types of violence
swa: Aina mbalimbali za unyanyasaji

eng: Besides physical violence, there is a range of scenarios which hinders children development.
swa: Pamoja na unyanyasaji wa kutumia nguvu, kuna matukio mengi ambayo huzuia maendeleo ya watoto.

eng: In fact, 40% of young Malagasy's report having worked before the age of 18.
swa: Kwa kweli, 40% ya ripoti za vijana wa Madagaskar hufanya kazi kabla ya miaka 18.

eng: Laureate Rasolofoniainarison, national administrator of projects at the office of the OIT (in English ILO: International Labour Organization) in Antananarivo, explains how this perpetuates the cycle of poverty:
swa: Laureate Rasolofoniainarison ambaye ni kiongozi wa kitaifa wa miradi katika ofisi ya OIT (kwa kiingereza ILO: Shirika la kazi la Umoja wa Mataifa)mjini Antananarivo,anaeleza namna unyanyasaji huu unavyoendeleza mzunguko wa umaskini :

eng: Parents often say that they send them to work instead of going to school because they are poor.
swa: Mara nyingi wazazi husema kuwa wanawatuma kufanya kazi badala ya kwenda shule kwa sababu wao ni maskini.

eng: In reality, making their children work is what makes them poor, by perpetuating a cycle in which education and the possibility of rising socially have no place.
swa: Kiukweli, kuwafanya watoto wao kufanya kazi ndicho kinachowafanya kuwa maskini kwa kuendeleza mzunguko ambao elimu na kukua kijamii havina nafasi.

eng: Young girls are even more vulnerable to this violence.
swa: Vijana wa kike wapo katika hatari zaidi kwa unyanyasaji huu.

eng: Early marriage is part of the Malagasy tradition and is a problem for minors.
swa: Ndoa za utotoni ni sehemu ya mila za jamii za Madagaskar, na ni tatizo kwa watoto.

eng: More than one-third of girls between the ages of 15 and 19-years-old are already married or in a relationship.
swa: Zaidi ya theluthi ya wasichana kati ya miaka 15 na 19 tayari wameolewa au wana mahusiano.

eng: Very few teenagers use contraceptive methods (less than 8%) which considerably increases the number of unwanted pregnancies.
swa: Mabinti wachache hutumia njia za kuzuia mimba (ambao ni chini ya 8%) ambazo zinafikiriwa kuongeza idadi ya mimba zisizohitajika.

eng: In fact, 30% of the minors in the island have a child, as reported by a rating from the World Atlas 2015.
swa: Hakika, 30% ya mabinti katika kisiwa wana watoto. , kama ilivyoripotiwa na tathmini ya World Atlas ya mwaka 2015.

eng: This number reaches up to 50% in some areas of the capital.
swa: Idadi hii imefikia hadi 50% katika baadhi ya sehemu za mji mkuu.

eng: Another alarming statistic is the rising rate of sexual exploitation of girls for commercial purposes, particularly near petroleum and mining sites.
swa: Takwimu nyingine ya kutisha ni kuongezeka kiasi cha unyanyasaji wa ngono kwa wasichana kwa madhumuni ya biashara, hasa karibu na vituo vya mafuta na machimbo .

eng: A new tool to better fight violence
swa: Zana mpya katika mapambano dhidi ya unyanyasaji

eng: Before this report, children's needs and rights were unknown in Madagascar.
swa: Kabla ya ripoti hii, mahitaji na haki za watoto vilikuwa havijuliakani katika Madagaskar.

eng: This latest report is seen as a tool which allows child protection advocates to better understand, prevent and respond to these risky situations.
swa: Hii ni ripoti mpya ambayo inaonekana kama zana ambayo inaruhusu uwakili wa kueleweka vizuri kulinda watoto , kuzuia, na kujibu hali hizi hatarishi.

eng: It is also a first step towards a more comprehensive national policy which aims to reduce violence.
swa: Pia, ni hatua ya kwanza kuelekea uundwaji makini wa sera ya taifa inayolenga kupunguza unyanyasaji.

eng: It can also be used as an argumentative tool to convince people to let go of traditional practices which can be detrimental to children.
swa: Inaweza pia kutumiwa kama zana ya kurejea katika kutoa hoja ili kuwashawishi watu kuacha mila na desturi ambazo zinaharibu watoto.

eng: In total, UNICEF has deployed 240 social volunteers on the island to provide psycho-social support, communal dialogue and social mobilisation.
swa: Kwa ujumla, UNICEF imeajiri wanajamii wakujitolea 240 katika kisiwa kutoa msaada wa saikoljia, mazungumzo na uhamasishaji wa jamii.

eng: UNICEF has also established partnerships in order to develop a code of conduct for all mining employees and sub-contractors in Madagascar, in an effort to end young women's sexual exploitation.
swa: Pia, UNICEF imeanzisha ushirikiano ili kuanzisha kanuni za maadili kwa ajili waajiriwa migodini na wakandarasi wadogo nchini Madagaskar katika jitihada za kumaliza unyanyasaji wa ngono kwa vijana wa kike.

eng: This practical approach should hopefully have a progressive impact on their protection in the next few years.
swa: Hii mbinu ya utendaji inategemewa kuwa na matokeo endelevu kwa ajili ya ulinzi wao miaka michache ijayo.

eng: Ugandans protesting the rampant murders and kidnapping targeting women.
swa: Waganda wakiwa kwenye maandano kupinga kutekwa na kuuawa kwa wanawake kulikokithiri.

eng: Photo Credit: Katumba Badru, used with permission.
swa: Picha na Katumba Badru,na imetumika kwa ruhusa.

eng: Since 2015, at least 42 Ugandan women have been kidnapped, maimed and murdered in and around Uganda's capital Kampala, half of them in a space of only three months in 2017.
swa: Tangu 2015, karibu wanawake waki-Ganda 42 wametekwa, kulemazwa na wengine kuuawa katika mji mkuu Kampala nusu yao ni ndani ya miezi mitatu katika mwaka 2017.

eng: Some of their bodies were found with brutal signs of sexual violence.
swa: Wengine walikutwa na alama za kuteswa kikatili na kufanyiwa unyanyasaji wa kijinsia.

eng: The string of murders, all bearing gruesome similar details, has horrified the country.
swa: Mlolongo wa mauaji ya kutisha nchini Uganda yanafanana yanavyotokea.

eng: The motivation behind them remains unclear, but witchcraft is a popular theory. Authorities are yet to charge a single suspect.
swa: Hakuna juhudi zozote zilizochukuliwa lakini uchawi ndio nadharia maarufu inakubalika Mamlaka hazijamshtaki mshukiwa hata mmoja.

eng: Tired of living in fear, the women of Uganda felt they had to do something.
swa: Wanawake wa Uganda waliona wanahaja ya kufanya jambo.

eng: On June 30, 2018, the Women’s Protest Working Group (WPWG), with the support of feminists from other countries, staged a peaceful demonstration in the capital city of Kampala to protest against the rampant kidnapping and murders targeting women in Uganda.
swa: Tarehe 30, mwezi Juni 2018, maandamano ya kikundi cha wanawake wafanyakazi (WPWG) kikuungwa mkono na wanaharakati kutoka nchi nyingine, waliamua kufanya maandano ya amani katika mji mkuu Kampala kupinga utekaji na mauaji yanalenga wanawake Uganda.

eng: And so I March.
swa: Regina Zawedde 60, Bulaga Mityana

eng: To remember them, they were not given any justice and no one was held accountable for their gruesome deaths.
swa: Kwa hiyo naandamana, niwakumbuke, hawakupewa haki yoyote na hakuna aliyekamatwa kwa ajili ya vifo hivi vya kutisha.

eng: But I recognize them.
swa: Lakini nawathamini.

eng: At the march, which Global Voices attended, WPWG leader Dr. Stella Nyanzi told the crowd that the women are pursuing key interventions such as justice for the families of those murdered and also to push for action on violence against women.
swa: Global Voices ilihudhuria maandamano hayo na kiongozi wa kikundi cha wanawake wafanyakazi Dr. Stella Nyanzi aliuambia umati uliohudhuria kwamba wanawake wamejitoa kufanya ufuatiliaji wa haki kwa familia za waliouwa na pia kushinikiza kuchukuliwa hatua dhidi ya unyanyasaji dhidi ya wanawake.

eng: Fellow activist Patricia Twasiima then read out the names of the 42 murdered women.
swa: Halafu, mwanaharakati mwezao Patricia twasiima alisoma majina ya wanawake 42 waliouwawa.

eng: Earlier, the police had attempted to block the protests claiming that the issues the women were protesting had already been resolved after President Museveni addressed the nation on his 10-point plan for restoring security in Uganda.
swa: Mapema askari walizuia waandamanaji kwa kudai kwamba masuala ambayo wanawake hao wanayapinga tayari yalishatatuliwa baada ya Rais Mseven alipohutubia taifa juu ya mikakati yake 10 ya kurejesha amani Uganda.

eng: A letter from the Commissioner of Police stated:
swa: Barua kutoka kwa kamishina wa polisi ilisema:

eng: This serves to inform you that the intended demonstration to raise awareness, express displeasure about the spate of killings and kidnap of women/girls cannot be allowed to go on as scheduled.
swa: Mnaarifiwa kuwa maandamano yaliyolenga kuongeza uelewa na kueleza kuchukizwa kutekwna vifo vingi vya wanawake / wasichana hayawezi kuruhusiwa kufanyika kama yalivyokuwa yamepangwa.

eng: The women were determined to go on with the protest anyway:
swa: Hata hivyo wanawake walidhamiria kuendelea na maandamano:

eng: We will no longer settle for speeches, thought and prayers, from the police force and government funded with taxpayers’ money.
swa: Hatutaacha kuzungumza, kufikiria na maombi dhidi ya nguvu za askari polisi na serikali ambavyo vinatumia fedha za walipa kodi.

eng: The attempted ban triggered even more support from Ugandans including journalists who vowed to join, with men and women alike.
swa: Jaribio la kuzuia lilichochea wananchi wakiwemo waandishi wa habari, wanaume na wanawake kuunga mkono zaidi na kuapa kujiunga katika maandamano.

eng: Writer Daniel Kalinaki wrote an opinion piece in the Daily Monitor that made rounds on Twitter on why he would be joining the protest:
swa: Mwandishi wa habari Daniel Kalinaki alitoa maoni yake katika gazeti la Daily Monitor kwamba ujumbe mwingi kupitia Twitter ndio uliomfanya ajiunge katika maandamano:

eng: So I will be at the march. With my daughter.
swa: Hivyo nitakuwa kwenye maandamano na binti yangu.

eng: We will hold hands and walk, unarmed and peacefully, along with others.
swa: Tutashikana mikono na kutembea pamoja na wengine bila silaha na kwa amani.

eng: I want her to love her country and learn, as a young African woman, to stand up and speak up.
swa: Ninamtaka aipende nchi yake na kujifunza kusimama na kudai kama mwanamke kijana wa kiafrika.

eng: When she grows up she, and others like her, will be the saviours of the broken, the beaten, and the damned.
swa: Atakapokuwa pamoja na wengine kama yeye watakuwa wakombozi wa waliovunja moyo, waliopigwa na kuupuzwa.

eng: Welcome to the Black Parade – and I hope the police are smart enough not to stain it blood-red.
swa: Karibu kwenye paredi ya waafrika – na ninamatumaini polisi wapo makini vya kutosha kutotia doa la damu maandamano.

eng: TV journalist Mujuni Raymond said that he would also join the protest:
swa: Mujuni Raymond ambaye ni mwandishi wa habari za runinga alisema kuwa naye angejiunga na maandamano hayo pia:

eng: I have been to the murder crime scenes of atleast 13 women, I have seen the gruesome nature their lives have been ended.
swa: Nimekuwa kwenye matukio ya mauaji ya wanawake karibu 13, nimeona maisha yao yalivyokatishwa vya kutisha.

eng: It's inhuman to only offer hope and prayers.
swa: Ubinadamu ni kuwaombea na kuwa na matumaini.

eng: Action must be taken.
swa: Lazima kuchukua hatua.

eng: Eventually, police gave in to the pressure.
swa: Mwishowe, askari polisi walikubali.

eng: The women’s march observed strict guidelines set by the police.
swa: Maandamano hayo ya wanawake yalifuata sana miongozo iliyotolewa na askari polisi.

eng: This is the first peaceful protest led by activists since the passing of the controversial Public Order Management Act 2013, which grants the Police's Inspector General wide discretion to permit or forbid public gatherings.
swa: Hii ni mara ya kwanza maandamano ya amani kufanywa na wanaharakati tangu kupitishwa sheria tatanishi ya usimamizi wa amani ya umma ya mwaka 2013, ambayo inampa mkuu wa polisi uhuru mkubwa wa kuruhusu au kuzuia mkusanyiko wa watu.

eng: Past protests since the Act was published have turned violent.
swa: Maandamano yaliyofuata baada ya sheria hiyo kupitishwa yalibadilika kuwa vurugu.

eng: The March wields more pressure on authorities not only to provide a safer society for women but also to uphold Uganda’s constitution and respect citizens' right to freedom of assembly.
swa: Maandamano hayo yalileta msukumo mkubwa kwa viongozi sio tu kuhakikisha usalama kwa wanawake bali pia kusimamia katiba ya watu wa Uganda na kuheshimu haki ya wananchi ya uhuru wa kukusanyika.

eng: Ugandans are standing up against a new tax on social media and Mobile Money.
swa: Waganda wameinuka kupinga kodi mpya ya mitandao ya kijamii na akaunti za fedha katika simu.

eng: On July 1, 2018, the Ugandan government started taxing citizens a fee of 200 Ugandan Shillings (USD $0.05) for using social media, raising substantial condemnation from Ugandans.
swa: Tarehe 1 Julai 2018, serikali ya Uganda ilianza kutoza kodi mitandao ya kijamii kwa wananchi kulipia shilingi za uganda 200 (sawa na dola za kimarekani 0.05) kwa kutumia mitandao ya kijamii hali iliyoibua lawama kubwa kutoka kwa waganda.

eng: With Uganda's average GDP per capita at USD $604.00, daily use of social media or messaging apps could eat up three percent of the average Ugandan's annual earnings.
swa: Kwa wastani pato la taifa la Uganda ni dola za kimarekani 604.00. Kwa matumizi ya mitandao ya kijamii na kutuma ujumbe kila siku inagharimu hadi asilimia tatu ya wastani wa mapato ya mwaka ya mwananchi wa kawaida wa Uganda.

eng: The fight to resist the social media tax took a legal twist on July 2 when concerned citizens approached the courts, claiming that the tax violates Uganda's constitution.
swa: Mapambano ya kupinga kodi ya mitandao ya kijamii ilichukua mlengo wa sheria tarehe 2 Julai pale wananchi husika walipopiga hodi mahakamani wakilalamika kwamba kodi hiyo inavunja katiba ya Uganda.

eng: Petitioners argued that the tax contravenes the human rights of Ugandans as enshrined in "the specified provisions of the 1995 Constitution of the Republic of Uganda".
swa: Walalamikaji walitoa hoja kwamba kodi hiyo ni kinyume na haki za binadamu za waganda kama ilivyoelezwa "katika vifungu vya katiba ya mwaka 1995 ya Jamhuri ya Uganda ".

eng: Kenyan newspaper The Daily Nation reports:
swa: Gazeti la Kenya linaripoti:

eng: The petition, filed by a team of young advocates under their Cyber Law Initiative (U) Limited and four individuals, Mr Opio Bill Daniel, Mr Baguma Moses, Mr Okiror Emmanuel and Mr Silver Kayondo against the attorney-general, is challenging the Constitutionality of the (200 USH) daily charge for access to social media platforms.
swa: Ombi liliwekwa na timu ya mawakili vijana chini ya kampuni yao ya Sheria ya Mtandao kwa kushirikiana na watu binafsi wanne ambao ni Mr Opio Bill Daniel, Mr Baguma Moses, Mr Okiror Emmanuel na Mr Silver Kayondo dhidi ya mwanasheria mkuu wakihoji kikatiba uhalali wa kulipa kila siku (shilingi za Uganda 200) kwa ajili ya kutumia majukwaa ya mitandao ya kijamii.

eng: The petition is particularly targeting several sections of the Excise Duty Amendment Act 2018, which provided for taxes on Over The Top (OTT) services from mobile telephone usage.
swa: Ombi hilo lililenga baadhi ya vifungu hasa vya sheria ya marekebisho ya mwaka ya 2018 ya ushuru wa bidhaa na huduma , ambayo iliweka kodi kwenye huduma za matumizi ya simu.

eng: The petitioners also implored the court to issue an order that will permanently halt payment on the social media tax.
swa: Pia, walalamikaji waliiomba mahakama kutoa amri ambayo itaondoa moja kwa moja malipo ya kodi ya mitandao ya kijamii.

eng: PCTech magazine reports:
swa: Gazeti la PCTech linaripoti:

eng: They want the court to issue an order, permanently stopping the government and all her agencies, authorities and officials from imposing any tax on internet or social media usage.
swa: Wanaiomba mahakama kutoa amri kwa serikali, mamlaka nyingine zinazohusika, mawakala na maafisa wake kusimamisha mara moja kuweka kodi yoyote kwa ajili ya mtandao na matumizi ya mitandao ya kijamii.

eng: In addition, they also want an order, directing the government and government regulatory body of the communications sector; Uganda Communication Commission (UCC) to only regulate OTT services in a manner that guarantees free access, net neutrality, and open internet.
swa: Pia, wanaiomba kutoa amri inayoelekeza serikali na chombo cha kudhibiti mawasiliano; Tume ya Mawasiliano Uganda kudhibiti huduma za mtandaoni katika njia inayowafanya watumiaji kupata mtandao kwa uhuru na kwa uwazi.

eng: Ugandan lawyer Silver Kayondo vowed to "fight up to the African Court on Human and Peoples Rights":
swa: Mwanasheria wa Uganda Silver Kayondo aliapa "kupambana hadi mahakama ya Afrika juu ya haki za binadamu ":

eng: #SocialMediaTax Petitioners have been joined by Raymond Mujuni in defence of OTT journalistic sources and #digital broadcasting.
swa: Raymond Mujuni aliungana na walalamikaji wa Kodi ya mitandao ya kijamii katika kuwalinda waandishi wa habari na matumizi ya mitandao ya kijamii na matangazo ya kidijitali.

eng: On our way to Court to file against the AG. UCC and URA added for consequential Orders. We'll fight up to the African Court on Human and Peoples Rights — Silver Kayondo (@SilverKayondo) July 2, 2018
swa: Tunaelekea mahakamani kuandikisha kesi dhidi ya mwanasheria mkuu, Tume ya mawasiliano na mamlaka ya mapato Uganda.Tutapambana hadi mahakama ya Afrika juu ya haki za binadamu.

eng: The Global Voices community, which we represent, has also taken a stand on the issue and organized a tweetathon in solidarity with activists in Uganda, set to take place on Monday, July 9.
swa: Jamii ya Global Voices ambayo tunawakilisha imechukua uamuzi juu ya suala hili na imepanga kutuma ujumbe wa mshikamano kwa wanaharakati wa Uganda siku ya Jumatatu, Julai 9.

eng: #NoToSocialMediaTax campaign poster.
swa: Hapana kwa bango la kampeni dhidi ya kodi ya mitandao ya kijamii.

eng: (Image designed by Innocent Amanyire @NinnoJackJr and used with permission)
swa: (Picha na Innocent Amanyire @NinnoJackJr na imetumia kwa ruhusa)

eng: As the legal battle ensues, questions around equity, justice, and access remain and need further investigation.
swa: Kutokana na vita ya sheria, maswali kuhusu usawa, haki na upatikanaji wa mtandao vinahitaji uchunguzi zaidi.

eng: According to a survey by the National Information Technology Authority, 77 percent of Ugandans cannot afford basic internet usage costs and only 22 percent of the total population currently uses the internet.
swa: Kutokana na utafiti uliofanywa na mamlaka ya taifa ya teknolojia ya habari, asilimia 77 ya waganda hawawezi gharama za matumizi ya msingi ya mtandao na 22 asilimia tu ya idadi ya watu katika nchi ya Uganda wanatumia mtandao.

eng: Rather than investing in infrastructure that could expand Ugandans' access to broadband connectivity, the government has imposed a social media tax seriously limits access while bringing more money to its own coffers.
swa: Badala ya kuwekeza katika miundo mbinu ambayo ingepanua upatikanaji wa uunganishwaji wa kihamisha taarifa-pepe kwenye mitandao kwa waganda, serikali imeweka kodi ya mitandao ya kijamii ambayo inazuia kabisa upatikanaji wake na wakati huo ikichota fedha kutoka kwenye hazina yake yenyewe.

eng: Critics see the tax as a form of double taxation because airtime and data were already taxed.
swa: Ukosoaji unaona kodi hiyo kama ina sura ya kodi mara mbili kwa sababu muda wa maongezi na taarifa –pepe vinakuwa vimeshakatwa kodi.

eng: Now, many users say they simply can not afford to pay the extra 200 USH per user per day to access web-based social and communication platforms, also known as over-the-top (OTT) services.
swa: Sasa watumiaji wengi wanasema hawawezi kukabili malipo ya sh. 200 zaidi kwa siku kupokea na kuwasiliana kupitia majukwaa ya mtandaoni; pia kama inavyojulikana matumizi mtandaoni ni muhimu.

eng: The tax widens the internet access gap not just for Ugandan youth and the poor, but also for women, furthering the gender digital divide.
swa: Kodi hiyo inaongeza na kupanua nafasi ya kutopata mtandao sio tu kwa vijana na watu maskini lakini pia kwa wanawake na inaongeza jinsia kutengwa kidijitali.

eng: Exempt the Rich: Tax the Poor. #SocialMediaTax pic.twitter.com/nUz0SdLNBr — Rwakakamba Morrison (@Rwakakamba) July 2, 2018
swa: Kuwasamehe matajiri: Kutoza kodi maskini. Mitandao ya kijamii

eng: Ugandan youth on social media frontlines feel the social media tax squeeze
swa: Vijana wa Uganda waliopo mstari wa mbele katika mitandao ya kijamii wanataka kodi ya mitandao ya kijamii kupunguzwa

eng: Uganda struggles with one of the highest unemployment rates in East Africa.
swa: Uganda ni nchi yenye kiasi kikubwa sana cha ukosefu wa ajira katika Afrika Mashariki.

eng: A 2014 Ugandan census report indicated that out of over 18 million people between the ages of 14 and 64, 58 percent were unemployed.
swa: Taarifa ya sensa ya mwaka 2014 Uganda inaonesha zaidi ya milioni 18 ya watu wenye miaka kati ya 14 na 64, asilimia 58 yao hawana ajira.

eng: At the same time, 52 percent of Ugandans owned mobile phones and 71 percent of these users live in rural areas, according to a 2014 report by the Uganda Communications Commission.
swa: Wakati huo, asilimia 52 ya waganda wanamiliki simumpanguso na asilimia 71 ya watumiaji simu hizo wanaishi vijijini. Kutokana na ripoti ya 2014 ilitolewa na Tume ya mawasiliano ya Uganda.

eng: Youth ages 15 to 24 years old are on the frontlines of smartphone usage and make up 28 percent of the population.
swa: Vijana kati ya miaka 15 na 24 wapo mstari wa mbele katika kutumia simumpanguso na ni asilimia 28 ya watu wa Uganda.

eng: Many rely on their phones and on WhatsApp to engage in businesses that run on mobile money.
swa: Wengi wao wanategemea simu zao kupata kazi hasa kupitia mtandao wa WhatsApp ambao huendeshwa na fedha zilizopo kwenye simu .

eng: They say they feel that the social media tax will only stifle entrepreneurship, ease of business, and creativity.
swa: Wanaona kuwa kodi ya mitandao ya kijamii inaua tu ujasiriamali, urahisi wa kufanya biashara na ubunifu.

eng: The Collaboration on International ICT Policy in East and Southern Africa (CIPESA) points out that just one gigabyte (GB) of data will now cost users nearly 40 percent of their average monthly income:
swa: Ushirikiano wa sera ya TEHAMA kimataifa katika Afrika Mashariki ilieleza kuwa gigabaiti (GB) moja tu ya taarifa-pepe itagharimu watumiaji wa mitandao karibu asilimia 40 ya wastani wa mapato yao kwa mwezi:

eng: Part 1: The cost to connect for #Uganda’s poorest will jump by 10%, resulting in just 1GB of data costing them nearly 40% of their average monthly income.
swa: Gharama ya kumuunganisha mwananchi maskini wa Uganda itapanda kwa 10% ambayo itakuwa GB moja tu ya taarifa-pepe ambayo itagharimu karibu 40% ya mapato yao kwa mwezi.

eng: The richest Ugandans will experience an increase of 1% in their cost to connect! @A4A_Internet #SocialMediaTax pic.twitter.com/aiYTtNReky — CIPESA (@cipesaug) July 1, 2018
swa: Matajiri wa Uganda watapata ongezeko la 1% katika gharama za kuunganisha!

eng: An affront to already over-burdened citizens
swa: Kutokuheshimu wananchi ambao tayari wana mzigo mkubwa

eng: The social media tax comes on the heels of the controversial social media "gossip tax" in April 2018 and is seen as an affront to already over-burdened citizens.
swa: Kodi ya mitandao ya kijamii imeanzishwa kutokana na mkanganyiko wa "kodi ya umbea kwenye mitandao ya kijamii "mwezi Aprili 2018 na inaonekana ni kutowajali wananchi ambao tayari wanamzigo mkubwa.

eng: At that time, President Museveni wrote:
swa: Wakati ule, Rais Mseveni alipoandika:

eng: I am not going to propose a tax on internet use for educational, research or reference purposes... these must remain free.
swa: Sitapendekeza kodi kwa matumizi ya mtandao kwa ajili ya madhumuni ya elimu, utafiti au rejea…..hayo lazima yatabaki kutolewa bure.

eng: However, olugambo (gossip) on social media (opinions, prejudices, insults, friendly chats) and advertisements by Google and I do not know who else must pay tax because we need resources to cope with the consequences of their lugambo.
swa: Hata hivyo, Ulugambo (Umbea)katika mitandao ya kijamii (maoni, chuki, matusi, maongezi ya kirafiki) na matangazo kupitia mtandao wa Google na sijui nani mwingine ambaye atalipa kodi kwasababu tunahitaji rasirimali kukabili athari za lugambo.

eng: The government's categorization of social media platforms as a luxury activity exposed a deep lack of digital literacy among policymakers in the Museveni government.
swa: Serikali kuainisha matumizi ya mitandao ya kijamii kuwa ni shughuli ya anasa kumefichua ukosefu mkubwa wa elimu ya kidijitali miongoni mwa watengeneza sera katika serikali ya Mseveni.

eng: Ugandan journalist Daniel K. Kalinaki succinctly summarized the impact of both the "gossip tax" and the "social media tax" on everyday Ugandan citizens:
swa: Mwandishi wa habari Uganda Daniel K. Kalinaki kwa ufupi alieleza matokeo ya kila siku kwa wananchi wa Uganda kutokana na "kodi ya umbea" na "kodi ya mitandao ya kijamii ":

eng: There are basically two problems with the social media tax.
swa: Kimsingi, kutokana na kodi ya mitandao ya kijamii kunaleta matatizo mawili.

eng: First, it shoots the wrong person twice: A Facebook user has already paid tax on the mobile phone, data and electricity; they are, except in a few cases, the product, not the revenue.
swa: Kwanza, mtu asiyehusika anaingia gharama mara mbili: Mtumiaji wa Facebook anakuwa ameshalipia kodi kupitia simu ya mkononi, taarifa-pepe na umeme pia; mara chache sana wanavyovizalisha havilipiwi kodi.

eng: The tax is like taking money at the gate then also charging for the seats in an empty stadium.
swa: Inaonekana kodi inachukua fedha mlangoni halafu tena inatoza gharama ya viti katika uwanja mtupu.

eng: Secondly, people generally don’t gossip or insult others for a living; they do so because they are idle, sad and often unemployed.
swa: Pili, kwa ujumla watu hawafanyi umbea au kutukana watu kwa ajili ya kuishi; wanafanya hivyo kwa sababu hawana la kufanya, wana masikitiko na hawana kazi.

eng: Imposing a tax to keep them quiet is the cyber equivalent of asking starving people who don’t have millet to eat red velvet chocolate cake instead.
swa: Kuweka kodi ili kunawafanya wawe kimya badala yake ni sawa na kuwaomba watu ambao hawana mtama wale keki ya velveti chokoleti nyekundu.

eng: This and the mobile money tax have taken many young and poor people, including many in the countryside who have never paid a direct tax, through the organ grinder of our tax system.
swa: Kodi ya mitandao ya kijamii na ya fedha ya muda wa maongezi kwenye simu imewafanya vijana na watu maskini wengi ukijumuisha watu waishio vijijini ambao waliokuwa hawajalipa kodi moja kwa moja kupitia mfumo wetu wa kodi.

eng: You can hear the screams from Kidera to Kyotera.
swa: Unaweza kusikia kelele hizo kutoka Kidera hadi Kyotera.

eng: Riot police closing in on protesters on May 5, 2018, in Moscow // DonSimon, CC0
swa: Kikosi cha polisi wakiwazuia waandamanaji hapo Mei 5, 2018 mjini Moscow // DonSimon, CC0

eng: Anti-corruption activists who protested against Vladimir Putin’s fourth inauguration as president have seen their tweets, and in some cases their retweets of others' publications, used by authorities as evidence of inciting mass disturbances.
swa: Wanaharakati wa kupinga rushwa walioandamana wakipings kuapishwa kwa Vladimir Putin kwa mara ya nne kama rais wameona machapisho yao waliyotuma na yale ya watu wengine walioshirikisha katika mtandao yakitumiwa na mamlaka kama ushahidi dhidi yao kwa kuchochea usumbufu kwa umma.

eng: On May 5, the Anti-Corruption Foundation (FBK), Russia’s leading opposition organization, held a series of rallies across Russia under the common slogan “He’s not a tzar to us."
swa: Hapo Mei 5, Shirika la kupambana na Rushwa (FBK), likiwa ndio chama cha upinzani kinachoongoza nchini Urusi, kiliandaa maandamano nchini kote wakitumia kauli mbiu moja ya "yeye sio Tzar kwetu."

eng: The demonstrations were met with violent resistance from both the police and loyalist groups.
swa: Maandamano hayo yalikutana na upinzani mkali kutoka kwa polisi na vikundi vinavyomuunga mkono Putin .

eng: In Moscow, the rally on Pushkinskaya square was attacked by men in Cossack uniforms (whom the government often uses as paramilitary squads to harass the opposition while avoiding blame for direct police involvement,) as well as by regular and riot police.
swa: Ndani ya Moscow, maandamano katika viwanja vya Pushkinskaya yalishambuliwa na wanaume waliokuwa wamevaa sare za waCossack (ambao serikali huwatumia mara nyingi kama kikosi cha wanajeshi cha kuwabughudhi wapinzani wakati wakiepuka lawama za polisi kujihusisha moja kwa moja,) pia kama mgambo na polisi wa kuzuia ghasia.

eng: Dozens of people were injured, including at least 25 reporters, and more than 1,600 were detained.
swa: Mamia ya watu walijeruhiwa wakiwemo wanahabari wapatao 25 na watu zaidi ya 1600 waliwekwa kizuizini.

eng: Several dozen participants were put to trial for "taking part in an unsanctioned protest" or "resisting police."
swa: Mamia kadhaa ya washiriki walipelekwa mahakamani kwa "Kushiriki katika maandamano yaliyozuiliwa" au "kubishana na polisi."

eng: Alexey Navalny, FBK’s leader who was arrested at the Moscow rally, was sentenced to 30 days in jail for “repeated violations of public order.”
swa: Kiongozi ws FBK Alexey Navalny, ambaye alikamatwa katika maandamano ya Moscow alihukumiwa kwenda gerezani kwa siku 30 kwa "kurudia rudia kuvunja usalama wa umma.”

eng: More arrests came after May 5.
swa: Ukamataji zaidi ulikuja baada ya Mei 5.

eng: Over the next weeks, 28 FBK organizers and activists in total were taken into custody, charged with inciting riots based on their tweets or retweets, according to the organization's lawyer Ivan Zhdanov — who himself was arrested on May 24.
swa: Kwa majuma yaliyofuata waandaaji na wanaharakati 28 wa FBK kwa ujumla waliwekwa kizuizini, wakishtakiwa kwa makosa ya kuchochea maandamano kulingana na machapisho yao katika mitandao ya tweeter, kulingana na mwanasheria wa shirika, Ivan Zhdanov — ambaye naye alikamatwa Mei 24.

eng: While some were only fined and released, others were sentenced to the longest possible term for a misdemeanor under Russian law, 30 days.
swa: Wakati baadhi yao walipigwa faini na kuachiliwa, wengine walifungwa siku 30 ambapo ni vifungo virefu zaidi katika sheria ya makosa madogo ya Urusi.

eng: Leonid Volkov, Navalny’s longtime campaign manager, said:
swa: Leonid Volkov, ambaye ni meneja wa kampeni siku nyingi wa Navalny alisema:

eng: Ivan Zhdanov has just been detained outside our office.
swa: Ivan Zhdanov amekamatwa nje ya ofisi yetu.

eng: He’s facing the same article 20.2 (but it’s his first time, so he’ll only get 10 days, not 30), so there goes another “organizing a rally by retweet.” Looks like this time they’re just locking up everyone.
swa: Atakumbana na kifungu kile kile cha 20.2 (lakini hii ni mara yake ya kwanza kwa hiyo atafungwa siku 10 tu na sio 30), hivyo hii tena inakuwa ni “kuandaa maandamano kwa njia ya kushirikisha machapisho ya tweeter” Inaonyesha kuwa kipindi hiki wanamfunga kila mtu.

eng: Elena Malakhovskaya, a news presenter on Navalny LIVE, FBK's YouTube channel, was arrested near her home for covering the May 5 protests on the channel — or "organizing an unsanctioned rally," according to the police.
swa: Elena Malakhovskaya, Mtangazaji wa habari wa Navalny LIVE, ambayo ni chaneli ya FBK huko YouTube alikamatwa karibu na nyumbani kwake kwa kurusha maandamano ya Mei 5 katika chaneli au " kuandaa maandamo yasiyo na kibali," kulingana na polisi.

eng: News presenter @elmalakhovskaya has been detained near her home.
swa: Mtangazaji wa habari @elmalakhovskaya amekamatwa karibu na nyumbani kwake.

eng: In most other cases, the incriminating evidence against FBK activists were their tweets or retweets.
swa: Katika kesi nyingine, ushahidi wa kuwatia hatiani baadhi ya wanaharakati wa FBK ulikuwa ni machapisho yao huko tweeter au kushirikisha machapisho ya watu wengine.

eng: For example, Kira Yarmysh, Navalny’s press officer, was sentenced to 25 days based on the following message:
swa: Kwa mfano, Kira Yarmysh, afisa habari wa Navalny alihukumiwa siki 25 gerezani kwa sababu ya ujumbe ufuatao:

eng: We did not vote for those in power.
swa: Hatukuwapigia kura hao waliopo madarakani.

eng: To go out and protest on the 5th of May means to say to yourself and those around you: I don’t agree with what’s happening.
swa: Kutoka na kuandamana hapo Mei 5 ni sawa na kujiambia wewe na wale wanaokuzunguka kuwa: Siafikiani na yale yanayotokea.

eng: Since we have been deprived of our right to choose, the only way to make our voices heard is this: https://t.co/2k3nFrTs1S
swa: Kwa kuwa tumenyimwa haki yetu ya kuchagua, njia pekee ya kufanya sauti zetu zisikike ni hii: https://t.co/2k3nFrTs1S

eng: Yarmysh’s tweet links to a YouTube video on Navalny’s channel promoting the May 5 rally.
swa: Chapisho hili la Yarmysh liliunganishwa na video kutoka chaneli ya Youtube ya Navalny iliyokuwa ikihamasisha maandamano ya Mei 5.

eng: The video has accumulated over 3 million views at the time of writing.
swa: Video hiyo imejikusanyia zaidi ya waangaliaji zaidi ya milioni 3 kwa wakati alipobandika chapisho hilo.

eng: Another Navalny LIVE host, Ruslan Shavetdinov, was also jailed for 30 days based on his retweet of a similar message — although he was merely one of many thousands to do so.
swa: Mtangazaji mwingine wa Navalny LIVE Ruslan Shavetdinov, alifungwa gerezani siku 30 kutokana na kushirikisha ujumbe huo huo wa chapisho la tweeter ingawa alikuwa mmoja wa maelfu ya watu waliofanya hivyo.

eng: Human rights groups are saying this is part of a larger trend where more and more Russians are jailed for their online activity.
swa: Makundi ya Haki za Binadamu yanasema kuwa hii ni moja ya mwenendo mkubwa ambapo Warusi zaidi na zaidi wanafungwa kutokana na shughuli zao za mitandaoni. .

eng: Agora, a pro-bono law firm that offers legal assistance to defendants in such cases, says the number of prosecutions for posts and even reposts on social media in Russia is growing exponentially.
swa: Agora, taasisi ya kisheria inayotoa huduma za kisheria bure kwa watuhumiwa katika makosa kama hayo wanasema idadi ya watuhumiwa kutokana na machapisho mitandaoni au kushirikisha machapisho katika mitandao ya jamii nchini Urusi inaongezeka kwa kasi sana.

eng: According to their latest report, in 2017 a Russian internet user was sent to jail every eight days.
swa: Kulingana na taarifa yao ya hivi karibuni, mwaka 2017 kwa kila siku nane mtumiaji mmoja wa mtandao huko Urusi alikuwa akipelekwa gerezani.

eng: Orkhan Dzhemal, 51, a veteran war reporter from Russia, killed on July 31, 2018, in Central African Republic // Screenshot from Echo of Moscow, YouTube
swa: Orkhan Dzhemal mwenye miaka 51 ambaye alikuwa mwandishi wa habari mkongwe wa Urusi aliuwa tarehe 31 Julai, 2018 katika Jamhuri ya Afrika ya kati// Picha ya YouTube kutoka Moscow,

eng: Three Russian journalists were killed on the night of July 30 in Central African Republic, at a checkpoint outside the country’s capital Bangui.
swa: Waandishi wa habari watatu waliuwa usiku wa tarehe 30 Julai katika Jamhuri ya Afrika ya kati kwenye kituo cha ukaguzi nje kidogo ya mji mkuu wa nchi hiyo wa Bangui.

eng: Veteran reporter Orkhan Dzhemal, award-winning filmmaker Aleksandr Rastorguev and cameraman Kirill Radchenko were shot and killed by unidentified assailants who emerged from the bushes at roadside when they arrived.
swa: Mwandishi wa habari mkongwe Orkhan Dzhemal, mshindi wa tuzo ya mtengeneza filamu Aleksandr Rastorguev na mpiga picha Kirill Radchenko walipigwa risasi na kuuawa walipokuwa wanakaribia kuingia mjini na wauaji wasiojulikana waliokuwa wamejificha katika vichaka kando kando ya barabara kuu inayoingia mji mkuu Bangui.

eng: The attack took place amid an on-going conflict between the country’s government and various rebel groups.
swa: Shambulio hilo limetokea wakati kuna mgogoro unaoendelea kati ya serikali na vikundi mbambali vya waasi.

eng: Their deaths were confirmed by the Investigations Control Center (TsUR, Tsentr Upravleniya Rassledovaniyami), an investigative reporting outlet funded by Mikhail Khodorkovsky, a former oil magnate currently living in exile in London.
swa: Vifo vyao vilithibitishwa na kituo cha kudhibiti uchunguzi(TsUR) kinachotoa taarifa za uchunguzi kinachodhaminiwa na Mikhail Khodorkovsky ambaye ni mfanyabiashara wa zamani wa mafuta anayeishi uhamishoni hoko London.

eng: According The Moscow Times, Russia has supplied arms and deployed training teams to aid CAR government security forces.
swa: Kutokana na gazeti la Moscow Times, Urusi imetoa askari na mafunzo ya kijeshi kusaidia majeshi ya usalama ya serikali.

eng: According to TsUR, on whose assignment Dzhemal, Rastorguev and Radchenko went to CAR, the journalists were pursuing a news tip about a group of armed Russian mercenaries sighted in the African country.
swa: Kutokana na taarifa ya kituo cha kudhibiti uchunguzi, waandishi wa habari hao walikuwa wanafuatilia taarifa ya kikundi cha mamluki wa jeshi la Urusi ambao wapo katika nchi ya Afrika.

eng: This armed group's existence has never been officially acknowledged, although numerous journalistic investigations pinpointed the so-called ‘Wagner Group’ in hotspots such as Syria and Eastern Ukraine.
swa: Kundi hilo la jeshi halijawahi kuthibitishwa rasmi kuwepo ingawa uchunguzi mwingi wa kijeshi zinataja kundi linalojiita ‘Wagner Group’ kuwa lipo katika maeneo ya hatari ya Syria na mashariki ya Ukraine.

eng: Although he is consistently denying the allegations, the ‘Wagner Group’ is widely believed to be funded by Evgeny Prigozhin, a powerful businessman with strong ties to Vladimir Putin, sanctioned by the U.S. for his alleged — and, again, never acknowledged — involvement in the 2016 presidential elections.
swa: Ingawa mfanyabiashara mashuri Evgeny Prigozhin amabye ana mahusiano makubwa na Vladimir Putin anahusishwa na kulidhamini kikundi hicho cha ‘Wagner Group’ ingawa yeye amekanusha madai hayo mara nyingi. Kutokana na madai hayo Evgeny Prigozhin aliwekewa vikwazo na Marekani vya kutoshiriki katika uchaguzi wa Rais wa mwaka 2016— hata hivyo hakukubali.

eng: Dzhemal, Rastorguev and Radchenko were highly respected media professionals, recognized by the industry.
swa: Dzhemal, Rastorguev and Radchenko walikuwa ni wanahabari mahiri walioheshimika sana na waliokuwa wanatambuliwa katika taaluma hiyo.

eng: Orkhan Dzhemal was a renowned war reporter, his career stretching back to the early years of Russia’s independent press.
swa: Orkhan Dzhemal alikuwa mashuhuri kwa kuripoti taarifa za vita, na kazi yake ilianza mwanzoni mwa miaka ya uhuru wa habari Urusi.

eng: Alexander Rastorguev was praised for his vivid chronicle of Russia’s failed anti-Putin opposition surge in his 2013 documentary “The Term” (Srok.)
swa: Alexander Rastorguev alipongezwa sana kutokana na kuandika tahiri mwaka 2013 ya kuongezeka kwa upinzani dhidi ya Putin.

eng: Kirill Radchenko worked as a TV reporter in war zones such as Syria.
swa: Neno Kirill Radchenko lilitumika kama mtangazaji wa runinga katika kanda za vita kama za Siria.

eng: Detail from the graphic made by Pictoline.
swa: Taarifa kutoka kwenye picha zimetengenezwa na Pictoline.

eng: The numbers reflect the number of politicians assassinated since the beginning of the electoral process.
swa: Namba zinamaanisha idadi ya wanasiasa waliouawa katika kipindi chote cha mchakato wa uchaguzi.

eng: “Mexico is living through the most violent electoral process of recent years and the statistics are alarming".
swa: “Mexico ipo katika kipindi cha vurugu za mchakato wa uchaguzi katika miaka ya hivi karibuni na takwimu ni za kutisha".

eng: Image used with permission.
swa: Picha imetumika kwa ruhusa.

eng: This is the third installment in our series on Mexico’s upcoming elections on 1 July 2018.
swa: Hii ni sehemu ya tatu ya mfululizo wetu wa uchaguzi wa Mexico unaofanyika hapo Julai 1, 2018.

eng: In the first post we looked at the background of Mexican democracy after 70 years of a hegemonic party in power.
swa: Katika chapisho la awali tumeangalia historia ya Demokrasia ya Mexico baada ya miaka 70 ya chama tawala.

eng: In the second piece we looked briefly at each of the four aspiring presidential candidates.
swa: Sehemu ya pili tuliangalia kwa ufupi kila mgombea kati ya wagombea wanne wa urais.

eng: In this latest post, we turn our attention to the opinion polls and the general state of the country.
swa: Katika chapisho hili la sasa, tunaangalia mitazamo ya kura za maoni na hali ya nchi kwa ujumla.

eng: What do the polls say?
swa: Kura za maoni zinasemaje?

eng: Following the three debates officially organized by the electoral authorities, there are approximately two weeks left until Mexicans go to the ballot box.
swa: Kufuatia midahalo mitatu iliyoandaliwa na mamlaka rasmi za uchaguzi, zimebaki angalau wiki mbili Mexico iingie katika sanduku la kura.

eng: The pollsters (Consulta Mitofsky, B&L, GCE to mention a few) and analyses of polling averages (Oraculus) all identify a clear leader.
swa: Watafiti wa masuala ya uchaguzi (Consulta Mitofsky, B&L, GCE kwa kuwataja wachache) na wachambuzi wa uwiano katika upigaji kura (Oraculus) wote walimtambua kiongozi sawia.

eng: All consistently report Andrés M. López in the lead, approaching 50% of voting count, followed – although not closely – by Ricardo Anaya.
swa: Mara kwa mara wote waliripoti kuwa Andrés M. López ndiye alikuwa akiongoza akikaribia asilimia 50% kwa kura zilizohesabiwa, akifuatiwa lakini sio kwa karibu na Ricardo Anaya.

eng: As we discussed in the last part of this series, Andrés M. López was put forward by the political party he founded (Movimiento Regeneración Nacional – MORENA) after having made two previous unsuccessful bids.
swa: Kama tulivyojadiliana katika sehemu ya mwisho ya mfululizo huu, Andrés M. López aliwekwa kugombea tena na chama alichokiunda mwenyewe (Movimiento Regeneración Nacional – MORENA) baada ya hapo nyuma kujaribu mara mbili na kushindwa.

eng: As noted in the first piece, Mexico has been suffering the consequences of an armed conflict since 2006 when then-president Felipe Calderón declared 'war' on organized crime.

swa: Wiki chache zilizopita Eduardo Guerrero alimtaja mshindi kwa hakika katika uchaguzi wa 2018 katika makala yake ya El Financiero.

eng: He did not make projections with the data taken by the polls.
swa: Hakutoa makadirio kupitia takwimu zilizochukuliwa na mamlaka za uchaguzi.

swa: Hakumaanisha uchaguzi wa urais.

swa: Alikuwa akizungumzia vikundi vya uhalifu ambavyo bila hata kupiga kura huamua uchaguzi.

eng: We can be sure that the criminals will win, the security expert said.
swa: Tuna uhakika kuwa vikundi vya uhalifu vitashinda, mtaalam wa masuala ya ulinzi alisema.

eng: They will win because they are eliminating their enemies and because they have dominated those who will occupy positions in the town halls which are vital for their interests.
swa: Watashinda kwa sababu ya kuwaondoa maadui zao na kwa sababu wanawahodhi wale watakaoshikilia nafasi hizo katika mamlaka za miji ambapo ni muhimu kwa maslahi yao.
